formatted_address: 727 7th Ave, New York, NY 10019, United States
name: Lagos TSQ

reviews.text: was my first time going to Lagos, I had a great experience at this restaurant. The food was very flavorful and delicious, definitely cooked with love. The atmosphere was welcoming and comfortable, making it a great place to relax and enjoy a meal. I had the jollof rice with slow cooked chicken as main course and macaroni and cheese with crabmeat. GREAT 🍸 also...On top of that, the service was excellent, the staff were friendly, attentive, and made sure everything was perfect. I would definitely recommend this place and would be happy to come back again. Great location, in time square, close to the train station. Its best to make reservation.

Had a great time at Lagos TSQ.

Food: I’d heard great reviews and was happy to finally try it. The food didn’t come out quickly though — we waited about 40 minutes. I ordered Nigerian stew with a side of rice and fish as the protein. The stew tasted legit, but the rice wasn’t what Nigerians would typically use (jasmine), which threw me off a bit. I was pleasantly surprised that it came with two large pieces of fish. Overall, I’d say the price point was fair.

Service: The place was packed. I went with my siblings on New Year’s Day around 5pm, and despite the full house, Hailey really tried her best.

Atmosphere: We were seated on the top floor, which felt more geared toward upbeat partying than quiet dining. The music was loud, but still great. Shoutout to the DJ.

Atmosphere was lovely.  The hosts and server Haley were very welcoming, and professional.  Great atmosphere, we didnt venture to the 2nd fl, but dining area and bar are spacious.  The loaded Moi Moi was spicy and delicious, we had Lagos fried rice, curry goat, snapper, all of which were huge portions, we each had left overs.  OMG the lychee martinis are to die for.
Overall experience 5 out of 5.

Vibes vibes vibes! And more vibes!
We made reservations but, they were so busy - they forgot us at the bar. Ended up spending our time at the bar which was still amazing. The bar tenders kept us entertained while also providing great recommendations for food and drink. The food was very well portioned for the price and everything was veryy tasty

Update from 12/30: I truly love this restaurant, which makes this experience even more disappointing. I’m a loyal, returning customer, but the way I was treated on the 30th was unacceptable.

I ordered two plates of white rice with red stew and turkey, as well as jollof rice. Instead, I received plain white rice with no stew and curry fried rice. When I called to report the issue, I was placed on hold for over 30 minutes. Eventually, I was told I had to request a refund through Uber Eats. Unfortunately, Uber Eats did not issue a full refund, so I essentially wasted $140 that day. The only thing I could eat was the turkey, and even that was disappointing—it was overly large and poorly seasoned.

If jollof rice was unavailable, I should have been called instead of having my order substituted without my consent. And I truly don’t understand how white rice can be sent without stew. What made the situation worse was the lack of remorse from the staff. Someone took my phone number on Tuesday and promised a call back, but it’s now almost Friday and I still haven’t heard from anyone.This experience was extremely disappointing.

I’m in NYC for work and I order from this restaurant at least twice a week—never once had a complaint. The food is consistently delicious, the portions are generous, and the quality never misses. My go-to meal is the rice and stew with peppered turkey, hands down the best thing on the menu.
Today I finally dined in person and loved every moment of it. The DJ was a vibe, and the fried yam and snail are officially my new favorites. I truly love this place, and y’all definitely will be seeing a lot more of me while I’m still in town!

formatted_address: 2267 Adam Clayton Powell Jr Blvd, New York, NY 10027, United States
name: Africa Kine

reviews.text:
Wow the food was amazing meal ,, in fact marvelous improvement. Shawarma was super, wheat and vegetable soup sweet ,, finish my portion . Any Time I end my food like it means the food is good
Shout out to African kingdom
The food is delicious and the wait time is low. It’s nice to see authentic restaurants like this. The portions are ENORMOUS 🤯 wow, definitely worth the price.

Africa Kine is a whole vibe. I’ve been twice now, and each time the food has blown me away. Senegalese cuisine is officially becoming a fave, and this spot is leading the charge. The Dibi? Fire. The grilled fish? Perfectly seasoned. The hologram and vermicelli combo? Chef’s kiss.

The portions are generous, the flavors are bold, and the service is always warm. Bonus points: it’s right next to Shrine, a live music venue with an Afrobeats party that goes off—so you can eat good and then dance it all off.

Ohmygosh, I loved the food and finished all I ordered and I don’t usually finish. I got the lamb dish with peanut sauce and definitely recommend trying the ginger juice!
Wish they had a branch in DC area but now I know and will be back!
And the portions are pretty good! I struggled to finish my food but am visiting so didn’t want to waste any of it 😬

I spent a memorable evening at this place. Staff was exceptional!! The dishes deliver flavor, freshness, and visual appeal consistently. Superior choice. All features here work for me and I'll become a frequent customer !

formatted_address: 243 W 116th St, New York, NY 10026, United States
name: Pikine

reviews.text: Went there for dinner with my mum. Had the impression that the fish served was already used by prior customer. Also it tasted very dry and barely flavour. Also the dibi meat was very poor quality and not what you imagine under dibi Senegal. It was rather roti. Very disappointed.

My brief visit was highlighted by this excellent meal. The portions are big and the staff is very friendly. You'll want to keep this discovery to yourself. Our dishes took extra time to arrive and drink service was lagging behind. This place earned my repeat business.

It was for lunch after my daughter’s college graduation. The service was slow to me. We sat there  for a good while before someone came to our table. I don’t think they gave us a menu. However, we ordered the food and drinks. Pineapple ginger beer was the best drink I had. Food was also very good. It was a lot of food. I wish the server explained more about the dishes. They were more attentive for other people. Maybe they were regular customers? Even though I was not impressed by their service, the food was worth it.

The food was incredibly good. This spot was recommended by a Senegalese friend. We asked the cashier (who doubles as the waitress too) what dishes she would recommend and she didn't miss. The ginger juice is definitely worth having.
It got very noisy as more patrons came in and I wish they can try to watch this part because it can be slightly annoying when you can't hear the person you are dining with.

Lovely foray into Senegalese cuisine. The Thiebou Djeun (fish stew) and Thiebou Yapp (lamb dish) were phenomenally plated, generously portioned, and tasted as flavorful as meat and carbs can be. Lively, down to earth atmosphere that’s cozy and feels authentic to the area: you see mostly locals and people who know how to eat good food. Be prepared to take your time and breathe in the good vibes and good company :)

formatted_address: 239 W 116th St, New York, NY 10026, United States
name: La Savane d'Afrique

reviews.text: Each and every item was delicious, and it was such a variety of flavors. We had the Dibi Mouton, which was extremely juicy and flavorful. Just keep in mind, the mutton quantity is quite large. I can eat a lot, but even I couldn't finish it. Even the atieke and the salad that came with it worked as beautiful mouth refresher. Fataya too were tasty. Overall, it was a great experience.  Will come here again.

La Savane d'Afrique is serving some of the most delicious dishes from western sub saharan Africa with the attieké, alloco, multiple types of grilled meat, and fish.
The food was absolutely delicious. The service by Zeinab was nothing short of exceptional. A better job could be done with the wine list, but that's another topic. They do offer some cocktails. They environment is clean and well decorated. I recommend this place the next time you go to Harlem.

So good!
The location itself is quite small and they ran out of alot of their seafood options but still what we ordered slapped.
We got the fried, whole fish with jollof rice. The fish was super fresh and crispy yet flatlet on the inside. It came with a small container of hot sauce that wasn't ridiculously spicy but perfect and then a very well seasoned vegetable salad/ marinade mix that was also so fire.
Price and portions arent bad either. You get full off $25 and may still have leftovers. Highly recommend!

You'll notice the friendly service right away. The team handles busy periods smoothly. Their plates arrive with satisfying amounts. This restaurant pairs good looks with sincere welcomes. Coming to this spot was the right decision!

The popular opinion seemed suspect until my own experience confirmed it. This place combines strategic location, helpful people, and fair prices. The flavors are clean and natural. The manager is professional and friendly. This spot deserves continued patronage.

formatted_address: 601 Lexington Avenue, 153 E 53rd St, New York, NY 10022, United States
name: Teranga Midtown

reviews.text:
Fantastic West African food spot nestled in a food hall with lots of places to sit. The food was absolutely incredible. Expect a bit of a kick, but the Chicken Suya with mango salad and sweet plantains is to die for. It’s also well priced! I got my bowl and a drink for like $20.

The mint limeade is like a sweet twist okay those super juices with protein and fiber and all, but like actually delicious? Can’t wait to show more people this spot.

The food here was absolutely delicious, even in the middle of a busy food court! The cashier seemed a little tired but still remained polite and pleasant, which I appreciated. Everything we ordered tasted great, and it’s a perfect spot for anyone looking for vegan, vegetarian, or gluten free options. Definitely worth trying!

Delicious food court meal; and had I been served this in a fine dining establishment I would also think it was really good.
I had the spicy chicken with yellow rice because they were out of red rice, along with beans and mango kale salad.

The Hugh has such a wonderful atmosphere to grab lunch. Very open, natural light, and lots of seating. The food was great. I really love the plantains that come with the food and felt full after eating. The jollof rice was overcooked but had great flavor. Put some salt and pepper on the food especially for plantains. Little interesting taste from the warm chicken to the cold peas.

I got the grilled chicken with rice, plantains, and kale and mango salad. It was delicious — remarkably fresh and each item was expertly prepared. The chicken was super tender and flavorful (the pic doesn’t do it justice), the plantains were the best I’ve ever had, and the kale salad was so refreshing. The man working there was very kind, too. I highly recommend this place and wish I lived closer so I could get it regularly. I’m already craving it again. 🤤

The Hugh is also a nice place to eat. There’s a good amount of seating and a clean restroom.

formatted_address: 348 Lenox Ave, New York, NY 10027, United States
name: Azara Kitchen LLC

reviews.text:
We happened to come across this amazing place and we couldn't have been happier!
It's small, gorgeous and the best background music. All the food was perfect and we tried all new things. The chef came out after our meal to check on us and we were able to rave about the food and experience. Highly recommend!

Wonderful restaurant! My friend had his birthday dinner here and the staff was so friendly and kind, and the owner was constantly making sure we were good. The food was amazing as well! I loved the Dibi Lamb, the Bissap and Ginger juices tasted so nice, but the suya was phenomenal. Also, they make a fantastic Tiramisu cake!! Highly recommend and you’ll enjoy your time here :)

Absolutely delicious West African food! Wow! The chef here - from Burkina Faso - really knows what he is doing. Stunning find. Highly recommended!

Maffe lamb - so tender with the tastiest sauce.

Jollof w/ fish - so delicious! Best I’ve had outside of Senegal.

Service was friendly and accommodating.

My fiancé and I were so excited to try this place. We saw reviews online stating that the food was delicious. We came in on Wednesday afternoon at about 5:45pm. There was only one other couple seated to eat. The waiters took our order. We initially ordered the Vegetable Nem as an appetizer, and also ordered our entrees at the same time. Literally 25 minutes goes by and the waitress tell us they are out of the Vegetable Nem—— why did it take so long to tell us idk. So we reluctantly ordered the Brussel sprouts ( i’m pescatarian). They arrived another 20 mins later— they were SOOOOOO BLAND. No seasoning at all and with a tiny dish of what tasted like French dressing. We already knew from then that everything was about to be below standard. About 15 mins after that the waitress brings my meal, and I at first refused to eat because my fiancé didn’t receive his entree. After about 10 mins of me eating she comes over to use to confirm our orders….and we have to remind her of what his meal is! I am sure she never put the order in. After my fiancé’s insistence I eat so my food won’t get cold: I had the Atieke with fish. The meal was very subpar, flavors were off! I am Malian, I know my Atieke, this was NOT it. My fiancé’s food literally come another 20 mins later. He was so disappointed in the lack of flavor. His meal - the Jollof Rice w/Lamb literally came with 3 chunks of lamb with only ONE having actual meat and the other two fatty pieces. The waitress was apologetic and she did offer us a complimentary Crème Brûlée, which I mean was good- but not made fresh. I would NOT recommend this restaurant. We came all the way from Brooklyn to try it out left EXTREMELY DISSAPPOINTED. Don’t waste your TIME OR hard earned $$$$ in this economy.

Once a month I get together with my sister friend for a meal at a new place. Don't need to write a lot of this place. The food was 🔥🔥🔥. Don't be afraid to try African food from different countries. you will not be disappointed.  We can't wait to get back their.

formatted_address: 120 W 116th St, New York, NY 10026, United States
name: Le Baobab Gouygui

reviews.text:
Omg! I've been craving some delicious, authentic African food. My beautiful coworkers recommended this spot. I been seeing them eat this delicious Djollof and finally decided to try it. I was so excited to see a fish option with the Djollof rice. It was amazing, delightful flavoring, a bunch of large pieces of veggies like cabbage, eggplant, carrot... I will definitely be back for more. I can't wait for my Father to try this Blessed African food from Senegal. Blessings, Protection and Positive energy over my indigenous Brothers and Sisters worldwide.

No evils or negativity shall prosper against my Family, Friends and Devotees in any Time, Dimension or Space.
Love Always Wins and
The Love is Established.
Asé

I was born and raised in Harlem, but obviously had not spent enough time in Little Senegal. When I tell you my eyes welled up upon tasting their Thieboudienne a.k.a. “OG Jollof rice”…

Had later told my date “He had ruined me; and this is the only rice I ever wanted to eat.”

I want to marry that beautiful Senegalese man. 🤫shh…

The team here creates a warm feeling that enhances every meal. This place impresses time after time. The food offers guilt-free deliciousness. The employees showed kindness in every interaction. I intend to dine at this restaurant again.
The food here is extremely tasty, and you get a huge portion for the price. I would highly Highly reccomend for takeout or a quick bite in the area

Le Baobab Gouygui has earned our sincere recommendation to others. The workers' care for guests is why this place succeeds. Their excellence is evident in meal preparation and service behavior. The atmosphere avoided stiffness, embracing warmth. The restaurant will satisfy your needs.

formatted_address: 1111 Fulton St, Brooklyn, NY 11238, United States
name: Buka

reviews.text: Great food but they have gotten smaller with the portions over the years. I ordered goat soup for $17 and I got 2 pieces of meat…. The egusi, spinach and okra all came 1/3 full. Do better…. Couldn’t even share with my friend.

I had an amazing lunch experience at Buka Restaurant! The food was delicious, atmosphere was cozy, and customer service was top-notch. For $20-$30, I got great value. The staff were attentive and made my meal stress-free. I truly enjoyed my lunch and would highly recommend Buka Restaurant to anyone looking for a satisfying dining experience.
Delicious food and the staff was so kind!! Highly recommend! We got the beef tomato stew with egusi, palava sauce, white yam fufu and eba. A must visit for comforting Nigerian food 😊

So this is what they said cost $17??? For pepper soup? There was barely any soup. What you see here is me adding water to it and had to add my own spices to make it up. This is wild!! And when you go there, pepper soup didn't even have the price listed on their menu. I will NEVER go here again. Not only that, I ordered Jallof rice which $7. That's fine, but the guy then asked if I wanted to add chicken to the rice. Who would've thought adding chicken would be $16??? And it didn't even taste good 😕 the price of adding chicken wasn't on the menu either. This is a huge disappointment in the West African community.

My mom said she was in the mood for Fufu. We called an African restaurant but they didn’t have it. The lady was so nice, she told us to go to 1111 Fulton street so we did. We were not disappointed. The owners greeted us as soon as we opened the door. Very nice people. We ordered two Fufu meals and paid about $44 altogether. We tried the beef and goat along with Egusi and Ego. Mouth watering food okay. That goat SLAPPED !!! I think they just made me fall in love with Nigerian food. The restaurant has limited seats and it’s not really a cozy set up to eat in, I would order out which we did. I’ve already recommended this place to others. I will certainly be back.

formatted_address: 10 Lincoln Center Plaza, New York, NY 10023, United States
name: Tatiana by Kwame Onwuachi

reviews.text:
I have been looking forward to this place all year only to be disappointed. First it’s the atmosphere. They play good music but that’s about it. The place is small with tall ceilings but the tables are right next to one another. Nothing impressive about the decor at all. As soon as we sat down for our 9:30 reservation, they waitress told us they ran out of the pastrami and caviar for the corn bread. The food wasn’t that impressive. Three pieces of oxtail in a giant pot. They were too large in size in my opinion and the sauce was regular and nothing impressive. The rice was bland and the branzino had a good sauce on top but I don’t think that frying it was best. The goat patties was the best thing in my opinion.

Overall I think this restaurant is taking traditional Caribbean cuisine and instead of making it more flavorful or even fusion style, it lacked.

You’re basically paying for a location and a hard to get into place.

I finally made it to Tatiana in Lincoln Square, and I can absolutely see why it was rated the #1 restaurant in NYC in both 2023 and 2024. I’d been hearing about this spot since the summer, and getting a reservation was extremely difficult, definitely one of the hardest in the city. One thing I really appreciate is that they don’t charge a reservation fee, unlike places that hit you with $50 per person just to hold a table.

The atmosphere is incredible. The restaurant is all glass, the lighting is dark and elegant, and the décor is beautiful. When you step outside, you’re right in front of the Lincoln Center fountain. Even the view from the bathroom is impressive.

Drinks: The POG Nutcracker was great, but the Panchito was the standout for me. The cinnamon grapefruit cordial gives it a smooth, memorable finish. Highly recommend.

Food: We ordered the Curried Goat Patties, Papaya Piri Piri Salad, Braised Oxtails, and the Brown Chicken. Every single dish was spectacular, bold flavors, perfectly prepared, and truly deserving of the hype.

Dessert: We finished with the Paleta, and if you’re feeling full, I highly recommend it. It’s refreshing, light, and something you can actually finish after a big meal.

Just a heads-up: the restaurant is very loud. I didn’t mind because the vibe is fun and the R&B throwback soundtrack is amazing, but you’ll definitely need to speak up to hear your guests.

Price: Yes, Tatiana is pricey. My total came out to about $350 for the bill plus a $100 tip but trust me, it is worth every penny. This isn’t just dinner; it’s an experience.

The hospitality here is next-level. From the moment we walked in, we were greeted warmly and taken care of. Our server, Carla, was extremely professional, kind, and explained the menu in detail. The Dominican gentleman who brought out our food was also very friendly and professional. Everyone made us feel welcomed and important.

Overall, Tatiana exceeded every expectation. The food, drinks, music, atmosphere, and service were all top-tier. I will definitely be back in December.

As good as you have been told, however I really want to highlight the service which may have been the best I have experienced. The waitress was an older Latina woman who was spectacular. The braised ox tail was the tenderest version of it I have ever had. The stewed chicken was the perfect amount of spice, I loved it. The mango chutney with the empanadas was awesome. The rib was great also. The side car cocktail was awesome. The rice, doubles and the cosmic brownie was great but I definitely have had better versions. The music was perfect pure vibes and at the correct volume. The staff really shines here I cant explain how good they were. Overall worth the hype they receive. Would absolutely return.

I went to Tatiana during my birthday trip to New York, and honestly, it ended up being one of the best dining experiences I’ve ever had! We showed up on a Saturday around 3:50 with no reservation, and there was already a line forming. By 4:30, the staff came out with complimentary tea for everyone waiting, which I thought was such a thoughtful touch.

Right at 5:00, the doors opened and we were able to choose between sitting outside or at the bar we went with the bar, and I’m so glad we did! The energy was perfect great music, good vibes, and the friendliest staff you could ask for. Everyone was so polite, warm, and genuinely happy to be there.

We ordered the lamb ribs, pastrami, oxtails, and curry goat empanadas. Let me tell you the lamb ribs were the best thing I’ve ever eaten in my life. I’m still thinking about them days later! The empanadas and oxtails were also full of flavor and perfectly cooked. The pastrami was just okay to me, but everything else completely made up for it. Since it was my birthday, they surprised us with a complimentary dessert a brownie, powdered doughnut, and ice cream and it was the sweetest ending to an amazing meal.

Between the food, atmosphere, music, and incredible staff, I couldn’t have asked for a better experience. If you’re ever in NYC, Tatiana is a must. I’d rate it 10/10 highly recommend!

I’m gonna give this a perfect score. I feel like people commonly criticize the prices but my feeling was yes, they are a bit high and going even higher in the last year, but look at it as a location surcharge. Look at where you are dining. They probably have rent to pay like any restaurant and I’m sure it’s not cheap. Overall the food, service and atmosphere were top notch. The most unforgettable element for us was the service. From the minute we stepped in the door we were treated like the most important people in the room, and this was made all the more impressive later in our meal when we realized Jay Z and Beyoncé were dining on the other side of the restaurant. This didn’t stop the maitre d from checking on a couple of walk ins multiple times throughout our meal, and our server offering us a complimentary dessert because he could tell we were really torn between two options. It’s incredible to feel so taken care of. Beyond that, everything we ordered was delicious, hot, complex and really interesting. Hats off to this team, we will be back!

formatted_address: Inside Giant Farmers Market, 324 Main St, Hackensack, NJ 07601, United States
name: Voilà Afrique

reviews.text: Voila Afrique did not disappoint! I ordered the pounded yam with oxtail and goat soup, and it was packed with rich flavor and the perfect amount of spice. My mom had the chicken with tomato stew and jollof rice, and she loved every bite. Everything tasted fresh, well-seasoned, and authentic. We both truly enjoyed our meals and will definitely be back!

i normally don’t leave reviews, but i absolutely had to for this place. everything was amazing from start to finish. we were honestly lost for words. i had the jollof rice with salmon and it was cooked perfectly, so flavorful and fresh. my mom had the fufu with egusi and fish and loved it just as much. on top of that, the owner was incredibly kind and even gave us some donuts, which were really good. amazing food, amazing service, and such a welcoming atmosphere. we’ll definitely be back

I ordered the egusi with beef and pounded yam. It is the first time I tried egusi. I have been so curious about fufu & egusi my whole life because I’ve been seeing it all over my tiktok. I ordered in Uber and i was choosing between 2 restaurants but I’m so glad I bought here cause their egusi is so so so good!!! Very tasty!! Worth the money!! I’m so amazed.

Delicious and affordable! The place is takeout-only so you’ll need to find seating elsewhere. Flavors were intense. The fufu slid smoothly on the tongue and tasted so clearly of cassava. The egusi was infused with fish and extra umami (crayfish powder?)—I want to eat this regularly! And the jollof rice had the classic aromatic tomato base, but the version here had a good deal more oil for richness. Such a lovely meal.

First time here and this place is definitely a hidden gem! The owner is so welcoming and helped me pick out some options. We had a few different fufu combos and while each was awesome in its own right, I think I'm going to be dreaming about the okra stew!! Will definitely be back soon! Thank you for an awesome dinner!

formatted_address: 140 E 41st St, New York, NY 10017, United States
name: dùndú

reviews.text: Food is amazing and affordable! Very well seasoned. It was my first time trying Nigerian food and the staff were super informative and friendly. Found my new lunch spot. Huge portions as well.

Another customizable lunch bowl place but it's Nigerian food.  I figured I would go for one of their signature bowls and I went for the Party Bowl with the goat stew.  It would have been great if I go a bit more goat meat but it was very flavorful and tender. The jollof rice was also fantastic.  Perfect comforting meal for a dreary wintry day.  Looking forward to going back and trying something else or customizing my own bowl.  If you don't know what to get, the staff is super friendly and helpful and can guide the way depending on your preferences.
Awesome lunch spot! Food was absolutely delicious. I normally dont write reviews, but I really enjoyed this salad. Plantains were to the God's! Spinach was bomb also! Will definitely come back!

We were very excited to try Nigerian that was so close to Grand Central.

We went there a bit early. Goat stew was not yet ready. But, the person at the front and was quite friendly and explained everything.

I got the chicken dish with sweet plantains, spinach and such. My friend got Acara, which seemed quite good.

I am not an expert in Nigerian food, but I thought the spinach and sides and the chicken itself could use more spices. It could me taste buds, but it was a bit on the bland side.

The place looks nice, people good and has a lot of potential. Do consider spicing up a bit. (Or add as a choice)

I walked in was greeted by very friendly staff. They walked me through the menu and recommended I try the chicken party bowl for my first time. The best part of the bowl was the jollofrice. It was cooked perfectly and very flavorful. I felt the chicken could have used a little bit more seasoning. The plantains were a little hard and could have also used some additional seasoning. I wasn’t sure how I felt about the Moin-Moin. Good for getting something quick and the food portions are bigger than they look online. Limited seating inside, better for takeout.

formatted_address: 63 E 125th St, New York, NY 10035, United States
name: Accra Express Restaurant

reviews.text:
We were starving and ubered here from the Met Cloisters. The person working gave us samples for the spinach rice, egusi, and jollof, which was very nice of her. Food portions are MASSIVE and lasted us 2 meals (took most of it home). Paid $40 for fufu + egusi and jollof and rice - great value. Would come back

- Fufu and egusi w/ mixed meat: 10/10, first time trying fufu - LOVED the texture, and it was yummy w the egusi. The egusi was a little more sour than I expected but still so yummy
- Jollof and rice: 10/10, I REALLY liked this. Sauce was tomatoey and so flavorful. Rice was also soft

Great food and ambiance. I’ve been eying this place for a while, and I’m so glad to finally try it. We got the fufu & peanut stew, and Jollof rice and fish. We also tried a side of the turkey tails. Everything was flavorful and a good level of spicy as well. 10/10 will be back!
The food was fantastic. The waakye, stew, and groundnut soup were perfect, and literally tasted exactly as I remember they did in Ghana. I look forward to trying more dishes here.

First time trying the West African food. The staff here were so nice to let us try out everything for free!

Food itself was great!We ordered three different curries (soups) and the portion is generous!
Our first foray into West African food. The portions were generous but the food was just okay. It’s counter service but the woman behind the counter was super nice. The place was clean.

formatted_address: 1168 Bedford Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11216, United States
name: Joloff

reviews.text: First time trying Senegalese food, and WOW, I am so excited to continue ordering more from what this restaurant has to offer! Today I tried the Mafe Yapp with jollof rice. Perfectly cooked rice, tender lamb, deeply rich flavors in both.

First time trying West African food! We came here for lunch after visiting the Brooklyn Museum. Ordered a Chicken entree, fried plantains, veggie pastis, and the lemon ginger drinks. We loved everything equally. The flavors were on point and had just the right amount of heat. Chicken was fall off the bone. Seated right away and service was wonderful. Generous portions and my husband and I split everything. More than enough and we took a small container home. Will return!

Wonderful spot.  Good food and such a cute, colorful spot.  We got the okra and tomato chicken and the Senegalese fish dish as well as the fried yucca and veggie pasteles.  We loved everything.  We split 2 entrees 3 ways and had more than enough (did have apps)

This restaurant has the best African vibes — Afrobeat music in the background, beautiful décor, and a warm energy. The jollof rice and suya were absolutely delicious, full of authentic flavor. Staff were super friendly and explained the dishes well. I loved the cultural touches that made the experience feel like a trip to West Africa. Highly recommend!

First time ordering after seeing a friend post their food on instagram. The atmosphere is very inviting I wish I would’ve dined in. They opened at 1pm and I was at the door at 1259 lol. I walked out with my food at 107 and I am impressed. My food was fresh and the rice was fluffy and perfectly cooked. I ordered the croaker fish and jolof rice. I rate this food 4/5 only because I wanted a little more of a Smokey taste in my rice.

formatted_address: 55 St Nicholas Ave, New York, NY 10026, United States
name: Safari

reviews.text:
Because of Safari, Somali food has now become one of my favorite cuisines ever! We ordered the Beef Suqaar, Mango Curry Chicken, and Hilib Ari. Literally everything was absolutely delicious!
The owner was extremely hospitable and I honestly cannot wait to go again. Make sure to ask for bananas to enhance the experience with your rice!

The food is good, but I suggest not going without a reservation.
We came in on a Friday night around 7 p.m. There was a huge group and a few other tables. Sadly, we were unable to get our starter until 8:30 p.m. and our entree at around 9 p.m. We were very frustrated to see that the staff was busy serving other tables and ignored us.
However, the food is delicious and authentic. If we can revisit this restaurant, we will definitely make a reservation.

We stopped into Safari in Harlem for lunch, and at first, the completely empty dining room made us question our choice—but I’m so glad we stayed!
Service-wise, our waiter wasn’t the friendliest or most attentive, but honestly, the food was so good it didn’t even matter.

We started with the Chicken Sambuca—perfectly thin, flaky dough wrapped around juicy, flavorful meat. Light, tasty, and a fantastic appetizer. For mains, we had the Goat (Hilib Ari) and the Lamb Shoulder. The lamb was a little on the dry side, but the goat was absolutely sublime—so tender it melted in your mouth, with amazing flavors and seasoning. The accompanying rice was aromatic and beautifully spiced, pairing perfectly with the meats.

Next time I’m in NYC, I’ll definitely be coming back!

I had the pleasure of eating here on a Saturday night with two others and it was an absolutely fantastic experience. Our server was Abe and he provided an excellent dining experience. We opted for the floor seating which was so lovely and cozy! The rugs and cushions were very comfortable which made the ambience and meal feel more special. Abe was very friendly and took the time to give recommendations and explain the menu. We got the shared platter for three and thoroughly enjoyed the meal. The lamb shank was fantastic and our choice of protein was marinated chicken. Overall, phenomenal experience

I have been here more than a few times and have enjoyed every meal.
The customer service is always great.

I’ve had the sorrel, some mango punch I think it was, beef sambusas (which comes with amazing side green sauce; so good I wanna drink it lol ), side Alfredo pasta, chicken suqaar, and my favorite is just to have traditional Shaax Somali Tea there and get work done. They keep it hot with a little tea candle just underneath the tea pot. So clever and cute.

The tables could use some updating, but besides that the environment is very welcoming.

formatted_address: 1664 Park Ave, New York, NY 10035, United States
name: Sylla

reviews.text:
This place is a hidden gem. We arrived on a very rainy day, yet once we got inside there was sunshine everywhere. My friend and I were so happy. The food was just delicious and the service was top notch.
I am vegetarian 90% of the time, however, I had fish that day and it was superb. We had the Poisson Grill, the Sweet Plantains, and the Ris Gras with no meat. Let me tell you, I ate slower on purpose!! So flavorful and so smooth… The sauce that came with the Ris Gras was amazing too!!
This experience could not have been the same without Amy!! She was the best waitress ever. She greeted us like we were family and her smiles, amazing knowledge of the menu, and energy was just perfect. I used to train servers and Amy made it look so easy. Please support this off the beaten path restaurant! Tell them Chase sent you!!!

Amazing food, fresh fish and good jollof rice. the portions were very generous we had 1 fish and side of jollof with plantains for 3 people, total costs $50 very affordable. will come back for sure. the place was relatively empty so no reservation required

I wanted to grab a bite with a friend before I headed to the Richard Roger’s amphitheater. It’s an 11 minute walk from there. In spite of the construction outside, we couldn’t hear a thing inside. At 5:30 pm, the vibe is upbeat and quiet. The large screen with urban music pops against the black interior. The service was quite attentive initially. I enjoyed the food a lot in spite of my friend finding it a bit greasy (it is 😋). Around 7:30pm, this place filled up and got quite lively. We had to work through the crowd to pay our bill. I ran into the owner on the street. He greeted me and ensured I had a good dinner and time there.

My fiance and I went here on our first date, and we loved it! The peanut butter stew is the right amount of spice and the plantain fufu was delicious. The fish and atikeh were also so well cooked and flavorful. The portions are big, so we carried home to go. We’ll definitely be back!

Had the lamb with sweet plantains on my first try, needless to say it was extremely delicious. The next time I had the red snapper with a salad and omg it was od delicious and extremely flavorful. I will surely return.

formatted_address: 2041 Davidson Ave, Bronx, NY 10453, United States
name: Accra

reviews.text:
They gave absolutely no meat, everything was bone and fat. Extremely disappointed. Spices were great but this was disrespectful. You know how frustrating that is to see when you get home hungry thinking you’re about to tear it up? Tear what up? Spent 43$ on the thought of dinner. The other plate was 98% rice. I thought this was going to be so much better based on the rating. Don’t be fooled.

They were really nice though so they have that going for them.

The food was very tasty. There were so many choices that I had a hard time making up my mind on what I wanted. I came around lunch time so it was very busy.  I stood in line for about 30-35 min. There were 3 ladies serving customers. Whoever is taking your order is the one you have to pay.  I noticed everyone was paying cash. I had cash as well,  so I'm not sure if they accept card. The toilet was very clean.

Affable workers. They are good and have very nice and delicious dishes. With less than $20, I enjoyed my delicious Ghanaian fufu with peanut butter and light soup. I highly recommend you give it a try. You will love it👍

The food was decent, but the ambiance left much to be desired. I’m still on the lookout for a truly warm and welcoming (West) African restaurant. That said, the service was excellent — the lady at the counter was very friendly and attentive.

I asked to wash my hands before eating, the woman with the glasses asked me will I buy something, I told her should I show her my Ghana Card even though we’re in the United States. Then I ordered Light Soup and she put it in Aluminum Foil Container. I asked her where were the Bowls, she said they throw them away. Why would you let people throw away the bowls. Do they throw away the bowls in Ghana? This place needs Proper Training. You can’t be Called Accra, call the Place Trench Town😂

formatted_address: 327 Nostrand Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11216, United States
name: Dept. of Culture

reviews.text: Just came back from the restaurant and I feel so content and happy. I am not really into fine dining because a lot of the time it can get too intellectual, but I feel Dept. of Culture really made it experiential. The food is very good, I can feel the culture, the identity and the love in the food. I love Chef Ayo spend time explaining the dish, the culture and sharing his personal stories. He is not only a chef but an artist! This is a very unique, culturally and wholesome experience I had in NYC. We will definitely come back!

My other half and I visited here on a Saturday evening. There are 2 sitting an evening and the menu is a set 4 course menu (which you don’t see beforehand and is regularly changing). You also have to prepay the $85 per person when you book so just be aware of that. The restaurant is BYOB, something which we knew from reviews but was only shared with us by the restaurant about 60 minutes before our reservation.

We arrived promptly for our 6pm reservation and had our pick of seats on the communal table. The setup is one communal table and a few bar seats so if you are particular on where you want to sit then arrive right at your reservation time. Annoyingly someone was late to our seating so our service was delayed by about 25 minutes (by which point the person still hadn’t arrived) and this did result in the meal being slightly rushed.

We started with the Pepper Soup, which was out highlight of the evening (I would return just for this dish). The fish was perfectly cooked and the pepper soup had a good kick to it, a really well balanced dish. The next dish was a Nigerian cheese dish, I am not a cheese fan so can’t fairly judge this but the tomato sauce it came in was lovely (I just hated the cheese). Next we had Herring and Yams, I found this dish a little stodgy and the picketed herring flavour was slightly overwhelming. I enjoyed a small amount of it but found the dish difficult to finish. The meal ended with caramelised plantain, which was very sweet but a nice way to end the meal.

I really enjoyed the experience and the chef coming out and explaining each dish was a nice touch. Overall we had a nice evening but not sure we would rush back. The portion sizes were pretty small (although the yams were filling) and for the price point I think I would rather visit somewhere else. However I do encourage people to try Dept of Culture at least once.

This was a fun evening and I absolutely applaud what the chef aims to do here to in a communal setting, shine a spotlight on
Nigerian cuisine in an elevated manner while sharing insights into the culture there in a fun way. We had a fun evening chatting with the neighbors at our table while enjoying our wine (it’s BYOB) and sampling some very unique dishes. There were four courses in all - the highlights for me being a homemade Nigerian cheese dish and a goat pepper pot. The only issue I had, which others have also raised, was the price. For four small dishes, the price felt very much on the high side. Nonetheless, it has encouraged me to seek out more restaurants featuring food from this part of the world which feels underrepresented.

I had high hopes for Department of Culture, but overall it didn’t quite live up to the hype. While the food was good and had a comforting, home-cooked feel, it didn’t justify the steep price tag. It reminded me of the quality you’d get at a spot like Accra in Harlem — solid and flavorful — but dressed up with fancy French plates in an attempt to appear upscale, which felt a bit forced.

The communal table setup wasn’t really for me, and the pacing of the meal was painfully slow — four dishes stretched out over two hours. When each dish was finally presented, the chef spoke so softly that it was nearly impossible to catch the explanations, which took away from the experience.

In the end, it felt more like a casual dinner with a drawn-out timeline than the refined, contemporary dining experience it’s trying to achieve. Not a bad meal by any means, just not worth the premium or the hype.

3.5 stars but rounding up for DOC's potential. Let me explain.

On food alone, Dept of Culture is a solid 3 stars. The quality is there, but there's a lack of diversity in the offerings and far too few dishes for the price: $111 (including tax and tip) netted us a tiny bowl of Goat Meat Pepper Soup (4 sips max), a slighter larger bowl of Asaro with Smoked Crayfish Sauce, a main dish of Abula (large appetizer-sized), and a small dessert of Dodo.

There should've been at least one more entree (or large app), and either an amuse bouche or a palate cleanser for the price. In fact, when they brought out dessert, our dining companion actually blurted out, "That's it? I could've done with at least one more dish of food."

So those are my critiques with Dept of Culture. Now here are my praises.

Chef Ayo Balogun is a clear culinary talent with a natural flair for storytelling. His explanations for each course were a delight and transported us to his childhood in Nigeria.

The communal dining table is all about good vibes, and we had a blast getting to know our seat mates. Great concept that should be adopted more often in other restaurants. We even had another Nigerian person in our group (from a different part of the country than Chef Ayo), so it was great to get his perspective on the dishes.

But mostly, Dept of Culture is--I truly, truly hope--a harbinger of better times for African food in upscale dining. I want it to be the Chez Panisse of Nigerian food (or even West African food if we're not ready to get so specific)--the trailblazer that introduces a specific cuisine to the American populace.

For too long, boring, bland, Euro-centric cuisines have dominated fine dining. East Asia entered the chat a while ago, South America came next, and even South Asian flavors are on the rise, but this snooty world has repeatedly ignored Africa despite us owing pretty much all of what we have in food to this motherland continent.

I had my 23rd birthday lunch at a hole-in-the-wall Nigerian restaurant in Chicago and have introduced (sometimes dragged) countless friends to different African restaurants throughout the years. I don't pretend to be an expert--I just love shining a light on great, overlooked food. If Dept of Culture--for its somewhat flawed but mostly steller model--can put Nigerian food on the map of Western fine dining, perhaps we can finally get more African restaurants that aren't bare bones hole-in-the-walls or fusion-with-European (a la Marcus Samuelsson) spots. Perhaps African food can finally get the top accolades it so richly deserves.

formatted_address: 1239 Amsterdam Ave, New York, NY 10027, United States
name: Massawa

reviews.text: Wonderful East African restaurant serving Eritrean & Ethiopian fare. The space and the staff are warm and inviting. I had a hot cup of cinnamon coffee while I waited on the rest of my party to arrive, I recommend it. Laid back cozy vibe, with space to chill while waiting for your table. We had lunch and the prices were great, and the portions generous. We had samplings of the vegan and vegetarian offerings, they offer different levels of spice and their were five in our group with everyone stated and happy. One person in our group also had salmon and attested to its tastiness, it certainly looked like it was prepared perfectly. The injera was light and had the perfect balance of tang - again, ample portions too. Swollen and happy, we had to decline dessert. Overall a wonderful experience. Great for groups, friends, kids, or an intimate date - soooo good!

MASSAWA is an Ethiopian restaurant located in Harlem. It is a casual upscale restaurant, modern and elegant without being pretentious. The food and drinks were amazing! The cocktails were great. We had a MANGOTINI and a BUBBLE GUM MARTINI. For food, we had the vegetable platter which allowed us to try a whole host of things. We added a protein to that , a spicy beef stew. Everyone has a fun tome eating in this unique way. The minor pet peeves I had was that the waitresses didn't explain each dish, and the beautiful and clean toilet had problems flushing. All in all, a very fun, satisfying and unique dining experience.

After hearing great things about Massawa from a dear friend for years, I decided to give it a shot. Last Friday, the two of us shared a trio of sambusas and an Alitcha Beghe entrée. Everything was delicious! We even had to order another pair of fish sambusas, as that was our favorite of the trio. All of the food is 10/10 though we never received napkins, a must when eating injera with your hands.
Our server was kind and pleasant, but slow and inattentive. She did not give her name, but volunteered her young teen age when we asked for drink recommendations. I received the tasty agave ginger lemonade, instead of the alcohol-based ginger lemonade I ordered. When I did get it, it was pure completely unpalatable. After dinner, we ordered pumpkin lattes with oatmilk. After 20 minutes of waiting, our server returned to tell us that the bartender left to buy oatmilk from a local store and scurried off before we could cancel. It took about 40 minutes to receive lukewarm lattes.
My friend loves this place and wanted to share it with me. The food was wonderful, but the service dampened the experience.

I came here for a Sunday night, dinner and really enjoyed the food. For our first experience of Ethiopian food, I enjoyed the flavors of my salmon dish and the red lentils. Ingera bread was tasty and something different. The Samusa was really good, but I did not care for the sauces. My Agave ginger lemonade drink was ok.

Very delicious Ethiopian food. We were a group of four, including one vegetarian. The very nice server recommended the goat stew and roasted chicken dish, along with the vegan sampler. This allowed us to try many of the top flavors. It was all delicious. Would recommend to all looking to have a fun experience with Ethiopian food.

formatted_address: 89 Canal St, New York, NY 10002, United States
name: D. Salam African Cuisine

reviews.text: My first experience at D. Salam surly wii not be my last. I had an amazing and meaningful experience especially to find out that the woman who prepared the meals prepared them on her own for the day and although there were supposed to be other cooks to help her out there she'd been the only one to take on the responsibility. I enjoyed the music selection while waiting on my meal to be prepared. I also had the opportunity to watch the one coworker that did attend prepare Sorel for the fridge and happened to receive a complimentary bottle withy meal. The food had been amazing. It's a must try

This is one of those places that makes The City feel like the center of the universe.
Lots of great classic West African comfort dishes served by a real cool and kind dude.  I'd never been before but he set me up with a great sample plate of vegetarian stuff with some delicious hot sauce.
Tucked away in a far corner of Chinatown,  but worth the diversion from all the good noodle and dim sum shops.

Food is wonderful! Owner is incredibly kind. He let us sample to make sure we were happy with our choices. The art in the store is also made by the person that makes the food. They have ginger sorrel in the back. That was refreshing with a slight kick. Recommend take out!
The staff is so friendly and the food is soooo freshhhh!!! They have art for sale, live music, a Jamaican AND Senegalese chefs here! It’s amazing place!

Delicious cuisine! I tried the Jollof rice and the mafe (peanut butter sauce)... absolutely fantastic! The staff were wonderful, and the service was top-notch. I’ll definitely return. There’s truly nothing like enjoying authentic African dishes in your own neighborhood.

formatted_address: 291 Greene Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11238, United States
name: Radio Kwara

reviews.text: An excellent experience from start to end. We ordered every dish on the menu for a group of 5, and the flavors were so bold and unique. Everything was great, but some personal favorites were the goat pepper soup, the toast with mushrooms, the cabbage and the beef short rib. The staff was exceptional and very attentive. Loved the simple and minimalist atmosphere too. A strong recommend without a doubt.

Ordered the entire menu with no regrets. To be specific with the absolute bangers: the mushroom bread, the pepper soup, and the puff puffs. The bread and mushroom has so much flavor and should be your first stop to start your palette. The soup is POW flavor with a delicious spice. The puff puffs are lighter than they seem and the guava will have you digging at the bowl for every drop.

Great food. The menu is short, but everything stands out. There is a clear preference for complex spice mixes on relatively simple bases. Plenty of starch, but also some vegetables and protein. I loved the texture and flavor of the moi moi and the yam. The octopus was a bit chewy.

A group of us had the opportunity to dine at this restaurant as part of Tasting Collective, where a pre-set menu was created to showcase the cuisine. While I understand that a tasting experience may not fully represent the regular menu, it provided a glimpse of what might be expected.

One area of concern was the spacing of the restaurant. It is quite compact, which made it challenging to be comfortable throughout the meal. Despite my petite stature at 5’1”, I found it difficult to stretch my legs.

We began our meal with the goat pepper soup, which was enjoyable and had a bold flavor profile, though it was quite spicy and may not have been the most suitable choice as the first dish for all guests.

The subsequent dishes featured minimal meat, leading to the perception that we were enjoying a primarily vegetarian experience, which may not have aligned with everyone’s expectations given the higher price point of the tasting menu.

Before dessert, we were informed that the planned “Nigerian Sweet Dough” was unavailable, and we would instead be served ice cream and caramelized plantain. It was a bit surprising that a restaurant would run out of key ingredients for a tasting menu, especially since we were the first seating of the evening and had provided an exact count in advance.

While I appreciate the effort put into the dining experience, I must admit that it may not be on my list for a return visit to Brooklyn for a redo.

PERFECT meal. Everything was so delicious, Im only sad I couldnt try it all!!!! The octopus was cooked perfectly the moi moi loved, and the iyan ati egusi BLEW ME AWAY. Also the puff puff for dessert was the totally perfect taste and texture. I can not say enough good things about this. Also its BYOB but there is a wine store next door.

formatted_address: 911 Broadway, Brooklyn, NY 11206, United States
name: Native Restaurant and Lounge

reviews.text: This place is so underrated. The vibe is actually amazing. It is right on Broadway and every time I go it is never crowded, which blows my mind because it deserves a packed house. They have themed nights Monday through Friday, the food is on point, and the drinks are strong and good. It is a West African restaurant and they also have a location on 125th Street. Mondays are karaoke night and it is always a good time. More people need to put this spot on their list.

My waiter was Ola. He was really making the night worth coming out. He was pleasant and energetic. He was also very sweet. Definitely have to come back. I had the Pounded yam with Egusi soup (I had mixed meat). My friend had the Jollof Spaghetti with Salmon (I obviously had to take a bite from the food). For drinks we had the Ziti Bo (hibiscus, ginger juice and pineapple juice!) It was all delicious. I don’t know which was better the drinks, the food, or the music!!!!! All was a great experience.

It wasn’t my vibe but it was cool. If u are into loud music, hookah, and females twerking at their table then “welcome home”!

Food was good, very flavorful, drinks were great, service pretty good. Some negatives: we were a group of 9 and we were REAAL close to one another. Also the photo op was behind booths that was occupied the entire time. Also the bathroom was neglected not too dirty but garbage overflowing.

It was okay. My 2nd time trying African cuisine and I was disappointed that there were non-spicy options. The mixed meat was very delicious. My friends all enjoyed their meals.
The music was too loud for dinner conversations and we couldn't hear each other. We asked that it he turned down on several occasions but that never happened. It's pretty expensive & not worth the hype. The server was wonderful and all in all the service was great!!

Arrived early enough for happy hour even though my reservation was set for 6:30. The vibe for a Friday felt a little mid—maybe because it was still early—but the food was really tasty and super good. The only downside was the hibiscus margaritas. I love anything hibiscus, but these weren’t strong at all. I ordered two and could barely taste the tequila. Because of that, I’d rate the place 4/5. Aside from that, the DJ was great, the service was attentive, and the space was aesthetically pleasing. I’d definitely come back!

formatted_address: 2 Center St, Newark, NJ 07102, United States
name: Swahili Village - Newark, NJ

reviews.text:
Time to break out of one’s culinary groove and explore a cuisine loaded with flavor, history, and a diversity of textures and ingredients. African cuisine holds quite a range, depending on the country and culture it originated from.

Across the US, from vibrant food markets to trendy fusion cafés and transmigration-owned restaurants, one cuisine is rising fast: Kenyan food. It’s not as globally mainstream as Thai or Mexican yet, but in 2026 it’s becoming one of the most talked-about international food experiences, especially in multicultural cities like New York, Chicago, or LA.

My partner, our friends, and I made a reservation at Swahili Village off of Center Street in Newark before the Saturday night performance at the nearby NJPAC. A reservation was easily made hours in advance via OpenTable.

Upon arrival as first-timers, we were greeted by the host at this husband-and-wife-owned establishment. We were promptly seated at a high table by the bar in one of the three spacious dining rooms blending traditional elements paying homage to African heritage with modern touches; Afrobeat music enhances the festive atmosphere to create a warm and welcoming vibe.

The menu is built around East African dishes influenced by the region’s historical ties to Arab traders, Portuguese explorers, British colonizers, and Indian immigrants.

As a starter, we opted for the Samosa. For our main meal, we decided on Suya-Nyama Choma (Beef), Lamb Chops, Grilled Chicken Breast-Kuku Choma, and Oxtails. They came with two sides and got Jollof rice, Mokimo, Sweet Plantains, and Spinach. Our drinks (Flaming Margarita, White Sangria, The Motherland, and Heaven's Nectar Martini) were strong enough and tasted great, with some unique options.

One reason why we fell in love with Kenyan cuisine was its balance of flavors. Instead of being extremely spicy or very mild, Kenyan dishes were aromatic, warmly spiced, and tastefully rich & savory. The portions were healthy. We didn’t have room for dessert. The service was impeccable. Our server, Fabrice, took the time to explain everything on the menu & recommended drinks and entrees.

Overall, it was an amazing experience. Hands down the best food we’ve ever tasted!

OMG!!! Really sums up my visit at this amazing establishment. Went to the Boy Is Mine Concert, my friends went out after the concert and came back raving about the time that was had…. had so much fun we went for lunch the next day. Our waiter Asani 10/10, Cassandra I just love her💜. Food was chef’s kiss 😘. My ONLY question is when y’all coming to Philly??????

I love Swahili Village in Newark. I go to many concerts at the New Jersey Performing Arts Center across the street so this is a great place for pre show or post show dinner drinks and wonderful atmosphere. I didn't get at chance to sample the cuisine as I was on my way to another commitment but stayed for a great glass of Chardonnay. Great crowd, lively atmosphere, beautiful decor. Will definitely return for dinner.

A time was had at Swahili Village this weekend. Assani and Casandra (Mgr) were amazing! We had the samosas, jollof rice, wings, and the shareable tasting platter and EVERYTHING WAS AMAZING!! The peri peri sauce (spelling) was wonderful and took us back to a trip to Africa we took a few years back. PLEASE OPEN A LOCATION IN PHILLY!! We would welcome this atmosphere and amazing cooking with open arms and empty stomachs. If you are ever in Newark for a show make sure to stop by before and after. The restaurant closes at 3am and the DJ on Saturday after the concert was awesome. My husband and I had so much fun that we stayed until the lights came up and came back at noon the next day for lunch. IT IS JUST THAT GOOD.

I had the snapper with collard greens and jollof rice. I originally wanted it fried without sides but they did not have that option available even though I was told over the phone by a worker. The fish was good but too much onions and peppers for me. The rice was cool,  not spicy how I would like it and the greens were bland to me. Overall the food was a 6/10. The sides portions was small for what I paid. The drink I had was very good . The service was just slow and not enough workers.I just wish they had the option of fried Snapper alone please. I was really craving it 😭

formatted_address: 2375 Adam Clayton Powell Jr Blvd, New York, NY 10030, United States
name: Ponty Bistro

reviews.text:
Ponty Bistro is the perfect blend of West African and French fusion done right.
From the moment we arrived, the vibe felt warm, stylish, and intentional.
The passion fruit mango margaritas were refreshing and perfectly balanced.
The escargot surprised me in the best way rich garlic butter, a hint of cognac, and incredible flavor.
The truffle mac and cheese and rack of lamb were both standout dishes, cooked beautifully and full of depth.
Seafood lovers will appreciate the creamy risotto packed with shrimp, mussels, scallops, and lobster sauce.
Dessert sealed the experience, and I’d absolutely return to explore more of the menu.

I visited Pony Bistro in late September 2025 for a work dinner.   Let’s just say I’m glad this was a work dinner and I didn’t spend my money at this restaurant.  We dined from a Prefix menu.  I was concerned the food would be spicy as it’s an African/French restaurant.   For appetizers we were served chicken wings, calamari and some type of puff.   The puff was spicy and the chicken wings were the only thing that was good.  For dinner I order the steak which came with some type of sauce that wasn’t good.  The steak also had an after taste to it I stopped eating it.  For dessert I ordered the chocolate lava cake which wasn’t any better.  It also had a weird after taste to it.   I also tried the crème burlee which also wasn’t good and had that same after taste.   This isn’t a restaurant I would be visiting again.
The food was good and flavorful. My only complaint is that I wish the calamari came out fresh. They do live jazz music on Thursday from 7pm till close.

I just happened to find the Ponty Bistro in Harlem while looking for a place to eat. I walked in and was greeted by the bartender Sheick, who was very courteous and pleasant.  The ambiance is quite lovely and cozy, and clean.
I saw a customer eating salmon with vegetables, and it looked so good I quickly changed my salad order to the salmon and veggies.
In the meantime, I ordered a cosmo and was very specific as to how I want it.  Sheick made it exactly as I ordered.  Maaan..that was delicious 😋!
My salmon and veggies arrived and let me tell you...I have never had an array of vegetables and sooooo delicious.  It was string beans, broccoli, carrots, and Bokchoy, and 2 perfectly sized potatoes.
They were in a sauce to die for.
Now, that salmon, perfectly prepared the way I requested, was past delicious.  I kept telling Sheick how tasty it was, and he was very grateful.
I will definitely return to dine at Ponty Bistro.

I had the pleasure of dining at Ponty Bistro for the first time as a birthday treat from a dear friend. The atmosphere was warm, elegant, and inviting.

For my entrée, I ordered Le Poulet Parmesan, which was rich, creamy, and bursting with flavor. I only wish I'd taken photos before we dove in!  Dessert was the perfect way to end the meal. I chose the chocolate fondant, which had a gooey and velvety center served with vanilla ice cream. My friend ordered the profiteroles, filled with vanilla ice cream and drizzled with chocolate. They were fresh, crisp, and just as enjoyable.

The only thing that felt a little off was the music. During our visit, the restaurant was playing pop music and I wasn't expecting that. In my opinion, it didn’t quite match the vibe or the cultural essence of the menu. A playlist that aligned more closely with the restaurant’s identity would’ve added another layer of richness to the experience.

Still, it was a memorable day with good company, great customer service, great food and desserts. I’d definitely go back!

formatted_address: 165 W 26th St, New York, NY 10001, United States
name: BB Halal Food Inc

reviews.text: Good atmosphere. Food lacks some seasonings but it was good. A relaxed atmosphere. It's a buffet style and offers good food options.

Good selection of buffet-style halal eats, grab whatever you want weighed at 11 dollars a pound.

Seating’s pretty limited so it’s good for takeout.

I never really tried African food before and I found this place from TikTok because my SO really wanted to try fufu with stew.

The price for food was really good and I thought it was delicious even though idk what I ate honestly because none of the dishes are labeled. I just took pieces from dishes from trays that were almost empty because I assumed these were popular.

I would definitely come here though if you have no dietary restrictions and want to try African food without breaking the bank though.

This place excels when serving dinner. The employees delivered outstanding service and fast food. Being new to this neighborhood, I was excited to discover this spot. The food tastes exceptional and costs what it should. I must return to give them better stars.

African buffet paradise! There’s no place like this on the west coast. So many protein, veg, and carb choices, there were like 30 dishes available. My favorite dish was probably the ceebujen or the okra. They take card.

formatted_address: 2479 Frederick Douglass Blvd, New York, NY 10027, United States
name: Chez Jacob

reviews.text:
Chez Jacob — Harlem’s Senegalese Gem

Chez Jacob is without question the best Senegalese spot in Harlem. I order there every single week, and it never disappoints. They have all the real dishes you’d want if you know Senegalese food — mafe, thiebu jen, thiebu yapp, domoda, borakhe, thiebu kethiakh, thiou, dakhin, mbaxalu saalum… the list goes on. And if you’re into grilled meats, the dibi and michoui are on point — perfectly seasoned, juicy, and straight up delicious.

What I love most is the authenticity. The food tastes just like home — rich, flavorful, generous portions, and cooked with care. Whether you want fish, lamb, chicken, or something saucy with rice, you’ll find it here.

This isn’t a place for “fusion” or watered-down flavors — it’s the real deal. If you want to experience true Senegalese cuisine in New York, Chez Jacob is the spot.

The food was very VERY bad. My mother and I came to try this place, and they didn’t have the snapper upon request so we settled for the chicken. The chicken was SO dry! It was nearly impossible to even chew. I also ordered a side of rice and vegetables. The vegetables were not fresh and they were the kind you get from the frozen section. You could clearly tell the food had been sitting around for days and it was not fresh at all. Definitely won’t be returning.

This place delivers quality worth returning for regularly. The employees know their business while showing personal care. They use special components to create excellent meals. I was astonished by the quality. Chez Jacob exceeds the rating scale.

Chez Jacob creates meals that satisfy both hunger and curiosity. Friendly, accommodating, hospitable, competent. No-fuss dining here. Their dishes aligned with my taste. The complete experience here was perfect.
The overall experience here keeps me coming back. Nice food, attentive people. The employees make dining pleasant. The taste experience needs no explanation. This place shows mastery in every area.

formatted_address: 76 E 119th St, New York, NY 10035, United States
name: New Ivoire

reviews.text: This spot understands flavor in a way others don't. Tasty dishes that don't strain your budget. The place looks inviting and staff reinforces that. The employees deliver outstanding customer support. This restaurant should gain wider recognition.

The chef here clearly knows how to impress customers. This place knows cooking, knows design and knows service. Their food teaches your palate something new. All workers were exceptionally obliging. This restaurant creates flavor magic!

The food here exceeds what you expect from a local restaurant. All workers here have pleasant personalities. This place offers elegant visuals. Their dishes stand out even among excellent restaurants. This establishment meets every standard.

I ordered the dibi lamb on my last visit and it was flavorful, but a little tough. The fries did not taste fresh (probably because they were cooked in an old oil). Also, make sure to call before coming here because the restaurant is not open 24h.

REVIEW FROM 5 YEARS AGO: I love the grilled fish with fried yams. I wish there was more consistency in the size of the alloco slice though. I also love the salad, mainly because of the dressing. I would not recommend the dibi nor the leg of lamb as they are overcooked. The staff is friendly, but the service is lacking. Patrons can be too loud and the restaurant can benefit from a renovation.

It’s been a while since I went there, every single time I go there it’s a disappointment. This time i purchased a tate de mouton but when I got home all that was in there is a bone and soup for $19 wow.

formatted_address: 32-20 34th Ave, Queens, NY 11106, United States
name: Nneji

reviews.text: My friends from elsewhere tried the place I recommend and totally agreed. The workers demonstrated real kindness. Workers make you feel welcome while assisting you. The meals contain surprising combinations that work harmoniously. I question the experience of those rating lower.

Nneji is a restaurant with delicious food for takeout in Astoria, Queens.

I had egusi, which is made from a protein-rich seed. Egusi is one of my favorites, for sure. I also got black-eyed peas with sweet potato, black-peppered salmon, gari which is a coarse flour made from cassava, and the ancient grain fonio.

The food I ate had excellent flavor. It is definitely a place I will go back to.

Super friendly staff.
Meat is falling of the bone, spicy but not overpowering.
The tomato soup dish (Egusi) is amazing.

Delicious food and friendly staff! They took the time to talk about the dishes with me and gave recommendations. I had the chicken, jollof rice and okra! Loved them all. So flavourful without being overpowering. Wish they had tables and chairs so I can dine here with friends
The mixed meat jollof rice is so good and you get a HUGE portion. The restaurant is takeaway only and smells so nice inside.

formatted_address: 2300 Grand Concourse, Bronx, NY 10458, United States
name: Papaye

reviews.text: Horrible service!!! Acted like they didn’t want to greet or serve us!! Paid 20 a plate and we got the bottom of the pot burned rice!!! I use to like them back in the day so I figured I would go back I had a taste for some African food… but I will for sure never go back and I hope they do better on their customer service and food but they won’t get my money anymore

🍽️ Papaye – A Bronx staple that never misses on flavor.

I’ve been coming to Papaye for years—since living in the Bronx—and it’s truly a household name in the community. The food has always held it down, especially the kebabs, which are still one of my go-to orders whenever I’m back in the city.

The service has improved over time, but there’s still room for more warmth and enthusiasm. That extra effort would elevate the customer experience, but it seems like they know their food speaks for itself—and honestly, it does.

Flavors are solid, portions are generous, and it’s one of those spots that stays real to its roots. Definitely worth stopping by if you’re in the area.

There is this one woman there that always deter me from going inside. She is so rude. The cashier guys are lovely and the food overall is good. But her attitude makes it hard to give the restaurant the best ratings. Even my fellow Ghanaian friends says the same about her. She changes the prices of the meals based on her attitude that day. So sad because I am forced to go to Accra Town. They are more friendlier.

My first time here. The food was extremely delicious and flavorful with just the perfect amount of spice. They give a generous amount of food also. I would definitely go back…no disappointments at all 10/10.

Came here for lunch a few weeks ago and it was a little disappointing. The line had about 10 people ahead of me and still had about a hour wait. How ridiculous. The owner was working the register but he seemed more like the help as he has SOOO many questions for the staff about pricing. I ordered okra soup w pounded yam. The soup was VERY oily and it red... Red? some of you are thinking the same thing as me. Unless they discovered a "new" vegetable how is the soup red??? It must of been Banga soup or heavily doused in palm oil as I only had 1 piece of okra in the entire bowl. The jelloff rice was fine it tasted like it was made in a pressure cooker instead of over the counter which takes longer and more effort but the flavor and quality is worth it. Moving on I would recommend you grab and go if you stop by for lunch. Although there is seating it isn't advised.

formatted_address: 1895 Eastern Pkwy, Brooklyn, NY 11233, United States
name: African Pride

reviews.text:
Delicious. Food is packed with flavor- like every bite is a party. The goat and fish were cooked perfectly- tender and full of spice and savory. Jollof rice had an aromatic smokiness to it which I loved.
Everyone was welcoming and friendly.
The fuufu was the best pairing for the food. Tried the amala too (I think base may have been cassava and it's more dense) and whole wheat fuufu too but neither topped the original.
Incredible! The jollof rice and yams were delectable. The goat curry is one of the best dishes I have had in my LIFE. Went with a group and we adored it!

I bought egusi soup with fufu $28 something. I asked for mixed meats they gave me bones of goat meat! They were not meat on theses bones AT ALL. But that is not my concern bcs sometimes, it’s can happen. The most scary part is that I feel like it’s the rest of someone food that they gave it to me bcs the way there was no meat on the bone is like someone did it intentionally! I’m so disappointed and confused.

The food here is great. Soup is flavorful and the assorted meats so far have been a hit every time.   Service is below average but at least they’re not rude like every other Nigerian restaurant I’ve been to. It’s a new restaurant so I hope it doesn’t go downhill once it becomes more popular. I would definitely recommend as I’ve tried the food several times already!

The restaurant delivers quality dishes with nice service. The staff focused on assisting me first and responded to my inquiries with genuine courtesy. Waiters delivered great service with inventive food options. This establishment offers a good atmosphere. I'll return to this restaurant without delay!

formatted_address: 1235 Fulton St, Brooklyn, NY 11216, United States
name: Le Baobab

reviews.text: The restaurant proves its reliability in both food and service quality. Employees are exceptionally pleasant and helpful, bringing dishes quickly. The food is abundant, well-executed, and delicious. They maintain high standards and freshness despite emphasizing quick, casual service. You would enjoy eating here.

They make everyone feel important. The complete staff maintains superior standards. If environment matters to your dining, you'll like this place. Their plates come heaped with food. This restaurant will get my business again.

This spot offers tasty food with helpful employees. The space and offerings both impress. Their portions exceed what you'd expect. All employees kept our drinks filled while consistently ensuring our dining experience remained positive. I intend to visit again without much delay.

The whole experience here was just right from start to finish. They know flavors, they know beverages and they know aesthetics. I was amazed by the food quality. The personnel balance friendliness with professional skill. This place earns honest recommendations.

The negative feedback nearly scared me away from a good meal. They brought out so much food, with each plate topping the previous one. The employees here are clearly well-trained. The setting encourages deep breaths. All in all, the dinner was exceptional.

formatted_address: 2028 Jerome Ave, Bronx, NY 10453, United States
name: African Home Restaurant

reviews.text: Customer service great. Food so good. Great portions too. I ordered a lil bit of most things off the menu for my family Day 1 Kwanzaa meal. I will be eating here more often.
Food was good the staffs are pretty friendly. Space is limited here though. You’re better off doing a takeout.

Happy Jamaican here 🤣
Ayoyo and stew
And egusi with fufu. (Jah Jah it nice)

I use to go to Mama G but now this place has won my heart and they were so nice and willing to give me the experience I wanted at home through DoorDash it felt like a culture experience for my children and I and thank you for your customer service! It was truly felt!
Their food is very bad nowadays, you guys need to work on it , it used to be my favorite spot but now it’s bad, your cooks need to do better especially on the jollof rice
Food is really bad, sweet plantain looks like it’s been sitting there for weeks and they sold it to me. Wasted my money for nothing, highly disappointed

formatted_address: 1139 Fulton St, Brooklyn, NY 11238, United States
name: Hadja Marley

reviews.text: We brought many people, but the restaurant seated us quickly and served us attentively. I shared this dish with my friend. The proprietor and workers make guests feel welcome. Servers make you feel special and the meals are too. This spot calls for your prompt attention!

Hadja Marley is truly a gem in Brooklyn, New York for anyone craving authentic West African cuisine. What can I say? The buffet spread speaks for itself! Even at 11 PM, everything was fresh, and the place was buzzing with energy. I wasn’t surprised—it had been on my oldest’s list for a while now. He remembered eating here as a youngster. We came as a family of five, and it exceeded all expectations.

The variety was incredible—fragrant rice, tender braised meat, perfectly fried whole fish, and an array of chicken dishes, each more flavorful than the last. Every bite was absolutely mouthwatering. The boys were so impressed that they insisted on packing extra for lunch the next day!

On the car ride home, the conversation was unanimous: it’s not about the decor or ambiance—it’s the food that truly matters. And Hadja Marley delivers on all fronts. We’re already counting down the days until we can go back!
