This place was truly enjoyable. The inside setup of this place caught me off guard. The cooking satisfied while service excelled. Restaurant workers notice when assistance is needed. This place has an exceptional nature.

So I called in to inquire about a specific african dish and the people who answered the phone were so rude. I was going try this restaurant for the first time, I quickly changed my mind. Remember without  customers you will have no business. It cost nothing to be polite

This restaurant combines good food with enjoyment. Customer attention here exceeds quality expectations. Not once have I been disappointed by their food. The staff is pleasant with a comfortable vibe. I vouch for the experience here.

formatted_address: 124 MacDougal St #1247, New York, NY 10012, United States
name: Meskerem

reviews.text:
Staff was friendly. Food tasted good but small portion for the price. Double portion of the combo was same size as the single portion.
Small place and the waitress had some difficulties figuring out how to accommodate 6 of us. It was relatively warm and uncomfortable.

I love Ethiopian food. The meal was satisfying. I enjoyed it. I do feel $30+ was a higher price I wanted to pay for the atmosphere and service. The bathrooms were clunky.

The yellow lentils are delicious. The samosas were tiny. The spice level was on point. The paintings and other touches were lovely. It’s a mixed bag :)

Meskerem has got to be one of the best Ethiopian restaurants in the City. I’ve been there a few times and the dishes I’ve had have been excellent. Every time I’ve come here it’s been a great culinary treat. This time around I had beef sambosas as my appetizer. The beef was mixed with peppers, onions, and garlic inside flat bread. Kind of like a samosa. So good, with a slight bit of a spicy kick. Along with the sambossas I had gomen bessega which was beef with collard greens. They went really well with the injera. Overall this a great place to sample some Ethiopian dishes at very reasonable prices. I already look forward to my next visit. If you’re in the neighborhood then this is definitely an interesting and tasty option. Give it a try!

Portion sizes were the same for double vs. single, as people have mentioned (which is not a great practice) and the chicken from the doro wot tasted unfrozen/frozen multiple times. The waiter served us a beer that was 2 months past the "BB" best by date, which is legally fine (I think), but it was also flat.

To not draw attention, we quietly asked him to take it off the bill, which he politely did. This is where it gets strange: a few minutes *after* we paid and tipped 20%, he tried to justify why serving the beer was fine by showing us something he had googled. Two other customers chimed in that they agreed with him, which wasn't his fault, but he acknowledged their comments to us. We reminded him that the beer was also flat and he just seemed to care a) that we didn't report him or b) to simply justify he was in the right. It's a shame because the food and price was enough to argue not coming back, but this total lack of customer service really sealed the deal.

Pretty good Ethiopian food, better service! Our server recommended some great Ethiopian barley beer because they were out of honey wine, and also helped us package our leftovers to go (because rolling up injera bread is not too easy). We ordered the Meskerem and the Vegetarian combo platter as well as a chicken dish, but were somewhat disappointed with the portion size. Next time we might try to order specifics to get larger portions.

formatted_address: 146-12 Liberty Ave, Jamaica, NY 11435, United States
name: Africana

reviews.text: Been eating here for years never no complaints food is 10/10 highly recommended everything on the menu you won’t be disappointed ❤️

The food tastes made just for you, served by people who seem to serve just for you. Nothing memorable about the taste profile. Plainly put, their customer attention exceeds expectations. i'm glad to say the restaurant met the standard. This place understands excellence.

I landed in JFK, all famished, and I wanted great African food. I booked a hotel near the airport, and by chance, this place was within walking distance. I came by just minutes before they closed for the night. I ordered take-out. I got beef soup with two fufu, and let me tell you! It was what I had imagined of what I was craving as soon as I landed back in NY!

Auntie was super friendly and served me the perfect amount of food. Thank you, Auntie! Your food was so, so delicious!
The staff was very helpful. The food was great. We traveled 45 minutes to eat here and were very pleased.

TThe owner pretends to not see customers
We walked in while she was dealing with a customer. She dealt with him then went to the back to call a worker to deal with us . She ignored our presence the entire time we were there . She did not even wanna serve  our food . The server that dealt with us (the Indian girl) she was the reason we stayed there .
If you’re not African don’t go there expecting good service .
Ps they don’t even have menus in the restaurant.
You’re expected to go on google to see what they have .

formatted_address: 2249 Adam Clayton Powell Jr Blvd, New York, NY 10027, United States
name: Chez Maty Et Sokhna (Keur Sokhna)

reviews.text: Girlllll I will definitely be back here again. I don’t know why I don’t go as often. I know about this restaurant and I’ve gotten food from here before but it’s been years since I stepped foot in there or got food from there and when I went, it was so nostalgic. It reminded me of back home and the food was so good. It tasted just like it does back home. The waitress was so nice and understanding she accommodated for me in literally every way. And the portions are HUGEEEEE like I only ate half of my food and I took the rest home because I was so full and everything was seasoned to perfection. It was just an overall 10 out of 10 experience

I'm annoyed at myself for the delay in coming here. Satisfying dishes. Remarkably helpful employees. Tasty spice combinations. Fair bills and pleasant staff. The neighborhood stays active after dinner hours. This restaurant achieves total quality.

This local spot adds real value to the area. The kitchen delivers undeniably quality dishes. They feature options for different appetites. The employees treat customers well and adjust to needs, plus food arrives rapidly. Amazing meals and incredibly kind assistance.

We received fresh dishes, attentive service, and had a perfect dining experience. Their menu selections all satisfied me. The restaurant maintains quality. Chez Maty Et Sokhna (Keur Sokhna) shows exceptional expertise. This spot has my endorsement.

The kitchen serves meals that highlight the quality of fresh ingredients. Both what was served and the surroundings were great. Chez Maty Et Sokhna (Keur Sokhna) shows care through small considerations. The employee's friendly nature enhanced our experience. The entire meal provided continuous enjoyment.

formatted_address: 717 Franklin Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11238, United States
name: Brooklyn Suya

reviews.text: First tried this place months ago when they were vending at the Brooklyn museum! My partner and I ordered Takeout from them and were thoroughly impressed! The food was so flavorful and the servings were a great portion! The bad thing was there was a piece of foil stuck to the chicken on my partners food :( just want to bring this to the attention of the staff because Suya is SO good and I’m sure it was a mistake.

About time I left a review for this place. Been coming for almost a year now. Love it!! Food is fantastic!! The vibe is too!! It's a fusion of Nigerian, Caribbean & soul food. Healthy, nutritious & flavorful. I usually go for their salmon or chicken bowls. The Suya spice is the cherry on top (quite literally haha). The people who work here are very nice as well, especially the owner. It's a grab-and-go spot with one bench outside for seating but they have a new location that opened up on Rogers with an indoor dining space. A very happy customer here. Thank you, Brooklyn Suya for being a neighborhood 💎

Excellent bowl of chicken, tofu, veggies, and rice.  Came out to be more expensive than I anticipated, even though I was warned the veggies would cost extra (around $1.5 I think). Not sure if the additional protein cost me more as well.  It probably did.  In any case, I did not expect to spend almost $25 (incl. tip) for a bowl.  Again, delicious food but just a bit pricey.

If you’re going to bring a dish from Nigeria to life in Brooklyn New York do it the right way ! First and foremost my pictures speak for themselves. This is not how SUYA beef is sliced for consumption. Why would you serve big chunks of meat like that in a bowel on a bed of kale. Next it was tasteless no flavor in the meat only the sprinkle seasoning on top had flavor. First time and last time   I was so disappointed waste of money ! Tough dry big thick pieces of tasteless beef. If it was flavored beef that has been marinated and juicy I could go home and slide it up, fair enough  I would not have been so upset. But these huge pieces is not easily edible SUYA IS SERVED IN BITE SIZED PIECES not these huge pieces bigger then an Oreo cookie. And  for a salad bowl this is crazy. Y’all gotta do better this is not fair to customers! The good reviews yall were lucky based on the protein yall picked cause the beef was a big fail! Not to be compared to real SUYA in Nigeria !

I was truly looking forward to tasting Brooklyn Suya based on the reviews. However, after trying the beef and chicken suya, I was very disappointed for several reasons. First, this isn’t suya. This is broiled beef with seasoning, chicken cooked with sprinkled suya seasoning, appreciate the salad and brown rice. I suggest the owner visit London UK or Nigeria the origin of suya if they really want to sell suya. People here giving good reviews most likely never ate suya before. Secondly, this had never happened to me before, but as I was chewing I felt something sharp in my mouth only to discover a piece of glass. Like whaaaat? This could have sliced my throat. How did a piece of glass got into the food? Thirdly, my daughter find a piece of long black hair in her food entangled on her broccoli. Seriously health and safety issues.  I would not recommend this place. Sorry!

formatted_address: 454 E 168th St Unit 44, Bronx, NY 10456, United States
name: Grin

reviews.text:
I recently purchased a bottle of natural milk from Le Grin African Restaurant, expecting a fresh and high-quality product. Unfortunately, my experience was nothing short of disappointing and concerning.

When I opened the bottle and took a sip, the milk tasted absolutely terrible—clearly spoiled. Trying to understand what went wrong, I checked the expiration date on the label, only to find something shocking. The original expiration date was clearly January 20, 2025, but someone had manually altered it to March 20, 2025, using handwriting. It was obvious that the date had been tampered with in an attempt to make it seem like the product was still good.

This is completely unethical and dangerous. Selling expired dairy products by simply changing the expiration date is not only deceptive but also a serious health hazard. Consuming spoiled milk can cause food poisoning, and I find it unacceptable that a business would risk the health of its customers like this.

I am beyond disappointed. This is a serious food safety issue that should not be ignored. If a business cannot ensure the quality and freshness of the products they sell, they should not be selling them at all. I strongly urge other customers to double-check expiration dates on perishable products from this restaurant before purchasing.

Le Grin African Restaurant needs to immediately address this issue. Selling expired food with falsified expiration dates is unacceptable and a major violation of customer trust. I will not be buying from here again unless they take full responsibility and make sure this never happens again

I've yet to find something here I wouldn't recommend. They serve hearty portions here. This place is an absolute gem! The team balances knowledge with approachable interactions. This restaurant is fantastic!

Guys, believe me the food there is great! Ok, let's put it this way: it is not a restaurant in the way you are used to - it is pretty small but for people who appreciate tasty and good priced food - there is a place to be! Salad, fish, chicken - everything is delicious and the portions are enormous!  Owners are smiling and friendly. What would you ask more?!
Awesome milk drink and fast service.
My first time trying African food, it was soo good, got the dibi chicken & couscous w onion sauce

formatted_address: 247 Morris Ave, Springfield, NJ 07081, United States
name: La Braise African Grill - Springfield

reviews.text:
Excellent experience.

Everything was high-quality, flavorful, and clearly made with care. We had the snapper, lamb, fried rice, and claclo, each with its own sauces and spice dips. Unique flavors, great portions, and genuinely friendly service.

The pepper sauce was also bomb and made fresh.

So many places serve tiny portions, mediocre food, or have unfriendly staff — but not here. Will definitely be back.

This restaurant was a new adventure. Our waiter, Emmanuel, helped guide us through a culinary experience of the Ivory Coast. It started with delightful homemade juices; Bissap (hibiscus) and Ginger. The flavor was concentrated and adding sparkling water empowers the taste. We then opted for typical food from the Ivory Coast; Ciacio couscous, Beignet of plantain, Branzino, and grilled chicken.  The spices and marinates were full of flavor. Even the plantains had a hint of pepper to heighten the natural sweetness. For dessert we enjoyed the sweep crepes with fresh strawberries. Everything was made to order. We enjoyed listening to soft musical background Afrobeats while we waited. The place was inviting, bright, and clean. The secret ingredient to everything was LOVE. Everything was so delicious, We wanted to thank the Chef. Thank you again Chef Karen! Our experience was wonderful! I am looking forward to returning (so is my Aunt Kathy)!

Phenomenal food! Simply amazing. Everything was so delicious and well-prepared. A whole chicken disappeared like nothing. The lamb was tender and the onions perfectly caramelized. Best fried plantains ever! Cassava couscous goes perfectly with everything, and don’t sleep on the sauces!

The staff were so friendly and hospitable. So glad we stopped by!

Food is excellent!! The snapper and lamb are very well seasoned and delicious. Beautiful presentation as you can see. We called ahead and food was laid out hot and ready by the time we arrived. Customer service is top notch. The owner and chef is friendly and personable as is her staff. The place is small and resembles a take out joint, so not fancy by any means, but clean and comfortable. We stopped by on our way to a show at NJPAC. Can’t wait to go back!!

From the outside, the restaurant looks very low-key and unnoticeable. I have been looking forward to experiencing authentic African dishes for a long time and couldn't find one yet. Luckily, this location showed up on my Google Maps when we were ready for lunch in a nearby area. The space is tiny and fits only 3 tables. We ordered quite a lot for 3 girls and all the dishes came out distinctive, even the sauces (red is tomato taste & green is chili spicy) which we got so addicted to that mixed them in every single thing. However and frankly, we waited likely 1 hour for the food and I still gave it MAX stars because the food soothed us heavenly and made it all up. The waiter was nice and the chef lady was friendly and communicative. She suggested calling ahead for food pre-ordering then coming to enjoy with a short wait. So you gotta be ready to stay excessively patient if you walk-in. Only 1 chef and food is made fresh when an order is placed. Regardless of whether you are a fan of African food, you should give this place a shot. It's enthusiastically endorsed.

formatted_address: 263 W 30th St #3, New York, NY 10001, United States
name: B&D Halal Food

reviews.text:
8/10. Don’t let the minimalist style fool you.

For what it’s worth, it’s amazing. It’s African food, serve yourself, pay by the pound, and no frills or airs whatsoever. It cost me less than $20 for both my meals; it was so good I had to have 2 plates. The lamb was melt in your mouth, but you need to discern which kinds are tastier and more tender, you’ll get an eye for it either through trial and error or by asking a seasoned vet.

My only complaint is that the some dishes are warm, some are cold. Tip! Dig to the bottom of the tray.

The cashier is friendly and the atmosphere is relaxed and laidback. A bunch of Africans patron this restaurant so you can tell it’s authentic.

It’s literally a minutes walk from Penn Station, and I think I’ll be frequenting this place next time I’ve got time when I arrive to Penn Station. I feel closer to my African roots just being here.

Another pro tip! Get the lamb, skip the chicken, such a good deal and deluxe flavours. Hidden gem in NYC.

Techmo Seal of Approval.
I love this place. Buffet style restaurants where you pay by weight have a special spot in my heart. There's so much variety and so many good flavors.

This place is brilliant!! I was here for a casual lunch with a friend on the weekends and their food trays were filled with fresh food and none of them looked empty/sad. It has everything, rice&beans, chicken, fish, salad section, fruits, and of course all the African specialties as well.

It’s buffet style, which I love because then I can try a bit of everything and they charge you based on the weight at the end. Today I got some fish, chicken gizzards, pig feet, fried chicken, avocados, rice and of course some veggies. So yummy!! It came out to be around $10 for me but I imagine someone with a bigger stomach might spend closer to $15 but it’s very affordable for midtown NYC.

There’s also a drinks section where you can make tea/coffee yourself.

Will be back!

The joy of discovering a new favorite place never gets old. The interior beauty doesn't overwhelm. The employees offered outstanding service quality. The food arrives perfectly prepared. I'd make this a regular spot in my life if possible!
The food was so good. Great prices. Friendly staff. The bathroom was  little bad :(

formatted_address: 263 Хендрикс-стрит, Brooklyn, NY 11207, United States
name: Festac NYC

reviews.text: Went with my wife after church service, instead of take out, we dined in. The food is great, service is impeccable. While we were there, they attended to almost 20 orders. Everyone was just in and out with their orders. Very respectable. The following Sunday, we had to do a take out. The Iyan and egusi soup was so good that when I could barely finish the food, they thought I was done with the food, and they came to clean up... I was like nope, I'm just resting I will finish it 😀😀. Good food

The jollof rice is solid.
The meat pie was dry, like cracker dry.
The chicken, well see for yourself never have seen wings so thin and rock hard like some of the other reviewers mentioned. There were some feathers still visible on there too. Thus I will not chance eating the chicken. I ordered via Ubereats and the food was still nice and hot which was a plus.

I’ve ordered food from them plenty of times, the food is flavorful but you do not get a lot of meat at all, plus the cow foot is always very hard. Maybe that’s how they cook there meats traditionally but I had to put mine in a pot and cook it some more when I got it home. The jollof rice is good.

I stopped by after the lunch crowd left and had a great meal. Both the meal and atmosphere contributed to satisfaction. The team's service approach deserves praise. The yelp community knows about this restaurant. This place creates a lovely environment.

The food here is very promising! I do not think the ponmo is worth $18 at all. But the $4 meats are usually one big piece in a little bit of stew which is fair.
I have not tried their soups just stew and plantain.

formatted_address: 604 Parkside Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11226, United States
name: Akwaaba Restaurant

reviews.text: Most walk by without noticing this place. This restaurant knows how to set the perfect scene. The taste experience works, service flows naturally, and food quality justifies the cost. Staff combined warmth with good information. This spot should be prioritized.

I notice every service interaction. Their dishes matched my taste perfectly. I discovered a true hidden gem!!! The employees balance efficiency with real connections. I'll return to give them higher scores.

Went there twice! Try their Fufu and Okro soup, DELICIOUS!!! The place itself doesn't look like anything.  You'll go there and leave. They don't have a menu, so you pretty need to know what you want ( can check the Google reviews,  and see what others had ordered before). They are very friendly,  give you vibe like you go to a friend house. I love the FUFU, Goat and Okra soup. Give it a shot, you'll not regret.  It's is mostly take out and cash only.

Really cute African restaurant on Parkside Ave, not on a main road so you won't see it unless you randomly pass or search for it. The staff was very friendly and helpful. I had the jaloff rice with beef and veggies. The rice and veggies were really good however the beef was extremely dry and chewy. The only options that day was beef or fish.The dish cost $15.

The food was a good portion, but not especially cheap most things were in the $20-25 range, and cash only. I was in a group that got several things. I myself got the goat with okra and fufu. I usually never have problems with food textures but the texture was disgusting it was like a bunch of sticky slime, and only two small pieces of meat, and a bunch of hard cartilage like stuff. The flavor was ok as in if the texture was ok it would be neutral not good or bad. The smell of the dish was awful it smelt a bit like rotting meat and dog food, everyone in the group I was with agreed it smelt like rotten meat and wouldn’t eat it. Since you eat this with your hands i got some on my hands and then washed my hands after, but later that day and even next day my hands smelt like rotting flesh even after thoroughly cleaning under nails and everything many times. Everybody else in group thought their food was alright with the exception of the other person who got the same thing as me, he couldn’t stomach it.

formatted_address: 125 W 116th St, New York, NY 10026, United States
name: Keur Coumba

reviews.text: The dibi was trashhhhh. They used to be so good. They used to grill it. Now just boiled and it’s very salty. This sucks the onion sauce suck

Worst experience ever! From a loyal customer that I was to them , they gave me rotten food. The food was gluey and smell bad ! Can’t believe I got scammed 60$! I want my money back ! When you order to go they give you bad food !

I was very disappointed with my experience at this restaurant. The drinks were the only good part, but the food was terrible. I ordered the dibi lamb, which was just okay, and my friend ordered the fish. The fish was soggy, loaded with ginger, and basically inedible—she didn’t even eat it. Despite that, we both ended up sick with severe stomach pain after the meal. To make things worse, the bill was wrong. The food was supposed to cost $50, but we were charged an extra $20. Getting sick, being overcharged, and being served such low-quality food is unacceptable. I do not recommend this place to anyone.

This restaurant serves food that makes you smile. Staff members delivered prompt service with a smile. The kitchen delivers on taste, servers enhance the experience, and food quality stands out. The quality here is impressive. The area is improved by this spot's presence.

I'd make this my personal cafeteria if I could afford it. This restaurant balances good flavor, reasonable prices and friendly staff. Total rating. This place has excellent atmosphere, spotless conditions, and minimal decor. From entering to leaving, everything flowed well.

formatted_address: 1174 St Marks Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11213, United States
name: Wakky's African Restaurant

reviews.text:
I absolutely love Wakkys African Restaurant! Every dish I’ve tried has been nothing short of amazing, and my husband swears by their jollof rice, he won’t eat it from anywhere else lol. The flavors are always on point, and the quality is consistent. Egusi, Ogbono, ayamase and stew rice, okra soup!! Everything.
The only downside is the recent change to the meat pies. Whoever tweaked the recipe, please bring back the ORIGINAL ! The old version had the perfect taste and was honestly unbeatable. Still, this place is hands down one of my favorites in Brooklyn. GET THE OLD MEATPIES!! …you’ll thank me later!

The food was very great! I enjoyed the experience and it seemed to get lots of orders and the wait wasn’t that bad. The food in my opinion was very good but for the price I feel I could’ve had more. The Egusi soup was $25 but I felt there could’ve been a little more and the Jollof Rice with lamb was $20 which I think was worth the price. Though I believe these portions are quite good for one person. The flavors were amazing with a nice burst in your mouth and tasted nice and smoky. The goat could’ve been a bit more tender but the sauce over it was amazingly top tier. I with I could’ve smothered my Jollof rice in it too. I would definitely come here again despite it being a whole hour away.

I have only ordered delivery from this restaurant so I can only speak on the food. The low star rating seems unfair so I wanted to share my experience. My regular orders are jollof rice with turkey, egusi or vegetable soup with mixed meats, and the mixed meat stew that’s in a dark red sauce. I usually get the regular fufu (pounded yam) to go with the soup or stews. Can’t go wrong with any of those items. The jollof rice is fresh, beady, flavorful, and best of all not dry! It’s my favorite thing to order here.

Fantastic delicious food! Portharcourt soup was amaze balls! Suya took me back to Lagos, almost challenged Glovercourt Suya! Nkwobi delish!
Wakky Ds will take all my money ooo!!
The soup portions were huge! If you finish the soup in a sitting, you must go and run 3 miles the next day!
It's the worst restaurant in all of New York for service, not to mention they're a bit unhygienic. The staff doesn't treat delivery people well. I don't recommend it....

formatted_address: 242 Court St, Brooklyn, NY 11201, United States
name: Awash

reviews.text:
Awash Ethiopian Restaurant was a great experience.
Food: delicious and filling! Meat combo had a very filling portion of meats and lentils and veggies with injera.
Service: quick and friendly. Restaurant is clean and well-maintained.
Atmosphere: quiet and good for a small group. Would have been nice to have some background music or sounds for ambience.
Incredible food and vibe. I went with my family of four and we got the veggie combo for two and the meat combo for two and it was perfect. I will definitely bringing friends back here.
This place is a 10/10. I’ve been trying many Ethiopian spots around the city and this may top the list. Definitely best traditional gluten-free injera that I’ve found.

Incredible restaurant with delicious options for everyone, including vegetarian/vegan. The lentil dishes were my absolute favorite. So much flavor and quite hearty when ordering the platters. Great service here too, servers are attentive and kind. Drinks were a hit, with options for everyone from cocktails to wine/beer. Very good, will be back again and again.
Unbelievably good. Got the BK special for 3 people (pictured) - so flavorful and filling. Love this place. Please go

formatted_address: 2200 Frederick Douglass Blvd, New York, NY 10026, United States
name: Des Ambassades

reviews.text: Consistency is paramount for me, and my initial visit to this Senegalese restaurant "Les Ambassades" in 2021 during a business meeting left an indelible mark with its unforgettable fried rice, setting an unparalleled standard. Revisiting in 2023, 1 found that the restaurant's commitment to excellence remained unshaken, and their lamb dish proved that great things truly come in small spaces. My friends from Florida, sharing this delightful experience, were equally impressed. I eagerly anticipate my next visit at this remarkable restaurant.

I’ve been coming here since 2013 because they have great food. Unfortunately, the pastries and the food have not been as good. The decline started when they separated the pastry shop from the restaurant area. They increased the price of everything. The pastries taste old. This eclair is soggy but expensive. The chicken is dry. There are less tables, and the tables are sticky. It’s very sad. I remember this place used to always be full of people indoors and outdoors. Their breakfast egg sandwich was unmatched. No longer the case.

I want there for dibi atieke  , dibi  was  not cook trough but was ok. the atieke was the worst ever,  totally dry probably took it out Of the freezer , i had to trow it away. Atieke is not a senegalese dish i can tell,   i got home totally disappointed i am definitely not going back. I felt like i travel too far to go waist my money , that was not worth it.

I decided to trust the collective wisdom about Des Ambassades and wasn't disappointed. Enjoyable meals served with genuine friendliness. You won't need to order side dishes due to size. The workers' kind demeanor transforms routine meals into fun experiences. We plan to return very soon.

I've practiced describing their best dishes to entice friends. Just incredible flavors from start to finish. I was pleased by how attentive and polite everyone remained. This restaurant combines quality and service perfectly! This place pleases me and I'll definitely return.

formatted_address: 2795 Frederick Douglass Blvd, New York, NY 10039, United States
name: Benyam

reviews.text: This was my first time trying Ethiopian food and I loved it! Friendly service and nice ambiance. We had the Sambusa (meat and lentil) Asa Tibs, and Meat & Veggie Sampler for two. It was delicious and so flavorful. Nice portions and filling. We also had the baklava which was yummy. Highly recommend this spot!

What a lovely experience! The restaurant has such a cozy vibe, and the staff were incredibly welcoming from the moment we walked in. We were lucky to get a table — almost every one was reserved, which says a lot! The interior is warm and inviting, with little touches that let you learn more about Ethiopian culture. And the food… absolutely delicious! Every dish was full of rich flavors and clearly made with care. Can’t wait to come back!

First time trying Ethiopian food, and I’m so glad Benyam was the place we chose. My girlfriend and I shared the meat sampler for two, and every single item was incredible. The spices and flavors were absolutely out of this world . Nothing tasted the same, and each sampler really stood on its own. The sampler plate was a full experience, and it made our first time trying Ethiopian food unforgettable. Highly recommend this place to anyone looking to try something new or enjoy amazing Ethiopian cuisine.
Cute, cozy, artsy place with great food & great service. Plenty of vegan and meat dishes. One of the few Ethiopian Cuisine gems in Harlem. Gotta try it!

So delicious! The cabbage was seasoned with a type of mustard oil and very flavorful. The injera was the perfect texture, not too dry. The different veggies were all cooked with different spices so each one had a unique taste! The Ethiopian tea was also so warm and flavorful. 10/10

formatted_address: 1057 Fulton St, Brooklyn, NY 11238, United States
name: Bati Ethiopian Kitchen

reviews.text: Went on a chill Sunday night to experience some smooth jazz and rnb covers. Music was amazing and the crowd response matched. Food came out shortly after ordering. Every dish ordered was cooked to perfection. Staff was very friendly and extremely helpful with the ordering and serving of the food. Definitely would recommend. Ill be back for sure.

here alllll the time lately! at least 1x/week for about a month and a half now! every staff member is welcoming, caring and embodies hospitality. the food is authentic and delicious, the menu wonderfully curated. the espresso martini is like none i’ve had anywhere else, it reminds me of a yoo-hoo chocolate milk! great place to spend the evening.

Wonderful food, excellent service, shout out to Brian, who patiently helped us with the menu and what we would like. We tried a variety of things, all of which were delicious, good sized portions. The food was seasoned well, but not too hot.

Recommended place to try Ethiopian food.  All five of us had a great meal and great time.

First time trying Ethiopian and I really wanted to like it and leave a glowing review, but I can’t.

The service was very warm and inviting and the interior was beautiful, but the food just wasn’t hitting.

I got the 7 Hour Doro Wot, which is the national chicken dish cooked in a spicy onion and Berbere stew, served with a hard-boiled egg. It comes with two sides, and my waitress recommended the Missir Wot, which is stewed split lentils, and Shiro, a saucy chickpea dish.

It all came served on a bed of injera, which is a spongy, sour, pancake-like flatbread, and they gave me a small plate of extra injera on the side. The food looked flavorful, but I was super disappointed once I took a bite of the chicken. I was expecting tender, moist meat, and instead it was hard and dry. The stew wasn’t flavorless, but it also didn’t have much going on. The lentils were okay, and the only thing I really liked was the chickpeas.

On the bright side, it was a pretty filling meal, though that might have been because I had a double smashburger an hour earlier.

Very Authentic!

We stopped by with out a reservation and got a seat. Very thankful it wasn’t very crowded on this night. But as the night progressed the place did fill up! (Make reservation)

The area is up and coming and I actually got parking on the street around the corner. This was very convenient. I was with some meat eaters so they ordered meat dishes and I had the vegetarian option of course. They kept mine separate! Very happy they accommodated.

Place was quiet and very open. It wasn’t cramped. Very clean Bathrooms. I must return to try this place again.

formatted_address: 828 2nd Ave, New York, NY 10017, United States
name: DF Nigerian Food Truck

reviews.text:
My coworker and I were craving West African food for lunch and found a Nigerian food truck nearby, so we decided to give it a try. We ordered the jollof rice with jerk chicken and asked for it extra spicy but the rice ended up being pretty mild with no kick to it. The jerk chicken was flavorful but was unfortunately dry.

We also got the egusi soup with beef and fufu. The beef was actually quite flavorful, but the egusi was a little too bitter for my taste. They did throw in some complimentary puff puff, which was a nice gesture, but it was a bit burnt so I didn’t really like it.

It was also a bit pricey… Meh.
I really enjoyed the fufu and egusi soup with beef. This was my first time having Nigerian food and I loved it! Will definitely be back!

If I could give zero stars I would do so. This place is so unprofessional is laughable. You call the number and no one answers. If they think you are American they try to over charge you. Ever since this truck as taken on new ownership it has been a problem. The owner who pretended he was just a worker tried to charge me $22 for okra stew with no meat or swallow. Imagine if I was silly enough to pay it. This truck is owned by a scammer. Just making our people look any how because of greed!!! It is very disappointing and is an embarrassment to our culture. Avoid at all cost. Stay blessed everyone.

I want to sincerely thank Divine Catering Services for the excellent job they did at my daughter’s wedding. From start to finish, their team was professional, attentive, and truly dedicated to making the day special. The food was absolutely delicious, beautifully presented, and enjoyed by all of our guests. Many people are still talking about how wonderful the meals and service were.

What stood out most was their attention to detail and the way they went above and beyond to ensure everything ran smoothly. They didn’t just cater the event; they helped create a warm, joyful atmosphere that made the celebration even more memorable.

I highly recommend Divine Catering Services to anyone looking for quality, reliability, and a team that genuinely cares about making your occasion perfect. Thank you again for helping make my daughter’s wedding day so unforgettable!

Divine Flavor exceeded my expectations in every way. The food was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented. Delivery was prompt, and everything served just as ordered. The staff is professional, friendly, and attentive, which made the experience even better. I highly recommend Divine Flavor Food truck to anyone looking for quality meals and outstanding customer service. I’ll definitely be ordering again!

formatted_address: 182 Avenue B #1, New York, NY 10009, United States
name: Haile

reviews.text:
It was very delicious and filling! Service was slow. We walked in on a Friday night, but they only seat full parties. The tea was lovely. You get to try so much of the menu because each meal comes with many of the plates.

Vegetarian and meat plates!

The lamb was the best part by far!!

Id never had Ethiopian food before. Definitely will be going back!

The host was amazing, we asked her to recommend the best dishes. She brought us a combination of lamb, beef, chicken, and a few veggies. They serve it with traditional Ethiopian bread, which doubles as your eating utensils.

Great service, great food, great place.

Ethiopian food is my favorite, so i've checked out several spots in nyc. Haile is definitely my favorite. The food is really delicious, and i find that the injera here is the best i've had in the city. Big portions at a reasonable price too. The ladies are super sweat and the place is quaint.
Had such a lovely anniversary dinner here! Great neighborhood spot for Ethiopian classics to share + delicious honey wine, plus really sweet and kind service. Will be returning!

This place is super cozy! It’s run by women that make you feel at home. They clearly work so hard and the place has such positive vibes. The food was so authentic and layered with flavors. The service is attentive and warming.

It was my first time trying Ethiopian food and I don’t know why I was nervous! I really wanted a delicious meal and I definitely got one here. Highly recommend this place!

formatted_address: 338 E 6th St, New York, NY 10003, United States
name: Awash Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: Everyone left feeling the meal was worth what we paid. Both cuisine and staff friendliness exceeded expectations. Their dishes showcase unusual talent. You receive generous servings at reasonable rates. I am definitely going to be a frequent diner here now.
Shared the sampler dish and it was delicious, had been craving Ethiopian food and it delivered! Nice atmosphere and service!

You can close your eyes and point to anything on the menu here. Their prices match the taste experience. Their staff combined professionalism with a warm approach. The bill always seems fair for what's received. The pricing is fair for the excellent food quality.

It may look like your average neighborhood restaurant, but the food is amazing!I  wandered in with two friends on a Sunday afternoon, and was immediately greeted by the friendly staff. Restaurant was not that crowded.
We ordered Meat Sampler with one Premium Sampler Item and three boiled eggs (For three members together) You can get it individual plate. But we thought of eating Ethiopian way.
The service person really explained everything about the ,menu and the quantity go the food. So we were not at all confused with anything. Food was so tasty and we could not stop eating. You can get Ethiopian beer in this restaurant. Only one negative thing I noticed is the washroom. It was not that great and may be its NY. So we need to adjust.

Few places manage to get everything right like they do here. Their interior styling stands out. The food quality shows in the taste. Their dishes and employee attentiveness were commendable. This place performs with excellence.

formatted_address: 1451 Bedford Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11216, United States
name: Cafe Rue Dix

reviews.text: My wife and I have ate at this place several times mostly on the weekends but my wife have eaten here doing the week after work. The food is amazing especially the branzino and the burger with blue cheese . The Gambas is wonderful. On Saturdays the DJ is in the house and is really good. The lighting is just right for a nice night out with friends or a romantic night out . You can sit  at the bar or sit at the floor tables. The manager Chris is a wonderful host there was a time on my wife's birthday we didn't realize he was on vacation and we called him and he went above and beyond to put in our order before the kitchen closed. The staff is amazing and friendly making you feel like good friends every time you arrive. Yanick the bartender with is signature drink the hibiscus margaritas is amazing and cris his is also fantastic!

This is a great spot on the corner, cozy and open on nice days. We were seated immediately though it did get very busy quickly. We tried the duck croquette confit appetizer which was very good, the spicy sauce made it a hit for me personally because I love spicy food. We ordered sandwiches and a salad because we were here for lunch and they were great. Mine was chicken and had what tastes to me like a similar spicy sauce which really made the sandwich. I've never had Senegalese cuisine before but would definitely be willing to come again to try dinner next time.

Yes, I love the vibe and the food here! It’s such a great neighborhood gem! I love how cultural the whole vibe is, chilled and relaxing. And the food is absolutely delicious! I try the fataya for the first time. It’s hot but yummy hot! The bread pudding is exceptional as well! We need more small businesses like this in the city!

The food and service here were great! I had a snapper dish - sooo flavorful !
Definitely worth a visit.

Menu is a combination of Senegalese and more traditional bistro items. We went for the Senegalese options and really liked them. Service was great. Really attentive even after the restaurant filled up later in the evening. Really causal, neighborhood vibe. Look forward to going back.

formatted_address: 1300 E 222nd St, Bronx, NY 10469, United States
name: EazyLife Restaurant & Lounge - West African Cuisine

reviews.text: Went with a friend. I wasn't too pleased. Joloff rice tasted like left overs that were microwaved. I didn't like it but I ate it. Everything else was good and seemed fresh. I came from BK. I probably won't return

They are flopping big time would order from them and it be great, lately the food is thrash I ordered on grub hub on dec 16th pepper goat soup which was amazing, but the Edikang Ikong soup was horrible  super dry hardly no meat just bone and it's like just threw the vegetable on top.. wasted my money not buying from here  again

Got jollof rice,  poundo yam with egusi. The meal was nice, and the portion was satisfying, not bad at all. My only issue was with the egusi; it was a bit too dry for my liking. Other than that, everything tasted great!

It is always an amazing experience when you are in New York City 🗽🇺🇸 exploring the city. As soon as my friends learned I was in town, they insisted on taking me and my family out for dinner 🍽.

My brother from another mother who was a childhood friend that we grew up together, Barrister Christmas Akpodiete had to drive three hours from the State of Connecticut 🇺🇸. My other friend for many years in Nigeria Mr. David Seyi Otaru Miliki also came in from the State of New Jersey 🇺🇸.

They both ensure that we drove in convoy to a prestigious Nigerian restaurant in the Bronx area of New York City 🇺🇸 called Easy Life restaurant for a dinner. It was for me a joy to see my children observe the generosity of my friends right on their faces.

One of my children was to later tell me that "Dad, now I can see and feel the reward of your hosting your friends and visitors nearly every week at our home."

We enjoyed a lavish Nigerian dinner cuisine, full of flavorful dishes. The food was absolutely delicious, and the company was even better. It was a beautiful night, filled with laughter and good food, creating unforgettable memories.

Please join me in appreciating these great men who devoted their very scarce timing to give us these fabulous entertainment. May God bless you guys🙏

#NYCAdventures #NigerianCuisine #FoodieFriends #DinnerDate
#FriendshipGoals #GenuineConnections #MakingMemories
#highlightseveryone #followersreels #followers #highlight #usa
As the name suggests, relax and make your life easier with  refreshing drinks and food.

formatted_address: 453 Granville Payne Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11207, United States
name: Ewe's Delicious Treats

reviews.text:
Absolutely the Best African Food Spot Around!

If you’re looking for authentic, delicious African food that tastes like home, look no further than EWES Delicious Street! I’ve been buying from this gem of a restaurant for over four years now, and I can confidently say that the food has never disappointed.

The Ogbono soup with CowFoot is rich and flavorful, the okra soup with goat meat is always tender and perfectly seasoned, the okra soup hits every time, and don’t even get me started on the pounded yam — soft, stretchy, and the perfect complement to the soups. It’s the kind of meal that makes you close your eyes with every bite.

What truly sets this place apart, though, is the owner. Her customer service is truly on point. She treats me like family — honestly, like a daughter — and it’s that warmth and care that keeps me coming back just as much as the food. I had been a loyal customer for years before we even met in person after I moved closer to her restaurant last year, and it felt like we had known each other forever.

I literally eat from EWES Delicious Street every day if I can, and you’ll always find me there on Fridays and weekends without fail. I always get the same meal because it’s that good, and she always hooks me up! The prices are more than reasonable for the portions and quality you get.

What’s even more beautiful is that my children have grown up on her food. My youngest has been eating it since she was one — she’s turning five now — and my oldest has loved it since she was four. She’s now eight. That’s how deeply connected we are to this restaurant. The food is not just a meal, it’s a part of our family tradition as a born Jamaican.

The flavor, the authenticity, the love in every dish — and the owner’s vibrant, kindhearted personality — make EWES Delicious Street a place I’ll always recommend to anyone craving real African cuisine. Five stars isn’t even enough!

I should’ve read the reviews thoroughly. The staff was VERY kind and friendly, however the food was VERY undercooked. I ordered chicken roti and fried dough.
You can see in my photos, the chicken roti meat was *PINK&RED*, and it had a lot of mini bones in it and large bones (roti isn’t supposed to have any bones)
The fried dough balls on the exterior were crispy but as soon as you bite into it, the inside is gooey and stretchy like cake batter/undercooked flour.

This food could’ve made me very sick had I not stopped to observe. *none of the food was thoroughly cooked. I was only able to eat the roti flour but not the meat or the fried dough. I had to throw my food away* The staff is wonderful, but the food needs to be observed very carefully.

My fiancée and I also ate here and it was delicious. The staff was friendly and the food was organic and tasty. Definitely we will have to return again some time in the future. This review should and sounds like a 5/5, what's wrong with Daniel Wleh.

In all honesty, Ewe's Delicious Treats delivers incredible flavors and service. However, the true magic of this place are the man and the woman running the show. Dining at their establishment makes you feel like you're being fed at a loving family. I've never had such a delicious meal prepared by such caring people before, so please experience this for yourself!
My wife and I ate here and it was delicious. The staff was friendly and the food was organic and tasty. Definitely we will have to return again some times in the future.

Generally, I always enjoy Nigerian food but this was not it. The stew chicken was barely warm on the outside and it was cold on the inside, it was also tuff (probably microwaved or stale). The efo was bland, and had chicken instead of fish? The goat was alright. All of the dishes plus the jolloff rice were over powered with tomato sauce/paste. Try Buka in Crown Heights, they have a better flavor profile & it’s not a waste of money. Everything besides the goat was thrown out.

formatted_address: 1639 Bedford Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11225, United States
name: Hafiya Restaurant

reviews.text: Great food and wonderful service for a good price. All food is weighted. The beans were on point

Authentic African dishes. Customer service is ok; the young lady took the time to describe the dishes. Pretty worth it for the price and lots of variety.
Cleanliness could be better.

The portions are huge but tasteless and oily.  They use so much oil. The goat meat is hard. Once I spent $15 on food there and had to toss it.  Some of the dishes are prepared well some aren’t. It’s really a hit and miss

I would post a picture but I ate my entire platter (2 people could've shared that but I ate all of it). Everything was delicious- it looks like they had not so great reviews a few months ago but maybe they fixed the issue because my meal and fresh juice was fantastic, especially for the price.

I ordered from this location a couple of  times, and the food was ok. But the fact that the restaurant never picks up my calls freaks me out and makes me wonder if this place is even legit. So I am concerned about the lack of transparency, which is why I gave 2 starts… prove me wrong, and I will update my review…

formatted_address: 4120 A White Plains Rd, Bronx, NY 10466, United States
name: Krystal African Restaurant

reviews.text: I ordered from this restaurant on the 2nd of October with UberEats. I ordered Fufu with Egusi soup and Thiebou Guinar. It all costed me $48.42. With that price I paid I expected it to be amazing or something like that. No. It was not good. The egusi soup was not authentic. In fact I only got 3 pieces of meat. Lol. I don’t think they should serve it because it should be made authentically. The Thiebou Guinar was okay. At least my husband thinks so. It was lacking some flavor. They probably didn’t add a lot of Nokoss (seasoning). Honestly I don’t recommend this restaurant. I give everything a 6/10. For an African restaurant….do better.
Wasn't please with my order  one loaf of fat instead of meat and big bone and I could count all tiny bitter leaf,  can do better nothing cost for not to cook right way . And some love into it ...

The food was dry, my order was wrong. I bought one grilled and one fried tilapia, I received both grilled. The both fish were dry and one was burnt, and on top of it all the presentation and packaging was horribl.

Nice people, Good service
Excellent food 👌🏾 I very recommend you

Great service and also the food.
I wanted to try fufu for the first time so I ordered fufu and Okra Soup (it tasted great). Love them

formatted_address: 62 E 116th St, New York, NY 10029, United States
name: Cross Culture Kitchen

reviews.text:
Update : place seem is permanently close as I  predict , not what I wish for them , but putting the wrong poeples as main servers can have devastating result on any business...

Hopefully new management will
Be able to reopen .

I didn't change my review below for my prior experience at this place .

Please can someone write review when you see any recent menu with prices ?

I love to go back to help this business owner once they have serious poeples in charge of serving customers and not ripping them off .
And if the owner is the same person that scamming poeples on prices ,than never mind.

Lunch time , they were seeving jamaican dishes.
I heard in the evening, it become african dishes.

name: Adom African Cuisine inc

reviews.text:
A Taste of Home in the Bronx

Walking into Adom in the Bronx doesn’t feel like stepping into a restaurant; it feels like crossing a threshold back into your grandmother’s kitchen in Ghana. The air is thick with the perfume of smoked fish, slow-simmered palm oil, and the bright, earthy tang of shito. It’s not just food here, it’s inheritance, cooked low and patient.

The service? Unscripted warmth. No forced smiles, no transactional pleasantries. They greet you the Ghanaian way, like family who’s been gone too long. A staff member placed a hand on my shoulder and said, “You’re home now. Sit. Eat.” That’s not hospitality; that’s belonging.

I started with kelewele, plantains kissed by spice and char, each bite humming with ginger and hidden heat. Then came the fufu with peanut soup, a bowl that could humble a man. The broth was fiery and honest, layered with the slow burn of Scotch bonnets and the soul of chicken meat that had given everything to the pot. Each swallow was a pilgrimage.

The waakye arrived like a quiet sermon, beans and rice stained deep with sorghum leaf, crowned with gari, fried plantain, spaghetti (because Ghana does what it wants), shito dark as midnight, and a boiled egg standing guard. It wasn’t pretty. It was powerful.

What makes Adom extraordinary isn’t innovation or spectacle; it’s fidelity. They’re not reimagining Ghanaian cuisine, they’re preserving it, unaltered, unapologetic. In a city obsessed with reinvention, Adom dares to remember.

Anthony Bourdain once said, “You learn a lot about someone when you share a meal together.” At Adom, you learn about Ghana, its fire, its comfort, its unshakable pride. And if you’re Ghanaian, you remember who you are.

Adom isn’t just serving food. They’re serving home, and in this city, that’s the rarest dish of all.

A simple spot serving delicious West African comfort food. We had the Jollof Rice and Egusi with Fufu, and the staff were super welcoming and great about explaining the menu and meat options. Both dishes were richly seasoned and deeply satisfying.
Food was fantastic! Would love if this place was near me, Ghana makes the best jollof!!

10/10, if not 20/10. Great food and hospitality. The nicest host and the food was amazing. Can’t go wrong with any option. We had Jollof, Waakye, fried rice, and fried yam. All were amazing. The plantains too. If you like good African food and trying new things. Come here!

Adom Cuisine isn’t just a restaurant — it’s a homecoming. From the moment you step inside, the warm hospitality, rich aromas, and vibrant atmosphere transport you straight to West Africa. Every single dish is a celebration of Ghanaian culture and tradition, prepared with authenticity, soul, and care.

The food is nothing short of phenomenal. Their jollof rice is perfectly spiced and deeply flavorful, the kind that lingers on your taste buds long after the last bite. The waakye is hearty and comforting, with layers of texture and taste that make it impossible not to devour. And don’t even get me started on the fufu — soft, stretchy, and paired with rich soups that are bold, complex, and deeply satisfying. Every plate here tastes like it was cooked with love in someone’s kitchen back home.

What truly sets Adom Cuisine apart, though, is the experience. The staff treats you like family, eager to share the story behind every dish and ensure you leave full and happy. It’s rare to find a restaurant that captures the essence of a culture so perfectly — but Adom Cuisine does just that.

If you’re craving authentic Ghanaian food or just want to experience one of New York’s most soulful and flavorful meals, this is the place. Adom Cuisine isn’t just the best Ghanaian restaurant in New York — it’s one of the best dining experiences in the entire city. 🌍🍲🇬🇭

I also tried attieke for the first time and, although I was hesitant, it surprised me with how delicious it was, especially when I sprinkled a little Maggi cube over it. The plantains were cooked just the way I like them, slightly overripe and sweet. I wanted to try the sorrel juice, but since they were out, I went with the ginger juice instead, which was refreshing and full of flavor. The atmosphere was lively with great music, and the prices were very reasonable for the quality of the food. Overall, the food, service, and vibe were excellent, and I’ll definitely be returning to try the lamb and the sorrel juice next time.

Authentic Ivorian Flavors and Good Vibes at YopCity – Arthur Avenue, Bronx

I recently visited YopCity on Arthur Avenue in the Bronx with friends and family, and it was such a vibrant experience! As a fan of African cuisine, I was excited to try this Ivorian spot—and it did not disappoint.

I ordered the grilled fish topped with onions and peppers, paired with attieke (cassava couscous) and sweet plantains. The flavors were rich and satisfying, though I found the food a little on the oily side for my personal taste. Still, the seasoning and preparation were excellent.

One thing to note: my friend’s daughter has a peanut allergy, and when we asked if any dishes were made with peanut oil or peanut-based ingredients, the server wasn’t quite sure, so she played it safe and ordered French fries. It might be helpful if the staff were better informed about allergen information.

Two of the ladies in our group ordered the Dubi with sweet plantains and really enjoyed their meals. We also had bissap (hibiscus juice) and ginger juice, both of which were refreshing and delicious!

The music and atmosphere at YopCity were definitely a highlight—great energy, friendly vibe, and a space that made you want to dance. It’s a wonderful spot to enjoy a taste of West Africa right in the Bronx.

Overall, I’d recommend YopCity for anyone looking to explore Ivorian dishes and soak up good vibes. Just be sure to ask about ingredients if you have food allergies.

Walking into Yop City felt so warm and welcoming. We even got a chance to speak with the owner, who was super kind and passionate about sharing Ivorian food and culture. The food was incredible — the attiéké with fish was perfectly seasoned, and the alloco was fried just right, crispy and sweet. Portions are generous, and you can really taste the authenticity in every bite. This spot definitely makes you feel at home, and I’ll be coming back again and again.

The workers are so nice and kind and treat costumers with respect and kindness. The owner can out and greeted us and was so nice. The food was also very delicious and flavorful!

I did not dine at Olaide, but I had take out there. As a Nigerian, Olaide hit all the high notes and none of the wrong ones.  The food made me sing and reminded me of home. The food was outstanding, portions plenty and the execution and presentation A+++. Olaide's Kitchen is a welcome addition to the community and adds to the rich tapestry of foods available in Jersey City Heights. I will definitely be back, hungry and with friends.

formatted_address: 1344 E Gun Hill Rd, Bronx, NY 10469, United States
name: OSU - R.E. Grill

reviews.text: So glad the restaurant I was going to down the street was closed or I wouldn’t have found this place 😍 amazing customer service & the food is so so delicious . I ordered banku & okra stew. I wasn’t familiar with the menu and the man in the front was very helpful. I’ll be back whenever I’m in the Bronx .

Really good I like like the chicken and jollof rice. The lamb suya is also really good fried that for the first time the other day kinda pricey but portion is decent and they got some good interesting beverage selections there

So I was excited to find Ghanaian food in walking distance. I ordered the Waakye combo and I was not happy at all. Goat was tuff and fish was dry. Couldn't eat it. Feeling disappointed and angry. I also ordered a second plate, the fried rice chicken combo. I started to not eat it after the first plate but when I did WOW! Redemption!  Everything was perfect and the flavor was amazing.
I say this with love. If it is not right don't serve it. Yes I wanted Ghanaian food but I also wanted to support the business. Win brother by doing it right with all off the food. You got this  👍.

The best Ghanaian restaurant in NY, the food here gives nostalgia to eating good food in Ghana.

The Jollof rice was 10/10, the Fried Rice was really good too. Ate Waakye on another visit and that was equally good. The chicken was good too, and the salad was the most Ghanaian salad I've had in America.

The service was okay, but it was a little difficult getting the attention of the servers (probably due to the large amount of orders they deal with).

The food here is one of the most authentically Ghanaian ones I’ve had in the East Coast. Choose between the Osu RE Kenkey or the turkey tail (tsoffi). They also have a stock of Ghanaian beers and drinks - malt, Star beer 🍻. We had lunch with a group of friends and cousins when we visited the Bronx and it was a memorable experience. Parking is hard to find in the area.

formatted_address: 2037 Webster Ave # 1, Bronx, NY 10457, United States
name: The Point African Restaurant

reviews.text:
I PLACED MY FOR DELIVERY AROUND 2: 40 SOMETHING PM, THE LATEST DELIVERY WAS SUPPOSED TO BE AROUND 3:43-47PM AND CHANGED FROM THAT TO AN HOUR LATER I.E. 4:43-47PM.

I SAW THAT THE 1ST DELIVERY (WHOM I CHATTED WITH & HE RESPONDED BACK) GUY REFUSED TO WAIT ANYLONGER FOR PUCK-UP OF THE FOOD.
ANOTHER DELIVERY GUY CAME ALONG AND I CHATTED WITH HIM TOO, ABD ALL I WAS WAITING FOR WAS THEGUY SUPOSEDLY WAITING/GOING TO DO THE FOOD PICK-UP..🙄🤦🏾‍♂️.

AT 4:00PM, WAS WHEN I SAW ON THE APP THAT THAT 6 ORDERS OF DIFFERENT FOODS THAT WERE SUPPOSEDLY PREPARED, WAS CANCELLED.

NOW, SOMEONE, TELL ME HOW PROFESSIONAL & HOW A RESTAURANT CODE OF ETHICS WAS/WERE.

AND THE SYSTEM SAID THAT IF THEY CHARGED TO MY ACCOUNT, THEN I SHOULD WAIT FOR 24 HOURS...
PLEASE READ THE EXACT WORDS FOR YOURSELF BELOW;

"😳Receipt will be generated within 24 hours after your payment has been processed or within 24 hours after your order delivery. Please,check back later😳"

They act like the food is not for selling. So rude to the consumers, and they don’t want to give you the amount you order?!! (So dumb) what’s the point of the business then. On top of that my meat pie came back uncooked, I wish I can add a picture to this.

I’ve given The Point African Restaurant multiple chances, but every visit has been disappointing. The server is consistently rude and disrespectful. This dude lacks MANNERS. There is absolutely no sense of customer service, no greeting, no courtesy, just attitude and frustration directed at paying customers. He makes it seem like you are begging him for free food.
On top of that, hygiene is clearly not a priority. The server handles food without gloves, which is very concerning. It’s uncomfortable and makes you question how clean things are behind the scenes.
I won’t be returning, and I don’t recommend it to others. I know the server/partial owner is going to read and reply to this. The massage to you is, I hope you change your ways.

The Point restaurant have always been me and my sister's favorite place to buy food but the food we bought recently (April 23rd, 2025) was spoiled because it had this slimy texture and it smelled so bad. Please you guys did not do well at all. Our money, just gone like that. How could you guys 😮‍💨? Why? 😢😢😥 very disappointing.
I buy food here all the time. When I tell you….chef kiss!!! I always order the jollof rice with fish. I travel where ever am at to get this food because I tried numerous place and it ain’t it!!
