name: Dee & Pea African Catering services

formatted_address: 76 Canal St, Staten Island, NY 10304, United States
name: Bridge's Kitchen Liberian Cuisine

reviews.text: First time and it won’t be my last, the food is so good and flavorful, I ordered jollof with Kala, and I ate everything on the spot, looking forward to trying everything on the menu, 10/10 don’t walk, RUN!! 🥳 #ForeverLIBFood

The staff/Brigitte are welcoming and warm just as much as the food!! My mom absolutely loved the Palava Sauce & Fufu. I ate a lot of the Cassava Leaf / Rice throughout my day and am looking forward to visiting again to eat more! :) Highly recommend you also try the muffins and the fried donuts

Brigde's Kitchen is a mobile food truck serving authentic Liberian foods. If you haven't tried Liberian food, she serves burgers, chili, wings & fries. There's jollof rice, cassava leaf & rice, banana bread & take home jarred habernero pepper sauce. You can put the sauce on everything! Come visit soon. Everything is so delicious. You have to try it...NOW!!
Updating due to disparaging & untruthful review. Being disappointed & probably hungry at the same time does not mean one should make untrue statements. The truck is clean on the outside and inside. The food truck is in a clean open space between two businesses. The truck is kept behind a chain linked fence amd locked for safety purposes when closed for business. Give the small minority woman owned business another try after checking their hours. I visit the truck once a week & purchase several meals. It is always clean & the owner always welcoming with a big smile and tasty food.

I ordered both the palm butter with fufu and palava sauce with rice and both were really good! The pepper sauce was amazinggg. But most importantly the customer service was superb and that was very much so appreciated. I will definitely be a returning customer & I can’t wait to see this business grow
Finally got a chance to get Liberian food from Bridge's Kitchen. Her Jollof rice is off the chain plus her fried chicken was very tasty. Next time I'm gonna try her chilli.

formatted_address: 180 Rockaway Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11233, United States
name: The Green Place

reviews.text: All parts of my visit exceeded normal expectations. Their plates have enough food that two people can easily share. The place delivers the goods. Employees' warmth makes this place worth visiting. I'm glad I came across this wonderful restaurant.

Worst service from Emily!! I was given dry beef cubes instead of Suya. She apologizes and says they ran out of suya so just call the number of green place and she will give me suya the next day as replacement. She keeps me waiting for two days, and when the suya is ready she says no I need to pay for it on Uber Eats and starts fighting with me over the phone that nothing is free even though they messed my order up!!! Horrible horrible service, horrible attitude!! I will never eat here again

My Nigerian boyfriend and I always come here for their egussi and Efo riro. The flavors are simply amazing. We have also tried their jollof but it’s not our favorite as it’s a bit too smoky for us. They also only take cash which is inconvenient. Overall, I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone who loves flavor in their food.
Very Nice Place to Eat Anytime you are in Brooklyn.
The moi-moi I just received had a very horrible odor. I knew it wasn’t fit for human consumption once I opened it up. Now questioning everything I bought from this place. (Uber order)

formatted_address: 237 Madison Ave, New York, NY 10016, United States
name: LÉLÉ

reviews.text: Upon entering this establishment I was taken away by the ambience and atmosphere. Everything looks upscale and high end. The seats were comfortable but it was really cold. They had a good mix of music. The service was lackluster for our expectations given the price point. We ordered chicken wings, shrimp, oxtail and lamb chops with a side order of Haitian white rice. The food was definitely lacking the true authentic Caribbean flavor especially given the price of each meal. We paid about $60 for an entree of oxtail. We were only given 5 pieces of oxtails and one of the pieces were inedible given that I had to chew it for minutes and still could not swallow it. The shrimp app was good but for $36 it definitely wasn’t worth it. The lamb chops were good but for the price it didn’t even come with a side. We had to pay extra for white rice . The wings were ok but had too much dry rub on it. It had no flavor but the sauce that came with it was good. All in all it definitely doesn’t taste good enough for the place to be charging the prices it does.

This place served EXCELLENT Haitian inspired cuisine. We came here to celebrate my mom’s birthday and left extremely happy.

Some of the highlights include their homemade punch, the chicken wings and the oxtails. But honestly, everything we had was delicious. Highly, highly recommend this spot.

LÈLÈ

Review summary:
A beautiful intimate space with strong potential. With clearer communication, more intentional service, and a deeper expression of Afro-Caribbean warmth/hospitality LÈLÈ could truly shine.

Detailed review:

An Afro-Caribbean restaurant with striking gold accents, lush greenery, and a prime East Side location.

The experience was good overall, but the hospitality lacked clarity and consistency. I arrived late to my reservation and understood when my table was released. When I asked about bar seating, I was told there was no space—yet I noticed several open tables. I returned to the host stand to ask one simple question: the wait time for the next available two-top. I was told there was no timeframe and we would need to wait indefinitely, which felt misaligned as open tables sat unused and a line formed at the door. As we prepared to leave, we were told we were “just about to be seated,” a moment that felt poorly timed and inconsistent.

Once seated, anticipation was high—elegance, warmth, and a sense of Afro-Caribbean hospitality. Unfortunately, that elevation didn’t fully translate. Service felt transactional: minimal menu guidance, little storytelling, and no sense of a curated experience unless prompted. Support staff interactions also felt uneven and could benefit from more refinement and intention. For a restaurant of this caliber and price point, the experience should feel more polished and guest-forward.

We ordered the hamachi, akra, pikliz, sweet plantains, oxtail, curry goat, white rice, drinks, and ice cream for dessert. While enjoyable, many of these Haitian staples fell slightly short of expectation.

Overall the dining experience was very nice. We went on Friday night and it was carnival night so they had dancers dressed in costume playing Caribbean music. There aren’t that many upscale authentic Caribbean upscale restaurants in NYC and this was 10/10. Food was delicious, vibe and ambience lived up to the hype for this new restaurant. It’s definitely a date night/birthday celebration location. Decor is beautiful. Highly recommend.

We visited LELE’s on a last minute trip to NYC on my birthday. I was so nervous asking if they would take a walk in table of two. Knowing you needed a reservation, than we asked if they may have two bar seats and thanks to the big man up stairs they escorted us to the bar. We were immediately greeted by a goddess bartender who had the most beautiful smile.

She made us drinks fairly quickly and gave us a good menu. We ordered plantain, and the curry goat. The mango sauce with the plantain was the most delectable refreshing light sauce. And the plantain were crispy and sweet a perfect balance. The curry goat was the best I had it was in a stew, and the goat was shredded giving each bite a full taste.

Being happy with the everything I asked the bartender if we could talk to the chef and he came over and was super nice. LELE’s was 10/10 I hope to return next year.

formatted_address: 101 St Marks Pl, New York, NY 10009, United States
name: Cafe Mogador

reviews.text: Host is quick & attentive. Servers are sweet & polite. Food portion & presentation is poor. I expected the lamb dish to have more starchy vegetables. All the meats were tender. The lamb taste was an 8/10. The skewers, sausage & salad were a 10/10. The “fresh” nonalcoholic drinks were questionable. Timing was also off from the kitchen (additional salad came 10 minutes later). The price for 2 people was $80 before tip. I would not come here again. Thank you for service.

Perfect spot for breakfast. The Middle Eastern breakfast was light, flavourful and delicious. There were a lot of great options to choose from on the menu, I could go there every day for a week and get something new each time. Had a black americano too and it was great. They were quite busy, so staff were not super attentive but welcoming and friendly  regardless 💫💫💫💫💫

Food definitively the highlight of this location. Food prepared with balance and care. Hot sauce with hummus was amazing and eggs very well prepared. Salad with beets and vinegrette excellent. The postcard with the image of the owners grandparents made the visit more meaningful. Busy but service prompt and seating quaint. Will visit again.

I fell in love with Moroccan food the first time I ate at Café Mogador. The food is consistently  delicious, and the whole place has that warm, cozy, late-night vibe that I love. My must eats? The lamb shank with stewed apricots and prunes, the sautéed calamari, and for dessert, the knaffeh topped with roasted pistachios and rose water syrup. Reservations are highly recommended, as the restaurant is always bustling. Dinner at Café Mogador? Always a win.

Cafe Mogador was outstanding. The food was incredibly flavorful and beautifully prepared—everything tasted fresh and thoughtfully made. Service was friendly, attentive, and efficient without feeling rushed. The atmosphere was warm, lively, and inviting, making it a perfect spot for a relaxed meal. Easily one of those places that lives up to the hype and is worth coming back to. Highly recommend!

formatted_address: 947 Amsterdam Ave, New York, NY 10025, United States
name: Awash Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: 5/5 Ethiopian food!!! I’ve now been here three times in the last two years, and have traveled from all over Manhattan to come eat at this Awash! I love their Kitfo and vegetarian sampler platter. I’ll have to keep coming back so I can try everything on the menu! This isn’t fast food and it’s meant to be enjoyed slowly, so don’t eat here if you’re in a hurry.

04/23/25
Started with the tella (a honey wine, coffee and jalapeño cocktail) and Timatim Fitfit for an appetizer. We had the awash chicken and the Yatakilt Alicha. Everything was incredible and fresh and flavorful. Prices were reasonable and service was good. My first time having Ethiopian food, it couldn’t have been better.

Awesome food!  I love that you get to eat with your hands!  There may be a cultural disconnect with the way that they wait on you but they are very respectful and nice with smiles!  Get the platter with meats and veggies! So good!

The Best Ethiopian food compared to CT and FL.
We have been regulars for 20 years.
Be sure to go for dinner, especially on the weekends and you will be rewarded with the best chef!!

I ordered on uber eats and it came faster than expected. Super delicious, the injera is fresh and the lamb with collard greens very nice. The portion is huge! My favorite however was the lentil dish - I think it was misir wat. Will def order again.

formatted_address: 55 Bleeker St, Newark, NJ 07102, United States
name: African Pot Eatery Food Truck

reviews.text: Honestly the ambience here is amazing. From the minute you walk in you have such a great feeling very clean and well kept. The setting is very inviting. The food was great exactly as I expected. Will definitely be coming back! The chef also was very professional. Great place

I decided to give this African food truck a try because of how good the reviews were after doing deeper research I see 98% of the reviews are from 2 years ago. The goat pepper soup was a 3/10 the soup was watery and filled with salt! The goat was so hard to chew and needed to be cooked much longer. The goat meat was filled with bones and hardly any meat. The egusi was filled with oil and SALT did not  taste good at all. The food was extremely OILY . The egusi had two small pieces of turkey meat a big cow foot bone no meat. Not to mention this salt filled meal cost nearly 50$ you’re better off going to an authentic African restaurant for better food and a better price. ZERO STARS
I feel like I went to Lagos. The food is amazing I had the kpomo and then the grilled fish ! Amazing home cooked feel and environment ❤️

A Beautiful Touch of African cuisine, Neat, spacious and very conducive.
Highly Recommended.

Had the jollof rice and goat meat.  Never had jollof before so can't comment on authenticity but I liked it.  Goat meat was, no exaggeration, the texture of shoe leather.  Grew up on goat meat and that's 100% poor cooking technique.  Either give the meat another 2-3 hours to soften up or use some Asian velveting technique to speed up the process.  You can't keep selling this.  If doing a better job just means cooking the food a little longer then you not doing that simple means you don't care enough to do better.  $17 for a lot of rice isn't going to get you a lot of repeat customers.  I certainly don't intend to return.  Also goat didn't taste like goat.  Probably it was mutton, which is legal in the US to do, but sketchy.

formatted_address: 1039 Belmont Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11208, United States
name: Ecowas Kitchen (Amala Junction)

reviews.text:
I absolutely loveeee okra soup and eat it all the time at my favorite restaurant in Connecticut (CT). Since I moved to Brooklyn I wanted a good place to go to so I was recommended by the African restaurant worker I go to in CT to come here. Finally made the time to go and food tasted great but portion size for the price is a joke. I believe the okra soup was 18$ with meat. As you can see from the photo, it was maybe a pot spoon amount of okra and the meat came with a bunch of oil on the top (I used two forks to show the amount/depth of food they gave me). I had high expectations just because of the recommendation but I will not be returning to get only a pot spoon of food for almost 20$. I’ll gladly wait when I have time to go back to CT or make it myself!

On a positive-ish note, the pepper soup was good and good portion. The meat was hard and could have used pressure cooking.

I saw some negative reviews, and the restaurant responded by saying, “God will reward.” Let’s be clear—customers don’t come from God. They come from good service, good food, and a solid reputation.

I ordered over $100 worth of food, but what was delivered was so tiny that I felt embarrassed, especially since I had a guest that day.

To make things worse, after placing my order, they called to ask for an additional $2 for goat meat—this was after I’d already spent over $100.

Yes, I do plan to visit the restaurant and share my experience with them directly.

In the restaurant business, good customer service and good food are essential. Relying on “God will reward” as a response to poor customer experiences, which cost people money and time, is not just unprofessional but also quite foolish.

Despite this, I’ll give them another chance and will be sure to share my next experience as well.

After waiting 20 mins for my order, I went to the counter and they had forgotten my order.  I should've left but I really wanted to try African food. Waited another 30 mins. and started eating some crackers when the food finally came out but I wasn't hungry anymore. Paid $15 for yam and chicken. Went back to the office and the yams were okay but the chicken...the chicken was soo rubbery that I couldn't take a bite and the knife couldn't even cut it. Like is this even chicken? So I paid $15 for yams (which i would just buy at the store for $3) and rubber chicken. I would pay that for quality food but not for what I was served. Will never go here again and can't say that I would ever recommend anyone to eat here.

Hours later and I'm still upset because I'm hungry and wasted my money. If rubbery chicken is how Africans cook their chicken then no thanks, I'll stick to my stew and curry chicken.

Please don’t go here I been going here for years but this last few months have been a disaster there slow and they charge you for things you don’t get I ordered a Jollof rice and goat meat, which I got then I ordered Goat Soup they charge my friend $50 just for Jollof and Goat meat I don’t know who is managing this place now but there the worst and slow and think it’s funby
They served me cold food .was not properly warmed and when l requested for egusi soup 80 percent of the soup was stew .the crazy thing is k told the attendance l don't want stew but egusi soup

formatted_address: 601 15th Ave, Newark, NJ 07103, United States
name: Modupe African & American Restaurant

reviews.text:
When conducting business, customer service and integrity are crucial to me. Having dealt with many Nigerian businesses, I’ve found that integrity and customer service is often lacking; however, Modupe is a remarkable exception. Her customer service is A+.
I recently ordered from her restaurant through Grubhub twice, but for some reason, the order was canceled both times. Instead of letting it go, she took the initiative to ask for my address and delivered the food to my house herself—unbelievable! As a business owner, I know that is truly going the extra mile. I just want to say thank you so much for your incredible service!
Ordered via uber eat, I got Efo Elegusi and poundo, it was well seasoned . The poundo was not too hard, meat was eat to eat , and the stew was not spicy. So, really good ear overall.

Very fresh food and authentic Nigerian food. Fufu is very fresh and fluffy. The owner Modupe is very helpful with suggestions on what to try if you never tried it before. This is a great place that you must try and it’s a gem in Newark!  I loved the fried sweet plantains bc they were perfectly ripe and soft and sweet. She takes very careful care to make the food top notch. Parking is free on the street.

Wanted authentic African cuisine and looked up the great reviews from this location; place was small but very cute and extremely clean as well as well maintained, the owners were friendly and took time to explain all dishes,prices and recommended certain dishes as it was my first time there.
Ordered the chicken and also the fish  with the famous FUFU that everyone recommends ...IT WAS DELICIOUS and the fufu was soft and bouncy but was spicy my daughter recommends it but less spicy my son-in-law loved it ....HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS PLACE IF YOU LOVE AUTHENTIC AFRICAN CUISINE AND IF NOT ITS A DEFINITELY A MUST EXPERIENCE TO TRY...

Food - portions were small. Goat and chicken were palatable but not anything special. Jillof rice was good
Service - she was friendly but we waited for 40 mins. The "opening/operating time" is wrong - I had called ahead too. Spilled water on table. She was nice/sweet.
Atmosphere - Loud Fan with minimal ventilation.

formatted_address: 2017 Fulton St, Brooklyn, NY 11233, United States
name: Fingerlicking restaurant inc

reviews.text:
Yeah, finger licking indeed, I saw the head chef pick his nose and then lick his fingers. And he wasn't nice about it either, I've never seen a man shove 3 fingers in his mouth, and my poor daughter had to witness it all.

But the egusi didn't have a morsel of sand in it. Best egussy I've ever had in my life, despite the previously described experience.

Peace and love to the nation, I'm out.
Great place and good food. I love the ambience of the environment and its neat and clean.  Excellent service.
i just ordered egusi pounded yam goat on Uber App. There was a lot of SAND in the egusi. Very disappointing.
Very good food ,they need to work on their service.

Easy location and the price is right, but one of the staff needs to be friendly, customer is always right.

Please as a business owner, madam need to be more patient 6/16/2018. Thanks.

formatted_address: 821 Van Siclen Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11207, United States
name: Olas Kitchen

reviews.text: Absolutely disgusting!! I ordered okra soup and goat and got oil soup and over cooked chunks of goat. Spending $30 for this meal just to be inedible is ridiculous!! Will never order from here again.

I order the fufu and Egusi soup like once (maybe twice 🌚) a week. It’s SOOOO GOOD 10/10.Always fresh, the Egusi never tastes funny compared to other places I’ve tried, and the prices are affordable and GREAT PORTION! Also the staff are very sweet and welcoming . The first day I ever went to get food from them moving in to a new neighborhood they greeted me with such kindness.definitely check them out you won’t be disappointed

The purpose of this review is not to hate or harm this restaurant in any way, shape, or form. That being said, I hope you take this review as an informative review.

Atmosphere: I couldn't plan ahead in order to decide what I was going to order because their menu is not really clear in Google maps. When I got there, I felt like I was taking way too much time to order. Their place is clean for the most part. There are about four or six tables around, but not much space at the counter where you would usually order. Some customers were also by the counter waiting for their order, but they were friendly.

Service: Service was okay. Nothing out of the ordinary.

Food: This was my first time trying food from the beautiful African continent. I just wanted to try and didn't set any expectations because many cultures have their own way of preparing a certain dish. I didn't want to take a risk, so I ordered something familiar to my culture. I ordered the Jalloff Rice with Goat Meat. Now, I'm not sure if this dish is supposed to be like this, but I found the goat meat a bit hard and dry.

Price: Honestly, I don't quite remember the price, but I don't really feel like it was worth buying that dish with that quality of meat.

Today I ordered from here the first time after reading a lot of reviews online the food was good, only thing their meat is way too hard. If you don’t have good teeth, don’t order the meat just stick with the rice dishes. They need to cook them meat a little bit more softer than it would be fine. Like pink
Their goat pepprsoup is very watery and tasteless , literally taste like oil, water and pepper. I’d be scared to try anything else and you can forget about their customer service ! Terrible !

formatted_address: 852 S Orange Ave, Newark, NJ 07106, United States
name: Mama G African Restaurant

reviews.text: I was feeling hungry and my hotel doesn’t have a restaurant so I went into the Uber eats app to find something to eat. Mama G restaurant was one of the highly rated African food. I ordered pounded yam with egusi soup. It was so delicious, I had no problem with the portion but it is one piece of meat and one chicken thigh. The spice level is hot but I already knew that’s how egusi soup is. Thanks for the wonderful meal.

The other day I tried, Mama G African Restaurant, for lunch. I tried their Jollof Rice w/ Chicken. I was in a stretch of NEEDING Jollof Rice after I had tried it for the first time lol. Not too long after my first experience trying Jollof Rice, along with trying different places in different areas, I had rode past this place and decided to try it out. I am not sure if it was just the time or day that I came, but I was completely disappointed. The Jollof rice was more oily than you’d probably get at most places and the flavor was extremely lacking. Not to mention the rice tasted old, and/or reheated from the day before. The chicken was a bit cold and tough, but the flavor was fairly decent. The most disappointing experience was the price. I paid over $20 for the one plate, and at the time based off of my fairly limited previous experiences, I was like “Ok, this one has to be the best at this price!”. Again I’m not sure if it was the time of day (a later lunch time ~1pm), or the day I went (a Wednesday), but the experience was just not it. I would love to try this place again, but consistency along with quality is what makes a restaurant one you’d love to go back to again and again. Maybe if I am in the area again, I’d try it. But from my only experience it was pretty disappointing. Especially given the quality of the Jollof I was experiencing beforehand (I had it about 6 times before this one). If you’re in the Newark area feel free to check this place out.

Food arrived well packaged,  it looked good, tasted good until i went to bite into the meat and found hair, i grabbed the other piece of meat and found hair too, the other piece of (cow skin i believe) meat was coiled so the hair was inside of it. Pics included. This review is not meant to deter people from buying here but please let the chef know to cover their hair, head when preparing or cooking the meal. Threw away rest of the food. I ordered peppered meat too but havent come across hair yet. Otherwise fufu was delicious.

Customer service very rude. I bought 2meatpie, a fish roll n a drink the lady refused to give me a bag and said the stuff I bought was too small to give me a bag. Prior to that her attitude was very rude for no reason like how do you work in a restaurant u don’t greet ur customers and when ask for price you respond back rudely like the customer is the cause of your problem. The food taste isn’t worth the poor customer service. Meatpie and fish roll not fresh and super hard and cold.

Im sure the owner remembers me. (She remembers me as (Dre) the Amazon guy 😭) When you first walk in it might seem as if she has an attitude but she’s actually pretty nice when you talk to her and she even jokes around. I Discovered this place while doing doordash. Decided to come back again and try the Egusi and pounded yams as suggested by my best friend who is Yoruba. I got the assorted meats and everything was super spicy just like i liked it. I even had meat pie on the side. I’ll just remember to specify skipping the Pomo as I cant seem to like it, but the catfish, tilapia and goat buss 😋 I will def be coming back again ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

name: EKO Restaurant

reviews.text:
I visited this restaurant in October 2025 after recommending it to many people without trying it out. I was attracted to the name and vibes based on online pictures. I have a mixed review.
1. The decor and esthetics are beautiful. The seating can be tight depending on the side on the room but it is manageable. The loudness of the music is tolerable but made conversations difficult.
2. Food, drinks, and menu- The drinks were good 4 out 5 only because the cup used for soda is small. Please read the menu entirely with a magnifying glass and bright lights. Typical Nigerian restaurants serve soups with meat for one price. This restaurant charges you separately for the soup and separately for the meat. This was a major turn off. This makes the meal unnecessarily expensive.  We ordered the soup platter and jellof rice. The rice was ok 3 out 5. The chicken was ok 4 out 5. The soup was great 5 out of 5. Portion sizes were good.
3. Customer service- We didnt wait long to be seated on a friday without reservations. Party of 3. The host was polite. Waitress was a bit slow. She kept forgetting one or two things here and there. Forgivable. When we had issues with out food and bill we requested to speak with a manager. The manager made us wait until she finished a very long conversation with a staff before attending to us. The place is not that big so everything is obvious. She was not helpful but rather argumentative. Instead of explaining things, she argued that we should have read the menu. Her body language and tone was not acceptable. We paid in annoyance and left.

Would I recommend this place? Probably for drinks, appetizers, and vibes.

Would I return? I might give it another chance just to be fair.

I visited EKO 3 times, twice during the week for happy hour and once on a Saturday. I came alone each time for drinks and hookah. I was satisfied with my drink orders. The hookah is good, never had an issue. The music is always on point. Each time I went it was never packed. I would expect more people to be there. It’s a beautifully decorated restaurant. I never ordered food to stay but I heard good things about certain appetizers. I ordered pepper wings to go. Amazing! Very spicy but good. I will try another flavor of wings or dine in  and try a entree next time, so I am not rating food in this review

⚠️ WARNING: Dine here at your own risk!

My sister and I walked into this place with high hopes and excitement, but left completely disgusted, disappointed, and frustrated. Let me save you the trouble — this is not worth your time, money, or energy.

First red flag: the location. It’s literally stuck next to a Food Bazaar supermarket, sharing the parking lot. Not exactly the type of place you expect when you’re dressed up and ready for a nice evening out. But we didn’t let that throw us off. We stayed optimistic.

When we arrived, we were seated right away (we were even early for our reservation). That was the last good thing that happened. From there, it was all downhill. The place wasn’t packed, but service was still painfully slow. The lighting was so dim we couldn’t even read our menus, and unlike other tables, ours didn’t have a lamp. We had to ask for one — why wasn’t that common sense?

We sat for almost 30 minutes before our waitress even came by to take drink orders. Strike one. Then, the drink I wanted (their so-called “Love in Top”) wasn’t even available. How does a lounge run out of their own specialty drink on a Saturday night? Strike two.

The waitress suggested another drink. Fine, I went along with it. Another 30 minutes later, the drinks finally arrived — and that’s when the night officially ended for me. Sitting on my glass? A bug. Floating inside my drink? Another bug. YES, TWO BUGS. Absolutely revolting.

I flagged down another waitress because ours was nowhere to be found. Instead of apologizing, she looked confused, took my drink over to a brighter area to “investigate,” and then acted shocked when she saw exactly what I had told her. The solution? Not a new drink. Not a sincere apology. Not even a manager coming over to acknowledge the situation. No. The waitress casually told me they were “out of that drink” and asked if I wanted to order something else. Are you kidding me?!

Meanwhile, my sister’s drink tasted like watered-down juice. At that point, we canceled everything — but apparently, our food was already being prepared (even though drinks took forever). When we said we didn’t want it, instead of understanding, they still tried to bring the appetizers out! Then they had the audacity to bring us a check for my sister’s horrible drink. No apology, no accountability, not even a small gesture like comping the drinks to make things right. Just a receipt.

This was beyond disappointing. It was disrespectful. A manager never came to the table. No one cared about how we felt. No one cared about how serious it is to serve BUGS in someone’s drink. That’s not just bad service — that’s a health hazard.

I came wanting to support a Black-owned business in the community, but unfortunately, this was yet another letdown. And no, this isn’t a “bad night.” This was a total failure in service, cleanliness, and professionalism. Ruined celebrating my sister's promotion!

I can’t rate the food because we never even got that far — the bugs in the drink were the final straw. Consider this your warning: eat and drink here at your own risk.
Let me tell yall something this place was GREAT 10/10. Food was amazing . (I  cleaned the plate ) Service was impeccable. My new favorite spot . The server / Bartender Cheyenne was so great

I had an absolutely wonderful experience at Eko from Cheyenne & Louis … From the moment I walked in, the atmosphere was warm, welcoming, and beautifully designed — the perfect blend of cozy and upscale.

The staff was attentive, knowledgeable, and genuinely friendly, making us feel like valued guests throughout the evening. Our server gave excellent recommendations and timed everything perfectly.

Now, the food — wow. Every dish was a masterpiece, both in presentation and flavor. I especially loved the  which was cooked to perfection and bursting with fresh, vibrant

formatted_address: 642 Nostrand Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11216, United States
name: Akara House

reviews.text:
I’ve lived in the neighborhood for 6+ years, tried many places and I would have to say this is now in my top 3.

Three words to describe Akara House:
Fresh. Innovative. Incredible.

It’s a breath of fresh air. Amazing flavors and textures combine to create a one of a kind burger.

The owner was so kind, so helpful, very professional and humble.

I will be returning more than once.

God bless this business!

Also I don’t have a photo because I ate it so fast 😂 BUT it looked better than or just like the photo. I tried the LEKKI BURGER 🤤🤤🤤10/10

Akara House is a solid choice for quick bites. The Made in Lagos burger was a highlight, and the Jollof rice with fritters and the Kale salad were tasty. The staff were friendly, and the owner even shared egusi samples for us to try. Although the place is a bit small and got cramped when we were there, the fast service rounded out an overall good experience. I'd love to go again soon and have their classic Akara burger.

I am surprised by all the very high ratings. I was not exactly blown away by this place. I ordered the Made in Lagos burger and the homemade lemonade.
The lemonade was refreshing and a bit different in am undescribable way. Sweet but a little salty, felt very refreshing on a warm day.
The Made in Lagos burger was a little bit of a letdown. The toppings were excellent and flavorful, but the akara patty was so dry and dense, it really subtracted from the overall burger experience.
There are 2 benches to wait for your food and a small bar countertop with a few chairs if you want to stay and eat.

Hearty portions and deliciously rich flavors.
Got the oyster wrap this time and it was soo good and filling. I love the house made hot sauce.
Lemonade tea was also great.

Owner was dope. Don't expect the food to come quick, which a plus for me bc it let's me know it's being cooked from scratch.  The food was good, even the next day eating it cold.  Only thing I wasn't crazy about was the jollof, guess I expected something different from all the jollof rave videos I had been watching.

formatted_address: 161 Gramatan Ave, Mt Vernon, NY 10550, United States
name: Tasty Budz

reviews.text:
I’ve been a loyal Tasty Budz customer for 2 years now, and they’ve never missed. Their food stays consistent & flavorful. The jollof rice & goat meat is easily some of the best I’ve had; perfectly seasoned, rich, and cooked with that authentic taste. Their fried rice & chicken is just as impressive, packed with flavor and cooked to perfection.
Tasty Budz truly deserves their name. If you’re looking for quality food, generous portions, and flavors that keep you coming back, I highly recommend them.

My limited knowledge of Ghanaian cuisine did not hinder my appreciation of the fantastic flavors on offer at Tasty Budz. The Jollof and Chicken caught my attention right away and did not disappoint! This is no simple rice dish; it is heavily flavored and cannot be easily dismissed as a side dish! The chicken was also packed with flavor, perfectly tender, and complemented the rice wonderfully.

The "Morning Dew" smoothie was another treat. I don't recall all its ingredients, but the blend of almonds and banana created a creamy, indulgent treat that balanced the spice of the Jollof beautifully.

Tasty Budz is a must-visit, especially if you've never experienced Ghana's culinary landscape! Can't wait to try more.

If you need some good Ghanian food, drop by Tasty Budz! This place is a hidden gem in Mount Vernon! I had the goat and okra soup with Fufu and an amazing watermelon-ginger drink that they make! Wow and Mmmm is all I can say! Not only was the meal delicious but the owner and chef Kojo brought me an my homey Ameer our own bowls of soapy water in a basin so we could wash our hands before and after the meal!👏🏾👏🏾👏🏾👏🏾 It’s the true African way of dealing with food - cleanliness is next to Godliness! The place is super clean as well! Walk, no run to this place!😜😋😋😋 I’m trying the Jollof rice next time with fish! You will not be disappointed! Great food and service 5stars. Period…..☺️✌🏾✌🏾🤩🤩🤩

The atmosphere is warm and welcoming, the customer service is amazing and the Food is amazing and absolutely delicious, with a very unique selection. You won't be disappointed at all going their and once you go their once you will be going their often. I recommend trying their Spurilina Slushy, their Okra Soup, their Ginger shot and Cold shot,  their Jollof Rice and Chicken and so much more.

Great food and great service! It was my first time having Ghanaian food and I got the Fante Kenkey with Chicken and my friend got the Fufu with Goat and they were both so flavorful, the meat was tender, and the goat stew had a little kick of heat. Will definitely be back!

reviews.text:
I have eaten at Ghanaian restaurants across DC, Maryland, Virginia, Massachusetts, New Jersey, NYC, England , Scotland, and many cities in Ghana. This is literally the most authentic and best Ghanaian food I have ever tasted.

Up until discovering this place I thought I just didn’t like Ghanaian food, and I didn’t understand why. The food here made me realize I don’t hate Ghanaian food after all just that no one was cooking it well.

Shout out to the chef here my goodness you have it down! Consider adding meat pie to the menu too because i have not come across anyone who can make it like it is in Ghana.

My EMPTY plate should say enough….
I forgot to take pics in the beginning!!
This food was PHENOMENAL!!!
The Jollof was out of this world !!
My God!!
Lovely food, lovely people, lovely story of how this restaurant came to be!! Support this business!!
If I wasn’t only visiting for the weekend I’d be here DAILY!!

BTW, I’m Caribbean… I KNOW GOOD FOOD 🔥🔥

My first time eating from here was about two months ago and the food was ok. Since then, I’ve eaten here three other times. The second time, I had snapper fish with jollof, and the rice seemed old and hard. The third time I went, I had the snapper with black rice and the food was extremely salty. I was not going to go back, but my friend wanted it so I gave them one last chance. (might I add that He’s from the islands and I’m American. The first time he ordered, every other time I ordered. I’ll leave that there) Last night I got the snapper with jollof And we both were throwing up. 30 minutes after eating that food I had to use the bathroom and he was throwing up. I went to sleep and he was back-and-forth in the bathroom all night. This morning I woke up and threw up and have been in the bathroom all morning. I don’t know if I have some sort of food poisoning or what but my stomach feels queasy, and I feel nauseous. The food was overly spicy and overly salty.. I wanted so bad to have a good experience here, but unfortunately, I will not return.

Response to owner: It was definitely from your food. This was the only thing I had to eat all day. Aside from making me sick, it was overly salty and overly spicy. Don’t be so quick to respond without taking accountability. Learn From your mistakes And do better!!! From looking at your other reviews, I see a lot of people saying that the food is too spicy and the rice is old.
Good want taste, it felt bland and the meat was hard to eat
Jollof rice was nice; chicken was seasoned nicely, (but was a bit old and cold); didn’t like the plantains (too mushy).

reviews.text: My family and I visit Asante every once in a while whenever we’re in New Jersey or nearby, and it never disappoints. The restaurant is always clean, welcoming, and consistently well-maintained. There’s a great variety of food options to choose from, so everyone can find something they enjoy. On top of that, the owner is incredibly kind, thoughtful, and truly amazing—he makes you feel genuinely welcomed every time. Asante is definitely a place you can rely on for good food, whether you’re meeting friends, spending time with family, or stopping in for a solo bite. Highly recommend!

Cheryl is a DELIGHT!!! She’s present and kindly suggested I taste test the soups before deciding which one I was going for. The Palm Nut soup with the fufu won for me!!! My new go-to for 2026. What a blessing!!! Shoutout to Ed and Arthur next door. And to the kitchen DJ, your tune selection is immaculate and like the food, deliciously nourishing.

I discovered Asante’s around two years ago. THE FOOD IS PHENOMENAL! The ladies who work there are so kind and generous. I can tell the food is made with a lot of love. I’m addicted to their jerk chicken wings. They are the best around. Today I had jollaf rice with gravy and vegetables. Lots of great flavors. I recommend this restaurant highly!

I'm visiting from our of town and am blown away by how good this food is.  The service was incredible. Trina you are a queen! Thank you! Everyone is so kind and the oxtail and the Ghanian Jollof was so delicious I was smiling the entire time I was eating it.

The place is well decorated, with pieces of african styled art. The seats and floors were neatly cleaned up too, so that is an easy 5 stars. I would definitely come again.

reviews.text:
The appetizers puff puff was soft and fluffy and not oily, fish pie was also very delicious. The abula was fresh, delicious and a good quantity. Asorted meat option was soft and delicious; good portions and I will recommend.
The peppered ponmo is thin, quantity on the small side and very spicy nearly unbearable after having a few.

We actually came from Church on 12/21/25 to enjoy ourselves for end of the year treats with delicious African dishes. The place is roomy enough to accommodate at least 30 people, everyone said they enjoyed all the meals (e.g jollof rice, pounded yam, amala, egusi vegetable soup, efo riro, assorted meat, yam pourage with fresh fish, etc. All the staffs attended to us with professionalism, they are so friendly, good listeners, patient enough to attend to the large number of people that came. The service was so fast, no time wasted at all. In fact my people were so glad and impressed with them to the extent that they were collecting their contacts should in case they would need such service in future. Thank you for attending to us nicely. God bless you all. More sales in Jesus name.

Amazing place. I came for my friends birthday celebration and the food was delicious. The service is fast, the people are kind, and the atmosphere is great. I would recommend anyone to stop by and try the food for yourself. I enjoyed and I will definitely come back here again.

I'm honestly disappointed. I ordered pounded yam and got home to find a ridiculously small portion-barely enough to feed a child, let alone an adult. I called the restaurant, and the man I spoke to casually said it was the last portion, so that's what they gave me.

That's unacceptable. If you don't have enough, say so. Don't just package scraps and hope your customers won't notice until they're home and it's too late. I paid full price and got shortchanged. This kind of service is how you lose loyal customers. Do better.

Came here for a friend Father birthday after church, first time I tried Nigerian food and loved my experience, me the Chef Olainda, tried plenty of new things like Suya Beef and Other new things, would recommend to come back again!

formatted_address: 1933 Fulton St, Brooklyn, NY 11233, United States
name: Dabakh-Kine

reviews.text:
Great Senegalese/West African food with huge portions at decent prices. We were shocked at the amount of food we got for $20 (enough for at least 2 meals). While the ambience of the shop might not be great or the staff super friendly, the food and price is what makes it great and why I would recommend it.

The options are usually a protein and a carb and the protein portion is big, fowl would be an entire fowl, fish would be an entire fish etc. The carb options were vermicelli, couscous, rice, fries etc. They also have West African drinks.

We loved the fowl and fried fish and the vermicelli side the most.

My standard expectations were blown out of the water. The restaurant delivers good value consistently. The food comes fresh, tastes great, and offers many choices. The restaurant proprietor was sweet and considerately helpful. A really outstanding restaurant visit!
Good food, the staff and the owners are very friendly. The prices are worth it 👍
I loved the food here. It was delicious, it taste authentic and was full of flavor. I had the Fish with Attieke and it was  worthy of a review.

The grilled tilapia is fantastic! I didn't like the fowl chicken at all.
The food only taste good when the owner lady is there or cooks it herself. I've tested this several times.

First of all this is the best meat pie I’ve ever had in my life only thing that can compare is in Ashimowu Bakare street. I also ordered jollof rice and goat but I ate it too fast. The best Suya I’ve had in a long long time. The Egusi soup was also very good. I can’t wait to  try their upcoming menu. Definitely recommend!
I’m in love, the suya and the food in general too good.

reviews.text: Fouta Halal is an excellent African Halal restaurant that delivers bold, authentic flavors in every dish. Their lamb shank is incredibly tender and flavorful, falling off the bone with every bite. The grilled lamb is perfectly seasoned and juicy, while the fowl dish is rich and satisfying. The portions are generous, and the service is warm and welcoming. If you’re looking for a place that serves delicious, well-prepared African Halal food, Fouta Halal is a must-visit.
Alhamdulillah, very delicious food i went last week with my two friends still my mouth missing the taste 😋😋😋 and also service was really amazing, i come soon again and again ❤️❤️

Loved this restaurant when I came to New York with my husband 2 years ago. We loved the food and their Ginger Juice. I was looking forward to getting some ginger juice to take home this time. But sadly went there and no longer open. Wishing to find the same kind of ginger juice but no luck so far.

The customer service was great. I bought the grilled lamb with a side of salad. You're given a generous portion of meat. De-lic-cous! The salad was crisp and tasted fresh with the vinaigrette. The lamb tasted freshly grilled with the right amount of seasoning. The ginger/pineapple juice was mouthwatering spicy but gooooooooood 👍🏿 😁 😋 This was my first time trying this spot and this type of food. I thoroughly enjoyed my meal. I will definitely be coming back again. I shared this place with some people and now they claim it as one of their new eating spots to try. I’ve tried ayamase in 6 different restaurants in New Jersey and hers is the best hands down

formatted_address: 449 William St, East Orange, NJ 07017, United States
name: Fatu's Kitchen

reviews.text:
I was visiting New York from Florida and traveled two and a half hours to get here. I’ve never had Liberian food and I was excited to give them a try. I ordered the potato greens and the cassava leaf. I informed them that I would like to eat the cassava leaf at the restaurant and take the potato greens to go.

The cassava leaf was exploding with flavors and was a bit spicy but nothing I couldn’t handle. It definitely reminded me of a Haitian cuisine called Lalo but one of the key differences were this was packed with a variety of meats and spicier. The staff was really nice as I interacted with them while I was there. However, I’m a bit disappointed because when I went to pay I reminded them again that I was going to be getting the potato greens to go and that I would need to pay for both of my meals. To my surprise when I got home, I noticed that the container they gave me said goat soup. While I should’ve doubled checked, I’m not sure how they messed up since their food is labeled. Don’t get me wrong, the goat soup was good but it would’ve been better enjoyed with fufu and not rice but I was also looking forward to the potato greens… maybe next time.

Had Liberian food today and was so excited. I was headed to a different restaurant but saw this Liberian restaurant with great reviews so I went. I’m part African and I want to try all the cuisines from Africa and this was my first try for Liberia 🇱🇷. I guess maybe they did not see me as African so there wasn’t much attention to me and I asked for a couple of things from the menu but they didn’t have it. End of convo. The one lady just shook her head and turned away and walked off. lol..but don’t be turned off! -Customer service looks different in diff parts of the world and I won’t take stars off for that- I told the lady I want to try something here so what do you have and explain it to me. Can you help me with the menu so she did come around and explain almost everything to me and I ended up getting the cassava leaf because I’ve heard so much about it. Let me tell you. It’s absolutely delicious. Flavorful. Filling. Wow! There was so much mixed meat in it from cow foot, chicken, beef. (I don’t eat cow foot but the other meat was great) And she assured me there’s no pork in their restaurant. The Scotch pepper 🌶️ sauce on the side was sooo good and hot. The rice went well and they had Vimto soda. The ladies came to me to see if I liked it after and as a first timer I was hooked! I also got a slice of their rice bread that is similar to banana bread. It was so good and spiced. I would definitely eat here again.

Food was good, but My mother and I ordered because I leaf And rice and the potato greens and rice. both meals came with mostly meat no greens which is very disappointing because that’s mainly what I want. I don’t even eat the meat for real and it’s very disappointed because we spent $60 because we also got the beef stick. Beef sticks were good but it’s just because I believe in potato greens like we haven’t even eaten it because it’s just all meat. now we wasted $60 so disappointing because I eat here often.

ALL THEIR FOOD IS SPICY!!! IT MAKES NO SENSE WHY NOT GIVE US THE CHANCE TO ADD OUR OWN SPICE🤷🏾‍♀️🤷🏾‍♀️ AND THEN THEY DONT TELL YOU. ITS A GOOD THING I ASKED AFTER RECEIVING SPICY FOOD ( WHICH IVE HAD NUMEROUS TIMES BUT FROM ANOTHER PLACE WHICH ALLOWED CHOOSING IF YOU WANT SPICE OR NOT. THE DISH I ORDERE IS NOT TRADITIONALLY SPICY WHEN MADE IN THIS COUNTRY. BUT E V E R Y T H I N G IS SPICY AT THIS PLACE.

They don't serve Torborghee anymore on Saturdays but they do serve Cassava Leaf.

All of the food here has a fresh & deliciously savory, deep umami flavor. I highly recommended eating here.

formatted_address: 670 S 21st St, Irvington, NJ 07111, United States
name: African House

reviews.text: I made a quick stop to this house recently... Let me tell you... If you are not booking your party here, then you are missing out on a lot! This is not a paid review.
The African house sells good African clothes as well as  African foods. Service is always good.
Beautiful
This is purely for African types of foods more especially Ghanaian and Nigerian!  They have cheap fresh Yams and hot served Akamu on the go! They have anything you would find in an African Store! :-)
One of the best free parking for evening program. Medium sized parties the best location in Newark area. Thanks

formatted_address: 16 Washington Ave, Irvington, NJ 07111, United States
name: Garden City Restaurant

reviews.text:
Thank you so much for your service, food and wonderful atmosphere. We're Haitian,
and Mom is very....No....EXTREMELY picky about her food. So to see mom excited and wants to come back for more, is a huge reward/compliment. Thank you for this wonderful experience, see you soon

I ordered from this restaurant through Uber Eats and added the bean stew option to my meal, which had no listed price. Later, I noticed they adjusted the total and added a $3 charge without informing me ahead of time. When I called the restaurant to clarify, I was shocked at the response  I was told, “Were you expecting free things? There’s nothing free in America,” in a rude and disrespectful tone.
This kind of customer service is unacceptable. I don’t mind paying for what I order, but it’s basic courtesy to be transparent with pricing and speak respectfully to customers. I will not be ordering from here again.

Wowww, I am so satisfied with everything here. Food, Service and atmosphere is beautiful. Place is very clean, including bathrooms. The service was wonderful, they treated us with such kindness and respect. I'm definitely visiting again...this time with friends. Thank you so much 🙏🏽
Great people own this restaurant. Always friendly and the food is delicious!!! 100% recommend!

This is the only place I come to to get my food. It is absolutely amazing. I’ve tried other places and none can compare to this place If you’re a person like me and don’t like your food so spicy this place is for you you can taste a little kick just a little bit but you also taste the great flavors and quality of the food.The staff OMG the staff are so so respectful and pleasant to deal with thank you soo much

formatted_address: 492 Clinton Ave, Newark, NJ 07108, United States
name: Burkindi

reviews.text:
This was my first time visiting the establishment. Upon arrival, the cashier was engaged in a loud conversation with someone in the kitchen, but I chose to wait patiently for my order. When it came time to pay, she told me the total was $43, and I was prepared to pay that amount. However, I noticed that she had mistakenly entered $0.43 into the system.

I tried to bring the error to her attention, but I’m not sure if there was a language barrier. Instead of acknowledging the mistake calmly, she responded in French, telling me not to give her a headache and insisting the total was correct. After a brief argument, she finally realized and corrected the error. Still, rather than apologizing for her unnecessary comment or behavior, she ignored me completely.

Many people in my situation might have just paid the incorrect amount and walked away, but I chose to be honest. Unfortunately, I was met with rudeness and poor customer service. Because of this experience, I will not be returning.

Let me know if you'd like a version with a more formal tone (like for a complaint email) or a softer tone.

Stay away from this place.
First of all the place had a very bad smell, it was so bad that I had to wait for my food outside.
I ordered the whole fried chicken, jollof rice and some other stuff. They gave me an old refried chicken, with some missing parts.
Don't even bother asking for a refund, a replacement or a manager (she's the rudest person I've ever met).
This was a complete waste of money, I threw the chicken in the garbage.
The food was delicious and the customer service was excellent.
Food is yummy welcome is warned and believe me the taste is incredible.  You feel like as home and you have plenty choices od foods. Do and enjoy yourself

BURKINA FASO 🇧🇫
Excerpt from Eat the World NYC:
As reported on two years ago, the cuisine of Burkina Faso is not new to Newark, New Jersey.  The past five years have also seen two other Burkinabé sources of food open as well a bit further south. The first, in the back of a grocery that has expanded on Lyons Avenue has remained unfortunately elusive in finding the right time to visit, while the other is a full scale restaurant that has dedicated hours and plenty of seats and tables.

The more you settle into Burkindi, the friendlier it becomes, as the food translates to smiles across your face and the staff and other Burkinabé patrons keep asking "Did you like our food?" There is of course only one answer to this question, but thankfully it is no lie. The food is delicious, and as it always is, this will be the easiest part of life to share with folks you may not have anything else in common with.

What other nearby nations call jollof rice, the delicious riz gras on this order is plated with dibi ($15), whole chunks of grilled lamb with minimal seasoning. Here at Burkindi they rely much less on the mustard and vinegar-infused onion sauce that is usually heaped on the meat and instead serve it with a mild mustard on the side. The darker sauce in the rear is delicious but all fire and should be used with caution.

formatted_address: 736 W 181st St, New York, NY 10033, United States
name: Addey Ababa

reviews.text:
My wife, Marty, has been here before and did me the great favor of taking me here today, in my last hours before I turn over another year, birthday eve.

OH, MY! What a gem in a still growing neighborhood. Sure there’s a couple local diners, yer usual pizza joints, coffee places, Ethiopian is sooo much fun and the food is delicious, the decor is beautiful and comfortable, the service is great and welcoming.

Co’mon! Skip pizza or take out Chinese! Make tonight ETHIOPIAN! You’ll thank me later! Tell ‘em Marty and Fitz sent ya!

Food was so tasty, and the awaze (lamb) tibbs was our favorite. The coffee was great and the baklava was delicious. The best part was the friendly staff and the welcoming atmosphere. We genuinely felt at home.

The ambience is very casual but the service is superb; better than most fancy restaurants. The server was very attentive and seemed to read our mind before we asked.
The food was all top notch as well. Ordered the Ethiopian spiced tea, the beef combo, and baklava. The tea was bold and spicy, similar to a great chai tea.
The beef combo injera was absolutely delightful, with bold spice, tender meats, and some lentils too!
11/10 definitely recommend

They have a vegetarian section on their menu with 5+ options. Tried the vegetarian combo. It was tasty, though the misir wot wasn't as thick and spicy as I had at another Ethiopian restaurant. The spicy tea was nice.

The staff at this Ethiopian restaurant create a warm and welcoming experience, adding to the great quality food being served. 🇪🇹
In my visit to NYC I was looking forward to dining at an Ethiopian restaurant. I visited Addey Ababa as a first timer and the restaurant definitely deserves a second visit. I have to give the staff a 10/10 for their service and kindness. In terms of the food, the restaurant can cater to both vegans and meat eaters. I ordered the Shiro Wot, a very tasty, non-spicy chickpea stew. I also had a coffee, which was delicious and needed absolutely no creamer added. High quality restaurant. I recommend you give Addey Ababa an have the experience for yourself.

formatted_address: 1084 Flushing Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11237, United States
name: Bunna Cafe

reviews.text:
First time trying Ethiopian food and I’m glad it was at Bunna Cafe because this place was stellar! Absolutely loved the ambiance, service, and most importantly the food.

They start you off with a free plate of popcorn to snack on while you wait for your food which was so fun. Also, I happened to be in during their weekend Bunna Coffee Ceremony so I had a complimentary cup of the Bunna. It was very strong, spiced, and rich, with a prominent ginger undertone. Adding in the brown sugar cubes opened up the flavor so much. Delicious!

I tried the Lentil Sambusas which were super crispy. The filling inside was fine but adding on that cilantro lime sauce really tied it all together! There was a subtle spice too that I enjoyed.

For my main I went with the Beyaynetu Meal which was the 5 scoop option. I kinda wanted to go for the 7 scoop Feast to try more things but I’m glad I didn’t because the 5 scoop was very sizable for one person! I tried the Enguday Tibs, Shiro, Misis Wot, Yater Kik Alicha, and the seasonal option which was an Eggplant and Walnut Deberjan. WOW!!! Everything was so insanely flavorful and worked well with each other. I think my two favorites were the Shiro and the Yater Kik Alicha. Soooooo so so good I could eat a whole bowl of just those.

This was my first Ethiopian cuisine experience and I loved that they don't give you utensils for the full effect! The food isnt really a looker if you're not into pureed food, but the taste was delightful! Highly recommend and for any vegans or vegetarians craving some hearty food. I have gone 2 times now and they are just as good! The interaction (bread) they have is tangy and slightly sour.

From the moment I stepped into Bunna Cafe, I was completely charmed. Tucked away in Brooklyn, this all-vegan Ethiopian spot radiates warmth and culture, and an inviting, communal vibe. They even host an authentic Ethiopian coffee ceremony in the evenings, which adds to the immersive feel.

The staff was wonderful, warm, welcoming, and happy to answer questions about the menu and traditions. We kicked off our meal with Kategna, a crispy, toasty injera snack paired with Daata, a spicy side sauce that delivered just the right amount of heat. Simple, but incredibly satisfying.

Next came the highlight: the Feast. It’s a platter of injera topped with vibrant scoops of various stews and vegetables. Each one was distinct, bursting with flavors. The crimini mushrooms were earthy and umami-rich, the lentils hearty and beautifully spiced, and the collard greens brought a fresh, slightly tangy contrast. The Shiro, a spiced chickpea stew, was deeply comforting and packed with flavors. Honestly, it was impossible to pick a favorite.
Every bite felt thoughtful, nourishing, and made to be shared. I sipped on refreshing Hibiscus tea throughout the meal, which was the perfect complement to the bold, warming flavors.

Bunna Cafe is a celebration of Ethiopian cuisine and culture. Fun, flavorful, communal, and deeply satisfying. I’ll definitely be coming back.

I have gone here occasionally over the past several years and the food is always wonderful. I went today for lunch because it's Sigd and I wanted vegan food. The kale was amazing. The others really tasty too.

The food is good, but the portions are too small. I paid $21 for this. Is literally like sample sizes and the worst part is you’re not going to get full because the portions are very small. I feel like I could’ve went to chipotle or any other vegan place in New York that gives you a nice portion for like $12 or $15.

formatted_address: 2288 Frederick Douglass Blvd, New York, NY 10027, United States
name: Awaze

reviews.text: Service was incredible, received our food immediately and it was really good. The atmosphere is nice inside and would definitely recommend it for students or workers looking for a place to settle down and work on some projects. The portions were also good, we had more than enough food.

Mmmmmm, new Ethiopian in the 'hood!

With affordable prices (most dishes in the $20s and combs in the $30s) and plenty of flavor, Awaze will do just nicely in the area while offering slightly newer, more modern digs than its competition.

Over a catch-up lunch, my friends and I munched on the Awaze Veggie Combo for two, which offered loads of string beans, red lentils, collard green, chickpeas, cabbage, split peas and beetroot. We paired that with the Meat Combo for two, which came with doro wot, tibs, yesiga alicha, and two side veggies (we added more cabbage and collard greens).

Fun fact: Their combos for two can easily feed 2-4 people total. So enjoy those savings.

Also, we tacked on kitfo, our favorite Ethiopian meat dish. Don't know if it was because they were feeling generous or if we just won them over with all our gushing, but I feel like we were served an extra big, extra flavorful serving of it. Uncooked cow.....drool!

Some of us washed down our flavorful lunch with their Spiced Tea, which was bursting with cloves and cardamom.

Will definitely be back.

This was a top tier experience! First time ever trying Ethiopian food, and definitely won’t be the last. Our server was wonderful walking us through the popular dishes and sharing our excitement in our first taste. Food was hot and well balanced with multiple great flavors, the beer was sweet hitting the spot on a hot day, and the dessert was the perfect cherry on top to a wonderful lunch.

Can’t wait to take my friend and family here!

Awaze Ethiopian Cuisine made my trip a time to remember and fall to the city of NY!

The plate I ordered was a mixture of both fasting and non fasting ( vegetable, lentils, split pea with a meat in the center: KITFO and GORED GORED). They were all so tasty that made me decide to have another for a takeaways so my friends in D.C will try it.

The hospitality of the service, real Ethiopian coffee and the fact that the Chef himself  (Gech) checking on how the food tastes is a plus that made me want to write…

This is a perfect Ethiopian dinning place with a good value and service.

Thank you Gech and the Team!

We stopped in for dinner during the holidays and really enjoyed the adventure of trying Ethiopian food! Our server was really awesome and super helpful about recommendations and explanations! We ordered the lamb for two and both ate so much and had enough to take home for the next days lunch. The spices and tastes are fun and we would recommend you stop in for a visit. Maybe not with your kids.

formatted_address: 1049 Manhattan Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11222, United States
name: Bersi Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text:
Had a fantastic lunch here!
Food was so tasty, very kind service and overall a really great experience.
I recommend taking the combo because you get to choose 7 different kinds of entrees.
If you’re looking for a hearty vegan meal in Greenpoint - this is the place, and you are in for a treat 🧡✨

All gold!! Potent wonderful vibrant love and energy in the food and service. Hard work and dedication to the craft, culture and community. Bersi is a beautiful gem. Happy it’s 100% plant rooted and I recommend ordering 100% gf teff injera. Also THE BEST BAKLAVA EVER!!!

Love to everyone. Missing Brooklyn, looking forward to having it again. -RA (Chicago) 🧡

Party of four skeptics BLOWN AWAY.
We dropped-in on a recommendation and without knowing the menu was vegetarian. For the love of god, don’t let that stop you. We ordered the platter and once it came out it was game over. The food was hearty, satisfying, versatile, fresh, and deeply flavorful. Never in my life have I shoveled beets and carrots into my face with such urgency. We’re already planning our next visit and itching to dive deeper into Ethiopian food. Pretty unassuming, but hands down one of the best meals I’ve had in NYC in a long time. Can’t rave enough!

I love Ethiopian food. Bersi takes it a step further and is a vegan restaurant. Everything on the menu is vegan-friendly, which makes it easy for vegans/vegetarians alike to come here and order anything they'd like.

I ordered the Bersi combo, so I was able to try many different entrees. Some were spicy, some were not, but all were flavorful! The injera may be the star of the show... the owners' family business started out as an injera business. The quality is excellent. I recommend dining in person, as the interior is welcoming and the food is served quickly and fresh!
Wonderful service and everything we ate was delicious. The mushroom Tibs were a standout (Engudaye Tibs). Excellent value and also a lovely ambiance. Also highly recommend the Shimbra Asa.

formatted_address: 763 St Nicholas Ave, New York, NY 10031, United States
name: Tsion Cafe

reviews.text: I don't eat much Ethiopian food, never the less vegetarian. But this was delicious! Our server was great at advising all the best dishes to try. We left full and feeling great. Flavorful and filling. The vibes are good and intimate. Definitely get the dessert!

I really enjoyed Tsion Cafe, everything was flavorful and tasty. This was some of the best injira I have ever had. Most things were not too spicy but for someone who is sensitive there are still options.

I was recommended Tsion Café by my parents and was surprised to see that it was in Harlem! I believe it is the only ethiopian restaurant in the area.

Tsion Café offers a unique take on the Ethiopian dining experience with fusion appetizers that I’ve never seen or had at other Ethiopian restaurants. The injera chips with hummus and fava bean dip, to name a few, were excellentz

The entrées here are also comprised of very unique offerings. The mushroom tibsi and pumpkin were phenomenal. I wish more ethiopian restaurants experimented with stuff like this. The traditional ethiopian entrées are were Tsion Café lacks compared to other spots like Bunna Café. While the food is up to par, serving sizes are small and each order only comes with one of each type whereas other places double up on the various types of bites.

Overall, I was surprised by Tsion Café. It stands out among New York’s other Ethiopian restaurants in location and its unique appetizer and entrée offerings. On top of all this, the host was very ready to answer our questions and was a joy to talk to after the meal. Although I may not come here for my next Ethiopian fix, no one should shy away from coming here if they are in the area and are looking to try something new.

Dinner at Tsion Cafe was a beautiful fusion of Ethiopian and Israeli flavors in a cozy, welcoming space. The meal was perfect for sharing, with every dish bringing something vibrant and comforting to the table.

The Sambusas were crisp and savory, filled with warm spices and paired with a bright dipping sauce that added just the right zing. The Hummus with Silsi was creamy and rich, topped with a spiced tomato sauce that gave it depth and warmth, served alongside soft pita bread.

The Fik’re Lover’s Combo was a standout—a colorful platter of stews and vegetables over injera, each component offering unique spices and textures. It was a perfect introduction to Ethiopian cuisine, with lentils, greens, cabbage, and split peas all complementing one another beautifully.

The Duba Wot with Jollof Rice was hearty and full of flavor, with the sweetness of the pumpkin stew balanced by the spice in the rice. The Ful (fava beans) was earthy and satisfying, brightened by fresh diced vegetables and served with warm bread for scooping.

The Tel Aviv Quinoa Salad was light and refreshing, a welcome contrast to the richer dishes, with Mediterranean herbs and citrusy notes. The Shimbra Asa, a spicy chickpea stew, brought a lovely kick and deep flavor, perfect for fans of bold spices.

To end the meal, the Malawach with Silan—a flaky Yemeni flatbread drizzled with sweet date syrup—was delicate, comforting, and an unexpected treat. The Redd Foxx cocktails were strong, fruity, and a great match for the bold dishes.

Service was warm and attentive, and the space had a relaxed, intimate vibe that made the whole experience feel like a special gathering.

I ate at Tsion Cafe this past weekend and it was delicious! By far some of the best Ethiopian food I've had! The waitress was so kind and helped my parents, who are less familiar with Ethiopian, make a decision on their platter. Everything tasted so good and I hope to come back soon with friends!

The weather was super nice so we sat on the gorgeous back patio space!

formatted_address: 739 Franklin Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11238, United States
name: RAS Plant Based

reviews.text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Ras Plant Based – aka the Purveyors of Vibes 🌈

Ras Plant Based is one of those spots that keeps pulling you back in. I’ve been here multiple times: both dining in and ordering takeout, and it never disappoints. The food is vibrant, fresh, and full of flavor. The injera is soft and perfect, the lentils and veggies are seasoned beautifully, and every dish feels made with real care and authentically Ethiopian.

The vibe inside is warm and inviting, with staff who are always kind and genuinely happy to help you navigate the menu. Whether you’re vegan or just exploring, it’s an easy place to feel at home.

And here’s the pro tip: pickup is quick. If you’re hungry and need something delicious right away, this is your cheat code. Their orders almost always come out faster than the estimated time.

It’s the kind of spot that becomes part of your weekly rhythm: reliable, flavorful, and always there when you need a little Ethiopian comfort from the neighborhood.

From Texas my friend who lives here loved it and recommended so we came. It was my first time eating Ethiopian food and it did not disappoint. The spices, the flavor, the temperature 10000/10000 i wanted to savor every bite. The portions were decent i took half home. That vegan Mac n cheese is a dream truly! Our server was patient. Very intimate beautiful atmosphere. That drink was immature!! I was tipsy off one which I loved!!!! Not water down and the taste and name was soooo cuteeeee

Heard a lot of great things about RAS and glad we finally came by. We ordered some of the most popular items on the menu and everything was delicious. As far as Ethiopian cuisine, the food is just okay. We’ve had other Ethiopian vegetarian dishes which had a bit more of a wow factor to it. I love the vibe inside and the people are wonderful here. It’s a great place to try something new out and get some delicious drinks. Would highly recommend stopping by and trying this place out if you haven’t yet.
Everything was delicious and the service was amazing. The injera nachos were delicious and the platter for 2 was enormous. My mocktail was also reasonably priced. Definitely will come back!

Amazing experience at this place! The plant-based French toast was incredible! The staff were very friendly and attentive.

What really impressed us, though, was the owner - who I didn't even realize was the owner at first! He was sitting nearby, working on something, and struck up a conversation with us without being intrusive or sales-y. His warmth and genuine nature.

Always crowded, but the team handles it with ease. Highly recommend!" 5⭐️

formatted_address: 2084 Frederick Douglass Blvd, New York, NY 10026, United States
name: Lalibela Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: What a fantastic Ethiopian meal! The vegan sampler for 1 had much variety and came with plenty of injera. I love Kitfo (raw), and this portion was pretty large, so flavorful, even spicy! The waitress was attentive and so friendly as well.
Absolutely delicious and reasonably priced food. Every time I went most of the other patrons were Ethiopian - this is always a good sign for authenticity.

The absolute best gluten free restaurant experience I have had in New York until this day!

And I cost me only $24. It is absurdly cheap. I will be tipping extra just because the food should be priced higher for such amazing quality!!!

HOW am I discovering Ethiopian food like this is naturally gluten free.

Huge portions! The picture doesn’t show how much food you truly get!
I am moving away from this neighborhood next week, but I just found this place 😭
Lalibela sampler is delicious!!!  Tibs wot best ive ever had.  Large portion for the price too.   Finally, nice dining room, washroom all immaculate.

Lalibela Ethiopian Restaurant deserves its flowers. Five years strong — that’s something worth celebrating, especially for a spot that made it through the pandemic and came out thriving. Every time I’ve passed by or stepped in, it’s full of life — never empty, always welcoming, always consistent.

The service is warm, the energy is good, and you can tell people come here because it feels like home. The chef recommends the Lamb Awaze Tibs, and while I haven’t tried it myself (Uber driver pick-up life), I’ve seen enough satisfied faces to know it’s the real deal.

Shout-out to the whole Lalibela team for five solid years of culture, community, and flavor holding down Harlem. Keep shining — y’all built something special.

Flavors that last. Community that matters.

formatted_address: 515 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, NJ 07042, United States
name: Mesob

reviews.text:
Friendly and great service. It was our first time ever trying Ethiopian food so we greatly appreciated the server explaining everything to us and recommending specific items.
We were surprised by the yummy flavors of the various samples of sauces/dips and it was quite the experience eating with our fingers. We ordered a vegetarian platter for two and a meat platter for two. The chicken and beef dishes were my favorite but the cuts used were quite dry and tough. Be aware that the smell of the food will stick around on your fingers, even after washing.

Can’t stop thinking about the food we had! It was such a lovely dinner.

First of all, we were incredibly late, we reached 10 minutes before Mesob was about to shut. However, they didn’t turn us away, and served us the food with love. So, for me, the restaurant was a 10/10 since the start.

The food, oh my God, it was delicious. My first stint with Ethiopian cuisine, and it was brilliant. Images below don’t do justice to the food, but it was amazing! The vegetarian selection is great ⭐️

I will definitely visit again, and I would recommend everyone to.

I celebrated my birthday here and not this place did not disappoint! The staff were able to accommodate about 20ppl since my wife called ahead. They were very welcoming and friendly! Now since we had a large party, we did a family style dinner which included all 3 meats and 4 vegetables of our choice which you eat with their specialty bread injera. Everything was delicious. I was very happy with the service and food and absolutely recommend this place for anyone who wants to experience a different cuisine!

I haven't had Ethiopian food in a while and couldn't wait to get some! When I arrived I parked on the street nearby. I walked into a super cute restaurant. The restaurant is BYOB. Bethlehem was our server, and she was great! We ordered:

Ethiopian Coffee
Mango and guava juice
Buticha (Chicpea)
Ingudai Tibs
Ye'misir Sambussa (pastries with lentil,onions, peppers)
Doro Tibs (Chicken Breast)
Meat Sampler (beef, lamb, chicken)
Injera Bread
Baklava
Cappuccino Crunch

The food was really good! My favorites were the ice cream, the lamb, and that chicken! The restaurant was great!
Very nice Montclair location. Very good service. I'm not into spicy food, so the kitchen was able to make my choices on the mild side. Good selection, generous portions.

formatted_address: 1301 Memorial Dr, Asbury Park, NJ 07712, United States
name: Ada's Gojjo

reviews.text: I saw Ada's Gojjo on a viral tiktok video and knew it was going to be my birthday lunch spot on Oct 2nd. I love Ethiopian food and gladly drove over an hr from South Jersey because I just knew from Ada's aura in that tiktok that the food would be a hit. I WAS RIGHT!!! My sister and mother came along with me and we all were in awe of everything (food, service and atmosphere).  Ada is a top notch human, who is extremely welcoming, and attentive to her customers. We ordered 4 appetizers to start and every single one was amazing. We then got our entrees which consisted of Injera, 1 meat side and 2 veggie sides each. We couldn't get over how great the food was. Everything was a 10. As I said, Ada is attentive to her customers, so she paid attention when we first walked in and I was so excited, telling her how I found the place and came as it was my bday.
