I mentioned this with no intention of getting anything, just pure excitement, but Ada came out with a piece of tres leches cake with a lit candle and wished me a happy birthday. The cake was devine. If you are thinking about visiting Ada's Gojjo.....GOOOOOOO!!!! I will be back no doubt, because the hour+ drive is worth it.

This place is amazing!! It was my first time trying Ethiopian cuisine and I was blown away. I had Ada’s Special Ye Siga Tibs and the dish was perfectly seasoned, had good portion sizes and was overall delicious. The interior was welcoming and intimate and the staff were attentive and kind! Will definitely be back for more!

Saturday at 2pm was completely quiet. Our server was nice but seemed new and really unsure of just about everything. We wanted to swap vegetables for yuka, but no substitutions were available. The food was fresh but wasn't very seasoned IMO. Keep in mind this was my first time having Ethiopian food. We sat for a while and chatted until about 4:30...still no new customers.  Maybe there were takeout orders. It's a nice place but I don't know that I'll be back.

Saw a video through TikTok about this place and had to try it. 10/10 would try again! Everything was so flavorful and the service and atmosphere was top-notch. I got the Ada's special and it was so tasty! If you haven't tried Ethiopian food before I highly recommend this be your first pick.

This was our first time having Ethiopian food and I would highly recommend Ada’s Gojjo to anyone looking for a super flavorful, comforting meal. The food here is delicious! Staff and owner were so kind and friendly as well.

formatted_address: 46-11 Skillman Ave, Sunnyside, NY 11104, United States
name: Makina Eritrean-Ethiopian Eatery

reviews.text:
Just tried the newly opened Makina in Sunnyside and wow!! It did not disappoint. I’ve been a long time fan of their food truck, so I was beyond excited to finally visit the restaurant, and it absolutely lived up to the hype. The space is stunning—elegant and sophisticated, yet still warm and cozy. You can tell a lot of time and thought went into the design and all the little details really elevated the space.

The staff and owners were incredibly friendly and welcoming, and hearing them share the history of Ethiopia and Eritrea made the experience feel even more special and personal.

The food was bold, vibrant, and full of flavor with just the right level of spice. The injera deserves a special shoutout - soft, fresh, and perfect for scooping up every bite. Standout dishes for us were the mushroom dulet (a must-try whether you’re vegetarian or a meat lover!), prawns, awaze tibs, the injera bruschetta, and the tiramisu. Yes, we ordered a lot lol. Everything was so good.

I traveled from Long Island to Sunnyside and it was 100% worth the trip. I’m so happy they’ve opened a brick and mortar spot and I already can’t wait to go back!

Visited Makina, this new Ethiopian restaurant in Sunnyside on just their 4th day after opening, and it was absolutely worth the wait. I’ve been looking forward to this place, and it did not disappoint. The atmosphere is warm and inviting, and although we waited about 10 minutes, we ended up with a great spot and even got to chat with the owner during the wait — a lovely personal touch.

The food was fantastic. Everything is served with injera as the base, as it should be, and every dish we tried was delicious. A strong recommendation for the mushroom dulet appetizer — truly standout. From the thoughtful details like the expanding hand towels (just add warm water!) to the curated cocktails, wine and a beautifully done fish entrée, everything felt well thought out and flavorful.

So happy Sunnyside finally has an Ethiopian restaurant. Will definitely be back, and highly recommend giving this place a try!

honestly just found my new favorite spot. if you live in nyc you know it’s rare to find something that actually feels new, but this place is doing a mix of ethiopian and eritrean food with italian influences because of the history. I haven't seen this anywhere else.

the flavors are really bold and most dishes have a bit of a spicy kick, though it’s definitely manageable and not overwhelming. the kale and beet salad was great and the mushroom dulet is a must order. if you want a heavy main dish the doro wot or the lamb are both solid, super hearty. also the tiramisu is actually one of the best i’ve had in awhile.

eating with your hands is the traditional way to go, but don't worry, utensils are definitely available if you’re not feeling it! lol

the interior is also worth mentioning because the decor is beautiful. it’s all authentic vintage italian art deco and the lighting makes the whole place feel really warm. it doesn't feel like a typical sterile nyc restaurant. staff were also super friendly and fast with the food which i appreciate.

definitely worth a visit if you want something unique.

We were so excited to be at Makina Cafe's opening night in Sunnyside. Learning about the influences of the food, the story behind the resteraunt's design and meeting the team was wonderful! The food and drinks were all delicious from the injera bruschetta to start to the flourless chocolate cake to end on a sweet note. We also enjoyed a beer and smokey hibiscus cocktail. Makina is definitely a perfect new addition to the neighborhood! We can't wait to try everything on the menu!

Both the mushroom dulet appetizer and chicken tibs we had were an explosion of flavors, I was floored by how tasty they were. Plus they weren’t too spicy either, speaking as someone who usually can’t handle too spicy a food.

I also quite enjoyed the little expanding towelettes at the beginning of the meal, such a nice touch!

formatted_address: 3153 Broadway, New York, NY 10027, United States
name: Cafe Massawa

reviews.text: Simply outstanding food and service. The coffee and teas were excellent. The food was amazing. The deserts were outstanding too. The service was just heartwarming. Great value for your money to! The bean appetizer, chicken drumsticks and beef dishes were to die for. The carrot cake and rum soaked cake were divine!

Polite service, delicious food this was my first time having this dish and it was amazing! I would definitely come again. Just a bit pricey but worth it for a fresh meal that has flavor. Also the honey wine is the best wine I have had!!

Best experience having traditional Ethiopian food here everything was delicious. The service was great and I can’t wait to come back again. We got the injera and beef tibs + berber wings, they were to die for!

Came for lunch and got the zigni with timtimo and green salad. Outstanding. Service was faster than I am accustomed to in an Eritrean restaurant and I really appreciated that! Reasonably priced for how much food you get. I will definitely come back when in NYC. My only complaint is that they had a vegan sampler, but not an omnivore sampler. I like to get one for myself and eat on it for days 🙂 No liquor license yet.

Got the quesadilla and a meat + 2 vegan entree combination. You can’t go wrong with any of the dishes, honestly. Hearty, savory stews served with light, tangy injera!! And we got a rum raisin cake with coconut ice cream for dessert, naturally.

formatted_address: 973 Columbus Ave, New York, NY 10025, United States
name: Zoma Express

reviews.text:
I had an absolutely wonderful experience at Zoma Express! The food was incredibly flavorful—each dish was rich, aromatic, and beautifully prepared. But what made the visit truly special was the hospitality. The host welcomed us with such warmth and genuine kindness that we felt like honored guests in someone’s home. They took time to explain the dishes, offer recommendations, and make sure we were comfortable throughout the meal.
If you're looking for the best Ethiopian cuisine in the city, Zoma is the place to go. Highly recommend!

Super good! I didn’t go to this restaurant before it temporarily closed during covid, but apparently they were on the Michelin Guide.

Really cute and intimate space, classy spot. Service was great, the restaurant staff were really nice and attentive.

The food was amazing and also really well priced! Highly recommend the kitfo (tartare) and shiro. More than enough injera as they brought out more as we ate.

Really fresh and flavorful Ethiopian food! I remember the old Zoma location that closed during COVID so I was glad to see they reopened. We got the Zoma Tibs and Kitfo as well as lots of vegetarian sides. It was perfect for us as a group and the sambusas were freshly made!
Incredible food, and the kindest owner!! We tried a wide variety of their offerings and it was the best Ethiopian food we have all ever had
Awesome food that’s also really healthy! The owner was so friendly and welcoming. Absolutely loved the experience and will definitely be coming back

formatted_address: Clayton Rd, Brooklyn, NY 1123, United States
name: Makina Cafe on Governor's Island

reviews.text: My 1st time trying Ethiopian food and I am in love! The food portions is great! Flavorful and extremely yummy! I'm in love with the beet salad! The goat cheese is absolutely creamy and Divine! The French fries are hot and crispy! Well seasoned with a perfect hint of spice. The chicken rice bowls are seasoned well and the rice is cooked to perfection! You guys gotta try it! There are seats out front under shade and It's a perfect spot to grab a quick bite to eat and enjoy the nice weather! I will be back to try the other items on the menu.
Their hot chocolate genuinely warmed my heart on a cold day. I also appreciate that the owner chose to stay open on Thanksgiving—it made the holiday feel a little brighter.

Excellent, incredibly delicious food. The beef we had was herby and soooo flavorful and the listed fries were delicious. Very generous portions, nice outdoor seating options. So pleasantly surprised to find this spot and will visit again any chance I get! Mouth watering right now just thinking about it….
Great food with awesome service. Perfect lunch for a perfect day! Got the Chicken Tibs bowl with Injera!

Ethiopian eats on Governor's Island! Cute cafe with outdoor seating on a grassy field under lots of shade. The kids played some connect four while we waited for our food.

Really loved their beef tips wrap! Extremely flavorful tender beef pieces with a creamy spicy sauce, the lettuce added a balancing cool texture. We also shared the beef tibs and chicken rice bowls.

formatted_address: 11 Village Plaza, South Orange Village, NJ 07079, United States
name: Walia Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: I live near Springfield, Massachusetts and drive out of my way for hours, just to taste this amazing Ethiopian food. Their generous staff and impeccable food make it well worth the trip. The doro tibs, fasolia, misir watt and kik alicha are my personal favorites. The chef frequently comes out to greet every table to ask how our food was. One time, I mentioned that I gladly come from 5 hours away and she surprised me with a free entree for the ride home! I’ll never forget those kind of moments that make dining truly special. Whenever I’m remotely near New Jersey, this will forever be my first stop!

Loved the food, especially the vegetables and meat dishes.  I’m so looking forward to having my food catered by them for an upcoming event.  I didn’t like the legumes or cabbage as much, but everything else was on point.  So on point!  Oh, and the handmade Baklava (probably spelled that wrong), was a amazing!

What a great experience here! The food was yummy and the service was excellent.  Gluten-free options are available.

The place is clean, staff is friendly.  The place is welcoming and the food is yummy… please note, Ethiopian food is consumed with your hands.  There are utensils available if needed.

Parking is on street and difficult.  We were lucky to find a spot close by.

The area can be kind of sketchy at times, and while we were there, several police were on foot and on the hunt for an individual.

if you can overlook the other issues, it’s worth a trip.

Such a great place to eat! Please support our local black business :). I loved the food and the staff were so kind. The owner personally came to my table to ask me how I was and how was the food.

Run don’t walk there!! 🥰
Terrific experience and a first time here.  We enjoyed our meal and lovely service from everyone taking care us.

formatted_address: 45-14 48th Ave, Sunnyside, NY 11377, United States
name: Makina Cafe Eritrean-Ethiopian To Go

reviews.text: Serving such amazing food from a truck is impressive. Everything tasted amazing, although I’ll have to go again since they were out of injera. The food was amazing, and absolutely worth the price! The staff running the truck was so kind, and I absolutely recommend this place to anyone looking for quick Ethiopian/Eritrean food. Their house sauce was fantastic, give it a try!

I went here with my girlfriend to try out Ethiopian food. We ordered the Chicken Tibs with Sambusa.

When we got to the place., it’s in a shady warehouse which is awesome. We had high hopes.

However, you have to order online and you don’t get a notification if your food is ready.

The sambusa were super small with barely any filling for $6. The Chicken Tibs lowkey taste like Halal. In addition, we were missing our injera and a part of the vegetables ordered (chickpeas) for our chicken Tibs. Our food looked NOTHING like we saw and expected it to be.

This place cooks with heart and skill. The food clearly isn't premade. The service personnel deliver outstanding attention throughout the experience. The environment here is well-crafted. I appreciate this new spot in our area.

Makina Cafe Eritrean-Ethiopian To Go balances flavors in ways few restaurants can match. Their various menu items all show quality. Employee care was notably superior. Service exceeded expectations, food delivery was fast, and the cooking was excellent. I'll visit again when I'm in this part of town.

This place gets the perfect balance of good service and atmosphere. Employees maintain positivity without any coldness. Their food exceeded typical exceptional standards. This place is an unexpected treasure!!! This restaurant offers good meals.

formatted_address: 348 Douglass St, Brooklyn, NY 11217, United States
name: Ghenet

reviews.text: Delicious Ethiopian food that’s well worth the visit. Everyone here is so nice and the combo platter was perfect for 2 people, we couldn’t even finish it. Lot of unique things to try that were all great. Would highly recommend if you’re in the area and looking for a place to eat.

Ordered via Uber Eats. I specifically asked for no cheese on the kategna, but it still came with cheese—which I can’t eat. Really disappointing. Also, the food was bland overall, with little to no salt. Definitely expected better attention to detail.

Did it look nice? Sure. But If youre vegan, the veggies are undercooked, large unseasoned chunks. Really not worth the price. The meat on the platter was 1 big boned piece with tough meat around it. Looks like a decent place to share a meal with friends but definitely didnt enjoy.  Appreciate gf injera though.

Delicious food, attentive staff and it was easy to just walk in and get a table. I've been to a different Ethiopian restaurant in the city but this one is much better. Everything we ate was delicious and the sour bread was not too sour, it was perfect!
Delicious delicious delicious. The vegetable combo for two is a healthy hearty romantic food adventure dream. The Ethiopian beer is refreshing molasses heaven.

formatted_address: 290 Union Ave #1B, Brooklyn, NY 11211, United States
name: Ye Buna Negus NYC

reviews.text: Great place feast for two!!

formatted_address: 149-10 Linden Blvd, Jamaica, NY 11436, United States
name: Jollof Cafe & Grill

reviews.text: Ordering from Joloff Cafe and Grill was a very tasty experience. Depending on what you order, the food can be very spicy. Almost reminds me of how West Indians cook their food. Usually there's going to be a long wait, but I guess because the food is good, people don't really have a problem waiting.

100% halal Senegalese food. Must try their Chicken & Lamb Dibe with their Jollof rice. Also try their Fufu with their Peanut Stew (contains Goat or Beef). Wish I could give this place 10 stars for how delicious their food is. Definitely coming back!

Chill spot with a few seats, but mostly a order & go spot. The food is mostly made to order so everything is fresh. Please make time if you are not ordering ahead. This is my first time having Senagalese food. I got the jollof, lamb, sweet plantains, and also the pepper chicken, with a sorrel on the side. Me & my family devoured everything. The Jollof was perfectly seasoned without any bottom of the pot burn like you find at some places. My impression of Senegalese food is a mixture of all flavors in a dish. Sweet grilled onions, pickled onions with sour  & spices, flavorful savory jollof rice, smoky grilled flavored pepper chicken, & the lamb was so good. Their version of sorrel called bissap was full of flavors but still recognizable. The place was jumping with orders flying out the door so I will be ordering ahead next time.  Thankyou to the owner who was there. She was very kind and hospitable.

This African restaurant is one of the best I ever went to. Their customer service is excellent and the food is true amazing. If you eat here, trust me you will definitely want to come back. Me and my wife went here and we loved it. We especially enjoyed the jollof rice. I highly recommend it. 5 stars

Wow wow wow this food was goood! I waited almost an hour from the time I ordered to receive the food, but honestly, it was well worth the wait. Everything was fresh, flavorful, just so good. I ordered a bunch of stuff just to try everything. I ordered the lamb Shawarma, a chicken Shawarma, the tilapia dish with jollof rice, and the chicken and fish Fatayas, And I also ordered the dessert called thiakry. EVERYTHING WAS SOO GOOD. Im really impressed.

formatted_address: 115-43 Sutphin Blvd, Rochdale, NY 11434, United States
name: Kilimanjaro African Restaurant

reviews.text: I lived in Southside Jamaica, Queens, NY mostly my whole life. Where is Rochdale, NY?
Got a surprise bag from the toogoodtogo app. Had curry chicken, rice/peas, salad and potato salad. Food was good but surprisingly I loved the potato salad. That was the best. Best I've ever had.

formatted_address: 2 Center St Suite #174, Newark, NJ 07102, United States
name: A True Taste Of Kenya

reviews.text: Food was fire, the jollof was slightly dry but there was potential. The music is amazing ! Atmosphere was gorgeous. Waiting a long time for someone to take our order and bring the bill and wasn’t even crowded!

My appetizer was Suya and the steak pieces had a lot of flavor but too much fat. My drink I sent it back they put too much mango puree it tastes like syrup. They made me another  one it was also bad. I end up getting a Bahama mama drink and that was nothing but orange juice. The person making the drinks was not doing a good job. I told the waiter the drink was still too sweet and she  told me I was wrong because she watch them make it. So I said ok nevermind . I was not trying to go back forth and my dinner was ok.

It's a YES!  The food, the service, the ambiance was all stellar.... Dinner was filling, the people were amazing and made us feel welcomed, and the atmosphere was so calming and intriguing to the eye.   This is a definite must do again .

As an American Black man who appreciate culture and experiences, I received that and some dinning here . Im not from Jeresy but WHENEVER I'm back I will most definitely be going back , dressed to the NINES cause that's what their Giving !!!!!!!! 10/10 .

Can't wait to go again !!
Exceptionally fresh and authentic food. Beautiful decor, excellent service. Highly recommend.

formatted_address: 2046 Adam Clayton Powell Jr Blvd, New York, NY 10027, United States
name: Chez Alain

reviews.text: Ensure you experience this place. I feel at home in this spot. They give you enough food, prepare it properly, and make it taste good. Workers here show exceptional service. Drop in for a meal.

Great food but lost points for service (rather, lack thereof).

Granted it was a large group that went, there were missing cutlery, missing cups, not enough water, forgotten food, etc. Food took long but there were 11 dishes for us so it's understandable, but not everything else. Orders were taken down with pen & paper so you just had to cross orders off when its served. As for cutlery, cups & water, just count the heads and put that many sets and 3 full jugs of tap water on the table; we weren't exactly demanding first class service and are more than happy to pass things around Mong ourselves.

On the plus side, it was the first time our lothad Senegalese food, and we loved it. A few accidental bites into extremely hot peppers but no damage beyond a few tears, a brief panic and a lot of laughter. And it was nice that they set aside a large enough space for us when we called ahead to let them know to expect us.
The food was very good the portions were great. Excellent senegalese food

I came here with a friend and it was so good I had to bring my son. He loved it. The hostess was so beautiful and friendly. After my son was done with his food she continued to pour lamb and couscous onto his plate. The place  is not fancy but the food tastes just like home! If you can, you should go!

I went there last Sunday. I ordered the Dibi lamb with salad and ginger. The lamb was delicious. The salad was fresh. My friend ordered rice and maffe with lamb. I was surprised he liked it although he is not used to African food. To me, the service was ok. I go to different African restaurants in the USA. I gave up on csr. If I compare, the csr was ok. I just like the fact that my food looked exactly as the picture. I loved the onions, mustard, the freshness of the salad... Great job to Senegal! If I lived in NY, I will call them every weekend to deliver since delivery is free.

formatted_address: 2778 Third Ave, Bronx, NY 10455, United States
name: Le Dakar

reviews.text:
Good food but very horrible, discourteous and disrespectful service.

Zero respect for customers.

I do not think I'd be bringing my business back here.  Disgraceful!!!

I shouldn't have to spend my own money and get disrespect in return.
Food was delicious and the service was great. Thank you!

I ordered dibbi lamp aloco and djolof rice on the side, they served me dibbi white rice and djolof rice,
You are disrespecting your clients and your services aren’t even right,
This order waiting time was over 40 minutes,
Seriously guys?????????
In this place, no sorry, no please, no have a seat,
Slow services, poor on everything…….. ,
That’s African business with poor services……
Guys make sure do not order your food from Rebecca because she’s so rude and she doesn’t have any respect for the customers.

I visited the restaurant this afternoon (12/23/25) and was left standing outside in the cold. The door was locked, I tried knocking but the restaurant staff (who could see me at the door) couldn’t even approach the door to explain why I couldn’t have access to the restaurant. They kept laughing and gisting inside while I stood outside in the cold.

formatted_address: 3744 White Plains Rd, Bronx, NY 10467, United States
name: Bravo African Restaurant 2

reviews.text:
Terrible terrible service. The lady in the front keeps saying two mins two mins and after 25 mins she’s saying two mins and added that if i cant wait then I should leave. Avoid this place guys , they think time has no value. Probably illegal business. And if you are a delivery guy never pick up order from
Here. Terrible service

This was cray the amount of food we got for two plate at $27!!! I order a whole fish with plantain and lemon mustard onion pickle marinate. It was super delicious and the chef added an extra Half tilapia lol. He was checking me out.  Yaaaas I'm the Senegalese man dream lol apparently in NYC haha. My  second plate was dibi. Marinated grilled meat with grilled onion in a charcoal grill manner. With couscous and caramelized onion. Great price, taste and value...

Great experience always.
Excellent place for authentic and freshly cooked West African dishes

Not recommended for eat in. The service is horrible but the food is good. Large portions and tasty. The menu is not in English so if you don’t speak the language good luck. The waitress is also the host and cashier. Very bizarre.
Sadly the price hike isn’t justified.

Poor service evening time because of  the Senegalese lady, she talk bad to customers.  either you speak Wolof or she know your face to serve you , she never respect the line, she’s not doing her job at all. Guys if if you want good service be there before 5pm

formatted_address: 440 York St, Fredericton, NB E3B 3P9, Canada
name: Food by Fatou

reviews.text: We were trying Senegalese food for the first time. Chef Fatou was very warm, pleasant and welcoming. I had the special of the day: shrimps and grilled fish with plantains and rice. The portion of rice looked more like a side than a meal. My partner had the jollof rice with plantains and chicken and this was a decent portion size. The restaurant is quite comfy. I didn't like that the washrooms felt quite deserted at the back of the building.

Fatou is an outstanding chef. Her food is tasty, fresh and subtly flavoured. Poulet yassa, chickpeas and jollof rice have become staple dishes for our whole family. Not only that, but she is a wondefully warm, lovely person. For all of the reasons above, I did not hesitate to book her for a catering event for 40 guests. And oh boy, did she deliver! The food was amazing, plentiful and just first class. So I booked her again this year and she delivered again! The guests are still talking about it - the food was the highlight of the evening. Thank you Fatou, you're the best!

Food by Fatou seems driven by a belief that food brings people together like family. The warmth with which we were welcomed by Fatou transformed the modest basement space into a cozy and relaxing atmosphere made for unwinding.

The concise menu provides a range of both vegetarian- and non-vegetarian Senegalese options which range from sweet and spicy like today’s special of Goat with Peanut Sauce to savory and unctuous like the Senegalese Special Rice.

We were treated to a free appetizer of a hyper-modern shrimp roll, with a smooth shrimp cake surrounded by a nest of crisp phyllo strips, fried, and topped with a salty tapenade. It was easily one of the best things I’ve ever eaten.

In addition to the stellar food, Fatou also produces her own Bissap - an all-natural sweet drink that packs a ton of punch without overpowering the meal it’s meant to compliment. She offers tamarind, white hibiscus with ginger, and red hibiscus with mint (try this with the goat).

Come for the great food, stay for the fantastic service. Do NOT miss this gem hidden on York street!

I dont know how she makes these things so good! These are absolutely delicious and they were really cheap. If you want a cheap lunch this is the spot for you.

The owner also came and talked to me and she is so sweet. What a great business owner

Probably some of our favorite food in town. Fatou is a lovely person who is excited to share her food with every guest. I always eat past full because it just is so delicious. Haven't tried anything I didn't like or love yet.

formatted_address: 1473 Westchester Ave, Bronx, NY 10472, United States
name: Bravo African Restaurant

reviews.text: This restaurant is one of the worst in the world and it has to be here in New York. They shouldn't be here, they are useless, they are bad at attending, they are slow, they believe the one who is in their country... I don't know how they are allowed to work in a place like that when they are the worst, rude and disrespectful to attend to people.. They should get them out of here

I ordered Ceebu Jen for $14.00.

Although this dish was great, I’ve definitely had better Ceebu Jen. The rice wasn’t as flavorful as the Ceebu Jen I’ve had in the past, and the fish was cold. My favorite part of the dish was the yam. It tasted so good! The re-warmed cabbage on the side was hard to eat. I enjoyed getting some crispy rice on the side for crunchiness!

I waited a little less than 20 minutes for my meal.

If I ever order again, I’ll order takeout since I didn’t enjoy the slightly strong fish smell of the restaurant. And again, the fish tasted amazing even with its cold temperature.

The food at this restaurant use to be consitantly good....Not sure whats happening...my last 2 orders were horrible.My fish dinner is always missing something...I got home tonight ready to eat ...
It's ust the fish no onions...in addition their always out of rice...smh.The new girl is always on her phone and missing your order....smh do better

Great and Rich Taste
Best option to go with at evening is
1) Grill Fish with rice or salad
2) Dbee ( Grill Lamb ) with rice or salad

Please save your money and do not buy food from this restaurant the lamp Dibi tasted like literal lamp because it was under cooked . The chicken seasoning was dry and it taste horrible. This restaurant took over 2 hours to get me my food . But overall, in all honesty, they cannot cook. I am African. I tried African food from a lot of restaurants and this is by far the worst restaurant to get African food from.

formatted_address: 656 N Salina St, Syracuse, NY 13208, United States
name: Somali Restaurant

reviews.text: This was the best hospitality we have ever had. The cook and chashier was super sweet to our kids making sure they had food they liked. The food was delicious and big portions. We had goat and chicken with unique rice it was so aromatic, you could smell jasmine as it cooked:). It was a differnt flavor palate,but in a great way, not so foreign that the average person couldn't enjoy it. and somosas were yummy with light curry. The hot green sauce were unique and so good on the rice. And my son and i loved the mango drink also. My kids liked the food also and they are under 5, but green sauce is to spicey for kids, otherwise not spicey food just yummy.

The food can sometimes be good, but many times it is horrible and definitely not authentic Somali taste. There is no consistency in their cooking or food quality. My kids said they will never eat there again. Do not try their samosas or chapati—you will be disappointed on your next visit. The Somali tea is somewhat decent, but it has far too much sugar. The meat is overly seasoned and too salty. The most I can give for now is 3 stars. Good luck ✌️

Excellent wholesome Somali food. Friendly service. Samosas. Chapati and beef. And excellent chicken wraps. Mango juice was amazing too. So much flavour and reasonable prices. We will definitely come again.

i’ve been raving about this place all week! the women cooking were SO nice. the food was absolutely incredible. the fresh juices were so delicious. the sambusa?!?!? changed my life! this place made my fall in love with my city again! please check them out💜 also VERY affordable!!

This place is on my block and I’m glad it is! I had a night I was home alone so I went there. The owner was very nice in helping me understand my choices. The chicken sequaar was very good and the solmolian rice was delicious. I got some homemade hot sauce which was awesome but hot! Mango juice was outstanding and a must when you come here. The chicken somosa was excellent!

formatted_address: 224 Parliament St, Toronto, ON M5A 3A4, Canada
name: Wanaag Restaurant Somali Grill and Cafe

reviews.text: Delicious, great amount of flavors - Big plates and the location is beautiful. Really nice for group gatherings! They oud (scented) the space for good vibes and starts your meal with a warm lentil soup + comes with a drink, highly recommended! Thank you Ifrah for the service with a smile

Very delicious Somali food and traditional plates. GOAT meat was yummy and the dishes are so huge and plenty of food that you can’t finish. I highly recommend this place to others who want to try to check African food.

The food is ok, the lentil soup needed salt and had huge pieces of onion in it. The mango juice is watered down and they dont offer pop as a substitute like other Somali restaurants. We got lamb shoulder and goat meat. The lamb shoulder was good but the goat meat was all bone. The rice is also lacking salt and had whole cardamom pods in it that went into the bite I had, it was so bad!!
The portion size was small compared to other Somali restaurants and the the prices much higher. It was almost $60 for two meals!!! I can’t recommend because of all of the above.

We visited Wanaag Restaurant Somali Grill and Cafe today after Friday prayers with some friends. The food was pretty good — I’d give it a 7 out of 10. However, the service was really poor. We waited a long time, and no one came to check on us or ask if we needed anything. The customer service definitely needs improvement.

The food here is really good and the staff here are also very friendly I ordered the lamb and goat meat and it comes with like free drink and lentil soup which is also very delicious the seating is quite comfortable and the food is just amazing it's unlike anything else I've ever had the seasonings are very special and the meat quality and all the freshness of all the ingredients are very good

formatted_address: 836 Niagara St, Buffalo, NY 14213, United States
name: Mogadishu somali food

reviews.text: There was no effort out into making the meal feel unique no it’s not even that it’s the fact that the meal felt rushed and there was not enough seasoning. They can definitely do better next time. Today must have not been their day. Customer service was Great and their drinks Awesome though. Recommend the Mango Juice.
Best Somali food in town . Fast service great people.
Great food. Friendly service
Authentic and tasty Somali food.

formatted_address: 3678 White Plains Rd, Bronx, NY 10467, United States
name: Eko Suya Spot

reviews.text:
Eko Suya Spot in the Bronx truly shines with its vegetable and fufu dish! The vegetables are fresh, vibrant, and cooked to perfection, bursting with flavor and a delightful mix of spices. They pair wonderfully with the fufu, which is incredibly soft and has the perfect texture for soaking up the delicious accompanying sauces.

The dish is not only satisfying but also showcases the restaurant's commitment to quality ingredients and authentic preparation methods. Whether you’re a vegetarian or just looking to enjoy a hearty meal, this combination is a fantastic choice. The warm and inviting atmosphere, along with friendly service, makes dining here a wonderful experience. Highly recommend giving this dish a try!

The establishment is small but spacious it is clean. It is comfortable. It is cozy. The staff is friendly and knowledgeable. There is music playing for ambience. The food is made to order so if you are in a hurry call ahead 😉 Asé!

Great low key spot. Pleasant team - I hope they upkeep their services.

Food reminds me of my Granny recipes lol - Simply the best. Value for money and service excellence.

Opening hours varies, be sure to confirm open hours before you make that trip.

It’ll be nice to see door-dash deliveries/ take-out on their google adds.

Dinning area can conveniently seat 15 - 30 guests.

It’s my favorite Afro-American and frankly budget friendly.

First off the gentleman that greeted us when we came in was very professional and welcoming. He was patient with us explaining the different dishes' taste and flavor. He was also able to convey to the kitchen our need to eat less spicy.

Not related to us, but I was very impressed with his handling of impatient customers: professionally but practically.

We ordered the pounded yam to go with egusi soup with mixed meat, suya,fish with red soup. All these three dishes were finger licking 😋level and well cooked.  In my opinion the mixed meat portion could have been larger.

If you are visiting the Bronx, I highly recommend. I know I will hit that spot again to try other items on the menu
Delicious food!! I had moi moi, efo riro with fish and pounded yam and it was so flavorful. I will definitely be coming back!

formatted_address: 429 W 125th St, New York, NY 10027, United States
name: Mama Africa on Wheels LLC

reviews.text:
I had their lamb, which comes in really big portions and is topped with onions – my favorite. I also got the jollof rice, white rice, and saka saka. Everything was really good. I absolutely recommend this place; I’ve been there twice now and will definitely go again.

Unfortunately, I didn’t take any pictures after purchasing, only of how I plated the food. I’d give it an 8.4.

I tried it two weeks ago and been back 4 times already on repeat. Great lamb dibi slices. If you like your steak well done and  soft melting while you bite try this.

Also the pea carrot beef Djolof rice  is very very good.

I love the service. Very attentive. I had like 3 people working on my order at once for me to get it super fast.

I'm the Djolof princess Anta of tivaoune.They have Djolof rice.and the kitchen and food handling so up to point. I'm ocd but did not see major acts to make me scream lol . I think about the lamb dibi with meet Djolof rice on the side all the time now. In love ... Twp portions feeds 3 people. Sweet for groups, family and if you want to have a meal and finish the rest later when snacking. .
So there's no egusi soup and fufu here but there's different West African cuisine - specifically Senegalese.   V good peanut sauce.
The food is amazing the service is great nice environment I would definitely come back to this astonishing restaurant 🙏🏼

A wonderful and comforting spot that uniquely blends West African, American, and some Middle Eastern flavors into a warm Oasis from the hustle and bustle of 125th. There is fresh French bread rolls for take away, American fast food and Senegalese home cooking. A wide assortment of fresh fruit drinks.

formatted_address: 2319 Frederick Douglass Blvd, New York, NY 10027, United States
name: Native Harlem

reviews.text:
I've been hearing about and seeing this restaurant on IG. So I booked a reservation, the best decision ever.
This restaurant is everything and then some. The decor is upscale but not stuffy so you can still enjoy. You can tell alit of thought wss hiven to the concept of the space and decor. The staff at the front desk is very welcoming. The atmosphere of Native is a whole vibe. The music had us both singing a dancing in our seats, kudos to the DJ. The onstage  performance with the beautiful ladies, was liks nothing I'd seen before and they did the damn thing we loved it.Now this food yes and yes was absolutely delicious. The waitress was amazing, and offered recommendations. We settled on the  salmon tacos, basmati fried rice with snapper, penne pasta with shrimp and drinks. To end this beautiful experience we shared a delicious and moist large slice of red velvet cake.Overall this place is a definite vibe that everyone should enjoy and  we enjoyed every minute from arrival to departure.. there's a perfect spot in the front to take photos. If you're looking for an amazing restaurant for date nite or just to enjoy good food and drinks  with friends, make a reservation and stop by, you won't be disappointed or leave hungry.

What a night!! A few friends and I went to Native on a Sunday evening and we had an absolute blast!! First the host staff was very kind and welcoming, once seated I was pleasantly  surprised that they had a DJ.  We were moving before even sitting down.  We ordered the Suya wings, must try! they are soo good!! The calamari was our other appetizer dish, it was crispy, not chewy, and greasy.  Loved them and the sauce provided.  Our mains were the jollof with goat, jollof with snapper and salmon and mashed potatoes.  Baby!! All the food was scrumptious. The drinks! Woo, hats off to the mixologist! I had the native punch and another pineapple drink(?) both were very good.  My friends also raves about their drinks.  The price range was comparable to what any NY restaurant would charge for an establishment of the same caliber.  I was very pleased.  The cherry on top were the dancers! They have an elevated stage in the middle of the dinning room where dancers perform coordinated dancers.  They even pull people up there and leave them through some dances.  It was so entertaining and a nice touch!!! They even walked around to engage the guests.  The DJ kept the night flowing quite well.  The crowd joined in on a few dances and filled the aisles as we collectively got down!! Awesome night, superb food, great service, top notch experience!! I'll be back!!

I went there for brunch today 1/4/25.  The meal was delicious.  Although everything can be pricey, the vibe and all made the experience worthwhile.  That said,  black businesses need to do better in how they treat their clientele if they want sustainable support from the community.  Does it make any sense to charge $5 for some extra  sauce I requested for the rest of my jollof rice (I’d ordered the jollof with the goat stew sauce but the sauce they served was barely enough for half the rice). See pics below for the tiny bit of, dare I say it, tomato  sauce which cost my cousin and I $10 as we each requested one.  I understand it’s a business and you need to make profit but just be fair about it, it’s tacky otherwise.

It was my first time there with  my friend I was impressed how beautiful the restaurant is. And the food was delicious I got  jollof spaghetti with shrimp was delicious 😋 the coconut and  strawberry magaritas were perfect. The jollof had 2 peppers on the menu 🌶 but it was not spicy at all.  The red velvet was good not too sweet.  We got the chance to see dancing performance🕺🏿💃🏾🕺🏿💃🏾  there it was excellent 👏🏾👏🏾 I will definitely go back again. Thank you

First time dining at Native Harlem. I was with my girlfriends celebrating our sisterhood and we were blessed with Jen's 5-Star service. From the recommendations to her overall energy, my dining experience was a lasting one and I'll absolutely be back. I had the Beef Suya, Crispy Calamari, Braised Oxtail w/ Jollof Rice, Harlem Lychee, and Branson Colada. 10/10 for me!

formatted_address: 563 E 26th St, Brooklyn, NY 11210, United States
name: Káyọ̀dé Restaurant Mirage

reviews.text: Kayode Mirage is a business like none other. I have ordered from them consistently for 3 years all the way from another borough (because they are that good). They have never disappointed! The food is such high quality in taste, in volume and authenticity. Their customer service is very smooth, she always kindly places the order and follows up. Every celebration I have I order and have never been disappointed. Personally I recommend the jollof rice the ayamase the asaro, the puff puff, the amala!!! So so good! RUN don’t walk to place your holiday order. I just did and will be back again

Girlll, her food is exquisite & she’s so sweet with a warming personality. She even offered my wife & our son food/snacks. Definitely go support her immediately, she’s such a hard worker & she deserves the world! This is my new favorite spot, I will only be going here from now on. 🌺🦋😻

After seeing Egusi soup and fufu on TikTok I've been wanting to try it for the longest time and im glad I chose to at kayode restaurant mirage! The food was so delicious and flavorful and I was full after eating only half the portioned fufu and egusi soup. There was plenty of tripe, tendon, and goat meat, though the bones were a bit big. The owner is so so so sweet and kind and even gave me puff puffs on the house! The puff puffs are slightly sweet fried dough, very addicting and yummy. The story behind her restaurant is one I’ll never forget and she is an absolute angel. Please support her and her son Kayode’s restaurant—I heavily recommend this place and I'll definitely order again!!

Note* pickup is located in the back of the restaurant, so not on Flatbush Ave but on E26st. She’ll be opening the front of the restaurant soon though so look forward to that!

My first time eating Nigerian food was one to remember! I was welcomed in with open arms and left with a full stomach and a warm heart. I had the Swallow Amala Mixed Meat Egusi with fufu and it was great. I was also treated to complimentary puff puff and Sobol, which was super nice. Eating with my hands made it all the better!

Food is amazing, the service is great and you feel a home style atmosphere. I travel all the way from Queens weekly to get some great tasting food.. my son’s enjoy every bite and beg daily for me to pick up more food. Don’t think twice, order and you won’t regret it!..look I can’t wait to eat when I get home.. so I’m eating in the car.. lol .. peace & Blessings!.

formatted_address: 1322A E Gun Hill Rd, Bronx, NY 10467, United States
name: Mama G. African Kitchen

reviews.text: I order Egusi soup with spinach and meat and FuFu. they gave me just a bowl of spinach and the FuFu wasn’t even FuFu it was some brown ball and I don’t know what type of meat they using but it looks like a birds finger nail !

Luckily for me, I met the original mama.G owner back on white plains road when she was e216th by gun hill road in 2015 When I came here she greeted me with nothing but love and the staff was very welcoming ,this visit at the new location had an older woman and also treated me as if I was her grandchild serving me jollof rice,rice and peas,spaghetti with gari black eyed peas ,pepper sauce fresh tomato,onion with plantain and it's absolutely delicious every time cooked with love ❤️

Best Ghanaian food in the area. This location is way better than the restaurant on white plains road. It is larger and the food is better. My favorite is the spinach soup. I don’t advise getting pounded yam to go w it because you received a very small serving. Food is reasonably priced.
I ordered wakyye and the chicken wasn’t cooked and I ordered agusi they spinach soup…..just pitiful
Ordered the tilapia with jollof. Food was not fresh. I think they make all dishes ahead of time bc they had to reheat my food and it was still cold.

formatted_address: 549 Commonwealth Ave, Bronx, NY 10473, United States
name: AfroSpice BisTro

reviews.text: It was my first time dining at AfroSpice and I must say it was such a delight.  From the moment we entered we were greated and taken to our table. I came with my toddler daughter and was offered a high chair, I pleasantly surprised. Our server was awesome, she gave great recommendations. The food was delicious! The vibes were on point. The DJ was playing jam after jam! I will definitely be back!

I was craving Ghanaian cuisine and didn’t hesitate to make the long journey to the Bronx to indulge in some. The food here is delicious, and the service is excellent. However, I must say that the drinks are my favorite. I brought a friend who had never had Ghanaian food before, and she was equally pleased with her meal. I can’t wait to return for my next visit.

I Went here with my sisters tonight for our birthday, we had amazing service and amazing food. We can’t wait to come back and have some more amazing  food. Everything was so good but I could eat the groundnut soup and okro stew with fufu everyday. We got a platter and entrees and a few Sides, everything was seasoned so good. Bridgett was our waitress and even helped us by taking some pics for us and the owners/ managers kept coming around to check on us and make sure that we were good and satisfied. 10/10 experience!!! Thank you guys for a great night.

Local place that I really like. They have delicious Ghanaian food and the staff is very friendly and attentive. The fufu and soup is delicious together and has great flavor. Fish and shrimp was also delicious. Glad to have this place in the neighborhood.

Possibly the BEST African restaurant I've been to, yet. I got their jollof rice with fish and plaintains. It was SO good! My sister got their rice stew. For the drinks, I got the pink lemonade and my sister got malt.

The music was really loud but we liked the songs. I would definitely go there again. The service was great too and our server Kwame was very nice.

formatted_address: 6568 Woodward Ave Suite 100, Detroit, MI 48202, United States
name: Baobab Fare

reviews.text: Worth the visit! I give out a lot of 5 stars but if I could rate this place higher I would. The food was exceptional and not a single crumb was left on anyone’s plate after the meal 😅. I would recommend the mbuzi (goat) and the kumuhana (grilled chicken)! Both the spiced rice and coconut rice are delicious as well and you can get half and half. Overall for the price, the food, environment, and service are well worth it. This restaurant gives a great insight on Burundi cuisine and has joined my rotation of restaurants in the area! 10/10 would recommend.

This was our first time trying African cuisine, and we absolutely loved it. The flavors felt surprisingly close to Indian food in the best way. We tried the hibiscus tea and the spiced coffee—both were excellent. The plantain chips with the dipping sauce were a classic and delicious combination.

For the main course, we had Ugali and Intore. Ugali felt very comforting, almost like homemade South Indian food, and Intore was rich, flavorful, and reminded us of South Indian dishes as well.

The service was quick, and the ambiance was great. Truly one of the best restaurants in downtown Detroit!

Portion size was large and offer vegetarian and vegan options. The food was overly oily, the okra with ugali was extremely fibrous and oily. The mocktail was excessively sour. Can't explain but an unappetizing smell emanated from the kitchen area. The food looked better then it tasted
Absolutely amazing food. Chicken and beef unbelievably good. The passion fruit/avocado dessert was complex and rich in flavour. Hibiscus tea also delicious.

This corner spot is a fantastic place to enjoy some African food! The interior design is beautiful, and the view of the streets from inside is amazing. We had the Chicken and Lamb dish, both of which were delicious. I also loved the coconut and mango dessert. I’ll definitely be back!

formatted_address: 2324 Arthur Ave, Bronx, NY 10458, United States
name: West African Restaurant

reviews.text: Excellent! Really nice! Great music. West African food is the best! I recommend West African Restaurant it is a must!

name: IYA IBADAN KITCHEN & CATERING SERVICES

reviews.text: I LOVE THIS PLACE!! Pounded yam with egusi is so delicious! Nice and spicy and great portions. I always come here the BEST egusi and pounded yam.

This was my first time trying this restaurant, I tried the egusi and fufu the flavor was definitely there, but I went to try the meat it was tough and not soft couldn’t even eat it which was very disappointing because I paid $25 dollars for it.

Im pretty sure he might remember me as the Amazon guy. But I discovered this place while doing doordash, and decided to come back and try it the following day. The one thing i like the most is this place is open to 12am basically 7 days a week. I got Egusi with pounded yams and assorted meats. Chicken, and fish, and it was perfectly spicy as hell 😮‍💨🤌🏾 I came around 10:30 and it was two men there and he greeted me and made my order. He was very nice and I even told him that my best friend is Yoruba and that he put me on to Egusi and I’ve been addicted since. I told him I wish i they had a bigger sign because my house is right around the corner and I’ve never noticed this place  as much as I’ve drove past it. Also thanks for leaving the pomo out because I don’t have an acquired taste for it yet, unless I’m willing to trust someone again who makes it really good. Will definitely be back again to try the jollof  and fried rice. ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

Loved the food.
Great place to have a family get together gathering.
Jollof rice was good, my animal protein dish was still lukewarm and cold.

formatted_address: 373 Malcolm X Blvd, New York, NY 10027, United States
name: Jacob Soul Food Restaurant

reviews.text:
The story of Jacob Soul Food Restaurant is a heartwarming tale of community, family dedication, and an immigrant's dream realized in the heart of Harlem.
​The restaurant, located at 373 Malcolm X Blvd (Lenox Avenue), was founded by Rachid Niang, an entrepreneur from Senegal who was educated in France before making Harlem his home. He named the restaurant after his late father, Jacob, and it quickly became a neighborhood favorite after opening in 2009.
​The Great Story: Giving Back on Thanksgiving
​The most enduring story of Jacob's is its commitment to giving back to the community, which started just months after its first location opened.
​Despite being a brand new business, Niang felt compelled to show gratitude to the community that was supporting his dream. On their first Thanksgiving, he opened the doors of his restaurant and invited anyone in Harlem—regular customers and those who couldn't afford a hearty holiday meal—to dine for free.
​This tradition has continued for over a decade. Every Thanksgiving Day, Rachid Niang and his wife, Kim Lum Chan Niang, mobilize dozens of volunteers to serve hundreds of free, traditional holiday and soul food meals. Guests can choose from classic Southern dishes like roast turkey, candied yams, and macaroni and cheese, along with Jacob's everyday Caribbean and soul food favorites.
​The restaurant, known for its buffet-style selection of Southern, Caribbean, and Continental fare, is not just a place to eat; it's a true community hub built on family heritage and a deep connection to Harlem.
​Note on Location: The restaurant you are referring to is located at 373 Lenox Avenue (which is also known as Malcolm X Boulevard) in Harlem, New York, NY 10027.
Real SOUL food, every dish is made with love and great flavor.  The staff was kind and welcoming.  Good stuff right there.

My Uncle brought me here for lunch. I like the wide variety of food to choose from. The buffet has quite the spread. From chicken to BBQ ribs to corn to greens...quitevthe variety of soul food. I totally recommend that you stop by!

We came from California to try this place we heard about. The food was delicious and plentiful. You pay by the weight. From the oxtails to the short ribs beyond, everything was good! The live music with the older gentleman and his guitar and the drummer and bass player, definitely made the place lively and fun! Good food, good music,  what more can you ask for! Highly recommended..will be back!😋😋
I went here for lunch recently and the food was very good they had a decent amount of options and it’s affordable!!

formatted_address: 91 Baxter St, New York, NY 10013, United States
name: La Diáspora Bar & Restaurant

reviews.text: Shout out to Adrian and Charley who went above and beyond for us. So many drinks are made with housemade liquors and natural ingredients. Everything is made to order and tasted fresh, flavorful and yummy. Highly recommend the hibiscus freeze and naval margarita. The green tea shots I could have ten more too. The guacamole and house made chips outstanding. Big amount. The shrimp cocktail was better than anywhere in the USA. Big juicy shrimp in a sauce with buttery crackers and fresh avocado. The vegetarian quesadillas and tacos delicious. The corn toro are so tasty you can taste the corn. All the hot sauce and sauces are house made. Everything is made to order.  The steak frite my friend loved. This is nyc at its best. A. Jungle modern speakeasy in the heart of Chinatown.

This is a nice spot in Chinatown with some amazing cocktails and fun vibes!
Their tacos were my favorite.
Great to host private events as well. Someone was celebrating their birthday party when we visited and it seemed like an amazing event!
Definitely check out their amazing happy hour too when you get a chance

The worst service spot, insane wait times during brunch hours. Food was decent, michelada was nice but small (you don’t get the rest of the beer on the side so the mix can be very strong). If you have all the time to wait then this can be a happy hour you sit at for a while since its basically all day.. but for a larger group definitely not worth it.
Beautiful eating experience had a great dinner with my mom. The burger was to die for would definitely come again with friends. Drinks are very good as well. Don was a great server.

The restaurant features a nice neon and semi floral vibe and even has an extra room perfect for large groups. The service was quite slow; had to wait a long time for the food to arrive.

Divorced Enchiladas (2.5/5): While the presentation was incredible, the flavor unfortunately fell flat. The stuffing was bland, and both sauces leaned a bit sour, failing to redeem the dish.

Chori Queso Skillet (5/5): Super tasty!

formatted_address: 5652 Hollywood Blvd, Hollywood, CA 90028, United States
name: Flavors from Afar

reviews.text: The atmosphere is inviting and warm. Parking is a challenge. The service was warm and friendly. I went here dinner however the selections are very limited.  The dish I wanted to order is only available on lunch. The price is very expensive for the amount of food you get. The 3 sisters soup for $15 was just a tiny bowl.  I was given incorrect dessert item from what I ordered. Mint Lemonade was refreshing.

Absolutely delicious food.  This was the first time I've had African food, and I love it.  The Somali 'samosa' was a favorite, as well as the chicken over rice.

The coffee was great too. One of the better coffees I've had in a while.
The best fries and sauces I’ve had in my life! All our food was amazing and the service was warm and friendly.

The food was absolutely amazing! Everyone working there was so kind and accommodating. They took the extra time to help guide us with our order and were genrous enought to let us sample the various drinks. The lentil soup and tamarind drink were my favorite but the sambusas and Somali plate were also amazing. I can't recommend this place enough!
I did a cooking class there with chef Heidi through the Airbnb app. The team there was lovely, the food was delicious, we had a really beautiful time!

formatted_address: 7751 1/2 Melrose Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90046, United States
name: Weaf - West African Food

reviews.text: The food was good and owner was really nice. We got the Jollof meal, the Mafé meal, and the Degue for dessert.  The chicken in both meals was perfectly cooked.  The degue was a sweet yogurt with grains. We really enjoyed the mafe, we'll definitely get it again next time we go

This place doesn’t get enough credit for how amazing it is!! Amazing choices to choose from and such sweet staff. The owner is absolutely awesome and such a good person as well. I definitely recommend if youre looking to add some flavor to your takeout.

Forgot our order. There is no Egusi because they said people complained it doesn't taste the same back home. Fufu is 12 dollar per serving which is ridiculous price because a quarter of it was crusted.
Service here was impeccable. I thought the food was quite tasty as well. I don't have a lot of West African cuisine experience so I can't speak to the authenticity, but I'd go back.
Just what the doctor ordered. Beautiful. Plantains like they’re meant to be and rice and chicken with subtle flavor that leaves you wanting more but with a full stomach and happy heart ❤️

formatted_address: 15136 Stagg St, Van Nuys, CA 91405, United States
name: The Peppered Goat

reviews.text: I was REALLY craving nigerian food after trying it for the first time a couple months ago from a different place in Sacramento. This seemed the only place in the valley to get egusi and fufu so I tried it despite the mixed reviews and I thought it was great. It definitely hit the spot and came with plenty of goat. The goat smell was a little strong but it was all tender and I liked it. Its a ghost kitchen so obviously you'll have to order online and pick up.

Not happy I got goat and this plate was mostly rice for 25.00 the goat tasted old as if it was leftovers. And the goat was tough and mostly fatty. The kitchen was not as clean as I would expect the pots they were cooking out of was old and burnt.  First and last time I go there.
The ladies were sweet. But that it.

Honest review: food is amazing. Best naija food I’ve had in LA. I recommend ordering in advance if you plan to pick it up. Ordered stewed goat (tasty, spicy, soft meat), beans & plantain (this slapped omg! I’m saving some just to eat more tomorrow), jerk & jollof (spicy, smoked, and juicy chicken), and beef suya (tasted like authentic naija suya). Highly recommend! We will def be back for more.

ATTENTION!!!! PSA!!!!! HANDS UP AND TEN TOES DOWN!!! ABSOLUTELY DELICIOUS AND FRESH OOOOOOOO!!!!!
The service is customized (like what you want you get) and professional. Food is handmade and fresh, kitchen clean and nothing but smiles and flavor!!!!!
I ordered egusi, turkey in stew ( yassss turkey) jollof rice AND GOAT PEPPER SOUP.
Many other options as well
LISTEN THE GOAT IS SO TENDER WITH THE COCO YAM SHESSSH MY DEAR GOODNESS
THIS SPICE TO YOUR LIKING. Egusi 🔥 Turkey stew was falling off the bone and smoky 🤤 chile I swallowed my jollof rice 🤭
I will be coming back again and again!!!! Until I can't lol
Quality 💯 Taste 💯
Worth the drive, money and time.
Naija stand up 🇳🇬 because Sammy is representing 🫡

This is my second time trying this spot and will be the last. Bc it's alot closer drive than Aduke. The jollof rice was dry. The suya was the same textured beef as the the stew beef. It was cut up beef with NO seasoning.  The stew beef in this tiny container with a little sauce wasn't even spicy in the least bit. The Jamaican beef patty looked raw so I didn't even try it. A waste of 50.00 and a drive from the Valley. Smh. So disappointing.  I will just have to drive to Inglewood. Yes the staff in that kitchen in nice. But that's it.

formatted_address: 4818 Tacana St, Los Angeles, CA 90008, United States
name: Golden hands Cameroonian food

reviews.text: This is one of the most unique dining experiences. The restaurant is actually a home so you’re getting 100% home cooking from mama Ange. Call ahead to make sure she is available. I lived in  Cameroon and this definitely brought back memories.
The Cameroonian food in LA really golden hands thank you . Sorry we start eating but I put pictures like cause it was really good

The food was delicious. The services were impeccable. It is an amazing feeling to have a piece of back home here in America. Please support the business and the food you will not be disappointed. Laughter, conversation and a welcoming getaway. Good vibes.

I ate well-braised fish with good green sauce accompanied by plantain fries and miodo.  It was really well done.  The price was affordable.  Golden hand African food was really good and throughout my time the music was great.  It was just a fun time at Golden Hand African Food.
Angie is a great cook and an awesome lady!! Loved the ndolè and the grilled fish 🐟! She also has an amazing selection of dishes. Definitely a 5 star ⭐️

formatted_address: 1170 S La Brea Ave, Inglewood, CA 90301, United States
name: Sumptuous African Restaurant

reviews.text:
This spot has some of the best Nigerian food in LA fr. The jollof rice? Literally perfect. It’s not too spicy, not too bland, just packed with the right amount of flavor. So fire.

And the staff is always super nice. They’re really welcoming and chill, which makes the whole vibe even better. If you’re ever in the area and craving something flavorful and comforting, pull up. You won’t regret it.

This was our first time at Sumptuous, and we will definitely be returning soon! A good friend of ours who is Nigerian told us about this place, and considering that he drives all the way from Santa Clarita to eat here, we were intrigued. Not only was the food amazing, but the staff and owner were so remarkably kind. There are a handful of restaurants our family eats at on a regular rotation, and Sumptuous is now officially on that list. Thank you so much for providing such a delectable meal.

p.s. I write a review about once a year, so consider the source!

I gave this restaurant business when I first opened, but since then the quality has gone down, and the customer service is not good. I came in wanting to get an order of jollof and a few sides of fufu because my children particularly like the fufu. They refused to sell me sides of fufu Unless I purchased the soup. In the past, there was not a problem with me, ordering an extra side or two of fufu. The woman behind the counter was rude. Left me sitting at the counter after she saw me walk in when I told her I was ready to order then came back and told me I could not get a side of fufu when it’s on the menu for three dollars each per side. Food has energy and the energy in this restaurant is not pleasant. Therefore, I will keep my money and go somewhere where there is pleasant energy to go with good food.. And as a business owner myself it is disappointing to attempt to support small Businesses and be treated like my business doesn’t matter. Do better, it was just fufu. SMH

Joseph, the server is a decent person, as far as supporting the business’s reputation. I love the egusi soup but it was time for me to try the okro instead of assuming I know the flavor/ it’s something simple I can whip up.. I leave the restaurant with a rich focus awaiting to achieve life’s current challenges..

I Highly recommend Sumptuous African Restaurant for anyone seeking a true taste of Nigeria cuisine.
They truly lives up to the name (Sumptuous)…..Every visit is a rich, flavorful experience. I always find myself going back there for their Edikang Ikong with some goat meat and jollof rice with plantain and some fried turkey😋😋, which are consistently delicious and taste like home.
The Edikang Ikong is perfectly seasoned, with a hearty mix of vegetables and they have mixed meat too if that’s your choice. The jollof? Smoky, vibrant, and unforgettable taste.

What sets this spot apart is not just the food, but the value. It’s hard to find affordable Nigerian dishes that don’t compromise on quality, and Sumptuous nails it every time. Whether you’re new to West African cuisine or craving the flavors you grew up with, this place delivers comfort and authenticity on a plate and the people are nice too. Always feels like home whenever I visit there to get me some food.

formatted_address: 1432 Oak St, Los Angeles, CA 90015, United States
name: Mayowa Nigerian Cuisine

reviews.text:
My friends and I were working for six hours straight at a studio nearby and we were starving. Mayowa was around the corner and we’ve never had Nigerian food before so we excited ordered the Suya wrap and the jollof, plantain, & protein combo (we picked chicken).

The wrap was good, but the star of that order were the sweet potatoes that came with it. They were a bit firmer than regular sweet potatoes and came with a delicious spicy sauce that was perfect on every item.

The jollof rice was our favorite. It was rich and seasoned to perfect, with each bite of onion and bell pepper bursting with flavor. Wasn’t too salty either despite having so much flavor! The plantains had a mild taste and wonderful texture (which paired great with the sweet potato sauce). The chicken was good, a little bit dry but still very enjoyable with the rest of the dish.

When we picked up our order, the gentleman handing our order greeted us with a smile. He also included two hibiscus drinks on the house (most likely due to the extreme heat and humidity) which was greatly appreciated! They tasted wonderful—lightly sweetened with a soft tartness that chased each sip.

We would definitely return to try other dishes!

I grew up in Nigeria, so I know what real Nigerian food should taste like and this is one of the best I’ve ever had! The beef fried rice was packed with meat (no skimping here!) and bursting with flavor. The beef was tender and juicy, the rice perfectly seasoned. On top of that, the owner is incredibly kind and clearly pours his heart into the food. Highly recommend!

Wow! I'm very impressed with how delicious this Nigerian food tastes. I got the Egusi soup w/white yam (fufu), the Jollof rice plate w/stew goat meat, the Efo-Riro, and hibiscus drink. Everything was very tasty, flavorful, and cooked just right. The goat meat was moist & tender, just the way I like it. Yummy yummy to my tummy! And the portions are well worth the Do-Rey-Mi. Chef's Kiss!

Compliments to the owner: Timi is niiice. He rendered outstanding customer service skills. Very kind, humble, peaceable, respectful, joyful, patient, and helpful; enriched with a beautiful smile and charming personality. Can we clone him?!?

If y'all don't go to Mayowa Nigerian Cuisine, then you are depriving yourselves of some of the best quality, authentic, delectable sustenance in town!

Now please excuse me while I do my happy dance...

I called and did a pick up order. The owner, Chef Tanto, absolutely knows his way around the kitchen. His food is so flavorful. Upon first bite my mouth was in heaven. Whichever rice you get, make sure you get the sauteeéd peppers & onions to go with it! This stew sauce is incredibly and pairs perfect with the jollof and fried rice.  The plantains are perfect.  The Zobo is delicious. 10/10 ⭐️

If you’re a foodie and into delicious flavorful food, go to Mayowa. Your mouth will thank you!

These are tooooooo good! What! Food delivered on time. No stress in ordering and receiving the food. The food was well packaged! The person i spoke to over the phone was very respectful and nice. And to top it off, the jollof rice was great!!! And he gave me a drink as a gift too! OMG! 💯💯💯

formatted_address: 137 Arbor Vitae St, Inglewood, CA 90301, United States
name: Banadir Somali Restaurant

reviews.text: My family and I love coming here whenever we leave the airport. The food is so good and reasonably priced. The tea is delicious. I love it.

I’ve been coming to this place since 2013 and they never disappoint the consistency they’ve been having since then is amazing. Their lamb dish is the best you can have in southern Cali a must try for anyone who likes lamb.

I’m still sitting in the restaurant and had to write this review — it’s that good. The food is absolutely amazing: fresh, flavorful, and perfectly cooked. I ordered the lamb and rice combo, and the lamb was incredibly tender and cooked to perfection.

Service was quick and friendly, and the prices are unbelievable for the portion sizes. One plate could easily feed two people — serious value for your money.

Highly recommend, and I’ll definitely be back!
I don’t understand the hype. The food was decent. Portions were generous, service was good. Overall, it’s an alright spot if you’re in the mood for Somali food, but not a must-visit.

We’re very happy to find a halal restaurant near where we’re staying. This was our first time trying Somalian food. The food taste was delicious and interesting and the portion was generous, easily shareable between two persons. Our dish had lots of beef and very flavorful rice.

The restaurant ambience was also interesting, it felt like going back to 1970-1980.

formatted_address: 909 W Manchester Blvd, Inglewood, CA 90301, United States
name: ADUKE NIGERIAN CUISINE & CATERING SERVICES

reviews.text:
I had the jollof rice and beef suya.
The rice and sauce had good flavor overall, but it was a little bland for me so I took it home and added chicken bouillon and maggi to the rice and red sauce cus I just felt it needed a little extra seasoning. But Everybody has their preferences on saltiness that’s just mine. the flavor was still good on its own.

The beef suya was good it had a good flavor. It was tender even when it got cold. The spices on top were good. And the onions and tomatoes on top worked well together with everything else. I think the portion size for the beef suya could’ve been a little bigger for $15 for that lil bowl. But hey.

I kinda wanted to sit down and eat it but the vibes was not giving sit down and eat it.

Also, the menu they have on the wall must be outdated because the prices are not accurate.
Every price on the menu they had mounted on the walls were about $3 cheaper than what you’re actually charged.

Beef suya on the menu was $12, I was charged $15.
The jollof rice was $7 on the menu, I was charged $10.

So basically,
Everything was OKAY …. besides being charged more than the advertised price….The small beef suya portion And the food needing a lil seasoning.

I would try it again.

The atmosphere and the music running through the restaurant gave me a feeling this place would be good. The server was so nice & made my food really fast !! I haven’t had west African food since living in ghana (3yrs ago), and my meal (egusi & pound yam) tasted just like the motherland !!! Thank you so much for giving me a smooth first timer experience :)

I’ve now visited Aduke Nigerian Cuisine twice and each time has been nothing short of spectacular. This past weekend, I even brought out-of-town friends from Los Angeles who hadn’t had authentic Nigerian food in years, and they left raving about the experience.

Atmosphere & Service
From the moment we stepped inside, the warm, colorful décor and upbeat Afrobeats playlist set the perfect tone. Our server greeted us with genuine smiles and walked us through the menu, patiently answering questions as our table of six debated what to order. The pace of service was spot-on no long waits, but enough time to savor each course.

Food & Flavors
My all-time favorite is their Amala with Ayamase (Ofada stew). The amala was silky and light, and the Ayamase rich, spicy, and packed with tender bits of beef and peppers left me craving seconds. My friends tried the jollof rice (smoky and perfectly seasoned), the pepper-soaked beef suya, and the hearty Egusi soup paired with pounded yam. Every dish was bursting with authentic Nigerian aromatics, made from high-quality imported ingredients.

Menu Variety & Special Diets
Aduke boasts the largest, most diverse Nigerian menu in Los Angeles truly the first of its kind here. They’ve thoughtfully added vegan and vegetarian options (I can’t wait to try their plant-based Egusi next time), so everyone in our party had something delicious to enjoy.

Why It Stands Out
Having sampled nearly every Nigerian spot in town both long-standing and newly opened none compare to Aduke’s commitment to authenticity, flavor, and hospitality. It’s clear they take pride in every detail, from the homemade stews to the freshly baked floor-filling meat pies.

Final Thoughts
If you’re looking for the best Nigerian restaurant in Los Angeles, look no further than Aduke Nigerian Cuisine. Whether you’re a longtime fan of West African flavors or completely new to the cuisine, this place delivers excellence on every level. I can’t recommend it highly enough!

First visit to this restaurant just driving by and decided to see what menu they offered. Mentioned that I wasn't that hungry and wanted something inexpensive and very light. I felt like the cashier had dollar signs in his eyes and got irritated because I didn't want to spend too much money on a meal. So I said nvm, I'll come back when I'm hungry one day for dinner. As I was about to leave I saw that had beef patties and fish rolls which was less expensive. I thought how come he didn't suggest that to me.  So it was obvious he wanted me to spend more money and felt pressured.  I ask if sauce came with the 2 items and he said it would be $10 extra. I said I don't like my food dry and saw I was getting irritated so he gave me some sauce on the side for free. It was like pulling teeth for him to do that. The beef pattie was nothing to write home about and the fish toll wasnt fresh and I trashed it.  I wouldn't come back and definitely wouldn't recommend my friends or family. No good customer service or not friendly and welcoming.

There’s a whole vegan menu with tons of options. They do the tofu really well here, perfectly crispy and generously portioned.

Puff puff: It’s exactly as the menu describes, a fried dough ball. A bit dense so probably wouldn’t get this again.

Tofu suya: Loved this! Deep fried tofu topped with a savory spice mix, so simple and delicious. Texture was perfect, especially when it’s still hot. The standout of the meal.

Jollof rice: Classic side, compliments any other dish perfectly

Amala, gbegiri, and ewedu: First time trying this, it was so flavorful, super yummy. Tomato-based but I’ve never had another stew like it. Slightly gelatinous from the jute leaves. We got the spicy and it was on the spicier side but not too bad. If you’re sensitive to spice stick with regular. Perfect with the amala.

Can’t wait to come back and try more!

formatted_address: 6732 S Crenshaw Blvd #12, Los Angeles, CA 90043, United States
name: Vicky's bubbly cafe

reviews.text:
Vicky’s Bubbly Cafe was amazing! Vicky was so kind and her food is absolutely delicious. We ordered the pounded yam and egusi to go and she went above and beyond to make it vegetarian and allergy-friendly for us.

This was our first time having Nigerian food so she even told us the proper way to eat it and reheat it. The portion sizes are very generous. My new comfort food!

I would recommend to order early as the food is made to order and she can get busy!

Loveee Vicky’s cafe! As a Ghanaian who misses flavors from home, Vicky’s delivers! I first tried the jollof combo and ewedu soup a couple weeks ago and loved it so much I ordered catering for thanksgiving. I ordered a half pan of jollof, which was $40. The amount of jollof in that pan was generous and my friends LOVED the jollof. I also added in an order of egushi which Vicky graciously accommodated last minute. Delicious as well. Run, don’t walk to Vicky’s!

Vicky’s Bubbly Café na real deal! From the moment we walked in, Mrs. Arinze gave us that warm Naija welcome — pure vibes and hospitality! The food? Omo! The efo soup and pounded yam were on another level — rich, flavorful, and made with love like back home. You can taste the authenticity in every bite.

Generous portions, spotless place, and top-notch service — you can tell they cook with passion and heart. If you’re craving proper Nigerian food in LA, this is the spot. No stress, no wahala — just good food and good people. Big ups to Mrs. Arinze and the whole crew! 🇳🇬🔥

I don’t usually write reviews, but the food at Vicky’s Bubbly Cafe was amazing! The jollof, fish, and plantains were all cooked with so much heart — you can taste amazing flavor and love in every bite. The portions were huge too, I even had enough to save for the next day and it was just as good. Thank you for such a beautiful, soulful meal❤️

I'm sorry this took so long but I'm still snacking on what I ordered from here.  This woman cooked Rotini Pasta with Shrimp Scampi and Sauté Southwest mixed Vegetables for me by herself and honestly I wasn't expecting to get as much as I did.  The shrimp pasta was 40 and the veggies were 5.  The pasta could easily feed a family of 4-5 and it is absolutely delicious 😋 I added some Alfredo sauce to it but that's cause I'm a cheese head.  I would've eaten it without the sauce too because it was so good!  SHRIMP IS CLEAN no tails or fish feces!  I will definitely be coming back 🤗
