formatted_address: 16153 Victory Blvd, Van Nuys, CA 91406, United States
name: Springbok Bar & Grill

reviews.text:
Tastes like South Africa at Springbok Bar & Grill. Try the lamb curry or any sandwich; you can’t go wrong. Super fun atmosphere, especially for sporting events. Our server gets an A+.

One minor suggestion is for them to use better water with their coke, as the flavor was off a little.

Pretty cool place.
Service is attentive and polite. Fish and chips were excellent.  Not oily at all like other places. Place is clean.
Great 2nd experience

The service was great, all the waitresses were friendly and attentive.

I loved the dressing on the salad, it’s like a honey mustard vinaigrette.

Fries were average. Burger was under seasoned.

For $20, this was a great portion.

This place has some of the most amazing food.
Our server Cindy was the best. Great attitude and really informed about the menu. I tried the BBQ brisket, fries and a salad.
Friend has the fillet monyin sandwich, fries and salad. Very delicious! I recommend you visit them.
Great food specials, amazing service staff and my favorite place to grab a pint of Guinness.

formatted_address: 524 W Manchester Blvd, Inglewood, CA 90301, United States
name: Veronica's Kitchen - The Fufuland

reviews.text:
I rode the bus for more than 2 hours to get here to try the food, and that is huge for me because I wouldn’t travel that far for food.

I had the warmest welcome by the staff here, and I noticed how kind and courteous they were to every one and not just their own people.

My experience of the food was really good. I had Abula with Goat Meat. “Abula” is the combination of Ewedu, Gbegiri, Tomato Stew, and Amala.
The goat meat was really tender, and the food portion is very large in my opinion (which is very good).

The menu is very simple to navigate, and the eating the food takes one back home to the feeling of eating good food in Nigeria.

I will definitely be visiting this place again anytime I am in its environment.

THE BEST part of this was the lady at the register was very nice.
Otherwise, it was a disaster....

The food was horrible.. I'm sorry, I had sooo many expections about this place, it was suggested to me. I have lived in Cali 3 yrs and I finally got to Inglewood to try this food & I was soooo disappointed.. 🤦🏽‍♀️
The spinach soup tasted & smelled like vomit 🤢
The egusi was edible, but not great. I poured the entire 20.00 container of spinach stew out! No one in my house would eat it, it was sooo bad. We are from Texas & this is one of my family's favorite african dishes.
The fufu was beige color not white; maybe wheat? I dont know but it was ALL NOT GOOD, 60.00 bucks wasted 😔🙄
I ordered Puff Puff, I reminded them to put them in my bag & THEY STILL left it out.

I drove 45 mins to experience Veronica's and I was totally let down..

The food is decent, and I appreciate the hard-working cooks in the back. However, the cashier will be the downfall of this place.

I went yesterday, and she had a huge attitude with me when I wanted to add a side of rice to my order. It was last minute, but instead of simply saying no, she rolled her eyes and acted annoyed, so I changed my mind.

Later, there were customers eating together. The cashier accidentally overcharged one of them and gave her less change. When the customer pointed it out, the receptionist gave her attitude again. Shortly after, a man who was with the group asked for napkins. She grabbed a bottle of napkins and basically slammed them on the opposite side of the counter, forcing him to walk over and get them. He asked her why she did that when he was standing right there. The customer told her she needed to be more cheerful and that her behavior was extremely rude.

I definitely won’t be coming back here.

I was hesitant to try this place based on the reviews. You will see a mix of 1 to 4 stars. However, we were pleasantly surprised with everything. The food was great! Two of us ordered efo riro (I had fish, the other goat) and it was great. Tasted good and the portion size was great! It came out hot and we were happy. Our friend ordered pepper soup which was also good. The wait for the food wasn't short and also not extremely long.

For the price, we thought the quantities were great! The woman taking care of orders was also kind. Out of many Nigerian places we've tried, this one of the best ones.

We will be back and would recommend as well.

Like many other reviewers, I had heard positive things about this restaurant. However, I had to wait a half hour (15% tip was mandatory) for my egusi, which was actually quite disappointing. It was greasy and unhealthy

formatted_address: 1423 W Pico Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90015, United States
name: Jagabans LA

reviews.text: This is hands down the best food I have ever eaten in my entire life. Every single bite was packed with incredible flavor, and you can tell so much care and passion goes into the cooking. The quality of the ingredients, the taste, and the overall experience were absolutely unforgettable. I honestly can’t stop thinking about this meal. If you’re even considering eating here, do it!!!

Amazing service— despite us being vegetarian, they offered us substitute dishes. Some of the vegetarian soups contained crayfish, but they were kind enough to offer us sauce and fufu instead! The jollof rice was the perfect texture and so flavorful. The plantains, pasta, and sauce were delicious as well. 10/10

A friend and I were visiting LA and we both really wanted to try the iconic Egusi with fufu. We ordered the goat for our protein and we were soooooo impressed with the dish when it came out! The flavors were so well balanced with a little spice to it and it was just phenomenal! I definitely recommend trying this place out! Another plus, the staff was so friendly and service was quick!

Cozy restaurant that can fit no more than 13-14 people at a time. Went there twice! First time I had the goat meat pepper soup which was spicy and delicious but wasn’t a lot of meat. The GOAT meat Suya was delicious! The next time I came I tried the cat fish pepper soup, it wasn’t good! The owner is pleasant and personable. However the first time I came the server was slow and wasn’t paying attention. The second time the service was more attentive. It took too long for food to come out. The drinks were fine, I had the zobo. The zobo was made in house. They should always have ice cream for the puff puff. Which they didn’t have when I arrived. It’s a new restaurant so, I’m excited to see what they will do next. Oh there is street parking.

I can’t stop ordering food from here, it’s just that good! The beans and plantain taste amazing, perfectly cooked and full of flavor. The goat stew is rich, tender, and seasoned so well that it ties everything together beautifully. Every time I eat here, it tastes just as good as the first time. Definitely one of my favorite spots!

formatted_address: 14115 Crenshaw Blvd, Hawthorne, CA 90250, United States
name: Mother African Cuisine

reviews.text:
Recently, I had a great dining experience at a local restaurant. The atmosphere was warm and inviting, with friendly staff who made me feel welcome right away.

I ordered roasted fish and fried ripe plantains, and the meal was absolutely delicious. The fish was perfectly seasoned and tender, with a smoky flavor that showed it was freshly prepared. The fried ripe plantains were golden brown, sweet, and crispy on the outside—just the way I like them.

The food was served hot and beautifully arranged, and the service was quick and attentive. I really enjoyed the entire experience and left the restaurant feeling satisfied and happy. I would definitely love to visit again.

Excellent cuisine, she cooked for my family and I all through my pregnancy. Lizzy is very kind, will give me different meals not included in my orders, to try just in case I could tolerate. I am forever grateful for your  kindness, warmth, for always going above and beyond. I would give a 1000 stars if I could. Guys go try her meals you would love all, she is the best African cuisine in Los Angeles. God's blessings always.

Tasty, ethnic one of a kind! Delicious, healthy varieties from finger-foods, picnic food, party, food, and heavy duty catering you get the best from Mother African cuisine. She is creative, innovative and presents her food with elegance. Food display that tickles the palate before it hits the taste buds. I fill my freezers with her delicacies so I never run out. I’ll refer her any time.
The best of Africa dishes. I buy here most at times and I strongly recommend it for everyone.

Mother African Cuisine delivered an outstanding dining experience. the From warm welcome to the rich, culturally inspired ambiance, everything set the perfect tone. The service was attentive, and the food was full of authentic flavors. A must visit spot, I’ll definitely be back!

formatted_address: 5990 1/2 W Pico Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90035, United States
name: Awash

reviews.text: Haven't had much experience with Ethiopian food and didn't really like it the last time I had it. However, really enjoyed their veggie platter! Also note the portion sizes are quite generous

Awash is a true gem for authentic Ethiopian cuisine. The food tastes like it comes straight from a family kitchen, full of warmth, tradition, and fresh, high-quality ingredients. Every dish is seasoned beautifully, the injera is soft and delicious, and you can taste the love and care in every plate.

The restaurant has a cozy mom and pop feel, the kind of place where you instantly feel welcome. It is usually just one person serving, so patience is required, which is completely understandable. The service is genuine, kind, and attentive, and you can tell they take pride in what they do.

If you’re looking for fresh, flavorful, truly authentic Ethiopian food, Awash is the place to go. I will definitely be returning.

Thank You for My First Ever Ethiopian Cuisine Experience at Awash!
🎍The texture of the bread was divine!! I’ve imagined what it’s like but Awash delivered it even better than what I expected. I learned that the Injera bread is made from Teflon flour and each piece is likely 75-100 calories, so guilt free!!!
🥬 The veggitable platter had 7 different kinds on and each of them has a unique flavor and texture. The beef was tasty and soft. Portion was grandiose!
💁‍♀️ The staff there are very nice and helpful.
Thank you Awash for this unforgettable experience!

The street was quite calm in the evening, with few people in sight. However, upon entering the restaurant, we found it to be filled with diners. Although the wait for the food took a while, the flavors turned out to be really enjoyable. It was my first experience with Ethiopian cuisine, and I found it to be quite satisfying.
Really nice food and big portion too. Kuku is really nice lady and gives Habesha mother vibes!

formatted_address: 1036 1/2 S Fairfax Avenue, 1036 S Fairfax Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90019, United States
name: Merkato

reviews.text: If you like Ethiopian food or you want to give it a try. Don't be shy because it is a total experience.  The food is really good along with atmosphere in the restaurant.  It kinda makes you feel like you're in Ethiopia by the decor. They also have a little store connected to it. There you can buy all types of Ethiopian products, from jewelry, spices and clothing.  It's a win, win situation.  It is in the heart of Little Ethiopia 🇪🇹 on Fairfax between Pico and Olympic. Be bold give it a try, you'll love it.

Went to this place bc I am a fan of the movie series insecure but after visiting, food is bland. Not worth making a stop. Should have went to the restaurant next door, had a bigger crowd. Next time I will look into it and not follow bc of a show.

This was my first time trying Ethiopian food and I was genuinely looking forward to the experience. The food itself was good, but unfortunately the service was extremely disappointing and completely overshadowed the meal. There was only one server working the entire restaurant. While the restaurant is on the smaller side, our group was fairly large, and there was absolutely no sense of urgency or attentiveness. Even something as basic as getting water took a very long time. The server never once checked on our table, we had to actively look for her anytime we needed something. I understand she may have been overwhelmed, as she appeared to be doing everything : seating guests, bussing tables, packing takeout orders, and delivering food. That said, the lack of friendliness and hospitality made us feel very unwelcome. The server often had an expression that made it seem like she wanted us gone, which only added to the uncomfortable experience. I don’t know if this is a cultural difference or simply poor service, but it was not enjoyable.
This place clearly has a loyal customer base and many great reviews, which makes this experience even more disappointing. I truly wish I had the same experience others seem to have had, but I left feeling very underwhelmed and unwelcome. I will not be returning. One last thing to note! If you plan to pay with a card, be aware that there is a hefty fee. We were charged $13 for using a card.. almost 4% of our bill, which was over $300. That seems excessive, and I’m not even sure if it’s legal. Overall, good food, but the service needs serious improvement.

I rarely leave negative reviews, but this experience was serious enough that I feel obligated to warn others.

We visited this restaurant as a family of 4 adults and 3 children while traveling in California. We ordered a veggie combo, tsome firfir, and timatim fitfit. When the food arrived, it was immediately obvious that something was wrong. The gomen had a strong, unpleasant smell, to the point that we could literally tell it had gone bad before even tasting it.

We brought this to our server’s attention right away. Instead of apologizing or addressing the issue, she simply walked away without saying a word. No concern, no explanation, no attempt to replace the food or check on us. The lack of professionalism and basic customer service was shocking.

Unfortunately, the situation didn’t end there. That same night and the following day, multiple members of our family became sick, including the children, who were vomiting throughout the day. What was supposed to be a day of enjoying our visit to California turned into a miserable experience spent sick in our accommodations.

We attempted to handle this responsibly by calling the restaurant to speak with the owner. The first time we called, we were told the owner was “busy” and to call back at 9 PM. When we called again at the requested time, we were once more told that he was busy and couldn’t come to the phone. At that point, it was clear that there was no interest in addressing this matter or taking responsibility.

Between the spoiled food, dismissive service, and complete lack of accountability, this was one of the worst dining experiences we’ve ever had. Food safety should never be taken lightly—especially when families and children are involved.

I truly wish this could have been resolved directly, but after being ignored multiple times, I was left with no choice but to leave this review.

I'm giving one star because the Uber Eats order was put in a DoorDash bag, and because of the attitude of the woman with curly hair. Drivers represent the company, so I'm giving this one star on behalf of the customer. They don't even deserve one star.

formatted_address: 2717 W Manchester Blvd, Inglewood, CA 90305, United States
name: Nkechi African Cafe

reviews.text:
Wanted some Egusi soup so bad.
So I decided try this place that was recommended by my Uber driver.

Even though I am not African, I love African food .

I was soooo disappointed! The tasted of the soup just wasn't good. Tasted more salt then the flavor of authentic African seasonings.

One good thing I can say, the meat was tender, but seems as if they cooked the meat in boiling water and them just added it to the soup.

The fufu didn't taste like pounded yam, but more like box instead mash potatoes.
Verioncia's Kitchen is still my No.1  place for Egusi soup y'all.

I wanted to try African food for the first time and went into this place. The woman and man was arguing so loud. I spent nearly $40 on the meal. It was so disgusting , tasted like a burnt pot as well. Sooooooooo gross! They ruined my first experience. But I am in no way going to judge African foods based on this experience I just will
Never spend my money here again. And there were kids all around and the smell was terrible

The food was not as good. Whoever served us was in a foul mood serving us like he was doing us a favour and I also have no problem with children, I love kids but one should babysit in a cafe, the children were running all over screaming.
The meat was old. Not fresh. Not Worth $25 plus charged 4% to use card. I bought Jollof rice and goat/beef with plantain.
The customer service was amazing. She answered all my questions. The food was fresh and delicious. My kids who are picky eaters and have never eaten Nigerian food, ate it with no complaint!

formatted_address: 1034 S Fairfax Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90019, United States
name: Buna Ethiopian Restaurant & Market

reviews.text:
Loved the experience.
The food is amazing
Always go to little Ethiopia when I can.
Love the food.
Forgot to take picture of the dessert, but baklava and tiramisu where very tasty, they have the strong punch of Ethiopian food.

This is truly a hidden gem. We tried it based on the reviews, and wow was it ever worth it. Small almost hidden place but wonderful service and outstanding food. Our server made incredible recommendations. The coffee was so outstanding I bought a bag to go. Fabulous Tiramisu. This is great food, but it’s not fast, so don’t go starving. But it is so very much worth the wait. Can’t wait to go back! It’s a new must visit when I’m in LA for sure!

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Buna is an amazing family-owned restaurant with great vegetarian and meat options. The service is 10 stars and always so friendly! My friends and I love it here and come at least twice a week.

Buna is absolutely excellent. The food is authentic and delicious with really good vegetarian and meat options. I love the veggie combo, and the meat combo. The Kitfo is my favorite, and the Tibs options are tender and seasoned to perfection. The delightful flavor of the food, the intimate setting, and the outstanding service always makes me feel like I'm family, which is why I keep going back with friends and they can't get enough. We always end up ordering more food to go. Eyob and his wife Helina are truly wonderful people. Also, don't forget to try the tiramisu with proper Ethiopian coffee or superb macchiato. You will leave genuinely satisfied and wanting to return with friends sooner than later.
One of the best restaurants with a great menu, the best chefs, and the best hospitality with the biggest hearts! You will not be disappointed my favorite is the chechebsa #3 breakfast special

formatted_address: 21044 Sherman Way #100, Canoga Park, CA 91303, United States
name: Jaliz Cuisine of East Africa

reviews.text: Great way to try something new. Their tasty food is very healthy and fresh Go to the back of the house to order, or You can call to order as well
Phenomenal food with a friendly family wanting to share their delicious food with the world. Highly recommended!

I love this place, I drive for hours just to get some Ugandan food. The owner is so kind and welcoming, the food is delicious and tasteful. The smell of the goat stew will make you smile, the yams are so good you won’t stop eating.

I love this place. Been there quite a few times before. I love the food here. Original Ugandan food. Dinning arrangements in the back available but not conventional seating arrangements.  I love the ambience--- "wild" and "different'. Under tents like a living room set up or under the tree. Their meat is fresh and organic, specially the chicken. They don't use the regular frozen chicken. Hand slaughtered and fresh..... exceptional taste!! Rice with chicken, baked plantain, peanut sauce, chicken curry, fish, beans, bbq (order in advance) ---all Ugandan style. Go to the back of the house to order for dine in or carry-out. If you are open to experience something new, visit this  place (dine in), but if you are "picky person" go somewhere else!!

It doesn't make sense how something can taste sooo good. I hadn't had Ugandan food in over a year but oh my.. we found this little gem with the help of Google. The reviews done even do this place justice. The food was soooooo delicious. Had goat meat and chicken stew.l with matooke. Was worth the trip. And the hospitality of the owner was even a bonus. We will ve back when in LA

formatted_address: 4952 W Century Blvd, Inglewood, CA 90304, United States
name: Royal Cuisine Authentic African & American Food

reviews.text: Second time I was there, first time ordered multiple dishes. I liked the experience

Absolutely delicious!! We're visiting the area and decided to stop here for a meal and I'm so glad we did! The waakye is flavor packed. The goat meat was tender and delicious.. The shito has a nice hot kick to it.. TZ was also on point!

I went there 4 goat meat and jollof rice and what I got was nasty beef with lots of fat because he messed up my order. So I ordered goat meat to go with no meat  egosi...he messed up again and put my meat in the egosi. Got home and discovered he gave me beef fat and not goat meat like I ordered. Nice decor. The rice was good. But it took so long to service our food.  And if you order goat meat they won't give it to you! So disappointed!

The atmosphere was really amazing and welcoming the very moment I got there,

Aside the fact that the food(jollof) I ordered took a bit longer than I expected the wait was definitely worth it. Definitely a an amazing place to experience

My first time here I was in the area so why not. I have to say the food was authentic, flavorful and plentiful. Both Jane and Beatrice were inviting and professional. Wouldn't mind visiting again when in town.
Thank You

Came again on 10/31/2024

Clean establishment, fair prices, quality food, good portions and attentive staff. I personally could have used more spice in my soup. But I understand they accommodate to the multitude.

Mike- smile more 😁

formatted_address: 1041 S Fairfax Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90019, United States
name: Messob Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: The service was exceptional, the food was prepared perfectly and the whole spread was delicious!!! We did our best to clear the plate, sharing a two person meal between three and it was plenty. I will definitely return and highly recommend Messob for Ethiopian cuisine while you’re in Los Angeles.

Was there with one other person. We ordered and shared the doro wot and a lamb dish. Both were fantastic and served over injera, making it very easy to share. Portions were very reasonable. I felt full but we did not have any leftovers. It took a couple minutes for us to be seated, but we showed up at an odd time and I don't hold that against them (We were the only ones in the restaurant when we showed up). Would highly recommend and would go back if we are in the area.

We came 222 Messob for a late dinner. They could have denied us service as we arrived at 9:35pm and they closed at 10pm, but they didn’t. They welcomed us into the most culturally rich & warm environment where they would serve us delicious cuisine! Our experience was so lovely start to finish. We really appreciated that the menu was thorough in description of the dishes & the dining etiquette. Our food was perfectly nourishing & so tasty. We celebrated my cousin’s birthday & it was his first time having Ethiopian food. he hardly said much and remained focused on eating his meal, but he was definitely smiling in awe at his experience the entire time. Thank you 222 all the wonderful women that provided great service and made sure we were enjoying our dinner. What a pleasure!

I was very upset coming here 😒 we ordered samosa and they served every one before us that came after us the cost of 2 tej was $24 and the food portion is very small 😑 and we wanted to leave and only pay for the drinks the lady wouldn't let us. The guy owner does favoritism for the people he knows 🙄 and neglects his other customers. Very unprofessional Ethiopian house. They got are stuff wrong still didn't offer any discounts other places to go around there don't waste your time here. Ty

The food was DELICIOUS! The serving sizes were generous , we ordered 3 meals for our family of 4 where everyone walked out full and happy. The room is beautifully decorated and has a nice atmosphere. Definitely coming back again tomorrow. One of good memories from LA 😊

formatted_address: 6775 Selma Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90028, United States
name: ILE LA Supper Club and Caterers

reviews.text: David was an absolutely incredible host, storyteller, and educator! My partner and I had the most fulfilling, entertaining, and FILLING experience during our intimate dinner. Sharing stories, learning about West African food and culture, laughing and connecting across a table of beautiful and immensely flavorful and exciting food — it’s everything we could ever want in a dining experience! The joining of homes while also creating a pocket of home unique to the evening we shared. We had a blast and highly recommend David and the ILE team for a one of a kind experience! and shoutout to sous chef Jeffrey! We voted for puff puff to stay on the menu so hopefully there’s less baking in your future 😂 thank you guys again for a wonderful evening, we’ll run it back again soon! 🫶🏼

Let me start off by saying the food was delicious. However, for the price you can get just as superb food with much better atmosphere and service. I would not recommend this place.

They only provided water even though they promised a nonalcoholic cocktail that we were told we could bring spirits to mix into. Upon asking at the end of the meal, their excuse was that the head chef was out. So they could make an entire meal without the head chef but not a premixed cocktail? We ended up taking shots of our tequila instead of having a cocktail to mix it into. They could’ve even just offered some juice concoction instead of literally nothing.

The food was good but does not look like the pictures shown. It is family style so piles of food are served on platters. That’s fine, but the photos here are extremely misleading.

The experience was a bit unorganized and not optimized. There was a host fiddling trying to play videos on an iPad before the course was served but the audio was poor (in an echoey concrete loft) and the screen was tiny. Would’ve just preferred an intimate setting where they explained the food instead of trying to achieve (and missing the mark on) theater. Then the chefs were late serving food so on the last course the host basically rushed us out so their next seating could come in, so we scarfed down our dessert then had to catch up with friends outside in the cold instead of over the promised cocktail.

The space was small but I expected a smaller table for an intimate setting instead of two huge tables squeezed into as much space as possible, maximizing profits but leaving no logistical room to get to the bathroom or for the servers to remove plates except reaching through other seated patrons.

Ultimately I’m giving 2 stars for the taste of the food but for the price I paid, I left feeling let down and would not recommend. Better to spend your money at a fine dining establishment for better marks on everything all around.

I’ll start with WOW! This is experience was magical from start to finish. A dance with culture and food. Filled with great energy and people. I’d recommend it to anyone looking to experience a new level of taste. Chef Eros has brought his Nigerian roots to Los Angeles and his passion for food is definitely well received from every bite. I loved the family style dining experience and being able to connect with some new creatives. I can’t wait to experience it again. Thank you for having me.

This was such a magical night. The courses followed a beautiful love story, so we eagerly awaited each plate and the story that went with it. The presentation was incredible. The service was perfection and fun. Hats off to the chef because it couldn’t have been a better experience. I honestly can’t pick a favorite course because each was so delicious with many layers of flavor.
If you enjoy Nigerian food, get ready to reimagine your favorite dishes. Nom nom! Thanks Chef Eros and team!

Chef Eros gave us such an amazing experience! The ambience, the food, his stories… One word, AMAZING!
Would definitely recommend.

formatted_address: 242 N Ave 25, Los Angeles, CA 90031, United States
name: Jollof & Wollof Kitchen

reviews.text: Delivery order: I ate all of my peanut butter stew! It was good and comforting. Not salty but savory.  It does come in small Togo plate though but no complaints for that. I also had the Wollof rice with chicken. The chicken was slightly overcooked and needed more seasoning . The Wollof rice was good , but needed a side of plantain.

The reviews are REAL! I’m so glad me and my husband found this spot not too far from DTLA. Everything was delicious. The drinks are amazing! Try the Hibiscus. Sorry for sharing this photo of the food already demolished but I forgot to do it before eating. This is the best African food I’ve had since I’ve been in LA. We will be back!

I longed for authentic Senegambian food for the longest and couldn’t be happier with this place. The food is amazing! Flavorful, balanced and filling. You really get your money’s worth! The service was great too!

Wow - as a French-Beninese craving west African food in LA, I’m so glad I found Jollof & Wollof! I just tried their food for the first time and it was exquisite. I ordered a good amount for my team and everyone loved it. Will order soon! Thank you again!
(Tchieb, plantain & akkaras)

The best food on this side of Heaven! My first time having Okra Soup and fufu!! I wish we had more! I would definitely recommending catering for a family meal or special occasion. Excellent customer service!

formatted_address: 1025 S Fairfax Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90019, United States
name: Lalibela

reviews.text:
It was great!
Seems like a to-go heavy location as the dining room for lunch was very open.  Muna took good care of us.  Helped with recommendations and is very nice.

It does seem light on staff so be patient while waiting to be seated, maybe all hands on deck in kitchen for packing.

Very clean and pretty bathroom!  Free 2hr Parking is plentiful a block away.  The decor feels authentic and atmospheric if a little worn but very appropriate and good.

A very fun and mellow adventure.
An excellent option if you are looking for traditional Ethiopian food. Their shakes of mango and avocado are great!
Slow service, but the food is absolutely delicious. If you’re with a great group of friends or family, the time will pass quickly and you won’t even mind the wait. Highly recommend!

Delicious & beautiful sampler platter  served in such a welcome setting with lovely crisp table cloths. The place was nice and clean and service was wonderful with an attentive lady who came to explain the selections to us. First visit for my elderly mom who loved it!

Great food and atmosphere!
Service is on slow side because under staffed but doesn’t bother me much.
I always order meat combo #2 and vegi combo with fish (fried rainbow trout).

Pro tip:
If you like honey wine, go to grocery across the street. They sell injera, spices and honey wines too. Bring some home!

update 2025 Sunner
Taste of Lalibera $70 is very very very small portion for the price. Order regular one kind dish or other meat combo instead. I really don’t understand how they decide the portion for each menu but it wasn’t worth it and very disappointed.
Do they serve more if you say individual plate instead of serve all order in one plate? Every tine I go it’s so random 😔 How can I make sure we get enough food for the group? Apparently paying double doesn’t mean double the size 👎

Total spend $220

formatted_address: 14115 Crenshaw Blvd, Hawthorne, CA 90250, United States
name: Da PoinT Lounge

reviews.text: Love eating here and take out but my only problem with them is that their number never goes through always voicemail whenever I try to order. Please update your phone number
The food is the Business!! Staff is great very knowledgeable about the food!! Very important.

I felt like having some African food so I Google restaurant near me and this restaurant had a 5 star. My husband and I went there for dinner. On arrival we were greeted by a nice young man at the desk . This restaurant is actually a Lounge with over 7 big screen television for your viewing pleasure.  The music,  the vibe, the atmosphere was on point. We both met the owner and he literally had drinks with us so friendly. We ordered Goat Stew, Beef Stew, Jollof Rice , Fried Plantains paired wirh Palm Wine and Guiness Stout. Guys my palate experienced an Orgasmic explosion of all different Flavors and taste. The Goat and beef stew was so tender the Rice we took a small portion home and I literally ate every grain. Honestly I wanted to order extra plates to go. My husband is a renowned CHEF we are Jamaicans  I know all about good food with proper seasoning, spices and flavors. Will we return  most definitely will this place is a hidden gem that we will continue to Explore in the future.

Great food! Great atmosphere!
My go to spot to catch a nice vibe!

The is a place I would take anyone for good taste, customer  service  fresh food, I taste Nigeria food but this is fresh everything these people are Amazing thanks for me having comfort me an my family Enjoyed!!!!

formatted_address: 901 S Prairie Ave, Inglewood, CA 90301, United States
name: Nkwagala Concept

reviews.text: Drop everything and go eat at Nkwagala Concept! 😋 OK but seriously, plant eaters, meat eaters, everyone.... this is some of the best food I've had in my whole life! The flavors are mind-blowing. Like a homemade meal and the best restaurant food come together. I drove 30 mins to get it because sadly I do not live close. My faves: James Brown Salad and the Egusi! I actually ordered extra and froze it 🤣 Everything is delicious and I can't believe we don't have more amazing food like this. I've attached a bunch of photos, they are the JB salad, the Egusi, the Biko Soup and the Katogo (🤤). My preference is to eat it with rice instead of the fufu, but I know many people enjoy the fufu, I just find the flavors are yummier with rice (or just alone). Please support this restaurant instead of all those chains, one because they deserve it! and two so I can keep eating here! Thanks SO much Nkwagala, I'll be back sooooon. 😁

The food was absolutely delicious and the portions quite large! The husband and wife operate this place, were kind, patient and understanding as they took time to explain what their food was all about. These two take healthy eating to the level we all deserve… Wholesome, delicious food that doesn’t break the bank. My first order will not be my last and I suggest this place to anyone who cares about what they eat and where it comes from.

I was lucky to stumble across this gem. The food was amazing and Diverse I had the okra soup, It was delicious being Nigerian I had very high standards and they rose to the challenge. The okra stew was fresh and flavorful I had the foo foo made of oat, which gave it a light sweet/oatmeal taste that complements of the soup. I have buttermilk squash on the side which was a great addition to my meal it was like eating sweet potatoes but not as sweet or greasy. I followed up with her personal lemonade which was very refreshing. The meal was very filling and I look forward to trying everything in the menu

My experience here was very beautiful & I am so moved by the energy, hospitality, and souls that catered to my first time being here. The lady on the phone was very kind and inviting. I got lost while trying to find the building. Her voice and aura spoke a thousand words before I was able to place my order and meet the gentleman that came down just to make sure I was able to have my order taken. I ordered the Mac wings with cucumbers and the oh La la egusi soup. This was my first time trying Nigerian dishes and i really enjoyed the palette journey. I started with the wings & indulged in the cucumbers. I absolutely felt the love in everything that I ate.  I’m a big fan of going to restaurants that serve beautiful energy that washes over you to the point where you have a miniature awakening in the process. I’ve only encountered this once in my life from cooking outside of my own. This would be the second! Amazing job! I’ll see you again soon!
~Ja’Leezia

Wow...that's the first word i said when I tried their food...it was super yummy! My husband and I ordered the Egusi soup, fufu, pepperoni pizza, and chow mein. All amazing, high quality, and flavorful. We will be back for more. I highly recommend them for catering, meal prep, or even a day when you just want to eat oit but still feel healthy. We did their delivery service before and they packaged the food so neatly and it was still flavorful and high quality. They vacuum seal the food so no spillage. We will order when we go traveling since were alkaline vegan and its hard to find restaurants that cater to our diet. But we can always trust Nkwagala.

formatted_address: 7445 1/2 Sunset Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90046, United States
name: Moun Of Tunis Restaurant

reviews.text:
Wow this spot was a pleasant surprise we stumbled upon. I’ve been passing by this restaurant for years wondering about it and we finally made a visit. This is definitely one of my top dining experiences in LA for the atmosphere, service, food, and overall uniqueness.

Everything is a set menu with set price which make ordering so much easier. We ordered the Moroccan Feast for the 4 of us and after tax and tip came to around $60 a person which honestly is worth because this is a feast! And we enjoyed a belly dancing show that we got to participate in. This was so much and honestly helped with the digestion haha.

I cannot wait to come back with a group. It’s a very cozy spot and so welcoming more you’re in. Very much feels like a little getaway from LA once you’re inside.

EXPERIENCE. Period. What a time. First off owner was EXTREMELY kind. Sat down and walked us through our meal and Informed us how it worked. So even if you don’t know, the will help you!

Sadly no loners, find a friend or someone cause the meals are to be shared. No individuals.

I’m vegetarian and my fiancé eats meat. We got two veggie meals and they added chicken for her. I got a moroccan beer and she got wine.

The hummus came out with a side of pickled veggies and the waiter brought us a chili sauce. AMAZING and it just started.
We then got served each a Brik and a side of lentil soup. WHAT this was deep fried, crispy, and flavorful. Had a mixture of egg and potato inside. legit died when I added the hot sauce to the Brik. If there wasn’t 3 more courses coming I would have eaten at least 4 😭

We were then given fresh bread and mix salad dish. Very fresh and flavorful. The bread was still steamin when we opened it. The dish was so yummy we ate all the bread before the main dish came out. The couscous with vegetables was very flavorful, warm, and comforting. My finance really enjoyed it paired with her chicken kabob.

During our dinner a belly dance also appeared and put on a show. Very beautiful and great dancer! The music, performance, food, and overall atmosphere was amazing!

I absolutely recommend this place for a date nite or a celebratory dinner ⭐️

I had an amazing dining experience at this restaurant. Paul, our server, was exceptionally attentive and offered fantastic recommendations. We went with the Moroccan Feast, and every single dish was absolutely delicious—I adored it all! The atmosphere was cozy and intimate, especially since we had the entire place to ourselves on a quiet Sunday night. The hot tea was delightful. Parking was surprisingly easy, which made the evening even better. Highly recommend this spot for a delightful and stress-free night out!

Was in the area visiting and wanted Moroccan food so we stopped at this place. The whole experience was just incredible. The waiter was very hospitable and accommodating to our needs. The service is superb and being someone from North African descent, I have to vouch for the amazing authentic dishes. From appetizer to dessert, everything was delicious. The food is well done, the spices are amazing and everything just went together just right. Fresh green tea like my mom's and dessert like my aunt's....just mouth watering. This place is a hidden jewel. If you are looking for a unique different experience with amazing food, this place is for you.

Absolutely the best experience ever. This place is a gem operating for 40+ yrs.First, you wash your hands with rose water at your table, smells fabulous. We ordered the Moroccan Feast. This place and the food are gorgeous. Make sure you pace yourself because it is a lot of delicious food. If you come on a weekday with a group, make sure to call before 4pm if you want the belly dancing.  Parking is easy and free (hard to find in Hollywood). My pictures don't make any justice, the flavor and the experience can't be capture in the pictures. You have to come and experience it yourself.

formatted_address: 1044 S Fairfax Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90019, United States
name: Rosalind's

reviews.text:
I’ve been to Rosalind’s a few times now and every time I think the food tastes better and better. The vegan goodness is great for two people to get to try a bunch of the dishes. I also opted for the sampler 3 this past time and loved it!

Every time I’ve visited Rosalind’s I’ve been seated right away and the food came out really quickly. I really love the woman who is always working. She is so kind and I enjoy talking to her when they aren’t too busy.

I absolutely recommend and will be back often. Plus it’s an easy walk to LACMA and The Academy Museum so it’s a perfect spot to go to before an exhibit.

The food is flavorful and leaves your taste buds wanting more. They have a Vegan Goodness plate that is filling. I would recommend adding an order of Sambosas. The service was good, but the parking is limited. You got to jump on the first opening you find, even if the restaurant is half a block away.

We went during an off hour for a late lunch.  There was nobody in there except for one lady staring vacantly out the window. She looked rather put off that we went in and wanted to eat. She was grumpy and unfriendly. But aside from her the food was good. And even though it doesn’t look like a lot the two of us had leftovers. We’ll still go back.
Tip: bring cash for a tip because she asked for that.

Got the emperor which had 5 meat dishes, 6 vegan dishes and salad. None of the meat dishes stood out. However the vegan dishes were excellent. Injera was pretty good too. Service was slow and standoffish.

Update: Went on a weekday. Service was definitely better(service updated to 3 stars). The beef sambusa is amazing. The awaze tibs was pretty good too. The plantains are also pretty good. They provide plenty of injera with your meal.

We’ve been there pre Covid and it was very good. Really worried this restaurant couldn’t make it during Covid. And we are so glad it’s still open and serves very nice food. They have outdoor seating under patio. The menu is big enough and there are many options, you can choose meat/protein, vegan, sampler plate or signature dishes. The food is incredibly delicious and big. The Ethiopian flat bread is so unique and tasty. We couldn’t stop eating it. We had the appetizer and two main entrees. And it’s absolutely enough for two people. You should try the lamb stew. Perfectly good. The service is flawless. We definitely will visit there again.

formatted_address: 15355 Sherman Way Ste L, Van Nuys, CA 91406, United States
name: totos' African Cuisine

reviews.text: I don’t know what it is about Africans and Caribbean’s opening up businesses in LA, and not staying true to their authenticity. There was literally nothing jollof about the rice, no flavor/no pepper, no seasoning. The goat was tender, but definitely not the flavor profiles that I was looking for. I also ordered a meat pie that was as consistent as the other dishes. Overall disappointing. Sorry💔

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️☆

The egusi soup was absolutely delicious — rich, flavorful, and perfectly seasoned with just the right blend of spices. Every bite was comforting and full of authentic taste that made me want more. The only downside (and the reason it’s not a 5-star review) is the portion size. For the price, I expected a bit more — it was gone way too fast! Still, the flavor alone makes it worth trying again. Would definitely stop by again to try other dishes.

When you don't have a device, then you get no food. This location wants its customers to forcefully
use their own device to order. The owner of this restaurant has no care for its customers. It doesn't offer a menu with pictures of the foods as well as the ingredients.

The food was absolutely delicious! The red stew was sweet, savory and just the right amount of spicy. (Which was on the vegan menu, came with the side of fufu.) Fufu was nice and sticky, hand pounded yam. Plaintains came as a side item, very caramelized rich and sweet with a beautiful consistency, perfectly ripe.
If you want a full meal with Okra and fufu it is around $20, but this is authentic and yummy. Delicious and unique flavors. Will definitely try again.

This place is so good! The owners were incredibly friendly and accommodating. I got the fufu and eggusi soup with friend plantains. Everything was delicious. & they were really fast. My food was ready super quick. 10/10. Idk what the reviews are talking about, must be grumpy people reviewing or just an off day. This place is great

formatted_address: 1053 S Fairfax Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90019, United States
name: Meals By Genet

reviews.text: The food is delicious, top quality! If you go alone, keep in mind that you’ll get much more on your plate than you can finish. You’ll definitely end up taking some home!

I had the pleasure of dining here during a trip to LA and I would just about hop on a plane just to dine here again. The ambiance is that of intimate minimalism, which I found inviting from the very first second. Although the menu may be a bit more limited than other places on the same street, the dishes they do are executed exquisitely. I most definitely would recommend checking this spot out.

A friend recommended Meals by Genet and the experience was even better than they said! The food was absolutely incredible - the kind of meal you can’t explain to someone, they just have to try it for themselves. Chef Genet said hello to almost every table there. And our servers were outstanding!

So happy to read that Genet came back to serve meals at her restaurant Fri-Sun, it is an eating experience you will not forget.  My kids tried foods they would not normally have tried and of course loved eating with injera.  You need reservations, take your waiter's suggestions on what to eat, it doesn't require much research prior to going.

Wonderful place for vegetarian and people with GF restrictions.  Afterwards, Genet herself came out to check on how everyone had liked the meal, what a blessing it is to have her still cooking.

Meals by Genet is, without a doubt, my top recommendation for anyone seeking a truly unique and unforgettable dining experience in Los Angeles. This isn’t just a meal; it’s a culinary journey that rivals my best experiences from Napa to New York.

The food here is elevated to an extraordinary level offering an authentic taste of Ethiopia infused with love and warmth.

My go-to order? The Ethiopian tofu tips in homemade butter. It’s pure magic—simple, yet so profoundly flavorful. While the DoroWot often gets the spotlight (deservedly so), insiders know the tofu tips are where simplicity truly outshines. Pair it with an Ethiopian beer to start, and follow up with a dry Sauvignon Blanc for a great pairing.

Genet, the heart and soul of this establishment, is a gem. Dining here feels like being welcomed into her home, where she masterfully guides you through the rich and vibrant flavors of Ethiopian cuisine. It’s no wonder the late, great Jonathan Gold praised this place as one of the best he’d ever experienced.

This is my go to answer on if you had the choice for your one last meal. Thank you Genet.

formatted_address: 1909 Atlantic Ave, Long Beach, CA 90806, United States
name: Omalicious African Restaurant

reviews.text: This was my very first time having any type of African Cuisine. I got the Fufu combo with spicy beef Egusi soup. Food was delicious, did not disappoint. The lady at the front greeted me upon entering and I ordered my food. Was in and out in under 15 minutes, very fast and friendly. Will be returning!

First time here & trying Nigerian food. I didn't know what was what, plus eating vegan, but the lady there answered all my questions. All i got this time was jollof rice & fried plantains. Plantains were cooked perfectly, not too sweet or juicy & sticky ( I went at em soon as i got in the car). The rice was good to, good flavor, and the lady made sure I liked spicy before spicing up my rice. Looking at the menu & goggling the dishes, I will try the Egosi (made with ground melon seed) soup meal next time & the fried rice. Definitely going to be my fried plantains spot now.

I had a fantastic experience at Omalicious. I recently had the pleasure of trying the Fufu and Egusi combo with chicken and I must say, it was an incredible experience! As a first-timer with Nigerian cuisine, I was pleasantly surprised by the rich and authentic flavors. Parking was a bit tricky at first, but there’s more available behind the restaurant. The staff was friendly and patient, helping me figure out what to order. I will definitely be back for more! Highly recommend!

I have a great taste for authentic African food, and Omalicious African Restaurant came through perfectly! We went as a family for a taste of home and culture and wow, the Onugbo and Egusi soups were absolutely phenomenal. You could literally taste the love and skill in every bite.
The food was hot, rich in flavor, and beautifully prepared. The restaurant itself was clean, the atmosphere welcoming, and the customer service truly top-notch. It was an amazing experience all around — highly recommend!

First let me start off with my first experience with fufu was not good at another restaurant in Montclair/ Ontario.

I wanted to give fufu and egusi another shot I saw the pictures for OMALICIOUS and it looked delicious but from the moment we walked into the restaurant it smelled AMAZING !!  Justine was so kind and helpful when ordering we ordered the Jollof rice with chicken and plantain, egusi mixed meat and fufu .

BOTH PATES WERE DELICIOUS AND SAVORY!

The meat was fresh the jollof rice was so flavorful ! The sauce on the chicken was spicy and had so much flavor we finished both plates it was finger licking GOOD! We definitely found our new fufu spot 🤍 I gave recognition to the chef who took time in preparing the food he put his heart and soul in preparing the meal !  I would DEFINITELY recommend the restaurant to everyone, I cannot wait to go back and try their other dishes.

formatted_address: 630 N La Brea Ave #106, Inglewood, CA 90302, United States
name: Queen of Sheba Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text:
I’ve only had Ethiopian food a handful of times but have always enjoyed it, and Queen of Sheba exceeded my expectations. We ordered a giant platter with a variety of vegetarian lentil and vegetable stews, accompanied by fluffy tangy injera bread for picking up the saucy dishes. We also added a lamb entree with incredibly satisfying savory flavors that reminded me of a hearty tomatoey barbecuey stew.
To complete our dinner experience I had a tiny cup of strong Ethiopian coffee which balanced well with a lovely pistachio topped honey cardamom pastry.

Ethiopian food is eaten without western style utensils and injera is how one eats it. the injera here is a good, light flavor and texture. All of the vegan dishes were well seasoned - if you love spicy and flavorful go for yesimir wor (red lentil). if you prefer a more mild taste go for the cabbage or yellow split pea. Do get the ethiopian coffee and desert! Be kind. The staff is very sweet.

I enjoyed the food at Queen of Sheba. It was my first time trying the Ethiopian bread and veggies and it was very delicious. I also had their pasta. It’s a nice place for a quick meal or if you prefer carry out. I recommend the pasta, meat or veggie combo or better still try something out randomly. I did and was happy I did. I highly recommend.

Great find in this plaza serving up authentic Ethiopian food! A few tables inside so can get busy so recommend coming a little bit earlier side especially if you have a small group (3-4 people). We ended up getting recommendations from the host and got a variety platter and chose a lamb and chicken entree for our main. It came with injera that was made fresh. The food is meant to be eaten by hand with the injera and just tastes so better that way!

Brought here by my Ethiopian friends, who’ve tried over 7 Ethiopian restaurants in LA, and this one instantly stood out! The experience was nothing short of amazing. The service was warm and attentive, and the food… absolutely delicious. We also enjoyed the traditional Ethiopian coffee and incense ceremony, which made it feel even more authentic and special. The space is cozy and inviting, with beautiful paintings on the walls, spotless cleanliness, and plenty of parking available. A true gem, I’ll definitely be coming back soon!

formatted_address: 902 N La Brea Ave, Inglewood, CA 90302, United States
name: Two Hommés

reviews.text: One of the best meals I’ve had all year! After hearing so many great things from friends, my friend and I finally tried this spot and it did not disappoint. We ordered the Honey Berbere Chicken Bites, Lamb and White Bean Hummus, and I had the Garlic Noodles with fried catfish. Everything was incredible. I also had the Sentinela Sour and it was so refreshing. I wanted to try the sweet potato churro but I was too full. I’ll definitely be back soon for dinner and brunch. Highly recommend checking it out and supporting this amazing Black owned restaurant!

Stumbled upon this place for last minute dinner while visiting from out of town. We were seated relatively quickly at the bar with no reservation. It did take them a bit longer than usual to service us, but things moved quickly once they did.

The cocktails were delicious and a good reprieve from overly sugared ones the previous few days. The cuisine further sealed the deal — we started with the broccolini and lamb hummus, then shared jollof with catfish. We were so full we could barely finish. Will definitely circle back here next time we’re out that way!

The ambiance was intimate but lively. Great music playing in the background.

The service was great- Nina was so kind and offered great suggestions.

The food was robust with flavor and a generous portion.

The chicken bites were crispy, a little sweet and tangy.

The Jollof rice with crispy catfish was cooked to perfection. It came with black beans (delicious!) and sweet plantains.

The burger was good but definitely worth skipping and trying other menu items.

The house lemonade was so refreshing and not too sweet.

Overall wonderful experience. Will be back!

We went on a Wednesday night. It wasn't busy, busy but it was still loud and seating is cramped. I thought the table lights were neat.
We ordered and our food came out in less than 10 minutes. It obviously isn't made to order(probably reheated). Rootbeer short ribs were just beef that was a little dry and tough. There was no rootbeer anything. It was tasty but I was expecting a rootbeer flavor to come through. I also left most of it on my plate because it was dry and too chewy for me and what I expect from braised meat. The branzino was very charred and my aftertaste was burnt. The nucleus of the flesh was light and delicious but the outer portions were overcooked. The garlic noodles were fine but after three mouthful, I'd had enough. The broccolini was smothered in cornflakes and very oily but they were flavorful. My spicy pineapple drink needed more pineapple and definitely more spice. We were there a total of 45 minutes from start to end. We managed to box our leftovers amid the clutter of dirty plates and got our check. Card is preferred as they didn't have enough change for 100. I would go only to try their jollof to go. I hear that dish is amazing.

Came here w/ a dinner reservation last Friday evening. Unassuming, hole-in-the-wall from the outside. They have moderate space but can feel a little too close to other patrons, however seats were comfortable w/ relatively nice ambience.

Foodwise - simply delicious and flavorful. This establishment uses seasoning well and the entrees we had seemed a little sweet-forward (which I didn’t mind at all).

We loved the flavor profile of the Grilled Broccolini, the Braised Short Rib had perfect texture, and the Garlic Noodles were good!

Drink-wise the Sour was definitely a personal favorite, very tasteful. And the Young Fashioned had a usual kick you’d expect from that type of drink.

We also enjoyed the Sweet Potato Churro - what an inventive treat!

Lastly, Nita (Juanita on the receipt) our server was so lovely and personable - she made our first-time experience here that much more enjoyable. Thanks Nita - we appreciate your time and superb service!

We’ll definitely try to make another reservation to try out y’all’s brunch menu. 🤤

formatted_address: 1047 S Fairfax Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90019, United States
name: Rahel Ethiopian Vegan Cuisine

reviews.text: Came for the AYCE brunch buffet on weekend. Ate all the things and really enjoyed hanging out here. Got the coffee at the end and our server was very helpful.  Tasty Ethiopian and always a great place to visit to try other types of cuisine.
Delightful experience: family-friendly, tasty, and naturally vegan and gluten-free! Strong coffee and fun desserts, too!

a charming little place with such sweet service! we ordered the feast plate for 1 (but was enough for two) with sambussas. the injera was realllly good and some of the curries/veg were flavorful but other ones felt slightly bland, but with some chutney and pepper it was better. would definitely recommend this food if feeling sick or down, this is perfect home food with less spices and oil. but the sambussa was the star of the show! it was soooo good and crispy! also the bathroom is cute!

We had a wonderful experience for lunch for two! They had a lunch special which was a sampler platter and every single thing on it was amazing. We were in heaven! It was the best meal of our trip! We also had a delicious piece of mango cake for dessert. Our server was very friendly and took great care of us, and we were seated by the window which was lovely. By the way, we are not vegans! This place is not just for vegans. Seemed like a family business too, very sweet people and we felt good about choosing them. We can’t wait to go again!

Rahel Ethiopian Vegan Cuisine at 1047 S Fairfax Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90019

This is my second time going to this restaurant, it is a vegan Ethiopian restaurant. Both times I came here is for the lunch buffet, also it comes with a nice little dessert at the end. I bought a slice of their vegan cheesecake, but forgot to take a picture 😋 lol. Overall it's been an enjoyable time on both trips, I've been here. This time I actually drove and you can park up front if you can get a parking space on Sunday for free. Other than the parking, that's the only thing difficult about this area. It seems to have a lot of other Ethiopian type shops very close walk.

formatted_address: 1048 S Fairfax Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90019, United States
name: Little Ethiopia restaurant and catering

reviews.text: Short and maybe not so sweet - food was good, we both got their lamb dishes, one spicy and one mild, the yellow one pictured is the mild one and was tender, the spicy one was not tender at all. Was recommended to try their sparkling water Ambo later found out that it was $5 per bottle! Italian ones were cheaper... Bill came out to $40 for 3 items, cutthroat prices if you ask me for the amount of food (real stingy on salad), place was completely dead - that should have been a good indicator

LOVE LOVE LOVE LOVE EVERYTHING ABOUT THIS RESTAURANT.
Nice staff, like super nice, you get welcomed with a polite smile and greeting. Food worth 10 star, literally. Food portions are OK. The venue and decoration is very simple, cosy, and homie. Service is quick and food is delicious. You will need to use your all 10 fingers for having the Ethiopian food, so don’t expect it to be a fit for fork and knife. Prices are affordable and the menu is simple. They have a great Ethiopian white wine. Totally recommend.

I had better, but Ethiopian food is always good. We came in late so service was kinda slow even though we were the only ones here. Prices are at normal range for this type of food.
I played it safe and ordered the Alicha Wot which was delicious. Portions combining with a the Injera are more than decent.

This is my favorite spot to go to. They have very attentive waiters and the food is really good for the cheap price. I always go here because they used to have the $7 vegetarian lunch special and I believe a $9 dinner special. But when I went here a couple days ago, they had a new menu. The vegetarian dinner for two is now $15. The meat items are just okay like every other place in fairfax. If you're a meat eater like me, I recommend "Zula Eritrean restaurant" in Inglewood. Wow the meat flavors are on point! I reviewed that place and gave it a 5 star.

The nicest people with the most questionable business practices. I went here using  Groupons 1 day before they expired.  I made the mistake of saying I had a Groupon when we ordered.  As a party of 4 we ordered 2 separate dishes to feed us all (left photo) I came back the next day to use my other Groupon and didn't mention it until the bill came (right photo).  The size of the platter was identical but the difference in portions between 2 to 4 people is appalling.  I also bought a $7 beer that was nothing special.  The food was good-ish but all the other stuff far outweighed the entire experience.  Probably won't go back...#Disappointed

formatted_address: 3709 S Western Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90018, United States
name: Joan & Sisters

reviews.text: Have not eaten here yet but eva since I get deported bak to the states I have had no damn fry jack no Jonny cake , no REAL rice and beans or atu bean wit rice. Can I get gobnut here or hicitee.. I will be stopping by soon I can't wait to see what unu have.  Onion sauce . I had da best onion sauce bak inna da bush wit miss mampy at Maya crystal skull back a Altun Ha. I will update after I get fa taste heaven in hell.

Let me start with this...Everything was superb,  some things better than others. A personal favorite and lots of good memories brought back. Pictured... That's  a side of oxtail in the cup, tender flavorful ,more fat left on the meat really adds to the rich flavor. The big tray is rice and beans, potato salad stewed chicken and fried plantain. This food blends so well you can mix and match each bite. The odd shaped things are panades with fish the best i've had hands down. Yep that's a coconut tart big as your hand. The crust is buttery, not dry, the coconut is cinnamon goodness - which leaves a lasting taste in your mouth . Milk Cake with carmel  yumminess, bread pudding was moist smooth consistency the bomb..lastly it's the potato pound a little dry still tasty. It's a lot we ordered everything we wanted, I can't wait to get back. If you haven't been yet go it's so worth it.  P.S. there's a jam roll haven't tried it but.....

Got the veggie dinner no meat rice and beans potato salad was ok and fry plantain I also got  panades got 4 it was big and good they make it with tuna fish so there kosher the only problem was they play loud music so it’s hard to  hear what the cashier is saying she was the only person I seen taking orders  I’ll buy again but next time white rice with stew beans the food is affordable
I will say breakfast was great 👏 Best Journey cakes ever, the oxtail was very tender, well seasoned and fresh…Overall Yummy 😋

🇧🇿 BELIZE (via Eat the World Los Angeles) - There are some places in Los Angeles that have been part of the city's fabric for so long that the pandemic came along and never even phased them. They can measure their existence in the amount of times fresh blue paint was needed to apply to the morning sun-soaked facade and have survived so many milestones before this latest. The recipes that have survived everything Los Angeles and the world has thrown at them for the last 40 years are always going to satisfy new and old customers alike.

formatted_address: 4020 W Martin Luther King Jr Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90008, United States
name: Yordanos Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text:
TL;DR this is the worst Ethiopian/Eritrean food I've ever had for a totally outlandish price. How it has such high reviews is incomprehensible.

Last Thursday my friend, my wife and I had the most delicious Ethiopian/Eritrean food any of us had ever had elsewhere in Los Angeles county. We were glowing from one of the best meals in our years in LA, and having only been to one or two other places in Little Ethiopia that were decent but not revelatory, my wife and I were eager to try other Ethiopian options around the city.

We found the initial hole-in-the-wall impression charming rather than off-putting. You walk through a grocery store into a small windowless restaurant adorned with pictures of regional Ethiopian customary dress and other knick-knacks. The back of the restaurant opened to a pleasant large covered outdoor seating area with artificial turf. So far, so good as far as I am concerned.

Most of the options on the menu were a la carte $20-30. We wanted a sampler that was mostly veg but contained one meat item like I've had at other spots. We communicated that desire to the waiter, and settled on awaze tibs for the meat.

We waited quite a while, fumbled through my meagre few words in Tigrinya mixed with Arabic to an elderly Eritrean man who stopped in for a soda, and sat in the dark for a while when the power unexpectedly cut.

When our meal arrived, the first thing we noticed was relatively few items, just two kinds of lentils (misir wot, kik alicha), a small serving of salad, and of course awaze tibs. No collard greens, etc. That's fine. A decent portion for two people, and since we weren't starving we even had a small bit left over to take home. The injeera was good, but everything else seemed rather slapdash and unbalanced. Not much care was put into balancing the spices. The worst part was the meat was terrible quality; very tough. We ordered tea (Lipton's, steep yourself. Served with spiced water). We both kind of shrugged with the assumption it was going to be much less expensive than the previous experience being, as it was, a total dive. We were shocked when our bill came to ~$63 before tip. I begrudgingly tipped $9 and left wishing I had said something. But everything had been meticulously added to the bill and the restaurant wasn't busy so there was no way it was a mistake and thus nothing to really argue about.

For comparison, the place we had eaten a few days prior gave us no fewer than 8-10 different items including collard greens, delicious succulent tender meat, sweet potatoes, two different types of salads, all wonderfully spiced (and spicy!). We ordered a whole cooked trout which was among the best fish any of us had ever had. They washed our hands, we ordered house-made cardamom and berbere ice cream and got more than double the amount of food (we were three hungry people and had enough for another three meals left over). The place was fancy, was reservation only, beautifully and thoughtfully decorated. The owner came around and said hello. The price per volume for some of the best food in LA was comparable to what we paid here for half-edible slop and power cuts.

🇪🇹 ETHIOPIA (via Eat the World Los Angeles) - When you arrive at Yordanos in Crenshaw, the exterior does not hint to the joy that you will eventually find inside. But the warmth of the space and the wonderful aromas smack your senses as soon as the door is opened and you take one step past the threshold. The restaurant has the feel of a place that has been around for its community a long time, but in reality the grand opening was in the summer of 2019. Nowadays you will find groups of friends coming to talk with each other over beer, wine, or Ethiopian coffee, or enjoying an NBA game on the TV after finishing a meal.

It was my first Ethiopian restaurant to try and I liked the vibe and food types.
Sabusa is no Brainer try.
I just figured their mild spicy level is not very mild and is strong so be careful before the order.

Wow wow wow. So my friend and I wanted to go on a food adventure and we chose this amazing place.  The first thing that you take in is the atmosphere... peaceful, calming and inviting. Not knowing anything about Ethiopian food, I was wide-eyed and ready for anything. It was far too difficult to pick anything to order with no clue as to what things might be to our taste. So we went with the Mahberawi, an amazing platter with six different items, two very spicy dishes, and 4 other flavorful dishes.  Along with the platter came a bowl of what looked to be a thin bread but more spongy.  I was familiar wnough with ethiopian food from a prior visit that one takes a piece of the injera and scoops up a mouthful portion and enjoy.

... is tomato, spices with onions and ground beef with a tanky flavor. It was very mild and quite tasty.

.... is a bit like carne asada mixed with onion and seasoning which was very satisfying.

... omg the beef with collard greens was amazing. Flavorful and mildly seasoned paired well with the bread.

Yebeg Alicha... the bread, injera, was soaked with beef and seasoning with a tangy flavir.

Kitfo ... was ground steak tartar which will make you spice lovers extremely happy.

... an even spicier chicken and vegetable dish with hard boiled egg.

This dish was a wonderful way to sample such an awesome variety of foods and flavors.  If you have never eaten Ethiopian food, this is a wonderful place to wet your tastebuds.

The best part is that I can't wait to come back and try the vegetarian tray!!  See you soon!

Have never had ethiopian food before but very pleasantly aromatic, spicy, extremely delicious!!! My son had a dish with salmon, jalapeños and onions called Fish Kitfo that was very good and spicy. I had the lamb tibs called Yebeg Key Wet which was sooooo very good and spicy! Hand food served with traditional injera that they ferment for 3 days. Very very good. Had a small coffee jebena - strong and good!! Highly recommend here!!!!! Thank you for a very enjoyable experience!

formatted_address: 1278 Produce Row, Los Angeles, CA 90021, United States
name: Rivera Produce Corporation/ African and Caribbean Food Distributors

reviews.text: Nice place to buy products from. Workers are great! Female workers are amazing as well!

They have items you can not get in the regular grocery store. A lot of products from west Africa. The prices are high. Parking is terrible. Very busy little driveway. Not much parking in front of business. The selections of dried goods, canned and frozen ate not bad. With those prices you can splurge once in a while. Weekends the streets are crowded making it to this market. Which means trying to park. This store is on a loading dock. You have to go up about 10 stairs. No handicap access or parking.

You will get all that you need to cook your delicious meals, be it soups or stew or any dish. Check them out for your African, Caribbean foodstuffs, ingredients. You will find what you’re looking for 😃 🧑‍🍳
Good place to buy African and international food
Poor costumer service, I went there these guys with a mean face on acted like I was more bothering them than a potential costumer.

formatted_address: 800 W Olympic Blvd A150, Los Angeles, CA 90015, United States
name: Fixins Soul Kitchen

reviews.text: Came on New Years Day with a reservation at 5:15 for 3.  Would definitely recommend making reservations on nights and weekends as it is normally full.  Need to try more options things on the menu before a 5 star for food but so far its really good.  Mac&cheese, potato salad and collard greens are all good.  The yams are amazing,  tastes like they should be a dessert.  Deviled eggs are good just wish it was a little more.  Service a little bit slower but I think its because of how full it gets.  Wish they would validate parking but its L.A live so kind of expected.

Fixins Soul Food absolutely blew me and my fiancée away! The service was phenomenal—warm, attentive, and genuinely welcoming. Every dish was incredibly flavorful with generous portions that make you feel truly taken care of. The cocktails were delicious and perfectly crafted, and the location itself is vibrant and inviting.

What makes Fixins even more special is its mission. You can feel the pride in honoring Black culture, history, and family in everything they do—from the menu to the atmosphere. It’s more than just a meal; it’s an experience that celebrates community.

Highly recommend. I can’t wait to come back!

The restaurant was nice and felt warm due to the ambiance and the great customer service from the staff. We were seated immediately on the patio, under a heater; because it was chilly. We were able to people watch on a beautiful Sunday morning. The music was great! And the food was even better. We had the gumbo that came with some really good cornbread that tasted like cake. The serving was so large I had to pack the remainder to go. The chicken and waffles were very good. The waffle was soft and not over cooked. The Mac and cheese was delicious also. Parking was right across the street. Great experience overall.

My family and I visited here on a Sunday while in LA for a game. Everything we ordered was delicious, no complaints at all. The service was friendly and music was a vibe. I'd recommend a reservation,  it got packed as we were eating which was about time church let out. We will definitely be visiting again.

Vibes were good, food and drinks were ok. My drink, the Black is Beautiful Old Fashioned was unexpectedly very smoky, which I hadn’t realized when ordering it. I was unable to finish it, and it was $18. The artichoke dip was mediocre and not very hot. The fried chicken was solid, pretty tasty and crispy.  The highlights of the plate were the red rice and beans and the biscuit. Overall not bad, service was good, just a little underwhelming for the price, but understandable due to the location.

formatted_address: 6039 Washington Blvd, Culver City, CA 90232, United States
name: Industry Cafe & Jazz

reviews.text: This place has been there for a long time for music lovers in Culver City! (They will have 20th year anniversary special in October!!) The owner, Aron, his brother, and his staff are super friendly and create a supportive neighborhood casual atmosphere. Everyone is welcome, even you stop by solo. I go there for their music especially when they have classic Jazz like Miles Davis or Coltrane type. They serve Ethiopian cuisine with Eritrea twist and have a full bar. If my friends are not familiar with their food, we can ask Aron, he always suggests something we can enjoy.

Great food, great atmosphere, and great jazz. Went in on a Wednesday night and had the whole place to ourselves! Their sambussa was delicious, as were the zil zil and doro wot. You gotta try their carrot cake for dessert - divine. Would absolutely come back. Thank you for a lovely evening!

Nice and cozy place. The staff were helpful and kind. We ordered 3 different foods, served in one larg dish with vegetables around it. Felt authentic. Oh don't forget to try Asmara bear.(Eritrean bear). Tastes pure. Oh don't miss the soup. Jazz music soft, not load. Perfect

Wonderful jazz cafe in Culver City! Fantastic live jazz band. Yummy Ethiopian vegetarian plate with plenty of delicious injarra to eat it up, included. The hummus was topped with a pico de gallo type fresh salsa and queso fresco crumbles. Cheap for dinner and entertainment.

My First visit here and to an Ethiopian. Great atmosphere. Milian was there. (The owner or co-owner). Nice set up. Loved the artwork on the walls.
We were the only ones there.
He made a greens dish with cabbage & and garlic. Soooo delicious!
I ordered the Doro Wat. Chicken Tibsi, and vegetarian Platter. It was served on a big platter. The food was fresh and delicious. We enjoyed our visit. He was very personable.
There is live music here on Wednesdays they Sundays. He also writes poetry, music, and books.
Come on in and taste and enjoy your visit. We will be back for sure. Can't wait to come for the music!

formatted_address: 325 N Tustin Ave, Santa Ana, CA 92705, United States
name: All African Cuisines

reviews.text: Don’t think! Just go and get the food trust me it’s really gooddd!!!. I had a last minute plan for a Friendsgiving in a diverse friend group and I wanted them to try african food. I kept looking through different restaurants and their reviews and decided to give this one a shot. I was skeptical at first cause I’m from Nigeria and wanted somewhere with really good Jollof and fufu especially cause I know how good it should be. Getting from here was the best decision I made. I called and told her about my plans and the size of the group and together she helped plan how much food would fit my budget and made me feel taken care off. The quantity of the food was enough to go around. I got a pan of jollof and plantains and pepper chicken all for a good price. Trust me you won’t regret it!!

Location:
If you try to follow the map or the directions through door dash like I did, you'll get confused 😂 It's literally just in the Chevron convenience store where you pick up the food. I didn't realize that when I drove past it to the parking lot behind so I was wandering for 2-3 minutes until I called them to ask.

Service:
So friendly and sweet! They are glad to help and want to make sure you love what you order to eat.

Food:
It was delicious and satisfying! My first time ever trying actual African food of any kind. I've especially always wanted to eat fufu. I was super curious about the egusi but I'm a bit of a texture person and was worried I wouldn't like that particular one so I ordered the eforiro.

The eforiro was nicely seasoned and well cooked. I think it tasted good and hearty but light at the same time. It didn't make me feel heavy or gross after, so I liked it! The fufu was super fun to use my hands to eat the eforiro with. It was an interesting experience! The fufu texture is soft, pliable, and has a slight chew to it.
