Puff puffs were yummy! A familiar taste and texture. It's not overly sweet, just sweet enough. It would be amazing with powdered sugar and/or condensed milk on top! You could pair it with anything as it's essentially just a fried dough. These were crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside.

Overall, a great experience! It's just further than I can drive most times but I would love to try the egusi next time and a different fufu!

Delicious food prepared to order. We had oxtail pepper soup, afang stew, stockfish, akara, and two kinds of swallow. Will definitely be back. Hey, owners, do you think that you will ever add banga to the menu?
First time trying African food, very delicious! The Ogbono soup was very hearty and had a unique taste and the chicken in the soup tastes amazing with Yam Fufu. Thank you so much!!

First time trying and it was so good! I got the egusi with beef and yam fufu. Beef was tender and egusi soup was light yet flavorful. The gentleman who handed me my food asked if it was my first time having this and said I will like it —he was not wrong! I will definite be back

formatted_address: 2801 W Ball Rd, Anaheim, CA 92804, United States
name: Abyssinia Restaurant

reviews.text:
I am a longtime lover of Ethiopian food and was used to going to LA for my cravings. I went to Abyssinia probably a decade ago and just lost track of it with COVID and the like.

I finally convinced my daughter to go with me and it was absolutely fantastic. Our waiter (the owner's son) was very nice and explained Ethiopian food to her, while I just counted the time until our Dora Wat and Gored Gored came. We also had the veggie combo.

Apparently the new owners took over nine years ago and it was AWESOME. Better than what I had in LA, better than what I had in DC.

I had a great talk with the waiter and their mission was for more people to try Ethiopian food, and I agree with him!

Abyssinia is a must try! My daughter has the bug now, and we will be back.

We've been here several times. Love it. Great place to introduce people to a new experience. The food is completely normal meat and veggies, just served on platter with injera (sponge bread/pancake). Eat with your hands. It's just different. Enjoy!

melts in your mouth. came on a sunday evening for dinner and place was quiet with a few tables beside us also enjoying the vegetarian platter. we added a plate of lamb to it and it was amazing with all the vegetarian dishes. i ordered the spiced chai without the black tea bag, and it was so delicious and comforting on a cold night. our server was super attentive especially to my elderly grandmother. i love the decor and soft music playing in the background. forgot i was in anaheim in a random small plaza.

Oh my gosh, wow!! Just got home from an incredible dinner. The owner is such a sweet hospitable man. The food is incredible!! You can taste the care and quality in every bite.

I had the Ethiopian honey wine which is served cold and bubbly and packs quite the punch. It’s not sweet like I was expecting, which I really enjoyed and preferred.

We shared a veggie combo along with the number 1 from the lamb menu. Everything was so delicious and high quality.

After speaking to the owner, he told us he is a chemist, which makes total sense! His food and flavors are articulated down to the molecules. He serves filtered water NOT tap water which is so rare at a little ma and pop place such as this. We felt very cared for and takes care of.

The Ethiopian coffee is so good! They roast and grind the beans in house.

Everything is amazingly curated and so much food and an overall very pleasant experience. I would eat here every week and am looking forward to our next visit. Can’t recommend this place enough!

This place is amazing overall. The atmosphere is very calm and relaxing 😌 The staff is very friendly and accommodating. The food is Superb I live 2 hours away and whenever I get a craving for the most Delicious  Ethiopian food this is the place 😋 Food Is 5 🌟  I would definitely recommend to anyone!
Thank you for this experience!!

formatted_address: 17951 Sky Park Cir 35 J, Irvine, CA 92614, United States
name: Lynda's African Delicacies

reviews.text:
The best authentic African food I’ve ever eaten!
Lynda’s African Delicacies is an absolute gem. Every dish is freshly prepared and bursting with flavor. You can truly taste the love Lynda puts into her cooking—every bite is delicious and comforting. The staff is just as wonderful: always warm, welcoming, and ready with a smile. If you're looking for authentic African cuisine made with care and heart, this is the place. Highly recommend it!

This culinary masterpiece is an absolute delight for the senses! It was my inaugural experience with Fufu and shrimp, and I was blown away by the exquisite flavors. Every element was cooked to absolute perfection, with the Fufu being delightfully soft and the shrimp bursting with freshness and succulence. The seasoning was impeccable, ensuring that each bite was a harmonious blend of taste and texture. This dish is a true testament to the art of cooking, leaving me eagerly anticipating my next encounter with this delectable creation.

First time trying Nigerian food.
The beef and jollof rice tasted good. But it is evident that everything has been sitting in warming pans for a long time and doesn’t get mixed regularly. Whatever is on top dries out. Some of the beef had good texture, other pieces were incredibly dry and hard to chew. Same with the plantains. No complaints about the jollof rice.
The spinach stew is definitely an acquired taste and not to my liking. Oily with a very earthy flavor.
The hot sauce provided has a unique flavor and is VERY hot.
We liked the meat pie as well.
The restaurant has no inside seating. There is a communal area with tables outside. The interior is also a bit messy.
We ordered through an iPad and none of the employees asked if we needed help or spoke to us
I’ve tried African food for the first time in Irvine, CA at Lynda’s African Delicacies. The food is so good and flavorful and the customer service is amazing!

Lynda’s African Delicacies is an absolute gem! The West African and Nigerian dishes are rich, flavorful, and made with so much love. Every bite tastes authentic and home-cooked. The jollof rice, suya, and egusi soup were standouts. If you want real, delicious Nigerian comfort food, Linda’s is a must-try!

formatted_address: 6501 Hollywood Blvd 4345 Degnan Blvd, 700 Warren Ln, Los Angeles, CA 90028, United States
name: Sunday Tuco G LLC. Nigerian Food

reviews.text: This is the best Nigerian food. If you like Nigerian food give this a try when you are in Hollywood or Limert Park
First time trying and it was so good! Will definitely be coming back when in LA.
Fantastic food come try it
Best African Hollywood period!!!!
Guys!!! EVERYTHING IS PERFECT

formatted_address: 132 N Robertson Blvd, Beverly Hills, CA 90211, United States
name: Tagine Beverly Hills

reviews.text: I’ve been thinking of dinning here for a while and it was worth the wait!!!! Definitely one of my favorite places in LA. I loved the cosy and charming atmosphere, delicious food and amazing staff.

We celebrated my wife’s birthday here. The restaurant makes the best Moroccan dishes  in LA County in my opinion. The food was excellent and service was fast. We’re definitely coming back for more. This is a must visit when you craving moroccan food.

We tried the signature tasting (5 courses $97) and it was amazing.

The restaurant is very very small (8 tables total!!!) one server was working the entire restaurant. All the dishes were excellent and to perfection, i was very full at the end.

I got the rose (glass) and it was a bit underwhelming, maybe next time I'll research the wines before I choose it.

Great place for small groups, casual dinners or special occasion celebrations.

Experienced the best Moroccan food in LA at this cozy and welcoming spot!
Chef Ben’s hospitality made it even better. Highly recommend!
The pastilla was very tasty, as were the hummus and Moroccan salad! A great selection of fine French wines too 😊
Absolutely delicious, fantastic!! Every dish was spectacular. I would definitely return and recommend!! My husband had the tasting menu. I had the pescaterian tasting, amazing!!!

formatted_address: 1176 S La Brea Ave, Inglewood, CA 90301, United States
name: African Soul Food Restaurant

reviews.text: Need to try it after Dpeezy recommended it. 👌🏿
Nasty food and rude service.
Nice place

formatted_address: 726 N La Brea Ave, Inglewood, CA 90302, United States
name: Emma Habesha Restaurant

reviews.text: You'll feel the love and intention as soon as you walk in...the food is great for veggies and meaties... There's A beautiful outside space w/ lots of potential to host events or fun social gatherings.

The food is very fresh! Emma is very lovely and hospitable. The restaurant is nice and clean. This is a hidden gem. We had the vegan platter and the fried fish. It was the perfect amount for 2 people and very reasonably priced. The lentil sambusa was crispy and fresh and had fresh herbs. And that Ethiopian coffee was amazing!!! I am not a coffee drinker and I loved it.

Such an amazing restaurant. The food was delicious and the coffee was PHENOMENAL. Not too bitter, very rich, and someone else said it tastes like dark chocolate - it does! The atmosphere is so calming, especially if you sit outside. The service is wonderful too, the server was very kind and recommended us a few dishes. Will definitely come back again. Parking is also free and available :)

I am speechless. First time trying Ethiopian food and I came to the right place! Staff was very friendly. I’m usually not a fan of lentils, but the red lentils was super delicious!! It’s a must!!! I also got the honey wine and it was very smooth. It’s also house-made which made it even better! It got me feeling very relaxed ☺️ will be coming back!

You feel like you’re no longer in Los Angeles. We were attended by emma herself for a late afternoon lunch and have the lamb and crispy beef over this and incredible bread. You can sit at a typical Ethiopian wicker basket table if you want. It is a thoroughly exoticand enjoyable experience.

formatted_address: 3810 S Western Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90062, United States
name: Tracey's

reviews.text: This is a wonderful  carribean kitchen option on this side of the town. The sides complimented the oxtails sooo well. Very nice flavor and portion. My ocd could nit pick about the oxtail cuts, but not today. lol.
I literally love coming there atmosphere is great the people are great the food is amazing

You will be greeted with great customer service. Hands down the best Carribean food in Los Angeles!! My favorite plate to buy is the fry jack eggs chicken wings and beans. So savory. I always stay eating here. Good clean environment!! Will definitely recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for good eats!!🇧🇿💋

got the stewed chicken and it was delicious, well seasoned and the portion was big. will definitely be coming back to get the oxtail next time, i came at like 2pm on a Monday and they were already sold out 😭 but that's how you know the food is good!!

the guys who work here are really friendly and quick, this spot is a gem

I would highly recommend! This is a hidden gem in the heart of Los Angeles South Central.  For cultural RICH tasting food, do not hesitate! It’s worth the drive, worth the wait definitely worth a taste! BELIZE 🇧🇿❤️🇧🇿❤️🇧🇿🕊️
Breakfast 9-11am daily.
Call for more info.

formatted_address: 11355 Foothill Blvd, Lake View Terrace, CA 91342, United States
name: Ranch Side Cafe

reviews.text:
We just moved into the neighborhood and had such a wonderful experience at The Ranch Cafe. Our waitress, Lee, truly made our day. She was so welcoming, kind, and genuinely excited to have us there, which meant a lot as newcomers.

Lee gave us great recommendations and everything she suggested was spot on. The service was attentive, friendly, and made the whole experience feel special instead of routine. It was the perfect welcome to the area, and we’ll definitely be back. Thank you, Lee, for making our day!

The food was decent, but some of the food was burnt. The atmosphere was chill and the decor was nice and definitely unique.   The food that wasn't burnt was good. I would come back to try some of the other food.  The menu is very diverse and had a lot of items. They didn't charge for the burnt sambusa. The people working here were very nice.

We celebrated Mother's Day at this restaurant after a nice walk at the Mile Run in the Hansen Dam Park. When you walk in you'll be transported to the golden age of Hollywood cowboys with their murals. We were seated immediately and our order was taken quickly after. The restaurant was a bit busy so it took some time to receive out order but not much. The food and coffee were great. I got french toast, hash browns, and a side of Ethiopian veggies. The service we got was amazing because the owners are their working with smiles on. Come to the Valley and checkout this small and quaint family owned restaurant.

Incredibly good food tucked away in a very unassuming little Cafe. This little hidden gem is a sleeper up in the Angeles Canyon. The unexpected Ethiopian menu was absolutely delicious, we ordered the sambusa, the chicken and the anjeera with beef stew.
This is such a great little place, filled with halt regulars and staff.
Definitely worth a trip if you're anywhere in the area, they're Mexican and American menu are pretty good as well.
Highly recommend.
If you liked my review please give me a thumbs up 👍🏾 to let me know! Follow me for more fun reviews. 🙏🏾
Just ate the veggie plate and it was truly delicious!! And my wife ordered the BBQ tri tip sandwich with coleslaw and she said it was quite flavorful. Thank you so much, we'll be back ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

formatted_address: 2835 S Robertson Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90034, United States
name: Ackee Bamboo Jamaican Cuisine

reviews.text:
They catered a friends wedding a couple of months ago and as an L.A. native who enjoys Jamaican cusine, I'm almost embarrassed to say that I had never experienced their food before then. I was missing out but no longer. I've ordered a from them a few times since and they have never disappointed. Be ready for an abundance of food! The jerk chicken is phenomenal and my favorite sides are their plantain (I need more with my entree!), and festival bread. Love the rice and peas too. It's all flavorful and enough to last me for a couple of meals.

*I got delivery so I didn't rate on service or atmosphere*

The oxtail was delicious and the salad was good too. Portions were large. We split an oxtail for two. The flavors were off the charts. And a great way to end an afternoon of walking and shopping through Leimart park.

Came here for some Jamaican food after the MLK parade. It's a nice little restaurant. And the food was really good. Shared a beef patty with my buddy and I had the curry chicken wrap. Service was friendly and quick. Will come back.

It's very good. I think a little pricey for what you get though. We have a combo Jerk chicken, curry goat and rice & peas. Coupled with, wings, 2 patties and root beer, around $70 so not sure. Worth a try for sure, the flavour alone is great.

Huge portions and the best Jamaican food I’ve ever had. It’s even better than the food I had in Jamaica. The vegan options are ridiculously delicious and the portion sizes are huge. We had the small boxes and it was enough to food us twice each. Also the hot apple and spicy melon ginger beers are a solid 11/10. Takes a bit of time to recover the food but the wait is well worth it.

formatted_address: 5581 W Manchester Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90045, United States
name: Dirdawa Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: A bit tough to find (it’s upstairs and through the gate) and has the world’s worst parking lot (too small and cramped), but wonderful staff and great Ethiopian food - especially the vegetarian combo. The new dining room is big and it’s the perfect spot for great music and dinner with friends.

08/10/2025; I am ordered to go food, then the owner charged me $31:00 dollar with my debit credit card which I did'nt get my to go ordered food!  I called 4 times to delivery the food with uber dash, no body answer, even, coud'nt leave message; a voice mail is full; can't accept voice msg, said answer machine bad coustomer service

Loved the veggie plate! Very flavorful. I would’ve liked some salad on it too. I’ve been to other Ethiopian places where the lentils and split peas were a lot softer in texture, but didn’t take away the deliciousness of this place. Will come back!

Stopped here on the way to the beach when I saw the sign fire Ethiopian food. Glad I did. The food is delicious. I had the Salmon kit for and it was out of this world. Large portions to where I couldn't eat it all in one sitting. It was priced very well given the large portions. Will definitely come back again.
Delicious vegetarian combo platter. Friendly staff with laid back atmosphere. Would definitely return for another great meal!

formatted_address: 2018 W Washington Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90018, United States
name: Lucy Ethiopian restaurant

reviews.text: Everything I was craving for Ethiopian food! The service is so sweet and accommodating and they even gifted us a slice of cake from their friends birthday! Def can’t wait to come back!

Very friendly and authentic Ethiopian restaurant. We enjoyed the large vegan sampler, mango drinks, ginger tea, and the "Ethiopian Coffee experience".

It was all tasty and enjoyable, especially chatting with the couple who are the proprietors and cooks.

Felt like we were honored guests at their home.

My first time at this restaurant. I love Ethiopian, came here based on the proximity and reviews.

Overall it was decent. I had 5 star quality Ethiopian food in other restaurants.

We ordered the following items:
1. Lentil samosa - had far better ones in other restaurants, I left it to be honest after a single bite.
2. Veggie combo - great one
3. lamb tibs and doro wot - these items were good and will recommend them.

i love ethiopian food, and i love injera, however, i wish i could actually rate the food but i can’t because they denied to serve me. i walked in the restaurant at 7:10pm, they close at 8:00pm. they said they won’t serve me if i want to sit down and eat. they will only give me food if i do takeout l. i was wanting to make a tiktok of my experience being there to promote the restaurant because i was excited to give it a try, but i guess i wont.

I love Ethiopian food and finding Lucy was a blessing. It taste like I was back in DC, the other places on the west coast, I've found aren't nearly as close. I ordered the kitfo dullet and the tips and when I tell you it was goodt, it so was!! Mattaios was super nice and inviting, telling me I needed to come back to try the ramen. I definitely recommend trying this place!!

formatted_address: 243 San Pedro St, Los Angeles, CA 90013, United States
name: (abeautifullife) Jamaican Kitchen

reviews.text: I went with some colleagues last Friday afternoon and it was great! The service was wonderful, the environment, and the food was tasty! I got the jerk chicken egg rolls, the spicy jerk Mac n cheese (not pictured), and the jerk salmon platter which was all great. The best for me was $35 bottomless mimosa with a bunch of different flavors! I’d recommend this spot if you’re looking for a low key but fun time.

From the moment we walked into A Beautiful Life, the atmosphere was unmatched—Jamaican-boho aesthetic, warm lighting, and you’d never guess you were right in downtown LA.

Our server, Diamond, was absolutely exceptional. Her customer service, attentiveness, and amazing energy made the entire experience stand out. She truly elevated the night.

The food was equally impressive:
•	Plantains with jerk sauce: perfectly sweet with the right amount of kick.
•	Vegan wings and nuggets: crispy, flavorful, and a must-try for plant-based diners.
•	Oxtail Mac & Cheese: moist, tender, well-seasoned—hands down a 10/10.
•	Lamb chops: spicy, meaty, and cooked to perfection.
•	Vegan curry: flavorful, mild spice, another 10/10 dish.
•	Churros with caramel: sweet, soft, and melt-in-your-mouth good.

This restaurant offers an unforgettable dining experience—whether for a date night, a girls’ night out, or simply treating yourself. We’ll definitely be back.

They nailed-it, in terms of atmosphere. The ambiance was nice.

This was my first time eating there and I only stopped because I was hungry and happened to be passing by.

I ordered curry chicken with rice & peas and plantains.

The rice and peas were ok. The chicken was undercooked. The plantains were not as tender as I like them, however, they were perfectly caramelized. The curry sauce could've been seasoned better and thicker (it was a bit runny).

I will most likely keep searching for a good Jamaican food restaurant.

When I first walked in I was greeted in which it was one person serving the whole restaurant. I ordered oxtails in which was $40. It was horrible in flavor and  the gravy was super thin.The portion was small and The rice was hard. I also ordered a lemonade for $8 and it came in a tall thin glass. When it came to pay they automatically added 18% gratuity without acknowledgment. So my total came up to $60. It was definitely not worth it.

All I got are positive things to say about my experience dining here with my wife. We've never had Jamaican style food before. The flavors were all so exuberant. And the service we received was great. We got starters, entreés, and a dessert to share. Ended the dinner with a nice flavor hookah. Perfect place for a out of the ordinary date night!

formatted_address: 6619 S Western Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90047, United States
name: Baba's Vegan Cafe

reviews.text:
Came here to try this vegan spot.  Upon walking in , it feels like you’re in a hour or a clothing store.  But don’t let that stop you. The food is delicious
The staff are friendly. And took our order right away.  We waited 10 min for our food.
I ordered Baba's soul Platter
-Tuscan Greens, Hot Mac, Rice, beans, yamz, mixed veggies, Protein
The  vegetables were cooked perfect.  Season just right. This platter is the perfect combo.  I definitely want to come back and try some more items.

The food here is excellent and full of flavor. We especially loved the lentil fritters with the habanero sauce, they were amazing. The staff is friendly and laid back, creating such a welcoming and relaxed atmosphere. It is definitely a place with a great vibe.

I just wanted to tell you about my great experience here. I wish it was closer i would be a regular customer. I love all the afro centric art from the outside of the building to the inside. The food was delicious I ordered the soul food platter with fried black lentils. While we eat we played a game that we borrowed from their library. The customer service here was great they just need more ventilation for when you sit down and eat it gets a little stuffy other than that a new awesome place I discovered.

What a vibe! I tried BabA's Soul Platter and it was lit. I loved everything on it. The food cam out pretty quickly. The hot mac and oyster mushrooms were delicious. I live the vibe of the place. I love that you can get Sea Moss here. It's so good for our bodies. I live the merch that you can get there as well. I highly recommend if you are nearby and want some fire food.

This is one of my top places to eat vegan food! Also to purchase several self care items such as toothpaste, Shea butters an oils. They also sale different crystals outside of the storefront 2 days a week! Thank you guys

formatted_address: 109 E Pico Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90015, United States
name: Liberian girl kitchen LLC

reviews.text: I am not very knowledgeable about West African cuisines, but the staff was very friendly and introduced me. I got the fufu along with some meat dish. It was savory and very good. Although the meat was very spicy. The staff was so kind and served me with a complimentary sweet dish.

I got the dry rice platter. The food here was served hot and everything was so delicious! The red snapper was well seasoned and flavorful and I washed it down with a cold ginger beer. I couldn’t have asked for a better meal and was happy to take half of it home because I could not finish it all. If you need some comfort food, do yourselves a favor and visit LGK! Also, the Afrobeats and dancehall music videos they played created a nice vibe. I will definitely back!

I had an amazing experience at this West African restaurant (Liberian girl kitchen LLC) located 109 E pico blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90015. The food was absolutely delicious and full of rich, authentic flavors that brought back memories of home-cooked meals. I ordered the fried rice with fish and plantain, and every bite was perfection the rice was well seasoned, the fish was tender and flavorful, and the plantains were perfectly sweet and crispy. The portion size was generous, and the staff was warm and welcoming, making the whole dining experience even better. I’ll definitely be coming back soon! and I encouraged every one to try this place! I give it ten over ten.

I was drawn in by the positive reviews and LGK did not disappoint! This was the best Egusi Stew I've ever had. Texture and flavors are on point. If you like spice, please get it spicy, it's perfect.  Portion was good too. I'm excited to try other items on the menu.  There is some seating for dine in as well. If you're craving West African food, or you want to try something new, please give them a try!

I’ve only ordered the food from here on uber eats so I am unsure of the service and atmosphere. But the Egusi soup is delicious!!! The fufu is also the right consistency as well. Also, they aren't skimpy with the portions which I appreciate especially when ordering it to be delivered.

I’ve ordered Egusi soup from several other restaurants in LA and this is the closest to a home made version. Had it for the 2nd time today and just as bomb as the first time! Sooooo good! It makes me want to try some of the other items on the menu.

Note: I ate out of it before the pics lol

formatted_address: 6919 Melrose Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90038, United States
name: Casablanca Moroccan Kitchens

reviews.text: I ate here recently for lunch with friends from out of town, and the service, food and ambience were exceptional! Everything was truly delicious and presented beautifully, and the best part was how genuinely nice and welcoming everyone working there was. It was our first time trying Moroccan food and they went out of their way to explain dishes and make it such a special meal. You can tell they put so much love and care into everything they do. We left feeling very satisfied and grateful for such a fun dining experience. I highly recommend!

The service was incredible! I made a reservation and when I told them I have a reservation, she said Ariana? They made me feel so welcome and it was a beautiful restaurant. The food was great, flavorful, and I loved the assortment of salads. It was also so much fun because there was a Belly dancer and she did a bunch of performances and interacted with all of the guests! I would definitely come back !

We went on a Friday night without a reservation, and our server welcomed us so warmly right from the start. We ordered the dinner set with an appetizer and entree …everything was incredible! We had the lamb with couscous, and it was so tender and full of flavor. The chef even came out to chat with us, which made the experience feel so personal and special. It was my first time trying Moroccan food, and honestly, I couldn’t have asked for a better introduction. Such a memorable and heartwarming experience …we left so happy and satisfied!

Flies from Dallas to Vegas and drove 5 hours from Vegas to LA to get this memorable Moroccan experience. Feels like home… the food the atmosphere the service just perfect. I highly recommend the chicken bastilla and the chicken tajine we will definitely come back in our next visit to LA. Miss naima the owner really took care of us I felt like I’m visiting my parents house. This is the hospitality that we’re used to get in our home country Morocco ask for her she will do her best to make your experience memorable. Thank you so much for everything♥️🥰

Cannot recommend this place enough! I went here for my birthday and was absolutely blown away by the food and service. Everything we ordered was a 10/10 and the people serving us were an absolute delight. The interior of the restaurant is so cute as well. Will definitely be coming back!

formatted_address: 358 W 38th St Unit K07, Los Angeles, CA 90037, United States
name: 54tables

reviews.text: Placed an ordered online, paid for my ordered. Website says closes at 11pm and it closed. I don't live local, im about 4 hours from here. So disappointed. I need a refund

formatted_address: 216 S Spring St, Los Angeles, CA 90012, United States
name: (abeautifullife) Jamaican Cafe

reviews.text: I took my gf here to celebrate life, a dinner experience. We were greeted warmly by our waitress, escorted to our seats, and seated promptly. the vibe was incredible! the restaurant is a hidden gem in DTLA. It is tucked away, and the staff was on point. the food was so fresh and tasty and the drinks were perfect. she loved it! we will visit again soon!

So disappointed to spend my hard earned $42 on this mediocre meal. I usually follow my first mind and don’t waste my coins on a place with 3.5 stars. Saw the reviews, didn’t read the comments. This was my 1st time here today around 5pm. I walked in & after 10 minutes of standing there I got the attention of the bar tender after I was never greeted. Should’ve been my 2nd sign. I order the oxtails that comes with rice & peas, cabbage  & plantains. Got my food & 1st thing I noticed was how small this to go container was. I opened it & literally saw 2 small oxtails & 1 of those skinny size one, small size of rice & peas w/ some cabbage sprinkled on top. I should have asked where was the rest of my food because at best this was an appetizer size. I didn’t want to be an a hole so I paid & even though I order it to go I gave a $2 tip. It’s a Black establishment & I knew I was NEVER coming back or recommending this place EVER. I live in Orange 🍊 County so by the time I get on the freeway and started eating, I realized they NEVER gave me the plantains. FOOD WAS MEDIOCRE, bad service, OVERPRICED, UNDER PORTIONED, & cheated out of what all I paid for. This is only like my 4th review I’ve ever done in 10 years. HORRIBLE experience and I’m Upset that I didn’t follow my first & second mind. NEVER AGAIN

First let me say, it was refreshing to be in a space with no drama with all the liquor flowing😁.
The food was immaculate, everything was well seasoned and came out hot and fresh *as it should have for the wait*, but my four stars is for the service and forced tip; the waitress we had was amazing and very attentive *as much as she could have been* there were plenty of other staff walking around, dont know what there jobs were so don't wanna speculate. There is a mandatory 20% gratitude added to EVERY CHECK no matter the size of your party. The food is already "expensive" so adding on a 20% gratitude, expect to spend more. I don't mind the gratitude but that should be left up to the patrons, when most of the time those tips are pooled and the waiter or waitress helping you won't even see the entire tip. *even though I additional tipped my waitress graciously*, she deserved it.
The Oxtail mac was hot, bubbling
The Salmon and shrimp, seasoned but over cooked
The curry and jerk chicken, great and slightly spicy*obviously*
All was amazing
Would I go again, yes, just with a larger party to make sense of the added 20% gratitude

We tried a variety of their dishes and food was good overall! Tried the Chicken bowl, samon bowl, curry chicken, mac n cheese and a couple of their patties.

A couple of complaints I have are the following:
1. I ordered online. My receipt said to pick up in 40 minutes and I was there after about 50 mins. They had no idea what I had ordered. I had to give them my order and they started cooking it then, so I had to wait another 15 minutes. Very disappointing.
2. The mac n cheese we got  was very spicy which was not described in the online order.

This food right here! Amazing and delicious! I ordered the big plate of Oxtails as well the Jerk Shrimp Bowl and they are  Heavenly! Wow! Try tried the Beef Patty and was wowed again. Planning to eat my way through the whole menu! 😋

formatted_address: 7469 Melrose Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90046, United States
name: Ubuntu

reviews.text:
Ubuntu is a pleasure to eat at. West African inspired dishes. The flavor and spices in the food were a medley as beautiful as the music they were playing. I wanted to order practically the entire menu, but unfortunately, there were only two of us to eat. We started with the jollof arancini and it was so good. It only got better from there. The grilled cabbage had a flaky saltiness that made it hard to stop eating. My partner practically inhaled the red stew, and the lions mane pie was his favorite dish. He thought for sure it's be his least because he's not a huge fan of mushrooms, but he couldn't believe the flavors they made with it. The palm bisque started off bland, but with each sip, it grew in taste. It's my close favorite, too. The sweet potatoes had a fun texture. We were so full, we couldn't eat too much more of the sweet potatoes, but decided to save it for later.... except
Our biggest disappointment was forgetting our leftovers 😭😭😭.
...I highly, highly recommend this restaurant. It also happens to be vegan and 100% soy free. It is definitely a top favorite overall restaurant for us.

This place is exquisite! The garden and decor is gorgeous and I loved the tranquility of dining there. The host/waiter was very friendly and helpful. We ordered from the DineLA menu and the food was so tasty and perfectly spiced. I also loved the presentation. The rice balls were my personal favorite but everything was delicious. It's such a unique place and I highly recommend it.

Lived up to the hype!!! It was so fantastic. The flavor profiles and presentation were all amazing. We got the okra salad, jollof arancini, fonio grits, and peanut maffe. The okra wasn’t slimed at all and perfectly charred. The maffe was so so delicious and cozy tasting. Ibrahim was our server and he was impeccable as well. We had a great time.

First time dining at Ubuntu tonight, and it was a pleasure from start to finish. We were greeted warmly upon arrival in a beautiful, welcoming space. The atmosphere was great, with music at just the right volume.

Two of us dined on the jollof arancini, okra salad, and maafe peanut stew, sharing the dawadawa semifreddo for dessert. The food was perfectly balanced in seasoning and flavors—warm, complex, and comforting. The ingredients were fresh and vegetable-forward, and the portions left us satisfied but not weighed down.

We look forward to returning for more! Shout out to the fabulous staff for their wonderful service!

I am so glad to see this newly opened restaurant and that it features delicious flavors inspired by West Africa. We take friends on tours to Africa and we have so many people who want to try African food here, this is a great introduction.

You will want to order multiple items and enjoy the experience of sampling them with your partner or friends.

The Char Grilled okra salad was divine. I’ve never had a passion fruit vinaigrette before, and this was splendid. Bursting with flavor and highly recommend.

The Lions Mane Pie was also a fantastic choice I would recommend. The mushrooms give a great experience of a pot pie/Shepard’s pie.  The crust was delicious.

And the Jollof Arancini was amazing! Best burst of flavor I’ve had in a long time.

The vibe is cool, the music is not too loud, the decorations are fun and artistic, and we had the privilege of meeting Chef Shenarri Greens., Karen our server was pleasant, and the GM Oscar let me take photos while he made our delicious mock tail drink.

Congrats to Ubuntu on a delicious restaurant. We will be recommending and bringing friends to visit this establishment and to support the flavorful experience.

formatted_address: 242 N Ave 25, Los Angeles, CA 90031, United States
name: Mestico Afro Latin Cuisine

reviews.text:
I recently had the pleasure of trying Mesticos' award-winning chili, and let me tell you, it's no surprise why it's a winner! The blend of spices and depth of flavor is truly incredible, and the quality of the ingredients really shines through in every bite.
But don't just take my word for it - I've shared this chili with numerous friends and family members, and the response has been unanimous: this is the best chili they've ever tasted.
And it's not just the chili that's impressive - Mesticos' catering service is top-notch as well. From the friendly and professional staff to the beautiful presentation of the food, every detail is handled with care and expertise.
Whether you're looking to spice up your next event with some award-winning chili or need a reliable catering service for any occasion, I highly recommend giving Mesticos a try. You won't be disappointed!

This year's Sangode Thanksgiving dinner was made by Mestico. Everyone loved the well-seasoned and tender turkey. The black-eyed pea salad was amazing! And I took ALL the yucca mash, I can never go back to  regular mashed potatoes after having this!

Got to sample the food when they were a vendor at the Afro-Latinx festival event at the MOLAA earlier this year. As I trying to determine which food vendor to support as I wanted to sample food that was reflective of the event. He didn’t have his menu prominently available so I had to asked him what he was selling, he said the magic word oxtail and I was sold. Food was delicious and there sadly was no leftovers, as I scraped it clean. Not the cheapest but the food was tasty to justify, as well as the drink/juice. Definitely would recommend and would want to try the other dishes.

formatted_address: Proper Hotel, 1100 S Broadway, Los Angeles, CA 90015, United States
name: Cabrillo

reviews.text:
Cabrillo at the LA Proper Hotel makes a strong first impression with its inviting breakfast ambiance and upbeat café music. During my visit, I tried the PROPER BREAKFAST from their menu, which offered a satisfying start to the day. The spot also has a tasty selection of pastries, fresh smoothies, and coffee beverages—all ideal for a leisurely morning meal.

However, the service was a disappointment. Despite only a handful of guests at that early hour, the server was inattentive and didn’t once check on my table or offer to refill coffee or water, which took away from the overall experience. If great service is a priority, you may be let down here, but if you value good breakfast in a stylish setting and have time and budget to spare, Cabrillo can still be worth a try for the food and vibe alone..

Disappointing experience. The food was okay, but it took about 25 minutes to arrive at my table. While I was still eating, the waiter came over surprisingly quickly to ask if I wanted the check. After I told him I was still finishing my meal, he just walked away. When I was done, it took another 15 minutes before he came back with the check.

Also, it’s the classic situation where Asian guests are seated in the corner of the restaurant, even though plenty of bright, sunny tables were available.

My husband and I recently visited this restaurant to celebrate our 7th anniversary, and it exceeded our expectations. The food was outstanding, and the atmosphere was both romantic and beautiful. Special thanks to Megan, our server, whose exceptional service and charming personality made our day even more special. We highly recommend this restaurant. For context, my husband and I travel frequently and have high standards for quality food.

Good food with good presentation. I expected more for the French toast, but it tasted like ordinary. Hash bowl had a lot of stuff, sour cream, guacamole, lots of meat, and flavor. Smoke salmon was not bad but nothing special. I would order something else more unique.

Had to take off some of the tip because they charge customers 5% of staff health insurance thing (don't clearly remember what it exactly said). That is what the employer should be paying for their employees, NOT THE CUSTOMER. We already are paying and tipping for the service that is already included in the foods' price (the irony part of the concept of tip culture). This country is going crazy for real

Visited on a Thursday evening, very quiet with few staff on duty. Plating was beautiful and the food was mostly very good. Service was noticeably slow, ceviche arrived without chips (the kitchen noticed and brought them out though) and there was almost a 30 minute wait between the ceviche and the rest of the meal. The hangar steak, persimmon salad, and the ceviche were the standouts. Also the seasonal drink, it was delicious! I regretted ordering their sangria and the patatas bravas, very underwhelming. Ambiance is really warm and nice, but the bathrooms are all the way upstairs which is kind of a pain. I wonder if they are short staffed, either way, a lot of potential here.

formatted_address: 11711 Collett Ave, Riverside, CA 92505, United States
name: Saaraloge's Kitchen

reviews.text: This was my first time trying West African cuisine and it did not disappoint. The fufu and Egusi was incredible, the fried rice was great, and the spicy fish was fantastic. The puff puff was a great way to capstone this culinary experience. 🤤

i ordered the egusi with beef and fufu and it was sooo yummy! it’s really tasty i think a lot of people would like it. i was so happy to see that there is a west african cuisine so local to me!! the owner is so kind, you can tell that she makes her food with love too. support small businesses!!! im definitely coming back again :)

I recently found this place in riverside and have ordered two times already this week! The quality is very good, and packaged nicely. The portions are pretty large as well. I have ordered the puff puffs, fufu, egusi soup and jollof rice as well. I like my food mild so spice level three is perfect for me!

This was my first time trying her locations food and I have to say I’m very satisfied with her food the portions the taste the flavors the everything I’m so happy and excited I’ve found her that and have someone close to home that sells and makes this food !! It was my girlfriend’s first time trying this type of food and she was very impressed and satisfied I really recommend her cooking I am seriously coming back for more !! I’m so stuffed I had to leave some for tomorrow ! 10/10

Was excited to try something new, and was pleasantly surprised with how delicious the food was. The flavors were something I’ve never tasted before, and I am so happy and satisfied with what I ate. Very filling food with generous portions, 1 item is definitely enough for 2 people and has still leftovers. The egusi and turkey efo riro were exceptionally amazing with good flavor and you can tell it was made from the heart. I’m very glad to be supporting a small business and buying authentic and amazing food that obviously had effort put into it. Very sweet service and patient with me over the phone, which I really appreciate. Will come back again as a returning customer to eat more again, thank you so much. 💕

formatted_address: 1240 S Soto St, Los Angeles, CA 90023, United States
name: Mama D's African Cuisine

reviews.text: Fabulous food and wonderful service.  My first time eating the dishes and each were outstanding.  Highly recommend.  Be careful with the spice medium is plenty hot for this girl...we live in South Orange County and it was worth the drive.  We had ndole and chicken with jollof rice...rice was fabulous and had a serious kick...

CAMEROON 🇨🇲
Excerpt from Eat the World Los Angeles:
The namesake of the restaurant Mama D. herself, has been running a restaurant just outside of Washington D.C. for many years and at the time of this visit was off to Cameroon to procure necessary ingredients for her and her daughter, who is the chef of this new spot. When asked about her mother, it was mentioned she is "very picky" and could not allow the substitution of some important items, which often happens out of necessity in the city's kitchens serving the traditional foods of countries far away.

One of the ingredients that Mama D. brings from back home is the green called ndoleh used in the dish of the same name. It has a unique bitterness that cannot be replicated by spinach or something similar, often the case here in the states. For this reason, the ndole ($17) at Mama D's is a must try and uniquely Cameroonian.

It can be served with a couple different choices of meat and side, but in her home country Chef Claudia says you will see it most with shrimp and it goes best with a side of fried plantains. Although the ndole is stewed with peanuts, it remains intensely (albeit pleasantly) bitter and her recommendation of the slightly sweet plantains is a good one.

Mama' D's was great and like nothing I've eaten before. I mean I haven't been to Cameroon so makes sense. Was so magical to see the owner in the kitchen. My friend and I drove an hour from the Valley just to visit and it was well worth it. We ate in the parking lot, Covid style dining.
My friend ordered the beans and rice with plantains. He is vegan and that was their vegan options! The beans were a full meal with veg and so much spice. I had Ndole with shrimp and yam fufu. Ndole is one of the traditional dishes of Cameroon, it is a creamy spinach stew with shrimp on top. It was flavorful and delish. The yam fufu was this soft doughy ball wrapped in tin foil. It was kinda like a mash potato dumpling but more doughy and a bit sweeter but still very bland.  It was quite comforting to eat. We really enjoyed the food and will definitely be back.

Claudia is a complete sweetheart! Food is absolutely amazing!!!! Everything was tasty! Food and drinks! We could not get out the kitchen from standing there eating 2 plates each!! Even our dog was happy! My new favorite African restaurant. Will be a weekly customer! Family was cool too😄

Had a great meal from Mama D’s tonight. I ordered the Ndole with shrimp and the Jollof rice. Both were so flavorful and well-spiced. Looking forward to trying more items. Thanks for an amazing introduction to Cameroonian food!

formatted_address: 4002 Lincoln Blvd, Marina Del Rey, CA 90292, United States
name: Sumptuous African Restaurant

reviews.text:
Such a good, fun, and new food experience for the neighborhood.
The egusi is flavorful and delicious with fufu and chicken.
It was my first time trying and that hit it out the park. Nice portions, enough to share if you're not starving.

The Nigerian malt drink is like sugarcane soda. Divine! Will be back and a great family behind it all.

This place is sooooo freaking good! I usually get the curry chicken and the rice and beans. The portions are nice and full. I always have extra for later. Try the spicy goat although it’s spicy it has the most wonderful flavor! everything I’ve tried here has amazing flavor!

Absolutely incredible meal. We had the ox tail which was so tender and flavorful, with the spinach and fufu. Listen, if you love food, then you should give it a try. Oh and the Jamaican beef patty was on point! 💥💥💥.

Surprisingly tasty! Surprising because I’ve spent a lot of time in Ghana and West Africa and usually have low expectations for such food here in LA. Had ogbono, asked to have it Nigerian spicy and it was perfect. Would come back to introduce friends to Nigerian food without thinking twice.
Food is Amazing. My Favorite is the Egusi and assorted meat. Very reasonable prices for the portion.

formatted_address: 5354 Wilshire Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90036, United States
name: Panama international Restaurant

reviews.text:
The outdoor patio area was nice, and we enjoyed sitting out there. However, the customer service and staff personality could use improvement; it seemed like the owner was the one serving us.

Unfortunately, the jerk chicken was awful--it tasted off and was quite unpleasant. The oxtails with peas and rice were just okay, and I noticed they forgot to include the plantains.

The large red snapper was acceptable for my taste, although my sister thought it was good.

Overall, I wouldn't consider returning. With a bill of $161, I didn't feel it was worth it, and I chose not to leave a tip.

I like to feel appreciated and enjoy my food. It wasn't hot ( only fish)

Also all the owner do on these review is make excuses and argue Dang!

The food was great. The owners came and talked to us personally for awhile. The food was a little spicer with the Carribian background than my wife was used from her region of Panama. But each family is used to how their mom or grandparents make things. Overall it was delicious.
On an important side note they are relocating to Long Beach and having a name change to PTY, after Panama's airport.

I never leave reviews.  I ordered about $100 worth of food togo.  The lady wanted me to leave a good tip, so I was in a good mood and left 20% for takeout.  I was so excited I started to eat it in my car.  Oxtail and Jerk brown chicken.  Both extremely salty.  I even brought them home and rinsed in hot water because they were so salty.  I love salt and always salt my meats, but these dishes were not edible.  I would probably need a half a pot of rice to balance out the salt in the oxtail.  The chicken was overcooked and was stringy and dry and too salty.  Reminds me of heavy soy sauce, overcooked to make everything turn black.  Don't know how they stay in business with food like that located in an expensive part of town???  People can actually eat this stuff?

Ordered the Patacones, Jerk Chicken and the Stew Chicken. This was all AMAZING and so tasty. The chicken fell off the bone on the stew chicken. The patacones were just right- salty and crispy. The jerk chicken was just the perfect amount of spice. Also got a taste of the oxtail and it was so good. Empty plate club- Will definitely come back.

We placed an order online for pick up and unfortunately online said they had no empanadas but they did have a few left when I got there but we were in a rush and couldn’t get them. Food was extremely spicy compared to Panamanian food. Most of the country dont tend to cook with spicy ingredients but they over did it! Even the mild was very spicy to the point that it wasnt enjoyable and I can handle really spicy food and this was a lil too much. Great portion but I didnt even want my left over due to the spice level other than that, I think I would just call and place my order since we used a 3rd party ordering method.

formatted_address: 5955 Melrose Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90038, United States
name: Providence

reviews.text:
Providence remains one of those rare restaurants that does not chase relevance because it already owns it. This is seafood as high craft, quiet confidence, and discipline meeting deep pleasure. Every course feels intentional without ever feeling precious. The room is calm and composed, the kind of place where the noise of the city falls away and attention sharpens. You are here to eat, to notice, to slow down.

The tasting menu is a master class in restraint and clarity. Santa Barbara spot prawns arrive pristine and sweet, treated with reverence rather than theatrics. The uni course is luminous, briny, and balanced, never heavy, never fussy. Their legendary salt roasted Santa Barbara prawns deserve the reputation they carry. Perfect texture, pure flavor, nothing to hide behind. The lobster dishes show technical precision without losing warmth. Sauces are exacting and layered, built for depth rather than volume. Even the simplest preparations feel studied in the best way.

Presentation is elegant and modern, never distracting. Plates land like punctuation marks, not exclamation points. The wine program is world class, with pairings that elevate rather than overpower. Thoughtful selections, confident pours, and pacing that respects the arc of the meal. Cocktails follow the same philosophy clean, restrained, and purposeful.

Service is among the best in the city. Polished, knowledgeable, and genuinely hospitable. Questions are welcomed. Timing is flawless. You never feel rushed, and you never feel forgotten.

Providence is not trying to impress you. It simply does. This is Los Angeles fine dining at its most serious and most satisfying. A benchmark restaurant that earns its reputation every single night.

We had to wait for over a month to reserve a slot at 8:45. The restaurant was very popular. It was located in an inconspicuous spot by the roadside and didn't match the surrounding environment well. We chose the special recommendation from the chef, which was basically the three optional main dishes provided in the daily menu included. Each dish was not very large, and it was almost enough to finish in one or two bites. We finished the food in the set menu around 11:50. We felt very full. We also ordered the dessert (chocolate) to go. My favorite dessert is the one in picture number fifteen. Overall, I think the taste of the dishes here doesn't meet the standards of a Michelin star restaurant , delicious but not impressive.

If it's not the best restaurant in the LA area, it's in the top 3-5.
Been coming here for really specialy occiasions over the last 10+ years.
As a seafood lover, it's hands down my favorite restaurant in the LA area.

Service: Friendly, extremely knowledgeable, attentive, and unpretentious, exactly what you would expect from a 2-3 Michelin star restaurant.

Drinks were fantastic as you would expect. I tend to opt for beer and Providence consistently has had small brewery interesting and delicious beers.

Amuse-bouche - 4 bite size preparation with nice textural elements, and nice flavors.

Lots of preparations of seafood which were outstanding, the intersection of extremely high quality seafood, perfectly prepared or raw, in fantastic tasting sauces. Exactly what you would expect in a 3 Michelin star restaurant, absolutely perfectly done with interesting textures and tastes.

We opted for the Prawns, which were an addtion. Came with a cool show as they came encrusted with salt and cut tableside. Absolutely amazing, sweet and delicious with nothing more than a bit of salt and lemon.

Bread- Red Fife Sourdough- House made and delicious, i liked the story that came with it, and the butter of course... the butter!

Some interesting preparations of chocolate including a chocolate tea. They were good but I would say the dessert was the least memorable part of the meal.

Highly recommend if you are in the area and if it's in your budget!

Food overall was great. The dishes from the beginning of the night were a bit better so maybe 1-2 misses. Service was excellent. Forc the price though, not sure I’d come back again unless the menu was very different.

I came to Providence with very high hopes for an unforgettable dining experience, but honestly: “Quite ordinary.”

Appetizers: Caviar and uni were disappointing and uninspired. Then salmon with cream, crispy bread, and black truffle – ingredients I expected to be more creative at a 3-star level, but instead felt very common.

Sashimi & king crab: Nicely presented, but the sauce was overly salty and once again paired with caviar – repetitive and dull.

Santa Barbara prawn & egg yolk with uni: Lacked impact, not memorable at all.

Scallop with XO sauce: Finally, a highlight – flavorful and well executed.

Abalone – nothing special, slightly salty

Risotto with Italian white truffle: Overly rich and heavy, lacking finesse.

Duck breast & king salmon: Average at best, nothing special.

Desserts: The best part of the meal – especially the in-house chocolate, which was delicious.

Overall, I was looking for something extraordinary from a Michelin 3-star restaurant, but what I got could easily be found in many non-Michelin places. Outdated ingredients, unimaginative execution, and little creativity.

Don’t get me wrong – the food was good, but it was not remarkable in terms of ingredients or creativity.

I give this restaurant 3 stars (just okay), not because the food wasn’t good, but because it was overhyped.

Good food doesn’t necessarily come from the most expensive ingredients. True culinary artistry is about creating unforgettable flavors and experiences from even the simplest ingredients.

formatted_address: 2920 W Jefferson Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90018, United States
name: Harold & Belle's

reviews.text: I truly enjoyed my dinner last night. Great service. Clam chowder was amazing. The fried oysters were delicious. The Caesar salad with fresh croutons was best I have ever had. I ordered shrimp and crawfish etoufee. 10/10

Food here is always good. I normally get their gumbo but this time I tried fried shrimp and cat fish. It was good, even the part I took home and air fried later on for leftovers. Good food and nice atmosphere. Server was friendly and knowledgeable!

The elegant setting and delicious food brought me back to my visits to New Orleans! Customer service was top notch. It is definitely on the pricey side, so I will be returning on special occasions. The pork chop was the winner for me, but I also loved the etouffe, gumbo, and catfish.

The food and service were excellent!  We ordered a small bowl of gumbo, a catfish po boy, a shrimp po boy, and beignets.  The quantity was generous. We ended up taking some food home.  Our server, Nicole, was friendly and took good care of us.
My first visit was about 30 years and since then, I always thought that place. Back then, we lived over two thousand miles away. The recent visit was as amazing as the fist.

formatted_address: 2425 Daly St, Los Angeles, CA 90031, United States
name: Zizou

reviews.text: Came for brunch. It seems that it would be best to get here for dinner . I asked for the steak and fries, but it is 11:45 and we didn’t know we couldn’t order lunch . The Brunch selection is very small, not a lot of options. The ambience is great . So it seems if you visit early, it’s just for a small hang out and not a celebration until dinner time . Food was different. It took a while to get our food though , even though the restaurant did not seem busy. We got here at 11:10 and didn’t get our food until 12:26pm . I would want to come back and try their lunch/dinner menu. Maybe next time it will be a better experience here.

We were a walk in with zero expectations considering the neighborhood this is located in, but wow -- it was lovely.  The selections on both food and wine menus were limited, but very good.  Much like a proper european restaurant, they are not trying to be everything and OK at it, they do a few things on which they excel.  Atmosphere was great, much more Silverlake than Lincoln Heights.  I recommend highly and will be back.

The service was great.. friendly and very accommodating, which made the experience really pleasant. It’s definitely more of a casual spot, so if you’re expecting top-notch, no-wait, fine-dining service, this isn’t that. I was expecting more Moroccan-style dishes, but the menu was small and not really Moroccan. That said, the food we did try was all quite good. Overall, I’d recommend it if you’re looking for a laid-back spot with good food and warm service.

Dope little pocket of yum, in the Lincoln Heights area. Unexpected, which makes it more deserving of dedicated patrons.

We came for our anniversary dinner and were very surprised to discover the uniqueness of this place. There was a salsa DJ that night, and the dance floor was filled for hours.

The steak and frits were immaculate! Similar to and arguably better than the picanha severed at Fogo De Chão.

Come with people who respect the space, stay till midnight eating, drinking, and dancing the night away. Fun for all ages 21+.

Recommend making a reservation.

Five stars just because it is such a cool spot though I do have some notes below.  Zizou is both a beer/wine bar and mostly outdoor restaurant with a special event patio in back. On our recent Friday night visit found it busy with walk-ins being told that they were booked up for the night.  It's a French-north African vibe, specifically the vibe of the north African culture that developed in France after the decolionalization of French North Africa in the aftermath of World War II, so the food is both French and North African in influence.   Prices were very good for la.  Food was good but not spectacular, the calamari was over salted and the piece of meat they picked for my steak frites was poorly selected.  C'est la vie.  I would certainly return and my hard to please boo gave the vibes a 10/10.  Well done!

formatted_address: 351 N Fairfax Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90036, United States
name: Lucia LA

reviews.text: Such a beautiful experience from start to finish. The space is stunning—dim, elegant, and intimate without feeling stiff. The service was genuinely attentive and made us feel welcomed the entire night. The food was absolutely delicious, thoughtfully prepared, and beautifully presented, and the drinks were next level—especially the creative cocktail with pearls, which was both fun and perfectly balanced. It’s the kind of place where you want to slow down, enjoy the atmosphere, and savor every bite. Perfect for a special night out or a classy dinner with friends. I’ll definitely be coming back.

NYE 2025

The service was great. The seating area was cosy with the attempt to seat as many people as the dining area allowed. The lofted ceiling makes the place have a more roomy feeling. That said, onto the food.

The NYE menu had options for each course:

pre first course, the amuse-bouche, which is supposed to delight the senses. It was made of a Nigella Seed - Bammy with Plantain Cream / Caviar | Mango Sour. A traditional bammy is supposed to be cassava flat bread that is soaked in coconut cream then fried, steamed, or baked. The flavors were good but it was very chewy. It sat in my stomach like a starchy puck.

First course, we picked the Rock Shrimp & Bay Scallops Ceviche. This was really nice and enjoyable. The plate also came with some thinly sliced and lightly salted taro root chips; these were excellent. Makes me think I should try to make the taro chips at home in the air fryer. There were a lot of shrimp. With the bay scallops, the dish had more than four ounces of protein. This is a big deal because I am starting to get full after the first dish. The flavors were well balanced.

Second course, I ordered the Pastelón de la Tierra (Sweet Plantain / Short Rib Sofrito / Taleggio Béchamel / Green Plantain Crisp). My companion had the Calloloo (king crab with Spinach / Seasonal Veggies / Okra | Herbs). The calloloo looked to me like a king crab salad, except most of the greens were pureéd. My "big cake" looked like a half portion size of meatloaf, except it tasted a lot like very dense lasagna. I ordered it because I thought it was more technically complex to put together. Alas, instead of pasta, green plantain was used between the layers of the ground beef and sofrito. Now I am just about full. The individual components of the dish are not that hard for a serious home cook to replicate. The plating could have used something else to brighten the dark rectangle of food in a dimly lit restaurant.

Third course, I had the Soup Jomu Agnolotti (Oxtail Ragu • Squash-Truffle Cheese Filling • White Truffle), and my friend ordered the Spiny Lobster Roulade (Sauce Creole • Pickapeppa • Pistachios • Fry Bake Crumble). I have nothing good to say about the Soup Jomu Agnolotti, which I had to eat with a fork. I guess not really a soup at all. I didn't get past the first stuffed pocket of pasta. O.M.G. It was so salty that when the waiter came by our table I asked to have it boxed up to go because it was inedible. I only observed the spiny lobster dish. Unlike the ceviche, the lobster was covered entirely with a dark brown creole sauce. This makes it mysterious to look at, but not in a good way. What are you hiding? How can you do this to seafood? Anyhow.

This review is rated 4 stars because I want this place and all new experimental kitchens to survive in the LA metro area. If the restaurant doesn't last, I hope they open a bakery because the last course--the dessert--was freaking fantastic. I would eat another serving if it were available.

For the dessert course, we both picked the Coquito Tres Leches (Guava Jam • Pastelito Crisps). Everything about this cake is house made, fresh, fluffy, and oh so good.

Cocktails - I had the Lychee Margarita and it came in a glass typically used for an old fashioned. It was ok. The lychee "caviar" pearls that came with it were delightful to see and taste. There was nothing memorable about the margarita.

As I mentioned before, I hope this restaurant makes it in the fine dining scene; but there are so many restaurants to try out in the area that I will not be back.

Hollywood glamour? Or fancy club?

I think I am probably just tired of all the flashy things and environment. Nothing wrong with people who pursue a good night-life. Not suitable for me any more.

The food, when I recall, I could not remember something that really impressed me.

Not too bad, just was not what I expected through the pictures. Pretty small inside and outside was located in an area that I would never to think to dine in.

Every one might be liking the shell-like lightning at the back of a few seats. I like some of the designs. For example, the pearl-like lights around the bar table.

But overall, I am not satisfied and it did not meet my aesthetic needs.

Dined on 1/3/26
Original rating 3.3/5 before food poisoning

Lucia nails the design, vibe, drinks, and service — all were truly excellent. Unfortunately, the food didn’t match the rest of the experience. Several dishes were bland, others overly salty, and many of the positive reviews seem tied to a previous menu that I would have preferred to try.

What ultimately lowered the rating is that everyone in our party (from two different households) experienced food poisoning about 36 hours after the meal. I even remarked at the time that our starters came out unusually fast (3–6 minutes), which in hindsight raised concerns.

We dined at Lucia LA this evening and, based on the menu featured on their website, were really looking forward to the experience. The atmosphere absolutely lived up to expectations — easily a 10/10. The space is beautiful and sets the tone for a special night out.

Unfortunately, we were disappointed to learn that the menu currently listed online is not the menu being served in the restaurant. When we asked, our server kindly explained that the menu had changed a few weeks ago. While we appreciated the transparency, the new menu didn’t offer any dishes that were as appealing as what’s still featured on the website, and it honestly felt a bit like a bait-and-switch.

My husband ordered the fish, which was beautifully presented but lacked flavor. I ordered the beef patty, which was also well-presented but similarly underwhelming in taste. Portions are quite small for the price point, which added to the disappointment.

On a positive note, the service was great — attentive, friendly, and professional throughout the meal. While the ambiance and service were strong, the food and menu mismatch made this first visit fall short, and we’re not sure it would lead to a repeat visit.

formatted_address: 14770 Crenshaw Blvd, Gardena, CA 90249, United States
name: LECKY'S BUKA

formatted_address: 606-614 N Robertson Blvd, West Hollywood, CA 90069, United States
name: SUR Restaurant and Lounge

reviews.text:
SUR has been on my list forever, and as someone who absolutely loves Lisa Vanderpump’s restaurants — I’ve been to almost all of them — I was so excited to finally try SUR for brunch. The moment we walked in, the experience felt magical. The interior design is, as always, stunning: beautiful décor, amazing atmosphere, and that perfect balance of being both interesting and cozy at the same time.

We ordered cheese balls, the steak that comes with potatoes, and a couple of cocktails. For brunch, appetizers, a main course, and drinks, our bill came out to a little over $100 — which is absolutely fine, considering the usual quality at Vanderpump restaurants.

I got my favorite Espresso Martini — a drink I’ve tried hundreds of times in general and at Vanderpump restaurants at least five times — but this time it was extremely strong, almost like straight vodka. It was the first time in my life I didn’t enjoy it.

However, the staff handled it perfectly. Without any hesitation or questions, they immediately offered to replace the drink and brought me another cocktail, which was delicious. Truly excellent service — the team was kind, warm, attentive, and very pleasant to interact with.

When the steak arrived, the flavor was unfortunately much spicier than expected. The sauce and the potatoes had too many pieces of hot pepper, making the dish overwhelmingly spicy. I’ll attach a photo — we really tried, but it was difficult to enjoy it the way we did at Tom Tom, which is also one of Lisa’s restaurants.

Still, I genuinely believe things like this can happen to any restaurant, and overall the experience was lovely. We will definitely come back — adding an updated review with photos.

It was so fun to celebrate 🎉 NYE here.

I had been here a few times. Last time was 10 years ago. This restaurant survives.

Night life and sensual feeling just came back to me whenever I am here. I like here.

Long time ago, there was a pink car outside. Weho iconic place.

I had the truffle gnocchi with a cocktail (summer garden I think?), and it was delicious! Atmosphere was absolutely gorgeous. It surpassed my expectations in all aspects and I was blown away. The staff were also all very friendly, and more than happy to pose for photos and chat with all the guests. I came for the name but stayed and would definitely return for the food and drink. Thank you all!!

The place is gorgeous & very well decorated! Such a chill/mysterious vibe that is great for happy hour or a low key & comfortable evening with friends & family. Our server was nice but it did take about 10-15 mins to even be acknowledged by any of the bartenders, they’d walk by and ignore us although we were sitting directly in view- right across from the kitchen door. But after being greeted our male server was super sweet & helpful. The host was awesome too & dressed immaculately. We met Guillermo who was SO pleasant. He made our evening. Food was underwhelming but the atmosphere makes up for it. The guests I went with said their drinks were okay, but mine was delicious!

After living here for so many years, it was made to finally sit down with a reservation in the dining area here at SUR. The amazingly kind, attentive and fun Laurence was an extraordinary server.  One can tell people like this Lisa Vanderpump hires as they all have kindness and star power naturally within them. Lawrence was also very very familiar with the menu to a point where you wanted to absolutely buy and order more. ( I guess that’s the point right ? :) Sorry, Lisa, we were not drinking that night, but we usually do (and a lot ) so maybe next time. I like the ambience like most of these brands. It makes me miss Villa Blanca as well as Pump in it’s original corner location. We also adore and had our anniversary at Vanderpump Paris is Las Vegas. However SUR treats us nice and they are officially an OG within West hollyHood being a solid post pandemic survivor and I’m happy to celebrate it as it enters its 20th year.

formatted_address: 1405 2nd Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90019, United States
name: Angie’s Nigerian kitchen

reviews.text: The food was very good, I enjoyed my meal and the portion was very satisfying. I truly recommend. Thank you Angie
The food reminds me of when I stayed in Akwa Ibom. My personal faves are seafood Okra and Edikang Ikong. I highly recommend!
They cook very delicious Nigerian meal. Pick up, no dine in

Very satisfying and timely

It was quite sudden but she came in to help.

Highly recommended
Pick up only so delicious thank you Angie’s !

formatted_address: 9626 Venice Blvd., Culver City, CA 90232, United States
name: Jollof Abeg

reviews.text: I’m still eating the bowl as I type this. Ordered a large jollof rice with chicken and added some steak. This food is fire!  Tender chicken and hearty steak over expertly cooked rice. Love the extra kick from the sauce. Everything is proportionately balanced in this flavor bomb.
The food is so amazing. Jolloff could be a bit spicier but overall so delicious.

formatted_address: 10645 W Pico Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90064, United States
name: Ethio Kitchen & Coffee

reviews.text: A wonderful experience! We got there when they were almost closing, yet the chef decided to have us and cook amazing Ethiopian food for us. We were so happy and are so grateful for the kindness and for how delicious the food was.

I usually order the vegetarian combo, but I tried the Awazi Tibs this time, and boy am I happy and full. The amount of garlic and spice is so delicious! I appreciate the option to have the spicy sauce on the side. Their injera was so soft and spongy. 😋 I also tried their Tej (honey wine) and ginger tea, both made in-house by the owner, Josef. The tea was nice and strong, and the wine was sweet and went down so smooth. There is also parking behind the restaurant. I will definitely park there, next time. Thank you Ethio for making me feel welcome and feeding me so well. 🤩

The food here is neither spicy nor oily; gluten-free, it's healthy and delicious. The hospitality is exceptional, and the staff are always smiling. God bless you,  ጎበዞች በርቱ፣ ከቱሳን AZ, መተን ስለቀመስነው ወደነዋል። we came.From Tucson AZ, Bertu! Hector is not only a fantastic host but also feels like someone who has known us for a long time. He made us BBQ pizza, and it was one of the best I've ever tasted. I would highly recommend this place as one of the best Ethiopian restaurants in LA. We highly recommend this place as one of the best Ethiopian restaurants in LA.

Ordered online for pickup and it was ready in a hurry!  Owners took care of me beautifully while I waited for the final touches. The misir and yater kike alicha were perfect!  Great atmosphere for dining in. My pickup order was perfectly packed so everything made the trip home. Will definitely return to try more!

I recently visited Ethio Kitchen and it was the best Ethiopian food I’ve had anywhere—and I’ve tried Ethiopian cuisine in many cities. The owner, who is also the cook, makes everything herself entirely from scratch, and you can taste the difference in every dish. The flavors are fresh, balanced, and deeply authentic.

What made the experience even more memorable was the personal touch. She came out to our table, explained her cooking process, and spent time talking with us. It was clear how much pride and care she pours into her food. That level of dedication shows in the quality of each plate. Our server was also absolutely amazing and knowledgeable; he went out of his way to make sure we were having a good experience.

This is the kind of place where you can feel the owners’ soul in the cooking. Excellent food, warm hospitality, and a genuine passion behind it—an outstanding addition to LA’s dining scene. Highly recommended.

formatted_address: 1513 Centinela Ave, Inglewood, CA 90302, United States
name: BETTY MARKET & RESTAURANT

reviews.text: I recently visited Betty Market and Restaurant for the first time and had a great experience. They sell real teff injera, which is fantastic. I ordered breakfast, and the food was good, with the chechebsa, firfir, and injera being particularly lovely. The restaurant was clean, and the service was welcoming and friendly, which made the visit even more enjoyable. I highly recommend checking this place out!
Best ethiopian food in socal. And the service from the owner & staff is excellent! The food is fresh and delicious.

Had a wonderful experience from  the moment we stepped in until the moment we left. The owner treated us like family. Friendly, professional and with a great smile and great African stories. The feeling is of pure calm, relax and the ambience is super clean and airy. The food is EXCEPTIONAL. Every bite was a woooowww!
We recommend the n.4 spicy beef tenderloin in a thick rich tomato onion sauce. Looking forward to going back. Thank you.

I have eaten at every vegan restaurant in Los Angeles county and Betty’s is by far the absolute best! The owner makes you feel at home and like your family, the food is absolutely impeccable and always consistent in quantity, quality and flavor. The service is phenomenal and I never wait long. I love this place and I pray it stays open for generations! Please support Betty’s, share it via social media, word of mouth and bring any and everyone you love. They deserve every dollar and all the support in the world. This is and will always be my favorite place.

The location is not good, on a street with view of the cars but once inside the tiny restaurant is clean and cute.
The highlight is definitely John, the owner, attentve, polite, informative and with this great positive energy and greater smile.
Food did not disappoint, was fresh, delicius and tasted homemade. I will recommend it, you don’t have to be Ethiopian to love this genuine food. Taste the love they put in to prepare it. Will be back 🤩

formatted_address: 1743 Colorado Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90041, United States
name: Aunt Yvette’s Kitchen

reviews.text:
Wow, I wanted to love this place. The beautiful decorations and authentic-looking china made me feel like I was about to have a five-star Ethiopian meal.

I've been touring the country in search of the best Ethiopian restaurants; especially those that blend rich traditional flavors with gentle, balanced spices that are kind to the digestive system. I love Ethiopian cuisine for how vibrant yet comforting it can be, so I was eager to experience this restaurant's unique take on it.

Let's start with the positives:
Vegan Combo:
Both the gluten and gluten-free injera were beautifully made. The regular version (with a bit of barley) was still light and flavorful, while the gluten-free injera had that nostalgic sour tang I adore. The gomen was the standout dish of the night; cooked with kale, onion, and just the right touch of garlic, giving it that perfect al dente texture I love.

The alicha (yellow split peas) and atkilt (cabbage and carrots) were okay but a bit heavy on turmeric and jalapeño for my taste. I've never had atkilt quite so spicy before, so it caught me off guard. The yam/potato/carrot mix leaned a bit strong on chili powder, which overpowered the natural flavor of the vegetables. The Ethiopian salad was fresh but mild -- I found myself wishing for more beets to balance the plate.

The tofu tibs, which the waiter kindly suggested, didn't quite work for me. The seasoning was very subtle; I expected the deeper flavor profile typical of berbere or awaze-style tibs.
