The restaurant describes itself as "upscale and trendy," and that feels accurate. This isn't a traditional take- it's more of a modern or fusion interpretation of Ethiopian food. If that's what you're looking for, you'll likely enjoy the creativity and presentation here.

Time and again a stunning gourmet experience. This time with out of continent guests who equally indulged into the feast. Only criticism on that day (10-12-2025) was that the male waiter’s charm and attentiveness was rather missing. Asking 3 times for additional injera seemed was just the dot on the i.

PREVIOUS REVIEW
An absolutely stunning experience! From the start when we arrived for our reservation and were told to be brought in when the table was ready. Very cute and appeasing interior – almost ready to meditate.  Yvette herself and her staff all charming, knowledgeable and a pleasure to chat with.
Okay that in itself was wonderful, but the food including the starter tea and the dessert ice cream were simply virtuoso!!!
So glad to have Auntie Y in our neighborhood, definitely asks for coming back …

(Originally posted by me on yelp)

Aunt Yvette’s Kitchen is truly one of a kind and easily the best Ethiopian restaurant I’ve ever experienced.
From the moment we arrived, everything felt authentic and welcoming. The food was absolutely outstanding—rich in flavor, organic, fresh, and clearly prepared with passion and care. I’ve been to many Ethiopian restaurants over the years, but nothing comes close to the quality and depth of flavor here. Every dish told a story of tradition and craftsmanship.
The coffee deserves special recognition. It was my first time trying Ethiopian coffee with black seed. I usually drink regular coffee, but this was on another level—smooth, natural, incredibly flavorful, and surprisingly healthy. It wasn’t just a drink, it was an experience.
Our server, Samer, made the visit even more special. He was knowledgeable, patient, and genuinely passionate about Ethiopian cuisine. He explained each dish in detail and helped us understand the culture behind the food, which made the meal even more meaningful. We also tried the dessert with berbere—unforgettable and easily the best Ethiopian dessert I’ve ever had.
This place is more than a restaurant; it’s an experience you remember. Highly recommended to anyone who appreciates authentic food, great service, and something truly special. I will definitely be coming back.

My girlfriend and I took her parents for dinner on a Saturday night. Making a reservation is necessary since it’s a small restaurant so I was glad we did. We were seated right away and the service was excellent. I appreciated the elevated experience with the rose water to cleanse my hands, and the attentive bar and wait staff. We shared the vegan combo for four and ordered a beef protein. I found the food to be incredibly flavorful. Each dish was completely different than the next and it was great to have a unique bite every time. I appreciate the chef’s ability to take traditional Ethiopian dishes/cooking and add her own uniqueness. I’m excited to try other menu items next time.

Beautiful venue. Warm. Stylish. Intimate. The ambiance is lovely.

The food was very good. So many vegan options! I appreciated the variety of flavors and options. Im looking forward to bringing people to try this spot.

formatted_address: 1068 N Citrus Ave, Covina, CA 91722, United States
name: GS Cafe and Ethiopian Cuisine

reviews.text:
As someone who’s passionate about clean eating and mindful of digestive health, I’m always looking for restaurants that balance authenticity with freshness and care. My visit to GS Cafe was a wonderful experience that checked many of those boxes.

I ordered the veggie platter, which came with great portion sizes and fresh ingredients enough for a 2 or 3 more meals! The injera appeared to have some barley mixed with teff, so while it wasn’t entirely gluten-free (as other reviewers mentioned), it was still light, fluffy, and beautifully made. I did miss a bit of that traditional sour tang, but it was clear that real attention went into its preparation.

The Key Sir (beets) were the star of the show — tender, perfectly cooked, and incredibly flavorful. Honestly, it was the best beet dish I’ve ever had.
The Misir Wot (red lentils) was surprisingly mild — a thoughtful touch for those sensitive to spice like me. The entire platter leaned toward a gentler spice profile than most of the 50+ platters I’ve tried over the years, but the staff provided traditional spice mix on the side, which was a lovely option for those wanting an extra kick.

The Gomen (greens) had more of a creamed-collard texture than the al dente style I prefer, but it was still well-seasoned. The Fasolia (string beans) and Atkilt (cabbage and carrots) were cooked nicely, though a touch on the oily side — not enough to upset my stomach, but it could be lighter.

And wow! the Ethiopian smoothie was a beautiful surprise! A refreshing blend of avocado, mango, and strawberry, it struck the perfect balance of sweet, fresh, and hearty.

The staff were outstanding; kind, welcoming, and clearly proud of their food. The young man who served me had such a positive attitude that it genuinely added to the warmth of the meal.

Overall, GS Cafe is an excellent choice for those trying Ethiopian food for the first time or for anyone seeking authentic flavors served in a gentle, stomach-friendly way.

I seriously loved this meal! It was super filling. I also really appreciate the tiny details like the eating instructions. I have had some eating restrictions and the staff were kind and understanding of that, did not question my reasons. Would definitely come back!

Meal was a little pricier cause I got a drink but the Beef and Veggie combo platter is so filling it makes for a great dish to split. The flavor is very home-y.

I had a wonderful experience at GS Cafe and Ethiopian Cuisine! The food was rich with flavor and beautifully spiced, especially the injera and the veggie combo — so satisfying and authentic. The atmosphere was warm and welcoming, and the staff made us feel right at home. It’s a hidden gem for anyone craving delicious Ethiopian food in a relaxed setting. Highly recommend!

Absolutely fantastic food! I’ve been here countless times over the past couple of years and am constantly recommending it to friends. All of their meats and veggie dishes are great, and their tea is fantastic! Lots of people come for the honey wine, but I think the tea is even better!
This place is unassuming from the outside but is POPULAR (rightly so). I recommend getting here right when they open for their lunch or dinner hours to guarantee a taste. They sell out sometimes, so no guarantees if you get there at the end of the day. It’s also a smaller team, typically just the chef and the server (who is super sweet), so bring your patience with your appetite, I promise it will be worth it!

As someone who grew up in Ethiopia, I know what authentic Ethiopian food should taste like — and let me tell you, GS Café and Ethiopian Cuisine absolutely nails it. From the very first bite, my taste buds started doing the boogie-woogie and flip-flops right in the middle of my mouth. That’s how you know it’s the real deal!

Every dish bursts with rich, traditional flavor that instantly takes me back home. The injera is perfectly soft and tangy, the wot is seasoned to perfection, and the aroma alone could make you hungry all over again.

Honestly, I don’t even bother going to Little Ethiopia anymore — Covina has officially taken over. The food is incredible, the atmosphere is warm and welcoming, and the people behind this place are just as awesome as the food they serve.

If you’re looking for authentic Ethiopian cuisine made with love, GS Café is the spot. Absolute perfection — a true five-star-plus experience!

formatted_address: 1212 S Dale Ave, Anaheim, CA 92804, United States
name: Beteseb Ethio-Eritrean Restaurant

reviews.text:
Trying out this place since our old favorite has since closed after many years (Tana).
Came in the afternoon and there was no wait.
Got the vegetables platter which had split pea, puréed red bean, lentils, sautéed cabbage. Doro wot is a chicken stew with a hard boiled egg added. This dish was very satisfying.
The raw kitfo or beef tartare with butter and spices was also good but just a different flavor profile from what our family has had in the past.
Injera is also quite delicious, but charges for extra.
Coffee was smooth and so good, although was served without the usual ceremonial roasting and grinding.

I love this restaurant! The food is excellent, healthy, and rich in flavor. The flavors and textures are unlike any I’ve tasted in other cuisines. Delicious!

The family that runs this restaurant is absolutely wonderful. Rarely have I experienced such warmth and hospitality in a restaurant. They truly make you feel at home. Highly recommend!

This place is so good at the flavors it offers & the price! We got the key wot and vegetarian combo plate, with the tea at the end. Everything tasted great

The owner, who rang us up, was so sweet & welcoming.

Compared to prices in Little Ethiopia in LA, this was well priced. Cost us about $60 for everything with tax/tip

A must have if you’re in the area

Extremely friendly staff! Great food! It takes a bit of time to prepare so just be aware of that as everything is made very fresh! Inside of place is nice and clean. Went on a Sunday with my spouse and son. Would definitely go back to eat here. Also, portions are large so you could share one or two plates with three to four people easily.

So we paid 60$ total (including tip) for a combined veggie and key wot platter!!

The food was soooo nummy-licious. I say that as a foodie who loves spicy food, flavors, and texture. The service was so amazing, me and my friend went around 7pm on a Wednesday so it was mostly empty but the guy who works there (I presume the owner) was super kind and generous. The beef stew in the center was super delicious and spicy. I really enjoyed the collared greens, they had a slight sour flavor as well as the yellow veggies (idk what they are) but they had a pickled flavor to them and it was amazing. There were 3 types of lentils, all differing in flavor, my favorite were the green ones. The orange-brown paste were chickpeas, they were good too. The cheese was okay, it honestly just tasted like cheese.

If you’re not a foodie or into spicy or sour foods then maybe the veggie platter and the spicy beef aren’t for you, my friend didn’t like the strong flavors as much as I did.

But I definitely think it’s worth the try!! I’ll definitely be going again.

formatted_address: 18764 Pioneer Blvd, Artesia, CA 90701, United States
name: Awaze Ethio Fusion & Vegan Restaurant

reviews.text: Absolutely a must try!!! Sweet staff and beautiful decor. Dont let the outside fool you THIS IS A GEM! This was my wife's first time trying Ethiopian food and she loved everything. I did too. We got appetizers amd the veggie sampler. We could not finish it all it was so much and so good. Also so affordable. I WILL BE BACK!!

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ The best Ethiopian restaurant I’ve ever been to.
It was such a special experience
everything from the warm atmosphere to the food felt authentic and full of heart

I ordered the chicken and a vegan dish, and both were absolutely perfect.
The coffee ceremony was unforgettable
rich, bold, and truly one of the best coffees I’ve ever tasted ☕️

The restaurant is spotless, the guests are kind, and the owner is one of the sweetest people I’ve met.
It felt like being welcomed into someone’s home rather than just a restaurant

My friend was so touched by the experience that he actually started learning Amharic after our visit — that’s how inspiring it was 🌿
Can’t wait to visit again soon. Thank you for such a beautiful experience

My partner and my favorite date night restaurant. Always delicious and kind with fantastic service. The food is delicious and authentic. I can not overstate how much we recommend it.
My only regret is taking too long to write this review. Every time I leave I'm in a food coma from stuffing my face, and I forget. NOT TODAY! They're the best!

It was Saturday afternoon, and it wasn't crowded. Since it was our first time trying Ethiopian food, we got the $55 platter. It was so good! I was reading about their "injera" made from teff, which is like our "dosa" made from rice back in India.
The platter was awesome and delicious. Maybe the portion size could be a bit bigger because it's supposed to serve 3-4 people. It filled us up, and there were only two of us. I definitely recommend it as a restaurant in Artesia, and we'll go back.
I had delicious vegetarian lunch here. Atmosphere is very nice and hostess was very friendly. This place has best honey wine. Parking is also not a problem.

formatted_address: 630 N La Brea Ave #103, Inglewood, CA 90302, United States
name: planet Ethiopia & Mediterranean Restaurant.

reviews.text: I’m a little late but I came and ate here on 6/26/25. I just want to start off by saying I was a little worried when I approached. But after walking in and being introduced I quickly came comfortable. A woman runs this business and makes all her meals from scratch. If you’re in a hurry this place isn’t for you. She takes her time and delivers her meals with pride. I would highly recommend this place if you’re wanting to try something new and authentic. I will definitely be back. #CameFromOhio
My go to spot. This visit was a little disappointing. Food was bland. Customer service was amazing. Been there several times, but this visit wasn't a good one.

The vibe is very welcoming. The owner and staff friendly. The food is very organic and fresh and made to order. The coffee is hand roasted beans and tea is fresh and not sure with a tea bag..
You must experience this one of a kind
East Africa and Mediterranean cuisine.
Amazing

Charming little restaurant with very welcoming owners greeting us with Ethiopian coffee in beautiful cups.   Food was delicious! Thank you for a lovely experience and the gift for my mother.  ❤️

For those with allergies,  the owner/ chef is very attentive. 💫

This is very delicious food I ever eat  so yummy and very cleanest restaurant I ever seen in LA please come and visit you’re not gonna disappointed over this. I mean it. I even celebrate Valentine’s Day here so beautiful so clean so enjoyable Place  come visit you’ll enjoy it.

formatted_address: 3182 W Pico Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90019, United States
name: Melkam Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: Ethiopian food is my favorite and I have tried most Ethiopian restaurants in the LA area. Washington DC still has the best Ethiopian food I have tried  but this restaurant has consistent good food. I have tried a few different cooks here and the flavor changes a bit but it has always been good. Better to call in your order ahead. You can eat in since there’s always space because most customers just do pick up orders but right now is not the nicest place for a dinner date.

CASH ONLY as of this writing.

Food is very good, the staff friendly.  I ordered the seasoned beef (yeawaze tibs) and vegetable combo which was served on a large plate over a large piece of bread very similar to a fluffy crepe.  It is also served with a side of the bread (injera, 30% barley 70% "teff") which you tear off and use to grab pieces of meat and veggies (Lentils, cabbage and carrots, spinach greens).  If you're traditional you use only your bare right hand to eat with, which can be a bit off putting for some but it's how it's done.  Just wash your hands before and after in the very basic facilities.

The flavors are all there, about as authentic as you can get them in So Cal.  The atmosphere is about as close to what you might get sitting at a small cafe in Addis Ababa too.  Well seasoned food with a variety of flavors.  There is also a lot of food, and after ordering the two dishes I ended up taking him about half of it even with two people eating.

This is a very small restaurant, blink and you'll miss it kind of establishment with no dedicated parking, just street park where you can.  Inside the place is a very tiny main dining area (1 four top, 1 two top) and what looks like a larger social room but only for sitting on the floor (reserved or dedicated?).  I didn't really get the impression that being a restaurant was their main focus, as the kitchen was far bigger than the dining room (I think they make the specialty bread and sell it as a big part of their income).

I really enjoyed the experience, the very homestyle feeling of the place like you're walking into someone's home.  For some people the whole no frills experience might be a huge turnoff, but it was definitely not for me.  I concede it was odd to see a very limited selection of bottled beverages in a cooler that wasn't chilled, so I can understand why some people might not care for it.  For me though, it's discovering these kinds of little places that make me wish I had infinite Time, a vast budget, and a bottomless stomach.
Arrived to the store empty and waited patiently to be waited on only to be told they are not serving food and would not take my order despite restaurant hours
It says Open on Maps but it was not at 6pm on a Monday

4:30pm. Doors open but no food. Nothing to serve. Parking is non-existent. I'm stumped. She just waved us off "no, no no".
She wouldn't answer when there would be food. I was really looking forward to it too.

formatted_address: 1032 S Fairfax Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90019, United States
name: E & M Cafe

reviews.text: They let me have the ceiling fans

formatted_address: 1043 S Fairfax Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90019, United States
name: Marathon

reviews.text:
WOW !!! I’ve driven passed this place a lot and always wanted to try. And one word; WOW! I ordered off postmates today and decided on marathon as I had a complicated order, and no other restaurant could fulfill it. Dude from the restaurant called me & went above and beyond to make sure everything was perfect!!! Such a sweet soul. The food was INSANE! So good!

Also random side note; My boyfriend has stuffed sinuses but is sensitive to ultra-spice, and the food was just palatable spice level for them & cleared their sinuses entirely!!! THEY STILL NOT SNIFFLING AS I WRITE THIS A FEW HOURS LATER!!!

This is the SPOT !!

I went out with my family for some Ethiopian food but the people who work there were very rude and unwelcoming. The waiters didn’t greet us or smiled at all actually they gave us nasty look. I was as shocked at how they handled their customers. The food was terrible too. It was so old and greasy. When the waitress came back to our table again to tell us that other customers are waiting that we should hurry up. We got up and left. I have never saw such a disrespect and nasty behavior like that in my life. Horrible customer service and disgusting food. Please don’t ever try to go to their restaurant you definitely regret it. Save yourself some time.

Horrible customer service. One of my Ethiopian associates reported that the management of this facility became hostile and yelled at her because she requested a song from an artist that's from a different ethnicity (Oromo) than the management's. How can an establishment be so rude and discriminatory to their own customers especially ones that come from their own country. How ethnocentric! I also was told several times that the staff allegedly can't keep up with the infestations they have to tackle.

Never will eat there again and 10/10 do not recommend

This is the most overlooked restaurant in Little Ethiopia! My friends and I come to this restaurant on almost a weekly basis and we love it! It doesn't have the ambiance of the other restaurants but if you just want authentic Ethiopian food this is the spot! The Awaze Tibbs is excellent and so is the Kitfo. In terms of pricing is by far the most reasonably priced out of all the restaurants in the area. My friends and I usually spend around $10 per person here while the restaurant next door will charge you $14-17 for similar dishes. Don't be fooled by the the partially defective door and lack of decor, it's an authentic excellent restaurant!

I had the tsome firfir. It should be called Kar. Kar is Ethiopian word for heart burn.

Food was delicious. However, it’s too oily. Hope the restaurant finds another way to flavor food.

formatted_address: 339 N Fairfax Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90036, United States
name: Annie's Soul Delicious

reviews.text:
I decided to visit this restaurant due to a Instagram post that was a very convincing so I ordered barbecue chicken mac and cheese collard greens and Black Eyed Peas. They were quite busy Sunday afternoon so I understand why they took a little while than usual maybe? I ordered takeout so as I was waiting the waitress she gave me a free side of fried okra and banana pudding, which was really nice of her.
I do recommend the mac and cheese and collard greens. Unfortunately my barbecue chicken was undercooked and my banana pudding was okay it was more pudding than banana and cookie but still delicious. Overall decent experience, worth a dine in next time..

I would always order on door dash years ago I finally got to sit in the restaurant and it was worth it. Food was really good. The greens and yams stole the show. The oxtails were small but very good. The food was a little pricey for the small amount of meat. the staff was very friendly  and

I visited Annie’s Soul Delicious last night and had such a great first experience! We were seated right away, and the staff was extremely friendly and attentive. The owner personally greeted us and even checked on us during our meal — she’s very hands-on and clearly passionate about her restaurant. Multiple staff members stopped by as well to make sure everything was going smoothly, and the bathrooms were clean, which is always a plus.

Now for the food — I ordered the 8-piece wings (half Classic, half Hennessy) and loved that you get three sides, which makes it plenty of food for the price. The wings had great flavor and came out piping hot since everything is cooked fresh to order. My only small note is to ask for your wings “fried hard/well” if you prefer a crispier texture like I do. That’s the only reason I’m knocking off a star because I didn’t get to fully enjoy them due to the texture. The couple wings I did get to eat were packed with flavor, and I’ll definitely be ordering them again — just fried hard next time!

The sides were incredible — the yams, mac and cheese, and collard greens were all packed with flavor and tasted homemade. We went around 5:30 p.m., and while it was busy, there were still seats available.

Overall, the food, service, and atmosphere were all excellent. I’ll definitely be back again and again. Wishing them much continued success — they truly deserve it!

We absolutely loved our experience at Annie’s. We was visiting all the way from London, and wanted to try soul food for the first time. We was told we’d wait an hour but ended up being half that, and it was so worth the wait. We loved most of the dishes and we tried almost everything. We were suprised how much we enjoyed it all, we understand the hype now. Our waitress was also amazing, I’m not sure what her name was but she was half Arabic. Genuine and kind and made our experience 5/5. Would recommend to everyone 💕💕

First time visiting the area and HAD to stop at one of the premier soul food restaurants in Los Angeles. The oxtail, Hennessy wings and lemonade concoctions were standouts! Our server was especially welcoming and even sung us a little song before bidding us a farewell. Special shout out to Eddie as he was always on point.

formatted_address: 1032 S Fairfax Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90019, United States
name: Paradocs Coffee & Tea

reviews.text: This place is a hidden gem! The owner is very knowledgeable about everything he serves and the proper way to make it. The vibes are cozy with nice jazz music and a rustic feel, and the pastries super fresh.  The matcha latte I ordered was on point. Great spot

I’ve been coming here for years. Taka (the owner) makes the best coffee in LA at shockingly affordable prices. The vibe is excellent and Taka cares a lot about quality and taking care of his customers. His wife bakes the pastries which are also delicious. My favorite cafe anywhere

Hidden gem tucked in Little Ethiopia. Small venue with 3 tables and a few extra seating. Great coffee roasts that rotate throughout the month, so it’s nice to try different demographics of coffee beans. Croissant and baked goods are displayed in the front with a nice varietal. Definitely try the most popular: Ethiopia Yigacheffe or the Tanzania Kilimanjaro!

I’m always searching for new coffee shops in LA and this was a gem! There was a line of people waiting for it to open, so I knew it was legit. One of the best spots I’ve tried. It was GOOD. Had to give 5 stars for the barista who was taking orders AND making coffee quick and seamlessly. I tried the white chocolate latte and matcha croissant. I’m a fan! My only disappointment was that they didn’t have any of the breakfast items I was interested in like the bacon sandwich or chicken panini… only what was shown in the cases. I’ll definitely come back! Ambiance reminded me of a coffee shop in NY. No frills, not overdone but delivers.  Exactly what I need in my life. Also affordable and not overpriced in my opinion.

Great spot ! Kind of a hidden gem, the pastries are next level good. I ordered the pumpkin croissant and it was moist, flaky and  so good. Also got a latte which is hard to beat at this price, also good. They have a couple unique lattes and pastry options a few seats inside and the service was fast and friendly. Recommend stopping by

formatted_address: 1046 S Fairfax Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90019, United States
name: injera.com market

formatted_address: 508 Santa Monica Blvd, Santa Monica, CA 90401, United States
name: BERBERE by T&T Lifestyle

reviews.text:
First time my sisters and I experienced Ethiopian food and boy am I a fanatic .
The wish meal was a beautiful sentiment for our sister trip, Symbol of Love and Togetherness. The unique flavors of each meal was tasteful and welcomed, many warm and one cold .
Being a smoothie lover I am, these smoothies were delicious soothing I will say the blackberry superfood was my favorite too the breakfast smoothie.
The plant burger definitely has a quick if great but the wedge potatoes went well with tit. I definitely want to come back and gobble the oyster mushroom pizza.😍
The atmosphere was gorgeous; we sat by the window for am indoor outdoor vibe. Tarp ceilings, natural light and plants love made the ambiance welcoming.

Vegan!  ethio fusion! Fresh/organic! Great spot to have a lunch meeting-eat well and have a robust conversation! Great ambiance and decor. Friendly, professional staff . Easy parking in the back. Food is flavorful , creative and colorful. The portions are just right-you feel satisfied and light, food is not heavy, greasy or bloat inducing. Yay! A true happy meal.

the reviews do not lie, an incredible Ethiopian restaurant that is also all plant based. extremely delicious from start to finish (recommend the wish plate to share and dessert as well). friendly servers and an overall great experience, highly recommend!

I can’t say enough good things about this restaurant. T&T have done an absolutely phenomenal job making food come to life. You can taste the love and intention put into every single dish. I stopped here while visiting Santa Monica and it was so good, we came two days in a row. The Plant Burger, Eat the Rainbow and the Tacos were outstanding. The spices and flavors are so good! The service was also excellent. My friend and I came here for Sunday brunch; I had the pancakes, and she got the burger. I tried everything. 😂 I LOVED my pancakes, which came with potatoes and tofu scramble. Her burger was also amazing.

The service was great, and the staff was friendly. Prices were reasonable and it didn't take a long time for food to come out. I'd suggest this place and look forward to trying more Ethiopian food to learn about this part of the culture

Food is great. The service is excellent. Atmosphere is comfortable.

Lamb tibs, firfir , kitfo minced beef w chili powder.

formatted_address: 15040 Valley Blvd, Fontana, CA 92335, United States
name: Fontana Somali Restaurant

reviews.text: It is literally the BEST BOLD FLAVOR FOOD!! It’s first time I came out was because of curiosity, when I type food with rice and this place pops up.. not gonna lie when my mom and I first came it was a bit “sketchy” because the place is small and the lady said “this is not Mexican food” so I told her I am aware and just want to try new food, she was so sweet she was giving my boys free drinks while waiting for the food and when I mention I want spicy she would do it and fix the flavor as she goes, she ask me to try it until it’s up to my spicy level! my third time coming over here, it’s still the best, I always get the goat with rice but today they let me try the noodle, it’s the same.. BOMB!!! My meals always come with a banana and a drink which is awesome!! They’re really friendly with their customers and kids!!! It’s a really small “to go” place but you can eat there if you like.. I’m gonna super sad if they move!! Because IE would miss out on super flavorful food!! For $20 I think they give humongous amounts of food!! Oh forgot to mention that GREEN SPICY SAUCE.. I could literally request to get it in a jar!! They’re the best!!! I am Indonesians I think their food is perfect with my palate ☺️

This restaurant is amazing! The food is so tasty and full of flavor. I loved the rice, pasta, fish, and goat, everything was cooked just right. The goat was super tender, and the fish had great seasoning.
If you’ve never tried Somali food before, you should definitely come here. I’ll be coming back for sure!
The food is great the flavor also great but please the salt is a bit too much it’s my second time eating at this restaurant
Loved it here! Definitely coming back again! Food was 10/10 and service was 10/10
Don't let the aesthetics fool you from quality food.

formatted_address: 5510 Cherokee Ave, Alexandria, VA 22312, United States
name: African Chop Better ACB-LLC

reviews.text: First time eating from here I ordered a large cassava leaf and rice it was good just wish it was a little more spicy & also if they could have gave me more food if I ordered a large. Only thing I didn't like is I had a big chunk of meat in my food but I will come back & try again. Customer service was 10/10 ordered it over the phone & it was ready for pick up when I arrived.
Oxtail stew and jollof rice was good. Just wish I got more than three oxtail. Also, I ordered a fresh pressed orange juice and received a Tropicana juice instead

The food was absolutely delicious!!! We ordered the spinach and egusi stew, peanut butter soup, and oxtail stew, they were all 10/10!!!! The service was incredible too, the staff was very welcoming and kind. Great spot!!!!
I just finished getting a haircut in the building and came across this African cuisine spot. I ordered the Oxtail, Beef stew and Jollof rice. The food was very delicious, I will be coming back!
Food was amazing. Goat Fufu was my favorite because the goat was so tender and the soup base had a nice spicy kick to it. Owners were very nice as well. Highly recommend!

formatted_address: 2322 El Cajon Blvd, San Diego, CA 92104, United States
name: Flavors of East Africa

reviews.text:
I came to Flavors of East Africa today for the first time years. I brought my folks with me because they’ve never had East African food. Overall the experience was awesome and just as good as I remember from years back!

We ordered sweet jerked chicken, Kuku curry chicken, fried eggplant, plus two types of rice, collard greens, and mashed potatoes. Of course, these side items all have African names but for the sake of clarity I’ve written out their nearest English adjacent dish titles.

The chicken in both dishes was absolutely incredible! It tasted like it had been stewing for hours. The flavors were deep, aromatic, and memorable. It’s hard to choose a favorite between the two chicken dishes, but the jerked chicken’s sauce was incredible…at the same time, the chicken breast in the curry was extremely succulent and had a coconut-y vibe.

The veggies and rice were all pretty tasty as well, with the mashed potatoes and eggplant being highlights. The eggplant’s tomato relish topping is a little oily, so it pairs better with some rice. The turmeric & ginger juice I had was also delightful—they added some sugar or honey to it so it wasn’t extremely overpowering.

All in all, I definitely recommend Flavors of East Africa. It’s a really high-quality, consistent spot for amazing meat dishes—including oxtails, stewed beef, goat curry, and more—and it isn’t overpriced for the portion and level of craftsmanship they bring.

P.S. If you’re looking for a slightly cheaper version of the same great food, come anytime before 5pm to get access to the lunch combos, which bring the same punch for $3-5 less per plate.

Ann was so hospitable and the food and service were great! We tried the lunch combinations so we were able to try 3 types of chicken, beef, 4 veggies, all 3 rice and ugali. Lots of food for the money. We enjoyed sitting outside on a beautiful day.

The food tastes great, very well flavored. And the lunch portion was overflowing my plate. I ordered the spicy jerk chicken, beef stew, coconut rice, fried plantain, and eggplant. They gave me a sample of the ugali, which was delicious with the stews. I would definitely come back.

Ive been coming here now for 3 years, and every time, without fail, my meal has been fresh, flavorful, and fricken delicious. If youre vegan/vegetarian and you haven't tried this place, get off your ass and come check it out. Such a highlight in my life and I hope they never ever close.

We didn't go to the restaurant but we had their food at the Ocean Beach Farmers Market and it was INCREDIBLE. We had decent portions of both the sweet and the spicy (level 4 out of 10) jerk chicken, a bunch of different rices, collard greens, and fried plantains (oh the plantains...!). Highly recommend their food!

formatted_address: 25195 Desert Sage Dr, Menifee, CA 92586, United States
name: Tonge's Taste

reviews.text: The best Egusi and Okra soup ever and the sweetest lady making them! Definitely will be ordering again(:
Wow this food was great! Egusi, jollof rice, the puff puffs were all top tier. So far the best I've had in SoCal.

The food was good and hot. My mother had I had a good time eating and small talk. The atmosphere is a drive up to the home and let them know you are there. My food was not ready when I arrived. I had to wait an extra 20 minutes. I can say it was worth the wait. I will order again. I don't eay spicy foods, this right here was worth all the spiciness. My taste buds where very happy!!

This place is beyond amazing!! I have been searching everywhere for the authenticity and flavor Tonge's Taste has and provides, prices are great, Portions are generous.. you can literally taste the smell of the food before opening it. . and the spiciness is just right. Most definitely gained a loyal customer here, been here twice this week and will definitely be returning again .Thank you Tonge's! For your delicious food and amazing and accommodating service!

The fufu and egusi was a life altering experience, I have never tasted something so delicious! The egusi was the perfect amount of heat and had a rich amazing flavor, the fufu was the perfect texture too! 10/10 I had to come back today and try something new, the egusi I had yesterday was so good I’m definitely going to be an often reoccurring customer!

formatted_address: 952 4th St, Laurel, MD 20707, United States
name: Pleroma Cuisine

reviews.text: WOW! From the minute we walked in, it got better by the minute. Not only you walk into a very nice place but the service from the host, the waiter, the bartender and at the end the chef himself was excellent! The food was EXCELLENT; the flavors, the temperature of the food, it was just amazing! I ordered the spicy goat soup (and I love my food spicy) and I have to say, it has been the best goat I have ever had; it was an experience of flavors! We are only here for just two nights and have plans for tomorrow’s dinner but I’ll cancel and will comeback here as the menu is so expensive and everything looks great!

I visited the restaurant couple months ago ordering Jollof rice with fried fish, both flavors were amazing, I was totally impressed, especially it's my first time trying African food. And so recently I came back for to-go order, Whole Fried Red Snapper with Jollof Rice, with a high expectation that it'll taste as good as before, but it was such a big letdown. The jollof rice wasn't as good, in fact it didn't taste good at all, it was a bit off-taste, dominated by tomato sauce without any flavor and spiciness of habanero (which I really like from my previous experience), and clumpy. The fish was ok, but for $26 meal, the fish size shouldn't be this small (did not look like the menu photo in their website at all). Tbh, it's the worst $26 meal I've ever had. I arrived at the restaurant a little bit over one hour after their opening time but it was weird (and creepy) to find the restaurant was totally dark, no lights, nobody, as if it's not on business yet. I was standing there for a moment until the server brought my food out (from and to the darkness..). I've never been in a restaurant with this situation before. And it's not Halloween season. Anyway, I hope they can improve, but that will be my last time ordering food here.

The atmosphere was atmosphering, the vibes was vibing, the pammy was palming, if I had ordered the snapper, I'm sure that it would have been snapping. This spot was worth every dime spent.

I enjoyed everything that I ate and drank here. I recommend this spot to everyone that appreciates good things. My favorite bite was the spicy goat meat that I had as an appetizer.

Bathrooms were extra clean, staff get an extra 🌟 for customer service. I need the palm wine they serve here in my city!

From The Beautiful Decor, Flavorful Mocktails…To The Delicious Appetizers…Pleroma Cuisine’s Amazing Chef/Owner Bianka Made Sure Our Son & His Girlfriend’s Twin Baby Girls Shower Was Magical! …🥰🫶🏽💞💝 Please Treat Yourself With Indulging At Their Restaurant…You WON’T Be Disappointed & Can Thank Me Later!😊😋😋❤️

Amazing Experience at Pleroma Cuisine!

I had such a wonderful experience dining at Pleroma Cuisine! The food was absolutely delicious—fresh, flavorful, and beautifully prepared. Every dish brought the true taste of African cuisine to life. You can tell the chefs put so much care and authenticity into every meal.

The atmosphere was warm and inviting, and the staff was friendly, helpful, and made me feel right at home. It’s the kind of place that makes you want to come back again and again.

If you’re looking for great food and an unforgettable dining experience, I highly recommend Pleroma Cuisine. It’s truly a hidden. We will be back ❤️❤️❤️❤️

name: Calabash African Kitchen

reviews.text: Food is amazing! The best goat pepper I had! Snapper was scrumptious! First time ever having oxtail soup and don’t know how I have lived without it. We also had the chicken empanadas but wasn’t able to get a picture before we dug in. They were so good! Drinks are amazing! I highly recommend the Lemon Sip! The Royal Flush and Sideways Baobab were also delicious. Wonderful service!

My Nigerian husband and I visit Vegas quite a lot for work and have been on the hunt for a Nigerian spot. Our search is over! The egusi was FANTASTIC and the service was even better. Afrobeats playing, Nigerian beer and good vibes. Will be back for sure

If I could give ten stars, I would. Everything was phenomenal, from the service to the food. Our server, Nyla was beyond amazing as she provided some helpful information about some of the menu items and made some excellent recommendations. The Oxtail stew was so flavorful, and it was so good, that I was scraping the bowl after I was finished. This is needs to be on everyone's LV bucket list.

Delicious West African food. Well seasoned and flavorful. We had meatpies, the jollof with chicken, attieke with fish and oxtail with rice and I have nothing bad to say about any of them. The two cons is the wait time for the food to be served; but the wait is worth it for sure. Also the food is pretty pricey.

My experience at calabash was 8/10
The food was good and the service was really good too. I went there with my friends that come from Swiss for a work conference and they loved all the food. The only thing for me they sells empty jellof rice for $21 and sell meats separately $8 or so while on the menu they are vegetables and fish or meat but when it served it some how different. Too pricey. I recommend this place. Have lots of money in the bank lol

name: Mama Wale's Rice

reviews.text: I've ordered online from this restaurant a long time ago and everything was great but tonight when I came in person at the mall the portions were terrible!! literally barely half of the container of egusi. I don't know why they thought that was okay there's more fufu than the egusi. I'm hesitant to come back now

Been watching YouTube on all food experiences. Honestly I got more rice and had to take little bites of the meat. And she asked me if I wanted a 2 or 5 dollar FuFu and didn’t get either and was charged so I didn’t get the full exercise. Side of egusi as well. She was alone and I think she needs more help. I’m going to try them again and be honest as I am now. Happy New Year’s

I have never had Nigerian food before this and it was so delicious that I am searching for other places where I live. The spicy egusi and salmon hit the spot. I also loved the drink that starts with a "z" but can't remember the name. We sampled the rice and next time I'll get that too. The staff was friendly and patiently answered all my questions. I liked that they gave samples too because I would have had no idea what to get.

Imma just say this… if they aren’t African it ain’t even worth the drive… I literally drove two hours for this mess I called multiple times to assure they had okra stew I get here she had enough for a half a four oz container that was reheated in the microwave… my egusi was just warm I’m pretty sure in the temp danger zone… the goat was tough as jerky… now I’m waiting 15 mins for okra… I’ve been to the location when it was a restaurant which is why I took the time to come here… I’m so disappointed in this mall service mess… it’s definitely fallen off since I had it last… I won’t be back I promise
The food and service were very enjoyable. So much flavor!! Felt good after eating, I definitely will be back.

formatted_address: 1725 I St, Sacramento, CA 95811, United States
name: AfroEatz - Authentic Liberian Food

reviews.text: Came here for husband’s 50th birthday (no reservations) and chef and staff were so kind and welcoming. They gave us these delicious beef pies on the house for his 50th!  We ordered fried tilapia with jollof rice, egusi with fufu, okra stew.  All of the dishes were delicious especially the fish!  Even the cabbage and plantain sides were yummy.

This was my first time having Liberian food and it was delicious! I got the chicken plate and it came with a very large portion of jollof rice, two types of cabbage and plantains that are so well done. It came with three pieces of chicken. My friend got the fish with plantains which was also seasoned really well. The service was great, they came to our table to check on us and bring napkins and utensils.
I took a video of the decor in the bathroom because it was so bright and colorful, love the vibe here! The ginger beer made in-house is the strongest I've tried.

This was out first time having Liberian food. The food was really good. You could tell everything was made to order with fresh ingredients. The meat pies are so good. They were so good, the table next to us asked us, "Is it that good???👁👄👁" 😂 I think the sound of us enjoying the meat pies caught their attention. There was a hot pepper sauce that was addicting. The service was great. The waiter was really nice and polite. We cant wait to go back, especially for those meat pies! 😅

Enjoyed the Liberian / West African cuisine.  The portions of rice was very hardy and complimented with veggies. The FuFu was very nice and eaten with the soup.  We had a couple of chicken entrees and the spices quite unique and very tasty.  Staff was very friendly and service excellent.  The artwork was bright and happy.
Amazing experience. The cassava leaf was off the roof. It's the only Liberian dish I eat without guilt. The atmosphere is clean and quiet. Staff very respectful and neat

formatted_address: 5730 N First St #108/109, Fresno, CA 93710, United States
name: Triumph African Restaurant & Market

reviews.text:
Leave your Western culture at home when you walk into this restaurant. Be ready to not eat with utensils, having napkins, water. Be ready to eat with your fingers and a feel of African Culture 🤍🍽 Do not criticize this place if you cannot come in correct, knowing that this is a culture difference food experience.
I’ve been curious about Nigerian food and finally Googled this place, so glad I did! From the moment I walked in, I was amazed. The owner is incredible and the hospitality is unmatched. I tried the chicken dish, so flavorful, perfectly seasoned, and fresh, and the fufu is indescribable. I also had the Guinness Matilda drink, delicious!

The restaurant is a must try. I met people who drive hours just for this food. Be open minded, explore the flavors, and don’t miss it. Can’t wait to go back and try the okra dish. God bless this amazing lady and her restaurant, truly delicious!

My friends and I wanted to try Africa food for the first time. We tried the fufu and Egusi soup.  I was good! But what was so delicious in my opinion was the Joloff Rice with chicken. It was to die for. Not to mention the greens and fried plantains. The owner was super friendly. I will definitely return!

Been wanting to try the restaurant ever since it opened and I finally got a chance😍!

I ordered Pounded Yam with Egusi Soup and Goat Meat. When the food arrived I was thinking to ask for larger portion size, but after finishing was very glad I didn't. The pounded yam fills you up so much. My only thing I didn't like was that  it was so hot inside; cool air would of been so welcoming.

Nevertheless, I'll be coming back😁! Highly recommend
So good couldn’t get a picture before I ate it. Was my first time trying goat meat they didn’t disappoint. If you’re thinking about going, GO!

We had the strangest experience here. We walked into a dark dark restaurant seating area. No lights and it was dark outside and it smelled musty inside. A woman walked out and seemed surprised to see us. I asked if it was okay for five people to have dinner served. She gave us an odd look and said yes she was busy and would come back out in a few minutes. We waited for about 10 minutes and she did not reappear so we left. There was no one else in the restaurant. It had fairly good reviews though. Such a strange experience.

formatted_address: 409 Sawdust Rd, Spring, TX 77380, United States
name: OlaTee African Cafe

reviews.text: The question is who's Jollof is better? Nigerian, Liberian, or Ghanian, lol. First time    here and I'm also a Liberian. So...heard about this place long ago, but time wasn't on my side then. Of course all of Houston has many Nigerian restaurants, and all have             the same style cooking. But this place in Spring is amongst itself based on location. No too much competition. So I got dinner for tonight carryout. Jollof rice, the bigger portion, with two stew chicken portions for protein with gravy, and a side of spinach veges, plus plantains. I was craving this dish when I saw it on review. So for the taste...flavorful when you add it all together. Good dish. I will do this particular dish again. But probably dine-in on a good Saturday night to hear some afrobeats and feel cool vibes. Wall art are nice as well here. Will I try anything else on the menu in the future...only goat pepper soup. Why??? Because Nigerian's and Liberian's have same dish name but different taste. Not taking anything from no one's cooking, but Liberian Jollof is #1, more meat included and no sauce needed. So, 4 stars for my first time experiencing the food and service. The takeaway, meals aren't charged as one. Meats and sides are charge additional each.

This is by far one of the worst restaurants that sell African food in the whole of Texas. I’ve been consistently ordering from this place and  jollof rice with goat meat has always been my go to order but I usually get it via delivery with a piece of goat meat and chicken. This time I decided to get two pieces of goat meat and chicken but what was sent to me was ridiculous. The first goat meat was small which I was just going to ignore but the second was just a piece of BONE. I put a call through and whoever picked gave a silly response. It’s okay for your food to be pricey if it meets the standard but if you’re charging those prices but not delivering on quantity or quality then there’s an issue. This will be the last time I buy from you guys.

I originally came here to complain about a previous order where I was literally sent BONE instead of meat. I was given a number to call, but after calling multiple times with no response, I finally reached the owner today. Instead of apologizing, he immediately sounded skeptical and even implied that people “take advantage” of situations like this to get free replacements basically suggesting I was lying.

He then asked if I could delete my comment. I told him I would after the issue was properly resolved. He agreed and promised to replace the  BONE from my last order.

Based on that promise, I placed a new Uber Eats order for Jollof rice, Amala, with soup and assorted meats and chicken and I called him right after. He assured me everything would be taken care of. When my food arrived, nothing was corrected regarding my previous complaint, absolutely nothing. No replacement, no fix. When I called back, he claimed he “forgot” to tell his staff. Btw, this is a very laughable statement!

At this point, the dishonesty is obvious and i regret believing you the first time or even reaching out to you since you’re not even accountable.

I’m attaching a photo of the stale food I received today. (Yes! The Amala and soup was stale but the jollof was ok) This place does not care about customer satisfaction at all, they only care about their pockets and selfish interests. I spent almost 50 bucks on today’s order expecting the issue to be resolved, only to receive stale food and absolutely no correction at all. You care more about how people perceive your restaurant online but not willing to be accountable. Still the worst African restaurant in Texas, you’re never beating the allegations!!

Zero accountability!!!

As his wife, I want to clarify: You think we would spend $50 to fix a mistake that cost about $12? My husband explained the situation to you, yet you continue to make excuses and refuse accountability. This is your problem to handle, not ours. Shifting blame and claiming others “take advantage” of the same issues does not address the real problem. You repeatedly fail to take responsibility for your mistakes, instead making it seem like your customers are at fault. You even requested that we take down the post, yet no accountability was taken. Well, this post remains because it reflects the truth.

A very cool atmosphere very inviting like the vibes of the restaurant. I enjoy the wallpaper with information on the various leaders of Nigeria. The staff were very helpful in being able to not decide with the shoes, but in giving us a sample so that way we could taste some different cuisine. I’ve never had Nigerian food, but definitely would highly recommend this location. The vegetables were really well spiced and flavorful was delicious a little bit tougher than what I would like in eating meat, but I thought it was a great place to get Nigerian food.

Note my rating system:
1 Star: I wouldn't recommend
2 Stars: Didn't hit my standards
3 Stars: Average (nothing special)
4 Stars: Above Average. Would recommend. Still looking for the 5 Star.
5 Stars: Top of their game. Great food. Great service. Would recommend and plan on returning.

Olatee Restaurant is absolutely amazing. I went with my fiancé and we truly enjoyed every bite. The food was delicious, flavorful, and made with so much care. It honestly reminded me of home, which meant a lot to me. The atmosphere was welcoming, and the experience overall was wonderful. I highly recommend Olatee to anyone looking for authentic, comforting food that tastes like it was made with love. We’ll definitely be back!

I wanna start with the meat pie which was dry as hell and lacked any flavor. I was nearly choking on the damn thing. Then I got two beef and rice bowels and one of them didn’t even have beef. I wanna point out that they charged 5 dollars extra per bowel for a meat. And the one that did get beef is a freaking joke! Might as well not have given me any beef at all

best in bonaberi

name: A FAMILY AFFAIR SOUTHERN

reviews.text:
Large portions, delicious food. One plate is enough to share! Cornbread was just okay. I prefer buttermilk. Blueberry punch hits the spot. Turkey chops are the winners! This spot is better than Dulan's.
Parking is cramped but don't let that deter you. There can be a wait as everything is freshly prepared.
Greens ate!
Green beans ate!
Cabbage ate!
Mac n cheese ate! It is dense and heavy! Very filling.
My new go to Soulfood place.

Young lady recommended my meal due to them not having any more ox tails. Let me tell you! Them Turkey chops fried or smothered (she gave me sample of fried turkey chops) was the best thing I had in a very long time and I have to say I love me some turkey chop! Thank you for the recommendation 💚

Okay so this place.  It’s actually inside of a liquor store which I had no idea I’m driving up and down the street looking for the place I had to look at the address and realize it doesn’t have its own building it’s in a liquor store   But there was plenty of parking it’s not a sit down restaurant they have maybe 4 seats to  wait for ur food but for the most part I ordered oxtails macaroni and cheese greens and yams  the macaroni was very unseasoned. I don’t like it and neither did my 7 year old and he likes macaroni and cheese that’s his favorite the oxtails were good  they were like a 7 out of the macaroni was a 2 out of 10 the yams were good I’ll give it a 8 the greens were like a 4and a half outta 10 my son ordered fried catfish and 2 sides of macaroni we threw the macaroni out but the cat fish was good the customer service was top tier  and the wait time was about 15 minutes

Mannnnnnn, listen. I have been in LA for 4 years now. I’m originally from South Carolina. I have not found a place close to food I found at home until today. There will be a wait, but real food takes time and love. If you want it fast, they have a way to order online so when you get here it’s either ready or close. The catfish I had was crispy on the outside with a soft center. The yams took me back south. The okra was fresh, not the frozen pre dipped crap. Fries were excellently made and crispy. They don’t put the fries in a box so they don’t get soggy. And at the end I saved the cornbread for last. As soon as I opened the foil and saw a little melted butter, I knew I found my place. If you want to have good southern food and don’t want to spend thousands on a plane ticket, hotels, and Ubers to eat in the south, just come here. Get the green kool aid too. I will be back, a lot.

I have tried this location a few times and keep arriving at the same conclusion, it's not for me.  I truly get and support small, black business. I only come here for one thing,  the soul rolls.  My palate is a bit more discriminating to be able to enjoy the other menu items independently.   I'm not saying they're bad,  just not for me.   The rolls however provide a nice change of pace in the  culinary paradigm. My contention is when as a patron I'm told what I "can't do". The rolls are a coveted item and slated to be one of the restaurants claims to fame. On a previous visit I came to order a dozen and was told that needs to be done in advance.  I was told 6 was the max for a walk in order. I understand that. They are hand made.  Today I walked in and ordered 4. I was told they couldn't make that many.  The most I could get was 2.  Well ma'am,  there are 3 of us standing here.  She walks away and returns and agrees to the 3. Cool! Thanks! The guest behind me orders what,  a soul roll with no discussion.  🤔

As the business proprietor,  they absolutely reserve the right to manage the establishment as they see fit. No qualms there.  Post your limits however.  Max 3 soul rolls per visit...or whatever.  I don't like the rules changing sporadically.  If I'm told they can only do 2 with a stretch to 3 and you follow with an order behind me, I feel that lacks integrity.  My intended order was stated immediately with the desire to support the business.

The business acumen is what the distraction is for me.   Again, I only come for one item.  Will I return,  remains to be seen.

formatted_address: 2835 S Robertson Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90034, United States
name: Ackee Bamboo Jamaican Cuisine

reviews.text: Delicious new restaurant in the neighborhood - the chicken was literally falling off the bone. And these were the small portions! A little spicy, but that's what ice cream is for! 😉

If you're ready for fresh, authentic, delicious, Jamaican food you have to check out Ackee Bambo on Robertson. I promise you will not be disappointed. I ordered the large oxtail.. my God today..they were delectable, juicy, full of flavor and the best part they were WHOLE oxtails swimming in gravy, not cut in pieces. The rice and beans were tasty and with a good texture. The cabbage was fresh, the plantation were soft and sweet and let me not forget the festival bread it was crispy on the outside and soft inside best for sopping up that gravy😋 dont walk, but instead run down to there new location on Robertson you won't be disappointed. My hubby ordered the Iarge Jerk Chicken it was fire, not too spicy, but just right!! Oh I can't forget about Melissa she was my server very polite and attentive. They Top Notch!!
Amazing food, great staff ackee and saltfish combo with the rice best rice I had in years. Freshly made. Would definitely return
Excellent food, great value, and the staff is so friendly! Some of the best oxtails I’ve had in LA

Was working at the coffee shop next door and decided to stop by for lunch…so glad I did!!!! I ordered the curry chicken plate and it was seriously delicious. Such a large portion too! Will definitely be going back here.

formatted_address: 11707 Washington Pl, Los Angeles, CA 90066, United States
name: Rutt's Hawaiian Cafe & Catering West LA

reviews.text: Very comforting, typical dishes.  Exactly what you would expect to be catered at a Hawaiian-themed birthday party. No flairs, no frills, just solid classics.  Given that the restaurant leans more toward catering and take-out, the interior feels a bit like an afterthought, so don’t expect a very vibey dine-in experience.  There is a fun “tiki bar” inside the restaurant, however.

Had a taste for their famous Hawaiian Royale. Yum! We also got their Chicken Katsu plate and the Portuguese Sausage Breakfast plate. Everything was absolutely delicious! Love their friendly, warm neighborhoodly service.  A great place for casual dining with great food!

I had the boneless short rib lunch plate and it was pretty good, could use more sauce though since the short ribs were thick. The lunch plate already comes with rice so no need to order rice on the side unless you want to eat more rice. They give you a decent size portion, I saved some for dinner. Server was very nice and accommodating. The place has decent size people. Pretty social atmosphere.

The food here was nice and filling, but lacked something I can’t put my finger on. The loco moco was good and the gravy carried the dish. Overall a hearty meal that wasn’t super cheap but not super expensive.

The Original Hawaiian Royal w/ Fried Rice - Portugeuse Sausage, Char Sui (Chinese BBQ Pork), Eggs, Fried Rice, Sprouts, Onions / 5⭐!
Spam Masubi - spam, rice, sauce, seawood wrap / 5⭐!
Hawaiian-style Macaroni Salad / 5⭐!

I am a fan of Hawaiian food partly because it is a wonderfully, eclectic blend of influences from other cuisines and has evolved far enough to have its own distinct culinary identity.

Rutt's Hawaiian Cafe, an LA Hawaiian cafe with a few locations around the SoCal area, fully embraces the food that makes Hawaii special. Their menu includes a large list of island favorites. I was drawn towards the Royale dish, which is something that isn't available at lots of other Hawaiian places.

A Royale is an egg/omelette dish mixed with rice and fillings. I went with their original which includes sausage and char sui and I went for the fried rice version. It was amazing! So much flavor with all the ingredients mixed together. Every bite was magic. It was also insanely filling. I used some of the bbq sauces on the table to add a bit more kick.

I love Hawaiian style macaroni salad as well as spam masubi. Had I known how big the royale was, I'd probably have just ordered that but I was keen to try some other items. No regrets! The spam masubi is always a fun dish to have. It is a nice savory/sweet combo and hit the spot. Their take on the macaroni salad was also excellent.

The restaruant is bright and colorful. I like that a large copy of the menu greets you at the door. There are lots of seats inside and outside on a patio. The servers were friendly and helpful. My server is who convinced me to try the royale. There is a very small parking lot connected to the restaurant but it also looked like there was lots of easy street parking.

If you love Hawaiian cuisine or if you are curious what makes a great Hawaiian dish, give Rutt's a try! They have been open for a long time and have a lot of great food in their friendly, colorful location.

formatted_address: 6517 West Blvd, Inglewood, CA 90302, United States
name: Gold Spoon Jamaican Cuisine

reviews.text: It was my first time trying Jamaican cuisine, and Golden Spoon Jamaican Cuisine absolutely blew me away. The jerk chicken was simply heavenly, full of rich flavor and perfectly prepared. The owners were incredibly friendly, and the homemade juices tasted like they were sent from heaven. You can really tell they use special, healthy ingredients and prepare everything with love. I’ll definitely be coming back!

Wow. The Jerk Salmon was tun up! My first time and can say this was the best jerk salmon I have had outside of Jamaica and the best in Los Angeles. First I was greeted by Roberto who was so welcoming. It was my first time so I had a few questions which he was  kind to take time and answer. Even the chef answered a few. The welcoming was honorable like in Jamaica.

The atmosphere is chill with music, scenes candles, chill Jamaican vibe.they have two tables inside. While I was there they had at least 10 people come in to order or pick up to go.

When the jerk salmon came. Roberto kinda presented the dish and drink accordingly. When I took my first bite took me back to Jamaica.  The flavors and spices merged perfectly with the salmon, rice, plantains, cabbage, and seemed like a little Johnny  Cake. But wow the flavors. Each bite had unique and different flavors from thr jerk sauce. Just amazing. Also their pineapple ginger juice is the bomb. Must try. Their menu Is unique by having a selection with additional selections for each day of the week. I highly recommend. Thank you. I will be back for sure. Ciao!

Food quality 10/10. Portion size 10/10. Choices 10/10. Flavors 10/10. Atmosphere and welcoming 10/10. Cleanliness 10/10.

While visiting LA my friends and I had a craving for Jamaican food...We looked online and found Gold Spoon Restaurant....what a beautiful blessing. The place was clean and beautifully decorated...
The FOOD WAS AMAZING.....AMAZING...COOKED JUST LIKE MY MOM would....Best stop we could have made...They allowed us to taste the freshly made drinks and we picked the Soursop..Pineapple Ginger and Passion Fruit....took them home and had to share with everyone. We loved the atmosphere and the owners were welcoming. If you're in the mood for authentic Jamaican food please stop by...you will not be disappointed. Definitely plans set to visit again

I'M from South Florida, Broward County!!!!
I've been looking for a good Jamaican restaurant..
And Im pretty sure I've found it.
These oxtails are 10 out of 10.
And the look at the portion.  Not to mention the tenderness.
I will be back..
Can't wait try the snapper.

This is a wonderful little shop that serves freshly squeezed, healthy juices and delicious Jamaican fare. I tried the chicken patty--the wrapper was crispy and not too thick, and the filling was lightly spiced (just like it's made in the Caribbean). It went well with a fresh beetroot juice, which isn't too sweet, and is good for inflammation. I also tried the soursop and pineapple ginger juices, and if you ever need an energy boost, try the latter! Very zingy. Service is amazing and attentive (by the owner, on the day I was there), and he let me try different juices. I'll be back for the oxtail and the goat curry.
Edit: came back for the oxtail. Huge portion, excellent flavor, served with steamed veggies and plantains. Definitely have to try!

formatted_address: 7717 S Western Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90047, United States
name: M'Dears Bakery & Bistro

reviews.text: I ordered the chicken wings with waffles, and everything tasted amazing. My friends tried the fried chicken with a few sides, and everyone loved their meals. The portions were generous enough that we all ended up taking leftovers home. The server was warm and welcoming, which made the whole experience even better.

In CA visiting for a conference.  M'Dears was recommended.  We were seated right away. I had chicken wings and waffles . It was delicious!  The others had fried chicken and sides. The portions were more than enough. We all had to get take out boxes. The server was very friendly.  We did not have to wait long for our food either.
The food was delicious. 10 out of a 10. Our food was fresh and hot.

Hey, you guys, so im back with my review for M'Dears. I have been eating here for a while but I always get the same thing and it's always good even if you have to warm it u,  which I really like. I have been in person,  butit'ss really small and intimate,  so I usually order to pick up or delivery. This time I got delivery. The food still arrived good and fresh. They usually give you all the condiments you need, and they staple the bag, which makes me feel more secure, and they have the nice containers that keep the food warm. I get the chicken and waffle with medium scrambled eggs with cheese and grits on the side. Usually, it is about 57.00 for two orders. I get one for my child. My other daughter gets the pancakes and bacon, which is good as well. The chicken is so good and seasoned and flavorful. The waffles are so buttery and soft. The eggs are so soft I usually just add black pepper. The grits are so good and cooked to perfection. I usually add a little butter and black pepper and a dash of salt. The workers are normally friendly, and they make sure the order is right. Now, when I do order the pancakes and bacon, the bill is closer to 70.00 or so dollars so be prepared to pay. They also can be busy, and they dont have the food sitting around, so be prepared to wait about 20-30 minutes.

TO THE OWNER OF THIS BUSINESS…

The food here at M’Dears is something I’ve heard is a must try when in LA and was excited to visit. Upon my visit, however, a decrepit level of customer service was experienced by myself and company that completely turned us off and left.

To begin, there was staff working in the front entrance but we were not acknowledged at all upon entrance. After a few minutes, I made an attempt to try to get the attention of said staff but their back was turned to us and was not approachable. However, a second staff member gave from what looked like the back and immediately greeted us cordially (which I definitely appreciated). However, when inquires were made about dine in, she explained to me that

1. The outdoor patios were not available although there was a gentleman at the time sitting outside enjoying what looked like a very tasty meal.

2. The back section was closed for seating at the time, leaving only the front section where just about every seating booth was occupied.

At this point, the first staff member whom I tried to talk to upon entrance chimed in a few words, either confirming what was said by the other but in a distasteful way. At this point, I was flabbergasted at the amount of disrespect I had endured in a span of 5 mins and proceeded to leave instead of reciprocating the said level of disrespect back. I say all this to say a few things in conclusion:

* Your food looked amazing and would still like an opportunity to try it

* Your employees should undergo a new training of customer service because what I experienced was definitely not it

* Clarify the dine in options with proper signage to new patrons so that there is no confusion between who is allowed to dine outside and who isn’t

* There is no real point of having 5 star quality food for people to eat if you cannot have the equal level of customer service available to match it - no one wants to feel invisiable or ignored at a patron in a dining establishment

I hope you heed my suggestions so that your restaurant can continue to be received at a must dine experience in one of this country’s biggest urban regions. Thanks for reading and have a great day.

formatted_address: 4326 Crenshaw Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90008, United States
name: Taco Mell's Catering and Restaurant

reviews.text:
I have been coming to the Taco Bell on Crenshaw and 43rd for years, and it stays undefeated. The area is laid back and the vibe is chill. My go to is the 3 meat burrito with green sauce, and I swear I crave it like a late night plot twist. They make it fast, they make it hot, and they do not play when it comes to portions. My burrito is always packed, never flimsy, and they never skimp on the protein.

I usually grab the raspberry Kool Aid too, which tastes like childhood in a cup and completes the whole moment. The customer service here is decent, the team moves quick, and even when the line gets long they keep things flowing.

This location has been my steady favorite for years. Reliable food, good portions, quick service, and that same flavor every time. No matter how many new spots open up, the Taco Bell on Crenshaw and 43rd will always be my go to.

It's a inside taco stand, very tight/small. I gave  em THREE strikes!! I'm done. My first visit 4 1/2 weeks ago was chicken & shrimp burrito, black beans,  xtra lettuce, pico degallo .the shrimp melted in my mouth, the chicken was juicy and flavorful, It was so good I told my friend.  I went back ordered the exact same thing, but, oops my bad, I didn't  check my  receipt, or my burrito  before we left. It turned out to be a steak/chicken burrito, that was so bad the steak looked/tasted like ground beef, chicken was over overcooked and dry. Wanting to recycle my black dollars so we went again.!! And my last time the shrimp overcooked and chewy, the chicken over boiled and dry. No flavor no lettuce, no consistency! I'm done it's a hit & miss I don't want to try nothing else. Stick a fork in me, I'm DONE!!!
Veggie Heaven!! Ordered two BRC tacos with guacamole. Loved the sauces, texture was perfect. Lovely service. So fresh!! Will be back.

I got the 3 meat(Chk,carne, & shrimp) burrito and it was very good. The carne asada was close to being salty but my personal addition of crema toned it down.  A little on the pricey side but when seafood is involved, it's to be expected. We got there just before closing but did not feel like we, nor our food was rushed. Everything was made fresh, and that Kool-aid was a hit! I mixed the blue raspberry lemonade with the peach mango... just do it and thank me later. So in all I would definitely recommend and fully intend to have them cater some of my functions! Definitely worth the trip from the IE!

Oct, 2023 was amazing trip in LA.
All the way from Japan! shrimp tacos
is one of my favorite! Ima miss dis tacos spot!

formatted_address: 2159 W Century Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90047, United States
name: Trinistyle Cuisine

reviews.text:
Went here on a Saturday afternoon. Place was steady with customers. Parking can be hard to find. Also the parking space is tight for bigger vehicles.

I've seen videos of this place, and I've always wanted to try T&T cuisine. This is more of the street-style food. We got a goat roti and a chickpea double along with a blend of sorrel and ginger pine for the beverage. The kid at the cashier was helpful, but didn't greet us initially. They have an indoor or small outdoor area to eat. Walls were adorned with T&T memorabilia. Got our items. The drink was amazing. Refreshing, gingery, but overpowering with hints of plum. The goat roti was so damn good. Insane flavors, the meat was tender and the roti was thin, but held everything well. You eat with your hands. The spice level is pretty high up, but with the seasonings, everything works great. I also got a currant cake and that was the perfect finish to a complex meal.

Overall, absolutely worth the drive! So many options that you have to come here more than once to experience the different menus. The owner came out and she was very nice.

As a born and raised New Yorker- with Jamaican heritage- I’m so happy to have found this spot. Anyone with anything nasty to say it’s just miserable!!
This place is literally a gem . I drove all the way from Van Nuys to try the food and the roti and doubles did not disappoint…. The customer service was amazing and the food was so flavorful. I will definitely be coming back for chicken roti, goat roti , and doubles .

We Love Trinistyle Cuisine!

Family run spot, located in a strip mall with limited parking and a few seating for patrons.

Trinistyle delivers with traditional, authentic flavors!

Open on Friday - Saturday - Sunday

Food is made to order. Will take time because it’s made with love!

Buss up shot delicious!
Goat dhalpuri roti delicious!
Doubles delicious!
Ginger-pine drink delicious!
Currant pies delicious!

Love that they have a little store in their spot serving Caribbean tings. Please bring more goodies and hard to find items from the homeland.

Will always support this place as it is a gem, and truly a taste of home.

Thank you!🇹🇹
Excellent Trinidad / Caribbean style food which is freshly prepared.  The flavors and taste were authentic and very tasty.  Good vegetarian options.

I'm Guyanese, so sometimes I have to say "hold the Trini." That's in reference to the mango seed in the food. I can't speak for the meat besides the fish, but every thing is tasty. Spices, flavor, texture, and freshness are the closest thing to New York, which is the closest thing to home. I travel an hour+ to get here and it's worth the trip every time. Please support your local restaurants.

formatted_address: 1714 W Century Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90047, United States
name: Dulan's

reviews.text: Recommended by a friend and it did not disappoint. We had to stand outside and order our food at a window and pick it up at the side window. The person taking order was not very helpful with the menu and kind of rushed us but it was a line so I chucked it up to that. We ordered the meatloaf dinner with Mac and cheese and yams and my husband got collars and Mac and cheese along with sweet tea. I dont eat everyone's meatloaf but was craving it and I am soooo happy I did. It was some of the best meatloaf I have eaten. The yams were delicious as well and my fav side. They gave a lot of food and had leftovers for the following day and more. The tea was amazing as well but my husband did say it was mixed with lemonade so wasn't real tea but was delicious.  Hidden gem and will make sure to visit again when in the area.

Friend and I went for lunch, wanting homestyle flavor, I ordered meatloaf, collard greens, cornbread dressing.
The meatloaf seemed to be made with some type of soy mixed with the ground beef. I cannot describe the texture except that it was thick and processed as from a  vacuum sealed package, no flavor whatsoever. The greens were cooked well, perhaps canned, but again zero flavor. The dressing was from a box as well. For $20 the portions were acceptable, but overall I wouldn't recommend this spot. We went to the one on Century near Western. We ate outside. Aa the weather permitted.

So we're here to honor my grandfather and celebrate his life. The Honorable Judge Albert D Mathews of. Los Angeles, CA. Being a resident of Stillwater, Oklahoma I was in need of some good Soul Food. Oklahoma can't do it.  I'm sorry to disturb anyone that thinks different. I haven't found anything yet that passed my taste buds test. Anyhow,  We had large crowd to feed after the wake. This spot accommodated us. The staff were patient, helpful,and very polite. Several things stood out . They had fish on the menu. I don't eat catfish or tilapia. So whenever I inquired about what kind of fish , the guy said it's Swai . Cool. It was hot and seasoned to perfection. This was big for me. Also, The drink on the menu called Tiger Woods which is soulful remix of The Arnold Palmer - Lemonade and Tea Mixed together. Finally, Mr Dulan himself came and introduced himself and brought out food. Inquired if anyone needed anything. I will revisit this spot. My Cali family comes here very often and stated that they too enjoy the food as well. Thanks for being a pillar in this community. Also I was blowed away by the Smooth R&B that was playing. Banger after banger came on and made some of us dance. Especially when boots on the ground came on. Enjoy a great meal you won't forget! Good food does exist. 😍

I did not realize that this is the same family that owns Aunt kizzy's in Malibu The food was very good The owner came over and greeted us He was very personable the waitress was very nice
Our first visit on Monday I ordered the smothered pork chops with succotash which was very tasty on Tuesday I ordered the oxtails mac and cheese and cabbage and very tasty

I love this place — the food is great, the staff is friendly, and service is generally quick! There’s a family history that dates back to the fsmily patriach, Mr Adolf Dulan. I know this because I did my research. My fave location is at Westem Ave & Century Blvd, but the Inglewood location also serves great food! If you haven’t tried Dulans Soul Food Kitchen, all I can say is that you’re missing out!☝🏽🏆😍

formatted_address: 5440 S Central Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90011, United States
name: Granny's Kitchen Southern Style Soul Food
