reviews.text: Had the pleasure of eating here today and I can say they are #1 compared to the local soul food places I've tried.   They have a full southern menu.  The staff were friendly and made you feel right at home.   I got takeout but they have dine in seating.  I got the backed chicken dinner with Mac and cheese, greens and cornbread dressing!! It came with 2 cornbread muffins,  it was delicious 😋 parking can be a bit tricky due to it's in a strip mall.  They also take EBT hot meals program so if you ever in the area stop by at Granny's you won't be disappointed 😉

I’m very disappointed. This is the second time I’ve ordered from this restaurant through Uber Eats and had an issue. The first time, I received someone else’s order. Tonight, I ordered baked chicken, greens, macaroni and cheese, and yams. Instead, the greens were mixed with cabbage as one dish, which I do not eat. The macaroni and cheese was dried out and tasted old, and the baked chicken looked like it had been sitting out for a long time. After two bad experiences, I won’t be ordering again.

The name is fitting for this place & the food is absolutely flavorful & incredible a review that was long overdue. As soon as you step in there's a welcoming vibe & customer service is also very good. The food seems to transport you back in time & you might just smile as you remember the good memories the food can bring up. In my case, my grandmother who can cook very well but it's not just something I can get anymore. Accepts ebt - hot meal program. They also fry to order. Here I just feel at home with the delicious soul food & the quality is always consistent.
⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐

2nd time ordering. Not sure why its like this on a Sunday. We can do better. The greens are too sweet.
The Mac and cheese in the hungry woman plate was dry and rock cold compared to the extra side of Mac. The smotherd chicken gravy was cold. This means it was siting. The restaurant is only 10 min away. Why would it be Rock cold?  Other restaurants can pack and serve hot food that is hot when it arrives. Is it  best to order from a different soul food restaurant that is further away like Dulan's? Disappointed again.

This was my first time ordering. I got baked chicken (well cooked, but could've been cleaned better). It processed through my bowels, almost immediately. I threw most of it away.

I also ordered greens/cabbage mix. They didn't offer collard greens alone. The pot-liquor was heavy with vinegar and salt. I couldn't even eat the cabbage. It was not good. I just picked out the collard greens.

The baked mac and cheese was decent and the candied yams were good. Though, they should throw away the cortex of the yam, prior to baking, as it is not something I eat.

The cornbread muffins were ok. Not moist, just something to eat with the greens.

I wanted to order the Kool-aid. But, a 20 oz cup was $4.50. Please!

formatted_address: 3426 W Washington Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90018, United States
name: Natraliart Jamaican Restaurant & Market

reviews.text:
My homie and I wanted to try out a new food spot. I was a bit disappointed with the food.

Pros:
-Oxtails were flavorful
-Restaurant was clean
-Owner had a good, pleasant attitude with me
-Lemonade was fire!
-Lunch special price was around 20 bucks which is lower than most Jamaican spots I’ve seen in LA County

Cons:
-Size of the oxtails were tiny (I am understanding of the economy so I won’t be as harsh)
-Rice didn’t taste flavorful and was too mushy for me
-Cabbage seemed kinda hard and I’ve never heard of lima beans being in Jamaican food?

Great place for authentic Jamaican cuisine. I'm a frequent flyer at this place, and not only is the food delicious, they have a mini Jamaican market right next to them. It's a one-stop and shop for anyone who wants to get cooked Jamaican food, or to pick up items to prepare and cook at home.

Best Jamaican food in the area and the lady at the counter is very friendly. The Curry Goat and Oxtails were delicious and the sides were made very well with lots of flavor. Like a good home cooked meal.

Food had no taste at all. I would never buy from them again. Ox-tails, and Curry Shrimp with fried dumplings, the rice was mushy. The collard greens were OK but the cabbage texture was bad no flavor and I don’t know what else to say about it but I was very disappointed. I drove over 60 miles to try their food and the experience was not well.

Unfortunately, though I am a loyal customer ,believe I found a blue beetle in my curry goat that was ordered on either Uber eats or DoorDash last Saturday. I didn’t get a photo of it, but that really freaked me out. I do really like the food though so I might order again, but definitely questioning the hygiene practices of the kitchen

formatted_address: 5545 W Pico Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90019, United States
name: Stevie's Creole Café

reviews.text: Had to check out this highly rated creole seafood restaurant Stevie's Creole Cafe in Los Angeles, CA. Small location with limited seating but we were able to get a nice window seat in the corner. The menu has so many options that it is challenging deciding on what to order. Good problems! We ordered seafood gumbo, Stevie's Special Chopped chicken bowl (2), with macaroni and cheese and collard greens. An order of honey cornbread and biscuits with peach honey butter. Chicken fried and then chopped up. Then cooked on the grill with gravy and green onions and then served top white rice. This dish was flavorful and very good! The gravy is homemade with superb flavor and taste! The rice was a little gummy and it didn't matter the dish was still a 5 out of 5. The macaroni and cheese was good cheesy and seasoned with a 4 out of 5 rating. The collard greens had a good taste and the pot liquor was superb. Just wasn't a fan of the texture of this order of collard greens. The texture was the only reason these were a 4 out of 5 and not higher. The honey cornbread was really good and tasted homemade not from the box with a 4.5 out of 5 rating. The biscuits were also home made and fluffy with a good texture. Tasted okay texture and presentation great with a 4 out of 5 rating. The seafood gumbo was good. Great job with the roux. If you love King crab then you will love this gumbo. I would rate their gumbo a 4.4 out of 5. The presentation is a 5! The service at this location was Awesome! Everybody I mean everybody was friendly and they operate as a unit with everyone helping everyone! The service reminded me of back home in the South! I will visit this place every time I'm in Los Angeles for the rest of my life! If you like seasoned food with high flavor profiles then this is your place!

I love, love, love this place. I have eaten here 3 times. The food is amazing, the staff is attentive and kind, great service overall. King crab Mac n cheese is amazing as is the gumbo, chicken wings, chicken and waffles, shrimp and grits, and shrimp Étouffée. Don’t forget sweet tea and warm beignets for dessert! I will be back with even more family and friends next time.

Phenomenal Experience at Stevie’s Creole Café!
Stevie’s Creole Café is hands down a hidden gem and an absolute must-visit if you love authentic Southern comfort food with serious soul!

The gumbo was rich, flavorful, and packed with perfectly cooked seafood and sausage every spoonful was a warm hug. The cornbread? Unreal. Moist, slightly sweet, with that golden crust that just melts in your mouth. I could’ve eaten a whole tray!

And don’t even get me started on dessert. The beignets were pillowy, fresh, and dusted with just the right amount of powdered sugar like a little piece of New Orleans right here. I finished with the banana pudding, and let me just say: it was heavenly. Creamy, nostalgic, and made with love.

The staff were incredibly friendly, the vibes were cozy, and the food came out hot and fresh. You can tell this place is run with pride and passion.

My husband and I are visiting from Bahrain and Morocco, and we were absolutely thrilled with the experience. This was a true taste of Southern hospitality and flavor we’ll be talking about this meal for a long time!

Need not say much for the food,  there's already many great reviews about it.  Something that I must shout out to is the waitress (didn't get her name, but she has long curly hair) that attended to us, she is a such a cheerful, attentive lady. Always carrying a smile. She is one that serve with a ❤️ and passion. 6 stars for you. When we were leaving, she and her co workers also leave us a good impression. If anyone else complain about their service in future, I must say it must be a  (karen) customer.
Great service must go along with great tip, so please be generous to keep their fire burning

*I’m from a one stop light town in the south so I know Soul Food*

This spot is busy so don’t let that discourage you.

Me and my buddy were riding by saw a line out the door and figured why not give them a try.

Stevie’s did not disappoint!!

I ordered fried chicken, Mac& cheese and red beans w/rice although it was amazing I got plate envy from my buddies Gumbo. Man that was some good gumbo. 😋

Oh! The cornbread w/ peach cobbler whipped cream was 🤤

If you’re in the area please try this place even if you have to wait 45min. It’s worth the wait.

formatted_address: 3511 S King Dr, Chicago, IL 60653, United States
name: Yassa African Restaurant

reviews.text:
We were happy to come today and wanted the experience to be awesome.
So..... While the food was good, the service staff left a lot to be desired.  We had a party of 11 people, so imagine how much money we were going to spend?   A lot.  My wife was sorely disappointed from the staff who wouldn't accommodate a simple request. Then they didn't bring her order to the table.  Training is sorely needed.  Did I forget to mention that there were other folks that came in after we were seated who got served, ate and left BEFORE we were all served?  It will be some time before we return to Yassa.

☹️🤬☹️🤬☹️🤬☹️🤬☹️. #NotHappy. #NotPleased. #NotComingBack

Went to this place because I wanted to try some Nigerian eats but it looks like it has so many different choices like a good variety of African eats which is better. We ended up ordering some fataya, Yassa Lamb, Dibi Lamb Senegal both with Djolof Rice and then we also had a side of plantains. Food was so busss and the serving was HUGE. Definitely try the lamb if you go here. Food was seasoned well. I definitely would come back in the future. VIBES WERE IMMACULATE. They played great RNB songs for me and my king 😍😍😍 whoever was on the aux that day was bangin! Anyways, 10/10. TRUST

I ordered the Yassa lamb with aloco (sweet plantains) via the Relish app which is what we have at work. It gets delivered to a floor in my building and we pick it up from there. The order was ready by 12:15pm, the temperature was hot. It is very tasty and a very good portion. I will have some reserved for dinner. It is only 4/5 stars because of the packaging. I now make this a crucial criterion in my reviews. But I wouldn’t hesitate to come to the restaurant and order more food!

Visiting from SC. The food was amazing, my first time trying West African food such as this. The fufu was as delicious and sweet and meshed amazingly with the sauce graine. The sauce graine was cooked to perfection with shrimp and beef! Would definitely recommend!

Went for dinner for a birthday celebration. Food did not take long to arrive. Yassa is Senegalese but they serve authentic West African food including Ivory Coast Sauce Graine dish. Although the menu did not state which items were spicy, the spice was not unbearable, especially paired with the Baobab drink (it has dairy). We met the owner who was very welcoming and warm. You could tell the owner pours love into the food.

Photos:
1 - Nem (appetizer) 6 for $12
2 - Thiou Curry with Lamb and Fufu
3 - Sauce Graine with Fufu
4 - Stews Menu
5 - Non-Alcoholic Beverage Menu

formatted_address: 1126 E 47th St, Chicago, IL 60653, United States
name: Gorée Cuisine

reviews.text:
Truly exceptional and authentic west African cuisine. Make sure you try the attieke. The tilapia was 🧑‍🍳.
The lamb was soft and full of flavor and absolutely try the curry. Too bad we are out of towners otherwise we would be regulars.
And I really liked the wall art. All black American heroes represented.

Came here with my family of 6 and we ALL had an AMAZING experience! We were educated about various menu items and the owner catered to our needs personally. Our food was freshly prepared and seasoned perfectly! High five to You and your wonderful team, Adama! I look forward to returning and trying other menu items in the near future…

The food is excellent. We had the Saka Saka, jollof rice with plantains, however, the Saka Saka didn’t have shrimp and crab meet in it thought. Just FYI. There was no chicken so we also got the Yassa Lamb and Dibi Lamb. Everything tasted delicious. They usually only have 1 person as the waiter and server so if it’s busy, there would be a long wait
Incredible meal and hospitality. My second time having senegalese food and will certainly be back! My favorite was the maffe w fufu but the yassa chicken and house thieboudienne were also amazing

100/10 I had Mint Tea, Fataya, and Yassa Lamb. Everything was so delicious. Fast service for the level of exceptional quality.(you can’t really rush W. African food anyways) Flavor was perfect and spicy. The tea was refreshing even though it’s served hot. Goree made it to my top 5 restaurants in Chicago.

formatted_address: 1131 W Bryn Mawr Ave, Chicago, IL 60660, United States
name: Teranga African Restaurant

reviews.text: My 12 yr old daughter and wanted to celebrate Day 3 of Kwanzaa (Collective Work and Responsibility) by patronizing an African restaurant.  Teranga had great reviews on food atmosphere and service, the reviews were spot on. Our host greeted us upon entering,  we selected our own seats (near the window). This Sunday evening brought in diners, the place was packed yet seating was available upon entry. Our 1st time we ordered 1 main dish: Chicken Yassa that came with 2 sides, we had the jollof rice and  futu and 1 drink Bissap. This was enough food for 2 and we had a little left over. Our food was delicious, came out hot and served without delay. We were served by the Owner Pierre Thiam, and I'd like to acknowledge this gentleman's hard work and commitment to his business and culture. We will return for the great food and genuine charm. We recommend Teranga for anyone seeking to experience authentic African cuisine.

Teranga African Restaurant is an absolute gem! I’ve eaten here twice now. The food is fresh, flavorful, and beautifully authentic, the kind of West African cooking that warms your heart.

As a West African myself, every bite brings me back to the dishes I grew up with. The Yassa Chicken is tangy and perfectly seasoned, the Dibi Lamb is tender and smoky, and the Fataya is one of my personal favorites, crispy on the outside with that delicious spiced filling. Don’t miss the fried plantains, couscous, Jollof rice, and of course the fish dishes, which taste just like home.
What makes it even more special is the hospitality, and customer service with passion and humility.  You can feel that love and authenticity in every plate and every interaction.
Highly, highly recommend.

Excellent food at Teranga!
The quality of food was great, the service was excellent and the portions were right. Elhadj is a great host. We took the Yassa and Mafé and were delighted. We are happy to have African hospitality, culture and food around the corner 🙌🏼

I had such a wonderful experience here! The food is very, very good – full of flavor, fresh, and beautifully presented. Every dish tasted homemade with so much care. The staff were welcoming and friendly, and the atmosphere felt cozy and inviting.

If you’re in Chicago and want to try authentic Senegalese cuisine, this is definitely the spot. I’ll be coming back again and again!
Yummy! Get the ginger drink and the Yassa. The lamb dishes were so good. The service was so nice. The starters (fataya and Accara) were both equally good. I would definitely get them again.

formatted_address: 5973 N Clark St, Chicago, IL 60660, United States
name: Royal Africana Lounge

reviews.text:
I absolutely love the Royal Africana Lounge! The food is always tasty and fresh! If something is wrong with your order, they make it right quickly with no problem. The owner and employees are very friendly. I travel here from the South Side of Chicago at least once a month! The food is so good!

Pictured: Grilled Tilapia w/Plantains, Spinach & shrimp only w/fufu and Jollof rice (comes w/stewed chicken.

The food is authentically Nigerian. It was very tasty and flavorful. I got jollof rice and oha soup. The serving size was good. I was able to divide both meals into 2-3 smaller portions. I have 2 recommendations: 1. For the chef, to use less oil in cooking. 2. The atmosphere of the restaurant could be more organized and inviting. 3. The menu should be redone to be more descriptive, especially for people who are unfamiliar with the cuisine.

Lastly, I highly recommend this restaurant for the food whether you’re trying it for the first time or you want to be reminiscent of home cooking!

Tried Royal Africana on a whim and was pleasantly surprised. I had the jollof rice with goat and a side of plantains—super flavorful, goat was tender. Spent around $25 with a drink. Vibe was lively, music bumpin', but service was a little slow. Still, food came out hot and worth the wait. Feels like a legit spot for a night out when you want something different than the usual.

My Sun took Me to Royal Africana Lounge for my 53rd birthday; I must say I had a Royal time:) this place was cozy and elegant.
The food was flavorful, savory and comfortable filling.
I loved the music and decor.
We will be returning soon and I hope (RAL) stay consistent in such dynamic service that keeps you coming back for more😀

Yassa can't compare at all!!!
Royal Africana Lounge platers are worth every dollar, because it's finger licking good👍🏾

This place was overpriced and bland ordered a side plantain for 12 or $14. And they were not ripe and I specifically, asked the girl, are they ripe? and they were not, I know. African food, because I cook it myself. This place was horrible. I wish I could have my money back. Jallof rice was bland with no sauce . Horrible and the last part that took me over the edge was the girl tried to add her own tip. then, when I asked her, why is it so much? She took the tip-off. And it was not a service fee. The killer I drove all the way from a west suburb to come to this crap!!!!!!!!

formatted_address: 1947 W Howard St, Chicago, IL 60626, United States
name: Badou Senegalese Cuisine

reviews.text: I was visiting a friend and she said it was a must have--she was absolutely right! I got the vegan mafe, my friend got cebbu yap, and then we split the plantains and veggie pastel. All amazing! Can't wait to go back next time I'm in town!

I walked into Badou Senegalese Cuisine not expecting much—just a warm meal and a quiet break from the wind cutting through Howard Street. Instead, I ended up stepping into one of the most soulful dining experiences I’ve had in Chicago.

The evening began with the Fataya, small golden hand pies that arrived steaming hot. One bite and the crispy shell gave way to perfectly seasoned meat, and when dipped in the spicy house tomato sauce, it tasted like something crafted with memory, not just technique.

Then came the dish I will remember for a long time: Thiebou Djeun. It arrived like a feast—rice tinted the color of sunset, a whole tender fish laid across the top, and vegetables so soft and aromatic they almost melted under the fork. Every bite tasted like it carried history. Smoky, tomato-rich, slow-built flavor that can only come from hours of patience. It was the kind of plate you eat slowly because you don’t want the experience to end.

The Yassa Chicken followed, bright and tangy, with onions cooked down until sweet and glossy. The charred chicken was tender, but it was the lemon-onion sauce that transformed the dish—it hit every corner of the palate.

I thought I was done, but curiosity led me to the Dibi Lamb. Flame-kissed, mustard-marinated, and full of personality. Each piece was smoky with crisp edges and juicy centers, balanced by raw onions that added crunch and sweetness.

By the time I tasted the rich, velvety Mafe, I understood why this restaurant has such a loyal following. It’s not just food—it’s comfort, tradition, and pride on a plate.

When I finally stepped back outside into the cold Chicago night, I felt warmer than when I entered. Badou didn’t just serve me dinner. It gave me a story to take with me.

I’ve had Badou at The Taste of Chicago both this year and last. Their food is amazing!
However, know their restaurant IS NOT OPEN as of Oct 2025. I didn’t realize and ordered online today, but once got there, saw they’re closed. Called the # from Google and the Owner so graciously helped me get a refund!

Oh my Gosh. What a wonderful surprise. I went there not expecting anything fantastic to happen. Not good, not bad. Just expected to get a meal after a long, hard, day at work. Well Surpise, something fantastic did happen.  The food was delicious. I have to put this on my list of places to revisit. I ordered Jerk Chicken and Jolaf Rice. The chicken was spiced just right and the rice was fresh (not that hard, bottom of the pot stuff. No this was a softer texture and was very flavorful). I'm sure they can bring spice flavors down if you don't like spicy. But check their menu. The have lots of flavorful looking dishes.

I tried their food at the Rogers Park art fest this summer, decided to visit and order takeout! I got a vegetarian pastel and jollof rice with jerk chicken -- it was all really delicious and the staff was very friendly! i'll definitely go again!

formatted_address: 931 N Orleans St, Chicago, IL 60610, United States
name: Mogadishu Restaurant

reviews.text: This place is a gem. The food was delicious, huge portions and lots of options. Cooked fresh and authentic. The person who served us was really helpful and friendly and gave great recommendations. The place has a relaxed atmosphere.

This place seems like a nice little neighborhood restaurant with very friendly owner/stuff. We ordered K-Kay with chicken and the lamb shank. Portion was huge and price was great. The lamb shank was quite tender and juicy. But the food in general was  a bit lack of strong flavor. This is our first time to try Somalian food and we have no clue whether it’s authentic or not. But we want to come back and try more dishes.

Man, this spot hits hard. Spent like $18 and got the goat with rice—meat was fall-off-the-bone tender, rice was hella flavorful, and they hook you up with this banana on the side that weirdly just works. Portions are wild generous, like you’ll def have leftovers. Super chill vibe, no frills, just straight-up amazing Somali food. If you know, you know. I’m 100% coming back.

It was nice to experience a different cuisine and culture. It looked like everyone who hangs out here were really close and are regulars. The food is served like cafeteria style so it wasn't as fresh as I was hoping for since all the other reviews talked greatly about the food. The chicken itself was very dry and did need to be seasoned more. I wasn't impressed with the lamb shank it looked like it was boiled so it made it unpleasant to eat. With that being said the lamb shank was bland. I did think the rice, veggies, and the split peas were tasty. The samosas did not have any crunch to them but I did think the filling was good. The highlight of the dinner was actually the black tea, it had so much flavor and warmth I could drink that every day.
Small restaurant that is serving delicious and plentiful platters. Unfortunately missed out on the anjera but the beef steak with rice and lentils was incredible.

formatted_address: 4501 N Sheridan Rd, Chicago, IL 60640, United States
name: The Mukase Restaurant (Chicago)

reviews.text:
Forget any reviews you’ve seen. This food is fantastic and I’m from Chicago and tried the best African cuisine here. This location is top of the list!

Service is excellent and everyone is so nice.

It was soo good me and my partner ate it and came back in 1 hour to order again to take some home for dinner.

First of all when we enter the restaurant no one speaks to you it’s not inviting it’s not warm the service here it’s literally as if they don’t want you to order at all. This would have been okay if the food was good. I have tried a lot of African cuisines including but not limited to Kenyan, Senegalese (some of the best), Nigerian, etc. This restaurant boasts of authentic Ghanaian dishes. It was pitiful and the food was old. I ordered the suya fried chicken, oxtail and brown stew, okra with goat, and a regular jollof rice meal with goat. I wasted the $87 I spent at this restaurant. I expected so much more and this experience makes me not want to eat Ghanaian food ever again. Needless to say (from the old oxtail) I threw up my food shortly after digesting it. I wouldn’t recommend this place even if you were looking for food to feed your dog.

my family and i love this restaurant and order from here frequently, and have been for at least two years. we spend at least $200 when we go!! we recently ordered and immediately i noticed that they have made their containers smaller while the meal is the EXACT same price of $22!!! the white container is not from mukase but that is the size their containers used to be, the black container on the right is now the new size. and when you open the container it is not even filled fully, they simply fill stew around the meat. in the picture with my bowl i haven’t even dipped stew mind you, just removed meat and see how the stew is depleted. in my eyes this is a cheat and frankly, very disappointing. i love this restaurant but this is what will make me stop eating from a place when they do stuff like this to good paying customers.

Mukase is the best in the city IMO! My family and I have been visiting for a few years. I go almost weekly for takeout. I appreciate the cuisine being consistent with its flavor, freshness and satisfying portions, chef’s kiss! customer service I give 10/10 as well.
Great food! I’ve visited Ghana multiple times and this is 100 percent authentic!!!! Delicious and filling!!!  I can’t wait to go back!

formatted_address: 8311 S Baltimore Ave, Chicago, IL 60617, United States
name: Southside African Restaurant

reviews.text:
This place is very very good! I go often!
Customer service is good and the food taste great! Very fair potion size for the price!!
I always order the
Egusi  soup with fish or another soup kept in the glass container/warmer (small bowl) it is green has a boiled egg in it! It’s very good

I’ve also tried the pepper goat it was very tough both times and I’ve tried the pepper fish I didn’t enjoy it!
Very respectable workers. Clean and friendly atmosphere 👌 I visit at least  once a week. Great place, delicious food!
These guys have ZERO customer service skills. Need tire shine for your car? This is the place to be. Extra grease included.
OK my goat portion was very satisfactory. Full piece of fish and goat was tender. Egusi was so so good with fufu and pepper sauce.

This is the second time I’ve ate from here and was disappointed. Service was horrible . I asked for goat and was serve a meal with no meat and charged for it . The food isn’t worth the price . I wouldn’t recommend

formatted_address: 1901 W 87th St, Chicago, IL 60620, United States
name: SAMIFLORENCIA AFRICAN CUISINE

reviews.text: I lovedddd the Egusi & FuFu! Soooo good! I’ll definitely be back. The wings could’ve been cooked a lil longer but they still had a good flavor. The fried rice had sautéed veggies with a sauce on it that I wish my rice had more of. The customer service was amazing and the home feel and clean atmosphere of the restaurant made us enjoy the whole experience even more.

SOO GOOD LITERALLY NO NOTES. Super clean and nice restaurant, great service (timely and have complimentary soup), and the food was too good. My mom is a picky eater but I brought back some leftovers and she cleared it. We tried the Ayamase and seafood Okra soup!

I've been dying to find some African food, mostly Egosi soup I finally got it and my wife she got the okra seafood soup. This place did not disappoint. The food was very very good. I definitely will be back to try their peanut butter soup, it looked Delicious a as well.

Samiflorencia African Cuisine is an absolute Amazing.The combination of the flavorful, aromatic rice and the juicy, tender shrimp was pure culinary bliss. It was a dish that was both comforting and exciting, and I can't wait to go back for more. Samiflorencia African Cuisine not only serves amazing food but also provides an unforgettable dining experience. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for authentic, delicious African cuisine.

Ok so I haven’t been inside yet, I ordered Uber Eats and it is pricey ok but when I tell you once I took a sip of that goat pepper soup I would have paid more!!! Now don’t go raising prices auntie cuz I don’t got it but if I did I’d pay it ok! I ordered the goat pepper soup, jollof rice, and ginger pineapple juice. I had been sick and not tasted or smelled a thing but I tasted every single flavor in that soup and it brought me to life! Love love loved every bite and I’m so happy I ordered I don’t give a damn about that $$ 😂

formatted_address: 4623 N Broadway, Chicago, IL 60640, United States
name: Iyanze Bar And Cafe

reviews.text: The service at this restaurant was really good. The place is really clean and I can imagine when they are having a live event it would be fun. The food was delicious. The portions are pretty large. I got the okro soup and fu fu. It was made perfect and delicious. I also had to try the Egusi which was also good. I couldn’t leave without trying the Jollof. I had it with chicken and fish. To top it all off their drinks are really good as well. Thank you and I will return again,

I usually only stick to one place for egusi & fufu cause multiple times I ordered from different places it was trouble but today I didn’t feel like driving all the way south from north & I usually just ride pass this place but today I’m like let me just try it out and what can I say the food was phenomenal for the price & the portions for me as well. And I only spent 15 all together & that price included the tip I enjoyed it so much I had to personally call the restaurant myself & tell them what I thought 😁I surely will be trying again soon! It was such a honor to experience west African food.

I really enjoyed all of the food. Tried a few new dishes to me and all quite delicious. People complain about small portions but I think for the price the portions are okay. Probably could’ve been a little bit more meat for the $5 portion but I think they almost give enough. I have a pretty mediocre spice tolerance, and I thought everything had a nice solid spice level. Everything was seasoned well. Jollof rice was smoky and tasty and a large portion. Also fufu was a large portion.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Absolutely amazing experience.
This Nigerian restaurant truly feels like home. The food was fresh, flavorful, and perfectly seasoned,  just the way it should be. The jollof rice had that rich smoky taste, the suya was tender and spicy, and the egusi soup tasted exactly like something mama would cook on a Sunday.

Mr. Dapo attended to me, he was so warm and welcoming, and the service was fast and professional. The atmosphere was vibrant, clean, and full of good energy. You can tell they put love into every dish.

If you want real Nigerian food that hits the soul, this is the spot. Highly recommend, I will definitely be coming back again and again. 🇳🇬❤️

I honestly think this place should be shut down at this point. Why do you guys keep serving spoiled food to people? Depending on the time of day you order, the food is for sure bound to be bad. It’s happened to me a few times and luckily I get a refund on the delivery app. My friend ordered again today and the meat pie she got was bad.

formatted_address: 4801 N Broadway, Chicago, IL 60640, United States
name: Demera Restaurant

reviews.text:
First time having Ethiopian food and it was amazing! Messob appetizer and family-style messob were very flavorful; however, the beef was too tough. Also had the tiramisu and tea. Tiramisu was a home run, but the tea was very light in flavor.
Finally, the food is a bit overpriced for the quantity you get and tends to be oily for my taste.

Absolutely phenomenal. I’ve eaten at several Ethiopian restaurants across the county, and Demera rose straight to the top of that category. Every single dish was bursting with flavor. We enjoyed the messob platter (4 meats, 4 vegetables) among 4 people that surely could have served 5. 10/10. We also enjoyed the ye-asa tibs (whole fish), lega tibs (lamb), and sambussa sampler. The sambussa was the star of the show for me. I’d return for that in particular. We also tried the mitmita and orange crème brûlée. Woah… 20/10. Overall a lovely dining experience and packed on a Tuesday night. They deserve every penny. See you soon!
I had the awaze tibs, the samosas and the buna coffee. I thought every was great and it’s a fun experience since Ethiopian is quite different from the other major cuisines. Service was lovely.

We had a phenomenal experience at Demera. We ordered a couple Messobs and vegetarian dishes. Everything was top notch and tasted great. The injeeras were outstanding as well. Wait staff was very efficient in catering to big crowds. And oh, the Tiramisu was second to none!

Please order the creme brûlée. It’s so amazing and I can’t stop thinking about it. It was the perfect blend of sweet, salty, and spicy. The texture was also perfect. We wanted to order beef but they didn’t have it so they kindly offered to make a lamb dish not spicy. The food was made incredibly fast, especially for a substitution. Our server was very kind and helpful in answering all our questions. I love that there’s plenty of seating and nice outdoor seating, too.

formatted_address: 211 W Walton St, Chicago, IL 60610, United States
name: BULSHO restaurant

reviews.text: Came all the way from Philadelphia for this. I was on business and decided to check it out. The owners are so sweet and explained everything to me. I got a giant plate of food (spicy rice, chicken, and veggies) that I couldn’t possibly finish in one go even though I wanted to keep eating. Definitely worth the trip!

I had high hopes for BULSHO in Chicago, but unfortunately, it didn’t live up to the expectation. The so-called "traditional" Somali cuisine was far from authentic, with flavors that felt watered down and a lack of the depth you'd expect from the real deal. To make matters worse, the prices are absolutely outrageous for what you get. The portions are small, and for the quality of the food, it’s just not worth it. To top it all off, the restaurant itself was dirty as hell. The floors were sticky, and the tables hadn't been wiped down properly. It's clear that cleanliness isn’t a priority here. Overall, a disappointing experience. I wouldn't recommend it to anyone looking for good Somali food or a pleasant dining environment.

Simple place with basic interiors with decent food. Serves Somalian and is very popular with the locals. I liked the food here for breakfast. Had something that resembles a dosa ( crepe ) with a variety of curries for 12$

I am reminiscing on my visit here a couple years ago - I don't live in Chicago and I am not Somali.

I went here with my friend as I was in the neighborhood and wanted to try African food in the city. It is a hole in the wall locals only type of cafeteria. My friend and I were the only non-africans in this busy / crowded restaurant.

I ordered rice, beans, stewed vegetables and bread - I enjoyed my food a good bit but I don't eat meat so perhaps I didn't get the full experience.

BUT half way through eating our meal a little ring comes on through an intercom and everyone gets up and goes to this other room - I assume to pray.🙏🏽
Here my friend and I are the only ones in the cafeteria, eating our food in silence, whereas two minutes ago it was very loud. It was just an eye opening example of how  collected and community oriented people can be and still are. My friend and I were just about finishing up when everyone comes out of this room and the restaurant becomes loud again. It was probably the most interesting and beautiful experience I've had at a restaurant.

I hope this place is around for a long while.

First time trying Somalian food. A very local and unique restaurant that is cafeteria style.

I enjoyed the food and the bread flatbread was a must add on.

Very friendly service :)

formatted_address: 2835 N Broadway, Chicago, IL 60614, United States
name: Comfort's African Cuisine

reviews.text:
Objectively, comfort African cuisine is a very nice restaurant. They have reasonably priced food, nice staff, and fast service.

The jollof rice was especially delicious and flavorful. The fufu had a good texture, and the beef patty was really enjoyable.

Everything was objectively very well prepared.
With that said, and given the context I am autistic and have very specific food preferences, certain dishes were a bit overwhelming for me personally. This is to no fault of the restaurant itself; to the contrary, the flavors seemed authentic, and the vast majority of the dishes were delicious.
4.8/5 stars, Will likely come again for the jollof

This is the most disgusting place I have ever gotten food from. The food was in the fridge, who knows how many days old. I saw silver pans of food in a fridge, look like it was cooked elsewhere. I ordered beef and jollof rice. The beef was one big hard bone!! An inedible piece of mystery meat. It looked like a piece of meat they used to put in a stew to “flavor” the dish. I could not take one bite. Please do not buy from here they need to be shut down !!! $18 for bush meat and spicy unflavored rice! Disgusting!!!

I was craving some West African food on Thanksgiving so I decided to order from Comfort African Cuisine through the website. While waiting for my food I got a notification that the order was canceled ( duh of course they were closed lol).  I called the next day and spoke with the kitchen and they confrimed that they were closed and that the pending charge will back on my card which it was! They was so kind and apologetic for the situation which was totally not their fault. This is why I love the place and putting customer first. Looking forward to ordering there again soon!

This is truly a taste of home. The jollof rice chicken is perfectly seasoned, the poundo yam is smooth and satisfying, and the egusi soup with goat meat so delicious and rich in flavor and cooked to perfection. The suya is smoky, spicy, and absolutely delicious. Great food, and an authentic, Highly recommended!

In Chi town for a few days, decided to try this place.Ordered on uber eats, the fried rice was 3/10, the goat meat was boiled and stewed , why could you guys not just fry your goat meat so it tastes good. The turkey was one bony piece of turkey for $5:99. You could have just given a descent piece of turkey, but No.
I will say that the moinmoin in the leaf was really nice.That was the best thing from my whole order.
I don’t know if I would have been served something better if I had dined in.
Overall I was dissatisfied and would try somewhere else next time.

formatted_address: 7118 N Clark St, Chicago, IL 60626, United States
name: Qaato African Restaurant

reviews.text: I don’t know who the chef is but I can’t get enough of that egusi soup! I never actually went and ate at the restaurant but I always order and they deliver. I always get it not too spicy due to my heartburn. You get e nice portion of soup and the goat meat as well. Never been disappointed and will continue ordering from them!
The food is tasteless.  Not the Quaato of the past. The smell of the stew is just indescribable ( both ogbono and ewedu) and the jollof rice was tasteless. The chicken has no taste. Good bye.

Stopped by Qaato African Restaurant for lunch last Saturday—had the egusi soup with fufu and their beef kebab. Man, the soup was rich and cozy but fufu could’ve been softer. Service was friendly but kinda slow. Also grabbed their tamarind juice to wash it down. Overall, vibes are chill and decor’s colorful. Would dig more vegan sides next time.

I’ve been craving some fufu and decided to try this place. From the entrance to the register, the place did not look too kosher. A woman asked me if I called or placing an order? I told her ordering, and that was the last I heard from her. Stood there for ten to fifteen minutes and never took my order. That was the first and last time they will see me. Might need to do an inspection of the place.

If you're craving authentic West African flavors in the city, Qaato's the spot. I grabbed the Egusi Soup with Goat Meat and Amala—rich, hearty, and packed with spice. The goat was tender, and the soup had that perfect balance of savory and spicy. Portions are generous, so it's well worth the $20. The vibe inside is warm and welcoming, and the staff makes you feel right at home. Definitely a go-to for anyone looking to enjoy real African cuisine in Chicago.

formatted_address: 4655 S Lake Park Ave Apt 000, Chicago, IL 60653, United States
name: Abusua Kitchen

reviews.text:
Probably good food, but they only do catering, not a physical restaurant. Call to order for at least 6-10 people.
We were just 2 of us visiting Chicago, so it wouldn't make sense for us to order that much.

Very impressed with:
1. Customer service
2. Taste of food
3.  Great value for money (feeds 5-6 people)
Will certainly recommend! And can't wait to try more foods on the menu.
Healthy and very delicious dishes upon request! Words not enough to describe the experience. I'll definitely recommend them on any day.
Ordered beans stew with fried plantains, goat meat and fried fish. Wow! It was well cooked and the portion size is perfect for my fiancé and I.
The food tastes so good and it is really worth the price that comes with it. I would buy food from this place over and over again.

formatted_address: 1418 W Howard St, Chicago, IL 60626, United States
name: Nayos African Cuisines

reviews.text: Absolutely amazing Nigerian food! We ordered egusi with iyan, jollof rice, and both fish and chicken stew — everything was bursting with flavor and perfectly seasoned. The egusi was rich and authentic, the jollof had just the right spice, and the stews were full of tender meat and depth. You can really taste the love and tradition in every bite. We left full and happy — highly recommend this spot for anyone craving real Nigerian comfort food! The owner/cook/host Nayo, was pleasant.

The lights that are all around would be beautiful if the overheads were off to give it a grown and sexy vibe at night.
The Jollof rice was amazing!!! I have had Jollof before, but not like this. The fish was delicious. Warm, friendly atmosphere. Family friendly with seating areas.

My brother and I visited Nayo’s African Cuisine on New Year’s Eve and ordered the jollof rice with a side of plantains. The flavors were beautifully balanced with just the right amount of spice and tasted truly authentic. Everything felt freshly made and full of care. I’d recommend calling ahead to confirm entrée availability, especially on busy days. I’m already looking forward to coming back to try the egusi or okra soup. A great spot for real African comfort food.

My Man And I Went To Visit Chicago From Iowa And We Were Very Pleased To Dine In At Nayo’s African Cuisine. We Went That Afternoon For Lunch And The Food Was So Great ! The Restaurant Was Clean And Nayo Was Very Nice And Welcoming . When We Left We Started Craving For The Food Again , So We Decided To Stop By Nayo’s Again For Dinner And Again He Didn’t Disappoint. Thanks Nayo For Being So Kind And Welcoming To Us On Our Short Stay ! We Hope To See You Again Soon !

Tried Nayo’s Kitchen and had an amazing experience all around. The food was authentic, flavorful, and clearly made with care. Every dish brought back real taste-of-home vibes.

The service was friendly and welcoming, and the space had a comfortable, down-to-earth feel that made the whole experience even better.

If you’re looking for legit Nigerian cuisine in the area, Nayo’s Kitchen is the spot. I’ll definitely be back.

formatted_address: 6232 N Broadway, Chicago, IL 60660, United States
name: Vee-Vee's African Restaurant

reviews.text:
i’m highly disappointed at the service.

i ordered to go and they gave me basically 4 plantains and a size of fish that was the size of a bread roll. i never got my fish stew AND they admitted that my portion would be better if i dined in next time???? the portion to go should be the same because i am PAYING the same.

don’t ever order to go here.

The old man there at night way extremely rude. He kept insulting me because I took time figuring out what app i used to order. Door dash or uber eats. That was very unprofessional and traumatizing. And the jollof is not good it’s like white rice and palm oil no taste.

Great service and good food. The owner/manager was very accommodating and answered many questions about Nigerian food and culture. Turns out many foods I thought were Caribbean actually originated in Africa. I look forward to my next visit to try more things on the menu.

DO NOT WASTE YOUR MONEY! THE WORST AFRICAN FOOD I'VE EVER TASTED. I ordered the pepper soup and goat meat. The soup was tasteless and a small portion.  The goat meat didn't have any MEAT! I paid $30 for this mess! I don't understand how this restaurant is still open!

Rolled into Vee‑Vee’s African Restaurant for dinner—dropped about $25 on jollof rice with goat meat and a side of plantains. The flavors were on point—rice had that nice spice kick, goat was tender, and plantains were crispy-sweet. Staff was friendly and let me BYOB, which is clutch. Seating was cozy but packed, and wait was decent. Top-tier dinner spot north side—just wish portions were a smidge bigger. Will def be back!

formatted_address: 1127 W Thorndale Ave, Chicago, IL 60660, United States
name: Dynamic African Restaurant Cuisine & Catering Service

reviews.text: First time trying African food. It is delicious and like they have a self ordering machine which is convenient to order . I will definitely come back again 🤩

This place was amazing — the food was great, but what really stood out was the atmosphere. It didn’t even feel like I was at a restaurant. It felt like I was at my grandma’s house. That’s how welcoming and family-oriented the staff was. Everyone was so kind and genuine. You can tell they really care about their customers. Would definitely recommend to anyone looking for not just a good meal, but a place that feels like home.

Very sweet staff that went out of their way to make my family (of 4) feel comfortable. They explained the menu items and clarified that some items on the menu are only available via catering, which was fine. I initially was allowing the negative reviews out me on guard but I glad I stayed and support this Nigerian establishment. 5 stars!!!!

The pepper soup was really flavorful and good but the goat meat was chewy to an inedible point. The soup container was barely filled (see picture, I'd eaten some and the meat is in a corner so it was a little more filled than this but not much). I paid thirty dollars for this. A Togo box just full of white rice and a small order of plantains.  Not going again which sucks because the soup (sans meat) is delicious.

Every time I order from here, they always say we are out of that item. The staff is extremely rude! One time I was leaving the restaurant once again, disappointed with no food. The lady ran out and started yelling at me, saying, "you parked too close to my car! I'm watching you, and you better not scratch it!" So not only did I walk away with no food and no apology. I also get yelled at. I'm sorry but you lost me.

formatted_address: 4701 N Kenmore Ave, Chicago, IL 60640, United States
name: B&Q Afro Root Cuisine

reviews.text:
We were greeted when we walked in, and felt very welcome. She helped with some recommendations, I loved it. Super authentic and that’s what I was looking for. I walked out struggling from eating so much. I couldn’t eat more if I wanted to, Lol.
My plate was on the right, btw!

Very small intimate space, large portions of food, and affordable. Was a little unclear what to do upon entry, as no one immediately greeted us. Seemed like everything was run buy one lady and a kitchen crew. I'm not familiar with Nigerian cuisine so it was a new food experience for me and I enjoyed everything we ordered. I got the vibe that this the kind of place area locals know of and go to, without a lot of first-timers like myself. This was sort of a back-up choice since other area restaurants were packed, but it was quiet, with a handful of customers, and honestly it was good and felt like the better place to be! Would come back again. Cash tipping only. Street parking in the vicinity.

Very disappointed, I really wanted to try this place but unfortunately I was not able to. I had surgery earlier this year and so I can only eat small portions of food. I went in and try to order a side of egusi soup, which is on the menu, but she refused.  I even tried to tell her about my situation and why I can only eat small amounts of food and she still refused and said they don't sell anything in small portions. Even though they're the whole list of side dish options. Very disappointing and it's discriminatory.

I Tried to dine-in here to see if my last experience would be better this time around the lady just gave me ugly stares as soon as I walked in and as I was trying to place my order she walked off as I was talking so I just left she’s very rude and giving jealous vibes I’ll never come back and if you want good customer service go to comfort food on Broadway and the food Is the best
Very homey vibe; felt like I was in a living room. The egusi and fufu were quite good, though the chicken was tough.

formatted_address: 1027 W Wilson Ave, Chicago, IL 60640, United States
name: Osas African Restaurant - Nigerian cuisine

reviews.text: Highly do not recommend! My food was not fresh at all, and the service wasn’t pleasant. I literally had leftovers and old meat that was super hard to chew. They so called reheated as some of the food was still cold and tasted like food that sat in the fridge without being covered. In addition, the spinach soup was barely filled and there were so many tiny bones inside of it. Never again!

Just left 11 minutes ago and I have to say I will be back because I pulled over and ate the whole thing! Delicious food! Family atmosphere and family owned! Thank you and your beautiful family for giving me the best food and experience my first time eating egusi, tripe, and fufu the day before my birthday!
The food is tasty, fresh and always hot. Friendly staff and quick service.

I can’t believe i bought left over food for 22 dollars so disappointing a friend recommended this restaurant I ordered for beans and plantain take away got home to find out the soup is left over from someone bad restaurant I regret going there p

First time here and got the beef Egusi with Amala. It came piping hot, both the Amala and Egusi, but I dug in anyway. Ripping a piece of Amala, roll, and dip. African cuisine is often eaten with your hands, and I like to experience food the way the culture intend it to be. One of the staff was surprised I suggested eating with my hands and asked a bit about me. Guess it's uncommon for non-Africans to eat like Africans here haha

I emptied the bowl and plate, cleaned leftover stew with what's left of my Amala. It was that good. There are other options I should try, and I'll definitely be back to try their other items. Maybe next time I'll take a picture to share

formatted_address: 1010 W Argyle St, Chicago, IL 60640, United States
name: Afro Taste Cuisine LLC

reviews.text: I don’t live in the area but I was curious about this new spot since I love Nigerian food. I’m glad I gave it a try! Her food is fresh and tasty. Definitely will keep ordering when we are in the area!

The egusi soup/pounded yam and yam porridge are exactly as advertised in the images, but more than that, very tasty and flavorful. The food is a 100% one of the best I have had at home (naija) and abroad. It is a 1000% authically Nigerian.

I spoke with the owner yesterday and confirmed that they would be open. I explained that I was bringing my husband for his birthday today. We drove 40 minutes to this restaurant just to see that I was lied to on such a special day. I am so upset and I really wanted my husband to eat authentic Nigerian food….. I would not patronize restaurants that do not consider their customers.

Great jollof and egusi soup, and the portions were good too! Got it with fish and chicken and they were really flavorful and delicious. Spicy level wasn’t too bad either, I could really feel it but I could still taste all the flavors and it wasn’t numbing like Chinese hot pot.
Note - We weren’t sure if they were open, had to ring the digital bell on the door frame a couple times but glad we did because the food was fantastic.
amazing! first time trying nigerian food & it didn’t disappoint!

formatted_address: 4447 N Broadway, Chicago, IL 60640, United States
name: Nigerian Kitchen Restaurant

reviews.text: We ordered Jollof Rice, Fish Pepper soup, Plaintain, Snail, chicken 😋it was quite delicious and very Affordable ❤️💃
A comforting and flavorful takeout meal. The egusi with fufu was rich and satisfying, and the Jollof rice was super tasty and well-seasoned.

Not sure why there’s so many bad reviews, I got the egusi soup with pounded yam and it was excellent, the food was a good size, affordable and tastiest fresh and authentic, had a bit of good spice to it. People keep saying the lady was rude in the front, but I think many of you are very sensitive and expect people to greet you like your at an olive garden and bow down to you. She was direct and polite in my opinion. Again this isn’t Olive Garden, so wait times for food to be ready might be longer.

PLEASE DO NOT PATRONIZE!!!
The service was horrible, customer service was zero and they had the effrontery to upcharge me.
I generally prefer not to give a review than leaving a bad review, but this one was extra bad.
How can you provide me with a menu with prices, and upon payment you’re charging me a different amount.
It’s ridiculous really. All I got was sorry.
Please listen to the reviews and don’t go there. Except you love bland meals, horrible service and love being ripped off.

Ignored the reviews and enjoyed my first visit here. The second visit was so insultingly bad that I have to completely change my review. It wasn’t edible. You were chewing into bone and fat that wouldn’t be penetrated by teeth. Just went straight into the garbage.

formatted_address: 2407 W Lunt Ave, Chicago, IL 60645, United States
name: Yinkres Nigerian Restaurant

reviews.text: Tonight I found this place on Google I saw a picture of the Jollof rice and fish. I decided to walk in to order best decision so good just enough spice plenty of flavor no need for salt. Very nice lady!!

There are a few tables here, but most people I saw order for takeout. Once upon a time, during the pandemic in August 2020, my best friend and I ordered here. We really
liked the food. I went back in
December 2023 after her memorial service & the food is still yummy. If I remember correctly, I ordered the goat and rice dish both times. Huge
servings. I made at least 2 meals out of my 1 order.
Rest in Peace, dearest Ai (1981-2023).

Best jollof rice in the city! Very tasty and fresh. Tiny restaurant, you might have to call because they keep the door locked sometimes. But we are always greeted warmly when we stop in. Highly recommend

The food is very authentic and taste great but the packaging for the meats for the jollof rice the stew was wasted in the bag as well as the delivery drivers car so we did’nt have much left to pour over the rice.

I’m obsessed😩
Literally THE BEST African food on the north side!

I order at least once per week.

The owner is super sweet and makes everything fresh.

I love it!!

And YES.
Yes I will be eating this entire plate😋

formatted_address: 853 S Roselle Rd, Schaumburg, IL 60193, United States
name: Bisi Restaurant - Nigerian cuisine

reviews.text:
Food: First time trying Nigerian food and it was delicious. I was recommended this place by a client of mine. We had the moi moi, honey bean entree, and jollof rice entree. I loved the jollof rice with fish. Fish was fresh and light, not heavily battered. That was served with the best plantains I've ever had. As a certified potato lover™️ I do not say this lightly: the plantains were better than potatoes.
My partner had the honey beans with chicken and beef. He said he really liked it, but it was just on the spicier side. The moimoi was very good too.
Service: Excellent, kind, and welcoming.
Atmosphere: It's very nice inside, with thoughtful details in the napkins and the booth styling.

Tried this spot on a friend’s recommendation, and it was my first time having Nigerian food. The experience was excellent. Great food and a cozy ambiance. I started with the meat pie, which had a soft, warm crust and a flavorful filling. For the main course, I had Jollof rice with beef: the tomato-based rice was savory, the plantains were sweet and crispy, and the beef was seasoned perfectly. My server, Francis, was super kind and attentive. Highly recommend, and I’ll definitely be back!

My husband and I drove an hour and 15 minutes to experience this place and it did NOT disappoint! The food was delicious and the interaction with the workers was welcoming. The dining area is beautiful and cozy.
We enjoyed EVERYTHING we had and definitely will return. We had the meat pie which was delicious and simple. I had the Egusi soup with goat meat which was full of flavor. It has a kick of spice which stays in the mouth and pairs extremely well with the fufu. My husband ordered the whole fish which came beautifully plated with plantains. Now that dish is extremely spicy for those of you who like heat. It is also quite flavorful and cooked to perfection. We shared the Jollof rice with beef and that was SO good. The beef was definitely a great choice with it and again we were hit with lots of flavor. I'm certainly sad that we have to travel to experience this goodness but it was worth it and we will return again!

It was $27 for fufu and egusi and me and my mom could only finish that one order shared! Huge portion sizes!! They give you sooo much food and it is delicious. Highly recommend this restaurant, our server was so kind we loved him !🩷 we drove 45 minutes to come here and it is 100% worth the drive. We will be back !

Insanely expensive. Great service and OK food but wow they really ripped me off. I bought the fufu and egusi and jollof rice with chicken and plantain and that cost $60!! Sixty American Dollars. Absolutely insane. I know for sure they got over on me. There was barely any chicken! I should’ve questioned the bill, but sometimes I just go along with things and I regret that. The fufu and egusi was priced at $27 and the jollof with chicken was $19 yet my total was $60. Anyways, get a receipt ladies and gents. Don’t be like me.

formatted_address: 5352 N Broadway, Chicago, IL 60640, United States
name: Tesfa Ethiopian Cuisine

reviews.text: Loved the food so much — my whole family enjoyed the plate with vegetarian and meat/fish dishes and injera. We left with full tummies. I liked the Ethiopian margarita as well. Next time, I’d love to try the tea and dessert. The service was great as well!

First time to Tesfa, and our family was delighted with the atmosphere and food.  Yeah, the service isn’t the fastest, but that, in my opinion, is a plus.  Our server was kind and gracious.  The food was terrific. Perfect spice levels and good quantities.  There were four of us and we ordered a platter with 3 veggie and 3 meat dishes.  My favorite was the Asa be-Shiro (tilapia).  Loved the spices.
Lastly, the atmosphere is terrific.  Upscale enough to know this place is here for a date night or a family get together.  It isn’t here for takeout only.  TVs playing Ethiopian music videos and a football game.

I just love Tesfa and I was reminded of that tonight. I missed them being in uptown because it was so convenient. We've always had an amazing time when we dine here in uptown- you can feel the home cooking.

There new location is beautiful, spacious, modern and has a full bar.

We ordered sambusas for appetizers and it's so fire!! And for our entree- we did the platter for 2, with two meats and 3 veggies: zil zil tibs, doro wot, red lentils, gomen, and beets = everything was cooked to perfection and fresh. It was a lot of food 😋

You'll have to wait for a bit for your entree because I suspect they're making things to order. It's worth the wait 👏🏾

Our waitress was meh- she wasn't attentive, a bit aloof & she barely came to our table.

The two brothers who run the place are the best and welcoming!

The food is sooo good here and the vibes are amazing! Our waiter was telling us about how it’s his family business and they are working on getting enough business that they can open their rooftop patio regularly. It’s a beautiful space!! We got the family platter with four meat and four vegetarian dishes and everything was DELECTABLE. Make sure to get here early because they make everything fresh so it takes a while to get your food.

Decide to try this restaurant today  for Ethiopian cuisine. The restaurant Ethiopian decor was beautiful. The food was amazing and delicious. I left today very satisfied and full. The staff also show great hospitality and professionalism. This was a very enjoyable, welcoming and cozy experience. I recommend people to come visit this location.

formatted_address: 6635 N Clark St, Chicago, IL 60626, United States
name: Denden Restaurant

reviews.text:
Absolutely delicious food and the literal best coffee you’ll ever have in your life.  Make sure to order the coffee early as they roast the beans in a pot and it comes out later in beautiful presentation.

Low key and quiet atmosphere,  prices are very fair.  Been going to this place for years, such a gem!

I cannot for the life of me understand why this place is empty when I walk past it. The food was exceptionally good, the service was quick and attentive, and the inside is pretty with nice music. The prices being completely reasonable for the amount is the cherry on top as well. I highly recommend this place, both for people who are familiar with eastern African food as well as those looking to try something new.

The best Eritrean restaurant in Chicago! I prefer Den-Den over the pantheon of Ethiopian restaurants in Chicago.  Den-Den's superlative food is a highlighted, featuring the best Ye Beg Alicha, veggie plate, and awaze. They also serve the best Tej in the city, and their injera is uniquely made without the over abundance of  wheat. The Tej is salient. The coffee ceremony is also a highlight.  My family  lingers and enjoy the atmosphere staying for two or more hours during our visit.

Den Den Restaurant on Clark Street in Chicago is an extraordinary five-star gem that immerses diners in the rich, aromatic world of Eritrean and Ethiopian cuisine, where every bite tells a story of tradition and flavor mastery. The injera flatbread serves as the perfect tangy canvas for vibrant dishes like the zigni beef stew, simmered to tender perfection in a berbere-spiced sauce that balances heat and depth with fresh vegetables, while the vegetarian shiro offers a creamy, garlicky chickpea delight that’s both comforting and complex. The cozy, culturally adorned space buzzes with warm hospitality from the staff, who guide you through the communal eating style with genuine enthusiasm, making it ideal for sharing plates and creating memorable moments at prices that feel like a gift for such authentic, generous portions. Whether you’re a spice aficionado or new to East African fare, Den Den delivers an unparalleled dining experience that leaves you satiated, inspired, and already plotting your return.
We just finished lunch. The food was delicious, flavorful with large portions. We have  new favorite restaurant.

formatted_address: 308 E 51st St, Chicago, IL 60615, United States
name: Iyanze Bronze

reviews.text: The jollof rice had no flavor and was cold even though I walked in to order it, $5.29 for 5 pcs of plantain is ridiculous. No menu posted or handed out, you can’t see what you’re ordering. If you’re a first timer like me Goodluck! Also the moi moi looked like it’s been reheated multiple times and not freshly made daily. The cashier/server had an attitude over the phone and also when I came in, she didn’t put my meat and plantain in a separate container instead she stuffed it into the rice. No gloves, just attitude. I’m not going back here ever. You gotta have receipt sent to your phone even though you walked in.
The food tastes great and made freshly!! Love their puff pastry it’s the best n the mashed beans with ofe iyanze a bit spicy to my taste but love it

I wish I had read these reviews before ordering from Uber eats. I ordered the egusi stew with Nigerian chicken and fufu. The stew was not tasty at all. Has a slight burnt flavor. The chicken was so dry and tough I could barely bite into it. The only thing that was alright was the fufu. I was so Disappointed. I threw it all away.

I got the jollof rice with stewed chicken in tomato sauce and some sort of mixed soup at the recommendation of the woman at the register and disappointed is not the word. The jollof was tasted very burnt and the chicken was very dried out as if it was cooked for hours and then sauced to try to add moisture back into it.

The soup was okay but it was extremely fishy and the fufu was very bland. I’m upset that I spent almost $60 for this as I brought 2 of each item for myself and my husband.

I went for the first time. And this was my experience....The lady at the counter was not forth coming with an explanation about menu because I had no clue. She just handed me the QR code to pull the menu up. And when I asked a question about one of the items on the menu,  She told me all the menu items are not at the location I was currently at. WOW! but okay.  I initially ordered the beef pattie or meat pie and a Ting. But I was very curious about the food on display, She told me they have rice plate for $15.99 and you can add an extra meat dish for $16.99. I was like cool let me get the one with 2 options.
Basically she gave me 2 pieces of meat. A goat piece and a chicken piece. Which I wish I would have taken a pictures of,  cause the portion was so small. Anyhoo...I got it back to the office and the meat was sooooooo tough!!!!! I mean a fork was not getting thru it. I used a kitchen metal fork now and the meat fought me. Both small pieces. And I couldn't tell what part of the chicken I was eating so I just threw it away and saved the rice.
I paid $24.88 for a dry beef pattie and a plate of rice (because the meat was inedible). Oh lets not forget the Ting. This is ridiculous and horrible! I wish I could get a refund. So I just brought the rice home, made some shrimp in my air fryer and some left over veggies from last nights dinner.
Needless to say I won't be going back!

formatted_address: 8928 S Commercial Ave, Chicago, IL 60617, United States
name: African Food Palace

reviews.text:
Ambiance is good and clean.

The Staff I met was professional but not friendly.

Food took about 15-20 mins to be served, and that was because it was made fresh, not reheated, which I appreciate.

The white rice was half done and hard.
The Ayamase and goat Meat were not seasoned well, hence tasted bland and oily.
This is the main reason I gave a 3 star.

Portion size is okay, I wouldn't complain because these African ingredients have to be imported plus other costs of running a business.

Overall, I wouldn't recommend and won't repeat.

Excellent food and service. The best African restaurant in Illinois. Fried rice, turkey, chicken and vegetables soup taste so delicious. Best spot ever. The jollof rice is excellent too. Highly recommend.

the ogbono soup was disgusting  she made  me pay for something i told her i did not like and that i wouldn’t eat any further after i told her it was disgusting and i did not want it but she proceeded to not listen to me and told me i had to pay for it since it was my first time here which is diabolical and i didn’t like it because it had locus  beans in it and it made me want to throw up they’re business will never prosper handling business like that and treating there mistreating there customers and are money hungry people like that will never will win in life. i never knew you had to pay for something you didn’t like nor ate but i would never recommend this restaurant to anyone they’re completely rude to customers they have zero manners and i’ll never come back here ever again and i’ll tell people to not come here too. the restaurant give dirty vibes the bbb needs to check them out because it’s horrible & the portions was horrible i should’ve got more for what im paying for they played but that’s they loss not mines because i get more food at  different african restaurants than this one and she tried to argue me up and down about the locus beans i’ve been eating african food for years and never had that in my food ever and they never disclosed that which i felt like they should’ve and the meat was burnt i couldn’t eat that clearly she didn’t care about how  she treats her customers and i only had three things of meat

I have been ordering from lady c for years. She’s a wonderful human inside and out. We have done community events, catered parties and dined in as well. She’s very accommodating and takes such pride in her food, her ingredients and her culture. 11 out of 10. I’ll be back soon! Pictured here is a small amount of her always generous okra stew 💕

I got the egusi soup with chicken, fufu, plantains, jollof rice with two eggs, chicken and cow skin. I liked everything. However, the jollof could be a little bit more spicy, and the chicken is tough. I would visit this place again. I have been inside this restaurant and it isn’t perfect because it’s a small business. I didn’t see anything alarming about this place, and I visited at night.

formatted_address: 6324 N Broadway, Chicago, IL 60660, United States
name: Awash Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text:
Sooooo delicious! We ended up here by chance; we were out looking for Ethiopian food around 10:10pm,  after a concert. The first one we went to, closes its kitchen at 10, so we found this wasn’t far and called to confirm they were still serving food.

The ladies that served us, were great! They had great recommendations. We ordered sambusas; the lentil sambusas were so delicious, I ordered some to take home. My cousin enjoyed his beef sambusas. We shared the veggie combo platter; every item on it was packed with flavor; we cleared that platter! We also enjoyed the honey wine in the traditional glasses; what an experience!

This was our first time at Awash and we agree that it won’t be the last.

We has a delicious birthday dinner here! It was a Friday night, but it wasn't busy. The service was excellent, and we really liked how the incense was served with the tea & coffee. The meat sampler was spicy, which is how I liked it. My vegetarian husband enjoyed his platter very much, especially the collard greens. I think food eaten with my fingers tastes better!

Awash Ethiopian Restaurant is hands-down one of the best dining experiences I’ve had in a long time. The food is fresh, vibrant, and full of authentic flavor. I ordered the vegan combo, and every single item around the injera was seasoned perfectly,  rich lentils, flavorful greens, perfectly spiced veggies, and beautifully balanced sauces. You can tell everything is made with care. If you love Ethiopian food, or you’re trying it for the first time, Awash is absolutely the place to go. I’ll definitely be back!

Food is really good and is highly recommended for you to visit Awash for an authentic Ethiopian food experience. They will roast coffee beans and burn frankincense from time to time. The atmosphere feels good. The waitresses are real nice and hospitable. Vegan friendly food too! Very special to me.

I tried the meat sampler plate and oh my goodness it was so delicious! It was full of flavor. I would recommend here to anyone trying Ethiopian food for the first time. Service was great, kind waiter. I will admit there is a pretty long wait from order to food on your plate but, you at least know it’s fresh! The place is quiet, and you can have easy conversations.

formatted_address: 4548 N Magnolia Ave, Chicago, IL 60640, United States
name: Palace Gate Restaurant

reviews.text: You have to go to the laundromat next door for the toilet. Jollof rice with chicken was very good. The soup with goat and fish was spicy!

As a Nigerian, this was my first time trying Ghanaian food, and l decided to go with  Waakye because l have heard great things about it and wow it was delicious and the portion was great.......l was so full, l had to take off my pants to create space for the rest of the food !! My fellow Nigerians, and others please don't be hesitant to try Ghanaian food,  it's very delicious 😋.  Next time though l will get extra stew then also  try their fufu and light soup.
Not friendly. We were visiting from out of town and the owner stayed in the kitchen the entire time. The food wasn’t very good

This place offers you the rare opportunity to taste Ghanian food. Some dishes are very spicy so be careful. I highly recommend anything with plantains. The only reason I gave it fewer stars is that they don't have prices on the menu and I kinda suspect they just pick a number based on how you look. I had an appetizer that cost the same as an entree and was definitely overpriced. But, it was all delicious!

Overall Thoughts: This is a small, homey family restaurant serving up traditional, delicious  Ghanaian dishes. There was only one other party there when we came for dinner on a Sunday. My only suggestions are around the menu… it’s pretty hard to navigate if you have no prior knowledge of or experience trying Ghanaian cuisine, as there are no descriptions or even prices on the menu. It would’ve definitely been helpful to know the prices before ordering, but the prices seemed overall reasonable when we got the receipt at the end. The server (who seemed to be the owner’s daughter) helped answer any questions we had, and the food came out pretty quick. Otherwise, the food is wonderful and bursting with flavor— would totally recommend!

Food I tried:
- Kenkey with Fish (4.7/5): I liked this dish best out of everything we ordered. The kenkey itself had great starchy, umami flavor, and its soft, mushy texture paired perfectly with the fish which was crispy, well-fried, and flavorful. Combined the spicy shito and onions and neutral tomato, all the flavors came together perfectly.

- Beans (Red Red) with Egg and Plantains (4.5/5): There weren’t a lot of vegetarian options on the menu, but this dish was a delicious, filling option. The beans were full of flavor and the plantains were some of the best I’ve ever had— they were perfectly fried and the oil brought out their maximal sweetness and softness.

- Jollof Rice with Chicken (4.6/5): This was another favorite dish. The jollof was full of spice and flavor, and comes with plantains and your choice of protein. The chicken was super tender and fell off the bone; doused in flavorful sauce, the flavors were robust and hearty.

- Peanut Soup with Rice Ball (3.6/5): I wasn’t a huge fan of the peanut soup here… It wasn’t as peanut buttery as I would’ve hoped, but I recommend getting the rice ball with it, if you order this dish. It’s slightly sweet on its own, and really soaked up the flavor of the soup.

- Waakye with Beef (4/5): This was pretty good and flavorful. The beef was tender and the rice and beans were flavorful.
—

Price (relative to peers): 4.3/5
Food: 4.4/5
Ambience: 4.3/5
Service: 4.8/5
Overall Value: 4.5/5

formatted_address: 1914 S Wabash Ave, Chicago, IL 60616, United States
name: Nimba

reviews.text: I truly enjoyed my meal from Nimba ! I was craving jolof and stubbled upon this gem on doordash- initially the order wasn't received, but that didnt stop the business owner London from reaching out and doing everything she could to fulfill and actually deliver my order to me. Not only did i receive large portions of salmon pepper soup , jolof , and fufu , she also allowed me to try a new menu item samosa as well. Everything was so good and fulfilling ! I am so grateful for both the food preparation and the consideration that went into these meals- support this business and enjoy some great Liberian food 🤍

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Outstanding Carry-Out – Worth the Drive!
We ordered carry-out from Nimba, and it was absolutely worth the drive. The food was packed with flavor, perfectly seasoned, and still hot and fresh by the time we got home. Every dish tasted authentic and made with real care — you can tell this is food done right.
The portions were generous, the packaging was solid, and everything traveled extremely well, which is not easy to do with high-quality cuisine. If you’re looking for authentic African food in Chicago for carry-out, this is the place to go.
As someone who is opening an event venue, we were genuinely impressed and have already discussed working with Nimba for catering future events, as long as the distance works. The flavor, consistency, and professionalism would translate perfectly to private events, weddings, and corporate gatherings.
If you’re even considering trying Nimba, don’t hesitate. Excellent food, excellent quality, and 100% worth the trip. We’ll definitely be ordering again.

I lived in Minnesota for over 10 years, which basically makes me an honorary member of every African restaurant within a 50-mile radius. I’ve tried it all — if it came with spice, stew, or a side of “are you sure you can handle this?”, I was there.

This place is BY FAR the best African cuisine I’ve ever had — and trust me, I’ve eaten in a community so big it deserves its own flag. The flavors? Unmatched. The vibe? Immaculate. The cassava leaf? Listen… I don’t know what kind of ancestral magic they’re stirring back there, but that cassava leaf will change your entire life trajectory. I’m talking new goals, new purpose, possibly a new personality.

If you don’t try it, honestly, that’s between you and your taste buds — but they’re going to be mad at you.

Run, don’t walk. Your future self will thank you. 🍽️🔥

Nimba doesn’t disappoint! I had been looking for an authentic Liberian restaurant in the city for a while and stumbling across this restaurant changed my life. The food is amazing and portion sizes are just right! I’m a regular now for sure!
