And when in doubt, be sure to ask your server for suggestions.

formatted_address: 5959 Richmond Ave. #160, Houston, TX 77057, United States
name: Taste of Nigeria

reviews.text: My first visit was yesterday and it was not a good experience and needless to say I won’t be back. I ordered okra, goat, and pounded yam. The menu priced it at 24.99 + 1.75 for the swallow. When I got my bill it was $33. The manager tried to convince me that’s what I needed to pay since their prices increased as well as the goat. As a business owner, you have to ensure your menu prices match today’s price and/or ensure your servers give the disclaimer before the customer orders until your menus are reprinted. After waiting for long they still had trouble making the adjustment to give me the listed price and had the audacity to try to give me the same bill to pay as if I’m stupid and can’t calculate the cost and tax! The issue is that many people (especially Nigerians even in Nigeria don’t question or don’t know to question being overcharged. It’s a foul practice of Store owners.  In addition to that bad poor impression the quantity of food definitely did not justify the high price point. I can get much more for $2.00 in Lagos. Taste of Nigeria served a lunch size serving at a full dinner price and you really ought to do better and stop being stingy. The only good thing about my experience is the goat was tender. The okra was a bit too slimy….just like the overall experience. Look at this rubbish.

I would like to begin by saying, this restaurant should be removed immediately from all delivery services. Secondly this has to be the easiest scams. What you see in the photos below is $19 dollars + fees and tax + tip
Like I thought it was a joke. I’m seriously confused if this was a mistake or did I pay that much money for leftovers? Even the meat was like an insult.
My experience here has been very good and exciting. I really enjoyed the food and the African music. The cook in here must stay and keep dishing these lovely meals.

Worst Nigeria food experience in Houston.I ordered Amala and pounded yam, and beef pie all the food was bad, cold, slimy and all the food literally went into trash today. I will not recommend eating anything here. Waste of money, pls don’t go there if you dnt wanna waste money.

I’ve eaten here before and love it. But this time I ordered on DoorDash and it was disgusting. I took half of my food out of the container so that you can see how dry it is. My pounded yam was ice cold and that’s not how it should be served. I’m very disappointed and wasted my money. If I could rate zero stars I would

formatted_address: 401 Franklin St Suite A, Houston, TX 77201, United States
name: ChòpnBlọk

reviews.text: A great place to experience West African cuisine. I love the Suya, coconut bites (chicken) and the Cameroonian shrimp are all good. The drinks are great also. The Golden bowl is a favorite as well as the Buka bowl. The warm banana bread with fresh strawberries is a great way to finish. I have been here several times and will definitely be back.

Good flavor, small portion, bad service.
We arrived without reservation, was told a wait time of 45 minutes. Totally fair. However, we were asked to wait at the entrance to the restroom. Do you want to write down my name? No. Can you text us when the table is ready? No. Can we wait outside? No. It's kind of awkward to stand in front of the restroom for 45 minutes. So we decide to try another location at Post. No line, yeah. The cashier was in bad mood. (Sorry for her. ) No greeting, no smile, not a word but just stared at us. Fine, we are here for food not your smile. Ordered Motherland vegetarian version and Trad chicken version. The bill was $45 (not including tax and tip yet) and we got side order size of 2 bowels of curry over rice ( yeah, there are vegetables and 5 slices of chicken breast).
The flavor was soooo good. Smoky hint in the rice, tender distinguish African curry sauce that awake our taste palettes.
Was the food good, yes. Was it a good experience, no. Will we go back, no.

Service was quick at Chopnblok! Food came out fast.

Ordered the Trad and it was delicious! Includes jollof jambalaya, chicken, stewed plantains, & yaji veggies. The meat pie minnies were also tasty!

Motherland is a vegetarian option. Curry flavor was ok.

Overall a nice place in the POST to grab a quick meal.

Went on a Monday night. Dj was creating a relaxing mood . West African,  Carrie bean mix. Yes yes and yes. Be sure to get reservations. Service once again Houston you leave me highly impressed.  Put this on your list if your visiting.

Food is a certified crowd pleaser! The textures, flavors, and colors are so beautiful and well integrated into the “Golden bowl” my go to meal. The coconut curry is perfection, I always get an extra side of plantains always tender & sweet never green. The chicken is juicy and well seasoned the rice is delicious and well portioned. This plate never misses & I always have a little extra which tastes great even when reheated hours later. Needless to say the service here is always top notch ! Friendly and knowledgeable of the menu:) Much love

formatted_address: 6357 Westheimer Rd, Houston, TX 77057, United States
name: Aria Suya Kitchen

reviews.text:
Ariya Suya is a truly a hidden gem lost in the mix of the Houston area. The restaurant possesses an unbelievable taste and excellent services. I was there on a Saturday in the afternoon , with a constant flux of people entering and leaving. It's pretty small with less than ten tables making it very intimate.

To start i had one of their meat pies, which were flaky and golden on the outside, which reminded me of comfort food. It was a great snack to have before the main. For my entree i had the goat suya with sweet plantains as well as fufu and it was wonderful. It was a firm yet soft juicy meat with just the right amount of kick in it. It was the right amount of the heat accompanied by the sweetness of the plantains that rendered the dish sweet and savory and made me crave every single bite.

The waiters were incredibly friendly and helpful, they responded to the questions in regards of the menu, and came up with suggestions to match. The fufu was also suggested to be accompanied by the egusi soup and hobo drink that would've blended perfectly with the flavor of meat. The prices were very affordable especially in terms of the quality and portions.

In all, my visit to Ariya Suya was excellent. I highly recommend it to all people who desire something that is not merely delicious but also unique and contains an original African flavor. Ariya Suya is a restaurant to visit regardless of culture.

I had an outstanding experience at Aria, largely thanks to our amazing waiter, Abiola. From the moment we sat down, she provided attentive and friendly service, making us feel welcomed and valued. She was knowledgeable about the menu and offered great recommendations that truly enhanced our meal. His genuine enthusiasm for Nigerian cuisine made the experience even more enjoyable. Thank you, Abiola, for your exceptional service! I can’t wait to return.

I ordered to go recently before the restaurant closed for the night. At first glance I was surprised to see how big the asun was cut. After tasting, the asun wasn’t spicy at all with many fatty meat pieces. The jollof rice had little to no spice. Ultimately, the food was not up to par especially after paying almost $30. Brought this to management’s attention the next day. No one cared to remedy the situation. “I’m going to lose money” was the response. 0/10 recommend 👎

I had such a great time at Aria! The food was amazing — I especially loved the jollof rice and grilled plantains. Gina, our waitress, was super friendly and made our visit even better. The atmosphere is lively and welcoming. Highly recommend for anyone wanting authentic African cuisine.

Went here on a Friday night and didn’t need to make a reservation which was nice. The atmosphere is cool and the music is nice though just a touch loud to comfortably have a conversation. The serving was okay, not bad not good.

formatted_address: 14524 Piping Rock Ln, Houston, TX 77077, United States
name: Delight's Ghanaian Cuisine

reviews.text: My first time trying this particular restaurant. I have had African food at a couple of other places in other cities but wanted to try Fufu bread. So I ordered a side of that with the chicken and veggie stew and the pineapple beetroot ginger juice drink. The drink was absolutely fabulous! The stew was good, and very spicy. I was not aware it would be so spicy hot but that's okay I like spicy so that was all good. It was just a little greasy for my taste. Foo foo bread is an experience in and of itself is all I can say LOL you're supposed to eat it with your hands and use it to make little Scoops to eat the stew call my however the texture was too sticky for me to feel comfortable handling it with my hands so I asked for a spoon and used that instead to scoop off little bits of the bread and eat it with the stew. As I live clear on the other side of town this is not close to me, but I made it on my way home from a recent trip and took the Sidetrack off of I-10 to stop here for lunch. Will be bringing my sister back next time she's in town. Be aware you need to look online before you get here as they do not offer paper menus instead they have chosen to utilize a high-tech QR code order and pay at your table system. This is a disadvantage for senior citizens who don't utilize those kind of Technologies and many of whom don't carry a smartphone Thomas a word of warning if you're thinking about going here and don't have one as it does make things more difficult

OMG, let me just say this first….. I am a food critique, and it is hard to impress me. But DELIGHT….SHESSSH!

From the moment we walked in, the ambiance wrapped us up, the warm greeting,
complete with the biggest, most genuine smile, set the tone immediately. This was my first-ever experience with Ghanaian food, and whew it surpassed any expectation!

Every bite was a celebration. The flavors literally danced on my tongue. I ordered the egusi with fufu, turkey (since I do not eat beef), and plantain, and baby, perfection. My aunt went with the jollof rice and chicken, and let me tell you, there was not a single crumb left behind.

This was not just dinner…… it was an EXPERIENCE, the kind you keep thinking about long after you leave.

Do yourself a favor and stop by, and when you do, tell my friend Rhoda that KC the NP sent you. Trust me, you will thank me later.

I order from this restaurant through DoorDash and this will be my last time. Today a lady called me from the restaurant saying that they didn’t have the $20 size small tilapia fish which is on their menu but they have a $25 fish. They said to pay the $5 through Zelle or cash app, so I proceeded to do that thinking the size of the fish would be bigger. Once the food was delivered to me the fish was the same size as previous orders and to make matters worse the fufu had a smashed up dead bug inside of it. This order just left a bad taste in my mouth and I won’t be ordering from this restaurant again.

Response - There is no reason for me to lie since I’ve been ordering from you since 2024 and never had a problem before until this last order. The fufu already had black stuff on it before I even touched the fish! So I decided to further inspect the fufu by opening it up, which showed there was more bits and pieces of what looked like broken up bug parts in the middle of the fufu.Take a closer look at the fufu picture, the dark pieces of whatever it is, is rolled into the fufu and not from me touching the fish then touching the fufu( I also uploaded the picture again and circled the spots where you can clearly see it was deep inside the fufu and not from me touching it ). You can also see my finger and hands are clean and the fish was not even touched yet, I also use utensils to eat fish so it wouldn’t even be from me touching the fish and touching the fufu. It definitely looks like broken up bug parts, If it’s not a bug then there was something or fish debris on the person’s hand that rolled the fufu up into a ball, so maybe wash your hands first? I also read another reviewer stating there was eggshells in their banku and by your response to that person, you clearly didn’t admit to that mistake either. It’s disgusting how you would blame me for touching the fish and touching the the fufu instead of just owning up to the mistake. Secondly, you never called me to upgrade to a large fish at no cost a couple of weeks ago, you definitely have the wrong customer, because the last time I ordered from you was in June ( I uploaded receipts of all my previous orders).I have been ordering from you since 2024, so it was not my first order a few weeks ago, so that is another lie you have stated. I’m glad this whole situation happened cause you guys seem like you can’t take accountability and instead you make excuses and lie. So what was your reasoning for having me Zelle you an extra $5 outside of DoorDash? I thought the reasoning was you guys didn’t have the $20 fish at the moment so I assumed I had to pay the difference for another size fish. I don’t mind paying extra if the small fish wasn’t available , but the fish was the same size as all of my other previous orders for a small $20 fish! So what was the difference with the fish that cost $5 extra? Change the price on your menu if you guys have raised the price on your fish instead of calling customers to zelle or cash app you outside of the DoorDash platform. Also check your hands before you roll fufu up into a ball or check your batch cause it’s very unprofessional how you guys are blaming a customer for something you guys clearly did.

Oh my God!!!! This place is wonderful the owner is so sweet and she can cook!!! I only had the egusi stew but I will be back for more! I mad I can’t finish the rest of my food, but I’m glad I have some for later❤️

I am not sure why this place isn't packed. My server was super attentive and patient.  I have never eaten South African food.  She answered all my questions.  I even looked up the recipe for the Sobolo drink and plan on making it when I get home. The food was delicious.  I can't wait to come back and try more of this unique exquisite food.

formatted_address: 2616 Blodgett St, Houston, TX 77004, United States
name: OLATEE AFRICAN CAFE

reviews.text: This restaurant absolutely exceeded my expectations. My first order from them was for the leave moi moi and being Nigerian, I expected a lot. They did not disappoint at all,  the order was prepared on time, the staff were very helpful and polite and to sum it up, the food was delicious. My family and I practically order most Nigerian foods from them now and the overall experience has been great. I will definitely recommend as you would not be disappointed.

Absolutely incredible food! The flavors were rich, authentic, and unforgettable. The service was fast, the staff friendly, and the atmosphere cozy. Highly recommend the egusi soup and plantains—top-tier!
Always neat, clean, and food is definitely very tasty. Staff are also always prompt and very nice to customers. My number 1 place to eat african food in the houston area. I recommend 200%
Excellent customer service. Their delivery service is always quick and food arrives fresh, and well packed.
One restaurant I so much enjoy their meal…. Thanks OlaTee! Fully recommended !!!

formatted_address: 10014 Bissonnet St, Houston, TX 77036, United States
name: Safari

reviews.text:
First time at Safari and ordered fisherman’s soup (first time ever trying it) take out. The food was definitely a 10/10 and the server was really polite.
I do not normally give google reviews but this place definitely has great food 💯

Delicious Nigerian food. Not a big variety but each dish is tasty. Service is not always the best and don't like that menu prices aren't fixed and keep changing. Still, I always go back for the tasty meals.

The food is ok but the daughter is so RUDE that u wouldn't want to eat their , her attitude is off the hook. To the point I lost appetite  just getting their and seeing her unwelcoming and Rude attitude damnnn
I’m really happy I found this place. First time here and I got vegetable soup. 10/10 & tastes very authentic
This was my very first time experiencing authentic Nigerian food. A little too spicy for me but it was good.  I just kept eating 🤭

formatted_address: Main Medical Plaza, 10021 S Main St Bldg 7, Houston, TX 77025, United States
name: Fabaceae African Cuisine Inc.

reviews.text: I love this place so much. It is amazing that they have vegan options. This finally allowed me to try Nigerian food for the first time as I transitioned after I discovered it the quality is 10 out of 10 and so is the customer service. I have never not been greeted with a great big smile. They are the best.
First time trying African food & omg i can’t believe i waited so long to try it.. Her food is really amazing I’ll be back for some more :)

I want to applaud this restaurant for their inclusive menu.  By offering vegan and non vegan options patrons don’t have to take turns over health and togetherness.  We all dined together vegans and non vegans. There are a plethora of choices and each was better than the other, making choosing a chore. The meals were seasoned to perfection.  We dey chop ooo. The service was great, the owners were friendly, and professional.  Talk about patient, they made us feel at home.  Our food was made fresh and in a timely manner.  Yes!!! I highly recommend this hidden gem,

Just made #1 on my list for African cuisine. Spicy and good! 😋…. Okra, goat, ponded yam with passion lemonade!

I’m here at the new location! I had to update my review. Come and support the new location! Still GREAT food! And you can dine in, now!

Great customer service, super nice. Very clean if you want to eat inside. I LOVE that you can buy a la carte. I got jollof rice, plaintains and a side of stew. No meat. Everything was fresh and delicious. Cant wait to try more

formatted_address: 1701 Cypress Creek Pkwy Suite D, Houston, TX 77090, United States
name: Omalicha Kitchen

reviews.text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
This was my first time trying the food, and let me just say — I was blown away! I read the reviews and decided to give it a shot. Now, I’ve had this dish before in Dallas from a family member, but this right here put her food to shame! I ordered the seafood okra stew with pounded yam, and it was absolutely scrumptious. The flavors were rich, authentic, and perfectly seasoned. I’ll definitely be coming back for more!
I love spicy and it was hot spicy .. just the way I like …
10 out of 20 I recommend

I was really excited to try the abacha but I was so disappointed it had no taste and a strong fermentation that made the food inedible. I haven’t tried anything else from the menu and it was my first time ordering from them

We had never tried African cuisine before, but after seeing the great reviews for Omalicha, we knew we had to check it out. Like many, we’ve been curious about fufu and wanted to experience it for ourselves. Since there’s nothing like this in our area, we made it a point to stop in for lunch the next time we were in Houston — and we’re so glad we did!

The food was incredible, with flavors and textures unlike anything we’ve ever had before. Every bite was a new and exciting experience. Mike went out of his way to teach us about the dishes and how to eat them properly, which made the meal even more enjoyable. The combination of amazing food and warm hospitality made this an unforgettable dining experience.

If you’re looking to try something new and delicious, Omalicha is the place to go. Highly recommend!

I purchased the Seafood Okra Soup with OMG🤯 Perfection very flavorful I didn’t have to hunt for the seafood and the portion is perfect. The restaurant is very neat, clean and inviting. Employees are friendly also 1 trillion stars from me
Flavors are magnificent. I had catfish pepper soup Jollof Rice and peppered goat meat. 9/10. Make sure to call ahead if you are in a rush because they cook and make it to order.

formatted_address: 3645 Cypress Creek Pkwy #368, Houston, TX 77068, United States
name: Hunan Cafe

reviews.text:
Drove from out of town just to try: The Egusi Soup with Fish and Pounded Yam was a chefs kiss combination! I also ordered The Chicken with Jollof rice and Plantain and it was an absolute mouth watering. The prices were very reasonable considering the amount of food given. The ambience was very welcoming and relaxing. If you live nearby you must try this place. If you don’t live nearby it is worth the drive. Bought extra food To-Go as well.
* Sarah and the rest of the staff were nice!
Thank you 😃!

Had the best mommy–son day at Hunan Café. First time trying egusi soup and baby… it was so good I had to wear a napkin bib 😂
The vibes, the décor, the hospitality — all from a momma-owned spot with her boys holding it down.
Thank you, Hunan. We’ll be back soon! 🇳🇬✨

I got the egusi with beef and fufu and it's delicious! Great service, and they were so helpful in helping me know what to order and how to eat it! My table also ordered the jollof rice with beef and the curry fried with goat. Everything is so delicious!

The food here will leave you breathless, I am not saying that lightly. If you eat enough, a food coma is imminent.
The Asun is tender and perfectly flavored. I tried the tilapia meal also, splendid. The Isi Ewu (goat head) was fantastic. The prices are the most affordable for value I have ever seen and I eat at West African restaurants often.
Everyone in my party took home the things we couldn't finish. 100/100.

Absolutely loved this place! The food was flavorful, fresh, and clearly made with care. I tried a few traditional dishes and everything was well-seasoned and delicious. The staff were friendly and welcoming, and the atmosphere felt warm and authentic. You can really tell this restaurant takes pride in sharing African culture through food. I’ll definitely be coming back and recommending it to others!

formatted_address: 6101 Wilcrest Dr, Houston, TX 77072, United States
name: Unique African Cuisine

reviews.text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Absolutely Incredible Dining Experience!
From the moment we walked in, we were welcomed with warm hospitality and an inviting atmosphere. The ambiance was the perfect blend of cozy and upscale, making it ideal for both a special night out or a casual dinner.
The food was exceptional. Every dish we ordered was bursting with flavor and beautifully presented. The vegetable was cooked with goat meat 🐐 soup with Pando yam,  which was highlight—perfectly cooked and seasoned to perfection. The ingredients tasted incredibly fresh, and the portion sizes were just right.
Service was top-notch. Our server was attentive without being overbearing, knowledgeable about the menu, and genuinely passionate about making our evening enjoyable.
Prices were reasonable for the quality, and we felt like we truly got great value for our money. Whether you're a foodie or just someone who appreciates a good meal, this place is a must-visit.
Highly recommend i
t—you won’t be disappointed!, kudos 👏🏿 💐 🥳 🎊 👏🏿
Eugene was the best! Our meals were delicious, and the Bissap Hibiscus juice was amazing!
The fish and lamb pepper soup is the best. The chicken suya is so delicious. The customer service and attentiveness was top tier and the best!!! The hibiscus drink is sooo good!!!!!

The food here is hit or miss. There doesn't seem to be a recipe for the items as the same item may tastes different each time. I always ask for my food spicy but it's never spicy. The service is friendly though. The employees so seem to genuinely want you to have a nice experience. The atmosphere is where things fall apart. There is no AC, just fans blowing the hot air around and this place doesn't always smell the best. I wish this last part didn't have to be said (typed) but if you consider using the restroom here, take your own tp.

They’ve definitely changed the cook and management. I don’t think the person who is now cooking is Ivorian. I ordered a kedjenou and what they gave me was a spicy tomato stew with green bell peppers I was like umm yea no. Then only had 3 pieces of chicken. Same for the plate of grilled chicken with plantain. Only 3 pieces of chicken. For the price the portion are ridiculously small and the taste is no longer there anymore. It’s unfortunate because that used to be the place I would go to every time I’m in town. If you’re going to serve mainly Ivorian food make sure it’s cooked by an Ivorian!

formatted_address: 11965 Bissonnet St STE 110, Houston, TX 77099, United States
name: Dee Titolat African Restaurant

reviews.text: We found this place on Google while on vacation in Houston.  It's a  decent place with the atmosphere of an african restaurant. The food was the best part.   We ordered fufu and vegetables stew and Amala and Gbegiri.  Oh my goodness!  It was the best.  For a total of $47, the taste, quality and quantity exceeded our expectations.   We will come again if we are around this area.  Thank you for wonderful service and great food!

I went in there with a walker. I wasn’t attended to by the new middle aged Igbo lady who welcomed me. A Pastor’s wife came in after me, ran straight to the fried yam and dodo I was waiting for and took every yam and dodo by herself and the man who came to ring her out was yelling that the yam is too big. I spent 1 hour in the store without being waited on. The man had no apology but asked if I could come for him to ring me up before he starts having more customers. I was just looking at him. He still rung me up without itemizing what I purchased. The bitter leaf I asked to be warmed but it was served cold though I waited for it. This was my first and last time there. Horrible service.
amazing quality of traditional african dishes! the jollof rice and pounded yam were incredibly delicious and authentic.

Good customer service and experienced staffs and services.

I love the food also.
The food was excellent! I’m American and I prefer to have less spicy so my husband asked them not make it spicy…they didn’t. The food was fresh and delicious.

formatted_address: 14144 Westheimer Rd #120, Houston, TX 77077, United States
name: Komchop

reviews.text:
We were at Kom Chop on Sunday for our indigenous dining experience. From the moment we arrived, the atmosphere looked neat.

We ordered a plate poundo yam and banga soup, another plate of banga soup with oatmeal, and Nigerian Jollof, Dodo and chicken. For the drinks we ordered hibiscus drink. The food was beautifully presented. Ingredients tasted fresh, portions were okay, and flavors were balanced.

Okay, I won't be so extra with hyping up Naija Independence Day 10/01/25 too much however in Honor of the celebration we chose KomChop to finish the day well. Uzo, our sweet cashier greeted us upon arrival, answered every dish question, helped with selection that supports food allergies restrictions. Our order: White Rice & Stew (Beef) with the side of Spinach. If you haven't had African Spinach, my gosh your missing out on wonderful flavors. Fried Rice (Chicken) with the side of Dodo (Sweet Plaintains). Egusi Soup (Goat meat) with Oat meal (they beige ball/dough item). With tip our delicious cooked art ran us about $75; worth the entire first experience. If you haven't taken a trip to the land of flavor; West African Resturant, do yourself a favor and stop on by. We'll definitely be back!

⚠️ Extremely disappointing experience. My boyfriend and I ordered food from this restaurant yesterday, and thank God we checked before eating. When we opened the meal, there was a big bug inside the pounded yam. This is absolutely unacceptable.

What makes it worse is that this isn’t the first time! We previously received spoiled, slimy coconut fried rice that seemed frozen and just reheated. To have this happen again shows a serious lack of hygiene and quality control. We will not be ordering from here ever again, and I strongly urge others to think twice before spending their money at this place & check your meal before consuming it too!

First off I live almost 2 hours away. I use to come often few years ago. Im currently working 15 minutes away from Komchop so I was excited to get here for lunch! I asked the young lady who was very nice to give me a nice size fish and Jollof rice. And she did. Rice was fresh and light good. The fish i was slightly disappointed 😞 it wasn't seasoned to good. Chez Michelle's is top tier as far as flavor for fish .

Food arrived cold after a long wait. We weren’t greeted properly—just a quick “hello” before being asked what we wanted. Drinks didn’t arrive until after the food, and we had no silverware for about 10 minutes, by which time the food was already cold. No one checked on us at any point. We shared our feedback with the staff, but they showed a clear lack of concern and a “did not care” attitude. Overall, a big disappointment, especially considering all the hype.

formatted_address: 9705 Synott Rd suite 107, Houston, TX 77083, United States
name: Authentic African Restaurant & Bar

reviews.text: New, they have a great selection of food. Portion sizes for takeout could be improved, but the taste was good. Overall, it’s a nice and clean establishment with dining areas and a beer section. Menu prices are not all current, but the owner stated they were updating the menu but will honor list prices.

The food is delicious this is me and my girlfriend second time coming within the last two days. The food is really good really delicious and the service is impeccable thank you so much. We can’t wait to come back again. Order: Stewed Beef,jollof,puff puff,egg roll, and meat patty.

Authentic Africa Restaurant truly lives up to its name. From the moment you walk in, you’re welcomed with a warm atmosphere and excellent customer service that makes you feel right at home. The food is absolutely amazing—rich, flavorful, and prepared with genuine African authenticity.
Very friendly  and informative  about african food. It was my first time having it and I liked it! Harriet was amazing! I'll be back
Some of the best authentic African food I’ve ever tasted!!!! The service was incredible and the staff really went above and beyond!!! Definitely one of the hidden gems of Houston’s food scene!!

formatted_address: 17036 W Little York Rd, Houston, TX 77084, United States
name: Famous Princess African Kitchen

reviews.text: This was an otherly world atmosphere, in a good way! The parking lot was full, the line was out the door, and for a great reason! I tried the meat pies,  Jollof Rice, Ayamashe, and Egusi soup. I had to wait due to the highly sought after food during dinner time on the weekend, but the service was incredible. The man working the front seemed like a one-man machine, taking orders, payments, touching the tables, getting door dash meals, despite all of this on his plate he still found the time to give me a coke and puff puff roll (which were delicious) as I waited. When I finally made it home with my meals, you could tell this was an authentic cuisine. This momma threw down in the kitchen! I believe it was the Ayamashe and Egusi soup that had a different type of spice than I am accustomed to but the flavor was amazing! The meat pies and the rice were also extra good! I would definitely go back!

The wait here is very long if you go on the weekends but the food is soo delicious. It's my favorite go to for fresh, good tasty Nigerian food. The fufu and egusi soup is soo delicious. If you ever want to try Nigerian food, please stop by here.

The quality of Nigerian dishes here is outstanding. If you haven’t tried this spot yet, you're definitely missing out on that authentic Southwestern Nigerian flavor. It’s a bit more expensive than other places we've been, but for truly authentic pounded yam (the real deal, not the instant kind), it’s totally worth every penny. We now regularly grab a tray of efo riro and egusi soup—always a great choice!

I’ve been to atleast more than 15 Nigerian food restaurants in the United States across the east, South, Midwest etc but this place tops it all no cap. Amala, Gbegiri and Ewedu we all agreed is the GOAT of all food ofcourse ofcourse I’m a Yoruba man. This restaurant makes you feel at home, the food quality is top notch, the portion is way above the industry standard oh no the meat is unbeatable none of the restaurants I’ve been to (NY, NJ, MI, GA, IL etc) comes close to this particular spot. I had to take off my clothes 😂 just to enjoy this delicious meal cooked with love.

When it comes to Abula, I don't think anywhere in Houston can beat Famous Princess. It is literally 10/10 no notes! I've also orderd Efo Riro, Egusi, and Jollof rice. These are all good but I didn't love the Egusi or Jollof, to be clear - they were very delicious but just some minor nuances that are more my personal preference but the food is undoubtebly good! I would recommend this place to anyone in Houston looking to eat authentic Nigerian food.

The only thing that keeps this place from getting 5 stars is the service. I typically order for delivery and sometimes the communication isn't ideal. For example, I placed an order and an item was missing and they read my message and never responded or refunded the missing item.

formatted_address: 14815 Westheimer Rd, Houston, TX 77082, United States
name: Amala Zone

reviews.text: I just left a 4-star review a couple of days ago on doordash praising their consistency, but this order completely changed my mind. I ordered okra again, and as you can see in the photo, it’s literally just stew—no okra at all. What’s the point of that? We pay delivery fees and tip on top of it, and I personally always tip well. Charging nearly $30 just to send stew is ridiculous

I’m really disappointed with this place. The food is not authentic at all. I’ve been to a lot of Nigerian restaurants in Houston, and honestly places like Chef Benny’s, Didi’s BBQ, Titola, and even Taste of Nigeria are all way better for the price.

I ordered one small portion and one amala with three meats, and the meat was hard and tough. The beef was almost impossible to chew. The egusi had no real flavor — it just tasted like nonsense. And for $28, the portion was tiny.

Me and my friend spent $58 total, and the food was small, not fresh, and definitely not worth the money. We could have gone to any of the other spots I mentioned and spent maybe $40 for better, hotter, fresher food.

It’s been two years since I last came here, and now I see why my dad stopped bringing me. Never coming back. Unacceptable.

We ordered our food online and it was delivered promptly. The portions were a good size. The Egusi soup was not tasty. It lacked an authentic flavor and I've had better. I was disappointed. I should've adhered to the reviews before ordering.

I see why I stopped coming here. Came here yesterday after months because I was craving amala. $90 for two Amala and ofada that tastes like nonsense. The food quality has gone down! The restaurant SMELLS like sewage! Omg! Like why does my Ofada rice have the same smell has your shop?  The way she hypes her restaurant online is not the same experience you get in person.  At some point we have hold our people accountable. How can you open at 12pm but not service people until 45mins later. There were so many people outside waiting while the owner strolled in with a wig in her hand a makeup box! The employees behave as if they are being forced to work, zero customer service. Seriously do better. Never again

I paid Amalazone through Zelle for an order, but it was never delivered. When I asked for a refund, the seller promised to send it but it’s been hours and I’m still waiting and haven’t received anything.
It’s really disappointing and unprofessional to promise a refund and not follow through. I wouldn’t recommend ordering from Amalazone until they learn to handle their customers’ money responsibly.

I’m sharing this so others can avoid the same situation.

formatted_address: 3418 S Texas 6 Suite C, Houston, TX 77082, United States
name: Suya on the spot

reviews.text: The food is excellent and very flavorful. The scotch eggs are only on weekends but they were worth it. The place can get busy but it's because a lot of people know where to get good Nigerian food at. I recommend their samosas, there's a pop of sweetness in the meat when you bite into it because there's corn in it. The zubo slushy is the best drink.

Customer Service:

Nobody greeted me when I came in, and it took a while for the cashier to acknowledge me and take my order.

I came in around 6:30 pm and wanted to order suya drumsticks, but they had only two left. When I requested to buy them, I was told they weren’t for sale. This place closes at 9 pm, so I was curious why they couldn’t make more chicken and why I couldn’t purchase the last two drumsticks.

Food:

My dad usually buys us beef suya and drumsticks from this place, and I’ve liked the food when I’ve tried it, so I wanted to get more for myself.

I ordered beef suya on this visit—it was alright. I’ve always thought the meat was a lil tough and chewy, but it was more noticeable this time but still tolerable.

Online Presence:

This brand needs to work on their website as it’s not completely built despite being live. It’s not a good look—it appears unprofessional and makes it seem like the business is a scam.

Closing Remarks:

Despite the poor customer service and unimpressive food, I do see myself stopping by again, but mainly to use my $5 off coupon—I don’t think I’ll be coming back after that.

This used to be my favorite place to get Suya but the quality and service has severely declined even though the prices have increased. Today we placed an order for 2 beef Suya and asked to see the food before purchasing to ensure freshness. They refused. We paid for the order and sure enough the Suya was not hot or fresh. We will not be returning.

From what the other patrons told me the value is the quality of the food. Seems like a lot of prep work so that off sets the cost. Lots of take out orders. Be prepared to wait a little. Pretty decent experience.

Food was great however ima get chicken next time I’m not gonna lie the beef was not the most tender choice for me but still very tasty with the raw veggies I never ate raw cabbage before and the onions was fresh as well as the cucumber and cherry tomatoes.Tip please request veggies when you come. They fixed the food in front of you which is a plus they wear gloves and seem supper clean. They actually provided booths it was supper nice with African music videos.

formatted_address: 12703 Alief Clodine Rd, Houston, TX 77082, United States
name: Abula HotPot

reviews.text: Awesome atmosphere here at Abula HotPot. The Amala was awesome with some lovely assorted meat. Spacious and clean. Also found out they have a space to host party.
The Abula was absolutely delicious! The customer service was amazing. The owners and staff were so friendly and accommodating. Highly recommend! We’ll definitely be back!
The food is spectacular. It drives my blood pressure through the roof but I guess I will stroke out happy. It's a great value and the flavor always hits.

Very nice place...Family owned I believe and the Owner kinda checked on everyone to make sure we were enjoying the meal. One thing I found interesting was the speed of getting our orders out. Usually African restaurants have long wait time after taking orders. The food tastes great too... that's definitely a plus.
I ordered the poundo with ogbono soup with beef and it was delicious. It’s a very friendly environment which made the experience even better! Will definitely be visiting again!

formatted_address: 9405 Country Creek St, Houston, TX 77036, United States
name: Sabo Suya

reviews.text: The beef suya hits differently… you must visit this place and come back and give me a feedback…. I will be waiting

I moved to Houston about 3weeks ago and I was told I HAD to try Sabo Suya....I have been to the resturant twice in 3weeks...

The Ram suya is AMAZING! I recommend it over the regular beef suya...

Customers service is Great. The folks there were  polite both times I visited and the space is really clean....I don't walk out of the restaurant smelling like I made the suya myself.

The food is BEYOND amazing!!!!! The taste is something I never tasted in any other food. I’ve been eating here for about 9 years & I never get tired of it!! This food will have you addicted!!! & Adam & Ricky are so nice 🙂
Haven't been in a while been dying to go back super good RAM fresh onion and sweet tomatoes love love love
Amazing service at sabo suya! The staff was so welcoming and attentive, making our dining experience truly top-notch.

formatted_address: 12600 Bissonnet St, Houston, TX 77099, United States
name: Marie African Flavors

reviews.text: Went as soon as they opened and the food came out fast and it was delicious! The owner gives the best service and explains everything very clearly. My favorite place!

Used to be good the quality however is terrible I paid $23 for eru and this is what I got??? Spinach and oil barely any eru meat was boiled days ago and just added you can tell and they didn’t even fill this dollar tree bowl to the top… got so nauseous eating I had to spit it out…very disappointing I will not be returning
Stop doing business in United states like you are in Cameroon🥲🥲🥲🥲. The way she talk to you when you complain is unacceptable 🥲🥲🥲🥲. This was my last time here. 70 dollars and you serves burn fish🥲

I rarely leave reviews, but this experience was so unacceptable that I feel people should know before dining here.

First, the service was terrible from the very beginning. The main waitress came straight out of the bathroom and proceeded to handle menus and serve without washing her hands. That alone was enough to raise serious concerns about hygiene.

Things only went downhill from there. Service was painfully slow, with long waits even though the restaurant wasn’t particularly busy. When the food finally arrived, it was obvious that it wasn’t freshly prepared—it tasted like old, reheated leftovers. For the price they charge, I expected authentic, quality African cuisine. Instead, I got overpriced, subpar food that I wouldn’t even consider acceptable at a fast-food chain.

To make matters worse, when I pointed out the issues with the bill (being overcharged), I was told the manager refused to come and address the situation. That lack of accountability and complete disregard for customers was the final straw.

Between the unsanitary practices, poor service, reheated food, inflated prices, and unprofessional management, this place is a complete disappointment. I will never return, and I would strongly advise others to save their money and go elsewhere. There are plenty of restaurants that actually value their customers and serve food with integrity—this is not one of them.
Placed my order to be picked up and they gave me a fish that someone ordered more than 2 hrs ago.  It doesn't look fresh at all.

formatted_address: 6271 S Texas 6, Houston, TX 77083, United States
name: Amala Joint

reviews.text: The owner she was very nice. I got the ogusi soup, I could not really enjoy it because it was too hot and spicy. My wait time was about 15 minutes. If I'm back in the area I would go back and try a different dish.
First time eating African food, could not of have chosen a better spot!! This spot is amazing, great food amazing server and amazing music taste!!

I go here all the time for Abula and have never been disappointed. I’ve never had a bad meal here, the owner is also super sweet. I’ve had Abula, pounded yam, and Jollof rice and they are all so yummy.

To top it all, I’m under the weather and just ordered pepper soup for the 1st time through DoorDash and it is so yummy. It was so good, I called the store to compliment the chef. I will say that if you can’t handle spice to ask for less spice, but the spice really helps. Love this place and I’m loyal  forever.
The best African meal I’ve had in the United States. Friendly staff too - the lady from Haiti was very friendly. Had abula! Good service and food overall. Definitely coming back!!

Amala Joint – A True Taste of Naija 🇳🇬

If you’ve been craving authentic Nigerian flavors that hit your soul, Amala Joint is the spot. From the moment I walked in, the aroma of rich spices and slow-cooked stews told me I was in for something special.

I ordered the amala with gbegiri, ewedu, and assorted meat, and let me just say: PERFECTION. The amala was soft, warm, and just the right amount of stretchy. The gbegiri was silky, the ewedu had that traditional slippery texture that hugged the amala beautifully, and the stew? Whew deep, peppery, and packed with flavor. Each bite was a throwback to home-cooked meals in Nigeria.

The assorted meat was generous and well-seasoned tender cow foot, spicy tripe, juicy beef everything cooked to perfection and soaked in rich, red stew. They don’t skimp on flavor or portion size.

Customer service was friendly, and the atmosphere felt like a neighborhood kitchen with Naija pride. Whether you’re Nigerian or just love African cuisine, Amala Joint will transport your taste buds straight to Lagos.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Highly recommend for lovers of bold, traditional West African flavors. Don’t walk RUN for that amala!

formatted_address: 3030 Audley St, Houston, TX 77098, United States
name: Blue Nile

reviews.text:
Pros: interesting menu, delicious food, great ambiance, great service
Cons: not much parking, a tad bit pricy (but worth it)

If you want good Ethiopian food in Houston, this is the place! It's a hidden gem, but worth checking out! It's a little on the expensive side, but totally worth it. I would recommend this place for special events, such as a really special date or wedding anniversary. And you don't need reservations. I recommend any of their savory food (trust me--it's all great!), and any of the desserts that are freshly made the day you're visiting; if you ask for any of the other desserts, they'll have to pull them out of the freezer and the flavor will be... passible, but not as good. I'll have to come back for their coffee ceremony at some point!

Very nice ambience and a great experience. The food was so delicious. Mekdes was super professional and very attentive. As it was our first time in blue nile, she helped lot with her awesome suggestions from the menu. Pistachio cake and Ethiopian honey wine are must-tries. Definitely will come back.

We have been visiting Blue Nile since 2017, we loved the food here and the atmosphere which is usually quiet and elegant. Today, however, will be our last time visiting - we simply can't justify the amount of money being charged for the food/drinks.

They charged us 5 dollars for 1 CAN of coke (and no refills). I understand restaurants are already operating on a small margin, and smaller mom and pop restaurants have even a smaller margin at times. I understand that price in food may go up, especially year over year, and we don't mind paying for good food.

And pay we did, because when looked at our bill for lunch we had sticker shock, it was over 68+ dollars for lunch. We got the veggie combo and the meat combo, the same combo we've ordered for years. Plus tax and tip and it was well over 80 dollars for lunch. The last time we went earlier this year I could have sworn it was closer to 50 dollars total. Also, they didn't serve us the cabbage that's in the picture from earlier this year - so we got one less item.

The restaurant didn't have their AC on today and the ceiling fans were broken according to our waitress. So it was warmer than normal inside and she wasn't allowed to turn on the AC. The service was nice enough, but nothing stood out.

They're getting 2 stars for the memories and the food which was still very good, but we won't be back.

Good place entree portions are generous, too big to finish you'll need a to go plate.  Healthy food.

When talking to the waitress about other Ethiopian restaurants in Houston she was very gracious and had a positive attitude about other locations and didn't have anything ugly to say and that was very professional of her and she really gave a great service and had a nice vibe.  I liked very much how she didn't have a negative attitude about other places and was very complimentary of them.  It shows a good example of how businesses in the same industry should treat each other because there is an interest for businesses to promote excellence amongst each other and this place handles that very well.  Ethiopian food in Houston is represented great by this place and their people.
The food is very good, albeit a little pricey. If you stick to the sampler plates, you'll get better value. The lentils are delicious. Highly recommend the vegetarian platter.

formatted_address: 8731 W Bellfort Ave, Houston, TX 77071, United States
name: United Sisters

reviews.text: The food here is excellent. It tastes like authentic Nigerian cuisine . It’s sooo good. I’ve been coming here so long. Their oha, egusi, and vegetable soup, moi moi, coconut rice, jollof rice, plantain and vegetables are so delicious. The owner is also very pleasant. If you want some of the best Nigerian food in Houston then come here.

Worst African food I ever had! i ordered chicken and jollof rice meal and the chicken was hard and unseasoned. The jollof rice was mid at best. There was only one African lady in the kitchen as part of the staff at this place. All other staff were Latina...Laughable to  say the least! Don't waste your money here.

I love African food and this was an okay experience but I love the price of the meal. I got a side jollof rice and okra soup with beef. Okra was still crunchy and the rice isn't as seasoned as the Jollof rice from Cameroon. I will give them another try.

I taste many African food and this is the worst food I ever taste. When you go to a Hispanic restaurant or Asian restaurant you will never see a black person cook them how come is expanded cooking African food. I said I didn't want no meat in my food and it was a whole bunch of dry fish I will never go back there anymore. I had to put my own season in my own spice into the food to taste good so I don't waste my money.

I say the food was different for me but it was also a new experience.   I asked our server Saker about his favorite dish.  We got that and tried it.  We also got some Suya, beef skewers. Spicy but flavorful. We got some jollof Rice with Plantain, fried Tilapia dish,  Egusi Soup with pounded yam, We tried the stewed Goat in tomato broth.  That one was my favorite.  Everything was very good.   I enjoyed it very much.

I say one lesson by the staff for newcomers is to teach us how to eat the food.   I say every culture is different, so having a lesson I think is vital when visitors come.   I didn't know you put the fufu in the egusi soup and eat it.

I want to understand the culture and respect it.  It's all about a cultural experience.   For one evening, I felt as if I was a new country. Eating their food and partaking in their culture.

formatted_address: 15703 Homebriar Ct Building 15703, Missouri City, TX 77489, United States
name: Suya Power House

reviews.text: I'll start by saying that I've never eaten here. But here is what I'm complaining about. This restaurant has an online store for clothing and apparels. Why does a restaurant sell online apparel? No idea. But I bought something from their website through shop. A couple days in, they cancelled the order and had not refunded now are they answering emails about my request

Found this hidden gem and the food is really good! Customer service is excellent and preparation time is fast!!!

Ordered the beef suya, then we chose rice and plantain for our sides.

Suya Powerhouse offers the BEST SUYA in town. The food is absolutely finger-licking good, with spices and flavors that are simply amazing. Neba, the chef, is both professional and efficient, providing great service every time. I've already been here twice in just one week.The food is made fresh to order every single time, ensuring the highest quality and taste. Suya Powerhouse will definitely be my go-to spot for takeout from now on.
I placed a delivery order that was never delivered. I also left a voice email trying to get in contact with someone, but no one responded. They took the money and NO DELIVERY! SCAM

Placed an order and arrived at the location (which is a home?) and didn’t hear from anyone. Called a few times and no one answered. Rang the doorbell and still no answer. I even checked the Google page to confirm I arrived during open hours. After 10-15 min of waiting in my car, I just left and will be calling my bank for a refund.

formatted_address: 6991 S Texas 6, Houston, TX 77083, United States
name: Chez Michelle

reviews.text: I recently had the pleasure of dining at Chez Michelle and I must say it was an absolute delight. The food was perfectly flavored, with each dish showcasing the culinary expertise of the chefs specialy my fish. The staff was incredibly friendly and welcoming, making the dining experience even more enjoyable. The ambiance of the restaurant transported me to Cameroon, with its vibrant decor and warm atmosphere. Chez Michelle is definitely a restaurant that I will remember fondly, and I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a memorable dining experience.

I am giving this place 2stars because of the horrible  customer service.  5 times that I have been here the service that I've receuved is tremendously slow and aside from Linda, no one will even greet you or wait on you..unless you wave them over to your table. Well the tall tall lady only smiles when she is serving a table full of men...she gives them prompt service with a smile. My food on March 1st was horrible and undercooked fish with overcooked scorched unseasoned jallof rice AND hard plantain. I gave them 4 to 5 visits and with that...NO MORE. Also they advertise Oxtails but never have them and when they do,  They have to cook them and you wait for 1.5hrs. Poor poor poor poor choice of place to eat. No music no menus....Never again...I would rather go to any of the other African restaurants.
Been coming here for fish for the past 5 years now! Never do they disappoint! Great place to chill and have meetings.

The dish I order should have had beef. It only had gristle, fat and bones without meat.  The attached pic is the above mentioned contents. Rice was very oily, food was not eatable.  I threw it all away.  I am so disgusted with the contents. Unfortunately, I could not give them a zero.

Great Cameroon style roast fish. Get a great taste of our most cherished roast fish "burning fish" and other dishes. I have dined at Chez Michelle for over 10years and she has never, never let me down. This new location is a great and much anticipated upgrade. Highly recommended.

formatted_address: 9815 Bissonnet St, Houston, TX 77036, United States
name: Finger Licking

reviews.text:
Tasty meals, but the order combination is a bit different at this restaurant. I ordered a meal of edikaikong soup and was surprised when I got to the restaurant and was told that the soup, the meat (protein), and side were all separate prices. When you order soup, you get just the soup. The soup alone was about $20, the cheapest rotting was about $11, and the side of white rice was $5.

I also tried the bitterleave soup. Both soups were good.

Food was not bad, just expected more. Also the meat was not tender (goat or beef) we ordered egusi, fufu, jollof rice and meat pies. The goat in the egusi was flavorful but very chewy and the beef with the jollof rice was super tough, jollof rice did not have much flavor. Meat pies were great. Not mad just expressing, but the meat was tough, still enjoyed it though.

I will tell the truth! They have the BEST okra Ogbono soup I have had in Houston but their attitudes and customer service? TERRIBLE! They started taking my food to the back after they made it then coming back staring me in my eyes with this evil look, UNPROVOKED! It made me feel like they put something in my food. Nevertheless, that was their last time seeing me! Since I’ve stopped eating there, a lot of weird misfortune has stopped.

This was my first time trying this place and the customer service was terrible. As soon as I informed that the meat was too tough, the waitress had an attitude. I wanted to do an exchange for chicken instead something that wasn’t so dry and tough. They wait 15 mins to come back and tell me they’re out of chicken smh. They were not out they just didn’t want to replace my meat. The egusi soup was ok but I would never step back into this facility. They demanded that I pay for something that I couldn’t even consume, I requested mgr and she had the nerve to tell me it’s not even about the mgr, then proceeds to get the cook from back and try and convince me that the meat is supposed to look and taste like that. Rude establishment and do not recommend.

An evening out with my daughter and her adventurous white friend. Service was ok, no biggie. Server was nice but we felt a bit pressured to pay the bill before we were done eating.

Finger Licking is a Nigerian restaurant serving authentic Naija cuisine. They are big on “efo riro” (mixed African vegetable soup). We decided to try other soups today.

We had popular Naija drinks: Star Lager Beer and Orijin (spirit mixed drink with African herbs and fruit extracts.

For morsels, we each had pounded yam, accompanied with Bitter Leaf Soup and Tilapia fish (1); Egusi (melon) soup with Assorted Meats: beef, shaki (tripe) and cow leg, popularly called “bokoto”! (2).

Nice taste of home! 😋 Could be better though … to get the real local flavor in so those unfamiliar with Nigerian cuisine can get the best.

And they do home deliveries with Uber Eats, Door Dash and Grub Hub.

formatted_address: 11920 Westheimer Rd #J, Houston, TX 77077, United States
name: Rhay's

reviews.text: This restaurant is a MUST visit!  The vibe, the ambiance, the music!  You can’t go wrong!  It also has an outside patio with hooka.  The food is freaking DELICIOUS! I HIGHLY recommend the LAMBCHOPS!  Special welcomed me into the establishment and Christy set the tone.  Thanks for a very enjoyable evening!  See ya soon!

Great food!! Took my boyfriend there for his birthday. He told me that there was no soap in the men's bathroom.
I loved the food. Service was good too. They didn't have olives for his drink. He wasn't happy as much as I was. 😁

I recently had the pleasure of dining at a wonderful restaurant that truly exceeded my expectations. From the moment I walked in, I was greeted with a warm smile and an inviting atmosphere that set the tone for a delightful evening.

The menu featured a diverse array of dishes, each one crafted with care and creativity. We started with the Suya Taco which was AMAZING, then had the Rhays Jerked Pasta, oh my I could not have enough of it.

The service was impeccable. Our server was attentive without being intrusive, striking the perfect balance of professionalism and friendliness. They expertly guided us through the menu, offering thoughtful recommendations and ensuring our glasses were never empty. It felt like they genuinely cared about our dining experience, which made the evening even more enjoyable.

The ambiance of the restaurant was equally impressive. Soft lighting and tasteful decor created a cozy yet sophisticated environment, ideal for both intimate dinners and celebratory gatherings. The background music was just the right volume, allowing for comfortable conversation while still enhancing the overall dining experience.

Overall, this restaurant is a gem that I would highly recommend to anyone looking for delicious food, exceptional service, and a welcoming atmosphere. Needless to say I def can't wait to return and explore more of their menu!

My husband & I went for brunch. Did not have any wait time to be seated, drinks were AMAZING, Kay, was very accommodating and friendly. The food was DELICIOUS. Cooked fresh and perfectly seasoned. We got blueberry chicken n waffles, shrimp n grits, jerked charbroiled lamb chops, and plantain. Very beautifully designed, clean & nice energy. We will be back to try their dinner menu.

I recently had the pleasure of celebrating my birthday at one of the most elegant and beautifully designed Nigerian restaurants I’ve ever visited—and I can confidently say it was one of my best birthdays yet. With a party of 12, every detail was handled flawlessly from the moment we walked in.

The décor was absolutely stunning, blending traditional African textures with a refined, modern aesthetic. The ambiance alone set the tone for an unforgettable evening. The plating of each dish was nothing short of artful—each course looked as good as it tasted. From rich jollof rice to perfectly grilled meats and flavorful sides, the food was both comforting and elevated. It felt like a true culinary celebration of Nigerian culture.

What stood out even more was the service. Impeccable doesn’t even begin to describe it. The staff was attentive, warm, and effortlessly coordinated, ensuring that our large party felt welcomed and cared for throughout the evening.

The highlight of the night? They surprised me with sparklers and a birthday sign that brought so much joy to the table. It was festive, personal, and such a thoughtful touch—it made the whole evening feel even more magical.

This restaurant is a shining example of what upscale international African dining can be. We need more spaces like this—where culture, flavor, and sophistication meet. I highly recommend it for anyone looking to host events, celebrations, or simply indulge in a memorable night out.

formatted_address: 8330 W Bellfort Ave Ste C, Houston, TX 77071, United States
name: MAMA JOLLOF RESTAURANT

reviews.text: The food is tasty and clean, not too salty or peppery. They have the best fried rice in Houston. We had our thanksgiving lunch there. It was fantastic. We bought 3 other addtional dishes to take home. Highly recommended.

Great food and portions. My only issue is that there is not a ton of seating, especially for larger parties. We scoped out the place to introduce our non-Nigerian friends to the cuisine but I’m uncertain there will be enough seating to be comfortable.
Mama stand on Business when it comes to too Catfish pepper soup with okra and pound yams the best place to go I have been to other places they are trash .Mama gives you your money worth

My friend and I decided to try out this spot based on their appealing pictures. We got there and placed an order to go. The lady told us the food was going to take about 20mins. We decided to try out their overpriced $30 hookah while we waited. It took them 30 mins to bring out the hookah. I voiced my concern to who appeared to be the owner/cook/hookah maker. With no apology, he decided to give us a $5 discount on the hookah. The hookah itself was TRASH, worst hookah I ever had! could not even smoke it. Complete waste of money. The food took an hour to come out, it was bland, no flavor whatsoever. We all know a good suya is supposed to be bursting with flavors topped with fresh cut onions. I mentioned the onions while ordering the food, did not get them. The Jollof rice was also lacking flavor and dry. My friend complained about the flavor of his food as well. Let me just say this was a complete waste of $80, highly disappointed. Smh

This restaurant has the best Nigerian food in Houston hands down!! The food is always so flavorful and cooked to perfection. I’ve had the jollof rice many times and it’s always consistently delicious. The food always comes out in a timely manner. I love the atmosphere as well. The restaurant is very clean. I love the Afrobeats music they play as well.They also offer hookah as well if you are into that. This is by far my favorite Nigerian restaurant!

formatted_address: 13505 Westheimer Rd, Houston, TX 77077, United States
name: African tasty hub

reviews.text: I ordered 2 plates of Amala & Gbegiri and after a taste when Uber dropped delivered, I had to call the owner of This restaurant to actually thank her for such splendid cooking- I rarely eat out, cos I get disappointed easily when it doesn’t meet my expectations! But babyyyy this - I had to call the restaurant and ordered a pan of her yummiliscious “Obe-ata” for Amala- for thanksgiving dinner ! Everyone loved the taste and thought I actually cooked it cos it tasted like  home cooked! Just wow 🤩 And to top it off- so affordable!

If you’re looking for, authentic Nigerian cuisine and intercontinental dishes, this is your number 1 stop.
I can’t rave enough about the portions, and how delicious and fresh the meals are. The owner is very friendly, super accommodating for your catering needs. I ordered the Chinese food for my birthday party, it was 100/10.🤤🤩
I have also tried the Nigerian jollof rice, the coconut rice and the burst of flavor is unmatched.
All I can say is go check it out!! And thank me later! 😌✌🏾

I got an order of delivery from this food place and quite frankly I was extremely disappointed. It is unacceptable to use GMO  chicken drums in jollof or fried rice, food was bland had to use my own stew to eat the swallow.... the ewa agonyin was lackluster for lack of a better word the sauce was just bleh.... even the grilled fish wasn't appealing to the eyes....and the bill wasn't cheap either.... please do better GMO chicken has no place in Nigerian dishes just in case you do not know

Never been disappointed with any meal. There’s no place in Houston with the amount of variety they have. And if you need catering for parties, wedding or any big event, they do it best. Catered with them on several occasions and never regretted it. Their restaurant service is always very efficient with minimal wait times.

The Suya was so dry and tough to eat. The Kanu was frozen and not fresh.

All this for $40 from uber eats. Not worth it

formatted_address: 8633 Richmond Ave., Houston, TX 77063, United States
name: Crave Suya

reviews.text:
Absolutely Fantastic and Delicious. Probably the best Shawarma i have had in Houston and other places i have been to in Atlanta. I drove from New Orleans to handle some stuff and a friend of mine recommended we come here. Was very pleased with the spice taste and Flavour. 🤣🤣 when i called another friend and told them where i was they were sad because if they knew i was coming to this spot they would have joined.

Only issue is you have to place the order ahead of time so you don’t come here and wait 30 minutes but other than that everything was great!

Decided To Give The Place A Try After Seeing Many Ads On Instagram. Didnt Realize It Was A Food Truck Until I Got There But Thats Fine. Once I Arrived It Took Awhile For Someone To Acknowledge Me. Nonetheless, We Ordered And The Time It Took For Our Food To Come Was Insane. I Know They’re A Popular Food Spot But Jesus I Waited For Close To 50min. Once The Food Came Out I Was Happy. My Suya Was Pretty Good. I Asked For Extra Seasoning And They Gave Me Just That. I Tried My Friend’s Shawarma And Mighty God. To Me That Is The Star Of The Menu. I Instantly Forgot About My Suya And Wanted My Own Shawarma Lol. As Good As It Was Tho I Would Not Return Because The Hassle To Get The Food Is Just Too Much. The Parking Sucks And The Police Come Around Telling You To Move When There’s Nowhere Else To Go. I Didn’t Enjoy That So I Won’t Be Back But The Food Was Nice.

I got the crave bowl!
Before I went there I could smell it! This is my first time trying this food ever! I love the flavor in every bite was crazy!!!! I’m definitely coming back! So much food!!
The staff was sweet 😊

The food is good, but the customer service was bad. I ordered suya fries and opened the bag to see that it was full of cut plantains. In highly disappointed.

(Recently)
Came back the next day and they sorted out the matter really well. Overall this is a good establishment and the food is good, their workers just made a mistake.

We ordered the beef suya, and while the portion size was generous, the texture and flavor were disappointing.It felt gritty, almost like chewing sand, and I didn’t really enjoy the taste. Tomatoes wasn’t fresh and it tasted spoilt.

formatted_address: 11720 W Airport Blvd #1600, Meadows Place, TX 77477, United States
name: Suya Hut

reviews.text: This is the best Nigerian food I've ever tried! They give you big portions for great prices. It's a local owned restaurant so please go support it. The food and service is so amazing. 10/10 would recommend and I'm now going to be a regular!!
Suya is dry, the meat is wet and all I taste is salt and pepper, no other flavor what a waste of beef. If I wanted eat shitty food, I would cook it myself. N.O.

Quality authentic African food that’s worth the drive if you don’t live locally. Excellent customer service, wait time is a bit long but that’s because the food is truly made fresh to serve. Plenty of options, from rice, meats, veggies, and soup. If your spice palette isn’t strong then certainly stick with the milder options. We really enjoyed the fresh pressed juices that’s offered with every meal. I’d definitely go back for any occasion.

I wanted to try African food for the 3rd time ( I didn’t like it at the other places I went)and was told this restaurant has good food.  I came in and was greeted at the door, the young man at the front was very nice.  I ordered the egusi but was given vegetable stew with yam fufu instead.  I didn’t realize it until I left and showed my friend what I ate.  Neverless it was absolutely delicious, my husband had the Jollof rice and beef suya again delicious.
This place is very clean inside with plenty of seating. I highly recommend.  Next time I want the egusi please 😊

Some of the best Nigerian food  I’ve ever had  had. Came in before a long day of travel. Left with a homemade bowl of egusi soup made fresh to order. Anytime I find myself in Texas I’ll come back!!!!! So good !

formatted_address: 3533 S Dairy Ashford Rd suite i, Houston, TX 77082, United States
name: Royal Point

reviews.text:
The food wasn't bad, though for the time I waited, it should have come out hot. The suya tasted okay. It was generously seasoned with suya pepper. The extra pepper sauce on the side was nice as well, not for the faint of heart.
The grilled chicken was okay as well but came out partly dry and hard. Everything was about $30.

Really nice staff. Good food. My to go spot for grilled tilapia plantain and jollof rice.
In my experience, the fish is fresh 8 out of 10 times.

The fish I received was ridiculously small and quite disappointing. It always seems to happen when I order online, but not when I order in person. I called the restaurant, and the person I spoke to was somewhat polite. He mentioned that he followed the instructions given, stating that they have either very small or large portions available. This doesn’t make sense to me because I paid the same regular price and received a fish that was absurdly small. They need to do better! Normally, I don’t complain because I’m not really a foodie, but this is just too small!

DRY, HARD SUYA! Stale and not fresh. So hard that it cuts the styrofoam container! Can’t even bite it! Definitely reheated from previous days. Don’t waste your time. Bragged to my moon that she would enjoy, she couldn’t even chew the meat…  Been coming here for years, Suya was the best, today terrible. Whenever the owner is not around, the results will show. Called to provide feedback, the attendant, actually shouted at me… soo unfortunate. This is a place that catered our son’s first birthday, we shared laughs with the owner, she has really tried. The staff has watch it soon grow. A poor food experience is one thing, a poor experience by a staff member has ensured that I will not spend my money here again!

Dry, old, and cold Suya. When I called to tell them about it, she told me she cooked everything today and I let her know was it earlier today because this food is cold she told me to come bring it back to her and she’ll replace it but the whole reason for me ordering DoorDash is so I wouldn’t have to drive there and back which is a 52 min drive collectively, overall horrible customer service and plus they’re serving old and cold food and I told her the meat was hard as well. DON’T WASTE YOUR MONEY HERE!

formatted_address: 11214 Plainfield St # B, Houston, TX 77031, United States
name: Traditional Food Restaurant

reviews.text: I absolutely love their food.  I haven't tried many things because I'm always ordering the same dish which is the egusi. I'm going to try the fish pepper soup my next visit

8/13/24
I'm vegan and the Lady chef made feel comfortable and prepared my meal and it was quite delicious.
I had the spinach mixture with no fish, a lot of plantains, the tomato stew was to die for totally tastefully.
I will be back.

I called to make sure they have gluten free options because I was planning a dinner with a friend who has celiac disease.
I asked if they have gluten free options, and the lady answering the phone said she didn’t understand so I explained that my friend can’t eat anything cooked with flour. She hung up on me before I could finish explaining. I am so disappointed in her behavior. American here. Guess they don’t want to serve Americans. FYI

absolutely horrible, I placed an order on doer dash at 7pm they took forever making the food to the point 3 dashers had to cancel the order and pass it on to the next person, finally doordash support for in touch with them and they said it was complete. when the dasher arrived at 9 pm they told him they were closed and my card was charged twice even though they don’t close until 10 pm. When I got in touch with Doordash they said I couldn’t get a refund since they had to pay the store. I am so mad right now I can’t even fathom how rude I was treated. do not go to this restauran!!!

Haven’t actually had the opportunity to try the food, my review is based solely on my experience. I placed an order today via Door Dash. The order was accepted and to be ready around 315pm…order placed 55 min beforehand. At 257pm, I receive a message from Door dash that the order is canceled because the restaurant is closed. Per Google, the restaurant is open until 10pm. I call just be correct before I post a review, the restaurant is OPEN. So rather than cancel my order within 10-15 min after it’s placed, they wait until 15 min before it’s to be delivered. I despise writing bad reviews, especially for my own people, but this is very bad business.

formatted_address: 6800 Southwest Fwy, Houston, TX 77074, United States
name: Lucy

reviews.text: Went in for the first time and was greeted with the best hospitality. The service was amazing! We had a waitress named Rosa. She was very helpful with picking options since it was food we had never tried before. You can tell the food is made from scratch. We tried a few different things to get a variety and even got to try their tea and coffee, which were both very good! My wife got the lamb awaze tibs, my kids got the juicy chicken tibs, and my mom got beef girgiro tibs & I got the meat and veggie platter. Everything was amazing!

This place was such a vibe! It’s so moody and cozy! They had some really good music going and the ambiance was very nice. I had the chicken tibs. This was my first time trying Ethiopian cuisine and I must say it was absolutely delicious. Very flavorful fragrant spices. I am excited to get back and try my next new dish!

Very good food had the spicy lamb tibs, first question I asked is what they recommended as I do at most restaurants and took the advice and ran with it. Was not disappointed, I had it made spicy as I love spicy food (if spicy is not for you go for non spicy). Also tried the sampler and everything was made very flavorful. Definitely will be going back as I forgot to try the honey wine I was told about.
Delicious food, ambiance and service. Tried the Ethiopian wine and it was really good as well. Good portion and good value for their prices. Will definitely come back here.

Nice place to be. Had a good time to spend with friends. Nice sitting areas. They take time for your order because they make fresh food.  We had vegetarian options. Pretty much enough platter for 2 people. Kids had a great time as well. Colorful but little old interior.
Overall it was good.
Friends had their anniversary so they gave complimentary Tiramisu dessert. It was really delicious.

formatted_address: 2022 Wilcrest Dr, Houston, TX 77042, United States
name: Native Pot

reviews.text: Got here ordered via the screen after accepting payment. Only to get a 2nd text message after about 10mins of waiting that my order is cancelled with no explanation. Meanwhile my money have been deducted. This is just frustrating and a scam. I never come near here again and am from outside town
Really good food. Only complaint is that the beef and jollof rice had A LOT of rice and like two pieces of beef.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Native Pot, and I must say, it was an unforgettable experience. From the moment I walked in, the atmosphere felt warm and welcoming, but what really stood out was the quality of the food. Every dish tasted incredibly fresh, as if the ingredients had just been picked that morning. The flavors were vibrant, and you could really tell the care that goes into preparing each meal.I ordered their signature dishes, and every bite was bursting with authenticity. The seasoning was spot-on, balanced yet bold, and the presentation made the food look as good as it tasted. It’s clear that Native Pot takes pride in using high-quality, fresh ingredients, and it makes a world of difference. Whether you’re a fan of traditional dishes or you’re trying something new, you’re in for a treat here.The service was excellent too, with staff who were knowledgeable and eager to make sure every guest had a great experience. I left feeling full and satisfied, already planning my next visit. If you appreciate fresh, flavorful food and a great dining atmosphere, Native Pot is the place to go!

I was in Houston for a wedding with my husband a couple of weeks ago and was so excited to find a Nigerian restaurant close to our hotel—Nativeport did not disappoint! From our very first order, the experience was nothing short of amazing, and it stayed that way for the four days we kept going back.

The owner was professional, dedicated, and most importantly, can seriously cook! I fell in love with food all over again. Everything we tried was authentic and delicious. I even ordered extra food to take back home to California, and she kindly froze everything to make sure it would travel well on my flight.

P.S. My last meal before flying out? Fried rice, plantain, and peppered goat meat—perfection!

I normally don't do reviews, but this meal I just ate from Nativepot has forced my hand. My goodness, I am in a food high right now. First off, you will get conquered by the quantity, but because of how delicious the meal is, your mind will tell you that you can finish it... lies. I had to outwardly tell the food "You Win", and saved the rest for later. Rashida has to be some sort of world class chef to make naija food taste like I have never eaten it before.
