name: Broni Home Taste / Africana / Old Brothers Restaurant

html_attributions: Broni Home Taste / Africana / Old Brothers Restaurant

reviews.text:
I was looking for some place to eat something delicious and I found that place in Broni! I asked for a recommendation and the young lady behind the counter said I should try the on Engusi with beef and Fufu... So I did and I was blown away!! The restaurant is clean, neat and really bright atmosphere. The young lady behind the counter was very helpful and polite. After I order my food she came out to check and see if I was comfortable with the heat level of the dish I chose. And I told her I'm a nola girl, so yes definitely comfortable. The pricing isn't terrible based on portion and ingredients. My meals with tax I think was $28. Go check them out. You won't be disappointed!
Pro Tip:
Check out the menu before you go for a better idea of what you might want to try if you haven't experienced West African food already. And ask advice on what to try.

This is hands down some great food. I had the beef and jallof rice and the flavors where there it was packed well and I didn’t have a long wait. I will definitely be back. First visit and I’m so glad I found this place. Thank you guys for the great food and service.

I was at an event which was 7miles away from this restaurant. Found the restaurant online and placed an order. The okra soup was delicious and better compared to the ones I have tried in ATL. The fried beef was tasty and perfect the Ghanaian way. I will order again if I find myself around there.

Wow I really enjoyed this food! The Jollof rice is smokey and so delicious! The goat is the perfect compliment to it. I see some say the goat is dry, but you have to understand how they cook it. The sauce and flavor makes up for the dryness, in my opinion. None of it went to waste in this house! Everything was good, tasted clean and fresh.
I ordered on instacart, the driver had another order to drop off before mine and it still arrived hot!

I ordered delivery for waakye and banku. The food arrived warm and beautifully packaged. The waakye portion was substantial and delicious, the banku and okra came insulated and securely packaged cups. Would order again.

formatted_address: 560 Dutch Valley Rd NE STE 100, Atlanta, GA 30324, United States
name: Verdure Kitchen & Cocktails

reviews.text:
We hosted a baby shower at Verdura Kitchen & Cocktails, and overall the experience was absolutely phenomenal.
From the beginning, the planning process was smooth and stress-free. I worked closely with Gelila, the private party and events concierge, and she was professional, prompt, and extremely efficient with email communication. Every question was answered quickly, and when we had a last-minute emergency that required changing our event date, they responded right away and accommodated the reschedule with no issues at all.
The rental cost for the private space was very reasonable and feasible for what was offered, as it is the spending limit for your party.
The restaurant itself is classy, elegant, and located in a prime area. Verdura has several beautiful spaces available for private events, and their website is visually appealing and detailed, making it easy to choose the right space for your needs. The décor, branding, and marketing of this restaurant are truly stellar.
A day or two before the event, I connected with the manager to go over final details. One thing to note for anyone planning an event here: guests are required to RSVP through a reservation link and pre-select their menu items in advance to ensure timely service. While I understand the purpose, this was a bit challenging since not all guests RSVP promptly. It required a lot of follow-up on my end, and I even received reminder calls the day before and the day of the event that some guests still hadn’t selected their meals. With everything else going on, that part was somewhat stressful and worth considering when planning.
Upon arrival, we were greeted warmly by the hostess and escorted to our reserved area. The space was absolutely beautiful, and the ambiance throughout the restaurant was amazing. There was even a live saxophonist playing, which added such a pleasant and elegant touch to the event.
Decor guidelines are fairly strict. (limited balloons-8, cake allowed for $25 fee but honestly, the space is already so stunning that very little décor is needed. Our small setup was more than enough.
We hosted a baby shower brunch, all items—from the pancakes, eggs, chicken and waffles, appetizers, cocktails, and mocktails—was delicious and beautifully presented. Every single item ordered was delectable.
We did have a spending minimum based on our party size (25-30guests)we were aware of ahead of time. While this was clearly outlined in the contract, there were frequent reminders during the event that we hadn’t reached the minimum yet. A couple of check-ins would have been fine, but the repeated reminders felt a bit excessive and disruptive.
Unfortunately, our main challenge during the event was with our primary server, Rich. From the beginning, his demeanor felt rushed and abrupt. There were moments where he seemed impatient with guests, cut people off while they were speaking, and hurried food service in a way that felt uncomfortable. At one point, he attempted to remove my plate while I was still eating, despite me clearly stating otherwise. His interactions often felt tense, not only with guests but also with another server assisting us, Sienna, who was calm, patient, and very pleasant throughout the event.
As the hosts, we also felt rushed toward the end while cleaning up, despite actively packing up and ensuring the space was left neat. The tone and delivery of those reminders added unnecessary stress.
Once I requested to speak with the manager, everything shifted positively. Aaron, the mgr on duty, was absolutely exceptional. He was kind, attentive, and truly went above and beyond to make sure we were comfortable and enjoying the moment. He patiently assisted us with reviewing the bill breakdown (while still allowing us to pay on one check), reassured us that we had time, and encouraged us to relax and enjoy the celebration. Aarons(mgr) presence completely turned the experience around. Rich should relax.
The baby shower itself was a success. The saxophonist even played specifically for my sister, which was such a beautiful and memorable touch.

Omg!! Verdure is truly a hidden gem I didn’t know I needed in my life.** From valet to walking through the doors, the experience was flawless. We were seated immediately, and Hannah absolutely *made* our first visit unforgettable. She didn’t just serve us, she guided us through the menu like a curated culinary journey, and every recommendation was spot on.

Our drinks were the perfect balance of strong and sweet (dangerously good!), and the appetizers? Listen… they nearly took us out. The portion sizes were generous, but the flavor? Next-level. I had the most flavorful Brussels sprouts of my *entire* life. The crab cakes literally melted in our mouths.

By the time entrées came, we were so happily full that we decided to share the Braised Short Rib Special and it ended up being one of the best decisions of the night. The short rib was tender, rich, and clearly made with love. And I tried yams for the first time and WOW… absolutely delicious.

To top it all off, the live saxophone player set the most romantic, elegant vibe.

Verdure gave luxury, comfort, flavor, and an experience I’ll be thinking about for a long time. 10/10 recommend.

Great for date night, good drinks and a fine dining experience. Brunch is affordable and chic. They have live music some nights and play good afrobeats and amapiano. I’ve been for dinner and brunch. If you want a solid, affordable experience do brunch. If you want a really good date go to dinner. You can also walk right onto the belt line to walk off your meal.

This was the best experience ! My husband took me here for our Anniversary and I loved it. Our table manager Emoni took great care of us. From the warm hand towels, crème brûlée, the food! Amazing Ambiance. My husband is West African and I am American and this place is a true fusion of our cultures!! A gem here in Atlanta.

Appetizer : Fried Octopus
Entrees: Peri Peri Chicken for me, He got the steak dish
Moc-tails: Him Lavender, I got the coconut lavender

EVERY THING WAS A TEN 🥹💖💕

This is the perfect spot for girls night. Me and my friends go here to celebrate, catch a vibe and enjoy the best food/service. The bartenders are amazing and really make the experience fun. Easy parking and sits in a nice neighborhood, away from the crowded roads in the city. We enjoyed drinks and apps, shout out to Derrick on the beautiful holiday drinks. 🥂🎄

formatted_address: 3965 Rockbridge Rd SW, Stone Mountain, GA 30083, United States
name: Tolex African Grill

reviews.text:
Restaurant was busy food was fast.
It was decent/ good. Sits perfect! Wish it had more for the price. Egusi was decent. Meat a tad tough not spicy at all.

I had an issue with my order and when I called they were so quick to fix the issue! Very kind people! I was angry and they understood and the chef came and asked me what I even needed to make the meal better! I’m very VERY happy I came and this is great food and great people!

I had an amazing experience at this restaurant! I ordered the egusi soup with assorted meat and pounded yam, and it was absolutely delicious—rich, flavorful, and cooked to perfection. My friend had the abula, and they couldn’t stop talking about how authentic and satisfying it was.
The customer service was exceptional from start to finish. The staff were warm, attentive, and made us feel right at home. I was even personally greeted by the owner, which made the experience feel even more special and welcoming.
If you’re looking for great food, genuine hospitality, and a true taste of home, this is definitely the place to go. Highly recommend!

First of all i went online to check out the menu before odering. I ordered honey beans with plantains for pickup. My protein,  mackerel fish because there was no up charge for this fish, once I got in the restaurant I was told there is an upcharge on ALL fish. I told the young lady that took my order the online order system states a different  pricing, she said OK. My order went from $23 to $29, although she said ok I was still charged the upcharge. The beans were blended and the mackerel was 3 pieces the size of a 50 cent coin, my order was placed in a small white 2go box, beans spilled everywhere.  My co workers LOVE african food but when I showed them this food, it was a hard No! Presentation 0, Portion size 0. Taste 0, this is one of my favorite dishes, ive had it cooked for me and ive ordered it from different restaurants and ive never seen it look quite like what I was given
The beans were either prepped for moimoi or very over cooked because they were pureed or blended and it seemed water was added to thin it out. WHY a restaurant would sale a customer food like this i dont understand.  I would hate to think it was because im American and they figured I wouldn't know how its suppose to look or taste so give it to her anyway or because it was a pick up order and let me be shocked once I get to my location or they just didnt care but its so sad because the cook knew that wasn't right when she plated it, I dont have a picture because my phone wasn't charged and I didnt have enough power to snap it.
I eat african food at least 3 times a week and my co workers and I order something weekly, but we normally get it from restaurants further out, these are at least 9 to 10 new customers you could have acquired at least 2 to 3 visits weekly.

I had a great experience at Tolex African Grill! The girl at the front desk with the glasses was super friendly and had amazing customer service . she made us feel very welcome. The guy working with her was also really nice and helpful. The food was absolutely top-notch , fresh, flavorful, and authentic. I’ll definitely be coming back. Highly recommend!

formatted_address: 209 Edgewood Ave SE, Atlanta, GA 30303, United States
name: Afrodish Restaurant

reviews.text: Wow! Authentic African/Caribbean food. I had the jerk chicken with rice and peas and black eyed peas and spinach. I also ordered a beef patty and some coconut water. The owners/staff are so kind and you can tell the food is cooked with love. I wish I could try the goat and oxtail but I am stuffed. Large portions for a great price too. Don't miss this place!

Price was great for the portions I got with this. The jerk chicken had so many flavors as did the spinach, broccoli, and rice it came with. Would definitely recommend if you’re in the area and want a quick lunch. The guy that served the food was very friendly was well

I knew my daughter was at the Curb Market so I asked her to bring me something to eat. She decided to stop at this place and pick me up some oxtails.

The platter was oxtails rice and peas and cabbage. Although I've had a lot of oxtail planters in Atlanta this one was different. The taste of the oxtails, the gravy, the peas and the cabbage were totally on point.

The oxtails were tender but not overcooked. The flavor was very good. I have to say the rice and peas were completely cooked but not mushy. Many times when you get these platters either the rice is crunchy or the peas are crunchy. The only thing I would have wanted is more gravy. They definitely had a good flavor. Finally someone knows how to cook cabbage. Either is too much or has no flavor in other places. This place cooked it just right. I don't know how much the planter calls exactly but I think my daughter said around $13. This price is kind of unheard of right now in Atlanta. Inflation has got the best of the food in the street and we as patrons understand but it's always nice to see a business kind of work with their customers.

I would definitely return to get more and to try something different. Give this business a shot whenever you at the Curb Market.

It’s a cafeteria style place. Food is excellent. Service is sweet and pleasant. Their oxtail and goat curry have never let me down. We’ve been coming here since my freshman at Georgia state university. There’s always a line, but it move quickly. Parking is 1 hour free with validation.

Oh wow, real African food in Atlanta!  My wife just came back from West Africa and she said the goat curry and veggies are just like back there.

As for me, I just want my plantains, everything else just nice additions. :)

formatted_address: 5145 Old National Hwy, Atlanta, GA 30349, United States
name: Manding Cafe

reviews.text: This place was very clean, the services was nice and the food was excellent.  I highly recommend eating here. The best food i have eaten in a long time. Now for a nap lol

Nestled on Old National Highway, Manding Cafe is a true treasure that captures the vibrant essence and rich culture of West Africa right in Atlanta. As someone who has a deep appreciation for natural juices and hearty, wholesome meals reminiscent of the comfort food that fuels the spirit (much like what Popeye the Sailor Man felt) I was eager to dive into the offerings at Manding Cafe.

Walking through the doors, I was greeted with warm smiles and the enticing aromas of spices that instantly transported me to a place filled with joy and comfort. The decor, adorned with elements reflecting the Manding heritage, created an inviting atmosphere that felt like home.

I began my meal with a refreshing natural juice that was a harmonious blend of flavors, invigorating and uplifting with every sip. It was the kind of drink that fills you with energy and warmth, setting a perfect foundation for what was to come.

As I enjoyed my meal, the experience was akin to the delightful feeling Popeye gets when he consumes his beloved spinach; a sense of vitality and fulfillment washed over me. Each bite was nourishing, leaving me with a sense of deep satisfaction and comfort that warmed my heart. The textures were delightful, offering a fulfilling experience that felt both enriching and soulful.

The attentive and friendly staff added to the overall experience, providing insights into the dishes and the culture they represent. Their commitment to sharing the joy of Manding cuisine was palpable, radiating positivity and a genuine sense of family.

What truly resonated with me during my visit was the ambiance infused with a spirit of peace, love, and prosperity—values that seem to permeate every corner of Manding Cafe. It’s clear that this establishment is not just about food; it’s about creating an experience that uplifts and nourishes the spirit.

Overall, Manding Cafe is a vibrant culinary haven in Atlanta, perfect for anyone seeking the rich flavors of West Africa. It’s a place that nourishes not just the body but the soul, much like the comforting meals that bring joy and energy to life. I’ll certainly be back for more of that uplifting spirit and delicious nourishment!

Thank you Mrs. Binta!!!🙏🏾🙌🏾😇

I’ve never been here in the area yes but not here. I was looking for Jollof rice and called a couple of place and ended up with Manding. I can in and it’s a half African shop and half African restaurant. I came to the window and was able to look straight to the back where I’m seeing a lady washing dishes and another’s walking around cleaning and the other lady stated she’s coming. Cleaner and organize is what it can use but hey I’m just a 1st time customer.
I received my food and processed to go to my mothers for the night. Where I made her a plate that looked good at the time and I even added purple onions. About a minute later my mother beings me her plate and say watcher out for what you are eating I immediately looked over to her plate and there was hair hanging from a piece of me that my mother was holding up. I looked more and into it and I kid you not there was hair in majority of my plate. Which was that chicken Jollof rice plate. I’m pretty sure if it was not for the family and friends of the family or just friends giving good reviews it would not be in the 4.6 or a good place to eat. I just know I better not be sick!

I had to redo my review three times I’m not even sure how to do a review on this one. I mean, I got cassava leaf yesterday. It was not greasy. It was outstanding the flavor.  So About even more today.  It was extremely greasy it don’t taste like it tasted yesterday and I’ve been eating cassava leaf for over two decades.  So I definitely know cassava leaf. When I tasted it.  So I had to use several paper towels to soak the grease well the oil.  As I kept eating it it taste OK.  But it still doesn’t taste like the cassava leaf I had yesterday.  And definitely extremely greasy. I’m 85% maybe 90% sure that the cassava leaf was mixed with potato soup.  Because I had a sample of potato soup yesterday it had a slight spice to it.  Cassava leaf does not.  And this soup have a slight spice to it and like I said it don’t taste like 100% cassava leaf.  I think maybe it’s time for me to just take a break and just stick with my American food ….  And if score matters to anyone, I saw the score today while I paid attention today cause I only been there twice and the score is 84 health score.

Relaxed atmosphere everyone seems to be friendly, they have a variety of sells items. So it's pretty much a restaurant mixed with a store. Sort of like a one stop shop. It's been open for a long time which means stability. In addition, everyone knows everyone there by the way they greet and socialize with one another. Although it's catered to the African culture there's a diverse group of customers that frequent the place.

formatted_address: 2930 Old Norcross Rd #400, Duluth, GA 30096, United States
name: Serbea Living African Restaurant

reviews.text: Just great!! I'd never had West African food, and wanted to try everything. The owner, Serbea, was happy to make a sample plate for me. Everything was delicious, and she explained what was in each dish. If I lived in the area, it's definitely be back soon.

I ordered through Uber Eats yesterday and got two orders one chicken and the other order fish with jollof rice for both. The food overall was tasty, a little salty but good! I really liked the chicken, it was fried to perfection but the fish on the other hand was fried to the point that it wasn’t crispy but very burnt. I was barely able to eat any fish. That was the only problem I experienced with my order.

My friends and I went there for dinner and we all loved our foods. It was so delicious.  I was too busy eating forgot to take decent photos of everything.  There were 5 of us and we each got something different so we could share.  Everything was flavorful, well seasoned and had a nice kick to it. Their spicy sauce was spicy but sooo good and it went well with all the foods! I loved the plantains and red snapper. The service was great and courteous, and the food came out super fast. Highly recommended! This will be in our rotation. 😋😋😋

The owner is such a lovely nice person. The food was delicious and flavorful. I'm looking forward to trying more dishes. We got okra soup with fufu and jollof rice with chicken and plantains. Everything was delicious! There was enough food for the money.
Definitely recommend 👌🏾 👍🏽 👏🏽

Just ordered today with Uber Eats, my order was Chicken with dried rice, the food was terrible and saggy, the plantain was cold and uncooked! Wasn’t happy at all! please do better, it’s not because it’s an online order, the food has to be poorly presented or not taking it seriously!

formatted_address: 5658 Riverdale Rd, Atlanta, GA 30349, United States
name: Saint-Louis Cuisine

reviews.text: Food was delicious. We went in a Friday and it was packed with men and there were just 2 small tables so it's mainly a carryout place but the food is delicious. I loved it so much  My son had a party and the food was catered from there and it was wonderful so I went back for the first time today.  The lamb Dhibe was flavorful and the jollof rice was delicious. The restaurant is small but seemed extremely popular as there were about 10-15 people in there appeared to be waiting for food and people were coming in as we were leaving. The 2 tables seem to be for people to wait for their food. It was about 15 minutes so we just went to the grocery store in the plaza and when we finished shopping our food was ready. The prices were good as well as the portion sizes. Next time we will probably just order in advance since there really is no done in but they didn't take long to prepare the food even though the restaurant was packed.
Love this place my first time ...food is authentic and delicious...with love and helping government workers right now

First time trying this tucked away gem with food rooted from Senegal and the quality was amazing!!

Portion size was generous, the fillet fish and jollof was seasoned to perfection without using any additional sauces or condiments, the ginger juice taste authentic and the bissap flower juice taste like a popsicle.

My friends had the chicken with jasmine rice and the lamb with rice and both said their meals were excellent.

I appreciate great customer service and to add amazing food has made me a customer now for sure!

Forgive me for not taking a before picture. The lady at the counter was very nice. Small shop in a plaza. isn’t the best plaza. Delighted to see a good food option in the plaza. I ordered the grilled lamb, lamb wrap, and fried rice/Benechin/Thieb. Rice was the best but I like it better when there are vegetables in it. The lamb meat was fatty in it. I ate all of the rice. My lamb wrap wasn’t the best because the meat inside was over cooked and had a little off taste. It was poorly wrapped, I couldn’t finish it. The grilled lamb had good flavor along with those awesome onions on top. A lot of the meat was chewy and inedible which was a bummer. This is my second time eating from here and I wanted to like it more as it is closer to me than the restaurant I usually go to for this type of food. They are fair priced. Wanted to try the Snapper. The meat pies didn’t look filled so I didn’t order one.

Update 4-4-2025. Snapper and rice was delicious. Snapper has great flavor. For DoorDash, please tie up the bag well and if possible place in a brown bag. Because the bag was poorly tied, I didn’t feel comforted knowing that the driver could’ve done anything to my food. Consider better tamper proof packaging for deliveries. It’s so much better to call in and order than to go through DoorDash with those ridiculous convenience fees.
Its so much flavor in the dish i tried. It taste like a 5star meal and you go there you will get the 5-star experience.  Order the chicken the lamb and the fish. Its a 10/10 !

formatted_address: 3665 Club Dr #102, Duluth, GA 30096, United States
name: The African Grill Duluth

reviews.text: I spent $56 on two plates, and one of them only came with three tiny pieces of beef....seriously? We wanted to try something new, but that turned out to be a big mistake. Everything, even the rice, was overwhelmingly spicy with no real flavor. Definitely not kid-friendly, and honestly not worth the money.
The food was so good,nice and clean environment. Took a friend to try Nigerian food and she enjoyed the beans and plantain.

Don't buy food from this place!! It is dangerous and has absolutely terrible customer service. Please read about my experience and avoid this restaurant at all costs!!

I've been a consistent customer of The African Grill Restaurant, making large catering food orders for over a year with no problems, until a very recent incident which is now going to lead to litigation.

Sometime in November, I ordered a half tray of Beans, half tray of Beef Stew, and half tray Jollof Rice costing over $200. This was a regular order for me. I had some of the beans that night and put the rest in the freezer. I found the beans very nice, and even gave feedback to the restaurant when i went back to order more food at a later date.

However, on December 1st 2025, I decided to have the beans again and took it out of the freezer to thaw and warm up in the microwave. As I started eating it, I bit on a very large stone and broke my tooth. Now anyone who is familiar with Nigerian cooked beans wouldn't be surprised to find stones in it.

Although that shouldn't be acceptable in a restaurant, the actual problem was the size of the stone. It was quite large, and it seemed unbelievable that it was missed in the preparation process.

Notwithstanding, I decided to call the restaurant and let them know what happened. All I wanted was an apology and some empathy, but what I encountered shocked me. I requested to speak to a woman who I was familiar with in the restaurant. I believe she was either the owner or a manager there. She came on the phone and I explained what happened to her.

She recognized who I was on the phone, and she immediately started screaming at me, saying why would i call her about food that I bought a month ago? She asked if I would do that to an American restaurant? I couldn't even get a word out. She continued berating me on the phone, saying i should never call her restaurant again, and she was going to block my number. Then she hung up.

I tried to call back, but the system kept sending my number to voicemail. It seemed she had blocked my number as she threatened. The sad thing was, all i wanted was an apology and an acknowledgement of the mistake, but i will now be pursuing a legal recompense for my broken tooth.

This isn't Nigeria where you treat your valued customers like trash and have no regard for them.

The food would’ve been nice if it wasn’t being over killed with pepper. I have lived in nigeria and grew up in the states and even the food there is not hot like this. The only thing that wasn’t filled with hot pepper was the plantain. If you want to drain your sinuses you can find that place loyal to help you. We had the beans and plantain and eforiro with rice and fish. Omo my stomach was burning afterwards. This is America , at least make it mild. There’s a way you will pepper food and no one can even taste the flavor of the food and that’s how the food was. The eforiro had IRU (fermented locus beans) in it- if you cook with that you know that it adds lot of flavor to food. But for where? You can’t Taste it bc the pepper is consuming it. Please learn how to adapt to what is enjoyable. Just because you’re Yoruba and you cook with ulcer producing pepper doesn’t mean you need to do that overall in your business where you service different ppl. For Gods sake. I asked the server if there was anything mild and she’s like “no” she said it matter of fact.  Never again. I can cook let me stay in my house. But she won’t change. She will keep cooking like that (the owner) bc Nigerians can’t adjust with where they are. She probably doesn’t even read her own business reviews/ replies to them. Mschew.

This is the worst Afan soup I've ever had.
Scent leaf in the soup?
I had to eat the assorted meat inside not to waste the entire meal. You must not offer all soups, choose what leaf is available please.
It was TASTELESS & BITTER!!!

formatted_address: 495 Pat Mell Rd W #105, Marietta, GA 30060, United States
name: Toyin - Nigerian cuisine

reviews.text: The owner and her employees really need to work on their character and attitudes. Especially the owner, she wears ide Ifa signifying she is Onisese but her attitude is so sour, it makes the traditions look bad. There is never a thank you, a hello, or warm greeting. Every time I see that woman behind the counter or speak to her she is looking and treating me and everyone there like they are an annoyance to her or she dislikes them. The men who are there when she isn’t aren’t any better. I don’t know what’s troubling them all but I’ve been going hear often for a while because the food is good. But I’m switching to another Nigerian spot after this visit because I’m tired of the way they act. I hope they see this and work on it before they lose all their customers. Not good.

On the way, Heading back home to TennesseeI ordered the Egusi soup, Ero soup, plantains, and turkey wing with fufu. OMG it was so good. Thank you for the hospitality and the service. I do look forward to seeing you next time, I am in town.

The place is very dirty and you can tell just from the front door entrance alone. The inside could use some cleaning as well. The lady serving the food looks Hispanic and appears miserable. No good customer service and each time I asked a question she seemed irritated. The Egusi was okay but the meat was very hard!!!! Like it was barely cooked. Pounded yam was big and tasted funny, not what I prepare at home.

Toyin was a complete pleasure to eat in. The staff is very friendly and ready to introduce you to authentic Nigerian cuisine. Everyone in the restaurant was Nigerian and they said this was their favorite place to go. The prices were very reasonable and you get a large helping of food. I'm not entirely sure what I ate because a nice Nigerian gentleman behind ordered for me, but it was a spicy spinach and melon seed stew with flavors I can't really compare to anything else. The fufu that you eat with it was to die for. The tilapia was also delicious. However, be aware that it is not deboned if you order it if you don't eat much fish. I can't wait to try more Nigerian food! I recommend that everyone should come and try Toyin- Nigerian Cuisine.
Looking for a beautiful environment with excellent Nigerian food, look no further than – this is the place. Don’t forget to grab a bottle of Zobo or Ginger Shot…..this completes the tasty meal 👌

formatted_address: 1161 Ridge Ave SW Suite 15, Atlanta, GA 30315, United States
name: Ruki’s Kitchen

reviews.text: The perfect blend of Ethiopia and ATL. The food was incredible with familiar menu items, but with a hint of Ethiopian culture. The location is a hidden treasure- parking was convenient with available tables to dine in and enjoy your meal. Very personable and professional- I will be back! 10/10 would recommend.

I gave him all fives for a reason. With the exception of the salmon tips being cooked fresh to order the food was damn amazing. I didn’t agree with the portion sizes for the veggie plate for the price paid but for the price of the Salmon tibs I was very pleased. I do plan to order again in person. This environment is one spot with 3different restaurants sharing a space. It’s really a very good experience to enjoy.

If you’re looking at another place just stop and go here! Rukis has a quality that many places have given up on. I had the veggie platter and my husband had the Sega tibs combo. As you can see we demolished.
Really great food! It is in a small food hall with shared dining space. You order at the counter and the girl that took our order and the owner were both so kind. We will be going back!!

Got the veggie platter which was delicious, especially the cabbage. Also appreciated the outdoor seating option.

Only request would be a fan outside to deter flies, but understand that Ruki’s is one tenant in a larger food hall so might be out of their hands.

Best place to hang out .eat  good food ,Listen to Slow Jam ,it  have private rooms you can study drink coffees everythinf is beautiful
Great place to go chill and smoke. Lovely atmosphere great customer service and very clean environment.

reviews.text: Great customer service made ordering very easy.  The beef and shrimp fried rice was so delicious and adding the shito to this dish really topped it off. I had to try the okra stew with banku, and again I was not disappointed!! They have me as a customer that will keep returning. Just wow!

My wife and I ordered some African food from MAKAY chop bar for my birthday. The food is affordable, Serving the Best of West Africa cuisine. They serve delicious food, all meals are produced from scratch, they were no pre-made food, Meals were NOT frozen.

MaKaY always make you feel “Africa” in America with their sumptuous indigenous African dishes served in the “local style.” The interesting part is MaKaY is located 10 minutes from the Atlanta airport, so if you have are flying and craving authentic Ghanaian dishes, please don’t hesitate to call. They provide quality customer service. Well done MaKaY. Looking forward to seeing MAKAY grow and change the phase of African Restaurant in America.

Best food and service I’ve had in a while, Makay delivered my food fast and fresh. I like to place bulk orders because I don’t cook a lot. And the food is great value for the money. I will definitely recommend Makay restaurant to anybody.
We tried five dishes — all outstanding.

formatted_address: 3125 Briarcliff Rd NE ste c, Atlanta, GA 30329, United States
name: Bahel Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text:
Visiting Bahel Ethiopian Restaurant is always a delight for anyone craving authentic Ethiopian cuisine. The ambiance strikes the perfect balance between cozy and vibrant, creating an inviting atmosphere that enhances the dining experience. While I don’t often frequent Ethiopian restaurants, Bahel remains my top choice whenever I do.

On a recent Saturday, my cousin and I decided to have a late breakfast, early lunch date at Bahel, and it did not disappoint. We kicked off our meal with “lentil sambusa” , paired with a hot, seasoned tea that perfectly complemented the dish. For the main course, we shared the “Veggie Combo” and “Mushroom Dulet, both of which were incredibly flavorful and satisfying.

While the Veggie Combo was a hit, I felt that the Mushroom Dulet could benefit from a touch more seasoning, perhaps adding some “Mitmita” and “Korerima “to enhance its flavor profile.

The service was another highlight of our visit. The two waiters attending to us were friendly and attentive, frequently checking in to ensure we were enjoying our meal.

Overall, Bahel Ethiopian Restaurant is a standout choice for anyone looking to indulge in authentic Ethiopian flavors, and I can't wait for my next visit!

This is my first time trying Ethiopian food. All of us enjoyed the food. The dishes are so delicious and the service is amazing. I wish I can have this everyday. I visited Atlanta from NY and I went to his restaurant twice during my 3 nights stay at GA. That's how much the food was amazing. We got the platter both times and honey wine is also a must try. Sambusa is also very good. Tomato fitfit is also very refreshing. Highly recommended this restaurant ❤️
Lots of seating available. The food was delicious and reasonably priced. The wait staff was helpful in explaining details of the various dishes.
Excellent service from Hana and Abraham! Food was five stars. Great atmosphere with indoor and outdoor seating. They even have a gift shop with souvenirs from Ethiopia.

Its a great vibe with great food. Highly recommend getting the Bahel 3 shareable plate if you're bringing a small party. Recommend getting the honey wine and their iced tea if you love cinnamon. The service is polite and friendly. You will leave happy and nourished.

This place is fantastic. The Afrobeats were hitting all night, the DJ didn’t miss, and the energy in the room was just right. The food was actually tasty (very flavorful and worth ordering). Solid drinks, good crowd, and nonstop good energy. I’ll definitely be back.

Amazing experience at Red Room Lounge! The atmosphere was upscale, energetic, and perfectly curated for a night out. Definitely a spot I’ll be returning to.

I had an amazing experience at Red Room Brisco, and I can’t recommend it enough! From the moment I arrived, the atmosphere was inviting, stylish, and perfectly set for a memorable experience. Service Jass and Lyna were outstanding, professional, attentive, and genuinely friendly. They made me feel comfortable and ensured everything went smoothly from start to finish.

The attention to detail, energy, and hospitality truly stood out. It’s clear that Red Room Brisco values quality service and customer satisfaction. Jass and Lyna went above and beyond to make my visit special, and I left feeling impressed and completely satisfied.

If you’re looking for a top-notch experience with excellent service, this is the place to go! Frfr

The manager AY and the owner were great. I arrived early for a birthday party and they took care of me. The food was delicious. I had the turkey wings. Buyer beware if you can’t handle spicy food overall had a really good time.
