reviews.text: The food was good. Makayla our server was excellent! We sat outside and even outside we could tell you guys clean with Fabuloso. That is nothing more than glorified perfume. It's not a real cleaner, and it induces migraines. The Fabuloso affects everything, from the taste of the food to the entire atmosphere. If you changed the cleaning solution you'd receive all high marks. Respectfully.

5/5 highly recommend visiting! Security was friendly & immediately after the hostess matched the great energy. We ordered calamri & a hooka with 2 peach margaritas. The calamari was seasoned to perfection and the perfect texture! breading was life! The place packed up quick & it was all good vibes! ill be backkkkl!!!!

After a busy day, we needed a night outside. We achieved just that relaxing on the patio of TCU. We made reservations to minimize wait which was on point,for we were seated upon arrival. Our waitress was poised and eager to make recommendations; alerted us that its happy hour and reviewed the food and beverage menu. Overall, this Instagram mentionable was on point. Food was delectable,and great bang for your buck. We selected VIP Parking ($40) right at entrance … the venue is in the City of Atlanta and stay open till 3 am.

The wait was a little long to get served on my visit, which was around 9pm on a Saturday night, right before it started to get really busy. The long island was okay, but the margarita was basically just syrup. The chicken kebabs were really good, and the meat for the beef suya, but the suya seasoning was lacking true suya flavor and spice. The jollof was okay. It's a decent vibe, but at that time of night and day, parking was $20, $40, or $60, depending on how close you wanted to be to the restaurant. I'd go back to try the happy hour, but that's about it.

Atmosphere was great! Our server was awesome. Only issue was that I know that the shrimp was not cleaned properly. The shrimp was not deveined at all so the digestive tract and poop was still in the shrimp. The peel was not cut to devein the shrimp. Was not a fan of the garlic butter shrimp and crab. It was basically Alfredo sauce on top of the shrimp and crab. Lamb chops were delicious though!!!

formatted_address: 1860 Memorial Dr SE Ste C, Atlanta, GA 30317, United States
name: Spice Bistro

reviews.text: Excellent beef stew and jollof (red rice). I would definitely recommend this spot for a taste of the Caribbean and West African food. For such a well established restaurant, it's a shame that there are so few reviews online. Please give it a try for yourself.

Spice Bistro truly delivered an unforgettable experience! The jerk suya was packed with bold, smoky flavor and just the right kick. The goat was fall-off-the-bone tender and seasoned to perfection. The jollof rice was rich, savory, and the perfect balance to everything on the plate. And the red snapper? Absolutely divine—crispy on the outside, juicy inside, and full of authentic spice. Every dish was a hit, and the flavors transported us straight to West Africa. Highly recommend for anyone who loves bold, flavorful food!

Service was inappropriate- I came to get a pickup order and the man working there who I don’t know named Chris asked if I had kids and then made the comment that my “hips were spread”…? Also, the side of Mac and cheese was tiny and jerk wings were salty. I use to like this place but I won’t be going back.

First time trying Spice Bistro and I was seriously impressed. The jerk goat was tender and had the perfect kick, and the jollof rice was on point—rich, comforting, and cooked just right. I also tried the red snapper, and it was cooked beautifully, not dry at all. You can tell everything was made with care. Definitely bringing friends back next time.

Spice Bistro never disappoints. I came in craving something hearty and left beyond satisfied. The suya had that perfect char and the red snapper was cooked exactly how I like it crispy edges with a soft center. The jollof rice pulled everything together and the portion was generous. It felt like a home cooked meal in the best way. Will definitely be back soon.

formatted_address: 4855 Old National Hwy Suite D, College Park, GA 30337, United States
name: Lamp Cuisine - African Restaurant College Park Georgia

html_attributions: Lamp Cuisine - African Restaurant College Park Georgia

reviews.text:
I recently had the pleasure of dining at Lamp Cuisine in College Park, Georgia, and I must say, it was an incredible experience that I feel compelled to share. From the moment I entered, the warm and inviting atmosphere made me feel right at home, and the friendly smiles from the staff set the perfect tone for the afternoon.

The menu features a fantastic selection of authentic African dishes that truly celebrate the rich and diverse culinary heritage of the continent. Each dish is crafted with care, showcasing bold flavors and unique ingredients that left a lasting impression on my palate. I enjoyed the opportunity to try a variety of items, and I was genuinely amazed by the depth of taste in every bite.
What really stood out during my visit was the exceptional service. The staff members were not only attentive but also took the time to share their knowledge and passion for the food being served. It was heartwarming to see how much they care about providing a memorable dining experience for their guests.

To top off my meal, I indulged in one of their delightful desserts, which was the perfect sweet note to conclude the afternoon. It’s clear that Lamp Cuisine is more than just a restaurant; it’s a place where culture and community come together, offering an unforgettable culinary journey.

I wholeheartedly recommend Lamp Cuisine to anyone looking to explore vibrant flavors and enjoy a warm, welcoming dining atmosphere. I can’t wait to return and discover more of their incredible offerings!

#THANKYOU🙏🏾🙌🏾😇

Absolutely beyond 5 Stars ⭐️ the food is soooo Delicious 😋 mouth watering delicious 🥰 I had the whole fish with Jollof rice and I love it. I've eaten it a lot in Minnesota, but this is my first time eating it in Atlanta and I am very satisfied and forever a customer 💕😍👌🏽👏🏽

A coworker recommended this restaurant because I told her I wanted some peanut butter stew. This spot did not disappoint at all. The stew with the jaloff rice was amazing. The portions were an enough for to have left overs. The decor is bright and cheerful.

The food was flavorful, but the service left much to be desired. The young woman at the counter didn’t acknowledge me at all, yet when a man from her own country arrived, she skipped over me to take his order first. It seems that if you’re not an African immigrant, you shouldn’t expect attentive service. In any case, the lack of cleanliness in the establishment was also disappointing.  Avoid this place!!!
Great portion sizes. I tried their bouye and mafe, both of which were delicious-I can't wait to order these again. The yassa chicken was also good.

formatted_address: 2470 Windy Hill Rd SE Suite 148, Marietta, GA 30067, United States
name: Kelosa Kitchen/Restaurant

reviews.text: Literally said they were open today Sunday online , called multiple times no response , decided to drive down 35mins to and fro , only to find out they were close. Makes no sense , update your Google opening hours to avoid customers going through this . Makes no sense , will not return to such business. Simple things like this matters .

A hidden gem of a place!! The food took me home from the pots that look like those buka pots where miracles of flavor are found, to the banana leaf on the ceramic plate and the food served on top. The portions were amazing - and the food is so good, it was hard to stop eating 😅. Definitely give Kelosa's a try - you will not be disappointed!

Kolosa's Kitchen is a must-visit for anyone seeking an authentic Nigerian meal. The delicious food, as well as fast serving time, made a great dining experience.

Whether you're a local or a visitor, this restaurant is a true gem that deserves all five stars. I cannot wait to return and try more of the menu !

Oh my gosh where do I even begin? This was such a terrible experience. I used kelosa’s kitchen for Christmas. I ordered puff puff, fried rice, jollof rice and efo and samosa and spring roll. It was only the jollof rice that anyone had anything good to say. The efo was not fresh and the fried rice was spoilt before Christmas was over. Can you imagine? And when it was being delivered I asked for FaceTime to make sure everything was good so nothing was missing and the owner refused. This entire process was horrible. Communication was the worst! I don’t recommend this company’s food for any catering service. It was my first and LAST time ordering from them. What a waste of $600.

Update:
Owner is now truly upset I left a bad review. I will boost it to a 2 but I had a terrible experience with this company. That doesn’t mean your experience might be as bad.

I stumbled upon this Cobb County gem while getting my brows done next door in February and haven't stopped going since. Everything I have gotten has been good and authentic. Just wish they were open more, but I manage to get by the as I work and live close. Everyone I have taken there, whether a seasoned Nigerian food eater or first timer has raved about it since!!

formatted_address: 2532 S Hairston Rd Suite I, Decatur, GA 30035, United States
name: Queen Vees African Cuisine

reviews.text: The food is very old and not cooked Fresh today . I understand that African food cannot be cooked the order because of the time and essence of the cuisine. But I do expect it to be cooked fresh daily.  It was obvious that this food was frozen and reheated when ordered. It taste stale, old , frozen microwaved , And the okra soup was still cold in the middle. . This was a waste of my hard Earned money I do not recommend this restaurant and I would never order from here again. I can’t see that if you catch them on the fresh day, it might be good, but I definitely was given old food today when I called and spoke with the owner she was not willing to work with me. I didn’t want her to admit that the food was old, but ask her what would be a good day for me to come back and she can remake my order because I was aware of what happened today. She was not willing to work with me or suggest a time for her to remake my order when I was letting her know that it was obvious to me, and I knew that the food was old.  I tried to support businesses in our area, But I definitely would not eat from this location ever again and do not recommend it. The food is not good quality and the cooks and owner do not have integrity for the product of they are putting out.

I had the pleasure of getting my order taken by Queen Vee herself! So sweet and she answered every question I had about the foods I wanted to try. We ended up eating at the restaurant getting the goat pepper soup, Egusi w/ fufu, jollof with chicken, plantains and Suya. The restaurant was clean and bright, bathrooms were clean as well.

The goat pepper soup had the perfect spice level and a ton of meat!

Egusi was amazing as well. Think we had goat in that one too (a ton of it)

The suya was juicy, not the drier cuts. They use purple onions with the suya that are incredibly strong for the meat, so I’d recommend them soaking the onions in a cold ice bath or using sweet white onions instead. The suya also came with a side of refreshing cucumber pieces. It was a nice treat after experiencing so many tasty spices in one sitting.

The jollof, chicken and plantains was supposed to be to go, but once we opened the container, we couldn’t help but have a little taste…but tell me why we ended up eating half the to go container IN the restaurant! Momma Tami (I believe that’s her name) came out from the back and laughed so hard at us almost finishing it before we got home.

Overall great experience! Friendly local business that has great potential to franchise if they wanted.    I felt at home here and like these were my aunties and elders. Will definitely be back!!

So I used to buy fr this restaurant and it was good so I decided to stop by yesterday to get some suya and beef stew,this food was so nasty I couldn’t even eat it. I wasted $30 on food I couldn’t even eat and on top of that there very rude. I will never go back, if you can’t afford your ingredients to make the food the proper way just don’t make food simple.Food had no taste and I love African food, Guess I will go to Tolex and the one on Hambrick rd.

Today was my first time trying this restaurant I was excited the service was good but unfortunately the food was underwhelming the egusi soup was very watery n lacked flavor the beef was the best part don’t think I’d be willing to try again but the ladies were nice n accommodating

I have never had African food. This was my first experience and the employees was so very nice. She literally did a video for me so that I could post it on my social media. Please try this restaurant. I drove all the way from Macon, Georgia just to have this.

formatted_address: 6550 Mt Zion Blvd, Morrow, GA 30260, United States
name: GOLDENCROWN KITCHEN

reviews.text: I am not african... so take this review with salt due to that. But I tried the jollof with chicken. The rice was way spicy and the chicken sorta tasted vinegary... I could only get through half of it (with tons of fluids) before I decided I had enough. I ordered a 2 for 1 special so I have an extra plate that IDK what to do with... I'll offer it to my brother and see what he thinks I guess.

Got the restaurant recommendation from my friend and trust me I decided to show up. I am not easily impressed but this food was great. I got ayamase and rice and amala and egusi. The service was great and the lady there was very polite and patient also willing to help. So far this restaurant is one of the best African restaurants in Georgia. I will be there next time. Side note, we will appreciate an increase in the meat.
Thank you

Absolutely delicious! I was too busy enjoying the food to take photos of everything 😅. The samosas were bursting with flavor, and every single dish was packed with authentic, rich taste. We tried the egusi, efo riro, samosas, and shawarma — all 10/10! The owners were incredibly kind and welcoming. This restaurant just became one of our new Sunday favorites. Highly recommend!

Ohhhhh my goodness! Out of the 6 places I've tried (African cuisine), from Atlanta to Fayetteville Ga..... This place is the absolute best HANDS DOWNNNNNNN! MY KIDS AND I ARE SO HAPPY WHEN WE COME HERE TO EAT. I truly enjoy the customer service, food quality and the family oriented atmosphere.

I really enjoy this establishment. You can tell when food is prepared with love and care. The meat pies are a staple in my home. We order them by the dozen, freeze them, and pop in the air fryer when we’re ready to eat. Sooo delicious!!

formatted_address: 1245 Veterans Memorial Hwy SW STE 50, Mableton, GA 30126, United States
name: Flames Restaurant

reviews.text:
The food is amazing!!! Came to Atlanta to renew my passport and decided to do only Nigerian food because why not?!
Before flames, I ate at 2 others and I’m not going to put them down but…
Found flames the day before my return and OMGG, it was fabulous. Abula-on point!pounded yam and efo-slick!!, pepper soup-tasty and spicy (I missed having catarrh because of pepper soup 🥹😂). Thank you!!!

I'm not new to Nigerian food, but when I say I was delighted throughout this meal. Everything was so flavorful and well balanced. We ordered meat pie, gizzard and plantains, goat and suya. They gave us nice, meaty pieces of beef for the suya that wasn't just fat. And the seasoning was immaculate. We also order jollaf rice with fish and efo with fufu. Everything was amazing! The service was great and the staff was sweet. I will definitely come back. Especially for the meat pie!

Poor customer service extremely slow and rude . Kept assisting other people instead of taking care of the customer in front of her. Waited almost 1 hour for my food . Food was cold because it was sitting out and the portions were very small compared to the price . I don’t know if I was treated badly because I’m American but that’s exactly how the lady with blonde locs made me feel. I spent over 100$ and she treated me badly .

My brother and I always come here. My brother has been eating here since the restaurant opened. It’s one of his favorite west African cuisine restaurants in Atlanta.

The food is decent and fresh thankfully
and the lady who is the owner is also very welcoming and polite.

I ordered Egusi through uber eats. Who’s ever hands made my food also holds an immense gift blessed by GOD!!!! I’ve never Inhaled food so fast! And before getting the food I’m like “ahhh I’m not that hungry just wanna try it…….” WRONG! I LICKED THE PLATE CLEAN!!!!!The amount of food was generous but not overwhelming. The flavor profile was perfect and the level of heat makes me wanna cry it’s so beautiful 😭😭😭 thank you God ! Thank you Flames Restaurant. I had the worst morning with my mom in hospital, but this healed me 🥰🥰🥰🥰

formatted_address: 5439 Memorial Dr, Stone Mountain, GA 30083, United States
name: Minas Kitchen

reviews.text: My dad’s from Liberia and introduced me to this place when I first moved to ATL and I’ve loved the food here ever since and drive long distances to get here despite ATL’s variety of choices to get similar food. The spinach and rice is to die for. And the servers are so lovely and patient! Always worth the drive from the city!

Food good, the customer service is wack after I was never greeted when I came in. I was looked at crazy like I hadn't patronize the business for many years. The women seem to only be attentive to the men customer
All the hidden prices make it feel scammish. Not fond of not knowing the prices of items.

Order the spinach and rice 10/10 so good full of flavor and the spicy pepper so good omg.
i love Liberian spinach and it was my first time tasting theirs.  taste like somebody grandma in that kitchen lol!
service wasn’t the best but the food made up for it.
will be back to get more

I visited on a Friday night. The music was really good! The vibes was nice. My freind ordered a drink that was great. She ordered lamb as well. It was spicy. The portion was small for the price as well. The meal came with fresh onion. Not sure if that's a custom side 🤢. I would definitely go back. Hope more people start to visit. They also had hookah. This definitely is the next hot spot. I will definitely go back.
Some of the best oxtails I have had in YEARS!!! Service was great the decorations were easy on the eyes and made for a laid back atmosphere. This place was hands down delicious!

formatted_address: 2857 Buford Hwy NE, Atlanta, GA 30329, United States
name: Kategna Ethiopian Cuisine

reviews.text: The presentation and taste is amazing! I really enjoyed the colorful, lentil-rich veggie platter with doro wat. Generous portions-- two of us weren't able to finish the whole thing. Service was great, we felt very welcome, and we particularly enjoyed the coffee ceremony at the end of the meal, complete with Ethiopian dishes and incense. The coffee was rich and chocolatey, and the price of everything was quite reasonable. Definitely recommend.

Ethiopian food is one of those experiences that reminds me why I love exploring cuisines. The warmth of injera, the depth of spice in every stew, and the way every dish is meant to be shared — it’s food that feels like culture, history, and hospitality all in one bite.

I came to eat here after a workout and was nervous at first because it was empty. to my surprise the food was really good and am wondering why more people arent eating here. It was my first time eating Ethiopian food and they did not disappoint. The woman who took my order was super nice and explained a bit of the menu to me. The chicken tibs with cabbage was great. my partner had the veggie platter and they really enjoyed it. When you go, you have to order the sambusas. I definitely will be coming here again.

Our favorite Ethiopian spot in town!
The food is always fresh and consistently delicious. It’s perfect for takeout, and we’ve never had trouble finding a table when dining in. We’ve been loyal fans of the salmon tibs and lamb ribs for over three years—they never disappoint. Highly recommend!

Lots of good reviews for what I do not know. The food is downright awful. It's hard to even write a review. It seems as though I purge details from my memory, as a coping mechanism. Just read the less than stellar reviews before venturing down this path.

formatted_address: 3131 Campbellton Rd SW ste n, Atlanta, GA 30311, United States
name: Atlanta Meat & Fish Market & Restaurant

reviews.text: Grilled chicken skewers and grilled beef skewers were good. Onion sauce is delicious
Do yall understand my husband drove us all the way down here, like almost an hour away to get 2 PLATES of GOAT, the ONLY GOAT he will eat is from here!! This is the absolute BEST PLACE!
There is no place like home. This is the best place for preggors food cravings. Ask about the lamb yasa, jollof rice and grilled fish
I started eating here during the pandemic I usually get the kabobs and onions with mustard , a friend turned me on to that it’s sounds nasty but is actually good

The was very good and it's pricey. They only use cash app so be aware. The food took forever to come out because they do prepare after you order. The inside does need remodeling and cleaning. The spicy level on the egusi was everything and they give you more than 2 pieces of meat inside. I was pleased with the amount of food. Jasmine rice the kids loved and the jerk chicken was good too they said. Wasn't spicy which I was concerned about. Plantains was cooked just right not burnt at all. Just call your order in ahead before coming food takes 25 to 30 mins to prepare and have cash app ready. Hope this helps someone

formatted_address: 4166 Buford Hwy NE #1120, Atlanta, GA 30345, United States
name: Abol Cafe

reviews.text: It was a nice lounge with good vibes and live music/DJ. They provide Hookah and card games which I thought was cool and the food was good as well. Our waitress was nice and attentive. The lounge was kind of small but other than that is a place to get lit at.

Really nice place. The staff are very friendly. The waitress did a wonderful job with our food. She was nice.

The place is very cozy, neat and well organized. The food is delicious.

We were visiting Atlanta for a day and my wife and I decided to try the place out. My wife from Ethiopia 🇪🇹.  And it was a great dining experience..

The staff had great customer service. Very friendly and welcoming. The food was well cooked and the salad was well seasoned. Only complained is the lamb was a little bit too salty and the food was not delivered on a timely manner. The person I went with got the food later while mine was already delivered. I personally wanted to ear once we all got served therefore the food got a little bit cold waiting. Otherwise,  great place to checkout for authentic Ethiopian cuisine.

Hole in the wall Ethiopian wall. Inside is very modern looking, there was one server who was there when I went. I got the vegetable platter and my friend got the Kornice Tibs and Shiro. The shiro was delicious. Out of the vegetable platter the red lentils were my favorite. It was very flavorful overall. I love the injera. It wasn’t too busy when I went, food came out fairly quickly. The server was really nice and checked in on us.

I’ve patronized Abol since for about 4 years now. Lately I mostly order from home, sometimes pick up and rarely dine in. My delivery orders have been okay, hence the two stars but last night I dined in with my sister to catch up and I was horrified at the entire experience.

I remember abol as cozy and busy, yet a delightful cafe. We called ahead and ordered a veggie combo, well done kitfo and fish tibs with awaze. The person taking my order didn’t get the last part so I repeated it about 4 times both in English and the native language so we have no miscommunication.

Upon arrival, it’s empty but that means a quiet dinner which was good. Some of the tables were sticky and had used napkins so we sat at the cleanest one. Our food shortly comes out and in place of the fish tibs I reiterated was meat firfir, and the kitfo was rare. We send a portion of the kitfo back to be fully cooked and keep the firfir as we’re starving and don’t want to wait for the fish tibs to be made from scratch. 5 minutes into dining a few fruit flies appear, and 15 minutes later, there were so many swarming we were swatting fruit flies off of our faces with one hand while eating the other. Soon it became unappetizing and we had to take our food to go. Our waitress who is the only one appears to be manning the register and who was literally directly staring at us the entire time never once checked on us/the food or asked about our obvious discomfort of the flies.. nor to accommodate us better. The food wasn’t disappointing but it wasn’t great either, or so we thought. This morning we are both experiencing stomach related issues to say the least. We don’t live together nor share the same meals so that was the common factor in both our illness. Overall, the only redeeming quality was the mediocre veggie combo and kitfo which were all obviously contaminated. I hope management would put efforts into returning abol to the great, clean quality cafe it used to be. While the exterior renovations are nice, service and hygiene received an F last night. The photos I’ve attached is showing the first fruit fly that appeared while my sister went to wash her hands. If google would allow Live Photos you’d see them in action too.

formatted_address: 2263 Cheshire Bridge Rd NE, Atlanta, GA 30324, United States
name: Blu Lagoon Bar and Bistro

reviews.text: Terrible place, they have no chairs at the bar after 12, the stud Manager is very rude and unprofessional. The bartenders do not know how to make drinks, it's literally juice with a pinch of liquor. Please chose somewhere else to go, no wonder it's empty and filled with just workers.

As a first time customer, I’m highly dissatisfied and disappointed. The lines are not only long but there’s no seating for people who aren’t purchasing a section. Not to mention, the night before we attempted to purchase one, but the system kept giving a network error. Unbeknownst to us, we were actually charged. 322.25 to be exact. We came back hoping to get it rectified and better service, but we were treated even worse. We spent well over $100 in drinks in addition to $20 parking for 3 cars. The management kept coming thru the crowd pushing us even tho we didn’t have a secure place to actually enjoy ourselves. The waitresses were rude and disrespectful and the first thing I usually notice is a smile. They just frowned and yelled the entire time. I’m from the other side of the tracks, but I kept my composure. Instead of mgmt antagonizing his guests, he should’ve been asking us paying patrons how he can make our services better. Disgusting. I will never return and as a top rater I’d hope to see some improvements.

Visit date: 7/17/22, Sunday night/Monday morning. I enjoyed coming here. We arrived around 12am, party of 6. They sat us promptly. But I suggest you get here early if you don’t want to wait to be seated, because it got very busy within an hour of us being there. There were only two servers at the time and they did their best. The service was pretty good. Pictured is a rum punch which was very good! 10/10. The tables are a little tight to sit at if you have a larger party but the server was able to move us to a more spacious one. They have hookah here. They have a DJ that plays great music! Afrobeats, reggae, hip-hop, old school R&B vibes. They serve food here too but we did not order any because we had just eaten somewhere else. The bathrooms are clean. I paid $24 for two rum punches, so I’d say that is pretty fair. I’m from Charlotte and there is a lack of places with this vibe. I would definitely go back here when I visit Atlanta again. Enjoy!
Food was average, but the ambiance was dope. The waiter was on point. Would not mind going back. Fun times!

Wings were big and rubbery, jerk sauce wasn’t giving jerk… for some reason my server gave me my food in a to go box even though we have a whole section/table and are dining in. $12 for this baby lemon drop. Do not recommend

formatted_address: 1783 meadow lane sw, 590 ponce de Leon Avenue NE, Atlanta, GA 30315, United States
name: Deem Foods

reviews.text:
I recently had the pleasure of trying pepper soup from Deem foods, and it was an absolute delight. From the very first spoonful, I was transported by the rich, aromatic flavors that are so characteristic of traditional African cuisine. The soup was perfectly seasoned, with a harmonious blend of spices that warmed me from the inside out. The ingredients were clearly fresh, adding layers of depth and texture that made each bite more satisfying than the last. It’s rare to find a pepper soup made with such care and authenticity outside of Africa itself.
Deem Foods has mastered the art of bringing the essence of Africa to your table.

Highly recommended for anyone looking to explore the vibrant tastes of African cuisine in Atlanta.

My big sister, nephew, and I had the pleasure of trying the Amala, Gbegiri & Ewedu dish with orishirishi at DeemFoods yesterday, and it was absolutely delightful! The flavors were rich and authentic, with the perfect balance of texture from the Amala and the tenderness of the proteins. The Gbegiri & Ewedu soup added a wonderful depth to the meal. I was impressed by the generous portion size and the warm, welcoming service. Overall, it was a truly satisfying and delicious experience! I posted about it on Snapchat, and all my friends here in Atlanta and other cities/countries were impressed, commenting 'damn!' I can't wait to go back for more! It was yummy, and I'm checking if I can add pictures. By the way, my nephew had pasta with minced meat, and he was singing and asking if we could order again today!   ( faces covered) 😂
Today I got the goat pepper soup it was absolutely delicious!  Ola is so nice and her customer service is top tier.  Hands down prepared from the soul.

Deem Foods brings a taste of Nigeria right to Atlanta! My experience at this culinary treasure was simply outstanding. The flavors of each dish transported me back to the streets of Lagos, with authentic spices and ingredients that truly captured the essence of Nigerian cuisine. I highly recommend trying their signature dishes,you wont be disappointed….

Discovering Deem Foods was like finding a hidden gem for anyone who loves or is curious about African cuisine. This store is a treasure trove of African foodstuffs, offering an incredible variety of ingredients that are essential for authentic African cooking.

From the moment I walked in, I was struck by the rich array of spices, grains, and flours that are hard to come by elsewhere. The store stocks everything from yams, plantains, and goatmeats to exotic spices and seasonings that are the heart and soul of African dishes. Their selection of dried fish, meats is equally impressive, catering to all the needs of traditional African cooking.

What truly sets Deem Foods apart is the quality of their products. Everything feels fresh and is beautifully presented, making it easy to find what you need. Deola deserves a special mention for her friendliness and expertise. I highly recommended for the quality of their products and the warmth of their service, Deem Foods is a beacon for all lovers of African cuisine.

formatted_address: 2440 Piedmont Rd NE, Atlanta, GA 30344, United States
name: Tatso Peri Peri Grilled Chicken

reviews.text: Listen this food is so good I was nervous at first because I could find the place. It’s beside Dunkin Donuts in the building that says Uptown Taste. He has a small area set up to the left of the restaurant. You can tell they had the meat marinated, it’s full of flavor the cabbage cooked good. Bringing South African flavors to the A. I will be back. His customer service is amazing and supporting small businesses it’s what’s it’s about. See you soon! Happy Customer.

We had this at Sceptre Brewing in Atlanta. The brewery has a ghost kitchen and they were the flavor of the week. I could tell they were working hard, but struggled with efficiency. Orders were taking way too long for grilled chicken with sides.

I got the chicken tender dish. My chicken was dry and not very flavorful. It could use some better seasoning. I didn’t really enjoy
the sauces. I had the hot and lemon herb. I ended up using Chick-fil-a sauce at home. The mac and cheese wasn’t very cheesy. The rice was about the only good thing we had. The baked beans were okay.

I ordered on Uber eats. It was so good I had to let everyone know on here. Omg. The entire chicken was flavorful and moist, not just the skin. The macaroni and cheese was creamy. The baked beans were so tasty. Easily one of the best tasting restaurants I've had in Atlanta. I swear it.

Food was absolutely delicious! So glad they brought peri peri chicken to Atlanta! I’ll definitely be a frequent customer. Also, the staff was very quick and efficient. The lockers they have to pick up your order are a great idea as well. Overall, great experience!

This is, by far, the best chicken I've had in all of Atlanta.

I've had nandos in the US and the UK.... And this is better. Incredible wings, incredible food.

Please open before 9:30 - you will have weekly orders from us.

formatted_address: 4813 Old National Hwy, College Park, GA 30337, United States
name: Olyzubby's Kitchen

reviews.text: Ordered from Doordash... The food was excellent don't get me wrong, but I ordered the Egusi Soup with pounded yam... The dish allowed me to select 3 meats... I ordered goat, beef and cow's foot... Since I'm new to Nigerian/African cuisine.. I'm not sure if the goat or cows feet was missing... I've attached photos... The bones on the plate were laid how they were found inside the food... All I did was suck the soup off of it... Whatever bones you see is exactly what they had into the soup... NO MEAT!!! I did get two pieces of the 3 meat Egusi soup... They also had fish bones in the soup... I'm not sure if it's supposed to be cooked with fish bones or they decided to give me whatever meat they felt like I should've had... Again, the food is tasty though... If they are going to serve you the soup how they want you to have it, they shouldn't give an option on the meat choices... It defeats the point and you will constantly received alot of negative feedback around that one topic... If they would have gotten the right meats I would've gave 5 stars... Price is a little expensive. Can go to another place (Riverdale Rd) for a cheaper option with the same quality if not better. Meaning, you can actually get the meat selections you've chose as well as a bigger portion that would make you full without all the fufu. But if you're really feaning (nearby) and don't want to drive, and you want the food like "right now".... This place is not bad. Not bad at all.

Great place to get Nigerian food ! Located close to ATL airport. My new stop every time I land in Atlanta. The owner is great , good conversation and the food is amazing. I ordered Jollof rice and Suya.

Food quality is superb. Each meal is cooked to order, so if you’re in a rush call ahead. The quantity is small for the price, especially in comparison with other places. I order here at least twice a month. Pictured is the ogbono soup (fish, cow foot & tripe) with fufu (pounded yam)

I’ve been two Georgia a few times & always looking to try something new. I’ve been wanting to try this dish for a while which was the fufu with the okro soup and goat meat. Let me tell you it was one of the best food I’ve tasted in a long time. A lil on the high side but definitely worth it!. When I come back to Georgia I will definitely be eating at this place again!.

Kids watched TikTok and requested to try FuFu we landed at this place which came highly recommended. I really enjoyed the food it was made fresh and delicious... if you are unsure what to get I suggest the meat of your choice with pounded yam & egusi soup. $20 a plate but worth it!

formatted_address: 800 Forrest St NW, Atlanta, GA 30318, United States
name: Afic

reviews.text: highly recommend their authentic dishes, top-notch service, and cozy atmosphere. a must-visit spot in atlanta!

What a delightful experience ordering from African Tender! The Jollof rice with chicken I got for takeout was nothing short of phenomenal. Perfectly seasoned, rich in flavor, and the chicken was tender and juicy. African Tender truly knows how to deliver an authentic and memorable taste. Highly recommended for anyone craving a top-notch African dish. Will be back for more soon!
My turkey wing was cold as ice when I bit it. Definitely NOT fresh. Will never order here again. The oxtail was decent. 👎
Food not as described. I ordered goat meat pepper soup however I got boiled meat water stock and no pepper. It didn’t taste good at all. Waste of money
First time trying fufu. I thought it was good but my husband didn't. The tofu is spicy.

formatted_address: 357 Edgewood Ave SE, Atlanta, GA 30312, United States
name: Miss Conduck

reviews.text: My friend and I went just to hang out and found this diamond in the rough! This restaurant is amazing. The atmosphere is upscale yet comfortable. We felt so welcomed by the owners Emily and Latoya. Our server Angel took good care of us. The food was delicious. You MUST get the doubles!!!

Miss Conduck Caribbean restaurant is an absolute gem! We decided to book my father’s 80th birthday party as a private dinner experience and it was so incredible. Our family will forever have such a wonderful memory of this moment. The ambiance was amazing and the service was perfect. The food was cooked with so much love, we asked for the chef to come out and everyone applauded her. The evening was like being in the Caribbean and being served by loving family members. The hostess took our parties picture at the end of the night, it was truly a beautiful celebration for my father. We are so glad we booked this restaurant and we will definitely be booking them again if we have another event in Atlanta. Thank you so much to everyone at Miss Conduck!

Miss Conduck in Atlanta (357 Edgewood Ave SE, Atlanta, GA 30312) is my new favorite spot for authentic Caribbean flavor! We celebrated my Inlaws' 80th birthday at Miss Conduck, and they pulled out all the stops for us (party of 26 people). The atmosphere is vibrant and welcoming, making you feel right at home the second you walk in. Men! I don't even know which dish to recommend because everything was so good. Okay, absolutely try their Jerk Chicken. it’s perfectly seasoned and falls right off the bone. Not a meat person, try the  grilled salon; it’s cooked to perfection. The menu includes Brown Stew Oxtail, Curry Goat, Roti just to name a few.  Every dish tastes fresh and prepared with love. Miss Conduck is a true taste of the islands right here in Georgia. If you crave spicy, savory, and soulful Caribbean food, Miss Conduck is your place! Thank you all so very much!!

My husband made a good choice selecting Miss Conduck for our anniversary dinner! From beginning to end it was a 5 star experience. From the Caribbean inspired ambiance and decor, to the apps (we had the delicious doubles and jerk chicken egg rolls), the drinks, and the entrees (Rasta pasta with oxtail and the curry goat), you can tell they were cooked with love! The icing on the cake: they played Tony! Toni! Toné!’s “Anniversary” throughout the restaurant and provided complimentary glasses of champagne for us to end the night with a toast. ❤️❤️ Beautiful experience and we will definitely be back!

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐ – Absolutely Delicious Trinidadian Food!

We had the pleasure of dining at Ms. Conduck (a Trinidadian restaurant in Atlanta), and everything was absolutely amazing! I ordered the curry goat roti, and it was out of this world — the roti skin was soft, fluffy, and so fresh. I even reheated it twice (because the portion was generous), and it still tasted incredible — and anyone who loves roti knows that’s rare!

One of my girlfriends had the jerk chicken with rice and peas and callaloo, and I also tried some of the callaloo — so flavorful and perfectly seasoned. My bestie had the curry chicken with veggies and rice and peas, and she loved every bite.

The drinks were great, the food was superb, and the overall experience was wonderful. The next time we’re in ATL, we’ll definitely be coming back — and recommending Ms. Conduck to everyone we know.

Everything was a perfect 5 out of 5 — delicious, authentic, and unforgettable!

formatted_address: 3096 N Decatur Rd, Scottdale, GA 30079, United States
name: Piassa Restaurant & Mart

reviews.text: Yummy food, very nice Ethiopian restaurant, incorporate culture, history, and entertainment. Very nice service. Thank you, we had a great time.

This Ethiopian food blew my tastebud’s mind! I didn’t know such flavors existed! I ordered the “Chef’s Special” and was very satisfied. I had no idea what to get at first but this was the perfect combination of flavors. I was transported to a whole new country simply by eating this food. Next time I will bring the whole family! Thank you! ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

I love Piassa! I come here once every couple months with friends or family to order the Veggie Platter and the Lamb Tibs (the lamb is always charred so perfectly). This restaurant was my first introduction to Ethiopian food four years ago, and so far, no restaurant has topped it. Also, one of the waiters called me beautiful when I was picking up food and I don’t think I’ve ever received a more sincere compliment. The vibe is awesome and it always smells fabulous inside. Order the coffee for lunch and the honey wine for dinner.

If you're looking for authentic Ethiopian food then this is the spot. It helps to go with someone that knows how to order or is possibly Ethiopian but normal everyday people can figure the menu out for sure. Also they have helpful staff. The outside of the building is a little sketchy but sometimes those are some of the best places.   The inside looks like a little village and had a cool vibe.  The food was served in a unique way and the seating was nice and private.   We would like to explore the menu more on a return visit. I would also mention that the pricing was very good for the amount of food that you get.

Excellent service and food.
The owner put his heart and soul into this place to make sure everyone is well taken care of. Highly recommended!

formatted_address: 556 A Northside Dr SW, Atlanta, GA 30310, United States
name: Deola Cuisines. a.k.a. SS Express

reviews.text: Uber eats order: OLD FISHERMAN SOUP! Mushy crab hard fish. Very dangerous to serve. Please get rid of which ever one of those cooks that do  not care about the food they serve to people because I ordered The fisherman stew twice. The first time is what made me order it again. It was so delicious although it was spicy the second time it was not the same at all. I don’t see how fish can be tough. Also, my order took forever to get here it was two hours so obviously it was overcooked. I don’t want to take the chance again bad food although the first time it was delicious. Also the second time it was too spicy to eat and no snails. $40 is to much to pay to take a chance between good and horrible. I was afraid to get sick and threw it out.

I will NEVER come here again. I’m honestly really disappointed that I can’t get a refund on this horrible food. My food didn’t even fill the entire container, it was like 45% filled. The goat meat I ordered was sooooooo tough. I couldn’t even eat half of it, and it was full of bones and tough meat. The flavor wasn’t there either and looked absolutely nothing like the photos they show online. I literally had to ask them for the red sauce that’s pictured on their website. Please stay far away from this place if you care about not wasting money.

I ordered the chicken salad from SS Express All African & Halal Food, and it completely exceeded my expectations. The chicken was perfectly seasoned and grilled & juicy, flavorful, and tender. The salad itself was super fresh, with crisp lettuce, cucumbers, tomatoes, and a light, tasty dressing that pulled everything together. It was a great portion size, satisfying but not too heavy. You can tell they care about quality and flavor. Definitely one of the best halal salads I've had in the area—I'll be back for more.

I’m giving this restaurant 2 stars only because the person I spoke with on the phone was very polite. The food itself was terrible. I ordered Amala with Ewedu, Asun Jollof, and Ewa Goyin with Agege bread. The only thing worth mentioning was the Ewa Goyin. The Asun Jollof didn’t taste authentic at all, and the Amala with Ewedu was the worst. The ponmo was as strong as a rubber. My  first time here and definitely my last — wasted almost $100.

The okra was watery and was not properly cooked , not worth the amount I paid . Every time I take a chance to buy okra stew from this restaurant, it is always disgustingly made .This time the okra was not even chopped as it was supposed to be and the taste was so nasty . I will never purchase food from this restaurant again , I will make sure my friends do not buy from them again .

formatted_address: 1133 Huff Rd NW #D, Atlanta, GA 30318, United States
name: Twisted Soul Cookhouse & Pours

reviews.text: Quaint with a wisp of elevated elegance. From its art adorned walls to the twists on traditional southern dining, this is a wonderful contemporary restaurant.  The staff is attentive and Chaz was both friendly and polite.  The manager Keisha, (I hope I spelled her name correctly) added to the experience with engaging conversation about the restaurant. They truly want you to be pleased with the service and the food. The collard green rolls are exceptional as well as the fried chicken that's fried to crispy perfection. Even the bread basket has several variances that go well with any entrée. I would highly recommend and I will be returning. Thank you Keisha, Chaz and the staff of Twisted Soul.

We are in town for Women Evolved and wanted to try a locate spot.  Saw this place on Google and wanted to give it a try.  We were greeted as we came in and loved the atmosphere.  The staff was super helpful and explained the menu.  I had the fried chicken, and my friend has the steak.  The food was amazing.  Very delicious and serving are very generous.  We did try dessert, the peach cobbler and strawberry pound cake.  Both were tasty.  I would definitely recommend this restaurant.

Made a reservation for four on Saturday at 11am with the wife a our friends. Reservation was t needed as we were the only ones there for a while. We were sat promptly and our server was attentive and food was delivered quickly.

We shared the 'Bread Service Basket' and it was a good, tasty selection. Also had the 'Smoked Salmon Eggroles' which I didn't partake in. Friends seemed to like them, wife, not so much.

Wife had the  'Hoisin Oxtails' which were strangely missing the bok choi. Needless to say she didn't enjoy her meal at all. She couldn't put her finger on it but she didn't like it.

Friends seemed to like their 'Southern Marinated Fried Chicken' and 'Dirty South Fried Chicken Omelette' well enough though our friend did not finish her fried chicken.

I had the 'Steak And Eggs' which were good but not worth the $40 price tag, more than the menu online for some reason.

Overall decent spot to eat some soul food but won't be back for brunch. Kinda pricey for what you're getting in my opinion. We might try some dinner fare but we're hardly pressed to come back.

This place is in my neighborhood and I've driven pass so many days. Well tonight we went in and no regrets. Food,  service and atmosphere were awesome. We ordered the fried chicken, salmon rolls, bread package, collard rolls and Mac and cheese. Yummy 10 out of 10.

Black owned.
We walked in and were instantly greeted by the host and sat immediately. The decor was a mix of industrial chic, really vibes. Our server, Cierra, came and greeted us warmly. She went over special drinks and described the start of Twisted Soul and how the founder was a flight attendant for 30+ years and experienced many cultures and decided to share her experiences via food with a soul twist.
We ordered drinks and apps and Cierra brought out a bread basket--literally the best bread basket I've experienced. No butter or anything required.
We order the wings as an app and they were so good we order two more portions lol
For my meal I had their version of a fried chicken sandwich and it was delectable as expected but I couldn't finish it due to filling up on the bread basket and apps.
I really can't say enough about the food, I could go into what my friends ordered but the moral of all of their stories is that EVERYTHING was literally good. We will be back.

formatted_address: 822 Marietta St NW, Atlanta, GA 30318, United States
name: Virgil's Gullah Kitchen & Bar West Midtown

reviews.text: Finally made it to Virgil’s Gullah Kitchen, and the wait was absolutely worth it. We started with the jumbo shrimp appetizer—six large shrimp, plenty to share, and the sauce was incredible. I had the fried seafood platter with oysters, a very tasty crab cake, and catfish, plus red rice that was cooked perfectly. My friend ordered the chicken wings with a great sauce, along with collard greens and candied yams, and everything was excellent. Free parking, a really good overall experience. Our server, Xavier, did an outstanding job—especially impressive for his first day. Very attentive. They also offer a military discount, so I highly recommend this restaurant.

First impression visit at 5:30PM on a sunday.

Large black and white sign with a large front patio and balcony.  Located in a suite next to Paloma.

There is a parking lot right next door. Not sure if you have to pay- I did not and my car was fine.

We got the deviled crab eggs, fried green ma'tis, afta church plate, smoth'ad poke chop, geechee pasta, fried fish, and the slammin salmon. An appitizer, two entrees, and 2 non-alcoholic drinks cost about $100.00 with tip.

Pros
Great food and great service. The food was hot, fresh, and seasoned to perfection.
The restaurant  was able to accomdate my large party with alternative seating due to the loud music being played. I appreciate them acknowledging the problem and doing their best to help solve the issue.

Cons
As stated before, the music is very loud. Especially upstairs. This is not a chill dinner spot for family. More of a turn up spot with friends.

Would I Recommend: Yes, as a spot with music and good food. Not a spot for conversation.

I had the pleasure of having Cali as my server to celebrate my birthday on 1/11/26 and he was awesome. The food was great. The dj was so on point and even though it was brunch everyone was having a great time. The only thing was that it was so cold in there. We sat upstairs and it was hard to enjoy the food bc of the temperature. Upstairs or downstairs it was cold. I had the slammen Samon and it was amazing. Thank you Cali.

8/10/25 We were a group of 9 and it was after 9pm on a Sunday night. We were seated quickly and the waitress came immediately when we were seated to take our drink order. We the ambiance is a bar atmosphere that openly allow smoking and drinking therefore I would not recommend for parties with children. The music was very loud and somewhat vulgar. In our party we did have kids and only stayed because we were visiting from Chicago and didn’t have any other meal options for this time of night. Lets get to the food!!! We ordered the 2 after church plates, 1 smothered chicken dinner, 1?flounder and grits, 2 Jamin wings, corn muffins, the pasta with shrimp a side of macaroni and 3 extra wings. For this hour of the night and so close to closing (11pm)the food was surprisingly hot! The food presentation was nicely done. The fried chicken was nice and crispy, though not enough sauce for anyone in the party and it lacked flavorful seasoning. The collared greens were too salty for everyone and the sweet potato were not sweet to anyone although they had brown sugar sprinkled on top. The macaroni and cheese was dry and tasteless. The flounder and grits were delicious. The flounder was a nice portion size, light and crispy. The smother chicken was well seasoned and tender and the gravy with jasmine rice was good as well. The cabbage was a little tough and greasy but still enjoyable. The corn muffins were sweet and delicious and I loved the drizzle on them. The pasta and shrimp was hands down delicious! The shrimp were huge and the creaminess was perfect. The sweet tea was very sweet, the first glass of coke was weak and flat however the refills were on point. The bill for 7 entrees a side of mac and cheese, three wings and corn muffins came out to $277 which included an automatic 20% gratuity. I have to say that although I wasn’t over the moon in love with all of the food I would revisit this establishment at an earlier time and because the staff was good. I also would recommend this place because I think the good out weighs the bad.

Can get kind of loud. I attend after church and it was also SpelHouse Homecoming, so there was a little wait but no more than 20 mins. Food was seasoned good. The drinks definitely Hit, the DJ was doing her thang. I can't complain one bit. Came after my kids baptism, sat on the balcony on a great warm Sunday October. I have not one complaint. Looking forward to visiting the College Park Main Street location next.

formatted_address: 907 Marietta St NW, Atlanta, GA 30318, United States
name: Rock Steady - Atlanta

reviews.text:
I dined at RockSteady on Tuesday and had an amazing experience, thanks to my server, Lamar. From the moment I sat down, his personality was warm, genuine, and welcoming. Even though I already knew what I came in planning to order, Lamar was extremely knowledgeable about the menu and took the time to explain different options and make thoughtful suggestions.

He encouraged me to try something new, and I am so glad I trusted his recommendation because it was absolutely delicious. Throughout my meal, he was attentive, kind, and made sure everything was perfect without ever feeling rushed or overlooked. His energy and professionalism truly enhanced my dining experience.

Lamar clearly takes pride in his work, and it shows in the level of service he provides. Experiences like this are what make people want to return. I will definitely be back and hope to be served by him again.

We came out to Rock Steady to reconnect with friends we hadn’t seen in years, and this place turned out to be the perfect setting for it! The music was a great vibe and at just the right volume good enough to enjoy but still low enough for real conversation.

Our waiter, Lamar, was absolutely amazing attentive, funny, and very knowledgeable about the menu. He gave great recommendations that did not miss! I ordered the lamb chops and the Dem Suga alcoholic beverage. The lamb chops were a 9/10, but the drink was about a 4/10 for me.

Since my friends and I love to share, I also got to try:
•	Jerk Lamb Egg Rolls – 9/10
•	Empanadas – 7/10
•	Veggie Pasta – 10/10
•	Fire Shrimp – 10/10
•	Jerk Chicken – 10000/10000!!!! (the clear favorite at the table!)

For dessert, we shared the Rum Cake and Apple Pie, and let’s just say… ALL THE DESSERTS were 10000/10000!!

Overall, the food, the service, and the vibe were all on point. Definitely give this place a try—you won’t be disappointed!

Rock Steady has become one of my go-to spots in Atlanta. I’ve brought multiple friends here over the last few months — everything from casual nights out with lady friends, to business associates, and even my mom when she was visiting (and she’s notoriously picky). Every single person I’ve brought has loved the food, the music, and the vibes.

The ambience is classy — people usually dress up a bit, and upstairs they’ve got a lounge that can double as a chic night club on some evenings. Always a great energy with the perfect soundtrack in the background.

Service is consistently top notch. Lamar has helped me several times and is always professional and personable. On this visit, Rebecca the manager went above and beyond to make sure I was taken care of — when the kitchen skimped me a bit, she immediately made it right by sending out more oxtail and ensuring I left happy. That type of attention to detail is why I keep coming back.

Speaking of food, my favorite dish here (hands down) is the Oxtail Rigatoni (pictured). It’s rich, flavorful, and easily one of the best pasta entrees in the city.

If you’re looking for a place that blends great food, attentive service, and a sophisticated vibe, Rock Steady is it.

I went with a couple of friends and we had the best experience. We had a 7 o'clock reservation and were seated shortly thereafter. Our server, Vaughn was outstanding. He made great suggestions and was very knowledgeable about the menu. We each had the Curry Alfredo pasta with the Corvina fish and the bread pudding for dessert. Oh my goodness, it was great. When you go, ask for Vaughn, you won't be disappointed, he has the best customer service. The only downside is I wouldn't suggest it for a first date because the music is a bit loud.

Lamar was amazing! Loved his suggestions for drinks and entrees and he’s not bad to look at either. lol. Enjoyed ourselves tremendously! We had the lamb eggrolls, lamb chops, catfish , oxtail rigatoni, and rum cake. Delicious!  The drinks! dem sugar, hit!

formatted_address: 568 Poole Pl SW, Atlanta, GA 30310, United States
name: World Taste Atlanta

reviews.text: Came to after hours around 3:30 crowd was just showing up the vibes was good . Ordered they Fufu taco 10/10 hookah was $45 it lasted all night. Definitely a place to vibe & eat at on a Thursday

I really  enjoyed  my meal! The burger  was amazing  so worth  it! Loved the awesome  fufu tacos. And guess  what? Both dishes were  vegan! They have African  dishes that everyone  would love. My food wasn't  hot but very flavorful.   The place  is beautiful  inside.

The owner  Joe was  super accommodating. The chef is top notch and is so creative.  The food is fresh and handcrafted.
The food was very flavorful, it was my first time going and I can see myself eating there often. They also had great customer service.
Good spot to eat and see events with good music. My favorite thing to eat there is the palm butter wings!! Their rice is also bomb!!!

Disgusting experience and horrible customer service! Me and my lady were hungry after hours on a Thursday night, so we decided to give Taste a try. First off, we parked across the street because they were charging $40 to park in an empty parking lot, we explained that we were not going there to party, just to grab some food, they had no understanding. Secondly, we walk to the door and they charged us $60($40 men/$20women) to get into a practically empty venue, mind you we were just going there to eat. It was late and we were hungry so we went in. We go inside and we were not greeted by anyone, so we find a waitress and ask for a menu, she tells us that a menu is not necessary tonight because they only had wings and fries. So my lady decided to order the only thing that they had to offer, mind you, I was over it at that point so I didn’t order. I asked the waitress what was the tab and she told us $30 for 1 order of Wings and fries. Me and my lady looked at each other and walked out of the door. So basically we would have paid $90 for one order of wings and fries, no drinks included or anything, on top of the fact that they were rude and unwelcoming. I would not recommend this place to an enemy. It wasn’t about the money, but morally it was a horrible experience and we both walked out of the door feeling disappointed and disrespected. I do Not Recommend!

formatted_address: 4457 Cavitt Mill Ct, Ellenwood, GA 30294, United States
name: MAKAY AFRICAN KITCHEN CATERING . PRE ORDER IN 1/2 PAN, FULL PAN & BIG BOWLS ONLY

html_attributions: MAKAY AFRICAN KITCHEN CATERING . PRE ORDER IN 1/2 PAN, FULL PAN & BIG BOWLS ONLY

reviews.text: Excellent experience with MAKAY African Kitchen Catering. The food was flavorful, well seasoned, and very satisfying. Everything was prepared professionally and packaged neatly. You can really taste the authenticity in every bite. Great customer service and consistent quality. I would definitely order again and recommend to others.

"Amazing and super delicious ! "

Makay catered my graduation party. The food was delicious and the catering setup was magnificent. Very professional team, we specifically worked with Paulus Ackah who was amazing!

Excellent food and service from Makay African Kitchen. Food was delivered on time, and definitely good value for the money. Delicious dishes all around. What can I say about those yam balls? Delicious! Thanks Paulus, more orders coming your way.

Service and food from Makay African Kitchen was great. They set clear and concise pick up times, and food was prepared to my specifications with minimal spice & pepper. Both the palm nut soup and okra soup were exquisite and delicious. A beautiful delight indeed. I’ll be back for more 💥💥💥🦾🦾🦾🦅🦅🦅☺️☺️☺️

Makay has saved me a lot of meal prep hours and I’m able to concentrate on the things that matter the most. Without exaggerating, their meals will leave you salivating and wanting more. I live in a different state hence I was skeptical about shipping food but the packaging is second to none and the food arrives intact.

formatted_address: 2044 Teal Cove, Lithonia, GA 30058, United States
name: A.Y CUISINE: Food Delivery and Catering Services

html_attributions: A.Y CUISINE: Food Delivery and Catering Services

reviews.text: I ordered egusi, fufu, and plantains. I am vegan and my order was amazing. Thank you for offering delicious vegan options! It was hot and freshly delivered. The customer service is impeccable! May God continue to bless this establishment abundantly!
The food absolutely delicious! I had the jollof rice with beef gravy and plantains. My first time eating Nigerian jollof and it didn't disappoint! You have earned a new customer!

A.Y Cuisine was in our city for the weekend and I ordered takeout dinners for delivery. The meals came in their individual packages and different bags which made it so easy to sort. The food was fresh, delicious and the portions are big enough to satisfy. Thank you A.Y I will definitely order again.

The food was very tasty it had the right amount of flavor, and spice to it very homely. The pastries (meatpie, puffpuff, chinchin etc) were soulful reminds me of the Nigerian made one's I had save my lunch money up for to buy when I was younger😊😊. My overall experience with A.Y. Cuisine with her customer service, food presentation and delivery has been topnotch and I'm always proud when my referral to her come back with great satisfactory feedbacks. Well done!!!

Didn't get my order in on time. You have to preorder a day ahead. Made call and person I spoke with very pleasant and explained ordering process. If you want something fast and convenient I don't recommend However home cook meals are always worth the wait. Will order next time I'm in town. Be Blessed!

formatted_address: 5775 Jimmy Carter Blvd #160, Norcross, GA 30071, United States
name: Fufu Catering Kitchen and Grill

reviews.text:
I’ve been coming here since they’ve open and I have nothing but good things to say . Fufu Kitchen & Grill never misses! The food is always fresh, flavorful, and cooked to perfection. The fufu is smooth, the soups are rich and well-seasoned, and the portions are generous. You can really tell everything is made with care and authentic flavors.
The staff is friendly and welcoming, and the service is quick even when they’re busy. If you’re looking for real, comforting African food that tastes homemade, this is the place to go. Highly recommend. The owner is always so nice , she’s either giving some advice or free food lol . I’ll be back
Me and husband ordered egusi. Bad experience, extremely too oily! bad odor from food like it wasn’t fresh to order, plaintain weren’t ripe very hard and unsweetened. Pure waste of money.

Absolutely amazing service. The food was fresh, tasty, and beautifully presented. My guests couldn’t stop talking about the jollof rice and grilled chicken. Everything was delivered right on time and professionally handled. I’ll definitely book again for my next event

I went on Saturday to try their chicken egusi and fufu for the first time. It was bland (no seasoning)  and the chicken didn’t seem cook enough and it was too much bone in it for it to be a soup if I’m being honest. My husband tried the beef suya and jollof rice. He ate it but the beef was tough and the rice was dry. The service was good though. The waiters weee friendly. I just wouldn’t go back.

Came here wanting to try African food (especially fufu) cause I've never had it before. I think this may be more west African cuisine. The server and even another customer were super friendly in helping us choose what to eat. We got to try some samples for free to pick the dishes we ended up buying.

I was able to get the egunsi soup combo ($21.99) split with the spinach, it also would've came with a meat but we decided to get the yam porridge cause we liked the sample. This came with a fufu. Fufu was super interesting as the texture was a bit slimy. I liked it though and tried it with everything and it tasted good with everything.

Also got the ayamashe ($22.99) which had beef and fish, also came with an egg. It was quite spicy. I got sweaty eating it. The plantains were so soft and sweet.

They even have a bar where you can have a cocktail which I thought was cool. The music playing was good as well.

Hands down the best Ghanaian food I’ve had in the area. Makay African Food Catering never disappoints, the flavors are rich, the portions are generous, and the menu has all the Ghanaian favorites. You can really tell the food is cooked with care. I always recommend them to anyone looking for real African food.

I usually don’t write reviews but this was worth taking time to do. I booked Makay African food catering for my 40th birthday party. They arrived two hours before the ceremony to set. reviews.text: Walked in randomly after I saw this place on Google Maps. Got the assorted meats, egusi soup with goat, and fufu. Everything was delicious and I’m grateful they were open! I’d say worth the price for  an authentic meal.

As a Yoruba man, I highly recommend this place. I was skeptical initially but after trying the food, I changed my mind and ever since then, I’ve kept going back for more. The food is on point! 😄

The food portion is also very reasonable. It’s more, compared to other spots I’ve tried in Atlanta. Even in downtown Atlanta. It tastes better and the portions are bigger. I think this is her competitive advantage.

One last thing, make sure to try the meat pie. That was one snack I really missed from when I was still living in Lagos, Nigeria. Meat pie is my all time favorite Nigerian snack. I get it every Sunday. I dare say her meat pie is better than my favorite spot in Lagos. No cap. It was tastier, bigger and had so much more meat in it. Jites is good! That’s just the summary. You won’t regret it.

I placed 2 orders Jollof rice and goat and white rice and stew/fish and plantains. The rice and the stew/fish was extremely spicy. Lots of rice but small portion of goat.  It was all to spicy to enjoy. This was my first time there and I wasn't forewarned that the dish was spicy. The plantains didn't have any flavor.  However,  the service wasn't bad. The food is really expensive. I spent over $60 on food that I couldn't enjoy.
I don't think I'll go back.

My wife was asking me to take her to an African restaurant and we found this place. She ordered the egusi and she simply loved it. She got it with the croaker fish, tripe and beef with the pounded yams.

The portions were very good and the lady who helped us was very kind and took the time to explain what was inside the egusi. My wife said it was the best she had since she came to America.

If we are ever back in Atlanta, GA area we will be coming back to restaurant.

I visited this restaurant today with my family, and it did not disappoint. As other reviewers mentioned, the portions are generous and absolutely worth the price. The lady who assisted us (I guess she's the owner) was incredibly kind and kept me updated on the food preparation process.

After placing my order, the restaurant got busy, so there was a bit of a wait. She offered my daughter a drink, which I really appreciated.

I've found my favorite Nigerian restaurant!

formatted_address: 11130 State Bridge Rd D103, Johns Creek, GA 30022, United States
name: Ethiopiques cafe and Restaurant

reviews.text: Amazing place to try authentic Ethiopian food and coffee! The interior is beautiful, very clean, and the service is excellent. We ordered the Ethiopian coffee and it was outstanding. A must-visit spot for anyone looking to try a unique variety of coffee. Be sure to try it both with and without cream!

Very rarely am I surprised by ethnic foods. When done right food is "good" at best, usually. Not here at Ethiopiques Cafe. The food is EXCELLENT!!!!!!!!!

I have been eating Ethiopian food since I was a teen, many years ago. I have eaten Ethiopian food from Brooklyn,  NY to Washington, DC and downtown Atlanta.  I must say, Ethiopiques in John's Creek, GA is the best!

What makes it the best? The wait time is awesome, the ambiance is perfect,  for the peaceful tranquility of East African culture. The service is better than most 4 star restaurants,  and finally, the food is awesome!

Have their, Hibiscus Tea (hot or cold). It is a unique blend of East African spices and flowers for relaxing evening drink. The Vegetarian platter is a mix of the most popular vegetarian dishes.
Their Injeera, is great. I do not usually eat Injeera but they have a Gluten Free injeera made of "tef" grain. Delicious!

I love their "Foul" (pronounced fool). A dish made of Fava Beans, eggs, jalapenos and tomatoes (get it!)

You cannot go wrong with their Lentil Sambusas. Try everything on their menu, you will take a brief trip to East Africa right here in Georgia.
P.S. ask for server named Sky!

Second Visit, Still Impressed!
We had another great experience here! The chicken tibs were delicious once again, and we really enjoyed the nice ambiance. Everyone was very friendly, and I definitely recommend trying this place!

Ethiopiques Cafe and Restaurant is truly a gem!

From the moment we walked in, we were warmly welcomed by the very personable and attentive staff -

Our servers, Reese and Ethan, gave us the best customer service—attentive, friendly, and thoughtful throughout our visit.

There were five of us, and we ordered Lentil Sambussa, Mango juices, Ful, large vegetable platter and a small platter. The portions were huge, fresh, and absolutely delicious—more than enough for everyone. The flavors were incredible, and we enjoyed every bite while listening to soothing live music - def a relaxing  atmosphere.
Must try the mango juice and signature spice powders and sauces—they really do elevate the flavors! Liza, the owner is soo sweet! She is so personable & warm. She also shared that every Sunday from 1–3 pm they host a complimentary Ethiopian tea ceremony, which sounds like such a beautiful tradition. Def coming for that experience.

This place has it all—yummy food, exceptional service, and genuine hospitality. I’m already looking forward to my next visit. Highly recommend to anyone who loves flavorful food in a warm and inviting setting.

Highly recommend- You won’t regret it :)

I really wanted to like Ethiopiques. It's the only Ethiopian restaurant in the area, and I hoped it would be my go-to after moving away from Embilta and Desta (in-town Ethiopian restaurants).

The food is good, but the service and communication are poor. We ordered the Ethiopiques Special for takeout and waited at the bar for over an hour. No one asked if we wanted to order any drinks or offered water. I asked about the order status after half an hour, was told it was almost done being prepared, checked again after another 15 minutes, was told it would be ready in 3 minutes, inquired 10 minutes after that, received a vague answer, and eventually received the order 5 minutes after that. They thanked us for waiting the 75 minutes and explained that one of the items was initially not prepared correctly and had to be remade.  With a minimal apology and no kind gesture offered for the inconvenience, I will make the trek in town for Ethiopian next time as I realized that it would have taken just as long to pick up from BOTH restaurants in town. There was only one large table at the time, and they had already received their food by the time I ordered so I am very confused about why it took so long, even with the remake.

Pros: Ethiopian food is good (especially the Derek ribs and beet/potato)
Cons: long wait times, service, communication, portions, styrofoam containers, suggested tip starts at 20% (up to 35%!)

reviews.text: Got the palm oil rice, chicken and cow skin. The rice had no flavor, cow skin Soo tough. I love African food and I wanted my wife to try something new and she was very disappointed. The was my 1st and last time eating at Kays

This is currently my best place for Nigerian food. I got the fried rice, fish, turkey wing, ewa agoyin and yam pottage. Everything was good. Everything. Ordered on Uber eats. The ewa agoyin is the most authentic I’ve tasted here. Will definitely be back!

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ ABSOLUTE BANGA SOUP PERFECTION – CHEF KAY IS A CULINARY QUEEN! 👑🔥

Let me just start by saying: Chef Kay is a master of her craft! If you're looking for authentic, mouthwatering Banga Soup, prepared with love, skill, and pure West African soul, look no further.

I had the absolute pleasure of indulging in Chef Kay’s legendary Banga Soup, paired with the softest, most pillowy pounded yam, and it was nothing short of a life-changing experience.

The Dish – A Work of Art on a Plate!

Banga Soup is a traditional Nigerian delicacy made from palm nut extract, infused with native spices like beletete leaves, oburunbebe stick, crayfish, and a medley of rich seasonings that give it a deep, earthy, and slightly smoky flavor. Chef Kay’s version? Pure perfection.

She loaded this bowl of goodness with the most succulent goat meat, fall-off-the-bone stockfish, juicy prawns, and plump periwinkles—each bite bursting with layers of rich umami flavor. The soup had this silky, velvety consistency that hugged every scoop of smooth, stretchy pounded yam, making it the perfect match.

The Flavor Explosion – A Symphony for the Taste Buds!

From the first bite, I knew I was in for something special. The deep, nutty richness of the palm fruit base, combined with the bold kick of native spices and the smokiness of the crayfish, created an explosion of flavors that hit every single taste bud. The balance of spice, warmth, and depth was simply out of this world.

Every dip of pounded yam into the soup was a heavenly experience, soaking up all that rich goodness and melting in my mouth. The goat meat? So tender it barely needed chewing. The prawns? Juicy and flavorful. The stockfish? Bold and packed with umami. This was a 10/10 dish in every way possible!

Exceptional Service – A Five-Star Experience!

Not only was the food phenomenal, but the service was just as impressive! The cashier was an absolute gem, radiating warmth and hospitality from the moment I walked in. She was super attentive, friendly, and made sure everything was perfect. Her energy and professionalism made the experience even more enjoyable. It’s rare to find a place where both the food and service are equally top-notch, but Chef Kay and her team deliver excellence on all fronts!

Final Verdict? This is the Real Deal!

If you haven’t had Chef Kay’s Banga Soup with pounded yam, you haven’t truly lived! This was more than just a meal—it was an experience of true Nigerian culinary greatness. Whether you’re a longtime lover of Nigerian cuisine or trying it for the first time, this is the place to go.

Would I come back? You’d have to drag me away to stop me! If you want rich, authentic, and soul-satisfying food, Chef Kay is the one to trust.

🔥 Highly, highly recommended! 10/10! 🔥

the jollof rice was a flavor explosion, and the staff's warm hospitality made us feel right at home. a must-visit spot in atlanta!

reviews.text:
I love that I didn't feel rushed like most restaurants. I am not familiar with the cuisine and the waitress was very helpful in explaining everything.
I loved the jollof dish, the plantains, and dessert. I would pass on the beef suya fries, but not bad.
Very kind and accommodating owner and friendly server. Food was very good, and so I ate more than I should have.

We ordered via Uber Eats. Okra soup was spoiled. Plantains were stale and unappetizing. Fufu was average, but without the soup, my wife will not eat Fufu by itself.

My wife is African and she is very disappointed, not only with the food but with the fact African food is already underrepresented, hence if you engage in the adventure of selling it, not only is it an opportunity but a duty to make it excellent because you potentially carry the burden of a standard. People who have otherwise no other experience with African food may be left forever tainted by this place.

The food was excellent, cooked to perfection!! I had the Jollof Rice with Fish and my friend had the Light Soup and Fufu, the portion was nice. The owner and staff were very friendly and courteous! My only complaint is that they should have another location on the South side! I WILL be returning!!!!

Located in Peach Tree Corners this West African Eatery is a gem! Sweet sounds of African music can be heard as you enter.  A warm ambiance with touches of traditional West African decor. From assorted meats to vegan options everyone is bound to visit and enjoy. We tried a little bit of everything! Grilled Tilapia, Assorted Meat, Red Red,Parboil & Jasmine rice, beef suya and Ifeanyi’s favorite: Eugusi Soup & pounded yams.  Many fear the spice of West African cuisine but at Cafe Songhai they cater to the average pallet.  Nothing was overly spicy and everything was bursting with flavor. Great customer service, delicious food, and a fun atmosphere. If you haven't tasted west African food and have a craving for something different Cafe Songhai is the place to go to. Insider news: enjoy Kizomba dancing 1,2 & 4 Fridays.
