My overall take that food was delicious but some of the flow of the service was disappointing and I also noticed some stains on the utensils from hard water which doesn’t make the experience feel elevated for the given price point.

At the end of the service we were brought  terminal to pay and they gave us the wrong check but they fixed it. After paying we picked print receipt option but no one stopped by the table at all and then it was time to leave for our cab.

Overall, I think there are plenty of places nearby with more value and better price point for the experience, food was delicious but I don’t see myself coming back.

Chef Eric of Top Chef and Food Network fame comes through with his new Ghanian inspired restaurant.  At first glace upon
walking in, there is a cozy and sleek yet grown and sexy vibe that radiates.

The service at the restaurant is professional, prompt and attentive.
Chef Eric is also frequently seen working on the line in his restaurant and makes
a point of coming out to personally
visit with his customers.

The food is really good.  Regardless
of how knowlegeable a person may
be of Ghanaian food, this restaurant
stands out for their plating and
flavors.  The dishes are visually
appealing and feature different
flavors interplaying in harmony.

The pricing is standard for
DC fine dining.

Only catch would be that the
portions are on the smaller side,
particularly for those with larger
appetites.

Definitely worth a visit!!

formatted_address: 1990 M St NW, Washington, DC 20036, United States
name: Swahili Village - Washington, D.C.

reviews.text: I went this Wednesday with friends, there aren’t any restaurants in Dallas so this was exciting. Unfortunately we never were acknowledged until about 15-20 minutes of waiting so we asked a manager. She called our waiter and he got us situated, he was kind, but I don’t appreciate  the lack of customer service for how expensive the food is. The food is great and as a Kenyan myself I’m picky but it’s a 8/10 my friends are Sudanese and loved the nyama choma and ngima! Next day though I ordered through DoorDash and it was not as good, the food arrived cold and on DoorDash it clearly says the mbuzi bites are served with plantain and kachumbari so when I didn’t get any plantain I called. Michelle answered the phone and had a bit of an attitude when I explained that it says on DD the plantains are included, she didn’t seem to want to  listen to me explain. I wouldn’t have ordered if I knew. And her attitude was very off putting as she talked over me while I was calmly asking for clarification. This restaurant needs to update their menu and allow for included sides with plates it’s ridiculous! But for the price I’m not sure if I’ll be returning.

Me and my daughter were guests of a really nice friend. The food was excellent the workers are well dressed and very professional. We sat at the bar area and the bartender made us a really delicious mock tail with ginger lime and mint it was so refreshing. I learned a lot about the culture of the people just through eating the delicious food. I really enjoyed the music and the restaurant was beautiful and clean with great positive energy.
Our first visit to DC and by luck we started with this hidden gem!  Located in the lower level.  The food is amazing with an ambiance to match!  Highly recommend the collared greens and jollof rice!
The food was tasty, but the service was horrific and slow. I had to inquire with the hostess about finding a server. Definitely will not be returning. I'll take my hard-earned dollars elsewhere.

Decently expensive, but totally worth it. First off - friendly, knowledgeable, attentive service. Friendly atmosphere and very well decorated nice restaurant. We got the combo platter for 2-3 and left stuffed. Delicious food, high quality ingredients, tasted very fresh. I’ll be returning for sure.

formatted_address: 1330 Maryland Ave SW, Washington, DC 20024, United States
name: Dōgon by Kwame Onwuachi

reviews.text:
LOOK! Just walking up to this restaurant was bedazzling!❤️ I felt so elegant and special! Class on its own level! The crowd looked good too. Women and men were dressed nicely.👍🏽

It took me a few months to get a reservation! I was able to book it through my Mastercard Black card concierge service. The actual reservation is set up through the app Resy. FYI, if you missed that reservation, you will get charged $100 a person.

Those of you who have American Express platinum card, you could also book through your card as well. I’m sure there are other ways, but this is what I remember.

It is located in the Salamander Hotel. What a beautiful hotel. That review would be for another day,if I do actually stay there. 😊

The service was excellent in this place, given the fact that it’s a very busy restaurant! Everything was on point. You never had to wait for food, drinks etc. Thank you to our waiter Ceazer for his attentiveness.

I could smell the aroma of the food. The flavors were a mix of African and Caribbean.

The appetizers were delicious. I had never had pork Suya before, and it was tasty.
I will highly recommend the Bronzino fish! I actually ordered it to take home. This is the only reason why I don’t have a picture of that.
The snapper was good too. They also had a side of spicy pepper, which I really liked to mix into my food..
For dessert we had rum cake with cream on top. Delicious!

I highly recommend this place for the experience! 💕💕

There is Valley parking of course.😊

Wonderful location! My partner and I went for our 13th anniversary and had a blast. Its located on the ground floor of the Salamander Hotel off 12th St & Maryland Ave. Atmosphere was upbeat, music selection was on-point and the service was thoughtful. We tried the Coco Bread, BBQ Greens, Tuna and Chicken & Jollof Rice. Each dish offering something different and packed flavor. I got a non-alcoholic drink and my partner tried a Rum Punch. We received a complimentary glass of champagne to celebrate, as well. Shout out to the valet staff out front, too! They were friendly and insightful about the history of the hotel and Dogon, specifically. Will return, thanks!

I heard good things about Dogon via friends but had not gone yet. With the New Years Holiday, I thought it would be nice to experience Dogon with family. Our experience did not disappoint. From the Piri piri salad to the pork belly suya and the glorious red snapper. My family enjoyed every bit. The service was impeccable. We will definitely be back! Do not hesitate on making that reservation. Flavors were complex yet oh so good!!!

Had such a wonderful time at Dogon! The whole experience felt personal and special from the moment we walked into the Salamander Hotel and were guided right to the restaurant.

Huge shoutout to our waiter, Travis. He was amazing. He remembered our names, gave great recommendations, and made the night feel extra memorable. We tried the HOE crab, charbroiled oysters, and the chicken and rice. Everything was delicious and perfectly seasoned.

The ambiance is stunning, modern yet cozy, with beautiful lighting and great energy. It’s the perfect spot for a nice dinner in D.C. with amazing service and great food.

A solid 4/4.5 star experience! I was excited to try Dogon while visiting DC having visited their sister restaurant Tatiana in NY. The food was pretty good. I had the cornbread, hoecrab, curry branzino and rum cake, all of which were pretty good. I especially liked the branzino. I had the rum punch to drink, which was also decent. It was very fruity, without being overly sweet. Im not sure if the waiter was overestimating the spice but there appeared  to be less spicy options here than at Tatiana. While my server was very nice, as others have mentioned I do wish there was more of something said when dishes were laid down. Additionally, I would recommend that management advise staff that they shouldn't present the check to customers unrequested and that if they feel that they must they should confirm that the customer doesn't want anything else and say something like "no rush". Otherwise, it seems like you are rushing the customer out, which can really ruin an Otherwise good meal.

formatted_address: 5505 Colorado Ave NW, Washington, DC 20011, United States
name: Hedzole

reviews.text: The food was delish!!! A nice quaint spot! The Sorrel was balanced very nicely to me. The Hostess was very personable and lovely!! I emptied my plate!! I ordered some food to go. I will post about that when I dive in. The jollof rice was good! Im learning to adjust to different styles of jollof, its so dag on good!!

Our food was delicious!! The customer service was great! The ladies were warm and greeted us with smiles. The lady that took our order was very sweet and informative.  I have a lot of allergies so she explained everything that I was able to eat so I went for the salmon bowl and it did NOT disappoint! My sister had the oxtail bowl and she loved her food as well.  Everything was cooked to perfection! All I have to say is I really wish I was going to be in town lover because I would definitely visit again!  Chef’s kiss!!

Candice was so nice, she educated me on her culture which I really appreciate it. The food was so delicious, definitely recommend the salmon. Everything was so affordable. Would definitely come back here.

One of my top 3 favorite restaurants in DC. The food is always fresh and sooo flavorful. The owner, Candice, puts so much love and care into the food and atmosphere.

I get the same order every time (salmon, coconut rice with tomato sauce, shito, and a side of red red), but be adventurous. Literally, everything on the menu is delicious.

I decided I’m going to try something new on every trip. I decided to try African food, specifically Ghanaian. The owner was very sweet & took the time to explain the dishes and the history. It has a small, cozy feel. Good home cooking.

formatted_address: 2442 18th St NW, Washington, DC 20009, United States
name: Bukom Cafe

reviews.text: It's totally changed. I understand ownership changes, but quality shouldn't have to if you are in the restaurant business. Unfortunately probably my last time there for a while. Ordered 1 meal, pic included, and paid $30+ for a piece of goat and soupy fufu... I wanted to give it a shot and not complain. The pepper soup was bland and i asked for hot pepper and they gave some generic hot sauce from giant. Im used to african restaurants having good peppa, the goat had a nice texture and I barely could touch the fufu. Not worth the price imo.

In July 2022, we as a party of three had the ecowas okra soup, the egusi, chicken yassa with jollof rice, and kumasi nkatikwan. It was my second time visiting Bukom, after the first time going in September 2019. In comparison to back in 2019, depending on the specific dishes, the nkatikwan was lacking spices while the rest of the dishes were filled with spices. Not sure if it was a one-time thing, but it was still pretty good. Atmospherically, it was evident that the place was full of rich cultural elements, including paintings, music, and the overall style. We did not manage to have any fufu since they were out, so we had pounded yam instead. But in 2019 we have had fufu and it was simply amazing. I think for lots of people, this place could be a hit or miss. But when it hits, it definitely hits, so I would recommend going multiple times to ensure you have your good experience, because this place is very authentic from every aspect and is worth going multiple times.

We went here while visiting the DC area and it was my first time trying African food. We went for lunch as soon as they opened. They were just getting set but welcomed us in. Staff were professional but not necessarily friendly. It was rare to see them smile but they were helpful in answering our questions. Place is decent. Clean bathrooms as well. Now onto the food. We enjoyed our appetizers more than the meal.  Beef suya and goat pepper soup is a must try.  We also got red snapper, egusi, mama wings and fried plantains. All good food but not sure I got a wow factor. Slowly more people started coming in a the vibe was more homey.  Drinks were served in a small cup but definitely packed a punch. I recommend the Agege Slammer.  Parking can be difficult as it's on a busy main road so give yourself time to park. We will visit again if in the area.

The restaurant is large and beautifully set up. It has a back area and an upstair. The food is good. I didn't quite like the plainness of the okra soup but the flavor was rich. The take out dish was so tasty. The chicken had a good flavor and the rice was delicious. The young server was also good and attentive. I didn't get his name. I also enjoyed the music selection.

I preface this review to say Bukom used to be one of my favorite West African restaurants in the city, and I had great experiences under the previous owners/management. Had my birthday dinner here recently thinking it would be another great experience - Unfortunately, I will not be going back. Under new management, many things have changed, including the former recipes. Barely any of the food had any flavor and in particular the Egusi soup I ordered smelled and tasted off, like it had been sitting out for a while.

My party was given plastic silverware and overall the service was very slow as we waited long to be served our main meals. I would recommend calling in advance to check opening hours too because the restaurant opened late, after 7pm on a Saturday. Not worth the money, time, or tastebuds especially during a celebratory moment. I miss the old Bukom and really hope these issues can be addressed quickly by new management.

formatted_address: 2019 11th St NW, Washington, DC 20001, United States
name: Spicy Water African Grill

reviews.text:
Just a bit clear, food is really good especially the jollof rice! The service if you dine in is can improve.

I had the Beef kebab with plantains and the rice. It was okay. The chicken version tastes much better.

As to the service, we were seated and given the wrong menus (we arrived at eight and we’re given lunch menus, which only had a limited number of items.) after we were given the wrong menus by one of the . We waited about 10 to 15 minutes. No one came to take our order and we were the only ones on the second floor. I had to go downstairs and ask the proprietor and he gave me the right menu and then came to get our order after about five minutes.

He looked grumpy didn’t wanna be there and basically said they had none of the juices we wanted such as the ginger juice, which is very tasty.  I can understand that he may have had a bad day, but in a customer facing situation, you gotta put on your best face.

Like I said, we had the food before. It’s very very good but if you’re gonna dine in, don’t expect any great service. I understand this is a tin establishment, specializing in West African food.

Great African food. Location is in a good spot and distance from a lot of things. It was a little confusing when we first got to the door, and went through the kitchen to get to the upstairs dining area. I would suggest signs or something so it’s less confusing other then that, food was really good no complaints

My husband and I used to go to the shawarma place in this building so we decided to try the new place that opened up - BEST choice!! The food is phenomenal. Worth every cent and more. Staff was so kind and welcoming, too. On top of that, there's gorgeous West African wood carvings and textiles and other art to enjoy while you eat. We loved both dishes we tried, and I can't wait to come back to try the snapper next time we're in the area. Come do some food tourism in your own neighborhood and support a small business!

Very delicious food.  Durian took such good care of us.  We enjoyed the peanut butter soup, okra stew, fried plantains, jollof rice, and fish dish. Definitely try it out if you are looking for delicious West African food!
First time in this restaurant amd I loved it the atieke was way good with the sauce and chicken , if you passing by stop and enjoy some ivorian dishes

formatted_address: 1924 9th St NW, Washington, DC 20001, United States
name: Appioo African Bar & Grill

reviews.text:
With classic Ghanian dishes included and the vibe friendly enough for a good conversation, this establishment had many options for every dish on the menu such as vegan, beef, chicken, fish, goat, and oxtail, ranging from $22 to $25 as standard price points. The food here is very authentic and has been approved by many of my West African friends living in the DMV area.

My friends and I decided to order one kind of each dish along with one kind of each side so we can try a bit of each. The okra soup was a bit too spicy for my taste, but it contained a lot of flavor, which could be neutralized a bit by the fufu that I ordered. The peanut butter soup was very creamy and flavorful. The jollof was a bit plain, but since the spinach stew was flavorful, it was all good. The wings seemed like an outlier amongst everything else we had ordered, and they were a bit dry, but with two types of dipping sauces, they worked out just fine.

Even though there are so many West African restaurants within the DMV area, I find this establishment to be one of the most authentic ones. Since Ghanian food itself is already fire in general, one can't go wrong with coming here.

Fufu with goat. Peanut soup very flavorful with chicken. Store bought wing with cajun dry rub spicey. But not over powering. Spinach very good. Seasoned well and plaintains. Which were good. Small portion of plaintain and spinach. Food took longer to prepare made upon request. Looks like they have live music by small stage setup.  Volume moderate. Easy to talk. Parking hard to find.

Great Ghanan food. The meat in the jolof rice was super tender and it was very flavorful. However, they are very understaffed and naturally struggle to cater when there is a big crowd. Nevertheless, the servers are very kind and sweet. They deserve a lot, admin should consider increasing servers for better service!

I ate alone as I was traveling and always try to stop at authentic international restaurants that I can’t get back at home. My server was incredibly nice and super helpful in answering my questions about what would be the most traditional foods, etc. She was the only server there at the time and right after she took my order got slammed with many other tables, but she made a conscious effort to make sure I was taken care of even while trying to balance tending to her other tables. The food was fantastic, cost was reasonable, and Cynthia was incredibly kind and attentive. Highly recommend Appioo!
If I could rate more than five stars, I would. Exceptional service. Fantastic food. Relaxing atmosphere. I am not West African, but as a Jamaican, I feel that the food here is authentic.

formatted_address: 1805 Montana Ave NE, Washington, DC 20002, United States
name: Zion Kitchen

reviews.text: Stumbled on this restaurant by accident. I tried their Egusi w/ Fufu and chicken. Had major abdominal pain days later, went to the doctors to only find out the food was highly contaminated with bacteria that left lesions on my liver. The workers don’t wear protective masks nor hairnets/gloves when preparing your food. And they almost never get your order correct.

I’ve been coming here for years and they never disappoint. My food is always amazing and I can tell it’s made with love. I have been craving this for weeks and I said today is the day I’m free and nothing to do, so I stopped in and was greeted with a smile, it smells amazing. They have definitely came a long way, it’s been some renovations which look nice and the new menus was super helpful. I got the #1 combo, and it comes with jollof rice, chicken I sub for goat tho and plantains, I also added cassava all over.. and I had to get two of my favorite meat pies…. I’m about to crush this food. The best part is I don’t have to share ❤️😂😂😂

This has to be one of the most
disappointing Nigerian businesses in
the DMV. We have given this
business several opportunities to
correct their error. They have terrible
service,_and never give you the food
orders you place. It's a huge shame
and they don't even care. I can no
longer support this business. Also ordered Six chicken wings and got this below.
Disappointed to say but don’t bother wasting your money here the prices and the food ratio is wild I ordered the spicy goat for18.99 plus tax through uber eats and this is what I got 🤬🤬🤬🤬🤬🤬🤬🤬🤬🤬

We heard about this spot from Don but haven’t really seen him promoting it but he made sure we were treated right when we came. Place has potential just needs more light. I will be coming back again soon

formatted_address: 1427 H St NE, Washington, DC 20002, United States
name: LYDIA ON H

reviews.text: The good was DELICIOUS! First time visiting this establishment. I traveled from VA Beach and would definitely recommend it. The food was piping hot. My snapper was to die for.

Stopped by for Taco Tuesday.  Great music.  Good service.  Themed nights (e.g. karaoke, ladies night) and happy hour. They also have a good rewards system, earned $6 off next visit. Even though I'm not local, I'd return for those reasons. The food was just okay.

Jerk chicken tacos- 3/5 small.  Chicken moist but lacked flavor.  Needed a sauce, got some jerk on the side which helped.

Mac and cheese- 4/5 creamy,  cheesy cooked well.  Solid mac.  Could use a little flavor, like there's salt but no body if that makes sense.

Virgin mojito 3/5 okay, everyone makes them different. But $8 for whats essentially gingerale with lime & mint is on the expensive side. (Usually pay $4-5).

Rum cake- 1/5. Ordered to go. Not good or worth $12 for this slice. But honestly I should have known when I was told the fried oreos were better. Rum cake is essentially just an infused pound cake, but I honestly I can't tell you what this tasted like. The sauce gives Nutella and the cake was crumbly as you can see. I honestly am so upset I didn't not look at it before I left.

First time at Lydia on H St thanks and I have to say, the food was good, the service was better. Jay was incredibly attentive, offering great recommendations and was genuinely kind and respectful throughout my visit.

The beef patty might be the best one I've ever had, hands down! The jollof rice was flavorful, abeit slightly hard. The Frozen Piña Colada was on point. Loved the great music and ambience.

Jay's service made this visit memorable. Highly recommend and will be back.

Went here for a night out with friends and had an amazing time! The atmosphere was electric, great vibes, great music, and even better food. I ordered the oxtail dinner, and wow… it was absolutely fantastic. Not a single grain of rice was left on my plate. My friends went for the pasta, and they couldn’t stop raving about it. We all left full, happy, and already talking about when we’re coming back. Highly recommend! Lastly I’ve been to a lot of restaurants this restaurant fills your glass all the time that was very, very impressive!

The food was absolutely amazing, I had the Oxtails with Cabbage and Jollof rice and Mac and Cheese. The oxtails were slow cooked to perfection and the Cabbage was well seasoned , the Jollof rice was a little spicy (I’m not too big on spice) the Mac and cheese was okay, not the best but not the worst either. I enjoyed our waitress who was super nice and professional, it seems like it turns into and late night happy hour, this place was definitely a vibe.

formatted_address: 3124 Queens Chapel Rd, Hyattsville, MD 20782, United States
name: Spice Kitchen West African Grill

reviews.text: The food was excellent—full of flavor with just the right spice level. Prices were a bit on the higher side, but the generous portions made up for it. Overall, I’d definitely go back and recommend giving this place a try. The only downside was that not everything on the menu was available; I was really looking forward to trying the puff puff and meat pie. Hopefully, they’ll have them next time!

Purchased lunch for 2 ppl: The food was really great and I am picky about both my plaintain and chicken. The atmosphere was good atmosphere. The Mango drink was good also.  The pricing was reasonable considering the taste and portion size. The service was ok neither bad or great, it was average. You can sit in or take out.  I would return.

Updating my review from 5 to 3 stars as of July 2025 - I’ve been 2 more times since my initial review and each time the food has been soooo oily. My jollof was sitting in oil. Pictures as proof. I’m disappointed

Food was absolutely delicious! Legitimate smoky jollof and soft beef suya with half salmon. I like that I could do half and half of the proteins. Most West African restaurants in the area disappoint but this place exceeded my expectations. Flavors were nicely balanced no excessive maggi or salt.

The jollof rice is way to spicy. At least create a stew to go with the jollof rice. I'm from Sierra Leone, jollof rice has always been served without a stew. The shrimp is overly seasoned. But the suya is a little tuff.

I really like this establishment. I was first introduced to them in the parking lot of the Bowie Town Center. I had the spicy honey wings with jollof rice and plantains. It was immaculate!!! This occasion made me visit at least 2-3 other times.

On the 2nd or third time, I didn't really care for the wings because they were starting to get a little too big, and I like my wings on the smaller side. The rice is always great with the  sauce they provide and more than enough plantains. The last time I went, I got the lamb, and that was really good. I'll definitely return, but the area is kind of busy with traffic and not the easiest to get to when I'm commuting.

Post Update 6/29/25: I visited this establishment again for at least the 4th time. The side sauce that you eat with the rice was amazing! I should've gotten the jollof rice because the white rice was very mediocre. It was a little overcooked and not as fluffy and Shelly as the last couple of times when I had it. I ordered the half lamb, half chicken. The lamb was delicious and cooked to perfection. The chicken was just "ok," and I'll need to broil it at home to get it completely right.

I also found out that I had a free reward for an order of six chicken wings. The wings were fine but not up to par of where they were before. You can tell they were sitting because they were not as crispy when I visited previous times. Overall, the food was mostly good and suffice, so I'll rate my recent experience a 7.8/10. I'll be back but will not be rushing to return.

Also, as a side note, I was really hungry, so one of my pictures is clearly after I've begun eating, so take that Pic with a grain of salt, no pun intended.

formatted_address: 10800 Rhode Island Ave Suite N, Beltsville, MD 20705, United States
name: Swahili Village - Beltsville, MD

reviews.text:
Was excited to try Swahili Village! It was a must-try recommendation from so many people.

The ambience was great but was super disappointed in the food. May be we just went on the wrong day but was really a big disappointment for our experience. We tried a variety of options but none of that came authentic Kenyan apart from the mixed platter bitings. Also the prices were a bit too high so was expecting much better. Here are some of what our experience felt like; mukimo - made from the packaged pre-mashed potatoes thereby tasting like powder instead of waru, the green stuff also felt like powder and no actual greens, pilau was a big flop no taste to pilau, ugali like made from semolina or very soft flour. Lets just say even the protein options didn't hit. Everyone of us left a huge portion of their meal as can be seen on the last picture.

I hope others get to enjoy a different experience.

The food is wonderful! This is an unexpected gem in the middle of an old neighborhood shopping center in Beltsville, MD. Last visit was a group of 6 and everyone was very satisfied with the taste and portion size of every dish.

This spot hits every time I go there. The food and atmosphere are great. Of course, it’s busy on Fridays so good to reserve in advance.

But of course I had to get my whole tilapia (with the head on) because it’s my favorite. Africans can make great tilapia. My island people make snapper well too.

Ordered twice the first time they forgot one of my sides but otherwise the delivery was fine.

Second time they cancelled my delivery 2 hours after I made the order 1 hour after my driver was assigned and was on route. and when it was too late to order from somewhere else.(Right around the estimated arrival time). After cancelling abruptly, there was no communication they wouldn't pickup my calls and no one reached out either via call or email to explain the last minute cancellation.

Consistently horrible customer service.
Fantastic place with authentic African cuisine. The food is DELICIOUS, the wait staff are friendly and courteous, the atmosphere is relaxing and the music is great for digestion! 10/10

formatted_address: 8000 Flower Ave, Takoma Park, MD 20912, United States
name: Mansa Kunda Restaurant

reviews.text:
I was really looking forward to trying this place, but the experience was uncomfortable from the moment we ordered. I asked the owner for recommendations and was told the peanut stew was the best option. When I said I don’t eat peanut-based dishes, he replied, “If you want me to recommend, then I recommend this—otherwise don’t ask for my recommendation.” Wow. That’s not how restaurant service should be. I was genuinely trying to respect the food culture and be open to trying something new.

I then asked what fufu was and was basically told that if I didn’t know what it was, I should just get rice. There was no explanation, no patience—just an unfriendly and unwelcoming attitude. I honestly regret not standing up and leaving at that point.

As for the food, it didn’t make up for the service. The beef was dry and tough, the plantain tasted like it had just been reheated in a microwave, and the fish was also quite dry.

Overall, it was an incredibly ridiculous ordering experience, leaving me with not just a bad impression of this restaurant, but—quite unfairly—of African food as a whole. Hopefully this isn’t the norm.

While visiting D.C. for a short weekend, I was craving some delicious West African food and found Mansa Kunda Restaurant at the top of my search results. The menu looked amazing, and it definitely lived up to the hype!

I ordered the jollof rice. Honestly, I was surprised to see it at a Gambian restaurant, but wow… it was incredible. Saying it was delicious would be an understatement. I enjoyed every last grain of rice!

I don’t know why the jollof debate is always between Ghana and Nigeria. Gambia deserves a seat at the table too! But for me (and many others), Ghana jollof will always be la crème de la crème! 🇬🇭✨

I had always wanted to try food from a West African restaurant, and today I finally got that opportunity. It was a completely new and enjoyable experience for me, and I was truly happy. We enjoyed a delicious and satisfying meal.

The interior of the restaurant is beautifully decorated with West African elements, giving visitors a chance to see and appreciate valuable aspects of their culture and traditions.

There was only one thing I personally felt uncomfortable with. The seating provided included a leather drum used as a chair. As a Sri Lankan, we hold musical instruments in very high respect and would never sit on them. In our culture, doing so is considered disrespectful. However, I understand that this may be acceptable in their culture.

That said, the staff were kind, warm, and very friendly, which made the overall experience pleasant. I would definitely recommend this restaurant to anyone who wants to experience authentic West African food and culture.

Great food, nice vibes, friendly owner.  We tried akara fritters, peanut butter chu, jollof rice, plasas, and fufu.  Everything was delicious but the plasas and fufu were my favorites.  Great labeling for gluten free options and great vegan options too

My husband was very impressed when the owner personally made our reservation and stated that he was looking forward to serving us!  He greeted us and held the front door open and immediately chose the perfect table to seat us.  As our first time trying West African Cuisine, he suggested and delivered the most delightful and flavorful food, drink and desert that we completely enjoyed.  His African decor, music, service and conversation was amazing and unforgettable.  We look forward to dining in again and highly recommend Mansa Kunda African Cuisine.

formatted_address: 3511 Maryland Ave, Cheverly, MD 20785, United States
name: De Ranch Restaurant and Lounge/Bar

reviews.text:
Okra Soup so delicious! It keeps me coming back. Good for people with allergies. They listen to diet restrictions and make sure everything is safe.

First time trying the egusi soup!! It’s really good!! Will definitely be ordering again.

Very poor quality, food was loaded with salt. I even tried to doctor it up with some mixed vegetables and that didn’t work. They even charge an extra $5 for chicken that was old or over cooked. I definitely don’t recommend this place. It was not worth the drive or money

My first time eating here and I could say I would be back. The egusi soup with chicken was so rich and flavorful. First glance I thought there was no meat but no worries it was all at the bottom and plenty of it. My only complaint was the asu suya/soya n cup. It was a waste of money. There was little meat and the meat was over cooked and dried out could not eat it I had to throw the whole thing away. I don’t know if it was because it was old or what. Also I did not receive my rice and peas with my coco bread. If they do not add that as a side with it anymore maybe adjust DoorDash.

I love coming here! I normally get Egusi with Mixed Meat and Jollof with Goat Meat. Food is flavorful and spicy! Food always comes out in a timely manner and the staff is always so nice. I will continue to come here as a regular! Plus prices are reasonable. I highly recommend if you like real authentic food!
Authentic African food, nice relaxing African music, American section of menu too, delicious fried fish. I will return soon.

formatted_address: 1780 Florida Ave NW, Washington, DC 20009, United States
name: Keren Cafe & Restaurant

reviews.text: Didn’t know I’d fall in love so early in the year. It’s only the second day but here we are. The service was swift and thorough. We got spiced Ethiopian Tea and the #4 with beef. I do not know for the life of me why this isn’t #1. Everything was delicious and I will be coming back several times over the next few months. With me being observant I recognized several people walking by and patrons beside us with the same sentiments “we back!” The place was pretty intimate but not noisy. Love it here.

Keren is back!!  After a stint away, it’s back and people couldn’t be more happy. First opened in 1987, Keren is a small Eritrean restaurant just south of Adams Morgan. Walking in on a Wednesday at 5:30pm, we got a table for three right away. Service is quick and friendly. Within minutes, our honey wine and Keren Special were on our table. The Keren Special is a mix of beef and veggie dishes on injera. It’s very tasty!

KEREN IS BACK!!!!!!

So happy they've finally reopened after their extended closure. The food is absolutely as good as ever and still an incredible bang for your buck. I got the breakfast combo (for pick up) and it was fantastic.

The family who runs this place is extremely kind and they seemed overjoyed to finally be doing business again. Truly one of the best spots in Adams Morgan. Please go support them!!

The place was super busy so I waited a bit longer. Veggie combo was high quality and not greasy at all - the best I’ve had in DC. The owner was kind enough to offer me gluten free injera. Excellent and super friendly service!

I’m beyond excited that my favorite spot is finally back! I’ve been waiting for this for a long time and I’m so happy to say it was absolutely worth it. The food is just as amazing as I remembered delicious, fresh, and full of flavor. The owner and staff are wonderful and make you feel truly welcome. This is hands down one of the best breakfast spots in DC and they were definitely missed. I can’t wait to come back again and again!

formatted_address: 1907 9th St NW, Washington, DC 20001, United States
name: Ambassador Restaurant

reviews.text: It's a typical hookah lounge. The food is good. Seating comfortable. Patrons are listening to music they want and tv they want.. which ranges from Bollywood and soccer to hip hop and football. I stopped here to see why it might be rated so highly. Maybe it's the casual atmosphere or friendly service... I can't be sure.

Love this place! Like many have already mentioned, it’s a casual spot so don’t expect anything super fancy. That being said,
it was a very welcoming environment and the food was top notch! My server did a great job and came to check in on me, would love to visit here again.

The service was incredible! Very attentive and kind. The food was great too! This was our first time trying Ethiopian so we got a little of everything, including the veggie plate, chicken tidbits, and stew. My stew was a bit on the spicier side which I wasn’t expecting, but if you like a little kick you’ll enjoy it. The seating is a little low and can get uncomfortable after a while. Overall though I would come back for good, home cooked style food!

Definitely a locals place and locals vibe. Lots of old uncles chilling and talking about their day. Staff is a friendly part of that mix, and creates a warm vibe.

We had the veggie platter along with the chicken tibs and the Ambassador (beef) tibs. Everything was solid, pretty flavorful, and appreciated the chicken and beef quality.

Decor is a bit strange, very cheesy club aesthetic that doesn't go with the chill vibe. But it was all part of the experience.

There are a lot of Ethiopian and Eritrean spots in this neighborhood, and they're all about the same honestly in terms of food quality, but this place distinguished itself with the very warm and friendly service.
The food is fresh and made with love! The hospitality is amazing very welcoming cozy place. I will definitely be back!

formatted_address: 5124 Baltimore Ave, Hyattsville, MD 20781, United States
name: Chez Dior

reviews.text: This food right here is so good! That onion sauce they have needs to be placed in a jar and sold. The chicken kabob was decent but a little dry. However, the last time I was there I had the lamb kabob and it was SOOO good. Their jollof rice is amazing I could def order just that and be satisfied.  Their service is so so. The food came out pretty quickly as we were the only people dining in. Trying to get silverware was a little bit of a struggle ans they don’t check in too much. However, the little boy serving us was really kind and had sweet manners.

We stopped by out of curiosity to try some Senegalese cuisine, and wow, we were blown away. We ordered the attiéké and the jollof dish, and honestly, we’ve never had anything so perfectly spiced. The fish was on point, and you could taste the freshness in every single ingredient on the plate.

And the jollof? Say no more, these people got itttt. The staff were polite, the space was decent. Special shoutout to Mustapha, he was absolutely awesome.

I've been coming here for years and I really enjoy the food. Today I got tiebue djenne take out, fish fatay and bissap juice. My boyfriend got tiebue yapp and beef fatays. Also with bissap.

I wish I had more fish in my dish. I feel like the portions have shrunk over the years but the flavors are still there.

My boyfriend loved his lamb dish. He raved about the beef fatay. They were a hit.

We ordered take out for lunch. The food was ready within 30 minutes of me calling ahead. They rearranged the chairs and booths since the last time I was there. I don't quite like the new layout but it's not up to me. It's definately an older building and could use an upgrade but I still enjoy the food.

The food was good nothing out of the extraordinary. There is plenty of parking on the street. They have one table outside if you decide to sunbathe and eat simultaneously. But otherwise the inside is nice and cool. I was not a fan of the nems with meat in it thought they had a funny taste but the vegetarian one was much better!! And the meat for the rice was tough.

But the drinks were very nice 👍🏾

I was super excited to discover yet another great Senegalese restaurant 🇸🇳 in the DMV area! Safe to say that Chez Dior is a hidden gem… The food was authentic and beautifully plated.

The mom and pop restaurant hit the mark with all of the usual dishes that you would expect to find at a Senegalese restaurant. Everything was well seasoned, fresh and tasty.

The service was a little slow, and a few of the items that were ordered were never brought to the table - it wasn’t at all a busy time, so likely they just forgot to bring it to the table.

Overall those I had a great time and would definitely visit again.

formatted_address: 401 H St NE, Washington, DC 20002, United States
name: Ethiopic Restaurant

reviews.text:
Beza was so warm and inviting to all whom entered the Ethiopic Restaurant. As soon as I walked through the door I was greeted with the biggest smile from Beza. I partake in all of her food suggestions as she paired my meal with 3 fabulous wines. This place was truly a delightful place to eat and unwind from the busy world of work and life. Thank you, Beza for making my visit enjoyable. I will definitely come back.

Tanya Washington

This place is fantastic. Beza was kind and had great recommendations. The ambiance is low light and just a great all around vibe. The food is to die for. I had the Ethiopic signature tips for entree, sambusas for appetizer and the most decadent crème brûlée for dessert. There is a THICK layer of sugar caramelized on the top. This is the best creme brulee I have ever had and I order wherever they have them. I recommend doing a sampler if you come in a group. You will not regret it. Flavorful, great size and DELICIOUS. The servings are great proportions. Service is immaculate and all around great gem in DC.

This was my first time at Ethiopic and eating Ethiopian food.  The food was delicious.  I tried the vegetarian sampler II, sambusa, beef tibs and lamb tibs. The Ethiopian spiced tea was even a hit. Our server Beza was awesome! She helped me understand the food and demonstrated how I should eat it. I will definitely be back with friends.

I absolutely love this place! The entire experience was phenomenal. The staff here are so polite, very attentive, and friendly. We were seated as soon as we walked in and our server immediately tended to us. It was very busy in there and I could absolutely see why, but yet we experienced no delays in service! I loved the food here! We ordered the lamb tibs with a few other sides, was given injera bread, and another bread as an appetizer. Everything was seasoned to perfection and was very flavorful! You get great portion sizes for a reasonable price as well. I would definitely dine here again and highly recommend this place!

The food was phenomenal. Highly recommend the fried fish, lamb, and the veggie platter. The one star deduction is due to the enforced $10 "service fee" as tip. After bringing out the food, the wait staff just figure about us. Didn't refill the water. I had to ask for the go to containers several times. I didn't appreciate being forced to tip when the service was mediocre.

formatted_address: 8626 Colesville Rd, Silver Spring, MD 20910, United States
name: Koité Grill

reviews.text:
Soo, this is an unconventional review, because I was mentioning to someone how much I was craving some god jollof rice and they recommended this place and another… and imagine my surprise when they were at the Hst festival! I hopped in line, waited (amongst a crowd) for about 10-15 mins… they did have a fluid operation going for an outdoor event, so I can only imagine what a dine in experience is like! Very impressive.

But, can’t compare prices because it was an event… but the 2 items I got were definitely pricey and flavorful!
And probably enough for 2 people to have some sides if you chose a meat entree (which I didn’t), just the 2 sides (which would classify as vegetarian, Macn cheese and the jollof ( possibly vegan, not sure if the rice was boiled in a broth?)

The Jollof: The rice was very different, can’t explain the grain used, it’s very small, reminiscent of a tiny couscous… I’m told they use something similar in Hati, but with the other flavors and veggies with the grilled onions on top, it was just right.
But I was informed the Senegalese do jollof different.

So yes on the very different, but equally yes on the flavor, though different also, it was hints that are familiar while taking their own spin on it.

Will be on the lookout for them if I’m ever close to that side of Maryland.

I was so excited to stumble upon a Senegalese food truck at the RFK Market this summer in NE DC! 😍 It instantly took me back to my trip to Senegal—where I fell in love with lamb dibi, poulet yassa, and the amazing ginger and bissap (hibiscus) drinks. The food was quick, healthy, and soooo flavorful. And with Senegalese music playing in the background, the vibe was perfect and the owners were easy on eyes- tall, dark, and very handsome! Treat yourself to an authentic taste of Senegal in DC- you’ll thank me later! 🇸🇳✨

Koite Grill is a delicious and authentic Senegalese restaurant located in Silver Spring, Maryland. I recently went with my dining companion who happens to be Senegalese. We originally made a reservation, but it became clear when we arrived that this reservation had not been communicated to the 3 youths working the restaurant. However, after my companion spoke to them in Wollof, they quickly found us a table. The food is excellent! Tastes just like Senegal. Granted, whether you are dining in or getting takeout, they serve all the food in plastic to-go containers, it was all delicious. I had Senegal’s most famous dish, Thieboudienne, and it tasted just like I remembered it tasting in Senegal. My companion had the poulet (or chicken) yassa – which he stated “tasted just like home.” Do not come for the service or the atmosphere, but come for the absolutely authentically delicious Senegalese cuisine!

Staff is always welcoming and friendly feels like family.  Every item I've had on the menu is always delicious 😋.  Same consistency since day one and never changed for me. I would highly recommend Koit'e Grill to anyone who enjoys  GREAT FOOD

Everything was lovely! Food was tasty and wonderful. We loved the jollof rice for sure. Hibiscus drink was refreshing.

Service felt like you were at home! Very hospitable and warm!

formatted_address: 7463 Annapolis Rd, Landover Hills, MD 20784, United States
name: Jolloff Etcetera

reviews.text:
I have given this establishment enough grace. It's either they quote a rodent price for your over the phone and charge you fifteenth when you arrive to pick up your food or their food is just inedible.
How do you sell stew that's inedible. I grew up with Surulere atadindin and have bought atadindin from jollofetc before,  never have I, among my complaints about this restaurant,   ever been given stew that causes instant heart burn and is impossible to swallow past the first spoon.  How can you, in all honesty, as a restaurant, claim to sell this to people? NOONE, and I repeat,  NO ONE,  could ever digest this or go through a plate. This is a complete waste of money!! Completely inedible and tasteless BTW. All oil, no taste!!
Called them to let them know that if this is what they're serving to people, it's a hazard.  The lady I spoke to stated that this is how the stew is, which is a blatant lie.  I know that they sometimes ask if you want it mild,  this time no one asked when I called but I reminded them of that, they didn't honor it.
I have to throw this food away.  Appalling!!!

My family and I were visiting from out of state and intentionally went out of our way about a 30 minute drive to support a Nigerian restaurant. While the food itself was good, the customer service was very disappointing. From the moment we arrived, the staff was not welcoming, which set the tone for the rest of the experience. Although the food was on the expensive side, the cost was not an issue for us, we were happy to support and enjoy the experience. However, good food and pricing should come with equally good customer service. As a business owner myself, I strongly believe that customer service is just as important as food quality, especially when customers are making an effort to support their own community. Despite the service, we still left a tip because we believe in supporting businesses. I didn’t initially want to leave a review, but I feel that constructive criticism is necessary for growth. With improved hospitality and customer engagement, this place has the potential to be much better.
I tried the Oha soup with assorted meat....Very savory, not spicy. Music was native as well, made it feel like a great african experience! I will be back soon❤️❤️❤️

My daughter and I were planning to do carry out but when we arrived we were told to go @3 doors down to order carry out as there is a different place for dining and carry out. The costs seemed a bit high and the staff were not welcoming or engaging when we walked through the door. Based upon the energy of the staff and their toned responses to our questions regarding the menu, we had a sour taste in our mouth that good food would not even resolve. We didn’t even want to try it…and we actually love Jolloff rice.

Our group had a great lunch here. The ambience was lovely, especially the window table, the best spot in the house. The place was clean and cool, a perfect escape from the heat. The food was flavorful and satisfying. We enjoyed the Jollof rice, puff puff, plantains, and yam porridge. A tasty side sauce for the Jollof would be a nice addition.

Big thanks to our server, Yolanda, she was awesome and welcoming.

formatted_address: 1524 U St NW, Washington, DC 20009, United States
name: Abuare Bar and Restaurant

reviews.text:
Memorable food experience 😋
My first time with Ethiopian food and i truly loved every moment of it. The platter was wonderful - i had the most delicious lamb ever, and it came with so much veggie. The samosas were also very delicious. My most favourite was the tea - fragrant and relaxing. Overall 10/10!

I stumbled upon Abuare Bar and Restaurant by chance while walking down the street, and I'm so glad I did! This hidden gem is a must-try. I ordered the vegetarian combo, and it was absolutely amazing – bursting with flavor and clearly made with care. To complement the delicious food, I tried the honey wine, which was a unique and delightful experience. And the coffee? Excellent! Truly, everything I tasted was top-notch.
Beyond the food and drinks, the atmosphere was wonderful. The beautiful art displayed on the walls added a lovely touch, creating a warm and inviting ambiance. The staff were also incredibly friendly and attentive, making me feel right at home.
Abuare Bar and Restaurant exceeded all my expectations. If you're looking for a fantastic meal, unique drinks, and a welcoming environment, look no further. 5 stars all the way!

Hidden gem? Not sure—a friend recommended it to me. I wanted to try kitfo for a while, and I heard this place’s kitfo (raw ground beef) is amazing. Until the last minute, I was worried. But I kept myself hungry, and when the food came, I had the first bite—it was amazing. Big portions, though. We also tried their samosa and veggie platter, which were good. Recommend.
SO tasty! We got the beef tibs and it was phenomenal! It’s a very low key, kind of hole-in-the-wall spot, very authentic food and vibe. Definitely worth checking it out!

Very disappointing experience. We ordered the veggie platter and were extremely unhappy with the quality of the food. Everything was bland, poorly seasoned, and did not taste fresh. Some of the items seemed like they were taken straight from the freezer and reheated.

The lentils tasted unbalanced, as if all the seasoning was poured in at once instead of being properly cooked. The cabbage looked and tasted like it was simply boiled and served with no seasoning at all it literally tasted like plain water. The gomen was also flavorless and watery, with no depth of seasoning.

The salad was clearly not fresh; the tomatoes were stale and old. Because of the poor quality, we did not touch the food and left everything untouched. Even the tea was unpleasant and tasted bad.

What made this even more frustrating is that I have had much better food and higher quality meals elsewhere for a much lower price than what I paid here. Considering the cost, this experience was unacceptable. Overall, the food quality was very poor, and I would not recommend this place to anyone.

formatted_address: 1334 9th St NW, Washington, DC 20001, United States
name: Chercher Ethiopian Restaurant & Mart

reviews.text: We had a nice experience overall at Checher DC. The food was flavorful and satisfying — we ordered one lamb plate, two beef plates, honey wine, and two sambosas. Everything tasted good, especially the main dishes. The only downside was that the sambosas came out cold, which was a little disappointing. Other than that, we enjoyed the meal and appreciated the variety of flavors.

Overall, this was a solid experience with some real highlights. The vegetable platter was definitely the standout, very flavorful, well seasoned, and satisfying. The portion sizes were generous, and the spiced tea was really good and nicely balanced, not overpowering.
My only critique is texture-related: I personally prefer my yellow split peas to be softer, and some parts were a bit firmer than I like. My friend ordered the chicken tibs, and while they were okay, they didn’t taste as fresh as expected. That said, no one got sick, so it may have just been an off moment rather than a bigger issue.
All in all, the food was good, the vegetarian options really shined, and I’d come back, especially for the veggie platter and tea. With a little more consistency, this could easily be a go-to spot.

For my last day in DC I was torn between Bbq or Ethiopian cuisine; sooo glad I picked this restaurant. I've had Ethiopian food before in Canada yet every place has it's own savour.
Got the Vegan Special and I had a chance to try some items for the first time. I was truly enchanted since every bite had something unique to offer. My favourite were the String beans and red lentils. Really wanted to try Berbere chicken but it wasn't offered in any of the combos so that was a miss for me.
Overall I left satisfied.

Pretty tasty food, but the staff not very forthcoming in helping us as we have not had Ethiopian food before. 18% Service added to the bill, irrespective of the quality of the service.  Very nice atmosphere and busy in the week.

I have no complaints! The food was delicious, affordable, and an experience in of itself. The food service was quick and the server was lovely! I cannot emphasize it enough---Amazing.

The Ethiopian honey wine was delectable as well!

formatted_address: 1301 U St NW #111, Washington, DC 20009, United States
name: Eatopia Eatery

reviews.text: My wife and I went here for a date night and we had a really nice time. We got the digis communal platter and though it says it serves 2 it can really feed 4-6 people. The spices and flavor were very good, for those with spice sensitivity it could verge on too much heat for them. The only critique was that the beef was tougher than expected and could have been more tender. I also got the house Ethiopian wine and it was very sweet, but was still good.

My friends and I stopped by this place a while ago while exploring different Ethiopian restaurants, and we chose it because it was relatively new and we hadn’t visited before. The building itself, which previously housed other businesses, looks quite nice, and the food portions and pricing seemed reasonable overall. However, the beer prices were extremely high, which felt unjustified. What truly ruined the experience was the owner’s behavior he ignored us while spending time chatting with other customers, which came across as rude, disrespectful, and unprofessional. Because of that treatment, we have not returned since and have no intention of going back in the future.

Edited: Honestly, we don’t care whether he spoke to us or not, and it’s funny that you think talking to us would mean anything to us. However, as a business owner especially someone who asks other customers about their food and service experience he should have extended the same courtesy to us. Had he done so, we would have shared exactly what’s written in these reviews. Instead, he selectively asked other customers about their experience while ignoring us, which is not how a professional business owner should conduct themselves.

The ambiance is really amazing! Beautiful artwork and a lot of sunlight. The food was amazing. They have the local injera as well as the Ethiopian one so that’s a plus. The drinks were meh. The tubs were okay but not as saucy and square like other places or as tender. I would still recommend this place to have dinner or lunch.

✨ Eatopia Eatery – A Flavorful Journey to Ethiopia ✨

On a cold, rainy day, I found the perfect warm escape inside Eatopia Eatery—and let me tell you, this place did not disappoint. The moment I walked in, the atmosphere wrapped around me like a cozy hug: dim lighting, stylish décor, and a calming, intimate vibe that instantly set the tone for a memorable dining experience.

From the start, the service was welcoming, and the menu alone had me excited. I knew I was in the right place.

🌿 What I Ordered: I went for a mix of plant-based favorites and a classic Ethiopian staple—and everything came out looking beautiful. The plate was vibrant with lentils, cabbage, greens, potatoes, and stews resting on soft rolls of fresh injera.

The highlight?
⭐ The Doro Wot.
Rich. Deep. Flavor-packed. The sauce had that slow-cooked magic you can’t rush, and the tender chicken absorbed every bit of the berbere spice. Pairing it with the Ayib (Ethiopian cottage cheese) was a whole experience—creamy, cooling, and the perfect complement to the heat.

Every bite was comfort. Every dish tasted like care, culture, and tradition.

🌱 The veggie platter was just as impressive—earthy lentils, bright yellow split peas, sautéed greens, and cabbage all cooked with beautiful layers of spice. Nothing felt rushed. Nothing felt bland. It was soulful Ethiopian food done right.

The injera was soft, fresh, and plentiful—exactly how it should be.

🍷 And the ambiance?
Elegant without trying too hard. Warm without feeling crowded. The kind of place you lose track of time in.

---

⭐ Final Verdict:
Eatopia Eatery is a gem. Whether you’re new to Ethiopian cuisine or already a fan, this spot will make you feel like you’re dining in someone’s home—someone who can seriously cook. I walked in hungry and cold, and left full, warm, and already planning my next visit.

10/10 – A must-try.

We enjoyed the shared veggie platter for two. It was SENSATIONAL! The injera was perfectly light and soaked up the delicious flavors from the veggies. Our favorite part was the shiro. Staff was very kind and attentive. We would love to come back on a day when they have live music. We only wished there would have been some jazz playing over the speakers 🎶

formatted_address: 822 H St NE, Washington, DC 20002, United States
name: Open Crumb

reviews.text: Love this place and their vegan choices! Enjoyed the red red and jollof rice - I also asked for a side of pepper sauce which was delicious to add! Will def be a go to for us!

Exceptional food—by far the best food and most interesting meal I’ve had in DC. Family owned business that makes everything from scratch, made with deep cultural pride and a passionate commitment to the freshest, highest quality ingredients

The food took a little while to arrive after ordering, but it was clear this was because everything was prepared freshly from scratch and believe me, it was worth the wait

10/10 would go again and recommend to anyone I know

Only downside was the dine-in area was a bit low-budget and not airconditioned, but again well worth it for the food

This was the first time I had the opportunity to try West African cuisine. It was incredible. I got jollof rice, wakye, plantains, and the kutumeri + egusi with fufu. Everything was so rich, flavorful and filling. I'm sad there isn't anywhere like it where I'm from, but this is definitely a go-to spot for me whenever I'm in the area.
Had the blackened chicken over jolof rice w/ salad to go, and it was amazing. Generous portions and amazing taste.
We did take-out and the food was fabulous.  Perfect and plentiful.  The vegetarian/vegan options were great (loved the red red).  Also family loved the goat stew!

formatted_address: 3213 Georgia Ave NW, Washington, DC 20010, United States
name: Heat Da Spot Café

reviews.text: First time at Heat Da Spot after being recommended from a friend and it was a great experience with delicious food! The owner was so friendly with a smile and the food portions were generous and delicious til the last bite. Will be coming back!

The food is amazing and the staff is friendly. Timi took care of us. We had the veggie platter and a breakfast platter, both with tibs (beef). Very authentic and great place to eat. Can’t wait to come back again!

This is the real deal. I love you Ethiopian food and this one did not disappoint. The staff was super nice and friendly and they cooked the food with love! Please be patient because you want fresh hot food. It takes for a few minutes sometimes but it’s totally worth it.authentic Ethiopian and RN Washington DC national Mall area it’s only about 15 minute drive from the Capitol.

truly a neighborhood gem! i love the food and coffee here so much. i brought my friend here for her birthday and the owners are genuinely some of the kindest people i’ve met. will absolutely come back here and recommend everyone to go🫶🏼

The Ethiopian breakfast and a hot black coffee was my go-to order for years. Wonderful food. You can’t go wrong with anything on the menu, though, it’s all delicious!!

The folks that work here are a kind and wonderful family.

It doesn’t get any better than this folks.

formatted_address: 4715 Sellman Rd A, Beltsville, MD 20705, United States
name: Miya Lounge & Restaurant

reviews.text: After travelling for hours to get Cameroon food we found this spot. The food was so good and the service was excellent. I ate and even took some home

Their food is horrible. This was my second time ordering from them. The first time I did ,The food wasnt the best so decided to give them the benefit of the doubt and last night I ordered Achu from them ,Jesus help me ,The soup had 3 different colour's(you can see the video i attached ), The amount of salt in it🤦‍♀️ .Besides I have never seen 3 layered, colourd achu soup in my life .please you all can do better Jesus christ .I wasted 28$

where do i begin. Lounge looked like it was still under renovation. AC was out!!! it’s super hot inside the lounge. The two cashier barely spoke anything they were whispering literally.

Let’s get to the menu and food. First off the pricing is not accurate!! Menu says Suya with jollof $18.99 i got charged $22.99 ??? A big sign on the door says make your own Suya $18.99 and the you can’t even order that online the website keeps saying (page not found)!!

Food was below average. I paid $92 for two people. ordered two Suya and jollof & Eugsi soup one order of fried plantain and a side of extra jollof. Meet was dry (and i always eat african food) not new to African cuisine. Meat should not be that chewy. rice wasn’t that much for $22.99. i think for you should be more generous with your portion since you are charging $22.99 a plate.

The Egusi soup was also below average. a very small portion with two chuck of small meat and big chunk of Cow feet with absolutely no meat.

i would def not come back. i suggest you try other African places who can provide bigger portion and better quality meat.

If there’s a Black/African-owned restaurant you’re looking to support, pull up to Miya Lounge & Restaurant. I went once in 2020 and once again recently.

Here are some thoughts about what I know about Miya Lounge and my experience:

So the name of the restaurant is misleading because I think often times when people hear ‘lounge’ they think of a place that has alcohol/hookah. This place has neither.

If you truly care about good food and not the aesthetics at all, then you will really enjoy this place. It’s definitely more of a carryout spot, but there are plenty of tables and seats to sit at if you want to relax. I will say, if you also want your food quickly, call in your order first, because you are not going to receive it quickly (the dishes definitely take time to prepare).

When it comes to the food, they definitely have some of the best suya in the area. I wasn’t the biggest fan of the suya tacos though. I think the cheese takes away from the flavor of the suya and when it comes to jollof rice, I think it could use more flavor and spice, but I may be biased because I’m Nigerian lol.

The suya pizza was a fish suya pizza and it was really good. It was not fishy at all and had good flavor. The goat pepper soup was delicious. The goat was nice and tender. I also really liked the eru and now am wishing I put more on my plate.

When I come back, I also really want to try the grilled fish because it looks so good

We had a party of four people, the only clients in the restaurant at the time. It took over 2hrs to serve us achu. All drinks we asked for were sold out. Customer service was so poor. Staff would not respond to questions. Let me actually reduce your star for the rude response. I just read every review on your page and it's negative. Instead to correct customer complaints, you are chasing them with rude responses. To top it up, we refused to pay for our food? So the American express card you collected, was that from your village?

formatted_address: 1114-1118 U St NW, Washington, DC 20009, United States
name: Dukem Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: A happy hour date at Dukem was right on time! After a busy day of work and running errands, my wife and I settled on Ethiopian food for dinner and that’s when I remembered seeing Instagram advertisement and Google reviews for happy hour at Dukem so we decided to give it a go! The food was fresh, service was great and the establishment welcoming. Since the weather was nice, we decided to sit outside on the terrace area. We really enjoyed the special beef tibs, pieces so flavorful and tender, the sambusas, both the chicken and spinach. I ordered the Shiro and gomen, while my wife ordered the misir wot and alicha kik, awesome portion size for the price and shareable with the injera. While waiting on our order we had a chance to speak with one of the owners, Yodit, very sweet of her checking in on how the evening and service was going. We will definitely be back again and can’t wait to check out more of the menu. I recommend Dukem be your next DC Ethiopian restaurant to check out and also check out their happy hour specials.

The food came quickly and was quite excellent. I have never had Ethiopian food before this, but I will definitely be looking to come back. Our server BK took great care of my party of three and she gave us helpful recommendations as well.

I enjoyed eating here nice clean atmosphere with family vibes. Only complaint was I wish the food was spicier (i like very spicy African food) and a LITTLE more seasoned. 😊 Shared a combination platter with 2 others and it was a decent portion for all of us. We were served by BK and she was very nice.
Delicious food, u street fixture. Be sure to have an Ethiopian beer with your meal, st. George or Harrar are bother perfect.

It was our first time eating Ethiopian and the food was very delicious! The dishes came quickly and the waitress was really kind and gave us good recommendations on what to order. The ambiente was pleasant and the music fire as well :)

formatted_address: 11237 New Hampshire Ave, Silver Spring, MD 20904, United States
name: Jolloff Etcetera

reviews.text: This is really an amazing place to dine! I visited here with my family for lunch on a Sunday and we had such a great experience. Vivian was our server and she is such a jewel! Very polite, kind, and attentive. She made sure that we had all that we needed and checked in on us frequently. Now the food was truly amazing! I ordered the egusi soup with pounded yam and baked chicken. This was the closest to the home cooked egusi I've had! Everything was flavored and seasoned so well! My family had the oha soup with fish and stated it was really good as well. The prices are very reasonable and you'll receive great portion sizes. I must also compliment the atmosphere. Throughout the time, there was beautiful worship music being played that I truly enjoyed. It's also decorated so beautifully. I look forward to dining here again!

I ordered the grilled fish with plantains and it was very good! It was not spicy but very flavorful. Our waitress, Funke was extremely nice and she explained the menu to us. I liked the pictures on the menu. Be sure to get their Zobo drink, I’ll be back for sure!

Disappointing Customer Service at Silver Spring Location
I want to start by saying that my experience at Jollof Etcetera has always been excellent. Just yesterday, my family and I dined in at the Annapolis location and everything went well—the servers were polite, welcoming, and appreciative. We truly enjoyed our meal and the overall experience.
Unfortunately, the experience at Jollof Etcetera in Silver Spring was the complete opposite.
On our way back to New Haven, my husband and I stopped at the Silver Spring location to order food. The young lady at the entrance had a very rude, unwelcoming attitude when taking our order. We ordered oat with oha soup, paid in full, and were never informed that oat was unavailable.
After waiting over 25 minutes, another staff member casually told us the item wasn’t available no apology, no courtesy, and then walked away. When the food was finally handed to us, there were no napkins, no spoons, and the staff seemed eager to dismiss us as quickly as possible.
Good customer service matters. If you’re having a bad day, professionalism should still come first especially in the service industry. The contrast between the Annapolis and Silver Spring locations is shocking.
Sadly, this would be my last visit to the Silver Spring location. Customer service travels fast, and this experience was deeply disappointing.

I ordered take out and I was notified that it was ready very quickly and once I went to pick up it was brought out immediately.

This was my first time ever trying any African cuisine outside of Ethiopian and it was definitely a new experience but overall good! I ordered the Egusi w/ Assorted meat (which ended up just being beef) & Fufu, as well as an order of fried plantains and an order of puff puffs. The Egusi meal was fantastic as was everything else.

My only small complaint is that I wish they gave a bit more meat in the Egusi especially for the $30 price. Otherwise fantastic spot! Would recommend!

Very friendly staff. Great place. Nicely furnished and decorated.

The food was great and tasty just like it. If you want real authentic West African food, this is a great place to come. The debate between which jollof rice is better - Ghana or Nigeria??? It is still a debate 😂 😂 The jollof was really good. It tasted just like our, Ghanaian, jollof..

I will let you decide 😂 😂. Go and enjoy food. You will not be disappointed. They give big portions so go with an empty stomach..

formatted_address: 5640 Annapolis Rd, Bladensburg, MD 20710, United States
name: Agama Kitchen & Restaurant - Nigerian cuisine

reviews.text: I went with 2 leaders from my organization and they enjoyed the pleasant disposition of the owner and the courteous and friendly service.  It was my first time,  I plan to go there more in the future. It was worth our time. Thank you to the management of the restaurant.

Ordered the grill fish with sauce and plantains, the extra large suya and a meat pie. The food tasted great, fast service, and the food was well packaged. Very satisfied and I’m a fan. I’ll definitely order from them again!

Ladies, if you come in cute (which I already know yall do!), expect to be there for an additional 30mins. The owner is nice enough, but the staff will literally look you in your face without saying a word until you ask if you can be assisted. Last 4 times in ordered, I wasn't given the meats I wanted because they didn't have it.  No word, no "what can we substitute it for" just gave me whatever....and they wrap the plates with saran and aluminum so you won't know until you're ready to eat.
This review is specifically because we've been ordering less and less since the last situations.
Just wanted a tray of suya (dry and tough) and a tray of meat pie. Peep how raw the fillings are in pics. Plus a tray packed with rice and one piece of meat...times are hard, I know but $20 for oily rice and one goat meat thats literally skin and bone.

The jollof rice was very good, fried fish was okay. They also give you a lot of food for your money. However, the food is in buffet style trays that are not heated and exposed. The Guy serving the food was standing right over it. Restaurant also looks very dingy. I personally wouldn’t come back but since we drove far to try it, we decided to do so.

Ok.. I read the reviews before I went there an it seemed good but nahh the jollof rice is terrible.  They even gave me burnt rice, old food they probably cooked 2days ago and chopped big onions. Waste of money . I wish I didn't have to drive that far to get this food

formatted_address: 549 23rd St S, Arlington, VA 22202, United States
name: Enjera Restaurant

reviews.text: Omg!! What a gem / hole in the wall amazing restaurant! The chefs must be making magic because this food is BOMB!!! Run here and try it out!!! I’ve never had Ethiopian food but I loved every single thing in the veg platter with added chicken. So delicious! Quick and friendly service and great ambience! I would 100 💯 recommend!

I’m a regular when it comes to Ethiopian / Eritrean food, and recently tried out this restaurant in Arlington. The service was impeccable, the portions were generous, and the food was delicious! We tried the kantisha (mushroom tibs), beef tibs, and veggie combo for one. They also had traditional iced tea (available both with or without sugar) and beer which were very refreshing.

Great authentic Ethiopian restaurant in Arlington! The food was delicious and servers attentive. The portions are generous. Food has spice levels so you can tweak it according to your preference. The atmosphere is cozy. Will visit again.

This area has great Ethiopian food and Enjera is such a gem! I can't get enough of the vegetarian sampler but you really can't go wrong with anything here. Service is wonderful, everyone is so kind and attentive. I love the atmosphere as well -- it's just such a nice place to eat and the food is absolutely spectacular. 100% worth a trip if you love Ethiopian food!!!

We typically get takeout, esp because they offer full orders of sides, which is a great deal. I love their misir wot and awaze tibs, very delicious Ethiopian food and extremely friendly staff. Restaurant and bathrooms are always very clean, new outdoor patio is also excellent.

formatted_address: 6120 Kansas Ave NW, Washington, DC 20011, United States
name: Laud Naija Shawarma | Nigerian-Style Shawarma in DMV – As Seen on Fox 5

html_attributions: Laud Naija Shawarma | Nigerian-Style Shawarma in DMV – As Seen on Fox 5

reviews.text:
I was really looking forward to trying this place, but unfortunately, it ended up being a letdown. The shawarma was actually quite good—I'd give it an 8/10. It was well-prepared, and the sauce was really nice.

However, the experience went downhill with the sweet potato fries, which were badly burnt. I asked for a fresh batch, and the person serving me said he’d bring one out—but never did. After waiting 15–20 minutes, I went to check, and he quickly ran to the back to avoid me. I could clearly see that he had never even tried to fry a new batch.

At the very least, I expected a refund, but that never happened. I ended up wasting money on food I couldn’t eat. I won’t be going back—Prime Grill in Laurel is much better.

Love this place. Walk in the door and immediately to the right is Lawd Shawarma! A wonderfully warm meal of fish & eggs with vegan bread and Christmas-spiced Sorrel / Hibiscus drink. No matter what they call the next respiratory illness, no matter if you need to starve a flu or feed a cold. Problem solved for me. Lawd! I thank you.

Overpriced. Got the chicken shawarma wrap, but it barely had any chicken in it. Flavors were ok, but not worth $10. It was mostly bread with little pieces of cabbage and about 30 grams of chicken (which is a generous estimation). The service is
friendly, but the wrap took 15 minutes to prepare. Atmosphere was a vibe, but because it’s in a food hall.

My husband said it best when he described the portion size as insulting. The size of the shawarma was the width of three fingers and the length of about 6 inches. We used doordash so each one was close to $15. I wouldn't have expected to pay more than $3 for what we received. It was so disappointing because the flavors are spot on.

This is my favourite place to pick up lunch in Solaire Social. The fish shawarma, jollof rice and bread are very good👌🏿. I really love the almond milkshake - absolutely delicious. The people who run the shop are kind.

formatted_address: 2000 5th St NE, Washington, DC 20002, United States
name: Disbe Good

reviews.text:
I have ordered Jollof rice and meat - Black plate special via uber eats. I was so excited for the food, especially since I have ordered from this place before and enjoyed it a lot.

This time around I was extremely disappointed in the order I have received- the food quantity absolutely did not match what they show in the photos. This is false advertisement. I have gotten a portion looking 2 times smaller than the photo on the menu. I guess this place got too greedy. Do not recommend it to anyone, especially for the price they charge.

Look at the photo. My fork is basically bigger than the container. And meat? This is much less than advertised, mind you, it is sitting on too of more rice!

Another mystery halal food place. Traveling and looking for halal food late at night, I ordered lamb and spicy rice with add ons and jerk chicken side order.  Look at this pathetic food! I don’t what it is,  jerk chicken was nothing like chicken, some left overs or something.  Lamb was horrible, some sticky rice, and the pick up place, some weird place.
If negative rating is a thing, this place would minus 10.
