Kid size portions, chicken was well made though. Jollof rice was a huge letdown.  Wouldn’t recommend based off the first experience

Fantastic takeout out of Ivy City Food Works with tender, juicy suya, fowl chicken suya that I've never seen anywhere else, and otherwise teriyaki options with a good kick as well as burgers with amazing custom mayo!

Disbe Good should be called Disbe GREAT. Oh my gAWsh 🤤🫠. Lol. The eating that I have eaten here via delivery. Yum yum yum.

Okay, so it started for me with the suya bowl. I tried this restaurant because of the pictures, in spite of thinking "Hm, the bowl are not very saucy like a Chipotle or Roti, but I like suya so let me see."

Oh, did I see. Did, I, see. It was DELICIOUS. The suya spice on the mea tnad on the side, the Disbe Good sauce. WoW. I don't know how they did it but it was done. Everything went together sooo well, the cucumber tomato salad, the cilantro rice. Fantastico 👏🏾 🤌🏾.

So I ordered that a number of more times. You can really taste that they care about their food and make it with pride.

And then. Next, I tried the chicken fried rice. And next, the chicken suya bowl despite thinking, "I don't think the chicken suya will be as good as the beef suya, but they did that...so let me see,"

And—I SAW.

The chicken suya was (❗). Yes. That was a complete sentence. It was—somehow—competing with the beef suya, which I'm still not understanding because how??

Aaanyway...tonight I'm trying the Kabob Feast. 😎😀.
They've earned themselves a "Favorite ❤️" status on my GrubHub homepage.

I highly, highly recommend Disbe Good. Obviously! #🤤 #🇳🇬

Update after trying tonight's order—it did not disappoint 😋. And the Dirty Rice is the bomb!

formatted_address: 2000 5th St NE, Washington, DC 20002, United States
name: Miya Lounge & Restaurant

reviews.text:
These people can’t cook for nothing. My
Coworker and I ordered Okra soup. The soup was watery. I ordered Okra soup with Chicken only. The food didn’t taste fresh. When I called to complain, they stated to me that they grill their chicken separately then add it to the soups. I have never heard anyone cook their food like this. I wouldn’t even feed this my dog. NEVER AGAIN!!!!! SHUT THIS PLACE DOWN
Great music and vibe , service was slow but our server was great ! The food is amazing but not very hot as it come out

I ordered Egusi with rice and received some hot hard potato looking stuff wrapped in aluminum foil. My dasher had already pre warned me that the food wasn’t ready and he’d been waiting for a while and it was delay. They gave me barely a cup of Egusi it’s more oil than anything. Also didn’t receive the pepper sauce that I paid for either like what are yall doing. To the trash it goes,always read the reviews!

No thank you,this is the second time Ive had an issue with my food.

I go to Miya all the time, and it never disappoints. The food is always amazing—fresh, flavorful, and with a good variety to choose from. I usually get the grilled fish or suya tacos. You can tell they put a lot of effort into making everything taste great.

Customer service is excellent. The staff is super friendly and attentive, which goes such a long way with me. Highly recommend checking them out!

ate at Miya lounge recently and was really impressed! The food was delicious, everything we had was so fresh and flavorful. I especially loved their suya tacos and jollof rice🤤
The staff were super friendly and made the whole experience even better.
Definitely recommend this spot if you're in the area. I’ll definitely be back soon!

formatted_address: 2000 5th St NE, Washington, DC 20002, United States
name: Beyond Suya

reviews.text:
Great Late-Night Find with Excellent Service!
I ordered from Beyond Suya at their kiosk, and I was genuinely impressed. The staff was so nice, patient, and super communicative throughout the entire process. Even though it wasn’t a dine-in experience, they made sure everything went smoothly and made me feel like a valued customer.

The food was absolutely delicious – full of flavor and clearly made with care. What really stood out, aside from the amazing service, is that they’re open late! If you’re looking for something tasty and satisfying to eat late at night, Beyond Suya is a perfect go-to. I’ll definitely be back again soon. Highly recommend!

Suya “platter” for $30 lol. The jollof rice was an extra $10. Not worth it. I did order on Uber eats so I’m not sure if prices are different in person. But regardless, small servings. 3 stars because it was tasty tho
I ordered through Uber eats and I received the most amazing dish I've ever tasted. The jollof rice and lamb suya is phenomenal. Im so happy to have found this place.
Just tried this for uber eats this is the best suya from a restaurant that I’ve tried and this week it’s buy one get one free! Don’t walk run Ana support!!!!!

So disappointed. Decided to give them a try last night on Uber Eats. We ordered the 1) fries, 2) jollof rice, 3) chicken suya “platter” and 4) beef suya “platter.” The order was for two people but the portion they gave us was only enough for a child to eat. We found it offensive. I just saw their micro portions as a complaint in another review so apparently it’s their way. The fries were enjoyable. The jollof rice was not jollof rice. The flavor profile was way off. If anything it tasted more like boxed Mexican rice from the grocery store. Further, it did not taste fresh. I lie to you not, the chicken suya “platter” was like 5-6 small pieces of chicken breast for $14.25. The beef suya was tender but again the portion was so small and it tasted like beef teriyaki. Not authentic suya. Overall 0/10 experience and I would not recommend this place at all. The food leaves a lot to be desired. An absolute waste of $70.

formatted_address: 1608 7th St NW, Washington, DC 20001, United States
name: Dashen Restaurant and Lounge

reviews.text:
It’s a flavor explosion, an experience like no other!
I was visiting DC and was looking for foods unique to the area.  I learned that DC is home to a diaspora of Ethiopians who have quite the unique culinary variety.  I’d never had Ethiopian food before and decided this would be my chance! I did a bit of research and looked at different menus, but Dashen stood out to me because they had both a vegetarian and meat combination platter and would size them all the way down to a single person size. Traditionally Ethiopian meals are very social and platters are often shared.
It was very simple to get there I simply took the Greenbelt Metro to the Shaw-Howard U station and it was like a block and a half south of that. When I arrived they told me I could sit wherever I’d like, so I chose a seat facing the window (people watching).
I ordered both the veg and meat platters for one. I was hungry, but this was even too much for me, but I wanted to try as much as I could. It was an absolute delight! If you are nervous about Ethiopian food, take it from me, you’ll like it! Try a platter and I guarantee you’re going to find dishes you fall in love with. It’s a great way to try a variety of things they offer.
Also if you have friends with you twist their arm to go with you, it’ll be a lot of fun and super tasty!
The staff was so nice and friendly, they explained what everything was and how it was made. They make it fresh daily (I can’t imagine the labor that goes into that!). The chef came out and greeted me and later as I had requested coffee, she came out with a cast iron pan she was actually roasting the beans in! She carried it over to me and another couple people who had ordered coffee and stirred it while it roasted around the room so the room filled with the smell of roasted coffee beans! Delightful!
She then came out with a platter and poured the cups of coffee and even sat at my table for a couple minutes with me as we chatted and she too shared a cup of coffee! Such a nice experience!
They also have a special honey drink called Tej, it’s actually a house made honey wine, so be aware it is alcoholic. Very sweet and tasty though, they serve it in a very unique glass that I guess is traditional.
Anyway you eat the different foods with this flat bread that kinda has a spongy texture to it but tastes like sourdough. It was very good honestly and worked well with the dishes, trust me.
Totally recommend Dashen to anyone who wants a great culinary experience or a great social experience! Honestly you could go alone like I did, but I would really like to bring friends next time!

I came alone for lunch and felt so welcomed and taken care of. The staff paid so much attention to my experience and really made me feel right at home. The food was incredible and the coffee was super. I will definitely be coming back and will be bringing my friends with me.

Best Ethiopian food I’ve ever had in DMV - and I’ve had a lot!  Excellent vegetarian platter even tho we showed up for a late night meal.  Everything was fresh - the tomato was particularly amazing but all the dishes were outstanding quality.  Attentive service.  This is my new go-to in DC.

This Ethiopian restaurant is absolutely amazing! The atmosphere is so warm and homey — it instantly makes you feel comfortable and welcomed. The staff are incredibly kind and attentive, and the service is impressively fast. Every dish tastes authentic and full of flavor — truly the best Habesha food in the city! Highly recommend to anyone looking for a genuine Ethiopian dining experience.

Had an amazing experience at Dashen. As an Ethiopian…DMV is a hub for our food and I’m so excited to find a new spot with ETHIOPIAN BREAKFAST FOOD! Flavorful and warm! Had the non-meat fir fir and ful (bean dip). I ve tried the combo dishes too that were equally great so they earn a review. Quality service and ambiance with traditional coffee and popcorn! Must try! Great location/group friendly!

formatted_address: 941 Bonifant St # 1, Silver Spring, MD 20910, United States
name: Roger Miller Restaurant

reviews.text:
Roger Miller Restaurant is an absolute gem! The food is rich in flavor, perfectly seasoned, and the portions are very generous for the price. You can truly taste the authenticity in every dish.
The atmosphere is relaxed and welcoming, and the staff is friendly, attentive, and happy to guide you through the menu.
As someone originally from Togo, this place really took me back to Africa . the flavors, the warmth, and the sense of sharing a great meal together. Highly recommended for anyone looking for genuine African cuisine 🌍✨

SO good. The food had so much flavor and you get a good amount for what you pay. The restaurant has a chill atmosphere and the service was friendly and great. Very authentic Cameroonian dishes - it brought me back good memories from when I lived there! 🇨🇲

Roger Miller Restaurant left a lasting impression on me through the warmth and sincerity of their customer service. From the moment I walked in, I was met with genuine kindness and care. You can truly feel the heart behind this hard-working, family owned business one built on strong morals, values, and pride in what they do. The energy is welcoming, honest, and grounded, and it made me feel good simply being there. Supporting places like this really matters, and I’m grateful for the experience.

OMG so I’ve been coming here for 10 years since the original owner managed the restaurant. Unfortunately, as he grew older he couldn’t manage the restaurant as much, so orders and food were often incorrect. I came into the restaurant today and the food was amazing!!!!!! I ordered the Ndole with the fish. The fish has the perfect crunch and taste! Shout out to the female chef and new management that has taken over !!!

I’m Caribbean, but This is my favorite spot for great Cameroonian food. Their steamed Crocker with peppers and onions, Jollof rice, spinach, and plantains is what I dream about when I want a comfort meal. Service is always welcoming and friendly.

Pro Tip:
Ask for extra pepper sauce!

Just a great family operated small business. Support them if you can to ensure they keep their doors open to us!

formatted_address: 2000 5th St NE, Washington, DC 20002, United States
name: Jolloff Etcetera

reviews.text: A nice and clean environment. The food was delicious like homemade. I ordered pounded yam with Oha, and assorted meat, it was filling. My spouse ordered  pounded yam, egusi mixed with bitterleaf. I enjoyed my meal.

Amala and the stew served is not it at all. If you are going to get food from here probably try something else. Got my amala with double temperature and slightly burnt. Stew is not anything positive to be written about. GOAT meat asun taste good tho

We ordered 4 different mains and some additional items (e.g., meat patty) - unfortunately, literally every item was bland and seemed overcooked. The chicken was dry and tough, the beans tasted burned, the egusi was mediocre (my wife never leaves egusi on the table but she did this time), and the pepper soup was overly salty and completely unbalanced. This place has a high rating on uber eats but we can't understand why.

I ordered soup here and the sizes of the meat i received were HUGE, whats up with that. We're they too lazy to cut it right? I couldnt even finish it l, why not cut your meat in smaller sizes. It looked even scary, I couldnt eat it anymore and had to throw it away.
I bought Jolloff rice and assorted meat. The food I got was stale. To think I drove almost an hour to get there. Pls do better.

formatted_address: 1414 9th St NW, Washington, DC 20001, United States
name: Family Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: Phenomenal! This meal will live rent-free in my mind. Excellent variety and flavor! Plenty of spongy Injera! I’d been craving some Lega Tibs and Doro Wot for a while and this more than satiated my craving. I will absolutely revisit the next time I am in DC!

A great Ethopian restaurant in town! People like me belonging from India is where one would get the class in food that people would be looking for. We had a platter with meat and veggies and it was yummy. Really a class apart!

We came here on New Year’s Eve, were greeted and were seated immediately. I enjoyed the Ethiopian music playing over the speakers. We got the sambusas and Yebeg (lamb) tibs with a side of Diffen Missir wot. The sambusas stood out to us the most. The tibs were good but were similar in quality and flavor to other Ethiopian restaurants we’ve been to.
Delicious! Went with a party of three and got the meat + veggie family platter, very filling and delicious! The Habesha beer was yummy. Great service, highly recommend!

We shared a family platter and added and individual platter and it was plenty for two adults and two teens. The food was amazing - fresh, hot, and delicious. If you love Ethiopian food, or if you are looking for for somewhere to try it, you will not be disappointed with Family Ethiopian Restaurant!

formatted_address: 3821 S George Mason Dr D, Falls Church, VA 22041, United States
name: Nazret Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text:
I really like this food. It’s my first time trying Ethiopian cuisine.
The staff were very friendly and introduced us to the coffee and incense. The atmosphere was wonderful.
Exceptional! And such kind owners. The regular platter with lamb is stellar, and prime ribs live up to the hype. Excellent flavor for all, loved the veggies and lentils. Try the peanut tea!!

This is my third time eating at Nazret and I brought my friends to try Ethiopian for the first time. We cleared the deluxe platter in 10 minutes. Consistently delicious and I love the vibe in there. Best Ethiopian I’ve tried!

Delicious delicious food! Perfectly seasoned food, tender meats, and waiters were so so kind! One of the best Ethiopian restaurants in this area that we (me and my family) have tried so far. Definitely recommend.

My cousin, husband, and I had dinner at Nazret last night, and it was some of the best Ethiopian food any of us have had! We started with sambusa and telba fitfit appetizers then shared a VIP platter. It was a lot of food for three, but we just couldn’t put it down! The atmosphere was so warm and welcoming too - the owner greeted us as soon as we stepped in and even treated us to some amazing teas. I highly recommend visiting Nazret!

formatted_address: 6210 Georgia Ave NW, Washington, DC 20011, United States
name: Serengeti Restaurant Lounge

reviews.text: The Smoked goat was 100%. Fried whole tilapia was king. Served with Ugali, sukuma wiki, plantains. Chef was pleasant and knowledgeable. A must return. Open for Sunday brunch too.

I just moved to the DMV area and as I wanted to taste some authentic African dishes, I discovered Serengeti Restaurant online. I gave it a try with my wife and we were utterly satisfied with the meal I ordered. The food was fresh, the portions were more than enough and the flavors just took me back to the motherland. I highly recommend this spot to anyone and I wish the owner all the best !!
The samosas were excellent and the chicken very filling. The owner is amazing and the music was fun. Cozy experience
Nice International Quizine that includes american and african (Kenya and Ethiopian) dishes among others
So glad this place reopened!  Portions are huge, food is delicious, and this is definitely one of the top underrated spots in DC.  Don’t sleep on the plantains either!

formatted_address: 8123 Georgia Ave, Silver Spring, MD 20910, United States
name: Attia's Kitchen @Gulf Ultra Lounge

reviews.text: The fried snapper and dry rice is phenomenal. This is one of the best fish dishes I’ve ever had. I wish this restaurant was open all day. :( the woman that makes the food is also so sweet!

Attia’s Kitchen serves the most authentic Liberian food I’ve had at any restaurant. I ordered food for takeout and everything was packed well, fresh, and full of rich, traditional flavors. The owner is friendly and welcoming, and the service was genuinely great from start to finish.

Honestly one of the best Liberian restaurants I’ve ever tried. I ordered fufu and soup a couple of days ago all I’m going to say is try it for yourself. REAL authentic I look forward to trying other items on the menu especially the fried potatoes greens.

I really wasn’t happy with my experience here. I ordered through DoorDash for pickup and even drove almost an hour to get there, only to find out my food wasn’t ready. They told me the order hadn’t been checked, though I honestly don’t even remember the exact excuse. I was asked to wait 15 minutes, but it turned into 40 minutes with no apology or acknowledgment for the delay.

I tried to stay positive because I thought at least the food would be fresh, but I was disappointed again when I tasted it. The meal was extremely salty, to the point where the salt completely overpowered the actual flavor.

Overall, it just wasn’t a good experience.

Found her on Google, we created a tradition of eating at a West African restaurant on New Year’s Day, so we drove from Arlington, Virginia to her place.  We called ahead to let her know what we wanted everything is made fresh, she brought the food to the car. The car smelled so good couldn’t wait to get home and eat. She gives you so much food for your money more than generous portions, food was delicious 🤤. Fish was seasoned well and tender. I love the jollof and it was my first time tasting cassava leaves and I love it. Will definitely be back.

formatted_address: 3100 14th St NW #121, Washington, DC 20010, United States
name: Letena Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: Most authentic Ethiopian cuisine food here!! Loved the food, service was beyond amazing. The owner of the restaurant was very friendly and very polite with us all. Would definitely recommend going to this place for vegetarian food. 🥘

First time trying authentic Ethiopian food & it was delicious! We shared the Goat Wot and Beef Stew. The staff was super friendly and helpful in describing not only what we were eating but also *how to eat it haha.

They take reservations but at the time we went there was plenty of seating. I would recommend this place to anyone coming into DC.

The atmosphere was perfect, an authentic restaurant all around. This was my first time trying Ethiopian cuisine, and it was a great place to do this because of their "sampler" options. You can try many different dishes all in one. The kategna appetizer is a must if you like spice. The samosas I'd say were a bit underwhelming. We got the veggie sampler for 2 and had enough leftover for one more full meal. Overall a great experience, I'm glad I chose Letena for an Ethiopian dinner in Washington DC.

I judge all Ethiopian restaurants against the legendary Meskerem (sadly, long gone), and most places fall short. So I was delighted to discover Letena! We had their delicious vegetarian messob sampler platter (they happily made a substitution of one of the included dishes for us) and the lentil sambosas. I had the Tej honey wine, because, hey, we’re having Ethiopian food, and my husband had the Addis Manhattan; both were a great compliment to the food. The ambiance was chic but also felt authentic to culture. Would definitely come here again and again!

Long time DC resident who has been to close to a dozen Ethiopian restaurants in the city, and this is our new favorite. We discovered Letena as it participates in the To Go Green DC program (takeout containers are cleaned and re-used, so no single use plastic), ordered takeout and it was excellent - we especially liked the Yemisir Wot, Kit Wot, Gomen, and Chef’s Signature Tibs. We are looking forward returning to dine in person.

formatted_address: 8041 Centreville Rd, Manassas, VA 20111, United States
name: Lapaz African Cuisine

reviews.text:
AMAZING food but wait time was longer than expected. this small, family owned restaurant is serving up one of the best west african food i’ve had.
highly recommend the fufu with spinach stew + chicken and the suya rice with goat. the jollof rice was a good portion and the fried chicken was crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside. the eba with peanut butter soup+beef was not out favorite because it was fermented but the beef was good.
i wish they had music playing in the background cuz it was too quiet for the amount of time we waited but otherwise everything was great. definitely coming back!!

First time trying Ghanaian food? And it was quite good 👍

I enjoyed the jollof rice, but it was a bit monotonous after a bit. The fried chicken definitely helped.

The fufu was quite interesting to eat, as figuring out the optimal hand method was quite fun. And the palm soup was alright, nothing too good nor bad.

The star was definitely the fish, it tasted flavourful and we couldn't stop eating it.

My only compliant is the loooonnnnngggg waiting time for food. Place your orders  1 or 2 hrs ahead as despite us being only 3 people, it took us around 1 hour to get the food. Also, it wasn't spicy enough. The chili sauce, jollof rice, and fish weren't spicy enough to make me want to keep on eating. It was just there.

Overall, a good introduction to Ghanaian food?

7.6/10

I ordered akyeke & tilapia, banku & okro with goat meat, jollof rice with chicken, fried plantain, and waakye with goat meat. (Dine in and take out)
All the foods I ordered were exceptionally delicious. Great job 🇬🇭

This place was authentic and genuine as it gets. Made fresh to order so plz don’t mind the lil wait as others mentioned on some of the reviews.  I rather wait for freshly made food than get fast food.  People were super friendly as well. Will definitely come back! EXCELLENT.

My friend and I went here for lunch and it was our first time here, we honestly couldn’t stop talking about how good it was!!! Ralph is super kind and helpful as well by telling us what paired best with which. I got the Okra Stew with Eba and my friend got the Spinach Stew with fufu and a 10/10 from the both of us! We enjoyed how much of a great first experience this was for the both of us and how kind the staff were. The portions are also very decent sized as well for the price and quality of food it’s so worth it. I posted a picture on my social media and recommended it to everyone who asked about it! My friend and I can’t wait to come back and try their other options, thank you Lapaz!!!!

formatted_address: 514-c S Van Dorn St, Alexandria, VA 22304, United States
name: Calabash African Cuisine & Bar

reviews.text: This place is a hit or miss because it’s either open or closed, but you never know until you get there and they usually out of plantains. The food is really good though, on the pricy side but that’s African food in the dmv for you 🤷🏾‍♀️

After hearing rave reviews from a few friends, I decided to visit Calabash African Cuisine and Bar while I was in Alexandra this weekend, eager to see what the hype was all about. I must say, I was truly impressed! The restaurant boasts a unique decor and a welcoming ambiance that immediately made me feel at ease. The staff were professional yet warm, embodying the best of African hospitality.

For my meal, I went with a quick take out lunch option: Waakye with assorted meats, accompanied by a side of salad, Red-Red with fried plantain, and topped off with a light soup. Every bite was absolutely delicious. What stood out to me was the restaurant’s creative twist—pairing these traditional dishes with Caribbean flavors. The jerk chicken that accompanied the Waakye was a delightful fusion that I thoroughly enjoyed.

Kudos to the team at Calabash for such a fantastic culinary experience! I’ll definitely be returning with friends to explore more of the menu.

This was my first time trying West African cuisine, and it was absolutely divine!
We had the jollof rice with chicken and the fufu with beef— both were full of rich, bold flavor. Truly chef’s kiss 🤌.
The mocktails were super refreshing (and pretty look at too haha! ) . The staff were incredibly friendly and made us feel so welcome. 10/10- I can’t wait to come back

Lets start off with that they serve Ghanaian African cuisine. The food is truly fulfilling, tasty and well seasoned.  There's a  bar to sit at also the atmosphere is really nice, cute, and laid back it's perfect for a date, or hanging with friends or to eat solo.  The staff is very attentive and polite and you feel like family.  You get enough food for the price you pay.  I try to frequent this spot whenever im out Alexandria VA.  I Love Calabash

I’ve seen this place many times and was always curious to try it out. I finally went and have been hooked! The service is top tier and super hospitable. The hosts are super friendly and even educated me on their different entrees and how to properly prepare/eat meals with fufu. The female host was even nice enough to give me samples of food that I haven’t tried before. The food is very flavorful and came out piping hot, just how I like it. I had the egusi with chicken, okra stew with beef, waakye, and plantains. This place is a must try!

formatted_address: 8319 Old Branch Ave, Clinton, MD 20735, United States
name: Naija Cafe

reviews.text: I just moved to the area and have been looking for authentic African cuisine. This is my second week in a row I have went here. The cashier(Woman) was very welcoming and professional. The music in the restaurant was nice. The location is very clean. Lots of parking thank god that was not an issue. I ordered the “Asun” and my GOD it’s hot but so good. My meal was Cassava/beef with white rice. Everything was perfect. Comfort food is what I call it. I give this place 5 stars. I can’t wait to order the snails. They do make though you don’t see it on the menu. You have to call a week in advance if you want some. I will be placing my order next week.

Not good at all...the egusi was wirh frozen spinach  not much green, too much palm oil. I know good egusi and this is not it...will not be back and service is very slow. They told us they were out of jollof but then gave us a small order but it was old like it had been sitting out

The lady was nice but…. Food was not good at all. The meat was old and tough. I could tell it was old because it was dry and smothered In cassava leaf stew. And it was hard! I had a hard time cutting it with a knife. Perhaps if the food was freshly made it would have been more tolerable. But to sell old food is just disgusting. I would not recommend.
Absolutely the best West Africa Nigerian food in Southern Prince George's County!!!!  Portion sizes could be larger, but the taste you can't resist.

Pretty good overall; was expecting a bit more flavor based on other reviewers. the restaurant itself looks kind of like a dive, but that's not necessarily a bad thing as some of the best kept food spots are considered dives. I got the combination platter which was one entree with two sides. For the main I got fish, tilapia, and for the sides I got the rice and the moin-moin, which was described to me as a "bean cake" of sorts. The person that took my order was friendly and helpful. Prices seemed decent for the area. Menu is limited, which is totally fine. Food took about 10 to 15 minutes to come out, which is pretty on par. And my meal came out, it looked great and the portions were big. The rice was basically an entire bowl of rice put on the plate, the fish was a whole tilapia, and the moin-moin was shaped like a cup. The rice was fairly flavorful, but pretty spicy. It reminded me of Spanish rice of sorts. The moin-moin reminded me of refried beans, just packed tightly into a "cake". To me, it was kind of bland though. A tilapia looks good with some sort of green chile sauce from what I can tell on it. I thought it would be fried but it was probably baked or sauteed. However, I thought the fish was sort of bland as well. It wasn't bad per se, I guess I just was expecting a lot more flavor from it.

formatted_address: 2429 18th St NW, Washington, DC 20009, United States
name: Tsehay Ethiopian Restaurant And Bar

reviews.text:
From start to finish, Tsehay was an amazing experience that I can't wait to have again. We made a reservation for 7:30 on Friday night and got there about 15 minutes early. We were able to get a table almost immediately and were treated with so much kindness and hospitality! We ordered the vegan platter and a bottle of wine, and did not leave a single crumb left behind. The food was excellent and the service was just as perfect. We were there to celebrate my friend's birthday and were given a complimentary dessert and a glass of champagne each!

Thank you Tsehay for a 10/0 experience! I'm already looking forward to my next DC trip!

It was my first time eating here and it was a great first impression. The vibe was great and the food was excellent. A lot of the menu you eat with your hands, which I thought would be a problem but the food is so good that you fall into pretty quick. The service was also top class. I ordered an alcoholic tea and after a few sips it was clear it was too strong for my taste, it tasted great but it was just a bit too strong for me. Once the staff saw my drink untouched they took it off my bill and gave me just the base tea, which was great. All in all the food was great and the staff were a class act

True gem in DC: friendly staff and delicious food. I ordered the Lamb Tibs, which were tender, but what surprised me were the greens. I loved how the sauce on the greens added just a little more complexity to the dish. Of course, the injera was nice and soft. Combined with the gentle lighting and atmosphere, this restaurant is perfect.

It was my last stop in DC, and I would recommend Tsehay to anyone from out-of-town.

Absolutely devoured the food here, it was so delicious. I got the vegan platter and it was well worth it, a good tasting of all of their vegetarian dishes. I would definitely come back again, especially to share with a bigger group. The flavors are perfect and bring out each individual piece.

Ambience is such a beautiful and calm space and the service is pretty quick.

Update: (in response to owner below) My honest review of our experience is not to attack your business as "black owned".... it's my experience as a customer in your establishment. Service was poor and slow, food was superb, even if a very tiny portion. Simple as that. It took us over 1.5 hours to receive/be offered 1 drink, 1 entree and 1 appetizer. That's not an attack, it's my truth.

Original post: The staff was nice but the service was extremely extremely slow which is stopping me from going there again. They were either understaffed or extremely disorganized. We didn't even order multiple drinks in fear they would show up after we ate and we asked for our bill as soon as our food came. Food was great but the waitress dished onto the same plate without asking, considering my partner is vegetarian and I'm not. Atmosphere was okay and the ambiance was nice.

formatted_address: 2714 Georgia Ave NW, Washington, DC 20001, United States
name: Sankofa Video Books & Café

reviews.text:
Love this place!! It’s a great hub for community, books, videos, and a delicious bite to eat.

The place has an outside sitting area with several benches, its inside is warm and cozy, and there’s an outside sitting area that’s shaded as well.

Go for the books or various activities and stay for the vibes.

While you’re there, grab my book - Reflections of Healing

17th Annual Black People March on Washington

Go online, come-in or purchase a gift card for that special gift for that right person...or better yet,
Become the one known for "Giving A Great Book" as a gift!!  Support All our people providing knowledge to the masses!!

I heard great things about this place and I decided to check it out. Upon entering it was empty so I thought I picked the perfect place for studying. I have about 5-7 hours of studying to do so I was looking for a location that I could comfortably do that. I am a full time student and I found several locations in the DMV that you can study and bring outside food/drinks. I was excited because I wanted to think I could've added them to my list. I understand it's a business but I think this place misrepresents itself as a space for community and lounge reading. I had a personal snack and was not ready for anything heavy, also I don't have funds to spend in a cafe all day. I asked for a straw for my kombucha and the lady at the cash register made a weird face that I would ask for that. At this moment it would've been appropriate to inform me of the no food policy.  I ignore it and sit down and continue studying. I have been there now for over an hour and the same lady comes and lets me know that they don't allow outside food. That's ok, but it's how it was brought it to my attention. Walking back and forth, staring, but never greeting me as a patron. When she approached me she even mentioned the straw as if it was a problem that I even asked for it. I visit many different places in the DMV that advertise themselves as a bookstore and cafe, and I never feel obligated to buy as I sit and enjoy their space. Again, this review is for the person who is looking for a location to truly sit, study, and relax. I was not given the opportunity support the business, but the whole hour multiple eyes watched me to see if I would purchase, but I was never met with pleasantries. I guess they assumed an hour was more than enough time to spend some money. I am more irritated because at some point I would have decided to break away from study and have lunch. I felt like I was in a restaurant, with a focus on high turnovers and their over booked seating. If this is their business model then they should advertise as that, because I walked in this morning under the guise as this is a DC staple community bookstore/cafe you can lounge in and get work done and a great place to learn about new literature. The interaction I had today was so; "if you don't buying anything we don't want you here" energy that it prompted me to leave and go to another local business that offers the environment that I was looking for. I want to emphasis this review is for the people who have to study all day and want to feel welcomed regardless of how long you take to spend money. Bookstores are important for the community, engagement, resources, and I think it's important to support the ones that focus on that and not on how much money I can squeeze out of you as you enter the door.

When I say BLACKITY BLACK BLACK bookstore I mean that with every fiber of my being. The café was delicious! The coffee warms your soul, the food was amazing, & most importantly the books oh my gosh the books. There was knowledge and history flowing from every nook and cranny of this shop. It feels like a salon/barbershop were you can chop it up with all who enter. I will most def be back.

I love coming here when it’s just the women working but recently there’s been a new hire and he has messed up my order 3  separate occasions. Genuinely I have no clue how one messes up an order only consists of 2 patties and a drink several times. At first I was like he’s new it’s okay but it’s so annoying when my order gets mixed up every time. Asked for 2 beef patties, received one, another time was handed chicken patties, every time my drink was forgotten and I had to go up and ask again. Only when the boy is working. Other than that, this place is great.

formatted_address: 4939 Harford Ave, Beltsville, MD 20705, United States
name: Cape Coast Cuisine

reviews.text:
Looking for authentic Ghanaian cuisine in Maryland near Beltsville? Look no further than Cape Coast Cuisine!

Whether you're Ghanaian, African, or simply a lover of delicious food, this is the perfect spot to enjoy a true taste of Ghana right here in Beltville Maryland, U.S.

One of the highlights is their mini buffet section, where you can mix and match your favorites - from Jollof rice, Waakye, and plain rice to a variety of tasty sides. The best part? You're free to create any combination you like, and the portions are generous. No restrictions,  just good food 😋.

I can’t write this review without giving a special shoutout to my favorite Ghanaian dish: Kelewele. Cape Coast Cuisine’s version is 99.9999% as delicious as what you'd find in Ghana — spicy, flavorful, and absolutely delicious.  😋

And of course, a warm thank you to Auntie Monitor, whose friendliness and hospitality perfectly reflect the welcoming spirit of the Ghanaian people.

I’ll be coming back again, and again, and again.

Be prepared to wait 1 hour & 30 minutes for simple order of soup. Checked in 30 minutes later only to be told they don’t have the fresh fish so they are getting started on your order now, an hour later still nothing. Its truly a wonder this place is still in business when there are much better tasting, much faster places in the area. Not once have I come here where I haven’t wait over an hour for always subpar food. Trying it to let it slide the 1st couple times wont work because it will always be like this. Horrific customer service & always trying to explain away incompetence. Spend your money elsewhere and go to Hunger Tamer or Rahama instead.

I guess I expected more from others speaking about it.  There was only one person working at the restaurant. A woman and three workers in back. Had to grab our own menus.  Food came out after about 15 minutes.. the portion was a lot, which was good seasoning left much to be desired, but my husband liked his.   My food was ok at best,  probably won’t go back.

Waited 20 mins to get served our drinks and waited an hours for our food that never came out. As I walked up to pay for our drinks, the food that I ordered was scooped out from the buffet and taken to the back to get reheated. This could’ve taken 15 mins to do but we were ignored the entire time because there were 3 other tables there…there were only 4 tables…we also arrived second and placed our order before the other two tables. Won’t be going back nor will I recommend this place ever again! The nerve to offer my food to go after an hour of waiting. Do better!
Owner super sweet. The buffet is excellent. The peanut soup, wasnt the freshest. But other dishes were descent and tasty. The fish was nice. I suggest the buffet. Big portions 4 stars!

formatted_address: 569 Ritchie Rd, Capitol Heights, MD 20743, United States
name: Shaboss African American Cuisine

reviews.text: This place is DISGUSTING!!!!! I usually don’t leave bad reviews but DO NOT eat here. I got the jollof, chicken and puff puff. The jollof smelled burnt and fishy. I couldn’t even include a picture because I put it in the trash so fast. It was stinking up my house. And the puff puff, well the picture is included. The puff puff would have been good if it wasn’t all burnt up. I heard them microwave my food. I don’t even think they have a kitchen back there. I can’t believe they would even serve a plate like that. People used to take pride in their food. Luckily I was able to get a refund. I would never eat here again.

My husband and I were up visiting for the week! I was craving me some African food!
I came across this place ! When I say the food was absolutely bomb!!!! & delicious . I was humming while I was eating lol . I got the egusi Stew with goat and fufu my husband order cassava leafs with goat and coco bread ! We asked them to make it spicy !!! It was perfectly spiced and flavorful! The young lady at the register was very sweet and pleasant ! The best African food I’ve tasted in a long time . Will be back soon! Mind you we are all the way in NC 🤣 My pic doesn’t do it justice !

I finally crossed fufu off my foodie bucket list—and I couldn’t have picked a better place than Shaboss African American Cuisine. I’ve always been curious about West African flavors, and from the moment I walked in, I knew I was in for something special.

This was my very first time trying Egusi soup, and I went with chicken as my protein. I asked them to make it spicy, and they delivered—the heat was bold but balanced, letting the rich, nutty flavor of the soup shine through. The chicken was perfectly cooked, seasoned well, and fell right off the bone.

When I got home and dug in, the pairing with the fufu was perfect. The fufu was soft and stretchy, just right for scooping up that delicious soup. It was a full-bodied, comforting, and satisfying meal that made me wish I’d tried it sooner.

Shaboss truly impressed me with the authenticity and care they put into their food. This place is a gem. Next time, I’ve already got my eye on the peanut butter stew and the okra stew—I’ve heard nothing but great things, and if they’re anything like the Egusi, I know I’m in for a treat.

If you're curious about trying fufu or exploring West African dishes, make your way to Shaboss. You won’t regret it.

I ordered the cassava leaf w/ chicken and honestly I wish I hadn’t. For one, they gave more chicken then actually cassava leaf and I’m surprised because when I looked through the reviews someone posted a picture of a platter full of cassava leaf. But the taste is what was alarming. It had a distasteful after taste as if the water used when cooking was not clean or maybe it was the chicken it was flavorless as if it were boiled. I ended up trashing the food a complete waste of 20.99. I’m not sure if maybe it was because I order 30 mins before closing but still you would expect quality food. Cassava leaf was lacking flavor besides the spice level it had no peanut butter and just overall poorly cooked. Extremely disappointed

I’ve found an African food spot close to home and I’m super pressed lol I love a good jollof and casaleaf. Look at my plate ya! I tried it in the car cause hunger, and I couldn’t pull off w/o going back to tell the guy at the register “it’s so good, thank ya again” I’m now home feet up enjoying my jollof and beef casaleaf while watching my shows

formatted_address: 3608 14th St NW, Washington, DC 20010, United States
name: Chercher Ethiopian Restaurant and Bar

reviews.text: First time getting Ethiopian food. You know the place is legit when your Ethiopian Uber driver knows it, and everyone else at the restaurant was Ethiopian. We got a couple dishes to share and it was all so flavorful and the spice was perfect. I have no specific recommendations because it was all so good. It is very rich so don't order too much or you will not be able to finish it.

Very friendly service. Delicious food. I got the veggie platter with 10 things. It was really tasty. The awesome part is that it’s all vegan (plant-based). The prices are very reasonable. The food came in a timely manner. High quality Ethiopian food in a pleasant atmosphere with warm and gracious service staff.

There are lots of Ethiopian options in DC (and we’ve tried more than a few), but this one is EXCEPTIONAL. We ordered the Deluxe vegan platter and every dish was fresh and ridiculously flavorful. We also got the #3 meat special and it was so juicy, tender, and delicious we had to order a second one. Save this one in your favorites. 🤤

My friends and I thoroughly enjoyed our meal. The service was great. This was our first time eating Ethiopian cuisine. Our server was very patient in explaining the different meal options. She allowed us to taste the honey wine which was wonderful. The plating and presentation of the food was beautifully done. It was almost too pretty to eat. I would definitely recommend this location to anyone wanting to try Ethiopian food. The atmosphere and attitudes of the servicer was much better than the location on 9th street. We left the other location before ordering to come to the 14th Street location which is the one described in this review.

I’ve had the pleasure of trying international cuisine before, and I remember when this restaurant was just beginning to establish itself. At that time, the name was quite a conversation starter in the neighborhood, as people were curious about what to expect. Fast forward to about 3 or 4 years ago, and it’s clear how fresh and exciting this place still is. The buzz surrounding it has grown, highlighting it as a fantastic Ethiopian restaurant with a cozy sports bar element.

The enticing aromas wafting from the kitchen often give a hint of the delicious dishes being prepared. Furthermore, the prices for the meals remain very reasonable even today. While competition from other restaurants has posed some challenges, I believe this place has the potential to improve and elevate its offerings continuously.

During my visit in early spring this year, I indulged in a feast featuring spicy homemade lamb, beef, greens, and Fufu bread, which was absolutely delightful. I look forward to seeing how they continue to develop their menu and enhance the dining experience!

formatted_address: 1400 Constitution Ave. NW, Washington, DC 20560, United States
name: Sweet Home Cafe

reviews.text: Sweet Home Cafe is located on the inside of the National Museum of African American History and Culture. Unfortunately we didn’t have enough time to experience the food, but so far it looks good and smells amazing. We will definitely revisit.

Disappointing Experience at Sweet Home Café

I was really looking forward to enjoying an authentic soul food meal at Sweet Home Café during my visit to the National Museum of African American History and Culture—but unfortunately, it was a huge letdown.

To start, the collard greens were not only overly sweet (why??), but they were also mixed with mustard greens, which completely threw off the flavor. The macaroni and cheese tasted like something out of a box—mushy, overcooked noodles smothered in what seemed like powdered cheese. As for the fried chicken, I could’ve picked up better from Walmart, honestly. It lacked seasoning, crispiness, and overall care.

I drove two and a half hours from South Jersey, paid tolls and gas, and spent over $160 on food and drinks for my family—only to be served something that felt mass-produced and uninspired. For a place meant to represent the rich culture and history of African American cuisine, this was a major disappointment.

The museum itself is beautiful and moving—no complaints there—but it’s clear that things have changed in the café, and not for the better. Next time, I’ll be grabbing something from the food trucks outside. At least then I’ll know what I’m getting.

Do better.

The food wasn’t authentic Southern food to begin with, and it definitely didn’t taste like it was cooked by someone who knows how to season properly. Overall, this felt like fake Southern food and more like a money-hungry museum capitalizing off the South. Save your money don’t waste it here.

Wow—Sweet Home Café was truly the best soul food I’ve ever had. The moment I stepped up to the counter, I was overwhelmed in the best way possible. There are so many incredible options to choose from—every dish looked like it came straight out of a family kitchen with generations of love behind it.

We ended up trying a little bit of everything (because how could you not?), and every single bite was amazing. From the perfectly seasoned fried chicken to the creamy mac and cheese, to the sweet and tender yams—it was all cooked to perfection. You could really taste the care and cultural heritage in every dish.

We definitely ate—and afterward, we toured the museum, which was a great way to walk it off and soak in the rich history and stories on display. The café complements the museum experience beautifully, offering a taste of the culinary traditions that have shaped African American culture.

Bottom line: I’m 100% coming back. Come hungry, bring friends, and prepare to be blown away.

Sweet Home Cafe – A Soulful Stop Inside a Powerful Museum
Sweet Home Cafe, nestled inside the National Museum of African American History and Culture in D.C., is an absolute must. After immersing ourselves in the museum's moving exhibits, my boyfriend and I stopped here to refuel — and we were blown away.
I had some of the best fried chicken I’ve ever tasted — crispy, seasoned perfectly, and full of flavor. The collard greens are a must-have, and the roasted sweet potatoes were tender, slightly caramelized, and just hit the spot. The portion sizes were generous, and everything tasted homemade with love.
What really made the experience feel special was the atmosphere. The cafeteria is beautiful and welcoming, and it truly felt like visiting family. We noticed employees eating alongside us, smiling, chatting — it felt like a real community space, not just a food court.
Sweet Home Cafe isn’t just a hidden gem for soul food lovers — it’s part of the museum experience. Come hungry, come curious, and don’t miss this spot if you want your heart and stomach full when you leave.
#SoulFood #SweetHomeCafe #WashingtonDCeats #BlackHistory #HiddenGem #FriedChickenGoals #MuseumEats #DCFoodie #EatWithLove #CollardGreensDoneRight

formatted_address: 1201 Pennsylvania Ave NW, Washington, DC 20004, United States
name: Elephant & Castle

reviews.text: I can't speak on its qualiities as a bar, but this location serves as an adequate restaurant. Although the restaurant was pretty full, our food came out pretty quickly and the quality was pretty good. They had several interesting options on the menu, which is refreshing to see. My only downside is that it took awhile before our server greeted us and took our orders, but as stated earlier, it was a busy night. Overall, my party and I had a collectively good experience and it was worth the money (it was not cheap).

Food was super good! The star of the show was definitely the fish and chips. The fish was crispy on the outside, and moist on the inside, and paired really well with the chips. I only wish the serving portion of the fish was a tad larger.

The chicken pot pie was also good. While the filling inside was your regular chicken pot pie filling, the pastry on top was super flaky and not too heavy, which I find to be a problem with many chicken pot pies. The sweet potato fries were surprisingly good too.

Huge shoutout to the bread pudding. They serve it warm, and it was really moist. I usually dislike raisin and rum flavored things, but the rum and raisin flavor on the bread pudding was just right. The serving portion was also huge, and it would definitely take at least 2 people to finish it.

Our server was also super super nice. If I could remember his name I would give him a huge thank you 😭.

My only complaint would be that the air conditioning was rather weak. Granted, the temperature outside was 101 F, and it was really crowded inside, so I understand why it would be hard to keep the restaurant a cool temperature. But, by the end of the meal I was sweating. All in all though, it was a great experience, and I would definitely come again if in the area.

Food here was delicious! The ale onion soup was to die for. The aoli sauce that came with my fish and chips was so tasty 😋 My husband got the chicken wrap and his plate was empty in 2 mins. We sat at the bar so service wasn't the best but the food makes up for that!

Elephant & Castle is a true gem in the heart of Washington, DC. From the moment you walk in, you’re greeted with a warm, welcoming atmosphere that perfectly blends the charm of a traditional British pub with a lively, modern energy. The staff is friendly, attentive, and genuinely eager to make your visit memorable.

The menu offers a fantastic mix of classic pub favorites and contemporary dishes. I highly recommend the fish and chips — crispy, flavorful, and authentically British — as well as their juicy burgers and hearty shepherd’s pie. Their beer selection is outstanding, featuring a great variety of local brews and international favorites. For those who prefer cocktails, their bar staff crafts excellent drinks that perfectly complement the meal.

The food was AMAZING. The service was also amazing. V was our server and he was delightful (I do hope I am spelling that right, apologies if I am not). We ordered a Cesar salad with salmon, fish and chips, and a Shepards Pie. Everything was phenomenal. This was the best meal I have had as well as my group has had in a long time. I highly recommend this restaurant, please go!!!

formatted_address: 1919 9th St NW, Washington, DC 20001, United States
name: Habesha Market Carry Out & Restaurant

reviews.text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Outstanding Ethiopian Food & Amazing Experience!
We’re visiting from Canada and decided to try Habesha Ethiopian Restaurant and it completely exceeded our expectations!
We ordered the injera, beef stew (#37), ribs (#57), and mild lentils, and every single dish was bursting with authentic flavor. The food was fresh, perfectly seasoned, and beautifully presented. You could truly taste the care and tradition in every bite.
The service was just as impressive - warm, attentive, and full of great suggestions that made our meal even more enjoyable. Prices were very reasonable for the generous portions and top quality.
You simply can’t beat this food! If you’re craving real Ethiopian flavors and genuine hospitality, Habesha is the place to go. We’ll definitely be back on our next visit

I love this restaurant SO much. Every single time, everything is delicious. The portions are incredible and so worth it (the best value for the cost that I’ve found in the area). I love the deluxe veggie combo and the sambusas so much! It’s also one of the only things my body can tolerate right now (due to health issues) while still being extremely nutritious AND delicious. Thank you so much for your amazing food!

This is the kind of spot that I had a feeling going in would be awesome. It’s got that mom and pop vibe without crazy decorations or luxury ambiance, which means you know the food is fire.

I’m not too familiar with Ethiopian food so I asked for recommendations. The girl working the front helped me out and I went with the “pick 4” option that allows you to pick 4 meats/veggies.

Food was so good, and i have enough food for the rest of tomorrow as leftovers. Really great pricing too. Awesome spot!

I came to Habesha Market Carryout and Restaurant for the first time. It's an One Stop Shop. The place was clean. The ambience gives an Ethiopian Feel making feel like the establishment is Authentic. I ordered the Lamb Tibs Fir-Fir with Injera. There were plenty of tables to sit. There were Ethiopian People ordering food, which let's me know this place is legit fire. The bathroom was clean. The food was ready quickly and hot. I Loved it.

Very nice, helpful, and supportive staff.  Explained the items/food in the restaurant/menu and was willing to let me be adventurous.  Hole in the vibe with enough, but comfortable waiting area and to sit down and eat.  Food travels fantasticly and cannot state this enough excellent place to get Ethiopian food before hopping on Amtrak. I ordered the fish dullet, minced fish somewhat spicy with salad, yellow lentils, and injera.

formatted_address: 1129 Carrington Ave, Capitol Heights, MD 20743, United States
name: ELMAS Cuisine

reviews.text: So I love African Food I've eating at a lot of African restaurants and let me tell you... GREAT FOOD  taste amazing EVERYTIME went 3 days in a row!!! The service maaann let me tell you!! Sorry to say but African restaurants are NOT known for being the best in customer service.. But here GREAT SERVICE!! GREAT FOOD!! AND not hurt your pocket!!!!! This is Now Amy Spot and will NOT GO ANYWHERE ESLE!!!

Food BOMB I will never go any where else but here..I put my homes on to her and man they were impressed I LOVE african food that's all I eat really.

I'm American and can't stand it anymore lol
Real African Food For Real Africans. Not Black Americans
Wow, they’ve got the best African dishes in the DMV. I’ll definitely come again and again .

I had the best experience when l tasted their food.
I will always go back for some more.

formatted_address: 2010 9th St NW, Washington, DC 20001, United States
name: Ghion Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text:
Stopped here while working a night shift for some takeout, and the service was exceptional. The woman behind the counter brought me water and we had a great conversation while I waited for the food.

When the to-go box came out it was quite literally bursting at the seams with injera, so she recommended I eat some before leaving.

The injera was fantastic, the ribs were flavorful, and the sides (I got string beans and split peas) were to die for. You can't go wrong.

I have never felt so at home while trying to get takeout. I can imagine the service is even better if you dine in.

I went to Ghion because I had never tried Ethiopian food and it was so so so good!! The chicken stew with injera was awesome, and the owners are super nice. I am now a huge fan of Ethiopian food and excited to try it again!

Had dinner here with friends on a Friday night. Had the 7 vege combo with juicy beef between 3 people. Friendly service, the beer was tasty, and the food was delicious. The best I have had. The spicy lentils, collard greens, and beef were just a few of the favourites. I wish I could find a place like this in New Zealand.

This place is amazing. Everyone needs to eat here right now.

I ordered beef jerky and spicy lentils, and instructed the man behind the counter to pick his choice of Ethiopian beers. He brought back St. George, which was delicious. The entire time, his demeanor was incredibly friendly and welcoming.

My meal did not disappoint. Portion size was generous, and included a side of injera. The food was served hot, and the quality was fantastic. I ordered a second beer.

The atmosphere was bright and welcoming, with exposed brick, checkered table cloths, and vibrant colors on the wall. The warmly lit bar area created a friendly and inclusive vibe.

Several times, the man checked on me to ensure I was enjoying my meal. I was enjoying myself and let him know it. He insisted I write this review, and the rest is history. Halfway through writing this review, he brought me another beer, and now I’m done writing this review. And that’s how my night has been going so far.

We went to a show at the 9:30 Club and it had its good points. It was a long drive for us from where we live now and some parts of the evening could have been better. The little Ethiopian joint across the street, however, was amazing. In retrospect, Ghion was the best part of our evening. We stopped in for a bite before the show and I was hoping it would be ok. I had really talked up Ethiopian restaurant food and service. My wife had yet to experience it but the other places I had eaten were good and I was hoping for a repeat. Ghion made me look good. First of all, I defy you to get more stuffed for less money and on food that is that delicious anywhere in the city! We tried SO hard not to eat until we were uncomfortable and neither of us were completely successful. It was Just. So. Yummy! The beef we ordered was (I never use this word) succulent. It was perfectly seasoned and, among the flavors, the cardamom in particular gave the dish a surprising note of sweetness that really rounded it out into something memorable. And, the myriad vegetable dishes that covered our injera-laid table were so flavorful that, had we not ordered meat, I doubt we would have missed it despite being pretty typical American meat eaters. To top it all off, the staff were some of the nicest people I’ve ever encountered in DC. (And, I was born in DC 43 years ago.) I’m not exaggerating or making this up. They held our leftovers AND MY COAT until after the show and hugged us (my hand to G_d, they hugged us) when we came back. No, seriously! In DC! I said, “No, thanks,” to holding our food at first, but it visibly pained our server to throw out what we all know is the best part of the meal (the injera that’s soaked up all that goodness sitting on it)  and I finally agreed. She gave us a huge smile and told us how to turn it into the best breakfast ever. I won’t go into why I couldn’t take my coat into the show but they held that, too. We don’t look like anyone famous and we certainly don’t look like high rollers and I don’t think I’ve ever had better service in a restaurant, even ones where I’m a frequent customer. ...I’m not even sure what better service would look like. That is a good experience! Visit Ghion. If the show across the street isn’t great, Ghion stays open late and they even have a little bar. Cheers!

formatted_address: 13075 Wisteria Dr, Germantown, MD 20874, United States
name: Authentic African Restaurant

reviews.text:
I visited this restaurant yesterday, and it was my second time there. I had previously shared my positive experience with a friend, highlighting how good the food was the first time I visited. On my first visit, I enjoyed the stew fish with jollof rice, although I found it a bit unusual that they used a microwave for some of the food. I generally prefer meals to be made fresh to order, particularly when it comes to fish.

However, my experience yesterday was disappointing. I had the fish and stew with jollof rice and plantain, along with peanut soup featuring goat meat and white rice. My friend ordered okra and pepper stew with pounded yam. Unfortunately, the fish was quite dry and had an overpowering fishy flavor, while the plantain was also hard. The jollof rice lacked flavor, and the stew resembled spaghetti sauce more than what I would expect from a traditional stew, especially given the price. The portion sizes seemed small, with only two scoops of rice and a single scoop of stew, and my fish was served without any sauce.

Additionally, the peanut stew was quite watery, and the goat meat was tough and chewy. The okra appeared to be past its prime, as I noticed some sticks and vines mixed in, and the pounded yam had visible chunks that needed more thorough preparation.

I was genuinely looking forward to a great meal, so this visit left me feeling quite dissatisfied. I think there’s potential for improvement in both the quality and presentation of the food. I would recommend the restaurant focus on enhancing the freshness and flavor of their dishes to better meet customer expectations. At this point, I hesitate to recommend it to others based on my recent experience.

This was a great experience! We were immediately greeted and welcomed. The music was a nice touch and we were able to enjoy a few shows. Our waitress was Josephine and she was kind and friendly, she always checked in to make sure our food was good and if we wanted anything else. The drinks were also amazing. They make a ginger drink with fresh ginger which was strong and bold. It made me feel like my immune system was … . There was also sobolo which had a deep powerful flavor. My favorite was their hibiscus lemonade which was not as strong but had a great flavor. All of their food was outstanding. I enjoyed their peanut butter soup and rice balls. The flavor was great and warmed me up. It felt like I was back in Ghana. This was a great experience and I can’t wait to come back!

I visited this place for the 1st time yesterday with a freind. Im A foodie And an American I feel as if they took me for a fool. I ordered what I thought was the best fish on the menu ( for me) Red Snapper, jolloff rice,and plantains. 30+ dollars and drink their drink made by them.My freind ordered tilapia which was about 8 dollars cheper than my own snapper. My fish was horrible! Dry, no crunch on the tail, old,stale fish in which was the most expensive fish on the menu. I confronted the situation and she said "sorry". With that being said Poor customer service!Because if anything she could've offered my money back or offered one of their snacks (peanuts). I Will Never Go Back! Im really not a person that does reveiws but I felt violated Better Word I felt Scammed! Not only did I eat their to support the establishment I ordered their ginger drink Again,to support the establishment.
Total Bill 71.00 Experiece Priceless!

I would post picture of my food, but it was embarrassing how fast I ate it- man that peanut soup with beef was soo good! So glad I came after the gym. Super tasty and delicious. Amazing, hospitable team! So accommodating! I did carry out, but if I had time I would have dined in. The restaurant was very cute! Lovely decor, big bar! Definitely coming back with friends!

I went here last night and they had a buffet set up. I assumed everything would be held at a safe temp and thereby ready to go. So I selected what I wanted, they put it in a plastic to-go container and then placed said container into the microwave. I told them that I no longer wanted the food and they were very kind and understanding. They still gave me the bean soup since that was held hot and fresh. I also got a ginger drink and really liked it. Next time, I would dine in to be able to try their fresh options. I just found it odd that they microwave food off of their buffet line and I would have liked to know that ahead of time.

formatted_address: 500 H St NE, Washington, DC 20002, United States
name: Sweet Sweet Kitchen

reviews.text: I’m not sure who is cooking over at Sweet Sweet kitchen but I’ve been a customer for 5 years and I have NEVER received food like this! Burnt chicken and some type of sauce on top of my food that was extremely hot that I did not ask for. I am highly disappointed. When did yall start adding stuff without notifying the customer? I’ve been raving about this place all over social media and have sent hundreds of ppl here, just to get jail food in return is a slap in the face. Food was spilled all in the bag as well. Whole plate went in the trash.

Good Caribbean food and one of the best around the DMV area, if you’re in DC stop by, you will not be disappointed. Parking here is a bit tricky and hard to find since it’s only street parking.

5 stars for 5 reasons

1. The Ox tail is super yummy! So tender, soft and juicy meat! Must try! The cassava leaf with oxtail is a bit salty and it tasted kinda fishy but it was still good nonetheless! Good kick to it for sure! The cabbage is simple but delicious! I could it all day.

2. Second reason- When I entered the restaurant we were greeted immediately with smiles. The young beautiful worker was so nice and genuinely seemed to love her job.

3. The price at first seemed kinda high but if you think about it, the food was made with labor of love. It’s not your typical fast food where you pay 15 dollars for frozen packaged food! It’s labor intensive to make the oxtail.

4. They allow you to sample anything you want and they don’t skimped out when giving out samples.

5. The jollof was done to perfection! This ties all the food together and makes this an overall good food experience!

Will come back to try the jerk chicken which I heard was good!

Just left and was very disappointed the young lady was rude and food was trashhhhh… The first time I went I waited 20 mins for cabbage to go with my brown stew chicken after waiting in line the young lady said she was sorry but that she forgot I was waiting and sold the last of the brown stew chicken to someone else… (crazy right) against my better judgement I gave them another try today and was disappointed yet again.. Only got brown stew chicken just to try before I ordered a variation of things like I usually do.. Chicken was full of straight oil no flavor just grease.. A total waste of $20 threw it straight in the trashhhhhh!!! Will never support this place again and will tell everyone I know who will listen about the nasty food and poor customer service!!!

What drew me to this restaurant was the Jamaican flag on the outside. Didn't know what country was the other flag,until I went inside.. found out its Sierra Leone. I decided to ✔ it out, and I was so glad I did. The food did not disappoint, it was well seasoned and flavorful. I had the jollof rice and stew chicken. My first time eating Jollof and I loved it. The staff was very pleasant and inviting. Inside was clean, colorful..was loving the ambiance. They had music playing in the background. I definitely recommend this restaurant, you will not regret it.

Despite the rain all day, they opened on time and food was ready. I like the location because you can find a street parking right there. I came early to have seat in and for a first experience,  I enjoyed it. The food was well ✔ 👍 👌  but what I really wanted was not available yet as it was still cooking: the mighty Ox tail 🙂. Being familiar with it, I will come back for another day. Overall, it is a cozy place to explore. Bon appétit

formatted_address: 1300 I St NW, Washington, DC 20005, United States
name: Kitchen + Kocktails By Kevin Kelley - DC

reviews.text: First time here visiting from Alabama. Waiter "Jermaine" was very detailed and helpful. He made sure my aunt and I had everything we needed. The food & drinks were good and strong. I loveee the Mac n cheese. Peach cobler was not so great. Nice atmosphere and loved the music being played.

My sister and I had the pleasure of dining at Kitchen + Kocktails for the 1st time and it exceeded any expectation we had. Our server, Daryle, was extremely knowledgeable of the menu and everything he recommended was excellent.  His service was fantastic, our glasses stayed filled and our table was cleared as soon as we finished a dish. When you come ask for Daryle! The service was excellent! UPDATE!!! Daryle suggested we go downstairs to listen to the live band that was about to start performing. WHAT A TREAT! Our bartender, Mac, made the MOST DELICIOUS virgin blackberry margaritas for us! He was a great bartender! I'm truly pleased with the evening all the way around! Kudos to the management for hiring such excellent waitstaff!!!

We had friends in town and decided to go for Saturday brunch. There was a lively energetic vibe and the hostess team welcoming. It was hard to hear our server over the music but our order was correct and didn’t take long. I wanted a flight of margaritas but they only serve them frozen—so that didn’t work out. I ended up with the blackberry margarita, which was pretty good. I had the fried porkchop with Asian Hennessy sauce, deviled eggs + shrimp, and fried pickles. Food was good but a bit over salted. Overall a good place to try for the ambience and meeting new people, but the music level makes it hard to have conversations.

This was our first time here and we will definitely be coming back! The food was great, the atmosphere was comfortable, the service was stellar—— just a vibe. Our server, Sheena, was the sweetest and most attentive. She had great recommendations and even helped me find the menu on my phone ( I was struggling lol). Then, there was this peach Dusse drink… oh my… FIRE. Will be back for sure!

From the moment I walked in until the moment I left, the atmosphere and hospitality were outstanding. Mima was my waitress, and she was fantastic—making sure I had everything I needed, from extra sauce to napkins. Her positive energy and attitude truly made my experience a 10/10.
The chef even came out to greet me and make sure I had enough to eat, which I thought was a really thoughtful touch. Overall, the customer service was genuinely a 10/10.

formatted_address: 450 Prospect Blvd, Frederick, MD 21701, United States
name: Jollof On Point

reviews.text: What a great first experience here.  I am not familiar with Nigerian food, but no problem, they give 1st timers samples so you get what you like the first time.  The food was fantastic.  I got the jollaf rice and goat stew and my boyfriend got the fried rice and beef.  It was so good I forgot to take a picture before we dug in.  The prices are good too.  They give you options for different portion sizes, which is perfect for different appetites or if you couldn't decide between you can mix n match.  I also loved that the owner /cook came out to greet us personally and explained how she loves people from any culture to come in and enjoy the food.  You can tell she believes this by the welcoming environment and helping 1st timers pick something they like.  I would strongly recommend giving them a try.  I will certainly come back.

Have ever been to a restaurant, an African restaurant where you eat fufu with your hand and you nearly chew on your fingers? Yes, you read it right. Jollof On Point at the main entrance of the beautifully preserved city of Frederick is a restaurant like no other before. And if I’m telling you you better believe me. I grew up in the countryside of Ivory Coast and my mom was a great cook. So I know when a cook take pride in their art. At Jollof on Point, forget about the tasty food. The atmosphere, so welcoming. The reception is inviting and friendly. The young and sweet lady who serves food is so soft spoken and she even let let taste the dishes before you place your order. That’s how confident they are in their cooking. I go there at least twice a week. And I enjoy every bit of the bite. My favorite is egusi and the goat soup. Lord!
So if you wanna eat real authentic Nigerian cuisine come to Frederick and google Jollof on Point. It’s worth the drive from Dc. You will thank me later.

We threw a Nigerian wedding and catered with Jollof on Point! Our Nigerian food was lovingly catered by Miss Abby, and she was attentive and sweet throughout the entire experience! She ensured that we had a cleanup crew, she served the bride and room and bridal party specifically during the event, and the food itself was delicious. I and my husband were really pleased and honored to work with her, and she was a blessing to have in our lives and have in our celebration.

We’ve been coming to Jollof On Point for over a year now and are ALWAYS satisfied. From the very beginning, Abby and her team have made dining here a truly special experience.

First, they offer samples of different dishes so you can be sure you’ll love what you order—a thoughtful touch that shows how much they care about customer satisfaction. Second, the staff are always courteous, professional, and welcoming. And most importantly, the food is consistently delicious. We’ve tried many different dishes over the past year and loved every single one.

We happily travel nearly an hour just to eat here, and it’s always worth the trip. On top of the wonderful food, the prices are incredibly reasonable for the generous portions and high quality you receive. If you enjoy supporting small business owners who source their ingredients locally, this is absolutely the place for you.

And as if all of that weren’t enough, the heart of this restaurant is Abby herself. She doesn’t just cook amazing food—she pours love into the community. When Abby is in the restaurant, she treats every guest like family and takes the time to genuinely connect with people. That personal warmth is a rare gift that makes this restaurant stand out even more.

If you’re thinking about coming, don’t hesitate. Come once and you’ll be so glad you did—it’s the kind of place you’ll want to return to again and again.

We came to Jollof on Point for the food, but what we received was SO much more. From the moment we arrived, we were welcomed not just as guests, but as family. Abby, the owner and chef, sat with us like an old friend, sharing stories, laughter, and so much heart. Her presence alone is a gift, and you can feel that same love poured into every dish she prepares.

The food is rich, soulful, and deeply nourishing. Their scoop-style approach lets you sample different dishes, and the team invites you to taste before you choose which is something that felt incredibly generous and kind. Every bite tells a story.

It’s hard to put into words just how moved we were by this experience. The flavors were incredible, but it was the warmth, humility, and spirit of the people that stayed with us long after the meal.

This place is more than a restaurant, it’s a reflection of culture, connection, and community. We’re so grateful for the time spent here and can’t wait to return! 🙏🤍✨️

formatted_address: 9300 Annapolis Rd # 201, Lanham, MD 20706, United States
name: Simky African Carryout & Catering

reviews.text: Can’t even take calls. Says open , got there closed and number not available
Food is phenomenal! If you want authentic African food, come here ! ❤️

formatted_address: 1817 M St NW, Washington, DC 20036, United States
name: Fava Pot

reviews.text:
I was researching Egyptian food in DC and Fava Pot kept popping up. After scrolling through their menu and locations, the M Street spot felt like the perfect choice. I’d never had Egyptian cuisine before and wanted to pair it with a full “Destination Egypt” day: first I went to an immersive experience about ancient Egypt and then wanted a taste of the real flavors. Best decision ever.

I found easy street parking just a few blocks away. It was a quick walk to Fava Pot, which is located in the 1800 block of M Street. As soon as you walk in, you’ll find a cozy space filled with Egyptian art and cultural touches that immediately set the tone.

Inside, there’s a small, intimate dining area plus outdoor seating. Ordering is fast and simple with their self-serve kiosk. The menu includes classic Egyptian dishes and an assortment of spreads and small bites like hummus, baba ghanoush, and falafel.

For a late comfort-food lunch, I went with their chicken and mushroom dish in a creamy sauce, served with rice, salad, hummus, and fresh pita. I added a side of their smoky baba ghanoush topped with pomegranate seeds, and wow—everything was fresh, hot, flavorful, and perfectly seasoned.
