One of my favorite parts was the décor: murals and artwork celebrating notable Egyptian figures from entertainment to sports to business. It added a nice cultural depth and made the whole visit feel like an extension of my immersive experience earlier in the day.

Fava Pot ended up being the perfect final touch to a multisensory “Egypt in DC” adventure. I ordered to go, but I’d happily dine in next time I’m in the neighborhood. On the way out, I noticed their display of local accolades, which I took as a good sign. Fava Pot definitely earns its reputation.

I was wandering around DC looking for a good spot for lunch. I saw this place and figured I would try it, as I haven't had Egyptian food in a while.

The food here is fantastic. And the lunch special was quite a deal.

It is a small hole in the wall with a pleasant vibe. Lots of people came in for lunch. The falafel was amazing. Like pure flavor sensation.

Definitely recommend.

Three friends and I are from far out of town and found this restaurant on some reddit list. It happened to be a unique cuisine (Egyptian) and within a 30min walk from our hotel.

Tl;dr: cozy dining room, pretty much self-service. If you don't know what to get, ask Youssef for recommendations: he won't steer you wrong! Standouts: Gollash, the feta with the Fetter Meshaltet, the Hawashei sandwich, the Mosaka bowl and the Kunafa Nutella.

The location was easy to find and the interior was quaint and unpretentious. Wonderful mural highlighting famous and influential Egyptians in our world. We sat in the window which was cozy and out of the way.

Youssef greeted us as we walked in and when We told him that it was our first time having Egyptian food, he gave us menus let us pick our table and then explained what his favorite dishes were in each section of the menu. Since we were four, he recommended that we eat family style, ordering a few dishes and sampling each of them. Best recommendation he could have given! The dishes he recommended were wonderful. There wasn't anything bad that we put into our mouths that he recommended. Even if there were ingredients that we weren't particularly fond of, the dish was still good!

Even though he stood by our table and gave us his recommendations and answered all our questions, we still had to decide what we wanted and go up to the kiosk to order and then help ourselves with utensils and napkins. When the dishes came out, though we were eating family style, they didn't serve us utensils -- except for the Mosaka -- to serve each other family style. So we had to keep getting up to get more utensils for each dish as they came out. If you don't want to order any drinks, they do offer small plastic cups with DC tap water.

From the Starters we had, Macaroni Bechamel (like a macaroni and beef lasagna), Gollash (kinda like a beef quesadilla with flaky phyllo dough), and Fetter Meshaltet (the spicy feta was so flavorful and the honey was thick!) Each of us had our favorites. The Macaroni Bechamel does take a bit of extra time, along with the Mosaka bowl - because they're both baked in the oven.

We also had a few bowls: Mosaka, Chicken Kabob, Kofta, and Egyptian-style Liver. Our liver lover was elated with the liver dish! You can't go wrong with the chicken kabob; all are served over fluffy Egyptian rice, and the kabob is not an Americanized dish at all - still Egyptian flavors and style of cooking: it was very good! For our lamb lovers the kofta was cooked so nicely! The Mosaka was flavorful and the texture was creamy and rich. It worked really nicely with the sides presented.

We also had the Hawashei sandwich. If you're showing up for lunch and want a quick and easy bite, this is our pick! It's grilled and has a nice charred flavor without being too overpowering. And the meat was great! It would be a nice meal to walk and eat with.

The iced mint lemonade was soooooo good! We made sure to savor it and not drink it too quickly.

We finished off with the Kunafa Nutella and the Om Ali Pudding. The pudding had a nice flavor, and came to us warmed and not too hot. I do think it was a little on the soft side. It was the last one of the night, and maybe had sat a little too long, so it was a little goopy, but flavor was perfect! The Kunafa Nutella was amazing. The crispy shredded wheat pastry sandwiching the perfect layer of Nutella, served with the sides of honey syrup and pistachios to top as you like. Even when drenched in syrup the pastry was still crispy and the flavor of the honey syrup didn't overpower the whole thing. The pistachios added another crunchy element to it and brought another layer of complexity or the hazelnut of the Nutella. I'd come back for that dessert!

I was craving something new and different and got lucky to stumble upon fava pot. It gives an authentic Egyption food experience. I had the foul (fava) sandwich and enyption falafel and both were done properly. They were very tasty and the service was very quick. Yousef was great and helped me going through the menu. I like the vibe in this small place and prices are reasonable. Would love to come here again in my future trips to DC!

The restaurant is quaint little restaurant.
Ordering is very convenient on the little tablets.
The staff is very respectful and courteous.
Food was amazing especially the Baba Ghanoush and the Hummus
The Lamb Kofta sandwich is the way to go

formatted_address: 1627 K St NW, Washington, DC 20006, United States
name: Moi Moi

reviews.text:
I absolutely enjoyed myself ! Dining here for my birthday was nothing short of enjoyment. I had the opportunity to meet chef H.O. Personally and the passion he has for what he creates is so refreshing ; he loves what he does and he loves to feed people. And that he did !

Drinks : They do not sell liquor but instead amazing health conscious Mocktails

Some favs:
- Moi moi specialty
- Cucumber mint
- Arnold Palmer

They have a menu option to have a 3 course for $70 per person

Here’s some of the items I had :
- black eyed pea fritter
- smoked turkey sweet potato croquette
- Jerk wings
- Suya Shrimp
- Okra stew

- Jollof
- Lamb chops with Brussels & Mac n cheese

Their new menu is a must have ! Be sure to ask for Cici as she is well knowledgeable of the menu and would put you on to some great favorites

Thank you for having me ❤️will be returning

We really enjoyed our recent experience at Moi Moi. The ambience, food presentation and the mocktails were very flavorful. We had the Grill Shrimp Suya, crispy fried whole sea bass with a Jollof Rice, Sene-Gambian Style Jollof Rice topped with Sour Sour and healthy portion of vegetables Vegetables. Warm/Cold desserts... Chocolate cake with ice cream, Coconut bread pudding, and Pecan pie. A great place to gather with friends, for small meetings, and meet new people. #LoveMOIMOI

My experience here was pleasant, the food was amazing the flavor of the suya was crazy good. The guy that served us was super nice and cool, also love the music that was been played. My only complaint is there should be the option of having the rice with chicken or fish. Unless I'm wrong and I didn't read the menu well to see if they offered it. But in general the food here is amazing.

Let me tell you the food and vibe here was great.  They played a mixture of Afrobeats and R&B music.  It took longer than we expected to get our order taken (20-30 mins after being seated). We came on a Wednesday night, the orange blood and peach Bellini was awesome.  Everything was prepared very well.  I honestly didn’t care for the Jollof rice, my friend didn’t care for it either (he is from Jamaica). Everything else was really tasty.  I would come back again only if I get a different server; he took his time to get to us and seem to have an attitude towards my husband.

I got a chance to go to Moi Moi with my old roommate from college. We good time. I was very critical about their cuisine because I am West African myself. The jerk chicken was the best part of the meal. I was pretty upset of the quality of Jellof fries they served. Although it was good it was nothing like what I am accustomed to and grew up eating. The arugula salad was pretty refreshing. I was a big fan of the drink they had on the menu. The drinks were pretty strong which set off a good tone for the rest of the evening. I personally believe some of the food is overpriced but I enjoyed the meal.

formatted_address: 2800 10th St NE, Washington, DC 20017, United States
name: Pamoja Kitchen

reviews.text: Thank you Chef Phoebe & Frank for an Awesome & Delicious birthday dinner for my Son’s 21st Birthday celebration. Everything was Superb from the Goat stew, Mandazi’s & Samosas. Keep up the great work❤️👏

formatted_address: 1727 7th St NW, Washington, DC 20001, United States
name: Sumah's West African Restaurant

reviews.text: I read the reviews so I was prepared and able to exercise patience in order to enjoy my visit. It took a long time for us to be seated (like 10 min of being ignored) and way longer for the waitress to come over to get our order. She brought a sample plate since my friend never had west African food before. I loved getting to taste everything so that I could see which dishes they really do well. We ended up ordering pepper soup (with cow foot), egusi, and palava sauce. All of it was AMAZING!! I also tried the ginger juice since I wasn’t aware it was BYOB and neglected to bring a bottle. The owner was very nice and we thoroughly enjoyed our visit. The food was much better than it was at Appioo. I’ll definitely be back!

Amazing authentic food in a humble setting. The owner takes customer service to the extreme!   When we went to leave it started raining and he insisted that we borrow his umbrella!  Portions are large and delicious. I highly recommend this restaurant!

The food is delicious, a real authentic West African cuisine. Jollof Rice, white or brown rice served with different sources made out of Okra reach in Iron called Okra Soup, Sweet Potatoe Leaves and Greens both of which are very rich in Vits A, C & B6, Riboflavin and fiber. They have egusi Soup, Pounded Yam, Foofoo, Goat meat soup but above all I enjoyed the Cassava leaves the most cooked in rich Western African palm Oil.

Best African restaurant ever! I'm from Houston, I'm just visiting DC for a couple days and I had to tried it. I had heard so many things about this place and I was so excited to try it. Don't listen the haters guys. This place deserves 10 🌟. Great costumers services. I had a great experience. Ms Sumah looks like my mom btw lol. Anyway, I enjoyed  and believe me you will as well.
While I was very excited to visit, turns out this restaurant has been closed for a few years now. Bummer

formatted_address: 2000 5th St NE, Washington, DC 20002, United States
name: Bantu Fusionz

reviews.text:
Unique and delicious food. We was on vacation in DC with My family and my little boy was hungry, we ordered the wings for him and trust me, he ate up everything. He aint that person normally, thats how tasty they were.
The group platter for us, was the best.
I will definitely order again
The food is fantastic. The aroma of African dishes, woowww. Everything in Bantu Fusionz feels personal. Thanks for the treat. We shall come again.
Eating from Bantu fusions brings back those home memories 😊.I would definitely recommend anyone around Washington DC area to make an order with BANTU FUSION you will thank me later!!!🤝
The food is excellent. If you have not tried it, make sure you  get your plate August 30th. You will not regret.
Really great meals. I enjoyed the mix of spices and the interesting spread. The Fish dishes are mu favorite.

formatted_address: 6000 Greenbelt Rd, Greenbelt, MD 20770, United States
name: Jodeem African Cuisine

reviews.text: The customer service is awesome. The food is 10 out of 10. I had the stew chicken with plantain and rice delicious and the Moimoi. It had a nice spice to it, but not overwhelming. It wasn’t just heat. It was a lot of good flavor so everything was balanced and complementary. Would definitely come back here and tell others if you’re in the area to give it a try it is so worth it.

Unfortunately I should’ve stuck to my usual spot that I go to for good African eats instead of listening to ppl on Tik Tok. The Egusi is extremely watery with chunks of what I’m assuming is beef that is so tough it will break your teeth. A bunch of bones that aren’t noticeable so you will be spitting them out and to top it off I specifically asked for rice and received a big ball of some white stuff? I tried the cassava leaf years ago and it was decent. 0/10 do not recommend the egusi but you may have a different experience so try this place if it’s in your stomach to do so.
First time visit!!  GOD BLESS YOU!!  Every stew is delicious. Bitterleaf with fish & Amala; Isi ewu (goat) with Garri.  Hearty, smoky, satisfying!!  Looking forward to my next visit.

I ordered the cassava leaf with chicken over rice. The cassava leaf was watery, no palm oil, very fishy tasting. The rice no flavor; i am use to african restaurants serving either jollof rice or jasmine rice. The stew chicken was not peppery or juicy or much of authentic taste. Was very disappointed. All food was discarded and not eaten.

Jodeem Jodeem.
It’s one thing to move to a new land and it’s another to start your own business in a new land. It’s definitely another scenario having a successful business in this new land!

However Mr. Jodeem has achieved this remarkable task.

I’ve been a regular here for several years.
The food is always fresh
The staff is attentive & friendly.

I have so much joy in knowing delicious food similar to food from my original country is right around the corner.

I’m a fan of the fish stew with red sauce. I love the puff puff!
I’ve just been introduced to the pepper soup which pairs well with this time of year.
Thank you Mr. Jodeem and your wonderful team!

formatted_address: 1100 W Patrick St Ste M, Frederick, MD 21703, United States
name: Ayoka African Cuisine

reviews.text:
Kind people, simple atmosphere and amazing food. A friend from the Ivory Coast brought me here to try the cuisine for the first time.

The garba is a great beginner dish, with a generous portion of blackened tuna steak, couscous, and vegetables.  If you like strong ginger beer, you'll enjoy their homemade ginger drinks.  Five hours later, I'm still feeling full and satisfied.

The staff are very friendly and helpful... dont be afraid to ask questions if you're a newbie like myself.

We were traveling through the Washington, D.C., area on the way to Vermont.   We stopped for dinner at this small African restaurant (we had originally thought it was an Ethiopian restaurant, it is an African restaurant with a west African emphasis).  The decor is simple and they play African tunes as background music.  We ordered the grilled tilapia fish, pounded plantains, rice, and a special sauce. The fish, a fish's head, was good.  There are vegan options on the menu, but they are only available during the weekend (we were there on a weekday night). These service is friendly and definitely African. We were able to talk to our waiter about the cuisine and his background, he was from Ivory Coast.

The food was good, but the online ordering system was very confusing. I placed an order for pickup, but when I arrived, they had no record of it. I ended up waiting another 20 minutes for them to prepare the food.

This was my first time dining at this restaurant, and I had a pretty good experience overall! The gentleman at the cash register provided excellent customer service. He was super patient while I was figuring out my order and helped clarify the menu for me.
I went for the Yasa Chicken with rice and couldn't resist adding some Puff Puff to my order. The Puff Puff was served piping hot, and I just had to take a bite right away—so delicious! The rice was cooked to perfection, and the caramelized onions and veggies really elevated the dish, giving it a wonderful flavor. Plus, the portion size was great for the price!
While I enjoyed most of my meal, I found the chicken a bit dry and hard, and it felt like it might have been reheated from the previous day. I was also hoping for a little more heat or spice in the dish. As a fan of authentic African food, I was surprised that this dish didn’t have any spicy kick or peppers.
All in all, I think this restaurant is definitely worth a visit, as there are some tasty options on the menu. I believe in giving a place at least two tries, so I'm looking forward to coming back and sampling another dish!

Yummy jollof rice with a wonderfully spiced and sauced chicken and a generous lunch portion. Started with Fataya - an empanada-like appetizer in fish, chicken or beef......so good! My guest had the fried snapper and he really enjoyed it!

formatted_address: 2808 Portobello Ct, Waldorf, MD 20603, United States
name: Oreofe African Cuisine

reviews.text: I found this place from heaven on Google maps and when I say I have eaten food and 42 states I have this woman and her catering service is by far the best food in America that is from Nigeria. I totally suggest you trying her food and ordering her catering service because the food is delicious. You get exactly what you pay for and I can tell you now the service is impeccable.

I contacted Oreofe African cuisine for their surprise food package for my husband. We ordered for the largest food tray and included the talking drum and saxophonist. She was able to work with our day/time despite it being a work day. The surprise was a surprise not only to my husband, but to myself due to the fact that Oreofe delivered a top notch service. The food was delicious and yummy the packaging was amazing, live music etc. Everything was a money well spent🙌🏽 Also, we were not expecting the Saxophonist to give us some live music. It felt like we are in owanbe in our living room. My husband kept saying he felt like he was in Nigeria.
She is highly recommended and i will be using her service again.

Before tasting Oreofe African Cuisine's "Amala on Spot" I had not eaten abula for 25+ years and could have gone the rest of my life without it. However, one taste of her abula and I've been hooked. It was so delicious! Once you taste her food, I dare you to stop at one plate. Every time I host an event, Oreofe Cuisine is my go-to caterer. From gizdodo, to jollof rice, asaro, stewed fish and so many other options, her food has been consistently delicious.

She is very responsive and will have your food ready on time. Looking forward to placing many more orders at Oreofe African "oh-so-delicious' Cuisine.

Services was excellent and very timely. The food tasted so natural, like back home, we got our early morning surprise breakfast and other African food ordered were delivered timely...for a natural tasty African food Oreofe African Cuisine is d best in the DMV Area.
Oreofe African Cuisine is your plug for authentic Nigerian meals. I ordered a few dishes from her and they were so delicious, will definitely be ordering again.

formatted_address: 12425 Hedges Run Dr, Lake Ridge, VA 22192, United States
name: Asanka Delight Restaurant

reviews.text:
Let me add my voice to the many positive reviews already shared. Asanka Delight is truly one of the best Ghanaian restaurants I’ve visited outside of Ghana. The menu features a wide variety of popular Ghanaian dishes, paired with authentic homemade Ghanaian drinks.

I ordered yam with egusi stew and enjoyed every single bite. While my personal favorite is yam with kontomire stew, the egusi was a delicious alternative that did not disappoint.

The pricing is reasonable and suits all budgets, making it accessible for everyone. I highly recommend Asanka Delight for anyone looking to experience the true taste of Ghana. Pay them a visit - you’ll be glad you did!

It was really good. My partner and i got jollof rice with tilapia and peanut butter soup. The soup was thinner than ive had before but it was still flavorful and aromatic. Their jollof rice also settled the nigeria v ghana jollof race for me. CLEARLY Ghanaian is better. It was 43 after tax

I got the waakye and Volta special. Every thing tasted fresh and homemade. They customer service was also lovely.

Waakye - perfect if you love soft waakye. They give a large portion with angel hair spaghetti, gari, protein and plantain. I wish it included an egg as well. It was tasty and the beef was extremely tender.

Volta Special - basically okra soup with banku. It’s okra soup so it has that nice slimy draw which I love. It was a nice mix of crab, shrimp, fish and beef.

I stopped through this restaurant after grocery shopping. What a delightful surprise! I ordered the Volta Special (gumbo) with white rice. It took awhile but it was worth the wait. The perfect amount of heat and spices. If you don't like the slime of okra, this dish is not for you. I will return because it was delicious!!! Huge portion, expect to take some home ... or bring a friend!

Service was pleasant. Great vibes and nice atmosphere as well. Plenty of parking.

I’ve always wanted to try Fufu, and I’m so glad we found this spot! The flavors were incredible, the meat was perfectly tender, the soup was rich and comforting, and the fufu was everything I hoped it would be. The service was genuinely warm and welcoming, and the cozy atmosphere made the whole experience even better. I also tried Puff Puff for the first time, which was absolutely delightful, like a cross between cornbread and mochi. I could’ve easily eaten a dozen! 10/10, I’ll definitely be back to explore more dishes.

formatted_address: 1924 Pennsylvania Ave NW #3607, Washington, DC 20006, United States
name: Founding Farmers DC

reviews.text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Founding Farmers DC

Thanks. Emerson M for taking care of us today. I am really appreciated 👍👍

I had a great dining experience at Founding Farmers DC. The restaurant is well known for its farm-to-table concept, and you can really taste the quality and freshness of the ingredients.

I ordered the Uncle Buck’s Beignet French Toast and the Eggs Benedict with Crab Cake, and both dishes were absolutely delicious. The French toast was rich, fluffy, and perfectly sweet, while the crab cake Benedict was generous in portion and full of real crab meat. The poached eggs and hollandaise sauce were done just right.

The atmosphere was warm and lively, making it a great spot for brunch or a relaxed meal. Service was friendly, attentive, and efficient throughout our visit. Overall, this is a fantastic place to eat in Washington, D.C., and I would definitely come back again.

This was a very pleasurable experience.  I have been meaning to try this food for quite some time and my was it worth the wait. The environment was engaging. Our server Emerson was exemplary. The food was outstanding and very fresh. Drinks were phenomenal. Mimosas were exceptional and the freshness and flavor of food was like my taste buds was doing a ballet dance. I will definitely be back. Might make it a bday trip there. Keep up the great work. See you soon!!

Came in for lunch with no reservation and they seated us right away. The staff were really friendly! They had a wide variety on the menu so we started with the fig and prosciutto appetizer. It was excellent! I had the goat cheese ravioli with chicken cutlets, the goat cheese was creamy and blend of flavors was excellent. I highly recommend!

Went to Founding Farmers for a pre-Kennedy center Messiah sing along early dinner.  Promptly seated in the bar area.  The bartender (my waiter, sorry dude I forgot your name and didn't get a receipt) was awesome.  Not pushy, not over the top, just the right amount of customer service.  As it was happy hour, I ordered the deviled eggs and the fried green tomatoes for appetizers.  The deviled eggs were just "meh" nothing special.  The fried green tomatoes were awesome.  Came with a guacamole-type relish (accoutrement?) and an herbed cream cheese relish (I think it was cream cheese anyway).  Both were on point.
I had asked the bartender about a couple items I was looking at for dinner, and he was pretty forthcoming about what he thought would be good....I ordered the blackened blue catfish and it absolutely did not disappoint.  Be forewarned if you don't like spicy don't order this, the blackening season is fire *but also excellent*  Only issue I had with the catfish:  the cheesy grits seemed different (I want to say "off" but it's not like they were bad, there was just something about them that didn't seem right...I can't put my finger on it though).
For an early Tuesday afternoon (4-ish) this place was pretty busy.  Ambiance was cool, but sitting close to the front door kept it fairly drafty (sure I could have kept my coat on but who eats with their coat on?)
all in all a great meal.  I'd definitely go back!

A downtown restaurant, very close to the White House. The place is large, spread over two floors, and well designed inside, featuring a piano bar and a central counter.

The staff is quick, friendly, and efficient in answering any questions about the dishes. The food is excellent, and the prices are in line with what is offered. Both the sandwich and the meat platter were outstanding.

And if you want to finish on a high note, the cream-filled profiteroles are simply fabulous. Six big, delicious ones—I ate them all.

A small note: I would suggest adding a cutlery rest, and also serving more Brie in the Brie-and-apple appetizer—it was almost invisible.

Highly recommended!

formatted_address: 11454 Cherry Hill Rd, Beltsville, MD 20705, United States
name: RAHAMA AFRICAN RESTAURANT

reviews.text: When I ordered though Uber eats the order would be messed up. So I started ordering directly though the restaurant. Today I ordered Kenken, friend fish and an extra order of friend fish. One of the kenkens arrived opened. I called the restaurant and Fati offered to reimburse me $2 and some change on an order that cost over $30 when you include the delivery fee. The restaurant provided me with food already opened and I could not eat it. Fati hung up on me and never returned my call. Horrible customer service. I don’t live in MD and won’t waste my gas to go in person and continue to discuss.

Customer service is horrible from the little loud mouth girl in the back to the big man rushing orders out. I don’t think these people are smart enough to acknowledge just bc you talk about your customers in another language, doesn’t mean we can comprehend your body and eye language as negative. You would think you would be a little friendlier to the people who keep you in business.

As someone who loves to explore different foods, I tried fufu and stew at this spot. My first experience wasn’t great—I had the goat soup/stew with friends which was slimy and with not good flavor, and we didn’t enjoy it much. But last week, I tried the peanut soup with fufu, and it was amazing. I’ll definitely order it again whenever I’m in the mood for fufu. The service is a bit slow, likely because the place is so busy.

My family is Liberian and I was craving some good african food. My friend reccomended this restaurant and I tried it for the first time today. The food was awesome! I had Fufu and Peanut soup and a order of Palm Nut soup. The fufu nice and soft, both soup was very tasty and seasoned. Each entry is enough for two or three servings. I wish the meat in the soups were cut smaller, they both had three large portion, but was very good. I will definitely return and try something else. The lady behind the counter was also friendly and helpful. I give them 4 stars, took of one because of the meat portions but excellent food
Food is very good, I have been here 3 times. The only problem is the lady who takes food orders is always on her phone or has an earpiece on while talking and taking orders. This can be discouraging

formatted_address: 1201 28th St NW, Washington, DC 20007, United States
name: Das Ethiopian Cuisine

reviews.text:
First time in DC ,and tried Ethiopian food for the first time — .  This place is amazing, the food was so good . Best food I believe I’ve ever had ! Im not sure why I never tried it , maybe because the closest one to my home town is a 2 hour drive !
The Injera was a pretty cool, Im an immigrant myself so for me to try new foods is my go to !!! Eating with my hands felt like a sin ,but it was the coolest experience. **Injera is a sourdough flatbread with a porous texture, traditionally made with teff flour, used as both a plate ,and eating utensil. Staff was great, the atmosphere was perfect! I really wished I had more room to try the dessert, I can only imagine how tasty that would have been — next time I guess ! Im very happy to have randomly walked into not knowing how happy Id be leaving ! I cannot say enough about this place ! If you haven’t tried it yet you’re missing out . We ordered the meat sampler with short ribs . Mmm mmm mmmmm

We visited DAS Ethiopian Restaurant in DC for the second time with our family, and it was excellent again. The food is authentic Ethiopian and truly delicious. I especially loved the spicy beef dish the staff recommended—super flavorful and very spicy, just how I like it!

Service was outstanding and family-friendly. Since we had our child with us, they immediately provided a high chair, brought out complimentary rice for the little one, and even offered crayons so kids could draw on the paper-covered table. These thoughtful touches made dinner so much easier and more enjoyable.

DAS has also been recognized by the Michelin Guide with a Bib Gourmand award, which highlights restaurants that serve excellent food at a great value. Compared with very traditional spots, DAS keeps the cuisine authentic while presenting the dishes in a more refined, creative way.

Overall, we highly recommend it—especially if you enjoy bold, spicy flavors. It’s authentic, family-friendly, and Michelin-recognized. We love this restaurant and will definitely keep coming back!

We had dinner there, and it was amazing. The host was super-accommodating, and the waitress and staff were excellent. Everything is done family style, so the menu choices come on a single large plate while everyone gets their own injera bread. The waitress was great in pointing out what combos and selections had redundancies, so we were able to try out something different with each choice. We even met the owner, Mr. Alifom, which was really cool (after seeing him on PBS, he was kind of a celebrity to us).

Wonderful place, go here.
We had Chicken doro Kay wat  and shrimp tibs were fantastic. Sadly we were so full and couldn’t try the dessert.

We had an incredible Ethiopian lunch experience, post a morning of walking through the Tidal basin, watching cherry blossoms.

We got a few vegetarian entrees to share and one chicken entree among the non-vegetarians.

The injira was soft, supple and delicious.

formatted_address: 7317 Georgia Ave NW, Washington, DC 20012, United States
name: Gidi Chow

reviews.text:
I ordered the noodles with fat (beef) suya.  All the pieces of beef were fat smh.. every last piece.  The plantains were burnt.

The shawarma I ordered had sticks INSIDE of the wrap.

The woman taking our order was pleasant.

The atmosphere… ATROCIOUS.  So many young children loitering outside.  When we were placing our order, young folks were in our personal space and they were not even ordering.

Needless to say, the food was subpar and did not live up to the expectation.  Will not be visiting again.

The 3rd picture below is the suya we picked through to eat and every piece is fat.

My experience at Gidi chow was quite an amazing one. The restaurant's ambiance was warm and inviting, with afrobeats music playing softly in the background. The red spicy decor caught my eyes.

But what truly stole the show was the food. The Gidi burger combo especially for me.The Gidi noodles with suya also stood out for me as well. The meat was tender and flavorful, with just the right amount of spice. The Jollof Rice was perfectly cooked and seasoned. The fried plantains were sweet and caramelized.

The service at the restaurant was also top-notch, with friendly and knowledgeable staff who were happy to explain the different dishes and make recommendations. The portions were generous and the prices were very reasonable for the quality of food we received.

Overall, I highly recommend Gidichow to anyone looking to explore Nigeria’s street food at its finest.. It was a truly memorable dining experience that I can't wait to repeat.

Been African and haven’t been home in a while and seeing a taste of home away from home, I had to check it out. I have mixed feelings, a tad disappointed but kudos to the management for the idea. It’s giving home, very mindful and demure😁. BUT the quality is the food isn’t it at all, i ordered noodle,egg and beef suya and turkey suya. The noodle is a little salty and spicy so if you love spicy food then this will make you sweat. The beef is tasty but dry and same with the turkey suya. The turkey suya tasted like it was made days ago and it was warmed too long and the moisture is sucked out. I will give this place another try and see if anything changes. You can make your recommendation based on this review.

Omg I found a new plug . I had fried yam and plantain and turkey .  I requested my turkey separate but the yam and plantain with sauce wow is all I can say . This food is good  . I
Trying more delicacies 🤤 from this store .

I am impressed with the overall quality, portion size & taste of the food. This spot also has been nothing but sweet vibes any time I have visited. And, that Gidi Burger?! Hmm..the way I devour it! I highly recommend giving this place a shot. You won’t regret it!

formatted_address: 1967 Calvert St NW, Washington, DC 20009, United States
name: Mama Ayesha's Restaurant

reviews.text: It was my first time here. I was seated immediately and my server, Mohammed, was attentive, pleasant, and extremely helpful with helping me select my meal. I had the hummus, kibbeh, musakhan, white wine, baklava, and some lemon ginger tea. Everything was made from scratch and delicious!! The chef came out and asked how everything was and also gave me a little history on the place. They've been open for 75 years and have had presidents come and eat there, I can definitely see why. I highly recommend this restaurant and will be returning there in the near future!

Food:
The Bamiya (okra/lamb) bowl was filled with okras and exactly 3 pieces of meat. A LOT of okra and little meat. The lamb is what makes okra dish tasty!
The eggplant dish was heavy and plating was poor for the $23 they charge for it!

Service: took close to 40 minutes for food to arrive, had to wave at waiter to get water glasses refilled. Waiters overworked and under trained.

Atmosphere: they charge upscale restaurant prices but neither the atmosphere nor the food lives up to expectations and prices

I really wanted to like this place. The exterior is super cute, the interior has, for the most part, the structure of a place with charm and actual thought into the decor. In fact, I was so excited that I took the risk of bringing a visitor from outside DC this evening to try it.

However, the food was just bland and not good. The hummus, baba ghanoush, and foole tasted like what I could get from Costco for cheaper. The mujadarah was decent but the rice was not spiced well, just the onions.

But honestly what really annoyed us was that all of our food was vegetarian and when we additionally ordered grape leaves that we specified were vegetarian as well, we were served lamb grape leaves. When we told the waitress that we ordered vegetarian grape leaves, she asked us "Are you sure?" We were taken aback by this comment. I do think that the waiter that we asked about the grape leaves did mishear, and that's not his fault. But the waitress this evening asking us if we were sure we ordered vegetarian food when all the food on our table was vegetarian was offensive. Additionally, we felt the service was not attentive. Drinks came after our mezze, and water was only refilled once.

On the way out, I noticed that the fountain that was probably once gorgeous and a centerpiece was very dirty on the bottom, and the brush to clean it was serendipitously lying at the bottom of the fountain as well. This felt sad to see. You could tell that the interior and exterior were at one point designed so thoughtfully, and the food at one point must have been amazing and homemade. But everything, including us and our tastebuds, felt like an afterthought.

I think this is the most disappointed I've been in a restaurant in a while given my expectations going in.

Great food & service.  Everything we ordered was delicious, but the Zahir cauliflower is my personal favorite.  Was able to accommodate our large party in a reasonable amount of time.  Just FYI, there is a 3% charge for paying with a credit card.

We had a lovely time here for a Saturday dinner. Comfortable environs and pleasant service. The food was excellent. I recommend getting several appetizers to share, and picking things that might seem unfamiliar on the menu. We tried the halloumi, sausages, labneh, and the lentil/rice dish and a combination of stuffed items. All was excellent. Our drinks were quite good as well, highly recommend the pomtini. We will certainly come back.

formatted_address: 8730 Cherry Ln #4, Laurel, MD 20707, United States
name: The Hunger Tamer

reviews.text: The food was okay for me. I ordered attieke nd it came with no seasoning at all.  Nd then they put maggi on it to make up for it lol. The goat meat also  had no seasoning it tasted bland but soup was mid. My issue is the lady that was taking our order was very rude. She very aggressive and kept cutting us off. On top of all that she was rushing us when we were ordering.  I hope people know this business comes with service.

My first time eating here and though I ordered via the app, the owner was very inviting and considerate by tracking my order and giving me updates. My order was ready 10 minutes earlier than expected and the food was outstanding. Let's just say I inhaled everything on my plate. Will certainly be back!
Thank you.

After coordinating for catering services, the point of contact ghosted me. Very unprofessional when I was going to spend almost $2000 at this establishment for my wedding. They need better processes for catering. It was a major inconvenience to try to find someone else last minute.
———
Update after response from owner: the owner did tell me they had a family emergency on Sept 24. That night they provided the quote for my order. On Sept 25, the following morning I asked how should I pay and get a contract. On Sept 29 I sent a follow up text. On Sept 30, anxious because my wedding is Oct 18, I offered family condolences and asking if someone on her team could help me instead. I got no response whatsoever, so I rushed to find another caterer at short notice.
I have ordered from here a number of times. The food is always delicious. They offer a very small seating section for indoor dining but its always best to order your food to go/pick up.

So I’m Nigerian and the food here is made by a wonderful Ghanaian woman and wow I can’t lie the lady can cook !

I had to try a bit of everything to make sure i had something I liked. To my surprise I loved everything ! I got the jollof and this is probably the only place I’ve had good Ghanaian jollof like good to the point where I plan on coming back. The efo(spinach) , pounded yam, egusi my gosh it was all made to perfection even the meat and fish were 10/10.

I hate meat pie all meat pie Nigerian Ghanaian Cameroon dc I don’t like it but something said just give this place a try ! And I’m so glad I did because this is the best meat pie to touch this earth now I plan on making this my go to place when I need meat pies catered for an event. Everything was seasoned to perfection the portions were the right size and my food was even still hot when it go to me through delivery.

Rating this restaurant a 12/10 !

formatted_address: 2108 8th St NW, Washington, DC 20001, United States
name: Doro Soul Food

reviews.text:
I had a good time at Doro Soul Restaurant:

Honestly, I would have rated everything 5/5 if it weren’t for the buttery taste in the chicken. I wish the chef offered an option to choose between oil or butter for the chicken marinade. The flavor was a bit too heavy for me and my husband. That said, I think it’s an acquired taste, so everyone should try it for themselves.

What a unique concept that's executed perfectly! A takeout spot through a small window just north of U Street NW, Doro Soul Food takes some classic favorite dishes like fried chicken and mac and cheese and adds a Ethiopian twist.

I ordered the chicken tenders and they were perfectly fried. The breading is full of flavor and crispy while the meat remained juicy. So good! The mac and cheese was very, very good too. It may be my favorite in the city.

If you need comfort food with Ethiopian spices, go here!

Fantastic experience. It can be a challenge finding parking but the trip is worth it. There’s a wonderful atmosphere with very friendly and helpful staff, and the food is fantastic. Everything we had was delicious. My wife and I had the alicha char-grilled Doro plate, turmeric Cole slaw, collard greens (best I’ve ever had), sweet potato fries, berbere fries, and a goden taco. I would say even if you are a big meat eater, the goden taco is a MUST HAVE. For a veggie taco the flavors were spot on. Down is definitely a keeper!  Probably the only downside is parking can be difficult, street parking in DC. But go for it.

I'd been hearing the buzz about Ethiopian fried chicken made by a Michelin starred chef and had to give it a shot. I went with the 3-piece dark chicken combo. I'm not exaggerating when I say this might be the best fried chicken I've ever had.

The breading was perfectly crisp with just the right amount of salt, and the chicken itself was incredibly juicy and flavorful. I ordered it "hot" and it had a nice kick without being overwhelming. I'll probably go up a heat level next time. This is the kind of chicken that's absolutely worth breaking your diet for.

The mac and cheese had a little crunch to it, which gave it a unique texture. I also tried the lemonade. It was alright but could've used a bit more sugar.

You can grab a seat next door at Le Melange, order from Doro Doro, and enjoy your food there.

I met my cousin, who flew in for a conference. I hadn't seen her in almost a decade, as she lives in Arizona. Our bartender was extremely attentive, kind ans funny. The food was sublime and the location is a pure gem near Howard Hospital ans 930 club. Highly recommend if you want to be treated with top tier customer service.

formatted_address: 701 9th St NW, Washington, DC 20001, United States
name: Zaytinya

reviews.text: A fantastic experience. The space was wonderfully bright and open. A lot of blues and whites with a good eye for art and accents. We went for a special occasion and it delivered. The food was spectacular and very well balanced. We had the set brunch for menu for 2 and found it to be a good value(70 for the both of us). We were absolutely stuffed and had to take some home. Service made a couple of mistakes but all of them were addressed quickly and respectful (I think this was due to having a server who was training, so we completely understood). The drinks were also very well done. Over all a fantastic lunch.

Took the wife here today for her birthday. We did the chefs tasting menu. Man let me tell you this place was absolutely phenomenal!

From the moment we were seated, to the service we received and the food. Everything was perfectly prepared and presented. I even mentioned in the reservation that it was my wife's birthday. They brought out a separate cake dessert aside from our chefs menu dessert. We were blown away by everything.

If you're looking for a solid and delicious experience, especially for a celebration, absolutely come here! We will be back for sure!

Went to this restaurant sort of during lunch and dinner hours, and it was perfect. A lot quieter, service was good, and food was tasty. Try not to fill up on the pita because the food entrees are delicious. We tried the grilled platter, falafels and cauliflower. Their hummus was good too. If you pay using their QR code, they even provide a complimentary Lyft ride!

The atmosphere and vibe were great—very spacious, open, clean, and filled with natural light from the large windows. There were plenty of seats available as well. However, the food quality was disappointing. Maybe we expected too much, but aside from the French fries, which were good, the rest of the dishes fell short.

The octopus was overly burnt, and  I took one bite of the octopus and couldn’t eat any more. When we mentioned this to the staff, they replaced the dish with a less-burnt version, which we appreciated.

The seabass portion was extremely small—smaller than my hand—and tasted like a frozen fish you could easily find at a grocery store.

The cost of all food menu here was quite cheap, like the main menu items are around $20–30 each or about $75 for a course menu. We could understand when we see the cost, but I believe that they can definitely improve the quality of the food better.

Another thing to note: although there were many staff members, most of them were standing around chatting and playing phone. They didn’t greet or acknowledge customers when entered, Although the servers who took our order and helped us throughout the meal were kind and attentive.

We chose Zaytinya for our anniversary dinner, and it turned out to be an absolutely wonderful experience. The ambiance was elegant yet warm—perfect for a special occasion—and the service was attentive without being intrusive.

As vegetarians, we were genuinely impressed by the variety and creativity of the vegetarian options. Every dish we tried was beautifully presented and full of bold, balanced flavors. The mezze-style plates made it easy to sample multiple items, and each one stood out in its own way—fresh, thoughtfully seasoned, and clearly made with high-quality ingredients.

The staff made our anniversary feel special, from helpful recommendations to the overall hospitality. Zaytinya delivered not just a meal, but a memorable dining experience. Highly recommended for vegetarians and for anyone looking to celebrate a special occasion with exceptional food and atmosphere.

formatted_address: 250-252 Leith Walk, Edinburgh EH6 5EL, United Kingdom
name: Uwagboe’s Kitchen & Grill - Leith Walk (Nigerian Restaurant and Bar)

reviews.text:
This is by far the most beautiful Nigerian restaurant in Edinburgh . The customer service was impeccable and the food?? Absolutely delicious.  🤤

They had varieties to choose from and our palate were delighted.  Thanks to the server (RANGA)  who wasn’t only efficient but equally pleasant.  Highly recommend 💯

I visited Scotland and found this restaurant on TikTok, i was not disappointed. Food was so good, fresh and it was served quick. Ranga was our server and he made us feel welcome and taken care of. He was kind, attentive and respectful, i will definitely come back here and tell others about it.

The receptionist was great; he's welcoming (I think his name is Parang, but I'm not sure if I spelled it right 🫣). The food tasted nice; we had Abula. I must confess that this was only the second time I've tasted Abula in my life, and the first time was horrible. However, eating it at this restaurant was a nice experience, and I didn't have any stomach upset afterward, which is a major concern for me when eating out. I'll definitely recommend this place, especially since I read good reviews online, which encouraged me to it.

Uwagboe's kitchen and grill is the real deal, seriously. As a Nigerian, I honestly felt like I was back home with every bite. The service was super good, (thanks to Ranga who was very professional and polite), and the food was even better. Plus, it's surprisingly cheap for how classic and delicious everything is. You definitely gotta check this place out if you're looking for an authentic and satisfying meal.

The food was really good, the music excellent and the environment beautiful!! However the best thing was the service. The person serving us was so kind and helpful, we will go again for sure! Highly recommended!!

formatted_address: 5321 Ager Rd, Hyattsville, MD 20782, United States
name: Kitchen Near You

reviews.text:
I stopped by Kitchen Near You recently, and I gotta say—it lived up to the hype. This place is definitely one of those hidden gems where the flavor speaks for itself. I met up with a couple friends, and we were all impressed with how fresh and well-seasoned everything was. The menu has a really nice variety, but it doesn’t feel overwhelming—they clearly know what they do well and they stick to it.

I ordered the wings and mac and cheese, and both hit the spot. The wings were crispy on the outside, juicy on the inside, with a sauce that wasn’t just sweet or hot—it had real flavor behind it. The mac and cheese was rich and creamy, not dry or bland like you sometimes get at other spots. You could tell it was made with care, not just scooped out of a tray.

Service-wise, everything was smooth. The staff was friendly, welcoming, and moved efficiently even though it was busy. The vibe inside is more grab-and-go or quick casual, but you don’t feel rushed. It’s clean, well-lit, and the energy is good.

If you’re in the area and want something that’s satisfying and flavorful without being overpriced or fussy, Kitchen Near You is a solid move. I’ll definitely be back to try more.

My experience was good, just that I look like it gets better at night. The fish is good, just a little salty. The Achu was good, too abd the soya. For next time I will recommend coming at night for a better experience cause the  evening looks cold that is not too lively.

Went this past Friday for the first time, as a treat for my birthday with 2 of my friends. The music was good but the DJ wasn’t great at transitioning from song to song. We were told that if we weren’t buying bottle service m, which is $350 for a $40/50 bottle of retailed liquor, you couldn’t sit on the couches in the back of the wall. We moved to a table on the floor because, um no. We ordered food. The jollof was so spicy I couldn’t eat it, the fish was good, the suya was extremely over cooked by tasty, and the goat was fatty and tasted like nothing but tomato sauce. The service wasn’t that great, as the waitress wasn’t friendly at all. Will probably never return, even though I really wanted to like this place.

I place an order for boiled yam and you guys send me plantain’s when I called to ask why do you have to send me plantain and she said sorry we don’t have yams. Then refund my money because I don’t eat plantain .

Service was good, the food amazing. We oder one fish to eat and one to take away. My friend is new to the area and I took him there. He really liked it and he would like to go back. It was nice African music sound.

formatted_address: 11435 Georgia Ave, Wheaton, MD 20902, United States
name: Rhuths African Kitchen(Carryout)

reviews.text:
Drove over 30 min away just for him to say they didn’t have the fried spinach, when I told him I was on the way! Walked in here, food not ready. Now he says sorry we don’t have. Unprofessional!

Update: Response to owner

Thank you for responding, however it should have been told to me on the phone before driving way out there. I asked if the container was circular or square, because photos are showing both. He kept saying black container. How am I supposed to know as a NEW customer that just moved from out of state, that the fried spinach is just for catering? I went to Roger Miller restaurant around the corner and they were VERY professional and I told them my experience here. The owner’s wife spoke to with me also and made fried spinach for me at their establishment and it was good! Please train your employees to inform people of this instead of having them wasting gas driving far away. My relatives made fufu for Christmas and I had a few left over and was craving fried spinach as part of my heritage is of Nigerian, Ghanian, & Sierra Leone Heritage through my dad! I was coming here to support also!

This is a must stop for our family anytime we’re in the DMV.  The customer service is amazing and this restaurant saves me time and sanity. They’ve even helped coordinate delivery to my hotel when I was in town for a work event.  I no longer spend hours in the kitchen cooking soups and baking meat pies and sausage rolls for my Nigerian hubby. I simply call ahead and place my bulk order.  Rhuth’s kitchen tastes so much like my hubby’s mom’s home cooking that he’s just as happy. Bonus- he appreciates me having the time back to spend with him while our whole family enjoys.  We freeze a portion of the soups and pastries and bring out as needed. It’s a win-win for me.

Right, listen here, I’m absolutely livid. I went to Ruth’s African Kitchen in Wheaton, Maryland, the very day after my bloody birthday expecting something vibrant, authentic, a bit of culinary brilliance, yeah? Instead, what I got was nothing short of a catastrophic let-down. The two women at the counter had the audacity, the sheer effrontery, to lie straight to my face when I said, “I like it spicy, make it properly spicy.” And what do I get? A dish seasoned for toddlers, comfort spice, barely a tickle on the tongue. They clearly hadn’t the faintest clue what the assignment was. Now, moving on to the second crime. I ordered goat egusi, simple instruction, yeah? Goat. Yet when I opened that takeaway box, I was confronted by, good heavens, chicken feet! Bits of unidentifiable protein floating about like a science experiment gone wrong. I was mortified. The egusi was so atrocious I binned it on sight. Honestly, it was an insult to both palate and presentation. And the jollof rice, don’t get me started. Bland, spiritless, devoid of the depth, the heat, the soul that proper West African jollof should command. It’s as though the Nigerians out here have completely lost their ancestral touch when it comes to spice. When I say spicy, I mean fiery inferno, the sort that makes you sweat, question your life choices, and feel alive again. The Indians still hold the crown, clearly. So no, absolutely not, I shan’t be returning. This wasn’t African cuisine; this was a tragic Westernized parody of it. Call it African-American comfort food if you must, but don’t you dare pass it off as authentic. Zero stars. A culinary disgrace of the highest order.

First off , I’m Nigerian American so this cuisine is not new to me. I ordered from this place on Uber eats yesterday . I ordered red chicken stew with fufu . When I received my food the fufu was SPOILED. It had a very bad smell coming from it and the taste was sour . For those that are new , fufu is not supposed to smell or taste like anything. The bowl I received was not spicy just a HALF FULL BOWL of tomato sauce and two pieces of fried oily drumsticks. I immediately contacted Uber eats and got a full refund . I’m highly disappointed and upset for the price that I paid and the time I wasted waiting I ended up eating noodles instead . PLEASE DO NOT GO TO THIS RESTAURANT. Go to rainbows African cuisine in Gaithersburg instead . They will not do you wrong ! Their food is very delicious
Doesn’t taste anything like Nigeria food .just the name 🤦🏾‍♂️.. Pls do better . Egusi soup I bought was watery

formatted_address: 816 H St NE, Washington, DC 20002, United States
name: AG Afro-Caribbean

formatted_address: 3013 Georgia Ave NW, Washington, DC 20001, United States
name: ASTU KITFO BAR AND RESTAURANT

reviews.text: We went there for dinner prior to going to a soccer game, and we enjoyed our food immensely.  All the food items were great and delicious. The owner is friendly and nice and turned on the AC as per our request as it was really hot on that day.  It is definitely on the expensive side as all the side orders were expensive and we had to order the items a few times as it wasn't enough for us.  That is something to be aware of.  Other than that, the food, service, and ambiance were good.  I definitely recommend this restaurant for Ethiopian food.

We went for early dinner on Monday.  The owner and the employees were so warm and welcoming.  Food presentation and taste was just special and perfect.  The spices were just right.  We ordered a vegetable meal and each item complimented the flavors of the other dish.  Will come back again and again!

I had an absolutely incredible experience here! The staff was extremely attentive and courteous. The decor was beautiful. The location was clean and the music was catchy and set to a very conversational volume.

I ordered the small meat combo platter with a coffee and was astounded by presentation with which it was received.

The food itself was excellent and the combo platter was very well varied. It felt like the perfect sampler yet was well more than ample as a full meal. Each dish was colorfully unique, though my favorite portion was the Quanta Firfir which was rich and spicy.

Finally, the coffee was outstanding… and I am a coffee snob.

I would recommend this place to Ethiopian enthusiasts and new comers alike!

The service and atmosphere takes you to Africa. The scents the sights the feelings takes you out of DC for a little bit. The service was awesome, very attentive and alot of time spent explaining the various dishes as well as answering our millions of questions. The food tasted really great. If you have never had Injera Bread before, its the texture essentially of a not too fluffy pancake with a slightly sour taste, hope that helps. It was our first time so we went with an open mind and open pallets ready to taste the food in it's authenticity and its really unique, cannot be compared to anything else, you have to like it for what its is. There were yellow split peas, red lentils, beef with jalapeños, brown screwed beef, stewed chicken, chicken with a boiled egg, cheese (White stuff in pic) and kitfo (Semi cooked well seasoned ground beef) bottom right of the pic.

formatted_address: 1080 W Patrick St #4, Frederick, MD 21703, United States
name: EL AFRIK Cuisine & Bar

reviews.text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Hidden Gem in Frederick – My New Favorite West African Spot!

I’ve now been to this restaurant twice, and both experiences were so good that I felt compelled to write a full review. This place is truly a hidden gem in the Frederick area—easily my new go-to for West African food.

1. Atmosphere & Vibe

What first drew me in was how the restaurant actually allows you to sit down and unwind after a long day. I wasn’t expecting much, but the décor completely surprised me—modern, cute, lounge-style, and honestly “bomb.”
The vibe was lighthearted and fun… we even ended up doing karaoke! What shocked me was that no one minded. Guests were laughing, singing along, and the whole space felt welcoming and relaxed.

2. Huge Win for Parents – They Have a Kids Menu!

One of the biggest reasons I chose this restaurant over another was that I saw they had a kids menu. That’s extremely rare for African restaurants in the area.

My toddler doesn’t always go for West African dishes, so seeing chicken tenders and fries on the menu was the deciding factor. And let me tell you:
•	The portion was huge
•	The tenders were fresh, juicy, and seasoned—not the cheap frozen kind
•	The fries were lightly seasoned without salt because the staff was conscious of kids’ sodium intake. They let me add salt myself, which as a mom, I deeply appreciated.

That small detail alone meant a lot.

3. Exceptional Service – Shoutout to Albina & Osei

Both times I visited, Albina and Osei took care of me and they were phenomenal.
Friendly, attentive, not overbearing, and genuinely welcoming.

During my first visit they forgot an egg in my order and immediately comped me an extra one when they brought it out. Simple, thoughtful customer service like that sticks with you.

4. The Food – Fresh, Hot, and Shockingly Affordable

Everything I tried was amazing:
•	Suya – tender, juicy, perfectly seasoned.
And for only $10?! I truly expected $15–$20 for the amount I got. I thought about it for a week afterward.
•	Eggs – cooked to absolute perfection.
•	Okra stew with beef & pounded yam (my second visit) – so good I ordered it again to go.
•	Kids meal tenders and fries – honestly I could’ve eaten her meal myself; that’s how good it was.

Everything came out fresh, hot, and well-seasoned. No bland food, no waiting forever, no disappointment.

5. Cleanliness, Music & Extra Perks
•	The bathrooms were clean and easy to access (not always the case in restaurants).
•	Music selection was perfect—nice vibe without overpowering conversation.
•	They have a full bar, and almost every table had the same cocktail, so clearly the drinks are popular. I’ll be trying one on my next visit.

6. Overall Experience

I went in tired after work, just wanting to sit down and eat.
I walked out having had a whole experience—karaoke, great food, great service, relaxing vibes, and my child was fed and happy.

This restaurant checks every single box for me:

✔ Great food
✔ Generous portions
✔ Amazing customer service
✔ Kid-friendly menu
✔ Beautiful décor
✔ Clean bathrooms
✔ Fun, welcoming environment
✔ Affordable pricing
✔ Servers who make you feel comfortable and invited

This is officially my favorite West African restaurant in Frederick, and the one I will continue to patronize as long as the quality and service remain this good.

Albina and Osei deserve a huge spotlight.
They truly made both of my visits memorable

Great place for a delicious meal. Came here for a private party. I had the peanut butter soup with chicken and I also tried the beef samosas. Everything was delicious. They also have a great selection of cocktails and cocktails. I liked the ambiance and the DJ kept the party rocking. Will definitely come  back and bring my family to try some different dishes.

Authentic vibe and ambience, it is like stepping back into a restaurant in Ghana.
I got the fried croaker with yam chips; tasty, flavorful and well seasoned! + the pepper sauces that came with it,👌🏾.
Can't wait to try other dishes on the menu.

Casual Review: El Afrik Cuisine & Bar

If you’re looking for something different in Frederick, El Afrik Cuisine & Bar is a great spot to check out. The vibe is lively, with Afro-inspired décor and music that makes the place feel warm and welcoming.

The food is the real star here. I tried the jollof rice and suya, and both were packed with flavor — smoky, spicy, and just the right amount of heat. Portions are generous, so come hungry. They also have great grilled fish and plantains that pair perfectly with the beans.

Service was friendly and relaxed. The staff were happy to explain dishes if you’re new to African cuisine, which made the whole experience even better.

Overall, El Afrik is a fun spot to hang out with friends or enjoy a casual night out.

I’m a snob when it comes to food, especially Ghanaian food, as the son of a certified nutritionist and caterer. I make it a point to critique those who purport to know or believe they can recreate dishes from home, with the level of authenticity it deserves…

Most fall short… El-Afrik excels…

EL AFRIK Cuisine & Bar is a new Ghanian inspired restaurant and at first glace upon walking in, there is a cozy and sleek yet grown and sexy vibe that radiates.

From start to finish, everything is delicious. The space has a fashionable vibe, with the AfroBeats to High life classics subtly echoing in the background, adding to the overall atmosphere without being overpowering.

What really sets El-Afrik apart is the staff. They were professional, personable, and clearly understood not just the menu, but the broader vision and culture of the restaurant.

Every single dish is flavorful, well-prepared, and memorable, especially their soups and of course, its jollof…  it’s the kind of restaurant you look forward to returning to…

I continue to recommend El-Afrik to anyone who will listen,  seeking good food, awesome people, and an experience in Frederick, MD and its environs.

name: Bros J Suya

reviews.text:
So the other day...
I pulled up on Bros J Suya in Beltsville, and bruh—it went from “I’m just grabbing a bite” to “this is a whole experience.” From the jump, that charcoal fire aroma wrapped around me like a warm handshake from back home.

Let’s break it down:

Chicken wings kissed by flame—smoky, juicy, layered with bold, spicy seasoning. Not dry, not greasy. Just right.

Beef suya with that perfect char and spice blend that hits like a drumbeat—warm, loud, unforgettable.

Jollof rice so rich and flavorful, it could start an argument at a family cookout. Deep tomato base, just enough heat, and a finish that made me close my eyes and thank the ancestors.

And the vibe?
It had me channeling that Jay-Z/Kanye energy—“Ain’t nobody fresher than my clique...”
Because truth be told, this is the official Suya Bros Clique. A proud West African flavor gang repping real food, fire, and flavor. No shortcuts. No fake spice. Just grill-to-soul heat.

Pull up hungry. Leave in a food coma.
And don’t forget to dab your forehead—it gets real.

#SuyaClique #WestAfricanEats #JollofKingdom #CharcoalChronicles #BrosJSuya #FlavorUnited #ChakulaCheckApproved

Bros J Suya Review

---

Overview:
Bros J Suya is known for its delicious Nigerian-style suya—spicy grilled meat skewers—offering an authentic taste of West African street food in a casual setting.

---

Pros:
- Flavorful, well-marinated suya with the perfect spicy kick
- Tender and juicy meat, grilled to perfection
- Friendly and welcoming staff
- Affordable pricing, great value for money
- Good portion sizes

---

Cons:
- Limited menu focused mainly on suya and sides
- Seating area may be small or informal
- Sometimes a wait during busy times

---

Rating: 4.4 / 5
Ideal for suya lovers or anyone wanting to try authentic Nigerian flavors. A must-visit for spicy grilled meat fans!
