The food is wonderful, delicious and filling. One thing I would say is if you do not understand anything about the menu, call and ask. You can order food from this restaurant via UBER Eats. Contrary what some said in their review about this restaurant having mostly fish related food in their menu, that totally not true.

They serve beef and fish. Just choose clearly over the phone and in person their friendly staff are willing to help you get beef related food with Injera. They also serve raw meat too. If you want it medium, rare or well done make it clear to them.

There might be a language barrier depending on who is working or picks up your phone call. So speak slow and clearly. Please be advised, service can be slow sometimes.
Great food and service. I was there a week ago with my wife and went back a week later with one of my nephews. He definitely enjoyed the meal.
The food is the worst. I don't recommend anyone to go there for food period!

formatted_address: 3045 Columbia Pike, Arlington, VA 22204, United States
name: Bethel Cafe

reviews.text:
Oh yeah! Lunch was a vegetarian and a meat, was all fantastic and 2 entrees were more than enough for the three of us. 3 kinds of lentils, 2 kinds of greens, some salads, cheese, potatoes, all really good. Only a few things were only slightly hot (yes, I’m soft! So what??!!) but the seasoning was spot on, especially the raw beef when grabbed with the yellow lentils.

Service was great, nice folks serving great food. I won’t be going anywhere else for my Ethiopian dinners for a while.

Great place to grab an Ethiopian bite!

The server was so kind and took time explaining what we should get considering it was my first time trying Ethiopian food. She also brought us some complimentary fresh bread which was very kind!

The have a gluten free injera as well. We got the Bethel Special which had a variety of vegetarian dishes with a beef Tibs in the middle and it was absolutely delicious.

Would highly recommend!

First time ever trying Ethiopian food which I had wanted to for a long time. Ordeedr delivery through Uber eats and it was quick and efficient and had a very generous serving for only about $20. I ordered the veggie combo and it was beyond delicious. It was like an explosion of flavor that I had never experienced with so many notes that it was almost overwhelming for my mouth in an extremely pleasant way! Will definitely be ordering again. Food was beyond delicious and portions and quality is superb!!!

My 16 year old son found the restaurant for us to try. He was craving Ethiopian cuisine. From the time we walked in the door, we were treated as family. Genuine care and attention was put into explaining how the dishes were made. Without sounding trite, we both remarked that we could taste the love that went into our meal. We got the Bethel Special for 2 it was nicely portioned and presented and so very flavorful!!
They also sell Ethiopian spices at the restaurant and I bought a huge bag. Now I need some cooking classes to go with  my spices!! Please try this restaurant. It is amazing.
The food was authentic and delicious, and the chef personally came out to make sure our meals were to our taste. Excellent!

formatted_address: 2910 Bladensburg Rd NE, Washington, DC 20018, United States
name: Eden's Kitchen

reviews.text: I stopped by on a weekday afternoon. The food was delicious, and the service was excellent. They have plenty of outdoor seating, weather permitting. The price was about what I expected. Overall, it was a great experience.

Our first time trying Eritrean food - we got the vegetarian combo and lamb. The food was piping hot, the injera delightfully spongey and sour, the perfect vehicle for the flavorful dishes. Would recommend for a comforting delicious meal!!

Had an amazing Eritrean breakfast with a friend! Eden, the owner, was so kind and made my birthday feel special. We had Kitcha Fitfit with Selsi, and it was very flavorful!

Plus, the Eritrean art on the walls made the vibe even better. 10/10 experience!

Went for lunch after visiting the nearby Costco and looking online for restaurants in the area.  The outside front of the restaurant is cute, but the sign isn't the easiest to see.  Fortunately, the map app showed me where I was going.  There weren't any parking spots on the street in front because they were almost all filled by bright red taxi cabs, which looked like they were waiting to be repaired in a nearby body/mechanic shop.  Fortunately, I found a street spot around the corner on the side street (when I got into the restaurant, I was able to see that they had an outdoor dining area behind a fence on the street and at the back of the restaurant was a parking lot that can be accessed by an alley off the side street on which I parked).

There were only 4-5 patrons in the restaurant when I arrived.  You order at the counter/bar area and then sit at a table while your meal is prepared.  No one was at the bar when I first stepped in, so after a minute of waiting,  I rang the small bell sitting on the bar.  A woman immediately came out from the back and asked what I would like to order.  I advised her that I had never had Eritrean food but am experienced with Ethiopian food, and she confirmed that they are very similar.  I then ordered the platter of 6 vegetarian of my choice ($15-$20 -- I am not sure because there also was an option to just choose 4 and I forgot to take a picture of the menu).  I told the woman that I would love to have the cook decide what to serve me, and she said ok.

I then sat down and waited.  The wait was a little longer than I had expected, but I think that is because the cook (who might have been the same woman who took my order) was making everything fresh.  When the food came out, I already knew that I was going to have leftovers.  The food is served on a platter topped with injera and then with the selected dishes poured atop the injera, just like Ethiopian food.   For the most part, I didn't know what I was eating exactly (I knew one dish was collared greens, another a cabbage dish, and a third was a beautiful,  vibrant, fresh salad of lettuce, tomatoes, and onions in a light delicious dressing), but everything was outstanding.  I later learned that the other three dishes were a red lentil dish, a yellow bean dish, and an orange traditional Eritrean chickpea dish.  All three were delicious, but the chickpea dish blew me away.

When I finished eating, I asked for a carryout container and also a takeout order of the Derek Tibsi because I wanted to try a meat dish.  The woman asked if I wanted it spicy, and I said I did.  When I got home, I tried the Derek Tibsi, which was still steaming, and it was fantastic-- cubes of beef with what looked like okra in a sauce that had some heat (next time I will ask for extra spicy) with a side of the fresh salad and collard greens.  Total includes 20% tip was between $40 and $45.

Eden's Kitchen felt like a childhood invite to a friend's house for dinner. The food was fresh, well balanced, simple, yet delicious. This cozy restaurant has a great outdoor space and homey vibes.

We ordered the beef with collard greens and lamb spris with injera. The lamb cooked with fresh tomatoes and both came with a mini side salad. Injera was authentic in texture but I personally would've preferred a little more tang to the flavor.

Next time we'll probably order a veggie sampler with our meat dishes.

We came at 4:30pm on Friday with no reservation. Parking can be done on the street around the corner.

formatted_address: 2154 24th Pl NE, Washington, DC 20018, United States
name: ECCC

reviews.text: I had a great experience at the Eritrean 🇪🇷Community Centre restaurant. The décor is well done, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere. The veggie platter was excellent—fresh, flavorful, and well-prepared. I also loved the beer and wine selection—great choices all around! The service was top-notch, and the food was delicious. Thumbs up! I’ll definitely be back.🇪🇷
Delicious succulent food with amazing aroma, great service and friendly staff. Absolutely loved the food.

From the outside this place does not look inviting but as soon as you walk in the staff treats you like you were also Eritrean. When not if you go try the veggie platter. for $11 you can feed 3 people easily. And they make there own Injera bread there. If you have ever had Ethiopian food then you will love this place.
This is a great place that is a bit intimidating to enter. There are few DC restaurants that are cheap and delicious - this is one of them.
They serve really delicious Eritrean Cuisine.

formatted_address: 8301 Georgia Ave, Silver Spring, MD 20910, United States
name: Lucy Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text:
The food is AWESOME. If you want an authentic Ethiopian food and experience, this is the place to come. Everything will remind you of Ethiopia.

The people, food and atmosphere. The bar with people sitting there and other people just enjoying themselves drinking coffee or beer.

The best place to eat Ethiopian food.. 🇪🇹

When I tell you everything is great... EVERYTHING is GREAT. I have no complaints about the food, but they can definitely get a better drink selection. Add the fried fish with salad to your meal... The Lucy salad

This Ethiopian food is fantastic.  Very flavorful.  It wasn't until I ordered takeout from Lucy's when I realized how good Ethiopian food is and Lucy's is better than other restaurants that claim to be the leader here (we have tried the highest rated and Lucy's is always better, simply tastier!).  My favorite is the tibs sandwich.  The vegi combo is also very good.  Recommended!

This restaurant refuses to pay it’s meat supplier of many years for multiple deliveries. They have cut off all communication after bouncing checks. There are plenty of Ethiopian restaurants in this area with honest owners. Please consider going somewhere else

My Review used to be"Great food, great music, excellent customer service and amazing Buna😁" with 5stars...
That has changed drastically; Visited Lucy few times recently and it has gone down the drain. Their food is relatively ok but service is WOREST at best. Their coffee is full of ATELA🤣🤣🤣.
It's very different. WOULDN'T recommend

formatted_address: 8200 Fenton St, Silver Spring, MD 20910, United States
name: Lesaac Ethiopian Cafe

reviews.text: Leesac Ethiopian Restaurant on Fenton Street in downtown Silver Spring serves up authentic and flavorful Ethiopian cuisine that I really enjoy. The food is consistently good, and many of the waitstaff are friendly and attentive. However, the cleanliness and seating arrangements could use a bit more attention, and the manager or owner who’s often around isn’t particularly welcoming. Despite that, the overall atmosphere is pleasant, and it’s a nice spot to enjoy a good Ethiopian meal.

I’m giving this restaurant one star because of a very disappointing experience. I went based on a recommendation and ordered a combination meal that looked good at first — but once I got home and tried it, I couldn’t even eat one full bite. The meat tasted old, was extremely tough, and completely inedible. I only managed a few bites before I had to throw the entire meal in the trash. Not only was it a waste of money, but it also left me with an upset stomach. When I called the restaurant to explain, they refused to offer a refund and instead said they could give me a discount next time — but after this experience, there definitely won’t be a next time. I do not recommend Lesaac cafe.

The food here was exceptional. It was my friend’s and my first time experiencing Ethiopian cuisine, and it was nothing short of extraordinary. Every dish was thoughtfully prepared and bursting with flavor — a truly unforgettable culinary experience.
At the Heart of Silver Spring, You will find this nice Ethiopian Restaurant. Very nice food and service. Great management. Of course *Shifinfin* is my favorite.

Eat here every time we are in the area. Coffee is wonderful. Love the vegetarian platter. I always add beef tibs. Had my first breakfast platter a few weeks ago and now Im hooked. Clean and pleasant environment!!! Totally worth trying.

formatted_address: 2655 University Blvd W, Silver Spring, MD 20902, United States
name: Dessie Lanka Restaurant and Market

reviews.text: Really lovely and welcoming owner. They make some of my Sri Lankan childhood favorites. The hoppers are lovely and come with a really nice sweet onion (seeni sambol) and hot chili sauce. Fantastic kottu roti (Sri Lankan Street food). I wish they were in Baltimore!

Caution 🚨Worst food I’ve ever eaten. Website says “authentic Sri Lankan restaurant” but the only authentic thing there was the chili paste. Kothu, fried rice, lamprise all of it was terrible. Honestly, nothing had the real Sri Lankan flavor or any flavor at all. If you actually love Sri Lankan food, don’t waste your time or money here. Stay away.

This review is in hopes they improve their business and not a way to trash them. The owners are incredibly kind.

Couple of my complaints:

Before I got there, I made sure they were open on Google, even though when I called them, there was no answer. Once I got there, I saw the sign said closed. Luckily I decided to call once more and the owner said they were indeed open and when I went back, the sign had been flipped to open. That's an annoyance and would leave open to losing customers.

The biggest complaint is the amount of time it took to receive the food. When I went in, he said it should take 30 minutes to make it all. This was fine. At the moment, I waited over an hour and a half for 3 dishes. I ordered the fish rolls ahead of time as an appetizer, which itself took about 20-30 minutes. The owner was friendly but didn't understand the meaning of time. He even made the excuse of thinking I'm not expecting the food at the moment and he thought I would be heading out and coming back later, but I clearly indicated that I wanted the appetizers now while I waited for the rest of the food.

As for the food itself, it was bland and mediocre. There was much left to be desired. I ordered 3 egg hoppers, I only received 2. I ordered 4 fish rolls, I only received 3. He even took my order down, so I'm confused how they got this mixed up.

I had to wait additional time because one of the entrees I had ordered, I requested beef but for some reason, he stated they made a pork version. This is completely unacceptable and just wasted time.

If you're asking yourself, why didn't I go to another restaurant? That is easy, because there is simply no sri lankan restaurants in abundance as they are quite scarce. So to find one seemed like a win! Unfortunately, it was far from a win.

I cannot recommend this restaurant as they still have much to learn in terms of its customers time and food preparation.

Never in my life have I had this happen. I ordered the veggie combo with 5 items. When I get my order, it only had 4 items and very scarce portions. I called the restaurant. I was told that because I had discounts on DoorDash and the restaurant only received half of the money, they only gave me half of the food. They said they didn’t add the discount to DoorDash. Well, neither did I! Very unprofessional. They will never get my business again.

Please beware of ordering ahead here. I placed a catering order a month in advance and placed an over $200 deposit. The owner asked me to REMIND her a week in advance was already questionable but when I got there, my food was not ready. She said it would be ready in five minutes and I waited an hour after the agreed upon time and it still wasn’t ready. I asked for my deposit back onto my card and she said she didn’t know how to do that. I ended up leaving and had to rush to get food from somewhere else as this was for a big event (which is why I ordered the food a month in advance). Do not order food from here as they’re extremely disorganized and will NOT have it ready on time

formatted_address: 1505 Columbia Pike, Arlington, VA 22204, United States
name: Dama Restaurant and Pastry

reviews.text:
We had the meat combo with lentils, yellow peas, and cabbage as our veggie options, and it was perfect for sharing between two people. The food is delicious and authentically Ethiopian, and the service was great! Our waitress was attentive and happy to help, especially if you're new to Ethiopian cuisine.
The restaurant has a casual vibe, making it a great spot to enjoy a relaxed meal. We were missing Ethiopian food, and Dama definitely hit the spot.

After our meal, we stopped by the bakery for a slice of double chocolate cake, but I would pass on it next time. The cake was a bit dry, and the chocolate flavor didn’t quite hit the mark for me.

Overall, I highly recommend Dama Restaurant for anyone craving authentic Ethiopian food!

What a spectacular restaurant set in the Arlington-Fort Myer, and Pentagon footprint! I was incredibly fortunate to have stumbled upon Dama Pastry and Restaurant while I was in town for work and want to share my experience here with other inquisitive diners wishing to experience something novel.

From the Sheraton Pentagon City Hotel, Dama Pastry and Restaurant was no more than a stone-throw a way which made it an ideal dining choice for me. After arriving to town that day and settling in at the lodging accommodation, I soon found myself rather famished. Not the one to simply settle for the dining options and venues at the hotel, I wanted to explore the local cuisine. Almost immediately, Dama grabbed my attention when I did a quick search using Google maps.

The restaurant sits off of Columbia Pike (Rte 244) at the corner of South Oak Street. The parking situation at the establishment is limited, with 4 spots in the front of the restaurant, while the side of the restaurant has several spots (definitely consider this if you're coming here with a large party). Dama Bakery and Restaurant has 3 distinct sections. There is the bakery (left; make sure you don't walk into the extreme left of the building as it is a salon), the market (in the middle), and the restaurant (right); you can also walk freely from one section to another as they are all connected on the inside.

I happened to enter through the bakery from which the staff happily guided me to the restaurant section. Here, I was met with a welcoming host. The setting and ambiance were fairly modest with some portrait hangings that shed light on the history and culture of the establishment and cuisine. This along with the plain-straight forward menu was a refreshing change to the colorful, extravagant decor and menu pamphlets that can sometimes be overstimulating.

Although not my first time having Ethiopian food, I still required some assistance and recommendations from the host. Again, the menu descriptions were straight forward and to the point however it contained culturally named items that I was not familiar with. The host was more than gracious and patient to explain these items and make her recommendations based on my preferences. After relatively quick deliberation, I submitted my choices and eagerly awaited the entree. The dish I ended up ordering was the Awaze Tibs.

As I waited, I reflected and attempted to recall my previous experience with Ethiopian cuisine. Whilst I remembered the occasion and venue, I did not specifically have any take aways from the meal other than the fact that I simply enjoyed it.

When the meal was delivered, my eyes were the first to feast on the platter. While simple in plating and presentation, the notion that the meal was infused with flavor was immediately apparent from the colorful notes that coated the beef cubes and slides while chopped green jalapenos added another splash of color. On the side was a freshly prepared house salad. All of this sat over the injera that met with the circumference of the aluminum plate like a perfectly sized placemat. The meal was paired with more injera that was carefully folded like a crepe ready to be unfurled for enjoyment.

Followed by my taste buds, I could have not asked for anything more exhilarating to kick off my work-visit. The spice and aroma paired perfectly to provide a beautiful symphony that played out in my mouth.  Eating with just my hands (this is the way), I enjoyed every bite of the beef as it paired with the delightfully sour-y injera. Having some bites with the fresh jalapeno, and some with the house salad, I ate until my belly could no longer - and even then I craved more. I continued to eat the injera that soaked up the juices and stew of the Awaze.

Finally, after I was physically and spiritually satisfied, I surveyed the completed platter in a victorious gaze. What a wonderful experience. I would highly recommend to anyone staying at the Sheraton to give this place a try - there is no reason not to - as well as anyone in the Arlington area. It is a 100% must!

Amazing food! This was my first time trying Ethiopian cuisine. The service was great—our waitress was very attentive and helped us choose dishes based on our preferences. We ended up sharing a meat and vegetable combo, as you can see here. The bread, paired with the hearty meat and vegetables, was very satisfying. We were only able to finish about half of it between the two of us! This is a great restaurant, and I’d most certainly come again.

I've been to Dama a few times and honestly it's the best Ethiopian food in the DMV. The service is always quick and the food is so delicious.

Pro tip since you won't have room for dessert: make sure to visit the bakery side before dinner to grab some pastries to take home.

You'll thank yourself later.

This was near my hotel, so I walked over. I was greeted by a delightful woman. She explained some of the menu items. I decided to try the vegetarian buffet. It was very good. In retrospect, I'd probably try one of the meat entrées, but the buffet was good! I also had the tiramisu and hot tea. The tiramisu was really good!

formatted_address: 3813 S George Mason Dr Suite - E & F, Falls Church, VA 22041, United States
name: Balagger Ethiopian Restaurant & Bar

reviews.text: Great service with Best food with cold draft beer while enjoying the game. Whole fish or tibs Firfir are among my favorites.

Truly very impressed with this restaurant. I’ve been here multiple times and each time I’m not disappointed. The service was excellent. Our server Rozina greeted us the minute we got there and continued to deliver excellent service. The food was of quality with great price. Overall very satisfied with their service. The owner/ manager was very humble and made sure we had a great experience. Thank you!

I will not recommend this place, especially for the food. The taste isn’t bad; however, the portions are extremely small and overpriced. We paid more than $100 for three dishes and a couple of sodas, and it still wasn’t enough for three people. The customer service was average, and the restaurant didn’t seem very clean. I’m honestly surprised they’re still in business. Overall, a very disappointing experience.

Went here with a friend on a weeknight and had Tibs with a side of some wot (I forget which). Taste-wise it’s easily in my top 3 local Ethiopian restaurants. Plenty of tables, laid out spaciously so you’re not bumping into others.

Although the fish wasn't fully fried, the food was decent. I love the food. The only issue I had is that the waiter waited a while before bringing the check. Not very professional. Other than that, I will try again.

formatted_address: 5706 Lyngate Ct, Lanham, MD 20706, United States
name: Ma'a Mich Cuisine LLC

reviews.text:
Absolutely incredible dining experience! This African restaurant exceeded my expectations in every way. From the moment we walked in, the atmosphere was warm and inviting, with beautiful décor that reflects the richness of African culture.

The food was simply outstanding – bursting with authentic flavors, fresh ingredients, and perfect seasoning. I tried the baked fish with fried plantains, and it was easily one of the best meals I’ve had in a long time. The portion sizes were generous, and the dishes were presented beautifully.

"Ma mich" was attentive and friendly, making us feel welcome and ensuring we had everything we needed. Whether you’re new to African cuisine or a longtime fan, this restaurant is a must-visit! I can’t wait to come back and try more dishes on the menu. Highly recommended!

Ma’a Mich Cuisine serves authentic African flavors, prepared with a touch of tradition and warmth. Ma’a Mich herself is a delightful host, known for her great sense of humor. The restaurant is not only clean but also beautifully arranged, making it a wonderful place to enjoy a meal.

Best Cameroonian food in the DMV. This place was recommended by a friend and it has been my go to place whenever I crave food from the motherland. The Kondre, baked fish, achu, fried rice, and goat stew are my favorites. And the customer service is top notch. I definitely recommend this place, 10 out of 10.
I went there many time with my family to eat ashu grill Fish kondre. The service is perfect the food so good and mama michh amazing
The lady was really nice! And her food was soooo delicious. I would definitely recommend it to everybody

formatted_address: 6834 New Hampshire Ave, Takoma Park, MD 20912, United States
name: Conclave Restaurant

reviews.text: They have the best fresh tilapia with plantains, onions, and peppers. I believe that they are the best Cameroonian restaurant in Maryland.

BEST PLACE!!! This is the best African cuisine restaurant in the whole D.C. Maryland Virginia area BY FAR!! Service is amazing, food came out fast, and tasted like I was back home! I will definitely be coming back, thank you Congress Restaurant for the amazing food and experience !
If you want real tasty African food ,this is the place!!!

Ok first of all the ladies are rude. There is minors working here/helping out. Nobody
have any manners at all They DONT say hi, thank you, your welcome, have a nice day nothing at all. This place had no chicken, No suya, or no ice for the drinks.The way the respond to you is not in a nice way at all. One of the ladies attempting to rush me out even after I entered this place 50 mins prior to closing. She was like ” I can give you a container are you sure your going to eat all of that in here”.  Little do she know I am a quick eater, but she didn’t even give me a chance automatically she was emphasizing that I need to hurry up. Anyways the big problem is the way the act toward customers & they are not professional!
It was so delicious. I enjoyed the Eru which was extremely nice . Ohh the soya taste soooo good and it was perfectly seasoned. I think each time I get to Maryland I will always go there .

formatted_address: 2800 10th St NE, Washington, DC 20017, United States
name: Avenues of the Caribbean Catering

reviews.text:
Avenues of the Caribbean is a top notch caterer  which I chose recently for a large Haitian-themed birthday party.    I was initially impressed by the well- organized web site.

The owner, Jennifer Paul, worked personally with me over a month to ensure that every delicacy requested by the guest of honor would make it to the buffet table.  She even prepared and delivered an “sampling dinner” so we knew  what flavors to expect.

At the party,   every guest raved about how delicious the food was, and there were many comments about how certain dishes brought back fond memories of their own mothers’ home cooking!

This caterer has my highest recommendation!

Ordered Avenues of the Caribbean for a student org event and it was wonderful! Many members were asking where we ordered from. Lots of our Haitian members complimented the food as well, Will be ordering again!!

My work ordered catering from Avenues of the Caribbean twice over just a few short days, and it was a big hit!  Jen helped us create two unique menus for our guests, and everyone enjoyed the meals.  And more importantly, they sent JUST THE RIGHT AMOUNT of food, and at a GREAT price.  Thank you, Jen and AOTC!

I love Caribbean food but the food at Avenues of the Caribbean was off the charts good. I will definitely be back for more. The dishes were DELICIOUS! My favorites were the rice and green peas, baked ziti and jerk chicken. I've added you guys to my list of go to catering spots in DC!

I wish I could've tasted the food but ALL the guests we're pretty impressed!  I ordered a pretty nice package for my daughter's Quinceañera (15th Birthday) celebration.  Everything was as described and the guests we're ABSOLUTELY delighted!  Jennifer, was expeditious and offered GREAT communication, as I was coming in from ATL.

formatted_address: 6214 3rd St NW, Washington, DC 20011, United States
name: Peaches Kitchen Restaurant & Catering Service

reviews.text: I’m not sure why this place is still open. The food is horrible not to mention it’s always a very long wait for your food. After calling in a pickup order they tell you 25-30 minutes it turns into at least an hour or more. The food is never what they say it is and tastes horrible. I hadn’t been here a few years but tried to give it another try because I did like it when it first opened but it had fallen off. Well I see not much has changed. You can be the judge for yourself but as you can see the lay some sugar on me sweet potato doesn’t have ounce of sugar or anything else for that matter. Never again, is the least I can say about this restaurant.

Peaches was very good. I would recommend this place is you are looking for Jamaican and soul food in the DC area.
3 stars because of a few things that are near and dear to me personally. But some people may not care. Everything was seasoned and flavored perfectly. If you don’t like spicy curry, stay away 😂. My curry shrimp was spicy.

Oxtails- 7- I like mine to fall off the bone. I had to
Work on these a little. But great savory flavor.
Fried whitening-7- I would have given a ten. But these were not whole filets. They were broken. The sauce that was provided was a 10! 🤤🤤.
Curry Shrimp- 10
Greens-10
Rice-5 it was cold &
Mild Flavor( but the curry sauce made up for it.
Green beans- 10 so good!!!!
Plantains-10
Garlic Mashed potatoes-10

It was my first time ordering from Peaches but not my last.  I was pleased with the entire process from ordering to pick up.

The food is flavorful and plenty for two servings per meal.  My sister loved her oxtails, lay some sugar sweet potatoes and cabbage.

I enjoyed the stuffed salmon with crab and shrimp, cabbage and mac and cheese.

The meals do not come with plantains as I am accustomed to having so be sure to place an order as a side if you want them.  They were cooked to perfection and there's plenty in the order to share.

Overall very pleased.

I’ve been a fan of Peaches for some time now! I will sing their good graces from the mountain top!

My favorite dish to get is the jerk chicken Alfredo pasta. It comes with either a side salad or garlic bread. That pasta used to have me tearing up after like two bites. The jerk was jerkinnn, honey. This last time I had it, it wasn’t as hot but still packed a punch. I ordered to-go, so as pictured the jerk sauce came on the side.

The next time I ordered, I got the chicken stuffed with crabmeat and shrimp, cabbage, and curry potatoes. Everything was exceptional. But baby, those curry potatoes?? God sent.

Sometimes the food tastes awhile to be made, unless you’re ordering from the hot bar. Regardless of how long it tastes, I can assure you it’s made with love.

Bbaaabbbbyyy when I tell you that this food is AMAZING! I ordered the stuffed salmon with mashed potatoes and collard greens. Now I will say that the greens were just okay, they just need more seasoning but I understand that they have to be considerate of some people's health. Now I did add the jerk sauce ontop of my stuffed salmon. The salmon is stuffed with crab meat and shrimp and it was soooo delicious.  The mashed potatoes were a nice consistency. I'm a big foodie so I was blown away. I will be returning to try other food options because there was definitely love put into this meal.

formatted_address: 7800 Biggs Ford Rd Suite B1, Frederick, MD 21701, United States
name: Motherland Kitchen

reviews.text:
We tried African food for the first time at a restaurant, Not only did everything feel authentic, but the staff were very friendly and welcoming. It was just a very good vibe. The owner is very much involved and passionate about her place and her food.

I ordered the lamb with greens and Jollof rice.  My wife got jerk chicken with fufu. The portion sizes were very good and you can tell the food was made with love. There was so much flavor, spices, and seasoning. The lamb was really impressive, and the greens were more like a sautéed spinach than I was expecting, and it was really really good. The jerk chicken was moist and falling off the bone with a good level of spice and flavor and the fufu. was very nice to try for the first time

thank you for a great first experience and we will definitely be back!

We were looking into options while in western MD, and Motherland Kitchen kept popping up! It’s in the oddest of locations, between a Latino church and Estate store, and could easily be missed.

The owner was the hostess, chef, and server. Our bellies were not disappointed when we left, our leftovers reheated deliciously, and we’re excited to use our sauces! The dining area has a “home-y” atmosphere. We had the beef stew, fufu (corn), beef patty, goat, oxtail stew, chicken peanut butter stew, rice & beans, and okra. We would get it all again (and more)!

Driving towards Thurmont, I saw a fascinating little restaurant i knew served perk chicken. On the back from thurmont I took a left & experienced the best the best african/Caribbean  jerk chicken since Jamaica  🇯🇲

Who served...the magnificent owner & chef Sabina who is magnificent cook & i ate for 3 hours..a little bit of this..a little of that
I tasted like dim sum her entire menu

The peanut butter stew rated 12 out of 10 stars

The curried chicken was the best I have ever had...apparently the recipe of Sabrina's mother

The  Kathi Kathi chickens recipe dates to over sixty ago from Sabina's village of Cameroon

The 3 green sides sides is freshly sourced + lots of herbs and spices..the recipe is like the secret formula that will die with Sabina unless she willingly shares it with

The Fufu fonio is heavenly & actually "orgasmic" to your tongue & soul

Discover themis wonderful place for 1 or a party.

She told me she often caters parties

Celebrate Thanksgiving, Xmas or new years

The African/Caribbean way

Add some soul to your life  and before you die .add Motherland kitchen to your bucket list

What an absolute gem! I can’t believe I missed this place around the Frederick area for so long. The food is made entirely from scratch by a single woman who runs everything herself — and you can feel her passion in every detail. She brings such a holistic approach to preparing and serving food that it turns an ordinary meal into a special experience.
I went for the Thanksgiving meal, which featured a wonderful mix of different flavors and dishes, and everything was incredibly tasty. The friendliness, care, and authenticity here really stand out. Highly recommend checking it out — and if you want to try the Thanksgiving meal, it’s available through the end of December!

Well, we ordered jerk chicken and curry chicken.. when the curry came out we were told it’s jerk, and when the red dish came out we were told it’s curry. Kind of confusing especially as we are Caribbean so trust we know curry and jerk when we see it. We decided to eat anyway and although colorful, there was no flavor at all.
Establishment is very much mom and pop style with their belongings everywhere except the dining area.
Staff is friendly enough.
We were excited to try, but left disappointed.
🙏🏽

formatted_address: 55-57 S Potomac St, Hagerstown, MD 21740, United States
name: Motherland Kitchen and Catering

reviews.text:
Me and my family loved the food! Everything was fresh and packed with flavor. The portions were generous—more than enough to feed all three of us. The beef was tender and juicy, the sweet plantains were cooked perfectly, and the jollof rice was amazing. We’ve already decided we’ll be going back for more!

The staff were welcoming, informative, and kind, and the restaurant itself was clean with beautiful décor on the walls. I highly recommend Motherland Kitchen and Catering!

I tried the Chicken Peanut Butter Stew that sounds intriguingly delicious! I've never thought to combine those ingredients in a stew. The rich, creamy texture of the peanut butter melded beautifully with the tender chicken, creating a dish that was both comforting and exotic. The spices added a warm kick. Each bite was a delightful surprise, and I found myself going back for seconds. This unexpected combination has definitely opened my eyes to new possibilities in cooking!I've never thought to combine those ingredients in a stew.

Love the Lamb Curry, Ox Tail Stew & Jollof Rice! The Garri Fufu and Pumpkin Patties are delicious- if you are Vegan or Gluten-free Motherland Kitchen at 55 Potomac St in Downtown Hagerstown by the Theatre is true African cooking! The curries, peanut stews and shrimp pilaf are awesome!

The food here is the real star. Absolute comfort food with rich sauces and spices that hit the spot. The portions are so generous - when we ordered the vegan veggie patty, we thought we were going to get a tiny empanada or pouch, but this thing practically filled the plate! We had the shrimp cauliflower pilaf, the blacked fish stew, and the chicken bitterleaf with peanut sauce. The chicken was so much delicious food we had to take half home for another meal! So many flavors remind me of back home in New Orleans which makes sense because so much New Orleans cuisine owes a debt to Africa & the Caribbean. We will definitely be back - thanks!!
We tried Motherland Kitchen in Hagerstown. The food was good, great portions, and excellent customer service!

formatted_address: 11613 Rainier Ave S, Seattle, WA 98178, United States
name: Taste of Somalia

reviews.text: I can confidently say that Taste of Somalia offers the best Somali cuisine I've ever experienced! Every dish is crafted with incredible care and freshness, from the vibrant sauces to the perfectly seasoned meats. You can truly feel the passion of the owner in every bite. It's not just a meal; it's an unforgettable culinary journey. I'd give it a hundred stars if I could!

I got the half beef and half chicken Baris plate with green and white sauce on the side. The food tastes amazing. Happy I listened to my brother and made a U-turn to try it out. I loved it, keep it up, guys. You will see me again 😁

This was my second time coming to this food truck, and it did not disappoint! I tried the rice and chicken, the spaghetti with beef, and the chicken wrap, all of them were flavorful and well seasoned. But my absolute favorites were the loaded fries and the strawberry crunch cake. The fries were perfectly crispy and topped with so much goodness, and the cake was the perfect sweet ending. The customer service is always amazing super friendly and welcoming. I’ll definitely be coming back again!

I first tried their food through their catering service a while back and it was amazing. So I was excited to hear they recently got a spot to set up their food truck.

I got the sambus, chicken baris, and a slice of their tea-flavored milk cake. Everything was just as good as I remembered!

If you’re looking to try some good Somali food, definitely give them a shot!

I finally got a chance to try Taste of Somalia and let me tell you, it did not disappoint. The food has that real home-cooked flavor that you just don’t find everywhere. You can taste the spices in every bite, nothing watered down or “Americanized.” The rice was perfect, the meat was seasoned right, and even the portions hit the spot. What I really liked is you can feel the culture behind the food, like it’s made with pride. I’ll definitely be back — this is the type of spot you keep in your rotation.

formatted_address: 414 H St NE, Washington, DC 20002, United States
name: Lazizi Halal Cuisine

reviews.text:
Beautiful decor and vibes. Unique concept with the dry bar. Solid service and delicious food. We honey spinach chaat (10/10), ordered Malai boti (9/10) and Butter Chicken (it was made mild for my wife but still tasted good to me).

Mango and Sweet Lassi were delicious and authentic, although the mango Lassi was a smaller portion even though they're the same price.

I recommend the chai after your meal and we were both too full for dessert this time around!

Definitely a must-visit if you’re in the area! The space is beautifully designed with thoughtful décor that creates a warm and inviting atmosphere.

We tried a couple of their mocktails, which were refreshing and flavorful, along with the samosa chaat, butter chicken, and grilled kabobs. Everything was delicious, and the portions were generous—plenty for the four of us with leftovers to enjoy later.

The service was excellent as well, making the whole experience even better. If you’re in the DC area, don’t miss this hidden gem!

I visited Lazizi earlier today! It’s a cozy little place with a nice ambiance. However, I do feel there should always be one extra staff member around ,,  we had to look around a bit to find a server.

The Signature Lemonade was okay, but I really enjoyed the Malai Tikka Boti and fries — both were flavorful and fresh. Overall, a pleasant experience. Recommended!

My wife and I first came here for Eid dinner and were so amazed by the quality of the drinks, food and service. So much so that we agreed we needed to take my in-laws there when they visited (FIL is from Pakistan). We got to take them last night, and had an absolute blast. The number of times my FIL said how the food tasted just like home… I lost count. And the mocktails are out of this world good. So many seasonal options to choose from, and the presentation is incredible. We all sat there wishing we had 2 or 3 stomachs just so we could eat more of the food. Oh and I almost forgot that the decor is so beautiful (I’m a sucker for food closed brick), and they play Pakistani music that had me trying to sing along with my FIL while we ate. As we left, my FIL said “we need to come back here every time we visit.” I don’t think I can say anything better than that.

We tried Lazizi Restaurant in DC — the food was okay, but it didn’t really taste like authentic Pakistani cuisine. The drinks were good and the service was decent. Overall, it was an average experience.

formatted_address: 1010 St Paul St, Baltimore, MD 21202, United States
name: Posi's Kitchen

reviews.text: First time eating here and I am absolutely in LOVE. From the decor, to music, and most importantly the food everything was impeccable. I order a cinnamon toast matcha latte, shrimp fries, and my friend had the chicken bowl. The latte definitely lived up to the hype and the shrimp fries were crispy and flavorfilled.

Popped in for a snack on the way to my train. Great vibe, fantastic meat pie, and I loved the apple pie matcha.

Next time I'm in Baltimore I'll stop in for a proper meal, the full menu looks great!

From the moment we stepped inside Posi's, we knew we would be in for a treat. The decor was sophisticated and chic, with warm lighting creating a welcoming atmosphere. The attentive service was impeccable. Our server, Ola, was incredibly welcoming and offered a contagious smile from the moment we walked in. But the food itself stole the show. The meat pie was absolutely fantastic, with a buttery, flaky crust and a warm, seasoned beef filling. We also devoured the shawarma, where the perfectly seasoned beef practically melted in the mouth, and the jollof, which had a wonderful smoky flavor that perfectly complemented the umami of the roasted chicken. Ola made sure we were satisfied with all our food and drink, and his enthusiasm for the cuisine was contagious. Posi's is a hidden gem that needs to be shared. I highly recommend it to anyone who appreciates authentic and flavorful West African cuisine.

Ordered the Chicken Shawarma and was very disappointed. The majority of it was filled with hot dogs and not chicken pieces. Have had Chicken Shawarma elsewhere and it was a lot less money and was all chicken. The flavor was good, but for the price and what I received I will not order that again. It was the size of a small burrito for $15.

Not sure why it was full of hot dogs and I didn’t have time to go back since I was on lunch break.

11/10 every time I come here it’s a hit! They have a new menu now after being closed for renovations for 2 months and it’s even better than before. bowls, jollof, salads, coffee, matcha!!! OMG I love it here… I order almost everyday! This family business is one you WANT TO SUPPORT!

formatted_address: 17471 Jefferson Davis Hwy, Dumfries, VA 22026, United States
name: Safari AFRICAN RESTAURANT LLC

reviews.text: Stood at the counter waiting for couple of minutes but no one came out to acknowledge me until I rang the bell on the counter. I had some questions about the menu but no one was available for another couple of minutes. I was the only one in the restaurant until I placed my order. I was met with laughter when I asked about waakye. Like I did not know what I was talking about. Was told the food will be ready in 5 to 10 minutes. Waited longer than that. Zero engagement when I paid for the meal. I decided to eat a few bites my vehicle. Stew was not hot. Food was warm. All pepper. Very disappointed that I drove from Stafford to Dumfries for bad service and food I could have prepared at home.  Treat all your customers the same regardless of whether you think they speak the  dilect or not. Money is green! Y'all just lost a customer!!

Being a mystery reviewer and an African at the same time, I have noticed our own people are our own fall downs. From Rahama to Hajara to Safari to Aburi, 90% of the negative reviews are from African's. Let's give a simple scenario, you called to order wakye, order is taking, now you are asking me when it will be ready knowing you are 30mins away and wakye, jollof and Fried Rice is ready on an order.I have been in the restaurant answered a call for an order and 3hrs later, it was still not picked up, and this customer ordered things that are ordered to cook, like bake Tilapia, fried yam, boiled yam, kelewele, some soup s they want certain types of fish and meat, can you imagine, you are an African ordering baked Tilapia and when they give you an hour to pick up, you are mad saying that's going take too long. My sister, in my African accent, how long does it take you to bake Tilapia at home?
Am sorry I have a long story, but have you seen and heard what they do for the community. They feed our children twice a year for free, not to mention their portions. Support your fellow sisters and brothers. If you don't feel like baking your own fish and frying your own yam, expect to wait a bit cause we all know certain meals are not good cold. Just excited patience just like you do with every other American restaurant.
The Reviewer

If I could give zero stars, I would. The customer service here is absolutely unacceptable. The bald-headed gentleman working the counter was completely unprofessional he was dismissive and seemed irritated by customers simply asking about their orders.

To make things worse, the food didn’t even match what was advertised. Items listed on the menu were missing or replaced without explanation, and when I asked about it, I got attitude instead of answers. That’s not how you treat paying customers.

I ended up leaving because of how poor the customer service was, and I will never go back. For a place that calls itself a restaurant, you’d expect at least basic courtesy and honesty about what’s being served. Instead, I left disappointed, disrespected, and feeling like customer satisfaction means nothing here. Safari African Restaurant LLC seriously needs to retrain their staff and live up to the quality they claim to offer.

I came here one day with some friends. I was from out of town and visiting them for a few days. I did some research, and this place kept on coming up as one of the best spots in town. I don't have a lot of African experience, so I was instantly intrigued. After a morning of exploring the Prince William Forest, we came here for a good lunch.

As a guy who's not well versed in the cuisine, I asked for advice, and I was lead in the right direction. I can't seem to find the exact menu item, but I know it the main focal point was that jollof rice. Man, the flavors in that rice were very new to me, and very delicious. Lots of good heat, but not spicy at all. You gotta try it.

Also on my place was some sort of meat, some sort of delicious fish on the bone, a nice hard boiled egg, and some sweet plantains. Along with a small salad. Good meat, good sauce. Love eating meat off the bone, adds so much good flavor. Just a really nice meal.

I also got some Sweet Plantain Balls (Caclo)	as an app. These things were amazing! I usually don't like plantains, But these were very soft, coated in a tangy, umami powder, again a new thing for me.

Overall, I very much enjoyed this place. If you're ever in Dumfries, VA, I would highly recommend you stop by, as this was the best food I had the whole time I was in town!

Had a great time at safar- the woman that served me gave me Jollof on top of my order , I ordered fried rice and chicken everyone was nice ,calm and most of all they got serene place … now I’m stuck I can’t let go off safari yall lit 🔥🔥🔥🔥🇬🇭

formatted_address: 946 Swan Creek Rd E, Fort Washington, MD 20744, United States
name: Africaribbean Taste

reviews.text:
Despite the numorous bad reviews, I had the pleasure of ordering a combination dish of Julio rice with oxtail and curry goat, and the entire experience was outstanding. From the moment I walked in, I was greeted warmly and served immediately. The staff explained exactly what I could order with my choice of meat, which made the process simple and welcoming.

My food was prepared quickly and came out perfectly. The flavors were rich, authentic, and memorable. When I asked about their drink selection, they gave me a wonderful explanation of soursop—a drink I had seen a Jamaican coworker enjoy but had never tried myself. After tasting it for the first time, I can confidently say it won’t be my last.

Africaribbean truly delivers a one-of-a-kind dining experience. Between the incredible food, the attentive service, and the cultural authenticity, this is a place worth supporting. I highly encourage others to do business with them—you won’t be disappointed.

I ordered the Brown Stew Chicken with jollof rice and plantains. The chicken (thighs) were very tender, delicious, and flavourful. Here is my only criticism: The jollof rice may be seasoned with cardamon and hints of cinnamon. Because the brown stew chicken is so savory, it throws off the flavor a bit. Imagine someone sprinking cinnamon in your gravy.....that is what it tastes like. White rice would be more complimentary to this dish and the pallette. The plantains are very tasty, and they are cooked to perfection with a nice and subtle crisp on the edges; however, they do not pair well with this dish since the Brown Stew Chicken is already slightly sweet. Cabbage would probably be a better selection. I would order this dish again, but I'd take it home and eat it over white rice. Great customer service. Average price point for an establishment like this. The jollof rice is a hard pass for me.
Tasty Spinach Stew with goat meat and fufu. The stew just needed a little more palm oil. Otherwise, my dish was yummy.
First time purchasing food from here. I had the jerk chicken with jollof rice, plantains and mixed greens. Everything was really good. Staff was friendly. Will definitely eat here again.

I got a little bit of chicken for the price that I paid and they didn’t even have little containers to get sauce on the side. That’s the only reason why I wanted Jamaican food in the first place. I almost told her never mind. But she had already put the food in the container.

formatted_address: 1005 U St NW, Washington, DC 20001, United States
name: Oohh's & Aahh's

reviews.text:
I had Oohh’s & Aahh’s delivered since there’s no dine-in at this location, so I can’t really speak on the atmosphere or service. That said, the food itself was pretty good.

The macaroni and cheese was creamy and well done, and the hot honey chicken was flavorful with a nice balance of sweetness and heat. The strawberry cake was also a standout moist and enjoyable. The greens were decent but could use a bit more seasoning to really shine.

Overall, the food hit more than it missed, and I’d definitely recommend giving it a try, especially if you’re ordering delivery
It took us about 25 min to get there before we headed back to NYC and it was worth the trip and the wait. Everything was great, including that side of rice. Can’t believe we forgot the cornbread.

I went to howard years ago 2016-2020 and Oohh’s and aahh’s was in its prime. I’m back in DC visiting and I wanted to come get the food that I always loved and known. For one it was very bland the yams had no type of sweetness or flavor. You can tell by the picture the mac was HORRIBLE, it looks like box mac but tasted even worse and just not the mac I remember them making. I had to go back and get a different side because the mac was disgusting. They gave me a side of cabbage, the cabbage was also flavorless. The only thing that tasted the same was the fried chicken. When they was a hole in the wall before the renovations everything slapped and was on point they fell off so bad.

Fish was decent (fried catfish & grilled salmon) but the sides were way below average. I was not impressed. The mac n cheese was not good! Very bad taste & texture. Very clunky. I was honestly looking forward to that side the most. 😔Mashed potatoes were missing the gravy and were continuously still “hard” after re-warming up. 😕 No bueno. I would not return to this specific takeout location. I agree with other reviews that this establishment is overpriced for the output...

This place was straight bomb and the ribs was a decision hit I can’t say anything bad about them. It took three minutes to get my meal and lawd this was it best in this city of Washington DC I have had and I’m from Houston Texas. This is my goto must have when I’m in the city.

formatted_address: 9410 Walnut St, Dallas, TX 75243, United States
name: Shuri African Restaurant

reviews.text:
First time trying Nigerian food. The gentleman who runs the place was so kind and welcoming to us. He took time to explain all the dishes and flavors and even how to eat with fufu. He then gave us several generous samples of different dishes. I felt like we were guests at his house. The egusi was yummy as was the jolloff rice and okra.
Counter service spot with seating -  come for the food and experience!
The food was delicious. I ordered vegetable soup with goat meat, okra soup with assorted meat and jollof rice with goat meat. I will definitely return.

10/10 experience. From the staff to the rice and stew I ordered. I paid $20 for enough serving for 4-5 people with self control/portion control lol. I’m not one of those people and it was hard to not finish it in one sitting. Meat was veryyyyy tender… came apart with just a spoon. The stew tasted like my own version so I might not even stress myself to cook again. Can’t wait to try the okra soup and eba.

Authentic Flavor Explosion!

I had the pleasure of dining at this incredible African restaurant, and let me just say—every bite delivered bold, unforgettable flavor. I ordered the goat meat pepper soup, and it was outstanding. The meat was tender and well-seasoned, cooked to perfection with just the right kick of spice that warms your chest without overpowering the palate.

I paired it with steamed rice and a side of vegetable soup, which complemented the dish beautifully. The vegetable soup was hearty and flavorful, a perfect balance to the heat of the pepper soup. You can tell the food is made with love and authentic technique. If you’re craving real African cuisine that delivers on taste, this spot does not miss. I’ll definitely be back!

I’m new to Dallas and loving it. This place didn’t disappoint me one bit. Customer service was great! The food was soooo delicious, I couldn’t stop eating it. I will definitely be eating here a couple of times a week.  Thank you for the amazing egusi soup,vegetables and pounded yam.

formatted_address: 1405 Jupiter Rd #116, Plano, TX 75074, United States
name: West African Way

reviews.text: Had the Chicken Yassa, Egusi, Benachin Beef, Lamb dibi. The food was amazing and the chef was very friendly. The food is halal and portions were big as well. The lamb dibi was the best I've had in Senegal or abroad.

We have taken far too long to eat here.  It is definitely a family style business, as can be seen in the total lack of corporate concepts, like having everything on the menu; bringing all the food out at once; making sure customers were attended on arrival.

We wanted chicken wings, which we've had before, but they weren't available.  We wanted the lamb, but were told 40 minutes to wait.  And there's the thing.  Everything is cooked to order.  And it shows.

Wife got the fried whole fish; I got the grilled chicken and sliced, fried potatoes.  It's all delicious and the serving sizes are huge.  I brought most of mine home for later, and the wife ate the fish, but brought her sides home.

Come and get something really unique.  African food is very rare, although East Africa restaurants are spawning, West African, Ghana, Ivory Coast, Nigeria, these flavours are something to seek out.

This place exceeded my expectation!! Normally, I set my expectation very low when it comes to other countries' food;  that way I'm not disappointed no matter what enters my mouth, but I'm actually very impressed with WEST AFRICAN WAY!

I've definitely found my new go to African restaurant. The food and the customer’s experience 10/10. I got cassava leaves with rice !!

My husband and I got takeout tonight and absolutely loved the food. We tried the meat pie, plantains, yassa chicken, and dibi lamb. All of it was amazing, very flavorful, and full of spices but not extremely spicy if that is something that matters to you. This was our first experience trying west African food, and we will definitely come back. Do order earlier than you think you need to - we ordered on a Thursday night and were told 40 minutes, but it was probably closer to an hour.
exceeded expectations! Such an amazing meal and very great hospitality! Definitely going to recommend and bring more people to eat here.

formatted_address: 4515 Village Fair Dr Suite E4, Dallas, TX 75224, United States
name: Amie's African Kitchen & Grill

reviews.text: First time here. The egusi was spicy and good. But it tasted different than any other places I've been to. It was a lot darker as well, and no, i don't think it was because of the palm oil. Maybe it was overcooked, I don't know. It was still good to me. I'll definitely be back. I do wish they had prices on the pictures or a menu out with prices. I was charged more than the menu I say online. So that's my complaint. If you're in the area, check them out.
I had the oxtail as well as the egusi soup with fufu. They were flavorful and the serving sizes were good.

The food was good to the taste. My only concern was that as i was eating I noticed what felt like glass in the egusi and fufu. It was gritty like tiny shards of glass were in it, and i know thats not apart of the recipe. I understand people make mistakes, but next time please make sure you are being careful as your cooking the food.
Came from San Antonio stopped by this place and the food lived up to my expectations . Quick service , friendly and staff was nice. Coming back for that Egusi and Fufu!

I ordered two dishes mixed together and a side of rice if I known that, it was gonna be $30 just for a bowl of rice a bowl of egusi and lamb mixed together. I wouldn’t have gotten it, but it is good. That’s the only reason, but for $30, you’re gonna have to do better than that than just a little bowl and fufu

formatted_address: 9780 Walnut St #138, Dallas, TX 75243, United States
name: Kanny's Restaurant and Lounge

reviews.text: Excellent customer service. Very delicious food!!! The staff and the manager was very professional and friendly. The place was very clean and comfortable!!! The portion size of the food is not only amazing, but it will get you soooo full. I ordered 2 extra meals to-go because it was so good!
The food was amazing. super fresh, flavorful, and just the right portions. Definitely a spot I’d come back to! It was so good I had to come back with a friend the next day to have her try it

I really enjoyed my visit here! The food was excellent and full of flavor. I ordered the fish with plantains, and it came with coleslaw and spaghetti—I was pleasantly surprised by how generous the portion was. Everything tasted great. The owner was so kind, and the customer service was top-notch. I’m looking forward to coming back!

The customer service is top notch. The owner - Ola is so welcoming, friendly and helpful. The food was delicious!!! Restaurant was clean. All round a wonderful experience. I highly recommend this place
My friends and I are visiting from Chicago and this place was recommended. The food was great as well as the service. Will definitely be back!

formatted_address: 13021 Coit Rd # 98, Dallas, TX 75240, United States
name: Dallul East African Cuisine

reviews.text: Honestly It only got 1 star because the coffee was really good and the food and prices/portions were decent. This was probably the worst experience I’ve ever had. The interior was underwhelming and it smelled really bad of smoke, despite “no smoking” signs posted every other foot. somehow it was dead inside but we still got the worst service ever. Our server took forever to take out food order and instead talked to some guy at the bar for 20 minutes. Also, another table twice out size came in, got their order taken, and finnished their food before we could even place out food order. They also ate all their food, payed out, left, and had their table cleaned again (about a 40 minute experience) befor the server ever acknowledged us again. We were very clearly done eating by then and had to walk up to the computers to finally pay out and leave. I don’t know what all the good reviews are for but I’m literally from east Africa and can tell you there’s better food out there and there DEFINITELY is better service literally anywhere else.

Went here with 3 friends for dinner. Food isn't much more than $20 per person, and only after we got extra stuff.

This place seems like authentic African food, and it's refreshingly local. They even taught us the correct way to eat this one dish for the best enjoyment.

The food I ordered was great, a spiced chicken and rice meal. But there is a very rich menu available.

The staff were extremely friendly and happy we were there. Giving a comfortable atmosphere. Only thing we had to do was get attention of the server for the bill. Otherwise it was perfect, and we enjoyed it for hours.

Definitely seeing if I can revisit this place next vacation.

This was my first time having East African food so I was a bit nervous walking in but excited for an adventure! I asked the waiter for advice. They were really friendly and excited to share their favorite food with someone new. They asked me questions about what I liked, and what I’m game to try.

I had a large portion of spicy lamb and small portions of several vegetables. I’m not sure if it directly lined up to a menu item but less than $20 seemed fair, it was all tasty, and I hope to have some more soon!
Service was amazing. Music was bumpin. And food was bussin. 10/10 would definitely come back! Please give this place a chance :)
The food was so nice, service was so nice!

formatted_address: 945 W Stacy Rd #130, Allen, TX 75013, United States
name: Jollof Haus - West African Flavors

reviews.text:
Edit: just had my take home side of jollof rice. So smoky and with lovely spices!!
Everything was delicious. We had the goat efu with a side of poundo and zobo and suya bowl with pineapple and ginger juice and plantains. The flavors are PERFECT!! Very friendly service and a comfortable environment. Will 100% be back!

Delicious food. Great atmosphere.
I am not a big fan of meat and chicken; made the salad and shrimp my choice and it did not disappoint.
Jollof haus is my new favorite spot.
This was an excellent meal and I would highly recommend this place to anyone! The restaurant was clean and staff were friendly. The meal preparation was beautiful and the food tasted delicious.
I’m not normally a salmon girl but their salmon bowl is delicious!! The rice is so well seasoned. I also really enjoyed their chicken wings. Very flavorful! Staff is super friendly. We will be back!

I tried the jollof rice with goat meat and a pineapple ginger drink. The jollof rice has a smoky flavor, a bit hard, oily at the bottom & flavorless. The goat meat was great. The drink tasted like spicy orange juice. The environment is very clean & I received great customer service. I would try again but a different dish.

formatted_address: 9220 Skillman St #115, Dallas, TX 75243, United States
name: Aso Rock | Restaurant & Lounge

reviews.text: Great service from start to finish. Food was delicious! I ordered the chicken and Jollof rice. Side of plantain. The okra soup with beef was a little tough but overall okay. Would definitely come back!

Ms Bridget is a great server🥰. She remembered my bae and I from our last visit. I love her service, such a great attitude and demeanor. The food here is delish and reminds me of home 🤤🤤. The owner came over and checked in on us which was a warm greeting, he got us right with a couple house drinks. I enjoyed my time here and will definitely come back, again 💯‼️

The food was good, but the service was completely unacceptable — honestly, horrible. The waitress was rude. I sat at the table and she didn’t even come over to take my order. I had to get up and go place it myself.

As you can see in the photos, the food was served and dropped on the table like it was for a dog. And to top it all off, my whisky was served in a plastic cup…

It’s really sad how some employees can ruin an entire business with that kind of attitude.

I came in not sure what to expect especially because of the reviews online but I was pleasantly surprised. I can easily say they have the best jollof rice I have had in Dallas and I do consider myself a jollof connoisseur. It was Smokey and soft and just felt like home. Now the Nkwpbo was just WOW. So delicious, soft and I was simply blown away. If you can visit here and try the food! So good! I’m impressed! I’ll be back. Lmao I started eating in the car cause of how good it was ugh loved 10/10 for me!

Update: Thank you to the management of Aso rock for reaching out and promptly handling the issue mentioned in my previous review. To the team I met today, thank you for being awesome and kind. Like I previously mentioned the moi moi is a 100/10 and I’ll be back next month for my monthly batch. Best moi moi in dfw( trust me we have tried a few places and nothing beats Aso rock so far). If you want good moi moi, best believe they have what you need. 😝

formatted_address: 9205 Skillman St, Dallas, TX 75243, United States
name: Aggies Restaurant

reviews.text: The food was pretty good. The spices used to marinate the fish is great . The plantain is sweet and ripe perfect! I would say the environment is pretty dark, but it’s clean so I would come back
Aggies Restaurant in Dallas totally surprised me—in the best way! The food tasted homemade, portions were generous, and the staff made me feel like family. Left with a happy belly and a smile!

Aggie’s Grill & Bar never disappoints! Their food is absolutely delicious, and I love that they keep adding new items to the menu. Tonight, I had the peppered chicken with plantain and spinach, and it was packed with flavor—perfectly seasoned and cooked to perfection. A special shoutout to the Manager Lani, who provided top-tier customer service. She was super friendly and even recommended a Strawberry Margarita, which was a game-changer! I was surprised to learn that they now serve alcohol, and at just $8 per drink, I couldn’t resist having a few. If you’re looking for great food, amazing service, and a welcoming atmosphere, Aggie’s is the place to be. I’ll definitely be back to try the Mackerel Fish with plantain next time! Highly recommend checking them out.

This restaurant had me extremely shocked.

As soon as we walked in they didnt say 'hello" " welcome to our restaurant " nothing, just looked at us

(there wasn't a lot of people there)
(It was very dark in the restaurant)

There were two people at the cashier, and there was one lady she was on her phone THE WHOLE TIME we were ordering...

Anyway,  she told me the food will be ready in 10 MINUTES,  we walked in (it's been 10 minutes) and guess what... the food wasn't ready . So we had to wait half an hour

Moving on to the food
IT SMELLS AMAZING OMG

But this food cost 21 DOLLARS ?? The service made me a bit upset for my meal to be that much money

I will not be returning 😭

I usually order takeout at this restaurant but I sat there for the first time last week, a very hot afternoon of July. It was so hot inside. I'm not sure if the AC was off or not working properly.

Nonetheless, the food was great. I ordered the Spinach Parfait stew. It came with white rice. You can also substitute with plantain or fufu.

I definitely recommend but be mindful of the time of the day you're going if you want to dine in.

formatted_address: 3950 Rosemeade Pkwy Suite 100, Dallas, TX 75287, United States
name: Aldeez Afribbean, Restaurant & Lounge

reviews.text: We had a large group come in for a birthday lunch and came an hour after they opened. Mari was great. She was the only one there besides the cook and took care of us by herself. Everyone’s order was correct. She had a great attitude and it was nice to enjoy each other without any issues. We always enjoy coming here. We’ve been all different times.

I am very upset this time with the portion amount and the price that I paid for the side order of Jerk Chicken Side $8. I guess the tariffs have hit this place, I've never received so little! It wasn't fresh and over cooked. I've been to this place over 20 times in the past for their jerk chicken and fish!!! Will not be getting again, this has turned me completely off, all prices have increased and the portions have either stayed the same or decreased. Ebu, u failed me my guy 😭

Update 10/2/2025:
5 Stars

Aldeez has restored my faith with this one. I've been going here for years for their amazingly tasty Whole Tilapia. I said let me try again after my bad experience last month, this time they did not disappoint at all! I will be ordering my fish again soon!!! I’m still cringing over the price though but it’s to be expected in this economy!

Second time I tried to order food from this spot and second time I get home and noticed the the greens was a heep of mush mash mess. The rest of my dishes i ordered seemed just ok. Aldeez you need to do better of just quit trying with the canned greens.

Good - ****
Was looking for a good Caribbean restaurant open after 9 and found this. Had the jamaican beef patty as appetizer and oxtail, curry goat as entrees. Loved the flavor. The ambience is more of bar/dance so not a family favorable but the food was good. I wish the food had more heat which would have given a kick. Still the overall experience was good

Came into this establishment, was not greeted at all. The two hostesses sat behind the bar and had full-blown conversations and on their phones. There was literally maybe 10 to 15 people in the restaurant and when I asked for assistance with ordering, they stated that they will get a waiter and never did. I sat there waiting on someone for almost 10 minutes. I asked to speak to a manager, and the manager listened with her hands on her hips and a facial expression that stated she was disinterested. I have been coming to this establishment since it was transferred from Zenna and I will never be back again. I am extremely disappointed with the services, and I will be spreading the word to everyone I know. I will make it my mission that people know the type of horror service that you will provide.

formatted_address: 5200 W Stacy Rd Suite 100, McKinney, TX 75070, United States
name: Mabel's African Cuisine & Bar

reviews.text: My husband and I were in the area and we always look for good traditional Nigerian food when we’re out.  After reading the reviews I showed my husband the reviews and photos and we decided on Mabel’s. We made the right decision! The interior was beautiful, the service was impeccable and the food was excellent, full of flavor.  Presentation is everything because we eat our eyes first…the presentation of the food was lovely. My husband had the efo riro with goat. The efo riro has cut pieces of cow skin in it & was yummy. There was also puff puff that we had as an appetizer it came out fresh and hot. I had the Abula with assorted meat. I ordered a fish cake to go and my hubby liked the efo riro so much that he ordered some to go and I ordered the Asun with rice and plaintain to go for later. Later is here and the Asun was equally tasty. Please stop by if you have a chance and give Mabel’s a try. McKinney has been blessed with a great West African restaurant. May God continue to bless and prosper this business.

Wow! This place was absolutely incredible. Not only was the staff incredible kind, the manager and our waitress took the time to answer all of our questions (as this was our first time). They absolutely made the experience an incredible one, and we were soo appreciative about all the information they gave us. The decor was beautiful, everything was clean and comfortable. The food, was sooo incredibly flavorful and delicious. It was unlike anything I had ever tried before, the goat was tender and the spices were an explosion of flavor, the fried dough was delicious and not too sweet, I absolutely loved the fish rolls and the meat pie as well. The fufu and egusi is what we came for, but we left completely satisfied and blown away by the service. Absolutely recommend!

We went for lunch this afternoon and it was an amazing experience! Our server took the time to explain the menu, the flavor profiles and the heat ratings of the food. I have never tried African cuisine before and I will definitely be back! I tried the Crispy Crust Chicken Pie, Jollof Rice with Beef Tips and Plantains and Puff-Puff (its fried dough and was so good!). Cannot wait to try something different next time.

Absolutely incredible dinner. We ordered it to go but when we picked it up, the restaurant was so lovely that I wish we would have just dined in. But we will definitely be back. We had the beef meat pie, chicken meat pie, fish roll, spicy pepper beef tips, and the majestic sampler. Everything not only looked beautiful but was absolutely delectable. I've never had goat meat and I absolutely love the flavor now, and the seasonings were perfection. We can't wait to go back! It's rare to get this quality of food with this quality of service. The proprietor/manager was so welcoming, kind, and spoke with us at length about the menu and what we should try next. Highly, highly recommend!

I've passed Mabel's many times on my way to Fairview and each time I promised myself that I would stop in one day and check out the menu. Well, I did just that last week and I must say that I am happy that I stopped in! The interior is beautifully decorated with colorful art work and has a lively, casual yet upscale atmosphere which makes it a perfect place for dining with friends, family or business associates. The dining area was clean and large enough to accommodate a large group, but still had cozy feel.

The staff was very welcoming and immediately greeted us and brought out glasses of water and complimentary PuffPuffs (like donut balls, but less sweet). There were QR codes on the table to pull up the menu which made it easy for everyone to see the menu and to place an order with our server. Our server was very kind and attentive, she kept our drinks topped off and brought the food on time. I ordered the Egusi Stew with FuFu and a fish meat roll, my husband ordered a meat pie, Efo Riro with Amala,  and my sons ordered Jollof rice and Egusi Stew with FuFu and mixed meat. Everything came out on time, the meat pies were first to come out and were hot, fresh and tasty. When we were done eating the pies the Jollof rice was delivered, followed by the rest of the dishes. All of the dishes were very flavorful and were throughly enjoyed by each of my family members.  Overall we had a wonderful experience and plan to return to try out some of the other dishes on the menu.

formatted_address: 1499 Regal Row, Dallas, TX 75247, United States
name: Street Suya

reviews.text:
This was a disappointing experience.  I ordered the Lamb Chop and what I received was far from what was advertised and what I expected.

My plate, and the plates of others at City Hall, suffered from multiple issues.

The food was served cold, which was a major turn-off.  The vegetables were bland and mostly just onions, which seemed to be the only thing seasoned. The rice had an overpowering amount of some seasoning that made it unpleasant to eat.

Worst of all, the lamb chops were mostly bone with very little meat.  It felt like a ripoff.

I compared my plate to others in my group who ordered the same dish, and they had similar complaints.  It wasn't just an isolated incident with my meal.  It seems there are serious consistency issues in the kitchen.

Overall, this was a very poor dining experience.  The cold food, bland vegetables, over-seasoned rice, and bony lamb chops were unacceptable, especially given the price. I would not recommend.

I visited on a Saturday—their only day at the farmers market—and it was amazing! The experience totally won me over, and I’m already planning a visit to their brick-and-mortar location on Regal Row. Highly recommended 🫰🏾🫰🏾🫰🏾🫰🏾

Street Suya is hands down some of the best food I’ve had! The flavor is incredible — bold, spicy, and full of that authentic heat that hits just right. Every bite is fire in the best way. If you love real flavor and spice, this place does not miss. Highly recommend!

Was craving suya yesterday and decided to give Street Suya a chance since it was nearby. We ordered both the shrimp suya plate and the beef suya plate for pickup (there is no dining area on location). It should also be noted that the business is located within a culinary kitchen and does not have a lone storefront with its own signage — don’t get confused and leave like we almost did. Just look for unit 312 and know that you are in the right place.

Everything was made fresh to order and hot; therefore, we didn’t mind a little wait (order ahead if under time constraint). The jumbo shrimp and tender cuts of beef really hit the spot.
