I appreciated having the suya on the side, allowing me to control my sodium intake. The yuca fries were well seasoned and the bell pepper mix with onions had a pleasant light crisp to them. Service was also great.

We are so glad to have found this place and hope to visit again soon. Would be great to see these folk’s food truck around town, or perhaps a small space for them inside of a local food court for dine in.

Let’s support our local small businesses by spreading the word about this awesome suya!
My second time having it. First time I had the chicken suya, today I got beef. Both was amazing and the owner is super sweet and friendly, I will definitely be back.

formatted_address: 2905 E Arkansas Ln #100, Arlington, TX 76010, United States
name: Angie Winners Kitchen

reviews.text: Angie Winner’s Kitchen was a wonderful experience. The food is cook to order and fresh. You can expect a short wait however, it will be worth the wait. I had the goat stew and rice and my husband had the ground nut soup with goat and kokonte. Everything came out fresh and delicious. The owner and chef herself came out to greet us and answer any questions we had. Definitely a 10/10 and we will be back.

A Culinary Masterpiece: Angie Winners Kitchen is a True Winner!

​From the moment we walked in, the experience at Angie Winners Kitchen was warm and welcoming, perfectly setting the stage for the incredible meal that followed. This is, without a doubt, some of the best and most authentic African cuisine I have ever had.

I am confidently giving it a full five stars because every dish we tried showcased passion, expertise, and a masterful touch with traditional West African flavors. If you are looking for fresh, perfectly executed, and truly memorable food, this is the place.

​The mains were the absolute highlight of the meal. The Jollof Rice and Beef was a phenomenal combination. The Jollof itself was deeply infused with tomato and spices, giving it that beautiful smoky, signature flavor that is often missed elsewhere. It was cooked perfectly, with each grain separate yet tender.

The accompanying beef was incredibly tender and juicy—clearly marinated before being cooked down until it practically melted in my mouth.

​We also enjoyed the Gobe Beans, which were prepared flawlessly. They were rich, hearty, and perfectly seasoned, providing a wonderful, earthy counterpoint to the spice and richness of the Jollof.

​But what truly elevated the meal were the sides and appetizers, which sent the experience out of this world. The fried plantains were absolute perfection: gorgeously ripe, caramelized on the outside, and soft and sweet on the inside—they are an absolute, non-negotiable must-try!

And I still can't stop thinking about the savory delight of the Meat Pie. Its golden pastry crust was incredibly light and flaky, giving way to a robust, savory filling that was spiced just right. It’s the kind of comfort food you dream about.
​Every item served was fresh, hot, and prepared with incredible care.

The quality here is exceptional, the service is friendly, and it’s clear why they call themselves 'Winners Kitchen.' I will absolutely be back soon to explore the rest of the menu.

Do yourself a favor and visit—you won’t regret it!

I just had my first experience trying Ghanaian food, and I have to say, it’s absolutely amazing! The flavors are rich, bold, and truly unique, making it an easy 10 out of 10. Beyond the food itself, the warmth and kindness of the people here makes the experience even better. Everyone has been so welcoming and sweet, and it’s made me fall in love with not just the cuisine, but the culture as a whole.
Angie’s Winner Kitchen did not disappoint! Amazing food, great flavors, and top-notch customer service. My husband and I really enjoyed ourselves — highly recommend!

I had a great experience trying Banku with Okra stew, meat pie, and the pineapple ginger drink. The food was so good I forgot to take the picture of everything. I felt like I was transported into my grandmothers kitchen. The service was great, everyone was nice. I wish my Okra Stew had a little more pepper but that’s my only complaint! Will definitely be back!

formatted_address: 3920 Rosemeade Pkwy #100, Dallas, TX 75287, United States
name: Cafe Nubia

reviews.text:
Very average to below average experience. Would not return.

-Food was not good and was not hot upon arrival.
-Drinks were just okay and were made incorrectly (this was corrected).
-Received food before drinks, even though drinks were ordered first. We had to remind the server about our drinks.
-Had to ask a different server for plates after the food arrived.
+Enjoyed the live music performance.
-The DJ was too loud to hear people at our table.

What we ordered:
🍽 Cauliflower - Spinach Dip- Beef Suja
🍸 Espresso Martini - Strawberry Lemon Drop - Nubian Margarita - Beehive Bellini
***
UPDATE: We had a reservation. We mentioned it was someone's birthday celebration when the reservation was made and also mentioned it to the server when we were seated. Their birthday was not acknowledged. We'd ordered shots that never arrived and had plans to order entrees after sharing starters, but decided against it.

I really enjoyed my dinner at Cafe Nubia. Keyerra was very sweet and attentive with our order. We had the Nubia Wings, Beef Suya, and the Blackened Salmon. Everything came out at a reasonable pace and was absolutely delicious. Also the band was absolutely amazing. They had a great setlist and singer was phenomenal. I can’t wait to come back

Very delicious food. I initially ordered the Cajun pasta which was really spicy. The waiter and kitchen were so nice to make me another dish, which I appreciated. I enjoyed our drinks also. They had a live band play r&b music and it was a good time. The only thing I didn’t like was the alcohol service fee. Not sure why that is necessary on a bill but other than that, a good time!

My daughter took me out for my birthday dinner and always has a way of finding a new and unique place which is right up my ally.
The app was Beef Sambusa. I had the meat sampler and she had the tilapia in a spicy tomato sauce. All cooked in a Sudanese spices and style. You can see that they plate the food nicely as well. Everything was very delicious. 😋

Highly recommend ‼️

The $16 Wednesday steak dinner was delicious.  The waitress was attentive. The decor and vibe are 10 out of 10. The patio needed a good sweep and wiped down. I found Cafe Nubia on Eventbrite with the offer of smoking cigars on the patio. I was looking forward to the outside vibe. I definitely will be back for happy hour.

formatted_address: 9605 Clark Rd Suite 100, Dallas, TX 75249, United States
name: Bea's catering Nigeria & Soul Food

reviews.text: Did not like the food at all. I feel like I wasted my money and gas and time. Will not be back. Sweet lady trash soul food.
I loveeee this place! The food is so good, ms. Bea gives you a generous amount of food. She’s always so sweet and nice my daughter also loves it. Real authentic Nigerian food. I 100% recommend.

I had been searching for a place to get some good Egusi soup and fufu... I came across this place and decided to try it. It was so good I brought family to try it back to back. Everything is made fresh and is so delicious!

My Hispanic people… your going to love this food! This is a good spicy! Spices are so healthy it healed my sinuses and I’m sure much more! Food that is delicious and healing! I love it! Me and my daughter are hooked for good on African food 😍

Great food and customer service! Highly recommend if you’re looking for some authentic Nigerian food! The wings and veggie soup (with beef pieces) were my favorite but everything tasted amazing. Such flavorful food ❤️

formatted_address: 9191 Forest Ln # 2, Dallas, TX 75243, United States
name: Lalibela Restaurant & Bar

reviews.text: Lalibela Restaurant & Bar was a great find. The Ethiopian dishes were rich and full of flavor, and sharing them with injera made the meal feel warm and authentic. The staff were welcoming and added to the cozy vibe.

Yummy and delicious. First time here. So glad I tried the food. The veggie platter and 4 meets were excellent for two people. The flavors popped. Such comfort in the food. The service was excellent. The honey wine was so good. The coffee was also a nice finish to the meal. Thoroughly enjoyed it.

Second time here & it was even more amazing. Our first trip we tried the tibs which were the best in town we’ve had & the waiter recommended the ribs for our next visit. We got the ribs this visit & loved them even more then the ribs (which we didn’t think was possible). Absolutely great date night vibes, atmosphere & service. A must try in Dallas!!! 👍🏽👍🏽💜

AMAZING Ethiopian food!! We went here for dinner and it was a nice, laidback environment. This was our first time trying Ethiopian food and our server was so great helping us find what we would like!

We got the Lega Tibs and Doro Wot over the injera and everything tasted SO amazing. My mouth is watering thinking about it! Cannot wait to come back again.

We tried this Ethiopian restaurant late Friday night, and it was great! Everyone was friendly and the waitress helped walk us through the menu.

We got the vegetarian combo and gomen besiga to share, and everything was delicious! There was also more than enough food. We took plenty of leftovers for the next day.

formatted_address: 921 W Commerce St, Dallas, TX 75208, United States
name: Lagos Kitchen

reviews.text: I typically don’t leave reviews; but this is the toughest meat I’ve ever eaten. Not fresh at all. Taste like beef jerky. I couldn’t even finish it because my jaw was sore due to how touch it was.
I paid $85 and the meat was undercooked.. ALL of it.. The pounded yam still has powder in it… The taste doesn’t taste like someone African made it.. at all… I’m mad I wasted my money

Absolutely delicious!!!! I almost cried when the first drop of okro soup touched my lips.  My goodness! Chicken perfectly seasoned and not dried out like many other places. Perfect spice for those of us Africans born in America. Will definitely be a regular.

I placed an initial order from Lagos Kitchen and was extremely disappointed. The food arrived very poorly packed and was leaking so much it left a trail. The soup top was not secure and the tilapia dish container was smashed and leaking as well. I spent 20 minutes cleaning the liquid from the floor and table and then repacking the food so that it could be handled. The meat pies were another disappointment, tons of pastry and very little meat inside. I will not order again.

I never complain. In fact leaving this review pains me because I would love nothing more than to uplift and praise a fellow Nigerian. I seriously didn’t want to leave a bad review even after waiting an hour for my order but the Jollof rice is NOT FRESH at all. In facts it’s hard, I have had Jollof rice my whole life and this is just not acceptable at all. Plantains..burnt, chicken & Turkey…old. I even pushed that aside and tried the Ewa aganyin, it was goin in until I almost broke my tooth on rocks and stones in the beans. Thats was the tipping point for me. I’m sorry but this was the worst spend of my $80.

formatted_address: 8500 Ohio Dr STE 200, Plano, TX 75024, United States
name: BOXOCHOPS Modern African Kitchen - Plano

reviews.text:
I'm not experienced in Nigerian food, but I know when something tastes good. And this tastes damn good

Ordered the smokey jolof rice with turkey and a meat pie. Good portion, price and quick service. Jolof rice was incredibly flavorful and the smoke flavor really shines. The turkey was delicious but it was chewy. I will try goat next time. The meat pie was so good I had to get two more to go.

Definitely will be back to try more on their menu, and would recommend this to anyone easily.

This place is great! I decided to try it on a whim, and I'm SO glad I did. The staff was extremely friendly, offering me suggestions. I ended up ordering the chicken peppered kebabs with a side of jollof rice. It was a lot of food and the flavor was amazing. The kebabs had a little spice and we're cooked fresh and tender. The rice was a bit smokey and delicious! The food was so good, I ordered a meat pie to go for later! You have to try this place. You'll definitely come back. I know I will!

I wanted to try Eugsi Soup for a long time. We found this place today and made the drive on Sunday and so glad we did.I want to go back and order all the things. Amazing! The Eugsi is on the spicy side but nothing crazy, so full of flavor and spices. 10/10

10/10 recommend this restaurant  . I will try more items but the Jollof rice was nice and spicy and cooked to perfection and the beef suited this dish well along with the seasoning on top and red onion .. so yummy . This is my first time and they did not disappoint . The pineapple/ginger drink was super refreshing and very fresh .

Good food! Love the Jollof rice, not spicy at all. The plantains were really well fried!

Always love the puff puffs! Good to microwave the next day.

Drinks are interesting, favorite so far is the Chapman Punch.

formatted_address: 2902 Buckner Blvd Suite 255, Dallas, TX 75227, United States
name: La Marmite - African Restaurant

reviews.text: This is one of those hole in the wall places, it does not look like much, but the food is delicious and the customer service is A1. My fiance and I stopped here from Oklahoma City for a weekend trip and found this restaurant on google. As a West African girl, this was my first time eating Senegalese food and I loved It. The price is worth every bite. You will have enough food to eat and to-go. I love this place, we will be back. ❤️

I had the chicken fried rice and the peanut soup. They were both good. I also had the elusive soup and that was great but for 17.99 they don't give you much soup. Call ahead because I waited 40 plus minutes and I was the only costumer there.

We have been customers for a few months and service had been phenomenal until today. The lady was laying down on one of the benches with her shoes off speaking on the phone did not bother to even attempt to attend us just told us to go next door without any other explanation. Is this place used for money laundering?
Great restaurant! The food was amazing

This place was amazing! The food was delicious and the hospitality was better than any place I’ve visited thus far!
This should definitely be on your list of places to stop if you are a true foodie!!

formatted_address: 807 E Arkansas Ln, Arlington, TX 76010, United States
name: T's Buka

reviews.text: The cuisine offered is truly remarkable and deserves recognition. The flavors are distinct and will surely be a memorable experience. The individuals working there are incredibly welcoming and create a pleasant atmosphere. Interacting with them makes the dining experience even more enjoyable. The owner's kindness is evident in his interactions with guests. Their dedication to providing a great experience is commendable. You'll likely find yourself eager to return after your first visit. You will have a positive experience if you decide to try it.

delivered a truly satisfying meal. I ordered the panla fish in stew along with a piece of hake fish, and everything was done right.

The panla was perfectly cooked—tender, flaky, and well seasoned. The stew was rich, savory, and deeply flavorful, the kind that tastes slow-cooked and intentional. The hake fish was also well prepared, cooked just right, and clean in flavor.

Ordering the eba already prepared saves me time in the kitchen.

The young man who worked the front was really nice, although you could tell he was overwhelmed by the orders and some rude customers. I ordered jollof rice and beef. The beef was good, very tender, and had a nice flavor. The jollof rice, however, tasted burnt and like other reviews said kind of like cigarettes.

The egusi soup and fufu is very delicious, however, it’s a little too spicy. My hot Cheetos eating kid couldn’t finish the soup because of the spice. The fish is also delicious. I’ll buy the soup again but please take some of the spice out.The young gentleman (maybe in his 20s) took my order and was very polite. The young man went to the back and then the older lady and older gentleman came out from the back, looked at us and didn’t speak to us although we were the only people in there at the time we went. They just walked by us like we weren’t there. A simple “hello” or “how are you” would’ve been nice. Clean restaurant though.

I do not live near this business at all, but wanted to make sure on my visit to the area I stopped to get a plate before making the 2.5hr trip back home. I tried their food the first time after a relative came back from her vacation with a plate and I have been looking forward to the day I could make a trip of my own for their food. I ordered okra soup and egusi soup both with fufu that comes with 2 proteins, and once the same relative found out I was picking up an order, I had to turn back and place another order for her too lol! They give you plentiful portions to get full on and possibly even have some left over. I wish they had a location closer to me because I would definitely be a frequent customer. I forgot to get a picture of the food before I was already digging in.

formatted_address: 214 N Akard St, Dallas, TX 75201, United States
name: Carpe diem Kitchen & Cocktails

reviews.text: Really good food. I had blackened salmon and their deviled eggs with shrimp. Being from the Gulf it's good to have good fish to come too. Also found out they are open till 2 on Friday and Saturdays. Kitchen stays open as well. And my bartender Tish was a great hostess.

And I am glad I did. I came across the restaurant via Facebook and recently they have been on my tiktok page. decided to come in today because I was on this side of town. It was empty (which I know won’t be like that for long so I am going to enjoy it) the bartender was nice, drinks were good. The deviled eggs with shrimp were a nice appetizer. And for the entree I got Lamb chops, vegetables and jollof rice. Shockingly it was really good. If you are looking for decent Afro Cuisine they did a great job. I would come back

My wife and I came here for her birthday dinner and we should’ve left right after walking in. We walked in and not a single person was dining, this was a Friday night so this was the first red flag. There was no ac, no one greeting us, the workers that were there just stared at us as they sat. We decided to walk out and go find something else. As we were, a worker stopped us and insisted they had good food to eat and that they’d love to serve us. Feeling uncomfortable we ended up staying. Our server was very sweet, we ordered our food. Our food took a long time, finally came out and it was very average. My wife’s salmon was just okay and my meal was not as I expected. During eating we were getting hotter as there was NO AC. And they turned the lights off, music up so loud we couldn’t even speak, and it became a club atmosphere. No drinks and food was $80. Absolutely ridiculous to charge so much, care so little, and be so uncomfortable in this hot environment. I regret staying and don’t recommend anyone ever coming here unless you just want to drink in an empty restaurant.

I had a friends party here. The vibe, location, working with Marc Anthony the owner was great! I love the aesthetics. The drinks and food were amazing. Truly the only downside and one I hope they work on because I would love to see this business be a success is not enough servers, or skilled servers (but very sweet). It took way too long to get orders taken or received, maybe more people in kitchen. Everything was great, and as long as you are not in a hurry (at least on the Friday night we were there) you will enjoy yourself.

10/10 loved this place! The food was full of flavor, the music was lively, and the drinks were on point. Such a welcoming atmosphere — I really enjoyed experiencing the culture through the food and vibe. The staff were amazing and the waitresses were on point. I will be returning.

formatted_address: 1499 Regal Row, Dallas, TX 75247, United States
name: 5 Senses Nigerian Fusion

reviews.text: Our friends wanted to try something new for lunch and found 5 Senses Nigerian Fusion nearby on Google. We did not research enough and learned upon arrival that they were pickup or delivery only 😅 – no dine-in.  Chef Lola was so patient with us, and gave great recommendations on family-style platters. We ordered the herbed jollof rice, grilled chicken leg quarters, peppered turkey flats, and a stewed spinach dish. Since our order was quite large, we did have to wait about half an hour, so chef treated us with 2 boxes of fresh puff puff! These were like bite-sized Nigerian beignets, dusted with nutmeg and cinnamon sugar, and had 2 dipping options of habanero+mango and a sweet creamy glaze-like sauce. So thoughtful, and really curbed our hanger. Once we brought the food home, I did not take a great picture, because the smell was so intoxicating that we all dug right in. Everyone was super impressed with how flavorful, soulful, and filling each dish was. We had a young picky eater with us, and she ate every bite! We can't wait to try more dishes!
Food was really good a bit too spicy for me. The bread was really fantastic and the service was excellent. I did take out! The pasta is delicious and chicken really tasty.

The other reviews are giving friends/family of owner. Food is okay. I would recommend the puff puff and jollof spaghetti those taste similar to actual Nigerian food. However, they need to put salt and pepper 🌶️ in their food or somebody’s seasoning before calling it Nigerian anything.

A close friend hosted an event yesterday & food was catered by this restaurant.
I picked up the order at the establishment & the customer service was excellent.

Food was 10/10 delicious.

Refrain from visiting this establishment. While I was seated in my vehicle, I observed that the staff members were not wearing gloves, were consuming food while preparing my meal, and continued to touch my food after touching their mouths. The entire process took over 45 minutes to receive my order. Ultimately, I requested a refund, as it is unreasonable for food to take such an extended time for a single person.

formatted_address: 440 S State Hwy 78 Ste 220, Lavon, TX 75166, United States
name: Olobe's Kitchen and Catering Services

reviews.text:
OLOBE's Kitchen is truly a gem. I visited while in Texas, and the moment I walked in, it felt like a piece of home. The food was phenomenal — I got the egusi soup, jollof rice, and suya, and everything was perfectly seasoned and spicy just the way I like it. The flavors were rich, authentic, and comforting.

The owner was incredibly kind and welcoming, which made the experience even better. It’s rare to find food that tastes this good alongside such genuine hospitality.

Five stars without a doubt. Highly recommend!

This is my third time here and I honestly enjoy it. The atmosphere is amazing the music playing and the food very good size portions and very fulfilling.
I had mines to go

Olobe catered my brothers wedding, and I honestly cannot say enough amazing things about them. The Nigerian cuisine was absolutely outstanding—every dish was flavorful, perfectly prepared, and a huge hit with our guests. People are still talking about how incredible the food was.
The service was awesome from start to finish. The team was professional, attentive, and made everything run smoothly, which took so much stress off our special day. The ambiance they created was over the top and truly elevated the entire wedding experience.
On top of all that, the value was fantastic for the quality, presentation, and service provided. Olobe exceeded our expectations in every way. If you’re looking for exceptional African-Nigerian catering for a wedding or any event, I highly, highly recommend them!

The staff there were friendly and helpful with the menu selection. The food was so good, and I definitely look forward to enjoying other different dishes at this restaurant! It was a refreshing change from the same old food options in the area. Definitely recommend!

We were extremely disappointed by the experience trying to visit this restaurant today despite all of the amazing reviews and great food pics.
We initially planned to come for lunch based with the hours listed as 11:00 AM opening time on google. After finding the doors locked, and no one answering any phones we received a text message at 12:20 PM saying the restaurant  would open at 1:30 PM. We returned at 1:30 PM, and waited almost 20 minutes also giving the place a call only to find the doors still locked and no one answering the phone but the open sign was still on.
This is highly unprofessional . Wasting customer's time and providing misleading information is a very poor way to run a business. We were really excited to try the egusi soup, but due to this complete lack of reliability and professionalism, we will unfortunately not be returning to this restaurant.

formatted_address: 842 E Jefferson Blvd, Dallas, TX 75203, United States
name: Suya Feast

reviews.text:
Arguably one of the best suya spots in DFW! I love the jollof rice, and the beef is always tender and flavorful. I’m literally writing this review while eating because it’s that good… very impressed.
My only minor complaint is that my most recent order had a few burnt pieces at the bottom, and the beef wasn’t cut as small as usual. But honestly, that didn’t take away from how good everything was. I highly recommend!!!!
Best suya spot in the DFW. Very flavorful authentic beef suya & delicious jollof rice. I wish they were open everyday because I highly recommend.

As someone who's spent years in Cameroon, finding this Nigerian food truck was lucky. The vibe felt like we were in Africa again. We enjoyed the Foleré/Zobo/Hibiscus tea, the Soya/suya, and the grilled chicken. If you're shy about spicy food, order another zobo just in case.
The jollof here is banging. Not too spicy, not hard like stone. Just tasty with good texture. 1 yr old kid was gulping the thing hard and it's just $5.  Love the suya too.
The best suya I have ever had in the States! it is so great and underrated for my liking. Phenomenal. Would love the service to be a little faster, butttt honestly, it is still great.

formatted_address: 3007 S Carrier Pkwy, Grand Prairie, TX 75052, United States
name: Yemsade

reviews.text: One of the best places I’ve ever eaten at. Their egusi soup is absolutely top tier. It was so good that I drove two hours from Tyler just to have it. Unfortunately, they were out when I arrived because of how popular it is, which honestly says everything. I still highly recommend this place. Please come and eat here.

First time ordering from here and efo riro is one of my favorite foods. Initially, I would have given this a 3 star because the flavors were good but the proportions were a war crime. ESPECIALLY for the insane prices they charge. They gave me MAYBE 1/4 full small contain of both the efo riro and abula with barely any meat.

But then, 2 hours later, I was puking it all up and was thankful that the proportions were so small. Was sick for about 3 hours and will never eat from here again.

I guess I will just have to stick to other local African restaurants after today. I ordered okra soup with fish, although I usually order egusi. I have been coming here for over 2 years, by the way... The size of the container for the okra was literally half the size of the normal container they use (and I literally just came last week). That small container of okra soup was filled up abount 1/6th the height of the container. It was about 6 spoonfuls of okra..... Such a ripoff. I paid $18+ for this and foolishly left a tip before checking my food. The fish they added was not up to par. Today it was several hard, skinny leftover bits instead of the 2 large pieces I am used to. I ended going to Ts Buka for plain okr soup to make up for Yemsades sad dish. It was only $10, and they added free red stew and a freefuture, plus the container was large and full. I have supported Yemsade for 2+ years despite the shop looking unkempt and unsanitary, and despite some of the workers being of questionable character (once a troubled male, who claimed to be the owner's son, kept hitting on me and telling me about his legal troubles until I gave him a fake phone number). You have lost a customer in your greed. Never again.

I don’t even no where to start first time trying this place I came all the way from Desoto I got fufu egusi with goat meat I ate some in the parking lot it was good got home at some more but that’s when all hell broke lose I started throwing up like 3x started feeling nauseous. My head was spinning. Am my stomach feel like it was about to blow up my inside was burning. My left pelvic was screaming like oh my gosh I never felt no pain like it. I thought I was going to have go to the hospital I just prayed to God and started drinking water until I want to restroom worst pain ever dis lasted about 5 hours I had to eat a sandwich to make my stomach feel better I thank God I have a strong immune system as of 10:46pm I’m starting to feel better.

First time trying this place and it was bad. The beef must’ve been very old before it was served, far from edible and the same for my daughter’s chicken just not as bad. It was as if the food had been kept for days and then served. Intake fish fins throughout the entire meal but no actual fish.

And also order ahead before going it’s not a sit in restaurant boxes are everywhere. We didn’t know this.

formatted_address: 10051 Whitehurst Dr, Dallas, TX 75243, United States
name: Murphy's Mansion

reviews.text: The fish meal came highly recommended and it was tasty, a good choice to consider for Nigerian meals. Large with plenty sitting option and the atmosphere is popping
The Suya is delicious.  I haven’t been  during the evening in a while. They have done some renovations things look nice.  The service can be slow but they have always been friendly.

Murphy’s is an African club/lounge and they are now the new home of Venittis. Do you get two clubs in one. There’s a bar when you first walk in but service wasn’t so great, cups weren’t as clean, took a while and a few times to ask for my debit card back. Where as inside the other club that bartender was great. Nothing like Murphy side. It’s a large building they have a few pool tables and outside area as well. I didn’t have the chance to try the food. Yet it smelled good . Drinks are kind of cheap

Never, ever again!!  If I could give this place Zero Stars, that’s exactly what it would get!!!! This place is VERY Unorganized and chaotic!!! There is also NO a/c or fans, so it is extremely HOT!! The people( servers and bar tenders  walk around looking confused and angry!!! The people/workers do NOT speak or acknowledge you until you say something to them and it seems like you are bothering or inconveniencing them! The owner Murphy was just as rude as the workers and he was walking around looking clueless as well!! Do NOT walk NOR drive to this place!! Stay away and go somewhere else where you are appreciated and valued as a consumer!!!

I went on a Saturday night. It was a nice crowd, not too crowded.  We were able to get a table quickly ordered drinks called back that a** up ( it was not good) it was supposed to had been a margarita with some added liquor! It was like a water ice with liquor on top! Too too sweet. We also ordered a straight shot of cognac and a beer. For dinner I ordered a whole tilapia fish the options were fried or grilled, I ordered mines fried. It came with vegetables( some type of greens) they were good! Seasoned very well. The fish was pretty good it was a little salty but that may have been the sauce they put on the fish, it came with plantain. Ordered a side of Jollof rice (Al La cart). We also ordered fish pepper soup (very spicy) but good! This  place was decent had a live DJ pool tables ping pong table a dance floor etc. I would return, maybe not for food but I hang out.

formatted_address: 9790 Forest Ln, Dallas, TX 75243, United States
name: Seinyaa African Food and Kitchen

reviews.text:
I’m going to start with the meat pies I bought. The meat pies were thin, barely any meat, and flavorless but they were $2.99 in person. The Suya was ok but didn’t taste like usual Suya and wasn’t really spicy and tasty like Suya is supposed to be.

Then the goat meat pepper soup wasn’t delicious and barely had any goat meat. I would describe the goat meat pepper soup as marginally okay.

The Jollof rice goat and beef meat wasn’t memorable for good reasons. The rice was dry and hard mainly and not very flavorful. The meat was small and not a lot. Overall just meh.

Last but not least, they will add a surcharge for using a credit card. I wouldn’t recommend the cooked food. But the bread from Our Lady Bakery was $3.99 and seemed a reasonable price. Then I bought Palm wine, because when I asked the owner if there was alcohol in it the owner said “no.” I drank some of the Palm Wine and then looked at the label and it said there was alcohol in it. I don’t know if the owner just didn’t know it did have alcohol like I thought since it had wine in its name.
They were amazing with me. They even gave a free sprite. And the food is delicious. I recommend the lady is so sweet.
Wow!! What an awesome store! The owner and employees were so nice to me. The place was clean and the verity of goods were unmated. They will definitely be seeing me again.
Good store found ukwa I was so happy. The owner walked with me around the store to help me and tell me abou the products. I really felt good. They will see me again.
Very good cooked food here and The customer service is good

formatted_address: 8371 Park Ln, Dallas, TX 75231, United States
name: Arif cafe

reviews.text: Real deal, delicious Ethiopian food in an authentic environment. We got the veggie combo plate and could not have been happier. Would recommend to anyone coming to Dallas and looking for good Ethiopian food. Couldn't have had a better experience, and the woman cooking and running the place was so nice!
Feels like I’m at grandmas house away from grandmas house lol, food feeds your soul and the lady that run the place is welcoming and sweet! 10 out of 10

We recently found this cafe and the food was amazing!  We have been in the hunt looking for authentic Ethiopian food and this tasted great.  The chef asked us how hot we wanted it and we went with medium as the wife isn’t too keen on spicy food.  This was her special birthday dinner and we all enjoyed it.  There were no leftovers and we left completely satisfied.  We had beef tibs and veggie combos and sambusas.

Phenomenal Ethiopian food that is authentic and extremely well made. Pleasure meeting the cook and owner who welcomed us into her restaurant and made sure our questions were answered. The menu is very short but appears there are endless possibilities in combinations which can feel overwhelming.

If you’re looking to try something fresh, new, and delicious and don’t know what to order: try the veggie Combo platter with added lamb or beef (that’s how I say it).

The lamb is the most popular meat option since it is made FRESH and typically sells out midday. The first time I went, it was sold out so of course I went a second time and it was so worth it if you like lamb meat. Seasoned to perfection and flavorful with every bite. The beef was also good, I am more than happy with either choice!

The veggie combo platter comes with injera bread that you use to eat the various sides and meats. Actually all of the food sits on top of injera bread, soaking up the mix of flavors. There are also several rolled up injera breads to use as well. The best part is eating the bottom injera bread that has all the soaked in flavors. If you want extra bread to eat with the meal, she will provide at no extra cost.

I’m not sure what all the sides that come with the combo plate are, but they were all good! Collard greens, cabbage, and various sauces that are all veggie and may be vegan friendly as well.

For gluten-free: typically injera is gluten free if they use teff 100%, I wasn’t able to confirm that so please check with the owner! But otherwise I’d definitely say it’s easy to eat vegan and vegetarian here.

Also- no free water or refillable drinks here. There is a cooler with drinks that you can purchase per item.

Both times I’ve come (veggie combo with beef and then another time veggie combo with lamb) were priced just around $45 for two people and it was MORE THAN ENOUGH FOOD. I went with two different people and they both really enjoyed the food with me and spoke of how they each wanted to return.

The place is in a small shopping strip near north park mall. The parking is pretty scarce but I’ve always managed to find a place to park due to people coming and going constantly at the various stores. Arif cafe is very small, with seating for no more than 20 people. The whole place is outdated with old furniture but I don’t mind it one bit because I know I am supporting local and really enjoy the atmosphere.

Unforgettable food! Support local and give them a try!

@CRJetc

Food was wonderful, but what really made my experience was the owner. She was so kind to me and made sure I enjoyed my food, and also introduced my to new ones. Happy to be a new, and now returning, customer!

formatted_address: 3600 Gus Thomasson Rd #100, Mesquite, TX 75150, United States
name: MK's AFRICAN CUISINE & BAR

reviews.text:
10/10 highly recommend!  I’ve been looking for some good EGUSI in Dallas especially near by my home and look what God did 🙌🏾
It was so delicious and fulfilling.  This spot is ran by two sisters who just opened their new business about two weeks ago.  They were very kind and welcoming.  I will definitely be back soon to try other dishes

Me and my sister had an amazing experience. The food was delicious and so fresh. The meat was tender but also soft enough to pull apart easily. The portion size was wonderful and I LOVED the fact that it wasn’t full of oil/Grease..

Went there with my mother last night and the ambiance was amazing. despite being newly open, the people who work there are kind and lively. The service was to my liking and to me it was just perfection. Now the food on the other hand…. I can not tell yallll enough how good it tasted, plus this was my first time ever trying egusi and fufu. I loved it, best way I could put it is ”Phenomenal”. I’m for sure going again. 10/10

I tried the egusi soup with fufu and it was amazing! The egusi was rich, flavorful, and perfectly seasoned, and the fufu was smooth and paired beautifully with it. The whole dish felt comforting, satisfying, and full of authentic flavor. If you’ve never tried egusi and fufu before, I definitely recommend it — you won’t be disappointed

Went here for the first time tonight. The owners are Cameroonian and they opened about a month ago. The restaurant is clean, has plenty of space, the food was delicious, and they were so kind to me for my birthday! The service is excellent- very observant but not too obtrusive- the perfect amount of face-time.

We got the Egusi soup with pounded yam, the goat pepper soup, the jollof rice, the oxtails, and the Suya combo- we also got the puffs (fried delicious bread). My favorite was the goat pepper soup- spicy and truly delicious. The Egusi with fufu was also rich and flavorful. Honestly- I could use those same descriptor words for everything. The oxtails were tender. The jollof rice was smokey and flavorful.

We will be going back again.

Since they make everything on demand, they did say if you want to order the achu, that they need about an hour's notice. I want to try it next time so we will be calling in ahead of time!

I forgot to take photos of anything- and honestly I'm so sad about it- here's a pic of us eating to fill the gap.

formatted_address: 311 E Pioneer Pkwy # B, Grand Prairie, TX 75051, United States
name: Suya Stop Inc.

reviews.text: I had an amazing experience today. It was my first time eating African food and I was a little scared but immediately after the first bite I was amazed and satisfied. I would definitely recommend and give a thousand stars if I could. Thank you for the amazing atmosphere and good food . I will be back

This has to be the worst Suya I’ve had in the DFW area. I had high hopes for Suya Stop, especially with a name that promises great Suya. I drove all the way from Dallas to Grand Prairie, expecting something worth the hype, but it absolutely wasn’t.

The Suya lacked the authentic flavor and quality I’ve known as a Nigerian —it was really disappointing. I wasted both my money and my time driving over there when they’re much better Suya spots right in Dallas!

To be fair, they might have other decent dishes like their Asun or Shawarma, but if you’re going for Suya, I’d recommend looking elsewhere.

We have tried various spots in Dallas for Nigerian food but many left us disappointed. This place got it just right. We had the pomo, suya and asun and they were all so good. The flavors were perfect, portions generous and everything tasted fresh. Definitely our new go to for authentic and delicious Nigerian food.
I had beef suya today, and it was absolutely delicious! I highly recommend it—it's the best suya I've had in a long time. It was worth the drive, and I can't wait to come back for more!"
one of the best suya spots I've eaten at in Dallas. I would recommend the Suya and the spicy pomo

formatted_address: 3003 N Belt Line Rd, Irving, TX 75062, United States
name: African Village

reviews.text:
Do NOT come here. The  wait time was ridiculously long. I ordered samosas, and egusi soup with pounded yam. The meat inside of the samosas was cold, it was just reheated. I asked the waiter several times if the egusi soup was made with palm oil, he said yes. It was not. The egusi soup looked white and old and mushy. The pounded yam was not pounded yam, it was some other swallow that tasted nothing like pounded yam.

The waiter had horrible customer service. He was quite rude actually. Not to mention the food was very pricey. They served the food on paper plates. Which restaurant serves food on paper plates? Also, the toilet at the back also smelled horrible.

Would rate zero stars tbh.

The food was absolutely delicious, with every dish prepared with great flavor and care. The customer service was equally impressive—everyone was incredibly friendly, attentive, and genuinely made us feel welcomed throughout our visit. Overall, a wonderful dining experience that I would gladly recommend to others

Food was good. Greens that came with jollof was delicious. Service is abysmal. They brought most of our food out and forgot one of our dishes so we had to walk to the kitchen to ask about it and they still never brought it. Food took a while to come out. It was busy but would have appreciated communication atleast. I think our server left in the middle of our stay and no one check in on us afterwards.

It was my friend and I first time going there i was so disappointed, we ordered food 40 mins before we get there surprisingly we had to wait for another 30 mins before our food was served, They didn’t even have our order we had to reorder when we arrived. Poor service food expensive .

Moved to Dallas and been looking for some Nigerian food. I walked in and met the owner Ma Vero. The menu is so diverse and they make everything fresh. Please go check them out and give them a try. The place is warm and inviting and the food will hit the soul

formatted_address: 3435 N Belt Line Rd, Irving, TX 75062, United States
name: Lola's Restaurant & Lounge

reviews.text:
Home cooked meal. I already started eating before taking pictures of our food, so don't judge their food presentation by my photos.

I was reluctant to order efo riro because my sister makes the best efo riro ever! However, I was pleasantly surprised.

When I tell you the food tasted like I was eating at my sister's kitchen, it's the highest complement ever! The restaurant was clean. The serving portions were just right. We had efo riro and eba with assorted meats, also abula with assorted meats, and extra order of goat meat. They gave complimentary bottles of water.

They have a hand washing station within the restaurant.

The service was great. We will definitely come back again.

Goat head (isi ewu) with raw white onions is utterly fantastic. So flavorful and soft. Moderately spicy, a bit above sriracha. Huge portion too. The owner is so nice and helped me with the menu. This has become one of my favorite restaurants already.

I recently visited Dallas, Texas, and my driver took me to this restaurant because he said it is one of the best in the area… and I absolutely agree!
I ordered the ogbono and ponded yam with plantains on the side, and it was very delicious!
I highly recommend this place if you’re looking for authentic and flavorful Nigerian cuisine. I’ll definitely be back when I’m in the area!
Fantastic!! Food, vibes!! Charles was an excellent server and showed great hospitality!!! I'll definitely be back!!
I leave 50minutes away from this place but the food was worth to wait,so delicious,I highly recommend ♥️

formatted_address: 1102 W Pioneer Pkwy #125, Grand Prairie, TX 75051, United States
name: Kemi's African Kitchen

reviews.text:
I ordered jollof rice, plantain, beef and meat pie. This was my first visit to the restaurant despite driving by it for 15 years. Rice was cool. Spicy n cool. Not much meat came with huge plate of rice. Plantain was flavorful and meat pie was ok. Food wasn’t bad but it’s not somewhere I’d eat often. Dishes were actually fresh.

Restaurant seemed outdated and a bit sloppy/unorganized. Right behind cashier and in total view was a non working cooker/warmer, 50lb bags of rice in lobby and hanging cabinet doors.

All meats were very overcooked. The goat was very very dry… Ordered the goat and jollof rice and received 1 piece of meat for the entire plate. The meat pies were seasoned well but doughy. The fish was very good

I've been going here for almost 2 years now. This last time was disappointing. My meat pies were cold, first time ever. And the portion of the egusi was just unacceptable. The prices are decent. The portions just seem to get smaller and smaller. This time it was more sauce than egusi. I'm not asking for Texas size portions for $12 but give me more than just a big spoon full smh.

Everything tasted delicious and the lady was super nice. I'll definitely come back to try the pepper soup. I got fried rice, jollof rice with stew, goat, fish, and beef. Side of vegetable, egusi and stew.
It is absolutely one of the best African restaurants that I have gone to in quite some time. The food was fresh, and the service was great. I highly recommend them!

formatted_address: 415 N Main St #102, Euless, TX 76039, United States
name: Exotic Grill African Cuisine

reviews.text: My son was home from college and wanted to take us here. He's been a few times and loved it. He loves trying exotic cuisines. It was VERY good, very fresh, and made to order, so we didn't mind waiting just a little while, but the dishes came out as they were made, so everything was hot, fresh, and delicious. My favorites were the samosas, the fried plantains, and the beef kabobs. They have a sauce that you can add some flavor/heat to the food that my son and husband love, but I don't like a lot of spice, but there was plenty of flavor either way! At the end of the meal, we ordered 2 more samosas, and they brought out 6! We ate every last bite. If you want a super friendly, family home atmosphere, and love trying new flavors, give this place a try! We will be back!

I absolutely love this place. I’ve been to other spots and no one compares to this one they give you a very good portion size for the price they greet you with love and they put love into their food. It does take a while to get your food because they’re making it fresh. The goats to is a very tender tomato based still plantains are nice fresh and sweet

From the moment I walked into Exotic African Grill I was welcomed as if I had just entered my grandmother’s home for Sunday dinner. Jordy and Cecile created a warm environment by asking how I was doing and putting on great music. They walked me through the menu and since this is my first time they did a great job of highlighting the staples of the menu. I was able to sample a little bit of everything. The food was fresh and made to order. The chicken was so flavorful, well seasoned, and juicy. The ribs were so tender and tasty, it would have been disrespectful to dip them in bbq sauce. The plantain was perfectly ripe and fried exquisitely. Rice and beans were great sides to balance out all of the flavors. The Mikate (african donut holes) were the cherry on top for dessert and paired well with a generous helping of peanut butter. The house-made hot sauce (pili-pili) wasn’t just hot, it was a delicious addition that enhanced every dish. My experience was a 10/10 and I’ll definitely be back very soon with my friends and family.

This restaurant is cozy and the staff is friendly. We ordered Pork Ribs, Chicken, Tilapia, Yam Fufu, and drinks. Overall, the food was good and tasted fresh. The Tilapia is the whole fish with head and bones. The dishes are a bit pricey, but we had a good experience.
First timer. The lady was very kind. The young guy was kind of short with me, as I had questions. However, the food was prepared quickly.

formatted_address: 11422 Harry Hines Blvd #210, Dallas, TX 75229, United States
name: ALADINNS SPOT (Inside Shin-Chon Market)

reviews.text: Ive been to almost every African restraunt n Dallas. When i say this was the BEST one. I had the grilled Tilapia and Jollof Rice. Sooooo DELICIOUS 😋 n that's an understatement. I fell in live from the first bite! I ordered it extra hot and even tho it was spicy it was more flavorful then ANYTHING. I let my daughter taste it and she liked it so much she went to school talkin about it. Definetly worth the money. Highly recommend
I've never had fufu this was my 1st time and I loved it!!!! And I don't eat beef I loved the way he found away for me to taste the fufu with having beef. 10/10 will be goin back sooon¡!!!!!!

DO NOT COME HERE!!! HORRIBLE SERVICE NOBODY actually works here and it’s really just an empty space y  i have put a photo as proof as i waited for about 20 mins and no one arrived!!! Thank God i didn’t pay for it ahead or i would have been out of my money!!

I was craving egusi so bad on my lunch break and this was the closest place to my job. Hands down the best egusi and fufu I have ever tasted! The plantain had a pinch of salt, but it had a sweet savory taste, just right! I am so satisfied with this purchase!! I will definitely recommend going here. The surrounding is kinda intense with other restaurants and small stores around but the customer service at the restaurant was from such a sweet and patient young lady!! 10 stars for me!

The grilled fish and jellof rice was amazing. I've been to every African restaurant from Dallas to fort Worth and it's the best I've had by far. This is my second time here and there will be a 3rd and a 4th lol...keep doing great guys 👍🏾

formatted_address: 100 S Central Expy #50, Richardson, TX 75080, United States
name: Fusion Vibes Kitchen + Lounge

reviews.text: Today, I had an amazing experience dining at Fusion Vibes Kitchen & Lounge. From the moment I walked in, the atmosphere was lively, welcoming, and full of good energy. The food was incredible—every bite was bursting with flavor and beautifully presented. What really made the evening special was getting the chance to talk with Will, the owner. He took the time to chat, share the story behind the restaurant, and make sure everything was perfect. His passion for great food and creating a positive vibe truly shows. It wasn’t just dinner—it was an experience I’ll definitely remember and look forward to enjoying again soon.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Review for Fusion Kitchen in Richardson

I came to Fusion Kitchen for a birthday kickback on a Sunday afternoon and the whole experience was really nice. The food was good, the vibes were on point, and the decor and ambiance fit the mood perfectly. The staff was friendly and the owner even gifted our table a round of top shelf shots while promoting his upcoming events which made everything feel personal and welcoming.

My plate had highs and lows. The oxtails were the star for me. They were long cut, stewed to perfection, and the broth was so good I took it home. The greens had a good smoky flavor and the eggrolls had no meat but the sauce helped them out. The mac and cheese was my only real criticism. It tasted more like a Kraft-style base with cheese baked on top. Once I added some of that delicious oxtail broth it instantly elevated the flavor which made me wish I would have just ordered a full oxtail plate from the start.

Overall I enjoyed my time here. The service, the atmosphere, and those oxtails alone make it worth coming back. I would recommend it for a chill kickback or a casual dinner or brunch. Sam was our waitress and she was AMAZING!

THE OXTAIL IS PERFECT!! I had oxtail in Jamaica and this spot was just as good as the one I had there 👌🏽 The jerk salmon and plantains were also great, but the jallof rice needs a bit more seasoning or something, it felt too bland for my taste. But the oxtail, jerk salmon and plantains were fantastic! I highly recommend! And service from Kate/Kathleen was great, she was very friendly, helpful, and sweet.

The lounge was also a great vibe, just not great for talking. There was karaoke, drinks, line dancing, hookah, a great balance between fun party vibes and a chill lounge. I'd go there for a birthday celebration with friends, for sure.

We booked a brunch reservation for my sister’s birthday! Please note that this place is 21+ although it is not listed on the booking information. The food is absolutely scrumptious. We weren’t huge fans of the lobster mac and ended up picking out all of the lobster pieces. The mac by itself was good. There’s plenty of parking since this is located in a shopping center. Drinks are good as well. My sister had the Rum Punch and loved it.

The food was delicious and honestly the best chicken and waffles in DFW. I live in Weatherford Tx but it was worth the drive. Celebrated my birthday here and my family and I had a great time. Everyone was sweet and the we will continue to come. ❤️❤️❤️❤️

formatted_address: 1220 River Bend Dr Suite 112, Dallas, TX 75247, United States
name: Zambos Latin & African Food

reviews.text: My family travelled to Dallas for NCAA Women’s Final Four and decided to dine here  lose to our hotel. My daughters and I ordered different meals to sample each others plate. The food was amazing. Hospitality and atmosphere was unmatched. Highly recommend to locals and we will definitely revisit when in Dallas. My daughter ordered the fries tilapia that was seasoned to perfection….

Never had Zimbabwean food before but based on how good the food served here is, this won’t be the last time I have some. Tried the fried fish and also tried some samosas and I loved everything. Also had some lemon cookies that were sooo good. Definitely going back and 1000% recommend it!

Great Zimbabwean food! Could use a little more salt in some of the dishes but customer service is impeccable! They have different beverages that give you a piece of home. From viceroy, Amarula, hunters and many more. Been there almost every weekend since they opened. The chakalaka sauce with samosas  has me in a choke hold! Their fresh chips (fries) to die for! The fish! Just go try it out if u haven’t!

OMG !!Zambos Restaurant is a hidden gem in town that I can't recommend highly enough. From the moment you step through the doors, you're transported to the heart of Africa with the warm and inviting atmosphere, traditional decor, and delightful aromas wafting from the kitchen.

The menu is a culinary adventure through Zimbabwean and African cuisine, with dishes that are both comforting and exotic. I especially loved the tender Mazondo, which was rich and flavorful, and the spicy Maguru, which had just the right amount of heat. The Sadza was the perfect accompaniment, and I loved using it to soak up all the delicious sauces.

To top it off, the service was impeccable. The staff was friendly, attentive, and happy to recommend dishes and drinks. Speaking of drinks, the Amarula was an absolute standout. Creamy, sweet, and smooth, it was the perfect way to cap off a fantastic meal.

If you're looking for an authentic African dining experience, you won't be disappointed with Zambos Restaurant. I can't wait to go back and try more of their amazing dishes!

The smoked salt was amazing, maguru so soft and also amazing.  But the gango had two types of veggies, half not fresh other half not cooked. The gango definitely needs some revamping. The brown sadza was served beautifully in plastic rap however it wasn’t hot(not going to question when it was cooked)The vibe was overally fun, great music great people. Looking forward to going again though since this spot is new.

formatted_address: 12101 Greenville Ave #105, Dallas, TX 75243, United States
name: Desta Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: A must try! Desta Ethiopian has been around for a long time. Excellent food and service! The lamb tips were absolutely delicious. They have the best unsweet Tea! Hints of cinnamon and cloves. Very good!

Oh, where do I start with Desta Ethiopian Kitchen in Dallas? This gem is a must-visit for anyone craving bold, authentic Ethiopian flavors that dance on your taste buds! The lamb ribs were an absolute showstopper—juicy, tender, and packed with rich, savory goodness that had me savoring every bite. And let’s talk about the Goden ribs—fall-off-the-bone perfection with a spice blend that’s both soul-warming and electrifying.
The injera bread? Soft, spongy, and the ideal canvas for scooping up the mouthwatering miser lentils, which were a delightful mix of earthy, spicy, and downright addictive. Every dish felt like a love letter to Ethiopian cuisine, served with warmth and care. The vibrant atmosphere and friendly staff only made the experience even more unforgettable. If you’re in Dallas, run—don’t walk—to Desta for a meal that’ll leave you hungry for more!!! BB was super awesome on the margaritas…..yep so refreshing!

Really solid and super flavorful Ethiopian food. Have been several times and this is one of the most reliable choices for Ethiopian food in dfw. Service can sometimes be slow and/or indifferent but never unkind. The food more than makes up for it!

Food took a while, but that’s to be expected for freshly cooked food, so I thought. The injera was cold. The entire meal was lukewarm. The veggies and lentils had no flavor, none of the traditional Ethiopian flavors or spices very bland. Beef tibs were tough, chewed and spit out most of the meat, it was so tough. Overall a waste of money. I’ve had amazing Ethiopian food and this was awful.

Excellent food, and the atmosphere was great. The servers were so friendly, patient, and very helpful. Everyone made us so welcomed and we will definitely go back. The food selection was great and it tasted delicious and amazing.

formatted_address: 14875 Inwood Rd, Addison, TX 75001, United States
name: Queen of Sheba Restaurant

reviews.text: First try on Ethiopian cuisine and I’m glad it was at Queen of Sheba. Wonderful people with exceptional service, oh and Joe! What a guy he is! He educated me on the history of Queen of Sheba and on Ethiopian coffee, which you have to try btw. all in all, I am pleased and looking forward to being back

We went there for dinner and had an amazing experience. The atmosphere is soooooo beautiful—when you walk inside, it instantly feels like you’ve stepped into a palace, almost like being part of a royal family. The space feels warm, elegant, and welcoming.
The food is excellent, with plenty of options, including great vegan choices. The desserts are truly special—fit for a queen—and there’s a wide selection of alcoholic drinks as well as hot beverages.
What really stood out the most was the customer service. From the moment we arrived, we were welcomed with genuine smiles, and the staff made us feel like family throughout the entire visit. Truly a wonderful dining experience. One thing I want say I love miss Elsa  so great lady .

We loved coming here! Food was fresh and delicious. The vegan options weee impressive and savory!

Love this place, it’s so enchanting and can’t wait to be back. We had the pleasure of speaking with Joe and even got to say hi to his mom, both of which are so wonderful, knowledgeable and lovely to meet. Wish I had visited sooner! Amazing food! Can’t wait to bring some friends also :)
Great food, great options and service. Also offer gluten free inijera bread. It's very rare to find an Ethiopian place in Dallas that is gluten free friendly. Highly recommend.

Such a beautiful restaurant, tasty food, and friendly, passionate people running this place!
Everything was so flavorful and the textures surprised and amazed me!! 😍 I hope to be back soon!

formatted_address: 9790 Forest Ln, Dallas, TX 75243, United States
name: One Africa Grocery And Kitchen

reviews.text: I visited this spot n was delighted. It was nice clean n the owner was so polite n friendly..  I  returned a day later with my sister. We have been going at least once a week every  since. My only problem  was/is the amount of food. The bowl is to small.
Love this food and they’re very nice people no wahala go there please everyone ❤️
Nice and clean spot. Food was excellent.lady is welcoming too.great experience overall
Food was off. I couldn't finish eating it.
My rice was scorched

formatted_address: 7015 Greenville Ave ste 300, Dallas, TX 75231, United States
name: Yenat Guada Ethiopian Cuisine

reviews.text:
📍Yenat Guada Ethiopian Cuisine -- Dallas, TX with My Friend! 🔥🔥🔥🔥

Yenat Guada is an authentic Ethiopian restaurant off Greenville Ave. in Dallas! We ordered the Vegetable Combo for two (My friend is very supportive of my vegan/ vegetarian journey! 🥰) It's a combination of house vegetable dishes which included: Red Lentil Stew (which was my fave), Split Pea Yellow Stew, Chickpea Stew, Green Lentil Stew, Lightly cooked Collard Greens and Red Cabbage! We ate everything with Injera which is an Ethiopian Flatbread! We also had the Ethiopian style Rice with Marinara Sauce. When I say everything was soooo flavorful and seasoned to perfection!! I actually can't wait to go back lol 😍🌱💯

We also tried their Ginger Tea and Herbal tea as well!

#EthiopianFood #Injera #DallasTX #GirlsNight #Ethiopia

Visiting the restaurant after almost nine years.  Tried Doro Wot and Lamb Tibs with injera. The flavors were ok and the difference in the quality was evident.

The restaurant is spacious and well maintained. Plenty of parking is available. Service was fine with a few misses. They have a full bar with Ethiopian Honey Wine, which is a specialty.

Pricing : Moderate

I usually head farther north when the craving for Ethiopian food hits, but since I was nearby, I decided to give this spot a try. It was… fine. Decent, but not memorable. I may be a little spoiled by the incredible Ethiopian restaurants I’ve frequented in Washington, D.C., Atlanta, and my reliable go-to in Richardson. The flavors here felt muted, as if my request for medium heat took a detour and ended up at mild. Still, the experience wasn’t unpleasant—just a reminder that some cravings are best satisfied where the spices tell their full story.

The food was absolutely delicious! I loved the atmosphere and felt as if I was not in Texas. The male serve was polite and readily available. I ate my food so fast I forgot to take a picture. I ordered the veggie combo for 1. It was definitely enough for two light eaters. I gave a whole meal to take home. The lamb was flavorful and tender.

This little place is the best kept secret on upper Greenville!  It may look a little rough when you first pull in, but it is a beautiful restaurant inside and the food AND SERVICE are outstanding!

My dining companion and I arrived at an off time, and we were the only customers in the place. That was a lucky turn of events because we had a wonderful conversation about the food with the gentleman who was our server. He was exceedingly knowledgeable about the menu and it was the first time for each of us to have Ethiopian food.

We ordered the vegetable combo and a spicy beef gravy dish called the Zil Zil Tibs.  Here’s the thing: there are No utensils; instead you scoop the food up with stretchy, spongy, absorbent bread that gloms it up.

The presentation was beautiful, the portions were huge, and the food was simply delicious!  I don’t have a vocabulary to accurately describe the flavors, but everything was wonderful!  Wow!  I could eat some more right now!  Highly recommend!!

formatted_address: 5000 Main St Suite# 214, The Colony, TX 75056, United States
name: Zag Afro-fusion Cuisine

reviews.text:
I was excited to try authentic African cuisine at Zag, and the food did not disappoint. The restaurant is conveniently located with ample parking. When we arrived, only one other table was occupied, so we were seated immediately. The host was friendly and helpful in explaining the menu, though she noted the prices listed were outdated.

We ordered the Asun, which was fantastic but very spicy—beware if you’re sensitive to heat! The jerk chicken with jollof rice was another highlight; the chicken was perfectly seasoned and so tender it fell off the bone. The food was truly delicious.

However, I gave Zag three stars due to a few issues. The restaurant’s cleanliness needs improvement—our cutlery wasn’t properly washed and had to be replaced. There were also too few paper napkins provided.

Pricing: It’s on the expensive side, with one appetizer and one entree costing just over $50.

Overall, while the food was outstanding, the high prices and cleanliness issues detracted from the experience.

Been meaning to leave a review for a while. I absolutely adore this place and have been multiple times.

Usually there's only one person there running the place so the food is slow to come out but the wait has never not been worth it. I love the pepper stew the most but honesty anything here is awesome. I usually take my partner or a friend so we can have long talks with good food and the space has always been great for that.

I wish it was less expensive but honestly only because I would be there all the time.

Very nice place in the Colony. I had a plate of Jollof Rice, Jerk Chicken and cabbage on the side. Everything was delicious.

Fun fact: Chef Lanre is also the creator of Jiffy Jollof sauce. Look it up and try it!! It's really good!!

Bought fufu and the soup it came with I don’t remember the name. Came home and tried it. As soon as I opened the soup it smelled so bad. Taste was horrible. I have really great African food and went to this place since I was around that area. Not happy with the food or customer service. The lady who took my order was super rude. She didn’t even smile with me. And took more than 30 minutes to give my food. The place was empty when I got there. Maybe the reason is the food. Once you tried it you’re not going back for sure.

We had an amazing experience, and everything was absolutely delicious! My daughters had been eager to try pounded yam and Egusi, and it did not disappoint. Presentation was beautiful! The flavors were bold and authentic, and the dish was incredibly satisfying. The guava drink was the perfect complement..refreshing, rich, and full of flavor. We can’t wait to come back!

formatted_address: 9220 Skillman St #227, Dallas, TX 75243, United States
name: Monrovia Lounge

reviews.text: As the only Liberian restaurant in Dallas, 5 stars. The shopping center and building itself isn't first-class, but as a Liberian myself, the food here is the real deal. I had dry rice, cassava leaf (for take out) and fried plantains. My husband, who is American, tried their food for the first time and was VERY impressed. The owners are down to earth and everything was served with clean silverware. Worth a visit at least once if you are curious.

I really enjoyed this place the atmosphere and the staff were awesome  I got some recommendations and I went with the peppered soup with goat meat and fufu. They also has a seafood option. The soup was soo good but it is spicy. My boyfriend had the Cajun seafood pasta. We also had some yummy fried plantains. Would definitely go back!

The food was hot and fresh seasoned to perfection. i love the flavor and spicyness of the sauce on the side. The service was excellent and ambiance of the place was great. I had palava sauce and fried fish dressed with beautiful veggies. I had so much left overs as well as the group sitting next to me. Thank you, will be back soon.

This place is definitely a Gem! I don’t even know where to begin, the food was amazing, Chef definitely took her time and put her food in it. Hands down they have the best staff, bartender was on point. Everything about Monrovia Lounge was a huge success. I might just order me some cassava leaves and Jollof today now that I’m thinking about it! If you haven’t been yet, you need to go asap. You will not regret it! God bless the owners lol

It’s customary that I seek to find an African restaurant, especially a Liberian owned, whenever I traveled, especially when on business trips. It is imperative that we do support our own where ever we are!

Whilst in Decatur Texas, a research for such restaurant was done and the Monrovia Lounge was found in Dallas. I decided to stay the night closer to the airport, which would allow for a non-rushed experience getting to the airport, but also a non-rushed visit to the Monrovia lounge.

I must say, my experience at the Monrovia Lounge was great and I would recommend visiting there if in the Dallas area. Wow! The Attieke with Baked Fish, plantain, etc. was great and very cost effective!

I’m very proud of 2 beautiful children of mother Liberia, the owners of Monrovia Lounge! Continue to make mother Liberia proud and I wish y’all the best in your business!

formatted_address: 2376 Lavon Dr 106 A, Garland, TX 75040, United States
name: Salt N Pepper Kitchen & Catering Services

reviews.text: Absolutely wholesome experience at Salt N Pepper. The food was incredibly delicious but the abula truly stole the show. Every bite felt authentic and comforting. The atmosphere instantly reminded me of home, from the warm welcome to the familiar aromas and vibes that make you feel like you’re back in Nigeria. To top it all off, the owner Lekan is an absolute gem, welcoming and genuinely passionate about the food and people. This place is a true treasure for anyone craving real Nigerian food. I’ll be back again!

Salt and Pepper used to be my go-to spot. I’ve brought so many people here over the years – my mother-in-law, friends, even just random hangouts. The food has always been their strong point, and I won’t lie, it’s still good. But the service? These days, it's a real letdown.

Nowadays, it feels like there’s only one male server doing everything – taking orders, serving food, attending to customers. I don’t know if the staff are overworked or what is going on behind the scenes, but the change is obvious and recent. There used to be at least two ladies helping, now it just feels like a one-man show. The last time I came, the tables were scattered and dirty. I actually considered walking out. The next visit, things were cleaner, but the service was still painfully slow and not welcoming at all.

And that light-skinned bald guy at the front desk? Very unfriendly. Doesn’t say much, doesn’t help much. In fact, he almost adds to the frustration.

Food business is hospitality business – it’s not just about what’s on the plate. You can have the best jollof rice in the world, but if the service is poor, people won’t come back. At this rate, I might just stick to takeout. Sitting in has become stress.

I genuinely hope they can turn things around. I still like this place, but it’s not what it used to be.

– A disappointed but hopeful customer

I’ve had Amala in New York, Atlanta, and New Jersey—but nothing, nothing, beats the Amala I had in Dallas, Texas. Salt and Pepper. Y’all are different! The Amala melted in my mouth, the meats were unbelievably soft, and that cold Malt drink to wash it all down? Perfection. The host was super friendly, the service was fast, and everything about this place just hit the spot. I’m not looking anywhere else—this is my go-to from now on. Thank you, Salt and Pepper. I’m satisfied… no, over satisfied!

Food was good BUT $31 for 3 pieces of beef & rice is a bit much. For the portion size I received the price should have been between $14-18 definitely not 31 Buckeroos. I only ordered stew beef with rice, I almost want to believe the cashier charged me incorrectly for this order. Still a good restaurant will go back to support but management lets do something with the portion size or prices..

My family and I went to Salt n pepper kitchen to enjoy some Nigerian dishes. The meals we ordered were delicious and the portions were quite large and very filling. I ordered the Amala & Meat Okro while others ordered Abula and Amala & Ogbono! The obstacles in all the soups were tenderly cooked, so good and easy to chew. With things like cowleg sometimes I get worried it might not get cooked soft enough but in this case, it was cooked real well. We will definitely be back to enjoy more of their meals!

formatted_address: 4181 Main St #500, The Colony, TX 75056, United States
name: Sankofa African Market

reviews.text: Service was good, knowledgeable on ingredients we needed to make ghanian dishes. Cow feet, cow skin, fish, habaneros.

Sangees African Grocery Store is a fantastic place to shop for authentic African ingredients and products. The variety of items available is impressive, ranging from spices and grains to snacks and beverages that truly capture the essence of African cuisine.

The store is well-organized, making it easy to find what you need, and the prices are reasonable for the quality of the products. The staff is incredibly friendly and knowledgeable, always ready to help with recommendations or answer any questions you might have.

Whether you're a fan of African food or just looking to try something new, Sangees is definitely worth a visit. It's a great spot to explore and stock up on unique ingredients that you won't find in regular grocery stores. Overall, Sangees African Grocery Store is a gem in the community!

Clean, organized and the lowest prices for African/Ethnic groceries in DFW! It's always a pleasure to shop here. The staff is super kind and always willing to go the extra mile to help the customers. Compared to the many African markets I have visited in Dallas, this establishment seems to have practically everything! The owner was very helpful and welcoming the minute I walked in. Looking forward to shopping here again, real soon!

Ooo my goodness their customers service is superb. Been to a lot of African store and customer service is very poor. In this store when I walked in I was greated with a smile. The man at the counter was ready to answer any question with so much curtesy and grace. I am so coming back to this store.  Keep up the good service.

Sankofa Market is the cleanest African markets I’ve ever experienced. The owner is very welcoming, polite, always ready to help and very forthcoming! He has a lot of products and always willing to supply more items if you talk to him about it. I just moved here from NY, so the experience is very different from what I’m used to. I will always recommend this market over any other in Texas cause the owner has set a really high bar over any other markets! Everything is always fresh (especially the bread and the meat). I am able to enjoy food as if I’m back home. Thanks Sankofa Market! You’ll be seeing me regularly.

formatted_address: 9560 Skillman St #120, Dallas, TX 75243, United States
name: Banna Restaurant and Bar

reviews.text: The sides were all flavorful and the meat was good and tender. Loved everything! One entree + veggie platter was plentiful enough for 2 adults.

I ordered to-go expecting some decent Ethiopian food based on some surprisingly high reviews. Even with those high expectations, I was not prepared for the level of flavor that stops your night and evokes involuntary mouth noises with every bite. I’m
Trying not to sound weird here but the food was so good that it was an emotional experience! lol
Hands down the best Ethiopian food I’ve ever had and if you like food that makes life better, this is the spot! I don’t even have a picture of the food because we couldn’t stop scarfing it down from the moment we got it home.

Amazing food, amazing atmosphere. At all the Ethiopian restaurants this has been the most fresh and tasteful food. Services is on spot.

LSR. $LSR
Veggie combo was delicious . Sambusa ( lentils ) fried fresh and slightly spicy . They were out of chicken so we didn’t get to try the chicken tibs.

This place is truly a hidden gem. As soon as you walk in, you’ll notice how immaculately clean it is. The staff is very friendly and made sure we understood what we were ordering. We tried the veggie and meat combo platter, which was more than enough for two people—we ended up with leftovers! When the food arrived, the staff pointed out the different items and asked if we had any questions about how to eat the food. The dishes were amazing and full of flavor. They also offer gluten-free options. Lastly, don’t miss the chance to try a new beer; we really enjoyed the Eritrean beer we had.

formatted_address: 12101 Greenville Ave # 103, Dallas, TX 75243, United States
name: City Cafe & Bakery

reviews.text:
A Taste of Addis Ababa in the Heart of Dallas, TX

City Coffee is an absolute gem! From the moment you walk in, you’re welcomed with warm, attentive service that makes you feel right at home. The customer service is consistently excellent—friendly, genuine, and fast without feeling rushed.

The star of the menu for me is their macchiato, rich, smooth, and crafted with the same care and depth of flavor you’d find in Addis Ababa. It’s rare to find a cup this good outside Ethiopia, but City Coffee nails it. Their cakes are equally impressive: always fresh, not overly sweet, and perfectly balanced. Every bite takes me back to traditional cafés back home.

Breakfast here is another highlight, simple, fresh, and flavorful. Whether you’re grabbing a quick bite or enjoying a slow morning, City Coffee delivers a top-tier experience.

Highly recommended for anyone looking for authentic flavors, warm hospitality, and a consistently satisfying experience. Dallas is lucky to have this place!

Unequivocally my favorite breakfast spot in the DFW! I’ve been coming here for over 20 years and it’s consistent every time! My go to is the foul special with a cappuccino, but everything on the menu is great (you can’t go wrong)! Their desserts are made with quality ingredients and authentic to form. 10/10!

Sorry to give this low review but it is an honest review to help others that rely on google review to pick where to go.
