Free hot tea with every meal purchase even if it’s just some two dollar desserts you will not be disappointed!

Noorsha Restaurant is a true gem in Dallas!

Our visit to Noorsha was absolutely wonderful from start to finish. The atmosphere is warm and elegant, making you feel comfortable the moment you walk in. The service was outstanding — attentive, friendly, and genuinely welcoming.

The food was exceptional. Every dish was fresh, full of flavor, and beautifully presented. You can truly tell that high-quality ingredients and attention to detail go into every plate. Each bite was a delight.

Noorsha is perfect for a family dinner, a special occasion, or a relaxed evening out. We will definitely be coming back and highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for an unforgettable dining experience in Dallas. Thank you for a lovely evening!

What a great find in Richardson! The food at Noorsha Cafe & Bakery was fresh, flavorful, and authentically delicious. From the Turkish-inspired pastries and baked goods to the savory wraps and paninis, everything we tried was made with quality ingredients and care. The atmosphere was warm and welcoming, and the staff made us feel right at home with friendly, attentive service. Whether you’re grabbing a morning breakfast or a casual lunch, this place has a great vibe and fantastic food. Highly recommend!

Absolutely amazing! We came to Noorsha as a family, and it felt like we were back home in Türkiye. Everything we’ve been craving was here: fresh pastries, delicious breakfast items, Turkish tea, and that authentic atmosphere you just can’t fake. The place is beautifully designed and perfect for bringing guests; it’s cozy, stylish, and truly gives you that classic Turkish breakfast vibe.

The food tastes homemade, the service is friendly, and even the tea was spot-on (that’s when you know it’s real!). We left fully satisfied and already excited to come back. Highly recommend for anyone looking for a genuine Turkish café and bakery experience. Thank you!

Absolutely love this place. The service and family feel is so great. Also the menu is large and everything looks good. I loved the complimentary Turkish tea as well. I will be back as soon as I can. I took leftovers and wish I had got more to take with me!!

name: LynnRich Jamaican Cuisine

reviews.text: I'm honored to be graced by Chef Richie’s cooking. The Food is outstanding. From his unique flavors to the tender meat, you will fall in love with this Jamaican cuisine. He's a kindred soul with exceptional customer service. He makes you feel right at home. Great guy! 10/10 I highly recommend!!

Yooo...LISTEN. This food is everything. The jerk chicken and brown stew chicken are both out of this world and seasoned so perfectly, I had to sit back and reevaluate my life choices (because why did I order food there THREE times last week? 😅) And the rice and peas? Some of the best I’ve ever had, hands down. The veggies were fresh and delicious too, a perfect balance to all that flavor.

You can truly taste the love and authenticity in every bite. If you’re looking for real Jamaican food that hits every time, go ahead and make your way to LynnRich. Your taste buds will thank you!

The food is freaking amazing! I'm from Florida, and finding good Jamaican food in Dallas has been tough, but seriously, this is it. LynnRich is legit, no doubt. I can't stop thinking about it, lol. I'm gonna have to fit it into my weekly budget and schedule. Just greedy I tell you. Every time I've gone, the food's fresh and there's plenty of it. The oxtails just fell off the bone. The curry chicken was seasoned perfectly. And his jerk chicken, oh my gosh, I didn't think I could have jerk chicken better than what I had in Jamaica. Me and my husband said to ourselves, "We haven't ever had cabbage so good". But this food was better than anything I've ever had. My relatives came from Jamaica and wanted a taste of home, and even they said his food was better than back home. I'm wishing him nothing but success in the Dallas food scene.

It’s a yummy food truck. 10/10 tbh the oxtails are delicious and filled with meat. The cabbage is delicious, the rice is bomb and the plantains are fresh and crisp. One of the best spots in DFW lowkey. The owner/chef is also really nice everytime!!  My meal was $30 and I ate it almost 3 times lmao

My husband and I decided to try this new restaurant to support a black business in June for Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority Inc black business activity. The food was delicious and authentic. We bought the rice and peas and jerk chicken and the fried fish and white rice. The fish and jerk chicken is well seasoned and very delicious. I also enjoyed the white rice and the vegetables and plantains. My husband enjoyed the rice and peas and plantains too. We enjoyed it so much we came back. We highly recommend this restaurant. The service was great and the food delicious.

formatted_address: 110 Mile End Rd, Stepney Green, London E1 4UN, United Kingdom
name: Damal

reviews.text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Outstanding Somali food and hospitality at Damal!

I recently had dinner at Damal Restaurant in London, and it was an incredible experience from start to finish. The food was flavorful, the portions were generous, and the service was warm and welcoming — everything you’d want in a great dining spot.

We ordered one of their large mixed platters, which came with perfectly cooked rice, chicken, and meat. The presentation was beautiful — a big silver tray filled with fragrant spiced rice topped with tender roasted chicken, slow-cooked meat, and a mix of colorful vegetables. It looked amazing and tasted even better!

The chicken was juicy, coated in a rich red sauce that had the perfect balance of spice and tang. Every bite was full of flavor without being overwhelming. The meat was melt-in-your-mouth tender — seasoned beautifully and cooked to perfection. Together, they paired perfectly with the rice, creating a combination that was both comforting and full of depth.

The bariis iskukaris (Somali-style spiced rice) was just outstanding. Each grain was fluffy and aromatic, with hints of cardamom, cumin, and butter. You could really tell the rice was cooked with care. The vegetables on top added a nice freshness and slight sweetness that tied everything together beautifully.

The portions were huge — definitely made for sharing, and great value for money. It’s the kind of meal that makes you feel satisfied and happy, like a proper home-cooked feast.

The restaurant itself has a modern and relaxed vibe — clean marble tables, a cozy atmosphere, and friendly staff who make you feel welcome right away. The service was excellent; the team checked in on us often and offered great recommendations with a smile.

Damal is a fantastic spot if you want to experience authentic Somali cuisine in London. The food is hearty, flavorful, and made with real care. You can taste the tradition and pride in every bite.

Highly recommend this place — whether you’re trying Somali food for the first time or already love it, Damal will not disappoint. I’ll definitely be coming back for another platter soon!

Damal – East London (Somali spot)

Put on by a few East London brothers, so expectations were set. Execution-wise, solid.

Service was efficient — food landed fast, hot, no delays. Complimentary banana was a nice touch; shout-out Mukhtar for that. We went for the £35 platter for two and it did the job — proper portion size, filled us up straight after gym. Value for money is there.

That said, flavour profile was underpowered. Food was decent but lacked punch; could’ve used more seasoning to really stand out. Also, basic hygiene miss. toilet needs a proper mop and clean. That’s non-negotiable.

Bottom line: Good value, fast service, filling food. Needs flavour optimisation and better cleanliness to level up. Potential is there, execution needs tightening.

A party of 11 booked a table.

We ordered starters and 2 sharing platters, which were massive! We could take left over home in containers.

These grilled lamb and chicken were so tender, moist and delicious.  The rice was flavourful.

The restaurant opened less than one month when we went. It looked a bid disorganised and the service was really slow!

We waited nearly 2 hours before the main came to our table, but it was worth waiting.

The Somali tea was really nice.

It’s great for a large group.

Toilets however needed improving despite it was a new restaurant.

There is a room with carpet and stools to sit on. It looked really nice and I suppose it’s for a special occasion.

Happy to go back any time.

I have traveled from Kent to this place and it’s worth to travel that long and pay Blackwall tunnel fee as food was so delicious service was great price alright too definitely I will go there again as their food was so delicious and really want to enjoy again parking little issue so better to go after 6pm and then park left right or street or there is 10 minutes parking and park there but at end it’s worth to do that

reviews.text:
It was a nice restaurant. I ordered a lamb shank (kabuli polo) which was cooked very well.

The taste of the food was kind of nostalgic to me. I guess their chef was cooking in ceremonies! 😅 (just to clarify, that's a compliment actually).

So, yeah, the food was great. I liked it a lot.

Absolutely amazing!! Papa and I came here and he treated us sooo well. It was papas first time eating Indian food and what a great experience!! The man behind the counter welcomed us so kindly and the portions were large and perfectly tasty. The lamb was so soft and very tasty and well seasoned. Will def be back. Thank you so much! Great place!!! The Garlic naan was large and very delicious!! I will tell my friends about this place!! Thank you for the great food and the great customer service!!

Cafe Laziz is a wonderful place to enjoy delicious food in a warm and welcoming atmosphere. The food is fresh, flavorful, and beautifully prepared. The staff are very friendly, polite, and attentive, making the experience even better. The restaurant is clean and comfortable, perfect for dining with family or friends. I really enjoyed my visit and will definitely come back again. Highly recommended!
I stopped by Café Laziz in Dallas and had such a good time. The food was good and people working there were super kind. It felt cozy, like a place I’d bring friends next time.

Café Laziz in Dallas:

We had an amazing dining experience at Café Laziz in Dallas! From start to finish, everything was delicious and satisfying. We ordered Kabuli Palaw, Pacha, Kabab, and for dessert, the traditional Watani Shiryakh—each dish was full of authentic flavor and freshly prepared.

One of the best parts is the variety of meals available on the menu—you’ll have plenty of options to choose from. And impressively, they prepare everything fresh and have it ready in about 20 minutes!

I highly recommend this place to everyone, especially foodies who love Afghan cuisine or are looking to try something new. Great taste, fast service, and a welcoming atmosphere—Café Laziz truly delivers!

reviews.text: I ordered the salmon platter and Puff Puffs. The food is so flavorful, tender, and filling. The Puff Puffs are like little bread clouds. Everything was so delicious and the owner is so friendly and personable. These are the types of businesses I love to support and they deserve the hype.

OUTSTANDING, AMAZING, TERRIFIC, and most importantly DELICIOUS! That is all I have to say about this location. This review is long overdue. I came in after pumping gas at the Sam's Club nearby and only found this hidden Gem with a quick Google search. My wife has never had African food and I've never had Fufu and have heard wonderful things about it. Trust me y'all, it didn't disappoint. The sweet lady (Stella) was soo appreciative of me wanting to try her food that she had hooked me up with the most surprisingly delicious food I've had in a while. Sometimes it worth it to just be daring and try new things. I kind of don't want to spoil it for anyone reading this so skip the next few lines if you'd want to discover it for yourselves. It reminds me of a giant mochi ball. That you can enhance the flavor of depending on the sauce you eat it with. Stella was kind enough to give me 3 different sauces. Peanut sauce, their DREAM sauce (I want to say it is tomatoe base), and a Pepper sauce which I really enjoy. I also dipped the Fufu into the Egusi which is soo delicious that you can also use it as a sauce on it's own as well. Y'all we live here in KC and I would say the the Smoke brisket that they serve here can rival any place here. So if you like BBQ you'll love this place. I'd say it's BBQ with an African Twist. So Stella tells me that they are from Cameroon as their food would be categorized as West African food. All I know is that Good Food is good no matter where it's from. I'd dare say that they do their heritage proud with this Delicious representation of their culture. We opted to have the Brisket plate with Egusi and I can't help myself with the Oxtail. It was some of the largest portions of Oxtail and most tender and scrumptious that I've ever had. If you're wanting to be adventurous and be rewarded with some delicious food and excellent service please come by the mall and stop in at the food court and Stella may make your African Dream Cuisine come true and fill your bellies. I most definitely will come again with family and friends.

This place is AMAZING. This is my first time eating an African Meal. The fufu, and Egusi are delicious. The chicken, brisket and Oxtail were falling off the bone and were packet with amazing juices and flavors. 10/10 I definitely recommend this restaurant. If you never eaten African food and want to try this is the place to go. Customer service is off the charts amazing. Thank you

Ok so I'm new in the area and was looking for the best tasting African dish in Kansas and I believe I struck gold. I'm big on oxtails and egusi soup and ordered a plate of that and some puff ball pastries and was also blinded by such beauty of Stella the owner. I must say I'll definently take the 30 min drive bcz the food was very well seasoned and fresh thank you.

Stella is amazing and so is her food!!! She took the time to talk to me abd explain her food and how to eat it.  Way better than other places I've tried.  And the spicy sauce?! 👩chefs kiss!!! I will be back to try the oxtail for sure!!!

The owner was very gracious to go get the flower to prove that his puff puffs were gluten-free. Please work very hard to source all his ingredients and make sure that they are safe for us to eat. I have the goat and it was wonderful.
I swear I crave this place 2x a week if not more. The flavors are so amazing and mouthwatering. The staff is always so kind and welcoming. One of my favorite places in the market!

Very fresh, healthy, attractively presented food. I got one of the vegan combos with a side of plantains which were perfectly caramelized. I loved the root punch ginger juice drink, too. A refreshing change from the usual veg options available.

Mixed feelings about our experience here.  While the service was friendly and most of the food was decent, my entrée was not edible. Chicken,  rice,  and fufu were good.  The cabbage did not seems fresh and the goat was the worst I've ever had.  Near $50 for two just left us expecting a better experience.

reviews.text: The food (soup & swallow)is good but portion size is very inconsistent. This time when I ordered the soup I was given was what we would give a child it was the size of my hand and same with pounded yam one day you get two wraps one day only one. Not sure if it is because food is being ordered towards the end of the day but if you don’t have enough then the order should be canceled. The amount vs the price was an apology.

I can’t speak for the food, but the open sign was on, Google maps said they close at 11pm. I drove all the way down only to see no one inside and their sign inside says they’re closed!! What a waste of time and I was so excited.

Seems like a solid idea. It’s not a sit-in restaurant, you just order and pick up your food.
When I went to the place during business hours on Saturday around 10pm, the place was closed and I could not order. Calling and trying to order from the food apps said it was closed too.

For $24 and some change , the plate of rice that you get is not worth it at all. It was seasoned well but 24 dollars is just to much for the small amount. I got beef with my Jollof rice and at least I would have though I'd be getting a good amount of beef since the rice was little but I had 3 small pieces of beef . To add to that the 3 beef all were very tough , border line burnt. If you want good Nigerian jollof I would recommend elsewhere.

Best African Food in DFW hands down!!! Everything on POINT! Hopefully they don’t grow big and reduce quality of food. Thanks for pointing in all it takes to deliver the best food and customer service to your customers. It’s a 100/10 for me. Kudos!!!

Had to edit my review. Quality of food still remains excellent, service great! But quantity does not match the prices. Quantity of food too small and when they serve chicken for all the times I’ve ordered for chicken, I’ve gotten two small pieces and one of the two small pieces is all bones.

formatted_address: 108 Maverick Ln, Forney, TX 75126, United States
name: Mercy Brite Kitchen

reviews.text: They have the best shawarma wrap, the pepper soup and nkowbi is top notch. Their salad is also good. Overall good food and good customer services I recommend if you’re looking local naija cuisine in Dallas Tx

I was in Dallas recently on business trip so I googled African food restaurants near me and this popped up

The Ogbono soup was a savory delight, showcasing a perfect blend of traditional flavors and textures.

The party jellof  rice was also represented
If you’re looking for an amazing Authentic West African Delicacies, Mercy Brite Kitchen is the place. Isi ewu & nkwobi are my favorites on their my menu.

The food was so good
I really enjoyed the food especially the soup.
I will recommend my friends to your Kitchen
I ordered meatpie and Nkwobi. The food was made fresh and tasted very good. Will definitely be coming back.

formatted_address: 921 W Commerce St, Dallas, TX 75208, United States
name: Haut Pot

reviews.text:
Haut Pot Dallas left much to be desired. Despite advertising authentic Nigerian cuisine, the food fell short in both taste and quality. Dishes were disappointingly dry, lacking the flavorful essence one expects from traditional Nigerian fare. The owner's demeanor was equally unsatisfactory, displaying rudeness that marred the entire dining experience. Customer service was abysmal; waiting for an hour outside the establishment, despite a confirmed time, is simply unacceptable. It's disheartening when a business fails to deliver on its promises, leaving patrons feeling undervalued and dissatisfied. With so many dining options available, Haut Pot Dallas must prioritize improving both its culinary offerings and customer relations if it hopes to survive in the competitive restaurant scene. Until significant improvements are made, I cannot in good conscience recommend this establishment to others seeking an authentic and enjoyable dining experience.

Please also note the food is cooked from a ghost kitchen in south Dallas. Obviously, stay away and do not support this small business.

I recently had a disappointing experience with this seller. Not only was my order delivered several hours late, but the seller was also handling her phone and cooking at the same time (she mentioned this over a call I had with her), which seemed unprofessional. When I finally went to pickup my order, there was no apology for the delay. This lack of customer service and consideration for timely delivery has left me very dissatisfied. I hope the seller can improve their service in the future.

Who doesn't love a great atmosphere served with delicious food? Says nobody and that is why you need to check out Haut pot. This restaurant is beyond extraordinary, meets all elite standards. Every dish on their menu is top-notch, their level of service is amazing so please if you're in Dallas-TX, don't miss out; you definitely need to go check them out and anyone who visits Dallax, needs to go there. You won't regret it.

My friend ordered this food for an event , 2 events infact and it was a total disaster. Let’s forget the fact the lady who attended to us was very rude , we gave a time to pick up the food and she delayed us for an hour and she was unapologetic. The first batch we ordered, no one could eat fried rice , it was even curry rice not fried rice. All the positive reviews are from her friends. DO NOT BUY FROM HER. Once again very Rude to the core. I would have taken a picture of the friend rice but it was thrown out immediately. Once again, buy at your detriment.

Regrettably, the catering service provided by Haut Pot left much to be desired. Despite assurances of quality, the food was bland and lacked the authentic flavors one would expect from Nigerian cuisine. Additionally, the portion sizes were disappointingly small, and the presentation was lackluster. Communication with the catering team was also challenging, leading to confusion and errors in the order. Overall, a disappointing experience that failed to meet expectations

Business owner was very rude, didn’t offer any assistance or apologize.

formatted_address: 4611 36th Ave SW, Seattle, WA 98126, United States
name: House of Naku

reviews.text:
1st time ever trying this place & wow what a great way to start 2026☺️😋 with delicious food!! Customer service amazing / she answered all my questions before I placed an order online so it was very helpful! We ended up trying Attieke , Super Kanja (okra soup) + fufu pounded yam , meat pies , grilled chicken +rice & everything was 10/10 I would recommend!!!❤️ Please keep in mind to be very patient , it is well worth the wait , I can’t wait to keep ordering to try everything on the menu🤭 Thank you again guys!!

Ps . The entrance can be a little confusing you will enter the building and ring the bell/ door bell for “House of Naku” for online order/phone order  or just call in and they’ll be able to assist.

I love the food at House of Naku so much that I've tried everything on the menu and everything was a hit not a single miss on flavor or quality of food. Some of my go to dishes are the okra soup with fufu chicken yassa and jollof rice with lamb.
Egusi was so delicious! Service was great, not to mention Beautiful! The lady who took our order could be a model!❤️ anyways. Food was excellent.

Absolutely delicious. Had the super kanja soup along with fufu and a side of plantains. Super tasty, incredibly filling, and so happy that I finally got to try fufu. Friends had jollof rice and loved it, and the ginger drink has an incredible kick. Highly recommend.
The egusi is amazing.  Lots of flavor and the meat was super tender!  Fufu is good (little on the soft side).  Fried fish is also good!!  Overall portion sizes are very nice!

formatted_address: 8319 Wabash Ave S Suite C, Seattle, WA 98118, United States
name: Mama Sambusa Kitchen

reviews.text: Delicious and will be coming here again! Definitely getting more Sambusas next time

I went there randomly. Knocked at the door and Auntie came by, and told me everything's gonna take some time. I opted for just the Cheesecake as the neighborhood looked a little sketchy to be waiting around cluelessly. Mama was so sweet and endearing she gave me sambusas too. And the raspberry white chocolate Cheesecake was MIND BLOWING.
I found Mama Sambusa from a tiktok creator named ecsotixdivinity. I tried the Shwarma fries and OMG I wanted to cry the food was so good! I plan on going back to try the alfredo and spaghetti.

Big portions, very worth the price. I got the fettuccine with chicken and salmon and  gyro and fries. It was good. The meat sauce spaghetti is better than the the Italian restaurants, I won't be wasting my money there anymore. I'm going to get extra meat sauce on the side. That cheesecake is almost as good as mine, love the biscoff crust. I should have thought of that. 😉 Everything was fresh and hot but she does get busy so you may have to wait a bit for your order. She makes a very good orange sauce that goes on almost everything there She moved across the street to a brick and mortar, nice place.
The women who runs this place is amazing and knows what true good food tastes like. Don't let the area fool you. Seattle's best is here.

formatted_address: 14314 Greenwood Ave N #2, Seattle, WA 98133, United States
name: Jollof Hub West African Cuisines

reviews.text: Let me tell you something!!! That lady in there cooking that food up by herself and she doing her thang!! It’s great pricing great service great quality of food! Her meats were so tender! Her plasas has REAL cassava leaf it was the right consistency of okra in the okra soup the meat pies were 🔥🔥🔥I’ve gone from lynnwood to Tacoma and she wins HANDS DOWN !! Best African restaurant in Washington state.

10/10 best place in Seattle for western African dishes, ESPECIALLY the BENACHIN (jollof rice) ohhh myyy gosh the vegetables were cooked to perfection and that lamb was so tender. It fell right off the bone with the seasoning is perfect.I also odered SUPER KANJA (okra soup) & EGUSI soup was to die for!!! Not exaggerating at all!! I tried both wonjo & baobab juice aswell and it was sooooo deliciousssssss!!!!!! I cannot recommend this place enough!! I will be returning for more. oh, and I cannot forget the plantains ABSOLUTELY THE BEST PLANTAINS I HAVE EVER HAD IN MY LIFE. and don’t get me started on the service. It was absolutely outstanding. He was very sweet and Informative about each dish!

So sorry but this was one of the worst meals of my life. Very expensive and inedible food. Lots of bones, skin, eyeballs in the fish soup. The flavor was good but the meat in the rice dish was so tough and full of fat and gristle it was impossible to eat. The dough balls to dip in the broth were served wrapped tightly in molten hot plastic Saran Wrap which was very off-putting. I hate leaving a poor review for a small family-run restaurant but maybe this feedback will help improve the place.

We had a delicious dinner at Jollof Hub! The Lamb Afra had a wonderful spice blend and the onions were soo good. The owner is really nice also! We will certainly be back and look forward to trying out different dishes on the menu.

This restaurant is a true hidden gem! I ordered the egusi soup and my boyfriend had the lamb domoda, it was so tender it literally fell clean off the bone. We also shared meat pies and plantains, and both were amazing: the pies were flaky and savory, and the plantains perfectly caramelized. What really shines here is how thoughtful and authentic the cooking feels. You can taste the care in every bite. Comforting, and absolutely delicious. I can’t wait to come again! Thank you!!!

formatted_address: 5041 Rainier Ave S suite 107, Seattle, WA 98118, United States
name: Safari Njema

reviews.text: Very nice ladies that cook and serve you. I like the ginger drink they have cold. We are having goat curry stew and beef curry stew with fufu and rice with collard greens. Be prepared to wait for your meal. Lots a people order food to go from here.The goat is to die for and the meat pies are heavenly

First time trying this and it taste good! The cabbage had a sweet butter smell and it’s great with fufu. Goat was also soft and juicy.

Service was super slow tho, we waited for 25 minutes to get our plates. The utensils were not clean but they changed it for us.

I love this place because of the food. Authentic East African cuisine with a rustic atmosphere, that is reminiscent of a laid back setting. The personnel is kind and respectful and listens. You might have to wait a bit for your food, and the best way is to make a call and order 30 mins while planning the trip. It is not a Michelin restaurant but it is sure just a genuine local, “ungentrified” spot. It is surrounded by gentrified neighborhood and hopefully this spot won’t be pushed out of business.
Great hole-in-the-wall place for authentic Kenyan cuisine. The food was delicious and the people couldn't have been more friendly. No frills decor, but the food is worth the trip

The food here is delicious, Seattle you’re lucky!! I‘ve moved to Miami but I went to Safari again on my last work trip in May, first found this place after an intense hike with a friend 10 yrs ago and the fried fish and goat is incredible. Yes there’s some time to cook it but good things come to those who wait. Was just thinking about Safari and realized I haven’t posted my review so doing that now, I highly recommend!

formatted_address: 1009 Boren Ave, Seattle, WA 98104, United States
name: Gold Coast Ghal Kitchen

reviews.text: This restaurant is a slept on hidden gem in the First Hill neighborhood. Its presence is humble, for the windows are tinted and there’s minimal signage identifying the location. But once you walk inside, you’re welcomed with vibrant West African expression and hospitality. We visited in August, 2025, and the menu showcased authentic dishes from Ghana and Liberia with options such as fried plantain and Liberian pepper soup. To start, we ordered two well balanced cocktails, the Yaa and Ama. For apps, we got the kosua ne meko (boiled egg) and peri peri wings which were the best peri peri wings I’ve eaten (sorry Nandos). For mains, the whole Branzino came with cassava pearls, two pepper sauces, and fried plantains, and the short ribs with jollof rice, plantains, and a light salad. Everything was a beautiful showcase of flavor and texture, and we savored every bite. Overall, the ambiance was comfortable, the service was very friendly and welcoming, and I will recommend this spot to all my friends who come to visit.

Absolutely the best meal I've had eating out somewhere. The flavors are phenomenal, the atmosphere and staff were wonderful and helped inform my decision (have no experience eating west African food, but now I'm obsessed)
I had the jollof rice with the short ribs. The cole-slaw helped a lot to bring freshness to the dish. If I could complain about anything I wish I got a bigger portion of the coleslaw but that's just me.
I took the peanut soup with fufu on the side home and that too was amazing. Truly a must-try for locals and newcomers alike.

I really wanted to love this restaurant but the quality of the food was not great. The beef hand pies were very good. They were large and stuffed with delicious well-seasoned ground beef and came with a really good herby sauce. In fact, that would have probably been enough for a lunch. The chicken and jollof was seasoned well but the chicken was beyond dry and tough and the rice was crunchy and very dry as well. They tasted like they had been cooked a while ago and they just scraped the bottom of the pan and served it. Really disappointing. I hope this was just an anomaly.

Atmosphere was nice, service was good but the food could be much better. I’m excited it’s here as there are so few African restaurants in the city. They just need to make and serve freshly made food.
I had never had Ghanaian food before. It was fabulous. Will definitely be going back and taking friends and family with me. The peanut and goat soup😋!  Jollof rice and short ribs....fabulous.

Hands down one of the best food we have had in Seattle!!! Highly highly recommend!

My boyfriend and I were visiting and stumbled upon this jam. We got the eggs for the appetizer, the Goat peanut soup and the Grill Branzino. It was a perfect meal.

The Goat peanut soup was rich, well-seasoned, the meat was so tender, gamy, and yummy. The branzino was executed perfectly with crispy fish skin and tender juicy inside. As someone who grew up having fish, the delicate green peppery sauce that compliments the fish won me over entirely.

The staff were so friendly and did not hesitant to share their enthusiasm for their food with us. The atmosphere were great as well. The spot definitely worth the hype!!!

formatted_address: 209 1st Ave S, Seattle, WA 98104, United States
name: PDJ (Pass D Jollof) Nigerian Restaurant

reviews.text: The goat pepper soup was delicious. It had alot of flavor. My grandma is from Nigeria I grew up eating this west african food. My only thing I would say I would like alil more goat meat. I wasnt expecting 3 lil pieces with nothing but soup for 27.00. I am use to the goat stew to being red with alot more goat meat in it. I would like to come back and try some different dishes. That goat pepper soup was go fix for now.

I recently visited this Nigerian restaurant and overall had a good experience, though there were a few bumps along the way. The atmosphere was warm and inviting, and the music set a really nice vibe that made the evening enjoyable. The food itself was very good…full of flavor and definitely worth coming back for.

That said, the service was a bit confusing. The restaurant uses a self-service system, but it seemed to be missing some options that should have been available. We briefly spoke to a server, but they disappeared after a quick exchange, leaving us unsure of how to proceed. Eventually, I believe it was the bartender who ended up taking our order, and they were very kind and helpful, which I appreciated.

So while the start of the experience felt a little disorganized, the food and the overall atmosphere made up for it. With a few improvements to the service and ordering process, this place could be excellent.

Been here twice, and the food has been really good on both occasions.

The first time we had it in was in March. The ogbono and egusi had tripes and pomo in them, and we added extra proteins to the order for extra charge.

Next time was in May. (2 months apart)
I noticed the soups didn’t have tripes or cow skin in them, which is very okay with me since the chicken this time was bigger than the first time.

We also had the Jollof as take outs.

Overall, the food is really good, and it is worth eating here.

This place checks all the boxes of an African restaurant in a good way. Ordering is made simple with being able to order off your phone. So you can take your time going over the menu. They have an easily accessible sink to wash your hand, the music and set up help with the atmosphere👌🏾. We had Okra, fufu, chicken stew, plantain and jollof with goat meat. It took like 5-7 minutes after ordering and our food was out like all items. To top it off the food was really really good hand down authentic.

Pass d Jollof consistently delivers great food, and that’s why I came back for a second visit. The flavors are always on point, and when the food finally arrived, it reminded me why this place is so popular. That said, this particular experience was far less smooth than my first visit.
My group included my infant child, who was in a stroller, and the seating process was unnecessarily frustrating. The staff member who was seating us kept changing her mind about where to place us because of the stroller, which made the experience feel disorganized and honestly a bit annoying, especially when you’re trying to settle in with a baby.
After we placed our order, the wait time for the food was close to 45 minutes. During that entire time, no one checked in on our table to update us or acknowledge the delay. We eventually had to flag down a staff member ourselves to ask what was going on. When the food did arrive, we also realized we had no silverware and had to ask for that as well, which added to the frustration.
Thankfully, our server, Kasama, was excellent. She was warm, attentive, and genuinely apologetic, and she did her best to make up for the earlier issues. While this visit didn’t live up to my first experience, the food quality and Kasama’s service still leave me hopeful that this was just an off day.

formatted_address: 21027 International Blvd, SeaTac, WA 98198, United States
name: Mall of Africa Restaurant

reviews.text: The Kati Kati chicken suqaar and rice and beef suqaar were immaculate. I will be recommending this restaurant anytime my friends visit Washington. This was my favorite restaurant for my 5 day trip to Seattle. The service is very friendly and they explained the food options since we were unfamiliar

The food here was awesome. Friendly service answered my questions because I didn't know what to order. The lamb shank was delish.

I came here for lunch not knowing what to expect. Very chill atmosphere. Not many people here for lunch on a Thursday. Honestly I will be back next time I'm out in the area for work! The coffee is also decent and cheap compared to what you'd get in Seattle. The beans are ground fresh which was a plus. Big portions as well. Almost didn't finish everything on my own.

Absolutely loved the service and the food. This is a block away from the Best Western and was a fantastic option for Lunch and Dinner.

I had the Samosa and the Chicken Wrap. Sadly, they have toned down the spice on some dishes because local pallettes are not used to spice. However, I was able to request the authentic/standard level of spice for the Chicken Wrap. It was fantastic. Paired well with the green hot sauce.

I also had the Samosa and my Uncle thoroughly enjoyed. He said it changed his life and he has to find places to eat them in the future.

I went there seeing the website reviews and wanted to try African food. Unfortunately,
there was Extremely uncomfortable environment. I was with my mom, aunty and toddler. The moment  we entered, there wer two other their native  customers were literally staring at us like they have seen an alien. I seen nobdy to take order at the counter but from nack in the kitchen women were yelling and shouting. I rang the bell twice and a gentleman showed. I requested if any one can take the order and meanwhile another their native customer came to order. He took his order and i waited there for 15 minutes and left to my table back. My mom said lets leave, what kinna of a place is this and meanwhile another persona cane by saying we dont have checken burger but beef and I said please pack only one for my toddler and we decided not eat here and that took the person 20 minutes and around us all the customers got there orders and I was waiting. I went back to the counter and he is like it will take 20 more minutes.
In short extremely pathetic and almost no services and worst ever environment. I will never recommend.
All the food we ordered was so yummy! The owner was so accommodating. First time coming here from NC and Vancouver Canada. We will surely be coming back on our next visit. Goat is my number one!

formatted_address: 1510 NE 117th St, Seattle, WA 98125, United States
name: Jebena Cafe

reviews.text:
I was craving Ethiopian food, and Jebena Café kept popping up on Seattle’s “best of” lists, so naturally my second brain aka my stomach led me there. The place is quite small, and I’ll be honest, the surrounding neighborhood felt a bit shady. I even hesitated for a moment after parking.
But once I stepped inside, the space was squeaky clean and I was warmly welcomed by the owner. We ordered the vegetarian combo, and the sides were flavorful, fresh, and subtle on the palate. It’s not the best Ethiopian food I’ve ever had, but it’s definitely better than many spots around town. The ingredients looked fresh and tasted crisp, which I really appreciated.

They do close early, so make sure to arrive at least 30 minutes before closing.

I also ordered a samosa, hoping it would beat the ones from Whole Foods, but unfortunately it leaned more toward the inedible side. The mint chutney was fine, nothing exceptional.

Would I come back? Probably not.
Is it worth trying? Yes.
It’s easy on the wallet, so if you’re craving Ethiopian, it’s a decent spot to try once.

It’s a 3.5 for me 😐

A friend and I tried this place for the first time, and we loved it. The restaurant was clean, welcoming, and bright and the food was incredible. We ordered one of their meat combos, which came with injera, a couple of different meats, lentils, shiro wat, spinach, and salad. The portions were great and everything was super flavorful. We also had the foul, which was really nice, served with soft, pillowy bread. Also, our server was so kind and friendly. She checked on us several times and answered any questions we had. I would highly recommend this place and understand now why it's so highly rated!

Got their meat combo - was a great choice. Their lentil beans yellow and red both were much smoother than other places, the flavor of their meat are also unique and very tasty - definitely will go back.

I had not eaten Ethiopian food for several decades so I decided to give it another shot. I found Jebena Cafe on Yelp and decided to try it based upon the great reviews and I'm very glad I did!

I had the Jebena Combo, which is the largest meat combo, even though I was eating by myself as I wanted to try a variety of different things. All of the different dishes were amazing, but my favorite was the Doro Wot.

The owner, Martha, is an absolutely lovely human being and the service was top notch. I will be back in the very near future to try more deliciousness from their menu!

I've wanted to try ethiopian food for years and my great aunt brought my family for my mom's birthday. The food was DELICIOUS and was served by the sweetest woman. I will be bringing all my friends to experience this wonderful restaurant!

formatted_address: 11400 NE 132nd St, Kirkland, WA 98034, United States
name: Tess Kitchen Nigerian online Restaurant

reviews.text: She has SUCH good stews and great portions for each meal. Definitely WILL be coming back. I got the beef and chicken stew and it was AMAZING🤩

The food and service here is beyond amazing!!
I recommend everyone to try this restaurants...your life will never be the same!

Nice food especially their African dishes, one of the best I’ve had in the US.
When it comes to African dishes,Tess kitchen is absolutely the best and it’s highly recommended.
If you need any African/nigerian dish to your door step, this is your place. The delivery was very fast and food is top notch. I definitely recommend
Her food is top notch🔥my advice for anyone who want to order kindly get extra plate🤤her food is supper yummy

formatted_address: 16108 Ash Way #103, Lynnwood, WA 98087, United States
name: Dijah's Kitchen - African Restaurant

reviews.text: Place was recommended by an acquaintance as he was proud to let me know there was a Gambian restaurant in the area. Really enjoyed the jollof! Lots of seasoning not too spicy (I like spicy food so maybe it’s spicy for someone who doesn’t often eat spicy or spice-ful lol). They were kind to me and my dad and very proud of their Jollof trophy from this year haha. I liked the portions and flavors of everything. I do agree with one of the comments about maybe the place getting better ventilation, if not at least have the smell be of seasoned meat and not burnt oil. There’s not a lot of African eateries so let’s continue to support them so they can continue to be a wonderful member of our culinary community :)

This was the first visit for me & my partner. We tried their meat pies @ the Bite of Seattle and they were delicious so we thought we would visit the restaurant to try other dishes. We both ordered the meat pies and the red jollof rice with chicken. The meat pies weren't bad but they were better @ the bite of Seattle with the dipping sauce. The jollof rice and chicken was not very good. The rice tasted burnt and the chicken wasn't cooked all the way ! They did give us a refund for the main entrees but I had higher hopes the food would have tasted better. I don't think we'll return.
First time trying African food and it was amazing! Great flavors - the chicken afra was super flavorful and plantains were amazing! We tried egusi soup and fufu which came out super nice and hot!

This was my first time dining here. I came with my friend for lunch. The interior was beautiful, the colors of the seats and paintings popped, the tables were clean, the service was warm, the food was hearty and clearly cooked with a desire to nourish, not just feed.

Overall a wonderful experience. If only I lived in the area, I would return many times to explore the rest of the menu.
My family and I came here for dinner and the food was delicious 😋. The environment was cleaned and welcoming. Definitely pay them a visit if you are looking for authentic African food.

formatted_address: 7250 Rainier Ave S, Seattle, WA 98118, United States
name: Paradise Restaurant

reviews.text: Okay, so I just tried this Somali place in WA 98118 and wow, it was amazing! It’s a little bit of a drive out there, not super touristy, which I actually liked. The food was incredible – seriously, the goat was so tender and flavorful. The portions were huge, and the rice was perfect. I ordered the goat and chapati, and it was a steal for the amount of food you get. The couple running the place were so friendly and welcoming, really made us feel at home. Parking was a bit tricky, maybe go earlier to beat the crowds. I’d definitely recommend bringing cash, the card machine didn’t have a tip option. I'm already planning my next visit!

Okay, so we just tried this Somali place on Rainier Ave and wow, it was amazing! It’s a little off the beaten path, which was nice. The goat was unbelievably tender – seriously, the best I’ve had. Portions were huge, we practically left with four meals! The rice was perfect and they gave us a free banana, which was a lovely touch. It wasn't super busy when we were there, which was great. The couple running it were so friendly and welcoming. My only suggestion would be to bring cash, the card machine didn’t have a tip option. Definitely going back!

Just tried this Somali place on Rainier Ave and wow, it was really good! It was packed when we went, so we waited about 20 minutes for a table. The portions are huge – seriously, we were stuffed. The goat was amazing, really flavorful and tender, although a little spicy for me. Prices were reasonable. I’d bring cash as the card machine didn’t have a tip option.

The most amazing tasting and price worthy food I've had so far in Seattle ❤️ I was starving and after what I had previously, nothing seemed good and it was pretty late and boom. Stumbled upon Paradise Restaurant and I haven't had anything as good as this in a long long time!!! Cook to order food and the owner is really nice. I honestly was so close to tearing up from how good this was. I got the #3 with mild spice. So happy ❤️

The dishes were flavorful and the portions were so big I had to take some home. Lovely vibe and helpful staff throughout the night. Setting is gorgeous and the waiters are professional. 10/10! I’ll definitely return.

formatted_address: 4423 Rainier Ave S, Seattle, WA 98118, United States
name: ALEM RESTAURANT

reviews.text: Alem is one of our all time favorite places in Seattle! The service is great and the food is even better. Awesome prices, huge portions, and such savory brilliant food. 🙌🏼 we arrive excited, and leave very very full.

The Alem brings traditional Ethiopian dishes and affable service to the Seattle area. Bring your friends or family and share a veggie or meat combo platter to fully experience the variety of flavors and elegance of each item. My personal favorite had to have been the Doro Wat or "chicken stew" bathed in butter and spices. Another fun piece of our experience was using the injera style "flatbread" to grab our desired items from the platter. It brought a unique atmosphere that let us bond with each other as we shared the meal together.
Maybe because I got there when it first opened up, they weren’t ready, but my injera bread was cold. I was soooo sad. But they are good people! Maybe I’ll have to try again.

We decided to stop for lunch while driving down Ranier Ave. I found this restaurant on Yelp and decided to give it a try. We were able to park in front of the restaurant. Only street parking is available.
We arrived at the restaurant at 12:30 pm with 3 people, but there were no customers, probably because it was a weekday.
A woman in the store greeted us with a smile. We looked menu and chosen #1 meat combo and 3 of ginger tea. We always eat one plate of Ethiopian food for two people. This time, the meat combo was large, so we ordered one for 3 people. A meat platter with a mix of meat entries are perfect to try. Ginger tea tastes different depending on the restaurant. I usually like sweet ginger tea with honey. But there is no sweetness here, and sugar comes. So adjust sweetness by yourselves.
Meat combo comes with 8 kinds of ingredients on the injera. The taste was good and made us full.
I would like to try other menus next time.

My family loves Ethiopian food, so we thought we’d branch out from our normal go-to spot. The veggie combo was very flavorful and delicious.  The portions were smaller than their competitors but not significantly so.

Unfortunately, the meat combo was just awful (hence the one star). We were given two large bones, bones which didn’t have any meat that could be picked off. And the wee bit of meat that was left after removing the bones, was extremely tough and inedible.  The dish included a pile of cheese, a veggie dish, and an egg, which in my mind doesn’t count for meat when ordering a meat platter. And the portion for the meat platter was even smaller than the veggie platter.

Very disappointing! I was hoping this was our new go-to spot as it’s on the way home, but not.

formatted_address: 15215 Military Rd S, SeaTac, WA 98188, United States
name: East African restaurant

reviews.text: This place is the GOAT. My husband and I stopped in on a layover from Japan to New York. The place is unassuming, but as soon as you walk in you are greeted with incredible warmth and hospitality. Adan (sorry if I am misspelling that!) was unbelievably kind to us - just asked us what meat we liked, then said he’d hook us up and took the decision making out of our hands. He brought us a platter with delicious lentils, lamb shank, stewed chicken, tons of injera and delicious home made tea. He checked on us throughout the meal and ensured we had everything we need. We realize that they butcher much of (if not all of) the meat there, making it super fresh. It was just delicious and we felt nurtured throughout. Don’t judge this place by the fact that it’s in a strip mall. It was the best and if we lived in Seattle we’d be regulars for sure.

Absolute must try restaurant! We came for breakfast and tried the Suqar with chicken and beef, both were delicious! Came with piles of hot steaming injera bread which we used to sop up the sauce and tender meat with our hands. Our server recommended their sweet hot tea which was a delicious blend of spices including ginger and cinnamon similar to chai. Very enjoyable! You won’t be disappointed! Thank you to our server for a wonderful experience!

Had a wonderful experience! I have never had East African food or even lamb before and it was delicious! The meat was falling off the bone, perfectly prepared. The man who greeted us and the server were both very friendly and the server helped me pick a dish. Loved the atmosphere, it felt like everyone was just eating dinner in their family home.

So delicious! I had never eaten at an African restaurant before, but I will 100% be back! The person at the counter was super friendly and my husband and I were stuffed after trying to eat the whole injera platter. The ginger tea was also amazing!!!

Our beef steak and rice were very good. My 4 yo son especially loved the rice, which was cooked perfectly with lots of flavors. My husband and I enjoyed the beef with the green sauce (think it’s cilantro and chillies) and the fresh salad that comes with the meal. The owner was very friendly and accommodating. The location is very convenient within walking distance from the Tukwila light rail station

formatted_address: 306 23rd Ave S #104, Seattle, WA 98144, United States
name: East African Imports & Restaurant

reviews.text: The staff here is very nice and provides for a relaxed atmosphere .

Had the fish cutlet and veggie combo. Definitely feels like home here. Loved the veggies felt refreshed and full. Will probably return to try the meat combo. Was nice to have a meal and watch the game on a Sunday.
Food was really great with large portions enough to share between 2 people. Staff was really friendly and attentive.
Nice place to eat in the back room of a deli. Good Ethiopian food. Lots of nice Ethiopian people and families.
I come here all the time. I love the staff! I did get some berbere here and it was not great lol. But I get my tea spices, incense, and a bunch of other small things.

formatted_address: 19417 36th Ave W UNIT A1, Lynnwood, WA 98036, United States
name: Bantaba African Restaurant

reviews.text: Arrived an hour before closing, no one was dining in and the kitchen was very busy preparing many to go orders. So although our food took a bit to come out it was delicious. Meat pies had a nice flaky dough with tasty beef and onion inside. Afra chicken had good seasoning as well as the onions. Plantains provided a nice sweet accent and soft texture that went well with the savory meat, rice, and black eyed pea slaw.

Strip mall restaurant. Clean and tidy.
Giant portions. Fresh cooked. Spicy or not spicy options. The Afra is lemony and grilled perfectly. Not fast food and the wait is worth it.

If you have time, I suggest you call in your order. I figured ordering something simple as soup and a veggie rice plate would be quick but no it wasn't.  I had to wait 30 minutes. There was a family of 4 there that said they were waiting for an hour for their food!  Aside from that, the customer service was great and the food wasn't too bad. I ordered the goat soup and veggie jolof rice plate. The soup came with rice which had I known, I wouldn't have ordered the veggie rice plate...but oh well.
The soup tasted great but was very spicy.  So eating it with the Rice made it bearable. The veggie rice plate came with plantains, a piece of vegetable (I don't know what it was) and cabbage. The Rice didn't taste like it was cooked fresh, the plantains was hard and I didn't bother to taste the cabbage and vegetable. The amount of food they gave was alot though, so I ate it for 2 days so I wouldn't waste it 😆

I went during lunchtime. I ordered the deep fried whole tilapia ($20.99) and benechin-lamb ($18.99). It can take some time for food to come. The food was well worth the wait! Of the two, I liked the fish more, it was a little lighter in my opinion, even with the fish being deep fried, I also enjoyed the vegetables it came with. The benechin came with a ton of really tasty seasoned rice, it didn’t have vegetables. Hearty portions, definitely had leftovers.

Highly recommend this spot for all considering trying something new and curious. I was served by a nice woman named Mary, the food was prompt, flavorful, and a wonderful change in spots for take out. I’d be up for trying other dishes! Would highly recommend the plantains as a side with anything ordered.

The ambiance was simple, clean, and pretty busy for a week night.

Parking lot was full, and had plenty of parking. Seemed like a decent amount of to-go orders too.

formatted_address: 226 1st Ave S, Kent, WA 98032, United States
name: Rafiki Restaurant and Lounge

reviews.text: Great place to visit as a Kenyan. They deliver greatness in Kenyan cuisine. I enjoyed my meals there. Made me feel at home in all aspects. Keep showcasing home away from home!

We enjoyed our second visit to Rafiki (friend), where every opportunity is made to Karibu Rafiki (welcome friend).  On both of our visits, everyone has been welcoming and gracious.  As we entered, we turned to the left to the restaurant.  Turning to the right takes you to the lounge.  On Friday night, it was packed.  A few months earlier at lunch time there was just a few in the room.  For dinner, we enjoyed Tilapia, Chicken and Goat dishes.  The presentation was excellent and the flavors were wonderful.  At my lunch visit the collard greens were the best I ever had.  At dinner, the flavor was not to my taste, but good.  There is no dessert menu, which to my sweet tooth as disappointing.  When we reheated our leftovers from the large proportioned dinner, the food was almost as good as dinner the night before.  We plan to return to Rafiki for lunch or dinner soon.

We had a wonderful experience at Rafiki Restaurant! The food was fresh, clean, and absolutely delicious. Our waiter was attentive and paid great attention to detail, bringing everything out quickly and making sure we had everything we needed. What I loved most was how clean the whole place was — no flies, no clutter, just a comfortable and welcoming environment. I’ll definitely be coming back!

A restaurant with the right East African ambiance. Food, music and conducive environment. Did I say East Africa, their coverage is international. They are located somewhere in North America.

Geoffrey warm welcome makes me walk back in after walking out...yaani ni in out, in out in out. Am here right now, Kuja nikununulie whatever you choose from the menu.

Food was delicious! And the service was really good, the lady (Rebecca) was friendly, polite! Place was clean! The lamb dish was excellent! Nice & tender. Went with my mom & daughter and we'll be returning soon & often lol

formatted_address: 14223 Tukwila International Blvd, Tukwila, WA 98168, United States
name: Juba Restaurant & Café

reviews.text:
This was my first experience with Ethiopian cuisine and it was very nice. We had the  Ethiopian injera with goat and a chicken dish. Both were very flavorful.

The staff was very welcoming and the atmosphere was chill

The Rice, Chicken and Goat family-size dish was very delicious and big enough.

The spice tea was great with milk even without sugar for me, and with little sugar for my niece.

The service was pretty good at the counter. They listened with patience as we tried to place the order when we didn't know what the dish was called. It's my go-to dish anytime I visit but I still didn't know what it's called at the time and still don't. 🫣

The service from when we first got our tea, to when we got our plate, and even when we asked for smaller plates, extra spice and lemons was also great.

Matter of fact, I've visited about 4 times before today since 2023 and, each time, the service and food were great.

Just tried this place on Tukwila Blvd and wow, I’m hooked! The Ethiopian food was incredible – seriously flavorful with huge portions. I got the rice, chicken & goat dish and it was easily enough for a family. The staff were so patient explaining everything, even though I had no clue what I was ordering! They were really attentive, bringing extra spice and lemons no problem. It was busy, but moved quickly. Parking was a little tricky, maybe go earlier. Definitely worth a visit – I’ll be back to try more dishes soon!

I don’t even know where to begin—this place is an absolute gem! From the moment I walked in, the aroma alone told me I was in for something special. Every bite of the food was bursting with flavor, cooked to perfection, and honestly? Finger-licking good!

The dishes were not only delicious but beautifully presented. You can tell the chefs put real heart into their cooking. It felt like a mix of comfort food and fine dining all in one. I caught myself licking my fingers more than once—yes, it was that good!

The service was just as amazing—warm, attentive, and welcoming. The staff made sure everything was perfect from start to finish.

Highly recommend this spot to anyone who loves flavorful, satisfying food that leaves you craving more. I’ll definitely be coming back!

Best food, clean food, clean restaurant, good seats and seating. Customer service is above par in the area. Televisions are placed perfectly along the wall. Not long wait from order to receiving food. One of the best restaurants in the tukwila and Seattle area. It is also pro brown and good health💪Go and spend your money with Juba Restaurant and cafe and experience a somali cafe experience.

formatted_address: 14200 Tukwila International Blvd Suite 141, Tukwila, WA 98168, United States
name: TASTE OF CONGO

reviews.text: I am a little disappointed. I’ve had fufu and egusi so many times so I’m not sure what happened here. Online you advertise what fufu and egusi is supposed to look like and the kind of egusi I’ve had in the past. However today I placed an order with grub hub and it was not what I expected at all. The taste was kind of bland, I can’t really put my finger on what it taste like but it was not the traditional egusi soup. It didn’t even have the yellow color that it normally has. The meat was tender so I will give you guys that. The price was cheaper than other places I’ve tried as well.  I’m not sure if the fufu was over cooked or uncooked. It was extremely sticky and hard to swallow. It just kept getting stuck in my throat no matter how small of a piece I ate. Personally I didn’t like it very much and will continue to go to Pass D Jollof in seattle.
My food was prepared fast and was still hot when it arrived. The beef stew over rice was awesome and the plantains were perfect.
We had the beef stew. It was excellent. The portions were large enough to fill your tummy. The blend of spices is wonderful. I recommend that you give them a try.

Been searching for Fufu in the Seattle area for the past year & finally discovered a place that has it! Tried it for the first time and it was slightly different from what I expected. We ordered the popular chicken palmnut soup, chicken mayo, beef samosa, and beignet.

Love love the seasoning of the stew & mayo chicken! There can be a little wait but I bet there's only one person or so in the back working. So we didn't mind! The food was delicious so I know I'll be back to try other dishes.

I also love this general shared space called Spice Bridge (part of FIN), which supports BIPOC & immigrants start their businesses. Excited to learn about the expansion of this space to accommodate more businesses in the future!

This is my and my cousin's favorite African restaurant. My favorites are the chicken mayo, beef stew and of course the hibiscus drink😋 besides the food being top notch the customer service is excellent. Always somewhere to park, always clean. We absolutely love The Taste of Congo. 💞🫶🏾

formatted_address: 2123 E Union St, Seattle, WA 98122, United States
name: Adey Abeba Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: Absolutely delicious!!! My friend and I have tried a few Ethiopian places, and this was some of the best we have ever had! We ordered the meat combo and veggie combo which was more than enough food for 3 people to share, and everything was so hot and flavorful. The restaurant was fairly empty when we went at 6:30PM, and our servers were wonderful and very nice. Definitely a hidden gem 👀

First time having Ethiopian food, and was delighted! Adey Abeba has a welcoming environment and delicious unique flavors. They’re extremely generous with the portions and you definitely won’t be left disappointed or hungry. They provide plenty of protein and plenty of bread to pair with it. Definitely consider giving this place a try!

Great spot. Great portions for a great price. I've had better flavored Ethiopian before which is why I'm only giving it a 4 because I'm hunting for a Ethiopian spot that is both a favorite in taste and price. We got the meat combination plate and added a lentil dish in addition since that was the only veggie dish not already included in the combo. I would have passed on that addition because it was so oily that my husband and friend had some stomach issues later that night that we assumed was attributed from the oils.

The food was really good — flavorful, generous portions, and great value for the price. The service was good, nothing exceptional but nothing to complain about either. Just a heads-up: if you get seated near the bathroom, you can hear everything since the walls are pretty thin 😅. But overall definitely worth going for the food alone.

Went here for dinner with friends! Really loved the food! We tried the veggie combo - the miser wot was yummy! 😋 My companions liked their chicken dish (I don’t remember its name though 😅)

It was quiet when we went on a Wednesday evening. I’d recommend the place for their yummy food!

formatted_address: 7919 Rainier Ave S, Seattle, WA 98118, United States
name: Qeerroo Restaurant

reviews.text: I picked up a delivery order from this QEERO Restaurant. The staff were professional and the place looked clean. Everything went smoothly.
Everything looks and smelled wonderful! I got a vegetable Fatira and a chicken and rice entree. Absolutely delicious!!
Costumers service is good, food it good recent for new dinning set and outside dining come we eat !!!!
Excellent food and friendly, quick service
I loved the Ethopian food. This young man was so helpful and friendly. The mother owns the place  and he's just 21. He was ready to make me feel at home being my first time in WA

formatted_address: 3219 Martin Luther King Jr Way S A, Seattle, WA 98144, United States
name: Cafe Ibex

reviews.text:
ONE OF THE BEST RESTAURANTS IN SEATTLE

Order the lamb meat combo and veggie combo for a party of 4 (just trust me). It will be about $13 each before tip and the most delicious mix of diverse flavors and ingredients you’ve had in a minute. Your party will eat like kings on a budget. Hearty servings too.

I’m shocked this place doesn’t have better business. Please bring your friends here. Trust this random stranger on the internet. Just maybe ask them to make it spicier because they might hold back on you lol.

Thank you Cafe Ibex for making some of the most flavorful vegetarian food in the city! And impeccably marinated meats as well.

They’re open late and sometimes start dancing too. They’re just a vibe for real!

Wife and I have tried Ethiopian food one other time, and it was great too, but the atmosphere here was incredible. They did everything possible to make this a legendary meal from every angle. The smells, the sights, the vibe and service,........and the food,........the best meal in months, period.

Roasted coffee in a frying pan right in front of us and were burning the most aromatic resin or incense, just fantastic all around,...6 stars if I could!!

Thanks for a great lunch Ibex Cafe!!

LOVED THIS PLACE!! First time at a Ethiopian restaurant and I can’t believe I’ve been missing this my entire life you get to eat with your fingers great bread amazing tasting food the spices were amazing the atmosphere was so warm and welcoming I got to witness my first Ethiopian wedding it was just an incredible experience I will be back I love it and I hope more people come and eat here.

Two of us shared one plate of the beef combo (last item on the beef page), and it was delicious! We both couldn't finish the whole thing and took leftovers home!
Excellent value for money, and it was delicious!!!

This wonderful gem of a restaurant will surprise you.  Upon entering you are greeted by rich, earthy incense and a bright, golden-colored interior.  It is far roomier than you would ever expect from the outside; in addition to the main dining room there was a much larger back area with a stage.   They were easily able to accommodate our party of eight.  The traditional food was delicious.  Six of us ate family style sharing the chicken, lamb and the beef combos on one large injera covered platter.  The flavors were all rich and savory and three combos were more than enough food for six people.  Our servers were friendly and attentive and when it came time to pay the bill, they easily split it multiple ways. Check out Cafe Ibex, you'll be glad you did!

formatted_address: 8115 Rainier Ave S, Seattle, WA 98118, United States
name: Sunset Cafe

reviews.text: We were at Kubota Garden and wanted to go out to dinner nearby, and my husband found this restaurant on Google. We are so happy to have stumbled upon it.  We shared the Veggie Combo and had a glass of honey wine each and both left full and satisfied. The spices and selection of the combo are divine, and so reasonably priced; I will be dreaming about the flavors for a while 😋. I highly recommend this mellow & slow-paced with friendly service establishment for delicious Ethiopian food.
The kitfo was tender and perfectly seasoned, the tibs were juicy and full of flavor, and the fresh ayib balanced everything beautifully. Delicious food and great quality.

Phenomenal Ethiopian and Eritrean food! The sunset combo was such a great size, especially for the price, and really came with an excellent variety of flavorful toppings- we especially loved the cabbage, beef tibs and super spongy injera, which we ordered extra of, but everything was devoured. Filled with locals and fun music videos playing to watch while you wait for your food. The staff were also so friendly! Next time would love to try their big Eritrean breakfast menu, and their jebena specialty coffee :) great place to stop on your way to or from seatac airport!

I will definitely be returning! I’ve found a new spot for tibs. I ordered lamb tibs to go. The staff were very friendly. The lamb was the most tender and flavorful I’ve ever had at any restaurant I’ve been to in the Seattle area. Also, the portion was the most I’ve ever had at ANY Ethiopian restaurant I’ve visited. Especially for takeout. Hands down! For once I feel like I got what I paid for.

Only one thing I’d suggest them to do, and that’s decorate the place so it looks more warm and “home-ier” like most Ethiopian restaurants I’ve been to. Other than that small thing, I have no complaints, and the tender & flavorful food, large portions, and warm & friendly service WAY OUTWEIGH that small detail! 100% RETURNING.
Great service and delicious Ethiopian food — definitely worth a visit!

formatted_address: 13820 Tukwila International Blvd, Tukwila, WA 98168, United States
name: Aaran

reviews.text: Great place to eat for Somalian food! It might look like hole in a wall but they serve some good food! I went there twice in our stay in Seattle. Very good customer service. I highly recommend the rice! They make rice from goat broth don’t use water to cook rice! Lamb shank was very good also! I think lamb shank could be more tender but for me it was fine! They have family room for guests who want privacy. Rice was the best menu item! Sambosa was pretty awesome too! Made out of ground beef. Overall very good experience.

Absolutely delicious food that made me feel amazing after eating. The green sauce was very spicy and blended well with my dish. aaand they gave me a banana... what an interesringly odd yet nice touch.

The price / portions were also spot on in my opinion. I ordered the chicken Kati. Thank goodness they actually had the bitter bread. The portions are on the larger side. I had enough for a second meal later in the day. Yes, it was so good I couldn't wait to eat the rest. Usually I save left overs for the next day.

Since I got this food to go, I'll keep my review rating to just rate the food. The parking is pretty bad with only about 8 parking spots, but at least they have do have dedicated parking. I showed up at 9 am and the parking lot only had one space left just for me. There was already several people inside eating. Even more came and went while I waited.

The interior needs a full make over in my opnion, but it's all fairly functional. Also their drinking water situation was confusing as they didn't even off me water with my meal. Maybe that was my fault. I originally asked for my food to go but mentioned that I was so hungry I was gonna eat some as soon as they handed it to me. So they decided to give it to me on a dine in plate.

Don't come for a fancy date night or even to impress anyone. Unless you explain the interior design situation ahead of time.... it's like eating at an old uncle or grandparents house.

Their service is fairly average, but the employees are a super chill vibe. A lot of customers had very lengthy conversations with the teller regardless if they were ordering, just hanging out, or already done eating.

Honestly I've been thinking about going back all week. Next time I'm in the area, stopping in for a plate will be a must.

The name of the place has changed  so is ownership. Used to be Salama.

Now it is Aaran. There is big improvement.

Acceptable quality Somali food, if this type of cusinie appeals to you

It is a Somali restaurant standards, including hygiene, and tradition, and there  is big difference between American standards of Hygiene, and Somali Standards of Hygiene

Good friendly owner.
Large portions
Reasonable prices.
Parking is still that little tiny parking

Thoroughly enjoyed my experience here. It was my first time eating Somali food and it was quite tasty and flavorful. Customer service was excellent. Yulis answered any questions and made great recommendations on what to try.
East Africa, internationally known and locally respected. Sambusa is the best but everything is really good can't go wrong.

formatted_address: 3621 33rd Ave S c9, Seattle, WA 98144, United States
name: Fana's Cuisine

reviews.text: I love the warm pancake, eggs and the staff’s welcome hospitality!! Great casual place to be.
The Owner is very nice and polite. I enjoy each time I go!

Open means open.
Not come on down, the door is locked!
B.S.
Warm atmosphere with good food where the community comes together!

Very sweet lady
She does right by you
Very friendly to all

formatted_address: 2715 E Cherry St B, Seattle, WA 98122, United States
name: Cafe Selam

reviews.text: We have tried multiple Ethiopian restaurants in Seattle and we have given up trying to find a better place. Amazing hole in the wall. For two people, order the veggie combo and the meat combo and have them put both on one plate to share. It's more than enough food. They are not afraid of flavor or spice here.

Cafe Selam, hidden tiny restaurant tucked along the street. Yummy food, great service but definitely needs working on the ambience.
The vegetarian combination injera with lentils, cabbage, spinach, spices was an absolute delicacy! (Shiro wat, mesir wat, alicha miser, salad and spinach)
The Lamb (Special Tibbs) served with salad and chilli paste wasn't so special. The stir fry was a bit dry.
The injera was soft, fluffy, spongy and went so well with the entire flare!

The interiors are a bit down unless you are seated out, where you can find grape vines! And breezy Seattle weather adds to the ambience. There's one restroom for the customers and a separate one for staff (both not so great in condition!) Portion size is massive - two dishes easily gobbled by 4.
Street parking available, you'll have to hunt for a spot. Can be found though within the neighborhood.
Very flavorful food. My first time eating Ethiopian food and I’ll definitely come back. Prices are reasonable too.

I had the Foul with an extra egg (breakfast dish). Really delicious, and more than I could finish. The bread was light and fluffy with a perfectly crunchy crust. So good! I look forward to coming back for lunch or dinner. As for its atmosphere, hey, it’s just a little small business and so one’s expectations should not be on the atmosphere. That said, I found it to be homey and inviting in its own way. Highly recommend.

I have been here twice and both times the food has been immaculate! Delicious 😋 My fav is the red lentils they are spicy! Order anything it's all delicious! Plus the staff is friendly and they play nice music 🎶

formatted_address: 14432 Military Rd S #1, Tukwila, WA 98168, United States
name: Astur Restaurant

reviews.text: Cozy lively restaurant serving generous hearty portions of the best lamb in Seattle. Owner is really friendly. I'll definitely be back here often.

I had an amazing experience at this Somali restaurant! The service was incredibly friendly and welcoming, making us feel right at home. The food was packed with flavor, with every dish offering a perfect balance of spices and freshness. The sambusas were, without a doubt, the best I've ever had—crispy on the outside and bursting with savory goodness on the inside. If you're looking for delicious food and a warm, inviting atmosphere, this place is a must-visit. I can’t wait to come back for more! Highly recommend!

I visited Astur at their grand opening with my husband. My husband ordered canjeero and chicken suqaar, and I ordered fuul with chapati. The food was delicious and quick! The owners are kind, welcoming and made we sure we go excellence service! There is a small section for people to eat privately which was a bonus. Try their Somali tea, it is the best I have ever had. We are very pleased with our meal and we are excited to come back!
Amazing restaurant! Food is flavorful, service is impecable, and the vibe is warm and welcoming. We ate til we are full with fuul and ordered more for take out! That good!😋🥰

Owner was friendly and pleasant to us and our there young kids.
Food was fresh, came out fast and tasted great. Even our 2 year old enjoyed cevapi (sausages without casing) and lepinja (bread).
Reasonably priced. Will be back.

formatted_address: 1212 E Jefferson St, Seattle, WA 98122, United States
name: Taste of the Caribbean

reviews.text: It's been years since I've had good, authentic Jamaican food and this place did not disappoint. The waitress was extremely personable and the staff were respectful. The portion sizes made me feel like I was eating my Nana's food again.

Price: 2 plates of food, one vita malt, one side of plantains= $62 Only people who really love Caribbean food or are natives will like this price considering slow service, tacky ambiance . all others will be let down from the price. But still worth it for the true lovers. True value of the meal: $48, actually charged $62 with 15% tip totaling $71. No alcoholic drinks were included in this total but still surpassed $50 somehow….

My family is from Antigua so finding good Caribbean food in Seattle is definitely a challenge! We arrived, no hostess so we had to wait a little bit to be sat (there were only people sitting at the bar, the restaurant was empty). We ordered curry goat, jerk chicken and plantains at around 7pm. They were out of carrot juice, and coco bread what a bummer! Food arrived pretty fast and the curry goat was fantastic, the jerk chicken was also good, one drumstick was dry but the other was moist, seasoning was good. Having that curry goat really brought me back so I really enjoyed that. I put 4 stars because the service was extremely slow, although the waitress was super nice it's seems they have some regulars they like to socialize with so we had to physically get up to ask for the check after waiting and trying to flag her down for almost 15 mins. Ambiance was ok, the lights are super bright and the decorations are messy featuring Asian country flags but not even Antiguan flag :( I still tipped the waitress despite poor service, but if I go again and it happens again the staff will not receive a tip.
