I put 4 stars because often Caribbeans are pretty bad at customer service so I wasn't surprised but this place deserves to climb up and the only way they can do that is to make sure they meet American customer service standards in an American country! I would recommend this place to anyone looking for good Caribbean food!!

Our server, Roger, was absolutely fantastic! He was not only kind and professional but also made us feel like we were lifelong friends. This was my sister’s and my very first trip to Seattle, and we can’t wait to return to this incredible place! The atmosphere was vibrant and laid-back, filled with colorful decor that instantly put us in a great mood. To top it all off, we enjoyed amazing music by a renowned reggae and dancehall artist. It was an unforgettable experience!

We really enjoyed the spot customer service is great. The food was even better everything fresh oxtails tender. The pasta was cooked to  perfection and not overcooked. The rum punch was delicious as well. I don't think you can't get any better Caribbean food unless you go to the Caribbean.

This is probably some of the best jerk chicken I’ve had!! The chicken fell right off the bone. And the rice and beans and salad all tasted really yummy.

I think this place is family owned so don’t expect the service to be crazy fast! Sometimes it’s nice to slow down and enjoy the experience. It felt very authentic.

formatted_address: 14822 Tukwila International Blvd, Tukwila, WA 98168, United States
name: Halwo Kismayo Restaurant & Cafe

reviews.text: This place is definitely worth the wait. The food doesn’t come out fast, but you can tell it’s because everything is being made with care. Once the dishes arrive, the flavors speak for themselves. fresh, well-seasoned, and absolutely delicious. You can really taste the effort in every bite. It’s not a spot for rushing in and out, but if you’re willing to be patient, the food makes it more than worth it. I’d gladly wait again..

I've had the pleasure of trying some amazing salmon and rice dishes, but this place takes the cake – aside from my mom's cooking, of course! The staff are super friendly and make you feel right at home. If you get the chance to try their food, don't hesitate – it's clear they pour their heart into every single dish.

The restaurant was remodeled nicely and the environment looks better and the service was not bad. However, the food was not as great🥲. I ordered Katikati with chicken and not only they added less chicken but also the food was salty. I hope they at least use less salt in the future. Date of service: 11/23/25 between 1-2PM. Thanks
Very bad service the food was so salty and not even enough food the goat meat-was just bones no meat the  chicken steak doesn’t even look like chicken steak will never ever go back there again
New place looks really nice.. the rice taste just like home and the Philly is really good. They also have tea, desserts and coffee. Highly recommend

formatted_address: 7821 Rainier Ave S, Seattle, WA 98118, United States
name: Blue Nile Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: Meats were good I thought the vegetable dishes were lacking. Amazing atmosphere I’d come back with my friends for drinks and snacks. Cool how the place is open til 2am

The food was super awesome being my first time eating Ethiopian cuisine the lady who served us was kind enough to take us through the menu and we settled for what we ordered.The food was excellent and service was good.Am definitely coming back again.My partner and I are happy we are definitely going to be return customers.

Blue Nile Ethiopian Restaurant is hands down one of the best dining experiences I’ve ever had. The flavors are authentic, rich, and unforgettable — every bite feels like a celebration of Ethiopian culture. The food is simply top-tier.

Open late, felt super authentic, and was absolutely fantastic. I got the veggie platter (to go) & had intended to save some for leftovers but it was so delicious none made it to the fridge. Really fun atmosphere and everybody inside (diners and staff) were so friendly. Would love to go again next time we’re in Seattle!

Didn’t really like the setting inside. There was grass on the floor and tables weren’t clean. The food was okayish. Service was good. But I wouldn’t visit this place again. There are better Ethiopian restaurants.

formatted_address: 1219 E Jefferson St, Seattle, WA 98122, United States
name: Zobel Ethiopian Cuisine

reviews.text:
only $23 for the massive plate!!! DELICIOUS!!
such a calm, beautifully decorated place, with diverse food. the meat is cooked so well. also try their meat with jerky in it (second picture) the texture is amazing
The food is amazing and there's so much variety in a plate! Filling, flavorful, and not expensive. We had a great time there and will be visiting again. Wonderful place :)

I'm normally never out this way, and the two restaurants besides this one we're closed at the time. So what the hell, let's try something new!! The people outside and inside looked like they were enjoying themselves. So you order at the front counter your food and drinks. Take your number they give you to a table of your preference and wait. The ambiance of this place is super cool. One part of the restaurant is like a bike shop, if I remember correctly. It didn't take long for my Kimchi Bloody Mary to show up. Yes it sounds weird but it was damn good!!!! As some may know I love a good BLT!! This is not your regular smegular BLT. Wow of wow was it fresh and delicious. I finished that plate like I was starving!! I wanted another bloody Mary but I was driving home, so no bueno!! And don't be lazy put your own dishes away! Oh well til next time. Oh yes the bathrooms are clean

I am giving this such a high review because the pasta was AMAZING!!!! But the other food was definitely cooked in a rush and not cooked over many hours. The injera was quite dry and thin. The atmosphere was awkward as it was completely empty. The service was kind, but the food took forever to come out which really pushed me to think that it was definitely made last minute and not spent cooking and stewing through the day. I will definitely be back for the pasta though. The price was okay but for the small amount of meat in the pasta it was a bit expensive, but so good that I will be back.
This restaurant give you the best value for your money. The $23 Zobel combo will feed 3 people a full meal. Be prepared to eat with your hands.

formatted_address: 202 W Gowe St, Kent, WA 98032, United States
name: Chop Chop West African Cuisine

reviews.text:
The food is really good! I would especially like to come back during a cold day in the winter to warm my soul with the food here. I definitely want to go back and try other dishes. I didn't take the most flattering photos (the photos are not the full serving either, just what I served myself. I'd say the portions are a decent and fair size), but don't let that dissuade you; The egusi soup with chicken and fufu, jollof rice with chicken were both very flavorful and delicious 🤤 Whomever gave a 1 star is either doing a disservice or didn't try the food!
Take out only at the time we got our food

I recently catered an event for my Making of Modern Africa class using Chop Chop West African Cuisine, and the entire experience was extraordinary from start to finish. We ordered peanut soup, a half pan of chicken, futu, and vegetarian jollof rice and everything exceeded my expectations.

The team went above and beyond in every possible way. Kingsley delivered directly to my campus, offered a discount on delivery, brought extra serving supplies, and even helped set everything up in my classroom. The care, professionalism, and generosity were remarkable.

And the food? Phenomenal. The moment students started eating the chicken, the whole room filled with delighted groans, students literally moaning because it was so good. Multiple students commented that it “fell off the bone” and that it was some of the best chicken they’d ever had. The peanut soup was like drinking my favorite sauce.  The fufu and jollof rice were also great deeply appreciated in a class centered on contemporary life in Africa.

This was one of the best catering experiences I’ve had. I cannot recommend Chop Chop West African Cuisine highly enough for the food, the service, and the heart they put into everything.
I’ve pre-ordered the Jollof pan and Peanut Butter soup pan. Oh my goodness! I wish the chef was right by me. I would have tipped him again. The food tastes so delicious!

I ordered chicken Egusi and the flavor was 9 out of 10 , the man there was nice , and I think it’s a takeout spot but you can eat there if you insist.. it was worth the price ..I’m excited to finally have fufu in Kent
Ordered the beef peanut soup it comes with fufu and the grilled chicken with jollof rice. I’m in love with the fufu and the beef soup so flavorful and delicious! I’m going back for more.

formatted_address: 2722 E Cherry St, Seattle, WA 98122, United States
name: Zagol Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text:
This was my first time trying Ethiopian food, and I am so glad I came to Zagol. My friend’s family member, who is from Eritrea, told me I would love it and they were right. The place was cozy, the server was kind and welcoming, and the food was absolutely delicious.

I do not remember the name of the dish, but it was full of flavor and beautifully presented. I loved learning to eat with my hands and sharing from the same plate. The injera bread was amazing, soft, and perfect for the experience.

Zagol made my first time unforgettable. I will definitely come back every time I visit Seattle.

Great weekend lunch and dinner spot. Pigged out with two of my friends and it came out to $17 a person. Won’t find a better bang for your buck in seattle! Also lovely hospitality and atmosphere. Community hub - Def a regular crowd that comes here often.

Zero star. This was one of the worst dining experiences I’ve ever had. First of all, we found a stone in our food — yes, an actual stone.  But it gets worse. The waiter completely ignored us the entire time — not a single check-in, no apology, nothing. We sat there for 45 minutes waiting for food that showed up cold, stale, and clearly not fresh. The staff couldn’t care less, and the whole interaction felt like we were an inconvenience to them. No warmth, no accountability, just pure indifference. Absolutely disgraceful. Never, ever go to this place.
Food here was delicious and great service! Highly recommend and if you like spicy let them know, they have great spicy add ins!

Extremely disappointing experience. The waiter barely acknowledged our table, no service, no water refills the entire time. After a 45-minute wait, we were served stale food. Worst part: I found a stone in my dish and nearly broke a tooth. Completely unacceptable. Will not be returning.

formatted_address: 2801 E Cherry St, Seattle, WA 98122, United States
name: Ras Dashen Ethiopian Restaurant & Bar

reviews.text: Great place for a delicious dinner!  Ras Dashen Ethiopian Restaurant is a great place for a group discussion while eating dinner! I usually go there with my friends after an event and the food is always great! The hospitality and the space is A+. Sometimes, I also go there just eat great food in a quiet space.

We ordered the qanta firfir and asa dulet, and both were outstanding! This family-owned restaurant serves some of the freshest and lightest Ethiopian food I’ve had. The flavors are authentic, delicious, and not heavy at all.
Highly recommend Ra Dash to anyone in Seattle looking for amazing Ethiopian cuisine!
Delicious spiced tea, a prodigious veggie combo platter, and natural lighting with jazzy tunes to boot. Love the gluten free teff options

We had a wonderful dining experience at Ras Dashen Ethiopian Restaurant. From the moment I arrived, everything exceeded my expectations. The food was absolutely delicious  rich in flavor, beautifully presented, and full of authentic Ethiopian taste. Each dish was clearly prepared with care and attention to detail.
The service was excellent. The staff were warm, welcoming, and attentive, making sure everything was perfect throughout the meal. Their friendliness and knowledge of the menu made the experience even more enjoyable.
The atmosphere was vibrant and full of energy, reflecting the warmth of Ethiopian culture. To make the evening even more special, the owner personally came by to greet us incredibly friendly and engaging, even joining in to dance with us, which made the experience unforgettable.
Overall, Ras Dashen Ethiopian Restaurant offers an outstanding combination of delicious food, excellent service, and a joyful atmosphere. I highly recommend it and can’t wait to visit again soon!

Their food is just average, yet the prices are high. It feels like they only cook their best dishes for regular customers—if you’re not a frequent visitor, the quality is noticeably worse than what people show online or talk about. We were even told the owner and main chef weren’t there, so the waiter ended up cooking our food, and she admitted she didn’t really have the skill for it. Overall, I wouldn’t recommend this place to anyone.

formatted_address: 1740 1st Ave S, Seattle, WA 98134, United States
name: Africuisine

reviews.text: I ordered from this lady, it's out of her home. Orders are to pick up & to go only,  The eguisi & fufu were good! And it was my first time trying this. It was kinda spicy like I love. I only wish I knew what types of meat/ fish was in the soup (maybe post it in the description for future orders) all least for comfort and peace of mind of what we're eating in that soup because it looked like miltiple meats. Also the fufu was semi warm since it had to microwaved; as it was in the fridge when i picked up, she kindly warmed it up before giving it to me. I think I paid $22 for 6 in width/2 in deep bowl and two fufu balls that were decent size. (I would preferably pay like $17 in my opinion, since there is no seating, and the fufu wasn't hot all the way through or fresh off the stove- Nothing wrong with it cool in the fridge prepared but warmed through would be bomb for the meal experience) This was during a non summertime season last year, so im looking forward to when this summer hits, because maybe she may have her garage open with her signs out and food ordering table outside....instead of her signs & table inside the garage. I personally didn't mind this, plus the home was nice and pretty on the outside. And when she went inside, it looked neat inside too from the glance. Good first experience. Good job AFRICUISINE! ❤ I would try this again for sure,  9/10

Amazing , delicious  food!
Extremely sweet and kind family.  This is my second time ordering her food. Ive never ordered food this way.  I wasn't sure at first. But it is legit! And really good💯❤️ 10/10😁🥰

Amazing food! Can’t stop raving about the leaf moi moi! It’s Delicious 😋 If I may say so myself, coming from someone who is a food snub and a good cook.

In fact my out of state family members always look forward to eating her moi moi whenever they are in town. I will definitely recommend patronizing this business including raw African foods. Very happy customer for life!

Why would you create a website saying it’s a restaurant when you only cook from home ?
She took like 40 mins before she could come out to give me the food and she act as if every one is a con ..
Never again !

They hide bad comments about them but bout to report them to Google. Don't trust this business.

UPDATE: owner responded on another review saying I'm lying. The messages are all here love. Your office hours states you would have been closed for 2 hrs if I came at 7pm. Again sketchy.

formatted_address: 2334 2nd Ave, Seattle, WA 98121, United States
name: Marrakesh | Moroccan Restaurant

reviews.text: Officially our favorite place to dine at in Seattle. Step into Belltown's hidden gem and experience nothing like it. The service is incredible, the staff treat you with kindness. Our favorite was the spicy lamb and lamb shank. Lamb fell off the bone and the appetizers were a pleasant treat. 10/10.

Extremely Disappointing, Not Worth the Hype.
Recently dined here and opted to order from the à la carte menu rather than their overhyped five-course option - a decision that seemed to instantly affect the level of service we received.
To start, the lamb shish kebab order was completely botched. we were initially served chicken instead of lamb. After pointing out the mistake, what eventually arrived was a burnt, dry, and inedible excuse for a kebab. Calling it a "lamb kebab" would be a stretch by any standard.
The roasted lamb shank was no better. It was completely bland and lacking in seasoning.
Service was noticeably cold once it was clear we weren't indulging in the five-course option.

To add to the discomfort, the tables are placed far too close together, so cramped that you end up unintentionally eavesdropping or bumping elbows with the next table.
Overall, this was a subpar experience from start to finish with poor food, poor service, and poor ambiance. We won’t be returning, and I certainly wouldn’t recommend it to anyone looking for a quality dining experience.

The place looks nice but the food was so bad. First salad and soup came no salt in the soup. Ordered the grilled platter and it was so bad looked like they microwaved the meat so cold chewy and not tasty at all. Rice was so little just at the base of the plate. When I told the waiter that I couldn’t eat it he said he would never recommend that. He said it as though he knew how bad the food was. Did offer to get something else but even my friends food that I tried was horrible. Never coming back.

It was a delightful dining experience so please bring your loved ones, friends and everyone you know. The vibes, immaculate. The food, a feast that will leave you with a full belly, enough to bring home. Aziz served with such flare and warmth that will make you feel at home. We plan on returning with a bigger group for the whole lamb next and hopefully see the belly dancer perform.

How anyone ranks this place below 5 stars is beyond me. The owner welcomed us in like we were old friends despite it being our first time there. The vibe is unmatched. Between the curtains and the cushions, it’s like you stepped through a magical door into Morocco. Every meal comes with 5 phenomenal courses: soup, salad and bread, an appetizer, the main course, and dessert. He even brought us baklava at the end, so maybe 6 courses? The mint tea is phenomenal. This is the kind of meal I’ll remember for the rest of my life.

formatted_address: 2605 E Cherry St, Seattle, WA 98122, United States
name: Meskel Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: I had always wanted to try Ethiopian cuisine and this place leaves me wanting more. The owner was very excited to inform us on what to get and how it’s usually eaten. We both ate the veggie combo family style and shared a bottle of honey wine. Plenty of food with varying depths of flavor. The place also felt very laid back and homey. It was money and time well spent.

While walking around, I noticed the "Open" sign, and as soon as I stepped into the restaurant, I knew the food would be delicious. The ingredients tasted incredibly fresh and of high quality, and most importantly, the flavors were so tasty, even though they were new to me. The owner took the time to explain how to eat the injera, making me feel very welcome. She also shared the history of the restaurant with me. This was my first time trying Ethiopian cuisine, and I loved it! I visited alone, but I plan to invite some friends because the restaurant's vibe is cozy and warm, and sharing food with loved ones makes it even more tasty.
Great experience.  Food was tasty, owner spent alot of time talking about the dishes and even brought certain spices out for us to taste (we cook Ethiopian at home alot).

This place is absolutely incredible. It's a small joint but packed with big love and big flavor. The owner is a jack of all trades -- the chef, cleaner, waitress, hostess and more. You would truly never know it's a one woman show the way she gracefully and calmly carries herself around the joint. When we were there, no table went without water, wine, or food. She handles everything with such poise and peace. On top of that, the food is absolutely delicious. Packed with deep flavor and rich in culture. Would highly recommend this restaurant to anyone going through Seattle. Please take a trip to see her, even if it's out of the way. You won't be disappointed.

Overall, I love this place.  The food is delicious and the owner is lovely.  I appreciate how simple and straightforward the menu is.  The veggie platter is beautiful and each featured dish has unique flavors. It's hard to pick a favorite because they are all so good.  I'm looking forward to the warmer months when I can get the coffee ceremony.  ❤

formatted_address: 7729 Rainier Ave S, Seattle, WA 98118, United States
name: Yusra & Sabah Restaurant

reviews.text: Yusra & Sabah Restaurant is a must-try for incredible East African flavors! The goat meat with spiced rice (bariis) and tender suqaar are perfectly seasoned and melt-in-your-mouth delicious, paired with fluffy sabaayad flatbread and that fiery green sauce. Don’t miss the aromatic spiced tea (shah)—it’s the perfect finish. Everything halal, fresh, generous portions, and super welcoming vibe. Best Somali spot around; already planning my next visit!

The food was very delicious but the cleanliness of the place was below par. I really want to go back but I even got dirty cups for tea…that had uncooked rice on the outside. The smell of the floor was … and flies. As Muslims, it is half our imaan to be clean and keep things clean. Also, they people working there, not consistent with costumer service. It’s like hailing a cab in New York. You gotta work to get attention to order. I wish they wrote down our orders…

The breakfast taste pretty good. Nice pancake. Makes you want to eat more. The side dish is pretty nice. Lamb with bomb also pretty nice. Fried chicken taste pretty interesting as well. Not bad for one that isn't freshed fried. Enjoyed the meal in this small restaurant. Have to come back for some other dishes.

You can't order online. The website doesn't work.
Calling in doesn't work.
The restaurant is sorta dingy.

But damn the food is 🔥! An aunty came out and took my order, went back into the kitchen and promptly forgot. She came back out and confirmed my order. Then threw down in the kitchen. The food was legit amazing!

You know the dingiest place have the best food. Run to this spot. We had the whole fish, and the goat and rice was the best for me.

I fed four people comfortably for under $70. You can't beat that!

Visiting Seattle from Vancouver (April 2024), googled for a halal restaurant and this showed up, most likely due to FAKE reviews and ratings.
It's a horrible rundown restaurant that is Very Very Dirty! 🥴🥴🦠🦠Ceilings, Floors, Tables!!!
If the Hygiene is so bad, what to expect of food?
Washroom was a Biohazard. ☣️
It's surprising these people are operating a restaurant in Seattle, Washington. I've seen better Service and Standards travelling in 3rd world countries.
Also, it's in a rundown neighborhood, So I would caution for personal safety.!!

formatted_address: 2200 S Jackson St, Seattle, WA 98144, United States
name: Vision Ethiopian Cuisine

reviews.text:
I usually go for veggie combos so apologies, can’t speak much to the meat dishes. By no means is this a fancy place, but it has everything you’d need! If you like places that feel homey, this hits those vibes on the head. The server/host was friendly and quick, and she advised we go for the Shiro Wot.

The Shiro Wot is soooo good. I haven’t had this dish before in typical Ethiopian veggie combos so we ordered this on the side and it was the highlight!

Portions were generous, food was quick to be prepared, and I will certainly be back.

I used to come here on a regular basis when I lived in Seattle, before the name change when it was called Chef Cafe. I still dream of their gomen— it’s perfectly garlicky and so flavorful. It was a family owned business and the main chef, whose name I don’t recall, used to be a private chef for imperials in Ethiopia. This family was always welcoming, kind, and warm. I pray this restaurant is still under the same ownership using the same recipes!

First of all, the food was AMAZING. It had just the right flavors and it tasted so hand-made which I love. For the price, we were fed SO much. They kept refilling our anjeer bread and we had plenty of leftovers left. The service was super nice. I loved this place. Lots of vegetarian options too. 10/10 recommend.

I had a strong appetite for Eastern African cuisine and searched somewhere in the Seattle area with good ratings. My husband and I got lucky that the day we checked out this restaurant, they were celebrating a family activity. It was very endearing how they welcomed and serviced us, even bringing us cake from their celebration.

It felt aesthetically unassuming and their customer service was very attentive and sweet. We appreciated their help when going over the menu and selecting the right options. We went with a softer textured meat (can’t remember the name of the plate) and the Veggie Combo.

My husband cannot eat very spicy food, so finding less spicy food options can be a bit tricky. For example, please note that the salad comes with jalapeños. This would have been good to know in advance since we did not expect that.

They have a section with a pool table. Again, quite modest in aesthetic but it looks like it is a family-friendly option where they put on their own celebratory events.

Very worth a try.

This food was spectacular. They have a wide range of options, the seasoning was balanced and worked together. Their dishes were interesting and very well priced. We ordered the vegetable combo and the green chicken. They all tasted amazing together and large portion.

The service was also good, and the chef even came by to ask if we were enjoying the food. The restaurant was clean with plenty of room to sit. I would highly recommend eating here.

formatted_address: 5710 Rainier Ave S, Seattle, WA 98118, United States
name: Habesha Cafe

reviews.text: Delicious Eritrean food, clean space, and great service. The owner talked with us and was so warm and accommodating to our requests. Beautiful, smart and unique presentation of the food, and with a diverse menu compared to similar other restaurants. I really enjoyed the cozy atmosphere and I could see myself back here for work meetings. Top notch restaurant experience and happy to support this small business.

Went to Habesha Cafe for the first time. I discovered this place because it is very close to my neighborhood and my sister suggested it to me. Ordered their Spicy Beef Tibs Sandwich and Beef Sambusas. The others ordered these amazing dishes as well and they told me that it was delicious too! Very delicious and super fresh tasting! The atmosphere was very pleasant and cozy! Also, outstanding customer service!!! Highly recommended!!! Love love love it 😍!!!

This is our second time going to this restaurant. We don’t live in the area but made sure to visit it on our recent visit to the Seattle area.
The owners are incredibly helpful and friendly.
We once again got the combo vegan platter, which was more than enough to share for two people
Two of the items were a little hotter than we liked. The owner says next time be sure and let them know and they can substitute them out for less hot items. 😁
I highly recommend this casual restaurant if you’re looking for excellent Ethiopian food, an excellent price, and excellent service.

Went here for a Valentines Day meal with my partner and it was SO GOOD! The food was delicious and I loved how vegan friendly the menu was (there are plenty of non vegan options as well). We didn’t get to try any but the pastries looked amazing. The gentleman working (I assume he’s the owner) was so friendly and kind. I had a mocha coffee as well that was perfect and I can’t wait to go back to try the coffee service. 10/10!

Haven't had Ethiopian cuisine before and am very glad we chose Habesha. The atmosphere was really relaxing and the grocery and coffee pot section had some really interesting items. The gentleman who took our order was very nice and the food was excellent. We got the meat and veggie combo platter to share and it was a nice variety and more than enough for two. We also got chocolate walnut baklava and pistachio baklava to take home. Definitely a place to try again.

formatted_address: 1801 S Jackson St, Seattle, WA 98144, United States
name: Shewa-Ber®

reviews.text: This restaurant has such a nice vibe, AMAZING music that tunes out everything except the experience. The owner and staff are welcoming. I’ve never had ANY ounce of a bad experience here! GREAT Ethiopian Food! The BEST atmosphere out of any place!!

I ate there early May of 2023 with a group of 6 people (...very late posting, but this is how I roll). Since most of us were new to Ethiopian food, the server did a great job warning one person in my party he was ordering raw meat!

I got the veggie combo to share between two people and the portions were very good! Definitely enough for both of us as vegans. Thank you for being extremely generous with the injeera! The flavors of all the dishes are also very good.

The weather was great, and we ate out on the porch in front. The restaurant is located on a fairly quiet street.

Exploring Seattle with dining. One of great Ethiopian restaurants I have experienced. Mike (the owner) is very nice and welcoming. The food menu and the restaurant  atmosphere are appetizing. I have great experience ordering Shewa Combo!

As another African and lover of Ethiopian food, I wanted to love this place. Unfortunately it wasn’t really good. Service was okay but the food was a 4/10 , prices where high and portions were small.

I am new here, but last week I tried Adey Abeba and it was superb, great portions , great flavors etc so I would recommend them instead.

Shewa-Ber Bar and Restaurant just recently opened in the central district area, south side of the street between 17th and Jackson.
A group of us decided to venture out and want to try something new so we decided to check out Shewa-Ber. We are all WOW at how amazing the food and beer here. The food is full of flavors and deliciously cooked. The lamb and beef dishes were our most favorite. The Injera at this place is absolutely the best I ever had.
On top of good food, their customer service is above and beyond outstanding. Very friendly and attentive!
If food is not your thing then grab a drink at their bar. They have a nice full bar with a seating area. It funs looking at the bar, it is well organized, fun colors lights glowing and it provided a very nice vibe.
I also really like how cozy and clean the restaurant was.
The prices are reasonable. The only thing I can suggest for improvement is each portion can be a little more generous.
Highly recommended this restaurant to anyone who is looking for good Ethiopian food!

formatted_address: 5701 Rainier Ave S, Seattle, WA 98118, United States
name: Delish Ethiopian Cuisine

reviews.text: Generous portions and great flavors! We got the Delish Combo because we wanted to have both meat and veg dishes. The injera had a lovely tangy flavor and soaked up all the flavors of the stews and dishes in the combo. Every dish was packed with flavor and complemented each other nicely. My favorites were the shiro, kitfo, and gomen. I definitely recommend getting one of the combos because you get to try a bit of everything! Can’t wait to come back!

This is one of the best Ethiopian restaurants in Seattle. The customer service is truly outstanding—warm, welcoming, and consistently attentive. The waiters pays close attention to every detail and is always helpful, making sure guests feel comfortable and well taken care of throughout their visit.

The owners, Delish and Amy, are incredibly kind and friendly, and their passion for hospitality and quality food clearly shows. Amy, who is also the chef, prepares delicious, authentic dishes that make every visit memorable.

I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for excellent Ethiopian food, exceptional service, and a genuinely welcoming atmosphere.

My friends reserved Delish for my birthday lunch and I had a genuinely great experience here. The food was great, very homely and  tasted amazing. However, its the service and ambience that I loved most and everything seemed just authentic! We also tried their coffee experience which is great if you have a group of 5 or more. My friends are mostly vegetarian and they were so relieved with the options here!

Ps- Delish - the owner's husband is a cheerboy for his wife and they both clearly love doing what they do. Probably irrelevant but the chef and the waitress were so pretty🙈❤️

This restaurant left a great impression on me. The fish soup was incredibly fresh and flavorful, rich with umami in every sip. The combo portion was generous and very satisfying. The bread was soft, with a slightly sour taste that gave it a unique and layered flavor. The restaurant had a warm and cozy atmosphere, and the staff were very friendly, making us feel relaxed and welcome. There were Ethiopian words and scripts printed on the table, and while waiting for our food, we took some time to study them — they looked complex and unfamiliar but also really fascinating, adding a nice touch of exotic charm.

Extremely friendly staff, cute place, and delicious food. We loved the veggie platter and beef tibs. The Turkish coffee ceremony was also cool and tasty. The seating is cozy and comfy but it was a bit cold at our table by the door. Will definitely come back!

formatted_address: 11546-11552, 11546 15th Ave NE, Seattle, WA 98125, United States
name: Enat Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: We shared the Enat combination and it was plenty for 2 people before a show. I am grateful they offer a gluten free version of injera (teff only). The coffee was sublime. Food was flavorful and excellent. It has a cool hole in the wall vibe that felt homey. Our server was lovely and had the perfect balance of checking in and leaving us alone. We'll definitely be back.

Enat serves a huge portion of food for a great price and are generous with the injera. Even the gluten free injera! They served 3 pieces with a combo (not including the one on the plate, 4 total) and it was $24! This place is arguably one of the best food values in Seattle. You can easily feed 3 people on a single combo.
The combo quality was okay, the meat was kind of tough and dry but well flavored. There are two portions of cabbage+potato, a spinach and a romaine salad. Had a side of shiro wot was good.
They serve gluten free injera on request! It seemed fresh and was good. It’s the best Ethiopian restaurant for getting gluten free. There was no up-charge for us but not sure if that was the norm.

The service was quick and friendly. They take Apple Pay.

Very affordable and delicious family restaurant despite Derrick G.’s hyperbolic, xenophobic review below. I’ve been coming here for years and the ingredients are always fresh including the side salads, which is a smaller and understated component that people overlook when it comes to quality and freshness. If you come here looking for a yummy meal, you will quickly see the care that goes into their food and that nothing is rotting. The vegetarian combo is great for veggie lovers (omg the red lentils and potatoes!!) The aunties here are always very kind, they treat you like family here.

They used to be the best in 5/6 years ago, but now on They just providing garbage supposed to food. For example shiro made from weeks , raw meat / kurt/ sees personal face , their injera never being easy for digestive system ...supposed to be reviewed by health department or business to be closed. I suggested customers to go other restaurants near there.

I’ve been coming to Enat since I was a kid - nearly 25 years now and it truly feels like home. Hands down, this is one of the best Ethiopian restaurant in Seattle. The flavors are vibrant, comforting, and consistently incredible, and not to mention generous portion sizes. The staff is incredibly kind and welcoming, which makes every visit even more special.

formatted_address: 7425 Hardeson Rd unit b, Everett, WA 98203, United States
name: Ubuntu Meat Bar & Safari Spice Grill

reviews.text: Where do I start? This was my first time visiting, and I was thoroughly impressed — from the service to the food! Shan was incredibly friendly and pleasant to talk to, and I felt welcomed the moment I walked in, which means a lot. The interior is beautiful, the food is delicious, and the service is excellent. I think I’ve found my new favorite place to eat in Everett. I highly recommend checking them out!

Everyone should come here to try their food. It was the best meal I’ve had in a long time. We had no idea what to eat initially other than we wanted to try the fufu  but Shan was super helpful in helping us decide. She was super friendly and attentive, and elevated our experience even more. All the dishes she suggested,  we ordered and they were all absolutely exceptional. Meat fell right off the bone, the spices were mouthwatering, and overall great comfort food. We definitely will be going back to try more! Highly highly recommend.

The food was delicious and the service was excellent. Patrick was super helpful and kind in teaching us about the different dishes and sides. We ordered the lamp chops, goat stew, and tilapia. Such a great experience and the prices for the amount of food you got was amazing.

My wife and I had an amazing experience at Ubuntu in Everett. From start to finish everything was fantastic.

Shanetta was our server, bartender, and also the cook, which honestly blew us away. Even while handling everything on her own, she was attentive, friendly, and made sure everyone in the restaurant was taken care of. She did an incredible job and deserves a ton of credit for how smoothly she ran things.

I ordered the pichana steak and my wife had the rack of lamb. Both dishes were outstanding. The blend of seasonings and spices was unique, bold, and incredibly flavorful. Every bite was top notch. We also tried the African greens, Jamaican rice and peas, samosa, and the Parotta Madurai. Everything was absolutely delicious and cooked with care.

I highly recommend checking this place out if you want something different and full of flavor. If it is normal for them to have one person handling the kitchen, hosting, serving, and bartending, I would just suggest being patient. The food and service are worth it. Hopefully they staff up in the future because this place has so much potential.

We will definitely be back.

Absolutely loved our experience at Ubuntu Grill in Everett! The food was amazing - fresh, flavourful, and deeply authentic. The chef is Malawian, and you can truly taste the heart and tradition in every bite. We had the samosas, Nsiima, goat stew, and chicken wings. Each dish was spot-on and brilliantly done. The goat stew was rich and tender, the wings perfectly seasoned, and the Nsiima took us straight to Southern Africa. We’re already planning to go back often. Highly recommend!

formatted_address: 2800 E Cherry St a, Seattle, WA 98122, United States
name: Agelgil Ethiopian Restaurant Seattle

reviews.text:
Really good food. Not super familiar with Ethopian food. But seemed quite authentic based on clientele. The Injera was soft and soaked up the sauces really well with a good tangy flavor.
The chicken stew was very rich and flavorful. We had 4 of us and did the 2 person meat/veggie combo and added the chicken stew. We had leftovers but we're really happy sampling all the dishes. Loved the collard greens and chicken and each lentil dish tasted unique. (Some restaurants you feel like you get the same flavors with different proteins, but not here). Definitely would recommend to others. Friendly service.

Had dinner here on December 12. First time having Ethiopian food. Tremendous. Had the vegetarian combo and the meat combo. The teff injera bread was go good and so different from anything any of the four of us has ever had. Boxed up what we couldn't finish and mixed with eggs for breakfast the following morning. Still just tremendous.  When back in Seattle in February will be back here again!  Highly recommend!

Just had dinner at Filmon’s – seriously packed, had to wait 20 minutes even with a reservation. The portions were huge for the price, which was great. My veggie combo was a little intense with the spices, but the injera was fantastic, super tangy. The staff were really friendly and welcoming, felt like a proper neighborhood place. Would have liked the injera to be a bit warmer though.
Our favorite eithopian place in Seattle. I love that the meat can come spicy. Great portions and just amazing. I can't wait to try more things.

I recently visited the place at 2800 E Cherry St in Seattle and found a cozy, traditional ambiance with a simple decor that was welcoming. The place was quite busy during dinner, so there was some waiting to be seated, but it wasn't overly crowded. Staff were friendly and attentive. The portions were generous—especially those greens in the meat combo—which made for great value considering the price. However, I noticed the injera could have been a bit warmer. Overall, a nice spot with authentic Ethiopian cuisine, though maybe bringing your own blanket would help keep your food warm!

formatted_address: 1314 Denny Wy #103, Seattle, WA 98109, United States
name: Zema Bar & Restaurant

reviews.text: Really? Was craving some good Ethiopian food after handling my business for the day. Googled up places in the area, and this one had the most stars. So I guess I'd try it out when I got there. There was no parking available because the place sits off in a parking lot. Adjacent to a car lot and it's very tight to get in there. So I spent 15 minutes just to find parking. The place is clean. The atmosphere is clean. The host was attentive. I ordered my food and when it came. I was underwhelmed because I was expecting more of a traditional Ethiopian style. Food, but it seems like the food is more catered to people that are not familiar with the cuisine and it seems more americanized than the actual culture of the food. The plate I ordered was twenty five dollars altogether with tax and I ordered a light beer to go with it just not enough sides and the food was grilled as if to have ordered instead of stewed. I'm not gonna lie.I was very disappointed and it did not satisfy me.So I ended up going to tats  sub Sandwiches.

I’ve tried three different Ethiopian restaurants in Washington, and hands down Zema Bar and Restaurant is NUMBER ONE!

The location is right in the heart of Seattle. Parking can be a little tricky depending on the time, but I was lucky enough to find a spot at the restaurant itself and it’s worth the effort regardless.

The space is beautiful, clean, and you can tell the owners take real pride in creating an inviting atmosphere not just for guests, but also for their staff. That energy really shows.

Now the food …. WOW. Every single dish was packed with flavor, and the honey wine was absolutely delicious. Honestly, everything I tried was amazing.

On top of that, the customer service was top tier. Friendly, attentive, and genuinely welcoming.

If you’ve been wanting to try Ethiopian food, this is the place to do it. You will NOT be disappointed. I’ll definitely be back, this spot is a 10/10!

The food is impressive!! I have been to billions of restaurant of the world but this is the first time I can say I am in love with the food. The lamp is seasoned so well but not too strong. You can taste the real spice and herb not powder. I usually do not like pasta. Their pasta is heavenly. The tomato sauce is infused with spices. Vegetable platter has 7 different of beans and vegetables. Each one has it own flavor. Injera bread taste like a gelly bread. When combining with any good here, it just take the taste to another level.

Rarely you come across a restaurant who’s food takes you back to the country of origin. Zema blew away all expectations with each bite being perfectly balanced. While I do prefer more spice, I understand the people of Seattle are a bit more timid of heat.

10/10 one of the best tasting Ethiopians restaurants I have encountered in the USA

Had a great lunch here! The service was friendly and attentive, and the atmosphere was quiet and comfortable. The menu had a nice selection of entrees, which made it easy for someone new to this cuisine to find something to enjoy.

formatted_address: 1212 S Jackson St C, Seattle, WA 98144, United States
name: Africanita Market

reviews.text: Africanita! The best of the best in Seattle. I was very happy to shop at the store. And I appreciate the welcome from the staff.
Good place to be friendly and very kind they speak so many languages I love it I would like to go again
This was my first experience and Horrible customer service. No welcome at all the lady was on the phone all the time. Ask a question where products are just point and look you up and down.
Very friendly customer service!!
Unique selection and friendly 😁

formatted_address: 14857 Tukwila International Blvd, Tukwila, WA 98168, United States
name: Dubai Cafeteria & Espresso

reviews.text: Amazing food! We were starving after our flight and saw this location was near the airport. They did their best in helping us order and the portions were very large. The prices are very fair and the chapti was so delicious. We sat outside and they were very attentive about cleaning the tables so we could enjoy our meal! A must have!

My husband has always brought home (back in California) the Goat Pilau and it is yummy 😋.
He brought the Chapati once but they tasted like they had sugar added, so I told him that was a no for me.
This time around, I was the one who happened to visit this place and as my hubby had told me it is small and constantly crowded, sure enough it was. The service was quick and just got the plain pilau this time and still it was yummy 😋
My family knows anyone coming to California just bring Pilau from Dubai Cafe.

This place is solid vibes, and serves amazing fresh goat meat. I thoroughly enjoyed the goat with cahpti platter, which included chapti, kidney beans, and spinach, but wish there was a bit more meat included.

The Katkat platter with chicken was decent - chopped up cahpti in a semi-sweet yellow curry with onions, carrots, etc. Again, would have appreciated a bit more protein and less carbs in this dish.

Outdoor seating, good when the weather permits, but otherwise I'd recommend for takeout moving forward for sure.

The restaurant is using food coloring that has been linked to cancer risks. They are adding large amounts to enhance the appearance of their food, which raises serious health and safety concerns. I told them a couple times but they don’t care.
Quick ordering and got my food fast, $13.21 for a delicious, spicy meal. I ordered beef + chapati 🫓

formatted_address: 215 SW 152nd St, Burien, WA 98166, United States
name: Dukem Restaurant and Market

reviews.text: A limited menu means they do what they do very well and if you're looking for Ethiopian, this is a great spot. Early evenings, they've always had a table available. It often feels like we've dropped into someone’s kitchen, staffed by family. The dishes come out with an unmistakable made-with-knowing touch of authenticity. I almost hate to put up a review, it's such a local-to-Burien gem!

The food is a hard five stars. Really, really tasty stuff here, prepared with heart. And get the coffee, it doesn't get any better than this!

Service was polite and friendly and understood our purpose of experiencing Ethiopian cuisine to make food recommendations for different flavors. All smiles.

It's a few tables in a market, not at all fancy.

So glad to be here, and really... Get. The. Coffee.

Best bang for buck. Almost impossible to find an inexpensive place to eat in Seattle!
Enough food to feed 4 hungry people. We ordered the veggie combo $19 and the lamb $24. The food was delicious 🤤. In the veggie combo there wasn’t  my favorites dish, atakilt wat, the cabbage carrot dish but the other sides made up for it! The lamb was juicy and plentiful.

Unfortunately out of sambusa :(

We went at 5 pm on our way back home from a road trip and stopped here. Food took long, I’m thinking because we were there to eat at an odd time. Worth the wait.

Service is smiling and friendly. You could browse the store in the meantime. Saw some good olive oil from Palestine that caught my eye.

It’s a homey restaurant. Music was a little loud with a bass that you can ask to turn down. One restroom that wasn’t exactly clean and could do with a quick clean.

I love this place, I come here for lunch takeout and their sambusas!  The food is great and you get a lot and I love the sambusas, they have beans and ginger and spices inside and are cheap and filling.  What I love too is how friendly they are, every time I go in there no matter who is at the counter they are so nice and friendly!!  One time I was squeezed for time and he promised to get my order quicker and they did.  Great people, great food!

Ordered the meat and veggie plate the food was really good. It was my first time eating Ethiopian food. But the service was not great. It took my order very very long to get to me and it seem like staff was a bit disorganized. Price was fair and portions where large.

formatted_address: 1400 34th Ave, Seattle, WA 98122, United States
name: Cafe Soleil

reviews.text: I think this is a good neighborhood gem! Went for brunch and the place was cute had lots of natural light and plenty people but no wait on Mother’s Day. Food wise I didn’t think it was anything special or wowed me but again if you’re looking for something more simple and light then this would be a good place. Pricing matches portions I would say! Their orange slices were so good (I know it was more of a garnish). I got the spicy shrimp croissant which was tasty but had like three shrimps in it, so it was mostly bread.

Kuri and her staff are amazing! This is my favorite spot in this neighborhood. Service and atmosphere are welcoming and pleasant. The food is amazing-- both brunch and dinner menus offer great flavors. Highly recommend the Yellow Split Pea Alit'cha W'et  and the Eggplant Tomato Alit'cha W'et.
What a treat! Such a great little find for great breakfast/brunch. Beautiful setting as well with the amazing food.

Popular neighborhood restaurant with friendly and attentive service. Stopped by for lunch on a Saturday around 1pm and ordered the open faced sandwich. My partner ordered the roasted eggplant sandwich. The side potatoes were amazing, and the sandwiches were decent. Nice atmosphere and a great place for a quick lunch or catching up with friends!

Want to come back to check out their dinner menu (when they serve Ethiopian cuisine).

My wife and I were excited to dive into Ethiopian cuisine, and we stumbled upon this charming spot that exceeded our expectations! From the moment we walked in, the vibrant ambiance and warm, courteous service made us feel right at home. The culinary experience was nothing short of spectacular; every bite was bursting with flavor. I savored the lamb tibes, which was perfectly seasoned, while my wife enjoyed the delightful potato ke’yi w’et. Both dishes were served with bread that added an incredible dimension to the meal. We left with full bellies and happy hearts, already counting down the days until our next visit!

formatted_address: 4411 S Mead St, Seattle, WA 98118, United States
name: Massawa Eritrean & Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: Incredibly flavorful dishes and portions so big I needed a box! Lovely vibe and helpful staff. Setting is gorgeous and the waiters are very professional. 10/10! The kitchen has definitely stepped up their game.

Just grabbed lunch at that place on S Mead St. It was packed, seriously long wait even though the menu looked pretty simple. The food was decent, portion size felt a little small for the price. The staff were all super nice, even though they seemed a bit overwhelmed. Maybe a few more tables would help!

Just tried Kitfoo on S Mead St and wow, it was packed! Seriously buzzing with people. The collard greens were insane – seriously the star of the show. Portions were generous for the price. Parking was a bit of a nightmare, maybe go during off-peak hours. Would love to see them offer a little takeout counter outside, just for easier grabbing.
Delicious food, friendly staff. You'll need more injera bread, but it's so worth it.
I did not like the inside vibe but the food is really good. Especially I liked their flat bread.

formatted_address: 1212 E Jefferson St, Seattle, WA 98122, United States
name: Red Lounge

reviews.text: It truly is one of kind. The heart and soul for afrobeats and Caribbean culture here in Seattle. They provide a veggie “meat patty” if you arrive on weekends before 9. During the week, their specials on Tuesdays are unmatched. Multiple screens to provide sports viewing, while maintaining a great vibe for those enjoying food or drink. The bartenders are approachable without being overzealous in sharing their culture with you. It’s your honor to be here.

I wasn't a fan of the QR code menu but the bar attendant was somewhat  helpful.
Food was tasty , the club at night has a better atmosphere then the restaurant during the day.
Best oxtails in seattle 🔥

I went to the club on Friday 24th of October for some music and drinks. The bartender (who was a lady) got so mad because my friend forgot to tip her and when I went to get more drinks she refused to serve us and called the other bartender to serve us and started shouting ‘they don’t tip’. The guy bartender now who served us just gave us mocktails and I paid for cocktails. They literally bully you because you don’t contribute to their salary. I was planning on spending my Halloween there but not anymore. Do better

The vibe there was dope! Everyone was very nice and cool.  Drinks were great and the DJ was a hit, playing a good mix of all Caribbean music. I didn't eat any food but my friends said the jerk chicken and beef patties were both delicious. No complaints I'd definitely go back!

The music was amazing! DJ Y2K played Rwandan tracks, which made my night 🙌🤗. I really appreciate how he brings together sounds from Africa and the Caribbean—it creates such a powerful connection between the motherland and the diaspora 👊👊.

formatted_address: 6754 Martin Luther King Jr Way S, Seattle, WA 98118, United States
name: Momona Cafe & Restaurant

reviews.text: Just had dinner at Letina on South Market Street. Really cool spot! It was busy, but the staff were incredibly friendly and helpful – they even gave my granddaughter a little cup for water. The food was fantastic, super flavorful, and the pasta was perfect. A bit dark in there, but the portions were great value for the price. Would definitely go back!

Just had dinner at Momona in WA 98118. It was really busy – had to wait about 20 minutes for a table. The staff were so friendly, almost like family. I got the salmon and it was seriously amazing, really flavorful. Portions were good value. Just a heads up, double check the hours online, Kenny mentioned they were closed on Sunday even though the website said they were open!

Just tried Momona in Seattle – really interesting place! It was packed when I got there around 6:30pm. The injera was definitely a learning curve, a little tangy, but I loved the bread. Portions were good value for the price. Parking was tricky, had to walk a block. Would be great if they had a few more vegetarian options, but overall a solid experience.

I was blown away by the generosity of the servings. You get your money's worth here! The flavor profile has evolved into something sophisticated. Ambiance is chic yet comfortable. The team really takes care of you.
Momona is a nice Eritrean restaurant. The owner is very sweet and the food is authentically delicious 👍🏽 (my favorite is the salmon, pasta, alicha & salad) 🥗

formatted_address: 13919 Tukwila International Blvd, Tukwila, WA 98168, United States
name: Sahara Cafe Somali Cuisine

reviews.text: Must try the Sahara special and Philly cheese. Excellent customer service and clean restroom. Parking can be challenging or you can park at the mosque which is 50 meters away.

This place is DELICIOUS!!!! 🤤
I traveled all the way from the Washington fair grounds an hour away to try this food and it was SO WORTH IT!!!
I Tried the chicken/lamb rice special and the katata plate which is only comparable to drunken noodles but way more flavorful!!!
The sauces are worth trying each one! They're a little spicy at first but add so much depth to the flavors! The lentil soup was hot and fresh and exactly what I needed on a cold day! They have a nice sized dining area with a couple of large flat screens. The Gentleman there was very inviting and nice! I will definitely come back every time I'm in Tukwila! The fried fish is the next dish I'm getting i saw someone eating it and the plate is HUGE!!! Portions are huge quality is 10/10!!! I brought these two plates home to my kids who LOVED THEM!!! Thank you so very much for serving high quality food and treating me so well on my random visit! 💖

I have not had food this good in 35 years.
Rad place, very friendly people with positive vibes.
It’s open late

Good food and good service always lots of fun when get there order food get free drink or free cake the owner of Sahara is business man his goal always make sure each customer come to place.  Happy and blessed and make sure coming back that’s his goal

Went for the first time looking for a Philly cheese steak sandwich. It did not disappoint. Also got the chicken and rice which was very flavorful (came with a side of small salad and spinach, so was well balanced, also cane with a banana). The price, portion and taste was overall great. Will be going back. Sandwich needed a little hot sauce for me but had that on the side.

formatted_address: 8136 Rainier Ave S, Seattle, WA 98118, United States
name: Kaffa Coffee and Wine Bar

reviews.text:
Great little local coffee place.

Serve authentic Ethiopian food  & coffee. They also serve wine.

Their dishes are full of flavor. Reasonable prices.
Polite friendly customer service.
Many thanks go to Mille .She has good customer service
Clean spacious place.

Parking is a challenge
During Seattle Restaurant Week we enjoyed the featured large Meat and Veggie Sampler. Tasty and ample portions. The staff was friendly and provided gluten free options.

I ate dinner  with 5 other people. It's a small place but they do have room to handle larger parties  I thought the food was excellent as was the service.  I've had Ethiopian food a good number of times.

My new favorite Ethiopian restaurant. Flavor wise. Interior design wise, not so much. Regardless I see myself making this place my goto for ethiopean.

The Food was cooked to perfection. Perfection. The flavors are so defined and refined. My order was absolutely cooked with love and many precision. I've had good lentils in my life but I didn't know they could be made so well with a great balance of texture and distinct flavor. Each lentil dish was completely different and hard to stop eating with every bite. Their meat was cooked as perfect as I've ever had. So tender and juicy and even cut into nice sizes. The only thing missing was the egg I'm used to in the combos. I'm curious how theirs would have tasted.

The prices are appropriate for the proportions. I can't wait to share this place with others.

Probably the best Ethiopian food I have ever had. The vegetarian sampler and doro wat we’re just out of this world. The injera bread was perfectly moist and spongy, and all the veg sampler items were fantastic! We also had the chai and an Ethiopian coffee, and they were both great and it was fun to have the coffee served in the traditional jebena! Food was served very quickly and was toasty-hot and fresh! Our server was also very kind and attentive. :) 10/10 would recommend and hope to come back!!

formatted_address: 6464 Martin Luther King Jr Way S, Seattle, WA 98118, United States
name: Yetenbi Bar & Restaurant

html_attributions: ADOT ETHIOPIAN AND ERITREAN RESTURANT አዶት ክትፎ እና ስጋ ቤት

reviews.text: Amazing traditional experience! The food was amazing, and the staff were kind as well! Good portions, and the food was really fresh. My friend and I ordered the special Kitfo and Tibs for two, and it was overflowing! The interior is also really beautiful and fantastic! I loved the high ceilings and the interior's cleanliness! I will definitely be back with more friends.

I was travelling from Toronto to Seattle to visit my family, they took me yetenbi Ethiopian restaurant. It was anbelievable, amazing, The quality of food, price, amount of food, the way  they serve their customers with respect, smile.  I travelled many countries I never see this kind of restaurant. I wish wish wish to have this kind of Ethiopian restaurant in Toronto. Keep it up.👍

I don’t usually go to Ethiopian restaurants since I enjoy cooking myself, but we had a special occasion with colleagues and went for lunch as a group. The food was absolutely amazing, and the atmosphere was very enjoyable — it really made the experience memorable.
One area that could be improved is the service. There was no dedicated waitress, which led to noticeable delays and less attentiveness when we needed refills or were ready to pay the bill. It would make a big difference if at least one person could focus on table service to enhance the overall dining experience.
We’re hoping to visit again soon and look forward to a more streamlined service next time!

As someone who is a very selective meat eater, the kitfo at Yetenbi’s was one of the most delicious ones I’ve had (only second to my mother’s). It just melts in your mouth! The speed at which all of the food was cooked and served was impressive and quality was not at all compromised. Truly an amazing experience!! I felt very welcomed here and hope I will be able to go back soon when I’m back in Seattle.

First off, the name of this restaurant is changed to Adot Kitfo and no more Yetenbi, true to my visit date of Oct 26, 2025.
Secondly, me and my friend tried their Kitfo and Gored Gored, it really tastes great. I would definitely come back.

formatted_address: 1508 NE 117th St, Seattle, WA 98125, United States
name: Ahadu Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text:
We stumbled upon this place driving around looking for something that called to us, and wow was I glad this is where we stopped.

The employees were so friendly. There’s no paper menus but the QR code clearly defines each dish. We got the vegetarian platter which came with a piece of injera for each of us, a glass bottle of water (no ice) with 2 cups, no utensils (per norm) and when I asked about each dish the super friendly guy there explained each. The cook was really cool too.

The bathroom was tiny, clean, and I the peeks I got of the kitchen showed a clean environment.

The complexities and layers of flavor in each dish was just lovely. You get everything in the menu I screen shotted for the largest veggie dish for $25 - which is a SUPER reasonable deal and fed us both with a snack for later, not a large amount of leftovers but a good snack.

I had no clue collard & spinach went so well together but I’d eat Gomen at home all the time if I knew how to make it. The Shiro was very much a hummus reminiscent dip but with a very different flavor. My least fave was the Key Sir and that’s just a personal beet thing but we still smashed it.

We also had coffee which was strong and dark and delicious.

I can’t wait to go back and I recommend this to anyone interested in trying Ethiopian on a beginner level, they’ll help you out - if you’re a connoisseur try this place too! Freaking impressive & delicious.

PS: I love that there’s a couple of tables to sit at in front on nice days.

Great food, Great community, Great service. As an American Ethiopian, I enjoy coming here for lunch after a busy afternoon, sitting outside and sipping tea. The food is honestly the best I’ve had, reminding me of how my emaye used to make it. My favorite dish here was the foul. Would recommend to anyone open to trying something new or experiencing authentic tasting Ethiopian food.

I actually haven't been to this place in over a year (before I moved out of the area), but the three times I have gone the food has been awesome. I've eaten at a lot of Ethiopian restaurants in Seattle (and elsewhere) over the past 40 years and this place has my absolute favorite food (well, tied with Delish). I had never noticed there was another Ethiopian place three doors down. I'm back in Seattle for a short visit and wanted to make sure I ate here. Unfortunately, I accidentally went to the other place, thinking it was Ahadu and they had just expanded since my last visit. Upon speaking to the server, it was made known to me that it wasn't Ahadu, but it was too late to leave! The food at the place we ended up at was mediocre, at best. I won't be able to eat at Ahadu while I'm in Seattle because they are closed Tue & Wed and Thu is Christmas and I leave early the following day! Boo hoo!  Please keep patronizing this wonderful family and restaurant, Seattleites. I want to be able to eat here on my next trip back to Seattle!

Updated review: Ahadu has the best meat dishes around and really amazing food. I was disappointed last time I went because I was charged a hidden 5% fee. Also despite ordering 2 combos we were only given 2 pieces of injera and charged for extra pieces. Most places offer more injera. While I plan to come back I hope that they reconsider the service charge and maybe be a bit more generous with the injera and veggie portions.
The veggie combo was on the smaller side. Portions have definitely shrunk.

Old review:
Incredibly welcoming and kind people serving amazing food. It was a great experience all around.
A friend and I had the meat combo, we added an extra injera because our eyes are far bigger than our stomach.  We ate as much as we could but still had a ton of food leftover.
Finished with a delightful coffee and a fry bread. The coffee is must needed to reduce the impact of the food coma approaching.
Can’t wait to eat here again!
Best injera in town. We always get the vegetarian combo and it’s perfect for two people. Each dish is delicious. The staff are very friendly and helpful.

formatted_address: 1525 13th Ave, Seattle, WA 98122, United States
name: Ubuntu Bar & Grill

reviews.text: No good food people no speed

formatted_address: 4903 Rainier Ave S, Seattle, WA 98118, United States
name: La Teranga Restaurant - Senegalese cuisine

reviews.text: This was best and most uniquely flavored food I've had in a long time. I suppose if I were familiar with the cuisine of Senegal I'd say different - but I'm not and that is why this place is a gem! Owner/chef/server/all the things is also lovely. Highly recommend-be ready to sit at one of only 4 tables.

Bold, delicious flavors! Even the rice was flavorful. The owner/chef is very warm and helpful. Not good for large groups due to limited seating. Great for single, couples or carry out
Got the coconut goat curry

A gem.

The boyfriend and I headed here for dinner before a movie at the Ark Lodge. Coming from the DC-Maryland area, we don't have as many great West African restaurants as we used to. I was excited to have found La Teranga in a google search. As soon as we walked in, I knew the food was going to be delicious because of how amazing the dining room smelled. We ordered the couscous and veggie dish, lamb mafe, plantains with red sauce, and bissap juice. Everything was amazing and we will definitely be back! What a gem in Columbia City. Service from staff (and the chef himself!) was warm and friendly. Highly recommended.
Fantastic food. The owner/ cook was very nice and pleasant to talk to. The place is small, but, very intimate. Definitely visit again. The lamb is to die for!

A refreshing change from routine. The food taste is really unique, and in a good manner. Not only food but even the drinks are unique. Who could have thought ginger juice would be so great? It's so good! Back to food, the lamb was perfectly cooked and couscous was nicely textured. The whole place is not bigger than a walk in closet, so if you are in a group good luck with that. Owner is supremely hospitable and jovial. 5 stars just for the attitudef. For 2 people expect to pay around &$40. Yes for such a small place with no ambience so to speak of, it is on the expensive side. I guess ridiculous real estate prices here are to be blamed. After having food, I have no qualms paying that much. I hope the owner gets to expand his business to a much larger and much needed place.

formatted_address: 5901 Rainier Ave S, Seattle, WA 98118, United States
name: DINI KITCHEN

reviews.text: When it was owned by the two Somali sisters, it was so mashallah. Now that they sold it, it has been depleting. The chicken sandwich doesn't have any vegetables and is overloaded with mayonnaise and mustard. The rice is dry and they stopped using real juice as refreshments. It's still halal so that's great but it's not as good as it used to be. This is some pics of the food before they sold the place.
Superb, specially for the spicy sauce they served accompanied with their Roasted Chicken! & off course the banana....

This place blew us away, the service was nothing short of wonderful. While the menu was a little daunting to us whom had never had east African food before, the server made some recommendations before bringing us complimentary soup (which was  lightly flavored but incredibly pleasing) lemonade and water. We ended up with goat and rice, and lamb and rice. Both were spectacular and exploding in flavor. The lamb was so tender it was falling off the bone. We will be back again soon! And telling all our friends about this place.

It is always a treat dining/pick up from Dini, my friends eyes light up at the sight of the juicy tender lamb shank ;) the new owner is passionate and always goes out of his way to make sure you are well taken care of. Generous portion, tasty food, and excellent prices. Always a must stop when in the area.

Brought my husband and two year old here for lunch today and we really enjoyed ourselves! The samosas were delicious, and not spicy so my toddler liked them. The food was tasty and clean, my first experience tasting Somali food. The place felt welcoming and cheerful, with a home cooked flavor. The goat with spiced rice was excellent, and the KatiKati was very tasty. They serve a fresh homemade hot sauce tasting of jalapeño with cilantro... It’s a jewel because it brings a unique flavor to Seattle that leaves you feeling happy. The portions are very generous, as are the prices. Try it out!

formatted_address: 300 Vuemont Pl NE, Renton, WA 98056, United States
name: 237 Kitchen

reviews.text: On a random Monday, I happened upon a TT video of a mom and her babies trying the Fufu and Egusi. I was in from that moment on… I sent a message inquiring about placing an order. Yvette responded fairly quickly. I needed to wait until Friday to order, and everyday leading up to Friday, I was so excited! lol. I just knew in my heart it would be delicious! After hours of trying to pay her… my bank was being all in my business and wouldn’t approve my multiple attempts to Zelle her funds… I placed my order for pickup on Saturday… My drive home was about 20 minutes… I don’t know what kind of apocalypse containers she uses, but the food was turned-my-fingers-pink hot, even when I made it home! LOL! I couldn’t wait for the first taste. Y’all! It. Is. SO. Tasty! I had to try the Fufu and Egusi first! 10/10. Perfect! I LOVE Peanut Soup, and that was my next taste! 10/10. The Goat Stew holds a special place in my heart… read belly… too! 10/10. I ordered Pounded Yam Fufu and Egusi (chicken), Peanut Soup (no protein), Goat Stew, Garri Fufu, and Dodo. I will definitely order again! It tastes like love in a bowl! Run! Don’t walk! This was my first time trying a TT recommendation. I am SO glad I did! It was worth the wait!

I have been wanting to try this place out for actual months now. I'm torn between saying "this is worth the wait" and berating myself for not ordering sooner. Yvette has been so lovely, so responsive and kind.

We ordered grilled chicken, chicken egusi, fufu, and chicken jellof. The grilled chicken is probably the most flavorful grilled chicken we've ever had. Perfectly seasoned! Eat it with the green sauce and the jellof, and you have a perfect bite! The fufu was incredibly soft and the ideal vehicle for the egusi. I think I can eat the egusi with fufu everyday. That's how delicious it was. I love rice, so it's no surprise I enjoyed the jellof. I've already said this but I don't know how else to describe it but "perfectly seasoned".

It was very difficult for us to take these pics before devouring. 10/10 highly recommend trying out Cameroon food!

tldr: 10/10 recommend. Do yourself a favor and try Cameroon food (thank me later). Two words to describe it: perfectly seasoned.

1. You will pay first.
2. Pick up is at Kent not in Renton and you will only know address after the payment.
3. The owner forgot my order I placed order previous day so I waited another hour.
4. order and pick up experience was bad but the food was good.

This meal was everything!! The fish was perfectly seasoned and grilled to tender, smoky perfection—every bite was packed with flavor. The plantains were golden and slightly crisp on the edges with that soft, sweet center I love. And that pepper sauce? Whew—just the right kick to wake up my taste buds. I really, really enjoyed this. Definitely a hit!🤤🤤🤤

I’ve been looking for Egusi and fufu for a while and was about to give up until I tried once more googled and this gem popped up!! And OMG!! I literally ran to get it. It’s the best I’ve ever tasted 🔥 and I’ll be going back for the rest of the food she has to offer. Yvette is so sweet and personable. You have a lifetime customer now. Thank you!! See you soon.

formatted_address: 14200 Tukwila International Blvd Suite 141, Tukwila, WA 98168, United States
name: Afella Jollof Catering

reviews.text: The best beef samosa of my life, so flaky and flavorful! The incredible jollof rice and vibrant yassa chicken go perfectly with the plantains. And perfect compliment/condiment? The spicy green sauce!! We bought a little jar to take home. Wow!! We bought our meals at the Delridge Farmers Market and took it home. Like seriously full of great flavors, cooked PERFECTLY and served by lovely people. Find them at the Tukwila Spice Bridge Food Hall when the Delridge Market is closed!
Our ordering was perfect. Well the picture says it all
Poor customer service.

formatted_address: 8300 Wabash Ave S, Seattle, WA 98118, United States
name: Mama Sambusa Small Kitchen

reviews.text: 5 stars. Will be coming again. Definitely a hidden gem. Sambusas are a must
Great food available at odd hours. Made fresh. Salmon fertilize was perfect. Not over cooked. Samosa picked up next door very worth grabbing. So good.
Ordered beef sambusas and they even added free fried bread for me to try!
Good

formatted_address: Thornlie Square Shopping, Center/318 Spencer Rd, Thornlie WA 6108, Australia
name: LIBA'S Authentic African Cuisine

reviews.text: Tried Ghanaian food for the first time and it absolutely blew our minds in a good way. Everything was very delicious, full of flavour and felt very authentic. Service was friendly and food came out fast. Wonderful place.

There was that much in the way of service, the boy at the till didn’t greet and just waited for me make my order. The floors were also quite dirty and even a chewed piece of gum on the table.

But oh my was the food amazing. This is some seriously flavourful food. The chefs are working some serious magic in the kitchen and I will definitely be back to try more from the menu, I just might get takeaway this time.

I ordered the Pounded Yam and Egushi for delivery, it was my first time trying this dish and that was by far one of the most delicious things I’ve ever eaten. It was absolutely perfection and I’ll definitely be eating from Liba’s again!❤️
Food was so authentic and flavourful, definitely worth the price as two dishes were good enough for 4 people even though it was just 2 of us. Worth coming back!
Beautiful warm and welcoming service, the most delicious food ever and incredible value! We shared several dishes and also tried the sobo drink. Everything was fantastic and I can't wait to go again!

formatted_address: 2019 Hewitt Ave, Everett, WA 98201, United States
name: Heritage African Restaurant

reviews.text:
A place discovered during a recent search for African cuisine near Everett, this restaurant was a surprising find despite its good reviews and noticeable presence. My friend and I visited around 6 PM on a Friday evening and were the sole diners at the time in the spacious establishment.
Parking is street-only, so plan accordingly. Inside, the restaurant is large with ample seating.
We started with appetizers: the Fried Plantains were delicious, and the Beef Samosas were also enjoyable. For our main dishes, we tried the Golden Pompano from the Grill, which was good overall but a touch too salty for our preference, and the Dibi Afra/Suya (Grilled Lamb), which was tasty, though some pieces had a fair amount of fat.
The house-made drinks were highlights: the Bouye (Baobab Juice) was very good, as was the Ginger Pineapple Juice.
Portion sizes here are enormous. One person with a large appetite might finish a plate solo, but sharing is highly recommended. We took our leftovers home and still had enough food for another full meal the next day. Service was efficient and generally "Ok."
If you're in the area and looking for flavorful African food with hearty portions, this place definitely falls under the "should go" list.
Amazing food! Beautiful restaurant. Got the lamb with salad per the owner’s recommendation, get the hot sauce! Atima (the owner) was my server and very nice. Food came fast.

I got take-out from here a few nights ago. I'm relatively new to this cuisine but have been wanting to try a stew for a while now so got the black-eyed peas stew without meat, fufu, fried plantains and a side salad. Holy moly this place is good! had no idea what to expect but I have never been so grateful for leftovers the next day. Truly a gem in the neighborhood, can't wait to dine-in next time!

My family and I went to this restaurant to try it out. It was so good. I've never had African food before and it was phenomenal. Even my grandkids who are picky ate a bite of at least everything. I would highly recommend coming here. It is so good. The wait staff is so sweet and nice and the vibe is awesome. Next time my family and I are in Everett. We plan on coming again .

Food Quality Overall: 3
Food Quality Compared to Similar Places: 4
Food Presentation: 4
Staff: 3
Service: 3
Cleanliness: 4
Atmosphere: 4
Value: 3
