I’ve come to this restaurant a few times for takeout, and unfortunately, my experiences have consistently been disappointing.

The customer service here is very poor — staff are often rude and unhelpful, which makes the whole experience unpleasant. Good customer service is important for any business, especially when people are coming in and spending their money, and this is an area that needs serious improvement.

The food itself also does not live up to expectations. It doesn’t taste authentic, and it often feels like it was prepared without much care. On top of that, the restaurant could do much better in terms of cleanliness.

I honestly expected more from an Ethiopian restaurant, both in flavor and hospitality. With some effort in customer service, food quality, and cleanliness, this place could be so much better — but right now, I can’t recommend it.
This place was amazing.  The food was incredible and the atmosphere is a lot of fun. I'll definitely return.

The interior is very hole-in-the-wall/divey. My table was crooked to the salt shaker would slide off the table if I didn't hold it in place with napkins. It took 45 minutes for my food to come, and each item was a different temperature. Some warm, some burned my mouth. The meat combo I ordered was $18, but my bill itemized it as $20, which I also didn't appreciate. The flavors of the food weren't spectacular either. Some of my beef dishes were too fatty or chewy. Won't be coming back.

formatted_address: 1800 S Jackson St, Seattle, WA 98144, United States
name: Wonder Ethiopian Restaurant Sport Bar

reviews.text: So so delicious! I was thrilled to find a place with gluten free, 100% teff injera. But not only that the veggie combo platter was all also gf, and the friendly server was able to answer other dietary questions with confidence. A very wonderful meal and definitely will be back!

We had an amazing dinner here! We were helped out by Tsion, who recommended that we get veggie and meat sampler plate since it was our first time visiting. Everything was excellent! It was probably enough food for four people, but left us with plenty for leftovers. Reasonably priced too for the feast that it was! Photo included—plate takes up the whole table! Service was great, Tsion was super sweet. Would recommend! Friday night has live jazz so head over then!

10 piece veggie platter from the fasting menu was so delicious and nourishing, 1 plate is enough food for 2-3 people

Not much crowd even on Friday night with the band so definitely come support :)
Got the 10 kind veggie platter and some of the best I've had. Also perfect service!
Definitely need to try their brunch menu. I was blown away by this Ethiopian dish—the flavors, textures, and harmony of spices came together perfectly.

formatted_address: 1221 South Main St UNIT 202, Seattle, WA 98144, United States
name: HAHU LOUNGE

reviews.text: Hahu Cafe in Seattle is a hidden gem for authentic Ethiopian cuisine. With delicious dishes like injera, kitfo, and shiro, plus amazing coffee and warm service, it's a must-visit. The cozy ambiance and late-night hours make it perfect for a unique dining experience!

I ordered tibsi; to be honest that was the ugliest tibsi I ever had. I am not sure what is her name but the woman behind the bar was unprofessional and rude. She was even not happy when we ordered the food in the first place. I hope she is not the manager. But manager if you are able to see this make sure your employees treat the customers with respect and prepare quality food.
The place is remodeled and looks great. There are different Dj and they’re all good.
This place is one of a kind. The owners are awesome.
Good

formatted_address: 2321 S Jackson St, Seattle, WA 98144, United States
name: Simply Soulful

reviews.text:
That was a huge let down!
I’ve truly wanted to try this restaurant for years and  since it was the last day of Kwanzaa I felt it would be meaningful to take my family to a black owned restaurant. Unfortunately this was not the experience I was hoping for.

We waited for at least 90 minutes to get our food and we didn’t even ask for anything complicated. And once I got my food I received the saddest brisket sandwich I’ve ever seen. On top of that, they got my son’s order wrong.

I’ve had a lot of Soul Food in my life and this was nowhere close. Black businesses in Seattle are struggling, so the last thing I want to do is be a detriment, but they have got to do better.

We stopped here for dinner around 8pm and overall it was good. We were planning to dine in but the dining area was closed. I had the catfish with greens and red beans and rice. The greens were good. The red beans and rice was good. The catfish was cooked much harder than I prefer but it was ok. My son had the wings and Mac and cheese which was pretty good. The service was good. The young man at the front counter did good. Overall, it was a good choice. Our meal was about $25 per person which I guess is the norm for this area.

First visit here. Very nice staff. Plenty of seating inside.. maybe their outside seating was closed. We went for takeout for dinner. I got the catfish with Mac and yams. My wife got the catfish sandwich and fries.. unfortunately they were out of greens .. next time! But what we got was really good. Will make it back eventually to try other menu items. There is a happy hour too which is super cool!

We had high expectations. With no one in the restaurant, our order was taken right away at the front counter. We paid $20 each plus $5 for the sweet tea. Waited over an hour, for over deep fried catfish, undercooked eggs and a cold small piece of cornbread. I felt I was robbed in plain daytime.

Simply soulful is a PROPER southern meal. 5 stars across she board, the staff is kind, the food is grandma Sunday dinner type vibes. Fried chicken is Grade A. A must stop when visiting Seattle. Thank you simply soulful, we needed this fast or Georgia home.

formatted_address: 8333 55th Ave NE, Seattle, WA 98115, United States
name: Where Ya At Matt

reviews.text:
I was looking forward to this food truck as I have heard amazing reviews about how delicious the food is and especially in PNW, great Southern food is hard to come by. I also heard that the service here is great. My boyfriend and I caught them at No Boat Brewing and decided to bring our fur babies for a nice dinner. We arrived at the truck and sadly, the male worker seemed out of it and just in a apathetic mood, so it was uncomfortable trying to order. They didn't say much or anything about when to get the food. When I did pick up our food, I politely asked if the order was ready and not only do I not get a response or a nod, he just turns around and grabs my order before just giving it to me. No enjoy the food or thank you for ordering, and not even a ghost of a smile.

We got a small shrimp and grits, oyster po boy, and large jambalaya. The oyster po boy was the star of the order as it was delicious and one of the better po boys my boyfriend and I had, but it was also our first time trying an oyster po boy. The shrimp and grits were nothing to really write about and the jambalaya was just meh. Not sure if we came at a bad day but it's super unfortunate as I was really looking forward to this food truck for the longest time but it was the most disappointing Washington food truck that I have had visited.

$13.33 with tax and tip for a small gumbo.. that was mostly rice and barely any meat or okra, as others have said. Workers weren’t really friendly just a “what do you want” basically. A let down for the cost.

I used to love this food truck but feel like it’s a pale imitation of itself. The bread is soft and falls apart almost as soon as you start eating - it lacks the crisp outer crust you’d expect from a New Orleans po’boy. There’s also something wrong with the shrimp and grits seasoning, it tastes burnt/overcooked and bitter.  It’s been a few times now in the past few months I’ve eaten here and it’s been disappointing each time - shrimp po’boy, shrimp and grits, catfish po’boy, and the red beans (which were good).

I really needed some southern comfort food and OMG so happy to find this truck! I read through the reviews first because Southern food in the PNW is typically not Southern and kind of gross but I saw no complaints about the food! A few negatives over the friendliness but that just feels like some elitist nonsense. It's a food truck 🚚 and the food was SOUTHERN! Great job 👏

I go every time I see them on the schedule at one of the nearby breweries and everything I've ordered has been amazing. The muffuletta is great, and it's really nice to have the gumbo and jambalaya as options in the colder months. Good options for sides as well, and the beignets are incredible - better than most of the beignets I tried in NOLA. There are A LOT of food trucks around here and I'm grateful that this is one of them.

formatted_address: 13028 Interurban Ave S suit 100, Tukwila, WA 98168, United States
name: Lido Kitchen

reviews.text:
Amazing food! We had the chicken plate, steak plate, and sambusa. The meat in the sambusa had a delicious blend of spices, and was amazing! The rice is also very well seasoned with I believe star anise and other spices.
I've never had Somali food before, but it reminds me a bit of Indian. The chicken and steak were both cooked well and came with a large portion of rice and veggies.
If you're in the area, you won't regret stopping in. We come from out of state a few times a year to Seattle, and we'll be coming through again for sure.
The service was very welcoming and friendly too, happy to talk and joke with each person. We felt like guests in a home rather than just customers, a great experience overall.
Also try the tea after dinner!

We arrived at the restaurant which is located in a clean, nice neighborhood of a business park. The parking is free and easy in front of the restaurant. I started with some beef sambusa that were well fried and very crispy without being greasy. We had the Somali Tes, which is a tasty spiced tea. We ordered the goat plate with rice and the lamb plate with noodles. Both goat and lamb dishes were very well spice, and the meat was juicy, without being over or undercooked. We will go again when in the area.

The restaurant is family owned and operated.  The owner/chef came out to check on his customers to make sure everyone was happy.
Absolutely delicious Somalian food served by some of the kindest, warmest people. Nice ambience and good location. A definite must-try!

Stopped by here after coming back from a long flight from Chicago. So glad they were open that night! Incredibly kind owners that were very welcoming to us and provided great recommendations. We ordered the beef suqaar and goat meat plate. They were out of some other plates because they are so popular. The food was so delicious that we licked our plates clean. Great community and absolutely delicious East African food. They even gave us some delicious bottomless tea to go with our meal. It was great to see cultural religious practice rented out in the restaurant as well; really provided a beautiful sight of cultural diversity and inclusion. Thank you for your welcoming service and for sharing your delicious food with us. We will definitely be back next time we are in the area! (Only recommendation is improvement on the decorations and interior of the restaurant, but they had just opened a few months ago when we had visited.)

Got the goat plate as the lamb shank plate is sold out, the rice is just so so so good, maybe cooked with broth? So tasty, the vegetables and the rice are definitely 5 stars, and the lamb itself I would rate 4 star. The service is amazing too! Highly recommending this place!

formatted_address: 1950 S Parker Rd, Denver, CO 80231, United States
name: Jollof-Jollof Halal Food Truck and Mobile Caterer

html_attributions: Jollof-Jollof Halal Food Truck and Mobile Caterer

reviews.text: You can’t go wrong with anything on the menu but the lamb chops dibi and Senegalese friend fish are unbeatable!! Highly HIGHlLY recommend!! And everything is HALAL!

Absolutely incredible experience all around. Chef David was clearly so excited to share his culture with us through his cooking, and he did not disappoint. Our first experience with Senegalese cuisine and every bite was amazing. We got the lamb, and chicken brochette, which came with jolof rice, fries, fresh salad and perfectly crisp plantains.

OMG!  I knew it was going to be good food based I what I heard, but I didn't know it would be amazing.  Just spicy enough, and the flavor, the flavor out of this world.  The Hibiscus and ginger drinks are better than what I make at home.  So refreshing.   I'm happy!

I went to study abroad in Senegal and this food truck really brought back all the memories in the best way possible.
The food taste authentic and delicious, and the senegaleses teranga has traveled to the US with the lovely individuals who run it. Please go visit and support.

Just tried their food at the Five Points Juneteenth celebration and 🥰🥰🫠🫠🫠
Incredible - best food I’ve had in months. Even elements of food that I normally don’t like, such as tomatoes are paired with flavors that make everything sing.

The fries were perfectly salted and seasoned, hot, crispy, everything you’d want.

By some miracle there wasn’t a line (yet)
During our short wait, the music was absolutely 🔥 🔥 Couldn’t help but just vibe.

Absolutely making it a point to find this truck in the future.

formatted_address: 25151 109th Pl SE, Kent, WA 98030, United States
name: Somalian Foods

reviews.text: The address is untraceable.  It will take you in Kent apartments. The phone provided go unanswered.  Be extra careful not to loose your money.

This Somali restaurant is truly the best in town. The food is incredibly delicious and will leave you wanting more. Each dish is bursting with authentic Somali flavors and is cooked to perfection. Despite the high quality of the food, the prices are surprisingly cheap, making it accessible to everyone. The portions are generous, ensuring that you will leave feeling satisfied and happy. The friendly and welcoming atmosphere adds to the overall dining experience, making it a must-try for anyone looking for delicious and affordable Somali cuisine.

I recently had the pleasure of trying your culinary delights, and I must say, it was an extraordinary experience! Just wanted to express my appreciation for the exceptional taste and quality of the dishes I sampled.

The Somali Organic Chicken and Beef Sambusas were an absolute highlight – bursting with flavor, perfectly seasoned, and the crispy shell added a delightful crunch, my kids loved these Sambusas!

Equally impressive was the Somali Biryani Rice chicken version. The fragrant aroma, and tender meat made it a standout dish. The authenticity and attention to detail in your recipes are truly commendable.

I appreciate the the extra Sambusas 🙏
I look forward to indulging in your delectable offerings again soon.

Thank you for bringing the taste of Somalia to Kent, WA!
Straight up not somali food. Is that sandwich in your menu? That's crazy.
This is my first time trying Somali food and I really enjoyed eating baasto, Somali-style spaghetti.

formatted_address: 11805 Renton Ave S Suite C, Seattle, WA 98178, United States
name: Salima Specialties

reviews.text: The food at Salima Specialties was absolutely excellent! Every dish was full of rich flavor, perfectly cooked, and beautifully presented. You can really taste the freshness of the ingredients and the passion that goes into the cooking. The portions were generous, the spices were well-balanced, and everything tasted authentic and delicious. Definitely a place I’d love to visit again and highly recommend to anyone looking for great Pan-Asian halal food!

The best Halal Champa Vietnamese food in Seattle. Owner and staff are very friendly. Teh rice with beef brisket is great and I tried mamak Mee goreng spicy which has amazing flavor and perfect spices.

I love this place! My family and I order from door dash all the time and it’s the only take out food my mom eats ( short ribs are mouth watering).  I decided to dine in solo and try the pho, I was in foodie heaven. The food looks and tastes fresh and presentation did not disappoint.

Excellent food! I’m confident this is one of the best halal options in Seattle. All of the food was excellent, but the beef short rib plate was delicious, flavorful, and filling. I would definitely come back if I was in the area. Service was quick and friendly. Plenty of seating indoors and outdoors. Highly recommend!

I ordered the beef short ribs. Everything was delicious. Big portions and the ribs were juicy and tender. They have a lot of other options on the menu. Don’t hesitate to visit this restaurant, you won’t regret it.

formatted_address: 4556 Martin Luther King Jr Way S #2151, Seattle, WA 98108, United States
name: Bananas Grill

reviews.text:
Great customer care & support.  Very welcoming & kind. After we placed our order, we were immediately given a delicious soup. The appetizer was AMAZING. (We ordered the Banana's  Combination.) After we enjoyed our appetizer; falafel,  dolmas with a lovely consistency of a side of hummus; our meal came out. We were served a fresh,  lite salad paired with gryo lamb, chicken kabobs sided  w a hearty portion of nicely seasoned rice topped with grilled onions & chicken.

I was greatly pleased with the staff. Our server did excellent at understanding customer cues. He only asked if we were satisfied & if everything was well after we were finished w our appetizer. Then asked if we needed anything else as we were 95% finished & we were conversating lightly while enjoying looking out the window.  I really appreciate the server understanding & recognizing the customers personal space while not rushing our experience. He was so very pleasant with a kind smile.  We got baklava & it was delicious.
This meal was shared between 2. We were on a date. It did not leave us feeling empty,  but did leave us satisfied fully.  This meal was not vegan.  It does appear to have vegan options.  Greatly grilled & prepared proteins.  They are not skimpy with their proteins/ meats. Please enjoy! I highly recommend this restaurant.  What a pleasant experience.

After our fishing session at Mount Baker park I and my buddy decided to get some food to bring to our brewery. My friend suggested a restaurant right where he lives that makes really good Gyros, so he claimed. Later I found out he was not lying. Parking around dinner time might be a little tricky but not challenging. The food might take longer as well since they only have one cook I think. The space is medium size, clean and cozy. The owner and staff are friendly. We got 2 Beef and Lamb gyros and a Greek fries and we are stuffed. Would definitely stop by again if I am in the area.

I grew up in the vistas and would always come to banana Grill growing up and always got the same thing. The chicken wings were always my favorite but now I grown up and came back from traveling and I feel like they changed the recipe because the chicken wings are not as Delightful as they used to be with the color and the size I was expecting the same thing but seems like they changed the recipe still a great place though
Good service. We were given complimentary lentil soups which were tasty. The beef/lamb gyro was delicious. I wasn’t a fan of the wings- they were dry and unflavorful.
Delicious food. Lentil soup is so good. Everything I have gotten is filling comfort food. I love when I have to work in the area because coming here for lunch is the highlight of my work day.

formatted_address: 1501 4th Ave Ste 101, Seattle, WA 98101, United States
name: Cafe Zum Zum

reviews.text:
Pros: big portions for the price, quiet area inside a larger food court

Cons: chicken spinach curry was very watery and salty. Comes with something more resembling a tortilla than naan.

Overall, decent in a pinch but not that great quality wise

Very yummy curry! We ordered green pea lamb and spinach chicken. The rice is good, curry is tasty. If you are looking for something warm and quick, definitely come here. Also, the staff are friendly !

We had lunch on a Monday while taking a trip to Seattle, the food was delicious, fresh and warm. The atmosphere nice and clean. A great option for those looking for Halal yummy food! The owner was extremely courteous as well.

Decent place and good food. This is inside the building on the first floor with two more food places adjacent and a common seating around. Seems this place is here since the 90s. Owner was welcoming. I had the lamb and rice and it was delicious. The green tangy sauce that came along with it was my favorite. Next time I will ask for two more of those..
Great portions and price! Food is deliciously seasoned and I love the cafeteria style quick to order for quick lunches away from the office. This place is now a weekly staple!

formatted_address: 360 Corporate Dr N, Tukwila, WA 98188, United States
name: Soul

reviews.text: The food is always so good and well seasoned! She makes everything to order. Yes, it does take a little longer than average fast food, but you never have to worry about receiving old food that's been sitting around for hours. Its worth it!

I catered from Soul (Seattle) for a large corporate event of up to 120 people and the food was AMAZING. Everyone had great things to say about and it was all gone. Jennifer was so friendly and helped me order some last minute proportions as well. Thank you Soul (Seattle)!

The food is incredible! I was raised in South Carolina and have strong opinions about how grits should be cooked. The cheesy grits are on point. The hush puppies are the perfect texture and full of flavor. Yesterday I ordered the oysters and was thrilled with the generous amount I received. The catfish is perfectly seasoned and fried to that lovely crisp but not crunchy stage. There is no seating, so you order from their website and park at the side of the building. They run it out to your car. We have ordered 3 times now and it's been excellent every time. I can't recommend them enough

I don't know where these people are from but you ain't from the south with dry, tasteless cornbread. Dry tasteless red beans and rice. Banana pudding that is instant pudding with 3-4 wafers. The catfish wasn't bad and saved my stomach from tasteless food and Mac and cheese was okay. Oh yeah yams 😩 plantains not bad actually were good. You have no idea what soul means. I wish I could have rated you better but I can not.

The catfish tasted unclean and unseasoned. Couldn’t even finish the sorry excuse for gumbo  no sassuge very salty gravy  like mixture on top. Lemon pepper wings tasted like something was off in the texture Wingstop is a better option. Spent 100$ purchase very disappointed

formatted_address: 16324 International Blvd, Seattle, WA 98188, United States
name: Mecca Mediterranean Cuisine

reviews.text:
Big open spacious place, lots of seating options.
Reasonable prices

It is Somali restaurant,  serve Somali style food, and taste.  So everything is Somali standard, and ways , Not American standards including hygiene.
There is big huge difference in both standards
Name says Mediterranean cuisine,  but actually the food is not. It is Somali food, and Somali flavor.
In Geography Mediterranean region is all the way up in north Africa,and part of Europe,  and Somalia is all the way South Africa. So this restaurant name is very much misleading.  It Advertise as Mediterranean,  But actually  serve Somali food. There is a big huge difference in food, and flavor,and ingredients

Parking lot is rough, needs looking after.
There is grocery store inside catering to Somali customers,  and taste.

If Somali food appeals to you, then this place makes good Somali food

Food has lots of flavor , and tastes good to Somali Standards
Friendly accomodating server

Sometimes you take a chance and you get lucky, this is one of those times. The building is a bit run down, and they are catering to a specific ethnicity. But if you are willing to step out of your comfort zone you will be reward with a delicious meal. Well seasoned meat, fresh salad and rice that my wife said was the best ever and a lot of it.

I was staying at Ramada hotel and wanted something to eat near by, so I was walking by when I thought I should check this place out. To my surprise,  they have many options and very delicious food. Very nice people and even offer me to taste the food. They also gave me free lentil soup which was very good. The chia tea was to die for with perfect amount of cardamom, cinnamon, and sugar.👍👍👍I will definitely be back whenever I return to Seattle and I recommend it.

Food is great, but $30 for two breakfasts and two Jarritos is straight up robbery. They eggs and tomatoes was good but they advertised it for $7 but changed me $8.99, my son got some portion of beef and egg and they charged $11 and I saw nothing on the menu for that price, tax seemed right so the final price with $3 Jarritos came to $28.59... like I said, the food is good and authentic and all but even their tables here didn't ave silverware (had to ask) the napkins were empty or just not on the tables. They have stuff piles in the room with jenky Christmas lights. You would figure that a $30 breakfast would warrant a better looking establishment. That's all.

Super glad we found this place! It's a very unassuming place but the food was super awesome! They have a build a plate type thing. Goat meat, cream chicken, spinach chicken, veggies and rice. Everything was so good 👌 they also had dope chai tea to top it all off 😍 Hope to come back again!

formatted_address: 458 SE 185th Ave STE 105, Portland, OR 97233, United States
name: Alleamin African Kitchen

reviews.text: The food was absolutely delicious! The lamb shank was perfectly cooked, it was so tender it just fell off the bone. Every dish was full of flavor . Everything we tried tasted amazing. Highly recommended for anyone who loves rich, flavorful food!

Popped into Rockwood Market Hall after a long walk and decided to try something new, I'm very glad I did. The plate I had from Alleamin African Kitchen, tucked into the back corner of the main dining area, was some of the best food I've had in a very long time. My (HUGE!) $18 plate consisted of complexly spiced stewed red lentils, tender beef and vegetables, a fresh salad, and chewy, hot flatbread. Every part of the meal was delicious and interesting. In addition to the amazing food, the people running the place were so nice and welcoming and had a lovely chat with me about how they spice their lentils (because if I ever figure it out, I'm going to be eating lentils a lot more often!). Simply some of the best food I've ever had in a city that seems to be full of Expensive But Just Okay food spots, probably the best Food Pod restaurant I've ever eaten at. I would give eleven stars if I could, and I will be back to try everything else on the menu as soon as I can.

I had an amazing experience at Alleamin African Kitchen. I came in for dinner around 7:30 PM with two of my friends, and from the moment we walked in, the atmosphere was warm and welcoming. The owner was incredibly patient, kind, and genuinely hospitable.

What really stood out was his generosity and dedication — we placed our initial order right before closing time, and even 15 minutes after they had officially closed, he was still willing to prepare another order for us while cleaning up. That kind of service is rare and deeply appreciated.

The food was absolutely delicious, and as a kind gesture, he even gave me the remaining smoothie from the blender that he had made for my friend. It was a small touch, but it spoke volumes about the kind of people running this place.

Great food, great vibes, and truly outstanding service. I’ll definitely be coming back and highly recommend this spot to anyone looking for a genuine and flavorful dining experience.

I got the goat stew for my daughter and me. They were sold out of injeras, but the owner offered to substitute with rice and I was hesitant. Worried about the rice being dry. The aroma from the kitchen smelled so good, I decided to take a chance and order anyways. I am so glad I did! Everything was amazing!! The goat was tender, the cabbage and salad complimented the stew very well, and the rice was delicious. My toddler ate it all. We will definitely be back for more!

Fantastic food! We had the lamb shank plate (which was beautifully seasoned), and loved it so much we ordered a second one! We also had a berry smoothie that was fab! No added sugar or dairy and it was sweet and tasty! Thank you Alleamin!

formatted_address: 4225 Rainier Ave S, Seattle, WA 98118, United States
name: Lil Red Takeout & Catering

reviews.text: The food was delicious especially the pork sliders. But the only menu is on the top wall of the cashier. There is no printed copy to read while ordering at the counter. I went there at around 4 pm on Sunday afternoon. There was no one before me. But I had to wait for 30 mins for my order. The customers came after me were chatting and laughing very loudly in the waiting area with no consideration for other customers. The TV also played very loudly. So it was very uncomfortable to stay in the waiting room for such a long time. There are some tables outside of the restaurant, but no use while raining. So it is best to call and order, and then pickup later in order to avoid the long wait and the terrible environment. But I would just avoid it all together.

A co-worker took me here for his going away lunch. I got the ribs and mac and cheese. I would give the ribs a 4 out of 5. They were tender, juicy and meaty. But the Mac & Cheese was a 10 out of 5. Yes you heard me right a 10 out of 5. This was the best Mac & Cheese I've ever had in my life and I've had my fair share. I wish I could make a big batch of this for myself at home. This place isn't cheap but if the food is good it's all good to me. I will definitely be back. I plan on bringing my dad next time. So I can see the look on his face when he tries this Mac & Cheese!

My brother was in the mood for jerk chicken, and so we dropped in for some great food. I ordered some pulled pork sliders but received the pulled pork meal, which I really enjoyed. The garlic mashed potatoes were savory, the cole slaw was a little dry but good, and the cornbread was tiny but also very good. My brother had the oxtail, with garlic mashed potatoes and some greens that he enjoyed. Some sides we had were the jerk pork that were to die for, and some red beans n rice that were tasty.  The banana pudding was to die for, I almost ordered another, but I was so stuffed.

Unreal Jamican/BBQ!!! Nice workers/owner. I absolutely loved this place. Big portions and good prices for BBQ. I will definitely be returning and spreading the good word about lil Red's. Don't forget - the BBQ sauce and jerk sauce were off the charts. Well done, guys. This place is the truth - top tier 👌.
Learned about Lil Reds on tik tok before our Seattle vacation, couldn’t wait to try it! It was everything and more! Amazing food and wonderful service!

formatted_address: 2201 Rainier Ave S, Seattle, WA 98144, United States
name: Buddha Bruddah Seattle

reviews.text:
Super impressed with the portion sizing, large scoops and big plates is always a welcome surprise.
Love that the Thai tea is more than 16oz and it's very well flavored. I got the buttermilk katsu chicken and the coating is crispy and delicious.

Sadly, I had asked for a side of gravy and a side of teriyaki sauce and ended up with two sides of gravy so that was a little bit disappointing.
I also asked for and paid for double macaroni on one of our dinners and both arrived with the same single scoop of macaroni.

Overall love the flavor, quality, and servings of the food.

Adore the convenience of the packaging for their chili sauces.

Wish that there was a little bit more accuracy to the customerizations on orders.

We had the privilege of having Buddah Bruddah cater our wedding 2 weeks ago.  To start with Drea was a dream to communicate with.  It was mostly through email but we did have a phone call a week or two prior to the wedding to just make sure we were on the same page and go over final details.  The team was so nice and did an amazing job.  They catered apps during cocktail hour, provided bartending, had a delicious buffet dinner (Huli Huli chicken, Hawaiian Beef, rice, Mac salad, stir fried veggies, an delish sauces), water service, bussing, and even offered to put out our cake and cupcakes when it came time. I had so many compliments from our guests, several telling me it was the best wedding food they had ever had. To be honest they were so great that I feel like I barely interacted with them at all.  That's how good they were!

Anything to do with a wedding these days is soooooo expensive and I feel like for the food and services they provided the pricing was amazing.  Thank you Drea and team for adding to our special day!

We ended up coming here for dinner last Saturday after not finding any Korean spots nearby. Surprisingly, the food was pretty good! The place is neat and cozy with a laid-back, casual vibe. It’s not exactly authentic Thai, but more of a Thai-inspired spot.
We ordered the chicken katsu plate (which came with mac salad and coleslaw) and a Hawaiian-style beef dish. Both tasted good and were filling.

One downside is that we were really hungry and noticed that guests who arrived after us got their food first. Also, my dish wasn’t served hot instead, just warm, which was a bit disappointing.
There was plenty of parking in the backyard.

Overall, still a nice place to grab a casual meal.

I live in the neighborhood and this has been my most frequented local take out for the past 5 years. The owners are kind people. I wish I could say ive tried more of the menu but I cant not order the fried garlic basil chicken. Its my comfort meal!
I must also their amazing hot sauces. I especially recommend the ones with fish sauce, they have a crazy amount of flavor!

We ordered the huli chicken & short rib combo plate, which was enough for my husband and me. The place was nearly empty and the food came out really fast. First bite and my feet started tapping on the floor happily 😊 10 outta 10 will be back!

formatted_address: 1800 E Yesler Wy, Seattle, WA 98122, United States
name: Soulful Dishes

reviews.text: We were at the main Goodwill in Seattle and I decided to look for "cheap food near me" and this place popped up. Its in a run down store but the owner was super nice. The food was amazing. Everything was cooked and seasoned perfectly. If you are looking for some Southern Food this is the place to go. We had the Seafood Plate and the Chicken Tenders Plate. We had enough food to make two meals out of each plate.

Our big group of 9 came in right before closing time and it was a one man show for the staff on March 27, 2025.  I can’t remember his name but he was so patient and kind to us from the beginning to end.  We even asked him to take a photo with us.

We loved everything we ordered and we didn’t have to wait too long for our food.  A few things on the menu were not available such as fried oysters.  Free street parking.  Family owned business so stop by to support them whenever you come to the area or near by.

Food was delicious! You can tell it’s homemade. I had the cod beans and rice with slaw. Fish was so fresh and flasky and not ton of breading! My daughter had the Sammy burger..fries were cut from potatoes, first time I see that at a restaurant! A bit spicy for my daughter though. Simple, air conditioned and great kind service!

On Saturday, June 7, 2025, my sister and I decided to embark on a venture and try a new restaurant in the Central District area. We were in the mood for  soul food and opted to try Soulful Dishes. There was zero parking, and we parked a few blocks away.  Upon entry, the ambiance was cold & left much to be desired.  Also, there was no greeting or welcome whatsoever. Matter of fact, no one was ever present at the service counter. We waited a long time before a guy came out, he was the only one there. He did not apologize for the wait,  introduce himself,  or even offer any dinner suggestions. He just stood there with a blank expression.

There was no scent of food or any way to tell if anything was actually being cooked. I did hear the microwave beeping in the background after we ordered. We made our selections and sat down.  I ordered fried catfish, Mac-n-Cheese, and the potato salad.  My sister ordered the chicken tenders, Mac-n-Cheese, and the collard greens.

I liked the potato salad.  The Mac-n-Cheese was okay. The chicken tenders were okay. The collard greens were flavorful and tasty.  My catfish however,  was undercooked, and wet in the center. I was displeased and did not finish my meal.  The portions were very small to be so costly as it was.

As someone who is honest, direct and to the point, I told the guy that my food was not right and he just stood there with that glazed eyes/blank expression.

It was not a great experience so I would not recommend Soulful Dishes.  Worse, my stomach was very upset after eating there (my only meal of the day), and that lasted through the night.   We will not be returning.   This was our experience at Soulful Dishes.  Bad choice.

I’m gonna say my first visit was a good visit. The food was tasty and the service was very good. I can appreciate the young man Christian and his chef for accommodating my requests, and I look forward to going back to try some more of their menu.
Today I had the hot link burger, and the seafood platter plate-I chose the catfish and it comes with jumbo shrimp, I substituted my fries for collard greens and I would have had candied yams, but they were out so I tried the red beans and rice. Go check them out.

formatted_address: 1519 14th Ave, Seattle, WA 98122, United States
name: Nue

reviews.text:
Nue is a quirky and fascinating restaurant that truly takes you around the globe. You’re surrounded by eclectic international gadgets and trinkets, and it’s genuinely fun to look around while waiting for your meal.

Speaking of food, it was exceptional. I don’t know how one restaurant can perfect so many cuisines. The cornbread is sweet and fluffy 🤤. The South African curry served in traditional bread is a beautiful balance of sweet and nutty, and the Balinese ribs are saucy, tender, and generously meaty. The addition of peanuts on the ribs is a total hit.

Our server was incredibly kind and offered spot-on food and drink recommendations. Their drinks are also unique and absolutely delicious!

The food here is unforgettable—bold flavors that feel like eating at your grandma’s house with all your cousins gathered around the table. The ribs were tender and rich, and the Ethiopian injera platter was tangy, playful, and perfect for sharing. Every dish carries a soulfulness that keeps me coming back.

I truly wanted to give a five-star review, but I ran into a problem with the sangria. If you’re going to charge for a carafe, please give your guests the true value—not a carafe full of ice. On my last visit, it arrived so packed with ice that it only poured three glasses, compared to the generous carafe I enjoyed before. When I raised this, the server initially dismissed me in a way that made me feel like my integrity was being doubted, which was disappointing.

To his credit, he did backtrack and apologize after I said I would just write a review. Still, if the carafe can’t consistently deliver value, it should be removed from the menu rather than charging guests the same as individual drinks. BTW-that is a picture of the first carafe from the week prior. My phone died before taking a picture of the iced carafe.

That said, I still love this place. The flavors are powerful, comforting, and full of heart. When the service rises to match the excellence of the food, this restaurant shines as one of the best dining experiences anywhere.

We enjoyed the fried chicken wings tower! The brussel sprouts were nicely crispy and good with sauce. The pineapple cornbread was sadly really salty.
We came on a holiday Sunday and there was only one chef working. Had to wait a lonnng time for any food.
Will be back to try their chicken wings happy hour!

All servers were nice and all food was really good! I wasn’t expecting it to be as good from the names or the pictures I saw online but they are all worth the try! The price is definitely on the high end so up to your discretion

Our waitress Lopez was great 🩷
we didn’t like the other 2 female workers there. Besides that interesting restaurant with a lot to see inside and has outdoor patio seatings too . Mixture of diff cultures and diff music. We heard Spanish, Chinese, and English all mixed in.
The wing tower was great little spicy! They can’t give you other flavors once dinner hits. The roti was good too the curry was citrus flavored it was different! They had fresh lemonades and Arnold Palmer’s little watered down but atleast fresh made . The
The bathroom was like a little maze coming out lol. The food was like Indian finger food vibe where you can taste the cumin.
The wings was great little spicy! They can’t give you other flavors once dinner. The kids did enjoy the Australian fairy bread dessert for my bf birthday 🎉

formatted_address: 3656 34th Ave W, Seattle, WA 98199, United States
name: Kaspars Catering & Events

reviews.text: Kaspers staff did an amazing job in preparing and serving our office for our onsite holiday brunch. They were professional, courteous, and my event went off without a hitch. I can't wait to work with them again in the future. The food was delicious and it's obvious the staff loves what they do.

They did the catering for our wedding and it was FANTASTIC food. We had plenty of options to pick from and tried out the dishes and cocktails prior to the event. Kaspars did all the linens/set-up/take-down as well as the bar services and tray delivered hors d'oeuvres. We did buffet style but table service was also an option. Jen was so much fun to work with and it really felt like having another friend there at our wedding on the day of.

We had such a great experience with Kaspars Catering! They were prompt, professional, and a joy to work with from start to finish. The food was amazing and beautifully presented. Their team handled everything seamlessly, the cleanup was spotless and the staff was so friendly and attentive. A special shout-out to Sarah, who was lovely to coordinate with and made the whole process smooth and stress-free. Highly recommend!

Kaspars did an amazing job catering our wedding. From the get-go, they were responsive to emails and answered all of our questions even before we'd decided to book them.

On our wedding day, not only was the food excellent, but the service was fantastic. They were extremely attentive to me and my now-husband and to my guests. They knew their stuff, like suggesting that for our cake cutting, we cut the cake beforehand and then do a faux cut for pictures. This is something that would never have occurred to us.

They even went so far as to make sure my little nephew's chicken entree was cut up and had the sauce on the side. My nephew told his dad that the chicken was way better than what his dad makes, a true compliment! They also made sure to send me and my husband home with lots of food so we could really sit down and enjoy it.

Overall, I would highly recommend Kaspars if you're looking for catering for your wedding!

Thank you Kaspars for catering our wedding at JM Cellars, where they are one of the few preferred vendors allowed.

We worked with Sarah, who was fantastic and fun! She is very responsive and quickly answered all of our many (many) questions along the way. She did a great job helping us curate a menu that fit what we wanted. Kaspars has a fantastic working relationship with our venue and our planners, and have a great reputation among the greater seattle wedding vendors. They also provided us with bartending services and cocktails: espresso martinis and margaritas which were a huge hit with our guests.

As a vegetarian marrying a meat-eater, we wanted options that everyone would enjoy and Kaspars had BY FAR the best and largest vegetarian selection of any caterer we reached out to! We were able to put together a menu to satisfy everyone, and the food and service was top notch. We received so many compliments on the meal!

Thank you Sarah and Kaspers for the wonderful wedding day!

formatted_address: 2004 Westlake Ave, Seattle, WA 98101, United States
name: FareStart Restaurant

reviews.text: Loved it. The meal was amazing. The restaurant was warm and inviting with sparkles of candlelight and bright holiday music. Best part was the staff, students and volunteers.  Everyone was so attentive, helpful, and kind.

BEYOND AMAZING!
We didn’t know about this GEM in the middle of the city. Service has been outstanding, the food was marvelous, everything we asked for was done in the best way possible.
Extremely recommended for its amazing quality in food, excellent prices and service. The place is very clean and beautiful as well, we loved the rustic but modern, clean, calm and spacious aesthetic. It’s gorgeous how the sun comes through the big glass windows and hits every corner just right. Good and relaxed lo-fi chill ambience music in a very comfortable volume, you can enjoy it while working or studying, having brunch alone or in company, doesn’t compete with anything and no awkward silence.
We’re very grateful to have come across it on our trip through Seattle, already saved the place to revisit if we’re back in the city and we’re already thinking coming back tomorrow.
Do yourself a favor and do not miss FareStart if you’re passing by Seattle🙌🏽
I was genuinely disappointed with the food during my visit. While the staff were friendly and the restaurant was clean and welcoming, the meal itself fell short of expectations.
I love this place. It's great for lunch with some tasty affordable options and the staff are always lovely! Plus you have to love the mission!

Where else are you going to get a DELICIOUS burger and fries in Seattle for $15 at lunch time? Not to mention get to enjoy it in a delightful atmosphere. The new remodel is awesome, there’s tons of space, the food comes out fast and hot, and the staff are sweet and accommodating. Best of all? You’re supporting one of the best non-profits in the city. So what are you waiting for? If you work in SLU you owe it to yourself to grab a coffee or lunch here!

I was going to take a photo of my burger and fries but I ate it too fast, it was that good!

formatted_address: 2243 Mission St, San Francisco, CA 94110, United States
name: Bissap Baobab SF

reviews.text:
Delicious food in a large and fun space! They have both indoor and outdoor seating areas.
They offer flavorful dishes at a reasonable price. The drink menu also looked really good. the staff were nice and friendly and helped us navigate the menu.
The only improvement would be to increase the amount of fish, it was a very small piece of protein for that dish.
Had a great time here with some friends. There was a amazing DJ and they had some cool vendors. I bout some records form one of them

I knew Bissap for having eaten there before. It’s always a great vibe with good food, and one of the most fun place in SF in my opinion.

I recently asked them to cater the drink for my traditional and white weddings. I bought a dozen gallons of Bissap and ginger juice from them. The communication with Marco Senghor was outstanding, the juices were delicious, and they were extremely flexible and thoughtful.

Overall if you want some hospitality and sense of community teranga style THIS IS THE PLACE! I highly recommend!

Delicious food in a great atmosphere! Remember to make reservations on the weekends. The food was very delicious, had shrimp appetizer, fish curry and lamp. Their rice was also every good!

This place turns into a dance bar at night, we didn't stay for it but looked fun!

rare west african restaurant in the heart of the mission district serving authentic dishes at a good price! would love to come back for one of their DJ or dance nights. really felt like a community in there.

mafe with chicken and fufu: first time trying fufu and really enjoyed. chicken was nicely grilled and loved the mafe sauce.

plaintains: perfectly made, just the right sweetness level

formatted_address: level facing water fountain, 4 Embarcadero Ctr, San Francisco, CA 94111, United States
name: Teranga

reviews.text: FANTASTIC maafe stew, especially with the chillier weather in San Francisco! Tastes like an expertly made home-cooked meal infused with a ton of pride and love. The owner Nafy is super sweet, as is the delicious complimentary tamarind cider I was handed while waiting for my meal to be prepped! Looking forward to my return.

Such a hidden gem!! I was hunting for a different restaurant in the Embarcadero Center when I walked past Teranga and was drawn in by the aroma of spices. Another patron wrapping up his meal saw us pause and told us Teranga had the best food in the Center and we just HAD to eat there. He was absolutely right.

Food:
I decided to get their yassa bowl with chickpeas, and my friend got their feijoada with chicken. The yassa bowl was outstanding — super flavorful with perfectly spiced chickpeas, tons of caramelized onions, and roasted veggies over a bed of fluffy white rice. If you enjoy caramelized onions, you’ll love this dish. The feijoada was also outstanding; it was extremely rich and comforting with perfectly spiced black beans and a nice pop of sweetness from the sweet potatoes.

Ambiance:
There isn’t a ton of seating inside, but there are plenty of communal tables that belong to the Center right outside.

Servie:
The owner is also incredibly sweet! She walked us through the menu, gave great recommendations, and gave us free samples of tamarind cider as we were waiting. I can’t wait to come back and try more things — the other patron really knew what he was talking about.

The food here is delicious! There was a little bit of a wait to get our food, but it was incredibly worth it. There are limited seats inside, but it makes for a cozy atmosphere and the food was easy to carry out if needed. I'm so glad we stopped to try this place and very sad we don't live close enough to visit it again. The tamarind cider and the flatbread were my favorite!

New to the Embarcadero Teranga is a gem in the heart of San Francisco! I had the hot tamarind cider which was delicious and unlike anything I've had before. The beef samosa was packed with rich, flavorful filling and a perfectly crisp shell. The standout was the Djolof rice with chicken deeply spiced and hearty, definitely enough for two people. I would also highly recommend the Teranga brownie is dense, fudgy, and topped with just the right touch of spice. Will definitely add this to my lunch rotation!

A Taste of Senegal

I went out for lunch and planned to try a Korean restaurant I had heard about. On my way there, I saw a sign for a Senegalese restaurant called Teranga. Since I had never tried Senegalese food, I decided to try it.

I had no idea what to order when I entered, so I asked the lady behind the counter for a recommendation. She suggested a dish, and even though I didn't pay much attention to the name, I decided to try it. The gentleman behind the counter seemed to approve of my choice, which made me feel confident.

I received a Maafe Bowl, a traditional Senegalese peanut stew with butternut, sweet potatoes, and carrots served over Jasmine rice. It was medium spicy and delicious.

As I was leaving, the lady offered me a small shot of tamarind cider and some boiled peanuts to try, which I enjoyed.

Teranga is a small take-out place, but on a nice day, you can sit outside at one of the tables around Embarcadero Plaza and enjoy your meal with a great view. The staff is friendly, and the place is very clean. If you're in the area, I highly recommend giving the menu a good look - delicious food!

formatted_address: 907 Irving St, San Francisco, CA 94122, United States
name: New Eritrea Restaurant

reviews.text:
The food was very good. The way they cook their meats, stews, and even the potatoes has flavors that feel somewhat familiar to Latin American cooking, which made the dishes easy to enjoy. Nothing extremely out of the ordinary, but definitely a pleasant experience and a great way to try something different.

The ambience was very nice — warm, relaxed, and with a comfortable atmosphere. The decoration throughout the restaurant added to the experience.

The service was normal. Nothing bad, nothing exceptional, just straightforward and efficient.

Overall, a good place to try new flavors and enjoy a different style of cuisine.

I loved the food. This was my first time trying Eritrean food which is not surprising since the county is only two years older than I am. The food is very similar to Ethiopian food which is to be expected but I definitely detected nuances in the flavor profile that were distinct. However, I don't think I could verifiably state those differences. I was expecting a more spartan atmosphere but the design inside the restaurant was modern. The food was absolutely delicious and the service was praiseworthy. The price isn't too bad for being steps away from Golden Gate Park.

Tried a new ethiopian restaurant after really long time. Food was great! We got the vegetarian platters for two with the chicken. We also got the mixed veg sambusa. I think the lentil sambusa would have been a better choice.

Service was a little slow but they seemed a little understaffed at the time on a Friday night. I was not expecting the restaurant to be as large as it was.

This is my first time eating Ethiopian food, and I wasn't impressed. Got what seemed to be the most popular dish, which is basically some bread with dips. Maybe this is an acquired taste? Service was almost inexistent, as well as silverware. When the waitress finally brought some, at the end of my meal, after I had requested twice before, felt more like a sarcastic joke than compliance to a customer request. Should I have gotten up and asked for a manager? Maybe, but I also don't go out to cause trouble. Especially when I am hungry. Definitely overpriced for what you are getting.
They offer numerous vegetable and meat options. Enjoyed everything we had--cooked well with distinctive spices. Was all very tasty. The waitstaff was very friendly.

formatted_address: 121 9th St, San Francisco, CA 94103, United States
name: Moya

reviews.text:
Moya is a superb spot for Ethiopian food in this part of the city. Came here after another spot nearby was closed unexpectedly and so glad we did.

We came right as they opened for dinner so the service was quick and easy.

The food came out in less than ten minutes and what a feast it was. The vegan sampler platter was enormous contrary to the photo of it looking like a grain bowl. Everything on it from the greens to the lentils was full of flavor and absolutely delicious. Enough to feed 2+ people for sure.

I also had ordered a spicy tofu dish as well and THAT was something else. I don't see tofu being used often in Ethiopian restaurants but this was really a hit. Savory, spicy, and filling.

Our meal came with a side of injera and I was shocked at how fast it came out too. The quality of the injera was great too and made for the perfect vessel to get all the tasty food in our mouths.

Amazing Ethiopian food! We got the vegetarian samplers, the chicken and the beef. Everything was delicious and really well packaged for delivery. The injera was so fresh, and the perfect accompaniment to all the tasty dishes. Mel was also super friendly, helpful and kind. Strongly recommend/will be back!

As a tourist from Illinois who was fiending for Ethiopian food, Moya did not disappoint. I’ve only had Ethiopian food three times in my life: once when I was 16 in Milwaukee, another when I was 21 in Nashville, and now at 27, I got the chance to have it in San Francisco. The service is top-tier, the kik alicha was flavorful and filling, and the vibe was great. If I’m ever in SF again, this is the first place I’ll go. Women-owned, affordable, and quality.
The food was amazing. Gluten free injera was freshly made and came with small extra cost. Vegan sampler was so good. I would even recommend not getting any meat and sharing two samplers.

Delicious Ethiopian food with a good variety of options - it was difficult to decide so I went with the veggie sampler and it was a great mix of everything. The staff even gave our group a sample of a dish we wanted to try.  The meals are a little pricey but the portions are large and come with lots of injera. We left very full and will definitely come back!

formatted_address: 2640 Mason St, San Francisco, CA 94133, United States
name: KAYMA Algerian Eatery

reviews.text:
One of the best food experiences I have ever had in San Fransisco. Very vegetarian friendly with outstanding service. I got the “Earthy Eats” bowl, which was phenomenal and the mushrooms were some of the best I’ve ever had. The green tea with pine nuts was perfect on a cold night! Leave room for dessert as well, as the Baklava was delicious.
The owners are incredibly welcoming and made this a date night to remember!

Chicken skewer plate was tender and delicious.  Sahara tea with pine nuts was just the perfect drink on a rainy day.  We all loved the fries and sandwiches.  The baguette they used to make the sandwiches was really fresh and French-bakery quality👍🏼

The food is incredible. I come to SF often and I’m gonna make sure to grab a meal here every time I visit. The owners are very sweet and hospitable. I’m bringing my wife with me next time I visit. Great authentic Algerian food 10/10.
Best food in entire San Francisco area. Brother Mounir , the owner, makes you feel like being in your own home. Food is so flavorful and delicious that you can’t even stop eating. Must Try.

Loved it!! Super flavorful and satisfying. Will definitely come back whenever I’m in SF 😎😎

I got the chicken casse-croǔte sandwich but the beef one is also really good!

formatted_address: 295 Eddy St, San Francisco, CA 94102, United States
name: Z Zoul Cafe

reviews.text: Small restaurant and good for a quick meal in SF. We got the  roasted chicken plate, hummus and lentil soup. A pretty good value (~$20). The soup that comes with the chicken is not great and it looks like frozen veggies were used for that one, but the lentil soup was amazing. Will recommend for homely, hearty meals.

I was walking around Tenderloin and came across this restaurant. I was like oh I have never tried Sudanese food  and Halal!
so I walked into it and lo and behold’ the food was so good like you you could smell from just the air in the room and I ordered the lamb shank and the meat was so tender. They also offered a complimentary soup on the side, which was really spicy, it really made me miss home.

Small restaurant and good for a quick lunch in SF. The Lamb shank plate seems like their signature and is a pretty good value (~$20). Soup comes with it but is on the salty side - can mix together with the rice. The rice is a really large plate and I can only finish half of the rice.

Z Zoul Cafe is delicious and decently priced. Cam in looking for a taste of Sudanese food. While there could be a bit more variety for traditional dishes, I was satisfied with both of my visits so far.   Excellent price and values. Tasty plates and wraps. My recent visit was for a beef kebab plate. But ended up getting a Kofta plate instead. (yes there is a difference) Everything plated was delicious and satisfying.

I visited Z Zoul Cafe in San Francisco and really enjoyed the experience. I tried the falafel wrap and the shawarma wrap, along with their special hibiscus drink. Everything tasted fresh and flavorful. The hibiscus juice was especially refreshing and unique. It’s a nice spot if you’re looking to try something different with Sudanese flavors.

formatted_address: 1130 4th St, San Francisco, CA 94158, United States
name: House of Tadu Ethiopian Kitchen

reviews.text: What a great restaurant! The food is amazing! I love that you use the spongy, thin, bread to grab the food and eat that way. They also provide forks if you choose not to eat the traditional way. But they have a great menu with meat or vegetarian options. The sambussas are so good and have a little spice to them and the sauce they serve with them is amazing and spicy! Also love having Ethiopian beer with it. And finished it off with an Ethiopian tea. Can't wait to go back and try other items.

a cute modern n clean restaurant! i ordered the tofu tibs and the man at the counter recommended the spicy lentil dip as my side; it all came with enjera and side salad. the enjera arrived in 3 mins and the rest of the food took around 20, even though I was the only one there, that’s how you know they made it fresh!!! and it was so worth the wait. the salad had a healthy amount of olive oil, n the tofu tibs were actually insane. i’ve had ethiopian food before and nothing i’ve had was this flavorful and just plain delicious, the tofu was crunchy and sautéed with onions and bell peppers the depth of flavor was AMAZING. this is was so unexpectedly delicious the perfect combo of crunch and flavor. the spicy lentil dip was genuinely spicy and paired well w the enjera. the price to portion ratio was fair for san francisco. the bathroom was clean too. this was one of the best meals of my life and i wasn’t even hungry that’s how you know it’s good!

I was jonsing for Injera while watching a baseball game at Oracle park.  This place is walking distance from the stadium.  As a kid I was invited to my Ethiopian friends family gatherings and the food at House of Tadu Ethiopian kitchen brought so many childhood memories.  I had the meat combo platter.  The flavors were exactly what I remembered and the Injera was on point ❤️
I ordered the meat combo and got the gluten free injera. Everything was amazing! Loved this place!

We got the Bozena Shiro and the Meat Combo, as well as the Sambussa appetizer. I did not have any experience with Ethiopian food, but was curious to try. Everything was delicious and exceeded any expectations I had. The staff was friendly and helped me decide what to eat. Definitely would eat here again!

formatted_address: 484 Ellis St, San Francisco, CA 94102, United States
name: Tadu Ethiopian Kitchen

reviews.text: I’ve been to 2 famous Ethiopian restaurants, and both were quite greasy and heavy for me, so I was surprised that Tadu's dishes are not like that at all. The food is super fresh, with on-point, balanced seasoning. The sambusa is really tasty with an addictive dipping sauce. The smaller vegetarian with injera is filling and good to share between 2. Highly recommend trying their spice teas, coffee, and especially Telba (ground flaxseed and honey drink). The owner is really kind to offer me an injera refill without extra charge. Definitely come back next time!
Excellent Ethiopian food! I have dined here several times over the years and it is always very tasty. Glad they reopened  here at this location. I hope to come back again soon. I had the beef tibs.

We loved the food so much that we came two days in a row! The Beef Berbere Banatu, Derek Tibs, Special Kitfo, and all the sides were absolutely incredible. The service was excellent, and the owner, Elias, was the best host. We’ll definitely be coming back again!

Stumbled upon Tadu Ethiopian Kitchen while exploring San Francisco and decided to give Ethiopian food a try for the first time — and I’m glad I did! I went with the Meat Combination plate, featuring minchet abish, gomen besiga, and lamb alicha wot. Each dish had its own unique flavor, and the injera brought everything together beautifully.

The spices were well-balanced — flavorful without being too spicy — and the textures were satisfying. It was a totally new experience for me.

Humble and modest restaurant offering Ethiopian food.
It was my first time tasting Ethiopian food so don't have any yardstick to measure the quality on this one.
I found the food to be delicious. It's a unique and meticulous melange of spices and meat.
They got reasonably wide variety of vegetarian food.

formatted_address: 878 Valencia St, San Francisco, CA 94110, United States
name: Cafe Ethiopia

reviews.text: Absolutely loved every dish! I tried the Zigni, Tibsie beef, and fish, all were packed with flavor. This was my first time trying Ethiopian cuisine and it definitely won’t be the last!

Warm, no frills, delicious Ethiopian food! Service was just one guy, so a little slow to take our order, but food came out quick. Some of the best Ethiopian in SF! I got a honey wine / mead to go with the dinner. Been going here for the last 10 years, and will be back again soon!

Comfy place with a wide variety of Ethiopian dishes with good descriptions of each. Nice variety of vegetarian and meat dishes, and nice to have the option to order dishes individually or as combos for one person. They also seem to have a good selection of Ethiopian beers although none were available on my visit.

I am being introduced to Ethiopian cuisine with this restaurant.
I absolutely love the experience.

A shout out to all Indians - TRY Ethiopian if you haven't started already! Biriyani is love but exploring is better 🙏🏼

The main dish for the dinner was amazing. Kudos to the generous quantity as well.
Taste: 5/5.  Quantity: 5/5.  Freshness: 3/5, Value: 4/5  , Wait time: 4/5.

I felt the injera bread was not that fresh. It wasn't served hot. However it goes very well with the main dish. We ordered a mushroom and alooo peas main dish. It was really flavourful!

formatted_address: 543 Divisadero St, San Francisco, CA 94117, United States
name: Club Waziema

reviews.text: As a dive bar + Ethiopian restaurant, Waziema is the kind of slightly unusual combination that makes you glad to live in a city. It's been around for a while and every time I see it I'm glad it's still going. In fairness it's probably not the best Ethiopian food in SF but it's decent and when you're looking for a less formal meal (or just a drink) it's a good neighborhood option.

It's an eclectic dive bar but the food is really good! I was actually scared at first and almost left, LOL, but I'm glad I stayed and enjoyed a veggie platter. It's all you can eat and the food is great!

This is a gem. A dive bar that serves legit Ethiopian food? The owners are friendly and helpful. It's honestly off-putting how good this is, since they clearly just bought a neighborhood dive to make a business. I look forward to cementing this review in 30 years from now, when this place is an institution.
Stumbled up some cinco de mayo event flyer and checked out this restaurant/venue 😮. Nice vibe and will come back for the restaurant part next time

First of all, this place needs to have a better sign out front and a way of letting patrons know they serve food. I walked in here while bar hopping a while ago, and I had zero idea this place served food at night, I thought it must have been a day time thing because it is technically a bar, and nothing noticeable inside that showed they serve one of the best Ethiopian food in San Francisco.

Food, as I mentioned is great, service is good enough for a bar. It was quite empty when I walked in, maybe that's why the atmosphere didn't do it for me, but that's not going to stop me from going back there to get food again.

formatted_address: 5800 Geary Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94121, United States
name: Aziza

reviews.text: Came here for a casual brunch with the family. We ordered the two lattes, Burrata, French toasts, shrimp, and eggs Benedict. The Burrata was exceptional, except it only came with two small pieces of sour dough… I could use double the amount of bread. Everything else was good. No complaints.

We had a lovely family dinner here and an amazing experience with the kind and accommodating staff. Justin, the general manager, was so helpful and gave great recommendations for food and drink.

The restaurant was packed but we never felt that service was too slow. There was even a power outage in the middle of our meal for the entire neighborhood, but the staff handled it in stride and our dishes continued to come - beautifully plated at that!

We ordered the trio of dips (the almond one was particularly good) which came with a well spiced and chewy sumac flatbread, the burrata with carrot ginger dukkah and crusty bread that was divine, the prawns which were perfectly cooked and presented beautifully, and the cauliflower which was a standout as it tasted like an elevated cauliflower Manchurian for our starters.
Our mains were the cous cous with winter squash and the cous cous was so fluffy and creamy, as well as the whole grilled fish which was amazing and served with a side salad.
We also enjoyed the cornbread and the grilled broccolini as our sides.

We were too full for dessert and even had leftovers to go!

The drinks - cocktails and wine - were spot on, and I particularly enjoyed the desert dawn which was like an orange espresso martini.

Aziza is one of my favorite spots in the city and you can’t miss with a meal here.

Exceptional is every way! Every dish we ordered was phenomenal, truly. Not only  beautiful presentation, but unique and delicious flavors. Great vibe, friendly staff, and very good mocktail and wine list too. Best dishes included the cauliflower (wow!!) and the cornbread (melt in your mouth good!!)!! Highly recommend!

After our dinner service at Aziza, we were left with very mixed feelings about the place. Our seating was the high top communal table, which on its own is fine. What is not fine, however, is barely leaving any space between parties and forcing people to sit very closely together. We thankfully had some space between us and the other parties at the table, but that was only because a couple that was supposed to be next to us was upset and got relocated somewhere else. Otherwise our waiter was splendid, and the service was decent overall.

Moving onto the food, we ordered sumac flatbread, trio of spreads, charred prawns, basteeya, shakshuka, and couscous -- served in that order.. Aziza started off incredibly strong with the flatbread and spreads; the flavors were bold and vibrant, and the bread tasted freshly baked. The prawns were solid as well, with the green apples adding a nice touch. But after such an impressive start, the basteeya didn’t quite keep the pace. We were told that it's the restaurant’s signature dish, but it felt a bit more familiar than expected rather than something particularly standout. It was still a solid dish, just not as special as we had hoped.

Around the time we finished the basteeya, the restaurant became noticeably busier, and we ended up waiting quite a while for the shakshuka and couscous. Maybe it was coincidence, but it definitely felt like the kitchen slowed down once the influx of guests arrived. When they did come out, both dishes were enjoyable, though once again they leaned more toward straightforward and familiar than anything especially distinctive.

If the restaurant can sort out the communal table spacing and smooth out the pacing of the meal, I’d be more than happy to return. With service as warm and attentive as we experienced, I’d certainly look forward to coming back.

The ambience of this restaurant was fantastic. The food was great quality and flavorful. Dishes took some time to come, but it was a great opportunity to chat and you know everything is made to order. Loved the braised short rib, mussels, lamb shank, octopus and corn bread.

formatted_address: 1303 Polk St, San Francisco, CA 94109, United States
name: Aicha Moroccan Cuisine

reviews.text:
We were in town to visit. My family was in the mood for Moroccan cuisine. Specifically looking for bastilla. We walked in and were seated. We ordered a chicken bastilla and a veggie bastilla to start. For the meal we got a chicken tagine,a lamb kebab,and a veggie couscous.
The bastilla was nicely seasoned ,I really liked the sweet and savory taste. It has a dusting of powder sugar and cinnamon on top.The chicken tagine was fall off the bone tender. The couscous portion was big enough for 2 people. The kabob was ok. It could have used more salt.
My only negative was the bastilla, I'm pretty sure that they microwaved it to heat it up and finished it up in the broiler.(I understand as I worked in a restaurant. Sometimes to save time you pre make items. I just wanted it to be warmed longer and kept under the broiler longer. Mine was a little cold in spots)
Ive gone here multiple times, sometimes solo and sometimes with friends; this place never misses the mark. every dish ive tried here has been amazing. The chicken couscous keeps me coming back.

We had a delicious lamb kebab and vegetarian tagine.  The food is excellent but it’s not a place for a romantic first date. You go for the food not ambiance.  There is a lot of noise… every time a person enters the restaurant a beep is triggered.  From the kitchen area is a constant beeping noise from, I think, online orders.  But noise aside, the food is great!

Seafood Bastille is average. Way too much oil in the fry. Very little seafood.

Chicken Tagine is excellent as is the bread with  it. Slightly higher salt.

Mint tea came with sugar but was replaced without when requested. tasted good without the sugar.

Nice little spot. Good decor.

Friendly and efficient service.

The food was quite good though the service was a bit odd.
Ordered the Mint Tea but it just never showed up. Shame really

formatted_address: 1419 Fillmore St, San Francisco, CA 94115, United States
name: Sheba Jazz Lounge

reviews.text: What a quaint place, nestled in the Filmore District, that offers great nightly jazz entertainment, reasonably priced drinks and American and African cuisine. The Sisters that operate this lounge are so welcoming. I tried the Injera, for the first time.  Injera is an Ethopian style sponge flatbread. I encourage everyone to stop by and experience the vibes for yourself.  Wonderful atmosphere.

Netsanet was an amazing host!! And it was such a pleasure meeting her and her sister Israel, both are the owners. They all made sure that my friends and I were taken care of. Everyone was pleasant, attentive and gave amazing customer service! And OMG the food and drinks were amazing!!!! Top tier!!
I was celebrating my 40th birthday, visiting from Chicago!! 1st time in San Francisco. The entire staff and guests there sang happy birthday to me!!! Made me feel so special. I will definitely be back on my next visit. Thank you all so much for making my experience an amazing one!!

uch a cute restaurant with such good food and vibes! Came here for dinner with friends and loved that they had vegan options lol. I got the lentil and injira and it was sooo good! a little spicier then anticipated but still so yum and filling! Also loved that they had jazz playing through the night (can’t really see them though because of the layout). Also waited like 40 min from when we ordered to when we got out food which was a bit of a letdown but other than that no complaints!

Best Ethiopian I’ve ever had. Ordered the following:
Doro wat
Tibs wat
Misir wat
Lentil and beef sambusa

tibs wat and lentil sambusa were my favorites. Loved the live Jazz band as well!

we ordered the veggie sampler and the mushroom and spicy lentils sambusas and everything was DELICIOUS!!! so so so flavorful, some of the best ethiopian i’ve had in the bay!! and the live jazz was the icing on the cake (although it did start about 40 min late)

formatted_address: 101 Horne Ave, San Francisco, CA 94124, United States
name: Radio Africa Kitchen

reviews.text: Wow…this was some of the best food I had in SanFrancisco, hands down. You can tell the owner puts a lot of love into the food. I got the prawns over couscous, salad, and hibiscus drink. The food was made to order and super fresh. The chef was timely, attentive, and had a great sense of urgency. He made the food in minutes. It was so flavorful. The space itself was very inviting. There were books to read, spaces to work, and larger table settings for groups of people. I was so impressed with everything I ate. The portions were also really generous. This was a great escape from pricy, hyped up, city eateries. It’s truly a gem and an A1 establishment.
Only got takeout, but so far so good. Delicious couscous with shrimp. Prices are very reasonable and the setting itself is nice. Great quick preparation of the food.
What a beautiful little African cuisine. It's exquisite for its meals and the guy at the front is very charming and helpful.  I would definately come back again.
Amazing food. Great flavor and impeccable technique. Love it. The hot sauce is extra good.

The setting is pleasant, wonderful service every visit.  My first visit I tried the wild salmon, mixed green (kale, chard and spinach) and cous cous as well as black eyed peas with greens. If you like a kick of spuce be sure to ask for the hot sauce.......DELIGHTFUL

formatted_address: 1327 Peralta St, Oakland, CA 94607, United States
name: Swahili Spot

reviews.text:
We recently had the pleasure of having Swahili Spot cater our company lunch in Palo Alto, and the experience was nothing short of phenomenal! From start to finish, the entire process was seamless, and the food was an absolute delight.

Chef Priscilla Mkenda is a gem and a joy to work with. She was incredibly friendly, punctual, and went above and beyond to ensure all our needs were accommodated. She effortlessly catered to a variety of dietary considerations, providing delicious spicy, non-spicy, gluten-free, and vegetarian options that satisfied everyone on our team.

The food itself was absolutely fantastic—delicious, fresh, and bursting with authentic Tanzanian, Ugandan, and Kenyan flavors. We received countless compliments from our colleagues, who all agreed that it was one of the best catered lunches we've ever had. The quality and portion sizes were exceptional, especially for the price.

Swahili Spot is truly a unique find in the Bay Area, offering a taste of East African cuisine that is hard to come by. We would highly recommend Chef Priscilla to anyone looking for a memorable, delicious, and affordable catering experience and would absolutely work with her again in the future. Thanks, Priscilla and team!

I recently enjoyed a catered lunch from this local place. Never eaten East African cuisine before and definitely not familiar with it,I was skeptical at first..Once the lids came off and I got a whiff of that aroma, oh my goodness!

One of *THEE* best lunches I've had too date.Nothing too spicy , hearty and delicious..Absolutely perfect on a cold day or night. Warm and filling and made with love & perfection.Thankyou.

Amazing restaurant run by Priscilla a woman with Uganadan and Tanzanian roots. Try the whole fish and the chapati. I also loved the tamarind juice.

The food was super authentic and reminded me of my time in Kenya. Staff was super nice and music was great 😊

Will be back!

Took my Tanzanian exchange student there for a taste of home. Walked into a cozy place where the owner welcomed us and talked to my student and other customers as if they were good friends.
