We had the fried fish and curry dishes. Everything was so delicious--we enjoyed every bite. Especially the cabbage! Overall one of the best places I have eaten, perfectly authentic, with a wonderfully friendly atmosphere.

First time eating here. I got the Chicken Curry rice bowl with the sides and hot sauce. It was so delicious!!! Amazing. And? Next time I’ll ask for less rice and more food on top. It was pretty rice heavy and wished I’d gotten twice as many greens. And weird -  I only got one piece plantain, and?  regardless- the my meal was amazing. Service was kind and friendly.
Love this place!!!
Welcome to West Oakland!! 💕💕

formatted_address: 22431 Foothill Blvd, Hayward, CA 94541, United States
name: Golden Safari

reviews.text: Golden Safari Nigerian Restaurant offers flavorful, authentic dishes that delight the palate, showcasing the vibrant essence of Nigerian cuisine. However, the portion sizes feel modest relative to the price, resulting in moderate value for money. Service, while adequate, lacks warmth and engagement, with staff appearing somewhat distracted. As an observer, I suggest the restaurant enhance the first-time diner experience by proactively introducing signature dishes, such as jollof rice or egusi stew, to highlight their culinary strengths. Improving portion generosity and training staff to provide more attentive, welcoming service could elevate the overall experience, ensuring customers leave satisfied and eager to return.

Eaten at Golden Safari a few times and it's always very very good. I always get a Egusi with chicken, fufu, okra soup with chicken as well and jollof rice but this time I also got plantain and every single thing was spot on. I'm so happy that it's halal food and I can enjoy the deliciousness of other cultures.

First time trying Nigerian cuisine. Amazing. Waiter was helpful in guiding me to order Ebo Riro soup when they heard me order Fufu with nothing to dip it in. The GOAT was amazing. The Jollof rice was so flavorful. The chicken was also good but the GOAT was the star. Everything was so flavorful not overly salty just seasoned to perfection. I would definitely return here and am so glad I gave it a try.

I went to go try the egusi soup. It was a good but the  fufu was a little sticky/wet. The egusi soup was very good. There were people sitting in there that were really loud and their voices were echoing, so it made it extra loud in there.
Not really service with a smile, but the food is good .

Take out portions are ridiculous. Ordered the egusi and there was hardly anything in the container. So disappointed because I would have returned to patronize again the next day. Perhaps portions are better when dining, but not gonna return to find out.

formatted_address: 1498 7th St Suite B, Oakland, CA 94607, United States
name: Kojokojo Fusion

reviews.text: Very nice place. Me and my family stopped by and ate inside Service was a 10/10 highly recommend. Vibe and environment a 10/10. Jahwill was such an excellent host and made sure me and my family were comfortable. We ordered almost the whole menu the Agusi soup was delicious, oxtails was nice juicy and tender. The only thing is the goat meat could have been a bit more tender but everything was a great experience. The overall rate 9.5/10 . Also try his cold pressed juices . DELICIOUS!

We got egusi with oxtail & fufu, and a jollof rice plate. They also have a homemade sea moss drink here. The food was super flavorful and kinda felt like eating in someone's home, which we loved.

Really liked this meal and the owner is super nice!! I can see why there were so many regulars :)
Excellent flavors! Mackerel and goat were very special. Comfortable seating outside under cover. Super nice folks. Highly recommended.

My friend took me to this spot and honestly everything the great. The service was amazing, the man who helped and served us was extremely nice and accommodating towards our needs. This was my first time trying Nigerian food; we ordered the egusi soup with oxtails along with their jallof rice, and it was all amazing. I would recommend coming here if you are in the mood to try new cultural foods.

Some of the best food I've had.  Flavorful, filling and makes you feel good.  Bright and cheerful service.  Love their music too.  Just be mindful it's a bit of a rough neighborhood,  so make sure to lock your vehicle.

formatted_address: 197 Pelton Center Way, San Leandro, CA 94577, United States
name: Kendejah Restaurant

reviews.text: First time at Kendejah and it was pretty good. So happy it's all halal food! I ordered okra soup with chicken and turkey (loved the turkey flavor in it --  very smokey), jallof rice was very flavorful too, ordered egusi but I think there was some miscommunication so I got the goat soup (it was okay for me -- very tomatoes but the goat was very tender) and of course fufu is always good. Also, got the cornbread and mannnnn I are the whole thing without sharing! It was delicious!
Takeout only place. Got the Oxtail Served with rice. Good Oxtail. Mine was tender but my friend said his was not.
Extremely friendly and hospitable hosts. FYI, Takeout only now . The food was great! Highly recommended!

Food taste very good but you get more rice and beans than oxtails. The only seating area is outside the restaurant and I think they have maybe only two tables. So it's best to place your order over the phone or just order when you arrive.

I got the potato greens, which was good. I ordered online and it said it would be ready in 15 minutes, which was not the case. They did take about an extra 20 minutes to finish making and packing my food even though it was a special of the day. The food was well seasoned and I believe the turkey they used was just smoked turkey- eat in moderation given that smoked turkey is high in sodium.

formatted_address: 5250 Foothill Blvd, Oakland, CA 94601, United States
name: Ruth's Buka

reviews.text:
The food was amazing! This was my first time trying Nigerian food and the food did not disappoint. I’d give the food a 9/10 everything was full of flavor.

Service was decent, it’s more of a grab and go family restaurant. Which mean the atmosphere is basic as well. I will definitely go back for food.

⭐⭐ (2/5 stars)

I am disappointed with this place. I paid $47 for two meals that felt all fat and no meat. The "chicken" dish actually had turkey, which wasn't even advertised. The flavor was nothing special and overall not worth the price. Skip this spot unless you want greasy, mislabeled food.

I had such a great experience here. The atmosphere was warm and welcoming, and the hospitality really stood out. Emmanuel and his niece were incredibly kind, helpful, and genuinely funny, it felt like being welcomed by family.

The food was amazing. It smelled so good through the bag that I couldn’t even wait to get home. I literally ate it in my car because I had to try it immediately and I ended up finishing it because it was that good. Fresh and so flavorful!

This was one of those experiences where everything just hits: the food, the service, and the overall vibe. I’ll definitely be back and will be recommending this place to others.

went with family because of the high reviews, and safe to say that we were NOT disappointed! the staff was super welcoming and we really appreciated Emmanuel for taking the time to explain their dishes to us since it was our first time ever.

most importantly, the food was ✩ delicious, satiating, and very tasty! ✩ the portions were great and modestly priced as well. i will definitely be back and highly recommend it to all of my friends and family!

We ordered jellof rice. It was absolutely authentically made by Nigerian grandma’s recipe with smoky flavor in it. We couldn’t resist to buy a takeout after we had food right there. Highly recommended!

formatted_address: 819 Valencia St, San Francisco, CA 94110, United States
name: Gola Restaurant SF

reviews.text:
We came to GOLA as a group of family and friends, and since the menu isn’t too big, we decided to try almost everything — and honestly, every single dish was amazing.

From the lamb and chicken tagines to the grilled branzino and stuffed peppers, everything was full of rich, authentic Tunisian flavor and perfectly cooked. Even the sides like the cauliflower in harissa sauce and homemade bread were outstanding.

The service was warm, friendly, and genuine — you can tell everyone there really cares about the food and the guests. The atmosphere felt cozy but elegant, and we left already planning our next visit.

Great ambience and friendly staff. I can’t say the seats near the door against the window are the most comfortable though.

The food was flavorful and beautiful. Unfortunately the toasted bread that came with the riblets were incredibly hard and inedible. We also thought the portion sizes were on the smaller end (esp the chicken tangine).

really good. at first I was afraid that the entrees were too small, but be not afraid I was enormously satisfied by the end.

the waiters also made lots of helpful comments throughout (the flavor is in the skin, eat the lemon in the same bite, etc.)

would definitely come back!

Gola is something special. The food feels deeply authentic to Tunisia—bold, soulful flavors that taste rooted in tradition while still feeling beautifully refined. The seafood is outstanding, incredibly fresh, and prepared in a way that lets the spices and ingredients truly shine.

The dessert was the perfect finish—thoughtful, balanced, and memorable. Add to that a warm, energetic vibe and genuinely attentive service, and the whole experience feels both elevated and welcoming.

Gola isn’t just a great meal—it feels like a true taste of Tunisia, done with care and confidence. I’ll definitely be back.

Everything was excellent!! We tried the deviled eggs, brik, and lamb stew and all were incredible. Lamb stew had lots of beautifully tender lamb. Even the bread was really something special. Service was impeccable, ambiance delightful and cozy. Will be back and definitely recommend

Also - loved that they asked if we were ready for the next course once we had finished our appetizers. Sometimes I do want a break in between, and lots of restaurants in this area will bring out the entrees while you’re still eating appetizers which is a huge pet peeve of mine. Not at Gola - service was delightful

formatted_address: 1000 Larkin St, San Francisco, CA 94109, United States
name: Meski

reviews.text: So I did not eat this time but I did last time and it was a real nice meal with the most beautiful spices.  This time I went to meet meet someone so I had an espresso and a tequila signature drink.  Both where on point perfect.  I am sure there was no barista but the coffee was smooth and perfect, not bitter, I am sure some Ethiopian single origin somewhere.  Will be back because the vibe was real cool.

This place is SO GOOD. We had the best server- Magaly was incredibly attentive, kind, and full of good energy. She seriously made our experience. The whole vibe is cozy and sleek at the same time, and the food…..wow. Absolutely fabulous. The pollo guisado sambusas were so good we actually ordered them twice- yes, we finished the first order and immediately asked for another. Don’t judge- just try them and thank me later!

A true see-and-be-seen hotspot, this restaurant has serious star power—owned by Golden State Warriors superstar Draymond Green—and it delivers on both energy and flavor. The space is vibrant, stylish, and undeniably sexy, with a crowd that comes dressed to impress and a buzz that feels more like a nightlife destination than just dinner.
The Afro-Latin and Ethiopian fusion menu is bold and creative, and every dish we tried was packed with flavor. That said, the oxtail pasta completely stole the show—rich, tender, and unforgettable.
If you’re looking for a place in San Francisco with great food, an energetic atmosphere, and a glamorous crowd, this spot checks every box.

Unbelievable!
Just WOW!
First time and will not be my last.
Staff was incredibly friendly.
Sat at the bar and ended up getting 2 beers with food. Literally everything I ordered was PERFECT!
Had the salmon and chicken then the rice + beans. OMG! the flavors + spices were outstanding!
For just myself I spent $100 but was totally worth it.
I have to mention Jordan and Rutha for a great first experience. See you all again soon! 👍🏾👍🏾👍🏾

What an amazing meal! Staff was so nice, warm, and friendly. Food was quick to come and to die for!
The chicken sambosas were unbelievable! Best dish of the night.
Everything was great though. Highly would recommend. Drinks awesome too!

formatted_address: 5020 Telegraph Ave, Oakland, CA 94609, United States
name: Asmara Restaurant

reviews.text: First time trying Eritrean/ Ethiopian food and really had a great experience here. Came right around early dinner and found the restaurant not too packed. Service was friendly and welcoming, and the facilities were nice. Tried what may have been most traditional- honey wine, spiced tea. We also ate the meat combo (which was great since we weren't exactly sure what we wanted) and the beef tar tar which impressed us a lot! Overall, it was really fun to just get in there and scarf it all down. I found the lamb and tar tar to be exceptional. The beef had an excellent "stew" savory taste to its finished and I only found it a bit challenging to enjoy the chicken with injera since the chicken was on the bone (which I like, but not experienced enough to take advantage of it). We ate so much food and the price/ quality was wonderful. Great eating experience and looking forward to my next!

In town from Chicago and DC ( me and my sister) and the food is amazing! Everything was delicious and I love that this looks and feels like a family run spot and incredibly welcoming! Being from DC we know Eritrean and Ethiopian food and I cannot say enough about the food and the atmosphere- please please don’t miss this place. It was delicious all around!

The food is good, definitely one of the better Ethiopian restaurants in Oakland.

Unfortunately our experience was horrendous. We were seated while the restaurant was a quarter of the max capacity, and all of the other customers had already been served their food. Three waitresses passed by us for 20 minutes before we had to wave them down to get served, and were told "it's busy"; fair enough, I should have done it earlier. She left into the kitchen to place the order and we waited. In the span of 40 minutes, 5 different groups of guests had entered, been seated, orders placed, and food served while we waited for our two regular dishes. It was clear that our order was never placed, and I had to wave down the waitress to confirm this. She came back from the kitchen and said "it's almost ready". 10 minutes later our food arrived, and the comment we received was "sorry, it's busy." I am not blind to the myriad of other customers who entered after us to see that the order was forgotten, so not owning up to the mistake was disappointing.
Good Ethiopian and service. I would prefer the enjira to not be cold. The owner is quite friendly and nice.

Asmara is a staple of the neighborhood. The service is always sweet and earnest, the food arrives on time and is tasty. I don’t like that the injera is served cold- and the entrees are quite plain. We had the Chefs special - gored gored and it was delicious, if a bit fatty. We had a side of greens which was fine, and a delicious ginger beer. The restaurant is large and a bit stark, the delightful service makes up for it all.

formatted_address: 6101 Shattuck Ave., Oakland, CA 94609, United States
name: Shewhat Cafe & Restaurant

reviews.text: Shewhat Cafe & Restaurant in Oakland, California serves authentic Ethiopian and Eritrean cuisine in a cozy welcoming environment. We enjoyed the cuisine for the first time when we visited for dinner. We relished their Okra Kelwa, Chicken & Spinach, Red Lentils, Yellow Split Peas and Lettuce served with gluten free Injiras. The dishes flavoured with their traditional spices were delicious, not spicy and awesome. The ambience and decor are unique and our helpful host Alex made our evening truly memorable.

Eat here, now! You won’t regret it! The food, the service, everything is top notch. For three people, we got veg combo and the mushroom main, and it was the right amount of food. The honey wine was delicious as well. The ladies that work here are so kind and friendly. I have a feeling I’ll be a regular here 😆
Loved the food. Great service and the vibe was laid back. Also, get comfy with eating with your hands cause that's how its authentically done for ethiopian food  :)

The food was absolutely AMAZING!
Everything was delicious!
And the service was top-notch! Kind, warm, it really felt like getting a home cooked meal.
I will definitely be coming back! ❤️

Sooo good! For drinks we got the tea and the chai and both were delicious and unique. The sambusa was so good that I immediately ate them before taking the picture. It’s crunchy, not too oily and pairs well with the sweet and sour sauce that is served with the dish. As a vegetarian I loved having two combo options to choose from! I chose the Simo’s special and my personal favorites were the red lentils and the chickpeas. I usually hate okra but I didn’t mind it at all. My boyfriend got the Shewat Combo. Everything was good but the star of the show was the beef curry which had a hearty flavor.

10/10 Recommend this place!

formatted_address: 4069 Telegraph Ave, Oakland, CA 94609, United States
name: Cafe Eritrea D'Afrique

reviews.text: It’s been my favorite restaurant since moving to the neighborhood two years ago. The food is not only consistently fantastic, but it is always extremely deeply flavorful. The Lamb alicha, my current favorite, has a lot of warming spices that meld well, and every other bite a new one surfaces: green cardamom, later ginger, then a chili powder. Don’t skip the flax seed milkshake, which is toasty, rich, and flavored with honey. Service is friendly and quick. My favorite!

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Wow, what an amazing experience at this Ethiopian and Eritrean restaurant! The food was absolutely delicious, bursting with authentic flavors that left my taste buds dancing. Every dish was prepared with care and showcased the rich culinary traditions of Ethiopia and Eritrea. The service was exceptional—staff were incredibly friendly, attentive, and made us feel right at home. The hospitality here is unmatched, creating a warm and welcoming atmosphere that made our visit truly special. I can’t wait to come back and highly recommend this gem to anyone craving fantastic food and a heartfelt dining experience!
Very tasty! We got the house special sample and the vegetarian combination. We also got samosas for an appetizer.
What an awesome experience. The food was delicious and the server helped us pick out the exact perfect meal for us

This Ethiopian/Eritrean cuisine restaurant is by far the best that I’ve experienced in the entire San Franciso Bay Area! The owner, Zimam, and her staff are incredibly hospititable and exemplify courteous values with all of their customers. The food (especially the Veggie Combo) is incredible and I highly recommend it. The atmosphere has great incense and is great for both solo and social eating with friends.

formatted_address: 60 Morris St, San Francisco, CA 94107, United States
name: Nat & Betty's Afro-Caribbean Soul Food Kitchen

reviews.text: Love, love, loved the food !! Originally purchased around my birthday April 10th. Order again today. I was orginally unsure about side portions called and they immediatly called so kind and helpful. Told me the portions are genorus size . Which they were. Once I tried I was sold Mac n cheese was delicious. Collards greens seasoned perfectly. Red snapper was so soft and tender barely any bones. Jerk chicken was still fried hard, not soggy.

The food is DELICIOUS!!!
Everything is Bomb!!!! And totally worth whatever the price! And don’t sleep on the Gumbo and Oxtails (SMACKIN)
Pictured is the Seafood Sunday Special
Omg good
The food blew my mind! It's high quality and worth every penny. Absolutely love the Rasta Pasta, oxtail bowl, and the jerk chicken plate. Sending my blessings and compliments to the chef(s)
Food taste great! The presentation was on point even in the Togo box. Owner is very nice.  I had the catfish, mac&chs and greens.
Everything on the menu is delicious they really deserve 10 Stars I come almost every day my wife think I am having an affair on her I spend so much time coming here that's how good the food is

formatted_address: 1429 Mendell St, San Francisco, CA 94124, United States
name: Old Skool Cafe

reviews.text: Exceptional food and service. I especially enjoyed the live jazz band. I hope everyone gets to experience Old Skool Cafe. Highly recommend the Tongan Oto appetizer. Gumbo was also fire. The last time I came, I had the fried chicken. The food does not disappoint! Vibes were 10/10.

Yes. Everything about this place. The vibe. The jazz music. The incredible food. The Zoot-suited staff. The story behind it. It’s all exceptional.

Do NOT sleep on this place. Seriously, do not.

For drinks, I highly recommend their French 75 and the Sidecar.

For starters, the flaky catfish and the brussel sprouts.

For Mains, the pork chop or the fried chicken.

And for dessert, either the date cake or the lavender cheesecake.

Incredible experience here! The service was on point and the servers were so friendly and attentive! We ordered appetizers and listened to live jazz and it was the perfect environment with a cozy, elegant atmosphere!! we really appreciated how well cooked the shrimp was and how spicy the sauce was with abundance of flavor!! The crostinis were delicious and the server graciously offered to bring us more when she realized that we had to run out!

This is more than just a restaurant. This is an entire community mutual aid fund. You are supporting to care for the broader wellness of youth and empower those to break the cycle of incarceration & poverty!!!

We will definitely be coming back for more food, lovely, jazz, and the impeccable ambience !!

Everything was incredible. The food was insanely good. Everything we had - the shrimp, brussels sprouts, gumbo, mac and cheese, fried chicken and date cake (a must) - was perfectly cooked and had well balanced flavor. They even brought us these sweet potato biscuits that were probably the best biscuits I’ve ever had. The service was fantastic too - all of the servers were so friendly and attentive from the moment we got there to leaving. They had live music which was the cherry on top of a really nice dinner. Would highly recommend!

True gem in SF - get transported to 1920s speakeasy w live music and superb southern style menu dishes. Stunning chandeliers & decorations for a supper club experience you will not forget. Highly recommend the New Orleans style BBQ Jerk shrimp w crostini as a Starter and the fried chicken and/or short rib entrees. Staff are friendly efficient and will make you feel like part of the family. Great selection of mocktails as well as wine and cocktails menu. Will be back again soon.

formatted_address: 532 Green St, San Francisco, CA 94133, United States
name: Tajines Morrocan Restaurant

reviews.text: Authentic moroccan cuisine and the moroccan mint tea and decor is phenomenal. We ordered the lamb tagine, the lemon olive chicken and the taktuka and moroccan mint tea. The home made moroccan bread was delicious. Wish we could have tried more off the menu but we were so full!

Giving this spot 10 out of 10!!
The food was delicious and authentic. The Moroccan chef is extremly talented and responsive!
Def recommending!

This restaurant is simply amazing!
Every dish is delicious and the staff is wonderfully friendly.
It truly feels like a piece of Morocco in San Francisco.
I recommend this place

The food here is very comforting and feels home cooked. The Chicken Tagine was delicious. The sauce was flavourful and the chicken was tender. The lamb in the Lamb Couscous was a bit dry but the gravy improved it a bit. I recommend getting the Chicken Tagine.

A hidden treasure. People seem to queue by it while waiting for the pizza next-door, but they are missing out on a great experience. The food is genuine, healthy, flavorful and the owners are flexible in case of food allergies. And I love the real Moroccan tea. Overall, if you want something better than the std burger, pizza or sushi, go to this place and have some real food.

formatted_address: 5330 Terner Way, San Jose, CA 95136, United States
name: Jubba Somali Restaurant

reviews.text:
We visited this restaurant and ordered the chicken wraps and roasted goat cutlet, and the food was absolutely incredible. Everything was bursting with flavor and perfectly seasoned. The chicken was tender, the goat was beautifully spiced, and even the rice had an amazing taste with just the right amount of seasoning. It felt like true comfort food, and my husband and I enjoyed every single bite until the plates were completely clean.
What made the experience even better is that the food is halal, which is always a big plus for us. The blend of spices was spot on, with each dish full of depth and aroma without being overwhelming. The restaurant offers both indoor and outdoor seating, and there is plenty of parking available, which adds to the convenience.
The prices are slightly on the higher side, but considering the quality, taste, and portion sizes, it feels completely worth it. The food left such a lasting impression that we could not stop talking about it afterward. It is the kind of place that makes you want to come back again and again. Overall, a fantastic spot for delicious halal food and a truly satisfying dining experience.

This is one of my favorite restaurants in San Jose! I genuinely crave it monthly. This unassuming location is right by the VTA Station. A little outdated interior, but gets the job done. It can get really busy, so I recommend ordering ahead if you don't plan to dine-in. The staff here are nice and work quickly!

My recommendation is the Beef Suqaar! Each piece of beef is soooo tender and juicy. Flavored so well without being overwhelming or salty. I enjoy this with the rice and salad! As the beef gets fatty, it's a good balance. The green sauce is super spicy, but a really nice creamy kick! (I personally can't handle the heat)

Huge portions, high quality food, and GREAT prices! I ordered the Jubba chicken wrap, mandazi, and sambusa, all of which were a delight. The chicken was cooked to perfection, so juicy and tender. The yogurt sauce in the wrap complimented it perfectly. Very casual, laid-back environment. They also had complimentary hot herbal tea which was also a perfect way to wash down a heavy meal. I want to come back to try the plates too!

Had some Somali food for the first time in my life and had no regrets. The staff at this restaurant were pleasant to talk to. I had the Tilapia Fillets an the food was absolutely worth the price. Will definitely be coming back.

Update: Went again on 12/12 for their Beef Suqaar. Absolutely amazing, will be coming back soon.

We tried a bit of everything and it was all great. Chicken, beef and goat was all well spiced and delicious. Staff was friendly and went out of their way to accommodate. My kids scarfed down a bit of everything and we had lots of leftovers. They loved watching the trains go by as we ate. Wish it wasn't so far from my house because I'd be there every weekend!

formatted_address: 357-A Grand Ave, Oakland, CA 94610, United States
name: Enssaro Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text:
I ordered takeout from Enssaro for a work appreciation luncheon, and the experience was fantastic from start to finish. The young lady who helped me (whose name I don’t want to misspell) was incredibly kind, patient, and welcoming. While I waited, she offered me some tea and even shared Vegan Gluten-Free Ethiopian Hummus (Butacha) and Gluten-Free Injera. She also took the time to show me how to properly enjoy the food with injera, just as it’s traditionally done in Ethiopia — such a thoughtful and memorable gesture.

The food was excellent, the service was exceptional, and the hospitality truly stood out. I’ll definitely be back. Highly recommend Enssaro!

P.S. My apologies for the poor photos!  Only took one as an afterthought.

I love Enssaro so much! This is my go-to for a solo meal, big group, and dates. Everything is delicious and spiced perfectly if you like heat!! The appetizers are a must - especially the hummus and nachos (photo).The drinks are great too. Raphael & Solomon are great hosts and neighborly. Portions are generous and they have many combinations for meat lovers and vegetarians. I keep coming back!

I’m giving this a 4star because I don’t know Ethiopian food that much so not much to compare. But the food was delicious. Injera was just the perfect sour, red lentils were on fire like spicy! Cabbage and potatoes so so good, the chicken was yummy and the lamb tibs was so good a little lamb-y but good 😊
The service was awesome.. so nice and kind

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
I had such a wonderful experience at Enssaro! The staff greeted me with warm smiles and provided excellent service throughout my visit. The food was absolutely delicious — every Ethiopian dish was full of authentic flavor and made with so much care. I truly loved everything I tried.  I came all the way from Atlanta, Georgia, the meal was well worth the trip. Highly recommend Enssaro to anyone who wants to enjoy amazing Ethiopian cuisine!

Third time having Ethiopian food and it was a tasty experience. Our large platter for 4 people included beef, chicken, lamb, salad, vegetables and an other items. We enjoyed glutton free injera—which was completely satisfying. Service was prompt and personable even with a full restaurant.

formatted_address: 5849 San Pablo Ave, Oakland, CA 94608, United States
name: Café Colucci

reviews.text: Pretty good actually. The service was fine, good for Bay Area standards. The bathroom and the interior were clean and well presented. There's an open kitchen here. The injera was food and their kik alicha was supreme. If you like mashed potatoes, it's that exact same texture as that but with split peas. The vegan sampler was excellent. The meat sampler was rough. Nothing was really good imo. The mushroom tibs were great. The chickpeas are rubbish, don't get the mitten shiro.

The service was pretty good. The waiter answered all questions very sweet person..The appetizer was on point. It was like a samosa, but it had beef and lentils in it.I had a lemonade.The lemonade was really, really good.The main dish was okay but it wasn't super flavorful.It was the meat sampler.Maybe I need to try a different dish, but I didn't like it that much. Not worth for the price.

The best vegetarian Ethiopian food I've ever had! Highly recommend adding the tibs, eggplant or mushroom, to your vegan combination plate. The berebere mocha with oatmilk is delicious with just the right amount of spice and served in a substantial handleless mug that warms your hands. The tiramisu was a pleasant surprise and one of the best I've had.

Pro Tip: Go for the meat and vegan sampler on a big plate—it’s the perfect way to taste a variety of stews in one go. Every bite had something unique to offer. We also tried the lamb tips, which were melt-in-your-mouth buttery and absolutely delicious.
Shoutout to our server, who was incredibly patient as we bombarded him with questions about the different spices used in the cocktail menu. Speaking of cocktails… we may have ordered half the menu—and loved every single one. Here are the standouts we’d come back for:
1. Lion’s Mane – The shai kemin spice steals the show here. Complex, bold, and unforgettable—this was hands-down my favorite.
2. Give Them the Beans – Think espresso martini meets boozy chocolate milkshake. Rich, smooth, and indulgent.
3. Garden of Eden – Sweet, floral, and beautifully balanced. A refreshing contrast to the bolder drinks.

Absolutely incredible experience!
This was my first time at an Ethiopian restaurant, and I’m so glad I chose this place. I ordered vegetarian food — the spiced tea, sambussa, and the veggie platter — and hands down, it was some of the best food I’ve ever had. Every bite was flavorful and unique.

What made the experience even better was the amazing service. The staff took the time to explain what each dish was, which made it feel welcoming and thoughtful. You can tell they really care about sharing their culture and food.

Highly recommend — I’ll definitely be coming back!

formatted_address: 10 29th St, San Francisco, CA 94110, United States
name: Komaaj Pila Bazaar

reviews.text: I love Persian food and this is Northern Iranian food. It's different from Southern Iranian food. Just like other reviews, the food is sweeter than I am used too. Food was good and service was great. There are a lot of vegan options. This is a different food region of Iran, so don't expect Southern Iranian/Persian food. I loved the rustic interior, it felt very homey.

A true taste of northern Iran—authentic flavors you won’t find at regular Persian restaurants. The staffs are lovely and attentive, and the food is so amazing I always find myself craving it. Definitely a place I keep coming back to!

Spectacular and authentic food! Truly enjoyed the experience here at this beautiful restaurant featuring authentic north Iranian food. Motanjan (chicken) dish was our favorite, full of flavors. It really impressed us. The drinks were refreshing and great.

Service was equally top notch thanks to Nazanin.

I was looking forward to trying this place but I was a bit disappointed.

I’m not sure it’s common but all the dishes we had were a bit sweet even all the dips.

The mezze plate with different dips were good but definitely overpriced ($36?) since the portion is pretty small and they gave you few crackers (they call it bread but it’s close to a cracker) and we asked if we can get 1-2 more and the server brought 5-6 and charged. (At least you should get informed if we had to pay for it)

The chicken was good but also not amazing.
I don’t think I will go back.

That was my first try of an Iranian restaurant, and no regrets, I'd go back in a heartbeat.  I love the interior of Komaaj, feels like somebodys house or living room.  Very inviting and cozy.  We tried only two dishes. Their mezze platter for two and the tumeric. Chicken over pomegranate rice.
On their platter, every dish is rather special the only let down was the bread.  Tasted a bit like an old cracker to me, I wish they offer different options, even a fresh banquet would work. The olives were out of this world, the smokey eggplant is simply divine.
The chicken... Amazing just felt off the bone and complimented the rice.
Overall a really good experience., the wine ...  takes a bit getting used too.  We tried their Armenian reds.  I wouldnt rave about them, but hi we tried.
Certainly kudos to the chef and team, I will certainly come back.

formatted_address: N Texas St, Fairfield, CA 94533, United States
name: JayBaba's Kitchen, Home of Authentic African-Ghanaian Cuisines

reviews.text: We enjoyed our meal from JayBabas! We got Egusi, pounded yam, tilapia and jollof rice. I called last minute but he was able to have our order ready for pick up at a very good time. The flavors were delicious perfectly seasoned and the fact he asked what spice level was really a game changer. I’m Congolese so my spice level is very high but my young kids spice level isn’t as advanced as mine yet so the spice level option was perfect. The food was balanced, flavorful, and clearly made with love. My absolute favorite was the Fried tilapia & rice my daughter and I finished that one pretty fast. He seasoned it like a grandmother would so that should tell you what you need to know. Very kind guy and wonderful food. I will most definitely be a returning client. Thank you for the wonderful food and amazing customer service!

The most delicious meal I have eaten in recent memory. I ordered the egusi and fufu with chicken over the phone. Takeout only. They are a catering business. The owner was very responsive, professional, and prepared the food in a timely manner with such short notice! I thought the stew was perfectly seasoned, meat was cooked very well, as it was tender and juicy. A customer was also outside and told me he orders food for the entire week from this business. I will absolutely be back to try the other dishes and recommend this business to my friends.

I recently ordered a meal from JayBaba's kitchen, and I must say, it was an absolute delight! The jollof rice was perfectly cooked with a rich, savory flavor that was enhanced by the fresh green peppers and carrots. The spices were on point, giving the dish just the right amount of heat without being overwhelming. The added condiments were a nice touch, offering a variety of flavors that complemented the meal wonderfully. The presentation was also impressive, with everything neatly packed and labeled. Overall, it was a fantastic dining experience, and I will definitely be ordering again!

We were in town for a conference in the Bay Area and needed catering for 30 people (Needed Ghanaian food). A friend from Stanford university recommended him and We called him a day before the event and he delivered. It was yummy. Perfect spice level, he actually ask you how you want it. The black sauce on the side, he calls it Shito was so good.

We ordered Jollof rice, fried rice with grilled fish and chicken and he added fried plantains, salads and even added a drink made with hibiscus and ginger. This was perfect and everybody loved it.

I will recommend him but try and call him ahead of time.

Let me just say I live in the Concord area and it's quite a drive. But...Oh My Goodness. The food was just next level!! First bite you can tell the work put into this food! The seasoning was perfect and my boyfriend, who doesn't handle spicy well, ate this up!!! The turkey tails were our favorite! And I didn't even mention how great the service was. Jaybaba's kitchen is a MUST GO!

formatted_address: 303 Oakland Ave ste a, Oakland, CA 94611, United States
name: Desta Ethiopian Cafe

reviews.text: Beautiful sunny, quiet cafe in Adam’s point. The best Ethiopian food I’ve ever had. The food tastes very healthy, fresh, and simple but literally so full of flavor at the same time. Home cooking made with time and care. Just SO good. If you are thinking about going just go. Wow. And the injera is 100% teff and gluten free which can be hard to find these days. Plus the vibe inside is so peaceful and warm. I love.

One of the most flavorful experiences I’ve had. I would highly recommend the combo platter to share with another person so you can get a taste of all the flavors they’ve got to offer. The hibiscus tea was perfect for a hot day. Incredibly quick and lovely service.

I came here with my father for the first time yesterday and the way Sirgut and the other two woman treated us and prepared food was as if she was having us over at her home for lunch. Phenomenal food and service. We had the vegetarian combo and it was amazing. We then tried amazing espresso which was pan roasted right in front of us. We will definitely come back ❤️

We have been coming back here for a few times since we found this place last year. It's fantastic vegetarian Ethiopian food served family style. I highly recommend starting with the combo and then order more of what you like best. The food is ready and will be served quickly. The atmosphere is very cozy and friendly as the owner (?) is super nice and always has a smile for the guests. There are no meat options but I bet you won't miss them.

I live near four very good and praised Ethiopian restaurants in my city, and this place, without any doubt, has been the best Ethiopian food I have ever had. The environment is cozy and warm, the food is homemade and very well prepared, the woman who cooks is very friendly and nice. We tried many things, all of them delicious, including the tea. No complaints, only praises for this place.

formatted_address: 35 Grand Ave, Oakland, CA 94612, United States
name: Mela Bistro

reviews.text: Holy frickin moly. This is my new favorite Ethiopian place. The food was spectacular. I tried the chicken Tibs and the Asa Kifto (ahi tuna). If you can handle spice, I’d say go full spice. The spicy sauce is incredible and the flavors for the whole plate was amazingly unique. Lastly, the service was so good. Full credit goes to Favin ( I hope I spelled her name semi-right ) for her attentiveness for the dietary needs of my family-they are very anti spice. More specifically, she helped because I mentioned loving spicy food and brought out a small dish of just sauce. All in all, I couldn’t recommend Mela Bistro more to any person wanting to try delicious Ethiopian food.

Had an incredible dinner at Mela Bistro. Every course stood out and the entire experience felt thoughtful and unforgettable. The staff and owner are genuinely warm, and the space has a character and beauty you don’t find often. I left feeling like I needed to be rolled to the car and already can’t wait to come back. If you’re anywhere nearby, this place belongs at the top of your list!

The shrimp taco was out of this world for appetizers. We also had the veggie platter and tuna kifo was so delicious. The pistachio cake for dessert was a cherry on the top. We Will definitely will come back.
The owner is a pastry chef and amazing host! She was very attentive and food was truly amazing. It’s great to support and be nourished by a community member.

Delicious Ethiopian food with a great veggie selection and wonderful desserts!
Highly recommend the Tef Chocolate Cake for dessert.

formatted_address: 2955 Telegraph Ave, Berkeley, CA 94705, United States
name: Meskie's Ethiopia Restaurant

reviews.text: I’ve been here 3 times and it’s one of my favorites in Berkeley. I love the variety of the meat & vegetarian platters, especially the carrot and meat sides. There are so many different flavors together on these platters and all of them are wonderful.

I really didn't like the place. Overall the atmosphere is great and the guys working there are nice, but the food is bad.

I ordered beef, about half of the pieces were tough, it was impossible to chew them. Most likely cheap meat was used for cooking. In addition, the meat was very oversalted. For the first time, I probably didn't finish the meat. The mushrooms were tasty, at least they weren't so oversalted and they could be eaten.

I don't recommend this place for food

Great place! It was my first time having Ethiopian food, and Meskie’s didn’t disappoint. We enjoyed a big family plate. I liked the Chicken tibs and string beans. The Ethiopian wine was delicious. Our waiter was very attentive, and lit the fireplace for us. I’ll definitely come back.

We went for lunch, and the place was not crowded at all - maybe only 2 other customers. The back patio is a nice space. But we had to wait maybe 45 minutes for our food - even our drinks did not come for 30+ minutes, and the server did not tell us that the soups we ordered weren't even available until we asked where all the food was. While the food was tasty, and I suspect the restaurant was handling online orders, the lack of (proactive) communication about our order was really frustrating and significantly delayed our schedule for the day.

The service was very nice. The atmosphere was unfortunately affected by a very loud client, hopefully will not be there the next time we go.The server even gave me some roasted milled flax and instructions on how to make her delicious smoothie at home, explaining the significance of the drink back home.

formatted_address: 6100 Telegraph Ave, Berkeley, CA 94705, United States
name: Addis

reviews.text: Delicious food. The veggie combo was excellent! I couldn’t stop eating till I left my plate completely clean.
Delicious vegan lunch buffet, you can fill a big plate with the four items pictured and rolls of injera for $15, 10/10!

Friday nights at Addis... Wow! This evening there was a saxophonist performing with the amazing keyboardist! My friend and I REALLY enjoyed the delicious meal plus heartfelt jazz music...what a treat!
Excellent service and the aroma of the authentic dishes was mouthwatering!
Don't miss this restaurant on a Friday night 😎

It was great food. We ordered the veggie combo. It was plenty of food for the 2 of us, although we typically don't eat a ton we were quite hungry. It came quite fast. I gave 4 stars for service because it seemed like our waiter wasn't happy that we only ordered the veggie combo and we felt pressured to order more even though we didn't need to. But this was minor.

I used to love this restaurant. I don't know if they went through an ownership change but I can no longer recommend it. The service was thoroughly unpleasant and rude, the food was mediocre at best and to top it off, we saw rats around the back of the building when we left the parking lot. There are so many Ethiopian restaurants in this neighborhood, I would strongly recommend that you try one of the others. So disappointing on many levels.

formatted_address: 6430 Telegraph Ave, Oakland, CA 94609, United States
name: Barcote Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text:
The best Ethiopian food in the Bay Area!
Fresh, flavorful, and generously portioned — no skimpy servings here. The doro wot has the perfect amount of spice and a rich, well-balanced base sauce.

(No filters used on these photos — just look at those vibrant colors! They truly reflect how fresh the food is.)

Look no further — this place is a gem!

P.S. A little tip from an Ethiopian food lover: bring some gloves, or if you struggle to get the smell off afterward, wash with soap and toothpaste when you get home!

Great indoor and outdoor dining spaces. Delicious food - advice was to order both the vege combo and meat combo instead of the ultimate combo - gets you one of the lamb curries + all the veggies. The spiced tea pairs well with the lentil dishes. Service was kind and friendly. A very well run establishment.

Tried Ethiopian food for the first time and it was delicious. Lentil samosa was little bit oily and would taste great with tamarind sauce or mint chutney but it was served with chilly sauce, which was not a great combination. Highlight of the lunch was Shiro combo. It’s  a must order dish on the menu. Overall service was a little slow. Ambience was nice.
Delicious and satisfying lunch, with the spiced tea, beef samosas and meat sampler.  These flavors and spices are beyond words!

Food was incredibly substantial. Very filling and satisfying.

Entrees are very wholesome and healthy. However, not as spicy as I would prefer. I really missed not having some chilis on the side, or hot sauce etc available for adding as desired.

Salad is incredibly greasy and oily, not palatable at all.

formatted_address: 2208 Business Cir, San Jose, CA 95128, United States
name: Walia Ethiopian Cuisine

reviews.text:
The restaurant offers a warm, traditional Ethiopian ambiance, and the flavors genuinely make you feel like you are experiencing Ethiopia through the food. I do not remember the exact name of the dish I ordered, but it was recommended by the waiter after I mentioned that I wanted something hearty with meat and rich Ethiopian spices served with injera. It turned out to be an excellent recommendation — flavorful, filling, and very satisfying.
One thing I noticed was that the restaurant seemed understaffed for how busy it was. After my food arrived, I had to wait quite a while just to get a spoon and fork, since they were not brought out automatically. I also ended up going to the counter to request the bill because it took too long to arrive at the table.
That said, the waiter was friendly and clearly doing his best to keep up with the crowd.
Overall, I would definitely return to enjoy that unique Ethiopian dish again.

The restaurant has a traditional Ethiopian atmosphere and the flavors really transport you there. I’m not sure of the exact name of the dish, but it was recommended by the waitress after I told her I wanted something with meat and rich Ethiopian flavors served with injera. It was a great choice — delicious, filling, and satisfying.

However, I noticed there weren’t enough servers for how busy the restaurant was. I had to wait quite a while after the dish arrived just to get a spoon and fork, since they weren’t brought automatically. I also had to go to the counter to request the bill because it took too long to be delivered.

Still, the waitress was friendly and clearly doing her best.

I will definitely come back to enjoy this unique Ethiopian dish again.

This was my second time coming here, and it was just as great as the first! My boyfriend and I shared the veggie and meat combo; it was a generous portion, super fresh, and really flavorful. Everything was perfectly seasoned and tasted homemade. The owner stopped by a few times to check on us, which was really nice. Great food, great service, definitely recommend!

I ordered food for pick up, with delivery time of 20min. When I got there on time they didn’t ask for my name or provided any updates as I was standing for 30min past due their estimate. The place was dirty and I could see how messy their kitchen was. I felt lucky they were late because after I saw how bad the place smelled and how dirty it was I had already lost my appetite. I canceled my ordered and went back home. I will not be craving Ethiopian for a loooong time.

This is our new favorite Ethiopian restaurant in San Jose! Its absolutely delicious! We got the vegetarian platter with lamb tibs and the quantity is enough for 2 people and everything was so good, we couldn't decide what was our favorite. Can't wait to go back!

The only downside is the bathroom is outside of the restaurant in the same building but its not too inconvenient

formatted_address: 462 Santa Clara Ave, Oakland, CA 94610, United States
name: Cafe Romanat

reviews.text: Had the honor of checking out Cafe Romanat over the weekend, and it was such an experience! As soon as you walk in, the owner Adey greets you, & makes you feel like home! It doesn’t feel like you’re stepping into a restaurant, but like a family home! Great, attentive service, along with amazing drinks, & food! To anyone who would love to try traditional Ethiopian cuisine, with a side of great service, & drinks, check out this place! You’ll be telling all your friends and family to stop by for a bite to eat!
Great food and service. My family and I loved it. Their Injera is nice and fluffy and the Doro Wat was my favorite but both veggie and meat dishes there were great.

Undefeated in East Bay, this place is always delicious, the service always friendly and the atmosphere calming and warm.

I highly recommend the veggie and meat combo with doro derek tibs! And a super seed smoothie!
I wasn’t previously familiar with the Ethiopian game, but that lamb hit me so deep down in my soul I wanted to cry easy five stars

The people who run this place don't sell food, they provide medicine nurtured with love. You can feel the kind love energy when you walk into this place. And the huge glass windows for ample people watching is such a plus. What a beautiful life we get to live. Blessings and abundance to all!

P.S. don't freaking forget to get the sesame, flax, and sunflower smoothie! OMG, medicine never tasted so good and refreshing after spending time in the sun, honey bun!

formatted_address: 3212 Adeline St, Berkeley, CA 94703, United States
name: Lemat Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: Gorgeous in all ways. Our server was just lovely. The dishes were incredible, notably the chicken stew (wot? definitely a newbie to the cuisine). The coffee was unbelievable. The ambiance is perfect--feels just upscale enough to give that elevated dining experience while still being very approachable and comfortable. Obviously a place favored by many groups, families, regulars. The cultural artifacts and art are beautifully displayed and open up one's learning about Ethiopian culture (particularly their musical instruments and of course the revered coffee ceremony). We chatted with the owner after our meal, who is clearly on a joyful mission to spread love and insight about his deep and beautiful culture. Just a perfect meal and experience. For us, worth going over the bridge for, for sure! Continued blessings to you.

A lovely place tucked in Berkeley. Had the veg combo. The injera was soft and tasty. The plate had 2 greens, cabbage, 2 lentil curries and a beetroot curry.The red lentil curry was an explosion of flavours. The high point was the honey wine. The beautiful atmosphere was enhanced with a live singing performance. Service was on point and everyone was friendly and courteous.
A great place to pamper yourself with a good Ethiopian fare.

If you’re looking to branch into your first try at Ethiopian food, Lemat is the place — excellent ingredients and helpful staff make this a great place to go for East African cuisine in Berkeley.

Cocktail list is extensive and lots of options for vegetarian and meat-based preferences. Our group of four opted for the veggie and meat samplers and we weren’t able to finish all the food — plenty to go around for all. Nothing was too spicy or intensely flavored, though be prepared to eat with your hands (in the traditional Ethiopian style).

The waitress was friendly and helped us choose the best samplers for a first time visit. The ambiance of the restaurant was nice, though when we arrived it was quite smoky — as though something in the back had badly burned. It took awhile to clear the smoke and smell from the dining area, but otherwise it was a great visit.
Excellent dishes. Good variety of tastes. I've dined at many Ethiopian restaurants. This is the first time I've had fish, and it was cooked perfectly!

The restaurant excels in its food and offerings but is terribly slow in service. We had to wait 50 minutes for our appetizer, and the service was minimal, to the point where we weren't even provided with silverware or plates. The business owners don't seem to care about the waiting time and don't set any expectations.

While I appreciate small businesses, the service here was abysmal. Also, don't take your kids - they'll be starved waiting for the food to arrive.

The ambiance and cocktails are  great. This place is worth visiting if you have about three hours to spare for a meal.

formatted_address: 1910 Park Blvd, Oakland, CA 94606, United States
name: ADMAS ( ፒያሳ ) ETHIOPIAN and ERITREAN RESTAURANT

reviews.text:
Authentic East African taste reflective of expert usage of spice and availability of imported injera. High-quality ingredients (down to the use of olive oil and not seed oil) makes for an even better experience.

Quanta Firfir and Veggie Combo are both rock solid. In a city of so many East African options, Admas is a top contender.

Friendly and attentive staff. Contemporary paintings on walls from across sub-Saharan Africa.

Amazing food.
Wife and I got the Meat+Veggie for 2 and both loved it. Injera is really good. Wife’s not a huge meat person and liked all three.  I hate beets and managed to eat most of these (that’s a positive sign).  Veggie dishes were fantastic.
The only criticism I have is getting three Injera for the two person combo. We ran out (while also eating the food mat) and it seems like a fourth would be nice so each gets two.

Will be back a lot! 🙏

Edit: tried to order to go online but they’ve disabled the comments/request section.  Called for “Meat & Veggie for 1, to-go, NO BEETS.”
“No beets?”
Me: Yes, no beets, please.
“No beets?”
Me: Yes, correct, no beets.
Got beets as 1of3 veggies. Hate beets.

Kept it 5 stars because I still got enough food, plenty of injera for me, and I like their food. I will double check my to-go orders…

Admas: please enable comments for online ordering.

Went here with my family to celebrate my birthday! Great experience. The food was great. We ordered two combo plats of veggies and meat. Tons of food. One star was taken off because it was very warm inside. Parking was easy. Service was good.

My family went for Mothers Day and had a wonderful meal. The wait staff was very kind and the meal was delicious. Exactly what i was craving. The jebena coffee is great too! Its a lot of coffee, so just know that as well. Overall really pleased with our experience. They even have ful which is awesome, as an arab myself. Love seeing more restaurants open that offer non-american food. Good luck to yall!

Had a great time at Admas last night. The owner was really nice and helped us with our orders. We ordered a meat and veggie combo for my fiance and I to try several of their dishes. We asked for a recommendation for our third veggie dish and he recommended two dishes. He offered to give us the fourth veggie dish for free, which was really kind of him. Food was delicious and very chill atmosphere.

formatted_address: 2805 Telegraph Ave, Oakland, CA 94609, United States
name: Lula Restaurant

reviews.text:
Excellent Eritrean food with a top-injera and a wide variety of delicious vegetarian dishes!
Definitely get the Samosas!
Highly recommend for anyone wanting a full and hearty meal.

Great service and atmosphere too!
Absolutely delicious Ethiopian food! Highly recommend the Yekik Alicha. The owners were very kind!
Space is amazing the food even looks better and the service is on the topis that I ever saw Come today to Lula  And find the best hidden Oakland secrets  It's Ethiopian authentic food ,
We got Lega Tibs and Doro Wot. Service was fast and the dishes with the Injera were amazing!

Genuinely one of the most flavorful meals I've had.

Ordered the vegetarian samosa, mitten shiro, meat platter, and doro tibs. Everything was delicious, but the mitten shiro was surprisingly the favorite. Highly recommend everything ordered.

formatted_address: 5849 San Pablo Ave, Oakland, CA 94608, United States
name: Brundo Ethiopian Spice Company

reviews.text:
Colucci's vegan platter is so delicious that I -- famously not a vegan -- almost always order that when I get food there. It's all I can do to keep it to once a week haha. Cooking as wildly good as this, is quite rare and is something I feel very fortunate to be able to get.
The meat dishes are outstanding as well. Add a glass of tej and it's bliss.
Such a wonderful, welcoming staff and beautiful surroundings. I offer my highest recommendation.
Absolutely delicious food, wonderful energy, and excellent staff! We had the meat sampler and the hand squeezed lemonade — wow!! And we took home some injera and berbere spice. Amazing place!

I love Brundo's spices. The ingredients are always super flavorful and the colors let me know they're high quality and fresh. I also love how the spices come directly from their company in Ethiopia. If you check out their instagram you can learn more about where and how the spices are made, too. 5 stars all the way.

I LOVE BRUNDO! The spices are all so distinct and delicious and I've learned so much about Ethiopian food and cooking thanks to this company. They make it super easy to find exactly what you are looking for, or to be adventurous and try new things - either way you won't be disappointed. Local and black-owned too! Also their instagram is hecka cute and engaging and even educational. Love em.
Ordered the Hot Chili Pepper Blend for my dad for his birthday and he loved it! Shipping was super quick! Will definitely order again.

formatted_address: 2930 Telegraph Ave, Oakland, CA 94609, United States
name: Jebena Cafe

reviews.text: It is my first time trying Ethiopian food and it was incredible. Huge huge portions so its great for sharing. If you love spicy this is definitely the place to get it. The coffee was high quality as well and the workers are so sweet.

Had my first Ethiopian breakfast! It was really delicious and I got some guidance about how to eat it. Got decaf spiced tea and my daughter who can’t have dairy got an oat milk with honey. And there’s a cozy rocking chair. Such a lovely neighborhood place.

First time having Ethiopian food, and wow am I dying to try some more. Got the vegetable platter that came with injera (sour fermented flatbread) and it was not only plentiful, but also healthy and full of flavor! If I was from this area I’d come to this place every week. Very nice staff as well.

Just slid through and I'm having one of the smoothest lattes ive ever tasted. I'll absolutely be sliding through to check out the rest of the caffeine options but to my fellow coffee heads, this is a really solid choice.
It's close to downtown and temescal but far enough from both to find parking pretty easily.
Plenty of seating if youre not on the go, very open space inside, and a super chill vibe.

Food is delicious. I got the vegetarian combo {$17.50} (not pictured is a side of injera) and I had enough leftovers for dinner. Honey oat lavender latte {$6.75}is really good too. The employee who served me was very nice. I asked about the spice levels for a dish and she gave me a sample so I could decide if I wanted to order it in full. 🙂 I look forward to coming back.

formatted_address: 2504 Telegraph Ave, Oakland, CA 94612, United States
name: Cafe Dareye

reviews.text: First time trying this restaurant, my friend and I both got the beef tibs oalte, which comes with two hefty pieces of injera, salad, and lentils. The food is delicious and will leave you scraping the plate. Highly recommend it if you're in the mood for quality Ethiopian food.

This place is a little hidden gem! There are several Ethiopian restaurants in Oakland, many are very well known. Cafe Dareye gives them all a run for their money. A friend I and had just finished smashing things at Smash Kingdom a few sores down the block and were starving. We walked by Cafe Dareye and that wonderful smell of Ethiopian spices drew us in. It’s a very small space. We shared a 1/2 veggie combo platter and a Beef Tibs platter with Ethiopian spiced tea. It all hit the spot. It was very delicious and did not disappoint! There was only one person working and she balanced cooking taking, orders, serving our food, along with cooking for several take out customers with no delay and prompt friendly service. I would definitely go back there to eat and even order take out from there.

We absolutely loved this Ethiopian restaurant/cafe! The food was bursting with fresh flavor — every dish was perfectly seasoned and satisfying. The injera was soft and delicious, and the portions were generous. The staff made us feel so welcome and explained all the different items on the platter. Everything tasted homemade with so much love. Whether you’re vegan or not, this is a must-try spot!

Please try! You will not be disappointed ‼️‼️

This Ethiopian vegan restaurant is a true gem! The flavors are so rich and vibrant — every bite felt like comfort food with a cultural twist. The injera was warm and perfectly tangy, and each dish on the platter had its own unique seasoning and personality. You can tell the ingredients are fresh and prepared with care.

The team here is incredibly kind and welcoming — they made us feel right at home and helped us choose dishes perfect for our taste. The atmosphere is cozy and filled with beautiful aromas that make you excited for your meal the moment you walk in.

Whether you’re vegan or vegetarian just love delicious eats, this place is a must-visit. We can’t wait to come back and try everything on the menu‼️‼️‼️
Very nice people. The full order is just enough for 2. we had 3 so we got extra injera. We were going to a movie nearby so we just wanted to get something to try it. Very good lentils and cabbage.

formatted_address: 2786 Martin Luther King Jr Way, Oakland, CA 94612, United States
name: Selam Restaurant

reviews.text: a real hole in the wall. i walked under multiple freeways to get here. super yummy food, it feels like you walked into someone’s home kitchen.

No frills, hole in the wall restaurant with absolutely delicious Eritrean food. The kindest owner and server who is very friendly and helpful. The food is fresh, flavorful, light and so comforting. I will be back! It was so good I didn't even get a chance to take pictures.

The food here is so amazing you need to try it ASAP. After we ordered we were sitting outside waiting for our food and I commented to my partner that it smelled so good I wished my phone had a way to share the smell with other people (yes, I was high) and at that exact moment a guy in an electric wheelchair rolled by on MLK and said, "Damn! That smells good!

Spices were flavorful, and experience felt genuine. Wasn’t provided utensils but was expected to use bread to scoop and eat. Ended up being delicious enough to take home. Didn’t like the bread taste though, could be just a personal preference, since the person I came with enjoyed it.
Visited on a Sunday evening and felt like we wandered into someone’s living room. We ordered the veggie combo and one of the meat dishes. The food was great!

formatted_address: 160 14th St #102, Oakland, CA 94612, United States
name: Blue Nile

reviews.text:
A friend told me to try this place. I’ve been vegan for a little while now and a lot of their menu (and Ethiopian food in general from what I understand)  is either vegan or vegetarian and you can have it with meat by choice.

I took my kids so they had the meat with greens dish, one lamb, one chicken and one beef. I had two vegan plates and the appetizer I’m just forgetting the names right now (see pictures).

Everything had so much flavor and tasted super fresh. The spices and flavors were great, the owners are very nice and the environment is really chill. I will be going back here every time I’m in Oakland.

To the owners, thank you so much for the food, suggestions and the hospitality. They made it through the pandemic but people should really support this place.

My hidden neighborhood gem. I come here quite often because the meals are Fresh, Flavorful, Consistent, and Filling. For my needs (usually seeking quiet dining for things like getting work done), the atmosphere is conducive and provides outlets and a wi-fi connection (if you ask). The service is friendly with a family vibe (like eating at an aunts or a grandma's house) so I wouldn't expect to necessarily be waited on hand and food like other restaurant experiences. Let me also mention that the price is beyond reasonable for the offering.

Man I have a passion for Ethiopian food.  First time at this location. Greeted by two women who here attentive and welcoming. Ordered the chicken tibbs. Very spicy 🔥 but very good. Parking is not ideal . Restaurant had nice murals. Lots of injera which I love.

Absolutely enjoyed my lunch! They are vegetarian friendly with menu options specifically for vegetarians. Thought it was just a small place in downtown oakland but great ambience and the food was absolutely delish. There's a nice culture aspect here with seating i think Ethiopians use. Beautiful paintings and service was lovely. I tried the telba, quite skeptically, but it was so yummy. A sweet drink for a sweet tooth! I also got the Mir combo.

Love the place! The cultural elements are spread throughout the whole restaurant and makes up for great decoration. The food was amazing! However, some spots on  the floor weren't as clean, surely was a lack of cleaning after clients. There are also some flies around which disturbed me a lot.

formatted_address: 5200 Claremont Ave, Oakland, CA 94618, United States
name: Red Sea Ethiopian & Eritrean Cuisine Restaurant

reviews.text: The service was amazing. I didn’t have to wait too long for my food to come. The atmosphere was very calming, and the artwork on the walls was very beautiful. The food tasted amazing, and the pricing was reasonable. Would recommend coming here!

For a place that's been around for 45 years I figured they had nailed down the food (at least). The menu was filled with typos and the ordering site had its sambusa information mixed up.

The dive-y atmosphere seems to work for the folks who were hanging out in the (loud) bar that led to the dining room. But the music poured into the room and collided with the atmospheric (random) music.
I was intrigued and pleasantly surprised by the salad with injeera in it along with mayo pesto dressing. That was good and perhaps the highlight of the meal, though biting into jalapenos and raw onions somewhat made it unsettling.

We got the vegetarian sampler and the shiro. The discordant artwork on the walls and the lack of detail was reflected in the plate too. The potatoes and carrot pieces were too big and underwhelming. The shiro took a while to grow on me, but it definitely has a lot to address. The shining jewel was the okra in tomato sauce. If only the pigeon peas and red lentils were as flavored this would have been a good experience. The collard greens, as is the case in all Ethiopian restaurants, was forgettable.

Shrinkflation at it's worst. I ordered the meat combo for $20+ dollars and literally got about 2 oz of meat. I brought it home hoping for a meal for me and my partner, but ended up throwing in a can of lentils, a can of potatoes and 4 more ounces of seasoned chicken breast. I don't think I'll be ordering this again unless they make it like they used to. Btw, one of the dishes had only one bone with barely any meat on it.

This was always one of my favorite Ethiopian restaurants in Temescal when I lived down the street. After moving back to the Midwest where it's impossible to find Ethiopian/Eritrean cuisine everywhere this was one of my first stops when I returned for a visit. So happy to see the quality is just as good as I remember. Kitfo and shiro and the shrimp alichea are some of the best you're going to find.

I had the pleasure of trying this fish and vegetable dish served on injera, and it was absolutely delicious! The fish was tender and flavorful, cooked perfectly with a blend of sautéed greens, onions, and herbs. The vegetables added a fresh and savory balance, while the injera soaked up all the rich juices, enhancing every bite.

formatted_address: 2525 Telegraph Ave Ste. A, Oakland, CA 94612, United States
name: Abyssinia Market

reviews.text: I want to try making ethiopian food at home so I went here to get ingredients and they were super helpful and friendly. They even gave me advice for how to use certain items and to keep the niter kibbeh good.

I love coming here. It's clean and the ladies are nice each time I see one of them. I like to buy my kolo and injera here it is fresher than other places. We are lucky there are many other markets between Oakland and Berkeley so to each their own.  We need African businesses to stay open and thrive. Thus place is amazing and honestly so are most of the Ethiopians businesses and restaurants

I’m very unsure why people that have nothing nice to say feel it’s okay to broadcast it on a site where it will forever remain. I read all of the reviews prior to driving all the way from the Benicia area for injera and some spices. Despite the reviews, I always try new places. I am aware that everyone is entitled to leaving whatever comments they’d like. My experience will be my own. This place is very neat, clean, organized, and you are pleasantly greeted upon entry by an Ethiopian woman usually. Beautiful energy. I’m not in anyway offended by the language barrier when I am purchasing popular goods from another country that you can only buy in small businesses like this one. I mean what do you expect? Maybe we should learn the language of the people we are buying from. I’m just saying. Pricing for everything in this place is amazing and so is the injera! I mean it’s like it came from the kitchen of an Auntie or Grandmother that made it with so much perfection and love! I bought a beautiful hand woven basket for serving, spices, red lentils, and about 30 pieces of injera. I will be driving back to this place as often as possible. There’s even an Ethiopian bakery directly across the street! WHAT! If your planning on hosting and serving this style cuisine then you have scored big to come across this gem. I’m hooked as long as they’re open and no, I was not asked or paid to write this review. Just disappointed that anyone would have anything bad to say about an ethnic place trying to strive to stay in business like anyone else! Cheers! To many more years of good service!
Dont be a cheap for gloves. You should change ur glove when you sell Injera. She takes money doing  something and count injera using the same gloves. Have you ever take food handling class ?

Abyssinia Market is one of the first injera stores in Oakland-San Francisco Bay Area that features a special brown teff and barley mixture. Loved & popular for the past ten plus years, making it a staple in the community, their injera doesn’t bloat the stomach and has the realest taste and ingredients in comparison to most injera I’ve tried in the whole area. I assure you this injera tops the list as best in quality & taste how it digests and most like the injera back in Ethiopia/Eritrea. The best! And the owner is a sweetheart I love Abyssinia! Do not be mislead other stores injera have not been around as long and don’t emphasis on taste and ingredients. They either short hand you on authenticity or ingredient and taste. My favorite injera 🤤😋 Tadu’s Kitchen features their injera also please request it

formatted_address: 4301 Piedmont Ave B, Oakland, CA 94611, United States
name: Messob Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: Messob is my favorite Ethiopian restaurant; it is my go-to when I’m craving authentic, delicious Ethiopian food. My top favorite dishes are Kitfo, kuanta Firfir, if you’re looking for spicy 🌶️, and the fried fish with Messer wote. The veggie combo is yummy too. It is also a good choice for ordering takeout food when visiting family or friends. They will beautifully pack it; the presentation is colorful if you order veggie combo dishes, and you can request a Messob (an Ethiopian basket used for family-style eating; *need to be returned). I regularly use them for catering, too, for holidays and gatherings. Don't forget to try their honey wine; don't let the sweetness fool you.

We had lunch here today as recommended by our daughter. It was perfect for us. Lots of vegetarian options with great flavors. We ate the lentil-stuffed sambusa too fast to take a picture. We shared the vegetarian combo with buticha (chickpea dip). We also enjoyed their Ethiopian beer and honey wine.
I ordered doro tibs with a side of missir wot. The tibs were bone dry and oily at the same time. The missir wot did not taste fresh. Lastly, I found a long gray hair in my food.
This is our go to Ethiopian! Love everything they make but usually get the vegetarian sampler with butecha and mushrooms.
Don’t know much about Ethiopian food, but the meal is really good and suit my taste. The serving lady is lovely and warm.

formatted_address: 913 4th St, Santa Rosa, CA 95404, United States
name: Abyssinia Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: This place is amazing! Saba, our server was a really nice girl. She helped me pick finalize my drink and I picked the Telba. The food was tasty and flavorful. Definitely coming back and supporting this place 💥

This is a hidden gem and well worth the experience. Food is highly seasoned and hits your palate in all the right places. From tart, to sweet to spicy with a zip each dish takes you to on a journey. Eating with your fingers makes the food taste even even sweeter. Owner and his staff are friendly and helpful at explaining menu items which is an added plus.
I’m leaving a five star for the amazing food and excellent service. Everything is made fresh and lives up to its hype. If you’ve never tried Ethiopian food, you should give it a shot.

Amazing food! First time here so we weren't sure what to order but the lady helped us out and was very welcoming. We weren't a fan of spicy food so she made sure to point out the dishes that weren't spicy! She also reccomended us 3 do a large single sharing dish and showed us how to eat it with the bread. I highly reccomend the fish, non spicy lamb, and the non spicy beef dish! Very delicious all around

Nice, family-run, Ethiopian restaurant with authentic and delicious dishes in the heart of Santa Rosa. Always a pleasure to come back and try the various stews - from beef, lamb and chicken to many vegetarian options. Good stuff!

formatted_address: 5155 3rd St, San Francisco, CA 94124, United States
name: Walia Ethiopian Express

formatted_address: 1550 Evans Ave, San Francisco, CA 94124, United States
name: Hungry Cafe

reviews.text: This place is a gem!  Their food is incredibly sophisticated and delightful.  The guy running it us really kind and helpful.  And there are great outdoor spots nearby to eat.  Definitely considering coming here for lunch, breakfast or a smoothie!  (By the way, they are NOT located in an office complex.  It's a really nice community center, with a cool garden/playground.)
The perfect spot for peaceful cafe + nature + work spaces + food. Plus it has halal chicken as a bonus! unique latte flavors like orange blossom, rosemary and hibiscus and a beautiful space !

Excellent assortment of California-style Mediterranean dishes — perfect for breakfast or lunch, morning coffee or teatime with a work date or colleague.

Falafel with carrot hummus, dolmas, pickled veg, and soft boiled egg — deliciously light and satisfying.

Sumac Fried Chicken Sandwich, slightly spicy, a wonderfully Middle Eastern twist on a classic American. Thumbs up.

Elegant, sleek, but approachable dining experience with floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking a two-acre park. Work counters with outlets and couches. Peace.

Super friendly staff.
Comforting yet spacious space.
My wife and I spent a few hours here enjoying coffee and reading.
Free wifi available.
Great place to relax and read.

Soooo good, this place mainly has Egyptian food with some generic options as well.
The falafel is sooo tasty! Everything just works! Also, the presentation, it’s piece of art.
Coffee is also good. The vibe is very comfortable - good place to hang out and work a bit

formatted_address: 5176 3rd St, San Francisco, CA 94124, United States
name: Gumbo Social

reviews.text:
TLDR: solid food for fair prices

We got the lunch special with half shrimp po-boy, French fries and a cup of gumbo as well as a hoecake and a lemon pound cake. The shrimp were good and large, the hoecake was decent but I wish they gave us something to keep it moist like some kind of sauce. The lemon cake tasted like something you’d get from Starbucks, not really tasting homemade or fresh but still ok in taste.

Was visiting San Francisco for part of my birthday trip and stumbled upon this hidden foodie gem. The food was sooo good! I ordered the smoked turkey gumbo and a shrimp poboy. I've visited NOLA several times and eating this meal definitely gave me nostalgia. 10/10 definitely recommend! Can't wait to come back 🤤🤤🤤
The seaburger (fried fish sandwich) was one of the best fish sandwiches I've ever had!! Would come back just for that. Chicken and sausage was phenomenal too. Love this place!

This place was great. We stopped in for restaurant week and got half gumbo, half po’boy combos.
