We focused on the shareable plates and loved everything we tried - the flavors are truly authentic and delicious. Make sure you don't skip the complementary pickles; they're a standout! And the mint tea is the perfect, refreshing end to the meal.

What makes this place special is the service. The host and the entire staff are wonderful people who make you feel right at home. Great food, great people - we highly recommend Old Jerusalem for a top-notch dining experience!

Old Jerusalem is an absolute must-visit. The atmosphere is warm and inviting, but the food is the real star of the show.

Here’s what we had:
Chicken Shawarma Plate: The chicken was perfectly seasoned and tender. It paired perfectly with their fluffy rice and hummus.
Lamb Chops Plate: These were the highlight of the night! Cooked perfectly - juicy, and incredibly flavorful. You can tell they use high-quality meat.
Kunafa: You cannot leave without ordering this. It arrived warm, gooey, and sweet with that signature crunchy topping. It’s easily one of the best versions of this dessert I’ve ever had.

Got the beef shawarma, musakhan, and crispy kunafa and everything was good but the musakhan is such a stand out: well seasoned, tender fall off the bone chicken with lots of sumac and sweet onion, the bread underneath just soaking off all that juice. Will be thinking about it often! Everyone there is also so sweet and kind, will fs come back soon and often

Outstanding middle eastern food. Awesome ambience and service. Falafel and Kunafa were amazingly fresh and tasty. Other dishes we ordered were also top notch.
Good atmosphere and great service. Thanks!

I ordered the chicken kabob plate and my friend got the beef shawarma! The meat was cooked perfectly and seasoned well. The turmeric rice and hummus were also delicious. Wish the service was a bit faster. Enjoyed the side pitas and dipping sauces. I want to come back to try the other Palestinian dishes for sure.

formatted_address: 1805 Haight St, San Francisco, CA 94117, United States
name: Parada 22

reviews.text: This place is pure perfection and they definitely know how to cook puerto rican food in original recipes but would satisfy a modern taste. Everything was perfectly cooked and this very friendly restaurant is always either slightly buzzing or very buzzing and I'm super happy that it is doing well in San Francisco. So many good things on their menu and the prices are actually quite a bargain considering the typical price in San Francisco for that quality of food.

The food was beautiful. I ordered the monfongo supremo with tostones and a side of arroz con gandules. I wasn't expecting this but when I began to eat my food I was transformed back to grandmas house an experience I've lived 1000 times and the food brought me to tears. How beautiful the love is in the food. This place has Boricua soul and the vibe is right. Parada 22 better be on your list if you love food and soul. This is my soul food

I came to this restaurant with my husband and kids and we were blown away by  everything that was put in front of us. Everything was  tasty, fresh, and delicious! There were a few vegetarian/pescatarion options so if you are vegetarian or pescatarian, you definitely don't have to go somewhere else. They also had breakfast, lunch, and dinner options. We absolutely loved this lunch and would definitely recommend going here!!!
The food was delicious!  We ordered the sampler and two sides (habichuelas blancas and arroz amarilo), great options to try some of several menu items.  The server was very attentive and helpful.
Tostones were very good. The chicken and waffles was pretty average, they probably have other better dishes. The carne sandwich was good. Good service too

formatted_address: 2645 El Camino Ave Ste A, Sacramento, CA 95821, United States
name: Palace Bar & Grill - African Restaurant

reviews.text: I'm extremely disappointed with the food-to-go experience at this place, African Palace bar & grill. After spending $130, the quality, taste, and portion sizes were nowhere near worth the price. I imagine the cook was either high or intoxicated serving such. The plantains were burnt, meat pies were overly salt and had far too much dough. Egusi was completely plain with no flavor, which was shocking. The so-called beef stew was not a stew, it tasted like basic tomato sauce with a couple of pieces of beef thrown in. The goat meat was very tough, clearly not cooked with the stew, no spice or flavor. The jollof rice was dry, fufu wasn’t soft, and overall the food lacked the rich seasoning and care you expect from Afrikan cuisine. Between the poor preparation, lack of flavor, and small portions, this was a huge letdown. If you’re looking for good Afrikan food, save your money and go to the Bay for a better authentic Afrikan food experience. Not here. Listen to the other reviewers, they were right.

Greeted by a horrible host who seated us but never came back to take our order.  I waved to get his attention and he picked up his cellphone and walked back into the kitchen.  Another person from the kitchen came out, walked around and finally, as we are the only customer there, took our order and then came back after five minutes and ask about what we ordered again.  After 10 mins he comes with our food and gave us microwaved food.  I believe all they did was fried the chicken and put the sauce all over it.
The fufu (that I was looking forward to) was not fresh, small and not cooked thoroughly.  The food did not taste or looked like what I have had before.  The customer service was horrible, we didn't get any napkins and no water refills.  The same guy finally came back from the kitchen and just waited for us to ask for the check.  Don't waste your time or money on this place.

We really enjoyed this food.It was very authentic & Delicious. We didn't break the bank when we ate out here.Each person was the average twenty-five with appetizers. The service was.
Okay. The music was too loud for a restaurant at 4 o'clock. The music was so loud that we almost didn't come in. We thought we had the wrong place. It was like a nightclub. I'm glad we did. Other than the music level, we enjoyed the restaurant, which is beautiful.I would suggest a restaurant to go to.
For a first timer of coming to this place and trying the food I give it a 10/10. The service, food and atmosphere is amazing! Will definitely be back
Exceptional dishes from several African cuisine tastes. Swallows, fufu, and soups were all high quality and freshly made. Will definitely try again.

formatted_address: 2435 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94121, United States
name: Zitouna

reviews.text: Absolutely love this place! A hidden gem in SF serving incredible Tunisian and Middle Eastern food. Everything is delicious, full of authentic flavor, and beautifully presented. The cozy and beautifully decorated space makes you feel right at home. It’s a true family-run restaurant, and you can feel the warmth from the owner and the whole team, super welcoming and friendly. Don’t miss their Turkish coffee, it’s the best in town!

I love this place! Medhi and Anna are the best and when you come here you feel like family! A nice, varied manu. Everything is delicious and  fresh. You will not walk away hungry or without leftovers! All the dips are demolished!

Counter service but you still feel like you are being waited on.

If you’re looking for a restaurant that truly stands out in the neighborhood,  Zitouna on Clement Street is a hidden gem in Inner Richmond ! The food is fresh, flavorful, and authentically Mediterranean — not the usual “fusion” style you find elsewhere. The portions are generous, the prices are reasonable, and the service is friendly and quick.
There’s usually no long wait, and the location is super convenient. I really appreciate that they stay true to traditional Mediterranean flavors — it’s rare to find that level of authenticity these days. Highly recommend supporting this local spot so they can keep serving up their amazing dishes!

I loved the Shakshouka! it's  a North African and Middle Eastern dish of eggs poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce, often with onions, garlic, and cumin. Originating in Tunisia, it's a versatile dish enjoyed for breakfast...

Cute, vibrant atmosphere with deliciously authentic food! Everything was fresh and well made, just as pictured! The lamb was well spiced and the rice was perfectly cooked. Hummus was exactly like we had in the Middle East, creamy and delightful, served with warm pita. The owners were also super friendly and generous; customer service was on another level. (Pictured are their falafel, lamb kabobs, and combination dip platter.)

Beautifully located on a lively street in a great neighborhood, this Mediterranean restaurant stands out with its stylish interior and impressive high ceilings. The decor is tasteful and creates an open, airy atmosphere.

The food is of high quality, fresh, well-prepared, and flavorful. Portions are very generous, which is great value, but can be a bit much if you’re not a big eater or short on time.

Staff were friendly and welcoming, though service could have been a bit quicker. One small drawback: the acoustics. The high ceiling makes it a little tricky to have a soft-spoken conversation.

Still, a solid experience overall, especially if you’re looking to enjoy a slow, relaxed meal.

formatted_address: 2700 L St, Sacramento, CA 95816, United States
name: Naija Cuisine

reviews.text:
We’ve always loved ordering from this place because the food is really good! However, consistency is a big issue. The food we bought the other day had extremely chewy meat maybe it was rushed!
We ordered four stews: I specifically requested 2 ogbono, one veggie with goat meat and one with fish, but when I opened the containers, it was all goat meat!
Also, just because this place doesn’t have much competition doesn’t mean service should be lacking. When we called at 11 AM, we were told pickup would be in 45 minutes because the food was still cooking. When we arrived, we were asked to wait 10 minutes, which ended up being another 20 plus minutes, and then were told to wait 5 more minutes. This kind of service is frustrating and unprofessional.
Even if the food is good, the hassle and lack of consistency really take away from the experience!

Reminder: cash or cash app only. Super nice chef/owner and delicious food! Drop by to pick up food to take home or for a picnic. We needed some food separate for a child and she was very kind helping us find options that worked.
Ordered Amala with ewedu and goat meat it was really good would definitely be eating here again!!!
I had vegetable soup. I wanted it spicy and spicy it was. Fresh from the oven.

formatted_address: 313 W Lake St, Minneapolis, MN 55408, United States
name: Taste Of East African

reviews.text:
Discover the vibrant flavors of East Africa—right here in Minneapolis!

Taste of East African invites you on a culinary adventure filled with bold spices, rich aromas, and unforgettable dishes. Sip on fragrant African Chai, savor the tender, perfectly seasoned Rice with Goat, and enjoy the comforting classic Ugali with mouthwatering Goat Mea - each bite crafted with authentic tradition and passion.

Whether you're grabbing a quick meal or planning a flavorful feast, you can easily order online and pick up at the restaurant. Parking is convenient, with meters on Lake Street and free neighborhood parking nearby.

Join the many fans who keep this spot buzzing with energy and great food. Friendly service, incredible flavors - come experience the Taste of East African for yourself!

I’ve eaten here twice now, and both times the food and service have been incredible! The menu is varied, and everything i’ve tried is great! The people who run it are very kind and knowledgeable about what they have, I totally recommend this place!

The food was very delicious, and was a good introduction to East African cuisine. The service was extremely good. Everybody was super helpful, especially with guiding me and my friends through the menu. Would recommend if you are looking for some good, local food in the area.

ridiculously tasty food, wonderful service, the kindest waiter and cook, extremely attentive, insanely affordable for how full we got. Home made fruit drinks were tasty too. A family business with great food and kind ppl so well worth supporting. Will 100% be coming back with more friends next time

Food was absolutely incredible. Exceeded my expectations completely. All the meat was perfectly cooked and spiced, and the different breads - ugali, malawah, njeera. Our waiter was so friendly and we let him choose what to order us because we wanted to try an authentic Somali family style meal, and it could not have come out more perfect. The sambusas, and guava and vimto juices were awesome too. Highly recommend coming here for a delicious meal, especially if you have never tried East African food before (like us).

formatted_address: 1831 Nicollet Ave, Minneapolis, MN 55403, United States
name: Joe & Nya African Restaurant

reviews.text:
The GF and I visited on a Saturday evening, and while the dine-in area was pretty quiet, there were plenty of takeout orders coming through. The space is small, but the bright colors and upbeat music give it a cozy, welcoming vibe. The lady working was friendly, though it did take about 30 minutes before we were brought water.

The menu could use better descriptions, especially for those who aren’t very familiar with the cuisine. The egusi was flavorful, though a bit thicker than expected. The fish was served hot and crispy, but could use a bit more seasoning. The dipping sauce had a nice kick—very spicy, almost like a habanero oil.

I've seen different ratings from different food servicing platforms and wanted to try it out myself because it was the closest to me. I was pretty disappointed. I ordered the egusi soup with pounded yam 24 oz for $28.99 with extra pepper for $1. First thing I noticed was I did not get my extra pepper kala. It was $1 so, whatever. Food looked good but my first bite in was lacking a lot of flavor. It was bland and almost tasted a little bitter. Curious about the bitterness, I poked around and can see what it looks like to be burnt bottom pieces? For the meat, I can see that its all bony stewing hen pieces. Possibly the worst meat to eat as they are tougher and dryer with littlw to no meat. I wanted to like it but have to admit, this was the worst egusi soup I've had. I've had better egusi soup that came out of a 10oz container with no meat at all and was satisfied with the affordable price. For almost $30, it is not worth it. I'd tip extra to have my food delivered from outside of the area.
The food was SO good! We got the potato leaf and jallof rice. She even let me sample the cassava leaf and potato leaf before I decided. Grace is so nice!

I love the food, I called in about 9pm about to Close, after I called in and she waited on me, when she was about to leave, great place over hands down., services was great.  Great food. The food is cook fresh and ready. I will recommend this place by any time when you get to Minneapolis check it out.
Such a delightful and tasty spot! Super friendly staff, expertly seasoned and freshly fried chicken, and cozy jollof rice. Warm smiles and hot food, will definitely be coming back here 🥰

formatted_address: 1823 Nicollet Ave, Minneapolis, MN 55403, United States
name: Akwaaba Market & Restaurant

reviews.text: So far my favorite restaurant in the area. 10/10 for sure perfectly, tender and flavorful goat stew with fufu and goat jollof. Our order included a spicy sauce on the side that was really good, and it was nice to have it on the side so the younger kids could eat without the spice. We also got a few sambusas that were, of course, very good. Everyone was so friendly while picking up my order. My family really enjoyed our meals. Would definitely recommend and we will be back. Thank you ❤️❤️

First time I tried egusi soup was last Monday. I got it with goat meat. The meat was tender! The soup was very delicious and flavorful. I also got the cassava but it was my least favorite. I’ve had better cassava. I came back today for my second egusi order and this time I got the 24oz. I can’t wait to eat it and watch my shows. I’ll be back each time for the egusi and will probably try more of their soups.

Highly recommend this place if you want to try Nigerian food. I got the fufu + egusi + fried plantains + jollof rice. They gave us a sample of another dish to try to decide if we wanted to order it, which was such a thoughtful gesture. And they have a decent amount of vegetarian options. They have a sit down area in the back, but seems like a place more directed for takeout.

They’ve truly came a LONGGGGG way! When I first tried this restaurant I can’t lie I felt robbed a year later I return and wow I’m truly impressed! The price point is a bit up there now! But the quality is worth it! 9/10 for sure

I love this place it’s right around the corner from my apartment! Good portions baby you’ll be fed and full! It’s just in an area where some people are experiencing poverty, but don’t be afraid it’s not the  restaurants fault! Very nice staff and doing what they need to do! ❤️

formatted_address: 4326 N Lyndale Ave, Minneapolis, MN 55412, United States
name: City Afrique Restaurant

reviews.text: When I say hands down the best west African food I’ve ever had ! Everything was fresh , full of flavor , spice right on , fish great , cassava great , plantains, pepper soup all 10’s!! If she had more help in the front the atmosphere would be a 5 as well !! But the cook needs no help when it comes to that kitchen it was AMAZING !!
Comfortable place to dine, with friendly staff. The food was delicious with family style portions. Beautiful space for small dining or small lunch/dinner parties.

The food here is so horrible.I order some casava leef it was full of oil.The meat is terrible taste old.I will never eat here again.They should have the food inspection service come in. Be careful with eating here
Great place to take your Family! Amazing food! Excellent services with Good prices!

I was really looking forward to this place, but unfortunately, the experience was disappointing. It seems like most, if not all, of the food is prepared or reheated using a microwave. You can clearly hear the microwave door opening and closing, the beeping, and the buttons being pressed—not exactly what you'd expect when dining at a restaurant that’s supposed to serve authentic African cuisine

I came here hoping for fresh, quality food, not something that feels like it came out of a microwave. It kind of defeats the purpose of going out to eat, especially at a cultural spot where you'd expect more care and authenticity in the preparation. Sadly, I don’t think I’ll be returning.

formatted_address: 720 Washington Ave SE, Minneapolis, MN 55414, United States
name: Afro Deli & Grill: Minneapolis

reviews.text: One of my favorite restaurants around campus if not my favorite... Best sweet potato fries in the world. Chicken fantastic (pictured) and chicken curry are highlights, somali steak sandwich is also great. Been here many times and it's incredibly consistent.

I was staying at the Graduate Hilton hotel that is very close to this restaurant during a trip to Minneapolis in July 2025. One evening, a couple of friends and I decided to have dinner there. When we went, there was a small crowd. We immediately got a table and ordered four dishes. The food came pretty soon and were plentiful. Each dish was very tasty. Also, it was unbelievably cheap. We were very happy with our meal and would gladly go back there.

I recently tried Afro Deli for the first time, I ordered the Gyro Jabati wrap. It costed around 13 dollars after taxes.

The service was good, however it took around 6-10 minutes to recieve the food. With the meal it came with fries but there was no drink included. (There is free water though)

The atmosphere was nice, seating is a little limited but the space they did have was excellent.

My problem however is with the food itself, I had high expectations for Afro Deli. Ive heard about their operations for around a decade now and expected the food to be Excellent. I am also very familiar with Somali Cuisine.

The fries were great but the wrap its self had a few key problems which greatly impacted the experience, and I am not a picky eater at all. Unfortunately, the wrap was overfilled with Tzatiki sauce which blinded all other aspects of the wrap, also the rice was dry.
The Jabati itself was great condition and the gyro meat was great too. The given sauce container which I think was a spicy mayo was good too.

Overall the food I got here was better than most places but it did not meet my expectations. Every other aspect was expected and tolerated.
Had the Steak dinner and a Sambusa (Could have eaten 3) Delicious!!! Absolutely amazing experience.

A great on-campus spot when you need something quick and affordable. The space is pretty small so you'll have to squeeze if you are bringing a crowd.

I ALWAYS rave about their chicken fantastic and sweet potato fries, both are my absolute go-to's and I find myself craving them frequently.

Highly recommend for the amazing food and quick service

formatted_address: 6000 Shingle Creek Pkwy, Minneapolis, MN 55430, United States
name: Oga madam kitchen

reviews.text:
Jollof rice with chicken thighs ($19): it was soooo goood. Generous portion. I think it was worth it for the price point. Chicken was tender and juicy.

Egusi soup and fufu ($20). it was my first time trying this, so I wasn’t used to the texture and flavor.

Meat pie ($3.50ish): flavorful, has nice portion of filling.

This seems like a small family business, so understandably they seem to be understaff. The line was long and food took awhile to come out. Staff were very kind and friendly. We waited for a little more than 1hour total to order and to get our food. Definitely will come back here again though for the Jollof.

I usually don’t leave reviews but I was kind of sad I paid $18.99 for 4 slices of plantain, 2 bone in bites of a goat leg meat & what seems to be 6lb of Jollof rice (exaggerating) maybe 2.5-3lbof rice 😂😭 the egusi fufu was fire & filling, really meaty!! 🔥 which is all I really wanted but I wanted to try something new (goat meat).. I asked for extra sauce on the Jollof Rice with goat meat & they didn’t follow through maybe a sauce don’t come with goat meat.. idk if it’s because I had it delivered maybe it’s better in person idk I think the consistency of serving sizes shouldn’t matter regardless. I give 5 stars for flavor, taste was good no salt or anything needed to be added. But I give a 3 stars because 4 goat ankles would have been nice for the $40-$45 I spent lol. I’ll be back for the Egusi fufu though!

This Review is for the last week of 2025. I was craving some African food and seen this was the only place that was open and close to me. So I thought I’d give it a shot. As soon as I walked in I was not greeted and felt un-welcomed. Then I was met with an employee who appeared to be annoyed. I asked a few questions about the menu and he had no knowledge of what I was trying to order even though it was on his menu. I ordered the jollof rice with chicken. The Food was decent. I would not recommend this place if other options are available. Please address your staff’s customer service skills.

I ordered the jollof rice with chicken, suya beef, meat pie, and moi moi. The jollof rice was spicy, full of flavor, and the chicken was crispy and juicy. The suya beef meat was chewy, well seasoned, and the platter of veggies was fresh. Meat pie was a fantastic appetizer, haven't had a meat pie this good in a long time. Moi moi was good too. The wait time wasn't that bad, and it's pretty normal to wait for this freshly prepared food. Everyone I encountered with the staff were respectful and friendly. Oga Madam is an amazing place for authentic West African cuisine!

I came in to dine with my family and I must say I had an awesome experience.
Joyce attended to us in the most friendly and courteous manner.
The food is top notch, ambience is superb and perfectly African themed.
Will definitely stop by again whenever I am in town.
I am a food connoisseur and very hard to please when it comes to taste, so trust me when I say this restaurant is a hit!
Great job guys, keep up the good work!

formatted_address: 2325 E Franklin Ave, Minneapolis, MN 55406, United States
name: Taste Of Africa Restaurant & Deli

reviews.text: Had a good experience at this restaurant ! My Mom had never tried Ethiopian Food and it's been a while myself - the owner's son was very helpful in guiding us to decide what was popular and how we could try / share some of the food. They were big portions with a lot of injera bread. Would recommend.

The entrance is quite hard to find as it is all the way at the back of the building but once you get in, it is a nice little establishment. Comparing with the few Ethiopian restaurants nearby, the food is less spicy which is nice for me, and the flavor is great.
Everything was delicious.  The prices are very reasonable.  Would go back if I lived here.

Me and my family used to love this place but it’s not the same anymore. We ordered melewa to go and that was one of the worst melewa we have ever eaten. It was not fresh, i believe they must have cooked it 2 days ago or so. The price does not much the food at all. Very disappointing!

A little bit difficult to see when on Franklin Ave, but worth having to go around the block a few times to find this place.  Food was amazing.  I ordered  incorrectly and I was still very pleased with the food.  So tasty, not overly spicy, just great!

formatted_address: 1601 Freeway Blvd #1756, Minneapolis, MN 55430, United States
name: Jambo Africa Restaurant N Bar

reviews.text:
The food was very satisfying and delicious. Just like homemade.
I ordered both the chicken curry and beef fry(Karanga) with fufu. 🤤
Also order the Egushi dish to dip fufu into.
Tables and chairs are conveniently place to sit wherever you like.
The bathrooms were clean.
It was a very nice experience.
Will be going back for sure! 💯
Thank you for making delicious food and providing great service! 🙏

Ordering takeout is a privilege- a luxury if you will. So if I go spend my hard earned money, and drive 25 minutes to pick it up- I expect my order to be correct especially when I have to wait an extra 20 minutes. I ordered collards and okra stew.. They gave me the correct items but why did I come with NO meat? Excuse me? What am I paying for then? There is non a NON MEAT option on the menu so why was I given just greens? Of course I did not realize until I got home- so I tried calling and guess what? No answer. I called multiple times and no answer..

This shit is absolutely disgusting. I ordered cassava with fufu and rice. One didn’t get my full order, two the cassava was overly greasy and didn’t taste like ANYTHING no seasonings whatsoever,secondly there was only TWO pieces of meat in a 32oz,& finally the fufu was so dry and thick it’s actually ridiculous. If you want good quality African food I HEAVILY & WHOLEHEARTEDLY suggest going to Akwaaba. In this case it’s true that all good food comes from bad neighborhoods cause there’s literally no way. I’m so irritated that I even spent damn near 40 dollars on ts when I would’ve spent HALF of that at Akwaaba and I would’ve been satisfied I would’ve gotten my whole order and all. I can tell they ain’t make this with love they would’ve been better off just declining my order. Please do yourself a favor and eat somewhere else you won’t regret it like I am right now.
Cold food chapati is hard as stone no cabbage, & this is not goat meat call it what you want it but goat on god,,I throw away  the food. First & last time am order I don’t think this is Kenyan food

This place added a sauce that seemed like someone's leftover in my order when I asked for sauce the that was missing in my order. If you look at the sauce containers, one is not even up to half of the container, talkless of being full like the rest. The woman just picked it from the back so it seems like she didn't pick it from the stock but just a leftover from someone. Also, their food does not have the quality that it used to have. I will not go to this place again. They may be serving leftovers to customers.

formatted_address: 1831 Central Ave NE, Minneapolis, MN 55418, United States
name: Hodan Cuisine

reviews.text: Such a great experience! The best part? The gentleman behind the counter who took our order was incredibly kind. He was one of the most friendly people ever and he was so excited to serve us that he kept throwing in free items on our order. The food was absolutely delicious and it was a lot for what we paid! Loved the murals too! The worst part? The restaurant could use a bit more cleaning but nothing too bad. Would come again!

The owner is so friendly and welcoming and serve us with Somali tea! The tea was very good and I ordered beef sambusa half of rice with goat. The portions were huge and the beef sambusas were hot and fresh and the goat and rice were delicious! I have a lot of leftovers enough for 3 meals. I love this place and I will definitely come back again!

Too many cooks in the Kitchen and bad quality food. Go there if you don’t mind eating burnt expensive food that can risk your health. I will never recommend this place! I will let the burnt $17.95 Philly Steak below tell the rest of the Story!

Love the GOAT meat with rice! The green spicy sauce is super also! I always come here when I am
In town! The restaurant is small and can only seat so many but I recommend you try it out! The photo is the FULL portion of Goat & Rice! Must try if you are near the area!

Hodan Cuisine is that spot. Their loaded fries are honestly my favorite thing on the menu — so flavorful, perfectly seasoned, and the meat is always super tender. You can tell they care about quality because everything tastes fresh and made with love.

The customer service makes the whole experience even better they’re hilarious, and friendly, and make you feel right at home every time. It’s one of those places where the food hits every time and the vibe matches it. Definitely a must try if you haven’t been yet!

formatted_address: 6838 N Humboldt Ave, Brooklyn Center, MN 55430, United States
name: Taste of Africa The Best of African Cuisines

reviews.text: My experience has been quite pleasant, with friendly individuals and a positive atmosphere that contributes to an overall enjoyable visit. Additionally, the pricing is quite reasonable compared to other establishments. I also appreciate the diverse selection of authentic African dishes offered on the menu.
The Best African restaurant in town! Very delicious food and affordable prices.
They serve pork products as goat meat. Ox tail , but the bones of the meat and the thick skin of pork , like that of ham hock is not from goats.  Ox tail doesn't have

This is a very busy spot in the heart of Brooklyn Park and the food and staff is top notch. They feature a variety of African cuisine, especially Liberian. They have cassava leaf, potatoes greens, palava sauce, attieke and fish, palava sauce, groundpea candy, coconut candy, and more.

The best Jollof rice in MN !! Tried many restaurants always disappointed when it comes to jollof rice. I was so happy when they let me try the jollof before I bought it and of course they did their thing !! Authentic African food ! ❤️❤️😫😋

formatted_address: 8527 Zane Ave N, Brooklyn Park, MN 55443, United States
name: Glamaur African Kitchen

reviews.text: I enjoyed the combo rice (jollof and fried) with the big piece of chicken and stew. Suya meat was amazing! So tender and seasoned really well. Meat pie was ok. Moi moi was also good. Customer service was exceptional, felt like I was a welcomed guest in their home! I will need to stop in again when they have snail in stock.
Excellent food and everyone is friendly!!

Watch out when,ordering food they give people messed up food. They are not willing to correct there mistakes properly without the customer having issues with them .

Yelling, screaming,loud voice against customers and disrespectful,rude attitude is unacceptable at anycost.

The customers labor day and night for the restaurant to have roof over their head and shield-and just the honor greet them properly with honor treat them right is very difficult for Glamour Kitchen.

I hope they understand that tomorrow is different day, what happens tomorrow is God's willingness

The customers that you are mistreated are they ones that can help you in emergency or uncertain situations and stand up

They will turn back against them God forbid.
Guy tries charging me 60 bucks for two large Egusi. I’ve never paid that much for Egusi. I went right down the street for much cheaper…30 bucks can’t beat that. I will never come here again

I have been wanting to try African food for a long time but did not know where to go until today. I was brought to this establishment and I ate some of the most amazing food. The customer service was so friendly, and patient with me. They made sure it was prepared perfectly as this was my first time. It did not disappoint at all. The atmosphere was God centered with worship music playing and being able to eat, laugh and listen and watch live tv worship services in Africa was the highlight. Thank you so much I will be back.

formatted_address: 400 Wabasha St N, St Paul, MN 55101, United States
name: Afro Deli & Grill

reviews.text: You are seriously a dummy if you go to Minneapolis and don’t hit one of these. The beef sambusa with the green hot sauce and steak plate and plantains…nomnomnom and the girls working the counter are adorable and friendly. It rocks and I took mine on Amtrak to Chicago. It’s only expensive if you order too much! Go!!

Dreary Monday? Stop by the bright and friendly AfroDeli! The variety of seating (beautiful chairs in color and function) for wheelchairs and stand up people are all here for you  to eat the chicken Fantastic and other great menu options. The Chcicken Fantastic is aptly named and comes in veggie!! Halal, vegetarian, special orders- it is all here and delicious! Sweet potato fries like everything else are fresh and taste amazing. Especially the green sauce that accompany samosas! Yum!
Afro Deli has a catering kitchen around the corner so dont be confused by the 2 addresses.
Go to Candyland too by the catering kitchen. We

This restaurant is somewhat overhyped—it’s a very ordinary, typical Chipotle-style establishment. However, don’t get me wrong—Chipotle offers a better selection and tastier menu options overall.

During this visit, I ordered a chapati wrap with French fries and tea. The tea was decent—I’d rate it 8/10.

The chapati wrap was essentially a flatbread filled with pieces of beef, lettuce , and some vegetables. The taste was below average, especially when compared to Chipotle.

That said, the restaurant does have a nice atmosphere, good seating, and solid customer service.
Diverse menu, lunch was delicious. Our group of three enjoyed everything we got. Service was fast and friendly!

Honestly, after I got pregnant and started having an aversion to chicken I started coming here for their Lamb Gyros. I was still craving meat, I did not want chicken, I don't often want Burgers and their Lamb Gyros solved my problem. When I come here I tend to get a Lamb Gyro with a side of Fries. 100% Worth it. Not bad for $12 - $13. For a few more dollars you can get a drink. I have noticed other people also really like their Tea. Maybe when I am not pregnant anymore I will try it. Their fries are delicuous with or without the sauce, 100%. I love their regular fries, but I also love their sweet potato fries. I never have any complaints about the food, they are open until 8pm, the staff is always nice to me and the place is always clean. personally love going to Afro Deli & Grill. The food is good, the price is reasonable, I love their Lamb Gyros and I am so serious about the fries, with or without the sauce the fries taste great! The food is 100% worth it.

formatted_address: 3010 4th Ave S, Minneapolis, MN 55408, United States
name: 3010 Bakery and Kitchen

reviews.text: My family and I come here at least once a week (it’s seriously that GOOD)! The food here is incredible and the customer service is always exceptional. 3010 bakery and cafe is also family friendly. I can’t recommend this place enough!

Took my friend who moved to MN from Tennessee here who was upset about how little spice Minnesota has— he took one bite and I haven’t seen him smile that big in the 6 months he’s been here. The food is hearty and amazing, everyone in the actual restaurant was smiling and kind (got a compliment the second I walked through the door) and it’s immediately become a “yeah we need to become regulars” kind of place. We got 4 mystery things in a too good to go order and they’re allllll spectacular and they’re absolutely worth the sit down in the restaurant next time. Absolutely recommend and I can’t believe we hadn’t heard of it before

Very impressed with the quality of the food. They obviously care about what they are serving. Very clean restaurant. Staff was friendly. Glad I live close to this place. We will be back for sure. Bonus for recycling nerds like me, the to-go boxes are number 5 and therefore are able to be recycled in Minneapolis.

I went to lunch with friend here.  It was decidedly pleasant.  Fairly quiet and relaxing, bright and airy, with plenty of food coming out to try.  I heard they can get pretty busy, but it wasn’t when we were there. They serve a buffet style with different meats, all with savory combinations that are accessible to a midwestern palate.  Kind of a fusionesque mix of foods.  Also there were a few people that came in and got boxes of food to go, so seems like a good option if you want something different to take home.  Definitely have a couple glasses of the spiced tea while you dine!

I don't know if they realized I was there to eat their buffet and I wasnt sure what I was to do when I arrived and this is why I gave a 4 for service,  But after 10 or 15 min, I asked what to do and Isa, who was busy mopping, was kind enough to tell me the buffet is open and instructed me to help myself.  I really enjoyed the buffet.  It was very delicious.  I had the chicken wings with a very savory taste of spice and a hint of sweetness.  It was so good my taste buds where amazed as it was something new.   The chicken  alfredo was a familiar taste and also very satisfying and delicious! There were 3 other items (2 beef and another chicken) along w 2 types of rice dishes, fruits, and salad which were just as satisfying! The cold drinks were amazing I never had them before and the tea? Amazing too!  I plan on returning again real soon!  Thank u Isa! The food was so tasty! 🧡🙏🏽

formatted_address: 2700 Douglas Dr N #2700, Crystal, MN 55422, United States
name: Lagos Cafe

reviews.text: Authentic and flavorful Nigerian food. Great portion size. Best jollof rice and tilapia we have had in the twin cities!

I was driving by and did a double take when I saw their sign. I decided to stop in to see what they offered because Nigerian restaurant menus tend to vary. It’s a small carryout only spot. The woman working there was very nice and accommodating. I informed her that I’m vegan and inquired about a few of my favorite Nigerian foods: egusi, greens, jollof, and beans. She didn’t have egusi. She stated that she had greens but they’re made with fish. She then offered to make me a fresh batch sans the fish if I had time to wait. I most certainly do! It wasn’t a long wait either.  I got a hefty container of food for about $15. There was enough food for 2 days (if I wasn’t being greedy).

I tried my food right away. The greens were very good and clearly freshly made with quality produce. The beans were good. The jollof rice was SLAMMIN!!  Perfection in the flavor department!

I’m unsure how long they’ve been open, but they seem fairly new. They’re located in a strip mall with other small, locally owned businesses. Again, it’s carryout only; you cannot sit in and eat. (I ate in my car.) They also offer catering services.

Be sure to check out this spot if you’re in the MSP area.

I recently visited Lagos Cafe, and while the experience was a bit mixed, there are a few aspects worth noting. The cafe itself is small and distinctly yellow, though the atmosphere wasn't very inviting for a sit-down meal. There weren’t any clear seating arrangements, and it wasn't particularly comfortable—definitely more of a takeout spot than a place to linger and dine.

The staff was polite, offering me a recommendation, but the menu felt limited, especially for the prices charged. I ordered the Jollof Rice, which cost $17.84. The meal came with two small pieces of fish, but the overwhelming majority of the plate was rice. While the spice level was enjoyable, the portion balance was disappointing, with far too much rice compared to the fish. The presentation was underwhelming and could use improvement.

Overall, I feel like the meal was overpriced for what I received, and I would likely only consider returning for a quick takeout rather than a dine-in experience.
My dad and I just had our first ever Jollof rice and are now obsessed.  Food was absolutely delicious, super fast and service was awesome. Highly recommend to everyone!
Delicious, fast and friendly. Jollof rice spicy but not overwhelming--lots more on the menu that I'd like to try, especially the friday/saturday specials.

formatted_address: 117 Willow Bend, Crystal, MN 55428, United States
name: 3DS African Kitchen Amala Joint

reviews.text: The food was good and staff were welcoming. We had a good time there! Jollof rice, fried rice, okra soup and swallow were all so delicious.

I really enjoyed my time here! The hostess was nice and was informative of the food. I tried the egusi soup and fufu. It was very good, chicken was very tender. I will come back to this place and try the cassava leaf!

The Jollof rice and fish was good but the Egusi and fufu came out room temperature. The meat in the Egusi consisted of smoked turkey necks and dry day old chicken which was not very appetizing. We ordered their Ayamase but didn’t not get to try it because it took so long, we had to cancel it. Additionally, we were charged for their large Egusi because they supposedly only serve that size for dine in. Their menu indicated their large is a 24 oz but our serving was in a small bowl closer to 16 oz. There were also many angry customers leaving without their food because the wait was so long, not to mention the server was not very friendly. Overall customer service was lacking, food took too long and didn’t not come out hot, and pricing was inconsistent with their menu. If I had a second chance, I would definitely skip this spot.

Ordered fish gravy, the fish was not descaled and it messed up the whole dish, total waste of money. The soups were dry. My collard greens were sweet (yuck) spinach was okay turkey was tougher and dry. Ton of flavor though. prices are way too high for the food they give out. Employees are rude. I will not order from here again food is gross.

I ordered the cassava leaf and it was not good at all. I couldn’t even force myself to continue to eat it. Not what I was expecting at all and I asked for beef and smoked turkey but I got smoked turkey and chicken. I would not spend my money here again. If you want good African food..go to African deli on Brooklyn blvd and it’s cheaper there 🤦🏽‍♀️

formatted_address: 2401 E Franklin Ave, Minneapolis, MN 55406, United States
name: Iftin Restaurant

reviews.text: Came here for a lunch and wowie! The food was SO flavorful! There are pictures on the menu so you can get a peek of what everything is. Food came out quickly and there's a small parking lot behind the place! Highly recommend

Here on a DoorDash pick up.. This place is NASTY inside. Not clean at all.. I’ve stood here 8 minutes and not 1 person has said 1 word to me. I said something about it and I was just ignored. The city needs to come in there and take a look around. It is DIRTY in there!! I would NEVER eat ANYTHING from out of this place. GROSS!!

If you're in the mood for a culinary adventure, I highly recommend a visit. I ordered the Biryani with Chicken Steak, and it was an absolute delight. The combination of tender chicken steak and aromatic biryani was very good.

You know those hole in the wall places that's like a hidden secret? This place is a bona-fide gem. Never had Somali food until now. I have been missing out. We split 3 things between 4 adults and 2 kids and had a little left over still. I'd describe Somalian food as somewhere between Indian and Mediterranean cuisines. The rice was amazing! The beef and the chicken were so gooood!

I almost called to complain because I thought they gave me chicken when I ordered fish… y’all this FISH taste like chicken, soooooo good!! They really put their foot in the food. Made with love! Top tier! Superb! Everything was better than expected. This is now my go to African spot :) the fufu had the consistency of grits tho, still good in taste.

They also gave me a free banana and water bottle… because they care

formatted_address: 2913 27th Ave S, Minneapolis, MN 55406, United States
name: Quruxley Restaurant

reviews.text:
Lunch break, decided to lunch here for the first time after grocery run at Aldi. Wished they had a menu available earlier for people waiting in line, though the menu linked online in maps reflects most of the named items though may not include descriptions.

Ordering was easy, got the chicken schwarma that comes with a cold drink. I got the vimto, not knowing what it was, and it seemed to be close to a very flavorful hibiscus drink, highly recommended. Also got a black coffee with some sugar, hot and tasty.

The schwarma, cut in halves, was delicious, savory, and filling. The fries were warm, crispy, and well seasoned.

The booth I sat at was cozy and well cushioned. Warm, cozy temperature as the weather dips into 30s.

Great value overall, highly recommend!

Worst restaurant I have ever seen. Food was below standards, salty, expensive and tasteless. Employees are not trained properly, and the management are also unprofessional.

I ordered rice with lamb, and they brought me something I didn’t liked. I asked the waiter if he can help me since I didn’t get the food I expected. He replied me rudely: was better to say that before you eat. I can’t help you now and he walked away.

Things get worse when the owner of the restaurant said the same words. Despite the fact  that they are losing me as a customer, I warn others to not go this restaurant which I believe it will not last longer. Five years ago, this restaurant was shut down because of Improper sanitation and lack of cleanliness.

Since they reopened five years later, I would say they are worse than before. I would have been happy if I can rate zero but I rated 1 because of Google.

Worst Somali restaurant, poor service, no customer care and very expensive they are even charging Somali sauce (Maraq), we ordered isbartiimo food for 4 p and they brought food for 2, and if you want extra rice nobody wants to come and take your order, they want you to go to the counter be in the queue and order again.

I believe this was the 3rd time I’ve been. They’ve improved the number of staff & the taste of the food from when I was here last which was quite awhile ago. Today I got a beef sambusa, mango juice, goat meat, & chicken suqaar w/ rice. It comes with a complimentary soup that I don’t recall how to spell the name of in Somali, but it’s delicious. I had them prepare what I ordered “spicy” as well & that was a wise decision on my part. Everything tasted great & as always I had another serving to take home for dinner. African restaurants portions for the price are almost always hearty.
Customer online is 10/10  I asked for an extra salads which I got . Thanks for taking time to read the note and alway send my orders as I asked the loyal restaurant I know .

formatted_address: 1401 11th Ave S, Minneapolis, MN 55404, United States
name: East Village Grill

reviews.text: Dishonest Crooks. Overcharged me 20% for a takeout sandwich. Menu says $12.99 for Gryo sandwich and I was charged $16.00 when he typed it in. Price includes a drink but all he had was warm Pepsi and I don't drink cola. Grabbed a bottle of water just hanging out on the floor in a package. There's a fountain soda machine but no cups. Never going back. Why be so blatenty dishonest? Gyro wasn't even that good.

There was a mistake with my order, and I was extremely polite and patient And I tried real hard to understand what they were saying which the server understood just enough so that I can get my food.  But when the mistake happened with my order, he talked to the cook through the little window. The cook came out and Said he didn’t speak English and wave me away with the swish of his wrist before turning away.  Needless to say, I never got the correction of my order in person and he was very rude.  He did not attempt to give me my money back so I had no choice but to walk away.   I’ve heard the food is very good there but now I’ll never know.  I would not go back there because I was so disregarded as a customer and dismissed.

East Village is hands down the best Somali restaurant around!
Their sambusa is absolutely delicious — crispy, fresh, and perfectly seasoned. The chicken salad is next level: clean, flavorful, and beautifully presented. The quality of the food here is unmatched, and the service is always friendly and fast. If you’re looking for top-notch Somali cuisine, East Village is the place to go!

Food was delicious price is decent they prefer cash than cards convenient!!
And the food is just out of this world taste is on point the staff are respectful and delicate to your order
Would say great over all!!
I took three bites and threw my food on the ground. It was old meat, I  got my money back!

formatted_address: 6020 65th Ave N, Minneapolis, MN 55429, United States
name: Ms. Kamara African Cuisine

reviews.text: Loved the service! I received my food just in the nick the nick of time and it was so good! I’m definitely telling my friends to order. Great job! 😋

formatted_address: 320 Cedar Ave South, Minneapolis, MN 55454, United States
name: The Red Sea Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: During a recent trip to Minneapolis, I went there for dinner on a Sunday evening in July. They are located close to a train station, which made it easy for me to go there. I was greeted warmly. I ordered a chicken dish, injeera, and spinach---they were glad to accommodate my request--the menu does not include spinach. The food came pretty quickly, was warm, very tasty, and plentiful. And the food was relatively cheap. I would gladly go there again.

Service was stellar - even at 11 in the evening. Food was amazing  - a little heat & so much flavor. As a vegan, it's not often I have so many choices - especially without any customizations. Will definitely be back!

As much as I thought they had economical options, their food was overall sloppily made and didn't contain enough flavor. I believe they toned down the seasoning a bit to potentially serve people that couldn't handle spice, which resulted in their food overall on the plain side relatively. There are still some highlights worth pointing out, though, which I will try to do.

I thought the ater kik and the shiro were overall well made, and one bite with a chunk of injera offered a traditionally tasty experience. Miser was okay, and could use more seasoning in my opinion. The doro wot also didn't have enough spice, and the chicken didn't necessarily have an "off the bone" quality like I would have loved. The lantil alicha was pretty good because lentils, which wouldn't normally be considered tasty, were pretty tasty. Both the yabesha gomen (kale) and tikel gomen (cabbage) were unfortunately bland as well in comparison.

Spending just around $13 for a veggie firfir, which was a veggie sampler for one person, was a good deal, though. I think those who are around the Cedar area can still have a good time here.
this was my first time trying Ethiopian food and it was great! Our server was super patient and kind. The mango juice is great and I got the half and half

Look if you want to feel like back home go try  this lady food , Been cooking since I was a baby , every time you order say to her can I get the butter added with my meal  😋,  real authentic Ethiopian food

formatted_address: 6930 Brooklyn Blvd #13, Brooklyn Center, MN 55429, United States
name: African Deli

reviews.text: I can't even describe how good this food is! I had the Edward's Special on the menu. (Beans & plantains, with collared greens and beef)... and these yummy sweet fried dough balls! Shut Up! 🤤 OMG! So good! One order is big enough for two meals for me. $21... a good value!

This was my first time in African deli I was greeted, and the man took the time to explain to me the difference between two dishes that I was looking at. I was very pleased with the customer service. I ordered the fried red kidney beans with fish and oxtail, which I had to pay extra for the oxtail, no problem, then I got some Jollof rice and I got some puff puff and a hibiscus pineapple tea. Each meal that I ordered was $13. I don’t know how much extra I pay for the oxtail or how much the puff puff was because I didn’t get the itemized receipt that I asked for they just gave me a receipt with the total of $40.16 on there (just to give some context on pricing). I ordered the tea later, it was $4. Grand total spent, $44.16. I was super excited about this food. When I got home I tried the jollof rice, it tastes like nothing but aluminum can tomato sauce, and the fish was okay. My fried red beans didn’t have the mild spice as requested but they were okay. The puff puff was slightly chewier than I am used to but they were okay too. All in all, I may give it a second chance because it wasn’t terrible but it wasn’t as flavorful as I am used to when it comes to African Food. 6/10
First time here and it exceeded my expectations,  fried fish, potato green and egusi

The 4.6 star rating is deeply misleading. This is some of the worst African foods I have tried in Minnesota. My jollof rice was spicy with absolutely no discernible flavor aside from pepper. I ordered fufu to go with my egusi and got poundo instead, which I absolutely hate. The Egusi itself was flavorless with no discernible taste except for pepper as well. I thought because this had high ratings the food would be great but it is not. This is coming from a Yoruba person that has eaten both foods all of my life and cooks them myself too, not an outsider who doesn't know what the food should taste like. Anyway, I will not be eating here ever again.

I had a bad experience w/ African food before this place and I was wary but oh my gosh, this place is SO good. I literally ate it for nearly 2 weeks straight 😅 I always get the spinach with turkey necks and pepper sauce on side. So delicious and flavorful. Now I’m showing all my friends & family this place. 🥰 Just wish they weren’t closed 3 days out of the week 😭

formatted_address: 517 Northtown Dr NE, Blaine, MN 55434, United States
name: JTC African Cuisine

reviews.text: Ordering on the kiosk was easy and the wait is well worth it for the delicious and fresh food. I ordered the meat pies (3 for $10 is a great deal), fried rice with fish, suya beef, grilled tilapia with plantains, and a side order of moi moi. Food here is cooked with love! Everyone in the family enjoyed the food. My Mom even said the meat pies "tasted like home". I especially enjoyed the flavorful fried rice, tender fish, sweet plantains, and some sauce for added heat! Good heat and tenderness on the suya meat as well. JTC African Cuisine is amazing for authentic West African cuisine. We will be back!
Food was good until I found a bunch of hair in my food. I hope that it was at least a beard hair and not from a different place :( eeeyyuucckk

Where do i start? Professionalism, hospitality, class and food authenticity!!! Big shout out to JTC, Cameroon and all of West Africa also the owner a Beautiful and Respectable woman. She personally prepared my food as I do not eat meat only fish. Many items are to order as is and she made an exception for me. I had a fried whiting fish on spinach covered in a flavorful medium hot red sauce with added bell pepper, onion and a side FuFu. The food I cannot share because it is out of this world lbs “its gone”. I’ve been eating African dishes for many years this is the one. Stop by and experience JTC inside of Northtown mall you will love it!!!

I am so glad we stopped here for dinner tonight. Alice prepared us wonderful food. She was so accommodating and kind! My husband and I enjoyed it very much! It was our first time trying Nigerian food and are happy this was our first experience. If you haven’t tried it and are open to new experiences, I highly recommend eating here.

I ordered takeaway, I was really craving jollof for a while, I am new to MN and was wanting jollof as good as what I was used to ordering in London,UK where we have amazing African food. This place hit the spot so much so I had to leave a review! I will be ordering from you again & exactly the Nigerian Jollof I was craving & plantains were sweet and perfect! This was my pregnant craving I was not able to eat properly all day so glad I ordered from you & will be a life long loyal customer! Credit to the chef🙌🏾

formatted_address: 7648 N Humboldt Ave, Brooklyn Park, MN 55444, United States
name: Milah's Royal Bistro

reviews.text: Delicious! Everything was fresh and flavorful. Portions were a little small except the fried fish was large and meaty.

These guys are doing a fantastjob here! Cooking great food and being nice and friendly.  Appearances are deceiving,  the building is old, but they are making it work! They are working with what they got and doing a FANTASTIC job working it and working to climb to the top!! Super friendly,  beautiful smiles and delicious EVERYTHING! COME ON BY!! You will love this place!

Really enjoyed my first visit to Milah’s Royal Bistro. I ordered the cassava leaf torborgee with white rice and the Royal bistro dried rice special with fish. The fish was flavorful and spicy, and the dried rice was well seasoned. I also really enjoyed the cassava leaf (which included beef and turkey) with the rice. The wait was not long either. I know other reviews mention poor customer service but that was not an issue on my visit. Great West African cuisine here!

I brought my entire family here for our first African food experience and we ALL agree that this is an absolute hidden gem! The collard greens, chicken, and rice dishes were flavorful, to say the least. We will be back soon!
Decided to try on a whim.... Holy smokes is this place amazing! The Collared Greens were phenomenal, the fried rice was extremely well done, and everything was just amazing! We'll definitely be back!

formatted_address: 7609 Welcome Ave N, Brooklyn Park, MN 55443, United States
name: Value Foods African Market

reviews.text: Ordered the fufu and egusi. fufu was fine however the egusi had mostly bones and literally TEETH inside of it!? not human teeth but seems like cow or goat teeth. egusi is supposed to be boneless. photo taken from my trash cause there was now way i was touching that again.

If I could give less than one star I would. Truly disappointed. I called ahead for an order was told 20 minutes. I arrive and im told 10 MORE minutes. After that, I ask about my order only to find out they sold a portion of my order. Im not sure if communication isnt apart of the training or work ethic but it absolutely needs to improve amongst the staff. The cooks dont know how long the food will take even though they cook it everyday, the cashiers dont know who's order is who's which is basic restaurant common sense. Im livid because I DO NOT have an 45min-1hr to sit and wait for an order that I was told would be ready in 20 MINUTES.
I ordered egushi and fufu and this is what they gave me. Just spicy red oil and a bunch of meat. This is my first and last time ordering from here. Non-recommendable.

Last week no pepper soup but made up for it w drinks, cassava was delicious
Today, pepper soup is not best, didn't add fufu, cassava leaf watered down, not best

Never again. Gave me items I did not order and charged me for it! The potato greens were waaaay too spicy! My lips started burning and could not take more than two bites!! 18$ down the drain..server was rude and avoided eye contact. Please isn’t the cleanest as well.. I was told they had good food so gave that a try ..won’t do tht again.

formatted_address: 818 E Lake St, Minneapolis, MN 55407, United States
name: Hamdi Restaurant

reviews.text: delicious food, friendly staff, and a great price for the meal! I had the salmon with rice and it was so good. I love that the banana and drink were included in the price, super great value. Staff was very nice and helpful and we had a great time here!

One of the best—if not the best—Somali restaurants in the Twin Cities when it comes to both food quality and customer service. I especially love their lamb wasla with rice—a perfectly cooked lamb dish prepared in a truly unique way. Whenever I’m near the cities and need a good meal, I make it a point to visit this restaurant, no matter the distance. I’ve been dining here for the past ten years, and their dishes have consistently been delicious. The flavors even remind me of Mandi meat from Saudi Arabia. The service is outstanding as well, especially thanks to the server Abdihakim, who is incredibly welcoming and friendly.

Hamdi Restaurant is an amazing Somali restaurant with some of the best food I’ve had. The flavors are rich, fresh, and full of tradition. Everything is cooked really well and tastes homemade. The portions are generous and very filling.

the host/server is so cute!! /swoon

we got the goat with rice and dude…yum! the free hot chai was great to warm up after outside protests.

Food was very good!! Service from restaurant staff was awesome. I highly recommend this restaurant. They are also halal restaurant if you are looking for halal food. They also have free Somali tea. Loved that tea!! Please try some of their tea. We had fried chicken and goat meat. I loved both of the platters. Highly recommend!!

formatted_address: 312 W Lake St Suite 2947, Minneapolis, MN 55408, United States
name: Canabey Restaurant and Banquet

reviews.text: Always a Hit! I’ve been ordering from this spot through DoorDash for a while now, and they never miss. The food is consistently delicious, always fresh, and smells amazing the moment it arrives. Big shoutout to the team—y’all keep it flavorful and reliable every time. Thank you!
Incredible food made with care, so delicious. I love my Somali neighbors in Minneapolis, wonderful humans 🫶
My new favorite Somali restaurant to order from. The food is always good!
The food was amazing. It’s a beautiful place to go with family. They are really friendly and nice customer service!
Service was amazing, staff were super helpful and kind. I’m glad I accidentally found this restaurant! Definitely coming back and telling my friends all about it. The food was spectacular also.

formatted_address: 912 E 24th St unit A121, Minneapolis, MN 55404, United States
name: derisuroon restaurant

formatted_address: 6408 Bass Lake Rd, Minneapolis, MN 55428, United States
name: Toni’s African Deli

reviews.text: Stopped in for the first time to order some authentic African food and I got it! I've been looking forward to trying Egusi and fufu. I ordered soup with 2 fufu, unfortunately they didn't have Samosa or Greens today but that's okay, another reason to come back. I ate as much as I could and still have another serving for later. The Egusi soup was perfectly spicy, and made my eyes water.

**Toni’s African Deli: A Flavorful Journey Through Authentic African Cuisine**

If you’re looking for a place that offers a true taste of African cuisine, look no further than Toni’s African Deli. My recent visit to this gem left me craving more of its authentic dishes.

I decided to try the **Amala and Ewedu soup with fish and goat meat**, and it was nothing short of amazing. The Amala was soft and smooth, just as it should be, and paired perfectly with the rich, savory Ewedu soup. The flavors were incredibly well-balanced, with the Ewedu bringing that classic, slightly earthy taste that complements the mild, fermented undertone of the Amala.

The goat meat was tender and perfectly seasoned, with just the right amount of spice to give it a flavorful kick. The fish added another layer of deliciousness to the dish, flaky and well-cooked, soaking up the savory goodness of the soup.

Beyond the delicious food, the atmosphere at Toni’s African Deli is warm and inviting, with a friendly staff that makes you feel right at home. Whether you’re an aficionado of African cuisine or trying it for the first time, Toni’s African Deli is a must-visit.

If you’re in the mood for something truly comforting and hearty, I highly recommend giving Toni’s African Deli a try. You won’t be disappointed!

OVERPRICED ! I’m a mom who cooks at home often , and I rarely get takeout because it’s overpriced and not the most healthiest choice. I HATE wasting my money especially in these times ! Let me say this,  I LOVE African Food and have tried many different restaurants in the cities.  I decided to get dinner here, my first time visiting this place. I paid $20. and some change , for Spinach/rice, they did throw in the ‘hot pepper’ since I guess you have to ask for it and it’s an additional charge and they only take cash for items under $5.,  I didn’t know you had to ask , I just thought about it from experiences at other establishments and then wondered if it came with it, ok fine. Moving on to the food, the spinach bowl was small for $20. in my opinion, I mean who’s counting the rice , its rice and I got plenty of that, you’d think it would be the other way around. There were 3 medium size pieces of meat that pretty much overpowered the whole bowl of spinach with regards to size , I think the amount of spinach had to be no more than a ice cream scoop and unfortunately it was super oily and bland, NO flavor , just heavy on the grease and chewy meat with a splash of red sauce on top which was spicy. My stomach is bubbling right now !! Unfortunately after about 3 try’s , I couldn’t take another bite and my kids didn’t want any, so I had to cook anyway !!! I’m so frustrated with restaurants playing in my face! I think the restaurant should take some time and reevaluate their recipes and  the overall flavor if they feel that they deserve what they’re charging, and try ASKING customers if they’d like to add a side of pepper or let them know the food is already spicy  !!! reviews.text: After losing Fasika in St. Paul, I was craving the same delicious food. Lo and behold, this is a very good restaurant. It’s low key, but it’s popular for the right reasons. Enter the right hand door through the grocery store to get into the restaurant. A server will take you through to be seated. You can pay at your table. Portions are generous, flavors are delicious and service is top notch. Ginger tea is complimentary. I’m so glad I brought my friend from out of town to dine here. I will be returning with friends for more dining experiences in the future. Thank you Betty for a wonderful experience.

"I recently ate at KATAR ETTHIOPIAN RESTAURANT. The reservation was simple to arrange, and the staff was exceedingly helpful in addressing our unique needs. The overall ambiance was excellent, and the cuisine more than met my expectations. We tried the house recommendations, and if you go to the restaurant, you should too. This is a must-try if you're searching for a great, intimate dinner place.”

"I can't say enough positive things about the service at this establishment. The staff is very tolerant of small alterations and goes above and beyond to assure visitors' satisfaction.’’
Bravo!"🤜🤛
Keep it up Family!

One of the best Ethiopian meals I’ve ever had in Minnesota!
The kitfo kochikocha (chili)was absolutely delicious every bite was full of rich, authentic flavor. The tibs were especially outstanding so flavorful and perfectly grilled. On top of that, the service was wonderful! The staff was incredibly kind, friendly, and helpful, which made the whole experience nice. Highly recommend

Katar River Ethiopian Restaurant is a true hidden gem tucked away in a quiet corner of town—and it deserves every bit of praise. From the moment we stepped through the grocery store door, we knew we were in for something special. After walking through the grocery Store, the warm, inviting décor set the stage, but it was the food that stole the show.

We began with the combination sampler platter, a colorful array of perfectly seasoned lentil stews, sautéed greens, and creamy split-pea dishes, each piled atop soft, fresh injera. Every bite was bursting with spice flavor. Next came the Doro Wat, rich and tomato-forward, with tender chicken simmers in a luscious red sauce that left us scraping the plate for every last morsel. We also tried the beef tibs, seared to order and tossed with fragrant garlic, fresh jalapeño, and just the right pinch of rosemary.

What really elevated the meal, though, was the service. Our server Isaac was patient, kind, and deeply knowledgeable about the menu. When we hesitated over which combo to choose, he guided us toward the perfect balance of mild and spicy dishes—and he was spot on. It felt less like ordering off a menu and more like discovering family recipes.

If you’re craving authentic Ethiopian cuisine—fresh, artfully seasoned, and cooked exactly to your taste—make a beeline for Katar River. Whether you’re a longtime fan or brand-new to these vibrant flavors, this restaurant is not to be missed. Highly recommended!

Do NOT let the humble exterior and unpolished interior dissuade you from grabbing a seat, ask for a coffee, and ordering something you’ve never tried before off the menu. You really can’t go wrong! Come with clean hands (those are your utensils!), an open heart, and an empty belly — KATAR RIVER RESTAURANT IS SECOND TO NONE! Though Blue Nile had its distinct ambiance and family-style seating and serving, Katar River is far and away the BEST Ethiopian food I’ve ever had!

I ordered the Vegetarian Combo and had a coffee — and the food was a divine experience! So very delicious…and that’s not an exaggeration! If my wallet could afford it, I’d eat here frequently.

I have a new favorite world restaurant — it’s Katar River!

formatted_address: 1813 Riverside Ave, Minneapolis, MN 55454, United States
name: Dilla Ethiopian restaurant

reviews.text: Great flavors. Been wanting to try this for awhile. Did not disappoint. I ordered the Beef Alicha Fitfit (which actually uses lamb instead of beef) and paired it with Ethiopian honey wine. The server was great: very friendly. There's many menu items I want to try someday!
When I come here, I feel like I am treated like I’m a part of the family. Lovely restaurant. Great food!

Dinner with friends here was amazing! We shared the #53 Yetebaberu and every bite was packed with flavor and the perfect amount of spice. Our server was super friendly and the owner gave us the scoop on their new St. Paul location. Can’t wait to come back!

Delicious food! We ordered some Kitfo with Kocho. The tartar was so rich and creamy. We got Doro Watt, which was tender and flavorful.
The Injera, sour fermented flatbread, that's served with stuff is a bit odd if you've never had it before. They were also out of several items when we tried to order. Not the cleanest either, but still amazing food and will be coming back.

I was in Minneapolis for a quick work trip. I love Ethiopian food and ended up at Dilla after another place I went to was closed upon arrival. What an amazing unexpected experience. The idea of an Ethiopian food spot open late and with a sports bar atmosphere is one of a kind. I sat at the bar and ordered a meat Combo and a half veggie combo. I wanted to have left overs for lunch. Saying it was delicious doesn’t even do it justice. I had some of my favorites like an incredible doro wot and greens, lentils etc. and some new things like beets and green beans. I enjoyed it all. The female server was delightful and kind. The owner was too. He came out to say hello and thank me for my visit.

If you are in Minneapolis and love Ethiopian food like I do, go to Dilla. You won’t be disappointed.

formatted_address: TAMU Grill and Catering, 1829 Riverside Ave, Minneapolis, MN 55454, United States
name: TAMU Grill and Catering

reviews.text:
The restaurant offers an incredible and authentic taste of Kenya right here in Minneapolis. I was thoroughly impressed by the traditional street food and drink offerings.

The authenticity and quality of the dishes were outstanding, but the real star of the show was the sauce. It was perfectly balanced, flavorful, and elevated every bite. If you are looking for genuine, mouth-watering Kenyan cuisine, you absolutely must visit this place!

Low key eatery, and nice atmosphere to chill with small group of friends.
Slower than usual food service, plan an hour to wait and at least, even while seated.
Clean bathrooms.
Has a small TV on upper wall playing some nice low volume African music.
Sweet cinnamon tea is too sweet and hurts my stomach even after a small sip, don’t recommend it, it’s premade and not made fresh- too much sugar in it.
Food is average, nothing competitive or super appealing.
Kenyan food is fusion, so it’s not really as authentic as we’d hope.
Dish menu claims to have rice, but rice was not served.
Don’t plan on coming back unless I need a low key place to chill and not be bothered. But the seating is limited, and the architecture of the layout wasn’t very well thought out.
Chairs are comfortable and a lot of open space. Not cramped at all.
But, the task urgency of this place is very lacking.
I would recommend this restaurant get an expert business consultant to remain profitable- I see tough times for this business ahead.
Food and task management is not competitive at all.
There are much better places for African food with much lower prices just a few blocks away.
I like the effort, but just not a place that has the ability to truly standout.
Seasoned fries also, are not tasty at all- the taste combination is not appetizing or appealing.
Food came out lukewarm, like it was sitting out for a while.
We didn’t bother taking any left overs, just not enough uniqueness or style.
Don’t recommend eating here unless your taste pallet cannot distinguish authentic cuisine.

The food is of Kenyan origin and the restaurant offers a Kenyan fusion kind of experience.
In terms of service, for smaller orders, they come out quickly with beef samosas as part of my favorite side. Bigger meals can range from 10 to 15 minutes, sometimes twenty and this depends on the type of food ordered and the flow of other clients in the restaurant. They also make food from scratch and this allows customers to get the freshest meals while exploring the Kenyan fusion.
In terms of atmosphere, the place is loaded with African music and Afrobeats is always playing on the background. Might not be child friendly but you can always ask the waiter to change the music if you are eating with children. Great place!

Look out for Tilapia, coconut curry beans and chapati, Chicken curry rice and Goat soup (hangover soup only on Sundays

The vegetarian samosas were bland, even for Minnesotas. The "spicy" sauce did not compliment the item.  French fries had no seasoning, were limp, and barely warm so lots of ketchup was necessary! One of my companions had the beef sausage which they described as dry and "nothing special."

Everything was so good and flavorful! First time eating here and ordered the beef curry, chapati and cabbage, jollof rice, and chips marsala + veggie samosas. I would recommend everything and want to try the beef samosas when I go back!

reviews.text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

A Culinary Gem - Sanag Restaurant

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Sanag Restaurant, and I must say, it was an unforgettable experience! From the moment I walked in, the ambiance was warm and inviting, with a beautifully designed interior that sets the perfect backdrop for any meal.

Food:
The menu at Sanag is a delightful fusion of traditional and contemporary dishes. I started with the spaghetti and camel meat which was bursting with flavor and beautifully presented. For the main course, I opted for the spaghetti and it exceeded all expectations! The ingredients were fresh, and you could really taste the care that went into each dish.

Service:
The service was exceptional. Our server was attentive, knowledgeable, and genuinely enthusiastic about the menu, offering great recommendations. It felt like they truly cared about our dining experience.

Atmosphere:
The atmosphere was lively yet relaxed, making it a great spot for both casual outings and special occasions. The Quran was just the right volume, allowing for easy conversation while still creating a vibrant vibe.

Value:
For the quality of food and service, the prices at Sanag are very reasonable. It’s clear that they prioritize quality over quantity, and you definitely get what you pay for.

Overall, I highly recommend Sanag Restaurant to anyone looking for a fantastic dining experience. Whether you’re a local or just passing through, make sure to stop by—you won’t be disappointed!

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Sanag Restaurant, and it was truly an unforgettable experience! I ordered the amazing race dish, which was a delightful explosion of flavors that left my taste buds dancing. However, the highlight of my meal was undoubtedly the lamb meat—hands down the best I’ve ever had! It was tender, juicy, and cooked to perfection, showcasing the chef's skill and dedication to quality.

In addition to the incredible food, the service at Sanag was exceptional. The staff were not only attentive but also genuinely kind, making me feel welcomed throughout my visit. The restaurant itself is clean and beautifully designed, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere that enhances the overall dining experience. I highly recommend Sanag to anyone looking for a top-notch meal in a fantastic setting!
