reviews.text: If I had to recommend 1 unique restaurant to visit in Minneapolis, this would definitely be it. Everything is so fresh and packed full of flavor. Ive been here a few times, tried multiple plates, and every one of them has been incredible. Highly recommend!

A friend recommended this place, and I'm so glad she did! We came here with a larger party of 9 people. They were able to seat us no problem and virtually no wait. Our waiter was great, informative, and checked in with us often. Despite being a larger party, we didn't have to wait too long to receive our food. The food was SO good. By the end of the meal, all of us were stuffed! And there was still food leftover. The food is also reasonably priced and not bad at all if you want to share dishes with your friends. The only and biggest downside was the heat in the restaurant. We went on a hot day in the evening, and the temperature was hotter inside the restaurant than it was outside. Most of us were sweating the whole time, and the heat was really hard to ignore after a while. Overall, I'd still say it was worth it, though.

Great flavors and options for a lovely Ethiopian meal. Our large group shared several plates and everything was delicious. Service was a bit slow and we were waiting on water refills or the chance to order now drinks a few times. Our group of seven were seated in a small booth with deep seats that felt a little cramped and warm. Overall, a nice dinner with a few small issues.

Popped in for lunch on New Years' Day...DELICIOUS!! We've eatten at most of the Ethiopian restaurants in the Twin Cities, and Bole is far superior to them all. The food was fresh and uniquely yummy. The Sambusas 10/10, the Vegie combo 10/10, the Zil zil Tibs:11/10, the gingery tea: perfect!
We loved the warm decor and the music...the waitress could have been more friendly (we were the only customers in the place, but she was completely engaged by her phone). But all in all, a hearty 5 stars! We'll be back.

Delicious food, fast and friendly service. Love the tibs! Great vegetarian options too. Nice indoor and patio seating. The injera is good and they serve a generous amount with each entree. The best Ethiopian food I've tried in the Twin Cities!

formatted_address: 823 University Ave W, St Paul, MN 55104, United States
name: Demera | Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text:
Demera is runned by a lovely couple Senait and Dawit. They have good food, coffee and are attentive to good service.
My husband and I often come to the restaurant for their Machiatto coffee and its delicious and a great pick me up. They also have very good Sambusas. Food is also very good and served with Injera. We highly recommend this restaurant!

On the hunt for some tasty East African fare in the cities? If so, this is definitely a place to try! This is an unassuming little place that offers spectacular food.

I was in for dinner with a group of business associates, including one who is a little older than me and had spent something north of a quarter of his life living in Ethiopia. He spoke a couple of dialects and did a great job explaining the whole experience to everyone at the table. I've been eating Ethiopian food for a couple of decades but have nowhere near the knowledge of their food, country, culture, etc. Certainly a learning experience that went well beyond the food.

We had a couple of platters for the 5 of us: one vegetarian and the other a meat-lover's paradise. I consider Ethiopian to be a cuisine so packed with flavor that I generally eat vegetarian. That said, the lamb, chicken and beef dishes all were incredibly delicious.

There are 5 vegetarian dishes that come with that platter. All were delicious but my favorite had to be the misir kay wot: red lentils with berebere and a bunch of other good stuff.

There were at least as many meat dishes and all were wonderful. The standout was probably the doro wat. I'm not sure I've had this one before but the flavors absolutely filled my mouth while I was eating the dish. Super tasty!

This restaurant is DELICIOUS!! The staff are so kind and welcoming, and I keep coming back to this spot. I came in the summer to get a meat combo platter (delicious btw) when their electricity was out, but when we asked if we should come back at another time they were kind enough to still serve us! They have incredible hospitality and a fun atmosphere.

I love the Lamb Tibs

Overall, the food was worth the visit. The Key Wot was delicious, bit the other dishes were a little lackluster.
The place felt just a little bit better than almost clean, whereas the bathroom felt like it needed some work.

It was completely empty when I went to lunch on a Tuesday, which I felt was odd, but maybe Tuesday is just their slow day.

I would probably go back again and try other dishes, given I have enough time.

My husband and I recently had the pleasure of dining here, and we were impressed by the food and overall experience. The highlight of my meal was the lamb tibs and the vegetarian platter.

The lamb tibs were cooked to perfection—tender and juicy, with just the right amount of spice to give it a flavorful kick. The seasoning was rich and aromatic, making each bite a delightful experience.

The vegetarian platter was a feast for veggie lovers like us. It included a variety of vegetable stews, lentils, and other delightful plant-based dishes. Each item was distinct in taste and texture. The portion size was generous, and the dish was served with injera, a soft and spongy flatbread.

The restaurant itself had a warm and inviting atmosphere, with friendly staff and a cozy ambiance. The service was prompt and attentive, making the dining experience even more enjoyable. Overall, I highly recommend this Ethiopian restaurant for anyone looking to enjoy delicious, authentic cuisine.

formatted_address: 15609 Grove Cir N, Maple Grove, MN 55369, United States
name: Bole Ethiopian Cuisine Maple Grove

reviews.text:
First time at this restaurant on the recommendation of the Maple Grove Facebook group! All of the good things they said about it is spot!

Nice atmosphere. Lovely servers. Met the wife/mom who was delightful and told me about their spices they sell.

We had the Crispy Kitfo Roll, which our server suggested. It was delicious! Very flavorful and crispy.

Our dinner was the Tokkuma! The flavor was phenomenal! Plenty of injera to scoop our food. There was SO much food. We definitely went home with a lot of leftovers since it was just 2 of us.

While the food had a good kick to it with spice level, it didn't overwhelm the flavor! Cleared my sinuses, but didn't linger.

Already planning to go back as soon as possible!

This was our first visit to an Ethiopian restaurant. Plenty of vegetarian options.

Enjoyed our family dinner. Excellent food and great service by our friendly host Betty!

If you haven’t been there yet, try them… you won’t be disappointed. Ask for their spicy sauce if you like a little heat like I do. Also try sprinkling a bit of Mitmita spice on ingira (bread) for a change - I liked it that way.

Disclaimer: I might have gotten some of the names wrong. Verify.

Went here last night with a couple of friends to celebrate my birthday and woooowww, did we pick the right place! Everything from the beautiful dining room to the drinks (best mocktail I've ever had) to the food....the FOOD! We had three apps and the vegetarian platter for TWO and it was so. much. food. Every bite was just incredible. Plan for a leisurely paced meal and you'll have one of the best meals you've had in a very long time. Honestly, it's the best restaurant in Maple Grove!

The owner served us and gave us recommendations + information on Ethiopian food (such as how to eat it properly) as my partner and I had never had Ethiopian food before. The owner was very nice and was very happy to educate us! Food was excellent and the owner made our experience exceptional! We're so happy to have this place a convenient drive from where we live in the outer suburbs ❤️
This place was absolutely delicious! We loved the sambusas and tibs and are already craving more! If you haven’t tried Ethiopian food, don’t waste any more time and go give it a try!

formatted_address: 308 E Prince St STE 140, St Paul, MN 55101, United States
name: Erta Ale Ethiopian

reviews.text: Fantastic spot! I ordered the vegan platter and enjoyed all of the variety it offered. A standout was the jalapeño dish. The food came out super quick and the staff was great
Delicious and great prices! 4 adults split the Erta Ale Special. It was tasty and offered a variety of proteins and vegetables. We recommend ordering a tea. They bring a cute little tray.
It’s one of the best Ethiopian restaurants in Minnesota, food is Amazing, the best spiced tea I have had in The US, the service was Excellent!👍

We thoroughly enjoyed our meal at Erta Ale Ethiopian!
On walking in, the space feels very welcoming and warm with interesting wall art and a beautiful tea set display. The server was busy tending to a group so the bartender came and sat us and helped us. Everyone was very friendly and kind, and the food came out quite fast.
We enjoyed most of the food very much-
The sambusa had a great lentil filling but I especially enjoyed the shell which was super crispy but thick enough to also have some chew.
All the food had wonderful flavor and different from other Ethiopian food we’ve tried, had more texture (wasn’t just mushy), which was pleasant.

Would recommend and will come back next time we want Ethiopian!

While we were in Minnesota for our event, we had the absolute pleasure of dining at Erta Ale Ethiopian Restaurant. The owners, Amy and Derje, were the best hosts we could have asked for welcoming us with such warmth and genuine hospitality.

They treated us to a wonderful buffet that was overflowing with authentic Ethiopian flavors. The kitfo, aybe, and gomen were out of this world fresh, perfectly seasoned, and truly unforgettable. Every dish, from the injera to the wot and tibs, was prepared with care and love, giving us a real taste of home.

On top of the incredible food, the customer service was exceptional. Amy and Derje made us feel like family, ensuring we were comfortable and that every detail was perfect.

If you’re ever in Minnesota, Erta Ale Ethiopian Restaurant is a must-visit for the delicious buffet, the out-of-this-world kitfo, aybe, and gomen, and the amazing hospitality that makes you feel right at home.

formatted_address: 1220 Rice St, St Paul, MN 55117, United States
name: Tin cup plus Ethiopian restaurant

reviews.text: We tried one of the meat and veggie combos for 2 tonight. All of it was amazing! We really appreciated the differences in the spices between dishes, making each one a unique experience. I just wish this place was busier. The space was empty for so long, and the neighborhood needs gems like this!

I finished grocery shopping next door and decided to pop into tin cup, for the 1st time, to grab coffee to go. I stayed because the environment was so pleasant and Ahman was welcoming! He asked if i want a to go cup or the coffee ceremony - I had time to wait so I chose the ceremony and im so happy I did. The Ethiopian coffee ceremony elevated my coffee drinking experience to the next level (look it up if youre unfamiliar) and I plan on coming back again soon!

I have been to a lot of Ethiopian restaurants, and this was by far the best meal I’ve ever had. I had the veggie platter and my partner had the first item on the beef entrée list. The flavor was phenomenal. The owner was super kind and wonderful. The only bad part is the place hasn’t had much traction yet. So we were the only people there. But that could be because Rice Street is closed… But it’s still very easy to get to. Highly recommended. Support this wonderful business!  🙏
I live in the neighborhood and brought my mom and sister. The food was excellent (we got a combo platter for two) and the coffee was absolutely fantastic! Definitely will be back.

The restaurant itself is beautifully decorated, creating a vibrant and lively atmosphere. The flavors in each dish were perfectly balanced , and the ingredients tasted incredibly fresh .

Thank you for making it!

formatted_address: 1960 Cliff Lake Rd suit 138, Eagan, MN 55122, United States
name: Sodere Ethiopian Restaurant & Bar

reviews.text:
We were the first customers on a Monday so took a few minutes to get their attention.
Once we ordered, food came out pretty quickly.
Portions are decent sized -I was not able to finish mine and took the rest home. My husband finished most of his meal.
We each got a veggie sambusa and a veggie combo platter. Food was good although they were out of potatoes which was disappointing.
The veggie combo includes portions of 3 lentil dishes, cabbage with carrots, beets, and collard greens served on and with injera bread.
We shared Ethiopian coffee for dessert.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Authentic, Flavorful, and a Must-Try!

I had an amazing experience at Sodere Ethiopian Restaurant in Eagan! The food was beyond delicious, and the flavors were unlike anything I’ve had before. We ordered the Meat Combo Wat, which had Kitfo, Shekla Tibs, and Quanta Firfir, and every single dish was packed with incredible spices and fresh ingredients.

The service was fantastic, and the atmosphere was warm and inviting. Whether you’re new to Ethiopian food or a longtime fan, this place is a must-visit. Highly recommend checking them out if you're in the area!

📍 Sodere Ethiopian Restaurant
1960 Cliff Lake Rd, Eagan, MN 55122

#SupportLocal #FoodieFinds #EthiopianCuisine #GreatConnections
First time having Ethiopian food and it was a great experience. We had the Kifo, Shekla Tibs and Quanta Firfir. It was great service and very friendly people.

This is now my favorite Ethiopian spot in the twin cities. I’ve dined in and ordered takeout here. Every time I am so satisfied and leave feeling happy .The shiro is my favorite dish. I love the combo platters too. Get the coffee ceremony- you won’t be disappointed- Ethiopian coffee is the best you will ever have! Service is lovely- had a nice chat with the staff that prepared and served our meal. 10/10 recommend!
Best injera I've ever had. Not bitter. Veggie combo perfect if you can't take heat. Bright and clean, friendly owners. Definitely going again!

formatted_address: 1025 Currie Ave, Minneapolis, MN 55403, United States
name: Yemama's kitchen

reviews.text: NO LONGER OPEN, although the website still allows you to place an order and pay. The phone number goes straight to a message saying there's no voicemail. We used half of a $100 gift card, then never got our food, and I couldn't get ahold of the restaurant. I had to  drive down there to try and get the food or a refund, and spoke to someone in the building that said she moved out suddenly and nobody knows where she went.

formatted_address: 691 Dale St N, St Paul, MN 55103, United States
name: Jegol Ethiopian Kitchen

reviews.text: Absolutely fantastic food, and friendly service! Everything was delicious, and left feeling nourished. Would highly recommend the goat - tender, flavorful, and cooked just right. It was clear the staff was passionate about serving Ethiopian food. We had a good chat with the chef, and she even offered us a jebena coffee on the house for the table (also would highly recommend - strong, warming, and floral coffee). Perfect way to spend an evening with friends.

I was at a doctor’s appointment in the area and after being cold and hungry I stopped in here for an early dinner.

The server was very kind and helped me pick out the goat awaze tibs. While I waited I was brought a delightful veggie soup with a side of spicy sauce to put in it.

The tibs were super tasty and I had plenty of leftovers for later!! I also had a cup of tea which had a great flavor

Overall a superb experience and it warmed me right up on a cold winter day. Can’t wait to bring my partner here and try some other dishes!!
Amazing experience!! We ordered to go and it wasn’t ready so I ordered a coffee, omg, it was absolutely amazing!! The spaghetti was fabulous and vegetarian dish was superb!!!
amazing food, and very nice costumer service would recommend for everyone

The food was very good, excellent taste and the meat was soft enough to fall of the bone, the food proportions are enough to feed a whole party. They have a special on Friday called Hanid,  delicious goat meat on the bone cooked to absolute perfection, it comes with yellow rice and salad on the side. The restaurant is very clean with lovely, relaxing music playing in the background and the service was wonderful.

formatted_address: 1625 University Ave W, St Paul, MN 55104, United States
name: Dilla Sports Bar and Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text:
Real Kitfo! Just wish it was spicier, but the mild flavor allowed it to be enjoyed by more people.

Great stews all around as well.

Fast and friendly service. Highly recommended for authentic Ethiopian.

This is my favorite Ethiopian restaurant! The doro wot is absolutely delicious, the service is always so friendly, and the atmosphere is warm and welcoming. I highly recommend this place to anyone who wants to enjoy authentic Ethiopian food in a cozy setting.

I have past this place many times. Today I stopped for dinner. I was seated immediately. Service was fast. Love the traditional Ethiopian atmosphere and music.
A big thanks to my service provider Tsion was fantastic.
I had the Sambusas for appetizers. I received 5 of them with sauce. Other places only give you three. Very delicious with a a good spicey taste. Then had the Dilla Sandwich with a side of fries. The sandwich was with beef, bell peppers, jalapeños, red onions and a bit of mayo on a sub style bread. It was absolutely delicious.

Hands down worthy of a return visit. They have a nice bar as well. A must visit business.

Came here on a Saturday night as a good neighborhood option for dinner. Pricing is a little higher than other Ethiopian restaurants but the setup is nice.

When we were here their air conditioning did not work and there were big fans all over the place. It was warm but comfortable.

The food was good but our server forgot to bring our injera bread out and we were confused as to how to eat our food without injera bread.

It's an ok place and a good alternative to the food in this neighborhood but if you want better food and service you'll probably want to go somewhere else.

It’s hard to find delicious veggies. But I found them at Dilla. I got the veggie combo plate which includes a little of about 7 different vegetarian dishes, and baklava for dessert. It was possibly the best baklava that I’ve ever had.

formatted_address: 2516 7th St W, St Paul, MN 55116, United States
name: Dukem Ethiopian Restaurant, Sports Bar & Lounge

reviews.text:
I wasn’t sure what to expect before visiting — I thought it might be more of a sports bar or club — but it turned out to be a great restaurant with delicious food at very reasonable prices.

The atmosphere was welcoming, and the staff (and guests) were all very kind, which made our experience even better.

My only small critique is that there was incense burning during our visit, which gave off a strong smell. It seemed like it may have been covering up tobacco smoke, though we didn’t actually see anyone smoking inside.

Overall, the food, value, and friendly vibe make this place one I’d definitely recommend!

EDIT: Rating is still a STRONG 5, but now I have been here and eaten here multiple times.  Recently I came here on a Saturday afternoon.
This place is packed on Saturdays, lots of activity, lots of TVs with multiple sports playing, and a very fun and boisterous crowd.  Despite the crowd, service was still prompt and everyone was super nice.
Just give it a try!

Original:  It took me way too long to give this place a try. I walked in and was greeted at the bar with a smile, and a cold glass of water.
I was just in to get some food to go but grabbed a beer while I waited. It was served ice cold in a nice glass.
The menu has a great selection of items and everything sounds delicious. Ended up getting the ZilZil tibs and would highly recommend that dish.
I’m very happy with the taste, quality and portion I received for the price, and cannot wait to come back and work my way through their menu.
Also, if you are into espresso drinks, definitely come by and give this a try, their set up is impressive.

A neat place tucked away. I was here before volunteering for a community event and the staff were incredibly kind/helpful. The food they offered was fantastic and it was a fun atmosphere. I'll definitely be back, so 5 stars from me!

They are very slow one staff you wait very long time to get your food. You wait very long time to order. It’s just not a good customer service. I was very disappointed. I came with my dad is very sad. We couldn’t eat for like two hours. we’re waiting and then we have to leave. I will never come back to this place again

Food looks really good and smelled wonderful. I am a chef. I did not order any but I will be back soon to try it. Atmosphere....the large tables with ornate chairs are unique to a sports bar. The people there were very kind and welcoming. There was nowhere to sit except a few empty chairs at tables with patrons. I was offered a seat at many tables. I was the only white person there to watch a soccer match and I felt welcomed to be there. Beer was cold and crisp and only $4 dollars for a Summit Saga. Service was awesome.

formatted_address: 518 Snelling Ave N, St Paul, MN 55104, United States
name: Sabrina's Cafe & Deli

reviews.text: Found this spot randomly on a Friday night. I was so glad I tried it! I ordered the beef chapati wrap, fries, and beef sambusa. The sambusa was nice and crispy with lots of flavorful filling. The chapati was so delicious. The chapati was stuffed with tons of meat and some lettuce ! I got it spicy and the sauce was so good in it. I will definitely be coming back and telling friends and family about it.

The chapati wraps are fantastic! They are packed with flavor and there are 5 different types to choose from (fish, gyro, beef, chicken, and egg). I also ordered gyro meat with soft pita bread and the chicken over rice platter. Those were also enjoyable. Everything is made to order and it comes out so quickly too! The family enjoyed all of the items. We will return to Sabrina’s Cafe again!

My roommates and I ordered from Sabrina's Cafe tonight, Our very first time ordering from this place. I ordered the Chicken and Rice. Food was delicious & came pretty quickly! I was quite satisfied! and so was everyone else! We will be return customers. Only negative I have is that the price shown on the menu was different than price paid on app through delivery, paid 4 dollars more. Not to upset as the food made my belly happy.

Food was solid and service speed was ok. The chicken chapati was delicious, if messy, and the fries were lightly seasoned, but still solid. Drink selection is pretty small. No restroom and you'll have to ask for the WiFi password. Dining area is small, but neat and clean.

Enjoyed the chicken over rice.  The grilled chicken was tasty and succulent. The rice was tasty still as well.  Just getting introduced to Somali Ethiopian food.  The ambiance in the restaurant could use some TLC.

formatted_address: 2910 Pillsbury Ave R408, Minneapolis, MN 55408, United States
name: LATIVA RESTAURANT INC

reviews.text: Most delicious Ethiopian Enjera with high level spicy food a one can eat. Highly recommended. Location is 4th floor with #R408 in Karmel Mall
Best food in karmel mall Masha Allah. You should check it out.
Amazing food and good customer service

formatted_address: 324 Cedar Ave, Minneapolis, MN 55454, United States
name: West Bank Diner

reviews.text: I'm a student at UMN. After studying at Wilson Library next door in the evenings, I come to this restaurant for dinner. I've eaten here several times, and overall, I find it just average. 1. The service is extremely slow, especially for Asian or white customers and other non-Muslim groups. On multiple occasions, I've waited over half an hour before going to the front desk to inquire. I was told they hadn't even started preparing my order yet, and they didn't seem to care. If I hadn't asked, I doubt they would have served me at all. The front desk staff are rude, and there are no consistent servers. 2. The environment is mediocre. Tables are often left uncleaned with trash on them, and there are various unsavory characters hanging around. 3. The portions are generous and extremely affordable—this is the biggest advantage, making it very budget-friendly for students.

Please always watch you orders they shortened you portions of meat you have paid for, I have order sports few times with 3 different choice of meat like Philly steak, beef sukar and chicken legs. I only received Philly steak. I call store to report not successfully. I do have pictures to proof this statement.

This place was awesome. A customer was even helping me out, because he liked the restaurant so much. The food is amazing. I actually cant wait to go back to try out more dishes. They also have delicious soup. The soup is there for you, while you wait for your food.
Their food is so good but it takes for ever , restaurant is understaffed and you have to be in line for almost an hour.

Portions were very large. We ordered the somosas, goat, chicken steak, and chicken suqaar. The goat was tender and cooked to perfection and the flavors of both chicken dishes were delicious. The mango lassi and tea with milk was perfect with the meal. It was my first time trying somali food and definitely not my last.

formatted_address: 3749 Cedar Ave, Minneapolis, MN 55407, United States
name: Lucy's Market & Carry-Out (Ethiopian Restaurant)

reviews.text: My wife and I have been wanting to come here ever since we moved to this neighborhood. Saw they were open tonight and went on a whim! One of the best whims we've ever had! The most lovely service, INCREDIBLE food, bright & happy ambience perfect for forgetting about winter outside... We got ginger tea, lentil sambusas, beef fried rice, and tilapia goulash. Servings so big we'll have leftovers for a couple days, so we definitely got our money's worth. But the highlight was the wonderful woman serving us! I didn't catch your name, but I promise I'll be back for baklava soon!!!

Absolutely loved this place! The owner was extremely accommodating and pleasant to deal with. We went in for a late lunch on a weekday and it was empty and very toasty inside, but she immediately cranked up the AC to make us comfortable

I got the fish goulash on rice, and my coworker got the beef tibs on rice. While I enjoy injera, I loved the option of rice so I can eat while working on a computer without worrying about getting it saucy. I am not sure how many other Ethiopian places offer rice as a carb, but it went well with both dishes

Both entrees were very tasty, and I highly recommend the fish goulash. The tibs were tasty as well, but I wasn’t as much of a fan. Spice levels were accurate and definitely packed a punch

The interior was neatly decorated, though there was not a ton of seating, so it could be difficult to find a spot if/when it is busy. There are items available for purchase near the ordering counter, but I didn’t get a good look at the variety

Please try it out if you are in the area, she truly deserves the support!

This was my second time in but my first getting some food!

We got the vegan sample plate, kitfo and lentil and beef sambusas.

Y’all those Sambusas were probably the best Sambusas I’ve ever had! The filling for both beef and lentil were well spiced and the outside was nice and crunchy! Served with a green chutney.

The mains were also very filling, delicious and had amazing portions for the price (especially the vegan platter). 100% recommend this place!

The service was 10/10 the owner is so sweet and she made sure we got everything we wanted and that it was correct!

If you’re new to Ethiopian food, this place is great for trying out a new cuisine because they have a platter with it all.
Their green sauce with the samosas was great!

4 star - Would enjoy going back!

This is my new favorite restaurant in Minneapolis.  Just left with a warm heart and a full belly, the owner was a wonderful and friendly host, the food was phenomenal and plentiful, and it's such a great local business. I am beyond happy, they even offer cooking classes, which I will definitely be taking! Awesome vegetarian and non-vegetarian options. There wasn't a single thing I didn't love. Seriously, check them out asap!

formatted_address: 920 E Lake St, Minneapolis, MN 55407, United States
name: Moroccan Flavors

reviews.text: I used to live in the Mpls area so I still visit my family often. I needed vegetables! My husband and I went to Morocco a couple of yrs ago and loved it. I was pleasantly surprised to see a Moroccan restaurant in the Global Market! The food was divine. The variety of vegetables was an awesome surprise. The gentleman who suggested food and waited on us was pleasant. We ordered the lamb shank and vegetables. Along with the chicken and grain bowl. My Mom loves pickled beets so she was ecstatic to eat them. All of our food was tasty and well presented. There were 3 of us and we only ordered two entrees and had leftovers so their portions are hearty. I'd come back here in a heartbeat.

Stopped by Moroccan Flavors inside Midtown Global Market and loved it! The chicken couscous was tender, full of flavor, and perfectly paired with the vegetables and spices. The traditional mint tea was refreshing and a great balance of sweetness. I also enjoyed the side salads—fresh, colorful, and tasty. The whole experience felt authentic, and the staff was welcoming. Definitely recommend if you’re looking for a real taste of Morocco in Minneapolis!

Its our first time eating Moroccan food. We love it! We tried shrimp Tagine and Lamb Tagine. Love the sampling salad with several flavors and refreshing. Mint tea is refreshing too.
Delicious food, good portion, reasonable price. Owner is a chef. He is friendly.
They have 6-7tables.
The location is a bit hidden in the corner. It may not be obvious if you walk pass too quickly

Moroccan Flavors – Minneapolis
An excellent find! The meal was absolutely delicious — flavorful appetizers, perfectly cooked couscous, and a rich, satisfying dessert. Special thanks to Hassan, whose warm and friendly welcome made the experience even better.
If you’re in Minneapolis, don’t miss Moroccan Flavors — you won’t be disappointed! A French family 😉.

The food is nothing short of spectacular. Every dish bursts with layers of flavor — rich, slow-cooked tagines with tender meats that fall off the bone, couscous so light and fluffy it could be a meal on its own, and mezze plates that showcase the perfect balance of savory, tangy, and sweet. The lamb with prunes and almonds was a standout, melting in the mouth with a hint of sweetness, while the Kofta - Marinated Ground Beef was a delightful surprise
Equally impressive is the service. The Owner is warm, attentive, and eager to share the stories behind each dish. You don’t just eat here — you experience Moroccan hospitality at its finest.
To end this meal, the mint tea ceremony is a must. Watching the tea poured gracefully from above into delicate glasses is as much a performance as it is a treat. Paired with honey-drenched pastries, it’s the perfect finale to an unforgettable evening.

If you’re looking for more than just a meal — if you want a culinary escape to the heart of Morocco — this restaurant is absolutely unmissable.

formatted_address: 1049 Dodd Rd, West St Paul, MN 55118, United States
name: Yadot Ethiopian Bar and Restaurant

reviews.text: I can't say enough good things about this Ethiopian gem! From the moment I entered, I was greeted with warmth and hospitality. The ambiance was cozy, with traditional Ethiopian decor adding to the experience. The menu offered a wide array of options, and everything we tried was absolutely delicious. The injera was soft and flavorful, and each dish was bursting with authentic Ethiopian spices. The service was attentive without being intrusive, making for a relaxed and enjoyable meal. If you're looking for an unforgettable dining experience, look no further than this five-star Ethiopian restaurant

Wonderful aromas when we entered the restaurant. Great vegan options. All the vegetarian options were vegan. My wife and I split the vegetarian platter with leftovers to spare. Very filling. All the items were delicious, though my favorite dishes were the red lentils, and the potatoes with carrots. There was a spicy puree that I enjoyed, as well as a bright yellow lentil dish that was great. My son had a delectable chicken dish with tasty rice that he finished, though he nearly burst. My mother enjoyed a fish dish she ordered. The waiter recommended a strong wine with honey for my wife, which was warming and delightful. He recommended a popular Ethiopian beer (a well-balanced lager with a nice malty backbone) that I enjoyed. The dining area was clean and well-maintained. One area of opportunity: the lighting was too bright. The space could have used softer, more intimate lighting. But that wasn’t a deal-breaker. The food was excellent, and the service was great. We’ll be back.

This was my first time trying Ethiopian food and I'm so glad I tried it here. The food was amazing. The owner was so nice and inviting. He answered questions we had and made sure we had everything we needed. Try the coffee!! I would definitely eat here again.

This restaurant is the best! Delicious food and really nice staff. I will definitely recommend this restaurant to others. We split the veggie combo and sambusas and it was so good. Also, don’t skip the tea!
Was here last year, a lady came in and told the owner that they forgot to pay for their subscriptions. Lady threaten to call cops. Great show. 10/10

formatted_address: 804 University Ave W, St Paul, MN 55104, United States
name: K's Cafe

reviews.text: Hidden gem!!! I came across this restaurant instagram page and the food looked amazing and had to try it out myself. The rice combo was amazing!! Will for sure be going back when I’m in the area!
Money well spent over here!!! The injera, quesadillas, and fries specialties!! Well rounded and diverse!
Fire

formatted_address: 1114 Mainstreet, Hopkins, MN 55343, United States
name: Gedi Grill

reviews.text: This is a quality East African cuisine option in Hopkins. You can't beat the combination of prices and portion sizes. Goat meat with rice, salmon with rice, gyro wrap, and chicken sambusa were all delicious and enjoyed by the entire family. So much seasoned gyro meat that I could barely fold the pita bread. The goat meat was tender. The salmon was juicy and the sauce on it was solid. I never had chicken sambusa before and it was incredible! Quality service and the wait times aren't bad at all (worth it for the fresh food). I will return to Gedi Grill.

What a Wonderful Meal! My first West African dish💯🥘I had the Chicken Suqaar When i say The West African flavors Shined, They Did Indeed!! Super Delicious! The Basmati Rice, secret spices, tomatoes, lettuce, with the spiced Green sauce and Suqaar Chicken, plus the Coriander seeds i believe made the dish something to remember.😋😋 Not only that, the cook was very informative and nice to me. Customer service was beyond what I thought of. Thank you Gedi Grill🥘. 5 Stars!!!!!!

Recently visited Gedi Grill in Hopkins for halal food. It's a new restaurant with groceries and money exchange in one place. Like the overall place, food was good and prices were reasonable. Highly recommend their Gabeyre Wrap with chicken.

Wish if they could add partition between grocery items and sitting area.

We ordered wings and it came with fries. Beautifully fried as well. This could be a meal in itself! The steak (was AMAZING) and rice. Steak was sliced so thin and marinated and juicy. Sambusas were some of the best I’ve had. All the sauces were amazing. And the chai! Very spiced and very sweet and delicious. This is reminiscent of masala chai, so don’t expect a teabag in hot water! Took about 20 to get the order as well! FILLING servings!! And they are open for Ramadan!

formatted_address: 2940 Harriet Ave, Minneapolis, MN 55408, United States
name: Channa Kitchen

reviews.text: I have not been to Trinidad, but have enjoyed its food in NYC and elsewhere, and Channa really seems to deliver on the authenticity! There is great care put into the preparation and packaging of all the various dishes, and the quality of ingredients is evident in the vibrant flavors. And it’s such a pleasure to interact with them on each order… they put a lot of love into their operation!

Channa Kitchen is such a treat to find at the farmers markets! The doubles are incredible, soft golden bara filled with spiced channa (curried chickpeas) topped with the perfect balance of pepper and chutney. Ask for heavy peppa if you like it spicy! It’s the kind of food that warms you from the inside out! A real Trini comfort food.

The owners are always so friendly and full of positive energy. You can tell they love sharing Trinidadian culture and building community through their food and conversations. I always look forward to their weekly specials, which bring even more delicious Guyanese and Trini comfort foods to the table.

Every visit feels like catching up with old friends. real nice vibes and real good food!

After 5 years as a Caribbean-American in MN I’m SO glad I found Channa Kitchen. The food is authentic, delicious, and reminds of what I grew up with. Truly haven’t had anything I haven’t liked as yet and doubt I will. Keep an eye on their instagram for specials!! Anisa’s pepperpot for Christmas time nearly brought tears to my eyes with how much it reminded me of home.

Tried Channa Kitchen for the first time at the NE Winter Market in April, and WOW—I’m still thinking about that curry chicken roti. The flavor was perfect: warm, just the right amount of spice, and packed with rich, aromatic curry goodness. The roti was soft and chewy, wrapped around a super generous portion that totally filled me up and made my whole day. You can taste the love and skill in this food. Highly recommend!

I've been searching for authentic Trinidian food. Seriously carving it so bad and by chance I came across Channa's Kitchen. Absolutely amazing food! Reminded me of my childhood and really made me miss my mommy (in a good way of course). It's never been easy to find authentic Trinidian food here, as there was only one Harry Singh's which is now closed. I'm so happy for Channa's Kitchen, not just the food but the people (Anisa is amazing) So you want to taste real authentic Trinidian food? Then get online go to Channa's Kitchen and place that order. You won't be disappointed. 🇹🇹🇹🇹🇹🇹🇹🇹

formatted_address: 2851 Central Ave NE, Minneapolis, MN 55418, United States
name: Chimborazo

reviews.text:
Very flavorful and soft potatoes. The green sauce is slightly spicy but goes great with the potatoes.

Really juicy, flavorful, soft sandwich. Well seasoned pork, the sweetness from the plantain only adds to the sandwich. Fries are slightly crispy on the outside and soft on the inside.

The flank steak was well seasoned though a bit tough and dry. The rice and beans were good sides. Really liked the plantains again.

Went on the perfect day to sit outside! Tons of patio seating. Ate so much. There was a large variety that was absolutely delicious. I want to go back. Perfect for a long lunch or dinner, conversing and munching on perfect Ecuadorian cuisine. Large gluten free menu options- and if you aren't gluten free it doesn't matter!

Delicious. Blew through with my wife one weeknight and very happily enjoyed an early dinner for two with nearly no wait. I was here a few weeks ago in an early evening so I can't remember the name of what I ate, but it had chorizo, papa con queso, arroz con huevo, y ensaladita. Estuvo delicioso 🥹

My wife had the halibut and it was the star of the show.

I had asked the waiter for his recommendation since I had never eaten Ecuadorian food. I wasn't thrilled or wowed, and I think I should have chosen the other option, but everything seemed made with care and to perfection. Rice was soft and sticky, plantains were just ripe, potatoes weren't dry, and all the textures were good. Wish I had more flavor, maybe salt? Better less than too much. Great guisos and accompaniments.

It was a lovely little spot and I will absolutely come by again.

Looked for great brunch places in Northeast Minneapolis and Chimborazo was recommended on multiple places (Reddit, google maps etc.) so decided to stop in.

The flavors were on point. From subtly savory to tangy and refreshing. Can’t wait to come back and try the cheesy potatoes with chorizo.

¡Tan buena comida!
everything was so so good! everything was just absolutely bursting with flavor and richness, but never too heavy. a perfect spot for any occasion, immaculate vibes and immaculate food

formatted_address: 2300 University Ave NE, Minneapolis, MN 55418, United States
name: Eastro Restaurant & Event Center

reviews.text: Love this place! Friend and I were looking for a quick lunch nearby, saw this and decided to give it a go. Guess what? This place is legit! I've already been back myself several times now for lunch and dinner. The quesadilla was so good that I forgot to take a pic and ordered takeout just to snap a pic for this review.  The food is tasty, portions are huge, staff are great. What else can you ask for?
First time definitely not the last time the homeboys from handy stopped gas station Saline hit me to it beautiful environment great tasting food and very polite staff hamdullah

I recently dined at Eastro and was blown away by the exceptional quality of the food and service. From the moment I walked in, I was greeted with warm smiles and attentive staff. The menu offered a variety of dishes and the flavors were perfectly balanced. The atmosphere was cozy and inviting. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a great meal in a welcoming environment.
First time, and won't be my last. I wasn't sure what to try but glad I went with chicken suqaar and pasta. Looking forward to trying more menu items!

This people know how to do business. Thank you for hosting us this Saturday. Very tasty Somali food. Eastro will soon be one of the best event centres in Minneapolis very soon. They have plenty of space, sound system is awesome and the space is very clean and has lots of room. Will recommend their service 100%.

formatted_address: 1197 University Ave W suite 100, St Paul, MN 55104, United States
name: Hodma Restaurant

reviews.text: This was an amazing experience. I had never had Somali food and wanted to try it while in the Twin Cities. We definitely chose the right spot for the first experience!!! The lamb was literally falling off the bone and seasoned perfectly. The rice was sooo good, and we were even given a banana to try with it (a must!). The chai was spicy and warm and delicious. Aisha helped us choose our dishes and was an extremely accommodating host. 10/10 recommend and if ever back in the Twin Cities, this might just be my first stop!

This place was AMAZING. I don't eat Somali food often so the worker gave some suggestions and it was all GREAT 👍🏾. First time eating rice with a banana, so I wasn't sure how to eat it, when I asked a worker she smiled and said do whatever you want. Every worker was so caring and giving 110%. I'm excited to go again

Great food. Fun staff.
The customers helped fill in my gaps on knowledge or understanding. Even offered to grab my meal, but I had already paid.

So it says a lot about the atmosphere and the service they provide.

Im gonna make this routine for sure.

The atmosphere was welcoming, clean, and full of warmth — the kind of place where culture and comfort meet.
The food was incredible. From the first bite, you can tell everything is made with care, tradition, and love. The flavors were rich, perfectly seasoned, and reminded me of home-cooked meals passed down through generations. The portions were generous and the presentation was beautiful.

I eat here every week, and am always excited to walk in the door. The food is delicious. We order pasta and chicken most often, big portions. Family run with incredible service. Have also loved the lamb + rice!

formatted_address: 1939 S 5th St, Minneapolis, MN 55454, United States
name: Oasis Mediterranean Grill

reviews.text: Delicious food, fast service, and very pleasant staff!  Even though it was dinner time, we were the only people dining in, but I think they were filling lots of online orders.  We definitely got our money's worth when it came to portion sizes, too! Supper, snack, and breakfast all in one 😂. I got the gyro plate and my husband got gyro sandwich. The fries were great! Crispy and hot!

The chicken shawarma plate is excellent. A generous portion, all the ingredients are well prepared. Definitely enough to share.
There's a walkup counter where you order, food is prepared quickly, your order is called and you walk to the counter to pick it up.
The atmosphere is very simple but clean. Eating inside is available at a high top counter, no tables inside. There are several tables for outdoor seating.
I was only disappointed in the price of a can of Diet Coke...$2.50. My meal was reasonably priced except for the soft drink.
You'll pay at the counter as you place your order, given a screen to add a tip (not sure what I was tipping for).

Order to go or order for here and they will bring it to you. The outdoor seating is nice but a bit loud with the hospital nearby. They have a handicapped accessible entrance. Enter and walk to your left. Sanitize your hands. Figure out what you want and then step up to the counter.
Baklava: Great. Dairy free. Walnut paradise.
Samosa: We got the Veggie and Beef. The picture doesn't do it justice. It's delicious.
Chicken shawarma: make it dairy free by removing the oasis sauce and adding hummus. The hot sauce is palatable fire

I had the Somali fries at the fair but just went here for the first time. Definitely going to be a new go-to spot. We had the falafel wrap, chicken shawarma, tabouli and some of the juice. It was all so good! We also got it in the middle of the day and everything was super fresh. Highly recommend this place!

Have you ever been full but wanted to keep eating because it was so flavorful and delicious? That was my experience here. The portions are fantastic and the food itself is fresh and loaded with tasty herbs and spices.

formatted_address: 1632 White Bear Ave, St Paul, MN 55106, United States
name: Joyful African Foods

reviews.text: Fish was rotten. This cost me 16$ went and showed her the pictures and she shifted the blame on me and whom she bought the fish from. This cost me 16$ and a few cents. I could not tell from frozen packaging fish was bad. I got it on 9/6/25 and defrosted overnight and in the morning it looked like that after cleaning. I even cut it and took a picture. It smelled old and stale. All I wanted was accountability and offer me a discount at least on a different fish or item. She had to hurry and go because she is busy inside. Others have been buying the same fish with no problem or she has not heard complaints. It is a small business. Goodbye and I am not stepping my foot there. I will be going to Minneapolis or get stuff online. Knowing her and shopping there for years I was not too surprised by the odd behavior. Unacceptable.

Wasted my gas going here because it said it was open only for it not to be. I called and someone picked up and then hung up in the middle of me asking a question. I honestly just wanted some suya seasoning.

Please do yourself a favor and go spend your hard earned money elsewhere! This woman is so RUDE! I went into her store today and spent almost $45 (on only 3 overpriced items). As I was checking out, the credit card machine would not print my receipt, so I tapped it a couple times and it accidentally printed a few copies. She then went on to loudly accuse me of “wasting her receipt paper” and stated, “why did you do that?!” When I pointed out that it was an accident and that yelling at your customers who are bringing you business is pretty poor customer service, she proceeded to tell me to leave her store and never come back, shouting, “I don’t want business from you people!” (Assuming she is referring to African Americans). Mind you, my 11 year old daughter was also present in the store with me. This is not the first time I have encountered her rude behaviors and I will NEVER go back! She is constantly on the phone, her food ordering process is disorganized, and the kitchen is a filthy mess! Please save your money for a store that actually cares about good customer service and is not discriminatory against others of their own race! Stay away from this store!
Customer service via the call is extremely rude and short. They kept disconnecting the call mid sentences, I absolutely do not recommend this place if you live over 1mile away

Her service wasn't hospitable she had an attitude and assumed I had one with her when I was ready to go back home then proceeded to say that I didn't confront my daughter in front of her face which was none of her business because it's my daughter, not hers. I was making sure she was ringing my stuff up correctly because on the screen it said brown rice and not palm oil she had an attitude because I asked about that but I was clarifying because I was confused and she got her panties in a bunch over that like I care it wasn't that deep ever. Lastly, she said I can't come back here like I care there are other African stores I don't need to go to hers at all because she had a chip on her shoulder about something and wasn't woman enough to speak up and her prices are expensive I wouldn't come here if I was you she's rude and has horrible customer service I wish I would've recorded it.

formatted_address: 6810 N Humboldt Ave, Brooklyn Center, MN 55430, United States
name: Value Foods African Market and Restaurant

reviews.text: Love love love I mean the chef needs to be slapped hard!! That food is fire!!!! Egusi and potato leaf something that was the best African food Ive ever had.

Best African food restaurant in Minnesota, particularly Minneapolis recommended. They the best, go try them jollof rice fish or lamb’s, bommnmnmmmmnnb .Different flavors, menus.All Minnesotans need tryouts for THE VALUE FOOD RESTAURANT.

The Skinny Cashier dude who claimed to be the manager of the store needs to be disciplined if not fired.
I was there a few times before just to buy rice with no issue.  Recently, I went there to buy two bags of 100lb rice.  As I came to the register and paid for the rice, I ask him to see if there's anyone can help me with the two bags of rice to my car.  He paused for a little while and said, "I can try to help you but we will have to talk".  I said okay thinking he was just teasing.  As we walked to the rice, he said "we do not have people to help you, you see, like at the walmart or target, they don't help you carry your groceries to your car, do they?  We're the same.  At that very moment, I starting to get angry and said, oh wow, really?  Fine, maybe I should go buy rice elsewhere from now on - I added.  He then said it's up to you.  Then unhappily helped haul the rice to my car and I helped him carry them into my car and left.

Friends and family members, do not go to this store unless you are willing to feel bad/angry like I was.  I have never ever go back since.  I hope the owner of this store can see this comment and do something about it.

Grocery store already tried several times to charge for what I didn’t picked
And always when you talk to them
They will always apologized but keep doing the same

We call that stealing
Saw cockroaches, their droppings, eggsacs, and also a rodent inside a food container.  Please contact the health and safety department!

formatted_address: 2220 Lyndale Ave S, Minneapolis, MN 55405, United States
name: Baba's Hummus House & Mana'eesh Bakery

reviews.text:
Smelled really yummy right off the bat

The waygu shwarma sandweesha was really well seasoned and tender. The potatoes that came with it we lightly spicy but really good. The two dipping sauces were also good.

The hummus bi lahme was super delicious but there was not enough pita bread with it.

Seating options were a bit unique.

🥙✨ Baba Hummus is a great spot for anyone who loves authentic Middle Eastern food!
The flavors are rich and fresh — especially the hummus and kebabs 👌.
Service is friendly, and the atmosphere feels warm and welcoming.
Definitely worth a visit if you’re craving real Mediterranean taste.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

We were recommended to try the Ba'bacon hummus bowl at Baba's Minnesota State Fair stand, and even though it's not something we would usually order, we're so glad we did. It was surprisingly delicious! 🤤

The dish started with a creamy sour cream and onion hummus base and was topped with beef bacon, crispy sumac tater tots, and caramelized onions. The flavors were perfectly balanced, with a great mix of creamy, crispy, and savory. It was a total standout and one of the best things we had at the fair!

Great spot! It has a modern hippie vibe with plenty of tables and sofas that give it a cozy coffee shop feel. The schwarmas were generously packed with meat—definitely satisfying. The fatoush salad was fresh and flavorful, but it had a bit too much dressing and came out a little soggy. Next time, I’ll ask for the dressing on the side. Pepperoni pizza was amazing.

Some of the best food I have had in the Twin Cities, to the point that I returned twice within one month. Not only was the flavor on point for a lot of their dishes, but also the texture offered a very pleasurable experience overall. I thought their mixture of hummus with all kinds of materials was amazing because both flavor and texture were truly elevated that way. I could not have finished my food any faster, honestly.

I would highly recommend the Hummus Bi Lahme Bowl, because the minced beef shawarma was so flavorful that it provided a good amount of extra flavor to the hummus that made one bite along with some pita puffs just a whole bite of flavor bomb. Almonds added a very nice layer to the bowl because it wasn't overpowering in flavor or texture, but rather provided that nice little touch needed. I also would highly recommend the Jerusalam-Style Bowl because the chickpeas were so flavorful and not too hard, and along with tahini and olive oil drizzle, it was just tasty in very simple and powerful ways.

The tahini dake shake was also amazing! As much as the paper straw I was given wasn't strong enough for me to consume the drink, a simple spoon would do, and I felt like the shake itself could be a meal because it had an abundant amount.

While I didn't try a lot of the other dishes, they received positive feedback from the ones around me. The only constructive feedback I had was about batata hara, the one that came with the sujok sandwich, which was too salty because I think the seasonings used for the pepper may have been too strong. I finished all the potatoes but not the vegetables around them, unfortunately.

Regardless, I am already putting this place as one of the best in the Twin Cities if I treat my friends from out of town visiting me, and I also highly recommend this place to anyone that seeks for amazing Middle Eastern, specifically Palestinian, food!

formatted_address: 9590 Noble Pkwy, Brooklyn Park, MN 55443, United States
name: Nadia's Jamaican Kitchen

reviews.text: So hospitable!! Totally.ade us feel welcomed. They made me actually WANT to be there.. The food was SO delicious! The meat was very tender and flavorful. Each component complimented the dishes.

Everything was delicious! The flavors are on point! We ate there for our first experience - it was clean and nice and the family was super nice and welcoming. Atmosphere is simple - no bells and whistles or fancy decor. But the food is so good, who cares? I highly recommend getting your grub on here! Mama Lu’s Oxtail & Butter Beans was just as DIVINE as the owner promised! 😍Everything was flavorful - I will definitely be going back! It’s a lot of food.

Nadia's Jamaican Kitchen is more than just a restaurant to me - it's a culinary oasis that has not fail to impress. From the moment I step through the doors, I'm enveloped in a warm and inviting atmosphere that sets the tone for a truly exceptional dining experience.

The service is top-notch, with friendly and attentive staff who seem to anticipate my every need. But it's the food that's the real star of the show. Every dish I've tried has been expertly prepared with a beautiful presentation, filled with flavor and love.
Their menu always features innovative and exciting new options that keep me coming back for more.

But what really sets Nadia's Jamaican Kitchen apart is the love and care that's clearly been poured into every aspect of the restaurant. From the subtle-chic decor to the carefully curated drink list, every detail feels thoughtful and intentional.

In short, I'm utterly obsessed with Nadia's Jamaican Kitchen. The service is top-notch, with friendly and attentive staff who seem to anticipate my every need. But it's the food that's the real star of the show. If you haven't been yet, do yourself a favor and come in ASAP - I promise you won't regret it!

I don’t write reviews but I had to for this restaurant. The food was delicious, service was so friendly and welcoming, and the restaurant itself was clean! Definitely coming here again and telling everyone to try it out!

The island curry chicken was incredible. Everything on the plate was delicious. Including the coleslaw, which I normally don't eat. We also got a side of plantains, which was a great sweet finish to the meal. The customer service was outstanding. I haven't been so impressed by a restaurant in a long time. 11/10 will be back!

formatted_address: 125 SE Main St, Minneapolis, MN 55414, United States
name: Aster Cafe

reviews.text: Amazing and best service around!  From MJ greeting us to the waiter and team, we had a great time, food was ALL delicious and the atmosphere was relaxing and enjoyable.  We had 15 people last minute and haven't that type of service in a long time - highly recommend!

I visited Aster Cafe for New Year's Eve diner with a friend and had a wonderful time! The menu was short and concise with a little something for anyone. The staff was kind and attentive, always checking in even with a completely packed floor. The mood lighting, live music, and overall decor of the place really wrapped the experience together as a thoughtful, meticulously crafted experience.

My son and I (both from different states - from MN, - and from each other,)  hung out here for lunch. It was a beautiful day, and their outdoor seating was perfect! Our food was fantastic, but I hated the flavor of my Virgin Mary (cumin, maybe?) The server was very attentive, and the food came out piping hot.  I definitely recommend this place!

We are here before the Paul McCartney concert n a Friday night. We had the mushroom flatbread, a bottle of wine and the barbecue pork sliders.

Sliders were great. The flatbread was basically a pizza.  It was just okay.  It was a beautiful fall day and we sat outside.  WARNING - there were hornets everywhere and I got stung badly as I went to pick up our wine bottle and put a refill and did not realize a hornet was sitting on the bottle. Ouch!!

Not a place to go if you are allergic to bees!

Food was great, wobbly tables on the patio where annoying, service was slow, wasn't offered a free refill, and the hostess that sat us didn't give us menus as we watched her seat other people and give them menus so my wife had to get up and get me her and my mother a menu while we were there with our special needs toddler.

Definitely no complaints about the yummy food though. It took forever to get our bill and it took a long time just to get some water.

We wanted to sit inside but they said it would be a $6 cover charge for each of us including our special needs disabled child because there was a live band playing inside.

When I looked inside there were literally two people sitting up at the bar and then one person eventually sitting at the bar and nobody actually sitting inside to eat.

formatted_address: 2308 W 50th St, Minneapolis, MN 55410, United States
name: Broders' Cucina Italiana

reviews.text:
Broders has delivered on the same promise for decades: food that’s delicious, consistent, and executed with precision. As a pizza chef in the neighborhood, this is where I go when I’m not eating my own.

The care every team member brings to the art of hospitality Broders is known for is a direct reflection of an exceptional management team and staff that continues to beautifully carry forward the standards Molly and Tom set so many years ago.

I first met Tom Broder Sr. when I was nine years old, ordering a slice of cheese pizza before walking over to the Edina Theatre with a buddy. This place isn’t just nostalgia from my youth it’s a cornerstone of Italian food in our community.

Now, with a dining room that feels like it was always meant to be there, Broders continues to set the bar. We’re incredibly lucky to have this gem.

Thank you to Broders, and to everyone who continues to honor the standards Molly and Tom established when it all began.

Chicken parm with fettuccine was very good.  Only complaint is that the portion was not very big, but it was probably consistent with the price.  Italian cookies were very good. Almond horn cookies were great. Rainbow cookie was larger than most but was just ok, but both at $1.95 per cookie were very expensive.  I’m used to paying by the pound for Italian cookies.  Overall great little spot in a safe area with street parking.  I’d go back.

Decided to go to the new location on a whim and glad we did. Very similar setup to the old location, but the deli and dine in are switched sides. Food is still the same quality and great! Parking is still off the street and limited. Staff is friendly, so stop in, order at the counter, and they'll bring the food out to you. Seating area is small, but they appear to be expanding at the time of this review, so it should get better.

Some people may say broders pizza is nothing special, unremarkable, forgettable. These people are wholly misinformed. Broders pizza is generational — of legend, even. The handsome cashier, whose name I have forgotten (frank? francesco? frappe?) was a charming delight. While I may have forgotten your name, I will never forget your soft features, natural charisma, and delicious, delicious pizza.
Thank you,
Henrik

Please help Guthrie T, who is on the "Hospitality Team," better understand what "hospitality" means. We've been coming regularly, especially when our kiddo is craving focaccia, since the deli is a short walk from our house. They have their focaccia available by the door, on a shelf beneath the cash register, or in the kitchen. We learned previously from other team members who voluntarily offered - a fresh batch is sometimes available in the kitchen. Since then, we ask in case a batch just came out of the oven (and warm!). When we asked on the latest visit, the team member checked and came back and told us that some would be available in 15 minutes. Guthrie was standing at the register next to the team member. We asked if we should pay then, or when we come back. The team member told us to just pay later. We came back a little before 15 minutes. The team member who was helping us (shoulder length dark hair, painted nails) was assisting another customer. Guthrie stepped up to assist us without a greeting or smile - ready to argue. He proceeded to tell us while bobbing his head, rolling his eyes and gesturing with his hands that they did not fulfill our order. They're not going to make another batch for us because there were already some available. We did not ask the original team member to make a batch for us. That was OFFERED, and we happily accepted. But under 15 minutes, GUTHRIE TOOK IT UPON HIMSELF TO CHASTISE THE TEAM MEMBER WHO WAS ASSISTING US AND REVOKE THE OFFER. Wow. Again, we did not ask anyone to make a new batch. After expressing our frustration and receiving reluctant apologies from Guthrie, we ended up purchasing two focaccia that were already bagged - Only because our kiddo still wanted focaccia. The focaccia ended up dry, and not up to standard. Disappointing experience all around. What type of "hospitality" training did Guthrie receive?

formatted_address: 4301 Chestnut St, Philadelphia, PA 19104, United States
name: Kilimandjaro restaurant

reviews.text: We absolutely enjoyed every moment in here. It was good to be in the midst of our fellow Africans. The restaurant was clean, organized and well maintained. The food they served us were very tasty and the drink was typical African folere. The customer service was exceptional.  It was a good experience and I strongly recommend to all.

The food was delicious. We had the Lamb and Tilapia with Jollof, the onions on top add so much flavor. The Maafe with Chicken was also very good. We order plantains as well that were freshly fried and sweet. The Ginger and mange drink was taste amazing. They also had live music which added to the atmosphere. 10/10 experience

I love this place,my brothers and I go here all the time, the food is outstanding and the customer service is A+1 my favorite dish is Yassa Philly boneless chicken,lamb or beef,jollof rice with mixed veggies and ginger and mango drink so delicious mmm mm m lol

We brought a group visiting for a work conference as part of a food tour all around Philly and this was an exceptional experience. We focused on the diversity and representation of our multi-cultural city, of which none of our visiting guests had ever eaten West African food before. They all came back for multiple services of the Yassa Philly chicken, meat patties, and Senegal cocktail. Youma personally welcomed our group and shared some of her backstory - which was our favorite part of the whole experience. We can't wait to bring many MANY more groups back to Kilimandjaro. Thank you Youma and Abiche!!!

Let me start by saying how beautifully decorated the restaurant is. The vibrant colors and decor make you feel welcomed and happy., the customer service is excellent and the wait staff were very friendly. The FOOD.... I can't say enough how good the food was; it's African food (Senegalese ) everything was so flavorful and cooked right. I've had Liberian, and Nigerian food but this was amazing. The red snapper was delicious and grilled to perfection; I really didn't care for the athieke. It was over cooked and mushy, the plantains were amazing! It was paired with sweet carrots and onions in a tomato based sauce. My friend loved all of her food, she had the chicken and jollof rice which she stated that everything was full of flavor and delicious. My only complaint is that they did not have dessert.... We had to go somewhere else for a sweet treat. The menu selections are not much but what they do have is worth the visit. I recommend this beautiful restaurant to everyone please try 🙌🏽❤️

formatted_address: 6620 Woodland Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19142, United States
name: Le Mandingue African Restaurant

reviews.text: Lemandingue is one of the best African restaurant in Philadelphia the food is always delicious. I have been eating at this restaurant for couple of years but the food has been a savior for me because there’s no way that I will cook on my own if I can spend less than $20 and get the best of the best.
I crave the lamb but sometimes it’s a lot of fat on it but it’s still good and it came sizzling n hot the plantains are amazing this is my go to spot always
Food was good but it wasn’t what I ordered. Never had African food the fufu and egosi was good ordered red snapper jollof rice and plantain but I know damn well this isn’t jollof rice !

I’m not sure if they got a new cook but the fact I had to season my cassava leaf is crazy. The rice is too mushy, I can literally mash the rice up. This was my go to spot for potatoe greens and cassava. I’m not sure what’s going on with the cook from back then compared to the cook now but you guys desperately need a change. My past 6 orders have been BLAND and the rice is overcooked, it’s laziness on the cooks part because why isn’t the food simply seasoned? You guys need a new cook, get back to being the best African restaurant in Philly!

Ordered delivery and the food did not disappoint. Everything was delicious. This was the lamb with jollof rice, side of plantain and side of cabbage. The cabbage i wasn’t crazy about (too soft no crunch) but everything else was very good and would order again. They give you plenty of food. I believe the prices are fair for the amount of food you receive.

formatted_address: 400 Fairmount Ave #2808, Philadelphia, PA 19123, United States
name: SUYA SUYA West African Grill

reviews.text:
Came here with friend. Treated them to west African food for their birthday. We arrived around 730 which was right on time. After we ordered our food on the kiosk and set down a big crowd came in. So many people came to order food before the night was out. The food was delicious. The white suya sauce was good with hot drumsticks. I was super impressed with the food. Even my friend.  I also had cornbread with my meal and the corn bread was delicious too.
Both of our food together was about 40 to 45 dollars. Very reasonable.
When you dine in. Your food does come on a sturdy paper plate.  Felt authentic and home vibes.

You can see the food being prepared which I love so much.

Unsure if they have a restroom for the public.

I've been seeing this on tiktok for the past 2 weeks and decided lastnight to try.
When I came in I had to greet the lady working.  Didn't like that, I'm coming in to spend my money. Welcome would've been nice! She didn't even ask could she take my order.  My husband and I seen a kiosk and placed our order.  The food was a 6/10.
Jollof rice was flavorless, steak was chewy and had fat/Gristle on each piece.
The salad that came with it was good along with the plantains. The potato greens were watery and ok.  Overall I love supporting my people businesses but I probably won't be back.  Respectfully

I ordered online, and my food arrived fresh and hot, which I really appreciated.

I tried the Beef Suya (spicy) platter with plantain, cabbage, onion, and jollof rice. The jollof rice was definitely the best part it was flavorful and perfectly cooked. The beef Suya was tender with a nice texture and good spice, though I found it a bit too salty. I have a high spice tolerance, but even for me the heat built up and made it tough to finish, so I wouldn’t recommend it to anyone sensitive to spice.

Portion-wise, I wish there had been more plantain and onion, as the serving felt small compared to the generous amount of rice.

I also ordered a chicken Suya leg on the side, and in my opinion, the chicken Suya was much better than the beef.

This African spot is amazing! Definitely try the Suya bowl because it’s a great deal and packed with flavor. Some of the dishes were spicy even at the lowest spice level, so watch out if you’re not big on heat. You HAVE to get the cornbread as a side. It’s seriously so good. Loved everything about this place and will definitely be back. Seems like it’s easier to dine in and let the food come out when it ready instead of ordering online.

Located in northern liberties, so parking can be a challenge. I wanted to like this food. The price isn’t awful, but it’s not the great either. I paid about $15 for the steak bowl with jollof and plantain, and then another $4 for a meat pie. Everything was lackluster. The meat pie ingredients tasted muddled, I did enjoy the crust tho. The jollof rice flavor was mild, I wish it stood out more… as in more tomato taste, more richness… anything to resemble Nigerian jollof. The steak suya was fine… it was a bit tough, and majority of the flavor came from the sprinkled suya spice over top. The plantain was light skin and hard and they weren’t very sweet. I’ve been meaning to try the restaurant and I finally did. I’m not impressed.

formatted_address: 6422 Rising Sun Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19111, United States
name: Soul of Africa Restaurant LLC

reviews.text: I usually get my potato greens from le mandingue but I recently moved so I figured I give this place a try. Their potato greens and fufu definitely didn’t disappoint. I enjoyed the flavor, the only thing i didn’t like about it was pieces in the greens I couldn’t really chew. The fufu was also good - it didn’t stick to my fingers like other fufu I had in the past so I was happy about that. I also got white rice and I wish it came with their pepper sauce that usually comes with their platters. Other than that, I will probably go back again.

Ordered on door dash. This is single handedly the most appallingly bad food I have ever ordered! How can this restaurant in good conscience charge money for this! This is the saddest Liberian food I have ever seen. Look at this fufu and peanut butter soup! Both went straight in the trash, completely inedible, not to mention ice cold. The palm butter and egusi was barely any better. Nothing was cooked correctly. And apparently door dash here doesn't give money back for quality issues, which makes no sense, so I am unable to get my money back for this. Disgusting. This place should be shut down. Saddest part is I ordered this for my daughter's birthday meal.

I didn't pay for stale food. I couldn't enjoy my food coz it smelled so bad🤮. Whoever made this and packaged it, you can obviously smell it. It's extremely inconsiderate to sell it to your customers. Everything is going in the trash.

I’ve been coming to this restaurant for well over 10years I want to say about a year ago they switch owners. They had a young African gentlemen in there cooking initially when the new owners took over and his food was just like the old owners maybe even better. Although the wait was usually long I don’t mind waiting for quality food. This past week I got food from here and the quality was poor I ate to say. I travel about a hour and half to get the food from relocating out of Philly some years ago and I was disappointedz atteike was soft almost grits like and snapper was small. I spend the least every time I go 100 bucks to make it worth the trip. Not bashing the restaurant at all just want quality food to be better because it’s my favorite go to.

I had potato greens from here before and they were good but it’s been awhile. I got some today and there’s not really any flavor. They just taste like oily spicy spinach. I also asked for no meat and they gave me meat.

formatted_address: 2108 South St, Philadelphia, PA 19146, United States
name: Chateau Rouge

reviews.text:
Just visited for the first time, and my, am I glad I did! It was my 25th birthday and I wanted to go out to eat with my parents and siblings. I did a Google search for fine dining African restaurants in the city, and Chateau Rouge was one of the first ones to come up. As a fine dining line cook, I’m careful about where I go to eat out, but after reading the reviews, I had to try it out.
First, the restaurant is small but cozy in a home-y kind of way, so big thanks for Chateau Rouge for helping me arrange the reservation for all 10 of us to come. The decor was beautiful and not too much, from the pillows to the napkin holders, to the African masks and paintings on the walls. The chairs and tables are low, so if you have long legs or over 6’ like one of my brothers, it will be a bit uncomfortable after a while.
Secondly, the service was great. Our waiter explained the menu well and was helpful in choosing the right number of dishes for the table. Everyone was helpful all night in bringing out the food and drinks and clearing the table before courses.
Lastly, the food. THE FOOD. Bussin’ no discussion GOOD. We all ordered the pre fixe menu, $55 per person, 1 appetizer, 1 main, 2 sides and 1 dessert. You can pick from 3 appetizers, 5 main dishes and sides, and 4 desserts. Because it was 10 of us, we ordered a mix of everything so we could all share and taste everything. The puff puffs were great bread starters, not too sweet and bread-y. The veggie salad was dressed well, on the sweet side with the raisins and pineapple but balanced out with palm, bamboo and mixed greens. I would have liked more lettuce, but that’s my opinion. The pastels were very flavorful, I had to remind myself that it was tuna inside! The suya wings were so good! My siblings loved them so much, I need to get the recipe now! We all had the virgin pina colada from the bar, which was nice, a bit much on the mint and low on the coconut, but again, my opinion. The coconut sauce and the peanut sauce with the suya brochettes and the grilled chicken elevated the dish’s flavor to a new level. My siblings don’t like fish, but they liked the texture of the grilled fish and I liked the flavor. The yassa poulet and the haricot saute were some of the best dishes I’ve had in a while! The chicken so tender, it was falling off the bone. The flavor was new but familiar and comforting at the same time. The beans cooked to perfection, and so so good! Plantains and sweet potatoes were fresh and naturally sweet. I could tell the produce in the ratatouille was out of season and some of the rice was undercooked, but that’s because I have some experience in the industry. The dessert just completed the meal: the lava cake was light and chocolate rich, the fruit salad was fresh and naturally sweet, the banana flambé and caramelized pineapple were just delicious. This was not a tasting menu, so all the portions are the are the same are the à la cart menu, which are good sized if you’re a little hungry. This also isn’t a Michelin fine dining restaurant with the portions and platings, so don’t come expecting it. However, do come expecting flavorful food, you won’t be disappointed.

Just had dinner at Chateau Rouge, an incredible West African BYOB with a French touch on South Street! 🔥

It's a charming Black-owned restaurant with a well-executed menu that features several dishes with spices that come directly from Cameroon!

They serve incredible entrees, but have a stellar 4-course tasting menu that's only $55.

As you can see, it's worth a visit. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Had a truly great meal here. We had 3 different kinds of chicken and all of them were delicious, but brochettes were our favorite. Definitely do not forget to leave room for dessert, the caramelized pineapple and banana flambee were both fantastic. Great atmosphere inside (didn't see the outdoor seating), and super friendly service. Can't wait to return.

My wife and I had a great meal at Chateau Rouge last Thursday. Steven was a wonderful server and the fixed price option is great menu. Our food and drinks were fresh and excellently prepared. I ordered the chicken skewers to start, followed by a whole grilled fish. It was delicious. We will definitely be back.

Where do I begin, I went here with a friend and the food was pretty good. Upon entry we were greeted by kind friendly staff members.
