For a first time experience i enjoyed it, the owner came to my table personally and introduced herself. The environment was clean and well decorated to fit the cultural aesthetic. I highly recommend making a reservation prior to arrival they do have outdoor seating if you find the indoor seating too tight. The space is fairly small.

formatted_address: 106 Chestnut St, Philadelphia, PA 19106, United States
name: Eatwell Philly - African Restaurant and Lounge

reviews.text: I’m Puerto Rican with mostly Nigerian DNA (25% Nigerian. Everything else is 15 or less). The food is tasty. The rice isn't the same texture as traditional Puerto Rican, But the soul of the flavor is definitely there

Everything felt incredibly authentic and well done! The waitress helped up go through the menu and choose things that interest us without ordering in excess. I personally like my fufu on the side and not under everything. Some of the meats just weren’t my cup of tea but i’m sure others will like it. We recommend the Suya

First time trying Nigerian food. I took Efo Elegusi meal and jollof rice, I loved it. Food was so good. Good service and nice atmosphere (good music, not too loud). The place is very neat, I highly recommand.

Stopped into Eatwell for lunch and had a great experience! The food was fantastic, particularly the spicy suya, meat pies, and jollof rice. The menu was quite extensive, so there are plenty of options and we look forward to trying new things. It was our first time eating here, but the service was pleasant and helpful in explaining things on the menu. Overall, a great time!

I was walking when I spotted this place. I was excited to check it out as I am African and wanted to support an African restaurant. The Suya was a little dry to me, but I did still enjoy it. The puff puff was definitely worth it. The restaurant was clean and it wasn't too loud. I definitely recommend checking them out.

formatted_address: 6133 Woodland Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19142, United States
name: African Small Pot

reviews.text: so i came here yesterday 1/6/26 on a Tuesday for take out, i had the pepper soup and fufu and it was soo good i came back today 1/7/26 and i tried the peanut butter soup or peanut sauce with the lamb onions and yellow rice, it was soo good as well, lamb was seasoned to perfection and crispy like i like it and the Shaykh was very friendly and hospitable. he gave us recipes and talked to us as we ate. oh and the ginger juice was good too,, not over powering like some African eateries but still good, i would def come here again.

It was my first time me and my husband and my daughter we came in to try the food. It was amazing. Best experience ever so much flavor.
Recommend this place 100%
The owner is very nice , and clean place  .

We had African Small Pot deliver food to an event in Africatown, and they were extremely helpful. The staff was kind and the food was absolutely delicious. They made us vegetarian-friendly breakfast sandwiches, with eggs, peppers, onions, and garlic. Everyone who ate one thought they were incredible! They also gave us coffee and tea with the food. The delivery was on-time and the communication with the staff was reliable and consistent. Definitely consider ordering from them or giving them a visit!

My colleagues and I recently had the pleasure of visiting African Small Pot for the first time and everybody left with a smile. We had many different items from the menu (variety of fish, chicken, rice, greens, etc.) and everything was truly so delicious and flavorful! The entire staff including the chef and the owner were very welcoming and accommodating to us, as we were a large group. We are incredibly grateful! 🌟 See you again soon!

An absolute 10/10. The customer service was excellent, as well as the food. The owner was extremely attentive and made sure my friend and I were taken care of. I ordered some red snapper, with a side of rice, and some plantain. I will definitely be coming back.

formatted_address: 1901 Chestnut St, Philadelphia, PA 19103, United States
name: The Saints Restaurant and Lounge

reviews.text:
The Saints has an amazing atmosphere as well as food. Especially the red snapper and grape salad. The fries were good and my coworkers were enjoying their pineapple wings.The owner and staff were really nice and accommodating.
I had a phenomenal time with my crew after our 10 hour work day . We went back the second day, with a whole different group of crew members, but they were closing earlier.

Came across this 5 star restaurant when looking for a resturant/lounge on a Friday night. After calling to confirm they were still byob & would have a dj we dropped in. The lounge vibe and music (no dj) was cool but that's about the end of the pros. There was only one young woman operating as host, waitress, bartender & cashier. She was nice but service was extremely slow. Between that & the dirty glassware we should've dipped but we stayed and ordered the suya beef & chicken, fries and kale. Everything came out lukewarm and the "suya" spiced meat just meant it came w/ a heavy dusting of cayenne powder. The fries were good. The final straw, the $50 per bottle fee that was added to our bill for our two bottles of wine. After explaining this fee was not listed ANYWHERE on their socials they gave us a "discount" and took one of the fees off. Crazy for $12 wine. The table next to us had the same surprise as they were giving the manager a piece of their mind as we left. I can't understand the 5 star reviews.

Googled "African restaurants Philly " & The Saints popped up so I wanted to try it. It's BYOB. Our waitress was attentive, she kept checking on us to make sure we were good and even offered to take pics. I had Suya chicken, jollof rice and plantains. Everything was tasty and it came out in a reasonable time. The decor is nice and the music was good. I can see it being a vibe once more people start patronizing. Can't wait to go back!!
Went here for my birthday and enjoyed the food. Fairly new so it wasn't busy. Currently B.Y.OB. Me and my party tried the snapper, chicken wings, tacos and salad.  Everything was delicious 😋

I visited a few days ago. Cute vibes, decent food, but I will not be returning to this establishment for these reasons:
1. We were not greeted by staff upon arrival. The waitresses on duty weren’t as knowledgeable as they should’ve been. They were more occupied with smoking hookah.
2. Their website has several false advertisements:
There were only two main entrées that night where their website states four. I also asked for a salad, but they said they were out of the grape salad (not ceaser). That night they had snapper and lamb chops as main dishes. My party and I had to wait about 30 minutes for the food. I got the snapper. It was cooked well, the sauce they used tasted great, my only problem was the fish was not seasoned inside. The inside tasted bland. I also had a side of plantains and collard greens, which tasted well. My partner got the lamb chops. I was told that they were good. They had a side of jollof rice, which I tasted, and we both agreed it was extremely spicy. This was not the good type of spicy. It was the type of spicy where you had to focus on eating it instead of enjoying the meal. Also, nowhere on their website does it state that it's BYOB. The waitress told us it's a $50 cover charge if we brought our own bottle (…like huh??!). Their website states to “Unwind…with our signature cocktails, curated wines, and premium spirits”. We  didn't bring a bottle because we thought they would have drinks.  I tried calling their number several times to ask questions, but it went straight to message.
3. The music mix they had was very entertaining. However, the music was too loud! It's already a small establishment, the music should not be that loud. The waitresses placed us near the speaker. This could’ve been a contributing factor. It's a lounge not a club.I know they’re trying to create a vibe, but I shouldn’t have to be yelling across the table to have a conversation with my party.
4. This place does have the potential to be a really great scene, it just needs a little TLC. But, in the meantime, I will not be returning back in the near future.

formatted_address: 177 City Ave, Bala Cynwyd, PA 19004, United States
name: SUYA SUYA West African Grill

reviews.text: I was pleasantly surprised to see a West African Restaurant on City Line Ave. I was not surprised that their food was ABSOLUTELY DELICIOUS!!! Before I walked around the corner, I could feel the aroma wafting through the breeze as if it had my nose targeted. As soon as I walked in, I was greeted with the most beautiful smile. The menu was right there on the wall and I paid hard earned money for high quality food! I've been back 3 times already and tomorrow will be the forth!

If you want a place to get Nigerian food, you just hit the jackpot. I had egusi soup, jollof rice, suya and meatpie, and I had absolutely no complaints.
The service, from the moment I called, was friendly, welcoming, and very courteous. Felt like meeting an old friend.
Food portions were generous, and the suya was divine.
My only complaint would be the amount of oil in the egusi, it was too much. But that's just me. Some may like it that way

My absolute favorite place for lunch near SJU! The jollof wrap is a must-try, and the chicken suya bowl with high heat and Okuko rice is unbelievably good. The staff is super friendly, and the whole place has a great vibe.

If I could have given zero stars I would.  Food was dry, unfavorable, and so nasty. Meat was so tough could not even eat it. Just thru it away and now hungry and erked. Was a waste of time and money. Would never eat from there again. la mandique need to go give them lessons on everything... oh yeah I ordered 3 egusi and a side of the spicy (Not so spicy) chicken suya, paid for 3 pieces and only got 1. Fufu was mushy as well. Overall disappointed in how they pass this crap off as authentic African food. Do ya self a favor and don't waste ya time or stomach on this place

Were do I begin! I have restaurants that I believe are good to very good. I thought this restaurant was exceptional! So Let’s Dish! Customer Service was patient and informative as this was our first time in a West African restaurant. He did everything with a generous smile. The place where they were cooking was clean and organized. Now the food, clean, wonderful spices, and plentiful! The vegetables tasted like they were made in heaven! The plantains were a perfect sweet but not too sweet balance. Rice cooked perfectly. And my friend ate all the cornbread 😱.  I can’t wait to go try everything on the menu. The steak was slightly over cooked but the seasoning was on point. Run don’t walk to this place!

formatted_address: 5514 Rising Sun Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19120, United States
name: Palace african restaurant

reviews.text: Terrible Potato Greens & Rice was beyond nasty i will never go back overpriced and all i been to better African food restaurants for less money and way better quality taste! CHECK YOUR food  and look at it before you leave i shouldn’t have left that restaurant with the throw and not well done chicken! Super disappointed

For $30 I got 1/2 containers of food with 4 small pieces of meat and old sticky clumps of rice! I will never return to this restaurant EVER again!! The goat was so tough even a dog couldn’t chew it!! Don’t waste your time or money going there. When I called the restaurant the man said I paid that price for the RAW fufu lol no sir I order the Okra that came with fufu! So where is the rest of my food??? Will be getting my money back ASAP!!

I got egusi and fufu and it was good! It was oily but I assume that's how it's made. I ordered take out and the food was very hot when I picked it up. I ordered  goat but I was given chicken. I told the chef it was fine as long as I was charged for chicken. It paid $21 total so I thought it was a little pricey just for one meal. The place does not really support dine in as there was about 1 table with 2 seats and AC. I enjoyed. Wish it came with more fufu though. If you want to try African food, this is a good place to try!

I wish I could put a video in here to actually show what they gave me. Why is my cassava leaf soup? Who ever packed my ordered saw exactly how it was and you guys still gave it to me. It was not cooked properly and it was still served to me.

Their food is overpriced!! I will stick to the Liberian restaurant. Potatoes green and cassava leaves are mainly a Liberian dish, and they don't cook it right. They told me 25 dollars for some tilapia and plantain, and I was out and never returned.

formatted_address: 428 W Olney Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19120, United States
name: TOUBA African Restaurant

reviews.text: First time having Senegalese food -- but not the last! Got a dish called Yassa -- chicken, flavorful cooked onions, and rice. Amazing flavor. Also got a super fresh salad to start, and a really flavorful coffee. Constant flow of people coming in or taking out, so obviously a neighborhood gem I was missing out on. Staff was super nice too. Coming back for the lamb next time!

This is my first time trying Senegalese food. I got the lamb dibi with jollof and plantain. I spent around $23. The portion was fine. The lamb was delicious, and a hint of mustard. The plantain was very sweet, just a tad too greasy for my liking. The rice was my least favorite. Maybe it was the type of rice they used, I didn’t like the texture, it also didn’t have that much flavor.

We decided to dine in, and I have to say this place blew me away. From the start, the service was warm and welcoming. They brought out complimentary coffee and donuts, which were absolutely delicious and set the tone for the meal. When the food arrived, I had the Yassa with fish—and wow, it was hands down one of the best meals I’ve had in a long time. Everything was fresh, flavorful, and perfectly cooked. Between the incredible food, the amazing coffee, and the top-notch service, I’ll definitely be coming back!

This is my third time ordering from this store. The first time my order was correct. The second time I received different items then what was asked for over the phone and did not realize until I came home. This time I order a milk like purée that has black beans in it. Unknown to me, I thought this was the same item I’ve purchased from other ethnic African restaurants. I had bought 4 of these totaling $20 dollars. Even while in the store one of the products I had asked for I was told was a Guinean purée. I felt as though if the items I listed were Guinean they should’ve made me aware that the item I was getting was not the same as what they were selling. I tried calling upon eating the first bowl to resolve the issues of me mistaking a dish I commonly eat to theirs. The gentleman who answer couldn’t seem to understand how a simple mishap could have took place when similar dishes are served in Africa especially west Africa. He was very  ignorant and arrogant to tell me “that this was not a Guinean store” but still proceed to go through with the purchase I thought was similar to the Guinean purchase I usually buy. Will be disputing this charge because the other 3 items will have to be discarded. I was not informed of a no refund policy by this man who answered or anything just pure ignorance when I called.

New Senegalese restaurant!! Food is truly authentic! Price is affordable and good quantity! Order ahaead for take out, it can take 15 to 20 minutes to get a meal done! Natural ginger and hibiscus, nicely flavored! Definitely recommend if you are looking for a real Senegalese dish!! Will go back!!

formatted_address: 6735 Elmwood Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19142, United States
name: Djoliba Restaurant

reviews.text: The food improved my whole week! I got the fried tallapia and jollof rice. Fish was delicious and rice was a great texture. The cabbage, onions, and vegetables were flavorful and tender. I don't personally like coleslaw but even that was great! We got a ginger drink which was so spicy and the owner offered us the hibiscus drink which was sweet, both great! We had a lovely dinner.
Had the lamb shank (gigot) with rice. The portion was generous and the food delicious. The entire staff was very attentive. I would eat here again.

The dibi lamb was no seasoned well and they give you very small portions of meat for the price. The jollof rice and the plantain were good. I also liked the topping that came with it. The dibi lamb was mediocre and not seasoned well at all.
Husband and I decided to try Djoliba, and the food delicious and service was wonderful! We had the lamb and jollof. The sautéed onions over the  jollof is amazing. Im glad I found this place on IG
Got the chicken and jolof rice, It was so good I couldn't help but clean my plate! Great vibes and a great meal!

formatted_address: 5353 Woodland Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19143, United States
name: Baobab

reviews.text: This establishment is among the finest African restaurants. Their portion sizes are commendable. Their customer service is impeccable. They consistently demonstrate a gracious attitude.

My sister and I came to woodland to get or hair done, we wher so hurry looking for food I just googled and find Sahara. Boy if I tell  you abut this  food is gooooooooooood!!!  Fatima was very helpful and nice 😊
Very bad experience, they ask you to wait for long time, and give your food to another costumers, very bad workers
Great place with friendly staff and delicious food! The atchieke is too good! I will be back.
Delicious! I got the lamb with Jollof rice and it was so good. The onion mixture they put on top has so much flavor. Kind service as well! You have to try!

formatted_address: 6528 Woodland Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19142, United States
name: Sahara Restaurant

reviews.text: Everybody in this restaurant is nice they keep it clean and the food is reasonably priced the jollof and fish taste good and pepper soup and fufu is definitely recommend this place
Amazing food, amazing service. 100% would go again. The attieke was amazing and the fish well seasoned.

Great food! Had the attieke fish and lamb, and everything was seasoned amazingly! Customer service was great, Aisatou was a great hostess, which always makes the experience even better.

Would definitely check out if you are around!
The lamb was really good. Their jollof rice was not good. The peanut butter soup and egusi were amazing. Alot of food for a decent price.

I went there because of the positive reviews. But my experience was not positive at all. I order jollof rice with lamb. No plantains and was still charge $20. They switch the price every time I go in there and the lamb was hard full of bones. Is a big No for me.

formatted_address: Underground in the suburban station, 1500 John F Kennedy Blvd, Philadelphia, PA 19102, United States
name: New Era Nigerian Cuisine

reviews.text:
As a Nigerian myself, I am always eager to try Nigerian restaurants. The reviews weren’t great, but I try to form my own opinion. That being said, the reviews were spot on. Before I review the food I want to say that the owner was very kind and welcoming. The restaurant located underground of JFK was clean and inviting. I wish I could say positive things about the food. I ordered jollof rice with peppered goat, and the seasoned spinach , 2 meat pies and a bag of chinchin. My total was $61. Never have I paid that much for African food, and I have frequented many African restaurants in Philadelphia. I was literally flabbergasted when I reviewed my receipt. There was a 15% gratuity automatically included. How do you as a business owner do that, for a take-out order no less? The food took about 20 mins to come out after we ordered. We didn’t dine in. When we got home to eat, the portion was crazy… as in crazy small. I had to laugh because  surely this was a joke.

The jollof rice Smokey and tasty, but it was so salty.
The peppered goat: by far the worst item, was also salty and SO OILY. Literally baptized in grease and tough to chew.
The spinach was really tasty, good flavor but unfortunately also oily.
The meat pie, has no taste. The dough was nice and flaky. We welcomed the meat pie, it was a much needed palate cleanser.
The chinchin was crunchy and delicious with the right amount of sweetness.
All in all, I would not recommend this restaurant. It is overpriced and the food quality and quantity does not justify the price.

I tried New Era for the first time and it was great. Chef T was very friendly and had no problem explaining the menu to me. When I tried to order multiple things from the menu, she showed me a combo that already contained those things so I could get more bang for my buck. I really appreciated her honesty. Also, when the food took a little longer than expected, she offered me a free beverage for my wait. Her customer service was impeccable. You can tell she really loves what she does. The food was amazing! The jollof rice had a nice smoky flavor to it. The pepper chicken was juicy with a nice spice but somehow Chef T was able to get a crispy skin on it. The plantains were sweet and caramelized. The portion of food was great too! I will definitely be returning.
The food was really tasty and fresh, loved the flavors with Good portion size and quick delivery, will order again.

This place is so caring and really treat they customers good . They food is delicious i definitely recommend coming here . This is my new spot i love restaurants that really care about the customers and cook they food with love . A 10/10 its hard finding a good place that makes ogbono soup this place is in my top 3 . Delicious

I purchased food from New Era Cuisine 3 times.  The first time I purchased Chicken with Jollof rice.  It was tasty and the wait was a little long, but nothing too crazy.  The second time, I purchased Jollof rice and I placed my order on-line and by the time I arrived at the restaurant, my order was ready.  The third I made a purchase, I ordered Suya wings and french fries and this was the worst experience.  I placed my order on-line at around 12:49. I was scheduled to pick up the food at 1:30 and I arrived at the restaurant at 1:41.  When I walked in, there was 1 customer waiting and there was not anyone at the counter to help/service me.  I rang the little bell at the counter and no one came out.  After about 7 minutes, a young lady finally walked out and asked how could she help me.  I told her I was there to pick up an on-line order and she said give me a second.  I waited for another 20 minutes for my order.  It appeared that the young lady was the only person working in the restaurant at the time.  So that means she must have been taking the orders, cooking the food, filling the orders and collecting payments.  That is way to much for 1 person.  There should never be just 1 person working at any given moment.  So when I asked why the order was not ready at 1:30 when I received a notification stating that it was ready.  The young lady made up a lie saying the order didn't come in to them when I made the order.  She said she received the order 5 minutes before I walked in, which I do not believe at all.  She would have been better off telling the truth and said she was the only one working and she was overwhelmed and got backed up with the orders.  Which seems closer to the truth.  The food wasn't bad, but if New Era Cuisine would like to have longevity at the underground location, they have to do better.  The long waits are unacceptable.  I hope they get it together and I wish them well, but I'm taking a break from them for a very long time.

formatted_address: 5938 Chestnut St, Philadelphia, PA 19139, United States
name: Aku's Kitchen

reviews.text: The food and the customer service were both extremely well. The food was fresh and hot, and the owner Aku and Edem were both very helpful, friendly, and patient as I was trying to figure out what to order. I would highly recommend anyone in the Philly area to come to this genuine Ghanaian Restaraunt. Aku even signed my box I felt even more special! 5 stars ⭐️!!!
5 stars for amazing service and delicious waakye, soup, meat pie fried plantain! Highly recommended.

Called in ahead with my order, which was ready when I arrived.
Ordered kelewele (fried spicy ripe plantain), waakye (cooked rice and beans) with goat meat and all the trimming
Food came with a boiled egg and a side of pepper sauce.

Tasty food, good service and a cozy atmosphere in this Ghanaian restaurant.

Does not accept cash.
Only Zelle and Cashapp

Was worth the 45 minute drive.

Aku is amazing.
FYI: Takeout place only and you have to call ahead of time. We didn't know that but she didn't turn us away. She took care of 5 hungry people with delicious food!

Love her, love service and her food!

My boyfriend introduced me to Aku's kitchen and I must say I have been addicted to her food since. The food is delicious. The place is great very clean. The service is spectacular. Aku's smile is always welcoming as well as the staff.   Best Ghanian food is West Philadelphia- a true hidden gem. Too bad she is only open on weekends.

formatted_address: 6421 Woodland Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19142, United States
name: Ecowas African Restaurant

reviews.text: Got tired of mandingue bad customer service. I gave this pace a shot and I am not disappointed. Attieke was fresh and delicious. Meat flavorful. Customer service great. I ordered over the phone when I got there my food was ready. I just wish the meat had some onion sauce to it. Other than that love it . Thank you

If you’ve never had African food before you’ll probably enjoy this place. If you have, just skip it. It’s not bad but since it’s in an area with lots of African restaurants it doesn’t hold up to the competition in the area. Emma’s is a few blocks away and sooo much better. We tried the palava sauce and the pepper soup. It was not as spicy as most West African food tends to be but came with pepper sauce on the side to turn the heat up. The food had a good flavor but it wasn’t cooked long enough for the flavor to really get into the meat & bones. The cow foot was very tough and the fish in the soup was underdone. The fufu was not mixed well. It was edible but I was disappointed knowing I could have gone somewhere else nearby for much better food. Also, The bathroom smelled horribly and when I asked for soap I was informed they had none so I had to help myself to the dish detergent sitting just outside the bathroom.

The grilled fish and Achekeh was one of the best I have had in a long time. The fish was seasoned and well done and  the achekeh was not dry like other places lol. I will be coming back again for grilled fish
Authentic and delicious Liberian food. Big portions. Very good prices

(8/18/23) I unfortunately had to change my review. The young woman was going to send me off with old, nasty looking plantains until I mentioned who I was in relation to my husband (who is African and known to them), so she made new plantains and put them on top of the old ones. I was also upcharged (I questioned it and it was a sudden "change in price"). I believe in fairness across the board, and me not being born on the continent shouldn't mean I should get lower quality food.
.....
(3 years ago)
Their fish & plantains is pretty good. I was introduced to the meal by a friend and I have gotten hooked. The only thing is the price changes if you get the same thing one week versus another. It's a bit pricey, but there's probably a good reason for it. Overall, the meal is good with caramelized onions and mayo with vegetables.

formatted_address: 4708 Baltimore Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19143, United States
name: Dahlak

reviews.text: Such a beautiful renovation to the restaurant! Great music and amazing customer service!!! Sadly the food itself was not anywhere close to Eritrean or Ethiopian food. Injera is made of Ted, corn and wheat but didn’t event taste close to injera. The dishes lacked flavor. Lastly the presentation of the food was lacking as seen here in the photo. I ordered Alecha, gomen, tum tum and shiro.

Every single person who breathes life into this restaurant infuse an abundance of love into every aspect. Every bite is packed with love, history, culture. You are made to feel that you're being welcomed into the family's home to enjoy a meal with your most precious friends and family members. I've NEVER experienced something so moving.
Food was bland,  especially the okra.  Service took a long time and made mistakes (we didn't get any of the appetizers).  We were accosted by a homeless person in the restaurant.

Loving the new look with the mesob tables. I was expecting the authentic Ethiopian dining experience where they bring out a big round plate for the mesob and we all eat off of it, but we were given a small square plate to serve one. Food was great though. And the date cake is delicious. Do try it.

I wish they could import Tej. I fell in love with honey wine at an Ethiopian restaurant in Queens and haven’t had any since.

I really want to love this but I just can’t. At least not yet.  The good: friendly staff, love the location, the bar next store kills the vibe with their loud music but that’s not their fault. Really nice atmosphere and decor. Could easily be my regular spot. Food is really good! No complaints there. Only bad thing is the portion size for the price. I got the mesob which is a meat and two vegan sides for $20. I got like 4 nibs of meat and a small amount of sides. Whole thing took me 5 mins to finish. It was more the size of an appetizer not an entree.  They servings were thin and spread out to make it look like a lot. Should easily be 2x to 2.5x what I got.  Bill came to $22. Left. A $4 tip. Total $26 for an appetizer sized meal and I’m still hungry.  The review is not intended to be a hate post but to offer constructive criticism.

Edit: they told me to come back and ask for someone. But if you read the other negative reviews you can see they have been doing this for years rather than addressing the problem

formatted_address: 7201 Woodland Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19142, United States
name: Emma’s Liberian Kitchen

reviews.text: Food was amazing!! This is where you go if you know you want to eat some good Liberian food. I had the potato greens, no notes.

I order fish, dirty rice and potatoe greens in red oil. The potatoe greens had mold in them. I called the store to talk to the owner to make them aware of the situation. A man answered the phone I told him what happened and he hung up in my ear.

I went to get the dry fish and rice like I always get and it's good. I went today 9-2-25 and my fish haven't been cleaned. It's a lot of scales on it. I love the way the fish skin taste but not with scales on it. More money less fish. They are losing their touch on the food. I will not be going back.

Today I ordered some cassava leaf and it tased burnt as if it was scraped from the bottom of the pot!! You would think since I brought the food early in the day, it would taste really good! Food was horribleeeeeee, I regret going here & wasting my money!!!

I would have given them five stars. If the pieces of meat they gave me was not full of bone. I literally got two big pieces of bone no meat. The potato greens were good. Just wish I had some meat. Not to mention the bone took up half the container.

formatted_address: 2425 Grays Ferry Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19146, United States
name: Prime Fusion Afro Grill & Lounge

reviews.text:
The menu is very misleading. The prices do not reflect the portion size. I might say that the price is highway robbery. $22 for a tiny portion of suya. Also the menu says puff puff medley meanwhile it’s one 3, that’s very misleading and for $15, outrageous.

The drinks were good, got a couple cocktails, the service was good likewise.

But for the I wouldn’t recommend. I’d say they better adjust their pricing or adjust their portion size or else people will catch on and stop coming

This a a response to your reply.
The puff puff was not 5 pieces it was 3 I wish I had a picture. I don’t know if your staff don’t know the portions but please go and fix your business because I can swear on everything I own that I was only given 3 puff puff and even if I got 5, that is still not a medley. Go and look in the dictionary for what a medley is before using it.  5 puff puff for $15 does that make sense to you.

Also I don’t know why you’re getting heated, no one is trying to bash your business if things are done right we will leave a good review. Instead of you to take these reviews as constructive criticism you’re there insulting me, well that’s your own problem I’m doing well in life. Can’t say the same about your restaurant.

I recently dined at this restaurant and left disappointed for several reasons.

Ambience: It did not meet my expectations. The atmosphere felt lacking for the price point.
Distractions: There was a generator or some contraption near the bar area that was distracting to see.
Food quality and value: The dishes felt low in quality and overpriced. Each component seemed to be charged separately.
Example: Ordered Oxtail Rasta Pasta. For  $22, I received two pieces of oxtail and $18 for a bowl of pasta.  It felt like an overcharge for a minimal portion.
First impression: I should have trusted my initial instinct and left when I noticed the restaurant was empty.
Service inconsistencies: The server did a great job describing two happy hour options, but then returned to say only egg rolls were available.
Operational quirks: A bell was used to alert that food was ready, which reminded me more of a diner than a fine dining experience.
Added charges and tipping: There was a gratuity plus a convenience fee, which contributed to the overall sense of overpricing.
Outcome: I left feeling disgusted by the whole experience, despite tipping an additional $20 to the server on top of the gratuity, just to acknowledge the effort. I would not return and consider it a waste of time and money.

I wanted this place to be a gem but I got a rock instead. Get there and they didn't have over half of the menu. No goat, no shrimp, no fish and no oxtail and that's just for starters. The server was really nice but she seemed to have had a misunderstanding with the kitchen because she came out 2x and told us that they didn't have the dishes we ordered only to come back 2x and say that they have them.  There was only 4 people in the restaurant and it still took our food over45 minutes to come out. When we got our food all we tasted was salt. I mean it over powered everything. My stewed chicken was literally a drumstick with some type of sauce on it. For the price that they charge the food should be a lot better. The honey garlic wings were the best thing to eat outta everything that we ordered. I don't think I'll come back to this location even tho I like the atmosphere.

I really hate to leave this kind of review, especially for a Black-owned business, because I truly understand the challenges of building something from the ground up. My partner and I came here for a date night a few days ago, and I’ve been sitting with the experience, hoping it would feel different—but it hasn’t.

He ordered the fish with fried rice, and I got the chicken with fried rice. Unfortunately, what we received was boiled boxed rice, not what we expected when we saw the photos online. When we asked if it was supposed to be fried rice, we were told yes, but it didn’t match what was advertised or what we imagined. The fish was good and he really enjoyed it, but my chicken was disappointing—three small pieces, mostly bone with very little meat.

To top it off, we were charged $14 for two cups of water that were offered to us. We didn’t even drink them, and typically water is complimentary at most restaurants.

That said, the space itself is beautiful and has great potential. I just feel honesty and transparency are so important in business. Integrity builds trust—and I truly wish them nothing but success and growth moving forward.

I went here with my best friend a few days ago. Walking in we were immediately greeted and asked for our preferred seating area. Our drinks were ordered and the waitress suggested some items which was a kind gesture. I ordered the braised short rib with jollof rice and my best friend ordered the Rasta pasta with jollof rice. My short rib was overcooked so much I needed a knife to cut through it and I still struggled to cut it. It was not fork tender and tasted like an unseasoned hamburger. The jollof rice was also very dry and hard and was not spicy at all.

I was also frustrated to see that the waiter who served us our food exited the kitchen smoking hookah and when I received my plate his finger was slightly wedged into my meat. I made no concern of it because I could just cut that piece of the meat off where the man’s hand was to touching and that’s what I chose to do

I feel as though the food was very overpriced for the quality of what was received. Upon leaving there was still meat left on my rib bone that could’ve been eaten but I was unable to cut it off due to how tough it was.

We also felt a little bombarded when the photographer there asked us if we wanted to take pics and even though we didn’t make a decision she made the decision for us. I felt like we were forced to buy the photos because we weren’t shown the photos before they were framed at all and weren’t really given a chance to say no.

The atmosphere was great with low lighting, tv, and service was pretty good as well. I will not deny that. I just would have preferred better quality food for the price we paid.

formatted_address: 2957 N 22nd St, Philadelphia, PA 19132, United States
name: Mama Shan's African and Soul Food Cuisine

html_attributions: Mama Shan's African and Soul Food Cuisine

reviews.text: Very good food I love all the food I got from there so far and the service is good too clean place and the foods taste really good I like it

Every time I come to Philly  I  stop by and grab myself  and egusi soup with turkey  meat only and fu-fu and they are kind enough  to make it especially  that way upon my request. Staff are always  kind and food is always  yummy

I’m extremely disappointed with my recent order. I paid for a full meal with multiple meats, and what I received was one small piece of tough, low-quality beef. Everything else I paid for was missing. Considering how expensive their food is, the portions should be accurate and consistent  this isn’t the first time I’ve felt shorted by them, and I’m honestly furious.

On top of that, the phone experience was completely unprofessional. When I called about my order, the man on the phone made inappropriate personal comments about “looking for a wife.” I was simply trying to get the food I paid for, not be made uncomfortable or harassed.

Overall, the portions, the repeated issues, and the unprofessional behavior have made this place a hard no for me going forward.

I’m very disappointed in his restaurant. I definitely will never be ordering from this establishment any longer. I don't recommend anyone to order from here. I ordered potato greens & fufu, while eating my food, I pull a piece of metal out of my mouth it poked the side of my tongue. My tongue hurt so bad. I’m very disappointed and disgusted you’re not handling food properly. This places is unsanitary, I have never written a review of any business or establishment. I’m  pissed off.

March 2023: I am still dreaming of the cassava from last time....but my goodness the jerk chicken is amazing!!! So flavorful, juicy, and tender.

January 2023: Ordered here for the first time from uber this evening and my goodness, it really hit the spot! They didn't have any meat pies today but left a nice note letting me know and included plenty of goodies to make up for it. I have a new go-to restaurant, and I highly recommend it to others 🤩.

formatted_address: 4070 Lancaster Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19104, United States
name: Nii-Adu African Bukateria

reviews.text: The food here was very good. The owner is super nice  and was adamant about warning me of the spice. I'm jamaican and it did not bother me at all. The inside could use an update, but the food is "bussin." I got the jollof rice and lamb.

It was my first time trying this cuisine so i don’t know how the food tastes. But the food was okay. The atmosphere in there was not great but the lady working there was genuinely nice. Also they only take cash.

If you’re looking for good Nigerian food, this place is not the right place to order. I wasted $200 ordering platters of jollof, fried rice, moin moin, pepper stew, and egusi. Only the egusi was ok. Everything else wasn’t good. The moin moin was some greyish color and didn’t taste like moin moin. Do not waste your money!
Ordered Fufu and Egusi soup for the first. The food was very tasty. The owner is very nice.
Highly recommended she take cash in cash app.

formatted_address: 547 Church Ln, Yeadon, PA 19050, United States
name: Aunty K's West African Restaurant

reviews.text:
During my recent visit to Aunty K's West African Restaurant, I had a great experience. The restaurant was clean and well-maintained, with a few tables and chairs for customers to dine in. The daily menu and prices were displayed on chalkboards behind the counter, making it easy to decide what to order.

The staff was very friendly and welcoming. Sidique came out from behind the counter to greet me, which made me feel welcomed.

Although my favorite cassava leaf soup was unavailable on this visit, Sidique assured me it would be back on the menu soon. As an alternative, I decided to try the Peanut Butter Soup.

The Peanut Butter Soup was delicious. Its savory taste balanced the slight sweetness of the peanut butter. The soup was rich and hearty, with stew chicken and beef. It was served with a generous portion of white rice. They also provided a small container of hot pepper sauce on the side, allowing me to customize the heat level.

Overall, Aunty K's West African Restaurant is a clean and friendly establishment with tasty food. I look forward to returning soon.

Aunty K’s fried rice and mackerel were really good! You can taste the pepper and it was a lot of food. To my pleasant surprise it came with fried sweet plantains and a very spicy pepper sauce (use with caution). The lady at the counter was polite and i waited and watched their tv as they prepared my food.
Picked up to go. Sooo good . First time trying acheke + for the price lasted me at least 2 meals

Had a good time eating at this African restaurant for the first time, Food was good and the ambiance was excellent. Customer service by the owner was great. We had dry rice and beef. I will recommend anyone who wants to try a taste.
I tried this place after seeing reviews on google and i was impressed by the quality of food I got.  Really really delicious, not the your average prices but the quantity makes it ok.  Am hooked..

formatted_address: 6521 Woodland Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19142, United States
name: Susanna African Kitchen

reviews.text: Peanut butter soup and fufu was phenomenal. I have to get her to make me a whole personal pan. Loved it. Exquisite. Me and my roomie ate it together and she wanted more as did I.

I ordered
Potato greens
Cassava leaf
And now egusi . I love their food, it has so much flavor, smoked , peanut butter, and if you like hot it’s very spicy .
I love this place they are nice people and great food. I've been going here for years ! Everything's fresh! And tasty!

I was craving for fufu and searched on google map for an hour for authentic ones and finally chose this restaurant— I ordered from Uber eat, keep in mind that you will need to order at least 1-2 hours ahead during prime time because they may get extremely busy.

But their fufu is soooo goooddd 😭 this is my second time eating fufu and I notice Susanna’s fufu is so much smoother and homogenized than the first fufu I had at another place. I love both texture and taste tho.

The cassava leaf taste very authentic! I personally like the cassava leaf than the pepper soup that comes with fufu better but it’s all personal preference. Next time I will order extra fufu!!

Wonderful food Beautiful people!
I wish Susana's Kitchen would please get some cow foot for me please ❤️

formatted_address: 107 Fairfield Ave, Upper Darby Township, PA 19082, United States
name: Kings and Queens Liberian Cuisine

reviews.text:
From the online reviews I was looking forward to coming here. I’ve been to Musu spot, JD, Emma’s Liberian restaurant and others in the past.
This was the first time I had a dine in experience without a dine in experience.
We walked in and were told we had to order and pay before being seated. Did just that and got the food pretty fast. However eating my fufu and soup
With a flimsy tiny plastic spoon was unsatisfying. When we asked for an actual spoon they didn’t have. We got served in a Togo set up.

The potato greens was ok. The casavaleaf was a no, flavor wise and the pepper soup was close to salty. A little over seasoned. When we got our food we didn’t see no one again till we walked out in silence. As someone who has managed a corporate restaurant for years and still is. Dine in service also helps the business, interaction, asking if it’s your first time here? Gaining those new customers. Most time people go back for the service as well. No one was interested in asking how was everything? did you guys need anything? I  will not be returning. My suggestion will be Togo only and if dine In, then please give great service.

Dining in a restaurant and not being checked on once is rare. Good was not great. Worst $68 spent.

So, visiting my family and my sister knows I love trying food from the continent, so this restaurant was up.
We went, and ordered jollof rice w/snapper. The food is cooked to order. It was served FRESHH!!!👅That food was 10/10!! The rice was so seasoned! The snapper, seasoned and fried to perfection!!❣️ That hot pepper sauce that came on the side is radiant, flavorful and just the right tempo. I should have gotten an extra to go. The plantain, fried to perfection! The 🎶 had me moving my waistline💃🏾. Being as though this was my 1st try and the food was A1, I'll try one of the soups next time. Next time I'm in town, will patronize again.

Kings and Queens Liberian Cuisine has very good food and has very professional staff members that are knowledgeable about the menu if any customers have any questions. The staff are reasonable if you want to take out a certain ingredient in the food item you are paying for. Keep up the good work 👍
Stop what you’re doing and go here now! They have amazing food and a staff that makes you feel like family. Anything on the menu won’t disappoint! They even have vegan options!

Highly Disappointing!! I’ve eaten here once before with no problem but last night was just TERRIBLE!!!
1. My potato greens weren’t potato greens, they were collard greens finely chopped, oily and  unseasoned (they could’ve at least told me they didn’t have what I wanted instead of giving me anything.
2. My egusi tasted and smelled like they made it with smoked sardines, just complete fish juice, too overpowering to eat
3. My fufu was so sticky, like slime, I couldn’t properly pick it up because it stuck to my fingers, I tried to roll it in my hand and it stuck to everything like putty. And after putting it in the fridge, it has white slimy spots on it
Overall, Never Again!

formatted_address: 942 MacDade Blvd, Collingdale, PA 19023, United States
name: Wazobia Nigerian Restaurant

reviews.text: For the last three months I’ve been ordering the Egusi with fufu and smoked turkey about once a week. I find it to be absolutely delicious, though I haven’t had this meal anywhere else. Wazobia is local for me, they always have my order ready in no time and everyone I’ve encountered there is always polite. The smoked turkey has so much flavor and the portions are huge ( I usually eat for lunch and dinner). Pro tip: mix the Egusi well to maximize the flavor profile. Love this meal here and I would say don’t let negative reviews on the Egusi deter you, try it for yourself before drawing a conclusion.

I was passing by this place on my not usual way home from work when I decided to stop and try Nigerian food for the first time. And I’m glad I did!

First the food. Delicious!  I have a feeling most people come in already knowing what they want or at least speak Yoruba. The menu does not have any descriptions, but there are a few pictures on the wall to help.  Since this was my first time having Nigerian food, I asked them to choose for me, only telling them “no fish or rice” and that “I like meat and vegetables”.  Was rewarded with a healthy portion of efo riru (Nigerian spinach stew) with added meat (cubes of stewed beef) and a softball sized portion of hot fufu. Cost $17 and I was stuffed.

Although they gave me utensils, I ate it traditionally with my hands scooping the stew together with the fufu. The stew was really good! Very flavorful and not overly spicy. There was plenty of vegetables and was cooked just right. If I had to offer a suggestion - the added meat could have been smaller and in more even pieces. But it’s very small complaint.

Service: was good! My
Meal was ready quickly and was packed up securely with napkins and utensils.

Atmosphere : There are three or so booths to eat at, with lots of napkins and salt shakers, but it’s really a take it to go place - a “hole in the wall” neighborhood place where your money is going to the food, not the decor. I ate in because I live more than 40 minutes away and was starving.

There is a handwashing station so you can wash your hands before and after eating. Also got to watch some news on the large screen tv.

Value : $17 dollars and I was happily stuffed. I could have made into two meals but was very hungry.  I ordered a Second portion to take home. 100% Would go back!
Omg worse food ever eugsi was horrible out one spoon in my mouth and wanted to throw up..$17 down the drain and it stinks, get at your own risk

Customer service is completely awful. I asked the lady at the front about a dish and she yelled at me saying, if you don’t know it don’t try it. If this restaurant wants to survive, please remove her from the front, she has horrible customer service.  She also said “what type of questions is that” I’m confused, if you’re running a food business aren’t you supposed to have capacity to answer questions about your menu? To make matters worse, it was only 1 other person in the restaurant so it’s not like she didn’t have time. I left without even ordering because I don’t trust people like that making food I can’t see them making. People make sure you know exactly what you want
Food portions are huge! I was quite surprised. The jollof rice and chicken was okay. It could have been a little more flavorful. The soup was freaking delicious! Must get with fish.

formatted_address: 7200 Elmwood Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19142, United States
name: We Yone African Restaurant

reviews.text: I had their beef kabobs,and  chicken they were very good
Overpriced basic food. Service too slow.
Good food , love the snapper fish
Yvonis jollof and suya is delicious. i love her refreshers as well. The owner is a very nice along with her employees.

The owner is such a beautiful blessing of a woman♥️
I love african cuisine!!! If i dont feel like driving i order from uber eats and i love this place..tonight ubereats mixed up the orders and ihad the wrong food..iwould have ate it but my son doesnt favor fu fu..the owner was very very nice when icalled and since she isnt far from me i decided to go in like she offered bcuz to get the order replaced through uber would have never happened..when iwent in she was so nice to me and my son..she even sent me home with an extra meal..such a beautiful blessing of a Queen♥️

formatted_address: 140 S 20th St, Philadelphia, PA 19103, United States
name: Almaz Cafe

reviews.text: Came on a Saturday night for dinner, it was pretty busy but luckily there was no wait. The restaurant is overall very cozy and ambient which I appreciate greatly. The vibes are immaculate and the service is very warm and friendly. The food is amazing! We ordered the lamb and beef tips as a shared meal option that comes with some veggies and dips. It was my first time trying enjera (described as a pancake bread that tastes like sourdough) and I thought it was so interesting and tasty. The prices are quite reasonable for the area and overall quality. If I find myself craving Ethiopian food this will be my first choice.

Very Amazing mom and pop shop with a lowkey interior. The food was absolutely amazing!! We got the vegetarian platter and the beef curry and it was the best ethiopian food I have ever had!!!! Really great and not too heavy.
Ordered the veggie combo and it was an amazing burst of flavor in every bite! Food came out fast, environment is cozy and staff is very friendly. Definitely will be coming back!

Great little place to get really good Ethiopian food in the city.  We had the restaurant to ourselves and enjoyed everything we ordered.  Only complaint is they put one of the chicken dishes on the player with the vegetarian sampler and my wife is vegetarian.

Truly delicious!
Veggie combo is healthy and filling. One order was enough for two hungry people, but we got a second just for the left overs!

formatted_address: 7186 Marshall Rd, Upper Darby Township, PA 19082, United States
name: Le Mandingue African Restaurant Upper Darby

reviews.text: I absolutely love coming to this restaurant. The African food here is amazing, full of flavor, fresh, and cooked to perfection. I live in New Jersey, and I honestly don’t mind driving 45 minutes just to eat here because it’s that good. The quality and taste are worth every minute of the drive. If you’re looking for authentic, delicious African food, this place is a must-visit. Highly recommended!

The platters arrived hot, which I appreciated, and the two bags of Kallah looked okay. Unfortunately, my egusi was overly salty and mostly fat with barely any neck bones. The fufu was just okay.

I really wish I had ordered from our usual location on Woodland Avenue instead. After spending $45, this felt like a waste of money. I won’t be ordering from this location on DoorDash again.

This is by far the worse African cuisine restaurant near Philly. I experienced multiple occasions of missing or burnt food in my orders. The staff is unapologetic about longer wait times and running out of food to meet your order requirements. I experienced the rudest woman at the front desk on 12/20 that completely stopped me from purchasing here ever again. She completely ignored me as I asked her when my order would be ready and had a nasty attitude of entitlement when answering phones and taking other people’s orders. I waited two hours for one order and exemplified a ton of patience. Not to mention seeing rats playing by the back door of their establishment. The quality has been downgraded and they’ve become money greedy taking on too many orders via phone, in-person, and other food online ordering apps. Bring back quality and respect to your customers and stop the greed. I would never recommend this place to anyone even for their last meal. I’ve never left review on restaurant until today.

This place has completely fallen off, I ordered food from here several times in the past but my last two experiences have been horrible. Today 12/7/24 I ordered palava Sauce and my dish was very dry with no taste, no flavor and so sauce. They typically put different types of meat in sauce but today was only chicken. My rice was extremely overcooked and very mushy. It was so bad that I couldn’t bring myself to eat any of it. I will never come here again.

I drove over an hour due to hearing good things only to be given the wrong platter. I ordered lamb and was given tilapia. When I called to see if they would have take a remake another day the staff member female was rude told me to bring back the food when explained I lived over an hour away she hung up the phone. I had to call more than 7 times before a “manager” got on the phone. This is poor poor customer service. If that was not bad enough when picking up my food I used the bathroom and there was not soap in the bathroom. I should have known then to cancel the order and run far far away. I mean how are the employees being sanitary after using the bathroom . Absolutely unacceptable!

formatted_address: 90 S 44th St, Philadelphia, PA 19104, United States
name: Sheba's Soul Plate restaurant

reviews.text: Got the jerk chicken, fish curry, plaintains, Mac and cheese, and the peach cobbler. Let me tell you right now it was amazing. 10/10. Everything. Huge portions, perfect spice level, everything balanced. Only thing I can say is I wish that you could eat inside, but it’s not the worst thing ever. I really recommend this place and the Mac n cheese is bombbbb

This was one of the best places I ever ate for my taste buds crazy.It was so good!! I could not wait to get back there to buy more for my family.I wanted all my friends and family to taste your food, i've been by there two times and you've been closed. I'm trying to find out where in the world did y'all go. Are you gonna come back? I've been calling it goes the voicemail. I really need some of your food.
Hidden gem! What a great spot. I got the Jerk chicken platter and Mac' n cheese. This is home cooking done right. I can’t wait to come back.

First let me say I never like to write a bad review and I had previously wrote a review months ago complimenting this restaurant because they really do have good food. I have to say though in my opinion it’s very unprofessional how they operate. On Google the hours say 1230 to 8. You come on here and the business says open, you go there and they are closed. Not everyone has social media where they can see when you are not open (which is quite often!) that means people travel from all over to support your establishment and give you business just for you not to be open when google says you are.  Please care about your customers, their time and gas, and keep your times updated on here, so we’re not wasting our time and money in gas passing places that do care and appreciate our business.
Really amazing curry tofu, with sweet yams and collared greens! Excellent food! Interior was a little smoky and the food took a while, but well worth it.

formatted_address: 304 S 52nd St, Philadelphia, PA 19143, United States
name: Anna's Restaurant

reviews.text: I read the reviews prior to ordering from this place and yah told a lot of lies on here. It was am awful experience and less than one star was due this 'restaurant' if you could call it that. The casava leaf was spoiled, as if it sat out all day and half the night. The lamb was burnt beyond recognition, the jollof rice was green and the atteke was missing. You people should be ashamed of yourself to sell people this garbage. This food literally made me puke...and I would not exaggerate about something as serious as this. When I say never again...I mean never EVER again!!!  I had to take  pictures of this mess. Just purchased to 5/21/25 around 6pm. The outside picture I took after I threw the cassava leaf out prior to opening the burnt lamb. SHAME ON YOU!
I love, love, love this place!!  It has the best lamb chops, grilled chicken and fried rice topped with a sauteed brown onion gravy sauce.. Reminds me of my trip to West Africa 😃

If I could give 0 I would idk who this new woman Is but she is NOT capable made me feel like cause I'm american I get served last. I just left empty handed an I'm posting on social media how bad service is.

The food is very good. I've had different dishes different times of the year.  They serve many African dishes, a few American dishes, they're all very good. You may have to use cash if no one's available to accept your debit card.   It's easy accessible by car and by public transportation.

The service was nice the lady who served me was very friendly. But I’m sad to say the food was absolutely horrible . I ordered cassava leaf an fufu an my fufu looked like soup when I got home. I don’t no if it wasn’t made right or not but i do no it was not supposed to be that thin a loose.  The cassava leaf was ok but not great. It was kinda sweet so it didn’t taste rightist would give service 4 stars but food definitely a solid 1. You just can’t eat African food from every African restaurant. Lesson learned .

formatted_address: 6326 Sackett St, Philadelphia, PA 19149, United States
name: Food Geez Restaurant and Lounge

reviews.text:
I ordered the okra stew hoping for a warm, comforting dish. What I received instead was a bowl of bitter betrayal.
The stew arrived looking like it had lost a fight with a blender and some expired vegetables. The broth was bland, somehow both watery and greasy, and had the unfortunate aftertaste of regret and overcooked onions.
The seasoning, if it existed, was gone! I kept waiting for something — anything — to redeem the dish. A spark of flavor, a hint of spice, a glimmer of effort. Nothing came.
By the third bite, I gave up. Not even hunger could justify continuing.
If you're considering the okra stew: don't. Save yourself. Eat literally anything else. Lick a rock. Chew a napkin. Just... not this.

Absolutely love their food!! I originally saw this young man on Fox 29 during African Food week. We were in the area and took my picky eater grandsons here and met this man who was very patient with our ordering. We got the Egusi soup, potato collard with chicken soup, Jollof rice with plantain, and fried chicken and Jollof rice. None of us had Liberian food before. We loved it…all. We have enough for leftovers. Shared it with the family at home and they loved it too. Highly recommend. Also while we ate there, many take door dash type orders were coming in and going out. I only gave four stars for Service because there were some dishes that were not available.

We reheated the fufu by putting tbsp of water in it and heating in microwave at 15 sec then stirring then another 15 sec and so on until desired temp and consistency. No problem, still tasty with leftovers.

My nephew was craving fufu and egusi soup and after a quick search on Google maps and a call to the restaurant (no menu was available in maps), we made our way to Food Geez. Street parking is available, and there are residential streets nearby.

The restaurant clearly used to be a bar in the 90s, but has been updated with booth and bar seating.

The young man taking our order was new, so it took a little long to confirm our order and pay, but as a former foodservice employee, I know that he just needs more practice. We originally ordered our food to go, but decided to eat in.

Food took a minute to come out, but when it did it was piping hot and so delicious. They let you choose your spice adventure, as each plate has a container of pepper sauce on it. Food was delicious and leftovers were demolished the next day. Will definitely be back for a to go order.

Stopped in here the other day on our way back to DC and was pleasantly surprised! The food was good overall. I had cassava, and the customer service was excellent. The staff was friendly and attentive, making the experience even better. Would definitely stop by again!

I've been to this restaurant maybe 5 times within the last year. Twice I sat inside. And the others were take out. This place is hit or miss. When it's good it's great but when it's bad it's awful. The customer service isn't the best either. But I tried to support a black small business regardless. They are very unwelcoming when you go. A few times they got my order wrong and gave me a hard time about it. I ask for Spicy food. They give mild. I ask for pepper sauce and willing to pay for it. They charge you $1 for the tiniest sample of pepper sauce. I'm disappointed because I've had a couple great meals from here. But I'll never go back again. It's not consistent enough

formatted_address: 5121 Baltimore Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19143, United States
name: Buna Cafe Philly

reviews.text: This restaurant was really nice and the food was really good! First time having Ethiopian food and it was delicious! The host was so polite and helped me make a great food decision. I'll definitely be back to try a different dish.

This place is a gem in West Philadelphia. Sedakio, the owner has such an amazing and warm personality! The veggie platter is phenomenal - great flavor and taste. Highly recommend the Ethiopian coffee as well. One of the best, if not the best, Ethiopian spots in the city!
immaculate vibes and delicious food! everything i’ve tried is great and the people working there are really nice. cozy cafe. i hope they come back soon!!

What a fantastic place to have in the neighborhood. My wife and I come here maybe a lil too often, and it's the first place we take out of town guests. Best injera on Baltimore Ave, hands down! And some of the biggest portions. Warm service and the food is always excellent. Extensive desserts and café drinks. Board games and party games available. You can't go wrong. If you're having a bad day, Buna will turn it around 😊

Ordered one time now im hooked. The food is amazing and flavorful. I keep coming back not only because of the food but the owner is very kind and personable. Not too pricey great portion size , Vegan options.

Take away is packed with care every time.

formatted_address: S 61st St &, Grays Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19142, United States
name: Le Faso

reviews.text: The food was delicious, with generous portions. The staff was friendly, and the food was ready before the given time. First time here, indeed not my last time.

It's best to call in first and pick up your order. This place gets packed but you'll never know because most orders are done by phone.
Portions are hefty. It's family run and owned. The customer service is excellent, they make all their customers feel like family. ♥️
All the dishes are excellent.
I drive from Delaware to get this place so great and lovely food

Tomato Soup with rice was splendid!
The okra soup was NOT as good it tasted specifically of fish, which I have an allergy to. Please let customers know when a dish contains seafood

Cool people. ✌🏾
Tasty plantains, delicious chicken. 🤤🤤

formatted_address: 721 Long Ln, Upper Darby Township, PA 19082, United States
name: The Motherland Cuisine

reviews.text: i've been to this restarunt 3 times prior to yesterday which was tuesday 1/6/26 and i was soo upset at the lack of service!!! the food is amazing tho!!! like really good! everything i get from here is always good but if the guy Devon which i think is the owner, if he is not there i will never patronize this place again!!!! i had my daughter  from Houston who is Costa Rican come visit and she never had african food so i told her about this place! me her my wife and my father goes and we seat ourselves the lady was just soo rude and un attentive, didnt ask us did we want anything to drink, didnt come to our table to greet us, didnt cut the tv on or anything, we sat there for 13 mins until she came to the counter not our table but to the counter and asked us were we ready to order. we said no, she left and never came back. we got up and told her we were leaving due to your lack of service. we end up going to Kilimanjaro African restarunt.

This is not a review of a dining experience as I have never been to the Motherland and never will after the experience I had with a fraud dispute involving this restaurant.

I had a very troubling experience with The Motherland African Cuisine restaurant related to a fraudulent credit card charge. My card details were stolen and the criminal (who the restaurant CEO refuses to disclose her name or appearance) placed an order on Thanksgiving day 2025 for pickup. The transaction was processed as a manually keyed, card-not-present entry. Rather than addressing this professionally, the business claimed I was lying and falsely stated that I personally picked up the order in Pennsylvania.

I do not live in Pennsylvania and was not in the state on the date of the charge. I even provided security camera footage to my credit card company showing I was at home that day. Instead of reviewing the facts, the business chose to accuse the fraud victim of dishonesty. The Motherland CEO chose to state: she “picked her order up and her her [Sic] was correct. This is a false claim and there is no truth in this claim. Yours sincerely, Motherland CEO.” This raises serious concerns about their ethics and how they handle disputes. I strongly recommend caution and not visiting this restaurant.

My first time eating here . Love the decor very small restaurant only one person to server and cook. The soup with fufu was flavorful , and spicy like I love. Big portions for the price. That was the plus of the restaurant The problem was that they were out of quite a few things I wanted to order with my meal. And I told my family to come purchase some food from here. They told me they order the chicken dinner and didn't get the other items that were supposed to be included with the chicken dinner. But they were still charging the same price instead of at a discount price because it wasn't a full meal as advertised. Now they are upset with me for suggesting this restaurant that cheated them. I'm appalled at why they did that?
The food and the service was amazing! I cannot wait to go back. You must check it out.

First off by saying Dish I choose (Esgusi)  was amazing first time ordering something other than Peanut butter stew ! Art and music was a whole vibe . The man (sorry forgot his name ) that greeted us and than made our delicious dishes was super polite and also very informative on any question I did throw at him about the dishes . Definitely will be returning 🫶🏽!

formatted_address: 517 S Leithgow St, Philadelphia, PA 19147, United States
name: Marrakesh

reviews.text:
Marrakesh is an authentic family style Moroccan experience!  The food is delicious and the atmosphere is intimate.

We've eaten here with multiple groups of friends and family and everyone has enjoyed the food and ambiance.

Your experience starts when you sit down, you wash your hand with warm rose water and are given a towel to serve as your napkin.  The tables are intimate family style, you'll be sharing plates!  The menu is 7 courses with some variablity, portions sized to your party.
1.  Salad (cooked carrots, cooked eggplant, cucumber salad)
2.  Pastilla (savory meat pie with chicken, egg, and almond filling), topped with sugar and cinnamon
3.  Slow roasted chicken (you can choose between spicy or mild, I highly recommend the spicy chicken it's more flavourful and not too spicy)
4.  Slow roasted lamb (in a slightly sweet marinade) or beef kabobs (you can order a split of both)
5.  Couscous with potatoes and carrots topped with shredded chicken and raisins
6/7.  Tea and dessert (fresh fruit and baklava)

They are able to accommodate some allergies and provide an alternate option (e.g., egg allergy)

Marrakesh is quite a unique experience - a must try at least one time!

My friends and I came to celebrate a birthday. It was tight quarters, so we were sitting back to back with the group next to us. Expect to be a little cramped, it’s just part of the experience.

They rinse your hands with warm water and then throw towels on your lap. Then immediately start the 7-course dinner ($40pp). I won’t go into every detail, but the standouts were the spicy chicken (truly the best chicken I’ve ever had), beef skewers and the egg dish. The lamb we were not a fan of and couscous dish was bland. The baklava my friends enjoyed, I found it a bit too sweet personally.

There was a belly dancing performance which was great entertainment. The staff were all SO friendly and welcoming. We truly felt like we were transported into Morocco.

I’m not sure if I would come back, only because while I did really enjoy some dishes, others fell a little flat for me. And I believe you can only ever do the whole tasting menu, not a la carte. I’m still glad I got to experience it!

This was my second time here and I can’t wait to come back again! This family run place has been around for over 30years serving not just amazing food, but atmosphere as well. They have three stories of seating, although I would recommend getting a reservation because they are always busy. It is a set meal, 7 course experience with food reflecting what I had when I traveled to Morocco! Best to bring a group of at least 4 to enjoy the family style eating. It is also byob and they encourage good vibes and dancing! Cannot recommend this place enough!

Every Moroccan restaurant blows me away.  I wish there were more.  I don’t know if it is the rose water they wash your hands with, the soft cushions or the belly dancer…. But they always leave me wanting to return.  Make sure you go VERY hungry as it is a lot of food.

Our party of four had an unforgettable experience at Marrakesh! From the moment we arrived, the evening felt special, you actually knock on the door to be welcomed inside, which immediately sets the tone for something unique. The décor is stunning, with an authentic and stylish design that transports you straight to Morocco.

The meal itself was a journey. They serve a series of dishes from appetizers all the way to dessert, and you can choose between lamb, beef, or vegetarian options; everything was flavorful and beautifully presented. The atmosphere is made even more vibrant with Arabic music playing in the background, and we were lucky to enjoy a talented belly dancer who brought so much energy and fun to the room.

To top it all off, the owner personally came around to greet every table with warm Middle Eastern hospitality. That thoughtful gesture was the cherry on top of an already amazing night. Highly recommend Marrakesh for anyone looking for a truly unique dining experience in Philly!

formatted_address: 7200 Elmwood Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19142, United States
name: Cymel African Restaurant LLC

reviews.text: I got chuck rice and gravy, two meat on the stick and shrimp on the stick. All of the food was too salty, and the gravy was covered to the top with oil. The cashier (Hawa Diahn) energy was nasty, and unfriendly. Today was my first time going to this restaurant and will be my last.The high rating on here seems false to me after my experience today. I would not recommend this place, the food isn't worth the trouble.

I love it here! Someone told me about Emma’s which is close by, I went and they were so rude, the place stunk and everything so I took my business elsewhere where, good this place which was near by AND IVE BEEN EATING HERE EVERY SINCE!!! FROM THE TIME I CAME IN THEY WERE SO WELCOMING, PATIENT, ANSWERED QUESTIONS FOR ME AND MY FAMILY, GAVE RECOMMENDATIONS, AND TOLD ME CALL AHEAD OF TIME IF I HAD ANY SPECIAL REQUEST!!!! PLEASE GO NOW!! THE DRY RICE AND SNAPPER IS MY FAVORITE!! THE FUFU & SOUP IS MY FAVORITE!!!!!
Best dry rice and fish in the city. The grill food is amazing. The family is always courteous and nice to everyone.
She is the Best in SouthWest! Top Tier African Cuisine😋
You’re phone number is not going through
