reviews.text: This place is horrible. Just got the. Egusie soup and fofo and it’s not that just a bunch of dried up greens and red tomato sauce on top do not go here or eat from here they giving people anything disgusting. I will not be eating this.
Small sit down place serving authentic west African food. Enjoyed the food, good portions. Had the curry chicken. Very tasty
Delicious food, great prices and nice size portions.
Food was excellent huge portions and the lady at the counter was very nice will travel again to patronize them
My new favorite restaurant! Prices are on the high side but food is good.

formatted_address: 6517 Elmwood Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19142, United States
name: BI-RESTAURANT

reviews.text: I wouldn't waste your money dinner was awful would not feed it to my dog the waitrr didn't care abouty complaint just kept wanting to sell one of their food programs.  Spent 51.00 dollars meat was so full of fat couldn't even swallow it.  Asparagus so tough, I couldn't cut

Even after they changed locations (right next door) Food prices are reasonable considering the size of their dishes. I love their lamb and rice platters, for $22 depending on who you are you'll have enough food to feed yourself and others if you want. Great place for something to eat that's not your everyday fast food..
Food is basic... definitely overpriced tho! The environment is not the best, the restaurant needs some DEEP CLEANING! Specially the kitchen area.
I had the Acheke here and loved it. The rice and lamb were terrific, and the service was excellent. The staff is friendly and helpful.
I just had the best food experience ever!!! The food especially the rice is so good! The presentation is amazing and on point! This is my new spot! Every time I’m in Philly I’m always coming!

formatted_address: 908 E Baltimore Ave, East Lansdowne, PA 19050, United States
name: Mawa's African Cuisine (Authentic African & American Cuisine)

reviews.text: Authentic, delicious, plentiful, and memorable. This is an outstanding African restaurant with great flavor, value, and distinction. For those in Philly, it's worth the drive! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

A little annoyed bc I literally searched and searched for a new African place to try and thought this would be great but it wasn’t. Granted, I ordered through DoorDash but still, the quality of the food shouldn’t differ. I ordered potato greens and fufu bc I’ve never tried potato greens before and got a container that said OKRA and very mushy, clumpy, watery fufu that was like mashed potatoes and impossible to eat my soup with… Ive never had fufu like before so I’m very disappointed and don’t think I’ll be ordering from this place again.
The food is by far excellent. If you’re ever in the Delco area and hungry, Mawa’s is a must visit!!! The service and atmosphere is absolutely friendly.

🔥 MUST-TRY🔥I just had another incredible meal from Jammie’s Creative Food and I had to leave a review this time! This family-owned local gem serves food that truly tastes like home.

I ordered lamb, plantains, and vegetable rice, and just WOW! The lamb was tender and flavorful, the plantains were perfectly caramelized, and the rice was light, fluffy, and packed with veggies.

You can tell every bite is made with love, passion, and authenticity. Whether you order online or visit in person, you won’t be disappointed. Support this amazing spot—10/10 recommend!

Very good. Fufu was fresh and soft. Didn’t pair well with the potato greens but I just wanted to try something new. The potato greens were very good. I enjoyed this meal for 3days straight. Very full filling and delicious food. I will be back to try there other dishes

formatted_address: 229 S 45th St, Philadelphia, PA 19104, United States
name: Abyssinia

reviews.text: Probably the best Ethiopian joint in the city. Don't sleep on it. My favorite two dishes; the Abyssiania platter and the breakfast special, with scrambled eggs, beef and ful.

This is my go to Ethiopian restaurant and I would give it a five. I usually get The Meat Combo, but I tried Abyssinia s number 1 with the Kitfo. First time having Kitfo not my thing and it was oily. The greens were not that great today also and the Derek Tibs were not the best.

Went here for a late night dinner since my friend had never had Ethiopian food before and wanted to try it. This is a neighborhood restaurant with 2 bars and a dining room. Both bars were busy. The downstairs bar was updated, but the dining room was pretty nondescript and empty.

I confirmed the kitchen was still open and we sat in the dining room. The server for the dining room was helping out in the downstairs bar so it took a while for him to take our order. My friend had to go to the bar and order some drinks in order to get his attention. When he came in to deliver our drinks and take our order he only brought my friend’s drink (spicy margarita). My drink (mango tequila sunrise) took a while to come out so he comped it.

We waited for quite some time before he came in again to check on us. He told us he went to check on our food and the kitchen was in the process of closing and hadn’t made our food. I was waiting for him to say just kidding the food is coming out, but he never did. He had to go work it out with the kitchen.

Our food finally came out and it was tasty. I ordered the veggie combo and he had the Abyssinia 1 and meat combo together. My friend really enjoyed the beef tartare. He got it cooked medium. I enjoyed the veggie combo.

I suggest going to the bar and ordering food there if you go late night. That’s what I’d do if I go back.

I got Meat Combo and the Kurt Tibs and the meat was so tender and seasoned well (the veggies were seasoned well too). It was the first time me and my friends tried Ethiopian food and we can't wait to have it again! I just wish the Baklava was bigger for the price it is. We spent a total of ~$80 for 2 meat combos one order of Kurt Tibs and 2 orders of the baklava. There was definitely more than enough to share with 4 people.
Amazing food experience for a vegetarian - simple yet delicious food! Drinks were great too!

formatted_address: 4540 Baltimore Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19143, United States
name: Gojjo

reviews.text: First time. Popped in here one late afternoon. Three other folks were sitting at the bar with me. Super chill environment. The service was accommodating because I asked to change the TV channel and they were very obliging. Agreeable.

I can’t tell you how good the food was. I was fastening at the time I went to this retirement event. What I can say is that the atmosphere was great and the service was awesome. They didn’t bother us, they didn’t have an attitude or anything like that. We were deep up there on the second floor too. They also have a pool table which I think is great as well as two bars available if needed. Great place to throw an event.

Came here cause we heard they have a Kenyan chef. Servers had a flat effect and didn't make any effort, the dude behind the bar seemed like he didn't even want to be there. Injera bread was cold, could've at least put it in the microwave for 10 seconds. Ugali was too soggy, greens had no tomatoes and tasted like they were the frozen ones and just microwaved.  Beef fry was tasteless. I did like the beef that came with the injera and the samosas were the best item.

This place was a huge disappointment. There’s no staff, just one guy running the bar, taking orders, and serving everyone.
Service was incredibly slow, portions were small, and the food didn’t taste fresh. Then I found a hair in my food, and when I told him, he laughed and pretended to pull hair from his shirt to drop into my plate. I was completely disgusted.
No apology, no accountability, just a joke. Completely unhygienic and disrespectful. Never going back.
This is the bad bar of west. I did not know city wides were $15 here in WEST. Abyssinia is cheaper and right around the corner and has better food. Also Dahlak, which has a Michelin ranking.

formatted_address: 4421 Chestnut St, Philadelphia, PA 19104, United States
name: Kaffa Crossing

reviews.text: Ethiopian cuisine is easily among the top ten in the world when it comes to variety and flavor, and if marketed like other international cuisines, it could have a huge impact on the culinary scene. Unfortunately, this place doesn’t do it justice. The food lacks authenticity, with weak seasoning and poor cooking techniques. Most dishes don’t come close to the rich, flavorful, and finger-licking goodness of real Ethiopian food. The magic of Ethiopian cuisine lies in its seasoning and slow cooking, both of which are missing here.

Nice resturant. Its very low key which I like. The food was good and well priced. Ordered a vegetarian platter with kaffa tibs. Everything was delicious. Huge portion. Could definitely feed 2-3 people. There was 2 of us and we still had leftovers to take home

Excellent experience! Located in a less than desirable part of town but the food did not let us down at all! Everything was high quality and tasty. While some food may seem bland at times, you can simply salt to taste. Many spicy options are available. Great smoothies also! Menu is online, just scan QR code.

My first time trying Ethiopian food and I’m glad I tried here! The lady behind the counter was super nice and recommended the best smoothie (fantasy island) I have had in a long while. Everything we got came quick, fresh, and delicious. In addition, this place is very vegan/vegetarian friendly, and also have great meat options. If you had a group of friends with all different tastes and preferences, this is a great place for you all.

Absolutely wonderful experience!!

My lady and I decided to embark on an adventure and trying some different cultural foods and we came across the spot, and we were not let down at ALL!!! Kudos to the staff of this restaurant!!!There are very hospitable and patient with us.

formatted_address: 6600 Elmwood Ave 1 fL, Philadelphia, PA 19142, United States
name: Five Sisters Kitchen Inc

reviews.text: 5 Sisters Kitchen simply just might be the most underrated African spot. My boyfriend one night was doing work in the area and was told by folks nearby to try their food. He said he had been smelling the cooking all day. For dinner we decided to try them and we were not disappointed. First off let’s start with the most important when it comes to spending your money. CUSTOMER SERVICE was exceptional. We walked in literally 20 mins before closing and you wouldn’t have been able to know. They greeted us kindly with pure smiles walking in and even offered for us to dine in  but we went to go respectfully. From there we ordered our food discussed the menu with free will to determine what we wanted today. I’m Nigerian  and my partner is Caribbean so we were ready! Food came out fast and then we asked about an a la Carte item. They told us about it and even let us try it and boyyyyy SO GOOD. I’m gonna have to gate keep that one tho! Now onto the food! We have eaten from many African spots around the city. Our concerns across the board usually is too much oil , not enough food/stew to actually eat and poor meat selection. 5 Sisters met all that criteria to a T. The packaging and quantity is completely worth the price! The meat is tender, and it’s EDIBLE!! No surprises and no guessing. Oil isn’t spilling all over the place because they use good containers for to go orders. The food we ate was fresh. We’ve purchased food before from different place and could tell it was from either day before or stored from previous.  As a hybrid African girl. When I eat my food I want good meat thats simple to eat. 5 sisters did that! Between the experience, the quality and price I will definitely be back. Thank you so much 5Sisters for being a great African restaurant that leads by great example. We ordered PALAVA sauce btw (:
The food is AMAZING & the owners are so kind! We had the fufu and pepper soup and fried fish with plantains and it was incredible. Can’t wait to go back!!! 10/10

I won’t lie the food was very good but the only thing I’m concerned about is the cleanliness. Because one of the elderly ladies that cooks there keep putting her hands in her mouth trying to get something out with a tooth pick she didn’t have gloves on or wash her hands after doing that’s and then was touching the food…..that’s was the only thing that was alarming to me to be honest the sanitation ugh smh.
Came from Detroit to Philadelphia for my cousin funeral in December. I look up african food and this one  came up. The food  was great and the ladies are wonderful.

Humble place with a daily menu offerings. I biked a long way to have dinner here and was satisfied! The team was super hospitable and happy to welcome a foreigner, and I even received tips on how to eat my meal. The servings are generous and delicious!

formatted_address: 4511 Baltimore Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19143, United States
name: Queen of Sheba

reviews.text: I actually wanted to eat here but it took +1hr leaving Roots picnic that the kitchen was already closed when I arrived.  As such I had a couple of PBRs until the bartender gave last call an hour early.  It was a Sunday night and all the ladies left, can't fault that logic.

This review is long overdue.  My husband and I had dinner here several months ago.  We were served food that never should have seen the light of day.  The chicken was inedible, burnt to a crisp, hard as leather, mostly grizzle and completely tasteless.  It was covered in stuff, so you couldn't see it until you started eating.  We should have sent it right back, but we made an effort to try to find edible meat amongst the burnt bones.  I can't believe that the person in the kitchen thought it was okay to put this on a customer's plate.  We also spent the evening quite sick to our stomachs once we got home. I LOVE Ethiopian food, and we regularly eat at an Ethiopian restaurant near our home.  We were in West Philly and thought we would try one of the many Ethiopian restaurants in the area - should have gone home to our lovely neighborhood Ethiopian restaurant.
Will the Bartender's !! ALL THAT !! He's a good brother that mixes GREAT drinks, just ask him. Had a vegetarian dish that to me ,was GREAT !! Don't mind the picture 😄

The food was trash. Don't ever order the lamb the chicken tibs was a waste of money. TRUST ME SAVE UR MONEY..
The bartender was nice..
Different type of atmosphere cool place to eat and mangle

formatted_address: 1102 Germantown Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19123, United States
name: AMINA

reviews.text:
First time at Amina’s new Germantown location (I’ve been to the old one before) and it did not disappoint. Parking is super convenient with a garage right across the street. The location is also so much more spacious. Brought two friends for their first visit and they loved it—both said they’d be back.

Started with martinis, then appetizers: cornbread with butter (always a win), lobster deviled eggs (10/10, a must-order), and the beignet cheesesteak rolls (also 10/10). For entrées, we had the salmon, short ribs, and lamb lollipops. The stand alone ribs were a 10/10 with huge portions, lamb chops a 9/10. Mashed potatoes could use a little more flavor, but nothing major. Salmon was good with crispy skin, a smaller portion. We also tried the Brussel sprouts which were good.

Dessert was the  Caramelized Apple Pie Spring Rolls with ice cream—delicious if you like sweet desserts. Drinks are a bit pricey, but overall the food, portions, and experience were great. Would continue to recommend this spot.

More than anything, I desire the success of a restaurant as the dedication, time, and passion required to achieve success is not simple. Good food and good service are essential, but having good parking is also crucial. The extra effort of finding parking is worth it, as great food and consistency are key to success.

In this review, starting with the parking situation, it is quite challenging to find a parking spot at this location. Although there are side streets and a second street available, we had to park three blocks away, which was not an issue for me. Personally, I enjoy the exercise but for a higher-end restaurant, valet parking may be necessary. Partnering with a local lot would greatly benefit this location, especially for those who may have physical challenges.

This was my first visit to this restaurant, and I must say it is quite beautiful. The decor is tastefully chosen, accompanied by wonderful music. The bar area is very nice with comfortable seating, and there are high back booth seating along the walls. The seats are incredibly comfortable, something that some people may overlook. The table setting is luxurious with bone china or porcelain plates, linen napkin service, and classic stemmed water goblets.

We ordered mimosas, and a carafe along with flutes was brought to the table. Classic large four-tined table forks and knives were also provided. For the entrees, my two friends decided to order the stone-ground blue grits with petite greens, and Mississippi Fried catfish, which they both enjoyed. The portion size was quite generous. My companion ordered the king salmon served on top of warm fingerling potato salad, sautéed spinach, and mustard marmalade, which she found delightful. She also ordered a side of smoked turkey collard greens, which were perfect.

As a vegan, I opted for the avocado toast without the poached egg. It was beautifully made with a perfect avocado fan sprinkled with red pepper flakes, Black Eyed Peas caviar underneath, served atop seven grain toast, and garnished with cherry tomato halves. Two things that were missing were the microgreens and breakfast radish, which I only noticed the following morning when reviewing the meal. Attention to detail is crucial, especially with the accessibility of local markets.

The dish was delicious, and when we requested lemons on the side to squeeze over the dish, it enhanced the flavors even more. This meal deserves four stars but could easily be a five-star dish if it were complete. For drinks, we shared mimosas and I also ordered a Savannah glow mocktail with peach, lavender, and lemon topped with a dried lemon wheel, which was delicious. The dessert menu was not available online, but we shared a peach cobbler with a cinnamon sugar crust topped with vanilla ice cream, which was perfectly executed and left us wanting more.

The service was excellent, with Rachel providing exceptional service and Chef Issac showcasing his culinary talent. We look forward to returning for dinner in the future.

We drove from central NJ to Amina in PA to celebrate a friend's birthday, and the place itself was really nice, clean, with beautiful decor and an amazing vibe. Parking was tough since it's only street parking, and on a Saturday night there was none available, so we ended up leaving the car at the supermarket across the street. We had a 6:30 p.m. reservation, and I even called when they opened to remind them it was for a birthday, and the staff said they'd make a note. When we arrived we still have to wait to get our table which was fine. At first everything was great; we ordered the cheesesteak beignets, which were my favorite because the flavor and cheese just melted in your mouth. We also ordered deviled eggs but were given jalapeño cornbread instead. We didn't complain since our waitress had recommended the beignets and they were so good, but the jalapeño cornbread was just plain and nothing special. For my main dish I followed her suggestion and got the smothered turkey wings, which were amazing. The turkey was juicy and tender, and I loved the brussels sprouts and sweet potatoes on the side. For dessert we tried the caramelized apple pie spring rolls, but they took a long time to come out. While waiting I reminded the waitress it was my friend's birthday, and when the dessert finally arrived she just dropped it off, quickly said "happy birthday," and walked away. I understand Saturdays are busy, but there were four of us and we only got two spoons, no plates, and then she handed us the bill while we were still eating apple pie with our hands, saying other people were waiting for the table. The 20% tip built in our bill felt unfair since the service was rude. Overall the food was really good and the place looks great, but parking is difficult and the service on a busy Saturday night was disappointing.

This restaurant is amazing!!! I went with a large party(17 guests) and we all enjoyed the food very much. There were no complaints and we all left out full. I ordered the smothered turkey wings amd they were phenomenal. My meal was served in a nice cast iron pot which elevated the presentation. None of the meals came out on the same plate. Every entree type had its own beautiful presentation.

The atmosphere was beautiful. From the lighting to the music, this was a very enjoyable dinner experience. I cannot wait to go back with friends or just a date night with my wife.

Dined at Amina for my birthday a few weeks ago. From the arrival, the service was great. They were able to accommodate a last minute change to our guest count.

Our server was very personable and knowledgeable about the menu. She offered great suggestions made sure we received what we ordered.

Our party of 8 ordered a variety of drinks, all of which we enjoyed.  The food was on another level! The flavors and presentation were off the charts. I haven't stopped recommending Amina to everyone.

To finish off the night, the sent over a complimentary dessert for my birthday, which enough to share with the table. Looking forward to going there again soon.

name: Fork N Fingers African Restaurant

reviews.text: I took my teenage daughters today and was disgusted. The place was clean but empty. Not one customer. I ordered the fried rice with shrimp and there were only 3 baby shrimp and the rice was hard. I ordered the goat and couldn’t chew it at all. We didn’t order much and it cost $81. Upon check out I was asked how was the food and I replied that the goat was hard and he said I’m sorry.  No refund or anything.  I will be eating in the US from now on!

The food was very tasty full of flavor. Suya tasted like it was definitely re-heated… The food was not spicy at all made to cater to all taste buds. I would say if you are in the area give it a try there is a bit of wait for the food to be ready so call in ahead.

I am visiting Philly and I was looking for a Nigerian restaurant. I ordered online via DoorDash and the food was good. The jollof rice tastes nice. The gizzard dodo is equally nice but they had less gizzard and more dodo. The ponmo is soft and spicy. 🥵

I ordered assorted meat, but they gave me ponmo and beef. Ponmo and beef is not assorted. That was my only concern. Please don’t sell ponmo and beef as assorted 🌚

I recently had the pleasure of dining at fork n fingers, and I was thoroughly impressed by the quality and flavor of the dishes. From the moment we walked in, we were greeted with a warm and welcoming atmosphere, and our server was attentive and knowledgeable throughout the meal.

Overpriced food. My order was all bad... the meat pie was too salty (thankfully I only bought one just to try). The fish was too dry, you can tell it was frozen and they only reheated it when I ordered... and the egusi is dry, no sauce or stew, just dry overall. I definitely do not recommend this restaurant.

Jamaican  food is excellent. Very delicious. Yous who like Jamaican  food will love it

Awesome

The food is okay but overpriced and keeps changing prices...

name: ERA

reviews.text: The atmosphere of the restaurant was good for a game night dinner, go eagles. Service was good and the bartender was attentive. Food was okay, however as it could have been warmer and the Njerra fresher.

Picture a neighborhood dive bar with folks watching baseball and a huge beer list! Then an auntie in the back making delicious Ethiopian food. Does that sound good to you because it sounds good to me! A delightful place to hang out, grab food and drink!

Good food but the waitress seriously messed up. She said it was her first day but she clearly doesn’t speak English. We ended up paying extra for entrees we didn’t want because she misunderstood us. Would go here again but would leave if she was working that night.
Cozy warm local spot with a family feel. Good for drinks and unique food, as opposed to boring bar food. Owners are great. Gets packed on Wed for quizzo. Karoke on Sundays as of my visit last week

Great spot! It is a dive bar first and foremost. It has some beers on tap, but based on what people are ordering, Citywide is their thing! We had Magic hat, which was one of the beers on tap.

They also serve Ethiopian food and it was delicious. We got the combo platter, so was able to order a bunch of different stuff. It was so flavorful and exactly as described on the menu.  Looking forward to returning!

reviews.text:

Just post a host of pictures,  not related to gulu west African Market.
Love the Authentic West African Food.  Gus & Lulu (hence “Gulu”) are awesome.  The food is delicious, service is wonderful, the Ambiance is Welcoming and Take-Out is Available.
The food is good, prices are above average. Good atmosphere.

I just paid $15.50 for dry rice and goat.  Basically I paid 15.50 for white rice, some sauce, and goat fat.  After removing the goat fat and skin, I was left with about two tablespoons of edible goat meat.  I'm never coming here again.

Food was spoiled I've been violently sick since eating spent up to 60 dollars just to be sick.  I can't eat anything or keep it down due to this.  I had to leave work early I've been vomiting and deficating since I've disgusted the food.  First time ever and thought I was going to be good.  The pepper sauce was bad. I called her to let her know she blamed it on an allergic reaction which is not true I've been eating african food for 10 years and never experienced what I've experience. Don't eat her waste of money!!!!

I loved the potato greens, fufu, wings and the fried fish platters. Get their ginger drink to wash all this tasty food down!

Wow. The food was so delicious and a great portion too . Everyone over there is so friendly .l will  definitely go back.    thank you so much ladies for the warm welcome

Martine

The location is pretty basic but clean and comfortable. The ladies are very sweet and kind. My food has always been good, except the one time I ordered it on doordash. Otherwise,  I get the lamb, plantains, and Jollof rice.  Also, the potatoe greens are good. Wish they had a seafood one, but they make do.
The cassava leaf wasn’t good , the texture was like potato green it wasn’t flavorful at all , I wouldn’t order again but the atmosphere & the people are friendly

I thought this was Nafisa’s Kitchen. I was confused when I arrived.  I ordered potato greens. I was highly disappointed. It was spinach. They only had chicken in it with no turkey. Even the rice was bad. I live an hour away. A complete waste of money and time . Honestly do not waste your money . It’s terrible.

reviews.text: Food was amazing! I would honestly love to gate keep but they deserve their flowers!! Beef kebabs were 10/10. Plantains fried perfectly, snapper well seasoned with veggies and the rice was tasty as well. No complaints. I’ll be ordering again without a doubt.

Best African food in sw . From the diffrent varieties on foods . The cook she’s very nice and friendly.  u can tell she prepares the food fresh right then and there there . I love that they only use chicken and turkey not the mystery meat like everyone else a it’s not too spicy like just right . The egusi and cassava leaf is the best thing on the menu!
I had the Meat Potato & Greens, good experience overall. Spices were spot on and greens were flavorful, too oily however.
They had a cat in the kitchen i left and will never come back
Great food , nice vibes great customer service , parking , friendly

formatted_address: 5532 Greene St, Philadelphia, PA 19144, United States
name: Salam Cafe

reviews.text: Salam cafe is a beautiful little gem of a restaurant. The food here is phenomenal packed with flavor! Their shakshuka was delicious and the homemade injera (a type of spongey bread) was so good! You gotta come and don’t miss out on dessert the chocolate baklava was incredible! This place was so good and if you are in the area you should definitely check it out ❤️

Stopped with a friend and this cuisine is new to us. The woman explained things and brought us a little sample of a few things so we could see what we liked and that we ordered something we could handle the spice level of. We sampled, ordered our lunches and everything was out of this world delicious. The chickpeas were my favorite part, such a wow flavor. We will definitely be going back.

I visited Salam Café in Philadelphia on Saturday, November 15 with my best friend Marla, and it was such a memorable experience. It was our first time enjoying Ethiopian food, and being able to indulge with our fingers felt fun, authentic, and comforting. The injera bread was so unique and flavorful, and every dish was beautifully seasoned.

The atmosphere was warm with plenty of seating, and the convenience of public parking right across the street made the visit even better. If you’re looking to try something new with great vibes and amazing food, Salam Café is definitely worth the trip. Highly recommend! 🍽️✨

The best tasting Ethiopian food in Philadelphia although much pricier than other restaurants (over $60 for 2 people  hence 3 star rating instead of 5).   Their prices for 2 used to be much more reasonable and competitive, so sadly we will not be coming ( unless a special occasion) given the new pricing of over $30 per person for one main course each...no dessert, appetizer or beer! They are even more expensive than the ethiopian restaurant in Ardmore! The meals used to be under $20 each at Salam.  We were not given a menu (dishes are now priced closer to $25 each instead of the usual $15), so we were unaware of the large increase in price.  The food was spiced to perfection.  We had the special tibs in spiced butter and doro wot.  The food never misses the mark! The doro  wot comes with two sides....we asked for alicha kik and miser wot.  They put four sides (barely any miser wot) but made up for their error by bringing extra miser wot since four sides were not ordered and we don't eat collards and cabbage.  We always have miser wot and alicha kik as our sides with the doro wot and recommend them. We also recommend eating family style.

I found this place once I was driving in the area. I’m glad I did because this is the closest I can go to get Ethiopian food and they have not disappoint.
I love their food, It is well seasoned and a good portion.
The service was good.
The atmosphere was clean, quiet Music was playing in the background.
Overall, I give it five I enjoy, their food

formatted_address: 5200 Whitaker Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19124, United States
name: DF Nigeria Food Truck Philadelphia

reviews.text: Words cannot explain how professional they are let me not start on the food but just amazing I can honestly say I have tried everything on their menu and 10/10 never had a bad experience even when I ate their food years ago it just keeps getting better. If you can stop by or order online you will not be disappointed. Last thing there are plenty African cuisine spots in Philadelphia but none of them compare to the authenticity of the dishes they prepare over there at DF.

Not sure what all the bad reviews are about? I have ZERO complaints! The owner, and who I assumed was her daughter, were very kind and pleasant to interact with. I ordered a small Vegan platter of Jollof Rice, Sweet Plantains, and Spinach, as well as an order of Puff Puffs. The food was fresh, hot, delicious, generous portion, packaged with care, and made with love! I’d definitely eat here again. The music was great too! I had about a 10-15 min wait on the food but that’s not a complaint, it’s FRESH food!! My Puff Puffs were NOT greasy at all, it was literally doughnut texture/flavor without the frosting. I’ve tried Jollof Rice once in the past at a different location and wasn’t a fan because it was just pure oil/grease but DF’s rice was the PERFECT TEXTURE and not greasy at all!! TRY THIS PLACE!!!

I ordered a small jallof rice meal with jerk chicken and fried plantain. The Food was not good. Meat was dry and mostly bone although had a potential to have good flavor. The rice was overly smoked tasted bitter and burnt. The portion size is terrible I got 2 fragments of chicken. Not even a full piece, rice, and 2 small pieces of plantain. It was not worth $11. I will not be coming back and should’ve just went somewhere else, but I wanted to take a chance.

The service was nice and music was great though.

I had to call the owner and rave about the pepper soup!!! It had an authentic and distinct flavor that i haven’t tasted in any of the Nigerian restaurants in the city!!! And I’ve been to just about all of them.

I also ordered the Egusi soup and black eyed peas. The food was really delicious!! I highly recommend you give them a try. You won’t be disappointed

I absolutely LOVE this place! The food is delicious, the portions are generous and the customer service is ALWAYS impeccable. Every time I visit the truck or do a phone order, my encounter is always a pleasant one. They definitely have a loyal customer in me.

formatted_address: 6505 Woodland Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19142, United States
name: Palm Of Africa

reviews.text: This is  definitely an establishment for young people , music so loud they can’t hear your order hookah everywhere , people just hanging out as well as the employees, I specifically asked for white meat and was given a chicken leg , my food sat on the counter for approximately 10 -15 minutes as  I asked several times about my food and was told that it’s coming. I will not go there again, however my young adult children speak very highly of the food.

Outside and inside looks nothing like a place where food is served.  I never ate here before. I ordered food online and when I arrived to pick food up, i thought I was at the wrong place. It looks like a place where you get your income taxes done. I took 1 bite of food just to not judge a book by its cover. I didn't eat the rest. Good note is that there's plenty of chairs for you to sit down and wait for the trolley.
Delish. From the fish to the lamb. So polite, as if my order could be change and they didn't have a problem with it. They changed it. I tipped for the inconveniences. Great place will visit again.

Never actually been theer but have eaten their food once and the food was awesome...i had the lamb platter with jollof rice omg it was so good...my wife said she wouldn't eat from there because we never had food from there, but when she tasted my lamb i could not get her to stop wanting and eating it...idk about their service or the place itself dine in or out but what i do know is that their food is damn good and for it being my first time ever eating from there i am convinced i will go back...hope the food tasting good stays the same
The food was very delicious and I had a really good experience

formatted_address: 6533 Guyer Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19142, United States
name: Minchgirl African restaurant/Dry Rice only

reviews.text: I never that the original African foods are still cook since I left Africa until I came across this place. The owner is young but she has skills in cooking. The service is great. I love eating there. I don't want to say recommend. But go there if you don't like anything she cook, I personally will refund you. My name is LG. No joke good food

Stopped here after flying into Philadelphia airport and convincing my parents it was a good idea to try African food, which I really enjoy. This area is residential and although I mistaken thought the address next door was the business, was told quite abruptly that I wasn't welcome.

I'm not sure if Minchgirl is catering or what but frankly, I'm happy to have survived the experience and I mean that literally.

This is absolutely the very best place to be. This is what I call Africa in America, a home far from home when it comes to African (Liberian) variety of dishes and sealed with very good customer service. At Minchgirl Restaurant, customer satisfaction is number 1!!!!
They have the best homemade Liberian dish in southwest philly. FYI: they don't accept credit or debit cards. Cash and cashapp only.
I was intrigued by how delicious this dry rice taste. I 100/10% recommend this dry-rice! The best liberian 🇱🇷 Dry-rice I have ever had.

formatted_address: 2237 S 63rd St, Philadelphia, PA 19142, United States
name: lifelyfaceofAfrica

reviews.text: Never pick up their phone .how can u have a business and never pick up phone. I went there and it was in a residential place and no signs or banner of a business outside. Except if maybe it's in the wrong address but the address on google leads to a residential street. formatted_address: 6631 Woodland Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19142, United States
name: Ackee Tree Jamaican Restaurant

reviews.text: I highly recommend this establishment. The cuisine is exceptional and the portions are generous. I had to request that they reduce the serving size, as I couldn't finish it and didn't want it to go to waste, given that I'm visiting from out of state. I would definitely suggest this place to anyone seeking authenticity. I will certainly return here whenever I'm in town.

The food is hot, fresh and delicious. They package everything write in front of you and it's clean. My favorites are the rice and beans, cabbage and fried chicken. Everything has a good flavor. I like the fish gravy over the rice (a must try). The staff is very nice and friendly.

I had to change my review from a 5 to a 1 star. The very first time I had it, the food was fresh.

Fast forward 2 weeks later, and everything except the yams tasted old. I live 50 mins away, and we do not have great ethic food in my area, so I had to give Door Dash a hefty tip to pick this up only to be disappointed the second time then again a 3rd time and it was stale again. I tried giving them a chance, but unfortunately, in this economy, I can't afford to waste my  money. (70.00 each time because I ordered extra sides.)

Very Mid. Little to no flavor. Mac and cheese is just noodles … barely even cheese. The goat was so bad I don’t think I’ll ever come here again. Everything tastes the same on my plate. It Looks like my dog went to town on my platter. Not to mention the “workers” who talk about you in front of your face. Little do they know I can understand every word they’re saying.  Their only menu is taped across one table … with a “worker” sitting at the table so you can’t really see.

I got my car fixed nearby and was recommended to visit Ackee Tree for some Jamaican cuisine. I ordered stew beef and curry chicken with one of each of the sides (mac and cheese, collard greens, candied yams, and cabbage). The food was AMAZING!! Portion sizes were huge, definitely will have PLENTY of leftovers. Everything was seasoned perfectly without being overly salty. The carrot cake was also fantastic. Good people and good food! I'd type more but can barely breathe because of how full I am. Definitely try them out!!

formatted_address: 880 Main St, Darby, PA 19023, United States
name: JD African Restaurant.

reviews.text: JD African Restaurant has great food and the food is prepared with care. I went into the restaurant with my mom buying food to ship to Florida. That's how good JD's food is. Apparently, Florida doesn't have African Food but we specifically go to JD then anywhere else in the area. Keep up the good work 👍

The food is tasty but the platter is half empty. Why are you not putting the right amount of food in the bowl? I got cassava leaf two times in one week. The first time I gave a pass because it was later in the day but the second time I came as soon as they open and same thing. A small serving. The bowl not even filled to the top. Barely half way. Mainly unknown pieces of meat. Really no cassava. Very disappointing because the flavor is good. Tsk. Side note the guy that takes my order isn’t very welcoming at all.

I absolutely love the greens and rice that this restaurant serves it is very well seasoned with a hint of spiciness. It comes with a side of sweet cornbread.

The portion size is also good, but I’ve eaten half of what you see in the picture but you get more than enough rice.

There are lots of fresh juices and carbonated drinks. They only take CASH!

JD has reasonable prices and good food! His customer service skills are 10/10. I'm a regular customer and will continue to patronize his business cause I care about what I eat and they treat me as a customer 💯

I had the potato greens with white rice! It’s really good but they barely give you enough food in the bowl! It’s not ever filled to the top! That super cheap 💩 to do! 🤦🏾‍♀️ African food isn’t cheap either! Give people their moneys worth!

formatted_address: 669 Long Ln, Upper Darby Township, PA 19082, United States
name: Mama D Nigerian Catering, Cuisine, and Events

html_attributions: Mama D Nigerian Catering, Cuisine, and Events

reviews.text: The best meal I had in Philadelphia was at Mama D Catering. Her Jollof rice is banging, and Smokey, you will love it. She has handled so many dishes for me and my family, and I will recommend her. Her Amala on the spot is super duper good. Keep up the good work, Mama.

Mama D. ur food sweet no be small.as in kilode…am feeling the nija vibe as I Dey chop am. Everyone who ate the rice was like this is real Nigerian jollof.U don get me as customer o.God go bless Saylarry photos for introducing you to me.            first time customer
I enjoyed every bits of this meal, a wonderful customer service alongside a fresh meal

Mama D Nigerian is one the best African food place  in Philly to eat at. The food is wonderful and delicious.
GO AND VISIT THE PLACE!!!
One of the best amala I have ever tasted.The servers are very kind and patient I will definitely order again!!!!!!

reviews.text: I had the yam porridge today and it really loved it! The sauce complimented the yam and greens so well bringing all the flavors together. I definitely will be going back for more.
Best Naija food in Philly! Bring your family and friends you won’t regret it!
My favorite food truck! Love the Jollof rice and jerk chicken

formatted_address: 3675 Market St, Philadelphia, PA 19104, United States
name: Black and Mobile

reviews.text:
Message from Sister Soul Food:

Hey Family.

It has come to our attention that someone is using our name to SCAM people out of their money by placing orders on a website called Black and Mobile. THAT IS NOT US.

We do not use that platform nor do we have a partnership with them. We are unable to issue refunds if you have used that platform.

DO NOT place orders with black and mobile it is a scam.

To place an order with Sister Soul Food you must come inside or go through Uber and DoorDash. On Uber and DoorDash you can place a customer pick up or delivery order.

We do not accept call in orders and the only platforms we use is Uber and DoorDash.

I was amazed at the outstanding service I received. A lot better than UberEats. Hoping that there will be more updates and features for the app soon, but I'm pretty impressed. Will be using them again.
Scam. Never received my order and there’s no way to contact them. The restaurant I placed an order with through this website said they don’t know who these people are and they don’t offer delivery.
Great service, responsive support. So excited I stumbled across Black & Mobile made searching for soul food open Sundays in HOUSTON convenient.
Great food options and fast, efficient service. So much better than Grubhub and UberEats combined. I highly recommend them!

formatted_address: 75 S MacDade Blvd, Collingdale, PA 19023, United States
name: JSM Cuisine | Musu's Spot

reviews.text: Musu's Spot JSMcuisine has great food and the cooks make the food with care. When I arrived there will 5 women working behind the counter with great communication between each other. This store seems that they can handle a rush of customers if they have to. Keep up the good work 👍
Fish was extremely dry. Rice smelled weird but I’m not African so idk if it’s supposed to smell like that. Rice tasted ok though.

I wouldn't recommend this place to any friend of mines, first off all the place had an awkward smell, the service wasn’t the best and the food was even worse. I ordered potato greens with rice but when I got my food, it was flooded with oil, palm oil. I will never eat there again nor recommend their food to someone

Cassava leaf and rice were good. The Attieke, vegetables, and fish were good as well. The fish was a bit overcooked, though, making pieces of it inedible. The sauces that came with fish were a nice addition.

Overall, I was happy with my order. I'll definitely order from them again.

Delicious, hardy  and tasty. A bit spicy too. Didn't know what to do with the fufu  (cassava) and they were so nice explaining it all. The eggplant stew had lots of meat. I swapped it for fish. They have us free plantains too. Really great meal and wonderfulllll.

formatted_address: 631 N Broad St, Philadelphia, PA 19123, United States
name: Honeysuckle Restaurant

reviews.text: Wow what an awesome restaurant experience! The cocktails were top notch and really creative. I really enjoyed the broiled oysters, the legim, and the flan dessert. My husband tried the burger which he said was wonderful but hard finish since it was so rich! We did the à la carte at the bar which was really fun. The ambience is really cool and perfect for date night!

This is more than a restaurant.  Its a cultural experience, and an opportunity to be educated by people who's passion is apparent in every aspect of what they do and how they do it.  Service was stellar.  The menu was fun and inventive and a little bit rebellious which I loved.  Each successive course was more interesting, and more delicious.  The McDonalds Money Burger could easily have been over the top but it wasn't.  It was decadent and perfect.  The chicken is a good as any I've ever had (nods to Vernick) but even more unique in terms of flavor.  The only thing I would change is adding decaf to the menu.  Not having it seems to be the new thing with fancier places but it's kind of ageist.  Older people for the most part can't drink caffeine at night.

This is one of the Philly landmark restaurants. The food has amazing seasoning and representation, the staff is super nice and professional - they do not make you feel uncomfortable or rushing. The place itself is very interesting and the seating arrangements are diverse. A lot of wood, contemporary and modern paintings artwork and themes are around. I hope they will find a way to make food and drinks slightly cheaper so that most people can afford. It definitely is a place to go and enjoy.

The food was an experience! Everything was so delicious and thought out. Mixed priced menu offered a variety of appetizers, salad, main course, dessert- as well as special treats. The Nutcracker cocktail for 2 is recommended.
Oysters are great. Lovely atmosphere and service!

Had a very pleasant evening at Honeysuckle! The atmosphere is moody and culturally inspiring! The staff were all super friendly, professional, and knowledgeable. Really loved the chef’s ideology and devotion on providing farm to table ingredients from their local farm in Bucks county and mixing in their cultural flair. The execution of the food excelled in representing the southern and Haitian flavor profiles but I had some questions on their technique in some dishes.

The chicken entree, at least mine, didn’t have that crispy skin that I was hoping for hence the skin was chewy. This would’ve added that extra layer of satisfaction and texture to the dish, but nonetheless the chickens accompaniments were delicious. The McDonald’s money add-on was fun but the Wagyu and truffle were overpowered in this dish. I would love to have a crispier patty as well and stronger beef flavor, maybe a Wagyu katsu sandwich instead of a smash burger? The shokupan was the star of this dish and absolutely delightful and so were the beef tallow French fries! Lastly, we were also not given the amuse at the beginning of our meal which the adjacent tables received. The other dishes shown through the photos were delicious, fresh, and represented the restaurant well!

Service was great. Knowledgeable, professional, and absolutely beaming with smiles and positive energy! They were accountable to their actions but we found the pacing of the meal was a little slow at times and our water glasses were left empty far too long for Michelin standards. Aside from these small details, we were more than pleased with the level of service provided.

I am critical of this restaurant because it feels like they’re aiming for a certain standard, the Michelin standard. As the Michelin guide rolls out this year in 2025 for Philadelphia, I am eager to see what the guide says about Honeysuckle! Wishing them all the success and will be back to experience the new seasonal menu!

name: Nene international kitchen

reviews.text: Best African restaurant I’ve visited since I’m in Philly very good food especially the chicken with atchieke clean place with et very good service and they are very friendly people.

The food sold here is Ivorian/African food.

Nene is the absolute best and nicest person ever. The bisab is the best I’ve had in a loooong time. Please do well to patronize
Good

formatted_address: 134 Chestnut St, Philadelphia, PA 19106, United States
name: Malooga

reviews.text: Everything was amazing. The hummus, grape leaves, foul and lamb were all delicious.  The hot bread was so incredibly good. Really nice family style restaurant with a relaxed atmosphere. We were lucky to get a table. A lot of tables were reserved and it’s a cozy restaurant - so make a reservation if you can.

Malooga was solid. Service was decent nothing super special but not bad by any means. We got the big feast platter and we each had a bit to take home at the end which was nice. All the meats were solid, not my favorite middle eastern ever but it’s a place I would definitely come back to. I really liked their lamb kebab and the vibe was good to have conversations and just spend time for a while. They also have a lot of traditional Yemen dishes and kinda of something for vegetarians too.

Highly recommend to go taste the middle eastern food and make a reservation before hand. Delicious and flavorful food and definitely going back. The staff was very friendly. There is a choice for everyone. Desserts are not too sweet.
Great food. Very good staff. Ordered the mixed grill platter & a few other things. If you are a meat eater, it's a very good choice. Reasonable prices. BYOB as well. Make a reservation.

Easy to find paid street parking.
We were introduced to this restaurant by a social media video of a couple eating in a traditional setting by eating on the floor/pillow area. Glad we didn’t do this bc there wasn’t a small table provided, so you either eat while you’re seated, hunched over your plate that is on floor level or you are holding your plate the entire time while eating. Did not look comfy at all.

We ordered hummus shawarma, sambosa, chicken kabsah , lamb fahsah, and Yemeni latte.
Hummus and sambosas were so yummy, pita was fresh and warm.
Chicken kabsah (rice and roasted chicken) was good. Our waiter recommended for us to get the spaghetti noodles on the side and we were glad we did.
Lamb fahsah (pieces of lamb, potatoes, and okra in a sizzling pot) was an interesting choice. A yummy, salty dish. Texture was a bit tricky bc of the okra but enjoyable while it was still hot. Good with the pita.
Coffee was good!
Customer service was good!

formatted_address: 6451 Grays Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19142, United States
name: Sonia's Kitchen

reviews.text: A wonderfully welcoming, bright corner restaurant with a relaxing atmosphere and delicious West African food. My partner and I had the Jollof Rice with chicken, which was was out of this world, the plantain and the ginger drink, which were also great. We were served by the owners, who couldn't be nicer. Bring your appetite, and be prepared to relax, this is not fast food.

Mr Mohamed provided great service...the atmosphere was elegant but welcoming. The presentation of the meal was appealing while the  Jolif rice was very tasty and the fish was prepared very well. The icing on the cake for me was the pepper...the hotter the better and this was very hot. When you are looking for a tasty African experience pass by Sonia's Kitchen you will not be disappointed
Super clean. Great food pleasant friendly waitstaff. Welcoming atmosphere and I wasn’t rushed  to order. Whatever you get you will definitely love.
Best African breakfast!.

Their food is post card worthy.
Reasonable prices, tasty food, lovely owners, and most of all a hidden gem.

formatted_address: 48 Garrett Rd, Upper Darby Township, PA 19082, United States
name: Divine Time Nigerian Cusinie

reviews.text: My first time trying Nigerian food, it was amazing! Employees are friendly and patient.. Hot and fresh food, I tried the egusi with fufu .. it’s empty in here but that could be because the closing time says Saturday 6pm .. it’s 8:50 now .. it’s a nice welcoming place, I’d come back.

I love this restaurant. First, they were courteous, friendly and they made me feel at home the first time. The food is of great quality and they also helped me with taking the food to the parking lot. I would highly recommend this place to every African. I love this restaurant.

I was in PA and wanted some authentic Nigerian food. I found this resturant and decided to give it a try the food was great very flavorful and great portions. Price was also reasonable plenty parking. I would most definitely say if you are in the area to stop by and give it a try! The resturant is on the second floor inside SA Cafe!
Ordered jollof with stew and chicken and this is the best Nigerian food I’ve had in Philly by far. The meat could be softer but it was still tasty. The jollof and stew were extremely flavorful.

amazing food and service! will definitely be back. the restaurant is tucked away on the second floor and we almost thought we were in the wrong place - so glad we still stopped in because the food was delicious. we got the suya, egusi soup, and jollof rice with bone in lamb, and i would highly recommend each dish. the portion sizes were very generous and the service was great.

formatted_address: 8756 Frankford Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19136, United States
name: Sweeties Liberian African Restaurant

reviews.text:
Horrible waste of money. I called on the phone for my order when I got there I stated what I ordered; the person said something different then said give me a couple of minutes I had the wrong thing prepared.

I waited got home and the same wrong item she mentioned is what she got gave me. Horrible a waste of money when I called the only solution was to come back; I  already drove there had to drive home. I wasn’t close where I could easily come back.

Same your time and money and go somewhere else.

I asked for jollof rice and they don’t have it again. Lady then walked away from the counter. A male walked up and as he was talking on the phone. Pointed at chalkboard indicating this is what they have. I don’t know how this place is in business.

Save yourself the headache—and your money. The customer service is poor, and the staff often come across as rude and unapproachable. They frequently fail to acknowledge customers when spoken to and present a consistently unpleasant demeanor. The food is ok, though its quality varies depending on the day and who is preparing it.

I ordered the snapper with dried rice, it comes with pepper sauce. The snapper is big enough to feed a family. I also ordered the tilapia and Crocker fish by itself. The fishes were fried to perfection and this was one of the best pepper sauce I’ve had in a long time. If you’re ordering the snapper do it In person I don’t believe this is an order they accept over the phone. Even though I ordered it on the phone it wasn’t placed until I got there and I live 40 minutes away, I think that’s because of the price. I’ll definitely visit in the future

My second time having there cassava leaf. It comes with rice and taste so good. I never had African food before. The spicy level is high but i can handle. It has chicken pieces and i think i think piece of idk what skin or nerve if you know let me know

formatted_address: 125 Chester Ave, Yeadon, PA 19050, United States
name: Fork N Fingers Restaurant

reviews.text: Ordered 3 items, paid $45 and was highly disappointed. Do not go here or order from here. Does this look like $45 worth of food. 3 pieces of meat, spoiled veggies and moi moi not fully cooked

They should be closed down they were closed by the time i got home.Once i opened my platters i had cabbage that was under cooked taste like a carrot like that hard.Rice and beans with no seasoning dry as the bean once picked and oxtails under with a grave that taste like flour with soy sauce cooked smh and mushy plantain.My husband had stew chicken which was to my liking but the same dry rice undercooked cabbage and mushy plantain. I want my money back.

A friend took me to this place and the first impression was excellent.
The staff in attendance are neat and friendly. Plus the food taste real good. If you are an old customer and you have complaints about this place before, I'll advise you to try this place again. They got a new chef that cook real good now.
To avoid delay, just order ahead of time, because what you getting is a fresh cook food not a microwaved food common with most restaurants.
And parking is not an issue.

Delicious!  Go for the food, but set your expectations low on atmosphere.

If you like delicious Jamaican food, this is the place!   Spicy, citrus deliciousness.   Generous portions and pleasant staff in a very modest location.

I took a chance and ordered the sampler with beef, a side order of fried plantains and a shrimp skewer...and I'm glad I did.  I took the order to my hotel and couldn't finish it in one sitting (and no I CAN eat).   If it weren't for the atmosphere, I would have given it 5 stars.

I will definitely be back in future business trips.  I think I will be making it "to go," though.

I had the jallof rice with beef and an order of potato greens with white rice....wow. This brought me back to my childhood, I’ve been searching for YEARS for a place that cooked African food as good as my grandma use to make it, and I’ve found it. I would highly recommend the African food. (Didn’t try to Jamaican food yet). I know there are mixed reviews...chefs are not perfect everyday...but take the chance, the food is delicious!

formatted_address: 6825 Ludlow St, Upper Darby Township, PA 19082, United States
name: JC AfroSoul Kitchen

reviews.text: The Mac is terrible, it’s old and tastes like chicken bouillon. The potato greens are extremely spicy and watery. Pretty expensive for 0 quality. The lady was very friendly and helpful, that was the best part of the entire thing.

The food was sooooo good , the cabbage had curry sauce & it tastes magnificent, the butter garlic shrimp had so much flavor & rice was definitely seasoned & buttery asfffffffff . The cheesesteak was bussin !!!!!!If u don’t want to come to the bar at least come for the food !!!!!!💯💯💯💯💯💯

Although the atmosphere was nice and the service was friendly the food for me was terrible. Nothing like they advertised.  The egg roll was burnt and chewy, the wings were small and bland, they put seafood salad in the same platter with hot food, I can't even highlight anything good about their food. name: Eephee's Kitchen

reviews.text: Had a great experience today!! Sadly this is the only good option available, located inside what appears to be a long forgot mall. Today we came in at opening (1pm). The team of 3 were there and helpful with all our questions. It was my first time trying Nigerian food and it is exactly what I expected. Full flavor, slight kick in the back and filling. So happy we found this place. We will def drive the distance just for this. I wish them luck since hope they can get their own brick and mortar location in the future!

Went there for the first time and I went back for more the next day and subsequently after. The food is delicious 😋, the customer service is top notch 👍🏾👍🏾. I have tried almost everything they have on their menu, and I must say you can't go wrong with whatever you choose. The meatpie is nice and firm, the soups (ogbono, egusi, vegetable...) are finger licking 😋 good. Fried rice is 🔥, coconut rice is 😋 😋. But my favorite order is this: 2-3 meatpies (actually I want 5-6 but "one must exercise restrain"), 2 pounded yam with egusi soup with extra goat meat.

Home style Nigerian cuisine in the heart of south jersey and minutes away from Philadelphia! Finding a good quality and tasty Nigerian restaurant in our area is hard to come by and thankfully Eephee’s Kitchen came to fill the void. I highly recommend! My favorite dish is their vegetable soup with fufu and good ole puff puff!

Went there for the first time and the food was DELICIOUS! I got the Nigerian Curry Chicken and Jollof rice and it was so good. The portion size is generous too! Look at the size of those chicken legs!

I am thoroughly impressed and I will be going back again soon to try more dishes!
My Church (Christ Embassy Philadelphia) hired Eephee’s Kitchen to cater for our Pastor’s birthday. The food was great. People loved the jollof rice, pepper fish, pepper goat, Egusi and meat pie.

formatted_address: 36 E Lancaster Ave, Ardmore, PA 19003, United States
name: Eshkol Ethiopian Cuisine & Cafe

reviews.text:
I visited yesterday with my husband and a friend, and everything about this place was wonderful. The food was excellent—rich, flavorful, and clearly made with care. The owners were incredibly kind and courteous, which made the experience even more special. We’ve tried Ethiopian food at several well-known spots in Philly, and this was easily the best we’ve had. Highly authentic, welcoming, and delicious. I would 100% recommend this restaurant and can’t wait to come back.

Dishes:
Double meat combo
Chaltu’s special Minchet Abish (must try for spice lovers)
Misir wot
Fesoliya

In the suburban, Ardmore area, it is hard to find a good Ethiopian restaurant restaurants, but glad that we find one in this area.  It is family owned, service is very friendly and attentive.  Recommend to make reservation.  We had the meat combo, the vegan combo, banana bread, and traditional Ethiopian coffee.  The platters were fresh, good and authentic, the coffee was excellent, the banana cake was a little dry.

I am giving a four star because I think other Ethiopian restaurants in Philadelphia like Amsale Cafe food is a little more tasty.

This mom and pop owned restaurant is a hidden gem. The owners are so sweet and are very patient explaining each dish as well as showing the proper authentic way to eat the dishes. Great atmosphere and the food was delicious. You will not be disappointed even the left overs hit. The traditional macchiato was really good of course.  Side note the restroom was so pretty and very considerate having feminine productions (pads & tampons), lotions, and soaps. There are no negatives with this spot.

It's no coincidence that this place is 5 stars with almost 400 reviews. I have been to several Ethiopian restaurants around Philly but this is definitely at the top of my list. The food is authentic and fresh. Portion sizing is great. The large meat platter for 2 served four of us, with some still left over. The professionalism and kindness of the owner and servers are very apparent. Also, their restroom is a great addition (iykyk).

I really enjoyed my time at this place. I got the Doro Wot, and it was delicious! I will say that the injera is very filling, and the taste was a little surprising. It was my first time trying Ethiopian food and I was very pleased. Their banana bread is so good and tastes really fresh/homemade. The service was great, the chef walked around to each table greeting everyone. Thanks guys!

formatted_address: 4817 Walnut St, Philadelphia, PA 19139, United States
name: Amsale Cafe

reviews.text: Really enjoyed their awaze beef tibs, lamb stew, and the beef dish that’s mixed with greens. Vege combo is ok not too impressive. (Got lamb tibs last time which was not very good.) glad that we gave it another try and the other meat dishes are so good. Injera is super good too! Price is very reasonable. Would come again or get take outs!!!

Highly disappointed. I ordered delivery and received a box of varying items, all unlabeled. My first bite is the first photo. I pick up this substance and discover something almost out of a DnD campaign, a gelatinous cube of splintered bones, fat, and flesh. I don’t know if it was because I ordered late or what, but the number of bones and fat just disgusted me. This was truly a terrible dining experience, and I’m really bummed out. I would not typically write a review like this that was so harsh, but I genuinely feel repulsed by what I paid to put in my mouth, and I feel an obligation to let y’all know that you might receive the same.

Best Ethiopian restaurant for vegetarians. Food is amazing and the number of sides will leave you full. The shiro, yellow lentils, and cabbage are my favorites.  Their tea is perfect. Injera is authentic and you may even have enough to bring some home. Owners are super friendly and service is full of love.

We are a couple with two young kids, and we have been coming to Amsale Café on Walnut Street for years. Without a doubt, this is our favorite restaurant in Philadelphia, and it is also our children’s favorite! The food is as close to home-cooked traditional Ethiopian as you can imagine. It is delicious, affordable, and served by a family that is kind, friendly, gentle, and sweet.

Over the years, our kids and the owners have developed a special relationship. Our kids always hug them when we arrive, draw them pictures, and it is beautiful to see. When we tell our kids we are going to Amsale Café, they are thrilled, and so are we.

Our kids, who can be quite picky eaters, absolutely love the different options here, especially the amazing, delicious beef Alcha, which they ask for every time. We always order the meat and veggie combo, which is an incredible amount of flavorful, beautifully seasoned food with a huge variety to enjoy.

There is no doubt this is not only our favorite restaurant in Philadelphia, but our favorite restaurant ever!!! It has truly become like a second home. We all feel unbelievably comfortable there, and we will continue coming for years.

Thank you to the owners and their family for being so wonderful and for making every meal feel special!

Great spot!! We started with the Tematim salad (order this, so unique and fresh and zingy) and veggie sambusas.  Yebeg awaze tibs was amazing, such a flavorful dish and perfectly spiced. My girlfriend had never had Ethiopian food before and absolutely loved the veggie combo. The injeera was fresh and delicious. Service was good and staff were friendly.

reviews.text:
I think my husband found this spot on TikTok and we both wanted to try it next time we were in Philly.

We shared:
- Half Chicken, Lemon Turmeric
- Half Chicken, Spicy Berbere

The fried chicken was fantastic. I loved both seasonings. The spicy was probably my favorite. It wasn't all that spicy, but it was flavorful.

If you like fried chicken, I'd highly recommend checking this spot out.

Everything I’ve had here is great! The chicken is super crispy and juicy, and the drinks and dipping sauces are all good too. I got a chicken stew with injera yesterday, which was filling and flavorful. Can’t wait to try more of their menu!

Also the surrounding area is pretty and nice to walk in, and parking is always free and easy.

I had heard some great reviews from food bloggers - so my expectations were set to high.  Sadly I was disappointed.  My friend and I arrived right at opening time.  We each ordered the fried chicken sandwich.  It was dry and leathery.  My guess is they reheated the chicken from the previous day as it was hot on one side of the sandwich only. The pickles and sauce were tasty.  I am hoping this was a one off - and may try it again.

I’ll have to come back when I’m hungry I forced myself to come out here since I’ve wanted to try for few years.  Had the half chicken, collard greens n Mac n cheese all of which seemed under seasoned but idk the chicken was good n while I wish for more heat I forgot to add sauces.  Was hoping the collard greens would have ham hock but did not and was kind of blandish and Mac n cheese was ok wished for more cheese lol but I’ll have to come back for the doro bet which I’m told is spicy.  I got the sweet kerkede was too sweet for me this day lol.  I should have went with first gut call of the wings and doro bet. Nice staff and good service.

Sauces are the best part! Everything is delicious and I love that the fried chicken is gluten free since that’s hard to come by. The people there are helpful and friendly despite the pressure of the crowd. Even though it’s usually busy I’ve not had trouble finding a seat when I’ve gone. Take out is easy too. I do pickup and it’s always ready within 15 minutes.

Haven’t tried the gluten free tres leches cake yet but I really want to.

name: Guzo Cafe

reviews.text:
Absolutely delicious food! I had a mix of vegetarian dishes that all had fantastic flavor. I also had an iced Ethiopian tea (they make it in house!) and ohhhhh my goodness, it was so so good 10/10 recommend.
It’s really great having an Ethiopian restaurant in South Philly so I don’t have to go all the way out to west Philly/ U City every single time I’m craving it. The customer service is top notch and they make you feel so welcome and are happy to answer any questions. I will absolutely be adding this into my regular restaurant rotation.

Ethiopian and Eritrean food in south Philly! Found through 2good2go, so excited to try it all. Started with a classic vegan platter with delicious tangy injera and iced tea. Local art and lovely vibes available in a cute Parkside cafe!

My first visit to Guzo Café was an absolute delight from start to finish. The moment I walked in, I was struck by the warm and inviting ambiance — a mix of cozy café charm and authentic Ethiopian touches. The aroma of freshly brewed coffee and spices filled the air, setting the tone for what turned out to be a wonderful dining experience.

For our entrée, we ordered the Meat Combination, which came with our choice of 100% gluten-free teff injera as the base. We chose chicken as our meat option and paired it with Alicha (potatoes and carrots), Gomen (collard greens), and Misir Wot (lentils). Every bite was flavorful and perfectly seasoned — the chicken was tender and aromatic, the lentils had a rich, spiced depth, and the vegetables balanced everything beautifully. The injera was soft and slightly tangy, exactly as it should be.

To top it off, we each had a cup of hot Ethiopian chai, which was perfectly spiced and soothing — the kind of drink that makes you slow down and enjoy the moment.

The service was equally impressive. The staff were warm, welcoming, and eager to answer questions about the dishes. It felt like dining with friends who genuinely cared about your experience.

Overall, Guzo Café is a gem — great food, authentic flavors, friendly service, and a peaceful atmosphere. Whether you’re new to Ethiopian cuisine or a longtime fan, this spot is definitely worth visiting.

Cute coffeeshop with reasonable prices and very tasty food. It was a pleasant surprise to discover this place and eat Ethiopian food as a light lunch. The waitress is learning which requires some patience but overall very nice space and food and coffee!
Great food and atmosphere! They are doing free Ethiopian tea which I didn't know about but now love! Would highly recommend this place for good food and vibes.

formatted_address: 6008 Germantown Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19144, United States
name: The Nile Cafe

reviews.text: This is my go to vegan soul food spot in Philly. I gave 4 stars cuz I find the food is better when they aren’t busy or it isn’t late. I have eaten from here many times. I normally get the jerk chickpeas, okra and cabbage, but this time I got the bbq chicken, sweet potatoes and cabbage. It was tasty. The bbq sauce wasn’t too sweet or tangy which was good. I also got this white bean soup that was DELICIOUS! It was my first time having it and the owner said it was a crowd favorite and I can see why. For dessert I had the apple crumb bar and it was good per usual.

I came here from Atlanta in June of 2023 and I must say If you’re looking for incredible plant-based food in Philly, The Nile Café is a must-visit. This long-standing gem in Germantown has been serving up delicious, soulful vegan dishes for years, proving that plant-based eating can be both nourishing and full of flavor.

The menu is packed with hearty, satisfying options, from rich curries and flavorful stir-fries to their famous BBQ tofu and mac & cheese. Every dish is thoughtfully prepared with fresh ingredients and a perfect balance of spices, making each bite both comforting and deeply satisfying. Their homemade juices and smoothies are the perfect refreshing complement to the meal, adding even more vitality to the experience.

Beyond the food, The Nile Café has a warm, welcoming atmosphere that makes you feel right at home. Whether you’re a longtime vegan or just looking to try something new, the staff is always friendly and happy to guide you through their offerings. The café has a STRONG community feel, which makes dining here even more special.

Philly has no shortage of great vegan spots, but The Nile Café stands out for its rich flavors, soulful dishes, and the love that goes into every meal. If you’re in the area, don’t miss this place! I think I stayed here for a few hours and I couldn’t stop spending my money! Kudos and I’ll be back 🙏🏾

I have been coming to them for years.And the last time I was there.I see that they have expanded their building for outside seating.The prices are very reasonable and the food is awesome. I didn't care too much for the macaroni however.

I love this place. The jerk chicken and the stew fish are insanely good. The Mac n cheese is to die for. You absolutely cannot pass on the collards or the rice with gravy. And dessert is a must. The food might take a second and sometimes they run out of certain things from time to time but this place can do no wrong in my eyes haha.

This was my first visit to The Nile Cafe, vegan soul food on Germantown Avenue across from FUMCOG. The atmosphere is bright, clean, and sunny with lots of plants and light colored wood tables. You order at the window and they bring you your food. My Jerk Drumsticks were excellent, along with brown rice and gravy. I appreciated their being served in cute round cardboard containers, rather than plastic. Also, all set to bring home half my lunch for dinner. Be sure to get a drink. The food is SPICY!
Folks from Mt. Airy tend to go north to Chestnut Hill rather than south to Germantown - hence it took me a long time to check out Nile Cafe. I will return!

reviews.text:
This is an excellent African (Kenyan/Nigerian) restaurant. The food is authentic and flavorful, and the staff are so nice and welcoming.
We ordered samosas, fried fish, and goat stew, and they were all so delicious. Don't forget to get some plantain on side too, they are so good.
They also have fresh juices (mango-pinapple and sorrel) that are so fresh and refreshing. Make sure to try them, too.

We had dinner at Da Judas last night, and it was amazing! It was our first time trying African food, and the staff was so kind helping us decide what to order since we were a little overwhelmed by all the options. We got red snapper, egusi soup, beef stew, and fufu — everything was delicious and so satisfying. Definitely get the fresh in-house made juices — they’re amazing! The service was great and the whole place felt really warm and welcoming. We’ll definitely be back!

First time there and first time trying African food. Relaxed atmosphere and helpful with ordering. The food was delicious, reasonable pricing, came out quickly and had great portions. I will go back to try other things on the menu!

Great food. I felt like I was on vacation with no passport 😆🛂. Loved the mango 🥭 pineapple 🍍 juice 🥤. It was perfect!. Fish is big and fresh. Delicious. Great seasoning. Veggie Samosas are incredible. Friendly staff and great service .  Try the hot sauce is awesome 😎.I will come back again and will recommend to all my friends. Thank you 🙏.

Excellent Kenyan restaurant. If you’ve never had Kenyan food before, you must try this place. Every single dish was delicious. African cuisines are often deeply spiced with similarities to Indian cuisine, but they’re separate things. I’m definitely coming back to learn more about Kenyan culture.

Kenyan pilau’s flavor profile was unlike any similar rice dishes around the world like pilaf, biryani, or kabuli. It has four principal spices: clove, cardamom, cinnamon, and cumin. Each spice asserted its individual presence while blending into a warming and earthy cohesive whole. It has few ingredients as far as a spice mix goes, yet it’s complex and addictive—why is this flavor profile not more common around the world? Just be careful of the dab of chili peppers on the side, especially if you have a low spice tolerance.

The samosas had a stretchy chewy skin, more similar to Arabic motabbaq than pastry-like Indian samosas. The tomato-based goat stew was super tender with concentrated umami, made even more intense with the jollof rice and sweet plantains that had crispy bits and edges. Chips masala tasted like Indo-Chinese dishes such as Chili or Manchurian.

These dishes felt like a window to a part of the world many of us will never get to visit. And most importantly, the food’s delicious. I’m excited at what dish I’ll get to try next. I urge everyone to go here.

Thank you, Yvonne,  Fantastic Rhe next rime I will i Include yams ( I forgot to order at a later date) Served 30-40....Everyone ate and was pleased!!  ⭐💯👏🏾❤️

Blitz Soul food supplied the food for my daughter Sweet 16 Birthday Party this past Saturday. Everything was amazing. We had nothing but good remarks about the food. They were very professional and arrived on time with the food.

When I say the food was everything!!!  Blitz catered my wedding reception and besides marrying my sweetheart this was definitely my second best decision! My guest are still talking about the food 2 weeks after my event.  🗣 The service was impeccable!!!! I will be using Blitz for many more events to come 💯💯💯💯💯💯 💯💯💯💯%.

formatted_address: 4049 Market St, Philadelphia, PA 19104, United States
name: Sardar G Catering

reviews.text:
We had an amazing experience with SardarG Catering and couldn’t be more grateful to have had them cater for our big day. A special shoutout to Jagmit — he was absolutely amazing to work with.
