From the beautiful decor to the incredible thoughtfulness and timeliness, everything was handled with such care and professionalism.

The quality and aesthetics of the food were outstanding — not only delicious, but presented so beautifully. Every detail was clearly well thought out, and it truly elevated our celebration. We are so thankful for the incredible service and would highly recommend SardarG Catering to anyone looking for excellence and heart in their event.

Sardar G catered our daughters wedding on Oct 12. We are vegans and we requested that all food served at the wedding be made vegan.  They came through in a way we never anticipated.  We are absolutely blown away by the food, the communication and willingness to go the extra mile, the artful display of the food and how wonderfully it all came together.  This was art on a plate.  Just so beautiful to look at and explosion of flavors.  Our wedding was 1/2 indian and 1/2 non-indian crowd and everyone was raving about the food.  If we could give a 100 stars we would!..I dont believe any other caterer can come close to the quality and showmanship of what we got!  Thank you Sardar G !!!

Catered my engagement party and all of my guests could not stop raving about the food!!!! He came on time and set up, the food looked amazing and tasted even better!!! Chef Jagmeet was so talented and took a lot of pride in his work and it really showed!! The service was amazing, the food was delicious and the presentation was so enticing! Would love to work with them in the future and will be recommending them to everyone I know who needs a caterer for Indian food!

Jagmeet and his crew catered for a reception dinner in Philly. They were fabulous. The food was tasty and served hot. We asked them to serve a family style dinner (which is more complicated and difficult) - but he took a the challenge and surpassed all our expectations.
He is easy to work with, and responsive.
Also, he is willing to accommodate additional requests.  His setup is fun and the guests loved it.
I would recommend him 💯

Jagmeet catered for our daughter’s wedding reception. Wonderful presentation. Food was clearly labeled which was very helpful for guests with dietary restrictions. All the guests praised the delicious spread and presentation. Jagmeet and his staff are very responsive and polite. The rates are reasonable. We had a hassle free and wonderful experience. Highly recommend Sardar g catering

formatted_address: 820 N Broad St, Philadelphia, PA 19130, United States
name: Taste of Dacca

reviews.text:
I picked up from here several times and it’s always sooo tasty!
I’m a big fan of the Chicken Biryani, Spinach Paneer.
They’re often out of several menu items, which is a bummer, but everything they offer is just delicious!

If you’re craving authentic Bangladeshi flavors in Philly, Taste of Dacca is a must-visit! You don't have to go all the way to NYC for Deshi food, you can have it in your town. I recently tried their Kacchi Biryani, Beef Kala Bhuna, Daal, Fuchka, and Veg Pakora, and every bite was absolutely worth it. I wish I had ordered more food.

The Kacchi Biryani was hands down the star of the meal – rich, aromatic, and perfectly cooked, full of spices and the meat melts in your mouth! Kala Bhuna was tender, flavorful, and a great intro for first-timers. The Daal was surprisingly comforting and full of depth. The Fuchka was a delightful surprise – fresh, tangy, and honestly the best we've had in Philly. Their Veg Pakora also stood out with a unique taste and crispiness that sets it apart from any other place.

I ordered for two people and the portion sizes were generous, more than enough for a satisfying meal. The pricing is very fair considering the freshly cooked food and prime location.

The restaurant itself is clean, beautifully designed, and welcoming. The two-story interior is spacious, with a peaceful upstairs section that’s perfect for niqabi sisters or families wanting privacy. The staff were friendly, respectful, and made us feel right at home.

Overall, it felt like dining at a relative’s house – warm, cozy, and full of flavor. The owner is an incredibly kind and well-mannered person—made us feel truly welcome and the chef came out to greet us.

Highly recommend for anyone looking to experience real Bangladeshi hospitality and cuisine. Definitely a 5-star spot we’ll be returning to!

Dining at Taste of Dacca with my son was a wonderful experience. The food took me back to the authentic flavors of traditional Bangladeshi cuisine—rich, flavorful, and perfectly spiced. The biriyani was a standout, and the beef curry was incredibly tender. The staff treated us like family, which made the meal even more special. This is a place I’d gladly return to for both the food and the hospitality.

I’d never had Bangladeshi food and this was my first time. It was super good!!! The waiter described one of the dishes as a goat biryani but different, and that was not only true, but I would say it’s both different and better than most of the goat biryani I’ve had in Philadelphia. Ditto for the soup. My wife got the Rui fish, which it seems as brought in directly from Bangladesh fresh, and she likes it. (She’s vegetarian).

So, I’d give taste of Dacca a strong five stars. In a neighborhood with quite a few south Asian options, this one stands out. Will come again.

We had the BEST TIME at Taste of Dacca. Extremely friendly vibe, like walking into someone's home, and an incredibly well-prepared meal. Everything we had was delicious and we couldn't decide on a favorite. Cannot wait to go back. Plenty of gluten free options too!!

formatted_address: 613 S 4th St, Philadelphia, PA 19147, United States
name: Cilantro Mediterranean Cuisine

reviews.text: Amazing place!!! This is our last meal in Philly and it was incredible! Mixed grill was a huge portion and everything was delicious. The staff was super friendly and the service was amazing! Will definitely come back next time I visit Philly!

Absolutely amazing place! We ordered the Fatboy Choose 2 set — and wow, it’s definitely more than enough for two people! Ours came with beef shawarma on the plate and juicy lamb chops, both cooked perfectly and full of flavor. The food was fresh, generous, and beautifully presented.

I also loved the black tea with mint, which comes with refills — a perfect finish to a great meal.
Everything was delicious, and I’m just genuinely happy with this experience. Highly recommend Cilantro Mediterranean Cuisine to anyone who loves authentic Mediterranean flavors!

Absolutely incredible experience! We traveled to Philadelphia specifically to eat here, and it exceeded all our expectations. The food was worth every penny – everything we ordered was fresh, delicious, and there was so much variety to choose from. The atmosphere was just as wonderful as the food. On top of it all, the service was amazing; our waitress was attentive, served our dishes quickly, and cleared plates promptly. We will definitely be back!

Amazing place for an authentic Egyptian experience.
The food tastes exactly like Cairo. We had the rice wrapped in grapes leaves, it is served warm and has amazing fragrance and flavor. Just like Cairo.
We also ordered the mixed grill. The meat was tender and perfectly seasoned.
For desserts the OmAli was freshly made for us and it was perfect. The food here is delicious.

The owner was extremely friendly and accommodating.

We are visiting from out of town but we will go back because we dont have a restaurant like that. I would recommend a 100%

WOW!!!! Just WOW! We’re still sitting here drinking tea, as I write this review. Food was Phenomenal and service was outstanding! We got the cilantro mix for appetizer, that came in a very generous portion. At first, we thought we were not gonna finish it, but it was so good we got could not stop eating it. Second dish was the mixed grill for 1, which again was a huge portion and one meat better than the other. We also got the mint tea and had it with baklava. The baklava just melts in your mouth! We are definitely coming back here with our friends and our kids because it did not disappoint.

formatted_address: 6738 Bustleton Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19149, United States
name: Al-Sham Restaurant

reviews.text: My husband & I decided to try Al Sham after he saw a post on social media (instagram).We originally were going to go to another location, since it was getting late and we were in the area we decided to stop here instead. We did arrive later in the evening, however the service was great, the host/cashier answered ALL our questions and even gave us some menu suggestions. The menu is pretty vast and has a lot of options for American food or Middle Eastern- they even have breakfast! I got curry chicken and he got chicken tikka (pictured) and grape leaves. We dined in and were pleased with the service, food and portion size. We will be back!!! Everything was great, no complaints & very refreshing to not worry about is it pork in anything. We even got dessert! (Not pictured).The chocolate cake was very good. Pretty great size & was moist/fresh. Next time we plan to try one of their Lassi- they have a few different kinds to choose from, and maybe a pizza. I think we found a new favorite place for us. We will be back!
I ordered this for our family  for Christmas.  The service  was excellent.   The food  was delicious.    I have been there been before this and would go again. Highly  recommend.

I don’t really love burgers. I was hungry at work and they’re across the street. My expectations weren’t high. Apparently I didn’t order right lol they called me back to ask if I wanted a plain burger yet ordered a deluxe. He added that and even hand delivered it. This was an awesome burger! Fresh ingredients and still hot. Fries were crispy! Definitely going to try more on their menu!

What an amazing experience! The platter was a true feast — tender grilled kebabs with a perfect smoky flavor, soft butter rice cooked just right, creamy hummus drizzled with olive oil, and warm pita bread that paired beautifully with every bite.

The salad was fresh and colorful, adding a refreshing touch to the rich, savory dishes. The presentation was neat and generous — every item placed with care. Their serving style shows real attention to detail and love for good food.

The restaurant’s environment was cozy, clean, and beautifully decorated — creating a calm and enjoyable dining vibe.
If you’re looking for delicious food that satisfies both the eyes and the taste buds, Al-Sham Restaurant is the perfect choice!

Tried the Greek pizza and hummus, and both were amazing! The pizza had a perfect crispy crust with fresh toppings and just the right amount of cheese. The hummus was creamy and flavorful...
Must Try...😀

formatted_address: 2730 W Girard Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19130, United States
name: Butter's Soul Food To Go

reviews.text: Butter's was our choice for New Year's fare:  catfish and tilapia, collards and cabbage, hoppin john and cornbread, and an extra side of lima beans for me. All of it was well seasoned, plentiful (well, maybe not the cornbread), and tasty. Our order was ready when we arrived and Benjamin was prompt and friendly behind the counter. Sending best wishes to Butter's for a prosperous 2026!

I wanted to give this place a shot. It fell very short of my expectations. Its a B.O.B so yes I wanted to support.  My ribs were all burnt. To the bone of 2 of the 3 ribs they gave me which were the small end of the rack. My greens were ok but alot of stems not enough green. Candied yams were good. Mac and cheese was Sub par dry and alittle crispy aroundcthe edge.We were the first customers of the day. How did I get burnt ribs, the small end like that was all that was left to give us that goes for the greens and Mac and cheese too. If it was not for the fact that we drove across town on lunch hour to get this I would return it for a refund. So I am forced to just eat whats edible and chalk it up. At this point I would not recommend this place to eat from. Please step your game up and give the people a good meal. I would send a pic of the platter if this website would let me.

The ambiance at Butter's was relaxing, welcoming and nostalgic, wonderful! The service was accomodating, nice and courteous. The food was just ok. We had the turkey wings, mac/cheese, collard greens and chicken wings. The rich flavors one anticipates in soul food was missing.  Many of the items on the menu weren't available. However, it was explained that they'd been closed for 3-days.

It's a small dining area but comfortable and calm. The food, in a word "delicious" flavored and seasoned well. I really enjoy the yams and barbecue spirits. The staff was respectful and friendly. I would like to visit again.

Food was horrible fish had no taste potato salad was missing  eggs mustard and relish. Barbecue ribs tasted like nothing no flavor only flavor you tasted was the barbecue sauce and it wasn’t too good.. llama beans with rice the lima beans was horrible. The taste of the beans was so nasty.. I won’t be eating there no more. The only thing that was good was the service that’s it.

formatted_address: 1115 Walnut St, Philadelphia, PA 19107, United States
name: Masala kitchen : Kati rolls and Platters

reviews.text:
THE FRIDAY/SATURDAY/SUNDAY NIGHT LATE SHIFT CREW IS INCREDIBLE.

I wholeheartedly vouch for Masala Kitchen as a whole, but these guys in particular someone manage to be everywhere all at once while still keeping up the impeccable quality that i’ve come to expect with Masala Kitchen over the years. Thank you guys so much for your service & honestly some of the most welcoming & truly heartwarming hospitality in city brothers!

I got a to go order of the masala roll in brown "bread" with eatra onions. The sauces were kinda meh. I've had a lot of fast food Indian food - most of it toyally sucks. This is literally the only time I've had good fusion Indian fast food. I thought the food was gonna suck. Wow. Blown away. It was spicy, flavorful, light... I can't say enough good things about this place. Good on you!

I had a great experience here with my friends. The food was absolutely amazing—fresh, flavorful, and perfectly prepared. What really made the visit special was the staff; they were welcoming, attentive, and made us feel comfortable throughout our time. The overall vibe was great, and everything exceeded our expectations. Definitely a must-visit place, and I’ll be coming back again!

My husband and I used to love this spot but hadn’t ordered in 5 months or so. We ordered 3 weeks ago and the food was so spicy we could barely get through it (neither of us remembered it being that way) and my stomach was upset for days. I wasn’t sure if it was the food or something else so we got it again tonight and again, the food was so spicy we have a whole platter leftover and both of our stomachs hurt. It’s just not worth the risk anymore. Such a shame

We ordered Uber eats from here and delivery was quick and food came to us hot.

The aloo Kathi roll was amazing (pro tip - add an egg to it as it balances the flavor profile with added bonus of some protein). The hot sauce it comes with is really good as well.

The beef Kathi roll was decent as well.

Not overly greasy, well seasoned and good value for money.

formatted_address: 2550 Grant Ave APT 320, Philadelphia, PA 19114, United States
name: The Halal Guys

reviews.text: It was my first time at this restaurant and I opted for a regular combo spicy bbq chicken and regular chicken. The staff was friendly and always smiling, customer service was 10/10, Food delicious 🤤 I will be back soon.

One of the short hispanic ladies with the mole and eye glasses, is extremely RACIST. Me and my mom have been going to this location for years and never had any major problems until I decided to go a couple nights ago by myself with a reward to redeem. (Mind you, we were kinda iffy about going to this location after she started working here because of her attitude at times but silly me decided to still go). It was a sandwich. I had gotten the hummus as one of the toppings but the reward excluded that which made the order have a remaining balance of $1.07, which I didn’t have at the time. So I had the lady remake it, and at the end of her making it, she was like “oh you have another sandwich reward?” And I was like “No….? Did you take the reward already?” She said “yeah”. So I was like ok well you can give me the sandwich you just made instead of the one with the hummus. She then proceeds to say “well the other sandwich is still in the system and I can’t take it off” I’m like ????? “Why not?” She goes “because it’s $1.07 still left” I’m like “Ok, I don’t have $1.07, that’s why I had you make another sandwich without the hummus added”. She THEN proceeds to tell me “I can’t take it out because then they’ll take it out of my check” I’m like girl what😭 so I said “So I can’t get my sandwich????” And she just shook her head no with this sly smile.

So im just looking at her right because you’re gonna give me my sandwich because when you redeem a reward, that means you’ve been spending enough money to get rewards in the first place, so technically that’s still my money. Second of all, that doesn’t make sense that everytime someone wants to discard an order, it’s gonna come out of YOUR paycheck??? So after our staring war of me looking at her and back at the sandwich and her staring at me with her head tilt and the smile remaining——the smile drops and she irritatingly switches the sandwich that has the hummus, with the new sandwich she made while saying something under her breath in Spanish with the nastiest attitude and gave me the sandwich. I said thank you and she ignored me. I won’t be returning to this location after my encounter with her that night. Everyone else is really nice in there, but SHE has this hidden animosity towards me for some reason which is cool because I’m never coming back to this grant one. I’m a Muslim supporting a Muslim establishment, but I refuse to tolerate disrespect.
Alexa and Elizabeth customer service go above and beyond, the foods are brilliant 😊

Days ago I came to buy 3 plates of food because I love the food here but one of the women who works in this place has served me very badly she is rude and it is not the only time she has served me and I came several times but I prefer to wait for the woman in the yellow shirt to serve me there are two women, on some occasions there is a man who attended me very well. I do not know their names I differentiate them by the color of their shirts, the one who serves badly is short with glasses and a red blouse that woman should not work serving people if she does not have patience she is a rude despot I am Muslim and there should not be people like her attending this place and as long as she is there neither I nor my family will return, it is a shame because the food was delicious I waited for the fresh chicken but not for the attention of this woman I support this establishment but for women like this I will not enter again, I do
The food is delicious, it was the first time I ordered a dessert and I decided on the chocolate baklava cheesecake and I loved it.

formatted_address: 4201 Chestnut St, Philadelphia, PA 19104, United States
name: Kabobeesh

reviews.text: I had okra for the first time, and it was fantastic!  I cherished every aspect of this restaurant. The lamb chops were delicious!  I swear, this is the best rice in the city!  The level of customer service was excellent!  I adore this restaurant.

Overall my experience with Egg I’m Late was moderate. The service was okay, but there were some areas that could be improved. I was a bit confused about the $7.99 charge I received and wasn’t sure why it applied. Aside from that, the place has potential, and with a few improvements in customer service and clarity on charges, it could offer a much better experience

We came to Philly for the night to see a concert. Asked for the best place to eat around. Hotel recommended Kabobeesh. We told them we were excited to try Pakistani food, that it was a first for our group of 3. She made the recommendation of a 1/2 Curry and mixed grill special. We added on an extra salad, 2 extra naan and 3 Samosas. Absolutely incredible. Food was immensely flavorful and perfectly seasoned. It was more than we could finish!  This will be an experience to remember!

AMAZING food, my Bf and I came in here hungry and the lady recommended the mixed platter. The mixed platter was amazing and definitely recommend it, it filled both of us. Everyone also is super friendly :)

I’ve been here three times with my family since coming to Philly, and I’ve loved it every single time. If you want to take your friends or family for authentic Pakistani/Desi food, this is THE spot to go. Everything from the Chargha to the boneless chicken kabob was delicious, and had heart and soul put into it. I do wish they would give customers a beeper to signal when their food is ready, since you must grab it yourselves from the counter, but you’ll forget that by the time you eat your first bite. Trust me, the aunties will love the food and the chai as they gossip. 9.5/10, would go again.

formatted_address: 211 E Gibbsboro Rd, Lindenwold, NJ 08021, United States
name: Taste of Africa Liberian Kitchen

reviews.text: Im so happy I came across this place on Google. 10/10 food was absolutely delicious and the owner/cook was so friendly and helped us decide on a dish to try. We had the egusi and fufu. I will definitely be coming back to try everything else.

If I could give a hundred stars I would. This food was amazing. The chef was honest and caring. She knows her way around the kitchen. I would definitely come back. I got the fried fish, potato greens and dry rice. I TORE it up. The fish didn’t last. So good!

When I tell you, I’m so happy that I don’t have to go to Philadelphia just to get some great African food. The fish was so well seasoning. It was so tasty and she cooked it to my perfection crunchy the pepper salad. I don’t know the exact name for it I thought I wasn’t gonna like it. It was so good. The rice, exactly the way that you expected to be. Not just yellow rice have vegetables and it was good most definitely will be going back actually as I’m writing in his review. I’m going back today.😁

Okay I was craving Jollof rice. I looked it up near me and this restaurant was closest I asked for Joloff Rice and received Vegetable Joloff Rice. It was good, but to be honest it lacked a spicey flavor kick I expected.  I've  had Joloff Rice before from my African co-workers, Nigerian, Liberian and others and I know each is made differently. Only one I did not like and I really can't remember what country my co-worker was from. I'm glad I ordered even though, it was not what I expected.

This is my new regular spot. Everything prepared fresh. Professional services, the lovely host was patient with explaining every dish. The price vs quality of food very fair considering the cost of food..
No complaints!!

formatted_address: 1507 Hermesprota Dr, Sharon Hill, PA 19079, United States
name: MJ Homemade Cuisine LLC

reviews.text: Food is always so delicious & portions are beyond generous. Im excited every time I get a platter. Must try believe me.
I ordered off of DoorDash. I got the dry rice and fish. It was fresh and delicious.. 10/10 I’ll definitely be ordering again was to feed two ppl with the portions .

Is this business fake or can somebody tell me the accurate times they are open I have been calling for days and there is no answer??? Or is this a business that just doesn’t answer the phone??? Can somebody please help me to figure out what is going on thank you I’m jus trying to find some good food around here sheesh!!!
The best I've e ever had! Staff are well trained with customer service! I will recommend this to EVERYONE. Some of my fav dishes are GB, palm butter, dried rice and fish. Just a few
My platter was excellent nice amount and very tasty.

formatted_address: 185 Dudley St, Boston, MA 02119, United States
name: Suya Joint

reviews.text: First time visiting here. I flew in from California and I knew that this was gonna be a spot that I must visit with all that has happened this year to the restaurant. I must say that I have been to numerous restaurants from the West to the East Coast and this restaurant is by far the most timely, organized, spot on customer service and simultaneously delicious dishes. I highly recommend. Next time I fly into Boston, I will stop by again. A big thank you to all the staff for making it a welcoming environment to be in.

My friends and I are obsessed with this place. We saw it mentioned online and went to try it - so glad that we did! The flavors are absolutely amazing. Rich and tender. We always do the beef suya plate with jollof rice and the egusi stew with pounded yam and split it so we get some of everything. The fried plantains are magical. Highly recommend!

I think this is one of the best food spots I've ever been to.
I was recommended Suya Joint by my friend, and I was very excited to try it because I've never had Nigerian food before. First, the service was friendly and fast. We ordered the dry rubbed chicken wings and beef samosas. I don't know what seasoning they use but it was delicious and the perfect level of spice where we can still enjoy our meal. The beef samosas were so light and flavorful too. We also ordered the African platter which consisted of jollof rice with plantains, egusi soup and fufu. We ordered extra goat as well. It was literally so mouth watering and amazing. Everything was perfect, seasoning was on point, and I enjoyed every minute of it. I would also recommend the pineapple cake for desert. Best way to end a spectacular dinner!!!!!!

Delicious food. Tons of veg and vegan options. Server explained that most of the items on the vegetarian menu are vegan. Just ask to be sure though. Taushe stew with pounded yam (in image) was excellent. Definitely coming back.

Me and my girlfriend came here two weeks ago in our visit to Boston. I am very particular about how my African foods are made, but this place is absolutely amazing! My girlfriend is Guatemalan, and when she tried their egusi and fufu she ended up dragging us back the next day!! Will be coming back on our next visit to Boston!

formatted_address: 950 American Legion Hwy, Roslindale, MA 02131, United States
name: Safari African Restaurant

reviews.text:
The safari donuts was fresh and hot. I enjoyed everything I ordered, they were all delicious.
The ginger drink was amazing, not too spicy.

Love this new location, the renovation makes this a great spot for any occasion, good eats, events, dates and a fun night out (they are open late 🙂)

Love the atcheke and lamb dish there the best! Their ginger drink is delicious

Management staff are always out in the space connecting with customers so please say hello !
Amazing food, friendly staff and welcoming environment. Enjoy coming here for their different types of spicy meats and great carbs(jollof rice, atieke, plantains)

Had an excellent meal here. I ordered the thieboudienne, bissap, baobab juice, and thiakry. Thieboudienne is incredibly delicious, the rice was cooked perfectly and the sauce that the food was cooked in was outstanding. It came with a hot sauce that was also phenomenal. The bissap and baobab juice were great and refreshing accompaniments. Honestly, being able to get baobab juice at all in this region is really impressive. I took the thiakry to go and enjoyed it, its great on a hot summer night and the millet provides a really interesting and nice texture for a dessert.

Service was great and hospitable, and there are many tables available. You can tell they take their food really seriously at this restaurant. Also, I didn’t get something with fufu but I saw another table get it and the fufu looked massive - definitely got to try that next time.

Best West African food I’ve had in Massachusetts so far.

I ordered Egusi soup, fufu and donuts (puff puff or Mandazi) through Uber Eats. It was delicious, I like that they put the hot sauce on the side so I can add as I like it. I donuts were nice and soft. I enjoyed my meal.

formatted_address: 146 Belgrade Ave, Roslindale, MA 02131, United States
name: Obosa Restaurant

reviews.text: This is a well run Nigerian restaurant with nice interior decor. The menu is small and a bit pricey, but that means they’re good at what they make. The flavor was great and seemed authentic with lots of other Nigerian patrons (I’m not Nigerian). They’re fully stocked with Nigerian drinks. The lamb was slightly too dry but that’s my only complaint.

My first time visiting. I had lunch I with my sister, a local who has been here before. I had the Jollof rice and moi moi with chicken. My sister had the egusi with chicken. We shared some puff puffs.We were disappointed that they were out of the Suya ( beef and chicken).
We both enjoyed our respective meals, so much so that we placed an order of moi moi, Jollof rice and puff puffs to go.
Service was excellent.

Food is mediocre at best. I ordered Jollof rice with Goat stew. Food was cooked well, just lacked seasoning/flavor. Hopefully they can work on this. Lady who collected payment looked mean and was nonchalant. Also it doesn’t smell too great in there, they should definitely work on that.

I went to Obosa Restaurant on an afternoon lunch date for my first try at West African food. The younger staff were so pleasant & helpful. They saw we weren’t familiar with the menu & took their time in explaining & accommodating some vegetarian options.

All of their food was cooked to perfection.

-Their “puff puff”(not pictured because we shamelessly devoured them & ordered another round to go) was delicious.
-The fufu & stew was well portioned, beautifully plated & so  delicious.
-The jollof rice was *fantastic & their plantains were perfectly fried.

I tried their fish soup & quickly learned they don't skimp on spice- which I appreciate- but if you don't have a high tolerance for pepper, I'd proceed with caution.

Worth mentioning too, their restaurant was immaculately clean. If you’re trying Nigerian food for the first time, I’d start with Obosa.

Obosa used to be reliable, but something has changed recently. I ordered delivery two nights in a row. The first night, they forgot an item. I gave them grace, assuming it was a one-off. The second night, I specifically requested ripe, soft, sweet plantains. What I received were half-green, hard, and bland slices that looked like they were rushed through with water and oil. Not the quality I expected. Disappointed overall.

formatted_address: 389 Centre St, Boston, MA 02130, United States
name: Blue Nile Restaurant

reviews.text: The food here was delicious. The sambosa was crispy and filled with slightly spicy lentils. The meat dishes are all served on a slightly sour and very tasty bread/pancake called injera. I had the lamb (yebeg tibs) and it was great - so flavorful and tender. I didn't try the 2 kinds of beef or chicken that my company ordered, but according to them it was great! My side of collard greens was equally delightful. The reason it's not 5 stars is the price of the food for the amount you get. Ordering a combo (meat dish + a side order of a vegetable dish) helps the price but the helpings were noticeably small for the price. That being said, Blue Nile is a great place to check out if you're in the area.

Came in here on a cold winter night & was warmed every way, from the people to the food and drink. My dish was delicious, warming, perfectly spiced. Their injera is made with 100% teff and has a wonderful nutty flavor. I can’t wait to go back and try more dishes there. Well worth a visit.

This was our second time visiting Blue Nile since moving to Boston, and it has quickly become a favorite. The service has been consistently attentive and friendly, which enhances the dining experience.

We always order a vegetable combo at Ethiopian restaurants, and Blue Nile’s did not disappoint—fresh, flavorful, and absolutely delicious! Tonight, we also tried a chicken dish and a lamb dish (unfortunately, I can’t recall the names), but both were fantastic. The highlight, though, was the sambosa—we ordered 4 for our table of 4, and it wasn’t nearly enough! Filled with perfectly spiced lentils, they were some of the best sambosas I’ve ever had.

The restaurant is small, so I recommend making a reservation during cooler months when the patio isn’t an option. That said, dining outdoors in early fall was a treat with their lovely patio setup.

We’ll definitely be returning to enjoy more of their amazing dishes. Highly recommend!

Not worth it. Ordered the Doro Tibs Combo for take-out, got a half-empty container of pretty bland diced white chicken. The side dish (Misir Wat) was missing, and the chicken was overcooked and sitting in a pool of liquid. Definitely not worth $25+.

The best Ethiopian restaurant I’ve been to!

The pool of Ethiopian restaurants I’ve been to is not very large, but the food in this place is really delicious and they have gotten recognition for it based on the certificates on the wall and all.

We tried their veggie combos and their lentil samosas. The samosas were some of the most delicious ones I’ve ever had.

This is a great place for a date, meeting up friends, or simply for enjoying a delicious meal.

I’m sure I’ll be back there soon.

formatted_address: 924 Morton St, Mattapan, MA 02126, United States
name: Pelloma Nigerian Cuisine

reviews.text:
Great place to find everything Nigerian cuisine. Though not very spacious for large groups and parking can be a challenge, great for quick pickups, Uber Eats and the like.
They however may want to replace the menu QR code posted on the wall…it’s a little bit defaced.

I ordered Afang soup, which was very delicious. This is the only Nigerian restaurant I have found in Boston that sells Afang soup (correct me if I'm wrong).
But my concern is that the portion of the soup is significantly smaller than at other restaurants, and to be honest, I also think it's small for the price. Hopefully, they do something about it.
Overall, the food was good.

The food was delicious, but I felt like the pricing was not transparent. When I entered, there was no visible menu, and the prices were only displayed on a photo of the menu. I was charged $25 for jaloff rice, four pieces of plantain, and two pieces of beef stew, but according to the Google Maps menu, the price should’ve been $15. I usually pay around $15 or $16 for similar dishes at other places, so this felt overpriced. While the food was tasty, I believe the pricing should be more clear and consistent with what’s advertised.

Food was good, would like to return but service could be better, gentleman with the facial hair was very rude and sassy. We asked for to go plates and told him how much we wanted, and he said “that’s too much” he gave it to us anyways but still that’s unwarranted for. There’s things you should keep to yourself . When I asked for a drink, he asked me if I was okay because I told him I didn’t care about the brand of drink I wanted. On the other hand, there was a sweet woman there. As for the gentleman, please work on your attitude. Customer service is important and shapes the face of a company! Cheers!

Unexceptional Nigerian cuisine. Staff are nice enough, and the restaurant is your typical small scale affair, but the jollof and fried rice I tried were definitely not an exciting taste of Nigerian food, especially compared to the alternatives available in Boston and Worcester. Hopefully the soups will be better.

formatted_address: 84 Massachusetts Ave, Cambridge, MA 02139, United States
name: Tawakal Halal

reviews.text: Delicious halal Somali restaurant inside the MIT Students Center food court. Food was sold over a counter in Styrofoam boxes. We had beef biryani which was tasty. Beware of the hot sauce offered separately. It is very hot. We were given tea for free.

Finished MIT tour, we walked in student center 2nd floor.
Those meals are so special, but yam!
Chicken Flatbread is good!

We had a layover at Boston BOS, took a free airport shuttle to get to the Tawakal Cafe and had biryani, spaghetti and fries for to-go. While waiting we were served some free cookies and chai. Food are great, generous portion, fries are out of the world. Service was great. Will definitely come back as again insha Allah.

The best Somali food in town. Tried their chicken and rice - absolutely delicious, and they included Sambusa with my order 🤩

FYI: Found the place inside MIT on the 2nd floor. Got a bit lost with maps, but called their number on Google, and they guided me in. The Google pics show another branch in East Boston( not sure if the East Boston spot is open atm ), but the new spot inside MIT is where it's at.

Small cozy place! Really great family-feel restaurant and the servers really made us feel like we were having dinner at someone's house! It was my first time trying Somali food, and oh man, the flavors are so unique! A blend of Indian, Middle Eastern and African cuisines, I was surprised by the combination and loved it! The homemade chili sauce is to die for, don't underestimate the white one which looks pretty mild....you're in for a surprise :)

formatted_address: 10 Crescent St, Waltham, MA 02453, United States
name: Karibu Restaurant

reviews.text:
This place was... strange.  First I'll say the food was excellent.   We got the beef stew, chicken platter, spicy samosa, and fried donut.  The beef stew was some of the best stew I have ever had.  Everything else was top tier.

The strange part was the atmosphere and service.  First, the location is set back from the street and looks like a hole in the wall.  Once inside its a big room with tables and a small counter section with food partially visible partially not.  See the images.  No menu, no prices, no people.

Eventually we noticed a woman in the corner who got up, walked into the kitchen and got someone to help us.  They showed us some of the food, gave no indication of what prices anything was nor what would be purchased together.

After some back and forth with us asking about things not mentioned we randomly got things.  My wife got, a potato, some rice, some veggies, and chicken stew.  That was a platter for $22.  My beef stew was $9, and each of my two samosa and 2 fried donuts cost around $2 each.

I really want to rate this higher because of the food, but the atmosphere was so off for us I just can't.

My first time trying Ugandan food. When I entered the restaurant, it felt as if I was entering someone’s home as a guest, who like to take care of you before anything else. I wanted to try stuff so had the beef stew, chapati, beans, spinach , tea , kabalaga (pancake) and the mandazi (donut). The chapati with beef stew and the kabalaga with tea were pairs made in heaven.

We drove over three hours from Brooklyn, New York to Waltham, Massachusetts to go to this restaurant. We’d heard they had very good Ugandan food. My husband and I had all foods with a chicken stew and my husband had the fish. The fish wasn’t that great, but everything else was ok. The food wasn’t worth the drive, but it’s one person’s opinion. We also bought some Mandazi. Those were really good.

I went in with my girlfriend a little more than an hour before close. We did not understand how to order, when an old soft spoken lady came up to us. I thought she was a customer, but she was a server. She explained they were out of most foods because it's later, but they still had beef and rice. We told her it was fine and she told us to make ourselves comfortable.

There were some loud men, tough looking men at different tables speaking different languages. It was a bit off putting at first, but after we were there a few minutes we started to get smiles and greetings. It seemed they were just taken aback by us because we were different than everyone else. Everyone I interacted with was very friendly, and it felt safe.

It felt like I was being served by the sweet mother of a good friend. We were brought bowls of beef soup and large plates of rice. As we ate, she continued to bring out food. More beef broth, more beef, a vegetable salad. She would bring out the food, tell us what it was and make sure she got some approval before setting it down.

We got up to smoke at one point. She rushed over to cover our food with plates. I was very impressed by the attention to food safety they had, especially for a small resturant.

The food was delicious. The beef still had bone on it and had a pot roast texture to it. The rice had a chinese food fried rice taste to it, but all of the food had a blend of spices I had never tried before. It was not very spicy, but it was good enough it did not need to be.

I was wondering if I was going to get stuck with a big bill and the end as I had not inquired about the prices. The bill was just over $40 with two bottles waters. My girlfriend and I are big eaters, but we both ate as much as we could, had left over later that night and then for lunch the next day. The price for the portions was definitely good.

I haven't written many reviews, but this place deserved 5 starts.

Avoid !!!🥵 Was going to try East African food . Nothing looked palatable. Nothing what the other reviewers had was available ! This was at lunch time . Beef stew was swimming in oil
Be aware they charge different prices for different people .
I bought Mandazi , Somosas and Bhajias .
Mandazi was stale and sour , samosas had a weird taste . 🥵 As it was a takeout I called next day  to complain also found out I was over charged.

formatted_address: 51 Roxbury St, Boston, MA 02119, United States
name: Fasika Cafe

reviews.text: Delicious food with amazing service and atmosphere. They have a large traditional menu with generous portions. Every plate ordered was always scrumptious! The best Ethiopian restaurant in the Boston area! Whether dining in or ordering out, this place is highly recommended!

Today 10/8/2025 ordered kitfo from this restaurant, but what I received was not kitfo at all. When I brought the food home and opened it, it was overcooked, burned, and tasted like a spicy steak, nothing close to the traditional Ethiopian kitfo I ordered. It was so spicy and dry that neither I nor my friend could eat it.

I immediately called the restaurant to ask for a replacement, expecting basic courtesy and customer service. However, the person who answered, who identified himself as the owner, was extremely rude and unprofessional. Instead of apologizing or offering a solution, he insisted that he made exactly what I ordered. When I requested a replacement, he told me that I would have to pay again for a new order, even though the mistake was clearly on their side.

As a paying customer, I have every right under U.S. Consumer Protection Laws to receive the product I actually ordered. If a business provides the wrong or defective item, they are legally obligated to either replace it or issue a refund, not charge the customer twice. Refusing to correct an error and denying a replacement is unethical and potentially unlawful.

Furthermore, I noticed a concerning issue with discriminatory treatment. It appears that certain customers, especially non Ethiopian patrons, receive apologies and fresh orders, while Ethiopian or Habesha customers like myself are dismissed without respect. Discrimination in service violates federal and state civil rights laws and is absolutely unacceptable.

This restaurant clearly lacks professionalism, respect, and accountability. Until management is properly trained in customer service, consumer rights, and anti discrimination law, I cannot recommend this place to anyone.

If you value honesty, fairness, and cultural respect, avoid this restaurant.

So delicious, flavorful enjoyed by the 2 adults and two 10 year olds and two 12 year olds new to Ethiopian food!  We didn't know what to order from an extensive menu and Ms. Misty recommended the combo plates with a little bit of everything and it was perfect!  Kids loved beef, chicken, lentil ones the most.  I loved the chickpea and cabbage.  Also love the cozy, friendly vibe of the place.  We'll definitely be back!

I love revisiting Fasika every once in a while, because they are consistently excellent. It's a friendly, quiet, small business with made-to-order food. It's incredibly soothing and nourishing - the pure opposite of restaurants that rely on social media style gimmicks.

Authentic food & small family restaurant. Everything we had was Delicious! Meal for 2 Combo with 2 proteins, 4 sides. Gored Gored was cooked perfectly (Med rare, tender, Spicy) & Kitfo, also perfectly prepared with spice, Yemis Wot (Red lentils), Tikil Gomen, (yellow Chickpeas, mild) Tikil Gomen (potato/carrot/collared greens, mild), Ayeb Begomen (Cottage cheese with spices, mild). We added Ye Doro Tibs (medium spiced diced white chicken in BerBere). I've had Tons of Ethiopian food around the country & I can assure you this is what you're looking for in terms of quality & taste & value. Glad we ordered extra food so I can bring some back to central NH for the next day. I'm going to have one more bite before bed since I'm thinking about it now.

formatted_address: 266 Bowdoin St, Dorchester, MA 02122, United States
name: Restaurante Cesaria

reviews.text: Fancy nightclub is an accurate representation, wouldn't go back but food was OK

Omg my wife and I went there for the first time and we both loved! I got the katchupada refugada and I loved it my wife got arroz de marisco and loved to! Drinks were perfect. Thanks to our server he was constantly there checking us on our food and drinks! We will definitely be back.

Came here with my buddy on the recommendation of an uber driver. Food was great, prices were great, and the atmosphere with the live music and families dancing was exactly what I was hoping for. Very strongly recommend you give this authentic Cape Verde spot a try

I love the fact they have a buffet, that's all I come for it's not a lot of options but I still love it. There soup is very good and so is the rice n beans. I eat in at least 3 times a week. I love the vibe staff and food.
Burnt steak only 4 tiny pieces for $26 not worth it for a plate full of French fries. And the wait was an HOUR FOR THIS TERRIBLE FOOD!

formatted_address: 2306 Washington St, Boston, MA 02119, United States
name: RedRed Kitchen

reviews.text: We had Jollof rice, Turkey tail, Egusi stew and fufu and fried turkey! It’s the best African food I’ve eaten thus far in Boston! the turkey meat is so tender and other dishes are so flavourful. Worth the find! Customer service is excellent! 🌟🤩🔥💞🙌🏼

Great service & even better food!
Their lunch plates are the best deal and everything on the plates is done soooooooo generously. They also serve ginger juice and sorrel; the ginger is quite refreshing. I do recommend skipping the peach cobbler though.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ 5/5 Stars

Red Red Kitchen is an absolute gem! The food is full of authentic African flavors — fresh, perfectly seasoned, and made with so much care. Every dish feels like a taste of home. The jollof rice is incredible, the stews are rich and flavorful, and the plantains are always cooked just right.

The staff is friendly and welcoming, and the atmosphere is cozy with a real sense of culture and community. You can tell they take pride in what they do, from the presentation to the service.

If you’re looking for real African comfort food made with love, Red Red Kitchen is the place to go. Highly recommend — you’ll definitely want to come back for more!

Visiting from Canada through Boston to Rhode Island and found them on google. The food and service delivery was superb. Great customer service from the entire team.
Just wish they’d take the orders on phone especially coming from out of State. Not sure if that’s a Boston thing.

But food, service and atmosphere was ‘mmmwwwaaaah’ … will definitely go there again when next I’m in that area

Despite some negative reviews we decided to give a try to this place as there are not many Ghanaians restaurants in this area.

Fried rice with chicken was so good. Fufu was not available unfortunately (apparently they only have it on some days but it was not written anywhere). We also had Kenke and turkey which was so tasty !!’
The Dine-in atmosphere of the place is not that great but if you buy takeaway then you won’t experience it.

The goat meat was soft and tasty while the Chofi was very fatty! Will buy from them again.

formatted_address: 739 Massachusetts Ave, Cambridge, MA 02139, United States
name: Asmara

reviews.text: Great vegetarian options, and excellent friendly service. No silverware (you can ask for some). The combo plates are served with bread in the bottom and you eat with you hands, very cool. The Honey wine is also a must!

I got the Begeeh Mloukhiyah and my friends got the Sega Bebaynatu-Meat Combination. I found the portion size for the Begeeh Mloukhiyah to be quite small, especially for the price. The flavor of the Mloukhiyah was quite good. If the portion size was larger I would return. As far as the meat combo, the portion seemed much larger even though we only got 1 order of it. However, the meat was very dry and was quite disappointing because I think the potential was there flavor wise. We also had to order more injera with the food, and it is $3 for each extra piece which seems like a rip off. Unfortunately, I don’t think I will be returning here unless significant changes are made. If you do pay them a visit, I would still recommend the Mloukhiyah just for the flavor and the fact that you probably won’t be able to find this kind of food elsewhere!

Just wonderful all around! Friendly and helpful service, delicious food (similar to Ethiopian), and warm atmosphere. I’ve eaten in many Eritrean (and Ethiopian) restaurants, but never had the option for seating traditional style (around a basket filled with injera and dishes with small tables to the side for drinks) or western seating (at a flat table). Delicious, Italian-style desserts. I would definitely return!

Amazing, amazing!

The food is delicious and the arrangement of the food is appealing, especially on the traditional Eritrean stool/table.

The ambience is so beautifully Eritrean. It's homey: the curtains, the art, the flowers hanging from the roof, everything.

The service was excellent, kind.

I'd recommend going here for a date, especially in the evenings when the lighting is dim yet sufficient. It creates an intimate environment that feels romantic.

I tried this place out with my brother. We ordered the Sega Bebaynatu-Meat Combination. The server asked us “for two people?” And we said yes because we were going to split the plate. After we got the bill, they charged us for two plates. When we asked, she said it’s because we said it was for 2 people. I didn’t expect that our answer would translate to creating portions and plates for each person, because it came on just one big plate. I feel like when servers ask “for two people”, it means to split up the food between two of us, not to charge twice. In that case, I would’ve just ordered for the same plate twice! Like “can we have TWO sega…” Also, the desert options were available through a verbal menu only, so the price was transparent there either. We didn’t find out the price of everything, including dessert, until we got the bill. I ended up paying double than I was expecting and I just wish things were better communicated. For example, after we confirmed that yes, the dish we ordered is for the two of us to share, that they would reaffirm that they were going to charge us for two plates.

formatted_address: 291 Roxbury St, Roxbury, MA 02119, United States
name: Ashur Restaurant

reviews.text: Went on Saturday evening, great sized portions, delicious flavors. Lamb shank was very tender. There was a little odor in the dining area though

If you're a foodie seeking an unforgettable dining experience in Boston, Ashur, a Somali restaurant in the heart of Roxbury, is an absolute must-visit. The moment you step inside, the rich aroma of perfectly spiced dishes welcomes you, hinting at the culinary delight to come.

I enjoyed a generous plate featuring a variety of meats—lamb, goat, and chicken—each cooked to perfection and infused with an array of spices that elevated the flavors to new heights. The rice was a perfect complement, absorbing the flavors beautifully and adding to the overall experience.

The hospitality at Ashur is second to none. The staff are warm, attentive, and make you feel right at home, enhancing the dining experience. The artful paintings and decor add a unique charm, creating a vibrant and inviting atmosphere. Additionally, the ample parking outside ensures a hassle-free visit, making it convenient for everyone.

Ashur restaurant stands out not just for its exceptional food, but also for its inviting atmosphere and top-notch service. Whether you're a local or visiting Boston, this hidden gem in Roxbury is a culinary adventure you won't want to miss.

Their food taste African and delicious. I visit the area during convention, searched African restaurant near me & Ashur came out. I went to Ashur each day 12mins drive based on the positive online reviews & it was good. I tried the goat meat, lamp & chicken all taste good👌.You may be a bit discouraged by the environment but the food tastes good.

The food here was amazing—especially the white sauce and red sauce that were given as  a condiment. Personally, I felt that the white sauce blew any other white sauce out of the water. I have had white sauce at many other restaurants, and none of them were anything to write home about. The food itself was phenomenal. The place might not look like much, but it’s a hidden gem, and it’s because they focus on making good food. If you want halal food in Boston, this is the place to get it. The milk tea was also really good. Whoever created these recipes and cooked the food really knows what they’re doing.

I went here with friends. I wouldn’t really call this Middle Eastern cuisine. The spice level is less than mild. The food (goat cubes, lamb, chicken biryani, samboosas) also came out astonishingly fast, a sign that it was reheated. One of my friends said the chai was fantastic though. The restaurant was very community oriented- I’d come here again for the vibe, but not the food. The staff was very pleasant and polite. Something to take note of is that all of the patrons seemed to only have chai and not food. If you want something strong, spicy, and fresh at 7 pm, go to Nachlo- they also make homemade mango lassis. Their dishes are also $15 compared to the $20 here.

formatted_address: 63-65 Poplar St, Roslindale, MA 02131, United States
name: Evidence of Trust: African Wholesale and Retail Store:

html_attributions: Evidence of Trust: African Wholesale and Retail Store:

reviews.text: Very clean and organized. I love the quality and freshness of the products as well!

Small , but you will get anything here for making African dish. Their prices are actually cheaper than going to the big tropical stores. Very polite and friendly people. The only issue is nobody really knows they are there . They need to advertise. Their products are authentic and cheap. If everybody knows  where they are,  they will skyrock. Highly recommended
Have a lot of desirable items, and variability. The workers are kind, and if there is any load that might be to heavy, like yam, there always ready to help!
Nice store and they have everything you want and the mama there is nice person😃 ❤ 😍
I have been there several times, the owner is so nice and welcoming.

formatted_address: 1746 Washington St, Boston, MA 02118, United States
name: Mesob Restaurant and Bar

reviews.text:
Had the pleasure of trying out Mesob during their opening week and it was fantastic! We ordered the sweet red wine from Ethiopia and the Tej, a honey wine that they make in house. For our meal we shared the timtimo and tsebhi dorho. Super flavorful and delicious. As spice lovers, we didn’t find it too spicy- just right.

The owner Kirby and his wife were incredibly welcoming and gracious, explaining the different dishes to us. We had a wonderful experience and can’t wait to come back to try more of the menu!

Mesob is hands down the best Ethiopian/Eritrean restaurant in Boston. From the moment you walk in, everything feels just right. The atmosphere, the hospitality from the hostess, and of course, the food are all outstanding. My favorite dish was the Derek Tibs; the perfect char gives it an incredibly savory and satisfying flavor. The regular tibs were just as delicious and full of rich taste. Overall, I had an amazing night and a wonderful experience, and I will absolutely be returning in the future.

Absolutely loved this place. Delicious food, generous portions and very friendly staff and welcoming atmosphere. Everything tasted fresh and comforting, just like home. I’ll definitely be coming back. Highly recommend 👌👍

Amazing amazing meal. Highlights were the Tsebhi Dorho and Alicha Fajul - both were so flavorful. We ordered everything to share and truly everything exceeded expectations. The service was wonderful and cocktails were unique and well made. I would 10/10 recommend for anyone in the Boston area.
Great food overall. I tried the Derek and regular tibs, and finished with the lamb chops. Everything was excellent. Highly recommend checking this place out.

formatted_address: inside the food court mall, Squre one mall, 1201 Broadway, Saugus, MA 01906, United States
name: Mariam yummy kitchen

reviews.text: Someone told me to try this place. It did not disappoint. I got efo, eguis, fish roll and jollof rice. I really enjoy the jollof and fish roll. I have not eaten the fufu and efo yet. The staff was very nice and accommodating to all my questions. The price was fair compared to where I normally buy in Chicago.

I feel scammed for paying $30 for this. It was soooo salty (many other reviewers said the same exact thing), I threw everything out after a couple of bites. Very disappointed as I came here specifically after reading positive reviews on Google.

The Best Fresh Food!
This was my first time trying fufu!! The owner was so helpful and I tried two different dishes put together perfectly. The beef with greens and the chicken with pumpkin. Both were AMAZING!

Food presentation and taste was just horrible!!! The plantains were burnt, Jollof rice tasted terrible. Omg don’t even get me started on the Eva and okro soup. I have never seen or tasted anything so disgusting. It looked life leftover meals. Just so disappointed. Do not eat here!!!!

Trash. Overpriced for garbage food. I don’t mind paying high prices if the food is worth it. This was disgusting. Jollof Rice tasted completely burnt, I threw out my entire plate. And I am Nigerian so I Know what it’s supposed to taste like. Whoever is running this place needs to shut it down immediately, or ask for help!

formatted_address: 60 Seaport Blvd #325, Boston, MA 02210, United States
name: Grace By Nia

reviews.text:
Tyler, the hostess, was wonderful. We stopped by the night before as walk-ins, but there was no availability. Tyler suggested we return the next day, made our reservation, and even secured us a great seating location since we were visiting from out of town. The venue itself was beautifully decorated with a great, lively vibe.

The food was flavorful and well-portioned for the price of $48. My friend and I both ordered the oxtail and grits. The oxtails were a good size, and two pieces were included. The grits were creamy and delicious without needing any added seasoning. While everything tasted great, I would have preferred the food to be served a bit hotter—it was warm, but not quite hot enough.

The drinks were strong and well-made. The live band was also excellent—they interacted with the audience and were very entertaining. Overall, it was a great experience, and if I’m ever back in Boston, I would definitely return.

When my friend and I got there, we did wait at the bar until our table was ready, our bartender Sammy was awesome he was very engaging with us, we also shared some laughs, the ambience was awesome. Once we got to our table our server Jesu’s waiting on us, he was also amazing. He went down the menu and explained everything and answered all questions. He was very helpful and made sure that we had everything that we needed. The food was very tasty I’m not a crab cake person, but I did get them and they were so good with the salad that came on the side, The dressing was exquisite. The band was also amazing. It was an all out good time/experience. Would definitely go again 💛

Had a vibrant experience here , as expected based on the first hand recommendation I got( from a older couple ) and Google reviews.  I expected a   rich mix of Jamaican/ southern cuisine and that was up to par. My favorite was the upsidedown pineapple cake with coconut- to die for! That pasta was just delish - what an 👏 amazing sauce!
I booked a table at the stage which was worth the added cost for entertainment but be aware it can be very loud when its time to chat with your server and your diner guests. I think Because the area is so small and clustered at the stage is just felt awfully loud because the maximized all space so you're literally sitting at the stage. Lol
This ambiance is one for mingling and having fun..not your mellow jazz and eat, its more up tempo and very vibrant scene .
That weekend night a week ago was off to a delayed start. Almost a 20 minute wait for all 9:30 seating and Im wondering if its because its such a entertainment atmosphere,  people hardly leave their table , because are enjoying the show they paid for. Not sure, but my guess.
Other than that, great night. Pleasant staff, very charming!
I recommend this place for a fun night on the town- girlfriends,  couples outing if looking for a upbeat night.
Id go back, but not a big deal like that for me.

Service was amazing from the moment we walked through the doors. Our waitress was great, but the server who placed our food on the table was rude and rolled her eyes because we had a large group and she wasn't sure where to put the plates. It was a small confusion, and the eye roll was unnecessary and uncalled for. Other than that, great vibes, great music, and delicious food, especially the ribs and mac and cheese—great choice! The chicken was great, a large portion, and mine needed a little salt, but it was an excellent choice. We had a great time and felt very welcomed.

Came from Chicago for the Holidays.  The food, the entertainment, the service, the ambiance!  WOW!  Shout out to our server Jesus who took care of us; GREAT JOB!  Fantastic performance by Rahsaan Langley Project.  We went lite this evening on our meal (Caesar salad with Chicken, sorry no pics of our food), but it was very good.  Wife had the lemon drop; I had the unfashioned; drinks were spot on!  We will definitely be back!

formatted_address: 334 Massachusetts Ave, Boston, MA 02115, United States
name: Lucy Ethiopian Cafe

reviews.text: Lucy’s was one of the best restaurants I’ve had in Boston so far. The staff was incredibly kind, and incredibly helpful; however, the food blew me away. We got the chicken Combo platter which was full of flavor, and had a great spice level. The sides were delicious, and complemented our chicken very nicely. Beyond all of this I had just gotten out of class, so i had my backpack with my computer, and all of my class work underneath the table. In a moment of stupidity I left it overnight, but they held onto it for me without me even asking, and I was able to pick it up the next day. If you love flavorful food, and a cozy environment Lucy’s should be top of your list for a visit.

The food is 10/10. It's hard to find ethiopian food outside of the Boston area, and this place didn't disappoint. The combo options are great to try and little of everything, and delicious.
The space us very cozy, warm and inviting, perfect for a quick lunch or for a date.

The absolute best thing about this place is the staff. The staff were so kind, very friendly, and actually chased us down on the street to return a hat we left. Just fantastic people.

We'll be returning whenever we get the chance to be in the area.

Really enjoyed coming here.  Portion sizes are average (not especially large) considering the prices. I really liked the vegetable options, and the lamb was good, better than the beef imo.

Service was fine, ordering was easy through the QR codes, though you can also order up front.

Pros: Food tasted good and fresh. I also liked that you order through a QR code.

Cons: Portion sizes are definitely way too small for the cost. It’s actually frustrating thinking about how cheap lentils and that kind of thing are and then looking at the tiny portion. We paid $50 for a shared plate, it could’ve at least been filled full.

Wonderful service and while the prices may look on the higher side, you get a great portion. Injera was perfect and all the dishes were spiced wonderfully. Ethiopian coffee was strong and very tasty. If you’re in the area and need a quick bite, give this place a try!

formatted_address: 490 W Main St, Avon, MA 02322, United States
name: TamBo's Kitchen

reviews.text:
My first and last visit to this location. The experience was extremely disappointing.
The customer service was poor, the lady taking my order was rude and clearly annoyed when I asked a simple question about what was included in the meal.
More seriously, the food quality was unacceptable. After driving an hour home, the Egusi Stew smelled overwhelmingly spoiled, and the texture was gritty. Like sand was in it!! This was a wasted two-hour round trip and a total disappointment. Don’t  recommend this location. Buyer beware of the 3-star rating.

The staff is 100% rude but the amala was pretty decent 4/10. The ewedu was definitely not fresh!! I called last week Monday to place an order around 7pm for pick-up between 7:30-7:40pm. The lady was so rude and condescending over the phone and demanded that I arrived by 7:30pm. I was craving amala so I just accepted and made my way to pick-up. The way she grudgingly took my order was insulting. On the way, the staff called me rudely asking where I was, yelling that she was closing the store because she had to drive over an hour to get home in Framingham. I told the lady that their hours stated open till 8pm plus I was still within my proposed timeframe, even explaining that I met traffic along the way. She was loud and asked me to turn back. I had to beg her to let me get my order. Upon arrival she was so rude with no greeting or proper acknowledgment. I made sure to take my time to check my order after paying and she was disgustingly waiting by the door like I was bothering her. If you know you what a successful business, learn compassion and/or train your staff to value customers. I will not be returning!!!

Ordered egusi. I admit it looked like vegetable soup less of egusi but the owner came back and added more egusi! I’ll rate the food maybe 3/5. The tripe4.5/5 beef 4.9/5 and cow skin 3/5. The service was exceptional.

If you're looking for something outside of the usual New England fare and want to try something different- this place is fantastic. If you like Caribbean food or Jamaican food you'll love this place. I will say the flavors here are better than most Jamaican places - all of the dishes were bursting with flavor. The dining room is small but the woman who owns it greeted us and served us and she was about as nice as could possibly be. She served us some kind of red meat that was stewed with lots of tendons and cartilage - one of my personal favorite parts of beef - it was so delicious my daughter told me not to eat it all.  Will def be going back!

This was my first time here and also having fufu. It was very good!

We ordered the pounded yam, okra sauce with goat meat added, a large pepper soup they kindly split in two bowls for my friend and I to share.

The sauce that comes with the fried plantain is AMAZING, pairs perfectly with the sweetness of the plantain. (I find it to be mild, but it may be a little spicy if you don’t typically prefer spicy food.) I had to ask for extra.

Wonderful service, they made sure we had everything we needed.

formatted_address: 1127 Harrison Ave, Roxbury, MA 02119, United States
name: Khadija's Express cafe

reviews.text: Excellent halal food for reasonable prices (better than Ashur). It’s a hidden halal food gem in Boston. The downside is hygiene and cleanliness. Can definitely be cleaner
It looks like a ran down place on the outside, but the food is absolutely delicious 🤤 the owner is a very nice guy. The salmon is my favorite, the lamb is to die, the rice cooked to perfection.

VERY POOR CUSTOMER SERVICE. TERRIBLE CUSTOMER AS A MATTER OF FACT! THEY WILL LET GIRLS STAND AND WAIT TO ORDER  WHILE THEYLL PUT A MAN WHO JUST COME AFTER YOU. THIS ESTABLISHMENTS IS HIGHLY DISAPPOINTING AND DISRESPECTFUL. DO BETTER WITH CUSTOMER!!! DO NOT RECOMMEND EVER.
Amazing food absolutely delicious and worth every penny amazing prices but seems to have been moved anyone know where they moved to?
I got one thing: homemade samosas with fish in them. Guy on the phone was like, "Are you sure? We only have fish left." These were the most delicious samosas of all time!!!

formatted_address: 138 Boston St, Lynn, MA 01904, United States
name: Global kitchen and banquet

reviews.text: The fish here is truly delightful and perfectly seasoned. Since this is a function hall rather than a typical restaurant, it offers a cozy and spotless environment that makes you feel right at home. I had a wonderful experience and can't wait to come back many times. The owner, originally from Cameroon, offers a diverse menu featuring African, Italian, and other delicious dishes—there's something to satisfy every craving. If you're looking to indulge your taste buds, I highly recommend visiting! I love fish, and I must say, this is the best I've ever had in this country. It's quite affordable; I even brought some dishes home to enjoy later. If you're nearby, I suggest doing the same—that way, you can savor more later. For locals, it's absolutely a treasure. I hope you get to experience it yourself!

I literally came from Wilmington ma to get food because my people got food and it was bomb, well the fried beef. When I arrived the front end associate was not friendly nor was he professional l. Waited like another 4-5 min for my food when on the phone he was some what rushing me because they close at 10 but I told him I would be there at 930. Now it’s time to ring up the food and he looks like he is legit making a price up either way my meal was $33 for some rice and beef never again will I order from there highway robbery I mean when I looked up the price on the menu the rice was 10 and the meant was 13 idk where the extra 10 came from. Just sharing maybe if your there race it will be cheaper (it was giving)

Global Kitchen and Banquet stands out as Lynn’s premier destination for African cuisine. Whether you’re savoring tender goat pepper soup at the bar, hosting a celebration in their event space, or simply exploring new flavors, this restaurant delivers excellence. Minor service hiccups noted in early reviews have given way to polished, heartfelt hospitality .

I tried the shrimp fried rice and the tilapia with fried plantains. The food was absolutely delicious! Service was excellent and friendly. I was very satisfied with my experience here. Will definitely be coming back again.
The best place to get African foods, especially Cameroonian food  from Eru, achu,  rice-stew, suya and so on . The best spot in Lynn for delicious foods plus the staff are all amazing people

formatted_address: 2565 Washington St, Boston, MA 02119, United States
name: Nubian Markets

reviews.text: I love the Nubian Markets hot food bar and I’ve told anyone who will listen to me rave about this gem in Roxbury. I’ve had the Butcher Burger, the Crispy Chicken + Hoppin John bowl as well as the Chicken Bunny Chow and the Salmon salad! All so flavorful and delicious. The quality of ingredients is high and the portion sizes are very filling. I always leave satisfied and fulfilled after eating there. I’ll have to try the breakfast soon.

Good vibes and delicious food! Best breakfast sandwich in Boston!! I got veggies, but they do have meat options as well. I’m full and with nutrients needed to fuel the day, but still want to go grab another just because it tastes so good.

I came in, one side is a small limited marked with wonder niche drinks and other such items, as well as fruit and vegetables, and the other side is a lovely restaurant and study space.  I loved the vibe felt so relaxing on the Market side. The restaurant ordering, she acted like I was lucky she took time out her busy day. But since she told me something was old, I thought, great she did me a solid, so maybe she is just tired. Then I heard the kitchen staff talking too. A bunch of hostile folks for no reason whatsoever! I bought my drinks on the market side, because it was cheaper that way.

I know, it was a Friday, and the week is long, but why you mad at me for ordering food? That is what this establishment is designed for. So my first thought was:
1. This food was not made with love. It will likely not be good.
I hate when I am right about things like this.

When somehow the spices are not ground fine enough, so one of your bowls you feel like you are eating gritty sand the entire meal that has the occasional flavor of beef and ginger, and lentils so salty I could not choke them down without rice, and even then could not eat them, that is how you know, maybe is not the hot spot after all. Where was all the flavor I read about? What is this grit?

My cabbage, jerk chicken, and rice were great. Everything else was a NO. I even included a side shot of the lentils left over I tried to mix with rice that I threw away.

VERDICT: Hit the Market and only get the jerk chicken, rice and cabbage from the other side. Godspeed on this one.

This market is a wonderful addition to the neighborhood. It’s a small supermarket with all the basic groceries plus some extra, interesting and fun food items, including Mediterranean.

It’s located on a main street with parking in rear, in a new building. The interiors are well organized, spacious, well lit and pleasant.

The food is great, it’s fresh, tasty and authentic, and the service is very good.

Great experience, recommended !
The BEST burger ever! Loved the ambiance and the representation of the diverse African foods! Shoutout to the kitchen staff!

formatted_address: 377 Centre St, Jamaica Plain, MA 02130, United States
name: Ethiopian Cafe

reviews.text: Place had a wonderful Ethiopian vibe with incense and beautiful artwork that set the mood right away. The food was made with quality ingredients…tasty, flavorful, and very authentic. Service was warm and welcoming, and the dishes came out quickly. A great spot to enjoy a genuine Ethiopian experience.
Absolutely delicious. It was a very clean environment and everything on the meat combo plate with chicken and beef was so flavorful and fulfilling!

I have mixed feelings about this place...on one hand, the food was solid and the price was relatively cheaper compared to other options nearby. However, the service was a bit slow, and my stomach doesn't feel well afterwards, which could be something I ate there.

Still, the sambusa was solid, and the injera was not too sour, if that's what you prefer.
this place is incredible. we got the combo platter for 2, and everything included was perfect. will definitely come back.

This was my first experience with Ethiopian food and I am kicking myself for not trying it before! The food was delicious and it was such an amazing experience! The staff was so kind and very tentative, they answered any questions we had. Everything we ate was delicious, I don’t think you could get anything that wasn’t

formatted_address: 502 S Main St, Randolph, MA 02368, United States
name: Destiny African Market

reviews.text: I have been to a couple of African markets and I can say with certainty that, Destiny African Market appears unmatched! Polite staff, neat space, welcoming atmosphere, and well stocked. Mama Destiny herself, is one amazing lady who is ready to help customers navigate the shop. Try them out if you haven't already. :-)

Destiny African Market is truly a gem in Randolph! From the moment you walk in, you feel the warmth, culture, and community. The store is always well-stocked with authentic African groceries, seasonings, and hard-to-find items that remind you of home.

If you’re looking for ingredients to prepare a delicious cultural meal, this is the place to shop- they have everything you need and more! And if you get the chance to try their catering… trust me, you will NOT be disappointed. The food is flavorful, fresh, authentic, and made with so much heart. Everything tastes like a celebration!

So grateful to have this store right here in Randolph. Highly recommend to everyone looking for culture, quality, and amazing food!

Amazing people and store!! I reached out to them to highlight their store for one of my university project and they were so responsive and immediately willing to assist in my project. I went to the store and the owner was lovely and welcoming I enjoyed interviewing her so much that I had to support the business by buying some things. I happy to know I found an African Market since being from Florida there are not many.

What can I say? Merely, that there is no better shopping experience to be found than partaking in the plethora of goods available at Destiny African Market. Said market provides an astounding variety of products in a plentiful manner that grants the customer an authentic taste of the African Diaspora. I say, with confidence, that there is no other place in the Greater Boston area that can compare to this compelling house of African cuisine & culture!

I had a great time getting to meet Sola and Bukky in person!! This was my first time seeing the Market and they’ve got everything you can imagine. From Moringa to endless spices and herbs. Bringing you all the vibes of Africa culture and cuisine!

formatted_address: 535 Main St, Malden, MA 02148, United States
name: Habesha Restaurant

reviews.text: This was my first time eating Ethiopian food and I am incredibly impressed. Such friendly service, food was super fresh (you can taste that they use good ingredients) and very tasty! The portion was also perfect size (if you arrive very hungry, for me otherwise almost too big!) :)

Don't let the outside deceive you.
This is a beautiful gem. The food was amazing. The atmosphere fantastic and the service super friendly.

Ethiopian food is amazing.

I've always wanted to come to this restaurant and it did not disappoint. The ambience was very relaxing and friendly. I really liked the decor and most importantly, the food was fantastic. The only downside was that there are only two servers and so service is very slow. Also, it appears as though they don't have a bartender and the drinks we got took a very long time and they were not good. We had to send one back. I would come here next time for the food and skip ordering drinks. If they hired a bartender and more servers, it would elevate the experience ten fold.
