Unbelievably slow, poor service and borderline inedible beef
The low-lights:
-we were the first table to sit down, a table of six So the restaurant was completely empty aside from us. It took 30 minutes for the waitress to come over and take our drink order.
-immediately after getting our drinks we put in our food order in our food took almost 50 minutes to arrive. We ordered six different dishes nothing off menu, very straightforward.
-I noticed that they were fulfilling GrubHub and Uber eats orders left and right, they were coming in and out consistently for that almost hour before our food came out.
-The owner, or someone in charge was sitting at the bar the entire time drinking beer, laughing it up with other people and offered no help or intervention. We almost got up to leave, but literally a minute later our food came out.
- I ordered a beef dish that was honestly made up mostly of grizzle and tasted like I was chewing on rubber bands.
-I normally don’t leave a review like this, but this was honestly one of the worst experiences I’ve ever had dining in Boston. It took so long despite the restaurant was not even remotely busy, and the food was subpar.

Delicious Ethiopian cuisine .
The service was quick, the music was good  and the whole experience was nice.
The chicken and vegetarian options were great and the spicy tea was refreshing.
Anjira were soft and went well with the gravy .
There is a parking lot near the restaurant

formatted_address: 611 Columbia Rd, Dorchester, MA 02125, United States
name: Comfort Kitchen

reviews.text: Honestly one of the best food experiences I've had in a LONG time. Fusion cuisine often gets a bad rap but Comfort Kitchen's entire menu (or at least the things we got) were all artfully conceptualized and masterfully executed. The jerk duck is now served as drummettes as an appetizer rather than an entree, and it is fall off the bone tender and seasoned aggressively but intentionally. Would highly recommend it, and a squirt of the lime on the side makes the dish incredible. Absolutely must-order. The tea brined pork chop was extremely succulent, not dry at all. Couldn't really taste tea in the pork but the accoutrement on the plate were all intensely flavored and very good. Also highly recommend the fish chowder. The shrimp, clams, and mussels were all cooked perfectly, which is much appreciated - nothing worse than overcooked seafood in stew. My only regret is not saving room for dessert. Another time I guess.

I'm really torn on this place. I loved the vibe and the flavors were fantastic, but several parts of the experience just fell short.

The atmosphere is a definite win. The decor is cozy and stylish, the service was prompt and friendly, and we loved the historical details on the menu—a really nice touch.
When it came to the food, they absolutely nailed the flavors. The sauces were brilliant and everything was well-seasoned. The jerk duck was the star of the show—incredibly tender—and the Nepali chai was perfectly spiced and delicious.

The problem was that for most dishes, the textures were completely off. The pork chop was dry, the beef was tough, and the roasted okra was soggy instead of crisp. Adding to the frustration was our table. Our group of four was squeezed into a tiny corner with barely enough room to eat comfortably, which made sharing an awkward experience.

For the price, I just expected more consistency. I really wanted to love this place, and maybe we just caught them on a bad night, but I'd be hesitant to go back.

One of my favorite places in Boston! From the first welcome by the hostess, all the way to the last goodbye this place is infused with care, love and soul. Everything on the menu is exceptional and exciting. Unusual flavors blend masterfully with each bite, in a comforting way indeed. There is no feeling of heaviness or bodily discomfort afterwards, which is especially pleasant during warm summer nights.
I’ve been here three times this month only, and can’t wait to return!

My partner and I went here for our 5th anniversary and had an amazing time! The staff were incredibly welcoming and friendly. The drinks were fantastic. I would highly recommend Dream Street and Put that on Everything. I would order those again 100 times over. Our waiter warned us the food was spice forward and said they could accommodate a lower spice level if needed which was very nice to offer. My partner and I can handle spice so we respectfully declined. We shared the okra, jackfruit sliders and yuca fries to start. I am still thinking about the okra and jackfruit sliders. The flavor was dimensional and the jackfruit sliders were perfectly spicy and sweet. The yuca fries were pretty good but I have preference for sauce on the side rather than over fries and I know to ask for that next time. For our mains our waiter suggested the jerk duck and my partner said she doesn't usually order duck but this was one of the best duck dishes she's ever had. It fell off the bone and the flavor was incredible. I got the cauliflower and it was pretty good and definitely a lot of cauliflower. Like a half a head of cauliflower. I loved the smokiness and the spice. I'm not sure that I would order it again but that's just personal preference. I loved the vibe of this restaurant. It's the perfect date night place and honestly any occasion going out. Overall, Comfort Kitchen was one of my partner and I's favorite dinners we have had this year and we look forward to returning in the near future!

Our dining club of nine had dinner at Comfort Kitchen and, unfortunately, the experience didn’t match the price. We were charged $765 total (including tax and tip) for a pre-set group meal that included three eggplant entrées at $75 each, three pork entrées at $85 each, and three fish chowders at $95 each, plus a few shared appetizers and dessert.

When we did the math afterward, ordering the same items à la carte would have cost about $615 total with tax and gratuity—around $150 less for the same food. Portions were very small: only two plates each of beef, okra, and sliders to share among nine people, and for dessert we received half-size portions of mango ice cream (valued at $7 each).

We were also told there would be outdoor heat lamps, but there was only one for our entire group, which made the seating area uncomfortably chilly. In addition, one person’s pork dish was forgotten until we reminded our server, Avi, who said it had to be cooked fresh—but by then, most of us were already finished eating.

The flavors were excellent, but the portions, pacing, and setup didn’t justify the cost. If you’re organizing a group dinner here, make sure to coordinate in advance—ask exactly how many plates of each appetizer will be served, confirm the outdoor setup, and do the math ahead of time so everyone gets fair value.

formatted_address: 453 Centre St, Brockton, MA 02302, United States
name: Luanda Restaurant & Event Space

reviews.text: From the moment we walked in, Luanda offered warmth and hospitality that made us feel right at home. The food was authentic and absolutely delicious, with flavors that truly tagged the essence of the cuisine. The caipirinhas were standout—vibrant, well-balanced, and perfectly crafted. The service was attentive and friendly, making our dining experience all the more enjoyable. If you’re looking for a reliable spot with excellent food and a welcoming vibe, Luanda comes highly recommended.

Amazing experience!! We got there late, a table of 6 people around 8:15 pm and kitchen closes at 9 pm on Mondays, but the staff was great with us. Their service was amazing, always checking on us to make sure we were having a good time. The food was delicious!! The drinks as well!! I definitely recommend Luanda ... actually, we will be back soon and earlier! Thank you team Luanda!

Luanda Restaurant turned out to be an unexpected surprise. From the outside, it looks quite ordinary, and the interior design is nothing particularly remarkable. However, the food had a comforting, homemade quality that made the visit worthwhile. I started with the Caldo Verde, a traditional collard green and chorizo soup, which had an incredibly rich and flavorful broth—absolutely delicious and very satisfying. The chicken fingers, on the other hand, did not taste homemade and were somewhat average.

For the main course, I had a well-seasoned grilled chicken breast served with crispy fries and flavorful chickpea rice. The combination was simple but hearty and enjoyable. To accompany the meal, I tried two different caipirinhas, one flavored with passion fruit and the other with mango—both were refreshing and well-balanced.

The service was attentive and efficient, making the dining experience even better. There was an 18% surcharge added to the bill, but I didn’t mind it at all, considering the level of service provided. Overall, I would definitely recommend stopping by Luanda Restaurant during a visit, especially for those looking to enjoy comforting, homestyle flavors.

The food at Luandas is actually pretty good — that’s the main reason I kept giving this place chances. Unfortunately, the customer service and wait times really need serious improvement.

No matter how busy or slow it is, the average wait time is at least an hour or more. At this point, it feels like you have to order two hours in advance just so you’re not starving while waiting. That shouldn’t be the case.

One time, I ordered ahead, showed up over an hour later, and was told the kitchen never even started the order. That’s frustrating, especially when you’re trying to support a local business.

I truly want to see Luandas succeed because the food has potential, but the lack of communication, long wait times, and nonexistent customer service make it hard to keep coming back. Hopefully this feedback helps improve the experience for future customers.

Luanda never disappoints. Located in Brockton, Luanda brings out the delicious flavors of the Cap Verdean cuisine. Large portions, grounded cocktails, and amazing staff. The wait might be longer than other high scale restaurant but all worth it once you taste your food. Definitely worth a visit.

formatted_address: 1127 Harrison Ave, Boston, MA 02119, United States
name: Bintimani Restaurant

reviews.text: I had cassava leaves over there that I ate with chikwangue I had at home. But the next day I still had leftovers so eventually eat it with rice, really good, really spicy too though! It’s close to the Congolese way, there’s peanut butter in it.
Authentic and delicious! Josiah and his wife are phenomenal cooks and great company. The whole experience carries fantastic ambiance!

This place was unlike any place I’ve ever been. Go for the experience. The food, I didn’t love, but then I have zero experience with west African eating.
The ‘plaza’ it is in is an experience in itself. It reminded me of some very out-of-the-way places I’ve been to in the Caribbean. Then the ‘restaurant’ ... it’s a cluttered room no more than 10x10 with this guy lounging in an easy chair and talking on the phone. He was very chill and polite. He showed me into the kitchen which was ... I don’t know. There were four metal cafeteria serving trays. Cassava leaf, cray cray, and two rice. He gave me some of each. They both have chunks of chicken full of bits of bone, so eat carefully. He asked if I wanted to eat here. I didn’t see any place to do that, so I paid (do I need to say bring cash?), and went on my way.
It was worth going for the experience. I can’t really say if the food was good, having nothing to compare it to.  I’m glad I went, but I won’t go again-especially because I don’t live in Boston.

Sabbe talk krio? cam to Portland, Maine. I go be de best customer. I stayed at Hotel Bintimani on Lumley Beach.  I called. No answer. Disconnected. I would like foo-foo shipped frozen to me every day or week.
The cook of the Bintimani Restaurant near Dudley Station makes the most delicious African Cassava Leaf and Okra stew/soup, and she gives a generous portion for the inexpensive price.

formatted_address: 1029 Dorchester Ave, Dorchester, MA 02125, United States
name: Mouna’s Kitchen

reviews.text: Authentic African food she knows what’s she’s doing ❤️

formatted_address: 1105 W Boylston St, Worcester, MA 01606, United States
name: Tembo Grill

reviews.text: Tembo Grill is so good! We stopped in on a cold day for lunch, having never tried Kenyan food before. We ordered goat and chicken stews, with seasoned rice, coconut rice, vegetables and greens. We also got samosas. Everything was delicious! The meats were tender and flavorful, the sauces were perfect. The samosas were so good we wished we weren’t so full! The people who work there were also very friendly and professional. Highly recommend!

This simple and unaffected dining space belies the delicious food served. We enjoyed the crispy fresh samosas, which were delicious and only a little spicy, sausages, fresh chapati, goat and beef stews, greens and both spiced rice and coconut rice. The greens in particular were excellent, finely chopped and robustly flavored, while the meats were tender and the sauces were rich and savory. We wanted to be try the fish dishes, but they had prepared a huge catering order and had run out. I think we'll likely be back to try those as well.

I had the goat stew and the pilau rice, the blend of flavors was so fantastic and the goat was stewed to the perfect texture. The mural inside is also gorgeous and service was very courteous. I’ll definitely be back soon!

If I could give 10 starts I would!!!!! Tried it the other day and it was OUTSTANDING!!!!! the couple who owns it we’re so nice, the food was incredible and everything tasted out of this world!!! I literally never want to eat out anywhere else ever again because nothing compares to how great it was! Fish was excellent , rice was cooked perfectly and these were the best collard greens I ever had!!! My new favorite spot
This is truly a hidden gem. The food is exotic and exquisite. They have a wide variety of East African foods on offer. Try the samosas and the sausages. You'll thank me later.

formatted_address: 25 Kingston St, Boston, MA 02111, United States
name: Fete

reviews.text:
My partner and I visited Fete during our vacation passing through Boston, and the experience started off incredibly strong. The food was absolutely immaculat, rich flavors, great portions, and beautifully presented. We arrived during happy hour and ordered the Jerk Lamb Chops and Honey Biscuits to start, both of which were standout dishes and set the vibe for what we expected to be a top tier dining experience.

For entrées, my partner got the Oxtail with rice & peas, tostone/plaintain,  and a side of spiced peppers, and I had the Red Snapper with rice & peas, tostone, and mixed peppers. Both meals were flavorful, authentic, and cooked perfectly. We also tried two cocktails — the Better Fashion for me and the LaLa Land for my partner — both were well-balanced and very enjoyable.

Where the night dipped was the service toward the end. Things had been going smoothly, but the quality of attention dropped off significantly to the point where I had to go look for my server myself, which definitely took away from the overall experience. It wasn’t enough to ruin the night, but it was disappointing considering how strong everything began.

Overall, Fete delivers amazing food and great drinks, but the inconsistency in service keeps it at a 3.9-star rating for us. With a little more attentiveness, this place would easily be a 5 star spot.

I went here for the first time last week and this is the best black restaurant I’ve ever been to by far, I had Honey Lemon Pepper Butter Wings, Rasta Pasta, and a Haitian Piña Colada that gave my tastebuds an experience they’ll never forget. Also the interior of the place and vibes it gives just makes it stand out perfectly from other restaurants. In addition to what I said in the past, here are pictures of the food and drinks I ate and drunk during first time over there and times after that as well, like I said before this is the best Black Restaurant I ever been to.

We had a great time at Fete on Kingston celebrating my boyfriend’s birthday! The food was very good, drinks were amazing, and the customer service deserves recognition. Our waiter, Isaam, was super friendly and paid attention to every detail. He definitely made our night more special!!!

My experience at Fete was AWESOME, the lamb chops were super good and you can tell the food is made with a lot of love :) My bartender Bria was AMAZING. I never know what to order but she referred some really good drinks that was hands down 10 out of 10. Posted my meal and everyone wanted to know the 411. Definitely will be going back!!

I stopped in here the night before Halloween and loved the Pork griot! The pickliz had just the right amount of spice and the rice, beans, pork and plantains had so much flavor! The place has a really cool vibe and the service was amazing! The bar tenders were super friendly, talkative and attentive! I definitely want to check this place out for brunch and maybe one of their karaoke nights!

formatted_address: 782 Tremont St, Boston, MA 02118, United States
name: MIDA

reviews.text:
Super satisfied with Mida. Changed plans last minute and showed up at 6:30pm on a Saturday night with no res. Were able to get 2 seats at bar which was full service.

Complimentary bread and olive oil which is always a great touch.

Duck wings (comes with 3) were big and super tasty - have an Indian/asian vibe. Really saucy but good.

Gnocchi was very light but the sauce was lacking something. Overall good not great.

Caesar salad was standard for a Caesar but tasted great and they accommodated adding chicken which was appreciated.

Tiramisu was delicious - really glad we ordered it

We had a great dinner with friends here. The atmosphere is cozy and Italian. The food was good, around 4 to 5 stars! The service was fantastic, and we felt well taken care of. My short ribs lasagna was delicious but a bit small. The mushroom pasta was good too. The mussels appetizer was nice, and they have a good wine selection. The tiramisu was the only disappointment!

Great menu, everything you want out of a higher scale Italian place. Arancini had great balance in terms of richness and acid from the tomato sauce. Tomato sauce really stuck out in the short rib lasagna as well, portion well worth the price, great flavor. Gnocchi was unbelievably soft, definitely something I would order again but horrible to reheat so try to eat all of it and honestly just leave it if you can’t finish. Was celebrating a birthday and they gave us tiramisu on the house which was super nice and tasted great, the host and server also wished me happy birthday which was super nice as well. Great place for an occasion but it was a little loud and the tables are super close together. Not an intimate dining experience if that’s what you’re looking for, at the south end location at least. Loved the service over all, definitely worth the try for the food at any location.

Cozy and nice place for a dinner. Happy atmosphere, minimalistic design and furniture setting. Delicious food. The roasted chicken smelled heavenly. Don’t know what spice or oil it was infused with, but I was impressed. Eggplant parmigiana was very delicately cooked to perfection.
Came here twice during our stay. Once for brunch and again for dinner last night. Very good quality food. Would highly recommend. 💯 Didn't get photos of the pasta dishes, but they were outstanding.

formatted_address: 233 River St, Cambridge, MA 02139, United States
name: The Coast Cafe

reviews.text: I was looking forward to trying this place based on the reviews, but the food didn’t live up to my expectations. The chicken was over fried and lacked flavor, and it tasted like the oil may have been old. The mac and cheese was also on the dry side, collard greens were good, and best part of the plate was their cornbread. . Overall I give my plate 7/10..

This is a solid soul food restaurant! Their fried chicken, macaroni and cheese, and vanilla cake are very good. The collard greens and cornbread are ok. Small restaurant dining room so probably best to take out.

This place is AMAZING! We ordered the ribs, fried chicken, candied yams, mac and cheese, and vanilla cake. Everything, and I do mean everything, was a 10/10! The place is super cozy and cute. They have a wide variety of dishes to pick from on their menu which I really appreciated. I will be back soon! (I placed my order over the phone and it was all ready for me when I arrived about 15 min after I called) :)

Solid spot for Soul food/Fried chicken cravings.

First heard about this spot a year ago from my friends dubbing it the best soul food restaurant in the GBA. With limited opening hours, it took me some time to finally make it here, but this week, I managed to visit for lunch

The restaurant was quite small, with just seven seats squeezed into its modest space. Most people seemed to know the drill, grabbing their orders to go, but with a menu learning heavily on fried options, we decided to dine in while everything was still hot and crispy.

We opted for the Fried Chicken Thighs and Fried Catfish combo plates, and both delivered on flavor. The chicken thighs were our favorite—perfectly seasoned, not overly greasy, and juicy. The catfish was also nice with its tender and flaky meat. However, the portions felt a bit small for the price, and while we dove in as soon as the plates hit the table, everything was lukewarm.

Among the sides, the Mac N Cheese was our favorite. The other offerings—Candied Yams, Collard Greens, and Rice & Beans—were solid but fairly basic. From the hot oven display, we tried the Beef Patty. The flavors were there, but it was a tad dry. It really could have benefited from a good dipping sauce.

Not entirely sold on my friends’ claim that this is the best soul food spot in the area. Yet, with limited options for Southern soul food in Cambridge/GBA, I would probably come back if I’m craving for good fried chicken and Southern comfort food.

I wanted CRISPY fried chicken and bot tenders.  This place delivers. I loved seeing the giant pot of collard greens ! And the Mac and cheese is so thick I needed strength to pry it open ! So cheap so fresh so good

formatted_address: 320 Westminster St, Providence, RI 02903, United States
name: Suya Joint Providence

reviews.text:
I may have read significantly on the different cuisines of the world but have yet to try a good portion of them. Out of the cuisines that I’ve tried the least, Nigerian cuisines is the one that has always peaked my curiosity as it plays a significant role in the food of the South. It emphasizes bold flavors and contributed to the creation of what we know as Soul Food in the US, and shows the culinary heritage of the African Diaspora. The diversity in the country is also massive due to not only the land size but also from an insane number of different ethnic groups speaking over 500 languages. This uniquely Nigerian diversity (no other country even comes close to this) contributed to a very unique plethora of flavors and expression of food that one could only begin to comprehend through words and pictures. Comprehension as such can only come with experiencing the different cuisines first hand.

So while walking along downtown Providence before heading back to Boston, I came across Suya Joint and was excited to see a traditional West African option here! They weren't opened yet at that moment so I lingered in the immediate vicinity until I had my opportunity to walk through those doors! After all, I’ve been wanting to try more Nigerian food to understand their flavors better. The moment I walked in as their doors opened, I fell in love with their decor. It was clean, artful, and representative of the culture in a unique way. What further enhanced the experience shortly after were the patrons who came in one after the other. I would overhear different tables have conversations with the server detailing their African ancestry. And by the time I was finished eating, there were at least nine African nations represented inside.

As for the food, since I was still very new to this cuisine, I came with a very open mind willing to try anything and everything. Our server recommended the African dinner so I could easily sample their most popular dishes. I decided to add their unique meat to it by ordering “Orishirishi” (translates as “variety”), which included tripe and cow feet, to further enhance the experience. All I can say as the food came was this was definitely a culinary experience that finished this weekend beautifully.

I’m in love with the cuisine and now want to come back and try more items on their menu. Thankfully, they have a location in Boston as well so I wouldn’t need to drive back there just for the food. The Egusi stew, which is one of their most popular items, was tonguegasmically good. My eyes rolled with each taste. It awoken my soul and made me feel alive again. The Jollof Rice here shamed every other version of it I’ve had in the past…like they were not even good enough to be called copycats. And the Orishirishi? Epically good. It was so rich, so flavorful, so GOOD that I completely plowed through it like my life depended on it. What is this madness? Where have I been my whole life?

Whatever it is…I have to come back to Suya Joint again soon - either here or the one in Boston. I just have to have this food again.

BEST FIND in 2026 so far! Definitely recommend a visit!

My first time in Providence for the Zeta Phi Beta Sorority conference and I had to try Suya Joint! The décor was warm, welcoming, and beautifully reflected the African-inspired theme. The food was flavorful and well-prepared , the beans had a nice little kick of spice, the sweet plantains were perfectly caramelized, and the white rice balanced everything out nicely. The stew was rich and delicious, and the presentation (complete with the little Nigerian flag!) was a thoughtful touch.

A great spot for anyone craving authentic African flavors with a cozy, inviting vibe. I’ll definitely be back!

Food was delicious but quite spicy. When the server checked in and found that I was struggling with the spiciness, they took my stew to the kitchen and added tomato sauce to make it less spicy. Order "mild" if you have low tolerance for spicy food.

Drinks were all delicious.

They provide water bowl if you want to wash your hands and eat food with hands.

I had the pleasure of dining at Suya Joint. I had been wanting to try the viral fufu and egusi soup. This was the most highly rated place in reasonable driving distance and it DID NOT DISAPPOINT . We were greeted by the sweetest server. She was kind. And helped us find what we wanted. She gave us clear instruction on how to properly eat the entree. And was attentive despite having many other tables to tend to. The food was immaculate. The chicken and fish in the egusi soup was perfectly cooked. Crispy despite being smothered in the soup. I will be dining here and sharing this amazing experience with anyone looking for authentic African cuisine.

Super super super tasty! Tried egusi and possibly all of Nigerian food for the first time and was definitely a fan! The egusi was this delicious stew with the most divine chicken (the skin was perfectly crispy). The service was also exceptional - they were the right balance of attentive without being overbearing. They also anticipated when we would want a box at the end of the meal which just was an example of their attention to detail. While the beef suya wasn’t quite as delicious, it still was solid -  think the egusi just shone so brightly.

formatted_address: 84 Spring St, Medford, MA 02155, United States
name: Neighborhood Kitchen

reviews.text:
Love their chicken sandwiches but their catering is also delicious and service was responsive and timely. Our guests loved the 3 varieties of chicken tenders and both sweet and savory waffles. I would have liked an option for dipping other than just pancake syrup.
I first got their food catered 3 years ago and again this week. Still delicious!

Not a bad little spot. My wife and I ordered the chicken sandwiches. I had the spicy one and it was real good. Perfect amount of spice. Fries were great. My wife said her chicken didn't have much flavor but it was crispy and tender. Mac and cheese was good but needed salt. Staff was very nice and helpful. No public bathroom

I really enjoyed the food here, I got the crispy chicken sandwich with plantain’s & it was really good. It had flavor & it was nice & crispy as well as spicy. I also enjoyed the salt & peppery shrimp, the peppers went perfectly with the crunchy shrimp. Overall it was great & will def. Try the breakfast next time I’m around town.

Ordered in person for take out, the creole chicken with rice and beans plate ($13.00 pre-tax). It also came with two pieces of sweet plantains.

Absolutely delicious! Loved the pikliz as it reminds me of kimchi. The chicken portion and pikliz serving could be a little more, but overall fantastic!

Their "Asian" dishes are definitely Asian inspired, which is very sweet seeing cultural food fusions. We need more multi ethnicity celebrations like this in our communities.

A great concept Southeast Asian, Haitian, and American fusion restaurant. The food is delicious and made to order. The menu is also seasonal so you have to come back and try the new dishes. There are delicious vegan and vegetarian options along with the rest of the menu. You don't need to be in the neighborhood to try this delicious restaurant. I trekked over and it was so worth it.

formatted_address: 56 Central Square, Lynn, MA 01901, United States
name: Kokomma Nigerian African Cuisine

formatted_address: 1 Bow Mkt Wy, Somerville, MA 02143, United States
name: Nibble Kitchen

reviews.text: Loved the food. Yummy! Only criticism is the $9 spring roll appetizer I ordered — while very tasty was way too thin. For the quantity it should have been priced at around $6 but hey isn’t everything overpriced in Boston? The chicken bowl was just right.

I love the concept of having a rotating menu featuring local chefs; what a great way to highlight different cuisines! As a Filipino, I love to see some pinoy representation, so I came for lunch on Wednesday and got the pancit with lumpia and a calamansi drink. The drink was very refreshing, and the food was delicious! I especially loved the lumpia, it was so crispy and cooked perfectly. Pancit was also very good. The staff was super nice as well. I'm very glad I came and hope to visit again in the future 🇵🇭 Sarap!

I liked their concept of having rotational menus allowing different chefs to have a place to cook and present their cuisine. Definitely a concept that needs more attention and visibility in the Boston food scene. I can’t remember what I’d ordered but it was delicious.

Being only open for 2.5 hours once a week, Matcha Boy is a bit of an elusive find inside Nibble Kitchen at Bow Market. However, it's worth visiting if you can catch the window. The staff was super friendly and walked me through the menu. I was between the Azuki Matcha Latte or the CHAffogato but ultimately decided to go for the latter since it's not something I've seen at a matcha spot before.

For $6, I got a cup of sweet vanilla ice cream drowned in some hot hojicha. I originally thought that they would give me the hojicha separately to pour myself, but they do it for you before handing over your order, so be sure to have your camera ready if you are interested in recording (I missed my opportunity haha).

The ice cream was rich and the perfect amount of sweetness, which is what I love the most about Asian desserts. It also had bits of ice that added some texture variety with each bite. The hojicha added a subtle nuttiness that elevated the ice cream. If I had a biscotto or cookie to top this off, it would have been perfect.

Overall, I am really happy that I got to try this dessert, and I'll definitely be back to try the Azuki Matcha Latte.

We loved the Boukannen Afro-Haitian cuisine! The ingredients were fresh, the flavors were so delicious, and the portions were generous. We loved the drinks (lemonade/mint and passion fruit) as well! The owner Mimie was so kind to us and offered us samples to taste to ensure we loved what we ordered.

formatted_address: 5 Spring St, Watertown, MA 02472, United States
name: Lalibela Ethiopian Restaurant and Bar Boston

reviews.text:
Delicious food. Cozy and welcoming atmosphere. Great place to Spend quality time with friends and family over dinner. Absolutely wonderful host!

We ordered veggie combo, Lalibela special kitfo, and Ethiopian coffee which was more than enough for three people. Food is delicious, not spicy, and has a great spread.

So happy to have this restaurant in the neighborhood. The food is delicious and the hospitality is genuinely warm, making for a wonderful dining experience. We ordered the Lega Tibs and the Veg Combo, both were incredibly satisfying. Noticing that we enjoy spicy food, they thoughtfully brought out mitmita powder and berbere sauce without us even having to ask, which added an extra layer of flavor and heat. Still thinking about last night’s dinner and already looking forward to our next visit!

I’m no expert in this cuisine so I came humbly with an open palate to try their food since their recent opening. I just wanted to support a newly opened minority business representing their roots in the area and excited to try something different from the usual repertoire.

First impression is how quiet and sleepy this whole restaurant was. Perhaps, I was just early and the closed curtains prevented anyone from outside to see the inside. Only reason I knew they were finally open was the little sign that showed “open” as from the outside, everything just looked dark.

Service is definitely very calm and familial. Everyone just helped out in their own way. Didn’t expect more since it was obvious a family had taken over this spot to share their culture and make a living out of it. Isn’t that one version of the American dream?

Food did take a while after the order was placed. But when it finally arrived, I’m glad it wasn’t just some reheat and they had actually made a stew partially cooked to order. Flavors were pleasant and not overwhelming. Portions decent and the prices reflecting portion and experience.

Definitely help welcome this family restaurant to the neighborhood! I hope they stay and succeed and spread their food, culture, and hospitality!

Today was me and my family’s first time eating Ethiopian food, and we all thought it was really good and interesting. It was nice to try something new and it was a very valuable experience. The people working there were super kind and the owner of the shop even came to us and talked to us a bit. If you’re seeing this review, I highly suggest you come here to try it at least once. My favorites were the dora wat and the green beans and cabbage.

Fantastic food! My husband and I came the third day of their opening week. They have a limited selection of options, but everything was sooooo good! Especially the vegetable combo!Make sure to get an extra serving of the bread.

The only downer was the speed of service, but considering it was only the third day of opening, I'm sure they'll figure it out.

We'll definitely be back.

formatted_address: 196 Quincy St, Boston, MA 02121, United States
name: Gebeta Catering

reviews.text: Experienced unique flavor, featuring sour, spongy injera bread served with spicy, flavorful stews like doro wat (chicken) and shiro wat (chickpea). Excellent cooks!! Served 50 guests.
Good service. Recommended
Good Service

formatted_address: 1b Highland Ave, Malden, MA 02148, United States
name: Mulu Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: Best restaurant I’ve tried in greater Boston so far. Everything was packed with flavor, service was perfect and prices were reasonable for the quantity and quality of the food.
Had the Ethiopian Chicken 23 Combo for 2 and it was so so good. So filling, warm and flavorful with really yummy spice. Sambusa was warm and flaky outside. Awesome warm baklava too!
Had the Ethiopian combo special for 2; Delicious and versatile! Awesome decoration all around the place, and the lady there is super nice!

Great food, good service and really nice people. We ordered 2 starters, ye timatim fitfit, I really liked it. The sambusas were unique and we liked the filling. In main course we ordered 4 different dishes. Tagabino, meser wot, cabbage wot, kaye sir. We really liked all three. If you feel like having comfort food then this is the place. Dishes are not overly spicy nor too fancy. It makes you feel like you are having simple home cooked food, which is great!😊
The chocolate cake in desserts was nice, the baklava was too sweet for me.

Really good food. The three of us took two platters (one veg and one non veg) and that was enough for all of us. Plenty of parking space, which is a great plus. (It's really hard to park near the Ethiopian restaurants in Boston).

formatted_address: 223 Highland Ave, Malden, MA 02148, United States
name: Taste of Atlas Ethiopian Kitchen

reviews.text: Kinda dingy inside and very hard to communicate with the cook but the food was sooo good!! I think I ended up with tibs and injera. Whatever it was it was very tasty, I’ll be going back.

Atlas is one of the hidden local gems.  Every time you visit, you will be surprised with a new thing. Their kitchen provides authentic home made food. The Fatyra lahmah they provide is the best I tried here in the US so far. Mohamad and Ayman are so friendly and treat their customers as if it was a neighborhood local market in Syria (كأنها دكان الحاره). Always Mohamad gives me high quality meat that fit the best the thing I am planning to cook. If you throw a party over the weekend or having guests over, they will catering you table with home made authentic food.

Got the buffalo pizza. Really terrible. Shared it with my family and nobody could tolerate a second slice. The pizza did not taste fresh, the chicken was dry, the onions were soft, the taste was bitter. I wanted to like this place since it's a small local spot, but something was wrong with this. And I spent over $19 for the pizza 🤦🏾‍♂️
No longer halal butcher shop there, it’s an Ethiopian market that kept part of the name and setup from the old owner. I wish someone could tell me where the Halal butcher Mohamed and his wife went.

Update 2024: the business is under new management. There's no longer a Halal butcher here, just a restaurant and limited groceries. The new owner is Brazilian and they still carry Halal chicken and beef but the menu also has pork items now like chorizo and pork bacon. Cross contamination is likely, for people that are concerned about that.

I used to go here for meat when I lived in the area. The quality of the meat was always good but it was a bit of a hole in the wall. A good local butcher none the less, particularly since he stocks goat too. Oh, and once in a while they have Halal pastrami and other deli meats which are incredible.

I happened to visit recently and they had started serving food. So I decided to try a couple of items. They had a $5.99 deal on cheese burgers and for that price, you get a 1-inch thick beef burger with two slices of cheese and lettuce and tomatoes. It's not a gourmet burger by any means, but if you're all about the meat, let me tell you, this burger is satisfying.

The main downside here is the atmosphere, things seem even more run-down than the used to be in earlier years, but the staff is super friendly and take-out is a great option. Also, call ahead or order online since they make everything fresh.

formatted_address: 43 W Boylston St, Worcester, MA 01605, United States
name: Fatima's Cafe

reviews.text:
When people say that Worcester has a great food scene (‘if you can find it’) they are talking about Fatima’s cafe. I couldn’t tell you what’s better—the food or the welcoming service from Omar.

The food is HOT, made to order, and delicious. Well cooked and made with love. I had the E. African dinner plate with chicken stew, mixed vegetables and Bata (sweet potatoes, yuca), and the Somali Anjero (like a fluffy crepe). I don’t typically care for chai tea but Fatima’s chai was so repeatedly recommended on here that I had to try it. Absolutely delicious. If you like hot sauce, they make their own and it is perfect.

This was my first time at Fatima’s, and it couldn’t possibly be my last. Almost every patron that came in after me seemed to have a personal connection with Omar, the front man. He is so funny, and so warm. He welcomed me 3x, walked me through the menu, and explained how to best enjoy my meal. This place is a gem. Cannot wait to be back.
The man at the counter is so welcoming and nice!! The food is cooked to perfection and fresh, even when ordered for pick up. Seriously the best samosas in the city that I’ve tried!! 10/10 experience.

This place is service forward. We were the only ones in an hour before close so we had their full attention, but I feel like if they had more guests they would've been just as attentive.

The gentleman, presumably the owner, is a real down to earth dude. Honest and funny.

We split a platter and I'd say it's more than enough food for two people. It was suggested to us to get extra bread because it would've been easier to pick up the food with. I started to at first, but discovered it was easier to just dig in under the platter and get a scoop of bread and whatever mixture was above it. ..not the most authentic approach, but it worked for us.

The food itself was delicious. With so many options you're bound to favor one thing over something else. I loved the mixed veg in the middle. I thought the lentils were a little underseadoned. Everything in-between was wonderful.

We started the meal the Chai teas. Not too sweet with a good balance of spice. I could've easily ordered another at the end of the meal. Don't not get the Chai tea.

Bathroom on site, plenty of good seating. Parking seems to be in the back. We didn't turn quick enough and it's a one-way street so we parked down the street.

We got a take out order from Fatima’s last week and everything was amazing. We live nearby and I had searched Ethiopian food on a whim only to find out this place is around the corner. We will definitely be back!  The service was attentive and kind, the samosas were delicious and the chicken sandwich was sooooo tasty.  Everything was well spiced and flavorful. Grateful to realize this business is so close!!
Delicious food and a super friendly staff! We had an awesome lunch here and will definitely be returning!

formatted_address: 34 SW Park, Westwood, MA 02090, United States
name: Lordya Gourmet

reviews.text: Amazing and authentic dishes from scratch just like the mother country. Lordya the resident chef and owner did and exceptional job on my order. You desire gastronomic dishes from Crown jewel of the Caribbean this kitchen is your better best option.

Lordya’s Gourmet is amazing! I catered from her for a baby shower; everyone loved the food. The Haitian and American flavors were perfect; fresh, clean, and delicious. I’ve also ordered to-go; fast, professional, and top quality. Highly recommend!

Oh Lord! Lordya Gourmet is definitely the best food I’ve ever tasted. Everything tasted so delicious. It was like heaven. The service was great, all the staffs were very friendly. I highly recommend it this delicious journey of taste.

Food was great, service was exceptional. The only thing is that sometimes they run out of my barbecue Kreyol and it makes me sad🤣. I feel that I should get special treatments you know  y'all could save one for me in case I’m buying😁. I know I don’t get food from y’all everyday but I feel entitled ,being an OG customer and all. If you’re reading this Lordya I hope I’ve pleaded my case well enough , don’t you think?😁😁🤣

Lordya gourmet is wonderful dinner from every prospective it was my first time getting food over there I am very positively surprised first of all you have to try the fried fish it simply delicate and delicious…definitely going back

formatted_address: 1746 Washington St, Boston, MA 02118, United States
name: Teranga

reviews.text: Excellent service and really nice place, it’s such a pleasure to support such a Black business, different people gather at this place to enjoy Senegalese food. Don’t be fooled by the esthetic, the plates will get you full real quick. Oh and, Elisabeth is the nicest waitress in Boston.

Great food and atmosphere! It was so good I ended up coming back two nights in a row. Both the chicken and lamb dishes are extremely delicious and the staff is super friendly and helpful. I'd definitely come here again.
As a Senegalese national, I validate the taste of the food!! Everything was like I am back in Senegal! Owner and employees are very welcoming "Teranga"! The venue is clean and nice

Absolutely phenomenal food and drinks. We really enjoyed our meals and can't wait to go back. I'm usually a fan of couscous, but got a meal with Jasmine rice. It was incredible and I don't regret it all. Highly recommended!

There were 2 of us and the food was very good but the wait was too long and no apology. Waitress did not try to connect but was very friendly to a group of caucasion people a few feet away. She just kept refilling our water glass after every  sip. A gentleman that was there before we came in ordered after us and his plate was there in less than 30 minutes and we still hadn't received our salads we ordered before the actual meal. The chef stopped in after we paid and introduced herself and left a complimentary dessert which was very good. It was a nice gesture!

formatted_address: 1443 Tremont St, Boston, MA 02120, United States
name: NACHLO

reviews.text: Delicious food along with wonderful Moroccan hospitality. My first time in Boston from the UK. I came to eat after Friday prayers and loved every minute of the experience. I ordered a kebab wrap then was given Harira to try. All of it delicious. I highly recommend this place in every way!

From the moment we walked into Nachlo, we knew we were in for a special experience. This is, without a doubt, one of the best Middle Eastern restaurants I have ever had the pleasure of visiting. It's truly a hidden gem!

Every dish we tried was bursting with fresh, authentic flavors. The hummus was velvety smooth and perfectly seasoned, the falafel was crispy on the outside and tender on the inside, and the kabobs were incredibly succulent—clearly marinated and grilled to perfection. I highly recommend trying their signature dish (whatever that may be, maybe a specific slow-cooked lamb or specialty rice dish), it was a culinary revelation. Portions are generous, and the quality of ingredients shines through in every aspect.

The atmosphere at Nachlo is wonderfully warm and inviting. The decor strikes a beautiful balance between traditional and elegant, making it perfect for a date night or a family gathering. The subtle background music and the comfortable seating added to the overall pleasant dining experience.

Our server was an absolute delight—attentive, knowledgeable about the menu, and genuinely friendly. They offered great suggestions and made us feel welcome and well-cared for throughout the entire meal. The service was prompt without ever feeling rushed.

If you are looking for an authentic taste of the Middle East, look no further than Nachlo. It's more than just a meal; it's a delightful experience. We can't wait to come back! Go, you won't be disappointed!

I love the place!
The staffs are very friendly, full of smile. They are very accommodating for someone who is not familiar with the name of the dish.
The best part is the food, made fresh with halal ingredients and tasty seasoning!
It might be too spicy for some, but it is perfect for me.
The menu that I order always been packed with high protein from the meat or chicken and fiber from their salad.
The portion is so big, I can’t finish a meal by my self.

Totally recommended and will go back to try another menu.
We had the philly cheesesteak, wings, chicken fingers and nachos here. Owners were very welcoming. Food was decent too. Overall, a good experience.

Coming from an Egyptian, this is the BEST middle Eastern food I’ve had in a while. Try the chicken Shawarma wrap and the garlic sauce as well as tea to finish up the meal. very welcoming owner and very good customer service.

formatted_address: 805 Harrison Ave, Boston, MA 02118, United States
name: AllSpice Restaurant

reviews.text:
I had a chicken shawarma and a baklava. They were super delicious. This shawarma wrap reminded me of the ones I had over in Europe! Very flavorful and delicious.
The lady that prepared the food was very friendly and helpful!

My mom and I had the opportunity to eat lunch at AllSpice on a Monday afternoon, and so glad we decided to give them a try. The food was so delicious—even better than we anticipated, and the service was incredibly warm. What really impressed me were seeing the regular customers who clearly come in day after day, a true sign of a great restaurant to visit. And, you can tell they care about their patrons. Mom and I were visiting from out of town, but if ever in Boston again we’ll be sure to stop by AllSpice for a #1 chicken shawarma plate and sambusas! Next time we’ll try the lentil soup!

This is a very convenient middle eastern restaurant near Boston University school of medicine. It also has dine in and you can use the bathroom if need be. The owner was a very nice lady. I had lamb shawarma here and it was very fresh and delicious and a reasonable price.

At the hospital and hungry? DONT come here!! It was Sunday, and most places were closed, so I  grabbed a shawarma wrap. The chicken was sooo greasy it was just dripping everywhere. It wasn't even a pita wrap but a damn tortilla! It had no sauce and only topping was Sliced pickles. Sad excuse for a $18 dinner. Don't be a fool like me, and grab a slice of pizza next door instead.

Lovely spot to grab a quick bite. Ordered the chicken shawerma combo, and the sandwich was soooo good, perfectly seasoned. The fries were soo good too, not too hard or too soft. Highly recommend this eatery.

formatted_address: 548 S Main St, Webster, MA 01570, United States
name: Afro Fusion Restaurant

reviews.text: My boyfriend and I had an amazing meal here. We got light soup, fufu, and goat curry. It was DELICIOUS, flavorful, and cooked perfectly. The owners were polite, welcoming, friendly, and went above and beyond to make sure we were happy. Thank you so much! We’ll definitely be back!!

Saw this little spot on google,  saw the great reviews and had to stop by. From the initial moment my friends and I stepped in, the vibes were set with smooth 90’s/2000’s r&b. The owner was super nice from the get go, everything on the menu sounds delicious so it was hard to pick. She recommended the Peppered goat with the chili sauce, 10/10 tender, spice that makes you want more. I ordered the steak tacos, which were some of the best tacos i’ve ever had in my life, packed with meat. Impossible to leave here not full. From the beginning to finish such a chill and pleasant experience. Shout out trey songz on the speakers

Been wanting to come here for years and finally did.  This place is better than I expected.  Great fresh and delicious food. Like eating at your grandmother's kitchen. Cooked with so much love and pride. Everything just perfect savory and filling.  Must give this wonderful restaurant a visit and you will not regret it.  We will be coming back more and more.

This is the best taco I have ever had in my entire life. I live in Florida and I do not find a taco like this. These tacos are unbeatable and they are made with love and quality. You have to try once in your life. The picture is the steak tacos. All of other tacos taste incredible as well.

I cannot say enough good things about this place! I had a shrimp and chicken taco and it was to die for. However, it wasn’t just the delicious food that made this place great. The service makes you feel like you’re eating in someone’s kitchen and the food is definitely made with quality. 10/10

name: Anokye krom

reviews.text: This was our first time trying African food so we had no expectations. Our experience was good , the food was well seasoned and tasty .

The service was nice and they attended to our time. The meat was a bit tough to chew and the rice was a little dry, spice is tolerable on the rice plate. Fried chicken was good, it’s very typical. The fufu is limited to what they make during each day, so they do not serve everything that’s on the menu daily as it says. Make sure you let them know if you want less spice because the fufu was really spicy, just spice but not flavor.

I’m I seeing this right? No comment. I’m just disappointed after a long wait for this order and even having to wait because they said they were now frying the meat. Like how is this freshly fried. This is not the first time and this will be my last time EVER going to this place.

Don’t even bother stopping by. I took my boyfriend and my sister here after an African festival and was very disappointed by the lack of service we received for the first 20- 30 minutes. When we did receive service, nothing we ordered from the unnecessarily long and confusing menu was available. Apparently certain dishes are only available on certain days and that is not indicated on the menu.
We tried ordering some other dishes, but those were also not available so we settled on some small appetizers for the table.  Shortly after the server left, we saw a cockroach crawl up the wall behind us and took that as a sign to leave.
I don’t know if this was just an off day for them, but based on this first impression, I will not be returning.

The decor is basic, but the staff is warm and helpful. The chef came to our table several times to explain the food and help us with the spice. Had the Waakye and Goat meat and Jollof Rice & Goat meat. The seasoning was delicious. The Goat Stew has an amazing aroma. The Goat in the stew was fall apart tender and flavorful. I loved the flavor. The heat of the stew was strong but couldn’t help but keep eating.

The bar has limited options. Can’t wait to go back and bring friends to this hidden gem.

reviews.text: Guys!!! Southerner here (Louisiana), I can't begin to tell you how close to home cookin' Poppa B's is!!! I haven't had catfish done right in 20 years, but Poppa, Poppa did it right southern style. Cole slaw, yams, potato salad......Felt like I was back at a church potluck. This is hands down THE BEST southern food this far north.

Did take out catfish dinner. Food was tastey. Well seasoned. I'm a stickler on fresh fish. This was clearly frozen fish. Some parts of the fish was dry but that happens with frozen fish. Had greens and sweet potato. Both tasty but too much green juice spilled all over my clothes. 1 to 10 rating. I give it a 7.5  plate came with corn bread that I didn't get.

We really went for the soul food 😩 unfortunately they were closed so we tryed the west  African food the food had a good taste when I got my plate I was shocked to see one drum stick and a whole plate of rice with 3 plantian for 21.00 I try to support but I could have went and brought a 10 pound bag of drumsticks for 10.00 rice for about 4.00 and a bag of mixed vegetables for under 20.00 if food places want to stay open they have to treat the costumers right we work hard for our money as well

I ordered turkey WINGS when I returned home with my order, so had a few Turkey tails, bone and fat.  I called to speak with the person who took my order.

Instead of speaking with the actual restaurant, The call was directed to “ William” who was on an offsite location.

I told him the problem , he asked for a picture. I sent him a picture.  He attempted to tell me “there was a misunderstanding “.

I had Poppa B's fried Haddock Sandwich with a side of Mac & Cheese ... the fish slapped, perfectly seasoned and fried, and the mac was yummy!

formatted_address: 21 Turnpike Rd, Southborough, MA 01772, United States
name: Sentie’s Kitchen

reviews.text:
We had the absolute pleasure of working with Sentie’s Kitchen to cater a special community event — Uganda to Boston — bringing together runners, cultural leaders, and guests from all over the world ahead of the 2025 Boston Marathon.

Sentie went above and beyond to deliver an incredible spread that showcased the richness of Ugandan cuisine. Guests were raving about every bite — from the flavorful samosas, rolex, and chicken stew, to the delicious coconut rice, chapati, beans, and fried plantains. His attention to flavor, authenticity, and presentation truly made our event unforgettable.

Beyond the food, Sentie and his team served with pride and professionalism. Their delivery was timely, setup was smooth, and their hospitality made everyone feel welcome.

If you're hosting a corporate function, cultural celebration, or private gathering and want to leave a lasting impression — I wholeheartedly recommend Sentie’s Kitchen. We’re so grateful for their partnership and can’t wait to work with them again.

I got the opportunity to eat here with a trip with the Global Competency program at my school, and everyone there was so kind and the atmosphere was super welcoming. We had the opportunity to learn how to make the samosas they serve and then eat them, and they were delicious! I had only ever had Afro-Caribbean food once or twice before and going here was a great way to try some really delicious food and learn more about the culture surrounding it. We got to try a little bit of everything, so I had the mac and cheese, spicy jollof rice, jerk chicken, oxtail, fried plantains, collard greens, yuca fries, and samosas, which were all so incredible! All of the food was so flavorful and it was really clearly made with a lot of love and passion. I will definitely be coming back again and am going to recommend it to my friends!

I am a high school teacher who brought 20 students to dine at Sentie's Kitchen.  Wow- what an incredible experience!  Sentie and his wonderful staff were incredible hosts!  We made samosas, then Sentie prepared a delicious and plentiful buffet for us to try.  The food was amazing, everyone was so kind, and students shared with me they are definitely coming back with their families!  Thank you again to Sentie and staff for a really incredible evening.

Sentie's kitchen is my favorite place to go for Afro Caribbean food. Sentie is a master in his craft! The menu is extensive so you won't fail to find something you like. They have it all from East African, West African and Caribbean food.  My personal favorites are the Mac and Cheese, jollof rice, beef ribs, Smoked Brisket and oxtail. Catering options are also reasonably priced making hosting a breeze.

Oh wow! This place is really, really good! Hidden away on Route 9 in Southborough, afro-carribean food with flare for making great ribs. You can tell the food is prepared by an experienced chef. Ribs so tender, plantain done to perfection, etc.  I could have added a photo but I ate all the food already. This is our go-to bbq place with a really nice afro-carribean take. If you are into carribean-style beans and rice, you are going to lose your mind over this place! Wish it was in Cordaville Plaza or Southborough Crossing Plaza where it would have more exposure. This restaurant needs to be a part of the showroom of restaurants in Southborough. I don't think it is getting enough attention at the location in the Turnpike Road strip mall.Kudos to Sentie. Well done!

reviews.text: No lie the best food ever. My number one favorite food spot and I eat out more than most. The chicken, rice, plantains, kale, sweat potatoes, sauce, everything smacks. I only write reviews when needed. Had to give 5 stars

Thoroughly enjoyed this place. Fairly small family owned restaurant and the waiter was very friendly and explained all the dishes. Brought out kids food first to get them going and had fun shapes for the rice. Food  had a nice spice and very flavorful. I loved all of the dishes I tried.

I drove from RI to Worcester, about 40 minutes drive because I was craving some good waakye, Jollof and Banku. All the food was delicious! My two toddlers who are very picky eaters demolished the jollof. I was not happy because they finished the rice I drove 40 minutes for! The young lady who took my order was very kind and prompt. This is what i paid $18 for 3 pieces of dried meat a container of dried rice and they said it came with a side of stew.  That small container is supposed to be the side of strew. all ingredients were fresh and so appealing to the eye I had to try! I Was not let down, the food is flavorful and plentiful. I’ve ordered takeout for myself and coworkers a couple of times when we were craving jollof rice. This place does not disappoint. The service is fast, the restaurant is clean, and the food is consistently delicious, fresh, great portions and full of flavor. Leaves me wanting more as soon as I finish my plate.

I'd been looking forward to this visit since before it opened. The owner is one of the most unexpectedly impressive and refreshing individuals I know. The food, A1. It was delicious. Let me start with what I didn't know I would enjoy as much as I did. KALE. I don't know what they put in it, but it's yummy—perfect crunch, taste, and texture.

Next, the jollof. Clearly, the chef is a grandma or aunty because, again, delicious. No spice was overwhelming. The chicken is well-seasoned and cooked to perfection. In addition to the jollof bowl, I also had a veggie bowl, which was a hit with my very picky eater husband. If you're vegan, you'll find something, vegetarians, there's food for you. Of course, for meat eaters, everything on the menu is an option. I have by-monthly meetings an hour from the restaurant (and my meeting is 4 hours from my home).  Yes, I will make this 5-hour trip every other month to support this business. The owner is that amazing of a human, and the food is worth it.

So incredibly delicious! We did a 'make your own' ākra bowl with tofu, veggies, rice, plantains, with peanut sauce and a veggie bowl with the spicy honey. Both were INCREDIBLE- the perfect amount of flavor and so filling. ākra had so many plant-based options as well that it was easy to choose.

name: Infuse Afro Fusion

reviews.text:
OVERALL:
Infuse is close to my home, and I enjoy supporting them regularly. They have several dishes that are excellent and worth returning for. I’m leaving detailed feedback because I wish I had something like this when I first tried to order, and because I want them to continue growing. When they get it right, the food is truly delicious — and I hope the small inconsistencies improve over time.

This review is based on multiple visits. Here’s my honest experience:

THE GOOD:

Curry goat: Absolutely delicious — rich, tender, and full of flavor. One of my favorites here.

Suya beef: Also a favorite. The menu mentions peanuts, but I could barely taste any peanut at all.

Jollof rice: Tasted homemade and was very good.

Egusi soup: Hearty, filling, and flavorful. I wasn’t sure at first bite because of the fish, but by the time I finished it, I liked it.

Fried plantain: Soft and well-balanced.

Pounded yam: Goes with everything. Very soft, filling, and easy to eat.

Fufu: Good as well, but more of a neutral taste. I think I prefer the pounded yam.

THE OKAY:

Tsofi (turkey tail): Okay.

Okra soup: Not very slimy/stretchy — probably made milder to appeal to everyone, especially people who are picky about textures. Because of that, it loses some traditional flavor.

African slaw: Okay when it automatically comes with the rice (almost like a garnish), but I wouldn’t order it by itself or choose it as a side.

Banku: Generous portion. It’s supposed to be sour, and it definitely was. It's more of a medium sourness than mild, so just a heads-up.

NEEDS IMPROVEMENT:

Pepper paste: Needs work. It wasn’t as fresh as stated and leaned bitter in taste.

Samosas: The ones I tried were not it — if you’re East African, you’ll probably be disappointed.

Fried yam: This batch (pictured) was bitter, especially the dense pieces. The softer pieces were better, so it seems like it came from a bad yam. I hope they check batches because yam quality can make or break the dish; yam shouldn’t be bitter.

Friendly service, good music, great food! The beef suya with rice and plantain was delicioussss! The samosas were so good that I had to get two orders of it to go. My husband enjoyed his Egusi soup (not pictured ). I would highly recommend this place and will be stopping by again whenever we are back on that side of the country.

New spot with great appearance and large portions of food.  All of our dishes were fresh, tasty and hot.  The service was wonderful too. If you in the Lowell and want to try African food give they a shot.

The restaurant is beautiful and the staff and owner are welcoming. I've had some exposure to Caribbean food, but this is so much more. The waitstaff helped us choose a variety of dishes and explained some of the combinations and flavors. I was thrilled with my dish, a sampler featuring fish and a rice dish, and tasted meat pies, a whole tilapia and plantains. Can't wait to try the goat stew or curried goat. This is a must-visit!!! A great place to eat before a show at the Lowell Performing Arts Center or MRT.

I had been a customer of this restaurant for almost a year, and I experienced my biggest disappointment the day before Christmas. I accidentally ordered the wrong dish and called to cancel the order and request a refund so I could place a different order.  Also, the default tip amount on the website is excessively high without the customer being aware of it; I accidentally paid a 20% tip when I was not in a good financial situation. The person in charge refused to cancel my order, pretending not to understand what I was saying or perhaps not speaking English well. She kept trying to convince me to add something else to the order instead of canceling it.  Furthermore, the dish I mistakenly ordered, which eventually arrived, was incomplete, as the canned okra was missing.

reviews.text: Food was absolutely delicious. This will definitely be one of our new favorites. We got the fried plantains, suya, Jollaf rice with beef, and the curry goat. Everything was just the right amount of spice and flavor. The plantains were an especially big hit for my kids. We dined in and will definitely do so again as a date hopefully very soon!

Maddy’s Food Hub is a new eatery in town and we thought we’d try it out. …So glad we did!  The food was delicious. We chose the Kelewole appetizer, which are spicy fried plantains with a tasty dipping sauce. We also enjoyed Jollof with rice and beef and Jollof with rice and African BBQ spare rib with spicy hot sauce on the side. —So Good!  It was also a pleasure to actually meet Ms. Maddy, who graciously explained some of her featured dishes.  We felt right at home in her trendy, cozy bistro style restaurant. —Loved it!

So yes, we highly recommend Maddy’s Food Hub if you’re hungry and in the mood for something that’s deliciously unique and different.  Maddy’s IS the place for authentic African cuisine, and definitely worth a visit or two and more!  Great food. Generous food portions. Reasonable prices.  …And they do “Take Out” too.

The food is flavorful and plentiful. We had the fish of the day, the peanut butter soup and a vegetarian dish Maddy made especially for us and everything tasted delicious. The plantains were caramelized and are not to be missed!

Soooo. I've been twice in one week. I am so glad I seen the ad on FB featuring Patty's article in the Concord Monitor. I love Ghanaian food especially Waakye so I had to visit. My soul was so happy when I walked in and saw my favorite drink (BB Cocktail) in the cooler too. The food was good and I felt like I was back home with my Ghanaian hubby. 1st visit Waakye and 2nd visit jollof rice with chicken. Thank you Patty for the hospitality

DELICIOUS! I am so happy i found this gem! Its literally rihht next to the planet fitness so you can work out and get a hardy, tasty, so so so flavorful dish of food. Im just a 29yr old traveling professional and I feel lucky to have stumbled onto this place. 😁

Price was a little bit expensive as the place looked very ordinary. West African customers are the ONLY regulars. Next to a Mosque, halal food. The menu is on top lit board ...not printed, only their business card. Yummy food, nice server, only the place looked less than welcome.

Food was pretty good but for a rundown looking restaurant this place is very  costly. No prices listed anywhere . After ordering just a few different dishes idk how and why my total came to $80. Slow service. Definitely wont be giving it a second chance. Place is self serve

The food here is AMAZING! Everything was super fresh and flavorful, and you can tell they really care about what they sell.  Portion sizes were perfect, and the atmosphere Definitely a spot I’ll be eating from again.  I didn't dine in so I can't rate their customer service.

Review for Santé Yallan African Food Restaurant – ⭐ 0/5

This was only my second time trying African food, and I was excited to share the experience with two of my African friends. Sadly, our visit to Santé Yallan was a major letdown on multiple levels.

From the moment we walked in and seated ourselves, we noticed immediate red flags. Workers behind the counter had their pants sagging so low their underwear was fully exposed—on the food line. That’s not just unprofessional, it’s unsanitary. To make matters worse, the staff were laughing, playing, and horsing around like kids while the restaurant itself was filthy. Tables were dirty, old food and trash were scattered across the floor, and flies were visibly flying around. If they have time to play, they have time to clean.

It took about 45 minutes for our food—fish and lamb—to be prepared. While waiting, my friend politely asked about the order. The person we assumed to be the manager rolled his eyes and gave a rude, immature “It’s coming” response. Totally unnecessary and disrespectful.

Before eating, we all went to wash our hands—an important part of African culture when eating traditional meals. The bathroom, however, was disgusting: no soap, a soaking wet floor, no paper towels, and the toilet tissue was also wet. The lack of cleanliness was shocking.

When the food finally arrived, it was just okay, definitely not worth a 45-minute wait. The lamb lacked seasoning and should have been marinated longer. I didn’t try the fish because it was tilapia, but my friends said it was bland and had no real flavor.

When I went up to the counter to ask for napkins, the man literally handed me two single sheets of paper towel like they were rationing supplies. I had to explain it was for the whole table before he reluctantly gave me a few more.

After our meal, I went up to ask for a to-go box and just shook my head. This place has a lot of potential, but right now it’s not being taken seriously. The staff is unprofessional, management is dismissive, and the restaurant is not sanitary.

Food should bring people joy, culture, and connection. This experience did the opposite. Based on everything—the service, cleanliness, food quality, and attitude—I have to give 0 stars. This was my second time trying African food, and sadly, it was not a good one.

Santé Yallan, please do better. Your customers deserve it.

This place is so good! The dibi lamb, lamb tomato stew, maffe(peanut butter stew), the jollof rice! I haven’t gotten anything I didn’t like. I have a diverse palate and in my opinion they have flavor and know how to cook! It sucks when you eat out and waste your money and end up regretting it since you wasted your money.. this isn’t one of those places!

reviews.text: I’m at a complete loss for words.. this place was AMAZING!! Customer service was top tier. The woman was so attentive and helpful. This was my first time trying African food and it was delicious. Definitely will be returning whenever I am in the area. The music was such a vibe, literally one of my new favorite restaurants! 100/10 I totally recommend

We ordered the Attieke / Snapper Grilled. The presentation was nice, the seasoning on snapper was tasty.  We also had the African Garden salad, sorry so picture we ate it too quick, it was enough yo share 🤣.  You must visit this place if you are curious about trying African cuisine or craving it.  I highly recommend.  The decor inside was very nice, however with the weather being so nice we opted to sit on the patio and it was great. Tiffany was our waitress, she was very nice and helpful when we had questions about the menu items. Thanks for making our first time visit memorable.

Joy is in the Journey!

Afrique Lounge is an amazing spot with an unbeatable vibe, but what truly makes the experience exceptional is the staff. Khadijah and Jersia are absolutely outstanding at what they do. Khadijah, the hookah specialist, consistently delivers perfectly prepared hookah and truly understands the craft. Jersia, the bartender, creates great drinks and keeps the energy positive and welcoming.

Both Khadijah and Jersia provide top-tier service that creates a warm, inviting atmosphere every time you visit. Their dedication, professionalism, and passion for what they do do not go unnoticed. They are highly valued, reliable, and clearly committed to making every guest feel comfortable and taken care of.

I highly recommend Afrique Lounge for anyone looking for great service, great drinks, and an all-around great experience.

Step aside, ordinary nights out—Afrique d’Lounge just redefined our dinner game 💯. From the moment we walked in, the vibe was a delicious blend of upscale chill meets Afrobeat soul. But let’s not bury the lead—Grecia, our bartender and server, was the real MVP of the evening. 💃✨ With a smile sharper than a steak knife and a knack for mixology that deserves its own Netflix series, she turned our dinner into a full-blown experience.

Let’s talk drinks. My wife’s Mojito? Fresh enough to make a mint farm jealous 🌿🍸—bright, crisp, and dangerously sippable. As for me, I channeled my inner North Sider with the infamous Blue Motherfer Cocktail*—yes, that’s the actual name, and yes, it delivered a punch like the last 5 seconds of a Bulls game. 💙🥊

Food-wise, we were living the dream. My wife went all-in with the Liberian Dry Ice Fried Tilapia—smoky, dramatic, and oh-so-savory, it made every bite feel like an entrance at the Met Gala 🐟🔥. I tackled the Rib Eye Steak with Fried Plantains, and let me just say: if steak had a fan club, I’d be president. Juicy, flavorful, and perfectly seared, it danced beautifully with the sweet, golden plantains 🥩🍌.

Bottom line: the food? Amazing. The drinks? Next-level. Grecia? A legend in her own right. If you want flavor, flair, and flawless service, ask for Grecia—she’s not just behind the bar; she is the bar. 🥂💫

Highly recommend this spot—you’ll thank me later.

I went to Afrique D Lounge on Easter Sunday (4/20), and let me tell you 10/10/10. The vibes were immaculate from start to finish. They had a $25 bottomless mimosa special, and it was well worth it.

The customer service was top-tier something I haven’t experienced in a long time. I want to give a special shoutout to Vicky and Tiffany for their amazing energy and attention to detail. What really stood out to me was the owner himself  (Jerry) stepping in to help. He greeted us, served us, checked on us, and made sure everything was perfect. That level of care speaks volumes.

If you haven’t been to Afrique D Lounge yet, you’re missing out. I’ll definitely be back!

reviews.text: This was our first time trying African food. The fried chicken was delicious and crispy. Also the plantains were delicious and amazing. The rice was spicy and a bit oily. But took 1 point off because since the time we came, we had to wait 30-40 minutes. The guy at the counter came and explained to us that the food here is made fresh every time customers order so it takes a bit of time. WE WILL COME BACK. Don't miss JOLLOF RICE AND FRIED BANANAS

Very disappointed in the Food I received from here. The food is very inconsistent. The Food was overwhelmingly spicy which is completely uncalled for. I grew up eating spicy food but this level of spice is ridiculous, my mouth is on fire. The goat stew I ordered was not thoroughly cooked, very hard to chew, was a complete mess, my teeth was hurting. I couldn’t digest it. Insanely high prices for small portions of food. The prices can’t be justified. However the Jollof was some of the best I’ve tried. May go back, but place needs to pay attention to details.
Friendly staff and visitors are nice too. I got huge portions..however that isn't always the norm. Food is authentically Ghanaian

If you are looking for authentic Ghanian delicacies complete with the spices and aroma, then this is the place to come to. The food is freshly made while you wait, and the serving size is large. The staff were friendly and attentive. The furniture arrangement and the music give off the motherland's ambiance.
God bless the cooks- you will not have a bad meal here! And the music is top notch! Sometimes there is a bit of a long wait and a crowd for take out,  but it is a testament to how good the food is.
