reviews.text: Food is not good at all, chicken not cooked ughh. I ordered cassava leaf and it was awfully awful. Please you are feeding people so take time to cook. I will never step foot there not even for free food.

I've been here twice. The food does not smell like freshly cooked food. I don't like what I think is a rotten smell, whilst it doesn't taste that way, it's smells that way. I love cultural food, but please make me assume the food is freshly cooked every time.

I've tried 3 times but its always the same thing. Its too much oil. The soup is mostly oil.  2 out of the 3 times the soup tasted spoiled! Each time I ordered cassava leaf and each time I couldn't enjoy it. The lady that works there is friendly.

Food is horrible, pepper soup tasteless and fufu looks like a porridge, honestly it wouldn’t worth giving to anyone for free… this business is a ripped off. This is pure nastiness, the entire food ended up in the garbage, not meant for human consumption… pure wickedness..

The food is absolutely delicious!!! Very very kind and lovable owner! I told her it was my first time trying this type of food and she took the time to walk me thru everything.. even made sure I went home knowing how to eat fufu! I have gone back twice and absolutely love this place. Highly recommended! The spices are everything 👏🏼

formatted_address: 746 Huntington Ave, Boston, MA 02115, United States
name: Flames

reviews.text: Attentive , fast , & freshhh ! Had to extra cabbage it oxtail sauce on the rice ! The cocobread was so fresh will be back. Prices are more expensive now but look at the material treat yourself !
Really disappointing service. Guy behind the counter treated me like I was an inconvenience. Other than that, the food was just okay. The macaroni was the best part of the meal. Weird ambiance.
The food was great and had good flavor. I was warned that the curry goat was going to be spicy, but there wasn’t much spice. Still, the meal was good.

I went today for lunch. The food is okay. I got rice and beans and cabbage with oxtail. The weird was too heavy on the coconut flavor and was very undercooked. The cabbage was completely undercooked, raw with no seasoning.

I also got a beef patty. Worst beef patty I’ve ever had.

But the oxtail was tender and yummy. Not nearly enough for $24. But yummy.

The service is great! The people are super friendly and the restaurant is beautiful and spacious

TRASH customer service, trash attitudes, trash food. Flames has gone down hill more and more as the years go by. In this economy?!  Poor quality food and those prices are insane! The only location I have never had a problem with was Mattapan but let me not speak too soon because it’s been a while since I’ve been there.

formatted_address: 45D Central St, Providence, RI 02907, United States
name: Toyin African Restaurant

reviews.text: Can't complain. I got a lot of food that tasted great, and I didn't have to wait. The lady serving was nice. I'd recommend anyone to show up and get a lot of good tasting protein and carbs to hit their macros.

Toyin the owner is the sweetest lady ever! She welcomed us with all smiles and instant affection! Not only is she the sweetest but she can also throw down in the kitchen! This facility  is run by her and her family. Every single one of them were so kind and helpful. They truly  made us feel like we were in their home eating her home made cooking. I will 100 percent be back over and over again!
Food was good and their service was on point. Thanks to Toyin herself.

So I came here today for the first time. I will say the lady was very nice. I wasn't expecting for the place look like it did. It's a very big place inside that is not so well put together. For it to be a food place you should be able to smell the food not other smells. Now she gives you a lot of rice. But the greens you order does not match the rice portion. I will say no where's near. With what she gave me for spinach I was only able to eat a quarter of my rice. The other 75% of my rice I ate plan because my spinach was gone. The other thing is my spinach tasted like fish. I never up til this day had my spinach taste like fish. But her spice was there. I will say I had so much better and also had so much worse.

Food was trash my chicken. Was hard taste like leftovers definitely not fresh the spinach trash look like collard greens served ice cold which tells me again not fresh dont go deeh deeds kitchen has bad attitude but good food this place has great personality but the food is trash

formatted_address: Inside The City Kitch, 601 Milner Dr, Greensboro, NC 27410, United States
name: African Sister Restaurant LLC

reviews.text:
Amazing food and an even better experience. The dishes were authentic, full of flavor, and clearly made with care. Everything tasted fresh and well seasoned.

The woman running the restaurant is incredibly kind and welcoming. You can tell she genuinely loves what she does, and that makes the experience even better. I will definitely be back and highly recommend this place to anyone looking for real Nigerian food.

This is a wonderful place to get West African cuisine! The Egusi soup is delicious! My kids like goat and okra soup. And goat stew always finishes quickly.  Fufu is soft and tasty and comes with most meals. This restaurant has generous portions which works for those of us who like to eat!!! I have used this place to cater small gatherings and am always satisfied! The lady who runs the restaurant is sweet and extremely easy to work with.  My family prefers buffet style and she was so accommodating. Allow time to pick up the food, it will be worth the wait!
By the way, there is a place to sit but no restaurant area with waitstaff. If you have a lot of people, I suggest pickup or a delivery service.
Service is top tier owner was very warm & welcoming very informative about the food .I got the orka soup with goat jus expensive  😩 $31 but the flavor  is chef kiss very great  popping 😋 flavor.

Everything was very flavorful. First time trying to Egusi soup . It’s pretty good as well. I’m use to the okra soup that’s all I get from any west African restaurant. Today i had chicken , okra soup and rice . Omg that chicken is bussin . Taste like it’s smoked and packed with seasoning . The rice is also real tasty . 10/10 . The owner she is very nice and caring of your needs . I know the food is prepared as order so please be patient with her. If you want great authentic food A must try ..That chicken came from heaven by the way 😂

I have been wanting to try fufu and egusi for years and finally forced myself out of the house tonight.  Hubby and I split the fufu, egusi, yellow rice and jerk chicken plate.  Came out piping hot and smelling amazing.  The flavors are just wow.  I’m not even sure how to describe it.  You get hints of smokiness and definite curry but the other spices were new to us and very welcomed.  We will definitely be ordering here again.  I’m not sure if it was Kayanda that brought me the meal, but the woman was very nice.

formatted_address: 200 Main St, Pawtucket, RI 02860, United States
name: Village Restaurant

reviews.text: Food was absolutely amazing. I do not know much about Nigerian food and the owners son ,told me what he recommended and educated me on the food and culture. I ordered a little bit of everything to try and I’m glad I did. The spice and flavors were amazing. I will definitely be going back for more. My favorite was the meat patty and the designer sauce . ( had a kick to it)

First time trying Nigerian food and well worth it! Great hospitality. Felt very welcomed. I told the gentleman I knew nothing about the food and wanted to try as much as possible. He took his time to explain everything to me and made recommendations accordingly. My favorite was the rice, it had a nice kick to it and great flavor! All the food was great! The service was great! I will absolutely go back! Definitely recommend!

First time here today and I must say it will be my last. Ordered the jollof rice with stewed chicken, spinach with white rice 2 meat pies and a small side of their stewed meat. First off the guy who gave me the two meat pies gave them to me FROZEN as in literally the meat pies were rock solid and cold when i got them, I am pregnant and this is a major health violation. Even after i got home and warmed the meat pies up they tasted like they were days old I mean the photo speaks for itself, absolutely disgusting. I have never in my life received any frozen and cold meat pies at any restaurant considering there was a tray of warm ones in the front and this guy went to the back and grabbed me two frozen ones, im absolutely pissed. As for the side of stewed beef It was terribly overcooked i couldn’t even take a bite it was just not coming off the bone. everything else as in the jollof meal i never got any plaintains nor with my other spinach meal which was a major blow and i highly regret spending $45 for this terrible experience considering Ive had much much much better African food elsewhere. I would not recommend this place at all to anyone.

Update: my boyfriend got food poisoning the same day he tried to consume the food I brought from here. This place should be closed. Definitely will not be coming back!

First and last time ordering here. Food was hot and old, which was disheartening. Plantain so old they wouldn’t bend. Chicken hard. They put sauce all over everything and plated the food on top of each other. The absolute worse. If you want really good African food check out Suya Joint in Providence. Food, service, and atmosphere 10/10.

Let me just start off from our first interaction from the phone call. Aji was very helpful and assisted me to come in instead of just ordering and pick up to try the foods. I was undecided about the egusi and vegetable soup. I was able to taste each dish there was when I got there. Aji was very helpful , the food was presented nice and neatly. Aji had exceptional customer service skills. I decided to purchase the designer rice, red stew and vegetable stew along with plantain. I will definitely be back really soon. Thank you

formatted_address: 3711 SW Trafficway, Kansas City, MO 64111, United States
name: Teetasty Foods - African Restaurant and Bar

reviews.text:
Teetasty is a small cafe in a strip mall on Southwest Trafficway serving Nigerian and African cuisine.

We stopped in to try it for dinner the other night.

We tried the Vegetarian Plate, Jollof rice with fried plantains and spinach, it was also topped with a slightly spicy tomato based sauce which added some depth and rounded things out.  The rice has a surprisingly strong almost smokey flavor, but balanced out nicely with all of the other components.

The Vegan Egusi Soup with Fufu was interesting to try, not my favorite dish but it was pretty good and I think the SO enjoyed it.  The flavor was fairly mild and slightly salty.  The Fufu that it came with was a large ball which you tear off a ball and squish it into a scoop shape to eat the soup.  A little different dining experience.  It was soft, but not unpleasantly so.

We also tried their house made Zobo drink, which was hibiscus, ginger, cloves, and pineapple.  It was strong and pretty tasty, I wouldn't have thought cloves would work on a fruity drink like that but it was pretty good.

As well as the bottled Maltina, which was a malt drink with very strong overtones of molasses.  The SO loved it, I thought it was interesting to try but a bit too much like drinking molasses.

The service is table service, but seems a bit like a cafe that you should walk up to ... Their service was friendly and helpful.

The atmosphere was pleasant if not anything fancy.  A little oddly decorated with everything hung extremely high up the walls.  Various cultural art work, mostly of people.

I was here for my birthday dinner and it was an amazing time! Owner and Chef Tee and her whole team were highly professional and kind to everyone in the restaurant! Such a wonderful and hidden gem in kc, I will for sure be coming back!

Visiting from California, I went here with my SFL. Let me start with we came in through a back door. After seating ourselves we had to request the music (that is advertised) be turned on. Our server was very pleasant. We ordered the mini platter, which was good aside from the over cooked shrimp, the whole tilapia meal to which the fish texture was almost slimy, not a good fresh fish, plantain was hard, the jolloff rice taste like colored white rice that had been cooked on a grill, very smokey, puff puff with caramel drizzle was quite tasty, the zobo drink was very nice, but the egusi soup with chicken and swallow... the worst thing I ever put in my mouth. It taste like they got this dish straight from a septic tank. I truly do not know how they are in business let alone have 4.5 stars. They must be writing their own reviews. The food and safety administration should really follow up at this place and test that soup.
I have had plenty of African food and this makes me want to deny my  Nigerian (African) heritage and my SFL doesn't even want to go to Africa anymore after eating here.

The food was actually pretty good! It was my first time in Kansas City and the wanted Nigerian food. I got beef suya, chicken suya, basmati fried rice with shrimp, fried plantain. I ordered puffpuff but they didn't have any. My only complaint is that the food took time. I ordered off Uber eats and the driver said he waited a while for the food.

I wanted to try Egusi soup for years. Finally came here with my co-workers and been hooked ever since. I’ve tried the Egusi Soup, Seafood Okro and the beef Samosas! I can’t wait to try some more stuff. I live in Kansas & I door dashed it tonight, bc I had to have it and it was worth every penny!! Soo good! Staff are kind, food was hot and fresh! Try it, you will not be disappointed!!

formatted_address: 264 E Berkeley St, Boston, MA 02118, United States
name: Baleia

reviews.text: I love Baleia!! It is one of my favorite restaurants in Boston! The atmosphere is amazing, the service is so warm and friendly and the food is great! We did the tasting menu and everything was delicious. However, I would order individual dishes next time. The tasting menu was a lot of heavier food but still great. I loved the muscles at the beginning of the tasting menu and the pastel de nata dessert. Also, I HIGHLY recommend their house vino verde. It was wonderfully crisp and delicious. Wonderful restaurant overall!

Amazing does not come close to describing this place.
All the staff was hopping all night. The service was exceptional. The atmosphere was very lively and elegant. It was a little too loud. We ordered the Explorador tasting menu. Definitely a must if this is your first visit. Every dish kept getting better. We definitely want to come back.

Amazing experience! Authentic food that is not only presented well but is equally delicious. The vibe of the restaurant is very different and inviting! And the best part is the service- yes you heard it right- service! It is 10/5 and kudos to our server Igor who made our experience all the more special! We will be back soon

Came in as a group of 4 friends just catching up. Amazing evening, we did the chefs tasting menu which for $70 was great value seeing just how many dishes we got to try! Our server (so sorry I forgot his name!) did an excellent job recommending drinks and wines and we had a 10/10 evening. Like any chefs tasting menu you might not like everything you get but that is part of the experience! Highly recommend.

Came here for a celebratory dinner with friends and my husband. The atmosphere is very modern. The food is very good. I would say the means, such as a duck rice and the chicken were my favorite. The food comes out at a good pace and is varied. We also shared a bottle of wine which was a lovely red that was well balanced and finished with cocktails that were also delicious. This is a great restaurant!

formatted_address: 722a Shawmut Ave, Boston, MA 02119, United States
name: Soul on Shawmut

reviews.text:
I will not be returning to this place again. I ordered a steak and cheese and a chopped cheese for my wife, as well as some fries with buffalo Chicken egg rolls, which weren’t cooked all the way through. My first issue is with the owner/staff. While ordering my wife’s chopped cheese, I explained to the clerk that I only wanted ketchup and mayonnaise on the sandwich. The owner tells me they don’t use mayo, just their special house sauce, so I asked for it to be on the side, but I want just cheese on the sandwich. After waiting 25 minutes, I received my order and returned home, only to be highly disappointed that the chopped cheese contained everything I had not asked for on the sandwich.
Additionally, when we decided to try the buffalo chicken eggrolls, the chicken tasted uncooked and was unpleasant. The fries we ordered were cold as well, but the steak and cheese were at least edible. There was no authentic seasoning on the meat, and the amount for $20 just wasn’t worth it overall. I paid over 80$ for very, very mediocre food. They also had a kid working at the cashier, and the kid was in the kitchen playing with his hair near the food. This is unacceptable, and it will definitely be my last time visiting this establishment.

Wonderful spot for casual #halal dining. My wife and I stopped by for a late Sunday lunch and were welcomed by friendly service, chill vibes and delicious smells. The cheese steak and buffalo chicken egg rolls did not disappoint! Ask for the house sauce along with the cheese steak...it's awesome! Will definitely be back to try the other items. Easy parking in the lot next door

Soul food done right. The chicken was delicious and well seasoned. The sides were so authentic. The yams were a little sweet and very tender and the Mac had some amazing mix ins and was well seasoned. The service was friendly and nice, would recommend and will be returning

It was a lively place with regular customers coming in one after another.
The chopped cheese was insanely good!
The buns were crispy, and everything came together perfectly.

We used Soul on Shawmut to cater 2.5 meals on our woman's retreat.  The catering menu is amazing! We got the lamb, mac and cheese, Peruvian chicken,  cornbread,  rice and beans and more. Everything was delicious and everyone loved everything and kept asking where I got it from. Everything had such flavor and the Peruvian chicken sauce was soooo yummy 😋. I will certainly be using them again and again.

formatted_address: 140 Tremont St, Boston, MA 02111, United States
name: Black Seed Halal Grill

reviews.text: A cute little Arabic eatery with a nice view of the Common and Tremont St. Just beware of the sketchy types who gather outside (especially at night). Not much decor on the walls. They have a wide selection of drinks and side snacks, while their entree menu is small and simple. Their lamb burger is average, but their fries are great and seem to be fried in tallow (beef fat) for authentic taste. Lastly, their cute baklava squares are small but very good (you may want to order two).

Visited Boston for the weekend and wanted food that was halal. I stumbled upon this place and it did not disappoint! I had the Cheeseburger with fries and it was great! Fries are important to me and these fries were fried well and just right.

Our flight to Boston was delayed but we were so hungry. We didn’t fly all the way to Boston to eat McDonalds but couldn’t find anything open. This was about 11 pm. We stumbled upon black Seed Halal. It looked a little shady from the outside with lots of people loitering but the food was delish! We got the super shawarma and it did not disappoint. We also got the Cajun fries which were pretty good too. Perfect meal to bring to our hotel and crush before bed.

If you love good food, this place is a must! One of the best spots for delicious food!
The French fries are seriously the best in the world, and the chicken buffalo wrap was packed with flavor. I highly recommend it!

This is the first time I ordered anything from “Black Seed halal grill “ and I’m amazed how family oriented and caring the people of this restaurant are. I got to spoke with one of the owner I believe and he helped me through out my catering order for a college event. I had low budget but still he told me that it will be fine and I’ll have enough food to sever every one. Trust me food was not only more than enough it was amazing in taste as well. Rice, chicken shawarma, falafel and their signature garlic sauce was a hit at the event. I want to thank brother Yousaf and his team for providing us with an excellent and authentic taste of Mediterranean Food. I’ll be ordering here from now on!!

formatted_address: 185 Talbot Ave, Dorchester, MA 02124, United States
name: Fresh Food Generation

reviews.text:
For my first visit, I ordered the New Kingston jerk melt with a side of the herbed fries. I also ordered the strawberry mango twist smoothie. It was all exquisite!

While I and other customers waited for our food to be prepared, we were given fried plantain chips with (I think) a mild harissa sauce. Also while waiting, I was struck by how they knew the names of every customer walking through the door.

Excellent atmosphere, so much delicious and healthy food to try, and great location. I’ll be sure to return!

I’m actually surprised the food did not taste how it smelled. Portions 10/10, freshness 10/10, flavor 4/10. I ordered a jerk chicken plate with coconut rice and sweet plantain and kale Cesar salad. The Kale Cesar was the absolute best thing on the plate. Unfortunately I was expecting some sort of spice when it came to the jerk chicken but overall what I was given was baked chicken. There didn’t seem to be ANY Jerk seasoning at all. The coconut rice also just taste like white rice with a hint of coconut. Sweet plantain were good as well. I would return for the KALE CESAR for sure. The mini curry chicken empanadas were ok. Smelled like curry more than it tasted like curry.

We went mid week and had an amazing dinner. The team and the owners went above and beyond for us. They were super friendly, fun and anticipated our every need.

The food was outstanding. Jerk chicken might be the best in the city! The rice plates are creative and you get so much food.

The cocktail menu is inventive. The mango margarita was absolutely delicious. The old-fashioned with coconut water ice cube sounds amazing, it’s on my list for next time!

I thought the jerk chicken, wild rice, & red bean stew were delicious. Obviously not 100% authentic but a healthier version which I love & support. The chicken was well seasoned & tender. The beet salad was good, the carrot slivers threw me off though. I did not care for the romesco sauce on the side but happy this came with so many options to begin with at the price point offered. I’d definitely eat here again & I’m looking forward to trying a beverage or smoothie. Also loved the diversity of the clientele.

The customer service was remarkable and very homey I was offered water and fried plantain chips while I waited for my food the young lady with the beautiful fro was so nice two little girls came in from the neighborhood and their bday just passed so she gave them food and lemonade while they kept calling her pretty the salmon was so good and that was my first time having a ginger salad so that was very flavor and the sweet plantains was cooked perfectly the kale salad was delicious as well the fact they had coconut rice and wild rice was the main reason I came I definitely will be returning 🤌🏾

formatted_address: 481 Geneva Ave, Boston, MA 02124, United States
name: Cape Verde Taste

reviews.text: This food is Absolutely Fantastic! So flavorful, purely authentic, and super quick! I visited twice during my trip to Boston. They’re friendly once they warm up to you, but in their own way, so don’t go in expecting bubbly personalities and smiles from ear to ear. They’re simply authentic people who don’t fake a smile. Everything is good (I’ve tried the mussels, ribs, chicken, and steak dishes so far - with rice and veggies). The ribs were a bit dry, but it was likely an off day. Either way they were packed with flavor. This is a great spot to visit, and the neighborhood locals seem to come here often from what I’ve seen.

Food was amazing & great portion for the price. Will definitely be back. Got the lobster & shrimp and paella. Maybe could use a little more spice, but I’m also not used to the cuisine. Appreciate that they had some pescatarian options, some vegetarian ones would have been nice.

My son and I ate ribs and beef and rice yesterday and got very sick!When I called she acted like it wasn’t from her food but it definitely was that’s all we ate and we started feeling sick last night through this morning.I have eaten there for years and it makes me upset that she didn’t take any accountability for having tainted food.I spend $40.00 and didn’t even get an apology.I will never eat there again.

I know the owner and her family and friends. Ana provides the best service and has amazing dishes! If you haven’t had CV food you’re missing out! Reasonable prices and great portion sizes! Support your local black owned businesses. Her team is amazing
Great authentic CV food!

formatted_address: 25 Massachusetts Ave, Boston, MA 02115, United States
name: Cafe sauvage

reviews.text: Over all is good. Nice pretty place. Food is good, French onion soup was delicious. Kind of disappointed on the avocado toast. I don’t like feta cheese so I got another cheese, but still looks like a half complete version compared to another persons photo… only two pieces of carrot and cucumber, doesn’t look very delicate.

Café Sauvage is one of those rare places that instantly makes you feel like you’ve stumbled onto something special. The space is small but full of life—colorful, stylish, and buzzing without being overwhelming.

The food is where it really shines. Every dish feels like it has a story behind it. The flavors are bold and comforting at the same time—classic French roots with a creative twist. I loved how the menu had both familiar staples and unexpected combinations that just worked.

Service was warm and genuine, not forced or rushed, and the drinks were just as thoughtfully put together as the food. You can tell the owners really care about what they’re creating here

We stopped here for a quick brunch on Saturday before heading up to Salem. It was an easy walk from our hotel, and since we were determined to try as much local food as possible during our short stay, this spot made the list. We got lucky and arrived just before the rush, so we were seated right away on their small patio.

The food was absolutely phenomenal. I ordered the Filet-O-Fish sandwich, and the flavors came together perfectly with a lightly fried, perfectly cooked cod filet. I also had the Espressotini and honestly, it might be the best espresso martini I’ve ever had. No exaggeration, I’ve been thinking about it every day since.

Service was quick and efficient, and the whole vibe was relaxed. If you’re in the area, I can’t recommend this little gem enough.

I made a wonderful discovery today! The vibe was great, the service was quick, and the food was absolutely amazing. I especially loved the banana French toast, the duck Benedict, and the pulled beef on baguette. I can't wait to return and try more items from the menu!

I'm in love with this restaurant. Brings a bit of Paris to Boston. The food is outstanding!! Literally everything I've tried is such quality and reliably delicious. Service is great and atmosphere is cute. I love to come for breakfast -- omelets, the duck benedict, or my favorite the breakfast sandwich add bacon. All incredible, great portions and delicious.

formatted_address: 407 Ormeau Rd, Ormeau, Belfast BT7 3GP, United Kingdom
name: Mama Bobo Restaurant

reviews.text: We enjoyed visiting the restaurant during our visit to Belfast. The food was really tasty and the ambience just brings to mind the memory of home. They make all Nigerian/African meals and have drinks peculiar to that region. They could do with an upgrade of their services with regards to staffing, they seemed to be quite popular in the area and just one staff taking orders and serving customers can make for a bit of delay and long waiting times.
The was food was tasty and not too spicy  as well .I have tried the Beef Suya (سيريه)and the Jollof rice 🍚 and the people there were friendly as well

It was nice.
The Ayamase I had the first time I visited was really good; not too spicy too. However, my friend's soup wasn't fresh, she didn't like it, and only ate the meats. I visited yesterday and had swallow, and it was the same experience.

I wouldn't visit an African restaurant to have food that I can easily have at home, so I am a bit skeptical now. But feel free to have regular rice and play it safe with the soups.

Honestly, my friend who couldn't eat his own food was offered another meal (rice) instead, and wasn't charged for the first one. So, they try to make up for your complaints. Don't be afraid to give feedback.

Service was great, didn't know what to try but the server recommended really nice dishes, beef suya starter was super spicy but really nice, all the food was fantastic, pounded yam was really nice , big portions and very filling. Friendly atmosphere

Had the jollof rice, red stew, beef suya and spring rolls and was really tasty! the service was excellent, as the staf walked us through the menu and explained the items on it, allowing us to try some of the traditional food and drinks. i would really recommend, lovely friendly staff!!

formatted_address: 700 Albany St, Boston, MA 02118, United States
name: Did You Eat Yet?

reviews.text: Food was actually very delicious, customer service wasn't great, and several containers where food should have been were empty. Not many choices: a small amount of rice left, stewed chicken, pikliz almost empty, and griot, and fried chicken (like 3 pieces). It didn't look like they were open very little, having to scrape the sides of containers to make our plate. I asked for fried fish because there was a picture of it and it looked delicious; that's why we walked in. It wasn't available. Fried plantains were also not available. The restaurant is in a beautiful location, and I believe the owner should be there and give it some special attention. We got there at 2:45 in the afternoon; it was still early. I was expecting to see more food options available. I do plan on coming back with my husband because the food that was available was very delicious. Side note: the whole store needs to be restocked; everything was pretty empty. Love the food; can't wait to see the improvements.

Overall a really good experience. This isn’t a traditional sit-down restaurant, but everything was smooth and easy.

Annie was the server and she was great super friendly, attentive, and made sure everything was handled right. Customer service definitely stood out.

Food was good, quick, and hit the spot. The setup is simple and casual, which works for what it is.

Big shoutout to Annie she made the experience even better. Would come back again. Was our very first time

My first time coming here, the people working in the back where not friendly I asked questions and get mumbled replies. None of the food is labeled, the pasta was ok and the goat was not for me but I wouldn't have gotten it if it was labeled properly. For 21 dollars a plate it was mediocre.

I saw this restaurant on Chronicle a few months ago and have been wanting to try it ever since. Absolutely lived up to my massive expectations. Great staff, big smiles and excellent service. Most importantly: huge portions of delicious authentic Haitian cuisine. The black rice was incredible and the chicken was literally fall off the bone. Definitely will be going back and the owner Benz is a great guy! Go here. You won’t regret it!

Amazing food every time I go in there the customer service is phenomenal. The owner is so warm. He Actually, talk to you introduces himself and really cares about your experience in his restaurant. I highly recommend “Did you eat yet”? for your next Haitian cuisine night especially if it’s your first time experiencing Haitian cuisine. Top notch in the very best in the area for sure

formatted_address: 65 Lewis St, Boston, MA 02128, United States
name: MIDA

reviews.text: First grab drinks at the bar for a service was amazing. The hostess was pretty awful as she completely forgot to see us until I went back up to her, asking for an update. Our waitress was amazing. Food was amazing and wine was very good.

In a huge group for dinner. Outstanding service. Never waited for a drink or service. Food was solid but not extraordinary however it was a fixed group so it's hard to assess completely. The friendly staff and location with a view of the city are the strongest reason to go. Bar was spot on as well
We had the most incredible experience at MIDA! The food was spectacular! Every bite was better than the next! The service was excellent and the atmosphere was incredible! We can’t wait to come back!

This is the place you take family or friends when you want to impress. The views are expansive and make it one of the best spots to enjoy a great meal while taking in the Boston skyline.

Everything we ordered was excellent, from the pizza and pasta to the desserts. Each dish was well prepared and satisfying.

The service was efficient and friendly throughout the meal. The staff were knowledgeable and offered helpful recommendations that made the experience even better.

Amazing harborside restaurant with incredible views and refreshing natural light.

Reservations won’t be seated until the whole party arrives! You’ll wait at the bar which is chill, Eli was my bartender while I waited, friendly and fun guy. My server Josh was professional and attentive, good vibes.

Their menu has a map of Italy with all the regions on it, cool to checkout where your food and wine originates from. Not a huge wine guy personally but the vibes here were too immaculate had to grab a glass just to soak it in.

Got the paccheri bolognese, was soooo good. Literally the only thing I tried but I already only wanna keep getting this.

Would recommend this spot for a date night, sunset, or relaxing evening.

formatted_address: 156 Blue Hill Ave, Boston, MA 02125, United States
name: Merengue Restaurant

reviews.text:
Never giving this place my money again.

The first time I ordered from them, I got a fillet of fish in coconut sauce with white rice and beans. They put the food in a cheap foil tin, so by the time I got it from the Uber driver, the sauce had soaked through the bag and the food spilled all over my steps. Thankfully, I was able to get a refund through Uber because the restaurant staff told me that since it wasn’t their fault I would have to pay to replace it.

The second time I ordered from them, I found a label that appeared to be from one of their vegetables in my rice. I tried to call them to explain this, but the woman on the phone was dismissive and rude.

For the third and final time, I just ordered from them tonight, and the fish that I ordered taste rancid. I ordered it right before they closed so I guess they gave me whatever was left. I also called before I order to ask them if I could get the sauce on the side, and they said I have to pay three dollars extra. Like what in the world???

If you
decides to take a chance to order from here, ORDER THROUGH UBER. You have to pay for the fees, but it is worth it for you to get your money back if the food turns out to be not up to par  (most likely scenario).

Horrible quality from what could be a good restaurant.

I went here earlier in the year and my time was amazing over here. The interior of the restaurant is absolutely beautiful and the dining experience was so rich. I had the Mofongo Burger and Strawberry Smoothie and the meal tasted delightful. I will definitely plan to comeback here in the future.
Authentic Dominican cuisine! The place was full of families enjoying the food & atmosphere

I usually love this place but the recipe for their famous sangria has definitely changed and not in a good way! Wish they could go back to the original wine that they always used in their recipe. My waitress was great as always!

Foods wa very bland I don’t live far from the restaurant I waited an hour for my food and it was freezing by the time I made home 10 minutes away whole fried snapper fish no sauce no flavor maduros cut super thick and Moro bland with no flavor been in Roxbury longer than the restaurant has and this was my first and last time eating from them my kids like the empanadas but those were also sub par

formatted_address: 261 Walnut St, Newton, MA 02460, United States
name: MIDA

reviews.text: We were able to sample numerous pastas and salad through the “Mangia Monday” deal. Among the dishes we tried were the bucatini All’amatriciana, paccheri bolognese, house salad, another mushroom pasta, and the pepperoni pizza. The pasta dishes were fine but honestly nothing special unfortunately. We really liked the salad though and our waiter was great!

Overall a nice trendy Italian restaurant with a good selection of bites!

My partner and I shared three dishes and found that the star of the evening was the pistachio pesto burrata! We also had the mussels which were nice and sweet - the sauce it came with was a nice change of pace from your average red/white wine mussels. Also, the bread service was super fluffy and warm - really liked it!

Unfortunately, the mushroom pasta dish was not to our liking just due to how oily the sauce was. It left an overall greasy mouthfeel and I felt that the mushroom flavour was only very obvious if you managed to grab a mushroom with your bite of pasta!

Didn’t have room for dessert but the selection looked nice too.

MIDA is a celebrated Italian neighborhood restaurant  in Newton, Massachusetts. Founded by acclaimed chef Douglass Williams, MIDA Newton offers a warm, modern ambiance that blends urban sophistication with cozy charm, making it ideal for everything from casual dinners. The menu at MIDA Newton showcases a variety of Italian dishes crafted with fresh, seasonal ingredients. Pizza was great, pasta as well. Service is fast and friendly. Our early dinner was a highlight of the day.

I was so excited to go here for my birthday and try the dine out dinner special menu. However, the food was just alright. I didn’t enjoy the risotto, as I didn’t taste the squash and instead mostly just the flavor akin to store bought Mac and cheese. The nuts were also really unnecessary and off putting. I would’ve preferred a different topping. The pizza was undercooked on the bottom. Also, the pizza stand was there for about 20 minutes covering a whole quarter of the table which made it hard to eat. I don’t think the food was worth the price. The dessert also took around 20 minutes to arrive(just for a small scoop of gelato) and was also not worth the price as well. Adding on to that, it wasn’t the consistency of gelato, more like slush. I will not be coming back in the future but I hope they improve.

If you're looking for incredible Italian food and outstanding service, look no further than MIDA. The pizza was a masterpiece, and the tiramisu was heavenly—light, creamy, and absolutely delicious. Our server went above and beyond, adding a personal touch that made the evening so special. Celebrating a birthday here was a fantastic choice; the atmosphere and hospitality made it unforgettable. Can’t wait to come back!

formatted_address: 1391 Boylston St, Boston, MA 02215, United States
name: MIDA

reviews.text: The atmosphere was calm, upscale, and very inviting. Our waitress was top-notch—she gave excellent recommendations, which we truly appreciated since we’re from out of town. Every suggestion she made was spot-on. I ordered the lasagna with short braised ribs, and it was absolutely delicious—easily one of the best pasta dishes I’ve ever had. Honestly, it tasted like it was made in Italy. I’ll definitely be coming back to try more dishes. If you’re looking for authentic pasta and a wonderful dining experience, this is the place to go!

The restaurant is easy to find and has both indoor and outdoor seating options, menu is a bit small and little options for vegetarians. The seafood dishes were great though, the salmon dish was perfectly cooked and laying on a bed of cooked white beans, slightly different texture and different mix with salmon, very fulfilling and delicious. Cod fish was good on a bed of wheat, it did look like risotto but with a mild flavor. The appetizers were the cherry on top for our meal. The calamari dish was very tasty, crispy and citrusy, the sauce was very light and tangy and the mix was really good. Ricotta salad was also good but it did come with ham although in the menu it doesn’t include ham in description, I liked the oranges pieces in the salad as it made it super refreshing.

I never write reviews but feel like I have to for mida. This is one of my favorite restaurants in Boston. Every time I have gone the servers, bar tenders and front of house have all been amazing. It’s become a tradition to celebrate my best friends birthday there simply because she loves the arancini so much. The food and service is amazing for a price that won’t leave you bankrupt. I love mida and will continuing going until the day I die.

The best part of MIDA is probably the appetizers honestly. The croquettes were great and the pesto was delicious. The pizza is good, but being from CT, I've had better. The short ribs were also fantastic, but all the pastas were lacking flavor and one of them was a little overcooked.

This restaurant is BEAUTIFUL! Love the level of details here. We came for brunch and had a reservation. Service was phenomenal. I must return for dinner. Bar is well stocked and cocktails are great. The pasta is definitely handmade and delicious. I prefer gnocchi in heavy bolognese sauce, but the rich cacio e pepe was a hit and perfect for brunch. French toast and pancakes were great. All the pizzas looked fire. That biscuit...amazing! Thoroughly enjoyed our meal. Worth a visit or three!

formatted_address: 25 Thomson Pl, Boston, MA 02210, United States
name: Boqueria Seaport

reviews.text:
I almost never write Google reviews, but this experience really stood out. I left feeling genuinely happy, with a full stomach and a very full heart.

The vibe is cozy and elegant, the whole restaurant already smells like top-notch fried goodness, and most importantly, the server who took care of me was beyond amazing and warm.

I accidentally spilled my drink, and she immediately brought me new side breads and a drink refill. When I was finishing up, I was even treated with churros on the house. Sorry I didn’t catch her name, but I genuinely wish her all the best and hope she knows how much her kindness was appreciated.

The food itself was such a treat—everything was cooked to perfection. I especially recommend the gambas, with just the right amount of oil and perfectly crispy side bread. The Brussels sprouts with raisins were also very satisfying. Lastly the house signature margarita tasted light but hit strong in a delightful way.

The only small suggestion I have is that I’d love to see a bit more sour or spicy flavor somewhere in between to add an extra bold layer. But that’s more of an A to A+ comment.

Ty for the feast, and I would definitely revisit to try out more tapas and the paella.

We had a great experience at Boqueria Seaport and overall really enjoyed our visit. Our server was super nice and attentive, and the drinks were very good. The octopus was delicious and definitely a highlight of the meal. That said, we were disappointed with the choripán—the bread was extremely hard, which took away from the dish. The meat should be the star of the show, but the hard bread really overpowered it. A softer bread would make a huge difference. We’ve visited other Boqueria locations in DC and loved them, so we know how good it can be. We’d still come back and hope this was just a small hiccup.

We absolutely loved our experience at Boqueria. We went on a Friday at lunch time with friends visiting from out of town and our 4 month old.

Sometimes restaurants aren’t welcoming to babies and strollers but everyone here was extremely friendly and accommodated us in a spot we would be comfortable. They greeted the babe and we felt very at ease about it.

On top of it being beautiful inside, the food is FANTASTIC. We all ordered a bunch of plates and shared. We left very satisfied. The cocktail and wine selection was lovely.

We will definitely be returning and would recommend to anyone who looking for a place go eat in seaport.

After two months, I had the chance of returning to Boqueria for a lovely, delicious dinner.

I've had the fortune of traveling to Spain a few times in the last 4 years, becoming friends with locals, and delving a bit into their gastronomical culture and delights.

If you're looking for the best Spanish food, your best bet is to go to Spain, but Boqueria comes pretty damn close!

Right off the bat, classic Spanish tapas like ham croquettes, patatas bravas, Iberian ham, spanish tortilla, and pan con tomate stand out.

Aside from traditional tapas, they offer a variety of other options that pay homage to spanish cuisine with a little added twist: this is something I personally appreciate.

I opened with a Parra Jiménez orange wine, and some truffle goat cheese.

Then, I moved on to an order of patatas bravas, crispy brussel sprouts glazed with an Iberian ham vinaigrette, ham croquettes, beef and pork albóndigas (meatballs, AMAZING), accompanied by a glass of Cesca Vicent, a grenache, cab, and merlot blend from the Catalonian region of Priorat.

Delightful and fantastic! The Spanish generally pair their wine with food, and this wine was the perfect compliment for the dishes I ordered.

Everything was delicious. Additionally, the staff was SUPER friendly and kind. Thanks you guys for such a great dinner experience! I'll be back next time I'm in Boston.

Just had an okay meal here. Vibes and atmosphere were nice, but the food did not live up and we were disappointed with how long the end of the meal took. They were clearly short staffed, as we saw our server running around trying to help all of her tables and so we do not blame her—she was great! It just shouldn’t take 30 minutes to order dessert after receiving the menu. The meatballs and ham & cheese sandwich were my favorite, but still a 4/5.

formatted_address: 70 Sleeper St, Boston, MA 02210, United States
name: Para Maria

reviews.text: Overall it's good. Excellent breakfast with one of the best breakfast potatoes and Sunny-side-up eggs for big breakfast people like me. Dinner appetizers taste well although small portions.  Enjoyed the Duck Confit Bao Buns and Fried Avocado Tacos.

Gluten free aware - just let them know. Food was pretty good, very much tapas before drinking, dont expect to get full. The tequila shots we got were 3 different flavors. Tuna tartar is probably good with the gluten chips, but if you are gluten free they give you tortilla chips that don't go with it. Hotdog with Kimchi was interesting... and good. The shrimp was also alright, but small portion size.

I ordered the chicken dish and it was overwhelmingly salty, even by American standards. Honestly, the chef should try eating the full portion themselves before serving it to guests.

As a one-time experience for tourists who may never come back, this might make sense from a business perspective. But if the restaurant wants to attract returning customers, food this salty is more discouraging than inviting

Honestly, Para Maria didn't do anything outside of the norm. Located inside the Envoy Hotel in the seaport, it had a nice atmosphere and outdoor seating. Due to the weather, we sat indoors. Once we arrived we waited for someone to greet us. Our hostess was our waitress, cool. She took our order and checked on us a couple of times.
Now for the food... chips and guacamole, good. Shrimp tacos, ok. Pork tacos, delicious 😋. Now the kicker for me was the French onion soup. It was delightful until there was a soft boiled egg inside! The mixture they had with the added chorizo was great and here comes the egg that changed the overall mouth feel. For drinks, we opted for the white sangria which was refreshing but nothing to rave about. We added a shot of vodka for an extra kick. I will say for the price I need it to be worthwhile. The main course consists of the NY strip with sweet potato and the salmon with coconut rice. The flavor of the salmon and rice blended well. The steak was ok, I didn't feel like the sweet potato added anything to the steak. For dessert, we had the tres Leche and chocolate Dutch baby which also had bananas and ice cream.     The Dutch baby left something to be desired. The tres leche I was told was good.

My fiancée and I stayed at the Envy Hotel for the weekend and decided to try Para María, the restaurant located on the first floor. Unfortunately, the experience didn’t meet expectations.

We went for dinner around 5:30 PM on a Saturday and were surprised by how empty the place was. The space looked decent with both indoor and outdoor seating, but the menu was extremely limited—even the seafood options were few, and there were no real steak choices besides a steak frites dish. When we asked about appetizers, the waitress said they had some, but nothing was actually listed. A group of four came in, looked over the menu, and walked right out. I honestly felt the same but decided to stay for a glass of wine and try a couple of small plates before leaving.

We gave breakfast a try the next morning around 9:00 AM. It wasn’t busy—only a few other tables—but the kitchen was painfully slow. The waitress kept walking around repeating that “your food will be right out,” but everyone was waiting. When my fiancée’s pancakes finally arrived, they were burnt and inedible, something the kitchen tried to cover up by placing the burned side down. Thankfully, the waitress apologized and brought out a properly cooked plate, and only charged us for one meal.

While the staff was friendly and tried their best, the overall experience left a lot to be desired. The menu is too limited, and the kitchen is clearly struggling. I wouldn’t recommend Para María for a meal. If anything, it’s a decent place for a drink, but there are far better restaurants in the area worth checking out.

formatted_address: 825-827 NW 119th St, North Miami, FL 33168, United States
name: Moji African Restaurant

reviews.text: My first experience trying African food. I had the Jolloff Rice, with the Assorted Meats, along with Plantains. The rice was delicious, it had a nice flavor which I enjoyed. The service was very polite, and professional, and the atmosphere was good.

Everyone is extremely kind and welcoming. I absolutely loveee coming here! On top of the homey welcoming atmosphere, the food is to die forrrr. I love their fufu and jollof rice and 1000% would recommend.

The egusi was really good, and the yam was excellent as well.  Overall, the food was great.  The service stood out—the owner was very friendly and attentive, which made the whole experience feel very at-home and comfortable.

If you get the egusi, I highly recommend making it spicy—it honestly makes it about 20 times better. MUST GO!!!
Me and my boyfriend yesterday and the food was delicious! Everyone is very welcoming with great hospitality. Very kind and attentive. 10/10

I recently discovered Moji African Restaurant through Uber Eats and ordered fufu and egusi for the first time. My husband and I love exploring different cultures through food, and we truly enjoyed the meal. It was flavorful and left us wanting more.

Today, we decided to order again—but this time I called in directly to place a pick-up order to avoid Uber Eats fees. I clearly stated twice that I wanted two fufu and egusi, but the woman on the phone didn’t confirm my name, number, or payment—she just said “okay, come over” and hung up.

When I arrived (my first time visiting the restaurant), a male employee asked if I was picking up and repeated back “two vegetarian?” I corrected him again: “No, two fufu and egusi.” A woman then came out from the kitchen visibly upset, saying “You said two vegetarian!” and “You said it three times!” in a very confrontational tone. I calmly clarified again that I had ordered two fufu and egusi, not vegetarian.

After a few awkward minutes, the food was finally brought out and I paid. The man tried to lighten the mood by saying, “Sometimes people get confused,” but I didn’t appreciate being subtly blamed for their mistake—especially when I was polite and clear from the start.

Great food, but the customer service left a bad taste in my mouth. The attitude I received from the staff (especially the woman in the kitchen) was unnecessary and unprofessional. Unfortunately, this experience makes me hesitant to return.

formatted_address: 728 NW 79th St, Miami, FL 33150, United States
name: Afro fusion miami

reviews.text: Amazing food and great atmosphere ! Deff bringing my friends next time🔥🔥
Amazing atmosphere awesome food. Food is very delicious, tasty and well seasoned will highly and definitely recommend.
Loved this spot. Food was amazing. Vibes and service was also top tier !!
Went there with a group of friend the vibes was great, food was excellent and the hookah smooth. Deff our new spot

I had a great time at AF and I felt welcomed.
I was more than satisfied with the food and ambiance. The portions and flavors were on point! Especially the Plaintain Fritters!!! I will definitely be a regular. Miami Needed this!

formatted_address: 16595 NW 27th Ave, Opa-locka, FL 33054, United States
name: Sheri African Restaurant

reviews.text: Food was good. Cold then warmed in a microwave. No heat to the food at all. The fried rice had the most seasoning and was pretty good. Beef wasn't bad but the jelloff rice could use more seasoning and spice. No meat pies. No heat. But the plantains were nice. The lady's were super nice and friendly. Loved the sink in lobby so we could wash up before getting our food. Ask for spicy sauce and you willnt regret it.

This is one of my fav 😍 African restaurant down Miami they serve delicious 😋Nigerian dishes, you can get fried rice and jollof 😋 too
The food is always served 🔥full of flavor 😋 👌 big sizes protein 😋  They serve free bottled water 💧 and that's a plus because most restaurant serve tap water and l don't drink from the tap.

Absolutely amazing! The food was fresh, flavorful, and truly authentic. Every bite reminded me of real home-style African cooking done right. The jollof was rich and well-seasoned, the meats were perfectly cooked, and the portions were very satisfying. You can tell a lot of care and experience goes into the food. Hands down one of the best African food spots in Miami Gardens. I’ll definitely be back — highly recommended!

The food was amazing and the service was good as well, it was fun watching the music videos that they played while eating the food. I would totally eat there again and recommend it to people that like African food.
I have been here 4- 5 times since I’ve moved to Miami in June and I will say they have the BEST fufu and beef egusi soup. The taste and texture of both dishes are perfect! I enjoy every time!!

formatted_address: 19934 NW 2nd Ave, Miami Gardens, FL 33169, United States
name: Awash Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text:
Go! Trust me you will not regret it.
Anything you get here you will absolutely love. First Minar (I hope I'm not killing it) our server, was wonderful. She was attentive but not smoothering. EVERYTHING she suggested was sooo good.
There were 2 of us and we had the lentil sambusa (fab), also ended up doing the taste of Awash for 1 and spicy lamb tibs, wow! Never had lamb so tender and juicy in my life and it was all very generous portions. The honey wine and imported beer were also really great.
The cherry on top of the amazing dinner we had was the homemade chocolate cake and Ethiopian tea. This is a family place and you can tell by the love poured into everything, but the rich yet light chocolate cake with the floral accents of the tea was just the most amazing combination. I can't even deal!
We've been here before and its always great but this time was especially exceptional.
Please visit, you won't regret it. And get the cake and tea (no sugar) combo if they have it, they are life changing together!

We had an excellent dinner at Awash an highly recommend it.  The restaurant itself is unremarkable and sits on a strip mall next to a liquor store.  But the food is delicious and service very attentive and professional.  We ordered one of their sampler plates and every single item was delicious.  Ethiopian food is typically eaten with your hands by way of their sourdough bread rolls.  But if you don't enjoy this tradition you can ask for a plate and hardware and the staff at Awash won't blink an eye.  Everything we ate was clearly made from scratch and tasted exquisitely. Ethiopian beer was excellent and so was Ethiopian Cabernet Sauvignon wine. For dessert we had Ethiopian coffee, which is very strong and served with an incense burner (for relaxation) and... popcorn!  We'll definitely be back for more!

This was the only Ethiopian/Eritrean food restaurant in the south Miami area.  I really enjoyed eating here and appreciate the hospitality shown to me by the family owned and operated restaurant.   Sometimes the injera bread was not fresh, but cold.  They didn’t supply  you a large serving of bread to eat with like other similar restaurants normally give.  The serving size for the lamb was smaller than I’m used to and expected as well.  They charge extra for the small side salad that normally comes with the lamb tibs entree  and sometimes the lettuce was not bad quality.  It wasn’t green lettuce.  It was almost white in color so it wasn’t the good part of the lettuce that was being served when you ordered the side salad.  The lamb tibs entree serving size was not enough and sometimes too greasy.  The grease got all over the injera bread.  The lamb tibs entree was also served with a side of Berber which was always good.  It’s a traditional spice that used to give the food flavor and a spicy kick. I enjoyed talking to manager there who was very personable and was always opened to sharing his knowledge about the Ethiopian/ Eritrean culture and complexed history between the two East African countries that used to be one.  Overall,  always had a nice dine in experience.  Sometimes I’d go for lunch or dinner.  Thank you for always being so warm and welcoming and providing an amazing East African cultural cuisine experience.

Love, Light, Peace, Blessings, community
Our first time at this restaurant and we loved the flavorful food. The server explained the dishes in detail and the presentation was amazing. Delicious and can't wait to come back!

Very good Ethiopian in south Florida. Always take people here to get Ethiopian food. It’s in a strip mall that is a little sketchy but the food is very good and atmosphere inside is friendly. Often crowded in the weekends , they also have a variety of Ethiopian beers. Recommend !

formatted_address: 825 NW 119th St, Miami, FL 33168, United States
name: Moji African Restaurant

reviews.text: They wouldn’t take our order, or acknowledge that we were in the restaurant. Extremely rude people who provide bad service. My girlfriend is Nigerian which is why we came here and they were rude to her, would not provide service, go anywhere else! Set around for 30 mins and the guy just looked at us. When he did speak he was rude! That bathroom had no lights. The restaurant was dirty, really there was nothing good about restaurant because I have had much better African food at every other African restaurant I have tried.
Food was delicious. My first time trying. The owner will already know you want the FUFU when you get there lol. But it is a great dish.

The Ogbónò soup was sooooo so delicious...!! 😋 😍
Perfectly made and tastes wonderful.
Will keep me coming back.
Well-done.

We went to here there when we were on vacation. Mind you we did 45 min driving just to get there to have a bad service. Also the food was not good. As an African we were excepting good food. She gave not enough of okra soup and it was cold. The taste wasn’t there and I felt like the okra wasn’t even cook .the cashier was rude  when we were asking questions about the menu.
Same as Mojo. Not sure why they have 2 names. Call before going inside they are closed and did not leave a notice.

formatted_address: 4440 NE 20th Ave, Oakland Park, FL 33308, United States
name: Meal in a Pie

reviews.text: Walked out of akumin and something stopped me here and I'm so glad I did because I've only had the lamb curry so far, but it is so good! Can't wait to eat the other pies I got 😋

We originally stopped by Meal in a Pie for frozen Boerewors but couldn’t resist trying their fresh pies—and we’re so glad we did! We grabbed a lamb curry, shepherd’s pie, and beef sausage roll. The pie crust was honestly the best I’ve ever had: buttery, flaky, and perfectly baked. The fillings were plentiful, flavorful, and made with high-quality ingredients.

The chicken curry pie was especially delicious—the seasoning was spot on, warm, and comforting. Both the shepherd’s pie and beef sausage roll had rich, high-quality beef that tasted homemade and fresh. Everything came out hot, fresh, and full of flavor.

On top of the great food, the gentleman who assisted us was kind and welcoming. Overall, this is a hidden gem worth visiting. Highly recommend—5 stars!

Got some frozen pies for holiday gifts and grabbed a lamb curry pie for myself.

Oh. My. Goodness.

Buttery flaky crust beyond good and the curry was very delicious.  And fast - it’s right there waiting under the hot lamps - even by the time I got it home it was still quite hot.

This has to go into rotation for sure 😍

The biltong rivals that of any place back home in Sunny South Africa they got those quintessential spices with the cracked coriander. I like mine thin wet and fatty and they will oblige on your request .Tge droewsors is just killer its perfect .Now there pies are on another level I been around the world and have not found a better pie and including the UK aswell .Its got a fluffy crispy scrumptious crust you can taste the butter in it .The fillings are out of this world I am a curry snob and all there curry fillings like lamb,chicken or beef are tge best ingredients. The owner just a down to earth guy likes racing his cars and feeding people just all round good guy .
Love this place! The best bill tongue, great pies, nice people. Great goodies from south Africa!

formatted_address: 77 NE 64th St, Miami, FL 33138, United States
name: Fannoh Flavor African Food Truck

reviews.text: Quick friendly service and food was delicious. Please PLEASE try the potato greens..lawd!! They are sooo good. I've gotten snapper fillet both times I've eaten here.. great seasoning and flavor. Be careful with the pepper sauce if you are not experienced with spicy foods!

Couldn’t even finish the food it was soo nasty!!
Lol jk, this was amazing food. I just moved to MIA from out of town and have been craving Liberian food for sooo long. I was so happy to find this restaurant and try their potato greens. Omg it’s to die for, and the pepper sauce was excellent. Thank you Fannoh Flavor 💚 I can’t wait to order more food from y’all

There is no denying that Fannoh is one of the best chefs in South Florida. His portion sizes are HUGE, the food is authentic, and his personality is amazing. Highly recommend the attieke and fish or pepper chicken and the palava sauce with fufu.

My daughter’s graduation party is coming up and she wanted Liberian food. Reached out to Fannoh Flavor and even though he had to leave town he made sure to get our order made so we would have it for her party that is coming up. Haven’t tasted Liberian food in years. I appreciate it and so does my belly!

I’ve been struggling to find good authentic African food in the area for a while. So happy I came across Fannoh Food Truck! I ordered their Fufu and Chicken Pepper Soup and it was delicious! Super spicy and the chicken was so flavorful and tender! Everything was so fresh! Will definitely be going back to try more menu items asap! 10/10

formatted_address: 4401 NW 2nd Ave, Miami, FL 33127, United States
name: Savor Wynwood

reviews.text: Completely remodeled the outside lounge since the last few times. Now there are more sectioned seating area which was great for ordering/eating food. Cheri was the best server. Made sure everything we needed was taken care of and fast service. Highly recommend. The food was delicious and plentiful in size. Got there pretty early in the night and they didn’t start playing Afro beats until little later into the night. Got bit up by mosquitoes because we were sat at a table that had a pool of water under it. Always a great time here.
Really good African lounge! Great music, fresh food, and good vibes. I have had positive experiences each time I’ve gone. Kayleigh is a super server and makes everyone feel welcome!!

This the spot is low key and a vibe ! This music is international not just Afro beats. The hookah was amazing, the service was great and fast, and the food was on point! Highly recommended if you’re visiting Miami!

To begin with, Jai is beautiful. This is my first time here and Jai’s customer service is AMAZING. She explained the menu to me and my friends very thoroughly and gave us time to look over. I would definitely recommend this place and Jai and her section. The vibes were great. The lemon drop was strong and the Bob Marley was the perfect mix. Thanks to Jai I had an amazing time for my friend’s birthday.

The atmosphere is amazing, my server was Gabby! And she was amazing very attentive and attractive. She made me a blueberry mint hookah and it was one of the best I’ve had in awhile. I would def go back to see her again
:-). Thank you for the amazing experience.

formatted_address: 5007 Hiatus Rd, Sunrise, FL 33351, United States
name: Sankofa Kitchen International

reviews.text: I traveled 2 hours to buy food from Sankofa. Its my first time trying African (Specifically Ghanaian) food, and it didn't disappoint. The place is a cloud kitchen. There is no seating or indoor restaurant. You have to order through their website or third party food delivery app. The maps took me there without knowing those facts but the employee spotted me and took my order right away. She was very kind. She explained me everything. African food is hard to come by in Florida and this place just understands it. If you're looking for the best west African food in the state of Florida, look no further. I love their jollof rice with grilled tilapia, banku and okro stew and fried plantain. Try it and thank me later. :)

I have to share my experience. African food is hard to come by in Florida and this place just understands it. The amazing customer service that leaves a customer like me traveling from west palm Beach an hour and 20 minutes! Just to eat it. This is my go to on Saturday just like it should be yours. ( this isn't paid promo btw lol)

First time trying African Ghanaian food. I really wanted to try fufu and I found an amazing place.
The place is a cloud kitchen. There is no seating or indoor restaurant. You have to order through their website or third party food delivery app. The maps took me there without knowing those facts but the employee spotted me and took my order right away. She was very kind. She explained me everything. I got chicken pepper soup and fufu. I got sobolo drink. The drink was spicy. I was not expecting that. But it was delicious. The main entry was so good. Perfect amount of spices and tender chicken. The quantity was good. I want to try different foods from here

I travel 3 hrs every weekend to buy food from Sankofa. Philipa and her team are amazing. They provide great customer service and delicious meals that are decently priced. If you’re looking for the best west African food in the state of Florida, look no further. I love their jollof rice with grilled tilapia, banku and okro stew and fried plantain. Try it and thank me later

I came to this place twice in attempt to support my local west African community while giving them the benefit of the doubt with the first attempt being very disappointing. First , this isn’t a restaurant so you have no idea how your food is being prepared or how clean the environment is. 2nd you have to wait in the car just for them to bring your order to you. I ordered Egusi soup with fufu and was given oil instead of soup with the meat being undercooked and tasteless. The picture on the advertisement is different from what is being cooked. No accountability has been taken on the managers part in addition to being met with a disturbing attitude about my criticism towards the food. I spoke with another manager ensuring that I would be compensated with another meal for my experience. Given, that I left a heartfelt review explaining my experience and took it down to actually give them another chance because of the request made by Mr.Marcus.

I come back on a second attempt to order rice and chicken which was decently prepared and a go to meal that I’ve gotten before. Drove 40 minutes across town to pick up my food in sunrise only to be met by the same wicked manager that gave me a nasty attitude. Denying giving me what I paid for and saying she won’t serve me because of the review that I left although I paid for my food. She forced a refund and cut the lines so I wouldn’t contact the business.

Now if this is the way you go about conflict from a disappointed customer, you shouldn’t be in the food business along side your emotions driving you to make compulsive & irrational decisions that will sooner effect to your business. This lady is beyond cruel and emotionally immature & senseless. May God judge you and your wicked ways tenfold. The 5 star reviews left are very misleading and not accurate. I don’t see this place materializing into an entity where people can come in and dine. Customer service by management is awful because of one bad apple.

formatted_address: 7812 NW 44th St, Sunrise, FL 33351, United States
name: Rejoice Restaurant and Bar

reviews.text: First time trying out Nigerian food. It takes me back to that episode on "Good Times" where Thelma was dating this African guy and the family got to try out fufu. It made me want to try out some of that food. I decided to start out something simpler and more familiar. I went with jollof rice, chicken, and plantains. Food tasted freshly cooked and hot. I had no idea jollof rice was that spicy, but it was good. I really liked the chicken as well. The texture of the chicken reminded me of lot like our Jamaican brown stew chicken just with different seasonings. Shouldn't come as no surprise that there is a strong connection between Jamaica and Nigeria since our ancestors came from the southern part of Nigeria. I wanted to get a taste of what my Nigerian ancestors (especially Igbo) were eating. Will be coming back to this restaurant for sure. Maybe I'll try fufu with sauce next time?

Excellent customer service, excellent food!!!this was our first time and I was blown away. The beautiful young woman at the counter was so helpful, patient, kind and friendly. She was so courteous. We dined in and loved and savored every bite! I HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS RESTAURANT!!!! I will be going back and definitely thinking to celebrate my birthday here with my family and friends!!! AFRICA TO THE WORLD 🌎

Egusi was fire had good seasoning even tho wasn’t enough for the price of the plate . Goat was tender but not tender enough  though . Seemed like they mixed my egusi with some sort of goat soup, pepper soup I assume ? Gari was good Plantains were old and hard 6/10. Fried rice tasted instant rice . Chicken that came
In fried rice was okay but kind of taste less 4/10

Went here for the first time and I must give an honest review. The service was lengthy, thought restaurant is super adorable. I got the goat with the egusi soup and fufu.. never had this type of cuisine. The fufu was perfect, the goat stew was delicious but too much fat on it, the egusi soup was ok but not my favorite. We order some chicken too, but it was mostly bone rather than meat.

We visited Florida for Thanksgiving and wanted to kick off the trip with some authentic Nigerian food. A few days before we arrived, I started calling around to see who might cater on Thanksgiving day. Every place was closed including this restaurant, but after speaking with their catering lead, she graciously made a special arrangement just for us.

I’ll be honest, I was a little nervous about ordering without tasting anything first, but I trusted the great reviews. I’m so glad I did because the food was absolutely delicious! We ordered jollof rice, stewed chicken, suya, dodo, and efo riro. My family devoured everything.

The service is what really left an impression. We planned to pick up the food right after landing, so Bukola arranged for someone to meet us since she wouldn’t be there that evening. When I called, the young man not only answered right away, he offered to deliver the food instead of having us drive over. Within 30 minutes he showed up at our Airbnb with hot, freshly made food.

Outstanding service and amazing food. They truly went above and beyond for us on a holiday. Five stars all the way!

formatted_address: 1755 Alton Rd, Miami Beach, FL 33139, United States
name: Naomi's Garden - South Beach

reviews.text: I tried these plantain cups, and they were incredibly delicious! They offer a variety of flavors, including legumes, jacked chicken, and jacked jackfruit. The mango sauce is a standout feature, adding a delightful twist to the taste. I also tried the falafel and hummus, which were served with fried plantain chips. While the hummus was okay, the falafel was decent.

Amazing VEGAN options.
The owner is making sure you like what you eat, which made the experience 10 times better! Healthy & tasty food.

I had a great time at Naomi’s garden! Had the pleasure of recieving the incredible heartwarming story about the name and the passion behind the restaurant and its cuisine, given to me by Naomi’s grandson Noah. Thanks so much for the falafel and hummus, a classic dish, it was delicious. I’ll be sure to come back and bring all my friends! PS, it goes great paired with a refreshing tea from Syndicate!

Staff 1000% on point! Very friendly, patient and accommodating. Now let’s talk about the food!
I’m Haitian, so I can put my food critic hat on — the flavors are absolutely there. I ordered turkey tassot, plantains, rice and Beans, macaroni and cheese, and fish /legume taco w coconut water!!  When I tell you the piklizzzz was adddding to the experience! I will def recommend people to visit! 10/10 thank you again for the great service.

The absolute BEST caribbean food you can get in south beach! If you're looking for the most authentic, delicious and fresh haitian/jamaican food - you NEED to try out Naomi's.

They have deep roots in Miami and it is amazing that they have opened a location serving the south beach community.

Get the Naomi's Sampler with the oxtail, jerk chicken, fried turkey tassot + pikliz. I promise you'll want to come back for more!!

formatted_address: 316 NW 24th St, Miami, FL 33127, United States
name: Dukunoo Jamaican Kitchen

reviews.text:
wanted to take a moment to share my experience dining with you, because it truly left a wonderful impression on me. From the moment I walked in, the atmosphere felt inviting and the staff made me feel welcomed and taken care of. That alone already set the tone for a great visit.

The food, though, was the star of everything. Every dish was presented beautifully, packed with flavor, and clearly made with care. You can tell when a kitchen puts love into their cooking, and that’s exactly what I tasted. The seasoning was balanced, the textures were perfect, and everything came out fresh and hot. I especially appreciated the attention to detail — nothing felt rushed or sloppy.

On top of that, the service was warm, patient, and attentive without ever being overwhelming. It’s rare to find a place that gets both hospitality and flavor right, but you absolutely did.

Overall, it was a truly lovely experience. I will definitely be recommending your restaurant to others, and I look forward to visiting again soon.

Thank you for the great food and great energy. Thank you to Natalie and JD Cell
The food was delicious, the service was quick and thoughtful ans the music was a vibe! The decor is nice and cozy. The oxtail is amazing! Forgot to take pics cause it was so good! Thank you !

Sunlamp was fantastic from the food, service and vibe! The drinks were strong and delicious. Had the oxtail pasta and festival. Sooo good and can’t say enough about our server Jazz. She was attentive, fast and gave wonderful recommendations from the drinks to the food.

The hostesses at the front were friendly and attentive. Run don’t walk to this establishment, you won’t be disappointed.

They also had a DJ that played great jams.

Good flavourful food and some great tasting cocktails on the menu. Has a great vibe here with the DJ playing some bangers. Service was quick, didn't have to wait long to be seated or for the food to arrive. Server was helpful in going through the menu and recommending some dishes/drinks.

Just a bit overpriced but may be due to the area.

Highly recommended authentic jamaican food. It's pretty modern and catered to a more hip hop, jamaicany younger crowd. However the food was really delicious. And the staff very kind and friendly. I recommend having the oxtail tacos, the shrimp and grits were great too.
