reviews.text:
Naomi’s Garden is the kind of place I respect. No gimmicks, just quality. The Soup Joumou was excellent. Deep, layered flavor and authentic Haitian cooking done right.

The atmosphere is relaxed and well put together, and having Syndicate Kava Bar inside elevates the experience. You can enjoy a great meal, sit back, and actually unwind.

Great quality, excellent service, and parking.   I’ll be back.

This place is such a hidden gem! My family and I came here to get food before flying back home and we couldn't be more happy with our meals. I got the king fish, rice and peas, and plantains. The portions are hearty for the price range and everything is beautifully seasoned. And you have to get their juices!! Perfectly sweet and refreshing! Not only that but the people and owners are the nicest people we've met by far in Miami! I cant imagine how beautiful and lively this place is at night! I hope this business prospers for decades to come 💕💓

We went to the location in Miami Beach and it was a horrible experience.  There was little human interaction when you first walked in, just a kiosk to place your order.  There was a bartender there when we arrived but she was wholly inattentive and not very helpful (didn’t even realize she was the bartender as she was sitting at the bar chatting with her friends as if she was a patron).  With so many eating options nearby, this place has to step up their customer service game as their food alone (which was decent but not spectacular) is not going to sustain and drive the business they need.

Now I was really hoping the vegan food was great, but highly disappointed. The Legumes and Mac were good, but the greens and rice and peas were bad. The vegan greens did not have a lick of salt or any seasoning at all, bland. I mean I had to dress it up myself and was still disappointed. The rice and peas and curry chicken were bland as well. Not sure if it was because we went so late but nope I’ll pass.

Always an amazing experience. The food is excellent and hard to beat for the value. Vegetarian options abound, and the portions are generous. The ambiance in the back garden is beautiful, and the ladies behind the counter are always kind and helpful. Sabrina was super nice and took great care to explain every dish to me. Highly recommend!

name: Teff Fields Ethiopian Cuisine @ethiopiancuisine

reviews.text:
Amazing vegetarian food, very tasty and fresh that it gets over soon.
Make sure to go before 3 pm,

We had tasty injera and 9 different vegetarian sides all for 15$ or less.

This place is inside the farmers market area.

Simply the best!!! The women that make the food do so with so much love. You are in for a treat. Find them at booth 187 while you are at the Green and Yellow Farmers Market. You will be in for a treat. 😋 Dont forget to add a hot ginger tea to complement the meal.!

As someone who has enjoyed Ethiopian cuisine around the world — including in Ethiopia itself — I can confidently say this was a 10/10 experience. The flavors were rich, the injera perfectly tangy, and the spices hit all the right notes. Authentic, soulful, and deeply satisfying. If you love Ethiopian food or want to try it done right, this is the place.
My first venture into Ethiopian cuisine, and I was blown away. The vegan dish was full of flavor. The women who served us are so kind, and explained everything to us. Highly recommended!

The 2 sweetest little ladies, and absolutely incredible food. This place is consistent and delivers every. single. time. My wife and I ate the whole plate, completely disregarding the fact that we were stuffed.

Without a shadow of a doubt would eat here again.

formatted_address: 3301 NE 1st Ave, Miami, FL 33137, United States

reviews.text:
Food was delicious. My part had the Buddha bowl, avocado toast, and pancakes. The Buddha bowl was packed full of healthy and delicious flavors. I would definitely get it again. I tried the other two dishes. The avocado toast was on nice hearty bread. The pancakes were fluffy and good.

The gentleman serving us was pretty nice. He wasn’t overly friendly but was professional. My only complaint would be having to ask for something multiple times.

The atmosphere was nice outside.

I would go again.
The food was tasty. Portions are big and they looked amazing. The service was a bit slow and hard to get the attention of waiters.

Delicious Brunch & Outstanding Service!

We had a wonderful brunch experience—everything from the warm service to the delicious food was spot on. The menu had great variety, and every dish we tried was fresh and flavorful.

The juice tasted freshly squeezed, and the coffee was absolutely divine—rich, smooth, and the perfect start to the day. The overall dining atmosphere was relaxed yet refined, making it an ideal spot for a leisurely weekend brunch.

Highly recommend and looking forward to coming back!

This is a cute little spot in midtown. I came for brunch and everything tasted so delicious and fresh, even the ketchup. To drink, I tried the lychee rose and it was very refreshing. As the entree, I tried the any style eggs omelette with cheese, mushroom and organic bacon. This meal was very filling and tasty. The bacon pieces were big and crispy. The county potatoes were also very flavorful. The bread did need some butter to make it tastier. I also tried the French toast and it was delicious. I loved the amount of fresh fruits that it had. The service was a bit slow but worth it. The waiter was nice. We stayed there longer due to the weather and not once did we feel rushed, which was shocking seeing how small this place is. I would definitely return.

After hearing so much about this place, I finally decided to check it out. While I love the farm-to-table concept and the menu is definitely creative, the overall experience didn’t quite meet my expectations. Our server was a bit awkward and service was noticeably slow—we waited quite a while just to get our drinks.

As for the food, nothing really stood out to us except for the Shakshouka, which was genuinely delicious and the one thing I’d return for. That said, it’s great to have a spot like this in the area. The outdoor seating is lovely, especially for people-watching while enjoying a drink or some light bites. I’d probably come back for that kind of casual experience rather than a full meal.

formatted_address: 3500 NE 12th Ave, Oakland Park, FL 33334, United States
name: Red Sea Eritrean & Ethiopian Cuisine

reviews.text: This is a hidden gem!! Janet are server was quick, kind and on point with the menu. The owner Joseph was present , kind and extremely inviting. The food is extremely flavorful!! If you love spicy, this is the place for you. My cappuccino was spot on!! The Ethiopian tea was refreshing. Definitely a place to frequent!!!

First time eating Ethiopian food and we loved it! The waitress explained a lot to us and recommended some dishes. Everything was delicious and would eat again except for the Kale. If you are in the area definitely stop and check this place out.

A truly unique dining experience. Everything was perfect from the service to the food. It is an elevated Ethiopian/Eritrean restaurant- they did a great job decorating. There's ample indoor and outdoor seating. We ordered the four sampler vegetarian platter and a lamb dish. Both were extremely unique and delicious. The owner, Joseph, even came over to check on our table at the end. Please support this local establishment, a perfect addition to Oakland Park!

My wife and I recently had the pleasure of dining at Red Sea, a brand new Eritrean and Ethiopian restaurant in Oakland Park, and it was an experience worth savoring. Over three years, owner Joseph built this modern-yet-cozy space, creating a warm, welcoming atmosphere ideal for a date night or a relaxed evening with friends.

We visited on a Sunday when it wasn’t particularly busy, though it clearly picks up quickly as word spreads. Subtle Ethiopian jazz played in the background, adding cultural depth without being overpowering. Despite the sleek, modern design elements—like woven pendant lights and softly illuminated walls—the padded chairs were impressively comfortable, letting us truly settle in. The bar area, with bold-patterned stools and neatly arranged spirits, serves as a stylish focal point. Outdoors, a charming patio space is surrounded by greenery and gentle lighting, and the restaurant’s polished façade hints at the thoughtful craftsmanship you’ll find inside.

For the uninitiated, meals here are typically enjoyed with injera, the tangy, 100% teff (and also gluten free) flatbread, using your hands instead of utensils. It’s worth noting that Joseph spent several months perfecting the 100% teff recipe to suit Florida’s climate—ensuring the injera maintains its authentic tang and texture despite the region’s humidity. Conveniently, there’s also a dedicated hand-washing station off the dining room, so you won’t need to head to the restroom just to rinse up.

Red Sea’s menu is intentionally focused for now but will expand as the restaurant settles into its rhythm. What’s already available offers a mouthwatering introduction to classic Eritrean and Ethiopian fare. One standout is the Vegetarian Combination, where you choose four vegetarian dishes. We opted for Red Lentil (Mesir Wot), bold and spiced with berbere, onions, garlic, and ginger; Chickpea Flour (Shiro), a smooth, comforting stew with moderate heat; String Beans (Fasolia Wot), lightly spiced and fresh; and Kale (Gomen), offering an earthy depth thanks to onions, garlic, and mild seasoning. Other vegetarian options include Sunflower Seeds (Suf Fitfit), a refreshing cold dish with chopped seeds, jalapeños, tomatoes, and garlic; Beets (Kaye Sir), cooked with carrots, onions, ginger, and garlic; Cabbage with Carrot (Tikel Gomen), featuring cabbage, potatoes, and carrots; and Split Peas (Kik Alicha), simmered with mild herbs and a touch of turmeric.

For a meaty contrast, we tried the Beef Jerky (Quanta Firfir), featuring in-house dried beef cooked in a richly seasoned and berbere-heavy sauce with shreds of injera mixed right in. Each smoky, spicy bite was perfectly balanced by a side of crisp greens and diced tomatoes. Other meaty entrées include lamb dishes such as Lamb Tibs or Lamb Derek Tibs, as well as Chicken (Doro Wot) slow-cooked with onions, berbere, and spiced butter.

The Nuova Simonelli espresso machine behind the bar signals Red Sea’s commitment to quality coffee. Although we didn’t sample it on this visit, the menu includes Ethiopian Coffee, cappuccinos, and hot house tea, all excellent ways to wrap up a meal. You’ll also find draft and bottled beers, soft drinks, and Tiramisu—an unexpected but meaningful nod to Eritrea’s history as a former (albeit brief) Italian colony.

From start to finish, the service was exceptional. Joseph was attentive, knowledgeable, and clearly enthusiastic about sharing the cuisine’s rich heritage. Between the beautifully crafted stews, gentle Ethiopian jazz, and comfortable seating, Rachel and I felt at ease throughout the evening.

If you’re seeking high-quality Eritrean and Ethiopian fare in South Florida, Red Sea is a must-visit. The lovingly designed interior, bold and authentic flavors, and impressive espresso setup offer a refined yet intimate dining experience. We can’t wait to return as the menu continues to expand—and to finally try that espresso.

All I can say is "Wow!" It's been awhile since a restaurant has stirred my palate in a profound way. Red Sea did just that! From the  lovely decor, attentive customer service, amazing food and delicious dessert, everything about this place is all kinds of wonderful!

name: Queen of Sheeba

reviews.text:
Phenomenal! We have been searching for Ethiopian food since we moved to florida. My husband loved the chicken & the beef stew. The vegetarian platter is what everyone should get! The yellow lentils, green beans and cabbage were exceptional - everything was great, though. My husband loved the red lentils and the collards.
It was pretty packed by noon on a Saturday, but they were very kind and accommodating. We will be back! :)

This was a wonderful experience and it was my first time having Ethiopian food. The service was excellent,  so welcoming, made you feel like family. The spiced tea was great, was like Christmas in a cup. The food was absolutely delicious,  everything was good, the red lentils and cabbage dish were my top favorite veggie dishes but loved all of it. The Doro Wot was so yummy,  it's a very special dish to Ethiopia. The restaurant is beautiful,  I loved the art work and it just transported you to another place. Felt like I was on vacation.  I will definitely be back.

Everything is was very good. I didn’t have a chance to take pictures as my family ate all the food. Only when we got to dessert I had a moment to snap that one picture.
Make sure to make reservation ahead as the restaurant cooks food pending on number of reservations. This is family own and operated restaurant. We most definitely be back for another delicious meal.

Had a wonderful experience at Queen of Sheba with my sister and cousin. Some of the best Ethiopian food - dare I say THE best - I've ever had. Dining in, surrounded by artwork and listening to Ethiopian jazz, one really feels as if they've transported to another world. Get yourself a large platter of various things to share with friends, you really can't go wrong!

Get your passport ready!  If you ever wanted to know the flavor & culture of Ethiopia, you will have it here, without having to stamp the passport!  Queen of Sheeba is on 7th & Sapodilla, next to Heart & Soul Park.  The food here is unbelievable.  Very delicious & unique taste explosions.  I loved my Lentil Stew & Ethiopian Tea!  Beautiful decor & cultural art & artifacts.  Do call & make a reservation.  Open Wednesday-Saturday, but they open & close for lunch & dinner.  Dinner opens at 5:30pm.  Be prepared to eat with bread as your utensil...easy to clean your plate!  Also, know that the experience is to be savored, so relax & take your time & enjoy.

The best in miami

I liked that they took feedback about the food very seriously. Always striving to improve. Thank you for the service.

formatted_address: 295 NW 82nd Ave, Miami, FL 33126, United States
name: Ashoka Indian Restaurant - Miami

reviews.text:
We stopped by this restaurant on our way back from Key West, and it turned out to be one of the best dining decisions of the trip. The moment you step in, the ambiance leaves a lasting impression — elegant, spacious, and beautifully designed with just the right mix of modern and traditional elements. It has a lively yet relaxing vibe that makes you want to stay a little longer.

We decided to try a few appetizers along with their pav bhaji (spicy version), and everything tasted fresh and well-balanced. The pav bhaji had just the right amount of heat and buttery richness — exactly how it should be. The portion size was generous, and the presentation was thoughtful. The starters were equally good, flavorful, and nicely seasoned. You could tell that a lot of attention went into the ingredients and preparation.

The staff was courteous, attentive, and made sure our dining experience was comfortable throughout. The service was quick, even though the restaurant seemed quite busy when we visited. It’s always a great sign when a place manages to maintain quality and warmth during rush hours.

Overall, this is a wonderful stop for anyone craving authentic Indian flavors in Miami. Whether you are a local or passing through, it’s worth checking out. My only small wish — I wish they served a good cup of chai to wrap up the meal. That would have made it absolutely perfect!

We were traveling from Key West to Miami and stopped at Ashoka for lunch. The ambience immediately impressed us, and our waitress, Kathia, was exceptionally warm and helpful. As vegetarians, we found the appetizers quite tasty, though the main course was average. The prices were reasonable overall, and despite the mixed food experience, we truly appreciated the wonderful ambience and attentive service.

We visited with no set expectations and had a mixed experience. The veg biryani was delicious and the chola bhatura was quite good. However, the dosa sambar and chutneys didn't taste fresh. Additionally, the loud music made the atmosphere feel a bit overwhelming. 18% gratuity was too much , we were only 3 ppl who had dinner

everything was amazing!! we had these amazing garlic cheese truffle naans and i'm obsessed!! Everything was delicious, listen to the recommendations from your server to hear about new menu items! Kathy gave us amazing recommendations, and the service was excellent. Can't wait to come back!

I'm not normally the type of person who leaves reviews, but this is actually so ridiculous that I feel compelled to say something so this doesn't happen to others. I will keep it simple. I ordered the loaded butter chicken poutine for $18.99, description: "Delicious fries tossed in our butter chicken curry with cheese curds and topped with jalapeños, onions and scallions". Attached photo is what I received. Now, did they taste good? Sure. Was it worth almost $20 for glorified cheese fries? Absolutely not. I even paid extra for the chicken version instead paneer and there was not one single shred of chicken to be found (or jalapeños? Scallions? Onions?) I just feel like on good faith I have to give this one star. 👎 Save your money.

formatted_address: 1049 Washington Ave, Miami Beach, FL 33139, United States
name: Safron Grill

reviews.text: I’ve only ordered delivery, but it’s our go to spot for fairly quick and reliable service. I enjoy the doner gyro plate and love the rice, the chicken skewers are sometimes little dry,  Adana Kebab Wrap is really tasty. The Greek salad is good. The lentil soup is tasty but too spicy for me and is more of a purée. The tzatziki was too much garlic and onions so I can’t have it and the hummus is very garlicky so I can’t have that either.

I truly love this place ! Have been here countless times and tried various different meals. The owners are from Turkey and provide delicious, healthy cuisine. Totally recommended! Not a single thing in menu is bad. Salmon is one of the best I have ever tried !

I work for my amazing cousin, a gorgeous and busy businesswoman ! Her place is stunning and right on the beach. I meant to post this yesterday—lunch was incredible! The seasoning was on point, and even her husband gave it 5 stars they ate all of mine . Plus, she’s doing all this with a newborn at home. Talk about a lady who does it all! Honored to place the order on her behalf. Thank you, Safron best Mediterranean ever. I will be back today before I whip up my cousins makeup so please keep my food warm and,  look for my name Maylemia Shan  , for the superfast presentation and unforgettable hospitality. Ty my baby cousin approves so much so she ate all my food 5 stars ✨ would give 10 if I could

We ordered the mixed grill and the lentil soup. It was delicious, very tasty. The first time in a long time where we finished everything on the plate it was so good. The hot tea was also good. Our server Kenya was wonderful, a real gem. The service was fast and friendly and we got there late around 11:45 pm. We are from Atlanta and this was our first time here but definitely plan to return when we visit Miami again.

This is the place to go in Miami Beach! I’ve been here several times and I’m always amazed by the food. Today I came with a group of friends and we all loved what we ordered. The food is tasty, reasonably priced, and the service was quick and friendly. Nancy took great care of us and made sure we had everything we needed! We will definitely come back.

formatted_address: 200 NW 54th St, Miami, FL 33127, United States
name: Chef Creole Seasoned Restaurant

reviews.text: So refreshing to go here. Now here is a place you have to go because it does everything right. First off, they have a unique drive through system that does not feel like you’re in a cheap fast food spot, but it gives you a beautiful Caribbean familial vibe. If you want to stay, they have great parking access and two beautiful outdoor seating area. One is on sand the other has a hut vibe. Service is phenomenal. However I would go back just for the conch fritters (my favorite). Food so good. Must stop by place every time.

Hands down one of my fave Haitian Caribbean eateries. The atmosphere gives island vibes and the food is fresh (you will have to wait but it’s worth it) love the oxtail, the fish and if you’re vegan get the Rasta plate. The soup joumou delicious on New Year’s Day! Highly recommend. Our run crew stopped by for a photo op with the Chef!

Does anybody remember that brown cat that used to beg for food in the outside dining area? name: Ochio Island Grill And Catering

reviews.text: Came here from word of mouth, and I was pleasantly surprised. I came on any normal afternoon, and the nice lady taking orders recommended me a plate of food (it's my first time trying Jamaican food) and the other man was also very kind and hyped up the food. I came back to work, sat down, and ate, and the hype was worth it.. the food is top notch. Flavorful, seasoned to perfection, and amazing price. Would come again! ♥️

The food was excellent!!! Arriving to the smell of the grill was a good sign it would be great and we were right! We got the jerl shrimp, jerk chicken, and sweet potato pudding and man were the portions huge too! The spice was just right you could taste the smoke in the chicken and the rice with oxtail gravy was delicious. It took us 15 minutes to get back to eat but it was still piping hot! The pudding tasted heavy in bananas but was still very good, not too sweet, and we crushed the whole thing without feeling bad!

Ummmm — this might just be the best Jamaican food I’ve ever had! My partner had the oxtail, and I went for the vegan options (can I get a hell yeah for vegetarian/vegan options?!). The flavors were absolutely incredible — rich, bold, and so satisfying. I live 2.5 hours away, and honestly, I would make the drive back just for this meal. If you’re anywhere near Homestead, this spot is an absolute must-stop. You won’t regret it!
Chef Troy don't mess around! My entire family fulljoyed their dinners made with love...the best brown stew fish in the world! The service was great and everything sell off!! Thanks Chef! Blessings!

What can you say when you get together with friends and family to have a meal and enjoy each other‘s company along with great music and ambience and you find a place where you could do all of that and more. the food To die for the service is excellent. I’m definitely recommending this place to all my friends and family. My favorites Are escovish fish The jerk pork and to start me up the fried shrimp With the secret sauce just fantastic every time you take a bite it hits a different pallet a different flavor better than the last I will definitely  be back soon. thank you guys I had a great time.

i feel like this place is the only place at fiu where the food is actually fresh & healthy. Absolutely clean & you feel so good after eating it especially when you're on a diet. I also really like that they have vegan & vegetarian options as well. 10/10

Layali Express is the best place to stop at for delicous food in the middle of a busy day. The staff is incredible welcoming and the food is delicious. Highly recommend. If you haven't been, you're missing out!

Third time coming here for lunch this week. Have tried something different each time and have not been disappointed! Both A and Z have been super friendly and great in recommending different things to try.
Layali is new to FIU and has some much needed vegetarian & vegan options. Food was super fresh and employees were helpful and friendly.

reviews.text: If you want AUTHENTIC, delicious, satisfying Jamaican food that tastes like home. This is maybe the only place in Miami area to get it. It takes a long time to get the food so you have to call ahead and this is because they're making it from scratch fresh. It's definitely a hole in the wall, which is why I gave the atmosphere a 4, but it's nostalgic and a place for us as jamaicans to coalesce and feel at home. Love the owners as they are very hospitable and welcoming. This is a place that I can trust the food will be good everytime. Thank you for tasting like home !

My first time eating here I called ahead to verify if they had the cow foot dinner the woman on the phone was very polite she advised me yes so I went on door dash and order it …. The meal was excellent  9/10 a couple days later I took my cousin and we tried the oxtail plate that was also a 10/10  and the beef stew was a 7/10 I am in love with this place the quality of food they serve they have a new regular and it’s a must I come weekly now .
Food was delicious. Great customer service. Nice price for the amount food they give. Curry goat was amazingly good

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Cliff’s Restaurant – A Hidden Gem for Authentic Jamaican Flavor

If you’re searching for the best Jamaican food in Miami, look no further than Cliff’s Restaurant & Catering on NW 7th Avenue and 107th Street. This place may look like a humble hole-in-the-wall from the outside, but don’t let appearances fool you—Cliff’s is a powerhouse of flavor and tradition.

Every dish I’ve tried here has been absolutely delicious. From the tender jerk pork and rich curry goat to the perfectly seasoned brown stew chicken, the food is consistently fresh, flavorful, and deeply satisfying. Their lunch specials are generous, and the soups and stews are soul-warming in the best way.

What makes Cliff’s stand out isn’t just the food—it’s the feeling. You walk in and immediately know you’re somewhere special. The vibe is authentic, the staff is friendly, and the kitchen clearly knows how to honor Jamaican culinary roots.

Whether you’re a longtime lover of Caribbean cuisine or just curious to try something new, Cliff’s is a must-visit. It’s one of those rare places that feels like home and tastes like heritage.

Always drive by but today I Stopped for lunch and got curry goat medium size and the portion was good I couldnt eat it all at once. It was full of flavor and tasted fresh. I also had their pine and ginger drink which was amazing so refreshing. I can’t wait to go back

name: Sh'hiwa Express

reviews.text: Phenomenal food and experience. I’ve tried every Moroccan restaurant in the United States and this is definitely number 1 not number 2 not number 3 not number 4. This is the best Moroccan food in the United States of America. Very wide variety of food on the menu. I took a flight to miami just to try the food and it was definitely worth it. All these others Moroccan places claim to be authentic but this is the only authentic Moroccan food I’ve had in my 25 years of being in America. The chef is 90 year old Moroccan lady who has the best experience the kitchen. Eating at this place made me want to move to Miami. If I lived in Miami I would eat here for breakfast lunch and dinner.

Wonderful!! I visited Morocco several years ago and fell in love with the food (and the country). Ever since then, I’ve tried various Moroccan restaurants here and there in the states, and while some of have been pretty good, I  have always been mildly disappointed— nothing ever fully recreated the tastes I remember from Morocco. Until now— Jackpot! Sh’hiwa is delicious. I just tried it yesterday for the first time, and I’m already craving it again today. So happy to have this in downtown Miami!

I am in Miami with my husband for our holiday and can only be positive about this restaurant. It was great! And the food was delicious definitely recommend! We are not from the US but from the Netherlands otherwise we would certainly order again.
Food is amazing, the food taste so fresh! Highly recommend it!
Very nice people, and very delicious food. 10/10 going to order again. Really recommend it!

If you’re in Florida, Safari African Market is the place to shop a gem for anyone looking for authentic African and international products! What makes the experience even better is the excellent customer service from Brigitte and Clement. They are always welcoming, knowledgeable, and ready to help with a smile. Their passion for providing the best to their customers truly stands out.

If you’re looking for a store that brings the heart of Ghana and Nigeria to your doorstep, Safari African Market is the place to go. Highly recommended!

I had Ghanaian food catered for a house blessing to honor my local priest Father John. He had recommended this place. The food was delicious. It was ready when promised. Excellent service! Professional staff... especially Miss Bridget. At Safari African & International Market you are given personal attention that makes you feel special and like you truly matter as a person and not just a customer.

reviews.text: Fly Chef Garden Restaurant and Bar is an absolute gem in Miami! From the moment we stepped in, we were treated to the warm hospitality of Chef Craig and his team. The Eforiro with white Rice and Eba transported us straight to Nigeria with their authentic flavors. And let's talk about the Asun and Peppered Snail - simply divine! Each bite was bursting with flavor and made us crave for more. But what truly sets this place apart is the Chef's exceptional customer service. His passion for his craft and dedication to ensuring a memorable dining experience truly shines through. We're already counting down the days until we can visit again! If you're in Miami and craving tasty authentic Nigerian cuisine, Fly Chef Garden Restaurant and Bar is an absolute must-visit.
Truly love the authentic, tasteful Nigerian dishes. Ordered Red Snapper fried yams and sweet plantain. The spicy snails were delightful. Will certainly be back.

I ordered delivery from Fly Chef, and it was an incredible experience from start to finish! The food arrived hot and fresh, and the flavors were absolutely amazing. I had the jollof rice, and egusi with assorted meat, and it was perfectly seasoned, with authentic spices that made every bite a delight. The portions were generous, and the quality of the ingredients was top-notch. Even though it was delivery, the food tasted just as if it was served straight from the kitchen. Highly recommend for anyone craving authentic African cuisine. I will definitely be ordering again!

This is the Best Nigerian Food in Miami!! The food was fresh to order and had true authentic taste. While I was waiting for my food, I got a chance to speak with the owner and we had a lovely conversation. All of the staff is very welcoming and made me feel as if I was at home . Love this place and will be my go to Nigerian restaurant in Miami.

This place is an absolute GEM in Miami! Hands down, it’s the BEST Nigerian restaurant in the city. I was beyond thrilled to discover it, and if you’re craving authentic Nigerian delicacies, look no further. The hospitality and atmosphere here are unmatched—warm, welcoming, and vibrant. Chef Edwin works magic in the kitchen, while Sindu at the front ensures every guest feels at home. The Jollof rice? Pure perfection. The suya? Grilled to perfection, packed with flavor. And don’t even get me started on the puff puff—crispy, light, and fried in the cleanest oil. I’m so excited to have found my new go-to spot in Miami for incredible Nigerian food! Do yourself a favor a come!

name: World Famous House of Mac

reviews.text: World Famous House of Mac absolutely lives up to its name. The food is rich, flavorful, and ridiculously satisfying. The mac and cheese is creamy, cheesy, and loaded with toppings literally the definition of comfort food done right. Portion sizes are generous, and everything tastes freshly made. The vibe inside is super chill, the music is good, and the staff is friendly and quick. Whether you’re grabbing takeout or sitting down to eat, you can tell they take pride in their food. If you’re craving something cheesy, soulful, and unforgettable, this is the spot. I’m already planning my next visit.

House of Macs truly elevated our event with their catering. The food was fresh, flavorful, and exactly what you want when you’re looking for comfort with a twist. The mac and cheese fried croquetas were a hit— that perfect Spanish-American fusion bite that disappears off the tray in seconds. The honey fried chicken was perfectly crispy and tender, the lobster roll sandwiches were loaded and delicious, and the cornbread and banana pudding brought that warm, homemade feel everyone loved.

What made the experience even more special was the welcoming spirit of Syn, one of the owners. You can immediately feel the love and pride they put into their food and how they show up for their guests.

Supporting the service was AJoo Entertainment, who once again delivered exceptional hospitality. They made sure everything flowed smoothly, guests were taken care of, and the food was served with the same energy and professionalism they’re known for.

Amazing food, amazing people, House of Macs and AJoo Entertainment made the event unforgettable. Highly recommend for any gathering.

Hi my name is Ellie and I came to eat with my girlfriend just right now. We ordered for pickup and sat in a little table right outside. Purple saw us and came over with utensils and napkins even though we were not customers dining in! We ordered the chicken Parmesan Mac and cheese and it was delicious. I just want to emphasize the sweetest most genuine and authentic people that work there. Purple your kindness and sincerity made our night. Love this place forever ❤️

Food was amazing. But I’m more impressed with the customer service. I didn’t get his name. This was Wednesday night, 12/11 The gentleman That passed the food out and make sure everything was right. Maybe he was a manager. He was so awesome. Very nice guy. The server that took our order, she was very nice as well. Thank you for the great customer service. Oh, and I have ordered DoorDash from here before, I didn’t realize they had vegan options. I got the Philly cheesesteak vegan. Very good

A place that lives up to its name! With a name like World Famous house of Mac, I had high expectations. At the start you are teased with the best corn bread you've ever had. It was delicious. And then the main event. The Mac and cheese! I ordered a sampler because I couldn't decide. They did not disappoint. It was sublime!! I will definitely be back for this local diamond.

I wanted Authentic African food. I think I found it. Tucked away in Riviera Beach. I googled and Waalaa! Omg! I had them twice(before I post) and it's consistent.  They don't mix meats unless asked. Which I like. I had Egusi and fufu (1 meal), Jollof rice with chicken(2nd meal) it comes with a simple side salad(lettuce,carrot, onion)refresh the pallet and a sauce and dressing. It is so good and its not overly salty,  and not full of hot spice. The only thing its in a home. I know! But I get it, some of the best cooks are inside a home. Brick and mortar are very expensive to create and operate.  If you don't mind pre-ordering and taking a drive I highly suggest it. I call in advance, place my order and  it usually takes about 25 mins to prepare and ready..I say 30 minutes(for impatient people). Really nice gentleman  will bring the order out to your car once you arrive. Now, when you pick up go, pick up and try to mind your own business(area). You can look but not judge.  The area isn't so great, but what can one do about that when that's what they can afford. We can either help the situation (without taking over) or leave it alone and allow it to do what it do ya ya ya(Beyoncè voice..lol). We do not judge...unless you can 1st help(without taking over). I wish more people would understand this. Especially being none of us are raised the same. Anywho! I'll post the pictures. Try them. We love it. Dang I forgot to take a picture of the Jollof and chicken. I'll order again and add later......to be continued

Best fufu and egusi soup in town hands down. Great person. Cooks the food with love. I’ve been ordering for a year now. And I haven’t had not one miss. It always hit. It always tastes like the first time I ordered reason why I always come back. If you’re on the fence about trying fufu and egusi soup. Don’t hesitate with them. They cook the food with much love and very pleasant and friendly service. I highly recommend and encourage everyone to try them. Sincerely from a constant customer Ray.
Hi, I just ordered tilapia soup with rice and fufu. May I say just off the smell the food smells amazing. I have tried the food and it is as amazing as it smells. Will be coming back.
The food was delicious. Well prepared and served with a smile. I will drive wherever I need to and get it.

reviews.text: My dinner here was amazing. Everything on the menu sounded amazing but I decided on the wings and jerk chicken platter. Everything was delicious! Portion sizes are massive, you can share your food with 2 or 3 people. Service was great and The Citadel is the perfect backdrop for this culinary delight.

Went here on a Saturday night starving, love that they had vegan options. I forgotten what I ordered all I know is that it was delicious.. if you're not familiar with the area its hard to find the spot lol had to go down an alley way.. I mean it was in a pretty cool incognito area had a night club across the way. Pretty cool art to look at as well. Overall I love this spot, wish  they would have given me heftier portions because it was so good 😂.

Just tried this place today, the location on 83rd street is a no for me. The food had little to no flavor, and the service didn’t help— the young lady assisting us was rude and seemed completely over her job.
My rice was bland, the food came out cold, and while the wings were okay, I’ve had much better elsewhere. My friend ordered the grio, black rice with fried plantains, which also lacked flavor, but the portion was good.
Honestly, the only good thing on my order was the Fiji bottled water. I won’t be returning.

Manjay at the Citadel has some fantastic flavors and even better people. The staff are welcoming and kind, which makes the experience even better. My favorite meal is the griot with pikliz, rice and beans, and bannann peze. It's a perfect combination of bold flavors and textures. The conch fritters are also a must-try, absolutely delicious! The sauces take everything to the next level. The only downside was that the steak was a bit too well-done for my taste. Overall, though, I’d definitely recommend stopping by for an authentic and flavorful meal.

This was my first time here. I've never really had any Carribean food like this, and was I in for a treat!! So much flavor!! The jerk wings were probably some of the best wings I've ever had. The boniato fries were yummy, and the jerk chicken bowl with red beans and rice was tasty. I especially enjoyed the spicy pikliz!! My husband had the burger and said it was better than any he's had recently. We will definitely be back to try more, very soon!!

formatted_address: Inside RD International Market Food Court, 7534 Beach Blvd, Jacksonville, FL 32216, United States
name: Kess Kitchen African Cuisine

reviews.text: Kess is amazing and kind hearted. After hearing that it was our first time coming, specifically for her to try the fufu and okra soup, she came over to our table to see how everything was and even offered a bowl of water to wash our hands. I got the okra soup with beef, absolutely phenomenal and perfectly tender, the fufu was perfectly fluffy. I will most definitely be coming back!

Settled in a food cafeteria in an international supermarket, bringing cultures together, She cooks everything fresh and all by herself. How does she do it? Shes a hero. She brings happiness and joy to every person she feeds. Her regular costumers sat and talked to me and were so sweet and filled with love and appreciation for her and told me that every thing they order is always amazing and consistent. Her food brings everyone together regardless of background. When food is able to do that, then you know it’s really special. If you come and there is a wait then be patient. She’s doing it all herself and it’s worth it. Anyone who says it’s not the best is lying. Simply lying.

After seeing so many great comments on social media I decided to try Kess kitchen. The okra soup and egusi with pounded yam were highly recommended so I went with it. The last time I went I waited a while and was not greeted. I do believe she was working on a big order but still... so I left and ate next door. Today my husband didn't think they were even open. He had to call to the back to see which is weird. Anyhow the food made it home. The pounded yam was fine but the dishes themselves were very, extremely, super oily. I don't think it's supposed to be like that,  but what do I know. Well, I do know the beef was also very dry and he arrived early in the day! And overall for the price and taste I was very disappointed. I took photos before I touched it.

I’ve been wanting to try fufu and egusi soup ever since I saw it trending on social media! Jess’s Kitchen was amazing! Plus it’s set in a huge food market —RD International Market on Beach Blvd- with other food vendors which gives you a whole experience! Definitely check them out! Great experience!

Been wanting to try African food  for the longest and finally got to try it out my partner and I order the Egusi soup with beef , jollof rice with chicken and meat pie.
As we both wanted to try fufu for the first time but she was more excited about trying jollof rice
We both agreed on the Egusi as a lot of people recommend it online and seen a lot of people order it as well

The egusi soup was flavorful but does have an aftertaste of fish but the fufu tasted fresh and hot !

The jollof rice was spectacular

The meat pie was my favorite was a perfect balance of spice in there and a lil spicy kick !

formatted_address: 225 S Krome Ave, Homestead, FL 33030, United States
name: Yardie Spice

reviews.text:
An absolute gem and a must visit when in South Florida! We stopped on the way to the Everglades to get some dinner to-go. The owner is so sweet, funny, and kind. She made us feel right at home!

We got the Jamaican patty, curry goat, and oxtail. Everything was delicious and cooked with love. The portions were very generous! We also got the juice of the day which was incredible. It had the perfect balance of sweet, tangy, and refreshing.

It’s my first time trying Jamaican food. I ordered combo 1 ( jerk chicken, rice, salad, plantain). My husband ordered the brown chicken stew. Our son ordered the curry goat. We also ordered fresh mango juice. Everything was delicious. The owners were friendly and down to earth. We were too full to try dessert, but the rum cake did look delicious. This is definitely on our list for future visits to the area.

Love the food at this local spot. It’s tiny and feels like a hole-in-the-wall with only a few tables and counter space, but it’s cute and clean. Food is LEGIT, we've had all the jerk chicken, pork and tofu here and it's flavorful and spicy. Peas and rice are perfect. Locally owned and operated by a very sweet duo! This place is full when we go. Loved the vibe!

WE LOVED THIS PLACE!!!! Heading down to the keys for the week only to have the best food possible before entering. This little tucked surprise holds the most delicious conch fritters ever! The oxtails were best I’ve EVER had. Just EVERYTHING was delicious!! EVERY.THING.
Thank you Rochelle and Jean-Paul!!

Update! We came back for more! Add Jerk chicken to the list of delicious delights!!

We loved our experience at Yardie Spice! The owner was such a great server and host. It felt as if we were sitting down to have a meal in her home! We loved how she went through the menu with us and gave us her recommendations! She was so personable and kind. The food was perfectly spiced! We had the conch fritters and they were very flavorful being crispy and yet creamy on the inside! Our goat curry was perfectly tender and the rice was so beautifully spiced! My favorite part were the juices! You have to try both the hibiscus and the mango turmeric they were show stoppers!!!

formatted_address: 1109 W Waters Ave ste b, Tampa, FL 33604, United States
name: Steaming Pots West Africa Cuisine

reviews.text:
Absolutely loved this place!
The food was genuinely authentic African cuisine—rich flavors, perfectly spiced, and cooked with so much care. Every dish felt traditional and comforting, not watered down at all.
The ambience was warm and inviting, with a beautiful cultural touch that made the experience even more special. Great music, cozy seating, and a very welcoming vibe.
If you’re looking for real African food with great taste and atmosphere, this place is a must-visit. Highly recommend! 🌍

I had the best eating experience, I’ve  had in a long time .  When saying it’s a hidden gem, that’s is an understatement.  I was greeted by Laura( I’m going to presume she is the owner ). Very inviting demeanor. She explained my options when I arrived and I’m glad she did .. I normally grab, go and review. I was glad I sat and enjoyed the ‘all you can eat.’ I had 3 dishes ( mind you, these are not American sized plates and I promise you will not be disappointed) .. I was able to get 3 dishes: Egisi soup w/fufu, Jolof Rice w/fish and Wakaky w/beef.. all I can say I was. Comfortably full and can’t wait to come back . I had a sample of the Puff Puff and that was nice treat.  I can’t wait to come back and try other dishes .. if this is is anything like the food in Africa, I can wait to go and feast . Thank you for give is a taste of home.

Hands down one of the best dining experiences we’ve had thanks to our waitress Jennifer. On top of providing fast, professional service, Jennifer provided us with samples of food to try, explained the dishes and flavors to us, and offered helpful dining suggestions. Overall it made our experience perfect, because the food was absolutely delicious. Very flavorful dishes that taste like a warm hug. Fresh, flavorful food and an overall great experience. 10/10 we will be coming back soon!

Authentic Flavor + Amazing Service!
Just tried this Nigerian restaurant for the first time, and it did not disappoint. The food was excellent, rich flavor, great portions, and cooked with real care. But what stood out even more was the service. Julie and Sylvia were incredible! Very personable, warm, and genuinely helpful. They made me feel right at home from the moment I walked in. I’ll definitely be back.

Wow! This place is amazing.  Jennifer is the best.  She makes you feel like family, and she goes the extra mile, Top-notch Customer Service! Now the food,  the flavors are on point.  They do have vegetarian options and delicious drinks.  The ginger pineapple is great, and they have a mango variation.  Stop in. You won't regret it!

formatted_address: 3424 Red Rd, Miramar, FL 33025, United States
name: Jollof Pot

reviews.text:
Firstly they have a great customer service. The staff is very helpful in terms of helping us understand each food items they have. However the food itself were horrible. The meat was very dry and tasteless. We got the soup as well and they were very bland too not much flavor. They were also a bit on the pricer end especially the food was not great.

The place was very quiet and mostly people do take out. The place was also very clean too. But overall won’t be coming back again.

The staff was very friendly and the location is very clean and welcoming. I got the jollof rice with meat. The meat and the sweet plantains were good but definitely some getting used to the aroma of the jollof rice. The flavor of the rice was like when you burn yellow rice so I am not fully sure if that the rice was burned or if that’s an intentional flavor. I was also served a lot of bone and fat instead of meat. But the meat that I did get was good and flavorful.

Ordered egusi but it wasn’t really a stew it was more of a soup. With all water at the bottom
Kind of disgraceful to Nigerian dishes . There was more water than stew and meat smh. With their little containers. I didn’t know egusi came with the tomato sauce on top. I’m disappointed how can this be Nigerian food and african restaurant without knowing the proper ingredient to make egusi. All water no stew! They are just putting bone marrow and fat in the food calling it assorted. Last I called to see if my food had been picked up and she was acting like it’s none of her business is that how you run a business?

Amazing first time visit!

Efo-riro with pounded yam ★ ★ ★ ★ ★
Snapper with jollof rice and plantains ★ ★ ★ ★ ★
Chicken with jollof rice and plantains ★ ★ ★ ★ ★

First time trying African food and it was an excellent experience. We picked up our meal for to go and customer service was lovely. The restaurant doesn’t do call aheads as of now but the service was quick and friendly. The woman serving us and helping up check out and kind and happy to help describe the dishes to us as well as answer any questions we had.

The efo-riro and pounded yam were delicious!! The mix of spinach and various meats were so flavorful and great. The snapper and jollof rice were definitely the star. The snapper was huge, fluffy, meaty, and spiced so well.

Stop by to try Jollof pot!

Look at the pictures of the food!
Food quality has decreased from 2022 to 2023!
Jollof Pot is an okay Nigerian restaurant. I am so happy I found this little gem in Miami. The flavors are on point.
For non-nigerians: start off with getting the jollof rice with assorted meat/plantain -- this will not disappoint. It is smokey, sweet and filling!
If you are feeling daring, go on Saturday and try the ABULA! It is a traditional dish in Nigeria that we all go crazy for. I love the way she makes it and I love the quality of her ingredients. Please give this place a try, I'll be there every Saturday!

Update: After being here a couple of times, I would definitely remove one star because the workers are not the friendliest and the food is sometimes cold. The quality of the Jollof rice changes depending on the day; same with the plantain and the meat.

Update #2: My most recent picture at Jollof Pot. I decided to give it one more try and it is safe to say, I will not be going back for the Abula. The quality has gone down, taste is bland and the bowl is full of OIL. New staff have been hired that are not even Nigerian (also very disrespectful) and were telling me that "we do it a certain way here." Food was cold and unenjoyable. I will be looking for a new Nigerian restaurant. So upset.

formatted_address: 955 S Kipling Pkwy, Lakewood, CO 80226, United States
name: African Grill and Bar - Lakewood Colorado

reviews.text:
Wow - I will definitely be coming back here!

Walked in to an almost empty restaurant on a cold snowy day and the friendly and warm owners greeted us and we got seated. We knew we wanted the kelewele (fried plantains and peanuts) but didn’t know what we wanted as a main. The owner and waitress said “I’ve got you” and asked us certain questions about what we like and what came out was absolutely perfect!

I’m dying to go back again. Not only was the food wonderful and came out quickly, the owners were also so nice and inspiring - these are the places you love to support.

So yummy!! A nice family owned restaurant with delicious and authentic food. We got plantain fufu with oxtail stew and yam fufu with egusi & lamb. Both were excellent! Definitely give this place a try!

Great place for first timers with genuine African cuisine! It’s family owned and operated which we appreciated so much. The owners helped us choose our meal and we loved all of their recommendations. I didn’t catch their names - but the woman was spot on - no nonsense and could read me like a book as far as what she thought I’d like lol. The man who served us was hilarious and taught us how to properly eat our fufu. Such an awesome place with great vibes! We highly recommend.

Great people and delicious food! Everyone we interacted with was so pleasant and helpful. I wasn't sure what to order and the lovely woman who took our order asked me questions and brought me the perfect meal for me. We both enjoyed our meals which were so full of flavor!

Had a great experience at this restaurant. Service was quick and very friendly. I highly recommend the Ugali with beef - was absolutely delicious! The plantain fufu was also very delicious but beware if you get spicy, it’s VERY spicy! Will definitely be back.

formatted_address: 6603 Leetsdale Dr F, Denver, CO 80224, United States
name: Mama Africa Cafe Restaurant and Bar

reviews.text:
Mama Africa exceeded all expectations. From the moment we walked in, the service was exceptional—our waiter was not only prompt and attentive, but also had a calming presence that made the experience feel almost spa-like.

The food came out surprisingly fast, and they were happy to accommodate a lamb substitution in the veggie/meat combo for two, which we really appreciated. Every dish was flavorful and beautifully prepared. The honey wine was served in a charming little potion-style flask—a fun touch—and the chai latte was both delicious and generously sized.

The ambiance was relaxed and intimate, with table dividers that added a nice sense of privacy. This was easily a 5-star experience from start to finish. Can’t wait to come back.

I had my birthday dinner here and the food was incredible! The beef tibs were the best we’ve ever had. And the veggie platter was flavorful and delicious. They even set out birthday napkins, a card, and a candle. So thoughtful. Will definitely be back.

Seriously some of the best service I’ve had in a long time, our server was very excited to show us his favourite dishes. He also spent the time to educate us the different dishes available. The food was pretty alright, I’d certainly try more dishes soon! Also the honey wine was exceptional.
Finally got some takeout last night after driving by for years, the special kitfo is genuinely one of the best things I've ever eaten. And delicious gluten free injera!

First time trying this place and it didn't disappoint.  My husband and I decided to give it a try.  We had the chicken Doro wat and the veggie platter, it was absolutely delicious.  Service was great, The guy serving us was super attentive and friendly.  He checked on us several times. You must give this place a try If you're looking for  delicious Ethiopia food. You will not be disappointed 😌 🙂

formatted_address: 1670 Champa St, Denver, CO 80202, United States
name: Trybal African Speakeasy

reviews.text:
Trybal African Speakeasy is an incredible find. The atmosphere is amazing — warm, intimate, and thoughtfully curated, making it perfect for a night out where you actually want to enjoy conversation, food, and music. The space is smaller, but in a way that feels intentional and inviting rather than crowded.

Our waitress was very kind and attentive. They maybe could’ve used one more staff member to help out, but despite that the service was still solid. Food came out quicker than expected, and everything was beautifully presented with bold, delicious flavors that really stood out. The cocktails were also excellent and came out promptly.

The music selection was perfect — great energy, culturally rooted, and at just the right volume so you can enjoy it while still talking comfortably.

Overall, this is a fantastic spot with great vibes, great food, and great drinks. I’d definitely come back.

My friends and I went after work and this place is a WHOLE Vibe!! Nice atmosphere and beautifully decorated. The cocktails are a little pricey but very good. I had the Jua Smoke with Mezcal - perfection! 🤌🏾 My second cocktail was the Hibiscus Old Fashion. It was good as well but could not compete with that Jua Smoke! Three of my friends had the Guava Glow and they all enjoyed them. For food, I ordered the chicken suya and it was good, very flavorful and moist. The beignets were just ok. A friend got the plantains and they were very good, nicely caramelized. Service was great - the waitress was very good and attentive so I didn't mind paying the 20% gratuity that is automatically added to your bill. I was a little disappointed they they don't have an actual Happy Hour, being in downtown Denver, but I enjoyed it and will definitely return.

Absolutely loved our visit to Trybal! The vibes were amazing- the perfect setting for a girls' night out. The music, lighting, and overall atmosphere created such a fun and laid-back experience. The small bites were honestly some of the best l've had at a bar. We tried almost every cocktail on the menu. My personal favorites were the Guava Glow, Zamanj Espresso Martini, and Pineapple Juju- Each one perfectly crafted and so delicious. Customer service is a 10/10 from the chef to all of the front of house staff. A special shoutout to Jacob, our bartender, who was super friendly and made some great recommendations. Definitely will be going back.

The location is very beautiful. I just wish it wasn't as dark. I decided to go all out and ordered the Motherland Plate. It was flavorful with a nice sweet burn. I found the beef too tough to enjoy. Next time, I will order the chicken.

A unique spot in demver, feels high end like a fine lounge scene.  Lighting and art create a proper ambience for relaxed and casual energy with an elevated and classy feel.  The musc set the tone perfectly, this place is a proper vibe.
Jacob and Kedar took care of me at the bar, I really enjoyed the Ayo Twist w gin, the mezcal version was nice as well.  Kedar even  made me an off menu drink which was perfect.  Dont skip the Amarula martini either.
The beef suya was proper snd so was the jollof.  Next time ill be sure to try chicken suya and some puffs.
I will definitely return to this spot along the 16th st downtown corridor with friends, looking forward to another great experience at trybal.

formatted_address: 16251 E Colfax Ave, Aurora, CO 80011, United States
name: Akwaba Restaurant

reviews.text: The food was great! I tried the peanut butter soup and okra soup, both were flavorful and comforting. The service was great too! The gentleman upon entry took time to explain dishes from different African countries, which really helped me decide. If I’m ever in Colorado again I’ll definitely revisit!

My boyfriend and I went to try African food for the first time and were not disappointed. Absolutely delicious food, heavily recommend the grilled red snapper and the pastels. My only note is service was a bit slow but with how delicious the food was, that's a non issue. Wonderful experience.

I took my girlfriend to try African food for the first time together, this place is absolutely the right choice. My girlfriend got the palm butter soup with lamb and fufu, I got the grilled red snapper with joloff rice, we shared two of the pastels (meat pies) as an appetizer, and I had a ginger juice to drink for myself. Everything was absolutely delicious, easily some of my new favorite food. It was perfectly seasoned and cooked, they served me the entire red snapper which my girlfriend and I shared. I highly recommend, 11/10.

This place is a must go in Denver - Aurora! The food is incredible, service was great, and atmosphere was fun! The gombo soup and Fufu(plantain) were the best combo I’ve ever had. But just in general really great food and service. Overall, just an amazing dining experience while visiting the area.

First time customer, very recommend this restaurant fasho , nice clean environment with great taste in music and food , very welcoming , they allow tasters before ordering full meal which is what I did so definitely recommend pick tasting before making a full order if first time purchase.

formatted_address: 7225 E Colfax Ave, Denver, CO 80220, United States
name: Queen of Sheba Restaurant

reviews.text: We went here for New Year’s Eve. It was absolutely outstanding! The owner and staff were so friendly and welcoming. The food from the meat plate to the vegetarian one every part was wonderful. Our whole family is four and the children are young adults ate for $76 and took food home. We entered dinner with a delicious spice tea.Wow! What a lovely start New Year’s evening. We will definitely be coming again and you should too.

I don’t write google reviews but I feel it is my duty to share my experience.DO NOT COME HERE!!!!
I live 30 minutes away from Queen of Sheba and the phone does not work so you have to come in person to place the order I guess. I drove the 30 minutes and was so excited to try this restaurant. I pre planned what I was going order so that everything would go as smooth as possible. I enter the restaurant and before I can reach the counter the owner looks me up and down (I was wearing sweats and a hoodie because I was planning on taking the food to go). I asked to place a to go order was she answered “Maybe. I can try.” I have a gluten sensitivity and selected this restaurant because the reviews and menu stated they offer gluten free enjera. When I requested the gf injera she immediately interrupted and said they don’t have that today (which happens at restaurants so sad but no big deal). I said that’s not a problem as I can just give the enjera to my partner that is not gluten free. She said she wouldn’t serve me at all because I’m gluten free. I explained to her that it’s a sensitivity  and that I drove 30 minutes to try to food but was met with nothing but hostility. She said I couldn’t be trusted to not eat enjera and maybe if I bring my partner next time then she could trust me. I did start to tear up (I’m hungry and have never been treated with hostility in a restaurant to this degree) and she said “don’t be a comedian” .Take your hard earned money elsewhere. I recommend Nike Ethiopian in Aurora

Best Ethiopian restaurant in town. I love that this woman runs everything herself. Her love is in the food!!! You can taste it in ever bite. The chicken falls off the bone and the veggie platter is so delicious. Highly highly recommend!

Truly a gem. Food was out of this world fantastic. Chicken falls off the bone. Lamb is tender as could be. The lentils and Yatakelt Wott stand out on their own. Split the Queens Dinner for two with a friend and it was more than enough food for each. The amount of flavor in each bite is well worth dining here. The true star of the show is Ms Zebwe. The amount of love and experience she puts into every dish makes you feel like your eating your grandma's cooking.
Food was incredible, the owner was lovely and cooked it all herself! Truly an unbelievable dinner and for a great price; we will absolutely be back!!!!

formatted_address: 2816 E Colfax Ave, Denver, CO 80206, United States
name: The Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: “Flavorful” describes it. This is a very solid example of Ethiopian food (at least as served in the US — haven’t been to Ethiopia itself so no point of comparison). If you’ve been to Ethiopian before you will not be surprised by anything.  The menus all seem to be pretty much the same and this is no exception.  But that’s not a reason not to go.  It’s damn delicious.  And, for first timers like my kids, the joy of eating with your hands / injera is something not to be missed.

Delicious Ethiopian food, one of our favorite hidden gems in Denver. Super flavorful, hearty portion sizes, great service, overall an amazing experience. Would definitely recommend checking this restaurant out! The spicy beef stew was a particular favorite.

Holy Moly! This place is incredible and so authentic. I grew up in DC which is known as the epicenter of Ethiopian food. This place is just as good as any of the places in DC and it turns out because they used to own one that my family used to frequent. Run to this place if you want delicious food.

Don’t worry about Colfax construction, there was enough parking on the side streets that it was a quick walk. Totally worth every step my wife and I took.

Amazing experience at this Ethiopian restaurant! As a vegetarian, I loved the variety of flavorful veg dishes, especially the lentils and greens. The injera was fresh and perfectly tangy. The staff was friendly and helpful, making the whole experience even better. Highly recommend for delicious and authentic Ethiopian food!

This family run business deserves more than five stars! It's a shame I don't dine here as often as I should, but it truly is a hidden gem of authentic Ethiopian food.

The staff is always accommodating, kind, and thoughtful. When I dined here regularly, the owner of the establishment would remember me!

If you're looking for a unique culinary experience, I would highly suggest this place. The meats and lentils never disappoint, and their sour bread is to die for. Paired with one of their Ethiopean beers, I don't think you can go wrong with anything on the menu. Although suitable for a small group, I think this place is best with a large group as food is often shared and you'll be able to try more things on the menu.

formatted_address: 1535 S Havana St, Aurora, CO 80012, United States
name: Maandeeq East Africa Restaurant

reviews.text: Affordable, portions so big it came on two plates + another bowl for free lentil soup. Shop appears to be going through interior renovations but food was still good. Halal

I'll need to try this place for lunch/dinner for a better assessment. Although they were open at breakfast, it wasn't obvious that they were serving food. The black tea was good though.

Service was okay. The space is extremely basic with no decoration.

There is ample parking space.

I have had African food in London and New York and every experience was delicious! When you think of African you think great flavors and spices! I got none of that here at this place. This was by far the worst spot I ever been to.

I got the goat dinner with the spaghetti. The goat was not seasoned at all and it was overcooked.

The spaghetti had no flavor the noodles were not cooked well. I also got a beef samosa that was not seasoned at all and the beef was terrible and the actual samosa was not crispy at all.

This place was a total fail. I will not be back

They could invest in making the place nicer and more appealing, but beyond that I enjoyed both the meal and service. The lamb was tender and juicy and the rice tasty. All around a quite satisfying meal, and very filling

I'll be going back again.

Colleague and I decided to go outside of our comfort zone and try new dishes.  Decide to try some Somalian food and it was actually very tasty and good!  We ordered the fired goat with rice, lamb shank with spaghetti, and chicken shawarma cuts with rice.  Left satisfied and completely full.  The place is a bit worn down but the lady serving us was very friendly and explained the various dishes and gave us the recommendations on what to order.  Don't let the unknown and the insides keep you away.  Give it a go.

formatted_address: 10200 E Mississippi Ave Ste B, Denver, CO 80247, United States
name: Barwaaqo

reviews.text:
We went in as a pretty big group excited to try Somalian food! The service and the staff are wonderful and welcoming! You don’t get service like this anymore and it’s rare. They presented us with their daily menu and we ordered off of that! Each dish was huge and almost 2 or three meals out of each! Their smoothies were delicious and my salmon wrap was cooked to perfection. Everyone loves their meal! No-frills kind of environment, but there’s also outdoor seating and it’s in a strip mall! Ample parking!

If you’re ordering as a group be cautious because our experience was they gave us extra food (which was lovely) but when we asked for individual check based on what we ordered, we were given a group price. Some of us were too happy about that.

No complaints and anything else though. All the rest was exceptional!

Small simple restaurant. I had wanted to try it for a long time and I finally did. Goat and rice were very tasty! Also really enjoyed the green sauce that came with it. I'll be back to try more. Definitely recommend it for curious foodies or anyone who wants to eat East African cuisine.
Great food great service. I really enjoyed food.

The portions are huge!!! This is by far the most flavorful chicken and lamb I have ever eaten. Both were so tender and juicy. The rice alone is worth the trip! I didn’t think to take a photo of the leg of lamb until it was nearly gone.

Not only is the food quality fresh and delicious, the customer service is outstanding!

Thank you so much for lunch!

1. Sambusa
Sambusa is a triangular fried pastry dish often filled with spicy minced meat or vegetables. It is very similar to the Indian samosa. If you have guessed cardamom as the dominant spice in this dish, you have guessed very well.

2. Bariis Ishkukaris
Bariis iskukaris, we would say, is very similar to a rice dish called pilau. It is seasoned with fragrant spices and cooked in meat broth and generally speaking, tomatoes are added to the dish, making for a superbly tasty meal.

3. Malawah
We can not say much more about this dish other than tell you it is just as easy to make as a pancake.

4. Anjero
Anjero is similar to the Ethiopian injera with the main different being the size and how it is eaten. Anjero is usually a fraction of the size of injera and Somalis love to eat it with honey spread drizzled over it.

5. Halwa
Halwa or xalwo is a festive sweet treat reserved for special occasions, and is quotidian wedding treat. With the main ingredients including sugar, butter, and oil, this may be a treat you would only want to indulge into once a while.

6. Somali Tea special.
Who wouldn't enjoy a cup of tea?

7. Sabaayad
Sabaayad is a flatbread, the Somali version of chapati. It is yet another Somali dish which can be eaten for breakfast, lunch or dinner. If paired together we are better sabaayad and a dried meat delicacy to make a breakfast on the go.

formatted_address: 1074 S Ironton St, Aurora, CO 80012, United States
name: Fidel East African Restaurant

reviews.text: My husband worked on Christmas, so I got to order some spicy food. Fidel was open and after confirming that the meats are halal I ordered Awaze Tibs because I love Berbere spice and jalapenos. Bernere has become a staple in my kitchen because it’s excellent for blackening fish. The Awaze Tibs was delicious and I didn’t need to dirty up any utensils because… Injera 🤤 My dinner tonight was delicious and spicy enough to cause my face to flush a little. I look forward to dining in someday. Thank you all for a great dinner. I appreciate you.

You guys  didn't understand what I ordered, I told you every single order is a separate enjerra and spices but they give all together.

That is not fair and please make sure your customers.
Pay attention every single order.

The wait staff was nice but hard to understand and be understood. I had never eaten the cuisine so wanted an suggestion as to what was good. Only 1 out of the 3 dishes ordered by 3 people in the party was just OK. For the $60 spent it should have been better. I could not believe it cost me $2 for a bottle of water. It also cost $2 for a warm can of soda. If you want to try African cuisine go somewhere else.

The service was horrible. But the 5 stars is for the food. Today I decided not to leave a tip. And I plan on coming back to not leave a tip again. The poor service is saving me money... bc I usually tip generously. But when I finish 2 rounds of food without a refill and no plates are picked up, there will never ever be a tip for that. But no complaints though. As you can see I left a 5 star rating bc I don't NEED service. That's what this generation needs to understand about food service. You don't get a tip just bc you showed up
I really was looking forward to finding a Ethiopian restaurant that was close to my house not only did they make me wait an hour. They gave me the entire entirely wrong order. Do not recommend.

formatted_address: 5091 E Colfax Ave, Denver, CO 80220, United States
name: Sarr Maimouna West African Food

reviews.text: Very Nice service. And, very good food. As a Senegalese Liberian, I wasnt expecting less from my Birthland Senegal that has some of the best food in West Africa. especially the best Jollof rice aka Thieboudienne from Senegal the originators of the dish Jollof rice. Thank you Ms Meimouna. I really had a good time coming in today with my Friend. The thieboudienne, bisaap and thiakri were great. So yummy.

I will start off by saying I love African food, and was excited to see that this opened up just near me.

I walk inside(I am the only one inside), and pitch black, just one or two lights on. A guy sitting on the floor behind the bar, pops up, and asks what am I doing? I ask him for a table for 1, and he is confused, and we go back and forth. He says pick a table, I sit down, and then he says come and get your menu, so I stand up and grab the menu from his hand, and he sits back down on the floor.

I sit there for about five minutes and no one comes to me to take my order. While sitting there, there is a baby just wearing a diaper, running in and outside of the kitchen, obviously a workers kid. Not sure how this place passed health inspection, you can tell from one good look, that its going to be a rough experience. Don't use your money here.
My experience is always great here, I have eaten here more than two hands full of times..very flavorful meals, very fresh, and  my close friends also enjoy Thiebodienne as well.
I’m unsure if this restaurant is actually open for service. Tried to visit around 4pm on a Wednesday a couple weeks ago and all lights were off, door was locked.
I think they just opened and have really yummy take out! The chicken and rice and okra were all delicious and a lot of food for a good price!

formatted_address: 10180 E Colfax Ave, Aurora, CO 80010, United States
name: Tata & Nono Kitchen

reviews.text: These were great!  My 6 year old got the lamb, and I ordered the Sudanese chicken.  For a while the six year old was eating her sandwich faster than I was eating mine.  We will definitely return for more deliveries culinary delights.
We got the grilled fish plate, and were not disappointed. Fish was spiced to perfection, the rice hummus and salad were all tasty as well. Would definitely recommend!

We are lucky to live near this new spot in Mango house! Tata & Nono Kitchen was not only delicious but the family that runs it are very gracious. We got to try their fish which was amazing. We ordered the lamb and beef kabobs. The rice was so yummy and the spicy sauce on both dishes were perfect. 10/10

I felt very lucky to discover this gem of a spot embedded in such a lovely place. I met friends here and got the Sudanese chicken sandwich with fresh mango juice to drink and it was incredible! The bread was so soft, the chicken was deliciously spiced, and the veggies were fresh and so tasty! Amazing customer service as well!
I can’t wait to come back and try other dishes.

My wife and I went for a quick date night on Independence Day to celebrate our country's rich and diverse cultural heritages. We enjoyed the Sudanese Chicken Sandwich and it was absolutely divine. You will surely enjoy your meal here.

formatted_address: 12028 E Mississippi Ave F2, Aurora, CO 80012, United States
name: Home Style Foods Colorado

reviews.text: I have some African friends and they showed me this restaurant, and I have to say this is my new favorite spot!.
What a funny place. Just one thing per day on the menu?! Super good

At first when owner was there customer service was great... They hang up on you.  They advertise days of operation but be closed. If you call and you don't understand the menu they will hang up on you.  very impatient.

Wish I took a picture. Really enjoyed the food. I had spinach stew, jollof rice, some chicken/beef stew…all great tasting. I’m not African and lady at front thought I was lost. It was satisfying comfort food.
One of the best—if not the best—African food spots in Colorado! Lots of flavors and didn’t disappoint.

formatted_address: 7401 E Colfax Ave, Denver, CO 80220, United States
name: Lucy Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: Delicious food! We tried different dishes, and all of them were good. The kids enjoyed it very much, and so did we. Friendly service.

The restaurant was peaceful and quiet. The server was attentive and accommodating. The food was AMAZING! I do not eat spicy food but I couldn’t stop eating the lamb dish I had. I even ordered a plate TO GO

after extensive research, I decided to take my family to Lucy for our first Ethiopian cuisine experience in Denver - and it did not disappoint. a solid 5 stars for flavor alone - the food is well worth the wait (20-30 min).

the meal is an experience of flavor and texture, ending in complete satiety and meant to be shared and eaten with the hands. not to mention an amazing value - you could feed a family of 3-4 for around $35.

we started with 2 veggie sambusas - a fried pocket pastry with a flaky crust and a filling of spiced peas. it was. delicious. the crust was perfectly flaky and they came out super fresh. the inside was spiced right and had a nice contrast to the crust.

the main feature was the veggie combo platter - it comes with most of their signature dishes and injera bread. the injera had a sour taste like sourdough bread. it was soft, spongy, and dreamy - they even offered us more when we finished ours. everything was DELICIOUS. I cannot say enough good.

we left incredibly satisfied. don’t come here in a rush. sit, enjoy the food, ideally with others.

If you haven’t tried this cuisine before then this is the perfect place to try. It seems like a lot of locals frequent this spot and for good reason. I got their beef and veggie platter and it was really good. The flavors weren’t crazy overpowering and it seemed healthy too. I like how it comes in a big platter to share. This was a home run but I wish they had lamb when I went. Guess I’ll have to come again. Oh and the sambusa was very flaky and crispy. Highly recommend starting off with those.

The FOOD was amazing! The staff was friendly and happy to explain the dishes. I personally loved the way she poured the food onto the platter. Made it extra special. I loved the Beef tips so much flavor and so juicy! I can’t wait to come back! Keep up the good work Lucy Ethiopian Restaurant!!!

formatted_address: 802 S Public Rd, Lafayette, CO 80026, United States
name: Ras Kassa's Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: Amazing Ethiopian food! I highly recommend one of the platters to get a full experience. The honey wine is a perfect compliment to the food, the coffee is great and the brownie at the end is one of the best desserts I've ever had.

I went here with a few friends and I loved it. While it was my first time trying Ethiopian food, both of my friends had tried this cuisine many times before. We all agreed that the food was great. The injera was very tangy and soft and everything was plated up really beautifully. We ordered the vegetarian combo, as well as a sweet potato dish and a beef dish. Personally, my favorite was the spiced red lentils. Everything was very delicious and flavorful. The restaurant is also very nicely decorated and the overall ambience is very charming and relaxing. I would definitely come here again and I'd recommend eating here if you're in the area.
