While this type of spice flavorings are not my favorite, my family raves about this place. Owned and run by a family who was originally from Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, you would think that such smells and tasty food from North Africa would require getting on a plane and traveling overseas.

If you love the thrill of trying various food offerings, do yourself a flavor and head to Raska International. The sauce is authentic, the service allows you to slow down from the hustle and bustle of daily life, and you can sample foods like the eggplant that was really tasty.

Must tries - injera, stew, the homemade hummus is to die for, the eggplant, and the doro wot (chicken stew). They also have plenty of vegetarian options.

This is the best restaurant in Fort Collins. Hands down. The food is amazing. The ambiance is lovely like a warm hug in a wholsome home. The owner and chef pays the utmost attention to detail and quality. The dishes are Ethiopian fusion, unique, and delicious. I recommend it to everyone I know.

formatted_address: 707 Federal Blvd, Denver, CO 80204, United States
name: Island Jerk

reviews.text:
The food wasn’t good at all.

The beef patty was super dry. The curry goat was dry as well. Very disappointing.
Coming from the east coast , I’m a hard critic when it comes to Jamaican food . The oxtails here are decent . I ordered delivery and it came super hot and fresh .

The food was okay but definitely not Philly/East coast portions or quality. Usually rice/peas occupy the larger box, with meat & gravy on top—continued in one of the smaller boxes, with another side like cabbage in the other smaller box… making a full platter…

Ordered through a good service for delivery. What I received (jerk chicken salad) vs the menu was very different. What I DID receive was one of the worst salads I've ever eaten. I literally took 1 bite and threw it out.
Some of the best OX tail I had!! Also the spicy beef patties 🔥🔥. Can’t forget the cornbread as well!!

formatted_address: 2005 W 33rd Ave, Denver, CO 80211, United States
name: Ash'Kara

reviews.text:
The food here is terrible for the price. We paid for the preset menu which was $45 (without tip+tax).
Pita was warm but too soft and almost tasted raw. Dips were fine but nothing special.
The steak and potatoes were incredibly disappointing and a small portion. The potatoes were literally just boiled with salt/pepper on them. The chicken bowl had a burnt flavor and did not taste good.
Baklava was drowning and syrup and way, way too sweet, although it was a good portion.
The grapefruit sorbet was pretty good. I would not recommend this place at any price point.

We have visited this restaurant twice. Our first experience was great, which is why we returned. During that visit, we noticed the good quality of the drinks and food, although the portion sizes felt a bit small for the price. The service was outstanding, both the waitress and bartender were very helpful and attentive.
Our second visit, however, was less smooth. The host seemed overwhelmed, and when we asked for a table, we were told we could wait either at the bar or in the neighboring restaurant. We chose to sit at the bar and ordered drinks, the bartender was friendly and helpful. We waited there for our table, and asked twice about it; even though the table was ready the host was more preoccupied with staff than helping us, so we ended up having dinner at the bar.
The food was delicious, but unfortunately, we found a hair on one of the plates. The bartender handled the situation very professionally, arranged a discount with the host, and was understanding throughout. However, the host brought the check without acknowledging or apologizing for the incident, which was disappointing.
Overall, while the food and drink were great, the inconsistent service during our second visit affects our overall experience.

We had 34 people for our holiday party and Elyse coordinated our event for us. Everything was perfect!! We all had a wonderful meal, service and food were fantastic and they were so considerate of everything for us!! Thank you so much!!

We came in so excited after reading the reviews, but we were frankly disappointed. We showed up and waited 10-15 minutes before anyone notices we’re there at the front, the service was rushed and without heart. I didn’t feel welcome, I felt like I was just there to grab a quick bite. It was so loud, I could barely hear the people sitting right next to me. The food was pretty good, but the difference in quantity between plates was shocking… the steak was beautiful but small, the cauliflower was a huge portion, and you had to ask for more pita rather than it be offered proactively. Overall, I was not impressed and won’t be returning when friends visit unless they fix whatever is going on.

This is one of my favorite restaurants in Denver. We've been a couple of times and loved it both times.

Between our two trips with friends, we all shared:

- Hummus with marinated feta
- Saganaki
- Whipped Labneh
- Htipiti
- Roasted Cauliflower Tagine
- Oven roasted leeks
- Falafel
- Fried Halloumi & Panisse
- Hummus with Mushroom Conserva
- Carrot Kibbeh Nayyeh
- Lamb Kebab
- Zaatar French Fries
- Caesar Salad
- Wood-fired Pita
- Paratha Roti

The hummus with mushrooms, tagine, Carrot Kibbeh Nayyeh, and lamb kebab would be my must orders. Everything is delicious though so you can't go wrong.

Our second visit was for happy hour which is a great way to save some money. My number one recommendation is to go with a group and share everything so you can try more.

formatted_address: 1030 Havana St B, Aurora, CO 80010, United States
name: Eatopia: Eat Ethiopian

reviews.text: This place had good ratings so we decided to try it. And it did NOT disappoint. The service was very kind and attentive. And the food was excellent. This is probably one of the best tasting Ethiopian restaurants I have ever been to. Thank you for the great experience and I will come again! ❤️

The food is SO good here!!! Do not be fooled because it may not look super fancy. The food is amazing. And the cook is so lovely and friendly. She explained everything about the food and gave us helpful suggestions. The injera was super delicious. We got the vegetarian combo and the lamb stew. I think this is my favorite lanb stew I have ever had 😍
The vegetarian combo is also completely vegan and gluten free so that's amazing.
We also got the honey wine. It was really flavorful! We also had the beef sambusa as an appetizer. It came with salad (beware of the serrano pepper! 🌶️  its spicy haha) The menu is pretty affordable for such high quality food! Would highly recommend.🌞

The only non "5" star thing was the atmosphere and I actually loved it... It is just nothing fancy.  It is very plain but comfortable.   The food was amazing. We had someone in our group who lived in Ethiopia and other parts of Africa for a while and he said it felt very authentic.   The servers are very nice and helpful.  Plan on being there for a little longer than you might think,  which is good, because they make everything to order.  The tea service was delicious!!!  Go check this place out and when you pull up, don't judge a book by its cover!  😀

Service was great. Veggie combo was great.  Dry lamb was tough and chewy. Lamb stew was bland. Ordered cabbage and potatoes to go. Got home and potatoes were nearly raw in the middle.  Ethiopian coffee was sublime. Nice idea, but there are better consistent restaurants.

Food is fairly consistent and delicious! Service is probably some of the best you’ll experience at any of the Ethiopian restaurants. The only issues I find is that prices stay the same, or even go up, portions seem to get smaller, or things will disappear from a plate you’ve ordered multiple times before and the next time you come in you’re having to ask for it, or it’s just not provided. I really enjoy this place I hope it sticks around.

formatted_address: INSIDE of The Denver Milk Market, 1800 Wazee St Suite131, Denver, CO 80202, United States
name: Konjo Ethiopian Food

reviews.text: The breakfast burrito is so gooood! Highly recommend going Saturday or Sunday during the time they serve brunch. Well worth it! The hot sauce they serve with the burrito is rich and spicy. One of the best breakfast burritos I’ve ever had. Sambusas were also fire!

The food was wonderful. I'm vegan and GF and also in love with Ethiopian food.
My friend tried it for the first time and he loved it.
Great value for your money and your stomach.

Konjo’s new location at the Denver Milk Market is everything! The food, the energy, the service — all of it was exceptional. I had the Lamb Rice Bowl with Gomen w/ Dinich, and my husband had the Lamb Plate with Gomen w/ Dinich — both were absolutely delicious. The lamb was tender and full of flavor, and the sides were fresh and perfectly prepared. Every bite tasted like it was made with love and intention. The service was warm and attentive, and the overall vibe was inviting and rooted in authenticity. You can tell they care deeply about the experience and the food they’re serving.
We’re so happy to see Konjo thriving in this new space — and without question, we’ll be back.

1000/10!
Amazing food!! I had never tried Ethiopian food before and I was not disappointed!
I got the rice bowl with chicken and tikel gomen. Perfect amount of spicy and soo delicious! The owner was also very kind and courteous with all the questions I had. Food was fresh and served to me literally in 5 mins. Definitely a must in Denver!!

My visit to Konjo was amazing!! The staff were so warm and welcoming and the food was incredible!! I ordered a lot because I wanted to try as much as I could. The rice bowl with beef and gomen was delicious!! I had a sambusa as well and it was the perfect texture and so flavorful!! I’ll be taking my friends and family back soon! It’s so close to everything downtown!

formatted_address: 15373 E 6th Ave B, Aurora, CO 80011, United States
name: Gursha Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: I was hoping for a better experience overall. I’ve had Ethiopian food a few times before and I did not enjoy this restaurant the same. A couple friends came with me they loved the sambosa, and they enjoyed half of the vegan platter. I had lamb it was well cooked but very oily. I tasted the items on the vegan platter, most tasted like vinegar. I don’t really care for vinegar taste in my vegetables/lentils. The restaurant was cute! Bathroom could have used a clean up. Service was not bad.
Absolutely fabulous. Love the atmosphere, the music, and the restaurant is lovely and the FOOD is FANTASTIC. Got the vegan platter. It was everything I wanted today. Thank you Gursha!

My husband and I shared the vegan combo plate and the sambosas. AMAZING!!! There was the perfect amount of food for both of us (maybe even a bit more) and each different sampler of food was fantastic. Everything felt very wholesome and authentic, and even the injera on its own was very tangy and delicious. 15/10 recommend this, especially for vegans or vegetarians!

My daughter and I shared the sampler. Exceptionally good! My father had the chicken stew, very good if a bit unexpectedly spicy for his taste. Service is difficult as the server barely spoke English, but we were all able to get everything we needed. I would highly recommend.

What a delightful experience at Gursha. The food was so delicous (we tried the meat combo); the Ethiopian coffee with the freshly roasted bean was oh so good. The service was super friendly and welcoming. We will be back for sure.

formatted_address: 10180 E Colfax Ave, Aurora, CO 80010, United States
name: Natoli Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: Came here while I was visiting Colorado for a weekend training. I looked at the reviews and decided to come and boy was I in for a treat. The location is good because it has other food options within the establishment. So if your family wants something different, which they shouldn't, but if they do... it's available. The food was divine and so fresh. The injera was so tasty and the perfect amount of tartness that I like. I literally ate everything she put for me on the plate. It was shareable, but I was alone and so hungry from traveling. The last thing I wanna say besides thank you to the owner is if you are thinking of coming ... I definitely recommend. Definitely get the orange tea too. I've been dreaming about it since I left!! I really need the recipe 😩

Absolutely excellent Ethiopian food and injera made with 100% teff flour which isn’t as common anymore (and more difficult to work with). The woman who owns the store is very sweet and brings the food out to you.
Atmosphere-wise seating is within the food hall but I had no issues finding a seat. The chai was also delicious, highly recommend!

Natoli is wonderful. The owner, Ameena, is incredibly kind and helpful. She really elevated the experience with a passion for her country's cuisine and offering up explanations on menu items and even letting us sample the Special Orange Tea. She prepares the injera bread fresh daily and it is very good. We tried the Veggie Combo and Awaze Tibs, all of which is tasty with plenty of variety and quantity. The spice heat level can also be customized. The restaurant is located in the Mango House, a cultural activity center. There are shops and other food vendors with a centralized seating area. It's a very authentic experience and I highly recommend giving this place a try.

The food is excellent. I had the combo plate since I hadn't eaten anything all day, and it didn't disappoint. The spiced tea was some of the best I've ever had! I also got some orange tea to go, and it was very tasty. The lady that runs the place is very hospitable. She works hard to make sure you have a great experience, answers questions with patience, and I can tell she has a passion for what she does.

I give the atmosphere 5 stars because even though it is a food court and isn't all that fancy, it makes up for it with it's sense of community. I'm impressed with what people are building there.

Absolutely wonderful experience. First of all Mango House is a gem. We love coming here and this is the first time to try Natoli, and we will absolutely be back!

The food is delicious and Amina, the owner clearly takes pride in her food and makes it with love. We were unfamiliar with Ethiopian food and she helped us choose two very tasty dishes (the veggie combo and door wot).

Highly recommend, both for the food and the experience. I came there with my three daughters, and two of them enjoyed the sushi restaurant while myself and my other daughter had Natoli. That convenience to choose from multiple restaurants was wonderful too.

Can’t recommend highly enough!

formatted_address: 7031 E Colfax Ave, Denver, CO 80220, United States
name: Hadnet Cafe

reviews.text: A comfortable and clean interior immediately makes you feel welcomed and draws you in. The food is authentic, delicious, and made to order. I had the Breakfast Combo with a side of beans (fuol) and an Ethiopian coffee. Truly a delightful woman owned business.

Food was absolutely delicious! The women working are extremely nice and pleasant. Feels like your grandmother is serving you. I wanted to clean the table and wash the dishes afterwards they were so pleasant.

The place feels cozy. It's small somewhat intimate. The only drawback is Colfax. Iykyk. I'll definitely go back next time I'm in Denver.

We had a delicious vegetarian meal here. The food was extraordinary. The service was friendly and kind. The coffee was out of this world. I highly recommend this restaurant and I was very, very satisfied.

Had such a great time here with my friend the cafe has a really cozy vibe, the staff were super friendly and everything came out quickly we tried the breakfast combo/enkulal firfir with the traditional coffee, and it was delicious definitely a spot I’d come back to☺️

My husband and I stopped here after picking up items from an auction - cold and snowy day.  The atmosphere was so cozy and welcoming!  Our first experience with Ethiopian food - and it was wonderful!  The coffee service was so unique, and the food was incredible - we also learned about the culture from the owners, so when we left we felt we had truly had an immersive experience!  I loved the Ethiopian Frankincense - and the owner gave me a small amount along with the charcoal to bring to my daughters to experience.  We had the vegetarian combo and the Quanta FirFir (I sauteed the leftover Quanta FirFir in butter the next morning with a fried egg on top and it was still amazing).  I would come back here in a minute.  Just wish it were closer!

formatted_address: 350 Havana St, Aurora, CO 80010, United States
name: All-Stars Cafe

reviews.text: Me and my kids were there on Sunday like the place good food and excellent sevice .
Awesome 👌 delicious food and great customer service

I get the vegetable combo from here often, comes with a salad. It's very delicious and always hot and fresh. I'm not sure what's in it and it changes everytime I get it but I always love it. Definitely recommend, staff is nice and the environment is very relaxed.
It's nice customer service and fresh Ethiopian food the best shero...

Honest customer service
Amazing food test.
Neat and clean.
And reasonable price.
❤❤❤❤❤❤

formatted_address: 837 E 17th Ave, Denver, CO 80218, United States
name: Watercourse Foods

reviews.text: Such great food! My kiddo is dairy free and we wanted a place with Mac n cheese but yummy food for grown ups too. This was wonderful! She had the pumpkin cookie and loved it too. Also they have Rocky mountian soda and its sweetened with Agave and delicious! I got the turkey and brie sandwich with fig sauce and fries. So satisfying!

There are not enough stars for this place! The vibe is super welcoming and the food and drinks are delicious! Truly unbelievable that it’s all plant based. My only advice would be to check the bakery case before you order because there might be amazing surprise treats. I have the cauliflower wings, Cuban and a cocktail. Took the carrot cake to go and so delicious start to finish. And the friendly staff and welcoming atmosphere just makes it perfect.

The atmosphere, service, and food were all delicious — a wonderful place to relax and enjoy a meal. The staff were friendly, and the overall vibe was vibrant yet comfortable. For the most part, their menu feels thoughtful and nourishing, though they could take it to the next level by reducing some of the less clean/toxic ingredients for an even more wholesome dining experience. Still, a solid go-to for flavorful plant-based meals.

I dined at Watercourse on March 3rd, 2024 and i’ll never dine here again. Let me tell you why.

I honestly wasn’t going to even write a review but the more I thought about how poor my experience was, I realized it was important to share. I traveled from Los Angeles to Denver alone for work and I was excited to eat here, as I am plant based and did a lot of research on where to eat. I decided on Watercourse because I saw they had a three course option for a great price. I excitedly made my reservation about a week in advance. I arrived at about 4:20 and it was pretty quiet. I was greeted and seated by 4:25 and then completely forgotten about for almost 40 minutes. I’m not joking. The servers would look over at me, say something to each other, and then walk away. I had time to spare because I was just going back to my hotel afterwards, so I waited to see how long it would take them to remember I exist. A large party was sat about 20 minutes after I sat down and they were immediately taken care of, drinks and all. Again, there weren’t many tables at this time, the servers knew I was there and hadn’t been taken care of yet, and still continued to ignore me. I don’t remember the exact servers but I know one of them was a woman with very short hair - that’s all I remember. Anyways, when they finally bothered to come to my table, there was no apology for the delay. Very nonchalant. The actual food was ok, it was a bit cold and the only dishes I actually liked were the mushroom starter and the chocolate dessert. The seitan steak and halloumi (?) sticks were kind of gross. This whole experience was highly disappointing and I will never come here again. If they don’t care about their customers (especially single diners) why should I give this place even more money? I have vegan friends that frequent Denver and I tell them to avoid this restaurant like the plague.

I'm not really a vegan or a seitan guy, but they really make a strong effort on all their dishes 😉. The menus are more extensive on the QR code website vs what's on the physical menu. Great selection of alcohol at the bar as well!

formatted_address: 10 S Havana St Ste 110, Aurora, CO 80012, United States
name: Golf 1st Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: The guys here did not know me from a can of paint and welcome to me like I was a native son. I love it hear you know as a traveling photographer from Houston it warms my heart to come here like an immigrant person and feel welcome like I'm in my parents home country. Immigrant people know.  these guys in here are decent Good wonderful excellent people. Let me tell you about this food it was so wholesome and delicious if you're a vegan person, they have all kinds of lentils vegetables beets. Come on down and have a good coffee good music family friendly atmosphere. Good for me to catch up on my picture work.

I got the veggie combo to go. I've eaten Ethiopian in many restaurants in different cities. This experience was acceptable but not wow-ing Firstly, disappointed there are no greens.  NO GREENS... and the picture shows greens on the menu forvthe veggie combo. The cabbage was very good.  The beets were very good too. The yellow lentils were a total miss-- they were salty & dry for my taste.   Great ngera bread though....very flavorful. An honest rating would be a 3 out-of 5 but don't want the business to take a huge hit on their reviews.   I prefer other Ethiopian restaurants in the area over this one. But that's my truth.

The gentleman helping me was very nice.

So after looking at different Ethiopian restaurants, I picked this one to introduce my mother to Ethiopian food.It would turn out that I picked the right place because the food was very good. This place is very much a whole in the wall and doesn't look like much, but the food is good. The service is good as well. The guy even gave me a free coffee as I waited for my food. He was a little surprised when I told him no cream or sugar. I guess not many people drink it straight.
The owners are kind, a mom-and-pop type restaurant. Family owned, authentic recipes, delicious food and COFFEE. You pay for the quality. Visit them for sure!

Went here to grab breakfast and the food was great! Everything was freshly made and the coffee was good. I haven’t had Ethiopian food before but the owner guided me through the menu. The owner was very kind and respectful. He seems to treat everyone (including me) like an old friend.

Would highly recommend coming to this humble venue. From my experience, you won’t be disappointed with the service.

formatted_address: 2000 S Colorado Blvd Building 4 Unit 102, Denver, CO 80222, United States
name: Just Kool Jamaican Kitchen

reviews.text:
This is a new favorite lunch spot of mine. I love Jamaican food, and unfortunately, there are not many options in Denver for when the cravings come. So how excited was I when I learned Just Kool, which used to be a food truck in Aurora, now has a brick-and-mortar spot in Denver! They’re a Black/family-run business located in a food hall that has some other great options available, including Sonder for coffee. Great space for a casual lunch and large groups. I met the husband and he was friendly and nice as he answered my questions about the menu.

I was impressed with the quality of the food here. I couldn’t decide which I liked better, the curry chicken or the jerk chicken. Both are beautifully cooked, tender, and perfectly seasoned, not too salty or heavy. The rice and beans aren’t mushy! The plantains and corn on the cob are scrumptious. And the beef patty is flavorful and not too doughy or too rich. They have an assortment of Jamaican drinks that i can’t wait to try—I had the sorrel ginger drink recently and it was tasty and refreshing.

Food’s a 12/10! Been rocking with these oxtails since the food truck days, but love the new location (attached photos to help locate)

WILL NEVER SWITCH UP! My fav place to get oxtails in Colorado!
So happy this place opened up. The oxtail was GREAT. This is probably one of the best Jamaican food I’ve had in the Denver Metro Area. Kenny was wonderful, food was hot and you can taste the love.
Delicious food and lovely staff! I’ll definitely be coming back to keep trying the menu, there were so many flavorful options! Really impressed and glad this place exists. Great job you guys!

This place is actually inside Junction Food & Drink. The Jerk Chicken was very nice and not too spicy. The cabbage side with a little carrot was good. The corn on the cob was okay, but I would have preferred grilled corn.

Service was fast and friendly. Seating is provided by the food court and there's a lot of it both inside and out. The food court provides unsecured Wi-Fi for customers.

There's plenty of parking in free and paid lots plus a few on street spots.

formatted_address: 846 Albion St, Denver, CO 80220, United States
name: Le French - 9+CO

reviews.text:
Le French is nothing short of extraordinary.

I have to mention first, that I’m a well traveled person and Paris is among my absolute FAVORITE cities to visit and experience. This gourmet, casual-chic Parisian bistro delivers French cuisine with global depth and soul, beautifully honoring the sisters’ Senegalese heritage while remaining unmistakably refined. From the moment you arrive, it’s clear this is not just a restaurant, it’s a thoughtfully curated culinary experience.

Chef Babacar’s influence is immaculate and deeply intentional. Every dish tells a story. His flavors are precise, layered, and emotionally resonant. You can quite literally taste his journey through years of classical training and lived culinary experience. Though new to the Denver food scene, he is unmistakably a veteran of his craft, cooking with confidence, restraint, and profound respect for technique.

The service matches the caliber of the kitchen. At lunch, Lacy guided us through the menu with warmth and expertise, creating a seamless and welcoming experience. When we returned the following evening for dinner, Annalise provided equally exceptional service; attentive, polished, and genuinely hospitable.

General Manager Mike’s leadership is evident at every level. The staff operates with cohesion and pride, and his outward respect and rapport with the chef speaks volumes about the culture being built here.

Standout dishes:
• Pesto Chicken Crêpe (Lunch): Unexplainably delicious—comforting yet elevated.
• French Onion Soup: Deeply layered, patiently reduced, and executed to absolute perfection.
• Saffron Tomato Bouillabaisse (Dinner): The most balanced version I’ve ever tasted—the saffron and tomato walk a beautiful, disciplined tightrope.
• Risotto: The undeniable star of the night. Depth, layers, and flavor that linger long after the last bite—simply exemplary.
• Tiramisu: Fantastic. I genuinely wanted to lick the bowl.

You would be doing yourself a true disservice if you didn’t experience Le French. This is a rare, full-spectrum five-star dining experience—exceptional food, outstanding service, and heart in every detail. Denver is lucky to have it.

(Dear Google, please do not add captions to my photos. I did not name these dishes in the captions and have since deleted the incorrect names that were automatically added. That’s disturbing to say the least.)

A bit of a disappointment for us. It started well. We were running late and the hostess was very nice and accommodated our change of reservation time.
Our waiter was good at the beginning, but declined pretty quickly after that.
We ordered our food and honestly, it was bland. Everything had no seasoning.  I started with the French onion soup and it had potential, but just not good. We also had the nicoise salad. Not a complicated item to make, but again, it was just ok.
We ordered the Charcuterie,  and he brought us the Fromage plate.
I ordered the boeuf bourguignon. The meat was very tender and it was a generous portion, but not flavorful.
The last thing we ordered was the Jamon crepe and it was not good. A big disappointment.
After ordering, our waiter was pretty non existent. Even the hostess came by and gave us more water. She was more attentive than he.
Overall, the visit was a bust. We had high hopes, but it was a disappointment. Hopefully it was just a bad night for them, and I hope the service and food improve.

Wow. I had the most incredible experience at Le French tonight! I made a reservation for my sorority sister’s anniversary and they could not have been more accommodating! We all ordered different things, I got the chicken sandwich and wow, it hit the spot. The portion was so good I left full and still had food for tomorrow. Our servers, Sofia and Alyssa, made sure that all our needs were taken care of even though we were a tough bunch. If you want a flavorful and exemplary meal, check out Le French!!

Jeh was absolutely amazing. She provided such extraordinary service—providing high quality recommendations and even a wonderful introduction to the chef. Will definitely be back again and again. We are so fast we didn’t get time to take photos of the food! Don’t skip out on dessert!

I drove 25 minutes to try their "chocolate and fruits" crepe. I spent maybe 8 minutes in the restaurant and had the worst experience. The hostess rolls her eyes at me when I walk in and ask to place a to-go order. I was kind of shocked. The bartender, the only nice one, took my order. I asked if they had coffee and this other girl- I'm assuming a waitress, lists under her breath all the types of coffees they have, not as a suggestion, but more as a passive aggressive way to make me feel "dumb" for asking that question. So now I'm just super annoyed and wanna go. My food comes, mind you after tip I spent $30.63. All I ordered was a SMALL coffee and 1 crepe. This "fruits" crepe was $16+tax. I get in my car and look at 5 halves pieces of strawberries and that's it. Then half a jar of nutella inside. Nothing else?! Why is this called "fruits" and description says "berries" and there's literally 5 little pieces. This is the weakest crepe I've ever had and not worth the price what so ever. This, and the attitude of the workers- very clicky, very judgmental, very mean girl vibes. Not a fan.

formatted_address: 4163 Hamilton Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45223, United States
name: Darou Salam African Halal Restaurant - Senegalese cuisine

reviews.text: The best Senegalese food I've ever had in the US. It is superrrrr authentic, and it hits the spot. I've only ever tried their thiebudienne, but it's delicious and very comforting. The atmosphere is ok, I'd recommend getting take away and eating outside on a nice day.

Nice place that is hidden away in northside. Lamb is tasty and has a nice spice to it however some peices can be a little tough. Comes with nice pickled onions and a side. I got brown rice which was great. Can get very busy around dinner time. More suited for takeout

food from darou salem restaurant is incredibly yummy.

AND they make everything fresh fresh; there's a short wait between ordering and receiving order but it's more than worth it imo. plantains, dibi lamb, and fish are my go-tos!

i bought lunch here for my best friend too, and she LOOOOOVED everything especially the fish and plantains

now about atmosphere and structure. there's a chill, laid-back vibe within the restaurant. the order counter is clean and typically operated by gentle speaking and friendly persons. there's nice low lighting [easier on the eyes and it sets a nice vibe to decompress]

there's both indoor and outdoor seating too, though the outdoor patio seating seems to accommodate more than just darou salem guests. so that may lead to less seating available during specific hours and/or on specific days. idk, there's been seating available for my party everytime we went, but still something to keep in mind if dining in

overall though, i love it here! it's a whole vibe, the food is excellent, and the service, friendly🙏🏾
The food is very delicious!!! If you like african or Senegalese cuisine, the Thiebou jen is my favorite.

Don’t judge me I was so hungry 🤣🤣🤣
Probably billion calories , that was supposed to be rice and fish

formatted_address: 3814 Magazine St, New Orleans, LA 70115, United States
name: Dakar NOLA

reviews.text:
I’ve been wanting to make it out to Dakar Nola for a while and finally made it happen and glad to say it did not disappoint. Every dish was super flavorful and did a great job of demonstrating the connection between African and New Orleans/Louisiana cuisine. The atmosphere is formal without being pretentious with an overall great team that seemed to work together well to take care of each guest. Was it expensive…sure…but I’d argue the quality of the ingredients and care put into the food made it worth it.

Overall great experience and I can’t wait to come back and try it again!!

Had an amazing dinner at Dakar NOLA, the hype around this restaurant is real! Being of West African origin, I am very familiar with a lot of the ingredients used in food preparation. The recipes are ingenious, the food presentation and wine pairing were fabulous. The atmosphere was warm and inviting. This was a gastronomical experience not soon to be forgotten. Be aware that you need to arrive on time. Everyone in the restaurant is served each course at the same time.

The Food -
Absolutely delicious, the flavours were outstanding and the best way for me to describe the taste and feeling was luxuriously elevated home cooking.

The Service -
Was fine… you could tell the impetus was there to create an elevated dining experience but for varying reasons it just sort of fell short. The table constantly being wiped off with a wet cloth leaving a wet table to sit at, waiters stumbling over menu descriptions or badgering for drinks orders when we made clear we would save our cocktail order for the end. At the end of the meal we were brought our bill before being asked if we were finished (irony is they have an aperitif section of the drinks menu, but we didn’t get asked if we wanted one) …something that did suprise me, they served a hot sauce which I LOVED! I said they should sell this as I’d love to take it home. She said let me see what they can do, as they’ve thought about selling it! She came out with a pot and I was overjoyed, no mention of price or cost. Then to our shock there it was awkwardly on the bill at a price point of $35 - good hospitality venues either let you know the cost or offer as a memorable moment that keeps you coming back. That took me aback for sure!

The Atmosphere -
Was calm and pleasant but it just lacked something… better lighting? Slightly higher volumes of music? Unsure.

All in all it was a delicious meal. I’m not sure it’s worth $165 per person and I hate to be charged gratuity before dining but I was glad we tried Dakar as the flavours were unlike any other tasting menu we have been to.

We were excited to go here especially since it earned a James Beard Award. The meal started out great. Hand wash,  a wonderful ginger mint tea, and a flavorful cassava crisp kicked things off.  However, everything after was disappointing- the flavors didn’t blend together well and too many dishes were garnished with flavorless puffed rice. The fish entree was extremely disappointing- the fish was overdone and the sauce on the plate was bland. I appreciate that they accommodated a gluten intolerance. Unfortunately, I don’t feel the price point of the meal, plus the service fee charged, matched our experience.

An absolute treat. Every course was amazing. I added on the lobster, which was amazing. Participated in the communal dinner experience as a solo traveler, it was an excellent chance to talk with others. This was definitely the highlight of my NOLA trip. I would love to return to experience more menu options. I highly recommend if you love good unique foods.

formatted_address: 57 Green Ln, Ilford IG1 1XG, United Kingdom
name: Saahiibs Somali Cuisine

reviews.text: Tried the lamb shank with rice at Saahibs — absolutely phenomenal. The meat was fall-off-the-bone tender, rich with flavor, and perfectly complemented by the fragrant rice. A must-try dish. Highly recommend!
Highly recommend not only is good amazing but the customer service, they go above and beyond. Amazing price and portion. Thank you!

10/10 food. Never had lamb this tender and flavourful. Samosas were on point and the sauces were amazing. Great prices too, would recommend to anyone who wants to try something new or is looking to get some good munch.
Not only loved the food but also loved their customer service. The sauces were so yummy and spicy. 😋
The meat samosas are absolutely delicious… and the lamb is well seasoned, succulent, and delicious too. Highly recommend.

formatted_address: 5-6 Grand Parade, Green Lanes, Harringay Ladder, London N4 1JX, United Kingdom
name: Sabiib Somali Restaurant - Harringay

reviews.text:
Green Lanes is incredibly fortunate to have Sabiib. My family and friends absolutely adore this place! The food is not only amazing but also offers excellent value—we always leave completely satisfied and full. The interior is consistently clean and beautifully presented.

I've visited several times, and the service has always been outstanding. A special shout out to Zamzam, who took care of my family and me during our recent visit for breakfast. Her service was exceptional; she was incredibly polite and helpful. Thank you so much, Zamzam!

Sabiib has quickly become my favorite spot, a must-visit whenever I'm back in Green Lanes. I highly recommend the platter for two to experience a variety of their delicious offerings. The Haniid (slow-cooked lamb shoulder) is so tender it literally falls off the bone! I always order their Shaah (spiced chai) and mango lassi. Plus, their breakfast options are delicious, and they serve complimentary Maraq soup until 4pm daily.

If you’re curious about Somali cuisine, it is very much worth the visit! I’m still working my way through their whole menu, but everything I've tried so far has been delightful. I've heard great things about their timir date cake, which is definitely on my list for my next visit!

Really loved this place: the food was very good, the atmosphere and the decor was extremely pleasent to be in.  There are no music playing in the background which makes it adult and family friendly.  If you prefer a private booth, they have a few of those too but I'd prehaps suggest reserving in advance.  The restaurant also has an added bonus of a musallah and a wudu area, which I found to have been very clean and well maintained.

Special thanks to the two young sisters: Samira and Sabrina for their high level waiting and customer service.

Would I come back here again?  Of course I would.
Would I recommend friends and family?  In a heartbeat.

May Allah bless this place and all the people working there.

Went here for a date night and was an amazing experience. The staff were so lovely and friendly and Alvi gave us the best recommendations for food as it was our first time trying Somali food. Would definitely recommend as the food AND drinks were DELICIOUS. We had the sharing platter and had so much leftover and was very affordable. Amazing value for money, would definitely recommend!! Thank you guys for a lovely meal!

My first time trying Somali food and it did not disappoint. I had Maraq vegetable soup for starters nice and spicy, and Hummus Oodkac which is hummus and Somali dried beef jerky. Main course had the Haniid which was rice, spaghetti, lamb which fell off the bone, some salad. Traditionally you get a banana which you normally slice up and put in your Haniid. Good combination. For desert I had Timir Date cake was out of this world with hot caramel sauce yum, with Somali spiced Chaii tea. Beautiful interior and clean restaurant. They even had a prayer room at the back. Super friendly staff excellent service. I’LL BE BACK here very very soon😊👍🏾

I’d always been curious about Somali cuisine—it had long been on my foodie bucket list. So when a family member suggested dining at Sabiib, I didn’t hesitate to say yes.

We started with the Hummus Oodkac, a creamy, perfectly seasoned dip elevated by a topping of spiced Somali beef jerky. It was a beautiful balance of texture and flavour—a wonderful introduction to what was to come.

For mains, we ordered the sharing platter, a generous feast of lamb, beef, and chicken over fragrant rice—and, to my surprise, spaghetti. The unexpected addition of pasta hints at Somalia’s history and its Italian influence, resulting in a fusion that’s become a hallmark of Somali meals. As if things couldn’t get more intriguing, the whole spread was served with a banana on the side.

The lamb Haniid stole the show—so tender it fell effortlessly off the bone. The beef and chicken suqaar were equally impressive: juicy, well-spiced, and bursting with flavour. The two house condiments added depth and contrast, rounding out the meal perfectly.

While I noticed subtle Middle Eastern influences, Somali cuisine stood out as distinct from Ethiopian food.

I didn’t try the banana combination this time, as I was too busy savouring each dish on its own, but I’ll definitely give it a go on my next visit.

A special mention goes to Samira, our wonderful server, who patiently explained the menu. With her contagious smile, she also told us that Somalia was once the world’s largest banana exporter—hence the beloved tradition of pairing banana with almost every meal.

Sabiib truly delivered a memorable first experience of Somali cuisine—warm hospitality, bold flavours, and a meal that told a story, enriched by fascinating Middle Eastern and Italian touches.

formatted_address: 7, Landmark Commercial Centre, Commercial Rd, London N18 1UB, United Kingdom
name: Abow Bakes & Catering

reviews.text: Amazing food and service. Had a last minute booking with them for my baby shower and they was so attentive and helpful. I would 100% recommend Abow bakes. Food was delicious!!

Absolutely amazing! Abow Bakes is hands down one of the best spots for Somali food. The customer service was excellent: warm, friendly, and attentive, which made the experience even better. Truly a hidden gem and a must-visit if you want authentic, delicious Somali food. Highly recommend!

Huge shoutout to Abow Bakes & Catering !
Every dish on the menu is made with so much love and care and they seriously never disappoint. Everything on the menu is amazing, flavours upon flavours in every bite. The best baaris and hilib I have ever tasted, hands down! I always order from them, and me and my family are always returning customers.
If you want that true authentic Somali food experience, be sure to order from Abow Bakes & Catering !!

I can’t say enough good things about Abow Bakes. The food is honestly incredible — you can taste the love and effort in every bite. Everything I’ve tried has been so fresh, flavorful, and beautifully made. You can tell they really care about quality, not just putting something on a plate. On top of that, the service is warm and welcoming, which makes the whole experience even better. If you’re looking for food that’s both delicious and made with passion, Abow Bakes is the place.
Delicious Somali food! I had the rice and meat and it was perfectly seasoned and very flavorful. Friendly service and generous portions—highly recommend Abow Bakes.

formatted_address: 1151 S Redwood Rd Suite 108, Salt Lake City, UT 84104, United States
name: Noor Somali Restaurant

reviews.text: My Fiancé & I came here for dinner for the first time. We both ordered FuFu & chicken & it was so delicious!! 😍 Its a unique cultural setting & very clean. Definitely would recommend this restaurant to family & friends.
Food was delicious. Very flavorful. I will be back to try other dishes.

Hands down, the best Somali food in the United States! Every time I’m in Salt Lake City, Noor is a must. The lamb shank was perfectly seasoned and fall-off-the-bone tender. The chicken soup had that deep, comforting flavor that hits your soul, and the fish with pasta? Unmatched. The spices, the warmth, the hospitality it’s like stepping into a home kitchen full of love and tradition.

If you’ve never had Somali cuisine before, this is the place to experience it right. Consistent, flavorful, and made with care. Five stars every time!
Please do not complain if it takes a little while to get your food because the wait is worth it. Everything is homemade handmade..🇸🇴😘🫶🏿🙌🏿😋

cute cozy place. like most reviews, dont be put off by the location (although i thought it was a decent place). food was 10/10. Fufu with the lamb curry and sambusa. Both fresh and the quality was amazing. Definitely recommend if you want to try somali/african food

We were visiting a friend nearby and decided to check it out, never having tried any African cuisine. Although it looked like a “hole in the wall” we have found that type of place to be most authentic. The food was delicious 🤤 I had the lamb and rice, both very flavorful. The service was friendly.

formatted_address: 55 N Redwood Rd J, Salt Lake City, UT 84116, United States
name: Midnimo Somali Restaurant

reviews.text:
If you’re looking for comfort food with a homey feeling behind it, try this place out.

FOOD:
Although I’ve never had Somali food, I gave them 5 stars on food because it had good flavor.

- The Somali version of a Samosa is packed with flavor
- The lamb is juicy and has subtle yet delicious flavors
- You have choice between rice, spaghetti, or mix. I would just get their rice.

SERVICE:
Definitely ring the bell to get their attention, if no one is at the counter.

ATMOSPHERE:
The ladies that cook and serve are humble, quiet and respectful. They’re very sweet and always approach cautiously.
Great Food great people,  just in front Loves truckstop.  I had Liver best liver ever

Absolutely loved my experience here! The liver was some of the best I’ve ever had—perfectly cooked and full of flavor. I highly recommend giving this place a try. I’ll definitely be coming back for more! Also, I tried the milk tea for the first time and now it’s officially my go-to drink. Big thanks to the team for an unforgettable meal!

From the outside you wouldn't think much of it but the food is 12 out of 10. Simple yet incredible! The lamb was so tender and then got chapati and beans to go! Wow! Really large portions, friendly staff, chill atmosphere.
I was glad to see a place like this across from Loves. The food was great, the lady at the counter was very polite and kind, and I was surprised they offered water. I will come again.

formatted_address: 6447 W Washington St, Indianapolis, IN 46241, United States
name: Barako Somali Restaurant

reviews.text: My husband and I came to Barako for a late lunch and was greeted and seated at a table. I ordered the meat and rice dish and my husband ordered  chicken and chapati dish. The food came out fast (5-10min) with a side of salad and a banana. The portions are very large, at least 2 people can eat from it. The food was SO good, this was my first time having Somali food and I loved it. My husband felt the same. The workers were very polite and gave such good hospitality. They even gave us a cup of their tea on the house and it was amazing too  perfectly sweetened with a great cardamom flavor. Alhamdulilah it was great food and the people at this restaurant are so nice. It’s a simple layout for tables, which is fine for us. I would recommend to come here again! For parking, you must go down the dirt lot past the semi trucks to find this restaurant.

This is not our first time trying Somali food, but still it took our breath away. The foods are all halal. We highly recommend both beef and lamb with rice. The beef dish had plenty of meat and the lamb was juicy and tender. The rice was delicious and filled with flavor. Last but not least, the staffs were so nice and welcoming. While we were waiting they offered us almost half plate of meat as appetizer. They also served somali tea and salad for free. The price is a bit high in Indiana standard but totally worth it. Also they have a place for prayer, which is very rare in USA.

Went off the beaten path for lunch, was surprised to find this Somali Restaurant tucked in behind the main street businesses. As an eater with an international palet, just had to stop in and try the food. The dining area is open, sparse, and functional. Some items may not be available from the menu, but they are more than happy to cook something for you. I ordered the goat with rice, the goat was grilled and very flavorful. The rice was a real treat, almost like a fried rice with roasted vegetables, maybe a little Star Anise, and a touch of heat from some hot pepper (not too hot, but will warm the lips a little). My coworker ordered the fried Tilapia, he said it was really good, his rice was same as mine. The portion size is fairly large, I could only eat half, took the other half home for dinner😆  The service isn't very formal, so if you need something, just tell the guy behind the pick-up window and they will take care of you. A nice hole-in-the-wall if you are adventurous, well worth the visit, I will be a regular customer now🙂
My first experience with Somali food. I ordered Lamb the order was freshly made and really delicious.  For a single order it was large size sufficient for two.
The food was pretty good and it was a nice size portion to eat. I would come back to try more food.

formatted_address: 1151 S Redwood Rd #101, Salt Lake City, UT 84104, United States
name: Global Place Somali Restaurant

reviews.text:
The Food is beyond words
Customer service is very friendly
10/10
Note
🗒️
it’s open on Sunday as well

If you live in Salt Lake and haven’t tried this place, you’re missing out! It’s located on Redwood Road in a little plaza area with parking in the front. It’s a very busy place that’s always flooded with people. On one side they have a market, and on the other, the restaurant.

We always take our food to go because it’s busy and the area is a bit small. Kamal is the owner, and he is very generous. The first time we went there he gave us a few sambusas and black ginger tea on the house. They also include a banana and a bottle of water free with every meal. He was very hospitable. I suggest you order before you go as it can take them some time to prepare the food, but it is definitely worth it!

We always get the chicken soukar with rice, as well as the goat meat with rice. The rice is very fragrant and appetizing. We LOVE their green sauce. It’s so spicy and delicious. They give a lot of rice—it lasts us two meals! Even if you don’t know anything about Somali food, you should still stop by. If you’re afraid to try anything else, you can’t go wrong with the chicken soukar and rice. You won’t be disappointed!

I just Googled places to eat near me and thought Somalian food sounded good. Boy, am I glad I did! For an extremely reasonable price, I was given enough food to last me two meals (I guess I wasn't as hungry as I thought I was), and that food was absolutely delicious! Everything was good, but the rice, gosh, the rice I could eat every day and be very happy about it. Excellent customer service. Thanks for a great lunch!

Very much an authentic, hole-in-a-wall experience. I felt like a tourist because I was the only one speaking English most of the time.

I had the Chapati with Fish, and the fish was very good. The Chapati was good; it’s like a tortilla from cafe rio but thicker. Very filling and worth the $12.

I ordered chicken and rice. It came with plain lettuce salad. The chicken was dry and some pieces were burnt. The rice made up over half of the box. It was seasoned with cinnamon, but was good. The only drink choices were a can of coke or a bottle of water. We decided to eat outside because the tables were dirty. It wasn't a horrible experience, but it wasn't an amazing one either. The food was a little overpriced and the service was slow.

formatted_address: 3100 E Colfax Ave, Denver, CO 80206, United States
name: SPICE ROOM

reviews.text:
Spice Room absolutely lived up to its name — every bite was bursting with bold, unforgettable flavor! We started with the samosas, which were perfectly crispy on the outside and filled with a spicy, flavorful mix that woke up our taste buds right away. They also brought out complimentary crackers with a variety of sauces — each one unique and delicious (I couldn’t stop dipping!).

For the main course, we had the butter chicken and chicken tikka masala, and wow — both were incredible. The sauces were rich, creamy, and perfectly spiced, and the chicken was tender and cooked to perfection. The jalapeño & cheese naan and garlic naan were the perfect sides — soft, warm, and just the right amount of indulgent.

To top it all off, I had a mango lassi that was thick, creamy, and just heavenly — easily one of the best I’ve had anywhere.

Yes, the wait was a bit long, both to be seated and for the food to arrive, but once everything hit the table, it was well worth it. The quality, flavor, and attention to detail made it an outstanding dining experience.

I finally made it into Spice Room after so many recommendations and it did not disappoint. The butter chicken and cheese naan I got were delicious! The mango lassi was the best I’ve had. I strongly recommend Spice Room!

Undoubtedly one of the Top 3 best Indian Restaurants in Denver🔥. Besides the perfect execution of every single dish we had (5 dishes including dessert) - one thing that really stands out here is the amazingly curated menu.

The detailed descriptions on menu options that make every single dish seem incredibly enticing. If you or any loved ones have been reluctant to try Indian Cuisine.. there’s no better intro in then a seat at Spice Room.

It was full of white ppl so we were skeptical at the beginning but neverthless it was amazing. We loved garlic naan and lamb makhani. The spicyness is on white ppl’s scale. So to taste something you gotta atleast do medium. Chicken tika masalan was ok but again we fall victim to their spice level and ordered mild, which was completely bland. The only issue at the time of our visit was that the whole resturant was filled with a grease smell and we had our eyes burning. They need a better hvac/hood system
Soo good! Came to visit my aunt and she recommended. Korma is my favorite dish. Perfect for sharing. Karma is the best waitress/ bartender! She’s so sweet!!

formatted_address: Entrance C, 14200 E Alameda Ave #1039B, Aurora, CO 80012, United States
name: Momo Dumplings

reviews.text: I was excited to try the momo here after reading so many great reviews, but unfortunately, my experience was disappointing. The momo lacked authentic flavor, and the Gobi Manchurian was overly oily and not very enjoyable. While the prices were reasonable, the taste just didn’t meet my expectations. Sadly, I wouldn’t return?

We found our new favorite Momos in town! My husband and I tried quite a few from classic steam and fried to their Indian fusion styles and we loved them all! Their Rogan Josh, Korma, and Tikka Masala were all so delicious and flavorful and any of their meat, seafood or veggie dumplings will be amazing in them. Also loved their veggie momo which is not something I would typically order. If you’re in Aurora like me, know that we are some lucky ones to have them so close by!  This wonderful family-owned business has stolen my heart.

Got a variety of momos (chicken Tikka masala momos, veggie korma momos, chicken vindaloo momos--not pictured) and sides (chili potatoes and Gobi Manchurian) and everything was absolutely delicious! Quick services, and some of the best momos I've ever had. Each order comes with more than enough (there were only two of us so we totally over ordered, but no complaints here). Be warned, I love spice and the chili potatoes are spicy!

Will definitely be coming back!

Loved the Momo dumplings this is the place I have been looking for.

Prices are also reasonable.

This is not a separate restaurant we have to order from kiosk at entrance of Food Pickup point in the Aurora mall.

All food items are takeout only.

New: They were always surprising me with complimentary items(dessert or soda) on every order, thank you.

Super tasty and unique Momo's (Nepalese Dumplings) that come in all sorts of fillings and sauces that will keep you coming back for more!

Momo's are a type of steamed dumping and at Momo Dumplings you have so many different options. You can get traditional fillings like chicken and pork, but other options include turkey and lamb! They have a wide assortment of sauces/curries as well.

My favorites were the Turkey Korma, Chicken Tiki Masala, and Lamb Rogan Josh, all came in thick curry sauces that were delicious!

Momo Dumplings is located in a ghost kitchen and is available for takeout only, you can also get them delivered through apps like Door dash and UberEATS. Check these delicious dumplings out!

formatted_address: 213 Seven Sisters Rd, Finsbury Park, London N4 3NG, United Kingdom
name: Banaadiri Restaurant

reviews.text: Made to feel so welcome when we visited. Came here with my wife and mum and they walked me through the food options and I ordered, for £30 there was a great amount of food to feed us all and everyone was so friendly and happy to help us as we'd never tried Somali food before, we'd recommend this place to everyone and regarding the comments about hygiene and a lack of welcoming atmosphere I'm very surprised because everything was fresh, tasted great and the place was well maintained and we felt like welcomed guests and everyone was greatful that we came to take our time to appreciate Somali food and culture ❤️

Another goated spot in finsbury park with great Somali food, nice friendly staff as well.  There isn't a menu, so go the the front and ask questions about what they have and what your preferences are. The lamb is quality, and a starter soup is provided as well as a banana for dessert. Portion sizes are amazing and the whole meal costs around £12 which is amazing value for money. Pretty good spice level to the food as well

Best somalian food i’ve ever tasted highly recommend the beef steak and rice and definitely eat in, to all the Bengali’s in the area and everyone else pop in to this shop, it’s a must try, amazing portions great food and packed full of flavour, you won’t leave it feeling hungry and also very well priced. And also perfect for people who go to gym, get that protein in, loads of meats available and also everything is Halal👌

My 65 year old mother and I popped into this cafe for a coffee, as we had sometime before she could check into the hotel across the road. We were instantly ushered by the waiter behind a closed curtain. It soon became apparently that the curtain was to segregate men and women, as there was another man and woman behind the curtain, and on the other side men only. We instantly left. This café clearly would prefer to live under the Taliban than in a free UK.

I recently had the pleasure of joining a Somali colleague for a meal at Banadiri Restaurant on our way to an assessment. We tried the Sughaar with Haneed, and it was absolutely delicious—highly recommended! As a Pakistani at a Somali restaurant, I felt incredibly welcomed. The hospitality was truly outstanding

formatted_address: 2219 Gravois Ave, St. Louis, MO 63104, United States
name: Darba Somalian Restaurant

reviews.text:
Y'all!! I found it, the CHEAPEST lunch in the Lou, and it doesn't even rely on cheap carb basics like heaps of rice or pasta or bread!! I stopped in to try their sambusas since I'd never had Somalian cuisine as far as I knew. Upon entering there was a small grocery selection, but a quick walk straight back through the beaded curtain led to the restaurant.

I ordered two sambusas for $1.99 each and waited for a few minutes as delivery drivers
came and went while some locals ate. This is definitely a hole in the wall kind of place if you decide to dine in, but there's a decent amount of seating.

In any case, a few minutes later the young lady working the restaurant brought my to-go bag out, and imagine my surprise when it included a free bottle of water and a banana! I mean, were not talking about top-dollar stuff here, but I literally only spent $3.98 on my purchase pre-tax. The water and banana alone would cost twice that where I work.

If you want to try something new, on a dime, this is a decent lunch for four dollars! What an absolute bargain.

(And just as importantly, the sambusas were delicious! My favorite was the beef. Expect a curry-adjacent flavor profile with a slight kick and a deeper flavor profile than Caribbean or Indian curries, in my opinion.)

Absolutely delicious! Food was seasoned to perfection. I got the tilapia filets with fufu. Completely devoured the entire dish. I would also recommend getting the chicken sombusa appetizer, I got 4 extra to take home.

Super unassuming from the outside. The food was amazing and we had so much left over! The young man at the restaurant counter was very helpful. Have the dine in experience because we had a great time ordering everything we thought we wanted to taste. We purchased a couple of things from the store up front and had an overall good experience.

A small restaurant space in the back of a store.  Definitely lots of authentic Somali food as I tried the goat for a first time (will go with Chicken next time).  Service was friendly and the rice was excellent.   It lost a star as it could have been a little more clean (e.g. wash the dirt off the doors/wall and hang the fly catcher tape somewhere other than the dinning area)

My daughter, and myself decided to try Somalian food on Christmas Eve for the 1st time. What a complete winner! My daughter picked fish, rice, and salad. I tried ugali (stiff porridge), goat meat and salad. We enjoyed our food, and will be back! I loved the packed bottles of water with a banana for each of us. Very healthy, and a nice finishing touch. Thank you Darba!

formatted_address: 5600 S 3rd St, Louisville, KY 40214, United States
name: Banaadir Cafe and Grill

reviews.text: As soon as I walked through the doors I was transported back to East Africa.  The whole fried tilapia was cooked perfectly and the biryani rice full of flavor.  Samosas with meat and chicken left our mouths watering for more.  Great portion sizes.  This left me remembering village life in Uganda.  Thank you Banaadir!

Excellent Food and Friendly Service!
Everything we tried was absolutely delicious—clearly made with care and great ingredients. The food was fresh, flavorful, and perfectly prepared. On top of that, the staff were incredibly friendly and welcoming, which made the whole experience even better. Highly recommend!
Awww this is one of the best restaurants I’ve ever been their food is amazing and delicious and a very clean place

This place always you getting amazing food and it's clean, good service is fast and friendly. today I have Pick up load 5-mile away Banadir coffee in Louisville, KY 40214, United States

I was really happy because I was interested in Somali food, and I met Samiir a nice guy who was working the restaurant, He was a happy man😂😂  welcomed me and served me actually gave me food rice, meat, coffee and soup please visit Banadir Coffee if you are Louisville, KY 40214, United States

My wife and I ate here this morning based on other reviews and we were not disappointed.  The man who greeted us was very friendly and told us about the food. I had the goat and she had the chicken plate with saffron rice. Both were delicious and the green sauce gave it a nice spicy addition.  I also tried the chicken sambusi and it was very good and had a nice spicy flavor.

I don’t get to Louisville often but will definitely visit Banaadir again and tell others about this great restaurant.

formatted_address: 8000 E Quincy Ave Unit 1000, Denver, CO 80237, United States
name: shondiz mediterranean restaurant

reviews.text: Shondiz was an amazing experience. The food was absolutely delicious, and the hospitality truly stood out. It was our first time visiting Denver and we wanted to try Persian food, and they made us feel so welcome. They even brought us complimentary welcome treats, which was such a thoughtful touch. At the end of the meal, they surprised us with dessert as well. The service was warm, generous, and genuine. Highly recommend if you’re looking for great Persian food and wonderful hospitality.

If you’re looking for an traditional Persian/ Mediterranean food, excellent hospitality and a warm atmosphere you are right at the point. Mohamad is a gentleman with professional skills who makes your experience incredible. We enjoyed the food and dessert . Highly recommended.

Me and my boyfriend shared a koobideh platter and roasted eggplant + pita app since I wasn't very hungry. The staff was very nice and served us our food on two separate plates without us even asking for extra plates, and they still gave us a lot of rice and two tomato halves each!! their koobideh is some of THE BEST marinated meat I have ever had, and paired with the saffron rice is amazing. highly recommend! very good service as the waiter stopped by our table multiple times to check on us. this continues to be a go-to restaurant for us.

Stopped here for dinner. Food was good but pricey, though it was also a lot of food. We ordered 2 entrees and a hummus and pita. Price before tip was $62 the food was OK but probably been better if we had ordered some salad and just split the 1 kabob entree. As it was we had no veggies. Might be a good spot for lunch though depending on price. Staff were very nice and friendly.

Outstanding Persian Cuisine with a Modern Touch!
I stopped by Shondiz Restaurant near downtown Denver during our trip, and it was one of the best Persian cuisines I’ve ever had! The yogurt drink was incredibly tasty and refreshing. We ordered beef kabobs and chicken Kabab with Polo and the eggplant dish Mirza Aden’s 😊 - everything was perfectly cooked, flavorful, and beautifully served. If you’re looking for authentic Persian food with a modern touch, this is the place!

formatted_address: 2700 E Colfax Ave, Denver, CO 80206, United States
name: Samir restaurant & bakery

reviews.text: The fries are amazing, there’s a hint of spices that really makes them delicious. The shawarma plate was just okay. The tomato sauce in the barberry rice and chicken dish was tasty, though I personally would’ve liked a bit more sauce on the chicken and a larger portion of rice.

1st Visit - 3rd Qrtr 2025

Weekday, just before noon.

Ordered the Kobideh Plate, which includes skewers of grilled lamb and beef, rice, salad and naan.
We also had the Mushrooms for appetizer.

Food was excellent 👍.
The meats seasoned and grilled to perfection, if I may say so myself.
The mushroom app differs from the coated ones normally offered in other restaurants.  These were seasoned and had a little bit of oil/juice when served.  Still, very 👍.
Portion is also 👍
2 meat skewers but, big pieces, more than enough for 1.
I did not even touch my salad, opting to finish off the generous, heaping of rice.
They offer 2 types of dipping sauces for the skewers and though, they were both good, the meats were already very flavorful by itself .

Dining was quiet (at FIRST) but, as the location is right by a school, things turned 180 when students came for lunch.
This was a good sign as it looked like pizza was another good item to try next time.

Service was very warm and pleasant but, our order took awhile, primarily due to the huge swarm of student diners a few minutes after we arrived.
The wait was worth it as the food was 👍.

The gentleman at the counter who also took and served us was apologetic for the delay.

Overall, I still will be back and recommend them for you to go but, suggest dining as soon as they open at 11 or come for a later lunch at 1.

Colfax location is a parking problem right now so, take that into account as well or come on weekends to solve both issues mentioned above.
The soft felt-like placemats were a nice touch. Food was good, fries were seasoned well. Always glad to give a good restaurant open past 9pm some of my business!

This is a wonderful new find of us. Food quality is really good. We tried kabuli polo and lamb skewers, and lamb was so tender!!! We also loved the sides that came with the food. Definetly will be back

I’ve visited this place twice in a day, and each time everything was spot on. The food is delicious, and the service is attentive. If you’re craving Mediterranean flavors, especially Afghan dishes, I highly recommend giving this restaurant a try.

formatted_address: 1737 E Evans Ave, Denver, CO 80210, United States
name: Sawa Mediterranean Restaurant & Buffet

reviews.text:
We decided to try this place. Cost $50.00+tip for 2 wraps, 2 sides of tszeke, 1 side of humus with a little bag of pita!

What's worse was that there was hardly any meat in the wraps. I ordered the  gyro, and you can see by the photo that there was maybe one or two strips of meat. They made it appear big, filling it with a ton of lettuce, what they call in the business "perceived value". Now, I'm not against a business earning a profit, but this was not "earning" this was just THEFT. Not to mention, the little meat there was tasted like bits of week old griddle grease char.  My girlfriend said her chicken wrap was flavorful, but also had very little meat. Neither was in actual pita, but a tortilla instad. I don't like leaving bad reviews, but you deserve to know the truth. Save your money, very little value here. It cost as much to go for sushi, Asian food or even a nice steak! Maybe the buffet was worth it, but I will never find out, trust is gone, worst Mediterranean  food I've ever had. I will never go back!

what a not so hidden “hidden gem!”

staff is excellent and attentive, food is beautiful and has delicious flavors & great texture

[if youre considering the fried cauliflower with garlic sauce- just get it. seasoning/light batter is divine, dip is luxurious; didnt get a pic bc i basically inhaled it]

and very fair pricing for these two full boxes, plus i was able to order that accommodated my vegetarianism and more importantly my [sometimes quite troublesome re:restaurants] rare allergy issues.

the ambience is unbeatable, the food was fast and generously portioned, and i cannot wait to come back to try the buffet. its rare that a buffet joint can get this vegetarian to shell out but i’m figuring out how soon i will get to go back! considering getting yet another job, solely to have a dedicated budget stream solely for sawa

Bad choice. The only meat were meatballs for the spaghetti, I thought it was Mediterranean, not Italian. They also had chicken.
Not a lot choices to eat.
Parking is only one hour.
It’s pricey for what they offer.
I do not recommend this place. Don’t waste your time.
The attendant was not professional. He was even sleeping in the dining area.
The place was empty… that in itself should have been enough to not give it a try. Skip it… go somewhere else.

Very disappointing experience. The place was dirty, and the buffet bar was clearly not clean. We came in around 6:00 PM on a Sunday evening, which should still be prime dinner time, but the food was old, stale, and sitting in mostly empty pans. They weren’t even bothering to refill anything.
The staff didn’t acknowledge us at all when we walked in—no greeting, no eye contact, nothing. That set the tone right away.
On top of that, the food just wasn’t good. I’ve had better Mediterranean food at a mall food court. For a place charging $20+ per person, this is unacceptable.
This restaurant should be ashamed and embarrassed to serve food like this to the public at those prices. I won’t be back.

Food was acceptable but definitely far from the best Mediterranean I've had. Jerusalem restaurant across the street is WAY better. Food at the buffet wasn't a great selection and a lot of it tasted stale and dry. It took forever to get our food and I'm pretty sure the cooks were baked (moved slowly and clumsily, faint smell of weed in the back). Definitely not worth the time, especially not with Jerusalem across the street.

formatted_address: 2958 N Downing St, Denver, CO 80205, United States
name: Hayati Mediterranean Grill

reviews.text:
Edit: Found a hair in the watery, white sauce. The hummus tastes super weird like it has cheese in it almost. Definitely missing salt and lemon and seems like it is made with an oil that is not olive oil.

I came here after seeing great reviews. I got gyro and chicken shawarma plates. The chicken shawarma is pink, almost like tandoori chicken that completely lacks flavor. The gyro is burnt and very salty. The plate is predominately rice which tastes how I imagine creek water would with two watery, flavorless sauces, soggy cucumber salad, and a little meat. All of this for $18 per plate… The restaurant -if you can call it that - seems to be fashioned out of the storeroom of the adjoining corner store/vape shop. The premises are very dirty. The power outlets lack proper covers, tiles falling off the walls, etc. I don’t know how this place has such good ratings.

From the looks of the inside it did not seem very clean and was off-putting. Seems really in need of cleaning and repairs. The food was not great. I’m normally a big fan of Mediterranean. I think they may have some potential to improve but I wouldn’t go back again based on this experience.

Hayati Mediterranean Grill goes crazy. Hole in the wall joint serving it up proper. The gyros slap hard and you’re not finding a better bang for your buck anywhere. Shawarma plates? Premo every time. This spot just hits.

Just might be the best value in Denver. Gyro with a good amount of meat for 8 bucks. Not to mention it tastes better than most gyros double its price from places like Byblos and Zaman.

Not the greatest to sit inside, I’d rec takeout and go eating it at fuller park.

This place caught my attention because of decent reviews, but the food quality is super low. I ordered a gyro plate and got a little bit of meat and mostly rice.

Falafel is overly salty and not pleasant to eat.

Avoid at all costs.

formatted_address: 1260 Decatur St, Denver, CO 80204, United States
name: Sun Valley Kitchen

reviews.text: Been driving by this place for years never thought of trying. No big sign or attention. I was surprised how clean and organized it was. Beautiful layout and relaxed seating. Tried the avocado toast and eggs. Would definitely come back to try the breakfast burrito. Affordable and delicious. Great customer service.

I had some of the BEST biscuits and gravy I have ever had today! Biscuits was flaky and buttery and soooo soft and the gravy was delicious thick seasoned and just the right amount of sausage.  Thank you!

IT WOULD BE NICE IF THIS ESTABLISHMENT WOULD STOP PUTTING THEIR FLYERS ON MY DOOR. IT'S DISGUSTING HOW DESPERATE THIS BUSINESS IS TO KEEP PUTTING THEIR FLYERS ON MY DOOR AND EVERY BODY ELSE'S DOOR WHERE I LIVE. IF A PERSON IS INTERESTED IN WHAT YOUR DOING THEY WOULD GO TO YOUR ESTABLISHMENT AND ASK OR GO ON YOUR WEBSITE. AND SEEK.

Loved the BBQ Beef Bahn Mi
spicy bbq beef, marinated vegetables, cilantro, onion, cucumber, bahn mi sauce

Wow - just yummy

Sun Valley Kitchen has really surprised me with the quality of their coffee and tea beverages, food, and atmosphere.

The full service coffee bar has a range of standard coffees, lattes, and teas. All are very reasonably priced for Denver. I'm not sure the coffee bean they use but it is full bodied and delicious. The tea selection isn't very large, but they are all well steeped and really delicious.

Based on several lunches here, I feel qualified to say that their food far exceeds expectations. At a very reasonable price too. I'm positive you will be surprised as well, you can't go wrong with the daily special!

Aside from their products, the staff has done a wonderful job at creating a laid back cafe that's great for hanging out in. Big windows let lots of light pour in, plenty of tables and an array of big comfy couches makes the interior a wonderful place to stay a while. All of the staff members are delightful to talk to, kind, and very helpful.

Great job Evan!

formatted_address: 9905 E Colfax Ave Unit B, Aurora, CO 80010, United States
name: Miss Millie's Kitchen

reviews.text: When visiting our daughter in Denver we were able to enjoy an effortless and delicious Thanksgiving dinner thanks to Miss Millie’s Kitchen.  Ordering was easy via email and electronic payment options.  The food was delivered hot and on time and everything was prepared well.  We are picky eaters and the turkey, ham and sides were all wonderful.  Thank you for making this Thanksgiving so amazing!😊🍁

Unfortunately, my delivery experience fell short of my expectations. While I understand that the driver may have been a third-party contractor and not a direct employee, there was no effort made to establish a friendly rapport or even make eye contact upon delivery. Furthermore, the wire racks were unclean, and there were no sternos or serving utensils provided despite being listed on the invoice. We were disappointed with the overall presentation and quality of the food, and cannot recommend this service to others. I regret to say that we will not be utilizing these services for future events.

Great service! I work for Amazon and we booked Miss Millie's Food Truck & Catering to come up twice! First time she came out at 5:30am no other food truck would accommodate us at those hours but she did! Our employees raved about the food and we were so happy! We cannot wait to have her back. The chicken Cajun pasta and banana pudding  was so amazing and her food truck was so cool, super clean and her little helpers were adorable!

I ordered for a birthday party. She has menus that you can view but you're supposed to go to another site to actually order what's advertised. I didn't realize and so I didn't get what I expected at my birthday party. The chicken legs were good after being warmed up because the food arrived cold.  The chicken breasts were overcooked and very dry. The deviled eggs tasted just like the king soopers potato salad I had to leave my party to go buy as a side since my order came without any. The veggie stuffed mushrooms tasted okay but the presentation wasn't great.  Overall,  I can accept blame for not understanding how to order but the food was not enjoyable for the price paid.  Won't be a return customer.

This place is amazing. They catered for a party of 16 people. Easy communication beforehand, the food arrived on time with a very polite delivery person. THE FOOD IS SO GOOD. Shrimp and grits, chicken and waffles, fried catfish, wow! We ordered a large carrot cake which was the best carrot cake I have ever had. We also ordered a banana pudding cake which was the best cake I’ve ever had. Really impressed with Miss Millie.
