reviews.text: First off… The food is ABSOLUTELY AMAZING! I’m not from this area so when I found a place to get my favorite, I jumped on it. The packaging needs a lot of work.. it does not hold up at all. The only food packaging they did great with was the Suya. The amount of Suya you get for the prices doesn’t match up either.. will I eat there again?! Maybe.. it all depends on what kind of time I have to go somewhere else.

I’ve ordered here a few times and the suya is always good and cooked well (not over cooked like the Towson location). The place is well-kept and clean. Customer service is good, the staff is always pleasant, food is ready fast, and packaged well. The food is pricey and portion sizes are highly debatable by anyone’s standards given the cost. I’ve always found the beef in the stew to consistently be tough and over cooked which is quite annoying- especially for the cost. It’s nice to have a place to order Nigerian food in a pinch, but you will pay for it. They offer a modest rewards program.

I bought food worth of $160.
If you have a big appetite, this place is not for you. Their pounded Yam comes in small sizes. You have to pay separately for the stew to eat the rice you ordered.  The rice don't come with stew even if you ordered for the meat.
So I got rice and beans with assorted meat with absolutely no stew in it. How do you expect someone to eat rice with no sauce.
The only sauce I got was the ayamase sauce. The rest of the orders came with only the protein in it and no single sauce with it. When I called them, I was told I had to order the stew or sauce separately.  I have never experienced such a service like that before.
You have to pay for sauce that is supposed to come with the complete meal? That is crazy!
The food is extremely pricey for it not to make sense.
The atmosphere is beautiful but the food isn't worth it.
Will definitely not return back.

The restaurant's ambiance is top-notch. However, I agree with other reviewers that the food price is steep. The food did taste good, but I was taken back that we had to pay $14 to eat there. That didn't make sense to me but we paid. The guy that attended to us was nice.

The decor is top notch and has always been. Very clean environment and food display/presentation was great. I have been here a few times and I’m always wowed by the interior decorations. The food has never disappointed either but this place is slightly priced higher than typical West African carry out place. It’s easily a high end restaurant so bare that in mind when you see the price.

I see lots of negative reviews about gratuity being added to bill and I think the owner should address the issue to avoid confusion. Someone else complained about shrink wrap on the swallow when they warm up the food, not great. My only negative experience was that my plantain was delivered to the table after I was done eating. There’s always room for improvement but this restaurant is a positive representation of naija culture and resourcefulness so they have all my 5 star plus more.

Note: The level of spice is intense so thread carefully.

reviews.text: Swung into Dukem before catching an Amtrak train at Baltimore Penn Station.  The dinner was delicious and service was both quick and attentive.  Enjoyed the 7-part vegetarian dinner with a friend.  Will be back next time I'm in Baltimore!

WORST doro wat ever. I got the take out today and the chicken looked like it was microwaved a lot, and as you can see in the video it was super dry and very unappetizing. And 26$ for a dish like this?
Save your money and go somewhere else guys..

I recently visited Dukem Ethiopian Restaurant in Baltimore, excited to try Ethiopian cuisine for the first time. We arrived early for our reservation, but the server's blank expression didn't exactly welcome us. We kindly asked to be seated early and were shown to a booth.

The ambiance and aroma inside were pleasant, although the space felt a bit small. Fortunately, it wasn't busy during our visit.

Despite mentioning it was my first time trying Ethiopian food, our server made no effort to explain the menu or offer recommendations. Luckily, I had watched some YouTube videos beforehand, which gave me a basic understanding.

We ordered water, which arrived as bottled Deer Park – a bit unusual. It would have been nice to have glasses provided. Considering the spicy nature of Ethiopian food, not offering free water refills seemed unreasonable.

I started with the vegetarian sambusa, which was dry and could have benefited from a sauce. For my entrée, I ordered a veggie platter with fish. Unfortunately, the fish arrived whole, with bones throughout, making it difficult to eat. While it had good flavor, the bones made it hard to finish.

The rolled injera tasted fine, but the larger portion underneath the veggie platter was quite sour and lacked flavor. The combination of items on the platter didn't complement each other well. The only standout components were the greens and the red lentils with berbere spice.

Throughout our meal, our server never checked in or offered refills on our water. The check was dropped off without asking if we wanted dessert or coffee. The service was subpar, and I reluctantly left an 18% tip.

While I'm glad I got to try Ethiopian food for the first time, I'm disappointed that Dukem didn't live up to my expectations. I wouldn't return and would recommend exploring other Ethiopian restaurants with better service and more flavorful food.

Love finding Ethiopian places to eat when traveling, since we don’t get that opportunity locally. Not too busy. Had a ton of takeout orders being picked up while dining, which was a good sign. Will definitely come back when in town.

This was a completely new cuisine for me, so I didn't know what to expect. The crepe-like side dish (Njera?) was delicious and I could really eat it plain as well. The curries were all flavorful as well.

I would highly recommend the sampler of vegetarian curries. There were so many options that came on the plate and I was the most full I'd been in a while after down it.

The prices are solid, and both times I visited, they were consistently good. Come with really hungry guests prepared to eat with their hands!

When I called back to make sure they didn’t forget the extra oxtail, the owner said she gave me a lot and the rest of what was in the pot. Not to mention only 4 small pcs of plantain..Not worth the $36.

Usually the food is good but this oxtails was nasty.  Taste over cooked and cold.  The Drinks were too expensive.   The sorrel was great but it's small bottle was not worth it.  The malta was not worth the $4.50.  Serious over charge.  Go to the grocery store. You can get it for $1.00.  I love my people and will support especially if the food is great. But when you try to hustle and over charge me, I can no longer support and dont have respect.

My boyfriend and I stopped at KSB yesterday after checking the wait for another popular restaurant in the area. We decided to take a gamble since neither of us had ever been here and I'm glad we did!!!! We had the goat platter with rice n peas and plantain, smoke turkey egusi soup and goat peanut soup with 2 fufu to share. The drinks are pricey and smaller, but everything else was to be expected cost wise. The food was piping hot and absolutely delicious!!!!! Genuinely some of the most tender goat I've ever had 🥹 and the best egusi I've tasted too. We made it in the day before their last day of takeout orders, and the food is so good I would cater it just for the 2 of us 🤣 man. Ps, idk why all the complaints on portion size! I came across this restaurant when looking for authentic Caribbean and African cuisine and this restaurant delivered! I ordered their jerk chicken and oxtails and my husband ordered the curry chicken. The proportions are great and we had food for two days! The spice on the jerk chicken was phenomenal and it has been a while since I had jerk chicken with that spice! Definitely a restaurant to try and fall in love with! reviews.text: I’m very disappointed in what was sent to me after I ordered. I have been looking for cassava leaf near me for a long time. I usually drive to silver spring to get it. (Sweet sweet kitchen) I ordered through their website and they sent me a container full of OIL. Barely any cassava. The meat was so TOUGH. I could barely chew it. This was completely unhealthy and unacceptable. $47 for a container full of OIL!!!

I had a rather disappointing experience. I love African food and was hoping to find a spot to go to on occasion on my way to work, but I shall not come here again. To start, the atmosphere was rather uninviting-- one of two large overhead lights was out, making it fairly dark inside, and the snack display was sparsely stocked, and I think a bit dusty. There was no music so it was dead silent except for the Christian preaching radio outside. Also, it smelled a bit like fish. Nobody else was there and I could understand why. I had time to stay and eat but was not interested in doing so.

I ordered a meat stew and although the flavor of the spices was good, the meat was grisly and tough. I heard them using the microwave a number of times which had me concerned about what else they were skimping on in my $25 meal. The use of the microwave was also likely why the meat was so tough.

My suggestions to the owner:
-Put some garlic in the oven so the place smells fragrant and inviting.
-Keep the snack display well stocked so you present the aire of abundance.
-Have some African High Life music or other African music playing at a low level inside
-Fix the big light
-Dont use the microwave (just throw things in a pan. Water will be better retained that way, keeping meats relatively tender. I would have been happy to wait 20 mins rather than the 10 the waitress told me.)

Ok so I went to Tola today even though some of your reviews told me the place and food is trash and to go to hell instead of coming here but me I like to experience my own whahala when it comes to food so I’m just here to say you guys are liars and may GOD forgive you all😂

So let’s get to it, when you walk in it does smell like gas but that’s not an issue for me because I like good food infact it don’t seem like anything was burning or anyone was dying so which one concern me? 🤷🏽‍♀️

Anyhow let’s continue I got there and I called in advance to ask about the Acheke so as I walked in my aunty at the register was nice smile and said did you call about it, I said yes she disappear and went to get my food.

You people told me the kitchen give suspect so I stood on the side and watch them put my food together the whole time and nothing suspicious was happening at all. In fact it was just my three African aunties in the kitchen talking to each other and gathering my food for me and making it hot, one of my aunties even cut the tomatoes and onions for my food fresh as I watched.

Anyways my food arrived again two of my aunties came to the counter one told me to enjoy my meal and the other one took my card. They both looked on edge and as an African I think they thought i wasn’t American  and was trying to figure out if it was my first time trying African food and if I was going to like it, that’s my assumption or maybe they look like that because you crazy people have left so many madness as reviews so they were overly trying to impress me either way I felt welcomed so aunties thank you.

Finally I came and I have consumed this meal like someone who was starving for 10years. The food was hot in temperature and spices just the way I like it. Infact Jesus himself baked the fish. I am full and  happy. Highly recommend this place go there eat and enjoy and support Africa.
Oh and to my three aunties in the kitchen I’m from Liberia and listen this food was delicious!!!!!!!

The meat was tough and you couldn't chew it. The lady did not explain the the menu. When we walked in all we could smell is gas. I would not recommend this restaurant to anyone. The food I brought is going in the trash. My dog will not eat the food . The food is greasy with a lot of spices. It did not look clean. I should have listened to my brain and turned around and left. Do the health department know that that is a restaurant.

name: Seyo’s Sports & Grill

reviews.text:
I don’t usually write reviews for African restaurants. When I visit a place and the food isn’t great, I’m usually willing to give them a second shot just to be fair. But if it doesn’t improve, I won’t go back.
However, this restaurant, Seeyo, is a different story. I’ve been coming here for a while, and let me tell you, the food is incredible! The owner is super friendly, and the lady with the short hair? She's amazing too.
Honestly, I don’t mind waiting 2 hours for my food if it’s that good. But, if I’m being real, the portions could use a little more love. The stew portion was on the smaller side I finished it before I even got halfway through the rice. I was literally savoring every last drop of that stew, so please, just add a little more next time!
Also, whoever’s cooking now? Keep them around and give them a raise, they’re doing something right!

The owner was warm and welcoming, which I genuinely appreciated. Unfortunately, the quality of the meal didn’t match the hospitality. Once I got home and opened my order, disappointment quickly set in.

The meat portions were extremely small, practically pebble-sized, and many pieces were bony and lacked substance. The cow skin was so tough it was inedible. I had no choice but to throw it away. Only the tripe and one piece of cow skin were passable.

I initially hesitated to write this review. But after reading another customer’s complaint about the same issue posted nine months ago, it became clear that feedback isn’t being taken seriously. That’s troubling. If a concern has been raised and ignored for that long, it suggests the business isn’t listening to its customers.

Beyond the portion size, the stew was overwhelmingly spicy. While spice is integral to Nigerian cuisine, it’s common sense to ask customers about their spice tolerance or offer a milder option. Assuming all Africans or Nigerians can handle extreme heat is not only inaccurate, but also inconsiderate.

Dining at Nigerian restaurants in Maryland often feels like a gamble. Between the undersized meat, the tough cow skin, and the unchecked spice level, I wasted both time and money.

To make matters worse, the music inside the restaurant was excessively loud. And the Afrobeat videos playing on the screens featured semi-nude women, content that’s inappropriate for a public space frequented by families and children. This should be common knowledge. You wouldn’t walk into an American or Chinese restaurant and see music videos with nearly naked performers. They understand that a restaurant is a place for dining, not a nightclub. I still don't understand the need for those Afrobeat music videos with seminude women in a restaurant. It does not make sense. It has to be a Maryland thing. Whoever started that trend should be fined!

Nigerian restaurants have so much potential, but the standard often feels rough. I hope this feedback is taken constructively, though based on the pattern of dismissing past concerns, I’m not optimistic.

Food was a colossal fail, the beef was basically burnt i tried the beef suya have had way better, i had ordered the beef shawarma as well, i was actually put off from finishing when i started eating it at home it because the friend i was with found a small metal piece in his food. The beef in the sandwich was also slightly burnt which i was not shocked because of the suya.  As to if he said something about the metal in his food to the owner in Igbo or yoruba or whatever language they were speaking i doubt it.
The Suya beef and jollof rice is a must..shey. Great meat portion, it is wonderfully spiced and smoked. Plus flavorful rice! Abeg you have to try this Naija food from Seyo's!!! See photos :)
I got the chicken shawarma. It’s like a wrap. The taste was really good.

reviews.text: I came in during lunch time and the young lady was very courteous. I got a veggie platter with 9 options and a few veggie sambusa, everything was amazing. I have dined in and gotten carry out and I would definitely recommend this restaurant. The flavors were so good to me and the injera was soft and perfect.
The vegetarian platter is top tier! So good!!! Plus they do have Ethiopian beer and honey wine. We will return!

Such succulent flavors for one who misses great Ethiopian Food (yeah, I’m calling out NYC for their overpriced Ethiopian). The Awaze Lamb Tibs were perfectly spicy and not gamey at all. The Shiro (chickpeas) were also wonderfully spiced and paired perfectly with the injera! The lentils and gomen were top notch! Service was fantastic! Everyone was so friendly and attentive!

This place is a gem, and absolutely worth a visit!

By far,  one of the MOST DELICIOUS food I have ever had in my life. Oh my!  We found this place about 3 weeks ago and we have been back at least two times a week since. The atmosphere is groovy, very hip and chic evenings during the weekend. Very quiet and calm during weekday afternoons and evenings! It’s a bit small but if they could ever get live Ethiopian music in this place…oh man, I’d move across the street just to be closer and spend the rest of my life at this place. The staff is very friendly and overall incredible!!

My best friend is Ethiopian and her mom makes authentic food weekly. I love it each time. I was craving so I thought why not give one of these restaurants a try. I chose this location because of reviews and the good pricing. My experience all around was great. The guy I placed my order with on the phone was friendly and helpful. He helped me decide between two dishes. I chose the doro wot platter. It is the main ethiopian dish and the white on the top right is made out of cheese n milk its like feta cheese but a diff flavor n taste. The chicken was so tender and the meal its self was very flavorable . I wished it was a little spicer. I should have asked for berbere. Regardless I was full, satisfied and would go back.

formatted_address: 8701 Loch Raven Blvd, Towson, MD 21286, United States
name: Suya Spot

reviews.text:
My experience was not the greatest to be honest and I wasn’t too surprised because the reviews had hinted that. I got different Nigerian foods and none of them hit the “very good” rate for me. They were just very basic and quite overpriced. The suya was very dry, like very dry and the food aesthetic is actually a 1-start. For a restaurant that charges $26 for a dish, I expect you to use actual plates and not plastic plates and spoons to serve. The fact that the food does not also come with water for a dine-in- common!

The asun was just okay but very small for the price.

I will not be returning to the restaurant. It has several potentials for market at its current Towson location but I think it needs an evaluation of food taste, customer service, presentation, prices, to mention but a few.

Having been a soldier and traveling the entire globe I can consider myself a picky experienced food connoisseur. So I must reject some of the other reviews and share my own experience. The staff were thankful, polite, informative, and the food was ready relatively quickly.  The flavor varies between your own choices of heat and/spice levels.  My wife had shrimp suya and fish suya and jollof and loved it. I had the egusi with meat/pounded yam, and turkey tips.

The restaurant was clean. The bathrooms were clean. The ambience was delightful. The music was entertaining, and they boxed up our food before departing (huge in my book). Also, the restaurant is BYOB!! We cannot wait for the outside area to be open in the summer.

Extremely expensive $22  flavorless food. Tough meat seasonless tasteless jollof egussi was very spicy but still had no good flavor. Smelled weird very small bowl for $21 paid. Almost $50 for a disgusting meal never again

Amazing! Happened to be in the area and saw the restaurant and took a chance.  I am sorry to disagree from the other recent reviews here. But, we all have our opinions. This food was just great! My husband and I have dined worldwide and I’m not exaggerating. I consider him a picky eater. The fish soya, egusi, turkey wings (my husband had), and jollof were extremely flavorful. The staff were polite and even boxed up our meals after we dined in. That is hard to find anywhere these days! Give them a try.

Very terrible and horrible foods. Extremely expensive and displeased with the services. We drove very far away to try this restaurant for the very first time. Extremely limited foods they have at this restaurant. When you plan to eat out or dine in, NEVER order from here. Do not go here when hungry or craving African/Nigerian foods. Because you will be very UNHAPPY! Ridiculously more expensive than other African restaurants we have ever visited. All their foods are open and COLD inside the restaurant! The bow of fried rice tastes NOTHING like Fried Rice, we all know. Be WARNED ⚠️!!!

ONLY good thing about this restaurant is that the environment is OK and private parking space.

Nando's Peri-Peri in Baltimore offers a fantastic dining experience where the food and vibe truly jive—the atmosphere is vibrant and welcoming, perfectly complementing the delicious, flame-grilled cuisine. The wait staff is excellent, providing genuine conversation about their best-selling dishes without ever being pushy, making the experience feel personalized and enjoyable. Beyond the famous chicken, the menu thoughtfully includes several tasty vegetarian options, ensuring everyone can find something to savor with that signature Peri-Peri kick. Be sure to order one of their sensational beverages, as the lemonades are awesome and the perfect refreshing complement to the spicy flavors.

Note: You need to order at front counter or via QR code at table.

Chicken was delicious with spices and nicely grilled skin. The sauces are if you want to bump up the heat. We had 2 legs and 3 thighs plus corn on the cob and fries. All we're good and full of flavor. Fries were not hot, but that's ok for me.

reviews.text: The food is good and very tasty. I really enjoy the jollof rice. The serving for the jollof rice isn't bad but like others have said, the soup serving size needs to be more. Whoever is complaining about the spice should go sit down somewhere and not ruin the experience for people like us that love authentic Nigeria food. Maybe Nigerian food isnt for you. some of the most authentic nigerian food i've had in the area! the jollof is smoky and their fish stew is wonderful. the suya is also very good, although the portion could've been a bit more. they also called and warned me that my door dasher was not assigned yet as they were about to close, instead of just canceling my order, which i really appreciated. i will definitely order again

My favorite dish is the egusi and pounded yam. I continue to order here every time I feel homesick and it always make me feel better. This here is a real taste of Africa!

I can’t rave enough about how smoky the jollof was. I’m weird and sometimes like to pair my rice with egusi, and they didn’t disappoint at all. Would recommend to anyone who is as excited about food as I am, because it was a wonderful time.

Absolutely one of my favorite places to get food!! There’s always a level of consistency and quality that’s really hard to find. The portions are so great too, I usually get meat pies and the spicy stew, I’m in love!!

I urge you to review your communication processes and ensure that your business is readily accessible to customers during the hours listed on various platforms. Improving responsiveness will undoubtedly enhance the overall customer experience and contribute to the success of your establishment.

I appreciate your attention to this matter and hope to see positive changes in the future.

You have been opened for a while and have loyal customers, it seems like you are getting a little bit too relaxed now because you have too many customers. You will loose this customers if your staff disrespectful to your customers and their time.

Disgusting and flavorless. The meat pie was was flavor less and the suya was so spicy my child who eats pepper was crying. Not to mention how old and nasty the hallow and white rice was. The food is good but beware that they never pick up their phone and the wait is extremely long even when you order and pick up.

We are from Atlanta and it has been difficult finding a good restaurant here in BWI each time we visit.
I definitely will come back again.

I found this place while I was looking for African food near me. I was a little skeptical given the very few reviews and the fact that the address is an apartment.
It is indeed not a restaurant but a carry out run in the chef’s apartment.
I became extra skeptical when he wanted me to make payment upfront through Zelle or cashap so I decided to just order one item.
Fast forward, he texted me to say the food was ready. To my surprise the food came presented in really nice containers and well packaged. I couldn’t wait to get home and give it a try. I am happy to report that the food tastes really good. He literally killed every single item. I will definitely order more items and update my reviews.

Things to note:
-He’s currently operating out of an apartment, I think it’s take out only from my experience.
- I think he’s a real chef, no kidding.

100% recommend. I’ve been trying to introduce African cuisine to my son, but he wouldn’t eat anything after the first taste. He tasted Chef John’s okra stew and instantly asked for more. He was so  excited we  finally found African food he loved. It was such a beautiful moment for my family. The food presentation, quality, and portion size were all outstanding.

Chef John puts his heart into his meals and gives his client a wonderful experience. Recently I experienced his seafood okra aka ila a la se po... it was amazing! The whole family loved it even my young kids 10 & 8.

My kids had his turkey 2 years ago and requested for it again this year, that's how memorable his meals are. So as requested we tried his raga turkey, spinach aka efo riro and Jollof rice for Thanksgiving 2024 and he  did not disappoint!! Everything was tasty, people kept asking where the food was catered from.

Kudos chef, we enjoy your meals. And we will keep coming back.

Thank you!!!

To start, I ordered the White Rice and Stew with Ponmo, a delightful combination of flavors and textures that left me eager for what was to come. The freshness of the ingredients was apparent, and the careful balance of spices made each bite a true delight. It was so delicious.
Whether you're a food enthusiast seeking a gastronomic adventure or someone looking for a memorable meal with loved ones, Chef John's Kitchen is the perfect choice. I can't wait for the opportunity to return and savor the culinary delights that this kitchen has to offer once again. Thank you for the food. 🙏

formatted_address: 12600c Harford Rd, Hydes, MD 21082, United States
name: Amma's Kitchen

reviews.text: Yesterday my life was changed, because I walked into Amma's Kitchen. I was greeted by Amma herself, with a warm smile and friendly service. The atmosphere is chill, with comfortable chairs, nice tables, and positive affirmations spread around. The food? Take your pick. IT'S ALL DELICIOUS. The Red Stew was flavorful, aromatic, and cooked to perfection. Curry Goat. Jerk Chicken. AMAZING. FALLS OFF THE BONE. The Broiled Salmon with Mac n Cheese was drizzled with this zesty vibrant lemon butter dill sauce. I'd put it on everything. The cornbread....ha..You thought you've had cornbread? You'll never eat another cornbread again if it's not how Amma put her heart and soul into preparing those delicious morsels.

We drove from Baltimore to this restaurant that was featured and WBAL TV. It serves a combination of American, African and Caribbean cuisine. The employees were very nice. Made suggestions of what to try.
We had the fried fish with jollof rice, coco bread and a second entree of ginger chicken with jollof rice. Both entrees were cooked to order. Arrived hot and steamy. Seasoned well. 2 large pieces of Swai fish perfectly fried along with a flavorful jollof rice. Needed the cabbage but wasn't ready at the time
The ginger chicken was good. A little kick from the ginger but not overly spicy. Good portion size.
A portion of the proceeds are returned to help other countries with girls and women sanitary needs

came in after a long bike ride of intense cardio. I was greeted by a very kind woman, presumably the owner. She was a wonderful kind woman who explained the menu and what is good for my particular tastes, with a warm smile. The other two women there I talked to were equally as kind and helpful. I am not sure what their names are and who is Amma. I got the red goat stew and it was absolutely delicious. Huge portion, very fair price, lower than comparable food at other places, and perfect taste, just the right amount of spiciness and rich flavor. I will be returning to this place very soon and i reccomend it to anyone who is a fan of international cuisines and new delicious flavors.  Thank you Amma’s Kitchen. I am so glad you opened near my home.

Well where has this restaurant been hiding. Food is as good as my mom’s home cooked. Highly recommend the peanut butter soup. And the jollof is 😚

My family and I just came back from Ghana and the food here tasted even better.

I’m going back with some friends next time.

I love the food it is perfectly seasoned and it takes me back to my childhood. The atmosphere transports you to Ghana and the mission to help women in need warms my heart. You would be a fool not to eat here!

formatted_address: 44 Meriam Ct, Owings Mills, MD 21117, United States
name: AbakeFoodTalk LLC

reviews.text:
I ordered through door dash. Unfortunately, the price did not meet the quality or quantity of the food. The packaging is nice for average delivery but ordering food I'm more concerned about the taste.

I ordered Ayamase with White Rice it does not come with plantain despite the $40 cost. The meat tasted like it was frozen previously and re-heated. The texture of the ponmo was either very very very tough to eat (I just threw them away) or gritty and rubbery, overall odd in taste and texture.

I will not try this place in the future because the taste was unpleasant and the price was high. The price difference of $15-$20 from other similar restaurants is not justifiable despite the elevated plastic packaging.

Workers service 100% better then owner
You can’t change price on pickup
Otherwise good quality is perfect we always recommend this restaurant

Delicious, authentic cuisine paired with amazing customer service. I absolutely love it here, she makes sure you eat good! The presentation of the food was soooo beautiful and definitely worth every penny. Try her out you will not be disappointed!

Hello ,
I wanted to take a moment to express my gratitude for the amazing food and presentation. The flavors were exceptional, and I thoroughly enjoyed every bite. I will definitely be ordering more in the future.

Thank you once again for such a wonderful experience. I’ll be sure to spread the word!

This lady is a fraud!!! She changed the price of my order after I ordered and increased it by $13! How can you change a lunch item price from $42 to $55 AFTER I’ve ordered and waited for an hour for the food? For one person? Then you hang on me when I call you to ask about it? You are not serious and your business will not succeed because of your attitude. Good luck getting customers when you lack customer service. Nonsense!

formatted_address: 401 W 29th St, Baltimore, MD 21211, United States
name: Blacksauce Kitchen

reviews.text:
Blacksauce Kitchen is well known around the city for dishing up those big buttery biscuit sandwiches we've all seen at the farmers market.  I finally had the opportunity to try their brick and mortar location in Remington for a delicious early afternoon bite.

Blacksauce is a quaint little shop with limited seating options to enjoy your food.  I decided to grab my food to go and pop a squat down the street at R. House to eat my lunch. The staff at Blacksauce were welcoming and very friendly. I decided to go with the Cider Braised Chicken Biscuit, Sweet Potato Donut, and a Smoked Apple Cider.  The chicken biscuit was yummy, especially with the addition of the onion jam which seemed to appear more prominent and even more flavorful once the sandwich was cold.  I enjoyed the sweet potato donut however, I wanted more of a sweet potato flavor to shine through.  And the smoked apple cider drink was just what was needed for the cooler weather.

I follow Blacksauce Kitchen on IG and they always seem to have some really creative dishes they make on a weekly basis.  I definitely plan on stopping by to try more of their lunch/dinner style food on a Thursday.

Let's get into it!!!!! Ooooo weeeee!!! Blacksauce Kitchen is the truth. The menu changes daily so let's get into Thursdays (Aug 17th) menu choices. We ordered 1 of everything left on the menu: Oxtail biscuit, doubles, mac, cabbage, cobbler, fritters, sorrel and limeade. We stayed inside the restaurant to make sure we tasted everything fresh and hot. They have one table and a bar top with stools for dining in.

10/10 my favorite was the cabbage. Perfect seasoning, heat, cook - no complaints whatsoever. I could eat a pot full.

9/10 my second favorite was the oxtail biscuit. The picture below speaks for itself. Ghr biscuit was PERFECTION!! I could've used some kind of sauce or wetness on the oxtail. The fried onions were on point.

8.5/10 the fritters were great. The each chow chow gave it that extra edge. Because it was served in a recyclable container all the chose chow juices were absorbed in the container. J think it should be served in plastic. Or foil placed in the container.

7/10 the Mac was good. 8/10 Sorrel was great. We actually created a half and half of sorrel and limeade and that was fire 10/10. The doubles were good but could've been cooked longer. The only thing we weren't fans of was the smoked cobbler. Wag too much smoke for my taste. The smokey flavor overwhelmed the cobbler.

Most definitely going back to hit another menu soon!!
Rotating menu and well known biscuits food never disappoints truly unique experience.

I did an online order for a rotisserie chicken apricot biscuit and it was delicious! My order was ready right on time for the time that I scheduled to pick it up. It was also a nice portion size, which I loved. The peach jam on the biscuit really made all the flavors standout!

Had their yuzu plum donut when they were at the Ekiben Night Market today. It was one of the best donuts I’ve ever had. Not too sweet, great citrus flavor, and the crunchiness of the donut on the outside was amazing. I hope you guys make it a regular part of your menu because it was the bomb.

formatted_address: 3534 Brenbrook Dr, Randallstown, MD 21133, United States
name: Jembis Grillz

reviews.text:
The food here is EXCELLENT😋 and the owner Femi is  awesome! Haven’t met his wife yet but I’m  sure she’s amazing! She does the majority of the cooking. So my hubby and I visited when they first opened this summer and tried the Steak Suya Platter and it was absolutely delicious!!!
The platters here are very hardy and the food is flavored to the bone!! I decided to use Jembis Grillz to cater my brother’s wedding and all I kept hearing was how flavorful and delicious everything was! Our orders were ready on time and packaged well for the 1hour travel time. Femi even called later on to make sure everything was to our liking. Now that’s FIVE STAR customer service and appreciation! Definitely a must try if you enjoy Nigerian cuisine. Oh and you can control the spice levels, that was a plus for me!

One of the best place to get good and tasty african food. Lovely and neat environment with soft music to entertain customers while enjoying their meals. A place to be. You can't get it wrong with Jembis

I went to Jembis a couple of weeks ago, and i picked up a shawarma appropriately called Nigerian Shawarma and some suya. I see how people would like the Nigerian Sharwarma, i enjoyed it especially the sauce, i wish it had more meat tho. The suya was also delectable solid enough. I will go the again.

Absolutely spectacular, from food to customer service to overall ambiance. This place was lovely and delicious and as a first timer, the gentleman help in the front led me in the right direction. This place is fantastic and so unbelievably authentic. Thank you so much for being so welcoming. I will be dining here again soon!!

Impressed with the services here, Jembis suggested we tried the Suya Sharwama and Zino. It was very tasty and rich ! Naija standard sharwama

I highly you recommend you visit..

formatted_address: 301 Light St, Baltimore, MD 21202, United States
name: Soul Kuisine Cafe

reviews.text: The best food in Baltimore! We're visiting from New Jersey and we're going to miss this place 😭 food was so good we had to come back the next time and try some more

Being from the deep south (AL), it's hard finding real soul food. The DMV is a total bust when it it comes to true soul food. Came to Baltimore (yes, I know it's not the DMV) and found this spot, and the reviews did not disappoint. I got the turkey wings w cabbage and fries . My partner got wings w sweet potatoes and mac. Everything was delicious. Although it was a tad bit too salty. Just a little. And the mac wasn't my kind of mac, everything was still so flavorful. It's inside the food court area. You can't see it from outside.

The service is what you'd expect because everything is made to order. Took about 15-20 mins, but we didn't care because it's not fast food. Blackfamilyy owned and operated. Very nice people. Clean. And they had a 90s playlist going. I can't wait to go back. The prices were what you would expect for the area. It reminded me so much of what I had in Alabama. Delicious home cooking. The only thing I wish they had was cornbread!

Staying at Inner Harbor and was looking for a black owned restaurant to support and came across this place (it's inside the mall).  We arrived @ 2pm and they were already out of collards and turkey wings. Not sure if they were sold out or just didn't have any for the day. We ordered the blackened catfish, shrimp, mac n cheese, yams, rice, and green beans.  I thought the green beans were a little too salty but other than than we found EVERYTHING to be very flavorful and would go back again.

I’ve been searching high and low for good fried fish in Baltimore ever since my favorite neighborhood spot closed, and Soul Kuisine came highly recommended. Located on the first floor of Harborplace, it offers a convenient yet slightly tricky location for parking, though it’s manageable. I was excited to try their food after reading that they serve actual catfish—a rarity these days when many places substitute other fish. While they have tables for dine-in, I opted for takeout.

The fried catfish was the highlight of my order. After making a stop on the way home, I tried it straight from the box. It was a bit soggy by then and rated about a 6.5 or 7/10. However, a quick two minutes in the air fryer brought it back to life, transforming it into a solid 9/10. This tells me that if eaten fresh at the restaurant, it’s probably closer to a perfect 10. The flavor was authentic, and the fish had that classic crispy coating that makes fried catfish so satisfying.

The fries were seasoned frozen fries—not bad, but not the star of the show either, which is fine since I was there for the fish. Overall, Soul Kuisine has earned its spot as my go-to for fried catfish in Baltimore. If you’re a fan of fresh, well-seasoned fish, I highly recommend giving them a try—just eat it there for the best experience!

To the nice young lady and the nice young man here you all are amazing!!!!! I had the mac and cheese bowl with chicken on top and it was sooooooo good!!! I also got lemonade which was delicious!!!! I am thoroughly happy with my experience here and will definitely be returning!!!! Keep doing what you do guys and may God bless you always!!!! See you soon!!!!😍😍😍❤️❤️❤️

formatted_address: 4032 Falls Rd, Baltimore, MD 21211, United States
name: Chef BobbyD Restaurant & Catering

reviews.text:
I visited Chef Bobby D’s in Towson, MD and had a great experience. The establishment was clean, welcoming, and had a really good vibe. The food came out super hot and fresh, with large portions at a very reasonable price. I got the Oxtail Rasta Pasta and I have no complaints.

What really stood out was the customer service — truly 11/10. Everyone was friendly, attentive, and made the experience even better.

I would definitely recommend this spot and will absolutely be back soon.

What can I say about this place? I absolutely love it! Everything about this place is top tier in my opinion, from the food, to the restaurant decor and the customer service 👌🏾 I've been ordering from this restaurant for years on grubhub and doordash I don't have any pictures because the food is so good I never remember to until it's gone. 🤣 I recently went inside of this restaurant to order in person for the first time over Christmas break and even the atmosphere of the restaurant is warm and inviting also its decorated very nicely, and customer service is great! They were so fast, the lady said 50 minutes but the food was ready in 25. I love it here.

Food: I got the Jerk Chicken with the plantains and rice and pea. The food was fantastic! The chicken wasnt dry or too spicy and the flavor of the sauce was amazing. Be careful because there are some small bones in the chicken that you may bite down on. The plantains were sweet and melted in your mouth and the rice and pea had a rich flavor that complemented the rest of the dish. Reheating the food didnt dry it out and the sauce was even more rich the next day.
Service: The cashier was very nice but it did take a little bit for the food to come out. It was worth the wait because it wae piping hot! The prices were also great for the amount of food you got.
Atmosphere: The resturant had a cozy vibe and the dining area, counters, and bathroom were clean. It was a bit difficult to find napkins and it was pretty toasty inside the resturant. Everyone who entered was very nice and tons of doordash orders were being picked up. They had reserved parking in the back for customers so you dont have to park on the street.
It was my first time going and I cant wait to try out the Towson location!
Absolutely AMAZING food! I mean everything was a legit 10/10!!! Well worth whatever they are charging because its gonna taste damn good! Do your tummy a favor and order from here and often!!!

So I had been here a while ago when they first opened and was underwhelmed - but I'm so glad I went back and gave them another chance because this place is fantastic! Every dish my party ordered was well priced and busting with flavor. I got to try most things since we all share. I have to say that the Jamaican jerk wings and the entrees were the stand out stars. The salads and sandwiches are good but if you're coming to an island fusion place get the island flavored dishes because they spice them right. I'll be getting a lot of take out from here in the future.

formatted_address: 112 E Lexington St, Baltimore, MD 21202, United States
name: Next Phaze Cafe

reviews.text: I came here with my family after visiting the aquarium. We are out-of-towners. From the food to the spectacular service from Ms. Candy we will most definitely be back. The food is authentic and everything is cooked in house. I’m not sure what I liked more, the AMAZING fresh sweet potato pie with the graham cracker crust or the perfectly crispy chicken wings, the jerk wings were amazing and the salmon was banging. The sides were 10/10. Mac and cheese, collard greens and cabbage. Even the French fries were perfect lol And again, Ms. Candy was a pleasant waitress and hostess, she was for sure the queen of the spot! Google only allows photos and I took videos of the meals, but pls enjoy the photo of the French fries haha

I ordered through a delivery service. The food arrived and was absolutely awful. I was not even able to eat it. The quality was terrible. The greens string beans were 2 different colors ( old mix with newer) the fried chicken was clearly sourced cheep and of poor quality.

Me and my bf ordered from uber eats, i asked for cabbage got greens instead, no biggie, i usually pick at my chicken bc i dont like eating veins or chicken that has blood on it but this day i was literally starving so i js ate it without looking but the next piece i tore apart bc i wanted to dip it in ranch, i saw a bunch of pink immediately thrown off. I thought it was js tht one piece but no all of them were like tht. My bf ate like 3 pieces before i told him we cant eat this we’re gonna get salmonella. Sure enough the entire day i had the runs, my stomach hurted nonstop even when i didn’t have to use the bathroom. Thankfully i got my money back from uber eats but this is very unsafe i strongly advise the kitchen to do better.
The greens were a 6/10 needs better seasonings and the mac was a 7/10 not too bad.

I ordered via UberEats. I got the catfish platter with mac&cheese and greens and sweet potato pie. The catfish was DELICIOUS. The homemade tartar sauce was so nice and unique. The mac and cheese was interesting but the more I ate it the more I liked it. The greens were gross to me. I threw them away. Sweet potato pie had different flavors than I am used to but I also liked it. Overall I will order again but SKIP THE GREENS!

This food was okay ..not gonna lie my stomach became very upset after eating tho. The atmosphere was not what I expected, very dull and need some lighting. Looks like they don't get business much. I had crab cake greens & yellow rice. My rice was hard , crab cake was a 2/10 and the greens were phony! never again for me. lady at the front desk was very sweet tho

formatted_address: Macon Dr, Glen Burnie, MD 21060, United States
name: Afro Grill House [Pick-up & Delivery]

reviews.text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

I visited from the UK and had the chicken platter with sides and a smoothie, and it was absolutely delicious! The chicken was well-seasoned and cooked perfectly, the sides were fresh and flavourful, and the smoothie was the perfect refreshing touch. The service was warm and welcoming, and they made me feel right at home even though I was so far away. Definitely one of the highlights of my trip—highly recommend!

Food was delivered right on time and on point. Food so inviting and delicious. Packaging really sophisticated and presentable. Food uniquely different from the regular party food. The sauce spicy and tasty. My family absolutely loved the food.
I ordered two boxes of Guinea fowl with sides for my family. I must say we did not regret it at all. Really tasty with the right amount of spice! We thoroughly enjoyed it! We will be ordering again!

Afro Grill makes the best grilled guinea fowl, roasted yam and plantain in the DMV area. Customer service is top notch and the food tasted so delicious. I will recommend Afro Grill anytime. The grilled spicy guinea fowl with sides of roasted yam and plantain did not disappoint. Tasted so delicious. Keep up the good work. I'll definitely be back soon for continuous order 👍

I recently tried the grilled chicken from Afro Grill House, and it was absolutely delicious! The chicken was perfectly seasoned, tender, and juicy. The flavors were bold and well-balanced, making every bite satisfying. Definitely a must-try for anyone craving tasty, flavorful grilled chicken! I will try the rest of their menu soon.

formatted_address: 215 Philadelphia Rd, Joppatowne, MD 21085, United States
name: Oasis Sweets Spices African Cuisine

reviews.text:
I love love love their food. Very delicious and organic. Neatly presented. And their customer services is top notch too. Will be ordering every week.

Thank you
Excellent service and best african dish ever.The moin moin is top notch,fried rice has everything just as necessary,no excess oil and efoi riro is superb.A trial will convince you.

formatted_address: 3539 Brenbrook Dr, Randallstown, MD 21133, United States
name: NuShiloh Restaurant & Catering

reviews.text: If I can rate them a negative I would. This restaurant had been a go to for us especially for their Jollof rice. We buy frequently, we refer friends and family because we believed in the quality of the food, however this recent experience today with their customer service was absolute trash. You people should be ashamed yourselves, you are a disappointment to the African food community in particular. I called to order half pan of Jollof rice as we frequently do, and I was told it was $50. I was shocked and inquired further if the pricing was correct as I had just purchased the same pan a week or two prior or $35. The lady was so rude saying they've been selling it for over a year for $50 which was absolutely not true!! I explained to her the situation, and she said that's how they sell, yelling on the phone, I had to caution her several times to bring her voice down and then proceeds to hang up the phone on me. My household alone has spent over $2000 with these people since we moved to the area. You will not be getting another dime of my money or anyone I know, and I will be sure to let everyone I have referred know that your service is absolute trash. If I was the owner best believe whomever that woman I spoke to would be fired immediately. And absolute disgrace.

I eat here all the time, and for good reason—this place serves some of the best Nigerian food I’ve had outside of home. It’s super convenient since it’s close to my university, and after a long day of classes and athletics, nothing hits like food from Nu’Shiloh.

My go-to combo is the jollof rice with plantain and goat meat—it’s perfectly spicy, the plantains are always fried just right (crispy edges, soft in the middle), and the goat meat is tender and well-seasoned. You can tell they take their time with the cooking.

The vibes are calm and welcoming, whether you’re dining in or grabbing takeout. Service is friendly and they’re supplied with a great assortment of beverages!

Definitely recommend if you’re craving authentic, homemade-style Nigerian food. 10/10, I’ll keep coming back!

I previously had a problem and went to speak with the owner. She was very apologetic, understanding &  completely listened to my concerns . It could have very well been a misconception on my part. Sometimes all it takes is a conversation. The food is  consistently delicious & fresh. You can tell the food was made with love. Try them. You will not regret it.💕

I don't know how this so called "restaurant" is still in business, the food is disgusting, the pounded yam tasted like they put soap in it and the fish as well. I don't trust these people, the ladies here are very rude and nasty. Never again. This place is a disgrace. Messing with people's food is never good! God sees everything. Very wicked people. And the food is not fresh.

If i could give them a 0 i would. Only good thing about this place is how affordable their food is, besides that you’re in a for a ride. Food is old and stale, the restaurant staff are very rude, it’s like you’re begging them to do their job for food you’re paying for. 0/10 would not recommended.

formatted_address: 1841 E Lombard St, Baltimore, MD 21231, United States
name: Water for Chocolate Catering LLC

reviews.text: Absolutely DELICIOUS! I didn't think I'd love the barbecue shrimp and grits, but it was amazing. My Poinsetta was light and tasty without being too sweet or strong. The vibe was so relaxing, from the decor, artwork, and music. The only potential drawback is the parking, but I was blessed to find a spot next to the outdoor seating, which I can imagine is great when it's warm. I will definitely be revisiting with friends.

Best food I’ve had in Baltimore in ages. The food is MINDBLOWINGLY delicious, service is great, atmosphere is cozy and cute. They even have hooks for your purse :) and I liked being able to see over the counter into the kitchen. We had the duck poutin, WFC salad (THE CORNBREAD OMG), lamb chops, and blue plate seafood curry. Every single thing was phenomenal.

Last night was truly unforgettable. We had the pleasure of dining at Water for Chocolate restaurant, and the entire evening felt like a beautiful culinary experience.From the moment we arrived, the ambiance was warm and elegant, setting the tone for what would become an extraordinary experience.
The food was nothing short of spectacular. It genuinely felt as though the chef was cooking exclusively for our party — and in a way, he was. We had the rare opportunity to watch him prepare our dishes right in front of us, engaging with him as he worked his magic in the kitchen. That personal touch added a whole new layer of intimacy and appreciation to the meal.
Our server was equally impressive: gracious, knowledgeable, and attentive without being overbearing. He guided us through the menu, which we learned changes nightly or weekly i think keeping the experience fresh and exciting for returning guests.
It wasn’t just dinner — it was a celebration of flavor, hospitality, and artistry. I can’t wait to go back.

We tried this place for the first time during Baltimore Restaurant week. We oderednoff the pre fix menu and ala carte. They did not disappoint. All meals were freshly cooked and the server Thomas was super polite and welcoming. We were able to get a table with no reservations in a cozy nook. My duck risotto (not pictured bc ai tore it up) was creamy perfection. All items were delicious and the sweet potato bread pudding was an excellent highlight.

I’ve been thinking about planning another date night with my wife, and it hit me—I never wrote the review that Water for Chocolate truly deserves. So here it is.

My wife and I have been coming here for the last two years, and every single visit has been excellent. We’ve celebrated her birthday with brunch, enjoyed a Valentine’s Day dinner, and stopped in for casual date nights. Each time, the food quality and service have been consistently top-tier.

If you want great, flavorful food, go there.
If you want an intimate, cozy vibe, go there.  They do reservations, so do yourself a favor and make one.

Chef Sean works magic in the kitchen! Every dish tastes fresh and is full of flavor. Water for Chocolate is easily one of our favorite spots in Baltimore, and we’ll definitely be back again soon.

formatted_address: 9990 Washington Blvd N, Laurel, MD 20723, United States
name: Monikay's Kitchen

reviews.text: Waakye with goat and fried yam and fried turkey. This was the exact meal I needed after a long vacation. Ghanaian food gives me energy and this was the meal I needed to get my vim back. Didn’t pick up my call but when I got at the restaurant it seemed busy. My food came out relatively quick. Parking was fine. Shito was very good. Garrí was iffy not my favorite but still decent.

onikay's Kitchen is a hidden gem for anyone craving bold, authentic West African flavors with a surprising Caribbean twist. The restaurant blends cultural influences beautifully—offering classic dishes like jollof rice alongside flavorful Caribbean staples such as jerk chicken.

I tried the jollof rice with jerk chicken, and it did not disappoint. The rice was rich and well-seasoned with just the right amount of heat, while the jerk chicken was juicy and had a nice smoky kick. You can really taste the care that goes into the preparation.

While the food is definitely tasty and satisfying, the prices are a bit on the higher side for casual dining. That said, the quality and fusion of flavors help justify the cost—especially if you’re looking for something a little different.

Monikay's Kitchen brings something unique to the table with its West African-Caribbean combo, and it's worth a visit if you’re in the mood for flavorful comfort food with a twist.

For whatever reason this restaurant is underrated. They beat almost if not all of the nearby African restaurants in value and their food is better than average. You can dine in but it’s more of a takeout setup. Staff are friendly, food presentation is great and their environment is clean.

The management here is extremely rude. You can see from my review history that I rarely leave negative feedback, but I feel compelled to share this experience. A restaurant should be built on hospitality and respect for its customers—unfortunately, that is not what you’ll find here. I would strongly recommend avoiding this place. The place also didnt appeae clean.  It's unfortunate because I was attempting to support a minority owned business.
One of the workers there were extremely rude and non communicative. He got an attitude with us for a mistake he made. Food was good but was overpriced for the service received.

formatted_address: 101 E 25th St, Baltimore, MD 21218, United States
name: Terra Cafe

reviews.text: What an awesome experience!!!! My first time visiting and immediately felt at home. Food was hot and very delicious, compliments to the chef. Thursday night jam session was a refreshing experience with seasoned jazz musicians accompanied by some young up-and-coming artist from Peabody.
Amazing place for big gathering.  Best customer service in Baltimore! And the fried fish was amazing- so so soft and delicate but crispy seasoned exterior.  Would come again!

Incredible!!!!!  The owner is friendly and passionate about the delicious food and space he has created, about community, about Baltimore, about being a positive person and presence in the world.  Super fresh and flavorful vegan food, beautiful atmosphere, amazing experience—absolutely a new favorite!!!

Love Terra Cafe for a lunch or business meeting. They have a small bar, but I don't drink so I can't say much. But everyone there seemed to enjoy it. I'd suggest you visit Terra Cafe to see for yourself. And then, hit me back with your feedback.

Terra Cafe is an individually owned and designed cafe. It's not a chain. We went there because the owner sponsors her grandson's basketball team. The place has nice African-American motif art works,, and good, fresh food.

I had a chicken cheese wrap with salad. It was quite good, although there was a piece of chicken bone in the chicken. My wrap and my wife's sandwich were so big that we couldn't finish them. We had the second half of our lunch for dinner.

My wife had a smoked turkey sandwich. She enjoyed it.

There isn't a parking lot. We found metered street parking very near the entrance.

formatted_address: 3845 Falls Rd, Baltimore, MD 21211, United States
name: Wicked Sisters

reviews.text: Brunch was Delicious ! My first time there. Bloody Mary , excellent spice and flavor .  We also got baileys and coffee after brunch . They put baileys on the side which is fine but the waitress made our cups so cute with the whipped cream and coffee beans .  I got the TABS Benny and my friend she got the breakfast bowl. Everything was hot and fresh and my Benedict came with spinach and they don’t skimp on it . You will be stuffed and happy. Our waitress was Rachel S. She was amazing. She is thoughtful , friendly ,and prompt . We didn’t have a reservation and took a chance because I have never been  and was given a gift card. They made a sweet deal for us and got us in at 1130 as long as we were finished by 1 for the reservation . Hosts were great and accommodating . Great experience . Thank you so much.

We had a wonderful time with friends. Drinks, appetizers and dinner was fantastic. We started with the small plate of arancini and shareable brussel sprout appetizer. Their drink menu is fun. They have a menu for everyone and offer gluten free options. Danny W. took very good care of us! They have two bars and multilevel dining. I would recommend you give them a try when you're in Baltimore.

My sister and I went during Restaurant Week and got an excellent three course meal for $45 on a separate menu. From the variety of food selections, indoor and outdoor seating, as well as an understanding staff. Rachael, our waitress, was very kind and informative and recommended specific wines based on our meal. From the delicious meals, to good wine, and EVEN BETTER atmosphere. We were told that the bartender was the DJ for the night on the second floor, KEEP THEM AS THE DJ! Very relaxing and still a lively energy.

Came with my favorite foodie. Amy and Kendall are AMAZING staff members!
Brussel sprouts were EXCELLENT. Nice and crisp, very tasty.
We thought the donuts were the holes, they were actual full sized donuts. We didn't touch them immediately and when we finally did, they were STILL warm.
Breakfast bowl was delicious. Can't remember the names of our drinks but they were great. Mimosas were good as well.
We will definitely be back!

We did a little impromptu happy hour get together this week and the venue was perfect. I loved the outdoor patio area. Our server was great (I think it was Tim). The wings are excellent. The drinks were good. It was really a nice vibe. No complaints.

formatted_address: 1029 W Baltimore St, Baltimore, MD 21223, United States
name: Darker Than Blue Grille

reviews.text: I drove to the new location at 1029 W Baltimore St and there is not a restaurant with this name over here. I called the number, it played an automated message with the location changed and new opening date. Today is January 8th. I called to see if there is a person that can direct us to the correct place, but couldn't reach a person. Per Google, they should be open.

Amazing food and service!
We walked in without a reservation, and we were seated promptly and were introduced to the menu. Their signature peach ice tea was so delicious and sweet! The complimentary corn bread with sweet potato butter was to die for. We also had the crab Mac & cheese, the baby back ribs, and the fried catfish and grits. All were so delicious. The catfish and grits especially were really good. The service was great and our drinks were kept full.
One of the best meals in Baltimore for sure!

Black owned, family run restaurant. Food and drinks were delicious. The chicken was slightly undercooked and they didn't hesitate to put the skillet back in the oven. It came back fully cooked and delicious!

I'd recommend: Cornbread skillet (perfect for sharing), BBQ chicken w mac & cheese and collard greens, and BBQ ribs w mash and asparagus.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Darker than Blue in Baltimore, and I must say, the experience was absolutely amazing. From the moment I walked in, I was impressed by the warm and friendly customer service. The staff went above and beyond to make sure our group of 12 felt welcome and comfortable.

Now, let's talk about the food. Oh my goodness, it was simply outstanding! Every dish we tried was bursting with flavor and expertly prepared. Whether you're a seafood lover or prefer something more savory, Darker than Blue has something to satisfy every palate. The menu offers a wide variety of options, and each dish is crafted with care and attention to detail.

In addition to the incredible food, I was also blown away by the quality of the drinks. The bartenders at Darker than Blue truly know their craft and create delicious and refreshing beverages. I highly recommend trying one of their signature cocktails or exploring their extensive wine list.

Overall, my experience at Darker than Blue was nothing short of exceptional. The combination of delectable food, top-notch customer service, and inviting atmosphere make it a must-visit restaurant in Baltimore. I would rate my experience a perfect 10/10 and will definitely be returning in the future.

My experience here was perhaps one of my worst dining experiences In Baltimore. The bartender/waiter was not friendly at all. He gave off the energy that we were some how inconveniencing him by being there from the moment we walked in the door. They don't have a drink menu, had no beer at all, no burgers (we found out after ordering), and  the dishes were dirty. When we brought to bartender that our wine glasses were dirty, he said its from the dish washer and there was nothing  he could do about that but pour it in to another glass. As if we had to take it or leave it. Which my wife and are choosing to leave it and never consider going there again. We thought maybe the food would end up being good in the end despite the poor service but they missed the mark on that as well. We ordered the lemon pepper wings and they had little to no flavor. We were really excited to try this place since we are locals but unless there is a dramatic change in the attitude of the staff and improvement in the quality of service overall, they wont make it unfortunately.

formatted_address: 4405 Belair Rd, Baltimore, MD 21206, United States
name: AJ's Carry-Out local & international

reviews.text: I was very happy to find out that there's a new Senegalese restaurant in Baltimore and AJ's is great! We had the Thiebou Dienn (Jollof Rice & Fish) and the Dibi Lamb dishes which were delicious and plentiful! I highly recommend their Senegalese food! (Please note, there are no tables to eat at inside. It is best to carryout or have the food delivered from this location).

I was very surprised by how delicious the Dibi Lamb was! The flavors were amazing! I was looking for Dibi Chicken and the Baobab drink (Bouye). The only other places I could get Senegalese food was in Silver Spring or driving way across Baltimore. This location was close and their food was WAY better....OMG! The red onion sauce was spicy 🥵 🔥 I loved it! There is something about that Mustard sauce. Walahi you can eat a sneaker with that sauce! 🤣🤤

The Dibi Lamb portion was excellent 👌🏽!🔥🔥

The owner was very professional and kind and helpful. I found a new place for my Baobob fruit drink addiction!!

Go!!!🚗 They are legit. Mashallah. I'm very happy I went here this evening. Now I have a new place! They sell Nigerian and local American food also.

Man I dont usually leave reviews but this ish was AMAZING !!!! Ordered a fish dinner from here last night and I couldve fed my whole family off it. Large portion. Also customer service was A+++ . Thank you
The food is delicious, as always. The staff is very friendly and helpful. Also, I haven't tried drinks like theirs anywhere else, it is amazing! Recommend, 10/10.

I am so happy that heaven has come down in the form of this restaurant. Very nice people. I had their Cheh-boo Jen, and it was amazing!

I recommend everyone come on out and enjoy their food. They deserve the recognition!

formatted_address: 8459 Baltimore National Pike #14, Ellicott City, MD 21043, United States
name: Tigi's Ethiopian Restaurant and Market

reviews.text:
08/13: Sorry, I had to change the review after my daughter woke up with stomach pain and vomiting, and she has been sick since then. Last night, she only had a samosa and mango nectar from this restaurant for dinner, which I didn’t have( I ate something else), so maybe that’s why I’m fine while she’s sick. I’m not sure if the food she ate is the reason for her illness, and I’m also not sure if they cooked the samosa freshly.I may be wrong but just wanted to share my experience .
08/12 : Calm and cozy spot! Not crowded at all—likely because many do carry-out. Portions were generous. Loved the bread with sautéed tofu, bean curry  and the rich Ethiopian coffee—didn’t realize it’s served black 😀 with no milk, but it was smooth and flavorful. My daughter raved about the perfectly spiced samosa and refreshing mango nectar. Service was a bit slow, maybe because there were fewer employees, but overall it was a lovely experience. A hidden gem!

I didn't specifically rate the food, because it turns out I can't eat most of it and it doesn't seem fair to give them a low rating just because of my own sensitivities.

My date had a lamb dish that he said was "fine". Given that this was our first time trying Ethiopian food, he wasn't sure if he wasn't a huge fan of the specific cuisine or that specific dish. The vegan samosas were much spicier than anticipated, and the gluten free injera was extremely tangy compared to the regular injera (to the point that I really didn't like it but again that could be just me, but my date wasn't a fan either).

Service was good. Drinks were a bit slow to come out, but there was only one person working the customer side and she was serving restaurant customers as well as checking out grocery customers, so I think the slower service was due to her being stretched thin rather than inattention or lack of customer care.

The two of us probably won't be back, but only because this food is not really our thing. If you like Ethiopian food, it's probably a great place.

I'm not an adventurous guy but I love exploring new things. I know it is the greatest dichotomy of my life. One of the people I admired the most was Anthony Bourdain. He was a gifted storyteller. But what kept me glued to the tv when he was on was how he shared the humanity in all of us. He went to areas of this world where we were terrified of venturing into. And then we learn that these people that we fear are just like us. They are us. And I loved that about him. Instead of keeping people out, he brought them in and vice versa.
It was one of those episodes I watched on TV that had stayed with me. It was about Ethiopia with chef Marcus Samuelsson. After that episode, I immediately looked up Ethiopian restaurant in the area. Tigi's was the closest I found. I said to myself, I am going to try it out. That was more than 6 years ago. Life gets busy and you put things off. I couldn't believe that much time had passed. I saw something yesterday that reminded me-what I I said to myselfI back then. No excuses. I am not leaving this planet until I try this. And the timing was right because the wife asked me to pick up dinner. And of course I felt some trepidation about the unknown. I am willing but is she? So I did what every normal person does. I ordered Chinese as well as the Ethiopian. Always have a backup plan. I studied the menu and not knowing what to order, I order the meat combo 3 which covers a lot of their offering. The place was empty at 5pm with some carry outs. And I talked with the owner for a bit. Very friendly and personable. I looked around the market. Reminded me of the small tiny Korean grocery store you would find back in the old days. Forgive the ramblings of an old man but let's go on to the food.
Remember what I said about not being adventurous, and my wife even far less than I am. Well, the first thing I noticed was the scent in the car when I stepped in. It was not pleasant and I said oh no. I made a mistake. I drove home and that smell dissipated somewhat but I was still skeptical. When I got it in the house, there was no smell. I opened it up inside and I have to warn you, it is not for some people. The injera, which is a very very spongy textured type of bread is like nothing I have ever seen or felt before. I mean seriously, it looked exactly like the stomach lining of an animal. If you seen one, you know what I mean. So that aesthetic threw me off immediately. But damn it, I am going to give it a go. Wife was even more taken a back by the appearance. She asked what that was. I explained, as I had studied some videos before ordering. We broke the injera and used our hands as is customary and you know what? It was an incredible journey of flavor and texture. I loved the spices and everything about the meal. I am ordering everything dark next time because the darker items have the extra spices that I loved. And to my pleasant surprise, my wife loved it as much as I did. Yes, this is going in our regular rotation from now on. Keep your mind open to new people and things because you never know what you have been missing or needed.

This place in my view is an undiscovered culinary treasure. I ordered the vegan platter - and the dishes were flavorful, satisfying and fresh, not weighed down with heavy, processed ingredients. The atmosphere was relaxed and not rushed. The highlights were items I would never have imagined I'd like but did. Like the appetizer sardine salad (amazing!), which was not fishy at all but light, with a lemon and mild spice, and infused with onions, tomatoes, small-diced peppers. The highlights were the vegan dishes (some spiced with berbere spice) and then the coffee, a whole experience of its own. The chef came out and showed us the coffee roasting, then returned with a big plate of coffee and an incense burner, part of a traditional coffee ceremony. The meal ranks as one of my favorites in the area, I love this place.
Very friendly family run place authentic Ethiopian food, reasonable price

formatted_address: 416 E 30th St #118, Baltimore, MD 21218, United States
name: Disbe Good

reviews.text:
Life is good as I write this review and thoroughly enjoy my suya lamb fried rice. However I can’t deny that for a $7 side of jollof rice I was expecting a large serving than I received and maybe a little more lamb meat (or maybe I’m just a hungry college student) but this is barely stretchable 😭

It’s also my first time ordering from Disbe so maybe I’m making a rookie mistake and this is just their typical size? Someone lmk

Ordered from DoorDash
The shrimp rice noodle bowl with extra shrimp was absolutely amazing. The flavors savory, sweet, spicy. Would have enjoyed this even better if it were warm… I wish there was a dine in restaurant. (Hence)

I also not sure about some of the reviews. I feel like the amount of food I received was well worth it! I am so very full right now lol. Also you can’t take in account the dasher time this has nothing to do with the restaurant.

Pleased that I took a chance on this restaurant I did some research and really respect what the owner has accomplished. Look forward to trying the shiitake mushrooms next! 10/10

I absolutely loved my order of jollof rice, mushrooms, and quinoa! The jollof was amazing, and I forgot to take a photo. Jide was incredibly thoughtful and made sure everything was perfect for my vegan preferences. Thank you so much! I’ll definitely be ordering again!

We ordered thru Ubereats. The restaurant called to let us know an item wasn't available and gave us a suggestion on a replacement. The food was awesome and they threw in something extra. We will definitely be ordering again.

I was starving at 2:30AM & wanted something good to eat. Of course its late and options are very slim then I stumbled across this Gem on DoorDash. Man the food was soooo freakin good and fresh that it blew my mind. I dont play when it comes to food, I know good food and got dam was this food delicious. The Jollof was so flavorful and fresh, the shrimp were seasoned to perfection, the noodles were fresh and full of flavor, my plantains were so fresh they literally taste like they just got finished getting cooked in my own kitchen. Don’t hesitate to order its a 10/10. Its so good im ordering it again today.

formatted_address: 938 S Conkling St, Baltimore, MD 21224, United States
name: Union Hill Kitchen & Craft Bar

reviews.text:
I stumbled upon Union Hill Kitchen & Craft Bar while in the general area after reading positive reviews on Google. The atmosphere, food, drinks & service exceeded expectations. We enjoyed it so much that my birthday celebration dinner was held here a month later.
The dinner was held in the private room upstairs and was perfect for the occasion. The food was fresh & flavorful; the drink menu offered creatively crafted beverages that you won't find anywhere else. Everyone enjoyed the food and experience and a few people have already returned!

What we had:
Appetizers: Brussel Sprouts, Coconut Shrimp, Chicken Wings

Entree: Honey Gochujang Salmon (perfectly cooked), Pistachio Pesto Chicken (seasoned well), Jasmine Rice (so flavorful!), Grilled Asparagus, Union Salad (wonderful salad, we had to keep asking for more!)

Drinks: Smashing Basil; To Wong Foo, Thank You For Everything (with matcha, miso, wasabi and a few other things, I couldn't even imagine how this drink would taste. It was surprisingly delicious!)

I visited Union Hill with a friend before going to a show in Baltimore. We had a fantastic visit and I cannot wait to return when I have more time to sample the menu!

From the moment you step into the restaurant, you can see how much thought went into every detail. The vibe is welcoming and classy but not stuffy. The staff was knowledgeable and friendly. We even spent time chatting with the owners who are some of the nicest people you'll ever meet.

Since we didn't have much time, we only had starters. The goat cheese stuffed peppers and the short rib bites were phenomenal. The flavors and textures blended perfectly with every bite.

If you are a fan of dirty martinis, I highly recommend their version on the seasonal cocktail menu. We also had their pistachio pisco cocktail which was a perfect after dinner drink.

Can't wait to visit again soon. If I lived closer to Baltimore, this would definitely be my go-to restaurant!

Delicious is an understatement. My husband and I enjoyed a late lunch. This was our first visit. We received top notch service  from Naomi and Dreams! Plus the food was delicious. I’ll also add that it is the cutest venue. I enjoyed the steak frites cooked to perfection and my husband had the brisket sandwich. Highly recommend. We will certain visit the next time we are in town.

Experience far exceeded our expectations.

Tried 3 appetizers, all outstanding.  Churro ice cream sandwich dessert was incredible. Everything fresh and flavorful. (Watched the bartender hand- juice ~30 lemons and limes... no bottled stuff here).

Attentive, courteous service from everyone working the bar.  Draft beer, espresso martini, Cabernet...all on point.

Atmosphere is upscale yet warm and comfortable. Several diners sitting near us said this is one of their favorite places in Baltimore.

I had the best experience celebrating my birthday at Union Hill. The customer service was impeccable. From the planning via email with Matt to our arrival everything was just perfect. We utilized their beautiful private room upstairs and it was the perfect amount of space for our group of 20. They even added linens and came up with a playlist for our group! To top it off they were so accommodating and split the check by 20!! Such a seamless and wonderful brunch experience. Also how could I forget the food was delicious!!

formatted_address: 2839 Smith Ave Suite M, Baltimore, MD 21209, United States
name: Serengeti Steakhouse Baltimore

reviews.text:
Short review: an average, overpriced steakhouse

Long Review:
Location - weird. In like a strip mall. Doesn't feel like a location for a fancy, high end restaurant.
Aesthetic - nothing felt African at all about this place. Not in the food, not in the chefs, not in the clientele.
Hostess - disorganized on what I would call an average night. Had to repeat my name 3 times. Not a welcoming experience.
Service - just average, nothing special
Alcohol - not a full bar, don't expect them to be able to make every drink.
Steak - cooked to temperature perfectly but just average taste. Shocked that their steaks don't come with a side at those prices.
