Dessert - creme brulee was good but more vanilla pudding-y
Other - restaurant was freezing. Bathrooms were just as cold as outside.

Ruth's Chris is somehow a cheaper experience and 10x better.
It's on the expensive side, but the portions are generous. If you're looking for a nice night out to treat yourself, you will love this place.

Never had heard of or been to a kosher restaurant before. It didn't disappoint!

It is pricey however well worth the monster high quality steaks you receive. You have to try the brisket fries, they are to die for(pic attached). As far as desserts, go with the skillet brownie. Only knocked for service as our waitress disappeared a few times.

Small spot so definitely make a reservation. Get out there and check out their kosher options!

I've come here at least 5/6 times and called numerous times, Asking when will they have the French onion soup. It was the very first soup I had there and been craving ever since(2023) . Unfortunately the staff don't care to ask or know if they do, so I stopped calling and asking. I've always been generous while eating there but leaving a review means I've hit a boiling point leaving me unsatisfied. Today I drove up there and minutes from opening with a simple question in mind. I was shooed away. Unpleasant experience

The food was delicious! Our server was very sweet.BUT we had to wait the better part of an hour for our food! Also,at the time we ordered,we also ordered a sandwich to go so it would be ready when we got our check.Not only was it not ready,we had to wait  over half an hour for it! Both waits were waaaay too long and not acceptable.

formatted_address: 2219 Maryland Ave, Baltimore, MD 21218, United States
name: Yeiboh Kitchen "Yebo"

reviews.text:
I recently visited Yeibo Kitchen, and it was an amazing experience from start to finish! The ambience is really inviting—bright, cozy, and with a modern yet warm feel. It sets the perfect mood for a relaxed dining experience.

As for the food, it definitely didn’t disappoint. Everything we tried was packed with flavor and super fresh. The portions were generous, so you definitely get your money’s worth! We couldn’t finish everything, but it was all so good that we kept going back for more bites.

The staff were friendly, and the service was quick and attentive. Overall, I’m really glad we came here, and we’ll definitely be back soon!

My children took me to YeibohKitchen for birthday brunch, and I was not disappointed. The place is small in the inside, however the ambiance was beautiful, the music created a perfect atmosphere, and our hostess was exceptional. I enjoyed the fried strawberry shortcake biscuits along with my children who kept begging for a taste, fried lobster with egg and cheese on a croissant, and potatoes. When salt and pepper are not present on table, it is a clear indication that the food is undoubtedly delicious. OMG, that banana pudding was one of the best I had ever tasted, and it was prepared different from the usual. Also, the portions are generous( I started eating before we took pictures) and the prices are reasonable. A visit to YeibohKitchen is a must.

Went here on a Friday night w/o a reservation…BIG mistake it was packed for an hour wait! Came the next night upon opening and there were already multiple people sitting down so I’d highly recommend reservations! I got the shrimp&grits and it was good but not the best grits I’ve ever had, and the andouille was really good and extra spicy! The ambience is great, amazing playlist, great cocktails and mocktails too.

Absolutely 💯 one of the best breakfast sandwiches I've EVER TASTED! The price is what it is for seafood but the gravy wasn't overwhelming, the tail was expertly cooked, the croissant wasn't burned & toasted to perfection. After eating we didn't feel bloated or stuffed. The Omelette was very flavorful, nicely seasoned, we asked for the gravy on the side which was delicious (we ended up pouring all over the Omelette lol)& the cook came & asked if we truly enjoyed everything! Lord willing, we will be back lol.

EXPERIENCE: This was a great dining experience! The restaurant is stunning from the outside. An all black building, in the middle of a city block, separated from the sidewalk by an outdoor patio seating area.  Walking inside, we were greeted by a lovely, smiling, pleasant hostess who promptly seated us. The decor is intimate; simple, yet beautiful...black, navy, cream, and the lighting where we were sitting seamed golden (to me) perfect date night or friends night out. We didn't wait long before Ty (our server) greeted us and took our drink orders. Hubby ordered a Strong Island (not a menu item-that's just how he asks for them). I ordered the Maple Old Fashioned. Both drinks were delicious and made to satisfaction- I complained to Ty about the amount of the pour on the Old Fashioned but he told me to "taste it first". Man!...he was right. Ty took care of us- if you sit in his section, TIP HIM!!!
FOOD: We started with appetizers: brussels sprouts and crab egg rolls. Hubby is not a fan of brussels sprouts, but he ATE these...roasted, (without being dried out) served on a delicious sauce that was sweet, with a little bit of heat. The egg rolls were actually FILLED with crab meat, served on a delicious creamy sauce that didn't keep you from being able to taste the crabmeat. That sauce was tasty, but we dipped those egg rolls in that brussels sprouts sauce (see photo-sorry for showing remnants).
I ordered the shrimp and grits and Hubby got the burger with the shrimp on it (sorry-I forgot the name). The chef brought our food to the table and we thanked him and gave him "his flowers". The food he put on the table, allowed us to eat with our eyes first (see photos). I'm not a person who photographs food when we go out, but I did this time. Not only did it look good. It was a pleasure for all of my senses. The food came to the table nice and hot-the grits were creamy and cheesy, without being greasy, and the shrimp and sausage were well seasoned, but not overly so. Hubby's burger was flavorful...not just beef and shrimp on a bun.  The bun was soft and warm; the sauce was delicious and the burger was cooked perfectly. Shrimp was never something I expected to encounter on a burger, but what a yummy surprise! The potato wedges were nice and crispy on the outside, hot and tender on the inside and just plain delicious. My husband is the type that likes to season already seasoned food at restaurants...he did not mention wanting to add anything at any point while we were seated. Thanks again, Chef. May God continue to bless the work of your hands.
VISIT TIPS: 1. UBER/LYFT to avoid circling the block. The street the restaurant sits on is one with paid on street parking and includes a bike lane. 2.Try not to wait too late in the evening to go. The restaurant does not take reservations. I think we were lucky because we went on a weeknight. If you are a person who gets chilly easily, bring a wrap/jacket. 3.The tables are small so, unless you have a purse hook, ladies leave your big bag at home. 4. Extra tall fellas, be advised, the chairs sit a little low so maybe consider sitting at the bar. My husband is 6'4", when I asked him about it, he said he was only mildly uncomfortable, though he didn't complain during dinner-so it must have been worth it.  There is another area in the back of the restaurant - beyond where we were seated, perhaps the seating is different there?

Hubby and I agree. This is a place we will d see DEFINITELY return to.

formatted_address: 9810 Liberty Rd, Randallstown, MD 21133, United States
name: Mrs M's International Restaurant and Catering

reviews.text: Nasty. They just slopped it together and threw some meat in there. Watery and nasty. Ewww
The food was delicious but it's very small portions
Was given almost raw chicken n their jollof is trash
Unorganized and terrible service.

formatted_address: 840 N Eutaw St, Baltimore, MD 21201, United States
name: The Land of Kush

reviews.text:
Yesterday was day 25 of not eating meat. Really couldn't find anything healthy to eat outside. Remembered years ago going to the Land of Kush. The food was just as good as it was back then.The whole place was a  great vibe.My fiance & I was welcomed like family & greated also with fast service. The ribs gets me everytime alon with my favorite (Kale Salad). We even liked the smiles from the cashier & the preparer. Oh & don't let me talk about the potato salad (chef's kiss).We were Blessed to meet yet again one of the owners  Ms.Naijha  Brown. She treated us with much Love ❤️ She was such a warm soul
We just appreciated the whole experience. This is the place to eat clean
Been coming to Land of Kush for many years. It's the best vegan soul food. Everything is always fresh and delicious. Their one entree w/ two sides option is always a favorite.

Fantastic experience! Dunno what they put in those “crab cakes,” but they taste and feel like the real thing!! The collard greens and candied yams were on point too. And the sauces? Both the tartar sauce and mustard dip were so good I wanted them in a cup so I could just chug it. Highly recommend!

Their serve is amazing. Their willingness to serve in excellence is beyond my expectations. They went over and beyond with my service and blessed me at the end. I definitely will go back when I come back to visit . Every was good! The crab cake wrap. greens, cabbage, kale salad, bbq, tomatoes and cucumber. This feed me for 2 days.
In regards to the Mac, chief, I suggest a little more of your homemade cheese would elevate the taste, I would've like to taste more of your homemade flavor. I look forward to it in the future!

I love to make vegan macaroni and cheese.. I've been working on my recipe for a couple of years now. This macaroni and cheese is good don't get me wrong, but it's not the prettiest to look at. Sweet lady behind the counter gave me some curried gravy to put on it. Sounded strange but it really enhanced the flavor of the macaroni. I would definitely go back again for it.  I got the greens they were pretty good. The potato salad... meh.

formatted_address: 806 N Charles St, Baltimore, MD 21201, United States
name: The Helmand

reviews.text:
9/17/2025
My first afghan restaurant and on a nice rainy day. I ended up here with help of the timeleft app, was seated as soon as I walked in the door. I started with the AUSHAK and a glass of white wine. Both were great I love how tender the pasta is, the yogurt mixed with the cilantro sauce( they give for the table) by far is the best combo. The naan was thick and such a good touch to soak up all the pasta sauce. Ended up the meal with the afghan style  ice cream which had a taste that I was not used to. I loved the fresh fruits and the cardamom in the ice cream had my tastebuds singing. The seating has 2 areas and a nice little bar in the back.  I noticed a new customers coming in and requesting single seating which was not a problem for this spot. Our server was very punctual clearing plates, getting refills I just would have loved to hear about the new items and drinks that were on the table before I ordered.
Bathroom rating:5/5

Delicious and unique. Stopped by for a solo dinner, very friendly and professional staff, large space, good wine and cocktail selection and so many food options! Haven't had Afghani food before and this was a treat. Ordered the salmon specialty and some bread. Highly recommend and would come back on a future trip.

⭐️⭐️⭐️ 3.3/5 stars

We visited The Helmand on a Thursday night and were surprised to find it almost completely empty. Just two other diners were in the entire restaurant, which gave it a strange, somewhat lifeless vibe for a place that gets so much hype online.

The decor feels a bit outdated, and honestly, they could probably use some marketing help to get more people through the door. It really didn’t feel like a spot that’s supposed to be one of Baltimore’s most famous Afghan restaurants.

That said, the service was excellent. The servers were super attentive, always checking on us and refilling our water without us having to ask. They were polite and knowledgeable about the menu.

The food itself was… fine. A lot of the menu revolves around lamb, which was cooked well enough but didn’t blow us away. Flavors were decent, but nothing stood out as particularly memorable. It’s the sort of meal where you finish full and satisfied but not raving about it afterward.

We didn’t try any of the wine or coffee, so can’t comment on those, but the prices were fair for the amount of food we got.

Overall, it was a solid experience, but I’m just not sure it deserves the level of hype it gets online. Tasty, but not amazing. If you’re curious about Afghan food or just want something different, it’s worth trying at least once, but don’t go in expecting to be completely wowed.

I was first a little skeptical of visiting because I had previously DoorDash'd food from The Helmand and wasn't super enthused. However, they really delivered when it comes to in-house meals. I visited with a party of over 10 and they were able to accomodate us and serve us quickly. They have lots of fantastic vegetarian options revolving around rice, lentils, and curries. Everything we had was colorful and flavorful. Would definitely love to visit again.

This restaurant has gone downhill since the original owner died, which is a shame because this place was such a historic and iconic staple for the DMV Afghan diaspora. I’ve been to this restaurant in the past and always had an incredible experience. Now, the food is not authentic, the portions for some dishes are ridiculously small, and the atmosphere feels cheapened (they had paper tablecloths on the tables).

The mantu appetizer only came with just a single piece of mantu. I’ve never seen that before in any Afghan restaurant I’ve been to. Most restaurants give at least 3-4 pieces. Also, the mantu was served on a plate of dal (lentils). That’s not how authentic mantu is made in Afghan culture at all.

The chicken was very good, but the rice and dips really tasted like a terrible mockery/knock off of South Asian cuisine rather than authentic Afghan cuisine, which is supposed to taste more like a blend of West and Central Asian food usually.

The firnee did not taste authentic at all. The pudding had no flavor and it was missing crushed pistachios—which is one of the most key ingredients for firnee. However, the falooda ice cream did taste good.

Overall, this place isn’t terrible, but it’s not authentic, and you’d be much better off by going to DC or northern Virginia for Afghan food instead. This place just isn’t it anymore.

formatted_address: 211 N Frederick Ave # B, Gaithersburg, MD 20877, United States
name: Gulele Ethiopian Restaurant & Market

reviews.text: I visited here with family and we loved it! They were super friendly and accommodating, and the food was very tasty. We tried the vegetarian plates, the fish goulash and the chicken doro wot, and they were all great. I wish I lived close by so I could come more often.

I personally love Ethiopian food and the Gulele Ethiopian Restaurant didn’t disappoint one bit! The food was so good and it was a little spicy, which is my preference! Even the woman that took my order and checked me out, she was so kind! I’ll definitely be back!

I’ve had mixed experiences here. The female owner is always kind, welcoming, and very pleasant to deal with. Unfortunately, the male owner often comes across as disrespectful. He is usually on the phone or laptop instead of paying attention to customers. I honestly can’t stand it. We come here to buy with our money, not to beg for free. Every time I visit, I feel this way. It’s disappointing, because the lady is wonderful and represents the business very well, but his behavior really takes away from the experience.

The restaurant has a small cozy section for dining, but it doesn't disappoint with the quality of the food.  All the food items were delicious and we enjoyed our food immensely.  It is one of the best Ethiopian restaurants and I definitely recommend this place for good food.

I'm pregnant and I was craving Ethiopian food. I was in the area of Gulele, so I ordered the vegetarian combo to go. The staff was incredibly kind and the food turned out delicious. I got three days worth of lunches out of one vegetarian combo. The sambusas were also very tasty. I live over an hour away, but next time I'm in the area I'll definitely be stopping by. Thank you, Gulele!

formatted_address: The Charm'tastic Mile, 719 S President St, Baltimore, MD 21202, United States
name: Lebanese Taverna

reviews.text: We had such a great experience here that we came back a second time during our visit in Baltimore. The humus was exceptional as was the falafel, kebabs, and stuffed grape leaves. The puffed bread and tzatziki brought it all together.  The service was exceptional and attentive and the setting was fun. We had so much food that we took home leftovers and ate them cold the next day. How could they even be better cold the next day?!? But they were 💕

Enjoyed our visit today to Lebanese Taverna! Yummy salads. Hummus and bread is EXCELLENT...The white Sangria with chopped peaches was dddeeeeeeeelicous! Bread pudding was not great, but everything else made up for it. Wonderful service and fun, hip location by the Harbor.

The stuff is amazing and the food is great. Mehdi was very polite and helpful to make sure we understood the menus and the food we were ordering. We recommend this Mediterranean/ Middle Eastern restaurant to anyone who want quality food and time spent in Baltimore.

Lebanese Taverna offers a wonderful dining experience with some standout dishes. The fresh, warm pita bread was absolutely fantastic, and the appetizers set the tone nicely, especially the cheese rolls, falafel, and kafta rolls, all flavorful and satisfying. The tabbouleh was bright and refreshing, and with just a squeeze of lemon and a touch of salt, it became even more delicious.

A couple of items fell short: the eggplant fateh didn’t quite meet expectations, and the chicken kabob (taouq) lacked the depth of flavor we were hoping for. That said, the overall experience was still very good, and the highlights, particularly the pita and appetizers, made it worthwhile. This is a spot we’d happily return to for its vibrant flavors and welcoming atmosphere.

The best middle eastern food my husband and I had. So fresh and burst of different tastes! We absolutely loved it and service is top notch! If you are in harbor east in Baltimore it should be a must stop!

formatted_address: 1626 Aliceanna St, Baltimore, MD 21231, United States
name: Liquid Earth

reviews.text: I wish I could give ten stars, this place is amazing. The wings and homemade vegan ranch were out of this world; the Philly cheese fake and pumpkin muffin were also incredible. I also had the chamomile pineapple Iced tea, which was amazing. They also have an amazing selection of organic teas. The waiter was super friendly and knowledgeable. I will definitely come back here next time I'm in Baltimore.

This was my first time visiting this restaurant, and it definitely won’t be my last! The food was amazing, and the drinks and smoothie were delicious 😋. We ordered the buffalo wings, guacamole with chips, a sandwich (can’t remember the name), the peanut butter berries smoothie, and the Phat Beet juice. Let me tell you we were not disappointed!

Each item had its own flavor, and you could taste the freshness in every bite. The prices were affordable and reasonable, the staff was friendly and professional, and the chef was clearly on point with his cooking. I don’t live in the area, but every time I’m in town, I’ll be making sure to stop here for a good Liquid Earth meal!

10/10 STRONGLY RECOMMEND.

I was in Baltimore and wanted to support a vegan establishment, so I decided to try Liquid Earth based on the great reviews and proximity to my hotel. Although it's on a busier street, the surrounding neighborhood has tree lined streets (some cobbled) with historic rowhouses. I enjoyed my walk exploring the area.

It was a hot day, and I arrived hungry! I started with a cup of the gazpacho. It arrived with a wheel of lime to squeeze on top and some crisp baguette toasts.  The gazpacho was so flavorful,  cooling, and refreshing. I could feel my vitality being restored as I finished it off.

For the main course, I ordered the Sacred Salad and asked to add a scoop of the tofu salad. This was a power move! The salad was a feast for the eyes as well as the palate- a work of art! The tofu salad featured pleasingly firm chunks of tofu in a creamy base and it was perfect for scooping up with all the fresh veggies and greens. I finished things off with one of the 2oz juice shots, 'the uninflamed,' made with ginger, pineapple, and turmeric. Delicious!

If you're in the Baltimore area, and even if you're not vegan, check out Liquid Earth. The atmosphere is welcoming and homey, service is great, the playlist is on point, and the food here is something special!

A friend and I came here for the first time today. I was so excited to have a vegan lunch but can’t tell you how disappointed I was with what I ordered.

Food is supposed to delight the senses. Please see the photo. Nothing about this makes me want to eat it. On top of that, I’m not sure that your kitchen understands what a burrito is. The onions and peppers in a mash of black beans? No sauce? A toasted tortilla? Not a burrito.

I sent it back as inedible and had the pleasure of paying for the experience. No not ok.

I won’t be back.

The food here is top tier — fresh, flavorful, and thoughtfully prepared every time. It’s hands down one of my favorite spots to enjoy delicious vegan and vegetarian meals. Highly recommend if you’re looking for plant-based dishes that actually hit the spot! ❤️

formatted_address: 102 Clay St, Baltimore, MD 21201, United States
name: Puerto 511 Cocina Peruana

reviews.text: Hidden gem near the city center. Flavorful food of high quality which is beautifully presented. Puerto 511 only offers a prix fixe menu of either 5 or 6 dishes (depending on the day). Plan for a 2 hour dining experience as service is on the slower side but the food is well worth the wait!

Incredible, unassuming Peruvian restaurant in Baltimore! We did the weeknight tasting menu and loved all 5 courses, particularly the ceviche and anticucho. Highly recommend bringing your own pisco like we did as they’ll make you pisco sours. Will definitely be back!
Amazing restaurant hands down the best $60 meal I have ever had! You will have to ring the buzzer to get in. Every part of the 5 course tasting menu was delicious!

Excellent and authentic Peruvian food - you'll leave with revelations about potatoes.  I've been trying to recreate his leche de tigre at home for years. Still haven't succeeded.

It's an ever shifting pre-fix menu, so you'll always have the thrill of novelty combined with the certainty of success.

The interior is, unfortunately, painted millennial gray, but it's got lots of cheerful art and they've fixed the lighting, so it's still pretty pleasant to sit it. They don't refresh your cutlery between courses.

Chef Jose Victorio Alarcon is immensely talented and very personable. He trains people well, so even when he's not in the kitchen, you'll get food at his quality. He also operates the much more casual EMPA511 in  Fells Point, which is an great place for a very efficient and delicious lunch.

A very cute place with sincere food and I greatly enjoyed my visit :) It's hidden in the corner street and you'll have to find the white door and ring to get in. Great tasting menu with a reasonable price. Every dish was well thought-out and full of details. The dishes were generally on the sour side, which I greatly enjoy, but if you don't like sourness it might be too much. We also ordered chicha morada and I really liked it. The service was attentive while not disruptive. I also liked the interior decorations!

formatted_address: 8305 Georgia Ave, Silver Spring, MD 20910, United States
name: Langano Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text: Years ago this place was good! Now they have become a SCAM!!! On several occasions, I had ordered pick up on uber and they didn’t have what I ordered. When I go to pick up they tell me they don’t have what I ordered. “Sorry can we give you something else” but I don’t want something else!!! So I ended up losing the money I paid for!!! Please don’t go here they are scamming people!!! Embarrassment for the Ethiopian community!!!!

Great experience. I loved the way they served the beef tibs. They were served on a small fancy stove to keep it warm throughout the dinner.

Spacious enough for a big party or just for a duo. Family friendly. You can choose to sit outside if you prefer.

Parking could be hard to find on the Georgia Ave. Ride-share or use public transport if you can.

Sometimes I feel the owner of this restaurant and bar. A regular bar restaurant in the middle of Maryland purple line construction trying to hold in business over 30 years.  George avenue Silver Springs is the mecca of Africa hangout.

Friendly staff and great food. The Ethiopian coffee was excellent. I didn't take a picture of the coffee service but it's definitely a must have. The coffee arrives in an attractive pot with two cups and burning incense. The effect is visual as well as olfactory. The waitress poured what seemed to be a lot of sugar in the cup prior to pouring in the coffee but it was perfect. The coffee was strong but very flavorful. Whatever is done to roast the beans and prep the coffee resulted in me pouring multiple cups!

A waitress named SISAY has such a bad temper,I spend a lot in that restaurant ordering on uber eats almost 3-5 times a week,she had such a bad attitude eventoogh I love the food,I can't stand this woman,she purposely makes me wait ,all because I wasn't able to tip her for a beer I ordered while waiting on my food,she tends to ignore me while making me wait for the food,I'm done ordering from here, just because of her,the owner can look up how much I spend on this restaurant,thanks for the food,but you need to train your employees to have proper manners, Uber eats users are customers too even if they can't tip

formatted_address: 1622 Eastern Ave, Baltimore, MD 21231, United States
name: Ekiben

reviews.text:
The Neighborhood Bird Bowl was fantastic and way more than I could eat in a single meal. I got the spicy variant and was not disappointed. The pickled vegetables on the side go very well with the Taiwanese curry fried chicken.

As I believe has been mentioned in other reviews, there is not a lot of seating space. Just a few bar stools. I was lucky and happened to hit it right in-between busy periods, so I didn't have a problem finding a sera but something to be aware of.

My wife and I went to Ekiben after being at a nearby brewery. This was our first time to one of their locations and it did not disappoint at all. We both got the spicy neighborhood bird bun and it was the greatest spicy chicken sandwich we have ever had. The chicken was flavorful and and crispy, the bun was soft and pillowy, and the sauce had the perfect amount of heat without drowning out the flavor of the sauce.
I would recommend this place every single time and we will be going back very soon.

The food was delicious! 😍 The best Brokkoli I have ever eaten!
I heard it once and always remembered
Ekiban is the food of Baltimore 🙌🏽
The food was truly a treat, even though we had to wait for 20 min, the music was great and I cannot wait to eat there again ✨

This place was over-hyped all over TikTok and Instagram, so I had high expectations—but it was disappointing. The chicken was raw, and when I pointed it out to the server, he simply over-fried it instead of properly remaking it, which ruined the texture and taste.

On the positive side, the vegetables and rice were fresh, and the sides were decent. However, that doesn’t make up for poor food handling and service.

Would I go back? No. The hype doesn’t match the quality, and raw chicken is a deal-breaker.

Health: While fried food doesn’t lend itself to the most healthy diet, the blend of white rice, kimchi, and legitimate Asian/American fusion veggies tossed in soy sauce and not grilled in oil balances it out.

Price: For this taste and portion size? Excellent. Though not particularly “low”. Definitely satisfying though.

Experience: The most “alive” and “trendy” food scene in Baltimore. Small restaurant, big heart. I got my second meal there for free due to being a government medical researcher during furlough. But regardless, clean, convenient, and speedy. Great on all accounts.

Taste: A genuinely unique Asian/American fusion. Where other locations will rehash food drowned in oil, this place takes the best American and East Asian food elements and balances them excellently. Asian sauces over fried chicken. White rice with kimchi. Large protein and veggie portions with rice accompaniment (that’s the actual way real Asian food is served by the way). Honestly unique and Amazing.

Yeah I’m coming back here again. And I already have. So is everyone else in town. A core port of Baltimore’s food scene. A cornerstone of Asian/American fusion in general. Food and culture wise.

formatted_address: 3314 Eastern Ave, Baltimore, MD 21224, United States
name: Queen of Sheba مطعم الملكه سبأ

reviews.text: Queen of Sheba in Baltimore offers a welcoming atmosphere with its cozy and authentic Ethiopian decor. However, my experience with the chicken entrée was disappointing; it was over-grilled, resulting in a dry and lackluster dish. This overshadowed what could have been a flavorful meal. The restaurant itself is pleasant, with a friendly staff and a comfortable setting. Despite the inviting ambiance, the quality of the chicken left much to be desired. While other menu items might fare better, my particular dish did not meet expectations. Overall, Queen of Sheba has a lot of potential, but the execution of the chicken entrée fell short.

My Son and I had a wonderful time at Queen of Sheba, a Middle Eastern Yemeni restaurant in Baltimore. The food was delicious and authentic, with a variety of dishes to choose from. We especially enjoyed the lamb haneeth, the chicken gallabah, and the salad . The service was friendly and attentive, and the atmosphere was cozy and inviting. We also loved the complimentary hot tea that came with our meal. It was a great experience and we would definitely recommend this place to anyone who loves Middle Eastern cuisine. Thank you, Queen of Sheba, for a memorable night!

Hands down one of the best middle eastern food I’ve ever tried. Love food, and especially middle eastern food. It was sooo yummy and the mango smoothie?? Heavenly delicious I recommend don’t wait another second. We got some some lamb and chicken hanneeth some hummus and pita bread. Our dishes comes with salad or soup but we both got salads. We’ve had so many things we had to get to go boxes lol

I came to have Iftar Ramadan. As soon as I entered, they asked have you had eaten Iftar? And I haven’t eaten yet. They immediately brought the Iftar with less than 5 minutes. The food remained me of Home. It was super fresh and yummy. The servers were super friendly and welcoming. I highly recommend and I would definitely comeback again.

It was delicious, and great experience at this restaurant we have amazing dinner and the food was fantastic, and it’s felt like you are finally eating middle eastern delicious Yemeni food, they do all kinds of party’s weddings, engagement bookings great prices and wonderful Five-stars service, most definitely recommended

formatted_address: 9810 Liberty Rd, Randallstown, MD 21133, United States
name: nuellakitchen

reviews.text: Food was was good (but very spicy for me). Two main dish options . Nuella was very nice and helpful!
The best place to solve hunger, a neat environment, good customer  care . Tast like home food. To crown it all,I came all d way from Atlanta Georgia...... No regrets eating here.

Leaving love for you Ella❤️
Thanks for being our friends and making us amazing foods💗

The best Amala Spot in DMV no cap!
I emptied my plate because I enjoyed my meal and I’ll always come 😊

Wa gba! Amala, delicious 😋. The wooden plates, unique and special. The meats...eye candy delicious 😋 and filling. To enjoy your money, make your stomach happy. Visit Nuellla for an awesome authentic Naija flavored experience

formatted_address: 117 W 24th St, Baltimore, MD 21218, United States
name: Paradise Island Cuisine

reviews.text: Had food from this establishment at the 32nd St Farmer's Market. I ordered the mango shrimp on top of rice & red cabbage with plantains & kale. I've never tasted rice like this. It had a lighter texture & orange-reddish color. The red cabbage was sliced in big pieces but was cooked perfectly-not mushy but also not tough. The kale was not what I expected but surprisingly very good. It had a light crunch to it and paired well with the other foods. The plantains were soft but a bit crispy on the edges, just how I like them. Last but not least,  the shrimp were perfect.  Nice size & flavorful.  I really wanted to go here for lunch a few days later, but the street location looked confusing. I thought it was an actual restaurant, but the address is a former school. I called 3 times & the line was busy. The 4th time I called the phone just rang. Next,  I called & someone picked up after a couple of rings and hung up on me. That's how they lost me as a customer.

So glad you were at the Waldorf Fair! I had the bbq chicken with rice and sweet bourbon sauce and OMG it made my entire day. So yummy!! Perfect amount of spice. Insane flavor. Will be buying again for sure

Absolutely amazing Caribbean cuisine!! Something special about that crispy kale they definitely got it figured out all of the food was flavored individually! The staff was so warm and welcoming! Positive and pleasant attitudes. You must try this place!

My first time at this place( TRY ANYTHING ONCES). They comes to my job at the farmers market. I got the oxtail bowl and pineapple ginger drink no ice for lunch. Got back to my office open up the container And OMG 😲 they ONLY GIVE ME 3 TINY PIECES OF OXTAIL ( AS SHE SAID BONELESS) YOU CAN ONLY PUT PHOTOS ON HERE I WISH THAT YOU PUT A VIDEO SO THAT EVERYONE COULD SEE WHEN I PICKED THROUGH IT TO TRY AND FIND THE OXTAILS.. 😠 😡 OH BUT THEY PUT SOOOOO MANY ONIONS THAT YOU CAN'T TELL. SO I GIVE A ONE BECAUSE YOU HAVE TO PICK A STAR..THEY REALLY SHOULD GET 0 STARS.  OH AND I PAID 29.00 FOR THOSE ONIONS AND RICE MEAL.. NEVER AGAIN.

Found this good food at the UMMS Tuesday farmers market, and let me tell you, it was all delicious 😋. So glad you have a spot now..
See ya soon!

formatted_address: 519 W Pratt St SUITE B, Baltimore, MD 21201, United States
name: Pitamore Baltimore restaurant and Catering

reviews.text:
I ordered online close to closing time, which I normally don’t do. I’ve eaten at this restaurant before and usually enjoy the food, but this experience missed the mark.
The chicken shawarma was extremely hard to chew and looked like it may have been leftover meat. The chicken pita (I forgot to take a photo before discarding it) was very dry, and my sister couldn’t finish hers.
Customer service was fine. This was strictly a food quality issue. Based on past visits, I know the food can be tasty, so next time I’ll plan to go much earlier in the day to see if timing makes a difference.
Fast service! Can’t beat the fried eggplant! And the schwarma and falafel are excellent. Inside is a bit loud and worn.
Really tasty, friendly, under-stated neighborhood Middle-Eastern restaurant. Quality ingredients and great prices too.

Piatmore offers the best falafel and fries in Baltimore right now.  I always get the spicy falafel (which isn't spicy, but is flavorful).  The fries are cut thick and are never greasy.  Both the bowl and the sandwich are amazing.  I recommend choosing based on hunger level.  The bowl offers much more food.  There are tons of vegan and gluten free options.  There are meat options as well.   The bread is fresh.  The owner/manager -I assume he's a boss bc he's always there 😀 - is very friendly. He comes out to help the staff when they get crowded.  I love when everyone's working hard to get customers in and out!

I wish the meat was kosher/zabiha...so that if I ever want to cheat on my falafel with a shwarma, I can.

They also offer a rewards card, so you can get a free drink or dessert after several visits.

The baklava is sub par and the plastic utensils don't appear to be compostable. That being said,  I can compost all the paper surrounding the sandwich and fries-WELL DONE!

Decided to stop by this place bc it was close to the hospital (about 3 blocks away) and I wanted something different. I was able to order through Ubereats and pick up. I got the beef/lamb shawarma and fries. This was quite possibly the BEST sandwich I have ever had and I've had shawarmas before. The bread tasted fresh and was very soft. The meat and vegetables were juicy enough that I did not need any extra sauces. It was juicy enough but I had no problem with it dripping or being messy. As I think about it, I am suspicious that this was no shawarma to begin with...the shape of the bread, chickpea spread inside of it and the type of fresh veggies included makes me think that this is actually a Jewish SABICH sandwich?!? Anyway, it was delicious!! I do plan on going back!!..Oh serving size was also nice. Don't plan on sharing though. That sandwich is just enough for one person, couldn't finish my fries.

formatted_address: 30 Light St, Baltimore, MD 21202, United States
name: Pitamore restaurant and catering

reviews.text:
While it can be a little bit of a challenge to find parking, it's well worth it!

They have several choices in breads and wraps and pitas, as well as several meat and even vegetarian fillings with lots of interesting combinations of sauces and toppings.

Pitamore Restaurant and Catering was really good. Cozy, casual vibe with a friendly, welcoming atmosphere. The Mediterranean dishes were fresh, flavorful, and satisfying — everything tasted homemade. Service was attentive and warm. Great spot for a relaxed meal or catering a gathering with quality food.

In town for a conference and decided to give this restaurant a try after reading the excellent reviews. Great authentic Mediterranean food! I tried the lamb shawarma and was not disappointed. The lamb was flavorful, juicy and cooked to perfection. My choice of sides were hummus (Chickpea puree with tahini, garlic and spices), Mediterranean Salad (Tomato, Cucumber salad with red onion sumac and lemon; Mediterranean rice, Cabbage Salad (Green cabbage with carrots and vinegar), Fried Eggplant and Tzatziki Sauce (Yogurt sauce mixed with dill, mint and cucumber).  The “plate” portion is huge and comes with a warm fluffy pita bread. The restaurant staff were courtesy, friendly and efficient.

I have a deep love for the halal cart outside the court house when I’m on jury duty but…I think Pitamore may have them beat! It’s a few bucks more but there is so much customization and so many options. Plus the pitas are excellent! All this on top of having an efficient system in place that works even during the lunch rush. I loved this place and I’ll be back!

Came here because of a friend's recommendation, and it didn't disappoint. Absolutely great shawarma! The beef pita shawarma was on point. All of my fellow diners loved their dishes. The plate portions are robust and the topping selections are numerous. Will definitely eat here again.

formatted_address: 5621 Belle Grove Rd, Baltimore, MD 21225, United States
name: Miss Erica's Kitchen LLC

reviews.text:
I ordered the steak, egg, and cheese sandwich with homemade fries. The sandwich was good, but the home fries truly stood out, they reminded me of my great grandmother’s cooking. Absolutely delicious and one of a kind. The owner was lovely, and I really appreciated her warm, giving spirit. Highly recommend.

I ate the home fries so darn fast couldn't take a picture.
My first visit there and WOW!  Had no idea the food would be that delicious like Momma used to make.  I told 20 people and I'm going back!  I got  the Pot Roast, Collards and Mac and Cheese.

reviews.author_name: J A Z Z L E E
reviews.text: When I ordered I spent 100$ worth of food on 4/5/25 because I wanted to support a local black business. But was not happy. The quality of the food was not worth that price. I got the lamb dinner, the fish and beef sub, chicken and waffles, & party wings. The lamb dinner & wings was ok. my favorite was the fish sub, it was absolutely delicious 😋. However on the beef sub, she called me asking what I wanted on it. Which I requested lettuce, tomato, onions and mayo…and she put none of that on it 😑….It was sent with beef and cheese. the fries were burnt in all 3 dinners & the fish nuggets. It had a greasy old oil taste to it. And the fish nugget’s was burnt on the outside, undercooked & pink on the inside. It was mushy upon first bite and I spit it out. I placed my order on DD which I reported with them as well, in which they gave me a 15$ refund. The mushiness of the fish mess my head up, my tummy started turning & my whole appetite was ruined. if I could redo this order I would only ordered the fish sub & get collard greens instead of fries.

Not consistent. Today the home fries tasted very old and like they were warmed up. Not seasoned. Eggs weren’t seasoned either. Scrapple was burnt. I would not recommend this place and I’ve eaten here plenty of times and it’s gone downhill.

I ordered from this establishment today through ubereats. The service was phenomenal and the food was awesome. Even when something went wrong with my order they took it upon themselves to make it right. My husband tore those pork chops up and he is hard to please with outside food. Amazing.

If I had one suggestion it would be a little less vinegar in the vegetables (greens and green beans) but that's just my preference. I will definitely be ordering again. Keep up the amazing work.

formatted_address: 1332 Sulphur Spring Rd, Arbutus, MD 21227, United States
name: Our Recipes Cafe

reviews.text: I had the best experience here today. Everything on the menu sounded amazing! I had a hard time choosing, but I ordered the brunchwich.  It was delicious. The service was great too, and I love the vibes. I’m already planning to return and make my way through the whole menu. 🤗🤗🤗

Came here on a whim one day & we weren’t  disappointed. The food was fresh, love the honey drizzle they put on the homes fries when you get the waffles & crab cake. The chicken sandwich was fresh along w/ the fries. Went back a second time & wasn’t disappointed. Got a vegetarian omelet, it was a tad bit too much cheese for me, but it didn’t take away from the meal. My husband got the crunch French toast & he fell in love. The portions are perfect & the atmosphere gives very welcoming a nice daytime date spot, a lot of the seafood dishes that call for crab cakes are charged as market price, but the menu items outside of that are very reasonable. We will definitely be returning

It is a quaint little eatery. Very chill vibes. If you are looking for a relaxed Saturday brunch with a good friend, this is the place. The food is mediocre but the atmosphere makes up for it. I do believe it is black-owned

My experience eating at Tima African Restaurant was horrible today. I reviewed the menu with the young lady who was taking orders & cashiering. After realizing there were not many options for vegetarians the lady quickly spoke & assured me that they could cook one of the meals for me without any meat inside. She said this to me more than once and proceeded to suggest a few options. I decided on the saga saga potatoes leaves over rice. I wanted joloaf rice but she told me all they had was white rice. When I got back to work and opened the food, I could smell the meat inside. The smell was strong and the food was extremely greasy and oosing with fat juice from the meat that had been cooking inside. There were also peices of animal bone in my potato leaves dish. You can see a very large bone in the photo I shared. I called the restaurant and the young lady who originally helped me told me that they did not cook any meat inside my potato leaves dish. I told her it would make me sick if I ate it and she continued to lie to me, not caring. The cook in the kitchen clearly gave me the normal saga saga stew. She just simply pulled the meat out, failing to remove the animal bones. Why lie to me? Tima African Restaurant has a team of inconsiderate liars and that's a damn shame. Needless to say, I did not eat lunch and I went back to work hungry after paying $24.00, tip included. I am very disappointed with the deceitful service, disrespect and food recieved. I have lots of friends and family who are not vegetarian. However, I will not be sharing this place with anyone.

reviews.text: I ordered some fufu and chicken egusi soup on their website, and I enjoyed it. I would say the price for the meal was a little high ($35) but the food was fresh and flavorful so can’t complain.

It was my first time at Lagz, and the experience was okay. We got the grilled croaker with jollof rice & collards and the beef egusi soup & fufu. The egusi was fantastic 🤩, and the sweet tea with got along with our dishes was amazing as well and freshly brewed 👌🏽. The croaker and collards were good as well, but the croaker was fried instead of grilled (still delicious nonetheless 😊). The jollof rice on the other hand was subpar and burnt 😬, I couldn’t stomach it myself.

The next few things are what ultimately led to the 3 star review. The ladies room was a bit unclean and needs some work, it was very uncomfortable to use. The next thing is the waiter, she never had an attitude or anything like that, but I think she needs more work being more helpful, communicative and hand-on with the customers. She never re-filled out teas (we had to ask), she didn’t explain the types of fufu well and we ended up ordering another type of the SAME fufu due to the miscommunication, and she never brought straws for our drinks after bringing out our teas (after stating she would go get them) and started bussing tables instead… and we had to get our own straws. Overall though, we enjoyed ourselves and the vibes were right ✨😊

P.S. - the wait time was also reasonable & everyone was friendly 👍🏽

The decor was beautiful. The host/waiter was very wonderful. The bar was not open. The restaurant was out of several things we tried to order. The food came out hot and quickly. The food was a decent price. There is a dinner buffet every 1st Sunday of the month. I liked that the wings were thoroughly cooked. We had leftovers to bring home. Everything reheated nicely. The ladies' room needs some work with the tissue & paper towel equipment.

My boyfriend and I recently visited LAGZ Restaurant, and the food was absolutely delicious. He ordered the fried fish with jollof rice, and it was very tasty and well-seasoned. I had the Ayamase with rice, and it was cooked perfectly — rich, flavorful, and just right.

The service was extremely slow, but it’s important to note that our waiter, Desiree (I believe that was her name), was incredibly kind, helpful, and attentive. She was the ONLY server working that day and was also managing all the takeout orders by herself, which we truly appreciated. If you’re looking for food that brings flavor, culture, and pure joy to your event — Zoewee’s Restaurant is it! I had them cater a wedding, and when I tell you it was SO worth it 😫😫😫, I mean every dollar spent felt like a blessing on a plate.

From start to finish, the experience was flawless. The trays came loaded, fresh, and beautifully presented. The fried plantains were golden and sweet with that perfect soft-inside, crisp-edge balance. The seasoned meat (lawd have mercy!) was cooked to perfection — juicy, well-spiced, and packed with traditional flavor that made everyone pause mid-bite to appreciate it. That rich, authentic taste? **Review of Zanzibar Café – A Taste of Authentic African Cuisine in Charlotte, NC**

Zanzibar Café is a hidden gem in Charlotte, offering a vibrant and flavorful journey into African cuisine. Located at *3720 N Tryon St Ste 101* , this restaurant stands out for its diverse menu, warm atmosphere, and commitment to authenticity.

**Food & Menu Highlights**
The menu is a delightful mix of African and American fusion, with standout dishes like:
- **Grilled Specialties**: Beef & Chicken Kabobs, Grilled Blackened Salmon, and Whole Tilapia—perfectly seasoned and cooked .
- **Fish Meals**: The Fried Croaker with Plantains or Acheke (a West African side) is a must-try .
- **Liberian Dishes**: The Palm Butter and Cassava Leaf stews are rich, aromatic, and highly praised by patrons .
- **Unique Sides**: Fufu, fried plantains, and corn beef rice add an authentic touch .

For lighter options, their salads (like the Blackened Salmon Salad) and grilled chicken dishes are equally satisfying .

**Service & Atmosphere**
The staff is noted for being friendly and efficient, whether you’re dining in or ordering takeout . The atmosphere is casual and family-friendly, with TVs and a welcoming vibe . Reviews highlight the restaurant’s cleanliness and the owner’s responsiveness to feedback .

**Pricing & Practical Info**
- **Hours**: Open Tue–Fri (11 AM–8 PM), Sat (Noon–8 PM), closed Sun–Mon . *Note:* Some sources list slightly different hours , so checking ahead is wise.
- **Price Range**: $$ ($10–$25 per person) .
- **Service Options**: Dine-in, carryout, and delivery available .

**Final Verdict**
Zanzibar Café delivers an unforgettable culinary experience, especially for those craving African flavors. Dishes like the Pepper Soup with Fufu and Palm Butter come highly recommended by regulars . While the restaurant’s Google ratings are mixed, the passionate reviews from diners—especially those familiar with African cuisine—speak volumes.

**Rating**: ★★★★☆ (4/5)
**Recommendation**: A must-visit for adventurous eaters and anyone missing homestyle African cooking. Don’t skip the ginger lemonade! .
