Now let’s talk about customer service!!! Sonia & Bobby were amazing…such a delightful encounter, sweet and very personable. You can tell they take pride in their business and their customer interactions.They offered me a free cup of their chia tea while I waited for my order which was delicious. I’m a chai girly and like my chai how I like my coffee (strong and sweet), it could have been a tad bit bolder for my liking but very flavorful nonetheless 😋. The kind gesture alone has guaranteed me to be a regular going forward, thoroughly enjoyed the hospitality that came along with the great tasting food.

Brought my Bae back the next day and he also enjoyed…Overall I can’t wait to come back and try more dishes from Soma Bistro & Cafe 🤗😊

Fantastic experience. I ordered the chicken Manchow soup and it was absolutely incredible rich, savory, and perfectly spiced. Everything else we ordered was just as good: bold flavors, fresh naan, and generous portions. My wife and I are really happy to have found such a yummy, affordable spot so close to home. Friendly service, food came out hot and fast, and we’ll definitely be back. They also do cakes and desserts to go.

Today Visited the newly renamed Soma Bistro & Café (formerly Curry N Cake Indian Restaurant). Tried their pastry and Irani chai, and the experience was a bit mixed. The pastry was quite good—fresh and enjoyable. However, the Irani chai was disappointing and I’d rate it 1/5; it lacked the authentic flavor and balance you’d expect.

The ambiance is tiny but pleasant, giving the place a cozy feel. Overall, a decent spot for pastries, but the chai definitely needs improvement.

This place the truly a Charlotte “Hidden gem”. Legit, I ordered the Chilli Chicken Dosa, first time have Dosa, was given a great explanation, it came out HUGE, what you see in the pics is about half. Flavor base is amazing, could’ve been spicier for my taste, but they were trying to be considerate without asking.the butter chicken was SMACK! Again, not as spicy as I’d like, still extremely satisfying and savory. Both entrees had an amazing amount of meat, chopped in uneven chuck, making it feel more homemade. The chef, Muthu, is a blessed in the kitchen. You can tell he learn how to cook from his mother, aunty, and/or grandma. I highly recommend this place to anybody read in this and look for a chill spot with good music and authentic tasty dishes. 10/10, come through and get to Indian o!!!

Quiet little unassuming bistro that has a great selection of Indian foods. We really wanted to try one of the unique pizzas and we were not disappointed with the paneer tikka masala. The star of the meal had to be the gobi achari. It was perfectly fried and the right amount of spice at medium.

formatted_address: 4044 Connection Point Blvd B, Charlotte, NC 28212, United States
name: Halal Street Food

reviews.text: Halal Street Food serves strong flavors and fresh ingredients. My lamb gyros tasted good once they were finally finished. The problem is the service. I waited more than 40 minutes for three orders of fries. The cook started my two lamb gyros, stopped to help someone else, and left them sitting on the counter. He came back about four minutes later and finished them. I brought it up. He decided to make them again, which pushed my wait even longer. The food is solid. The service is not. If you go, expect delays and check your order before leaving.

It a good spot for Mediterranean food… Rabeya was very friendly and easy to order a meal. She had a great customer service experience. Food service is super quick and friendly. Thank you to make my first time easy and quick.
Absolutely obsessed with this place. I come here weekly and the staff is super friendly. The manager goes above and beyond for her customers! Thank you !!!! Food is always fresh and hot.

The chicken over rice is so good! My order came with pita, TWO white sauces, and hot sauce - I didn’t even have to ask!

Best halal in the area 🙌🏼

I am here to leave my review.  On more than one occasion I have ordered food and requested white sauce for my lamb gyro rice through DoorDash which was not given to me. I can only eat the food with the sauce. Without it it’s bland. When I complained nothing was resolved and the person on the phone was acting confused.  I won’t be ordering again.   This has happened to me repeatedly.  The pita bread I was given was also stale.  I paid for the food it wasn’t free so why are you rendering me a service like it’s free.

formatted_address: 7308 E Independence Blvd, Charlotte, NC 28227, United States
name: Mi Barrio Halal Latin Grill

reviews.text: Chicken stew, yellow rice & cabbage. Tasty, no complaints. Super full. $15

I was working in Charlotte for a month, then finally I found this amazing place. My last 2weeks  I ate here everyday. Food, service and staff polite and just as beautiful as the food served. Can't wait to come back. GOD WILLING!!

I love this place so much!! I am a regular and the staff is so welcoming and patient and the food is sooooooooooooo good! I highly recommend! If you are new to Charlotte and you want some authentic dominican food and some soul food this is the place to be! The mangu, The arroz, The pollo, The sweet potatoes,  The Mac n cheese, The flan(desert) and so much more!  OMG it’s all on point I promise you!  😋😋😋😋😋😋😋😋😋😋😋😋😋😋😋😋

The food here is amazing. The Mac and cheese tastes homemade. The chicken must be slow cooked because it’s extra tender. The rice is great. The portion size is also good so the price is worth it. I can eat it a few times since I’m a light eater. I’ve never been disappointed eating here. Try it out!

The food and service was ZERO STARS! My friends so spoke so highly of this place so we decided to patronize. We first placed an online order that was never received, called in and was told no one spoke English so they couldn’t help. i then switched to spanish and they confirmed they didnt have the order but I spent $40+ dollars so after speaking to online support I got and refund and we went in person. They spoke english with no problem when we arrived which made mw think they just didnt want our business. I asked for no onions and peppers and got them both in abundance. My food was cold and my friends that recommended the place also did not enjoy his normal meal.

formatted_address: 4832 Central Ave C, Charlotte, NC 28205, United States
name: Cedars Halal Market, Restaurant & Hookah

reviews.text: The food was excellent in quality and flavor, big portions, and very humble prices. We tried the combination mix kabob entree and all 3 kabobs are made very well here, I was surprised by how much I liked my food. I think it has become the norm to be disappointed by restaurants these days in my experience, but this place is awesome. The Tabouleh is tasty and the flavors pair very well with kabob, hummus was nice, and the delicious homemade dressing on the salad is a unique twist on Italian. The host made us feel right at home in this quiet gem of a diner. Loved the whole experience and enjoyed my leftovers the next day.

Been coming here for years. Love the authenticity of the food. The Mediterranean salad is always well seasoned.  The lamb and turmeric rice well prepared.  I like I can shop and purchase authentic seasons, teas , dates and olives. Small dine in eatery very quaint. Relax atmosphere.  Customer service is great. Always professional and pleasant.  Limited parking. Dinning area very clean and neat. Large supplies of olives my favorite. One of my favorite jewels in Charlotte.

I finally stopped in and picked up a too good to go bag and ordered $30 worth of food. I was not disappointed. I will definitely be back I want to get the some of the desserts and that hummus and labneh… so so good! The staff is also very friendly and happy to assist with any questions that you may have. They also have a storefront with many different options. Stopped in here again I am not disappointed The pistachio baklava is out of this world. They also threw in some samosas for me to try, which was so great. Do yourself a favor expand your horizon and go try this restaurant.

It was my first time eating here. I was greeted when I entered. It's a small grocery store that sells food and also raw meat. The rice was delicious. The chicken was good too. I had half a chicken and I had Lipton soup. I definitely will try it again. The prices were reasonable. The customer service you will receive Will be great. And the wait was nothing but roughly 5 minutes.

If I could leave 0 starts I would. If you’re looking to purchase a goodie bag from this location I would not recommend. I waited about 10 minutes for the food which was not a problem. After receiving the food I noticed the chicken was extremely dry as if it had been sitting out all day long. I did not eat the food due to food safety concerns. When I called to tell them they claimed to have cooked the chicken the same day but the chicken was old or either sitting out. This is safety issue for customers and against proper food safety regulations.

formatted_address: 11320 N Tryon St, Charlotte, NC 28262, United States
name: Halal Kitchen Ink

reviews.text: I ordered from Halal Kitchen Ink, The Mix Over Rice which is Lamb and Chicken over rice . One of my favorite dishes to order from Halal spots . This was my first time , hopefully not my last . Ordered directions sauce on the side . Tasted everything seperate and then together , as I was eating I felt something was just really salty . Really could not put my finger on it , it's one thing to be seasoned it's another to have way too much salt . I suggest who ever is seasoning possibly the meat or sauce watch out for the sodium . You can add salt but you can not remove it , which makes the dish less desirable.  When I first retrieved  my order from Uber delivery driver I held that order and was like this is pretty light . Opened my order and said really , for the price yall could of packed a bit more rice . Portion was way to small for that price , maybe If thee was some falafel  or a piece of Nan bread something it would complete the meal but it just didn't  hit . I read so many reviews and watch TikTok reviews; not sure what went wrong

I travel over 90 miles from Columbia, SC to Charlotte, NC just for Halal Kitchen Ink—and let me tell you, it’s worth every single mile. This isn't just a food truck; it's a full-blown culinary experience on wheels.

From the moment you step up to the window, you’re greeted like family. The service is top-tier, fast, friendly, and professional. But let’s talk about the real star: the food. The flavors are phenomenal. Whether it's the juicy lamb over rice, perfectly seasoned chicken, or that mouthwatering white sauce they should bottle and sell—it’s all cooked to perfection, fresh, and Halal-certified.

You can taste the love and pride in every bite. The portions are generous, the prices are fair, and the consistency? Impressive every single time.

This place has officially ruined all other food trucks for me. If you're in the Charlotte area—or even hours away like I am—make the trip. Halal Kitchen Ink isn’t just good, it’s destination-worthy.

🔥 Pro Tip: Order ahead. They get BUSY for a reason.

Got it the first time and it was good. The second time it was a mess. No consistency on the service.  Paid extra for no salad and extra rice but I got half of the plate salad.  The chicken was old and tasted bad.  It really depends on the time and luck.  Will not repeat. Funny, I had to travel 2.5 hrs thinking this is the best in NC. The same halal cart that got me excited, now it is making hate chicken or lamb over rice.

Great food, good location, will definitely be returning. I suggest the lamb and chicken combo w/extra white sauce. The best one I've been to, right amount of salad sides and distributes the sauce just right.

Halal Kitchen Ink is an absolute gem! The food is always fresh, flavorful, and 100% authentic halal — you can truly taste the quality in every bite. From the perfectly seasoned meats to the delicious sides and sauces, every dish is made with care and attention to detail.

The service is just as impressive as the food. The staff is friendly, welcoming, and always ready to offer great recommendations. Whether you're a regular or a first-time visitor, you’re treated like family.

If you're looking for top-notch halal food, Halal Kitchen Ink is the place to go. Highly recommended!

formatted_address: 3117 N Sharon Amity Rd, Charlotte, NC 28205, United States
name: La Shish Kabob

reviews.text: Such a great find, it was our first time and the owner was so nice and brought us complimentary appetizers and gave us advice on the best meals. The portions were huge and the food was cooked perfectly. A hole in the wall place that I would love to see have more business. I will definitely be a new regular here.

We ordered three items. The lamb shank was flavorful and enjoyable, while the half chicken didn’t quite meet expectations. The hummus was decent, but the pita bread was too dry and didn’t seem freshly baked. On a positive note, the rice was very good.

5 stars! The food here is authentic and delicious. The Baba Ganoush with green chili is a must-try, and the Beef Kabobs were incredibly juicy. I loved the texture of the Kibbeh and the crispy Falafel. What really sets this place apart is the owner’s hospitality; he truly cares about his customers' experience. Great food and great service. I’ll definitely be back!

La Shish Kabob is hands down our favorite spot for Middle Eastern cuisine! My husband, who is from the Middle East, introduced me to this gem while we were dating, and we’ve been hooked ever since. It was my first time trying Middle Eastern food, and this place set the bar incredibly high.

We’ve ventured out and tried a few other spots in Charlotte, but nothing compares to La Shish Kabob. The food here is always fresh, warm, and absolutely delicious—it hits the spot every single time. The menu is full of flavorful options, and we genuinely love everything we’ve tried.

The staff is wonderful, always so kind and attentive, and they bring the food to you as soon as it’s ready. The service and quality are unmatched. If you’re looking for authentic Middle Eastern food in a welcoming atmosphere, this is the place to go. We can’t recommend it enough!
The food was amazingly delicious!  The portions were large and the food was well prepared. The hummus was the absolute BEST I ever had!

formatted_address: 800 Sawbuck Dr, Austin, TX 78660, United States
name: gladwin kitchen

reviews.text:
Amazing home cooked food, the Jolloff rice is fresh and I love the spice levels. Strong tomato taste with a lingering beautiful peppery taste, long grained rice.

The hen is fresh, the white meat is tender with authentic west Africa taste.

The salad is expected, it has a clean and crispy from the snap of the peas.

Gladwin Kitchen is the to go place for party catering! I was skeptical to order at first because I have never met her or known anyone who knew her. I simply found her on Google. I'm glad I went with her because she is trust worth and my food was ready on time for pickup.

Very misleading – not a real restaurant!
I honestly don’t understand how they’re getting all these positive reviews. I drove 20 minutes to the listed address, expecting a restaurant, but all I found was a regular house 🏠. There’s no signage, no indication of a business—just someone’s home. The ads make it look like an actual restaurant, but it’s clearly not. No details, no setup, nothing that suggests this is a legit dining spot. Feels like false advertising to me.

I had the pleasure of booking Gladwin's kitchen service for my event, and I must say, she did an absolutely outstanding job. The food she served was not only delicious, but it exceeded all expectations. My guests and I thoroughly enjoyed every single dish.

I needed tasty Nigerian food for my baby's dedication, and a friend recommended Gladys. She was very professional and accommodating of my requests. The food was delicious, everyone kept going back for more. The fried rice was my fave. I will definitely order from her in the near future.

formatted_address: 10805 N Lamar Blvd J, Austin, TX 78753, United States
name: African Market/Nigerian Restaurant

reviews.text: Not going to lie, when we first walked in, it looked like a game room. We sat down and while looking at the menu, the owner? Not sure, came up and sat in our booth and gave some suggestions. We did want to try the egusi soup, but he said, “Umm, try the plain one before then come back and see if you’ll want to try the egusi.” After our meal, he came back to see how we liked it? I asked what it tasted like. He offered a taste, and let me tell you I’m glad he gave us the suggestion, but we personally wouldn’t have liked the egusi. Whatever he offered was very delicious ngl would definitely order to go next time.

It’s so great here. I didn’t even get to take a picture of my food. But I finished it. You should give this a try. An amazing Experience. If you haven’t tried different culture, food, peaceful in here.

Me and my friend came to try Nigerian food for the first point and it did not disappoint! We both tried the egusi soup and it was so good. Workers were so nice and welcoming and i’d definitely recommend! The place is small and has a home-like atmosphere. Would truly recommend if you’re looking for an underground spot with great food!

I’m Nigerian and it’s always hard finding a Nigerian restaurant than can deliver quality food but this restaurant really does it well. Food is always seasoned and portion sizes are always large. I do not eat meat or fish and this is one of the few Nigerian restaurants that will honor my request and not put any meat or fish in the soups, so if you’re vegan, vegetarian or pescatarian, I’d highly recommend this place as well.

Good African place to eat and shop.

This restaurant also offers a shopping experience to pick up your African food stuff.

The food is decent and prices are decent also.

They have loads of beer from many African countries . In all I enjoyed myself eating and watching the US presidential debate. All the best Austin. Thank you Sam and team

formatted_address: 5610 N Interstate Hwy 35, Austin, TX 78751, United States
name: Palatable Nigerian Cuisine

reviews.text:
Drove all the way from Waco for a nigerian food experience with my family. I thought it was a restaurant but to my surprise it wasn’t. I was impressed by the setup though; multiple food vendors, one location. That right there was a red light for me but I still tried it. I ordered 2x vegetable soup and poundo, they charged an extra $3 for goat meat and then the basmati fried rice.
Soup was watery, with a sweet taste, it was mostly the tomato paste and few vegetables, with 3 small pieces of boney goat meat and nothing else.
A $5  goat meat was compulsory to complete the order for the fried rice or else the kiosk won’t let you check out. And I had the-same 3 pieces of the annoyingly tiny goat meat in my pack. The Rice was good though, my kids ate it. But the vegetable soup was horrible, I would ask for a refund but the stress ain’t worth it.

I have tried to give this restaurant a lot chances, I’m new to the area and need places to get some good food. I have ordered three times online and once on the phone and all the times I have requested fish. It clearly states in the menu description fish or goat. I don’t like goat and also have hesitations eating goat in general. I put my request of fish in the special instructions and it’s never complied. Which makes me wonder if someone who has allergies or dietary restrictions puts something in the instructions and it’s blatantly ignored? When I eat the Egusi it is Oily and room temperature. The goat I receive is all fat/ cartilage and doesn’t seem properly cleaned. I am disappointed but will just save myself the trouble and eat elsewhere.

I loveeeeeee this place!!! I am obsessed with the egusi soup I want it everyday. I stay in Roundrock so I couldn’t get to it as much BUT they are now available on uber eats 🙂‍↔️ which I just found out yesterday and I’m so happy! Very delicious food and very happy to be able to order for delivery now 😊

I have always wanted to try Nigerian food and finally tried at this restaurant. The food was great and I really enjoyed it. However, it would have been nice if some meat was ready (like goat). I wanted to really try goat egusi but the fish one was really good regardless! so tasty

Quality of Food was poor - Food wasn’t fresh- and still was handed to me. What’s painfully annoying is that I made a large purchase. Paid over $300 for large portion of food and it was obviously not cooked same day. This will unfortunately be my last time patronizing this business.

formatted_address: 5933 Westminster Dr, Austin, TX 78723, United States
name: Tailat Kitchen (Nigerian Cuisine)

reviews.text:
This was my first time trying Nigerian food, and it absolutely did not disappoint! I ordered the egusi soup with fufu and the jollof rice with chicken through Uber Eats, and every bite was bursting with flavor. The seasoning was perfect—spicy enough to enjoy, but not overwhelming.

The fufu was a revelation—I’d never had it before, but its soft, mild texture paired perfectly with the rich, well-seasoned egusi soup. The jollof rice was amazing too, and the chicken was so tender it fell off the bone. Portions were generous, so we even had leftovers for the next day, making it totally worth the price.

I can’t wait to order again and explore more of their menu. Highly recommended!

Food was very yummy and flavorful! Went with three of my very close friends and we had a great time. The service was amazing and when the food came out it was sizzling and boiling, definition of fresh and hot! We had the seafood ila, jollof rice with chicken, egusi with chicken, and the efo riro with assorted meat (cow skin, tripe, and beef). The flavors were so good and the spice was great.

Mold or fungus was growing on literally every egg yolk in the salad. This is the third time now I have received spoiled, moldy or expired food or drink from this restaurant. This is a major health safety issue especially as it relates to food poisoning. They have good flavoring but I won’t trust the food quality. I won’t be giving them any more of my business.

Great place, and the food was tasty. The owner is very nice but one of the workers was rude. We called her, and she pretended she did not hear us. Plus I asked to change money  for tip but she said there was no change. When the owner came to the register, she said there was change and very willing to help us. The other worker was great. Even though she had a tongue tie, she tried to communicate with us and was all smiles.

The owner is really great and was very accommodating.  The place is clean and the toilet was clean too. You should visit.

1st time eating here and did a pickup in person order. The eforiro was tasty and had some assorted meat. The pepper stew had only 1 small piece of over fried hard fish, this was not worth it. The taste of the food was 3/5 but the value of $70 worth of food was 2/5. The pounded yam was a small one too. The asun had fried and not grilled meat and had some tiny pieces .

formatted_address: 94 Rainey St, Austin, TX 78701, United States
name: TCHIADAI

reviews.text: This is such a great spot.  You start with the friendliest owner and fantastic customer service.  His kind demeanor and genuine interaction were refreshing after a long day.  Next, you start smelling your order as he begins cooking it, building anticipation…and the anticipation worth it.  DELICIOUS!   Quite possibly the best meal I’ve had in a long time.  Great job young man!

AB knew exactly what I meant by im here for the flavor. Ginger 🫚  is his forte!

Chicken hit my stomach well and sometimes he's cooking up noodles with beans, ill need to try the OG rice because this guy can feed you!

Food was great. The menu was easy to understand. You can customize your spice level and spicy wasn't too too hot. The plantains were amazing. I've never had them savory before. Everything is served to order and the service was great!

Food and Service were excellent. I got the combo plate with the OG wings, rice, plantains, and salad. I got it spicy and it was a great level with a kick but not too spicy that it overwhelmed the flavor. Wings were juicy and crispy but not greasy. I also got the ginger drink out of curiosity. It was very strong ginger flavor and sweet, but I overall enjoyed it.
The chicken was crispy and delicious, the rice full of flavor, and jinjanma ginger drink cold and refreshing. Combined with the smiles and sincerity from the owner, absolutely earned a 10/10.

formatted_address: 510 E Anderson Ln, Austin, TX 78752, United States
name: Kitchen234 - Nigerian Restaurant

reviews.text: My food was very delicious !!! I got the egusi which is my very favorite. I did request no meat and I had bits of beef, which I was kinda bummed about but nevertheless it was my first time trying this place because the one I usually go to doesn’t deliver so I was skeptical at first but it was worth every penny. I also love the spinach portion. Very tasty

The BEST and most authentic Nigerian food in Austin. The owner is so kind and generous, she’s makes her food with the right amount of spice and taste. You won’t regret ordering from here! Oh and HUGE portions. I couldn’t even finish one bowl.

I got the egusi soup with some fufu. It was great, meaty and fishy with bold flavors. At first I had thought it was a bit pricey but I got 3 meals out of it and enjoyed them very much. I recommend trying it if you’re like me and wanting to experiment with some new cuisine flavors. I would describe the experience as confusing and intriguing at first followed by much warmth and satisfaction, it might take some time to get used to but I would get again. The fufu was my favorite.

Christiana was wonderful to work with! I called midweek to put an order in for two, and she had it ready the next day. We ordered fish stew, jollof rice, and moi moi (pictured), ayamase and white rice (not pictured). All of it was delicious, and we’ll definitely be ordering again!

They rob you when you order online. Literally they try to give you the smallest portion size possible. We ordered the soup and added meat to it but the cut these small pieces of meat and added it to the soup bowl so you dont get the full portion of soup ans huge bones with hardly no meat. This is a shame for what they charge you.

formatted_address: 15608 Spring Hill Ln, Pflugerville, TX 78660, United States
name: Lady T Kitchen African Restaurant

reviews.text:
Our go to’s are egusi, okra soup, rice and stew and meat pie! Each of them remind me of my late mother in law, the texture, the balance of spice, the deep flavour.

If you’re lucky you’ll walk in and hear Lady T singing while she prepares the food and you’ll realize that’s the secret ingredient. Each meal has been consistent and the experience of greeting Uncle makes walking in feel like home.

Thanks for your labour of love!

I’ve eaten at Lady T Restaurant before, and when the food is good, it’s really good. Unfortunately, today was a huge disappointment. The meal was bland and didn’t taste like African food at all. The beef stew, in particular, tasted like canned spaghetti sauce—heavy tomato flavor with no depth, seasoning, or traditional spices. It was nothing like authentic African cuisine. The Egusi wasn't fresh. It tasted like it was previously frozen. It was so bad that I couldn’t finish it and ended up throwing it away. Very inconsistent experience, and today’s food completely missed the mark.

I had about 4 good experiences until it finally happened…. The comments about spoiled food are right. I literally couldn’t belive the smell that oozed out when I opened My plate of jollof. Like how can jollof be that bad to the don’t where the smell is hard to ignore? And they still had the audacity to pack the food and give a customer. Greed is the biggest downfall of people.

They also have a habit of warming up food in the freezer. Their food is not fresh - they do not cook daily.

I’m very disappointed to leave this review as I hyped up this place a lot, but after that spoilt food I  will not be wasting my money in the economy. Best of luck to all

I gave this business 2 star because when asking the guy at counter a question about my allergy. He responded with its not their policy to answer to the public only to the health inspector.  Therefore the we  choose to not order from this business.  I have seen great reviews on the food.  But the customer service killed it for me.  Maybe consider replacing your counter person.  You business will grow.  I had some people with me who has never experienced African food.

Had west African food for the first time from here and I can say I’ve become a fan. We tried the Egusi soup with fufu, Jollof rice with goat meat, fried fish, meat pie and one other fried item that I don’t remember the name of but I don’t think it was the puff puff. As an inexperienced customer for this cuisine, I thought everything was perfect. Great portions and they all reheated well for a good meal for the next day as leftovers.
My partner and I throughly enjoyed everything we ate and we look forward to ordering from here again to try more items.

Can’t write too much about the restaurant experience itself since we got the food delivered.

formatted_address: 318 E 5th St., Austin, TX 78701, United States
name: Guinea Conakry

reviews.text: The food is yummmmmyyy. And the guy is so kind! The music vibes were also amazing. It’s just in a slightly sketchy place but didn’t have any issues. I will 100% be back.

AB was amazing. We got a combination of everything. Wings, the chicken, beef, and tuna fataya and fries. Oh MY GOD. It was soooo good everything we took a bite of was instantly the favorite. I couldn't decide if the chicken, tuna, or beef was my favorite. The fries with the onions and peppers were amazing, no sauce needed. We'll for sure be coming back!
Sweetest man behind the counter, let me split up my Fataya into Tuna, Beef and Chicken. I hate tuna, first time with whatever spices used I liked it. Overall, Guinean food, is incredibly tasty.

I visited this food truck a few nights ago. The food was so good. I got the fataya and fries. They were crispy and flavorful, just like the ones I grew up eating. The owner was so nice and accommodating, excellent service all around.

Had some of the best West African home recipes from TCHIADAI Guinea Conakry on 5th Street this week while visiting in Austin.  Located in the food truck plaza next to Westin Austin Downtown, and only 1 street over from the busy 6th Street corridor.  A definite MUST if you are ever in Downtown and wanting something flavorful.  The owner puts great focus on quality and customer experience...and be sure to try the home made Hibiscus or Ginger juices to go with the meal!!  Great for dinner or a post night out treat!  Keep up the great standards team TCHIADAI!  Will be back on my next trip to Austin for sure!!

formatted_address: 3801 S Congress Ave #107, Austin, TX 78704, United States
name: Taste of Ethiopia II

reviews.text: I cannot wait to come back and dishes which are unknown to me, and this place is perfect.  My first visit last month was made amazing by the service and atmosphere of the place. I literally had aunty's serving me and sharing stories of Ethiopia with the most beautiful smile and energy. I started with some hot tea, and can tell you that it puts to shame in flavor and health, the typical Texas sweet tea. I had a chicken dish which I sadly do not recall, and I wonder if, while it was good, it's flavor was dialed down for the American palate, because I felt it was but with safe a flavor. This dish seems similar to the POLLO GUISADO in many Latin American countries and It would not surprise me. since we get many of our culinary and musical history from Africa. The spot is large, yet cozy and the price was adequate for the serving of the meal. However, I highlight that I had a super friendly, fast and courteous serving and can't wait to go back and feast while getting a cultural education. This is a family managed spot and encourage you all to try it and support it!!

Flavorful, filling, and wholesome food!! The atmosphere is so welcoming and the staff is wonderful. Our favorite was definitely the lamb over their other popular dishes. Also loved the spinach sambusa and Doro Wot!

I cannot recommend this place enough. I was very happy!
I love Ethiopian food, and this place is very solid. I went with a group of 8, and their banquet options were perfect, especially with portion sizes. Half of us got the vegetarian banquet and the other half got some meat plates. Between us, we almost didn't finish!
I thought everything we were served was very flavorful, and there were a ton of options. Even the coffee and tea were very solid. Our waitress was also extremely nice and conversational with us. Definitely coming back!

Our 4th visit and it just keeps getting better! The service is always amazing!! and the food is beyond our expectations.
The vegetarian sampler is always a great option!
Highly recommend!

I brought all my friends here for our first time trying Ethiopian food and we were blown away! The food is served family style, perfect for a large group. We loved every single dish, my favorite was the eggplant and doro wot. The service was spectacular. Jeremiah was very helpful in explaining the ordering and dishes and gave great recommendations. Mariam brought the entertainment with her stories and jokes! It really felt like being around family. You can feel the love in this place. Can’t wait to eat here again

formatted_address: 1914 E 6th St ste c, Austin, TX 78702, United States
name: Canje

reviews.text:
Canje was just alright. The place is rowdy, the service is nice, and the staff's recommendation were pretty neat. But the food wasn't a complete home run.

The complementary pink pineapple was pretty good. I'm a fan of pineapple, so this starter was very refreshing. The sweetness, acidity, and spices melded brilliantly, making me devour the fruits quickly.

The Wagyu Beef Suya was easily the best thing I had. The presentation was cute, but the cook on the Wagyu was simply superb. It phenomenally seasoned and juicy, and the surrounding spices gave it a nice kick. The onions weren't too strong to make an impact and were pretty scarce (maybe make them pickled)?

The Wild Boar Pepperpot and Guyanese Roti came together. It makes sense because Rotis go well with a sauce, and it would be a waste to throw away the leftover Pepperpot sauce (apparently they use it to make their Cassareep Ice Cream). However the Pepperpot would've definitely matched better with the coconut rice because the sauce was quite sweet and not viscous. The Pepperpot is extremely similar to Szechuan Braised Pork Belly, so this dish had a very familiar, but welcoming feeling.

I was still hungry so I got the Jerk Beef Patties, but they were just over priced empanadas. I prefer the empanada to be gushing with flavor instead of having a dip. I wasn't impressed by the tastes and sizes, so I was pretty disappointed.

The Tres Leches was also just alright. I've had some pretty good ones, so I might have a preference in how they are prepared. The cake was light, airy, moist, sweet, and had notes of sourness from the seasonal jam. With all of that said, none of it fully delivered. I think the cake could've been at least 50% more sweeter, and the seasonal jam made the dessert more interesting/different instead of more tasty (to me at least).

Overall, I'm satisfied with the 5 dishes that I had and the price that I paid for. Although I had some good bites, I wouldn't give anything I had a strong recommendation. Do I regret coming here? No. Would I strongly suggest others to come here? Also no. I can see the appeal, but it wasn't for me.

First time coming here was amazing! Bar staff was phenomenal,  every bite of food was delicious, and the ambiance was top notch.
After the first time I've been so excited to return and share that experience with someone else who hadn't been there, so I took my sis on my birthday.
Food was every bit as good as I remember it but the service dropped significantly.
I've never had service ruin an experience that much but wow. She just seemed bothered by anything and everything going on.
Luckily the rest of the waitstaff was extra sweet and helped us out with little things like water to help us feel like we weren't forgotten.
Boar Pepper Pot and beef patties always hit though and the Guyanese Style Roti goes good with everything!
I'd still recommend but given the option only bar seating for me from now on.

Canje is okay, the food you’re getting for the price isn’t worth it in my opinion.

Presentation and service is amazing, but the actual entree dishes that we had weren’t great. The roti was the best thing there (actually really good, I would order two), then the ceviche and then the pink pineapple. Jerk chicken was dry, fish was eh. Ice cream was good, probably not a good idea to pour the rum on it. Overall has a lot of potential, but they need to work on their main dishes.

Had dinner at Canje.  I had no expectations going into the restaurant, but was blown away.  We had four people and the waitress recommended 8 dishes.

We started with the Pink Pineapple, Jerk Beef Patties, and Wagyu Beef Suya.  All were delicious with the Pink Pineapple surprising the whole table.  Our main dishes were the West Indian Curry, Wild Boar Pepperpot and Jerk Chicken with a side of Roti.  Where to begin?  It was all delicious!  The Jerk Chicken has some great heat and brought sweet to my brow.

We finished with the Tres Leches and Stewed Mango Pudding.  Their take on the Tres Leches was a little different (not saturated in milk) but good.  The pudding was phenomenal!  I highly recommend and look forward to coming back.

The staff here are truly excellent.  The food is amazing, I thought I knew what a good Beef Patty was and I now stand corrected! Every dish from wagyu beef curry to the Guyanese style roti was stellar. Get the fruit (Pink Pineapple, Passion Fruit, Basil, Aji Amarillo) Highly recommended!

formatted_address: 1100 Grand Ave Pkwy Suite 100, Pflugerville, TX 78660, United States
name: Taste of Ethiopia I

reviews.text:
I recently tried an Ethiopian restaurant for the very first time, and the experience turned out to be wonderfully memorable. I started with their lentil Sambusas ✨, which quickly became one of my favorite parts of the meal. The crispy exterior and warmly spiced lentil filling created the perfect balance of texture and flavor. They were so good that I immediately thought about ordering another plate—an excellent start to the evening.

For my main dish, I chose the vegetarian sampler 🥗, and it proved to be a great introduction to Ethiopian cuisine. Each item on the platter had its own unique taste, yet everything was mild and carried a gentle, natural sweetness. It’s an ideal option for anyone trying Ethiopian food for the first time or for those who enjoy comforting, balanced flavors. However, if you prefer your dishes on the spicier side, I’d recommend asking the restaurant if they can add extra heat, as the default versions are quite mild.
The injera was soft, tangy, and perfect for scooping up every dish, adding to the authenticity and enjoyment of the meal. Combined with the friendly service and warm atmosphere, the entire experience felt inviting and satisfying.
Overall, this is a spot I can easily see myself returning to—especially when I’m hungry for new dishes or craving a cuisine that’s different from the usual routine. It’s a great place to explore fresh, flavorful, and unique foods.

🇪🇹✨
Visited Taste of Ethiopia, and it was a delightful experience!
🥟 Sambusa with Lentils – Thin, crispy, and perfectly fried. They also offer spinach and beef options. The sauce served with it was spectacular — full of flavor, not too spicy and not too mild. A perfect start!
🍛 Sampler Platter – Great way to explore different dishes. It included two types of dal (one plain and one with masala), three vegetable dishes (beans & carrots, a green leafy veggie, and cabbage), and a fresh salad. Everything was served with soft, tangy Ethiopian bread that reminded me of dosa rolls — ideal for scooping up the curries. The flavors were mild and slightly sweet for my Indian masala taste, but still delicious and comforting.
🍺 St. George Beer – Light and smooth; pairs perfectly with the food.
🍰 Baklava – Fresh, flaky, and a lovely sweet ending to the meal.
The staff were extremely friendly, welcoming, and attentive, adding to the warm, homely vibe.
✅ Pros: Great flavors, excellent service, cozy space.
⚠️ Cons: Curries a bit sweet for spice lovers.
Overall, an amazing experience — authentic food and genuine hospitality! 🌍💛

Taste of Ethiopia was one of the best local restaurant experiences I have had since I was a child in my hometown. The owner and staff were truly the most friendly people, going above and beyond to get to know their guests and customize the experience without being overbearing.

Also the food was top notch. I’ve been to Ethiopia many times and this was as good if not better than what you can get in country.

Everyone should go and the world would be a better place if more restaurants were like this.

Awesome food. Never had Ethiopian food before so it was a great experience. We had the vegetarian platter and everything was delicious.  I also tried the traditional coffee and it was nice and smokey and tasted great. Definitely worth trying.

The food here is absolutely incredible! I brought my mom to try Ethiopian cuisine for the first time, and it couldn’t have been a better experience. We ordered the Doro Wat, the vegetarian sampler, and Ethiopian coffee—all of which were rich in flavor and beautifully prepared. The staff were so warm and welcoming, which made the meal even more enjoyable. I’ll definitely be recommending this place to friends and bringing them along next time. Everyone should experience Ethiopian food at least once—it’s truly something special.

formatted_address: 6019 N Interstate Hwy 35, Austin, TX 78723, United States
name: Habesha Ethiopian restaurant and bar

reviews.text: Soooo good.  We got the family meat for 4 and it was so tasty esp the fish and chicken tibs. The collard green were super tasty.  I wasn't feeling brave enough to do jalapeño tonite but evidently those were real super fresh.

We’ve lived in the same neighborhood as Habesha for 19 years, and today was the first time we’ve visited. We’d been going to Aster’s for ages, but Habesha was fantastic. Big, clean dining space. Friendly service. Most of all, the food was fantastic. Would definitely come back!
The food was absolutely delicious, and the service was excellent. Our waiter was energetic and full of life, which made the experience even better.

I stopped by here for lunch today, and it was my very first time trying Ethiopian food… I was not disappointed, they recommended some restaurant favs and I gave them a try and they did not miss! The iced tea is absolutely lovely! Black tea, with cardamom, cinnamon and cloves. The baklava is a must try.
If you’re ever curious, just go for it!

Will be back for sure

Keep up the good work

This place is truly a hidden gem. The food is absolutely incredible and Michael gave us the best customer service ever! He helped us so much from giving us food preferences to amazing hospitality. I definitely recommend you try what he recommends!

formatted_address: 730 Shady Ln, Austin, TX 78702, United States
name: Nyam

reviews.text:
They offer two vegetarian tacos along with yucca chips and corn fritters. The Yawdy was a little bit too BBQ flavoured for me but still a great portion and filled with fun incredients. I preferred the Yucatan- it had nice flavors with pineapple and red onion.

The fried yucca was fun and had a delicous chimichurri sauce. But my favourite were the crispy sweet corn fritters with chipotle mayo. I probably should have just ordered like three of those - they were perfectly crispy with big chunks of corn and other delightful peppers. Wow they were really good.

The food is very affordable and outside of Hi Sign brewery which is super fun. Would definitely order those corn fritters again!

Yawdy Bowl was the bomb! The food truck owners were nice and sweet. Def try other one next time!

Update: Just tried Yucatan Bowl and it's awesome 🥣! The cooks were extremely nice, and they deserved to get recognized.

So delicious!! I got the Yawdy Bowl and wow! The chicken is cooked to perfection, and all of the flavors go together beautifully. 10/10 recommend.
There’s plenty of seating outside as well as indoor seating in the brewery. The women working the truck were super sweet. I’ll definitely be going back!

I love Nyan. I have followed them through 2 locations and I'm happy they are near to me as they are dear. The tacos are packed. It's definitely going to leave you with that fresh homemade feeling no matter what you order. The owner let me try the corn fritters and I loved them and I always order the Yawdy and I can't seem to get off of it. I'd love to become brave and try everything because I'm confident everything is fantastic. Super moist and savory. 10/10
Really quality and delicious food with good portions. The tacos were amazing, good sweet potato fries, and my friend enjoyed her bowl.

formatted_address: 100 12th St #108B, Pflugerville, TX 78660, United States
name: Sumah African and Caribbean store (Nigerian + Jamaica + Haiti + Brazil + Ethiopian + Ghana + Somalia + Guinea + Islanders)

html_attributions: Sumah African and Caribbean store (Nigerian + Jamaica + Haiti + Brazil + Ethiopian + Ghana + Somalia + Guinea + Islanders)

reviews.text: excellent quality products especially the palm oil and coconut oil.  staff is very friendly and will source special items.  if you call ahead meals can be prepared and they are very nutritious delicious and halal.  highly recommend this shop!

This place just recently opened and I love it! The family that owns it are so warm, welcoming and are very helpful. I got some ready made cassava fufu and their yams were so good,with no spots. They also have fresh vegetables. Will definitely go back again and again.

Came in to grab some items I needed to make my Chicken Pepper stew and Fufu. Walked out even happier because I also got natural homemade Shea butter. I definitely recommend stopping by and checking them out. It will be worth the trip.

Sumah store is superb 👌, it gives you the quality taste of African products you want. The palm oil, yellow garri, white garri, ofada
are very nice ,no doubt, try it and shop more....

Had a wonderful experience with the staff.  They were friendly, knowledgeable, and willing to go above and beyond.  The store had a few selections but the space was small, only allowing for two 6ft shelves and a freezer and small reach in cooler.

formatted_address: 3804 W Stan Schlueter Loop #102, Killeen, TX 76549, United States
name: Aunty Mimi's Kitchen Restaurant

reviews.text: I got their fufu and egusi with goat meat and loved it, just wished the meat wasn’t too tough to chew. Customer service was great, she was so kind and friendly. Wait time for the food wasn’t too bad , I’ll definitely be coming back again ;)

Very friendly people and atmosphere. The restaurant has a wind down vibe and is very relaxing. I came here with my girlfriend and we had never tried African food before. Our waiter walked us through the menu and suggested things based on what we normally liked. The food was amazing. A wonderful introduction to African food. We will definitely be back again.

This is my 3rd time trying African cuisine in general and today was my first time eating at mimis. honestly this is my first time ever loving african food! 10/10 I would recommend. Best African food around Killeen

We ordered Egusi, seafood Okra & Afang with pounded yam. My daughter & I enjoyed everything, although some of the meat was a bit tough, but all 3 soups were very flavorful. Be ready to wait a while as the food is cooked to order, therefore, fresh.
They are always welcoming & the music makes you want to get up and dance!
So glad to have this restaurant not far from my home...

This is the type of the food where if you take one bite you automatically start doing the little dancy dance. Lol. The service was AMAZING! Food came out hot and fresh! She was so wholesome. I’m so sad to finally find a place that remind me so much of home to then have to move. I would 100% recommend! Everything tasted excellent! I couldn’t wait to get home, i kept eating it on the drive home lol it was that good! I melted! I started dancing in my car.

formatted_address: 8315 Burnet Rd, Austin, TX 78757, United States
name: Yeni’s Fusion (North Food Truck)

reviews.text:
How could I not give a 5 star rating?!
Food, delish, service was fantastic. A lil pissed I didn’t come sooner than I did. I’ve had this on my saved to go list for over a yr and I passed by at least 75x since adding it.
Looking forward to returning!!
I had the Indonesian fried chicken with rice n salad. Chicken was banginnn!!
Flavorful & wholesome!! We got the batagor/fried fish chicken wonton and the rendang/beef curry — both hit. The owner is really kind & wish them all the best!! :)

I freaking love this place and i wish i went more often. The food has been amazing from when this place first opened. When i first went there the dude taking orders was terrible, super rude and legit forgot my order, where the owner had to fire up the kitchen again because that bozo didn't want to do his job and the kitchen had already closed before receiving my food. I told she didn't have to but she went above and beyond.

There was a week or two when the truck was open for lunch and thats when i last had that amazing goodness. I love the fish and the beef rendang, i felt like the coconut curry brisket soup could have been more flavor.

I need to go back soon!

I wish I could give this spot more stars. It has been a challenge to find a food truck in Austin that has restaurant quality food and Yeni’s tops it. She keeps the dishes true to Indonesian cuisine with simple ingredients and complex flavors. The beef rendang combo was so tender and the chicken and yellow rice was so good. I will be back to try more dishes asap. If you want to try something unique with great flavors, stop here!
Foods and services were great!! Nearest Indonesian cuisine that you can find close to downtown Austin!

formatted_address: 9821 N Interstate Hwy 35, Austin, TX 78753, United States
name: Southwest Farmers Market

reviews.text:
I’ve been a loyal customer to this store since they opened! I’m highly displeased at my recent experience on Sunday. The very rude cashier packed my groceries in such a way it caused my loaf of bread to be flat. We didn’t noticed until we put the groceries in the car. I immediately went back into the store to inform her that the method she used flattened my bread and requested to switch for a normal loaf. She rudely dismissed me and told me to talk to the manager. He was very unhelpful and blamed me for flattening the bread. He said no one else will buy the bread if I exchange it. If I went to HEB/Walmart/Trader Joe’s this would not be a problem at all!
Please train your staff how to properly bag groceries and to have good customer service. Even the manager was out of line!
Imagine arguing back and worth about a $5 loaf of bread after spending over $300! Very embarrassing and poor service. Don’t get into the customer service industry if you hate customers.

I recently purchased goat at this place. I got 10 pounds of goat meat. After I purchased it I placed it in a freezer bag and headed straight home. After I got home I marinated it and let it stay in the fridge . Tell me why the morning of Christmas as I am cooking the goat it starts stinking up and falling apart. The goat wasn't even on the stove for 30 minutes. The meat was falling apart like it was pressure cooked but the skin was still hard . They sold us spoiled goat and when I called the owner they said we must have passed some place else before heading home. They refuse to refund us. This is honestly very upsetting and disappointing, I will not be buying any meat here again!
They have every African food stuffs u can think of.
Scotch eggs was basically like eating raw dough. Gave 3 stars because cashier was friendly. Otherwise the service at the kitchen needs better work.

The baker woke up and chose violence today on the buns. The stars is for the puff puff. The buns were a terrible disappointment.  I don’t think anyone even tasted these before they were put out for sale. Straight to the trash. I opened several to see if maybe it was just one but the entire batch of buns were tasteless, no sweetness at all and undercooked. It’s like they too puff puff mix and said let's add flour to it and call it buns.  Please do better.  We are already having to pay higher prices for your items so make them worth it please.

formatted_address: 5610 N Interstate Hwy 35, Austin, TX 78751, United States
name: Cravebowl

reviews.text:
I got the Asun Jollof rice and Ewa Agoyin,it’s so delicious.
Definitely coming back

formatted_address: 5011 E Cesar Chavez St, Austin, TX 78702, United States
name: Ethiopian and Eritrean Food Trailer

reviews.text:
Excellent food. Fresh and so flavorful! Wonderful, friendly service too. Vegan friendly! I'll be back!

UPDATE: Google says "temporarily closed". What's going on?? When are they re-opening? They're the best in Austin!

The food was great (I had the vegetarian meal sampler) and the portion was nice and big. This is an unusual (I think? I'm not from Austin, just passing through, maybe you all have tons of Ethiopian places) and fun way to eat, they gave me a bunch of soft fluffy bread (think sort of along the lines of sheets of pancake for texture) to place the assorted vegetables in to eat. Nifty, and filling. I could not finish it because I was running late for my flight to begin with, and I hated having to throw some of it away. The people running the truck were friendly and happy to help explain the menu. Looked like he was having a good time doing it, which is nice, he clearly loves his work. Only negative is the parking situation. It's in a food truck park, and there were like  or so parking spots, and the parking lot was a bit torn up. Pavement was rough. This is not something they have any control over. Price was good too, btw, especially considering how much food I got. Wish I could go back

I have eaten Ethiopian at two other places in town and Habesha grill is so, so good. I saw that this place had really good reviews so I stopped in and was excited to try this place. I’m very bummed to share it was in fact not good at all. I ordered the veggie combo with injera. Much of it was very bland and tasted out of a box. I wanted it to be good! But it was not. Would not recommend at all. Especially if you’ve eaten Habesha, you’re going to be let down coming here!!
We've been to other Ethiopian restaurants around Austin and the food here is incredible and the service is quick and friendly. Cannot recommend highly enough!

This is a great option for outdoor dining, lots of open picnic tables in the sunshine, everyone wears masks and the food is so delicious! I had the lamb dish with gluten free injera, all the food was fresh and flavorful. You can choose to get in to go container, or if eating there be served on actual plates to cut down on waste. Staff was friendly and great service! The menu is large, many options to work through on future visits.

formatted_address: 2013 Wells Branch Pkwy, Austin, TX 78728, United States
name: Megenagna Mart and Cafe

reviews.text: I love Ethiopian food and some of the dishes here were good, but there are others that were just not as good as some of the other restaurants. I like the injera when it’s a little bit more sour, and this was a little bit under fermented for my taste. And maybe this was just the lunch menu, but it seemed like they didn’t have as much in the way of variety as some of the other restaurants. And there was only one combo, which was a veggie combo. It would be nice to be able to order a combination meal with both veggie and meat dishes. The service was great and the people were very friendly. There’s a market next-door, which has East African staples which is kind of fun to walk around in since I lived in East Africa for a few decades, but overall as an Ethiopian restaurant, I would say there’s some other places that I would probably prefer, if for no other reason than the larger variety of dishes.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Absolutely Exceptional!

I had an amazing experience at this restaurant from start to finish. The moment I walked in, the atmosphere felt warm, welcoming, and beautifully put together. The staff were incredibly friendly, attentive, and made sure everything was perfect without ever feeling intrusive.

The food was the real highlight—fresh, flavorful, and cooked to absolute perfection. Every dish tasted like it was made with love and skill. The presentation was gorgeous, and the portions were just right. You can tell the chef really cares about quality.

The service was quick, the prices were fair for the quality, and the overall experience was unforgettable. This is definitely a place I’ll come back to and recommend to everyone I know.

If you’re looking for delicious food, great service, and a relaxing atmosphere

this is the spot. Highly recommended!

Ordered the kitfo special and alecha. Both were amazing. The Kitfo is beef tartare, but with a super savory, spicy taste. Soooo good! The Alecha was nice to cool off with… and the injera comes in great portions.
I’ve tried another Ethiopian place in Austin, and it was nowhere near this good. Will likely be ordering this a couple times a month now!

The customer service here is the best every one came by to check on the white boy who was eating the spicy food. The Duro Wat was the best I have ever had tender and savory, after the first bite I inhaled the rest of the bowl. The Awaze Tibs were fresh and cooked perfectly and if I had any more room in my stomach I would have finished them off as well. 10/10 would recommend this place since I will be back for more

The food was amazing - the nicely sour spongy bread, curries and veggie dishes, and especially the traditional coffee.
The service felt like we were guests in their home, so warm and welcoming. The hostess served us coffee and popcorn in the traditional way, which felt like a performance. We sat in special space, immersed in incense and the smoke & smell of freshly roasted coffee, sitting on traditional stools and chatting after the meal. A very memorable experience!

formatted_address: 10009 N Lamar Blvd b, Austin, TX 78753, United States
name: Selam International Mart & Cafe

reviews.text:
5/5 – A must-try hidden gem!
This was my third time at Saleem, and each time feels like discovering it all over again. The sizzling anjera, the perfectly spiced veggies, the rich and flavorful dips—it’s a full sensory experience. The smell of the food hits you before you even sit down, and the traditional Ethiopian coffee seals the whole moment. The owner cooks everything himself with so much care and passion, and you can taste it in every bite. He’s just now expanding the restaurant, and it deserves all the love. Warm, welcoming, and unforgettable. Don’t sleep on this place—it’s worth it!
Best Ethiopian restaurant in Austin.the food is Delicious and very nice people.
Selam Cafe has a perfect sized international market and great menu items for lunch/ dinner… big portions and fair prices, thank you Sitota and friends!

A real gem! Authentic, delicious and fresh food. Limited menu but the two dishes I had were amazing! Coming from NYC I have been looking for authentic ethnic food spots and this place reminded me of the favorite Ethiopian spots I used to go to. Very friendly and accommodating staff. Also a great place to pick up spices and other Ethiopian speciality groceries.
Selam mart the best i ever seen good food and good service

formatted_address: 410 W Whitestone Blvd, Cedar Park, TX 78613, United States
name: Injera & Beyond

reviews.text: Came here for the first time! We ordered shiro and vegetarian dishes on plant based menu! It took a quite awhile but the vegetarian plate we got was really good! Injera was perfect texture and tart flavor with delicious sauce and food items! Shiro needed some umami seasoning 🧂 but other than that our visit was pleasant. Would love to be back! Cheers 🥂

What a wonderful place to dine. Service was exceptional food was as well. The atmosphere is great and warming. We walked in late on Saturday 9pm they closed  at 10 so I was worried that it might have been too late to dine in and order.  It wasn’t.  My husband and I were the only ones there dinning. The waitress was so gracious and caring that we got  what we wanted.  We were visiting the city and wanted Ethiopian food. I have several fav restaurants for Ethiopian food in different cities and this is an added on for me.  The owner is very polite and loves what she does your can tell. This is a gem worth visiting and the foodie in me was doing a happy dance all the way to my Hotel!!

They're still in soft launch, so no expectations, and they blew it out of the park. We got the meats for 2 plate and Ethiopian spiced tea. The food was delicious and it's a nice, clean location. We'll definitely be back.

Heard about this restaurant from our son and went to try it out as a family.  We have never had Ethiopian food before.

It was amazing! 🤩 The injera was soft, spongy, and every dish had its own unique flavor — the greens, lentils, and veggie mix were super tasty, and the spicy stews were rich and full of depth. We also ordered a few dishes of lentil and beef sambusas which were very tasty when dipped in the hummus.

I loved how everything came together when scooped up with the injera — such a fun way to eat and share food. Finished it off with a Swiss roll for dessert that reminded me of tiramisu.
Portions were generous, the colors were vibrant, and honestly the whole experience just felt warm and inviting. The restaurant is nicely decorated and we got to talk to the owner. This is a family operation and it’s all authentic.  The real deal! The staff were all super friendly.

Definitely going back for round two soon!👍

Celebrated my friend’s birthday tonite and the food was ‘beyond’ delicious!  Started with the beef  sambusas and they just made us more excited for what was to come!  The dipping sauce was heaven :)  We did the yengus combo (meat combo) platter for 2 and loved it.  We always gravitate towards spicier dishes so the key wot (spicy beef stew) and doro wot (spicy chicken stew) were our favorites.  It would be nice to have a “build your own combo” plate but this was a nice option to have a little bit of everything.  The lamb tibs were so tender and flavorful and came with a spicy dipping sauce that I would love to bottle up!  Our servers were so friendly and attentive.  We’ll definitely be back!  Thankful for a piece of Ethiopia in our neighborhood!

formatted_address: 2804 N Interstate Hwy 35, Austin, TX 78705, United States
name: Aster's Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text:
Good food, good service. We got the combination plate which was like $30. You can select 4 veggies and 4 meats off of the menu except lamb or something. They were all flavourful and tasty. We even mixed and ate them, so many flavours from one platter, enjoyed every bit of it. I wasn’t a big fan of the bread… kinda sour..
But overall, nice place, workers and tasty food

Ode to Aster’s Ethiopian:

In Austin's heart, where flavors intertwine,
Resides Aster's, an Ethiopian treasure fine.
Though lacking fancied air, its charm's sincere,
Its true allure lies in the dishes, clear.

Authenticity permeates each bite,
Transporting taste buds on a blissful flight.
A tapestry of flavors, rich and true,
Unveils Ethiopia's culinary view.

For veggie lovers, a haven it be,
With ample choices, varied and free.
From injera's tang to lentils' gentle sway,
Aster's embraces vegetarians' array.

And at the lunch buffet, a feast untold,
A bounteous offering, a value bold.
Sample Ethiopia's heritage so grand,
With spices, stews, and bread by your command.

Though modest in ambiance it may be,
The soul of Aster's blooms triumphantly.
For in its kitchen, passion truly thrives,
Crafting traditional feasts that delight lives.

So venture forth and savor the embrace,
Of Aster's, where authenticity takes place.
Let go of frills, let flavors guide your way,
In Aster's Ethiopian Restaurant, today!

It’s our first time trying Ethiopian cuisine and I must say it wasn’t disappointing at all. Food was tasty and didn’t have to wait for too long. The texture of the flat bread was very interesting and felt like a lotus leaf - very soft. We ordered the vegetarian platter that has all blends from the house with Ethiopian tea and dessert.

My grandmother and I dined here while visiting Austin,TX. We loved the food, the service was great and the atmosphere was sweet and authentic, it felt very "homey" as they had family photos up, real ethiopian table cloth. You normally would eat with your hands, but they can supply their guests with silverware if you wish. We took an Uber there, so I cannot remember the parking situation. We shared a plate, which was more than enough. 5/5 would recommend and we wish to be back someday again.

Do you know the fairy tale with the small shack in the middle of nowhere, where you enter and there is a palace inside? Aster's is the place and if you don't even find marble and gold, you can find the best Ethiopian food there is! Generous portions and a menu where you want to try everything!

formatted_address: 5903 Wellington Dr, Austin, TX 78723, United States
name: Mama’z Soul Kitchen

reviews.text: I have had so many delicious meals from here. The plates are so big and yes can get a little messy but thats to be expected when they aren’t greedy with their servings. Great customer service and clean. The food is flavored so well and the lamb chops Ive had one mother’s day were fall off the bone good. Her tomahawk is divine!!  Her Boudin balls are so big and delicious. I have had a few and nothing comes close to hers. Seafood is my favorite and ever since I found this place I no longer eat seafood boils, anywhere but here. Her sweet tea is so fruity and tasty, a must try!
One of the best soulfood places in Austin. The food is delicious and flavorful and you definitely get your money's worth. Food,tea,and desserts are delicious 😋

Every time I order or go to pick up a plate, Tieisha and her staff are pleasant and professional. But, can we talk about the food? The plates she sells are portioned to feed at least 3 people. And the food is tasteful,  filling, and delicious. If you are ever in the area or looking for some good old soul food, this is where it's at. So look for the hot pink food truck. You will not be disappointed.
Very generous portions. Excellent flavor. Well seasoned food. Will not disappoint.

Always a great portion that is only overtaken by the great taste! This food truck offers tge best meals, serving size and her son makes the best tasting deserts I've ever tasted. The way she serves everyone with a big beautiful smile and treats every customer as her own family. Highly recommend ANYTHING and EVERYTHING off her menu. Them BBQ plates are my favorite

formatted_address: 2103 W Slaughter Ln, Austin, TX 78748, United States
name: Winston's Kitchen

reviews.text: Cheaper than a mortgage, but feels like home. Been wanting to try this place for sometime, I walk by all the time. Money has been really tight; I am sure a few of you can feel me on that. Took a chance and glad I did. I don’t know if the picture captures how awesome the portions are but I am certainly going to be able to stretch this a few days. That is a huge blessing to me. Food that has good energy without me having to cook. Especially, after a long day. Hard to find food made by someone that brings the joy of a home cooked meal. Worthy of stopping in as often as you can. Food fills bellies, but food like Winston’s food lifts spirits. Cabbage is best you’ll ever have by the way.

Delicious!  I visited the area because I was seeking Puerto Rican (PR) food, but the PR food truck closed early, so I decided to go to Winston's Jamaican food truck instead. Wow!  The jerk chicken quarters were seasoned and cooked perfectly over a bed of rice with beans and veggies.  Great price for delicious, plentiful plates!  I look forward to going back and trying even more menu items next time.

I have eaten authentic Jamaican cuisine in 5 states including at least 4 locations in 2 of those states. Probably 15 total places over the years that I frequented. Winston's food is the absolute best. My other google account was a top 1% food reviewer and as soon as I get it back I'll post on there. This is hands down the best Jamaican food I've ever had. And the oxtail is the second best meal I've ever had (and 3rd too!). Winston is the best, 2 of the best 3 meals I've had in my life. Jah bless you! I could not recommend it any higher. Much love Winston 🤙

Edit: I've had the curry chicken twice and the oxtail twice. Both out of this world. I can not wait to try the brisket.

Absolutely delicious!!!
We ordered jerk chicken plate, beef patties, chicken wrap, beef wrap, and plantains. At the last minute we added wings and they did not disappoint!! They were fabulous!! You can’t go wrong with anything on the menu. Not to mention the service was incredibly friendly. Highly recommend Winston’s!

I foolishly listened to some pale person to come eat here. The food is flavorless and honestly nasty and not authentic at all!! Generous portion sizes but of course they’re trying to get that nasty mess out the door. The nastiest Jamaican food I’ve ever had to be honest

formatted_address: 10630 Menchaca Rd Bldg A, Austin, TX 78748, United States
name: Austin's Habibi LLC on manchaca

reviews.text: Today I tried the Gyro Plate and the Habibi Fries, and both were absolutely delicious! The gyro plate was flavorful, fresh, and filling, while the Habibi fries were perfectly crispy with just the right seasoning. On top of the great food, the customer service was excellent—friendly, welcoming, and attentive, which made the whole experience even better. Definitely recommend!

Austin Habibi is always a go-to stop for me when I’m driving down Manchaca. The food is consistently flavorful and satisfying, and the team’s attitude is always welcoming and positive. It’s a small black trailer with a focused menu—variations on a theme—but they nail it every time. I’ve never once been disappointed, and every bite reminds me why I keep coming back. Highly recommend!

The combo plate was delicious. Everything from the rice, salad, hummus, and meats were so flavorful. We enjoyed our meal.

With hummus included, it would be great if it came with a little pita. But regardless, this was truly amazing.

Edit: Combo plate was 11/10. Even the rice was super flavorful. The only con is for $15 it doesn’t come with a side pita. Most places include at least a half or quarter pita.

Pita was perfect and fluffy, chicken and gyro were great, proportions were perfect, and the fries were fresh and crisp.

My only complaint is that the “spicy red sauce” on the fries tasted an offal lot like ketchup, not even spicy ketchup, just straight up Heinz from the bottle. I haven’t met a red sauce at a halal place i didn’t like but I absolutely hate ketchup. I discarded those fries and it came out to about the amount I wanted.

The pita was so fluffy that the ketchup is water under the bridge tho. I’ll probably be ordering the plate with a side pita next time anyways

After going to the Hive and passing this place up I’m glad I had your food for dinner! First I want to shout out the gentlemen Anise who helped me. He is a sweetheart & told me loves talking to his customers & said that he wishes the best for the owner of Austin Habibi food truck. He has great work ethic, and makes sure that all customers receive a great portion of food. I’m grateful for the connection we had. Second the food was delicious! I got the chicken plate, which was seasoned perfectly. I will be back to try more menu options! I enjoyed my food inside the Hive with no issues from anyone saying I couldn’t eat it inside. The food truck offers limited seating outside, but I believe it is provided by the Hive… give this place a try next time!

formatted_address: 4912 Monterey Oaks Blvd, Austin, TX 78749, United States
name: Chaat Ka Chaskaaa

reviews.text: They are really good w.r.t the authenticity of Chaat! One of the great chaats I have ever had in the US! Will really recommend the ragda pattice and dahi puri too and their paneer sp. sandwich! One of the gems of Sunset Valley food specialities 🙏🏻😊❤️

Tried the Dahi Puri and Sev Puri. Dahi puri was crunchy yet soft, creamy, and so satisfying! Sev puri had the absolute burst of flavors! The perfect mix of sweet, tangy, and spicy. However, would appreciate if they really add extra spice when we ask cause some of us like spicy food 🌶️

Great Desi chaat place with a variety of options. Loved the samosa chaat, dahi vada, vada pav, mirchi bajji and the pista Falooda. The aroma out of the food truck kind of enhanced our appetite while waiting. All tasted fresh and delicious. The samosa chaat has a bit of a kick with the right amount of spice.
The golgappa with ragda was the only item that we tried that was just average and a little bland.
Ambiance is just ok considering this is a food truck parked next to a gas station and car wash. There are a couple of benches and cots to accommodate seating for a dozen or so.
Overall, I'm very satisfied with the taste and service, and will keep coming back and try more items. Ja Simran Ja, aur kuch ley aa.. :)

Chaat Ka Chaskaaa – Chattar Pattar #1 offers a decent variety of street-style snacks. The flavors are satisfying and portions fair. It’s a nice spot for a quick bite when you're in the mood for something chatpata, though not the most memorable experience.
Taste was not good, too much oil in the food. They also added a default tip even after I asked to remove it, so people should double-check their bills before paying.

formatted_address: 12400 Amherst Dr, Austin, TX 78727, United States
name: Mama Sol's Soul Food Truck & Catering

reviews.text: I had Mama Sol’s  food tonight for dinner. I can honestly say I probably haven't left more than two reviews in my life for anything, but it is truly my honor to leave a review for Mama Sol’s. I had smothered pork chops, candied yams, and fried cabbage. The candied yams were the best I’ve ever had and I’m 67 years old and I’ve had a lot of yams in my life. The smothered pork chops were huge, & you get two, they were thick and very tender, and the sauce that they were cooked in was real tasty. The pork chops were served on a bed of rice, and the rice was also cooked perfectly. The fried cabbage was excellent. I don’t think I’ve ever gotten fried cabbage cooked as perfectly as mine was tonight. And then there was homemade cornbread as an added bonus. I didn’t eat there. I brought my food home for my dinner and I’m really glad I did because I had enough left over that I can eat at least one more meal if not two. The owner was very personable, and I loved hearing his story. He said that his mother and grandmother taught him to cook, and it’s always been one of his favorite things to do. You can definitely see and taste the love that he puts into his food! I would have never expected to get such great home cooking out of a food truck.  I will definitely be going back
This was literally one of the best plates of food I have ever had! You could taste the love that went into this dish. 🤤

I only got sides this trip but must say all were excellent. My opinion is one can tell a lot about a place by sides. The sweet potato fries, okra and fried cabbage all excelled. The sausage crumbles added to the cabbage was kickin and the spicing was right on point.
Everyone working was super friendly and seemed to enjoy being there. Quality food and attitude prevails. Thanks for being

Holy crap this place is good. I got the gravy pork chops and they were the best pork chops I’d ever had. This place is tastier than anything in a 10 mile radius, and the staff are wonderfully friendly. It’s a little pricey, but with the quality and portion size that you get, it’s more than worth the price. I’ll definitely be coming back to try their other dishes.

Outstanding food and customer service! We got the Smothered Pork Chops and the Oxtail - both were excellent. And the sides? Ohhhhh… fried cabbage, collard greens and okra. We will be back for more. Great value for wonderful food.

formatted_address: 817 W 5th St, Austin, TX 78703, United States
name: Austin's Habibi on 5 street

reviews.text:
I have been coming here for the last year since I live nearby and I always get combo hummus , which is $14 dollars (an entree item). Today I got the same thing, and now my blood is boiling - the portion is HALF of what it used to be.

Why would I pay $14 WHOLE DOLLARS for this extremely mediocre halal food! I despise this place. Pathetic. They gave me literally a PALM SIZED PORTION of meat for $14 dollars, I am so mad. SAVE YOUR MONEY, DO NOT COME HERE.

This is a food truck set amongst other food trucks on a corner of 5th. Seating is outdoors is outside and dumpy.  HOWEVER, The chicken plate with rice, hummus and greek salad was primo good. The chicken is small bits with curry taste served on awesomely seasoned rice. The greek salad is the norm and tasty. The hummus is something special. The whole thing mixed up and eaten together is bursting with flavor. I got a bogo deal on UBER EATS. So good and craveable. Usually Mediterranean food tastes blah to me but this- spicy without being “hot.”

Falafel plate with fries on the side was my order, and I loved it. The plate came decorated nicely with sauces, and the fries had that extra white and red sauce drizzle that made them so tasty. Service was fast, and the staff was very friendly.

Great food truck! Super friendly staff, great food, and solid prices. I live right by and eat here (far) too much - staff is always super friendly, food is consistently delicious, and the price is very reasonable!

The chicken over rice was so flavorful and came with that white and red sauce that makes every bite amazing. I also got baklava for dessert, and it was sweet and flaky. Staff were super welcoming from the moment I walked up.

formatted_address: 3301 Steck Ave STE 106, Austin, TX 78757, United States
name: Shishman Halal Mediterranean

reviews.text: I had a gyro from their truck at the US Grand Prix twice last weekend. It was delicious - but the fast and friendly service really set them apart from every other vendor. My wife had the falafel and it was fresh rather than being the dry and overcooked offering from the other food vendors.

It’s in a good location. But the gyro chicken plate we ordered was not the gyro we ate several other Mediterranean restaurants.
