They carve the chicken, but here they reheated chicken and served it on a plate. Falafel was sour and clearly not fresh. Sorry for the negative review. Maybe their equipment was broken, I dont know.

I recently dined at Shishman Halal Restaurant and was thoroughly impressed! The service was top-notch, attentive and friendly staff made us feel welcome.

The food was outstanding! Fresh, flavorful and generously portioned. The menu offered a wide variety of halal options, catering to diverse tastes.

Ambiance: Cozy, clean and inviting.

Will return for sure!

We decided to have Mediterranean for lunch and while googling I came across Shishman Mediterranean. When I first saw the Amazon gift card offer it didn't seem realistic but I ordered it anyway. I placed my order at 9:14am and it was delivered at 11:30am when I requested. The best part was that I received a $46 gift card before the food was delivered. I was planning on buying a Patio Chair for my backyard. I bought it with this gift card😍

Great service and a unique campaign! In addition to offering delicious food, Shishman  also gives an Amazon gift card for 10% of the order. This small but meaningful gesture shows that they are truly customer-oriented. I was going to order that catering anyway, so why not get a gift card in return?

formatted_address: 2008 S Congress Ave, Austin, TX 78704, United States
name: WEIRD FOOD

reviews.text: The food was amazing and the service is unmatched! I love how many vegan options there are and Saad was very nice. I also appreciate how late they are open everyday. 🙏🏼

Had the beef gyro wrap here late at night, and it was a game-changer. My friend and I were… let’s say, under the influence, and thought it was incredible. Returned another evening while entirely sober for double-check, and yes—it was just as delicious. Great late-night spot with friendly service.

Watched a band at C- Boys and had some awesome food from Weird Food which is located essentially in C- Boys side lot but Weird does have its own entrance from the sidewalk as well.  The food was excellent and the gentleman managing the truck was delightful to speak with.  I had the beef gyro with hummus and my wife had the vegan chickpea wrap. I came back during the band's intermission break and picked up an order of loaded fries as well which was very good! Highly recommend when you're in the neighborhood. Reasonable prices and fantastic food - a great combination!
You will be a better person having eaten here.  Order at least 2 meals, you’ll thank yourself later. Don’t forget dessert and tell Saag I said hi!
The food, service, and atmosphere was amazing ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️  i didn’t know what to get and Mr. Saj (the owner) provided a plate and it tasted so good and like home!

formatted_address: 1330 Aquarena Springs Dr Ste 103, San Marcos, TX 78666, United States
name: African Eats & Market

reviews.text:
So happy I found this place! It’s a small African store that has a bunch of essentials like jollof rice, palm oil, Agege bread, fufu, and different soups like egusi and ogbono.

They don’t have a full restaurant setup yet, but they do have frozen jollof and soups you can just heat up—and they actually taste really good.

The people there are super nice, and it just feels good supporting a small African-owned spot that’s trying to grow. If you’ve been craving a taste of home, definitely check them out!

Great place to get all of your international foods, very good prices as well. You can also order famous african dishes from their restaurant I highly recommend! Thank you for your acceptance and kind customer service. I am so happy & excited I found this place in the area I'll definitely be back!
Literal perfection. I use to have to drive out or order online to get African pantry staples. This place is very convenient.
This is your one stop shop for African condiments, spices, and food.
Amazing owner and great selection for cooking, also great snacks and readymade meatpies and scotch eggs! Definitely worth visiting

formatted_address: Pickup @ Expo Window, 3400 Comsouth Dr, Austin, TX 78744, United States
name: Whole Lotta Soul

reviews.text: I'd already read the glowing reviews, but I STILL was not prepared for the deliciousness that I was in store for! Man, you can taste the love in every bite!! I ordered my food online and it was simple, and received a call from the owner stating that one of the sides is ordered was not available but if I wanted to wait he would oblige. I opted for a substitute but how often does that level of service occur these days? The gentleman was super nice, the food was amazing, I would highly recommend Whole Lotta Soul!!!

Food is so good my big back ordered 2 plates. I ordered a first one had a little taste and went back for the second plate. The food came out quickly and it was so yummy! The gentleman that cooked the food ( also the owner) was also very kind. I am from Houston so it makes me very happy to be able to get some soul food😋😋. 10/10 everything was wonderful! I am definitely coming back soon.

The food was A-M-A-Z-I-N-G!! There was a short wait, BUT I didn't mind because the food was piping hot and fresh!!! The oxtails are 🔥! OMG...they are FULL of flavor! (11 out of 10) It is definitely worth the 35 minutes drive. The mac and cheese was good as well! They had the right balance of cheese and pasta; and a decent pull with the cheese. (8 out of 10) I am more of a creamy mac girl, that is the reason I gave it an 8 but the flavor is definitely there! The price was definitely fair for the amount of food that was given! The owner, Shaq, customer service was wonderful! You can definitely tell he puts the love and pride in his food! I am definitely going back to try the other items on the menu!! Worth the time and price for great food and customer service!!
Be mindful that this is a pick up location, with tables to sit and eat on the outside only if you choose. Very nice set up.

The owner, Shaq, cooks the food fresh. It's piping hot and delicious. We got the fried fish (not pictured because I devoured it too fast. But it was crispy and seasoned well. I ate it with no sauce it was that good.) and the oxtails with cabbage, mac and cheese, and candied yams. Everything was seasoned deliciously. Will definitely be back next time we're in the area.

The owner came and greeted us with our food and it was delicious, tastes amazing with plenty of flavor. got the red drink and chicken brown stew with yams and Mac. Yams were really good, brown stew was good. I recommend getting the cornbrea, it was soft and fluffy, goes well with the stew and red drink to wash it down. 10/10 would come again and worker does all the work BY HIMSELF.

formatted_address: 1011 S Congress Ave Bldg 2 Suite 180, Austin, TX 78704, United States
name: Aba Austin

reviews.text:
I used to visit Aba in Chicago and it was one of my all-time favorite spots,  so I was very excited to try the Austin location. And let me tell you… it did not disappoint!

Aba has a great wine selection, excellent cocktails, and the food is absolutely delicious. The ambience is beautiful, modern, and warm perfect for a date night, dinner with friends, or a nice celebration.

Reservations are highly recommended (just like in Chicago). But if you have to wait, the patio and bar area are super pleasant,  you can relax with a drink and enjoy the vibe while your table gets ready.

We ordered a variety of dishes to share and everything was outstanding:
• Crispy Short Rib Hummus – a must-order!
• Whipped Feta – creamy and so flavorful
• Shawarma Spiced Prime Skirt
• Lamb & Beef Kefta
• Grilled Halloumi

We were 3 adults (2 men and 1 woman), and this was the perfect amount of food. We all left happy and satisfied;  and again, no room for dessert!

Service was friendly and attentive both times I visited.
Aba is definitely a must-try in Austin.

Aba is a beautiful restaurant with a modern and quaint vibe. There’s both indoor and outdoor seating, and we chose to sit outside.  It was very cozy and the temperature was perfect.  It was a great spot to relax and enjoy the evening.

The service was very friendly and attentive.  We only had drinks and dessert.  The menu is somewhat pricey.   The frozen yogurt was light and refreshing. The pistachio panna cotta was interesting both the panna cotta and the orange topping were good on their own, but together the combination didn’t quite work for me.

Paid parking was difficult to find but this was a lovely spot with great ambiance.

Aba had been on our list of restaurants we wanted to visit and were finally able to get in this time around. The wait was worth it. The food is amazing!!

Great choice of cocktails and I'm pretty sure we ordered one of everything on the menu. The haloumi and fish were favorites from the main menu and the cake and frozen yogurt from the dessert.

Pro tip, reservations on Sundays sure easier to get. Lots of street parking available. Courtyard is beautiful.. I suggest sitting out there.

We had an amazing experience at Aba! From the moment we walked in, everything exceeded our expectations. The atmosphere was beautiful, relaxing, and full of great energy.

Our server Aiden truly made the evening special — attentive, friendly, and knowledgeable about the menu. He went above and beyond to make sure everything was perfect, and his recommendations were spot-on.

The food was absolutely delicious — we had Lamb & Beef Kefta, Charred Eggplant, and Beef Tenderloin Kebab with a mix of rice and salad. Every dish was cooked perfectly, full of flavor, and beautifully presented. We also enjoyed San Pellegrino Sparkling Water alongside our meal, which complemented everything nicely.

Highly recommend Aba for anyone looking for an outstanding dining experience with incredible service. Thank you, Aiden, for making our night memorable — we’ll definitely be coming back!

I’m pretty sure this is one of the trendier restaurants in Austin, and the interior proves it—beautifully designed with a warm, modern Mediterranean feel that makes you want to linger.

The menu has a wide range of spreads and entrées. We kept it light this time with chicken kebab, crispy potatoes, and traditional hummus. Everything was delicious and the hummus with fresh pita was a standout I’d absolutely recommend. As someone who loves Mediterranean cuisine, I’d happily return, especially to try their selection of Eastern European wines.

formatted_address: 3825 Lake Austin Blvd #201, Austin, TX 78703, United States
name: Quince Lakehouse

reviews.text:
We got here before our reservations time and had to wait for like 4 minutes to be seated which was not bad at all. This place is so nice and has a good energy!!! It’ll be a great spot for a date night. We sat in the patio and enjoyed the lake view. Food was absolutely top notch!!!! We got Shrimp Tempura in spicy aiol and Ahi Tuna Tosatadas as appetizer which both are PERFECT!!! As main dish, we got burger and pan seared Halibut and again both were amazing!! The fries that came with the burger did not disappoint at all! 😩 😋
My only concern is that we got two appetizers and two main dishes and didn’t fill like we’re totally full (stuffed)😄. So if you’re looking to go somewhere that you get bigger portions and maybe you feel stuffed afterwards that might not be your best choice! Their menu selection was small which shows their quality and the perfect taste that you’re about to experience!!! Would definitely come back here for special occasions since it was kinda pricey!!! Also they only had All Gender Bathroom and that was not fun. I did not feel comfortable washing my hands next two big dudes in the bathroom! 😑

The food here is amazing. My first impression of course was how stunning the restaurant was but I wasn’t expecting the food to be beyond amazing! The truffle risotto is to die for. With perfect crispy kale on top, the risotto has perfect consistency, heaviness and the right hint of truffle. The Nola eggs Benedict - I’ve never had anything like it. There is some sauce that makes it so good and the rosemary fries… don’t get me started. The grilled chicken sandwich was also SO GOOD. the mushroom and kale is seasoned to perfection. I’ve never enjoyed a chicken sandwich more. I highly recommend.

Food was amazing! Loved the Rock Shrimp Tempura. Service was great and of course it's right on the lake which is always a plus! We had such a nice server (I think his name was Khalid?) and the manager even came out and brought us dessert. Such a great sisters night out!

If you haven’t been to Quince Lakehouse, go now, it’s that good. Gorgeous lake views, lively crowd, and excellent food.
All the dishes (7) we ordered were good but these 3 stood out:
The tuna tostada was pure sunshine on a plate, fresh, citrusy, and perfectly crisp; the grilled octopus was tender and packed with flavor, and the melon & arugula salad tasted like summer in every bite.
We wrapped it up with their cobbler and tiramisu, which were the perfect sweet finish.
For service, the whole team was fantastic, but Ela was stellar — she made our night!

Thank you Carlitos$$. You really made our night, we could see John was doing a great job but had several busy busy tables. We're easy, so thanks for jumping in. Love the vibe here, fun but upscale. The ragu was delicious, the tortilla soup was perfect after a chilly boat ride around Lake Austin.

formatted_address: 9400 B Arboretum Blvd, Austin, TX 78759, United States
name: Eddie V's Prime Seafood

reviews.text: Everything was an amazing from the Espresso martini to the Banana Foster Butter Cake.  The crab cake had delicious buttery chunks of crab meat.  The burrata and beet salad was pleasant though I thought that it would be warm given the description of “roasted” .  The Parmesan sole was fabulous, the bone-in ribeye was perfectly cooked with a blue cheese crust.  It was a delightful birthday dinner  with my son.

I had the filet medallions oscar. I ordered my steak medium and got a rare steak. I wasn't very impressed by that, somehow, I feel like if you pay $70 for a plate of food, the cooks should know how to prepare the meat without it being sent back.

My cocktail was absolutely worth the $17 paid for the 3 ounces of alcohol. Wonderfully prepared.  The scalloped potatoes were also fantastic, and the lump crab flavorful.

The whitestaff was on point. I absolutely loved our waiter, Roger. He was attentive and engaging, and just overall very easy.

The atmosphere was quite antiquated, and if you're going to charge anywhere from $60 to $150 a plate, there shouldn't be three inches of dust in the bathroom on the doors. I understand that that is a weird thing to be picky about. But, if I'm going to pay that much for dinner, I expect the restaurant to be in immaculate condition. Classy even.

Overall, I would say it was a good visit for a new experience in a once a lifetime thing, but I wouldn't repeat the experience at that cost, again just based on cleanliness alone.

I have never had a bad experience here but this visit was exceptional. I reserved a table in the bar area to celebrate a work achievement, which I described in Opentable. When we arrived, the staff had signed a card congratulating the moment. The service was impeccable and the food was amazing. I would absolutely recommend the Arboretum location in Austin to anyone who asked.

I haven't written a review in a long time, but Eddie V's really does deserve it. My wife and I went for our 7th anniversary, and couldn't have had a better time. We got there a bit early, and while they offered to go ahead and seat us were also cool with us sitting at the bar to enjoy a couple of excellent cocktails. Even the bread and butter, which you'd think would be pretty standard, really stood out. From there we took our seats and were immediately greeted by Nona, who did an outstanding job of taking care of us the entire time. The food was delicious. Everything came out exactly as requested and if we had a baby sitter every Sunday, you can bet this is where we'd be.

We’ve been to Eddie Vs on many occasions and it is always outstanding. Today, my wife and I got our motorcycle licenses after a grueling two days of learning. So a celebration was in order. In this visit we spared no expense.

Had the shrimp cocktail, caviar, filet with lobster tails, wagyu strip with lobster tails, a 24 Karat cocktail and a smoked Old Fashion, plus the incredible crab fried rice. To end they made us a special desert and set it on fire, along with our crème brûlée. With tip, $525.

Our server Farzan (spelling…sorry) was incredible. The pinnacle of attention and caring. It’s quiet in general even when busy as it is a date or business dealing kind of place. An occasional large party may raise the volume. However it’s always respectable.

And for this visit, the wagyu and caviar were some of the best I have ever had. The caviar melted in your mouth and the warm blinis were amazing. The horseradish and Parmesan encrusted steak (cooked medium well…sorry) is literally the best steak I have ever had. I’m very serious. I’ve eaten at a lot of fancy places and all the way to Texas Roadhouse. This was the BEST steak. Juicy, tender, and everything you would expect from wagyu. But this one? Superb.

While we may not always spend this much at this establishment, it was well deserved.

formatted_address: 3901 Promontory Point Dr, Austin, TX 78744, United States
name: Distant Relatives

reviews.text: The brisket, mustard sauce and spicy Cole slaw were fantastic. The meat was perfect -- juicy and delicious. Combine that with the beautiful grounds and taproom at Meanwhile Brewing, plus some seriously good beer, and you have a winner. I'll be back!

Not only is the BBQ delicious, but the grits are the best we've had. And the black eyed peas were flat out superb.

AND the bread was GRILLED. As it should be!!
Wow this was great BBQ. Best I’ve had in a while. Chicken and pork belly were the standouts imo. Sides were terrific, especially black eyed peas and the grits.

The bbq is great, all of their food is good.
I have to say though, I have been here twice, the woman who works at the register could use some training in professionalism and courtesy. She barely acknowledges you, doesn't smile or says thank you. While I love the food their help could use some help! Lol

Finally had a chance to visit Distant Relatives trailer at Meanwhile Brewing after multiple friends recommending it. I’m glad I went and will definitely be back! I got the brisket sandwich and the sausage mac n cheese. I love the West and South African spices in the food. Food comes out quickly. I’m sure it gets quite busy on weekends. Thanks guys!

formatted_address: 315 Congress Ave., Austin, TX 78701, United States
name: Swift's Attic

reviews.text: Came for NYE dinner and everything was amazing. Service, cocktails, and the pre fixe menu was 10/10. So much attention to detail and incredible food throughout the entire night. It was a perfect way to bring in the new year!

A big shout out to Swift’s Attic for an incredible introduction to their new Executive Chef Nay Castillo. If you’re looking for flavors that pop with clear identity, Chef Castillo puts a lot of dimensions (sweet, sour, bitter, cold, crunchy, hot, melty, crispy) in each of the dishes. The big test was whether my wife’s sophisticated palate would enjoy it, and it’s a testament that we walked away a happy and very full family. What an amazing dinner and service! Our favorites were the hamachi crudo, lamb pops, and fried chicken. My son demolished the edamame with multi-salts and pop rocks. We had an amazing time. Go check out Swift’s Attic and Chef Castillo’s new menu!

First, I want to say that our servers were very kind, attentive, and doing their best throughout the night. No complaints toward them at all. They were clearly working hard in a difficult situation.

Unfortunately, the New Year’s Eve prix fixe experience was extremely disappointing. It took over an hour for our table to receive the first course, and several menu items were modified or substituted without any communication. It was also obvious that food was running short, as our table was served noticeably smaller portions than tables around us.

We ended up leaving close to midnight, and given the long delays, it would have been appropriate to at least offer a cocktail or a glass of wine. We purchased a bottle of prosecco as soon as we sat down, and it was nearly empty by the time our first course finally arrived.

There’s a sign near the entrance defining “hangry,” and the irony couldn’t have been more fitting. By that point, our entire section was hungry and frustrated, and the sign unintentionally summed up the experience.

Based on the restaurant’s reputation, we expected a well-executed New Year’s Eve service. Instead, the lack of preparation and communication made this a poor experience overall.

Absolutely outstanding experience at Swift’s Attic! Chef Nay delivered food that was truly off the charts—every dish was packed with flavor and creativity. The environment is amazing as always, with an energy that makes every visit feel special. If you’re in Austin and haven’t been yet, you’re missing out. Swift’s Attic is a must-try!

I visited Swift’s Attic for the first time yesterday and was  impressed. Everything I tried was delicious and felt different from what you typically get at other restaurants. The roasted cabbage was  amazing, the gem salad was fresh and had a nice crunch and even a spice to it, and the lamb chops were also great. I really liked the interesting approaches to their food, and it sounds like they change their menu periodically, which makes me excited to go back and try whatever new dishes they introduce. Definitely a spot I’ll be returning to!!

formatted_address: 10000 Research Blvd Suite 4602, Austin, TX 78759, United States
name: The Cheesecake Factory

reviews.text:
This is my second time dining at this restaurant. The place is beautifully decorated, spacious, and always filled with many customers. The lively atmosphere and the bar area make it even more inviting. I’m impressed every time I come here.

The staff provide great service—they are friendly, attentive, and make sure customers are well taken care of, which makes the dining experience smooth and enjoyable. The menu offers a variety of delicious American-style dishes.

I will definitely come back again.😊

It had been a long time since I’d been to The Cheesecake Factory, and in the past I only ever stuck to the entrées. This visit was different. I went specifically for the cheesecake — and, if I’m honest, for the company I was blessed to share the evening with.

The atmosphere that night was warm, dim, and almost romantic in its own way. The kind of setting where conversation comes easy, time slows down, and a simple dessert turns into something a little more meaningful.

I ordered the Peanut Butter Butterfinger Cheesecake, and it was incredible — rich, oversized, and full of flavor. It paired perfectly with their in-house Old Fashioned, the bourbon smoothing everything together. My friend chose the Fresh Strawberry Cheesecake with fruit and cream, and it was just as beautiful as it was delicious.

The truth is, the cheesecake was amazing… but the experience was even better. Great atmosphere, wonderful conversation, and a moment that felt a little special in a world that often moves too fast.

Yes, the prices are on the higher side, but some moments are worth the cost. This one certainly was.

We came in tonight with a reservation for 7:15 pm and were seated right away even with how busy it was! The hostess (I didn’t catch her name) had a great pleasant attitude even while dealing with a large number of hangry guests. We were sat in a nice quiet corner at a booth where Paige took great care of us. I got my favorite (Korean cauliflower) and we got some fried zucchini for the table. Paige was quick with the refills and offered great recommendations to replace things they were out of and the kitchen got our food our remarkably quick given the amount of guests in the lobby. I also decided I had enough room after dinner to get the strawberry short cake. While I wasn’t able to eat much of the the bit that I did was delicious! I love coming to this cheesecake and will be back in the future!

I went here as an invite to celebrate a birthday. I would have ordered the chicken tenders but I wanted to try something different so I ordered the crispy pineapple chicken and shrimp with white rice (without the snow peas). I made a great decision because it tasted amazing. The sweet and sour sauce is a bonus. And as always, I had to have my Cinnamon Cinnabon Swirl Cheesecake 😁💙

We visited this Cheesecake Factory location on a Sunday evening, and unfortunately, it was a huge letdown—especially when compared to the Toronto branch, Orlando branch, which we’ve enjoyed multiple times and it was our favorite place to go.

I ordered a burger that was completely tasteless. The bun was supposed to be crispy as described in the menu, but it was soft and soggy. The lettuce and tomato were low quality—definitely not fresh. The worst part was the sweet potato fries: they were soggy and stale. I asked to have them replaced, and the second batch was over-salted to the point of being inedible.

We also ordered the glazed chicken pasta, and it was disappointing as well. You could barely find any chicken in it—it was mostly noodles and sauce.

Honestly, both meals were far from what we expect from Cheesecake Factory. We left unsatisfied and disappointed.

I would appreciate it if management could contact me regarding this experience. If you want us to give this location another try, I believe the least that should be offered is a complimentary meal so we can experience the quality food and service Cheesecake Factory is known for. As it stands, we won’t be coming back based on this visit alone.

formatted_address: 10106 Menchaca Rd, Austin, TX 78748, United States
name: Armadillo Den

reviews.text: Plenty of food trucks with great food. The bar is big and moves quick. Lots of seating areas and TVs / one huge screen if you're there to watch sports as most people are. Dog friendly! Great atmosphere, nice and relaxing!

I’m such a big fan of the Armadillo Den! I have a good time every time I go. Good country music, good vibes, beautiful lights set up and everyone is always having fun. It’s the perfect spot for family gatherings.

This is an incredible venue. Big stage and a huge TV outside. Nice big roomy bar. Multiple fire pits and plenty of seating inside and out. Several good trucks with some pretty cool options are available.  There is a second floor with an outside balcony for events and if they are very busy. It's a fantastic location.  I will be going back.

Dogs are always welcome at Armadillo Den! No matter how much time goes between visits, the staff and patrons always welcome Penny our English Bulldog and her little bro Diggs the Dachshund — Armadillo Den is always welcoming, friendly, fun. Good drinks, solid food trucks with good options, and live music — or football depending on the season! One of the best south austin spots around for a chill weekend or evening

I was expecting a certain conservative loud messy crowd, but it wasnt. And it felt safe while having some great people watching. Music is okay.  Funny enough, the Dj set playlist is better than the live music we attended for.

formatted_address: 1807 S 1st St, Austin, TX 78704, United States
name: LENOIR

reviews.text: We came down from Dallas and were excited to try farm to table food . The service was absolutely amazing! The hostess the waitress and the entire team were kind and helpful.  The food was a disappointment.  We did the fixed menu. The oysters and crab were good. The second dish was almost inedible for us. It was really off putting and we didn't eat it. The whole fish was cooked well. The dessert was good but not great. For the price of the food we were underwhelmed.  The atmosphere was pleasant and clean. Unfortunately I don't think we would return do to leaving still hungry almost $300+ later.

Our dinner was absolutely delightful. We booked here for a birthday dinner after a recommendation and we were not disappointed. Everything was wonderful. It’s such a cute little place on the inside and the vibes were perfect. I thoroughly enjoyed the vintage/antique china and silverware used throughout our meal. Such a cute little touch.
Our server, Madelyn was absolutely lovely and made our experience even better. She was on top of everything, perfectly coursed out our selections, gave the best recommendation for wine, and was so sweet.
The kitchen was so impressive. It’s incredibly tiny (you can see into the kitchen in the dining room) and they put out some of the best unique dishes we’ve had in a while. It seemed to run like a well oiled machine with just two men cooking everything. Mind blown.
Thank you guys all so much for a great birthday dinner and making me feel special. We’ll for sure be recommending Lenoir to others and we’ll be back!
10/10

Creative and seasonal food! The chef is inspired 👏

Cute and cozy ambiance

Very friendly staff 😃

My partner and I enjoyed our date night here. We chose to eat at the bar, and enjoyed talking with delightful and fun bartender. This place has a lot of soul, character, and charm. Really love it keeping South 1st St fun and boutique! Keep up the great work

The dishes that stole show were:
- grilled jerk cabbage ginger coconut soubise, creamer pea conserva
- tangerine almond cake meyer lemon curd, grapefruit, agrumato

They stretched the limits on flavors and textures to create truly unique dishes. This is a small but mighty kitchen and with only ~4 tables and a bar (+ a separate wine garden), it’s cozy and unique to Austin.
The fish and steak entrees were my favorite - perfectly cooked and delicious unique flavors. The service was excellent. The outside dining area is beautiful.

formatted_address: 6513 N Interstate Hwy 35, Austin, TX 78752, United States
name: Pappasito's Cantina

reviews.text: Yup, I know. It is tough being a vegetarian and this restaurant was no help. Their only veg items were “Veg Fajitas” & “Cheese quesadillas”. Bummer. The veg fajita had 99% huge slices of zucchini, some guacamole ….. and three lousy corn  tortillas. No other veggies. Oh yes it had three small slices of red pepper. Ha ha. The saving grace was our server who tried to make us feel comfortable and worked hard. This place is overrated and really just a hyped up spot. Nope…. Won’t be going there again.

Our waitress was friendly and attentive even with have a few large groups. The food was very delicious and the chicken was juicy and tender. The ribs and shrimp were tender and spiced wonderfully. My only gripe was i wish the table was bigger since we ordered the family platter. But other than that it was quite an enjoyable visit.

No wait-time with reservation. Server was knowledgeable about menu and encouraged us to try a new dish. Our meal was served hot and was delicious. Server continued to check on us even though he had multiple tables to attend to. He was also very kind in supplying us with take home chips and salsa. Will definitely return!
Never had disappointing meals, atmosphere is a little loud sometimes and the service is always good. Love this place. Very consistent. Happy birthday to me.

Always good food and servers are polite, been going here for yrs. Love Wednesday fajitas special. Last night they made a small mistake. Brought the queso ( part of the special) out late. Again a small mistake, but they made up for it in a big way... we ordered 3 specials and they gave us 3 free desserts my family and dinner guests were very happy about this. Was a wonderful dinner, Pappasitos never let's me down.

formatted_address: 21611 Grand River Ave, Detroit, MI 48219, United States
name: Maty's Cuisine

reviews.text: Maty’s African Restaurant is more than just great food — it’s a place full of warmth, culture, and community spirit. Every dish tastes homemade and full of love. I’ll be recommending it to all my friends!
Super delicious food and great prices. One dish of peanut stew was enough for 3 people. And the tilapia was superb. Authentic, affordable, and immensely tasty.
I was in heaven eating their red snapper, like wow they really know what there doing here. All the sides were well cooked as well I’ll definitely be back

Let’s start us off by saying I don't leave food reviews unless the food is that good. This place is better than good. We got the half grilled chicken with yellow rice and the Saturday special which was a mix of seafood, meat, vegetables and rice. Everything was seasoned to perfection. The chicken had us chewing on the bones just so we get every last bit of seasoning. (The breast was a little bit overcooked but still tasted amazing.) The portion size was a lot for the price considering all the other restaurants today skimps you on food. The guy taking the order was an older uncle who was very nice and accommodating. The customers walking into the restaurant greeted us and made us feel at home. I have nothing bad to say about the experience at the restaurant. The two things I can see people complaining about is the outdated interior and the wait time on certain items (lamb shank takes long to cook) but that does not matter when the food more than makes up for it.

My first time eating African food and I loved everything I had. More so the waitress was awesome helping me and my friend who flew in from FL because he seen a video about them go viral. The hidden gem is the juice they make. The berry mint and ginger juice were easily my favorite. The chicken had so much flavor and was juicy. The portion sizes were very large and even being full I wanted to keep eating because it tasted so good. Loved the fried plantains & both appetizers. A hole in the wall place that packs some serious flavor! Great place!

********UPDATE*******************

Went back with some friends from FL and service was even better if I could give 10stars I would. The owner was there as well so we got a picture and even tried a new juice they make.

formatted_address: 19228 Livernois, Detroit, MI 48221, United States
name: Fork In Nigeria

reviews.text:
***I don’t understand all the rave 1/10 food Unfortunately I thought the food was disgusting.  My Nigerian boyfriend makes me Egusi and pounded yam often and I clean my plate everytime.  I ordered the stewed chicken plate and the jollof is decent but very greasy and wasn’t anything special.  I got 2 tiny plantains thar were HARD and almost black ( old ) when I bit into it.  The side veggies was only 1 big fork of purple cabbage not the carrots onions and mixed veg advertised in a lot of insta videos.  I also got the egusi and fufu ( yet it said pounded yam under the description - pounded yam and fufu aren’t the same thing ) the fufu was hard , taste old , the egusi was TERRIBLE , it had an off putting taste / taste like some chemical like cleaning chemical or something that didn’t belong , I like to eat I don’t throw food away yet I couldn’t eat this , I threw it away. ( I did however take it out trash and take it back up there which I was glad I got a refund but the owner couldn’t even speak 2 words to me to apologize for my experience ) I was so excited to try this food truck I even came up there the day before and realize I came the wrong day went home and came the next day - that’s how high my hopes were. What I got did not taste fresh was very greasy , no hint of spice period and that chemical taste in the Egusi and hard stale tasting fufu , I would NEVER try this food truck again. I’ll stick to my boyfriends Egusi and pounded yam.  Oshey.
*** my review might help someome else.  It wasn’t about it not being like my boyfriends - I mentioned food being old , stale , and having chemical taste ! A review is just that.

I live in Saginaw I drove all the way to Detroit because this is my new favorite spot. Hands down y’all this man put his all into his cooking. Everything was fresh meat not old. That darn Goat meat Egusi and fufu  was heaven sent. I finally tried the jelloff rice omgggggg babyyyyyy he did that. Soooo good bout to order more I decided to get me a hotel room haha and eat up. Hands down THE BEST IN MICHIGAN NO CAP…

I ordered the Jollof plate with chicken. I called not too long before closing, maybe about a little over 20 minutes, and placed my order over the phone because their online ordering site was closed for the day.

They confirmed which location I wanted to place my order with (I confirmed for the Livernois location, the food truck). I started making my way there and my food was ready when I arrived. I didn't eat my food until much later that night as I decided to explore the neighborhood since I was in town from elsewhere, and this was my first time in Detroit.

Later that night, when I rewarmed and ate my food, I was not disappointed. The portion was generous and I could not finish it that night, since I was not extremely hungry. But I finished it the next morning and it was just as delicious! I would recommend this place to others, and I would eat there again if I were to visit Detroit again, which I likely will.

Ordered two vegan meals and had it delivered with Uber eats. Boxed were packed to the max and the food is so fresh, flavorful and delicious. I called to tell them how happy I was and of course now I’m here to tell all of you! Can’t wait to try more of their offerings. Happy to support this local business again - we are lucky to have food like this so close by. YUM

Absolutely amazing food and service! Fork in Nigeria on Livernois never disappoints. The flavors are rich, authentic, and perfectly seasoned everything tastes fresh and made with care. Portions are generous, prices are fair, and the staff is always friendly and welcoming. If you’re craving real Nigerian food with bold flavor and great vibes, this food truck is a must-try. Highly recommend!

formatted_address: 2934 Russell St Shed 2, Detroit, MI 48207, United States
name: Luffy's Kitchen

reviews.text: Amazing food, very kind people! 10/10 great place

This is NOT Nigerian food, you can eat it, leave any star you want but Nigerians do not eat breaded fish or cook the way this restaurant cooks, it’s a poor  imitation of Nigerian dishes. He fooled me and collected my money twice. I threw away the food. He was not even apologetic about the stuff he served as “Nigerian food”. The food is not good in taste, does not taste like any Nigerian food.
Amazing food! Happy to have halal options.

Luffy’s is absolutely amazing - an Eastern Market hidden gem and a must-eat for my partner and me. Her prices are amazing and she is one of the sweetest people you will ever meet - definitely stop by if you have a chance (and get the Jollof plate!).
Visited Eastern Market and tried veggie and chicken pie. Absolutely amazing. I think it was the best crust I had so far! Great service as well!

formatted_address: 3181 3rd Ave, Detroit, MI 48201, United States
name: Detroit Jollof

reviews.text:
This is the best Nigerian food in michigan, period.

I see people on here talking about Fork in Nigeria, they had been my main source of Nigerian food due to limited options but the inconsistency made me leave them permanently.

They dont hold a candle to Detroit jollof.

I also see people complaining about time to get food. This food is fresh. This is not mcdonlads or burger king, you can tell they use quality ingredients and its made daily. So if time is what you are worried about, order ahead.

I use Uber eats and usually wait about 45 mins, mind you my home is 30mins away from the restaurant so logic tells me it will take awhile to get to me. Its worth the wait, everything is fresh, tastes just like my wifes food when she cooks. Mackerel is amazing, meat pies even better, tried a few items ive never had before and everything was a hit.

Had a catering order over the weekend, came out hot and fresh at the exact time we choose for pick up.

This is my new favorite spot!

Food is extremely good! Great portions. If you won’t authentic Nigerian food this is the place. Only thing I’ll say is the wait time is pretty long in person and on Uber Eats . Expect to wait 40 mins to and 1 hr after you order.

I had such an amazing experience at Detroit Jollof! This new African restaurant in Detroit is definitely a gem. The Jollof rice was flavorful, the plantains were perfectly fried, and the grilled chicken was juicy and well-seasoned. Everything tasted fresh and authentic, just like home-cooked Nigerian food.

The service was friendly and welcoming, and the vibe of the restaurant makes it a great spot for takeout. If you’re looking for authentic West African food in Detroit—especially Nigerian Jollof rice, suya, and fried plantains—this is the place to go.

Highly recommend Detroit Jollof for anyone in Metro Detroit, Southfield, or Dearborn who loves delicious African cuisine. I’ll definitely be coming back for more!
Kemi’s food reminds me of home, the jollof rice is nice and smoky and the Titus fish and stew are so yummy! Moi moi, meatpie and chin and chin are so also really good! I highly recommend!

Ordered on doordash because they had the 2 for 1 special on the chicken and jollof rice. I also ordered the parboiled beans and meat pies. It took so long to be ready doordash gave me credits for my time because it was severely delayed. When it finally got to me my order was incorrect and absolutely tasteless. It barely even smelled like anything. I was missing one of the jollof rice and chicken meals which was the whole point of getting the 2 for 1 (my boyfriend was going to eat the other one) The one I DID receive had one piece of the tiniest chicken I’ve ever eaten with zero flavor and mostly just rice and plantains. I reported the order on DoorDash and got my money back. MORE than disappointing and I can only hope they were just having a bad day or something because WOW. Something was jollOFF with that food…

formatted_address: 19032 Plainview Ave, Detroit, MI 48219, United States
name: Kalahari

reviews.text: The food is unlike any other restaurant. Perfect pan-African fusion of Nigerian classics, carribean classics, and American classics. Incredible taste. Small hole in the wall location but INSANE food & very nice people!
Excellent shawarma (chicken, easy onion, mild spice -- which still has a little kick!). The BEST.

Terrible! Plain and simple. I order djoliff rice, and got yellow gummy dry stuck together rice. Not only that, I experienced the cashier guy touching the food with his bare hands, literally fingers tips and palms in the food. I have never experienced just a slap in the face! I called to complain, and the guy said come back tomorrow he will make it right not bring the food back now he will correct it. The man said come back the next day after 4pm and he wil give me the right rice i order. I am completely discussed with this place.
Enjoyed the food and the service.

The people were friendly but the food wasn't as well seasoned as I'm use to African food being they were stingy with the sauce it wasn't nearly enough for the amount of fish or rice they give you, the rice needs to be seasoned, the onion sauce was good but not enough and the plantains had no taste and weren't sweet like I like them.  I was charged $5 more for my red snapper with no warning and when questioned I was told it was because they go by the pound and they gave me a big piece and it was just a average piece and nowhere on the menu does it say you would be charged by the pound but it says $15 which is what I expected to pay not $20, so I felt like that was deceitful they need to state that on the menu, because of that I probably won't go back but I might try their lamb and give them one more chance, not sure yet.  The food was decent but I've had better seasoned.

formatted_address: 14384 Gratiot Ave, Detroit, MI 48205, United States
name: Touba African Restaurant

reviews.text: Man you talking about 5 STARS . They deserve every bit of more than 5 stars . I originally pulled up to sell my own food in was told they were giving away food . Once I realized it was an African restaurant I stopped in . Once I started trying the food .. IT WAS SOO DELICIOUS. I kept eating more and more . I didn’t even wanna leave. . I AM SO HAPPY THEY OPENED IN MY NEIGHBORHOOD BECAUSE I LOVE AFRICAN FOOD AND THE FOOD I TASTED TO DAY WAS SO GOOD . I CAN SEE ME SPENDING ALOT OF MONEY HERE . Thanks

Stopped on my lunch break and WHEN I TELL YOU ITS GOOD??!! The C’est Bon is the best fried fish I’ve ever had! Go when you have time and be open to the changing menu (if you go on the fly that is) and you’ll have a great time!
I suggest you call ahead to avoid the wait. The food is fantastic. Very authentic Gambian/ Senegalese dishes.
Very welcoming environment food taste amazing if you love spicy food get here now ‼️
Yoooo I ain’t gonna lie, this dibi hit 🔥🔥🔥

formatted_address: 7636 Gratiot Ave, Detroit, MI 48213, United States
name: Saffron De Twah

reviews.text:
I’ve had the pleasure of visiting Saffron De Twah, a James Beard-nominated modern Moroccan bistro, twice now, and indulging in their chef’s tasting menu. Chef Omar is truly remarkable, and what he’s creating on the east side of Detroit is absolutely delicious. The restaurant has a small, quaint atmosphere, but the flavors are incredibly bold.

Saffron De Twah is worth the drive off the traditional path. It’s an experience that will definitely challenge your palate. Whether you choose to dine in and savor Chef Omar’s chef’s table meal at a very reasonable price or opt for takeout, this spot is a must-visit.

The flavors are simply outstanding! My favorites include the couscous and the harissa potatoes. Although we skipped the lamb shank on this visit, I can assure you it’s spectacular—something you definitely shouldn’t miss. The fish and chicken sandwiches are equally amazing.

Chef Omar, the chef-owner, is a two-time finalist for the James Beard Award for Best Chef - Great Lakes, with nominations in 2022 and 2023. Plus, in 2023, he became a Food Network Chopped champion! If you’re in the area, don’t miss the chance to experience this culinary gem.

This place rocks — easily one of my favorite meals in Detroit. I’ve dined here alone twice yet never felt lonely; the atmosphere is warm and welcoming. The moroccan fried chicken sandwich, tomato dip, labneh, and lamb shank tagine are all PHENOMENAL. Drown me in the hot honey!!

Had an amazing time! The chef has been there for 7 years! His parents also had their own restaurant! Very warm hearted and kind! The food was absolutely spectacular! We especially loved the lamb, potato's and loaded hummus. Note for people looking for drinks, it is a halal establishment with no alcohol, but there is a massive selection of nonalcoholic beer, wine, and unique pops! Thank you for a great experience! While this isn't a downtown or midtown restaurant, the food is worth the visit!

This place is sweet. there was only the chef/owner (im assuming) in the kitchen and one host/bus girl, so things took a minute to get going. you order at a window and then they bring it out. food was amazing. the loaded hummus was insane along with the pita chips. I would eat this weekly. fish sandwich was also delish would be 10/10 but I gave it a 8.5 because there were huge pieces of cabbage not shredded in the slaw mix. flavors were all on point. the bread pudding was incredible as well. try one of the NA malt beverages while youre there! very interesting. overall this place rocks and everyone should try it out!

Overall experience at Saffron De Twah was good. Parking is limited, you may have to park on a side street. Reservations are highly recommended, as this is a small restaurant with limited seating. You have to order at the front counter, and the menus are located there. My wife and I were seated at our reservation time, but waited about 10 minutes until a waitress greeted us. Once we ordered, it took about an hour to get our food, so when you come, be prepared for a long wait.

We ordered the orange blossom lemonade, which was amazing! We also started with harissa potatoes and brussel sprouts. The harissa potatoes lacked a punch but weren't too bad, standard fried potatoes. The brussel sprouts were fantastic, however. For our mains, we ordered the Moroccan chicken sandwich and lamb shank tagine. The chicken sandwich was the standout, and the lamb shank was good (fork tender), but also lacked a little flavor.

We were given strawberry laziza (non-alcoholic beverage) to try for the wait. I didn't enjoy it but my wife did! All in all, it was decent experience. The wait took away from the overall experience, and the food wasn't quite worth the $95 check (tip included). I might come again to try other offerings, but Saffron De Twah won't be my first stop.

formatted_address: 6500 Woodward Ave, Detroit, MI 48202, United States
name: Yumvillage

reviews.text:
Talk about soul food, you better put Yumvillage in the conversation!

Food was crazy good. Hit the spot and the chefs got that extra love that just hits when you bite down on the elevated fufu.

If you got a stop over in Detroit or you hanging around Stevie Wonder Ave, go hit them up!!

the owner gave me a sample plate because i didn't know what i wanted, very personable and passionate about his work. his customer service made me want to return before i even tried the food. everything was delicious. rarely do i tip on carryout, today i tipped. 10 stars for yumvillage!

Food is authentically delicious!  Very clean and excellent vibes as soon as we walked through the front door.  Staff's smile and warm welcome, we felt like family.  Midtown is a hidden gem in Detroit, and YumVillage is a must-go-to Caribbean foodie experience.  Will be returning!

The food is AMAZING.
So flavorful, and CONSISTENTLY good. Sooo many delicious vegan options if you identify as vegan/plant based.

On top of the spectacular food, the customer service is top tier. I have never had a bad experience, if they get something wrong they correct it with no issues. They are patient when you order and answer all the questions you ask about the menu.

The owner is really friendly and nice, and the staff is just as kind.

Stopped here for the first time on last Friday, July 17. Had seen the restaurant on one of the local channels several times and had heard good things about the food. It was everything I’d heard about, so delicious. I ordered the Food Truck village combo which included jerk chicken with garlic Parmesan sauce, truffle oil greens and my rice of choice was the turmeric rice. It also included hush puppies. The chicken had a Mediterranean flavor to me similar to a shawarma, very good! The rice and greens were delicious and the hush puppies were like none I’d had before. Sweet and lightly drizzled with a sauce which I believe were banana peppers? Not sure but trust me they were sooo good! My mom ordered oxtails, OMG Delish! Her meal came with greens and jollof rice and she ordered a side of plantain. We enjoyed our food so much and are both looking forward to returning.

formatted_address: 4219 Woodward Ave, Detroit, MI 48201, United States
name: Fork In Nigeria-Curbside

reviews.text:
When I tell you guys, I’ve known about this place for years! Ever since he only had his first food truck! This place never disappoints! And for anyone who says it isn’t good is honestly just hating. PJ took great care of me and my husband, and I will continue to spread the word about his food.

You must try it if you haven’t already!
We got the spinach and kale stew with fufu and it was amazing!!! The stew was basically like some really good greens. The fufu was perfect consistency. One of our new favorite places!!!

Review for Fork (Woodward Location, only ):
I normally don’t leave negative reviews, but this experience was extremely disappointing.

The only location open today was on Woodward, which is a 44-minute drive from my home. I had a taste for Nigerian food and decided to try this place because of the positive reviews. Unfortunately, my experience was frustrating from start to finish.

First, the parking situation is a nightmare. The instructions direct you to park in spots 29, 30, or 31, but those were blocked — one by their food truck, and the others by vehicles that weren’t even being used by customers. On top of that, the entrance into the lot is dangerous. The ground has broken bricks and uneven areas that feel like a real hazard to your tires. Honestly, I wouldn’t recommend pulling in unless they repair it.

I received a text saying my order was ready, while on the way and I arrived 15 minutes later. I followed the instructions, called the number, and was told they’d bring it out. I waited 25 minutes. During that time, I watched them serve others, and when I finally tried to approach, the staff disappeared inside. The directions specifically say not to enter the building, so I didn’t. I called again — no response. When someone finally came out (to give food to another customer), I asked about my order, explaining I had been waiting over 20 minutes. The response? A simple “okay.” No apology, no acknowledgment of the inconvenience.

After all that waiting, I was handed food with no courtesy, and to top it off,  the plantains were (large in size, great!) But, overcooked, sticky, and tasted like they had been fried in old grease. The lid wasn't securely attached it honestly felt careless.

This was not the kind of service or food quality I expected after driving 44 minutes and spending my money. I could have cooked at home or stopped at one of the many other places I passed, but I wanted to try something new. Instead, I left feeling upset, unappreciated, and disrespected as a paying customer.

Never again.
I catered here for my boyfriend’s birthday, the food was delicious and they even threw in a pan of fufu for free! Thanks so much for the delicious food

Ok so let’s get into it. I order the Stew Beans and Plantain. And the puff balls. The food tops the service.

First I order on Door Dash(not the app), I get the text to say my order is ready for pickup. I then have to download the app. So I can see the ADDITIONAL details.

I’m asked to pull into a ALLEY for pickup and let them know which number I’m at.

As a first timer this is confusing and frustrating and if I have a short amount a time for lunch, your promptness and communication skills much be 100.

Once I called the number to get location details, I had to wait an additional 7 mins for food to brought out to me.

The food was slapping, but next time I’ll make it at home. Spices aren’t as authentic as I thought.

formatted_address: 13001 Eight Mile W, Detroit, MI 48235, United States
name: Little Lagos

reviews.text: This is the BEST Nigerian food I’ve had! Everything is always so fresh and delicious. Also the customer service is amazing and she makes sure her people are taken care of.
This is great nigeria 🇳🇬 food everything fantastic

formatted_address: 465 Inkster Rd, Garden City, MI 48135, United States
name: KG’s African - American & Caribbean

reviews.text: The food is absolutely spectacularly bombastic! So full of flavor and I love the fact that they do a buffet on every first Sunday of every month. I have been going here for about a year and some change. Every now and then we have to leave town and head up there. This place has become a staple and I completely see why it's always packed! If I had to recommend anything I would try the yassa chicken, you can't go wrong with plantains, they have plenty of selections of rice and beans, the jerk chicken, and I believe they used to have red snapper, not sure what fish they have now but it's good! Everything just tastes so good and when you mix it all together the flavors combined to create a smorgasbord of delicious/delectable heaven on earth! I love me some Caribbean food, and African food is the roots that tie all life together so when you combine the two, how could you go wrong!?

LISTEN UP...I usually don't post. The Senegalese Dibi was TERRIBLE! Why rob customers of their hard earn cash with a meal full of a bunch of grease & fat-bones? I'm so very dissatisfied and disappointed! The Plantains were greasy too!!! Very sweet, yet DEFINITELY not worth the hard earned $42 worth of pennies spent. There were huge portions of Rice and the Rice/Grilled vegs. had more flavor than the Meat! This not something I would chase down or buy again.

Look at the pictures... the big piece one big hard bone! The other tiny pieces fat... bones!!!

I’ve been visiting KG’s for 4 years now and they have always been consistent with food both quality and taste, and service. If I could  make one complaint I would say sometimes the lamb dibi (pictured) could be cooked a little longer. Other than it’s one of my favorite “hole in the wall” restaurants.

I rarely put a good review but this place is so good they deserve 5 stars . The staff were very nice and the place is clean and friendly. I had a goat stew with Fufu and it was very good. I will definitely come back again. Also it’s Halal ! 💯. Amazing place

Small food portion. Wasn’t like this before. We normally get the thiebou yapp. My husband and I literally travel an hour No problem to get their food now they’re very stingy with the meat portions. We tell them how far we come to get their food and it does nothing, no longer worth the drive! We have Even convince family and friends to travel to get their food over 50 people. Sometime we come with a group of at least 10-20 half the time, you would think they would be more loyal to customers that go out their way to come get their food, but that does nothing. The clients we referred even feels the same that is not the way it was initially. Not worth the drive, the time or the money anymore. Don’t plan on going back

formatted_address: 32523 Northwestern Hwy, Farmington Hills, MI 48334, United States
name: Kola Restaurant & Ultra Lounge

reviews.text: Absolutely ahhhhmayzing experience, I felt like I was definitely away in the Muthaland of Africa 🌍 good Nigerian 🇳🇬 food, great waitress, the owners were polite, my drink was strong enough, the music was on point and did I mention the food?! I can't wait to visit again!

First I would like to start of with; worst African food I have ever I looked at and tasted! As an African I am extremely disappointed! The kids meal was TRASH, chicken was hard and rice tasted cheap! The stews just looked like they weren’t made with love! I spent $72 dollars and most of the food went to the trash! It genuinely didn’t taste like African food! The lounge was dope tho! The people were kind but food was TRASH 4/10

Visiting out of town and needed food later in the evening/night, I didn't know I was walking into a whole party lol

Our order was taken with attention and care, everything was correct, fresh and good when we got to our room to eat

The fresh ingredients, the veggies, were fresh and good, and the beef suya was tender and seasoned just right, blended right in with the Jollof rice

Nice first experience, the vibe was chill and relaxed

My first time here for an event.  The venue/restaurant was absolutely PACKED.  Despite this, the wait staff did an absolutely AMAZING job taking and filling orders.  I was very impressed also with their customer service:  polite, mannerable, and helpful.  And the food was DELICIOUS!  I ordered chicken wings and jerk chicken mini wings---omgggg, so gooood, no lie!  If you haven't, you gotta check out Kola!  I will be going back 😋

-Atmosphere-
The atmosphere is nice, plenty of room for seating and has a nice low-lit, club type ambience with good music and good times all around. Problem for me was my table was shaky as hell but I put a napkin under it and kept up the good vibes. They had a DJ and a dance floor and everyone was having a great time. Definitely for the grown and sexy crowd and if you like to do the hustle, this is where it’s at.

-Service-
The service was good, the server was nice but I think she may have been a little busy and overwhelmed so it could have been a little better but all in all it was good solid service.

-Food-
I honestly think I had the best what soup that I ever had here. The food was hot, tasty, and fresh to order. The prices were reasonable for the style of food and the portions were nice that I had leftovers. The drinks were good and reasonable. Definitely a must try.

4/5 🔥 for me, would definitely recommend and will return again.

formatted_address: 16368 Middlebelt Rd, Livonia, MI 48154, United States
name: Mediterranean and African Cuisine

reviews.text: Came in with a group of people. Owner was very friendly and kind as well as the workers. Prices were reasonable and the food was really good. Look how nice the placement is of this Chicken Saj Shawarma! I would definitely come here again! Also it is halal :)

So excited about this new restaurant. We tried halal pepperoni pizza, bread sticks, bacon cheese burger, chicken in a box, tabbouli , chicken nuggets, falafel sandwich, kafta sandwich and  boneless chicken. Everything was amazing!! The grilled chicken was my absolute favorite the red sauce they make is amazing.

The customer service was amazing, was given a breakdown of the menu and an explanation of what each category came with. The food was amazing and delicious! The employees were very kind. Will definitely come back!

Pros: Online ordering super nice and easy. Shawarma sandwiches were the juiciest I have ever had, excellent flavor. Large portion size, decent prices. Great garlic sauce.

Cons: French fries were undercooked, very plain.

Looking forward to trying other things this place has to offer.

Decided to try this place out, and we were so glad we did!! We had the chicken shawarma pizza and it was DELICIOUS!!! The only thing I would probably change next time is to go lighter on the items and cheese because it was heavy and messy, almost needed a fork to eat it, but taste wise it was the best pizza I’ve had in awhile and we will definitely be trying out everything else on the menu!

formatted_address: 19586 Middlebelt Rd, Livonia, MI 48152, United States
name: Mimi’s Nook Nigerian Cuisine

reviews.text: The Egusi (w/ my choice of chicken & goat), and pounded yam was so tasty; Flavorful and perfectly traditional 10/10, bout 6.5 on the spice level. I also tried the nigerian style pound cake; new fave🔥

One of the best if not #1 for Nigerian food. The owner was so helpful picking out the right dish. The FUFU was chefs kiis as well as the Afang with goat (in the pic). 10 put of 10. I also ordered the Egusi with fufu for the weekend. People really need to come and try the food.

My service was great , the ladies were nice and inviting. I purchased egusi soup with chick and jollof vegetarian rice. My rice was nice and fluffy 🥰The food was very flavorful and hot in temp and great portions sizes but I came when they first opened so I had to wait. That didn’t bother me. This is what I will say if you are use to fork in Nigeria the food truck then it’s more traditional because they don’t ommit the traditional ingredients ! Sorry I have no pic I ate it to fast

I was feeling adventurous and found this place and got great reviews. I decided to eat in inside. The only Nigerian food I had previously was Jollof rice from my old Coworker from the past. So I tried Isi Ewu. It’s a delicacy from what I told. The waiting took time but you I know I was getting some authentic home cooked meal from Mimi. ISI Ewu is very delicious; I ate it with white rice. It has the perfect amount of spiciness and taste. The meat is so fresh, tender and well cooked! I would definitely go back here again and try the other food! This place is a must try!

Today I decided to venture out and try Nigerian cuisine and was pleasantly surprised.

My starter was Ogbono Soup this unique dish was served along side pounded yams and right off the bat had such a blend of flavors that were unique and delicious while also bringing a nice hit of spice with each bite. The use of palm oil adds a distinct flavor profile to the dish but does coat the roof of your mouth so if you are a texture person you may want to avoid this dish however I personally really enjoyed it. 4/5

For our two entree's we got the Oxtail stew and the white rice, plantains and chicken

Both of these dishes were both pleasant, The sauce the chicken was cooked in was pleasantly seasoned and had just enough flavor to make you crave the next bite. Combining the sauce, chicken and rice took it to another level. As for the oxtail this unique dish is always one of my favorites and was seasoned very well. The only downside of oxtail is it can be a little fatty of a piece but if you dont mind the chew i highly recommend. Both of these dishes earned a 4.5/5

The service was great, the owner was just opening the restaurant when I arrived and got right to cooking and got my food to me in a timely manner. Overall the service was unmatched and was definitely a 5/5

formatted_address: 545 W Nine Mile Rd, Ferndale, MI 48220, United States
name: Blue Nile

reviews.text: Amazing! This was my first time eating Ethiopian food, and it was great! We went here for a birthday, and we ordered the veggie platter!

The place here is beautiful, and the customer service was lovely and kind.

I was, however, disappointed the injera had no fermented flavor. It was not sour, it was honestly plain tasting. All the injera I had before had a bright, sour flavor.

The different vegan platters as they say were good, some mediocre tasting. I think the bigger issue is their weird forcing of the dishes on you. You have to get the platter with the vegan dishes and you don’t get to choose a la carte or pick up to so many. It’s a set price and you have no other option truly.

We chose to get some a la carte meat, my friend got a drink. Everything totaled to $80 and some change. Incredibly overpriced.

The kicker, and why I’m really here, is that they don’t allow you to take this forced platter-leftovers home because they claim “it’s all you can eat”.

So who’s eating these leftovers? I’d see this if we’d ordered a second tray or even second tray of the injera. We did not. We had tons of food left that we paid for.

Other places like this have you pick up to three or do a la carte. They certainly let you take the food you pay for home. They claim this is health regulation or something strange….that’s a lie. The grift disappoints me, the injera doesn’t taste like it is defined to be, but the place was gorgeous and the food decent (certainly not fresh and local tasting though).
The whole experience has been pleasant, fulfilling, and satisfying. God bless me to have this experience, and it was great, God takes care of his Owen 👑🙌🏽🙏🏽💕

As it should be.. the staff and owners were consistently hospitable, accommodating and nice to us no matter how many times we asked for things and asked questions. By default you eat the Ethiopian way with your hands using the injera bread and there’s an option for a gluten free teff bread as well. A courtesy hot towels service is provided to better clean your hands before and after eating. You can get yourself a separate plate and silverware only by request. We requested plates, silverware and serving spoons bc we were a group of 8 and it just made us more comfortable to eat off our own plates with our hands, bread and/or forks. I’ve never tried the meat dishes here before but others in the restaurant seem to enjoy it. I have been a couple of times for the plant based vegan feast and it’s absolutely delicious!! You get 7 different authentic Ethiopian cooked vegetables and you can add on the fresh salad. It’s all you can eat and they’ll keep bringing more of whatever you like. The price is right, where else are you going to have all you can eat, seven different dishes all for around $25?! They also have delicious dairy free sorbet in different flavors. The atmosphere is colorful and cozy, feels like you’re in another country. I would highly recommend this place to vegans and meat eaters.

Everything was absolutely phenomenal. Not a single thing on the whole platter was less than incredible. Pricing is fair. A few other reviews mention you can’t bring home leftovers but it’s all you can eat and that’s pretty standard and to be expected. The staff was friendly and service was fast. Can’t wait to come back.

formatted_address: 2000 Wyandotte St W, Windsor, ON N9B 1J7, Canada
name: Jubba Restaurant

reviews.text: Wow. Amazing food. Rice cooked and spiced to perfection. Chicken was super juicy, tasty and also cooked to perfection. 100% the best rice and chicken I've had. I wish there was a location in London too. If you're in Windsor, it's a must try.

Had their One chicken leg piece rice- was really good and good portions as well
Customer Service could be better

This place made me fall in love with Somali food. The small and cozy place is decorated with Islamic artifacts and will offer you with the best hospitality in town. We ordered the Sports Plate which contained 4 chicken legs, rice, onion and stew gravy. The chicken was falling apart from the bone and the flavourful stew had a medley of different vegetables. The rice was very fragrant and the quantity for the price is unbeatable. We took the leftovers home and was able to get two more meals out of it. If you are in Windsor, don’t miss this!
The food was amazing, everything tasted fresh. They’re also very nice people! This is a business worth supporting!

Owner is incredibly kind! When you come into the restaurant, it feels like visiting a friend's house:) Food portions are GREAT and the 2 piece chicken leg is great! Also try the beef stew! Great hidden gem in the city and I encourage you to visit

formatted_address: 433 Ouellette Ave, Windsor, ON N9A 4J2, Canada
name: Lagos Grill

reviews.text: The Jollof rice was flavorful and well-cooked, the jerk chicken smoky and tender with a nice spicy kick. Sweet plantains and fresh coleslaw balanced the meal perfectly comforting and delicious overall.

I ordered assorted meat, white rice and a sauce to eat the rice with. I placed this order on UberEats and I got a call minutes after saying they didn’t have the sauce(sorry, isn’t this a restaurant for a reason, so prepare what isn’t available. Alright), I asked him what I’m supposed to do about that because I already paid and there’s no way to get a refund. He said I could have an alternative for an “everything sauce”, I asked what it’s ingredients are, he said mayonnaise and other ingredients, I asked what people eat it with and he said jollof rice. I reminded him that I ordered white rice and asked how he expects me to eat some mayo sauce with white rice. I got lowkey frustrated at this point because I’m talking to someone with an accent that signifies he’s not African not to speak of Nigerian or Lagosian. Why am I on a call with someone who doesn’t understand how Nigerian dishes work as a combo… suggesting I eat white rice with MAYO … well I was so frustrated because I was hungry and about to get delivered plain white rice and some meat… oh well.
The portion of the meat was NOT worth the price. Instead of just meat, I got a chuck of bone amongst those and beneath is a what I got picture vs what I expected(not in appearance but portion). I suggest that they include how many pieces of meat to be expected in the menu.
I wasn’t going to leave a review but I really could not contain my displeasure.

I came to this restaurant excited for a flavorful Nigerian meal. What I received instead was a full-contact culinary experience that felt less like dining and more like surviving a rite of passage.

First, the wait time. I ordered food and had enough time to question my life choices, reconnect with old friends, and consider learning how to cook myself. I genuinely thought the goat was still alive when I ordered it.  When the food arrived drenched in grease. Enough oil in it for america to start a war. Would I come back?
No.
Am I still thinking about it days later?
Unfortunately, yes.

One star for making a meal I will truly never forget, even if I desperately want to.

So the good. The food was warm and the salad was good. The jollof rice was very dry and there was no sauce and an unappetizing burnt flavour. The jerk chicken was decently spiced on the surface but the chicken itself was very bland. There was a ton of rice and 3 chicken drumsticks.  Overall would I go again? Defintely not as it was $21 and I expected better from a restaurant with much higher prices than others in the area. Sorry for the bad news.

Simply put, I had to throw out the Grilled Chicken Wrap. It was not enjoyable at all.
It tasted like the Lettuce was so soggy it was hardly edible.
The flavour of the chicken was decent. At some point I had to singularly pick out the chicken and onions from the rest of the wrap - not an enjoyable experience at all.
Maybe order something else when you visit.

formatted_address: 13745 W Nine Mile Rd, Oak Park, MI 48237, United States
name: NUBIAN TROPICAL CUISINE

reviews.text: Definitely is real authentic African food. Food was very fresh and delicious. I enjoyed it

Waited over 15 minutes before anyone even took my order, and they were out of a lot of things so I didn't get what I truly wanted to. The few workers I spoke to were pleasant and they did at least offer a free fataya (meat filled pastry) while I waited for them to make me something else that they did have available. Total time waiting for my food: a little over an hour! 😮‍💨. I ended up getting two beef shawarmas, an order of fatayas(comes with 5pcs), and two bissap/hibiscus drinks. The shawarma was a little cold and just okay. Fatayas with the dipping sauce was delicious though and the juice is good. It's inside of a market that could use some updating/TLC or a deep cleaning and better organization, not sure if I'd go back since there's no way to know if they will have other menu options next time.
The food was delicious I really like it and the service was amazing. I really enjoyed what I ordered. I highly recommend it.
My food was really good, and the service was quick and great I really enjoyed it
Great food! Highly recommend!

formatted_address: 18105 Wyoming Ave, Detroit, MI 48221, United States
name: Rendezvous African RESTAURANT

formatted_address: 752 Southfield Rd Suite 100, Lincoln Park, MI 48146, United States
name: House of Fufu

reviews.text:
Mannnn, this food got me reminiscing about back home and how food really should taste like...
I would 100% recommend to try it out with a open mind. Food is amazing, customer service is on point.

It was great the service was great the food was delicious. There was no where to sit although it was a food truck but it would've made things easier because I wanted to try different things but over all I will be coming back to try it again.

I came here having never tried Nigerian food before and wanting to try it. I was immediately greeted by the owner/chef who was very friendly and offered to walk me through the menu. I ended up getting the Egusi, which came with goat and fufu, okra which came with chicken and fufu, and the red snapper dinner which came with fried plantains and rice stew. The food was absolutely phenomenal. Portions were large, very flavorful and spiced perfectly. Owner/chef was very passionate and enthusiastic about his food. Highly recommend.

I don’t know where to begin. I was looking for a good African food restaurant and stumbled upon this establishment. The best thing I’ve ever done not only do they make their food with love. They have beautiful attitudes like family and the food they put love and I’m spoiled now if it doesn’t come from house of Fofo, I do not want it. I have the goosy soup with the stew, chicken and a Smashburger the best burger I’ve ever had and the best and gooey I’ve ever tasted the owner is so so so nice pleasant and have a great attitude and he welcomed me to the house of Fuufu family and I am happy to say I am part of the family now I will be eating here quite a bit and if it’s not from here, I do not want it and I mean that and I mean the food is amazing. I’m ordering a double smash burger tonight and I’m going to smash it. That’s for sure. Great great food you will not be sorry ordering anything from here. Everything here is good and I mean everything even the cans of pop lol

I recently had the pleasure of eating at House of Fufu, and I can confidently say it was Fire! The food was absolutely delicious! I found myself savoring every bite, and honestly, I would eat this food out of the garbage if I had to! The owner was a great guy and attentive, making sure I had everything I needed. If you're looking for a true taste of Nigeria, House of Fufu is a must visit. I can't wait to return and explore more of their incredible menu!

formatted_address: 15680 E Thirteen Mile Rd, Roseville, MI 48066, United States
name: Hola Nigerian Kitchen

reviews.text:
Disappointed is an understatement.
We drove an hour to try a new place.  After having an excellent experience with East African cuisine, I thought I'd give West African food a try.  This couldn't have been their best effort.
The plantains were the only part of the meal that kept me at the table.
The rice was nearly flavorless..outside of a hint of tomato and a slight spicy heat.
The chicken leg, one leg, was dry and honestly I couldn't take more than one bite.  There was a smell, something funky and very off.  Smelled terrible and tasted worse.
I also wanted to try a meat pie.  The dough was too thick which made the pie seem dry.
Wasn't bad,  wasn't good.

If this review seems poor, its getting worse,  this meal for two cost $48....rice/fried plantains/one drumbstick...what the what??
I can't recommend this place.

This food wasn’t good at all. Super gross. Egusi has a weird smell to it and tastes funny. Jolli rice is ok. But I’m sure all my food was heated up in the microwave because it doesn’t taste fresh at all. Then the kicker is I asked about specials and the boss said that’s from last year but the other prices are still the same. Mmmm that sounds crazy crazy and I spent 29 dollars. I got charged surcharge fee and some other fee. And I came all the way from Utica. NEVER AGAIN

Nice family owned restaurant. The waitress was super nice and welcoming, great service. Solid portions, they might look small at first but once you start eating you realize that the meal is very filling and good portion. Recommend getting plantains and the fufu and egusi, was really good and well seasoned, same with the chicken. The rice and meat pies were fine. Overall great experience and highly recommended this restaurant and will be here again. (Oh and some great Afro beats in the background while your eating)

Flavor was good, but price was pretty steep. For almost 19 dollars I expected more than a single drumstick. there was no beef either despite it being in the description. They also had no plantains in stock. They did give a massive portion of rice though, easily 3-4 cups worth. Still, given the price aswell as a 15 minute wait just to order, I don’t think I’m going to come back.

This is a fun, new restaurant to visit.  There is a lot of energy in the staff and the food is unique and different.  A delightful change from a traditional American meal.  If you are ready for some home cooking Nigerian dishes, place your orders or better yet visit the restaurant and get to know the staff.
