It’s true comfort food, and the quality and taste are always consistent, if not better each time. The staff is super friendly, and the portions are generous, which is a huge plus. If you’re in the Newark area, I definitely recommend stopping by for some authentic cuisine!

This place is a hidden gem. I was hesitant to visit because it’s a private property, but I’m glad I did. I live in Clifton and drove 30 minutes to Newark to satisfy my craving for the fufu & Egusi soup.

When I called, the owner was incredibly polite and answered all my questions. He greeted me downstairs with the food. The packaging was secure and prevented any leakage.

The cow skin and fish were absolutely fantastic. The flavor, texture, and spiciness were all top-notch 10/10.

However, the egusi soup was a bit different from what I had tasted before (different place). I’m not sure if it was the seasoning, but it had a distinct taste that I wasn’t familiar with. Nevertheless, I’d still rate it a 6/10.

The portion size was generous for the price, and I ended up eating it in two days because it was so filling. The next day, the cow skin & fish had an even more amazing flavor. I highly recommend this place!
Since I left Nigeria this is the first time I eat Nigerian food that tastes just like the food in 9jja. The food tastes so so good, I wish I can rate it 100000000 stars.

I was in the Newark area for work and decided to look for a Nigerian restaurant. I came across this vendor, and even though it's set up in a home environment, the food is amazing and the portion sizes are incredible. I’m giving them a solid 10/10!
$25 FOOD and sauce looks like I have asked .why do serve a big bowl of amala if there is no sauce to eat it all.

formatted_address: 666 Springfield Ave, Newark, NJ 07103, United States
name: 9ja Buka Restaurant

reviews.text: Terrible food quality, terrible food presentation, everything looked dried and not taste. The native rice was just terrible. Hard. Not fresh. And red stew was flavor less.

Bland taste. Worst African food I ever tried in Newark. Ayamase sauce was not saucing. The rice was cold as hell. The customer service was very poor. DOH needs to come visit this place . Ayamase 0/100, rice 2/100 . Very poor

The lady serving the food was very rude and lack customer  service and for what ever reason, in a rush to take the customers  orders. I went into this restaurant  to purchase food for myself and a friend that was visiting  from out of state and was embarrassed by the service that was provided. The character of the lady was extremely poor and tasteless. To the owner please train your staff and employees  on how to deal  with the public no matter where  your customers are from. The treatment  was unacceptable  and becuase of this I will never patronize this restaurant  again.

I just got my Uber eats order and was extremely excited. Then boom I eat my food and it taste horrible and old the only thing that tasted fresh was the pounded yam a 44 dollar order down the drain smh high priced trash. This is my first and last time eating here

Food is really great.Well made African and Nigerian dishes.I tried Ofada rice and the  sauce and it was fantastic.Also got a takeout the jollof rice which is always amazing.Food can be pricey but its worth every penny.

formatted_address: 242 Lyons Ave, Newark, NJ 07112, United States
name: Esther's Kitchen (Lyons Ave, Newark)

reviews.text:
I’m not one to drop reviews usually but I had an exceptional experience at Esther’s kitchen, the food came out fast, fresh and delicious.
I had the light soup and fufu and it was amazing.

I ordered waakye and it looked absolutely delicious. The rice was tasty but the stew and the meat was underwhelming. No seasoning in the meat at all, just fried. The stew too didn’t have any seasoning. The bigger disappointment was the shito. It tasted smokey/burnt with an overwhelming taste of ginger. The pepper added made it very spicy to the point where there was no flavor. There are actual pepper flakes added to this shito. No hint of ground shrimp just numbing spice. I’m hoping I just received a poor batch and other days will be better for them.

I recently ordered jollof and i was served with like. Week old jollof  the stew lmost fermented the meat were too soft nd spereated from the bones. I ended up throwing it away. You can do better pls put in some work.

Was charged $42 for the soup special and a fish platter. The food was not fresh, they literally gave us inedible beef and old food that’s been sitting out. It was cold to touch and only realized after I returned home. The host was a little rude as well. We walked in and she gave us a look and said “we serve Ghanaian food okay?” To which we both replied okay (we had already looked the place up to eat beforehand), so this seemed unwelcoming. After we were done ordering she said “you’re taking it to go right?” Like we weren’t welcome to sit down and eat inside. The whole interaction was unwelcoming & weird. The only good thing was the goat meat inside the peanut butter soup. I really wanted to try something different and support a local business but I don’t appreciate cutting corners. Especially when I’m spending close to $50 and included a tip. I expect fresh meat & hot food.

Love love the decor and ambiance of Esther's Kitchen. It's so reminiscent. You cant help but smile as soon as you see the Ghana flag!!Food was good. Service was classic Ghanaian hospitality... polite..with smiles and a warm welcome. Amazing work put into the space!!

formatted_address: 432 Central Ave, Newark, NJ 07107, United States
name: Jollof & Grill Restaurant

reviews.text: My second time visiting jollof & grill and I brought my friend with me. We were happily greeted upon entering and even got to meet the owner. She’s the sweetest person ever 🩷We ordered the beef suya combo and it was delicious. The jollof rice was flavorful. I love the raw onions and cabbage that comes with it. The beef suya was also cooked to perfection. The plantains were ripe and tasty as well. & Can we talk about portions? You get a lot of food for the price. I shared half w/ my grandma and she enjoyed her food as well. Will definitely be returning in the future!

Ordered via Uber eat , the food was well packaged on delivery. I had the Suya combo , with fried yam and plantains. The plantain was the best ripe state as I like them. The fried yam is a must with the side sauce , make sure you get it! There efo rioro is very spicy , so if your spicy level is very low, skip it. Also there efo is just plain spinach ,it doesn’t have little fish ore things like other places.
Overall, my top food here is their Suya , plantain & fried yam with sauce.

I called in to make inquires about a canceled Uber order and they were very helpful with their explanations.

Came for takeout. It had just opened and I got an order of the jollof rice and suya. The jollof was good but the suya was great! Plantains were fried to perfection. The staff was so kind.

Parking is tough but food is worth it!
Original Nigeria jollof rice experience without the usual hot spice! Combo with the barbecue meat (popularly called "suya") completes the unforgettable experience for me!🙃

I found this place via Instagram right before my trip to NJ! I was so excited to try it. When I called I didn’t know exactly what I wanted to order being a vegetarian and most of the jollof dishes came with a meat or seafood. The person on the phone explained that I should get the Efo Riro with the jollof. I’m no stranger to jollof and this place has good jollof! The staff was so nice when I picked up my order and that’s a lot these days! Highly recommend and can’t wait to visit again when I’m back in town. P.S. that hole in the jollof was from me trying it out before recording the video 🤭🤭.

formatted_address: 301 S Orange Ave, Newark, NJ 07103, United States
name: A Jaaraama Cuisine

reviews.text:
I placed an order through DoorDash and was very disappointed with the quality of the food and the customer service. The protein was undercooked, and the egusi had an extremely watery texture and consistency. I wish I could attach a video to show the condition of the food. The pounded yam was also cold upon arrival.

Additionally, the restaurant advertises eba on DoorDash. Before ordering, I called the restaurant to confirm availability and was told they did not have eba, which was misleading. When I called back to request a resolution, the staff member who answered appeared confused. After I stated that I would leave a review, the call was immediately disconnected.

Overall, this was a very unsatisfactory experience in both food quality and customer service.

Good is okay. The soup that I got was salty. I say too salty. It’s my second time coming here but it was just too salty. Also the meat smelled a little. It was dark and it felt that they didn’t clean it well enough. I am not planning to come back to this place. Of course everyone’s experience is different but definitely not planning to come to this place.

I recently ordered attieke with fried tilapia from this restaurant, and unfortunately, it did not go well. The food did not seem fresh, and I ended up suffering from a severe stomach virus that caused food poisoning. Given my experience, I cannot recommend this place to anyone. Please exercise caution when ordering from them, as the quality and safety of their food are concerns.

Take care and stay safe.

I don't know about anyone eslse.. but this food and the ppl were sooo great!  Can't ever use the words "tasteless" or no "flavor".  Granted everyone  may not be as adventurous with their taste buds, but this was My first time having West African food outside of what my husband and his family serves. It was sooooooo good! It had color flavor and ample servings.  The Joloff  rice was 🔥... I had that with chicken and the baked lamb.  If you are in Newark, NJ and looking for a belly  full  with quick service stop on in.  You won't regret  it!
This is a wonderful restaurant.  The food is great and the owner is extremely friendly and respectful.  Doordash orders are very fast. One of my favorite African restaurant in Newark.

formatted_address: 360 Washington St, Newark, NJ 07102, United States
name: Bamako Maliba Adams Kitchen

reviews.text: This is my husband and I's first Mali food. I was happy seeing the menu because I love fish so I got the red snapper and my husband got the chicken. It was mind blowing for us how it sounded so simple yet it was insanely delicious. Had fufu with the sweet potato leaf too. We are definitely coming back. The staff were as good. Very kind

Stopped by after a concert at Prudential Center, we’ve never tried West African food before but this was an insane introduction. We split the poulet rôti with jallof rice and fried sweet plantains and it was genuinely the best food that my girlfriend and I had had in a while. The staff were all super accommodating and welcoming, and we can’t wait for our next visit here

Edit: We came back and if I could give this place 10 stars I really would! The lady who helped us the first time we came recognized us and treated us like family, she is so warm, welcoming, and really makes sure that everyone feels at home. Today, we had the pompano, chicken skewers, and dibi and everything was outstanding. I had the pompano and the bones were left completely clean. My only wish is that this restaurant was in NYC or closer to us, but we will continue to visit every time we are in the area !!!

First time trying out West African cuisine and it has become one of my favorites already. My husband and I had a great time dining in, very friendly staff, love the energy. The food is so good, flavorful and cooked perfectly with generous portions. I had the pampano fish topped with their special onion sauce, jolof rice and side of sweet plantains. Definitely one of the best meals I ever had. Thank you and looking forward to coming back again! :)

A Hidden African Gem Worth Discovering

I recently visited this incredible African restaurant, and I’m still thinking about the experience! The food was absolutely delicious—each dish bursting with authentic flavors that truly satisfied my taste buds. What stood out even more was the cleanliness of the restaurant; it was spotless from top to bottom, including the bathroom, which was impeccably maintained.

The staff was another highlight—they were so warm, welcoming, and genuinely friendly. Their excellent service added a personal touch that made the visit even more enjoyable.

If I have one wish, it’s that this place was in a better location to attract the traffic it rightfully deserves. It’s a hidden gem that more people need to know about! I’ll definitely be coming back and recommending this restaurant to everyone. If you’re looking for an authentic and outstanding African dining experience, this is the place to go!

First time having Mali food and it was super tasty. The service was amazing! Thanks❤️
I got two plates of the tuna steak, puff puff, and plantains, the price for that only being 36 dollars is awesome

formatted_address: 208 W Market St, Newark, NJ 07103, United States
name: Aunty Lizzy's Oseikrom Restaurant and African Market

reviews.text: I have no idea what West African food is supposed to taste like. With that in mind, I ordered the beans and plantains/fried bananas and then asked if he had any rice because I typically eat rice when I have beans. He said yes and pointed to something on the menu that also had fish with it. So I ordered the rice with chicken. The person I was with ordered a goat meat stew. The rice was flavorful, had subtle spices and herbs that I cannot identify. The beans looks like a black eye pea. They had a slight smoky flavor to it. Not as strong smoky as I had in Belize, which was cooked on an open fire. Zach gives me the thought that these were also cooked on a charcoal fire if that is possible in New Jersey. The fried plantains were exactly as I expected sweet, very sweet. The chicken was good, mostly dark meat. That means that the chicken was flavorful. Yes the chicken was dry. We got there at 11:30 in the morning. The food reminded me of something that I would get while traveling in Central America. And that was exactly what I was looking for. Why did I give the atmosphere two stars, because I believe the place is more centered around takeout food than wine and dine. Yes if I am ever in the area again, I would strongly consider going again. I have no idea how much each item cost because there were no prices on the menu. The three items plus water and juice with a 15% tip came to a couple pennies under $60. One last thing to mention, I did try the goat, and there was a moderate to strong dried fish flavor.

If you are looking for a Ghanaian food that takes you straight to Ghana, it’s this place. The food was amazing and a lot. I will recommend this place. The Waakye, fufui,banku, tilapia and fried yams are amazing i almost forgot they have Jollof and other dishes as well.

The food was totally worth the drive from Malvern, PA. Good music, great services, kind people...the washroom was fairly clean with water and hand soap available (that was a huge plus). As for the Chofi, it's authentic Ghanaian Chofi for whoever is wondering how good it was. P.S. they are moving to a new location, please find them if you're craving some authentic Ghanaian delicacies.
The banku was soft and enjoyable, but the tilapia lacked flavor and felt disappointing for a $26 meal. The meat pie, however, was delicious and the highlight of the order
The ladies were very courteous and jovial. Loved the food and will definitely be coming back...

formatted_address: 388 S Orange Ave, Newark, NJ 07103, United States
name: Mama Africa Foods LLC

reviews.text: It is indeed an atmosphere of love that makes you feel at home on your local dishes

I ordered food off of Uber eats I ordered a egusi With assorted meat and spinach with assorted meat also a side of beef tribe the meat and all three were the worse. The meat you couldn’t even bite into it was so hard. I was so disappointed and threw the food away. I will never order from you guys again.

Been in the USA for about 10 years and have eaten Nigerian food from California, Florida, New Jersey, New York, and Georgia. Consistently had Nigerian food in NJ and NY.

This is by far the worst Nigerian food we’ve ever had. After spending more than $120 on Egusi soup, Ogbono soup, and other sides, the Ogbono tasted so bland you’d ask is this chef even a Nigerian? Surely not! The egusi soup, if you can even call it egusi soup was just a bunch of greens and a little egusi filled with so much palm oil you’ll ask “is this palm oil soup”?

On top of all that, only 2/6 meat were barely edible, one Kpomo and one goat meat, the rest was straight garbage that were so hard and chewy a dog wouldn’t even be able to chew through. Went straight into the garbage bin.

I’ve tried mama g multiple times in NY (before two years ago) and didn’t have this problem but there’s no way I will even order from the New York, who knows if that location is just as bad as this now. Not even upset anymore just very disappointed that we waited one and half hours for this food

Honestly I had no personal business here. I simply was picking up an order for a friend.

As soon as I walked inside, the smell hit me and it was not pleasant. I’m not sure if it was the meat in the freezer directly to the left when you enter or simply uncleanliness but that odor alone will ensure I never return.

Went in there to ask questions about the food I saw and got handed with a terrible attitude by an African lady. She told me don’t worry about what kind of meat it is despite me trying to acquire to purchase.I also was told to sit down and I wanted to stand but kept raising her voice for me to sit down.She was very rude to all the African Americans in the establishment but wasn’t to the non African Americans In addition, I notice after digging in her nose she did not wash her hands. Mentioned it to her and she told me her hands was washed after me watching her not wash her hands. Did not deserve the attitude and will bring my money else where. Thank you 🙃

formatted_address: 266 Mulberry St, Newark, NJ 07102, United States
name: One Lagos Restaurant

reviews.text: Really good food! With affordable prices! Didn't really see much parking tho if you're planning to dine in. Just picked up my order. Service was good 9/10
The food tastes like home food and I really enjoyed it. I shall be back here whenever I come back to Newark, New Jersey!!!🫶🫶🫶
Very quick service, if you want a taste of home they got it. I got  the amala with gbegiri and ewedu with assorted meats.
Nice well prepared food. My wife & I enjoyed the our dinner from one lagos NJ. If you are in the area and need Nigerian food that will give you a taste of home, stop by.

Absolutely delicious! I had the jollof rice with assorted meat, and everything was seasoned to perfection. The rice had that rich, smoky flavor, and the meat was tender and flavorful. The portion size was great, and the service was warm and welcoming. If you’re looking for authentic African food that truly hits the spot, this place is a must-visit!

formatted_address: 327 6th Ave W, Newark, NJ 07107, United States
name: Ghana Jollof Restaurant

reviews.text: They served me this old, dry, overcooked Suya Chicken and claimed that some places make the chicken juicy, but they make it dry and hard. My other order of chicken was literally just hard fried pieces of chicken fat. No meat anywhere throughout the 5 pieces I paid for. The jollof rice was burnt, and the spinach had a funky taste to it. Plus they had flies landing all on the windows and tables. Nothing but excuses and attitudes. Wouldn't order again.

Ordered through Uber Eats and the food was fresh and tasty. I think it’s the best in the neighborhood so far and I’m happy to see a west African restaurant on this side of town. My husband enjoyed then jollof rice and chicken and I enjoyed the egusi soup with fufu. We love west African food so this is a huge plus. The food was fantastic!

This was THE WORST jollof rice I’ve ever had in my life. I’m wondering if this place is actually being run by Ghanaians? Because the jollof does NOT taste like Ghanaian jollof—and this is coming from a Ghanaian. The rice tasted like old white rice with some smokey stew mixed in. The Chofi tasted like it had been sitting out all day. I am very disappointed in this food.
Food was extremely disgusting.. The rice taste burnt. And the beef had no seasonings. My first time trying and it was 0/10! Will never recommend or return.
I just left this place 10 minutes ago , they gave me 1 meat and a full plate of rice . Since when did you guys start doing this ????

formatted_address: 374 Littleton Ave, Newark, NJ 07103, United States
name: AGEGE BUKKAH RESTAURANT

reviews.text: Goat Pepper soup was amazing and spicy as everything. My Nigerian self loved it. My only complaint is that I wish fufu was included. I didn’t know on Uber eats that it wasn’t. Very tender goat. To die for

The service was great, staff is very nice. The food tasted amazing and very well proportioned. I got a great amount of pounded yam to go with my egusi soup, not to mention, the meat tasted great as well. However, I gave it 3 stars because there was a strand of hair in my food and I didn’t like that. I would just say they should be more careful and use hair nets so this doesn’t happen again. But other than that, everything else was good.

When I opened my bag and saw the hand written note I knew the food would be delicious.
I ordered off Uber eats and a lot of times it’s a hit or miss with that app.
This was my very first time ordering and I don’t regret it not one bit. I will definitely be ordering again
Thank you.

Croaker fish and Jollof.

In this review, I discuss service, price, food taste, and parking.

Service
Service was quite good. The proprietor of the location was very nice and informative when I called to inquire about food availability.

Price
The prices are reasonable for NJ and the price is as listed in the menu images on Google.

Food Taste
We ordered Amala, gbegiri and goat meat, a side of turkey and white rice as well as ayamase, plantain and rice. My friend who ate the bulk of the Amala food item complained that it had too much Maggi and the gbegiri flavor did not show up as a result. I then tasted it and I agreed as well.

The ayamase was not bad and the flavor was quite close to as expected but the tripe was over cooked and too soft. It did have an egg which was nice.

The turkey was quite good. I enjoyed it.

Parking
There is parking on the street but the location is close to a police station and it seems a lot of the cops park there. So, take a buddy and have them stay in the car while you run in to get the food.

I ordered efo riro with white rice and some fish on the side. It was juicy, soft and delicious. The little ‘bokotos’ in the efo were a delight. The sauce on the meats was so good with the rice too. Food arrived in good temperature like it was just freshly made and dished.

formatted_address: 811 Bergen St, Newark, NJ 07108, United States
name: ABOKI SUYA SPOT LLC

reviews.text: Don’t waste your time or money on this microwaved food. Food is freshly cooked and the wait is an hour or better. Customer service is poor along with the food. Small portions, the hollow is extremely dry and the chicken Suya. There was no meat on the chicken, please read the other reviews and save ya money. Try Burkina Supermarket on Lyons ave where they cook the food fresh, you can smell from your car. Food is flavorful and portions lasting. I will not return nor recommend. Please do better by your customers, this is your business take pride in it.

I accidentally found this spot, but they were closing, so I couldn't try the food. I returned recently, and the Suya was perfectly fresh, well-seasoned, and delicious with the Aboki bread. Despite some surprising reviews, the food has been great every time I've had it. My only fuss is the menu had Suya fish the first time I visited, but it wasn’t on the menu the few other times I've come. Even though it's almost an hour away, it's now my go to spot, totally worth the trip.

Accidentally stumbled upon this place and so glad I did! The energy is amazing - the food is even better. I have to add the owner is so welcoming. This also has to be the best suya I’ve ever had; I’ll let you folks taste it through the picture.

The worst experience ever, the suya had absolutely no taste, please don't waste your money i bought six sticks and ended up using my own suya pepper at home to re-season. It was dryyyyyy and boring to eat. Gosh please do better!!!!
A place with great testing Nigerian Suya and other Nigeria Dishes. I also enjoyed the freshly baked bread, it brought the test of being in Nigeria back.

name: Nima 2 Restaurant

reviews.text: The variety of food here is plentiful and the customer service is amazing. My favorite dish was the fried Tilapia with acheke (green sauce on the side) as well as the pounded yam with egusi. Call 30 mins ahead of time if you want Tilapia because they cook it to order. However, everything was delicious. I’d definitely be back! I did a full review on Tik Tok: Safiya Lin

ordered from here many times, including just this past Wednesday, and this experience was completely different. The staff member was rude and rushed me through my order. When I got home, I noticed I was given only three pieces of meat, which has never happened before—meat has never been counted or limited in my past orders.

When I called to ask about it, I was told this was the rule, which I know is untrue based on repeated visits. What made it worse was that the staff member’s entire demeanor changed once she heard me speak Twi and realized I’m Ghanaian. Before that, I was treated poorly and served differently.

This experience felt prejudiced and unfair. Very disappointing for a place I’ve supported multiple times.

I drove over an hr to come here but if your Amercian don’t bother they don’t care about you. They are extremely rude, I had a man cut infront of me and instead of the worker telling him to get behind she let him cut me and continued to service him and ignore me. Just RUDE I will never go there again.

Ghanaians are famous for having the sweetest Jollof rice, by sweet I mean most flavorful. If you want heat try Nigerian Jollof. However, this rice was burned, BLAND orange rice, served from a large clear plastic bag, with not even a tiny bit of cardamom, or any spices in it at all. No Akwawaba here. The banku was bogus, the fufu was loose,damb near watery and the pounded yam tasted like sour dough, simply disgusting and disappointing. The woman behind the counter simply saw $$$ when we walked in, offering us a small, half pan of imitation Jollof rice for $150. I have traveled to Ghana and experienced authentic Ghanaian food. I was hoping for even a hint of real Ghanaian cuisine. THIS,  was anything but.   DON'T WASTE YOUR MONEY HERE!
To top it all off, there are no prices listed inside.  If you're doing business here in the US, especially in Newark, New Jersey,  you should make a sincere effort to bridge the cultural gap, provide authentic food and even better customer service. This was a complete waste of my time and hard earned money.

Rude an rushed, I'm American idk wth I'm asking for, but I like to try..I went once last year, the ladys are rude...I tried again this year same attitude different lady, over priced for all tht rice an two pieces of meat.. Girl Bye

reviews.text: Hidden gem. Very fair prices, and excellent tea to boot. Julien is a great guy, super friendly and a pleasure to talk to (and helped me not get towed!) Will absolutely be returning.
1st time having African food. I’m lost in words how amazing this food is! It’s weighed by the pound and the price is the bang for the buck!!! If you’re ever in town it’s a must GO!!!

This place needs to be cleaned up a bit...feels like more of a warehouse than a restaurant. But the people are great...I tried their buffet. This is my first time trying Togo food. And I it was a shock...I got the buffet to go, the chicken had a weird taste as if it was fermented or canned. Whatever it was I couldn't put my finger on it...I have tasted every countries cuisine but eating here was a shock. The lamb and rice was okay. The peanut and chicken was average. This cuisine is just not for me. I will stick to more refined dishes.
Great service Food was served Hot and it's very good.
They used to be really good back in the days, but I dnt know what happened they fell off a little bit, but the food is still good when it fresh

name: Dolapos kitchen

reviews.text:
I decided to order some west African food. I saw they had egusi and ordered on Uber Eats. The egusi is advertised as “with assorted vegetables OR goat meat”. I selected the assorted vegetables option.

When the food arrived there was meat in a red sauce (not egusi). When I called the restaurant this man said assorted vegetables means assorted meat with vegetables. He was so sure of this he asked me to tell him what assorted vegetables means to me (as if I don’t understand the meaning of assorted).

I tried explaining to him they should change the description of the meal because it’s misleading. The man wanted to argue which I did not.

This place is not vegetarian friendly because there was meat in the side of vegetables I ordered.

I also doubt their credibility because they tried to pass off some red sauce as egusi. See video

I usually dont write reviews but i was curious about the reviews after i ordered and got nervous when i saw all of the negative ones!

I ordered the jollof rice/chicken and an order of puff puff and I thoroughly enjoyed it. The portion of rice is enough for at least two meals, and enough for me to make the chicken stretch as well! Just wish it was a little spicier! All in all, im glad i didnt listen to the reviews. I will order again.

Ordered jollof rice and it was so burnt it wasn’t eatable. It left the worst taste of burnt in my mouth from one spoon. I called the restaurant and all I got was sorry. I’m so disappointed in their customer service

I paid almost $28 for this.. it wasn’t uber eats .. I drive down there to get charged $28 for this. I don’t even want to talk about the taste of the food. Very little effort! Next time I have $28 to waste, I will just throw it in the bin atleast it saves me the stress.

Craving Naija food  so bad on my birthday today, I decided to find a place to order on my way back from my trip. I found this place, since it was the only one open. I ordered online, choosing the option to pay when I came to the place. Getting there, I met a pleasant lady who barely understood or spoke English. Somehow we communicated, and I realized that my online order was not valid, as she didn't get it. With minimal use of the menu, I told her what I wanted. The food took over 15mins as she had predicted. The taste of the food however didn't disappoint. I was pretty impressed by that, but everything else was just ..
And the picture of the egg roll is misleading.

I walked in today, excited to try the food. My partner is in the hospital and there aren’t many good food options. I don’t know what was going on there, but the one weird rude woman who was there, was terrible. She looked at me like I was bothering her for walking in. Then when I asked if they were open she asked me what I wanted without even giving me a menu. When she did, I had questions as I had no idea what most of the menu was and didn’t want to blindly order, she looked at me like I was an idiot. I walked out and ordered next door.
What a weird experience. Was she in drugs? Was she special needs? Does she just not care? What a weird weird weird place.

reviews.text: First of all, they were not fully opened when I went cos I was visiting, so I’m grateful for the opportunity.  The person who attended to me is from Cameroon and he was really nice! The meat was sooo good! I wish I had more than 4 piece of plantain lol  The rice wasn’t soft to what I’m used to.  The drink was good aswell. Overall, glad to have a taste of Naija while visiting NJ

The food was so so.  I wanted chicken wings but they didn't have any. So I got jollof rice and chicken.

We had a couple Tito's & cran & Rum Punches - then shots but, they ran out of Tito's.

Extremely disappointing experience. I waited nearly 2 hours for my food, and there were only about six people in the entire restaurant — no excuse for such a long delay. The bartender was rude, unprofessional, and unhelpful, which only added to the frustration.

When the food finally arrived, the stew chicken was dry, hard, and barely had any meat on the bones. Not worth the wait at all.

Unfortunately, this visit left a bad taste in every way. The lack of customer service and poor food quality make it hard to recommend this place. Definitely won’t be returning.

A friend of mine and I got together to get some food and drinks. When I arrived I parked on the street nearby. I walked A friend of mine and I got together to get some food and drinks. When I arrived I parked on the street nearby. I walked in and we sat at the bar. The place was dimly lit and comfortable. We were serviced by a nice bartender and she made our rum punch so good. For my meal I got the chicken jollof rice and it was so good and filling! The DJ came and we danced the night away. I had a good experience!

While the place is well decorated,  this place has declined poorly from the quality of the food to terrible customer service. It's best you dine instad of takeouts! This is $24 assorted meat pepper soup 😕 officially done with this place.

The owners are so pleasant. I’ve been coming here for like 4 years now and I’ve only been disappointed once and even then he made it happen for me!
I forgot to leave my review, but We went on a Thursday and had an excellent experience. Both items on the menu for Thursday were great! Going back again tomorrow
The food was excellent!!! Service was good also. We had FuFu and Potato Green and Palm Butter and Rice!!!!
The food has been consistently good for over 20 years. I’ve raised my children on this food. Great portions too
Food is expensive but the portions are small. Food was cold and not fresh. This meal was $20.

formatted_address: 382 Clinton Pl Apartment 3, Newark, NJ 07112, United States
name: NIGERIAN SUYA & TINZ

reviews.text:
Authentic Nigerian Suya in Newark. Nigerian Suya and Tinz is easily one of the best Nigerian suya spots in Newark. The beef and chicken suya are perfectly grilled, packed with authentic yaji spice, and served fresh with onions and tomatoes—exactly how real suya should taste.

The owner is friendly, service is quick, and the prices are great for the generous portions. Whether you’re craving West African flavors or trying suya for the first time, this place delivers consistently amazing food.

Highly recommend stopping by or ordering takeaway if you want truly authentic Nigerian suya in New Jersey
I just got curious and stopped in the beef suya was amazing and the service was kind and inviting

name: Adidun Cuisine

reviews.text:
If I ever tell you food is sweet, just know it’s SWEET,hands down!
I don’t cook rubbish, and I definitely can’t eat rubbish.
This Amala?
100 over 100 minus NOTHING! 🔥🍽️

Ordered via DoorDash from 12:43pm as of 3:55pm, the order has yet to be received. Contacted the restaurant and the lady who picked up said that the goat meat was not ready. By the way, the Dasher was there waiting (which is not fair for Dasher nor the customer). I get off work at 4pm and I missed my lunch. This is not the first time this has happened to me. If the order is not available just deny the order. Y’all need to do better. Check out how successful a business has been in business for many years. Horrible experience!

The menu is small but precise . I went here for the amala dish and I wasn’t disappointed one bit . It didn’t have more oil than stew like so many places and the meats were cooked great. They also had chi chin as “kpanu” while you wait for your food and that made the experience even better . I also got Malta Guinness which I couldn’t open because someone took the opener so if you are that someone kindly return to adidun! They also offer catering for large events as well!
Overall,I had a wonderful experience and would highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a delicious African food
It makes no sense to wait over an hour for food every time. It’s never a quick in-and-out. Customer service is slow, rude, and honestly disappointing. Y’all can do better — that’s big facts.

formatted_address: 810 Clinton Ave, Newark, NJ 07108, United States
name: Bistop African Restaurant and Naija Shawarma

reviews.text: I was lucky enough to stumble upon this gem while doing some work in the area and had a delicious chicken shawarma. The chicken was so tender and the sauce was delicious! The owners, Am Olu and his wife, were both so kind and welcoming which made the experience that much more enjoyable. This was my first time trying Nigerian cuisine and I thoroughly enjoyed it! I look forward to going back when I’m in the area again.

Unfortunately came in expecting a different kind of chicken shawarma but that is on me. I waited maybe 25-30 minutes for the shawarma and it was not great at all. It’s just chicken, coleslaw and a hotdog for $18.. The lady was nice though.
The Shawama was yummy and it was full in it which it a + first time customer from TikTok. Will definitely come back.
The lady was so nice and the food is so good I ordered yam and fish
The food here is so good 🔥🔥🔥, everything I have bought so far is always fresh and 100%

formatted_address: 500 Clinton Ave, Newark, NJ 07108, United States
name: DorBat’s Diner

reviews.text: My order was quite enjoyable. I had some large fish that was topped with rice that had been seasoned and sauteed onions and peppers. Since I had never really had African food before, I ordered something that didn't really fit with my order, so I really appreciate that they phoned me. The ginger beverage was flavorful, zesty, and refreshing.
Wonderful family owned African soul food Diner. If you are ever in Newark New Jersey you owe it to yourself to go by their spot. Wonderful people and great food!

I really enjoyed my order. I got a big fish which was covered in cooked onions and peppers and spiced rice which both were delicious. I really appreciate that they called me because I ordered something that wouldn’t make sense with my order (I haven’t really eaten African food before). The Ginger drink was delicious and fresh and spicy.

Fried shrimp: Adequate. Standard size. Flavor was average. You will need a glaze or dipping sauce to enhance what little flavor it has.

Fried sweet and sticky wings:  The sauce was a good flavor. I can't imagine the wings being good plain because the sauce is the total flavor profile of the chicken wing. The wings had a nice crunch but something was lacking. I'm not sure if it was how it was prepared, the freshness, or maybe the seasoning or lack thereof.

Strawberry cake: Purchased two cakes (stupidly). Both were bad but even more so the strawberry cake. The cake was stiff, dry, crumbly, and stale. I had the food delivered so when I saw the container I can tell it was refrigerated. I thought perhaps if I just sit it out for awhile some of the moisture would come back and regain softness but no it didn't. Avoid their cakes if you see it refrigerated. Unless it's on a cake stand / plate it's not worth the gamble with your money. I don't know how long they've been refrigerated or when they were baked.

Potato salad: The first bite all I tasted was water. More bites it was just on the bland side.

Fried whiting: Fine. Not too thin. That's what I was most concerned about when ordering whiting and it became the least issue with the meal.

Fried rice: meh

Jollof rice: I feel like the peas and carrots were just  edible ornaments. Much like the green sprinkles they had on the chicken and mac. No real additive  to the flavor of the dish and I personally didn't care for it. I mean it gave it a different texture in some parts and color but I rather good food than aesthetics. The rice has a spicy kick to it fair warning. I can't speak on the authenticity but I thought it was better than their signature fried rice.

Mac and cheese: I don't believe it should've been called mac and cheese. I tasted no cheese. When I think mac and cheese I think southern mac and cheese which is cheesy, has sharp cheddar cheese, and soft noodles.  This had none of that. It was like eating a side of stiff rigid mac noodles that was boiled in some seasoned water earlier in the day and now is being served later in the day where it's just stuck together room temperature elbow pasta.
Food here is absolutely delicious, red snapper and the loaded rice are my favorite 🥰 Do yourself a favor and go get something to eat from here

formatted_address: 1006 Bergen St, Newark, NJ 07112, United States
name: African pot with Temmy

reviews.text: Don't even bother coming to this place.. they literally TAKE FOREVER TO FINISH AN ORDER. Waited pver 15mins for a order that was placed.

My boyfriend has always loved their food and the meat items are always good. But veggie orders are not great. Ordered okra and came with shrimp pieces, I am allergic to shrimp. Luckily I found it after few bites so I was able to manage.

If I could give 0 starts I would.  Thos food is absolutely disgusting. We ordered the stew chicken with rice and plantains. Plantains didn't come rice is dry and too spicy. And yall can see the chicken which is 1 turkey wing cut into 3 pieces. 17.99 for this. What a Joke. Don't get me started about the lady who answers the phone RUDE.

This is very sad , i mean very sad. If you do not know how to make a specialty Nigerian meal, STOP and go learn. First time ordering designer stew and white rice from this restaurant  , in all honesty the designer stew was 95% water , no chunk stew to eat with , literally poured the designer stew on the rice and WELP all sunk under the plate. And they charged $20 for this , this is so sad. Stop making special meals if you are not capable. How do you eat designer stew at its watery state?? Literally had to stop eating and dump out in the garbage. And it has ZERO spiciness , like are you kidding me ?! What a shame.
The pepper soup portion is too small and also filled with bones and fatty meat . I didn’t enjoy it at all

formatted_address: 592 S 10th St, Newark, NJ 07103, United States
name: Watinomaa restaurant

reviews.text: You should come trie out for yourself it the best , trust me you won’t be disappointed!!!!!

formatted_address: 36 Union Ave, Irvington, NJ 07111, United States
name: Eatwell African Cuisine

reviews.text: The other day I ordered, Eatwell African Cuisine, for lunch. I had ordered their, Jollof Rice lunch w/ Mixed Meat. The mixed meat came with Beef, Cow Skin, and Tripe. I was under the impression it’d come with Beef, Goat, and Chicken. The Jollof was not bad at all. Ate all of it, and I am not a huge rice person. Mostly the Jollof meals are built around the rice and the meat if applicable are a complement to the meal. I made the unfortunate decision to take a sip of what I thought were the juices of the mixed meat. I found out the hard way that it was simply straight up oil and fat. The beef skin was ok, the tripe was inedible, but the actual beef meat was really good. I’d love to try this place again, hopefully next time with a better understanding. But my reviews are based on flavor and experience. The beef (tail????) was really good, the other meats we fairly inedible. The Jollof was lacking any depth of flavor, but was fairly decent. I give them a generous rating because the staff was exceptional, and kind. From the exterior of the restaurant you wouldn’t expect it to be so nice on the inside. I’d love to try this place again if I’m in the area. The potential is there and I think I may have just ordered incorrectly.

This is my first time ordering here and trying not to be too harsh. Very disappointed with my order and I wish I carefully observed every foods posted here and their plates. I got to say of all Nigerian foods I have ordered this have to be the worst. I know i am already harsh but seriously, why are my orders MICROWAVED before being handed to me??? I hate how it ruined the whole taste and smell. DOBETTER!

I placed an order with this restaurant today and I wished I could go back in time to rethink the decision. I ordered amala, gbegiri & ewedu. They decided to send me pounded yam, gbegiri & ewedu instead without my consent, a combination of food l've never tried before, I called the restaurant severally but no response. I was so angry I almost started crying. I just got back from work hungry and tired. I would have appreciated if they canceled my order instead. Their food is nice I won't lie, but I wished they weren't greedy.
Because only greed would make you do that. left the food on my table for hours cause I didn't even know what to do with it. Do better

Do NOT eat here, the food is not fresh, you can taste the difference between food that was just cooked vs food that was cooked days ago, they are real skimp on the meat and overdo it on the rice. The meat was tough, overcooked, couldn’t put a fork through it and they only gave 3 little pieces of meat. Just save yourself the disappointment and eat somewhere else!! I’m so serious

Eatwell has been consistently awesome for many years now. Everything on their menu is spot on. The service and food presentation are equally great. And you can also order off UberEats as well.

Unlike some other places, they're always looking to improve their quality and service.

formatted_address: 266 Lyons Ave, Newark, NJ 07112, United States
name: BURKINA SUPERMARKET

reviews.text: I always order the chicken with everything on it and it’s always so flavorful and fresh. The portions are large and the seasoning is spicy if you like. Can’t wait to try other items on the menu. 100% recommend.

The staff is welcoming, warm !  The chicken "flambé" is excellent, all the flavor is there, its like being on the land of integrated men. Congratulations to all the team, who keeps improving the decor !!!
Very nice place that welcome people from everywhere together.. delicious food specially from Africa and very nice communities.. make of this place your next stop. You won't regret it!!!😊😊
Perfect place to be with the new bar
Come and get another feeling and the difference of living peace love and all u deserve ✨ ❤

formatted_address: 132 S Essex Ave, City of Orange, NJ 07050, United States
name: Odabro African Restaurant and Lounge

reviews.text:
I got the chance to try this restaurant for dinner. When I arrived I parked on the street nearby. I walked in and was greeted and sat at one of the tables. The place was super spacious. I had:

Henny punch
BBQ Chicken
Plain Chicken
Nkwobi (Nigerian dish made with cow's foot)
Tilapia with jollof rice and plantain

The tilapia was my favorite and delicious! All in all I had a really good experience!

"I had such a fantastic time at Odabro last night! The atmosphere was amazing, cozy, lively, stylish, and the staff were all so friendly and attentive. The specialty drink jungle fever  was perfectly crafted, and there's a great selection of cocktails to choose from. It’s the perfect spot for a great evening out. I'll definitely be back!"
The food was literally top tier!! I ate it before taking a picture but if you want real authentic African food definitely come here :) this is my go to spot

Service was good.
Very pleasant staff.
Atmosphere was a party vibe…
Hookah was bussing as well…
A one stop shop…
You can eat, drink, and smoke…
Food delicious and vibes is chill. Bartender are cute and friendly. Definitely check it out!

formatted_address: 877 Springfield Ave, Irvington, NJ 07111, United States
name: TASTE OF LAGOS

reviews.text: Food was great, friendly atmosphere with good attitude, respectful service and great staffs , owner was really calm and drink friendly . would recommend!

Had a great experience at Taste of Lagos! The ambiance is vibrant, and the food definitely delivers on authentic Nigerian flavors. The jollof rice was well-seasoned, and the suya had a nice smoky kick. The portions were solid, and the service was friendly. Oh LAWD!!

I ordered lamb chops with the 2 side for $30 , I only received 1 side and 2 lamb chops. Then they proceeded to argue with me over my food and what I paid for. Food was dry and over cooked . Very nasty attitude and speak in their foreign language when I asked for my money back or to be accommodated. I was told tommorrow I could be accommodated . Very poor service never again. I Don’t RECOMMEND DONT GO !!!

I had an amazing experience at TOL!

The music in the restaurant was a vibe. The staff were helpful and accommodating and most importantly the food was delicioussss - I even went back for more!

I’d recommend Taste Of Lagos to anyone who wants to leave with a full belly and a smile on their face.

Can’t wait to go back :)
Food was amazing. My first time trying Nigerian food and I was not disappointed! Staff was friendly and informative and helped me with picking a dish that I absolutely loved.

formatted_address: 2726 Morris Ave, Union, NJ 07083, United States
name: Surulere Suya Spot Union

reviews.text:
We came here excited to try something new and left extremely disappointed. The service was poor, and the food was even worse.

We waited 55 minutes for our food—something that realistically could have taken about 20 minutes. No one communicated the delay to us at any point. We were only informed after we had already decided to leave, which was frustrating and unprofessional.

When we finally got the food home, it was unacceptable. The chicken was extremely tough, the rice was basic and underwhelming, and the plantains were nearly burned. For the wait time and cost, this was not worth it at all.

On top of that, the floors inside were very slippery, seemingly from oil, which felt like a safety hazard.

Overall, this experience was disappointing from start to finish. Better communication, food quality, and attention to cleanliness are seriously needed.

Waited nearly an hour for beef stew and stew chicken. Originally wanted to dine in but the meal took so long to make we changed to take out. The beef stew had 3 pieces and wasn’t tender at all. 2 pieces of chicken that was tough to chew. I don’t understand how chicken can be tough after a stew. Never going back and should have checked the reviews before giving this place a try.

This is so far the worst chicken suya ever. Today been the 31th Oct 2025. The owner is getting greedy and more greedy by the day. Increasing food price and reducing the food. It makes no sence if you decided to Increase price but have the decency of giving quality and quantity.  Nothing in this earth will bring me back to this selfish,greedy restaurant ever again.  I was the regular customer but today what they sold my husband was unacceptable and when he called ,they told him that their madam ask them to reduce the quality and quantity.  Even them the sales boys and girls said the woman is been unnecessary greedy.  Please guys avoid this restaurant with passion
Food tastes good but was very disappointed with the portion sizes. Can not justify paying nearly $60 for.

Giving this spot a 4.4. Ordered takeout with good and quick service. Had a craving for jollof rice, egusi, beef suya and sweet plantains. Have to say, almost everything was delicious. It hit the spot for good Nigerian food, but my only reservation was the jollof rice. It tasted burnt and was a tad stale or old perhaps. It was the least favorite of my order. Sad because I was really looking forward to enjoying it. But on a better note, the beef suya was perfectly cooked and oh so spicy with sliced cabbage and red onions, which I loved! I also like how it was served. The egusi was really tasty with stock fish and I asked for goat meat. The sweet plantains were mouthwatering and juicy! Perfection!! I am not African, but definitely ate like one that day. And yes, I ate everything together..lol. I certainly enjoyed the pounded yam, which I dipped in the egusi soup. Yum!!! My only comment to management other than please don't serve burnt food is, please do something about the air circulation. Walking in, the restaurant smelled stale. This is off-putting and can Overall good local African restaurant and staff was friendly. But certainly room for improvement.

formatted_address: 1020 Capitol Tr, Newark, DE 19711, United States
name: Catch 45

reviews.text: We went here for my son’s birthday and had an amazing meal. The inside of the restaurant is beautiful, there’s plenty of parking, the food is excellent and the service is great. Everything we tried was delicious and the portions were plentiful - lots of food to share family style between six people with a ton of leftovers to take home. Wonderful experience and we will definitely return. They handled my food allergies perfectly too, very accommodating.

Love Catch 45! The food is always so fresh and flavorful!! I’ve thanked the cook a few times!  The host(Jessica)  who is always working and taking orders is always professional and kind as well as helpful. We are regulars and I couldn’t recommend this food more! My only complaint is when they don’t have the vegan potato greens on the menu. Please keep them on daily! :-)

I visited Catch 45 for the first time and I had such an excellent experience that I will definitely be coming back. The guy that attended to me was so pleasant and welcoming, the restaurant is aesthetically pleasing with aftobeats playing on the Tv. Very clean and neat too. I should have gotten the name of the guy cos he went above and beyond. He explained the menu to me and even let me taste the beef pattie (meat pie) before I purchased. He offered me juice to go with my pattie, I felt like a princess with the 5star customer service. I came for just Jollof rice and chicken but I ended up buying the goat stew and dry rice as well. You have definitely earned a customer with this impeccable service 😊 . The jollof and chicken for $50 was a good portion too as you can see from the picture. I enjoyed the food and very happy I found you guys as you’re truly a catch 😉.

My party drove here from Maryland and it was worth every minute! Beautiful ambiance and decor inside the restaurant and great parking. I’ve never been to a Liberian restaurant this upscale before. Great for parties or dates. The bar was nice and the presentation was great. The food came out fairly quickly for a party of 7 and was very flavorful. Large portions (especially considering the price), great service, and great music! Wide selection of Liberian dishes, including Liberian desserts! Everyone in my party loved what they ordered so much we all bought at least 1-2 dishes to go! We will definitely be back. This restaurant was in a class on its own. Kudos to the owners!

Dis take out and dinned in, ordered the fufu with cassava leaves. Had a mixture of chicken,fish, and something else. It was delicious the first time, take out not so much. Ordered the goat soup was very flavorful and spicy. Lastly Jollof and rice with lamb was well seasoned very good both times. The second time also ordered chicken with jollof and i was very upset. I received 4 wing dings. Now come on now… i could’ve received regular size chicken wings. The time takes waaayyy to long, atmosphere doesn’t have a hint of African.

reviews.text: For my first time here I think I’m going to make it my last.to start I ordered 2 meals and one bowl off rice to go( jollof rice with goat meat,fufu and spinach soup,and just plain jollof rice no meat) for a grand total of 53.31..the jollof rice and 2 pieces of goat meat 25 dollars the rice had no flavor and tasted burnt and smelled burnt,the goat was only fat and bones.the fufu was regular and spinach soup was dry surprisingly for being soup. Everything was nasty tasteless and dry to be “AUTHENTIC” African food it didn’t live up to the standards of taste that I’m used to

Food is expensive there. Was told fish was made fresh,  but  texture was cement and temperature told otherwise. Barely had flavor and some spicy sauce on it.  Jollof rice missed the mark but the vegetables were ok. One server was NASTY and the other had class.  How could freshly prepared and cooked fish,  be so hard its  able to crack cement in half.

Gold pretty silverware and nice decor, but food was lacking.

Food looks great , nice , shiny , yummy , little do you know it has ZERO TASTE . Ordered the village rice , bro i could not eat 5 spoons . Tasted FLAT

The food is always on point and they never disappoint. If you don’t like what you had , reach out and they will compensate. Been buying all my meal here for over 5 years , started from the Springfield location and here in Clinton location

I spoke with the lady who is part owner of the place. She's very nice and accommodating. We live far from this restaurant but we'll definitely return in the future. There's plenty of place there for people to sit. You can even throw a small party in there.
The best African restaurant in Newark the Dibi is wow
Food and everything 10/10 definitely coming back!!!
Delicious food and great customer service
Food and services are amazing

name: B&B African Restaurant

reviews.text: Awful food ever, We ordered a variety of African food here thinking we got the best African food around us, I spoke to the manager (Benson) he was so rude and acting loopy on the phone. I have never tasted such sour vegetable like that in my life, The pepper-soup too was nothing to write home about. He won’t refund our money or care about how that makes us feel. If anyone is looking for a great taste that worth your money, This isn’t a spot for that. So horrible. This restaurant doesn’t represent what Nigeria Jollof stands out for.  👎🏾👎🏾👎🏾👎🏾👎🏾👎🏾👎🏾👎🏾👎🏾👎🏾👎🏾👎🏾👎🏾. Horrible
It was our first time ordering. We were in the neighborhood and we needed Naija food. Food was made fresh so it took a while but the food tasted great. We have no complaints.

Been here a few times. Maybe the people too lazy to come inside a restaurant to eat need to stop complaining about their orders. If you want something quick go to a fast food. If you want quality then you need to learn some patience. When ordering inside the restaurant Mr. Benson really takes his time. He even had brought our fresh cut watermelon while we waited. His food portions are huge. You get great service when you sit to eat! Food is tasty and cannot complain.
The egusi was so spicy and the pounded yam was too sticky

I went to the B&M restaurant in Oakwood Ohio on 08-23-24 arrived at about 6pm and did not received my food until 7pm. I was about 4 people ahead of me, but Service was very slow. ZThe floor was filthy as it had not been mopped for days with my shoes sticking to the floor. I overheard a lady who was waiting in front of me state that she would be coming back to this restaurant and I will not be either!

formatted_address: 257 Clinton Ave, Newark, NJ 07108, United States
name: The Origin Restaurant & Lounge

reviews.text:
It’s unfortunate that I spent $60 and received something not worth it in anyway. I do not know what changed in your restaurant. Please did you change your cook? I have eaten your food more than 3 times prior to yesterday. They were good. The one I bought yesterday was so bad looking, tastes bad, some meat tastes bad, and the pepper in it was blazing like a fire tunnel.

Infact I have been in and out the restroom as if I ate a food poison. I had to take a medication.

I don’t usually give a bad review, but this is so disturbing, couldn’t sleep last night and might stay out of work today.

Please fix your kitchen.

Girls trip. We traveled from two different states and The Origin kept coming up on our timeline for a must go to lounge.  We took a Lyft and was greeted outside where they checked our purses.  We were told that it was $10 to enter.  We paid it and went inside.  There was no one to greet us.  We sat near the bar for 5 minutes and we had to walk around the bar to find a waitress! She advised that we could sit at one another of the many open tables.  So we sat at 4 & 5.  Then another woman came over and told us that we could only sit at one table.  With four people we were very confused.  As to the fact that there was no one sitting next to us.  Picture to see empty table.  We were also told that we only had one hour to drink, eat and possibly smoke Hookah.  This is not the customer service we were expecting.  What a disappointment.

The closest experience to Africa you’ll ever get while in New Jersey/New York area. I guess that’s why it was named the Origin. A gem. Really loved every second of my visit. Reminds me so much of the night life in Nairobi, vibes on vibes. The staff are very friendly, helpful a and welcoming. They make you feel right at home from the moment you step your foot into the premises. The only thing that sucks is the fact that they don’t operate till morning, they close. It’s not their fault though, I guess it’s just an American thing. Places can’t operate till morning🤦🏾‍♂️. They sell Sheesha/Hookah and alcohol at very fair prices. I totally recommend this place. Gone twice and have all been epic experiences. Made me miss home less. Great crowd, great music, great African dishes. I’ll always Originate for as long as am in New York/New Jersey.
Hair in my soup ?20 for hair but after awhile the cook I spoke with was very understanding and he insured me that it was a honest mistake and have removed his other staff the food was delicious

I always have a good time when I go to Origin! I also feel like it's always very crowded upstairs on a Friday/Saturday. Upstairs is supposed to be VIP area. The food is good but they need to keep the consistency because sometimes it's not always as good. The service from waitresses is somewhat slow but I guess it depends on the night. Other than that Origin is one of the African Clubs I enjoy going to. Also after 11pm you have to pay to get in. Usually it's $10 or $20.

formatted_address: 42 Commerce St #4003, Newark, NJ 07102, United States
name: Eko Atlantic Restaurant and lounge

reviews.text:
I had high expectations for EKO Atlantic Restaurant, especially after seeing the buzz on TikTok and planning to stop by before a concert. Unfortunately, the experience fell far short of what we anticipated.
We made reservations for 5:00 p.m., knowing the restaurant opens at 4:00 p.m. However, when my group of three arrived, it felt as though the place had just opened moments before. Staff were still cleaning and arranging the space, which immediately set an unorganized tone. To add to the confusion, the bartender doubled as the hostess, and the cook was also acting as the DJ—an interesting setup, but not one that inspired confidence in a smooth dining experience.
Once we received the menu, we were quickly told that there was no fish available, which was extremely disappointing since fish makes up the majority of the menu—especially frustrating considering they had just opened for the day.
We decided to proceed with drinks, which were actually very good. We also ordered the sweet chili wings, and those were genuinely enjoyable. Unfortunately, the food took over an hour to arrive.
For our mains, we ordered jollof rice with goat (two plates) and one turkey option. The goat dishes were overwhelmingly spicy—not a pleasant heat, but an intense spice that completely overpowered the meal. On top of that, the goat meat was tough. The turkey wings were better in comparison, but still lacked flavor.
Overall, it was a bad experience. When all three people at the table agree, it’s hard to ignore. Maybe on another night or at a later time the experience would have been different, but based on this visit, it missed the mark. The restaurant is small, cute, and definitely has potential—but potential alone isn’t enough.
Given the hype and our plans for the evening, I expected a much better vibe and execution. Hopefully, with better preparation and consistency, this place can grow into what it promises to be.

Dinner | $30-50
Decided to pick this spot for my birthday, they seemed strict about making a reservations just to get there to an empty restaurant on a Friday night! This place has great aesthetics, but that's honestly where the positives end. The food was terribly disappointing, my friends complained that the hot wings were so salty they were barely edible. The drinks were just as bad; both the margaritas and Long Islands were absolutely disgusting. Let’s, not forget how there was only one bartender who left out at one point  leaving us there and told us  “she’ll be back”🤔before my Homegirl could order a drink!

The music was decent, but even that lost its charm once we realized it was literally being played straight off YouTube. (no dj as promised)
Customer service was the biggest downfall. When we politely said we weren't happy with the drinks, we were met with attitude and rudeness instead of professionalism. To make matters worse, we were overcharged by $30, only to be told it was a
"mistake."
At that point, my group and I decided to leave. If all you care about is how a place looks and don't mind bad food, terrible drinks, and poor service, then maybe this spot is for you. But please do not ignore the bad reviews like I did, because They are telling the truth. And they delete reviews!!
I had a great time. The food was delicious. Beautiful cozy venue. Yeah, I would go back.

Decided to visit based on good reviews and tik tok videos.  Parking is simply horrible in this area. $25.00 to park on the street is ridiculous. I was really hoping the food was going to be great. My family of 4 was truly disappointed. Due to the parking we had to do take out. The Rasta pasta and jollof  rice  was horrible and too spicy to enjoy.  Now if you like your food spicy you may enjoy it. The fried chicken look weird and was awful. My husband was craving the Agosi soup and requested soft beef and we got home it was not edible. The bathroom smelled like  sewage. They need to clean the bathrooms. No toilet paper holder-  just a bunch of used toilet paper rolls stack on a rack. I wish I could get a refund. Paid over $90 only to  throw it out. I do not recommend take out. Maybe dinning in would have been better.

When asking for an update the bartender had a bad attitude and acted like we were bothering her. When the food finally arrived it was bland and unappetizing. We really wanted to enjoy the night but the  treatment we got from the bartender plus the long wait time ruined it.

formatted_address: 150 S Dupont Hwy, New Castle, DE 19720, United States
name: SUYA HOUSE AFRICAN GRILL

reviews.text: I’ve eaten here twice once for takeout and once we dined in. Overall the food is good. During my visits I ordered Tilapia Suya twice, Chicken Shawarma twice, jollof rice, and peanut butter soup. I highly recommend the Chicken Shawarma. The Tilapia was a good option but my only recommendation is for it to be cooked less crispy because it was fried a bit too hard and was tough to chew. I enjoyed the sauce that was served on the side. I would recommend you try this place for yourself it’s worth it. The staff is very friendly. Items are made to order so be patient.

We recently visited Suya House in Newcastle, drawn by its strong Google reviews and our own curiosity to explore African cuisine. Since we’re not very familiar with the food, we asked our server for recommendations. She suggested the lamb curry with fufu and assured us the fried fish was much better than what’s shown online. She also mentioned that the restaurant is under new ownership—still operating as Suya House—but with improved quality compared to the previous management.

We ordered the fried fish, lamb curry with fufu, and a hibiscus drink. The drink was absolutely delightful—refreshing and full of flavor. The fish came deep-fried with crispy edges, bone-in, topped with sautéed vegetables, brown rice, and plantain chips. Overall, it was a satisfying dish, though the rice was unfortunately dry and hard.

As for the lamb curry, I’m not sure how it’s traditionally supposed to taste, so I can’t fairly judge the flavor. However, the lamb itself was dry and tough, which made it difficult to enjoy. We mentioned this to the server, but she didn’t respond, which felt a bit awkward.

We came with open minds and were excited to try something new. While some elements were enjoyable, others missed the mark for us. Still, we appreciate the opportunity to explore a new cuisine and hope the restaurant continues to grow under its new ownership.

Tried something different today. African Grill. Food was good! Small cozy place inside. Outdoor seating available. No alcohol at this time. Had Garlic Buffalo wings. Good. Goat with Rice. Also good. Goat done a little more than we’re used too, but was good. A lot of pieces throughout. Our waitress was polite and attentive.

While driving through Delaware, I made a stop at Suya House Africa Grill to recharge with some authentic West African cuisine. I went with the Jollof rice and fish, paired with an ice-cold Zobo drink infused with ginger - the perfect combo. 😋 The meal was absolutely delicious, and I highly recommend Suya House Africa Grill to anyone craving the bold, rich flavors of West Africa.

Their menu features popular dishes from countries like Ghana, Nigeria, and Cameroon, offering a true taste of the region. And yes, I have to say it: Ghana Jollof still reigns supreme 🥇. No other Jollof rice, not even Nigeria’s, comes close in flavor and deliciousness.🤩

Prices are very affordable, and I definitely got my money’s worth.👍A must-visit spot if you're in the area!

I drive all the way from Dover, DE for this deliciousness. The FuFu, the Wings, the Rasta Pasta, I could go on and on. Food so good, it never made it in the picture 😂🤌🏽 The music makes you feel like your in your house cookin, Jammin and eating 🥰 Called my family and got 2 to go orders.

reviews.text: Their food is delicious and customer service is amazing! I placed a large order for 10+ people and the quality, quantity, and packaging was perfect. The food aside, the service could be better given the lead time. The staff seemed overwhelmed when I visited to pick up my order.

I came here to celebrate my birthday with family and it was such a wonderful experience! The food was absolutely delicious, the service was phenomenal, and the atmosphere was warm and welcoming. I’m so glad there’s a Senegalese spot like this nearby so I don’t have to travel all the way to Harlem. They’ll definitely be seeing me again, 11/10 recommend!

This place is an authentic home style cooking restaurant. The food was delectable and flavored impeccably. I had the lamb with Jolloff rice and spring roll appetizer. Mohammed was the consummate host and gave us suggestions on what to order and pairings. The ginger and hibiscus juices are great too.

I finally had the chance to try fufu for the first time and this place did not disappoint. It was A+ service and food. Very flavorful and the drinks were great aswell. Desserts even better. Definitely a place to come too. Loved every minute. First time trying African food. And I loved it. Must try spot for sure.

reviews.text: I was really disappointed with my recent visit. The dish I usually order was sold out, and the staff made me choose something else instead. unfortunately, the alternative meal wasn’t satisfying at all. I feel that if certain items are unavailable, they should be marked as sold out online to avoid misleading customers. It’s frustrating to come in expecting something and then be forced to settle for something you don’t want. Restaurant should appreciate their customers by being transparent and answering a better experience.
I Love it here I come to this place at least 3 times a month sit Down in get my Eat on ...👌🏾

Restaurant located in Newark NJ. Plenty of food. Their chicken Yassa is amazing.  Had lunch and subsequently ordered dinner. Truly worth the price.
I'm revisiting my review by downgrading their service for 2 reasons:
1. You DO NOT increase your prices without prior notice to your customers. Neither on their menu nor on their site, there was question of increasing their price from $20 to $25. That's a whopping 25% increase. When they want to add a $5 delivery price on their service, they should give advance notice. Prices are increasing everyday, but businesses take the time to inform their customers ahead of time. But I put a phone order of $20 as I usually do, then 5mn later the lady called me back and said there is now a $5 increase on the price for delivery cost. And when I asked since when, she said that's coming from the boss. Mind you that ordering through Uber comes cheaper than that.
2. The Yassa came with more oil than anything else. I'm attaching the picture for you to see. I resorted to actually empty a lot of it to be able to use it. That's not healthy
3. I came one night around 9:30PM to get some food and guess what: they had no rice for an African restaurant. It's like having no chicken in an American restaurant. That was the second time they ran out of rice, and they never even offered to get rice from the nearby. Unthinkable. so both times, I left empty handed.
So at the end of the day, the food might have more value than the service

reviews.text: From entry, we were greeted warmly by our waitress Des. When seated, with ease and familiarity, she told us the best options for us on the menu. Though they didn't have Reisling at the moment she suggested white Sangria, that was simply delicious.  Now for the food every suggestion was delicious from the Staple Tacos, Jerk Chicken Empanadas, Vegetable Medley, Lamb Chops and Stuffed Salmon. In summary, we'll be back. The food at OKO Fine Cuisine hits differently — bold, soulful flavors that are authentic and cooked to perfection. Theres something for everyone’s your taste buds, including vegan and vegetarian options. The atmosphere is a cool vibe with a live band often playing. Try OKO Fine Cuisine and you will leave full, satisfied, and already thinking about your next visit.

Our waitress mimi was so beautiful.  The food and atmosphere is always a vibe. If you haven't been here what are you wanting for.  If you love good food and good people come to oko. You would have thought we was there with a few people because the service was still great and they were about to close. I wasn't rushed the service was great and the oxtail empanads. I will advise you not to get them. They will have you hooked.  I love supporting my people. Definitely a vibe.

I love supporting Black-owned businesses and this one I would definitely give a four out of five.

The food options were wide and everything was tasty in the Sunday brunch menu. As someone who hasn’t had very good experiences with African food or African restaurants, this one was definitely a standout.

The service overall was okay. At opening time they were still preparing and setting up so we waited a little bit, but everything turned out nice. The owner came out and took some pictures and a video of the buffet. He was VERY NICE and gave us suggestions on how to make seafood tacos 🌮 from the buffet.

The atmosphere was great. The only thing I would mention is that there was a heavy smell of bleach that caused a bit of a sinus flare for me so I had to sit close to the exit. After I left, I didn’t feel too great and that’s the only reason keeping me from returning. 🥹

2024: Sat at the bar. 1st the good. The food, drinks and wait staff are terrific.

Perfectly Fried Snapper (Our crispy deep fried mouthwatering snapper).  Pleasantly surprised by their take on the beef taco. Love the "The Aunt" (Amaretto, Irish Crème, Coffee Liqueur and Aromatic Bitters). And you gotta try Fried Basa Bites (Perfectly fried in our house batter served with our house bang bang sauce).

Now the not so good. It tough to get a reservation. This is an out growth from the owners (a really great guy) catering business now conducted in a brick & mortar. My suggestion is to just show up in the hopes that there is space at the bar. This place is well worth it.

reviews.text: Please keep this standard! As Nigerian that loves Ghanaian and Senegalese food, I am amazed . I couldn’t stop eating. Great portions and unbeatable quality . They give worth for the money. You will see me more often !
Great food but takes forever to be ready , don’t matter if you call ahead or order online . Can’t spend all day trynna get a food on the menu

This was a beautiful hidden treasure in Irvington New Jersey. The food was amazing I got the cooked yam and spinach soup the food was fresh and very tasty. The prices are reasonable as well and the customer service was amazing definitely going back!

I had an incredible experience at Potbelly African Restaurant! I ordered the banku and grilled tilapia, and it was hands down one of the best I’ve had. The tilapia was perfectly seasoned and grilled to perfection. The banku had the perfect texture and paired so well with the pepper sauce and vegetables.

The presentation was beautiful, the portion was generous, and every bite tasted fresh and authentic. You can truly feel the passion and skill that goes into their cooking.

The atmosphere was warm and welcoming, and the service was excellent, friendly staff who made sure everything was just right.

If you’re looking for delicious, well prepared African food, Potbelly African Restaurant is absolutely worth the visit. I’ll definitely be back, and I highly recommend it to anyone craving real, flavorful Ghanaian cuisine!
