From the moment you walk in, you’re greeted with a warm and inviting atmosphere that feels like a home away from home. The earthy decor, the traditional music playing softly in the background, and the aroma of spices set the stage for an exceptional meal.
If you’ve never tried Ethiopian food before this spot is a must try!You will not be disappointed. Food was great, service was phenomenal and the environment felt like home away from home.

I discovered this place at the “Festival of Nations” last year and was immediately blown away. Discovered when searching for them, that they were close to me!

Finally got the chance to try it, for takeout a few months ago. I ate it so quickly I didn’t get a chance to take a photo! Went there again recently and remembered to snap a photo.

Their sambusa is really good. The dried spices that come with it are just as good, and have a little kick to them. Get them!

Got the chicken tibbs and lamb (kelwa begged). It’s authentic, delicious, and LARGE portions!

Merhaba will now forever be on my list of go to places in U-City. If you haven’t been here, take the risk and go; you won’t be disappointed!
Stopped by this restaurant on a whim. It was well worth it. The food was delicious and service was great.

formatted_address: 3970 Union Rd, St. Louis, MO 63125, United States
name: Taste Of Bosnia

reviews.text: This place is fantastic. I got the doner kebab and it came out super fast. The lepinja bread was perfectly soft and crispy, the yogurt garlic sauce was superb, and the meat was tender and well seasoned. The sandwich was also huge for 13.50. It could be 2 meals for a smaller eater. I will absolutely be back when I visit St.Louis next!

My family and I came in today, on a Saturday at 2pm. The restraint was surprisingly busy. We got 3 entres. All were amazing!!! If you’re from STL and wanting to try Bosnian food for the first time, this is the place!!!!! 5/5 stars

Taste of Bosnia offers a charming and authentic dining experience that blends warmth, simplicity, and cultural flavor. Upon entering, one places their order directly at the counter—an informal touch that underscores the casual, homegrown feel of the establishment. The individuals running the restaurant are exceptionally gracious, offering friendly service and sincere hospitality that is increasingly rare in today’s fast-paced food scene.

The menu presents a satisfying array of traditional Bosnian fare, and I was particularly pleased with the quality and heartiness of the cabbage rolls. They were well-prepared, flavorful, and accompanied by sides that complemented them perfectly. While the cuisine is simple, it is executed with care and respect for tradition.

A particularly delightful surprise was the availability of Spezi—a cola-orange soda blend that’s a nostalgic favorite for those familiar with Central European beverages. Its presence on the menu demonstrated thoughtful curation and an attention to detail that I greatly appreciated.

Though the setting is modest and the format informal, the food and service elevate the overall experience. Taste of Bosnia is a solid choice for anyone seeking comfort food with cultural depth, served with kindness and pride. I look forward to returning.
Outstanding service and Bosnian comfort food full of flavor — from smoky ćevapi to golden, crispy burek, every bite delivered. Will definitely be returning!
This consistently tastes both delicious and the same everytime! Grateful to live close to this establishment so I can have a GREAT hearty meal

formatted_address: 1620 Delmar Blvd, St. Louis, MO 63103, United States
name: Gourmet Soul Restaurant and Catering

reviews.text: Really impressed with this place. I went on a Sunday. They have limited hours on Sunday. I was there a little before their opening time and the place got crowded quickly. Service was great. I sat at the bar (bar chairs were not that comfortable). Food was good especially the dressing and fried fish. Green beans tasted bland and like they were frozen or from a can. Other than that I would highly recommend. Prices were reasonable

I really enjoyed myself here. I have been looking for the best soul food spot because sometimes I miss my step-dad and he really introduced me to the culture.. RIP♡ I loved their greens BUT they didn't have vinegar 😔 I need my vinegar & hot sauce but their pork chop was so buttery good omg I want some more thinking about rn. Their wings was little salty but their sauces made it less salty I favorite hot & spicy sauce but their other sauce was good too. We came during the slower time so it was really nice to enjoy the place alone. It was such a good time.

Oh this place was the place! I definitely will be back! The food was incredible. As far as service there was only one sever on the floor and she still did her thing. If you’re a cognac type of person when it comes to liquor they carry D’Usse and Remy 1738. The ambiance was really nice and a classy/up scale vibe. “Best Soul Food in St. Louis” is a legit claim. ITS A MUST GO!!

Our last day in STL we decided to look for some good soul food to eat before we headed out. We chose Gourmet Soul & it DID NOT disappoint! My lady got the Old Bay Bowl which was phenomenal. I, myself, had the fried fish with candied yams & the Mac ‘n’ cheese. AMAZING! Let me tell you, not one thing on the table was less than 10/10! The environment was cute, cozy & with a little intimate vibe. Next time I come to STL I won’t pass up a meal at this spot!

This was my first time dining at this restaurant, and overall, the experience had its highs and lows. When we arrived, we were told there would be a 45-minute to 1-hour wait but to our surprise, we were seated in by  15-20 minutes by Ms. T. That was a pleasant start, especially considering how busy it was. It looked like there was some kind of convention going on, and for it to be so packed early in the afternoon, I took that as a great sign that the food must be worth it!

However, as our visit went on, it became clear that customer service is an area that needs attention. The restaurant seemed short staffed, and I noticed several guests looking for assistance with no one immediately available. While the staff members who were present remained friendly, it was obvious they were stretched thin.

We ended up waiting about an hour for our food, and during that time, we were only given one update. That lack of communication made the wait feel even longer. I understand that we may have come during a rush, but regular check-ins would have made a big difference. For future guests definitely don’t come hungry, just in case you’re met with a similar delay. The food was good! I enjoyed the sides mostly!! Yams, Collards and Mac & Cheese was delicious. My fries and fish was not hot, however, I didn’t complain! In the end Makala replaced the fries. She was amazing.

That said, I want to shout out Steve, who was working incredibly hard, clearing tables, helping customers, and clearly doing everything he could to keep things moving. Also, Makala, our waitress, was kind and tried her best to keep us informed and comfortable while we waited.

Unfortunately, there was a moment that stood out for the wrong reason. A staff member named Nya (or Nia) was visibly rude to a customer picking up an order. As a paying guest myself, I found the tone and approach to be unprofessional and unnecessarily harsh, especially in front of other patrons. Regardless of stress levels, how staff communicates matters! Customer service is the foundation of any great business, and experiences like that can make or break a customer's impression. If she holds a leadership position, I hope this is addressed, as that kind of behavior sets the wrong tone for the entire team.

In summary, the food may well be worth the wait, but customer service should never take a back seat, especially in a busy environment. With a few more hands on deck and a stronger focus on communication and professionalism, this place has the potential to be a favorite. I would return again.

formatted_address: 4341 Manchester Ave, St. Louis, MO 63110, United States
name: Sameem Afghan Restaurant & Catering

reviews.text: This is my second time coming here. As expected the food is very delicious and served hot. The prices are good and the service is great! I’ll be coming here more often. This chicken pasta is sooo flavorful 🤍 it didn’t take them a long time to prepare it either! I would only say that the theme can be improved:)

The food is absolutely bad no taste, nothing taste like afghani 3 box of the food had hair, I won’t recommend anymore, There is no Hygiene they need to work on that. 0 Star, the food smell and it’s not even fresh looks like from yesterday.
Food was very delicious. Please visit these folks if you like Indian cuisine. Service was OK, no music in the background made it very quiet, but the food made up for all of it.

Delcious. We loved the food. The Mediterranean sampler platter was so fresh and perfect flavors and textures. We wish we had gotten it for 4, so we had leftovers for the 2 of us. Afgani buryiani, mango lassi and chai tea were also delcious. Felt like a family run place with authentic food. The food came out really fast. I would highly recommend eating here. I do wish the inside had more Afgani decor or music playing, but was a really nice quiet spot.

The service and atmosphere was very simple, no frills; the food, however, was exceptional -- well seasoned and fresh.

I ordered the Emperor Platter (Combination/Sampler that offers a great variety)

It comes in two course:
(1) Naan bread, Shirazi salad (light and fresh with a nice cucumber crunch), eggplant burani (very hardy/savory, spice rich), and yogurt (on the side/excluded for nondairy restrictions).

(2) Beef, chicken, and lamb (all well seasoned), stew, tomato, and a very sweet/savory rice (hints of cinnamon, topped with raisins, very balanced flavor profiles).

Seems to be a generous amount of food for the cost. Quaint.

formatted_address: 4353 Manchester Ave, St. Louis, MO 63110, United States
name: Creole With A Splash Of Soul

reviews.text: The restaurant has such a nice and inviting atmosphere when you first walk in. The staff were really nice and attentive of our needs. My sister and I had the creole shrimp, the sauce they served with it was so good and there was a little kick to it. We also ordered the gumbo and the creole catfish, both entrees were really good and flavorful, I’m usually not trusting of catfish, but this one was so well seasoned and just melted in my mouth every bite I took. The portions were very sizable and we have left overs! Definitely going to come back!

The food was decent because I was hungry. No sugar or black pepper, which was disappointing. My food wasn't hot. The grits were luke warm. The server was a nice woman. I'll definitely try them out again to try the  alligator bites.

The food was even more delicious than I expected. I really enjoyed the atmosphere. We were greeted by Jayla and she check with us insuring everything was satisfactory. I could go on and on about the flavorful food. The whole experience was wonderful.  They definitely have new regular customers, we most definitely will be back frequently.

Literally the best shrimp and grits I have ever tasted. The atmosphere is so cozy and inviting. The staff was very sweet and attentive. Don’t let the wait get you because once you get your food, it will all make sense. Every single dish is fresh and hot. The flavors are beyond anything I’ve tried in a while. I absolutely recommend.

Amazing experience from start to finish! I came in before they officially opened, and the manager’s kindness blew me away — she offered me a Sprite and great conversation while I waited. Renisha and the young lady who made my mocktail were wonderful, and the food? The best shrimp and grits I’ve ever had, and my husband loved his catfish po’boy. Even the leftovers tasted fresh the next day.

formatted_address: 6130 Madison Ave, Berkeley, MO 63134, United States
name: Mandela Soul Food Cafe

reviews.text:
September 14 , 2025 2:23 pm

Mandela Soul Food – Review
⭐️⭐️⭐️ (3/5)

First time trying this spot. The cashier was very nice, the vibe was cozy, and the price was accurate (they rang me up on a calculator, no games). I spent about $79 total including tip.

Food:
•	Oxtails (9/10): Flavorful and tender, but not something I’d reorder here.
•	Mostaccoli (9/10): I really liked it, but I know it won’t be for everybody.
•	Cheesecake (10/10): Perfect.
•	Potato Salad (8/10): Solid, but not the best.
•	Mac & Cheese (7/10): A bit unusual, almost too busy.
•	Yams (5/10): Overly sweet.
•	Dressing (4/10): Mushy and too sweet.
•	Green Beans & Cornbread: Missing.
Overall:
Cheesecake and mostaccoli were the standouts. Some sides missed the mark, and I was disappointed about missing items. I’ll come back, but I won’t spend as much — and I know what not to order next time.

My partner and I were really disappointed with our experience at Mandela’s. After ordering our food, we noticed that the chicken was not cooked thoroughly — it was visibly red and bloody on the inside. Concerned, we brought the food back to the restaurant to speak with the chef, Mandela. Unfortunately, instead of listening, he was extremely rude and dismissive.

When we explained that the chicken tasted fishy, was overly greasy, and did not seem safe to eat, he responded by trying to lecture us, saying, “I don’t know if you cook chicken, but this is how it’s supposed to look.” It clearly was not. We also mentioned that the chicken our sister received earlier that day looked completely different — darker, seasoned, and fully cooked — while ours was pale, greasy, and undercooked. Even after showing a photo, he insisted everything was the same, when it clearly wasn’t.

We weren’t trying to argue; we only wanted to bring the issue to their attention so no one else would get sick. Instead, we were talked to as if we didn’t know what we were saying. The sides were decent, but the overall experience was awful. No customer should be made to feel belittled or challenged when raising a valid concern. A simple acknowledgment and solution would’ve gone a long way, but that was not the case here.

We won’t be returning.

Nothing less than amazing. I wouldn’t say the food is pricy because you get what you pay for, he isn’t skimpy on the sides. I got a lamb chop plate and it had FOUR large sides for $40 and corn bread? That’s a bargain. Food is high these days. My significant other got the chicken plate. Everything was delicious, fresh, seasoned well. Chef even came out himself when I was concerned about the sauce for the lamb chops and brought me an extra side of it. You can tell he really cares about his business and the hostess was very kind as well which was refreshing. Place gave luxury, super clean and beautiful. Some of the best soul food I’ve had in the city and the presentation was amazing as well. Quick too for the food to be fresh.

Although the atmosphere is nice the food is truly horrible. I only got sides because I’m vegetarian so they gave me a scoop of each. Old Mac n cheese you could tell it’s been sitting for hours, and very salty mash potatoes and dressing. The only thing good was the candied yams which they only gave me three pieces of…. First and last time.

Food was overpriced,had to wait like 35 minutes for 1 pork chop and 2 chicken wings to be fried. Didn't have any seasoning on the meats. Dressing was cold and funny tasting, macaroni was sweet and I don't understand why.Was charged 10 dollars for the 2 chicken wings.Sweet potatoes ok but cold also. Paid 65 dollars I believe for a kid plate and a regular plate that has one meat and 2 sides. And this is why I cook at home and never go to these so called soul food restaurants in Saint Louis these people here can't cook

formatted_address: 1507 Goodfellow Blvd, St. Louis, MO 63112, United States
name: Mom's Soul Food Kitchen & Catering

reviews.text: The food was absolutely delicious, service was phenomenal and the atmosphere was smart, calm and clean.  The owner came out and set with me and shared the history of the place.  But more importantly, I purchased three dinners all different entrées.  The smothered pork chops and collard greens were succulent,with a grandma’s hand.  The fried fish ( Jack)was hot, crisp with a tasteful cornmeal and flour breading seasoned perfectly.  The portion sizes were way more than I could consume but I attempted to sample everything.  I give Mom’s Soul Food kitchen a 9 out of 10 with succulent food, cleanliness and atmosphere.  The entire staff was friendly, engaging and welcoming.  If you have a chance you must patronize this establishment.  You won’t regret it!

Very disappointing everything was cold and nothing I mean nothing was Soulful about this meal .. Sweet potato are very hard Nsc and cheese was dry … I ordered dressing that I didn’t receive… this was by far the Worst experience ever …

Tried Mom’s Soul Food Kitchen & Catering for the first time unfortunately, it was a waste of $32.20🤦🏾‍♀️

While the service was good, the food just wasn’t it. The flavors were way off from what I’m used to. The dressing had a strong, almost vinegary taste that overpowered everything. The mac and cheese tasted like it was made with cheap cheese and lacked any real seasoning. The ribs? Tough not enjoyable at all. 😩

There are signs everywhere saying no refunds, only exchanges, but honestly, I wouldn’t even want to exchange this. The whole plate went straight to the trash. I wouldn’t feel right giving this to someone in need. Disappointing all around.

My daughter liked the greens the sweet potatoes were just okay. Her chicken was good plate just wasn’t worth 18.00.

The restaurant is extremely hot not only for the customers but for the workers.

Adding black pepper didn’t work.

I’ll say try them for yourself maybe I caught them in a bad day.

Ordered smothered pork steak only, lasagna. And dressing. Ended up with Mac and cheese which tasted like vinegar, dressing didn’t have any seasoning and was bland with flavor and the star of the show was undercooked. I’m 8 months pregnant and very disappointed. The Delmar location was so good tho .

Well well well...where do I start? I spent $42.00 and I ordered the smothered pork chops by the way you get one and two slides. I choose Mac and cheese and dressing. Dressing was horrible I couldn't even describe the flavors. The Mac and cheese wasn't a sauce based and had a oil base cheese probably cheaper cheddar cheese only on top.  So don't order these two items. Next I ordered a buffalo fish sandwich but no bread given... Now go figure I ordered a sandwich loud and clear. Next I ordered a side of greens with smoked Turkey...diffently throwing this away. Can't even describe the taste.  So bad really really bad.tasted like weeds...peach cobbler was good. So what a experience. Won't be going back. Take your own chances and I am a train chef... straight out of Texas.

formatted_address: 1608 W Friendly Ave, Greensboro, NC 27403, United States
name: SAINT LOUIS SAVEURS

reviews.text:
What a wonderful introduction to Senegalese food!

My partner wasn't as adventurous as me and got the Philly - which was delicious, but not the reason for this review. I got the Djolof Rice with lamb. I requested that the dish be made a little spicy, and it came out perfectly! Savory and well seasoned for sure.

I am no expert on Senegalese food - I couldn't tell you how authentic it is with the ingredients available in the States. I can tell you as a lover of good food that this place has it. The folks who served us our meal were pleasant and eager to make our food just the way we wanted it. And they did!

Clean, small place. International soccer playing on the TV, not too loud. I wouldn't suggest dining in with a large party, but if I were local it'd be my go-to takeout spot for bigger gatherings.

GOODNESS ME! Food this flavorful is a blessing! I ordered the dibi lamb and it was everything I could have wanted in a dish. The spices were so complimentary with the lamb and the onion and mustard sauce. The lamb was tender and perfectly grilled with sweet caramelized plantains.

Atmosphere is pleasing with unique attractive decor and extremely clean.

Family owned and proudly served with courtesy and hospitality.

The bissap was very sweet but rich flavor.

Fataya had a flaky pastry with seasoned chicken and a sweet onion sauce

I cant wait to return

The first thing for me are the owners of the place. They are very nice and understands good customer relationship.

I had the Djolof rice and Chicken on my first visit, and Djolof rice and Lamb on my second while my girlfriend had the Attieke with Tilapia.

The food, and plating was 10/10.
Coming from someone who has eaten both Nigerian and Ghanaian Jollof rice, this Senegalese Djolof tastes unique and different from others which have more tomato flavor.

The meats are also tenderly cooked and well seasoned, and that’s so impressive to me.

The food, portion size, and meat (“protein” size) are really good for the price.

PS to the owners, please don’t change the price drastically 🙏😭

10/10 recommend. Firstly, cleanest kitchen I’ve ever seen. Second, the hibiscus tea… try it. Sweet and slightly citrus. The food is authentic and looks and tastes delicious. Will be back and have already recommended to family and friends. You won’t regret trying this place out! Oh and want to add the fact the owner I presume took his time to bag my food, make recommendations, and was honestly just super friendly and respectful. This is a business you want to support.

A wonderful experience! I give my highest reccomendation for folks to try Saint Louis Saveurs. The food was delicious, my group ordered the yucca fries and egg rolls for appetizers, and djolof chicken rice, dibi lamb, okra soup with fufu, and a cheesesteak sandwich for our main dishes.  I would reccomend any of these dishes, though the standout was the djolof chicken rice and okra soup with fufu.
Also the whole staff was incredibly helpful with picking out dishes, their service, and bringing things like extra sauces for us to try. Make sure to try Saint Louis Saveurs for a new flavor in Greensboro.

formatted_address: 1771 N New Florissant Rd, Florissant, MO 63033, United States
name: Eat More International Foods - African, Caribbean, Hispanic store

html_attributions: Eat More International Foods - African, Caribbean, Hispanic store

reviews.text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Love this place!
Eat More International Grocery Store is a hidden gem! They have a fantastic selection of global products from spices and snacks to hard to find ingredients. The store is clean, well organized, and the staff is super friendly and helpful. Great prices and a great vibe. A must visit!

I bought soursop bitters from here, and it really helped me burn fat and improved my skin so much. I had xanthomas, and they have cleared. I feel good when using it; it revives my energy during the day. I don't feel tired like I used to, and I don't experience body pain anymore. I really love the soursop bitters, and I have been recommending them to my friends and co-workers. I need to keep getting the bitters; I love them.
They have everything and their products are cheaper than other stores. I come here for all my African foods stuff.
They have everything from Ghana, this is my go to store. They have the best shito too

I had a great experience at this African store! The staff were friendly and welcoming, and the store had everything I needed—from fresh African ingredients to cultural products. Very clean, organized, and the customer service felt like home. I highly recommend this place to anyone looking for authentic African goods and great vibes. Will definitely be coming back

formatted_address: 381 Lenox Ave, New York, NY 10027, United States
name: Saint Louis Restaurant Keur Yayou Dara

reviews.text:
The food here was genuinely good—well-prepared, flavorful, and clearly made with care. The ambiance was also very pleasant, with a cozy and stylish vibe that made it a nice place to sit and enjoy a meal.
That said, the lighting inside was quite dark, which made it a bit difficult to fully see the food and the space. A slightly brighter interior would really enhance the overall experience.
Overall, a solid spot for good food and atmosphere, with just a small lighting adjustment needed to make it even better.

Hole in the wall that produces the best Senegalese food Ive ever had. The lamb was incredibly tender and falling off the bone, spices were amazing and everything was well seasoned but not overpowering. The jollof rice complimented the dish well and the ginger juice was delicious and balanced out all the spices of the dish. The owner told me her mother was the chef and I absolutely believe it as it tasted like home cooking and was made with love. I have had this dish at other restaurants before, but nowhere has compared to this one. 10/10 will visit again.

Well, well well, where do I start?
I ordered dinner @Saint Louis Restaurant  Keur Yayou Dara. I ordered  Dibi Senegal, and it was super delicious. The tenderness of lamb is out of this world. Now let me touch on the seasoning,  I wont even say anything, you have to try it to know what I mean. The staff were super friendly, they were all smiling. Mame Penda took my order, she was very friendly and helpful beside that the fact that she gave me some excellent recommendations. The side orders were great and the portions are very reasonable.
In sum, it was a great experience. Now the burden is on you @SaintLouis Restaurant.  I highly recommend this place

Nice people, but the service wasn’t great. We waited over 45 minutes for our food with no check-ins. A guest next to us—who appeared to be a family member or friend of the staff received their food within 5–10 minutes, which wasn’t right. I was also told the Dibi lamb Senegal was already prepared, so I’m not sure why the wait was so long. Me and my mom were disappointed. Learning experience, to leave after 25 minutes max. Even our drinks took too long to come out. The dibi was cut into large chunks, I’m not a big fan of that, but it was flavorful. The food may be good, but the service needs improvement. I don’t think I’ll come back again.
For food reviews follow @briannascravings

A true culinary gem! The Senegalese dishes at this family owned and run  restaurant were bursting with authentic flavors and perfectly prepared - some by the mother of the family. The warm, vibrant ambience made the experience even more special. The service was welcoming, and the lady who served us was genuinely proud of her cuisine. A must-visit for anyone who loves great food and warm  hospitality.

formatted_address: 2FHW+596 M ok195, Rue Khalifa Ababacar Sy, Saint-Louis, Senegal
name: La Linguere

reviews.text: Good senegalese food and affordable prices. Had lunch here twice with my driver. First time I had thieup around 2pm. The second time at 12.40pm and the only choice available is yassa. Good customer service and good portion. It's nice that they put name cards and business advertisement on the table.
Some of the best Senegalese food I had during my stay in Senegal. The ceeb u jen is especially great. Certainly recommend to those looking for a yummy and inexpensive lunch in Saint-Louis.
Excellent food at very reasonable prices.
We enjoyed their French fries as well as quick service.

Absolutely delicious, homemade Senegalese food. We enjoyed the yassa poulet and the Thiep Bou Dien. Did you see the picture I took!? It is so beautiful! The flavours were lovely and the people working here were very kind and friendly. It's a wonderful little place you should definitely try.

formatted_address: 261 Rue Abdoulaye Seck, St Louis, Senegal
name: Fleuve Plus

reviews.text: Had some yassa chicken with baobab juice. 10/10, would definitely recommend. The owner is friendly, and the spot has a cozy and inviting decoration.

Plain and simple good food at excellent prices.  When in St. Louis, one must try the Thieboudienne, and this is a perfect place to start. Lots more on the menu and the fruit juice (tamarind for me) was tasty and fresh. staff are friendly and welcoming.

We had a lot of fun trying to communicate with the waiter since we don't speak French. He was such a nice man and the food all came out very tasty. We tried chicken cooked in a special way - poulet dibi which is like a smoked grill I think. It's known as chicken afra which is fun because we enjoyed chicken afra in Dakar. Anyway, it came with different sauces. I also tried the couscous which was too dry for my taste but still interesting. Very nice food and people!
Fantastic food in a very clean family owned restaurant. Our whole family enjoyed all of our dishes.
Had lunch there, came back for dinner. Best thieboudienne I’ve had in Senegal, other dishes were excellent too. Very hospitable and kind people.

formatted_address: 2FHW+CGM, Saint-Louis, Senegal
name: Chez Dasso

reviews.text:
4! of us that ate here spent the night in the toilet.  Will definitely NOT visit again.  The food was lovely, but not with that cost.

My original review: 5 stars
Fantastic food, lovely chef lady. Good prices. Will definitely visit again

My favorite restaurant in Saint Luis! The service is very slow, but it is actually named ‘slow food’ so I can’t complain and they have some books and mandalas to kill the waiting time. Unforgettable couscous viande 😍👌🏼very friendly staff, beautiful place.

Very tasty food, I ate there 3 days in a row (while I normally like to try different places). Takes a while before you get your food but its in their name "slow food". My favourite was their Mafé viande. Super tasty. Very friendly service too, always keen to have a chat with customers.

This beautiful place is cozy and serves wonderful homemade food. We enjoyed some bissap juice, spring rolls, a crepe with vegetables, the mafe and another traditional dish but I forgot the name - it had black eyed peas, veggies and coconut milk.

Everything was very tasty, the woman working here was so kind and the place is cute. We would definitely recommend coming here!

It’s a little gem on the east side.
The owner is so friendly and prepares everything on site and fresh - slow food as stated outside, so please bring a bit of time and enjoy.
I liked the Riz Dasso Crevettes

formatted_address: Ave Blaise Diagne, St Louis, Senegal
name: La Kora

reviews.text: A neighbourhood restaurant that you would be lucky to have at home. Serves a short menu of French bistro-style dishes, plus sandwich-based alternatives. Elegantly decor with a lovely tree inside the bar.

We came in last week and enjoyed our first meal here in Senegal. Very friendly staff, we arrived on motorbikes and they made us aware to be careful leaving them in the street so allowed us to sit where we can watch them. The food was amazing, my partner said it was the best burger he had ever had. The beer was served in a nice cold glass and the service was perfect. We would definitely return!

By far the best restaurant in St. Louis - it doesn’t even compare. After struggling to find a good place to dine, discovering La Kora felt like finding an oasis. The food was delicious and beautifully presented, the staff were very friendly, and the atmosphere and design were thoughtfully curated down to the smallest details. Truly a highlight.

Delicious vegetarian burger with chips (shared with mum, and they very kindly cut it in half/put it on two plates for us to serve - super helpful!)  Very tasty. Helpful staff. Yummy tea, and juice. Gorgeous little yard with beautiful tree in it.

La Kora is a beautiful restaurant with great food. It’s on the pricey side for Saint-Louis, but still very reasonable for most tourists. Ambiance is lovely. Great chicken burger, great apple goat cheese sandwich. And the grapefruit crème is delicious.

formatted_address: 2FGW+F7J, St Louis, Senegal
name: Patisserie Darou Salam

reviews.text: This is a fun place to watch a game. We came here for dinner and it was packed. We went for something a little lighter and got a chicken wrap. It was fine and the juice was tasty.
Good spot to try some local food in Saint-Louis. The service was good and the place fairly and prices very affordable. We had a thieboudienne and a fish yassa, all were nice meals. Toilettes were ok.

Maybe 12:00 is not a good time for them - anyway, the service was terrible. Though certainly not understaffed, they seemed weirdly disorganized, given the easily manageable number of customers there. The wait for taking the order and preparing the (tasty) sandwich seemed unnecessarily long. Judging from the many decent reviews this place is probably better when you come here at regular lunch/dinner hours.
One of the best in town. Must try! The staff was very friendly and helpful in providing recommendation for English speaking tourists. We had amazing food and drinks.

For your information, Darou Salam is both a pastry and a Restaurant. I give 5 stars for the restaurant without hesitation. If you want to taste the best of Senegalese dishes, especially the ceebu jen (rice and fish) then don’t look nowhere but Darou Saloum. 3 things that I like in the restaurant. 1-you eat good -2 they will give you more food if you finish your dish -3 they offer you desert and tea. Without to mention the warm welcoming of the waitress.
I highly recommend this Restaurant

formatted_address: St Louis, Senegal
name: Dibiterie Chez mamadou

reviews.text: We went here for takeaway dibi almost every night of our stay in St Louis, it was the best dibiterie we visited in Senegal. The guy with the meat clever clearly knew what he was doing! Also very popular among locals, but the wait wasn't too long even if it looked crowded at times. Recommended!

Food, the lamb barbecue was really good!!

Well spiced up .. it’s a local favourite spot on St. Louis

are you guys serious ? if this is the best grill food in Senegal I won't even bother to eat more , place was full of flies , the dude cutting tge meat was dealing with money at the same time ... I actually tried a few pieces , taste was good , but I'm praying not to get an infection .If you gonna eat this , you need to have the body for it .
Best dibi place in Senegal (yes, I said it!)! You get real meat, not bones & fat!
The best Dibiterie ever

formatted_address: 689 Avenue of the Cities, East Moline, IL 61244, United States
name: D’Savor House

reviews.text: Food was great! Giant scoop of fried rice with 5 thick chicken wings and sauteed veggies. It's all very flavorful and comes with 2 sauce cups - one earthy smokey and the other spicy gingery. About $18 per entree, dinner sized, could easily get 2 meals out of it. Interior is dank and shabby, but service is friendly and feels family-run.

We were absolutely blown away by this new hidden gem!

They're clearly just getting off the ground, so they haven't found their feet with service fully. The owner was running everything and while it didn't impact our experience, i hope they can get just one server soon to make things a little smoother. That being said, they're obviously putting their money to the quality of their food, and it shows.

Our meal started with ginger and pineapple juice. The ginger juice was bold and in-your-face with that wonderful ginger heat. I'm a big ginger fan and it really delivered.

They were out of our first choice of appetizers so we went with what was labeled a salad. What we got was essentially a potato salad. A good potato salad, but it felt strange to have as an appetizer, and I'm not sure i could recommend it for the price

The Jollof Rice was astounding. We got it with goat, which was cooked to absolute perfection. The rice itself was well flavored and the garnishes really added to the dish. i would definitely recommend this for anyone looking to do their toe into an unfamiliar cuisine.

The Kom was also wonderful, and the fish was cooked perfectly and not overpowering at all. It was served with a delicious sauce, and the owner suggested eating it with my hands. She provided a bowl to wash my hands in before and after, and i have to say that it added to the meal. this is also a big recommend from me.

With fresh ingredients, and a well deserved pride in the food they serve, we will certainly be going back, and look forward to trying everything on the menu.

It was a wonderful experience eating here. They spoke multiple languages and were able to help all of us. I read a review about the ginger juice being strong and it's very true. It's great! Great service and delicious food!

Unusual fare for the Quad Cities.  Every main dish that I’ve ordered are quite spicy.  The fufu was unique & is a good accompaniment to the spicy main dishes.  It’s primarily carry out, the dining room is the worn out Made Rite.

The man taking my order was friendly and helpful I got the Egusi stew with goat and fufu and asked for it to be spicy they gave me a little container of spicy something which was plenty the meal was hot flavorful and delicious. There plenty for me to have 2 meals out of it. I will definitely be back to try some more new foods.

formatted_address: 3405 S Jefferson Ave, St. Louis, MO 63118, United States
name: The Fattened Caf.

reviews.text:
Parking: Limited (On-Street)
Customer Service: Great
Cleanliness: Good
Quality of Food: AMAZING!
Ambiance: Family-Feel
__________

I have eaten Fattened Caf. food before, but I was never able to visit their location and eat there on site.

This was my first time going there, and I can honestly say that it was an amazing and delicious experience.

My group enjoyed the Kamayan buffet, which included an assortment of ingredients: Polish sausage, chicken, cucumbers, rice, cabbage, corn, edible flowers, and more. The BBQ Sauce is *chef's kiss*

When your group does the Kamayan buffet, you and your group are tasked with setting the table. Setting the table looks like putting the food directly on the table, no utensils necessary.

The owner, Darren, shared some cool background knowledge about the business and the etiquette for eating the buffet.

You grab the food with your left hand and then eat with your right to maintain group sanitation.

Amazing experience! I highly recommend the buffet or just grabbing a quick bite to eat.

This is a very nicely put together restaurant with excellent food, and an unusually welcoming staff.  The dishes are varied and of enough complexity of flavor that the restaurant requires several visits just to try them all.  The meats have a variety of marinades, and some are smoked on the premises.  They even have their own in house made soda.  There is no alcohol.  The presentation, as the photos show, is quite nice. Many of the dishes are made up to order, so there can be a wait of 15 minutes before the food arrives. The restaurant itself is clean and neat, so do not be put off b the occasionally funky neighborhood.

Fantastic food with delicious flavors. ..and presentation.  I had the Filipino Pork Steak.  Every bit of it...except the bone...was delightful...even the charred edges and minimal  fat areas.  All that remained after lunch was a clean bone.  The rice and cabbage and cucumber slices with a side of vinegar were great.  We also had a spicy chicken dish that was delectable.  The Uber latte was also good.  Really do try this place out.  Super casual with great caring service and food.  Yes, it is a family run restaurant and is casual and enjoyable non-pretentious.  Welcoming and inviting.  Kids seemed to like it, too.

Absolutely delicious food! I had the Pork Belly Tocino and Ube Longdog.

The chef recommended the Ube Longdog and I promise you, it is the BEST “sausage-in-a-bun” type-meal you could ever have. As long as dietary restrictions aren’t an issue, order everything as is and don’t be picky!

If you have an open mind, palate, and wish to try something refreshing in STL, please try this place out!!!

I follow this spot on social media and have been wanting to check it out. I visited around 130pm on a Friday and I can tell lunch rush was slowly coming to an end. The folks behind the counter were busy but friendly.

I chose the pork belly lunch plus a side of coconut milk braised collard greens and an orange Poppi, paid at the counter and found a seat in the back.

There was nothing that I disliked about this experience, from the service, to the atmosphere and the food. The meal was phenomenal and so reasonably priced. I would have paid $5 more for it. I liked that the marinated pork belly, the Star, was so seasoned and grilled and everything else on the plate could be simple. Red cabbage, rice, egg and pineapple.

The collards were cooked down nicely and had a hint of spice.

I devoured my plate.

I can see when they are busy, service might be a bit slow but you can see them working diligently behind the counter making beautiful plates.

I can’t wait to go for dinner to try the sissig!

formatted_address: 2463 W Sunshine St, Springfield, MO 65807, United States
name: Nathalie African food

reviews.text:
I ordered the fufu, stew, and a sambusa. My husband ordered a combo plate with a different entree and we both received the same thing. I chose not to get a drink (she asked me), but the combo plate came with one. When he went to pick up the food and asked about the drink, she said she was not giving him one, because I said I did not want one. The food was good, but I will not try it again due to her not offering the drink to him; it just seemed rude not to hand a bottle or can of soda over. Upon reflection, maybe she just did not like him, because she only took my order initially; we actually had to say that he wanted something, too.
I know Africa is a BIG continent, but honestly I was hoping for some injera, as Ethiopian is the most familiar I am with African menus. Lesson learned: check the menu online first.

I got two big plates goat  egusi with fufu and chapati, sambusa potato and pilau rice wit fry tilapia and  plantains all of them were amazing food,  I will definitely come back. The lady was so nice and she explained  everything until my daughter and I loved the food. Thank you Nathalie.

It's a little orange food truck in the sunshine food truck park. Amazing experience, I got the fufu with stewed goat! Hands down the best thing I've eaten in months. I got mine medium spice, the fufu cuts the heat well, I will get it spicy next time. So happy I tried this establishment.

I just ate here for the first time today, my husband and I both got the beef egusi with fufu and 3 sambusas! We have never had African food before but it definitely blew my expectations out of the water! I have been wanting to try fufu for literally years and when I found out about this place I had to have it! The service was wonderful, the lady who took my order was kind and she answered my questions! It took a bit for the food to be brought out to me but it was clearly freshly made and so delicious! If you want to have some traditional African food and meet some really nice people, you won't be disappointed with Nathalie's!!

My son wanted to try this as hes seen different ones on tiktok and it did not disappoint the fufu and egusi with chicken had such a amazing flavor the chicken was tender and flavorful I also got fried plantains it came with a red sauce that was really good definitely will be back

formatted_address: 7700 B Ivory St, St. Louis, MO 63111, United States
name: Kabul Express STL

reviews.text: First time here tonight. Food & service was fantastic!!! We tried several items on menu for appetizer.  It’s my birthday and I was given a yummy baklava with gold on top! Will definitely be back. Thanks for a Perfect birthday dinner with my family😊

We were in town for an appointment and decided to stop by. The menu has all the usual favorites like rice with kabobs, gyros, and more. The food was amazing – it tasted just like homemade! Even my 6-year-old, who’s a picky eater, tried different dishes without any complaints. The owner was super friendly and welcoming. We’ll definitely be back whenever we’re in town!

The flavor was fantastic. It was perfectly seasoned.  We got the mixed meat over rice, the Butter chicken and cheese fries with seasoning on top. I almost didn't try the fries because my husband gets them everywhere but I'm glad I did. Best cheese fries I've tried in St Louis 😋.  This was a great place for a taste of India.  They even have Indian style music on the TV. Thank you ladies for the wonderful service and meal.

I stay right around the corner from this place and visited again yesterday to try their spicy gyro. 10/10🤤 The atmosphere is very clean, aesthetic and beautiful. The owner was very polite and nice, took my order, cooked my food and brought it out to me (true hustler). I’ve been here before for the chicken and beef tikka masalas as well as the veggie sombosas which are also a 10/10 with the pita/nan bread. This is a hidden gem here in St. Louis 💎 Highly recommend and I’ll be back🤗 You can check out my TikTok of this restaurant @ lalitaeats 🩷

Bought the Chicken Tikka Masala when the owner was out and the girls did a bad job. I've bought meals from here several times but the last visit was my last. The Tikka Masala sauce was watery thin and after eating got food poisoning that lasted a few days. I called the owner to let him know and suggest he keep an eye on the kitchen. Was told it was a 2 day cold or flu. That is sadly, complete BS. Anyone in the medical field knows there is NO SUCH THING. Next time I'll call the health department as the owner clearly does not care one iota on his food rating or customer health after ingesting their food.

formatted_address: 5100 N Nebraska Ave, Tampa, FL 33603, United States
name: Tfk African food.

reviews.text:
The food was wonderful.
We ordered the suya, pounded yam, vegetables, okra and egusi soup all with goat. It was so good. We called to order in advance so our food was served quickly. The service was wonderful!!! Thank you so very much. We will definitely be back!

We came to Florida for vacation and decided to give this restaurant a try. The Food was so delicious  that we had to come back for lunch the next day.
Customer service 10/10.
I would definitely recommend this place 10/10

Asun is one of my favorite foods so I was very excited to try it from here. I feel so bad writing this review but… y’all. $30 for half a box of bones and few pieces of meat that could barely be chewed.
Upset I will still have to travel for good food.
Ordered for pick up. The service was great, very nice.

I am furious. Probably should be mad at myself for ignoring the reviews. The meat was so tough that it literally BROKE A TOOTH. Worse part is that it was dark meat chicken… supposed to be soft. Like what the hell?! I’m not happy at all. The photo is my TOOTH on my finger. Avoid!!

Entrance was confusing. Two doors and both were locked. You have to ring a bell on the wall to have them open it. The cashier lady has to come open the door and she was very nice and welcoming. I ordered the goat egusi and beef okra stew with fufu. Unfortunately, the meat for both were so LEAN and TOUGH that I couldn’t chew through them at all!!! The beef tasted expired as if it had been fermenting a while and looked like they scooped it  from another red sauce dish to add with some bland okra stew! It was by far the worst okra stew I’ve ever had! No flavor for both stews. I’ve made both from scratch myself and it tasted 100x better! They only give you 2 lean pieces of meat per dish and charge you over $20! Please pressure cook your meat and cut them smaller! I’ve seen other African ladies make it and they cook it for a long time! People know when they are being cheated. Definitely disappointed and will never go back.

formatted_address: 11001 N 56th St, Temple Terrace, FL 33617, United States
name: Queen of Sheba

reviews.text:
Brilliant!!!

My first time experiencing Ethiopian food and we couldn't have picked a better place!!! The food was obviously the star, but the hospitality elevated the entire experience to a whole other level!! Loved it!!!

With the warmest of welcome, our host Seble showed us to our reserved table. She walked us through the menu, lively conversations and promised to serve us food that we will definitely love! That confidence and the pride with which Seble served us the food, she won us over with just that!! We enjoyed the food thoroughly and wiped our plate clean. The joy of seeing our empty plate and her victory dance was the highlight of our night!!! What an amazing experience!!! Thank you Seble, you've set the bar really high now 😍

We opted for the Queen's 8 platter course and Seble connected the dots and realized that our Indian palate appreciates a higher level of spice and paid special attention to it. While we enjoyed the honey wine and some Ethiopian beers, the kitchen prepared our special platter and we enjoyed every last bite of the delicious plate of food served to us with extra helpings of the soft injera.
The chicken, lamb and beef were scrumptious! The lentils and veggies were equally delicious 😋 What a treat!!

Highly recommend this restaurant, the experience & we cannot wait to eat at Queen of Sheba again!

I loved this place, felt right at home , met the owner and she was the sweetest person ever,  the food was delicious!
She also invited me to have the Coffee ceremony with her and her friends,  we talked about life and built a great connection!
Definitely going back again.

We already started off on the wrong foot. Upon arrival, there was no one to greet us at the door, so we seated ourselves at a five-person table in a more private area, as we were a group of three women with purses. We were then asked to move “in case a larger party arrives.” Out of courtesy, we moved to a nearby table that was more out in the open and less comfortable. I had to ask for an extra chair for our bags, and it was wobbly—just like the table and the other chairs around us.

As we waited to be served, we watched another party of two women come in and seat themselves at a similar table without issue. They were given menus promptly and weren’t asked to move. Eventually, they relocated themselves to a smaller table—but the difference in treatment was noticeable.

We ordered sweet iced tea and were served hot tea instead. When we asked for the correct order, the replacement tea still wasn’t sweet. I asked for water instead, but it was never brought to the table. Throughout the visit, the staff did not seem particularly friendly or attentive.

What stood out even more was that the waiter explained the food selections in detail to most other tables—but when it came to our “chef’s choice” items, we had to ask for clarification ourselves. It felt like we were consistently overlooked, and that definitely impacted the overall experience. To top it off, when it came time to pay, the waiter had already preselected a higher tip amount—so double-check your bill before finalizing your payment.

That said, the atmosphere was quaint and charming—this spot has potential, and it was still worth the visit for a new experience. I just hope the service and consistency improve in the future.

A very lovely spot for some really good food! My friend took me here for my birthday and the staff assured us we could stop by even though our arrival was 30 minutes from closing which I typically try not to do, but they were the only Ethiopian spot open. They not only stayed open for us, they served us very friendly service and even brought out a dessert for my birthday.
The food was all amazing, we got the appetizer sampler and a platter to share and not a bit of it went to waste.  I will absolutely be returning! The restaurant is very clean and decorated in a way that feels as comforting as the friendly staff!

I truly enjoy my first experience at Queen of Sheba. The only downside was no one was there to great us when we first arrived, we just picked a 2 top and seated ourselves. The initial waitress was very quiet, but pleasant. The atmosphere is lovely and the decor was beautiful. I choose the 8 sample vegetarian platter (wish I had taken a picture). The presentation was on point and each dish I tried was divine.
I will definitely be coming back and will invite different friends to experience this place and food.

formatted_address: 13140 US-301, Riverview, FL 33578, United States
name: Africaribbean Royal

reviews.text: The food here is very impressive.  The jerk chicken is surprisingly good ..and this coming from a Jamaican.  This a definitely a must try.

I had such a wonderful experience at Africaribbean Royal! From the moment I arrived, the owners  made me feel at home with their friendly and attentive service. The atmosphere  and service is vibrant and beautifully reflects both African and Caribbean culture.

The food was the real highlight — fresh, flavorful, and cooked with so much love. Every dish was perfectly seasoned, and the combination of African and Caribbean flavors made it truly unique. I especially loved the jollof rice and  chicken — absolutely delicious!

If you’re looking for a spot that offers not only incredible food but also a welcoming vibe and cultural richness, this is the place. I’ll definitely be coming back and recommending it to everyone I know.
The food was soooo good. I had the jollof and jerk chicken, puff puff and the ginger drink. I really enjoyed the puffs and sobolo the most! I’ll definitely be coming back!
Great customer service! Great food portions! Will definitely be back. Riverview needed this.
The food was so good and, you can literally see that I ate all of it. And I very much recommend this for parties and other occasions

formatted_address: 1111 Bell Shoals Rd, Brandon, FL 33511, United States
name: Steaming Pots West Africa Cuisine Brandon

reviews.text: Not only were the drinks/food delicious but the service was amazing! The man running the truck was very kind and helpful in picking out what to get. I would definitely recommend and will be back.

This is the best west African food you'll have. I got the egusi soup with goat and it’s very authentic and very good definitely a must try if your in the Tampa to Brandon area 10/10 would definitely come back

Food was great. I have tried the egusi, okra soup, Efo Rio, and cassava fries….very tasty. The staff is always patient and friendly. They enjoy helping you pick a dish and allow you to sample items to try it out. I am glad they are in Brandon. I will be back 10/10 absolutely recommend. They are also on Door Dash!!!!

I’m a returning customer
The food was so good I skipped DoorDash & went to the restaurant
Thank you guys for the good food & good service:)
I love steaming pots! The best food Every time! I’m so happy I found the truck closer to my house!

formatted_address: 1908 W Dr Martin Luther King Jr Blvd, Tampa, FL 33607, United States
name: Ola's Foods Specialty Market - Africa On The Bay

reviews.text: I've been looking for a good African store in the Tampa bay area and thank goodness I finally found it!!!! They had everything that I was looking for. The costumer service is excellent. They greet you with the most beautiful, welcoming and warm smiles. They even have time to help you look for items and have a conversation with you.  At this store I found frozen Attieke (one of my favorite foods) as well as the boxed kind. They have African soap and real Shea butter and so much more. I can't wait to go back.
3x carton egusi + (rocks? debris?) shall take awhile to sort clean 😔😮‍💨

This store is truly the African Union! What ever you are looking for, you most likely will find it in Africa on the Bay. You'll find food items and products from a lot of African and Caribbean countries. Their prices are fair and I've not had any issues with the products/goods. It's the only African store in Tampa I go to and they do not disappoint. The customer service is great which is a huge plus.

The owner him self is very rude at times. He doesn’t greet people on their way in which I personally have no issue with. But if your going to check me out with an attitude throwing receipts at me like a dog that we not going to allow. This is not the first time I have notice this behavior from him. Very impatient man.
OGA….DO BETTER ON THAT END PLEASE!
Found my banana soy milk after immigration took mine coming back from LOS.. prices not bad either a

formatted_address: 4901 W Linebaugh Ave suite 4 & 5, Tampa, FL 33624, United States
name: Mitmita Ethiopian restaurant

reviews.text:
We tried Ethiopian cuisine for the first time and we were mighty impressed!

The flavors felt uncannily familiar to our Indian palate – bold, aromatic spices (like masalas), hearty lentil stews (like dal), crispy Veg & Chicken Sambusa (like Indian Samosa), and the tangy, spongy injera bread (like Dosa). The cheery on the top - eating everything by hand, tearing pieces of injera to scoop up the food.

Special shout-out to the wonderful manager/server for their incredible hospitality, made us feel truly at home especially with our energetic toddler❤️

Highly recommend this family-run place👍🏻

First time trying Ethiopian food, I thought everything was delicious! The flavor combinations and dishes were an experience in itself. This is a wholesome family run restaurant. One of the owners, Athena, serves the food, is extremely welcoming and makes you feel like you’re right at home. The food tasted fresh and I was delighted to try some new food and bold flavors. They have a sourdough bread called injera which was so good and tasted freshly made as well. The honey wine was sweet and the cherry on top of a delicious meal. We can’t wait to come back and try more dishes!

I had a good experience with the lady who served us she was kind and welcoming. However as a native Ethiopian born and raised in Ethiopia I want to share my honest feedback about the food. The dishes didn’t taste fresh, and it felt like the food had been reheated. The doro we ordered tasted like it was cooked days earlier, and I could even feel the bones while chewing, which shows it wasn’t prepared fresh. Overall, the food didn’t taste like native, authentic Ethiopian cuisine. I hope they improve the freshness and quality, because the service itself was nice.

What an awesome meal and experience! I've had Ethiopian food once before and was excited to experience it again. Mitmita did not disappoint! Loved the veggie combo and the lamb. And if you are going with multiple people it's fun to share a big platter. I had a great time speaking with the server as well, she may have also been the owner and she was happy to talk to me about Ethiopian food. She had great recommendations as well. Can't wait to come back!

I travel for work in one of the first things I do is find Ethiopian restaurants in the area. I was pleased with this find the food was authentically great. If you like your food spicy hot then this is the place for you. And the Honey wine was very nice. The service was excellent. I gave it a 4 for atmosphere because there was a family in there who was acting like they were at home. Very loud, with their kids running around. Other than that I highly recommend you go and try this cultural experience of food.

formatted_address: 2301 E Hillsborough Ave, Tampa, FL 33610, United States
name: YaYa Southern Cuisine

reviews.text: The food is delicious and flavorful. I had the dinner special (yellow rice and 2 chicken pieces). This was my 1st time tasting their food and as a Caribbean woman I was impressed with the flavor and tenderness of the chicken and the rice. I highly recommend trying them out. When you do, ENJOY!!😊

1st time visit it was a awesome experience. Ya Ya daughter who took our order she was patience and very helpful with answering the question about the menu very well and professional. Had the oxtail dinner and the turkey wing dinner everything cooked to perfection dessert was  banana pudding and strawberry shortcake.. Just like sitting at grandma table after church. Please don't change anything. Keep the recipes the same.. after eating that great dinner and dessert (I need a nap) moneys worth.A Awesome place to visit for great soul food. And we will be returning.. keep up the awesome work.

If you’re craving some good ole soul food, I’ll recommend this place. The staff were so nice,friendly and very helpful and the food was good. The only downside was that they had run out of most items, so I ended up with just collard greens and cabbage. The cook was nice enough to give me a little bit of Mac and cheese, It wasn’t much she gave me what was left.

The fish was cooked very well
The collard greens and cabbage were also seasoned well.
The Mac and cheese was my least favorite.

Overall I give them a 4/5 only because they didn’t have much of anything. I went around 8:30pm so be mindful and go early, because they do sell out fast!

Side note:
The lady at the front mentioned how they will be having patio parties. Once every month not sure what days they will be doing them. If you are looking for something to do. Definitely stop by and check it out.

Ok so I'm from Ohio but was in town for Breezy Bowl. I always make it a point to support black owned restaurants where ever I go. I googled a couple places for soul food and this one was fairly close with good reviews so I chose here. The restaurant decor is cute and gives a grown and secy vibe. I placed my order to go though. The service was AMAZING. The lady working the front was so personable and real, I felt like family. She suggested items and was up front with what they didn't have in stock. (I went close to closing time). I ordered the chicken dinner and she let me know that all the fried food is made fresh. She offered dessert options and said you can get banana pudding with or without bananas. I've never had this option before and was so happy to get it without bananas!! The food was hot and fresh. Portions were pretty big for the price of the dinners. I was so mad i didn't stop by and take some for the plane ride🤣. Definitely loved it here!!
We were visiting from NC & the food was great! The oxtails & baked chicken fell off the bone!  The greens, yams, Mac & cheese were super good! Highly recommended!!

formatted_address: 1930 E 7th Ave, Tampa, FL 33605, United States
name: 7th + Grove

reviews.text: This was my second time to 7th & Grove. We arrived around 5:15ish. Since it was early - there wasn’t a crowd, unlike my first visit. Also, I noticed the menu had changed a little bit from my first visit - no biggie. Mariah was our server, she was very knowledgeable, friendly and professional. We wanted to start our date night off with some egg rolls - but we were advised they didn’t have any - again - no biggie - I had missed lunch so I was hungry - so I ordered some cornbread and our main course. We both ordered Oxtail with mash potatoes substituted the mash potatoes with grits. The cornbread came quickly and the food shortly after with mash potatoes instead of the requested grits. I kept mine - but my husband wanted what he ordered grits. Mariah fixed it immediately by providing a bowl of grits on the side. While eating I found hair in my food - so I ended up sending my food back anyway. The manager America replaced my food with fresh food. If not for the hiccups I would have given this place 5+ stars.

This was our second experience at 7th & Grove, and it absolutely delivered once again. The music alone sets the tone—the vibe is unmatched, and for me, music is everything. From the moment you walk in, the energy is intentional and elevated.

The bar service was excellent, the regular menu was flavorful and well-executed, and the buffet was truly top tier. Everything felt thoughtfully curated, not rushed or overdone.

We’re visiting from Orlando, and this spot is well worth the trip. Consistent quality, great atmosphere, and an experience that stands out. We’ll definitely be back.

Marg is a FANTASTIC SERVER. Her attitude was beyond professional, she always checked in with everyone at our table to ensure we were happy with our food & drinks. I would highly recommend coming here. Be sure to show MARG LOVE AND LEAVE A TIP. Thank you for showing us some love.

First time there and I gotta tell you the food was fabulous. I try grits for the first time. It was so good. I’m already planning my next visit with my adult children next week. My coworker took me there today and we have a blast. The waitress was awesome. The food Was delicious. I definitely recommend this place. I give it a 10 out of 10

Great food. Loved the catfish and gouda grits with collard greens and fried okra. Drinks were delicious! I had the Meg the Stallion. The service was a little slow,  but all of the staff was attentive and very polite. The artwork made it a very cool atmosphere.  I will definitely be returning the next time I am in the area.

formatted_address: 4819 E Busch Blvd, Tampa, FL 33617, United States
name: Abu Naji Restaurant

reviews.text: Hands Down the best food we ate in Tampa and best service. The meat and chicken and rice is sooo tasty, soaked in the real herbs of Yemen. Fries were so crucnhy too. They didnt disappoint! They also have Arabic floor seating if you want to get the whole experience. The menu was easy to follow, the menu said serve two, well it served five and we took the leftovers for tomorrow's lunch MashAllah.

My husband and I came here for the first time and it was an amazing experience.
We ordered the spicy chicken hummus and it was hands down the best hummus I’ve ever had and I love hummus. Perfectly seasoned, creamy, and incredibly fresh.
We also shared a platter that came with a whole chicken and lamb over a bed of rice. Both the chicken and lamb were cooked to perfection, extremely flavorful, and well seasoned. Nothing was dry or bland. Everything tasted fresh and thoughtfully prepared.
The service was fast and friendly, and the portion sizes were very generous. The entire platter with all of this food was only $60, which is an amazing value for the quality and amount of food you get.
Freshness really stood out the most. You can truly taste the quality in every dish.
We’ll definitely be back. Great food, great service, and very affordable for the quality. Highly recommend.

Stopped in after seeing so many videos promoting this place. It definitely lived up to the hype. Even though it looks super small .. it's a good sized restaurant with options to sit on the floor in a private room or at a table. We opted for the private room and it was so comfortable and nice to be with family and not have others around. The waiter was amazing super helpful and very nice. The appetizers were 10/10. Smooth and smoky so good. The beef rib that they only serve on the weekend was definitely the star of the show. So tender and juicy and huge enough to feed 2. We also got the romancey fancy for 2. It was very good too. Huge portions with so much left over. We were a family of 4. Also the pitcher of mint lemonade. Nowhere in Tampa will u find like it. You can actually taste the zest of the lime, it kicks it up to another level. Overall it was a 10/10 experience all around. Definitely on our rotation of favorite restaurants.

It was my first time at. Yemeni restaurant and this place was so amazing And authentic. The ambiance was cozy but not too try hard, the food was wholesome, tasty, and generously portioned, and the jug of homemade mint lemonade was a hit with my family. Worth every penny and definitely an experience.

As a lover of tradition, the vibe and look was on point. Food and service were excellent, fun for the whole family. Serving sizes are based on extreme, so we could have taken it down a notch. We had 5 adults and 5 children and had plenty of leftovers based on a 6 person dish. Will definitely visit again.

formatted_address: 9718 N 56th St, Temple Terrace, FL 33617, United States
name: Mangos Cafe and Specialty Store

reviews.text: Drove 40 minutes to try this out.. 10/10 food and service experience. I had 3 orders of an oxtail plate for pick up and it was a wait for it but only because the food kept having to be restocked — meaning fresh trays of food in rotation!! The food definitely tasted super fresh and well seasoned. While waiting, the workers were so sweet and personable. I really enjoyed my time there even with me placing an online pick up order. Also the portions they give made the price worth it. Might have to share a plate next time since it was enough to eat 2 1/2 times!

I love love loveee this place! I go here so much and only managed to grab these 2 photos from 2 separate visits because I immediately dig in! The food is delicious! The staff has gotten to recognize me now and I love that for me lol. You can't go wrong with anything from here and they have vegan options. The garlic herb salmon, oxtails, red snapper, plantains are my chef's kiss favorites. Also don't forget your punch and cake! So yummy too!

Wifey and I have been trying to catch the Soul Food day but as you know, as soon as they open it’s packed like how they packed the food to go. Today was are first time trying Mangos and we made sure we came when they open to kick start my wife’s birthday. Right from the start of walking in, the staff were amazing and greeting immediately when walking in. Location was really clean and the had the chunes playing making it a vibe as you wait to get your order. S/O to Diana who was the extremely nice and made sure we were good with our order. I can’t express enough about  the customer service. The customer service matches the food. The food was so good!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! I don’t even want to go in to details because it still wouldn’t do no justice. Cornbread is on another level, oxtails were pack with flavor and so tender ……. Just pull up and find out. S/O to Mangos, I can’t express how thankful we are for the experience. Can’t wait to go back on Caribbean day.

We visited on a Sunday morning and it was already packed when we got there.  The staff is super friendly.  I got southern fried catfish which is prepared fresh so we did have to wait.  It was worth the wait.  All the food was amazing and the cornbread...so good.  A must try is the Sunset punch.  Thank me later.  When I go back I'm definitely trying the shrimp. That looked amazing. It is a small place so do not expect to dine in.

Let me start by saying, WOW! We came into the restaurant for takeout on a Thursday afternoon around 3pm. Lunch was over so I assumed it wouldnt be busy. Im heavily pregnant so was a little put off by the line but I needed to try this Caribbean food. I’ve eaten in alot of Caribbean restaurants in the Tampa area and they just weren’t a fit for me. When I got to the counter I was greeted so warm & kind it washed away the wait time. I then asked for oxtails and sadly it finished on the order right before me, I swapped to a small Jerk chicken and small curry chicken, we also got the pineapple drink and ice tea. The food? 1000/10 with no exaggeration I am also Caribbean and have been searching for this flavor in Tampa for so long! This is a unique Caribbean flavor, it wasnt salty (a lot of people confuse salt with seasoning), it was expertly seasoned. I also despise when they put too much oil in the food and this didnt have that oil puddle. I wasnt charged EXTRA for oxtail sauce on my jerk chicken it was offered which I truly appreciate. The food wasnt too spicy my boys 7 & 6 years old were able to eat it and rated it “on my favorites list”. I did let the staff know it was my first time and because I ordered the oxtails first but it was sold out she gave me some the bits in the tray to taste, that was also sensational. Our total (family of 4) was just under $40 for 2 meals & 2 drinks which is fairly priced to the quality of food. After a 40 mins drive to get here my only regret is that I didnt get two more plates for later. I will definitely be back.

formatted_address: 1930 E 7th Ave C, Tampa, FL 33605, United States
name: Madame Fortune Dessert + HiFi Parlour

reviews.text:
This hidden gem in Ybor City is absolutely amazing! The food was on point from start to finish. We had the honey-glazed turkey tips, sweet potato cornbread, Rasta pasta, seafood pasta, and gouda macaroni everything was well seasoned and full of flavor.
Our server, Jessica, was incredibly sweet and very knowledgeable about the menu which made the experience even better. The service and the food were both top-tier. I will definitely be going back!

I've been to a variety of restaurants from  simple fare to Michelin star establishments around the world but tonight I just ate at a place that has become my 3rd favorite of all time (next to the chargrilled oysters at Dragos in NOLA and the suckling pig at Las Galayos in Madrid).  Madame Fortune  in Tampa was a taste experience that literally compelled me to give the chef a hug 😆.   Everything from beginning to end was an outstanding flavor experience.   Sweet potato cornbread, braised oxtail pigeon peas rice and warm beignets.  SUPERB!  The vibe atmosphere and service was extraordinary.  Unforgettable flavor!!!! Excited to have a black owned establishment in my top 3!

We had reservations, buy had to wait a little while. They send you a password to enter. Our waiter was friendly and helpful. I ordered the oxtail pasta, which thr meat was too tough for my liking. The manager quickly rectified the situation and I ended up getting the lamb chops which were awesome. My husband had the oxtail Sheppard pie, which he enjoyed. The atmosphere was laid back with music playing in the background. I highly recommend making reservations.

Looking for a secret hidden gem - secret door to a whole vibe. Despite the wait time after making a reservation, it was definitely worth the wait. Front wait area show a little bakery “ Roast “ with some dope props that go with the theme. Pass the secret door was a whole vibe. The Dj was jammin’, playing all the 90’s - 2010’s R&B hits to match the mood of the restaurant. The customer service was 10 out of 10. We were a party of 6 and our waiter made sure we were good the whole time. S/O to him, wish I could remember. The food was really good!!! Hit the spot!!!! Highly recommend!! We stay away from the club scene, so this gave us the best of both worlds.

Atmosphere was great. Our table enjoyed the appetizers more than the entrees.  Sangria pitcher was on point.  The pepper pot oxtail shepherd pie was good but the oxtails were very salty.  Cabbage/collars w/the cornbread were the hit of the entree. Turkey wings were awesome, well seasoned and fall off the bone tender.  Mussels & shrimp had a slight kick amazing.

formatted_address: 3401 N Nebraska Ave, Tampa, FL 33603, United States
name: Mr B's Restaurant

reviews.text:
Tried Mr B's Restaurant, on a whim after googling for a good place to eat breakfast. Located on North Nebraska Ave in Tampa.
Not disappointed! Exterior not impressive but when you walk through the door, you find a really (REALLY, REALLY) inviting  place, beautifully decorated and welcoming. Jordan, my waiter, got it all right and I was soon enjoying grits and eggs over-easy + smoked sausage + biscuits + french toast made with Cuban bread & adorned with a delectable sweet cream, powdered sugar and cinnamon. Yes, too much but sssooo worth it! Definitely recommend!

Very glad to find this place.. needed a home cooked meal and what better way to satisfy that by stopping thru Mr Bs. I'm not from Florida but I'll definitely return when I'm around. Food was great service and atmosphere are 10 out of 10 👍

We stopped by this restaurant on our way heading out of town because I had a taste for oxtails. At the time no one else in the car really wanted anything else to eat so I got out by myself to order. As soon as I walked in, there was a wave of comfort and hospitality that greeted me at the door! Everyone was all smiles, and it didn’t seem fake. I ordered oxtails with collard greens and lima beans. Everything tasted as if my grandma cooked it and had it prepared, especially for me. Once everyone in the car saw my food, the rest of my family (7 of us total) came in to order as well. We intended to take our food to go, but we actually started to sit down and eat because the food smelled and taste so good no exaggeration. We can’t wait to get back to this place! Best soul food restaurant I’ve been to!

Mr. B’s is where the soul meets the skillet!

We stopped by Mr. B’s in Tampa and let me tell you—we didn’t leave hungry OR disappointed! I had the fried fish with cheese grits, and that fish was fried to golden perfection—crispy on the outside, flaky and tender inside. The grits? Creamy, cheesy, and straight-up comforting.

We also tried the fried pork chops with cheese grits and scrambled eggs. Those chops were seasoned with love and fried just right, and the eggs were fluffy and just how we like ’em.

And don’t even get me started on the French toast combo—fluffy toast with just the right amount of cinnamon, paired with scrambled eggs, breakfast potatoes, sausage, and toast. It was the breakfast plate of champions.

The staff was friendly, especially our waitress, Felicia, the vibe was laid back, and everything felt like a warm hug from Grandma's kitchen. Mr. B’s is officially on our “must return” list.
Food was really good for the most part. Extremely good atmosphere. Very hospitable and friendly. They know how to treat you like family!

formatted_address: 201 Ring Rd Suite 10, Ridgeland, MS 39157, United States
name: Afrishoppi Kitchen | The Only Nigerian Restaurant in Mississippi. We offer 100% Catering service, Order 24 hours ahead.

html_attributions: Afrishoppi Kitchen | The Only Nigerian Restaurant in Mississippi. We offer 100% Catering service, Order 24 hours ahead.

reviews.text: I had been wanting to try this place since it opened and honestly I was disappointed my first experience here. I purchased the lemon iced tea, which was not good. Ended up purchasing hibiscus tea after searching their website and saw it was offered in cups although it is not on menu. We purchased the Yassa with goat meat and chicken jollof. The wait was about ~20 mins and the jollof came out first. Although the person I was with did not immediately eat, the food was rather warm, not hot and looked almost as if it had been sitting out. The chicken was dry. I received my yassa with rice and the portion was not worth the cost at all for either meals. The meat was so very tough I couldn't finish and they were very small with majority having fat on it (which I don't eat). Mostly my meal had onions than anything so I ate that with white rice. We also purchased fufu. If I did not enjoy African food prior to this experience, I would not be intrigued to eat African cultured food again. Paid around ~$55 and no receipt was even asked to be given. Meanwhile leaving, the owners plate were filled with huge portions of food. Although the owners were very kind, I honestly will not return and I am saddened I did not enjoy this experience.

This was my first time trying African cuisine and I must say I was not disappointed. The oxtails were so tender and flavorful. I absolutely loved the cabbage, vegetables and rice. Everything was seasoned perfectly. This was truly a good comfort meal. I can’t wait to try the egusi and fufu next. Great experience here and great service as well. Thank you! I will definitely be back! Also I ordered takeout and my food didn’t even make it home lol.

Food was terrible, first of all it’s a hair salon. You have to call in an order and pay before you even get your food.
