Waited over 30 min to get it and when I did the plantains I ordered was cold, the egusi was so watered down with only a little bit in there with two big beef pieces that was NOT tender, I didn’t get fufu I got something else. It was terrible. Everything. Do not recommend .

This place is WONDERFUL. If you’re looking for affordable African Food .. THIS IS THE PLACE! EVERY THING WAS GOOD, FRESH, AND HOT! They even have specials😍😍😍😍only thing to me is that they need to add a little more food to your plate but other than that it’s AMAZING !
Authentic West African( Nigerian) food. Way better than the place across the street( IYKYK). The egusi was warm and flavorful. The jollof was spicy and savory. Very good.

formatted_address: 1901 N Howard Ave, Tampa, FL 33607, United States
name: Lucky Tigre

reviews.text:
Had gone to their food truck a while back and loved the food, so when we found out that they moved to a building so we had to go!

We came here on a sunday at about 1-2pm. It was pretty busy and finding parking was a bit difficult. We had to sit at the bar since there were no tables available inside, but not a big deal for 2 people.

We got the ube matcha and horchata matcha lattes, mochi fried chicken as appetizers, lemongrass bbq skewers and chicken adobo, and halo halo at the end. Everything came out pretty quick for being so busy! The lattes were amazing and the food was so delicious and cooked really well. The halo halo was good too, even as someone who isn’t a huge fan of coconut.

The service was great and super attentive! Would love to come again and try everything else!!

If you want good Filipino 🇵🇭 food from a family-owned restaurant and wonderful service, then Lucky Tigre is the place to go. 😋 This restaurant has only been open for 3 months. According to one of the owners I spoke with, they used to be a food truck, then a pop-up restaurant, and now a brick-n-mortar restaurant. The location is not desirable and the atmosphere has more like a 'diner vibe' but THE FOOD is what matters. Plus, they have just opened so I'm sure things will change as their business grows. We got there around 11:45am and they were busy the whole time we were there.

I've had this place on my "want to go" list for about a month. Then a close friend of mine sent me a text about the place and asked to go for lunch so we did and I brought my son too. 🙂

As a Filipino myself, I wanted to try a good variety of their food so we ordered several dishes...lumpia, pancit, BBQ chicken skewers, pulled chicken adobo bao buns, tocino dumplings, Lucky fries, Adobo, a salted caramel Ube milk tea, strawberry fruit tea, strawberry calamansi lemonade, a couple pastries (Ensaimada and Senorita Bread), and for dessert...Halo-halo. I took a couple pics after the 3 of us started eating (sorry 🙃) The portions are a good size and their plating presentation is with banana leaves, atchara (pickled side dish), and a cucumber salad. As most Filipinos know, we all cook our food different so flavors are going to vary for each Filipino like myself but for anyone else the food is delicious. One of their most popular dishes is the chicken skewers and I had one of their last 2 orders left for lunch. The chicken literally melted in my mouth and was very well seasoned. I loved it and I see why it's popular. I always make my skewers with pork so this really makes me want to try my marinade recipe with chicken next time. 😉 Their pancit was a bit bland to me but I added some calamansi and a little bit of the tocino dumplings sauce and it was delicious. All the other dishes we ordered were very good. 😋 My son enjoyed the bao buns and the fries. We had leftovers to bring home since we ordered alot of food. I had their version of halo-halo and it was creamy and satisfying for a dessert. My friend had their mango pastry and he said it was very good. I have not tried the pastries I bought yet so can't review those but I'm sure they are good as well. ☺️

I definitely recommend this place and I will be bringing the rest of my family here in the future to try more of their Filipino dishes. 🤩

We added Lucky Tigre to our list of restaurants to visit while in Tampa! We love bao buns and like to try them wherever we go. We visited on 12/23 around 7pm. The decor is super fun, lots of live plants and art. Bathrooms were clean and thoughtfully stocked and the food… DELICIOUS! We were kindly greeted when we entered. We ordered all the bao bun options, Lucky Fries, beef dumplings, and the 6pc grilled chicken skewers. For drinks we had a mango lemonade, strawberry milk tea and brown sugar milk tea. All were so good! 10/10 all around! We went back for lunch the next day!

I’ll start off by saying a friend of mine referred me here and we came on a Sunday. The restaurant opens at noon on Sundays and for some reason they were backed up on orders and didn’t let us in until 1235. They had a DJ playing outside in the outdoor eating area, but it was a little too loud that you could almost not have conversation. After they let us in the line to order with about five people ahead, probably took an additional 20 minutes. I didn’t get to place my order until 115 and the food came out at 1:30. (we got there at noon like I said.) so to essentially take an hour and 15 minutes to get food from opening time, is quite the wait. The food was good however they mentioned that they were out completely of boa buns. One of the people in our party her food didn’t come out until about 1:40. I ordered the pork dumplings with an add-on of chili oil as well as the fried pork belly with the rice. The pork belly was extremely tough, like incredibly hard to chew, and didn’t have much flavor beyond that. And for those two items, I paid $25. I would love to give a place another chance but as a first impression, it was really throwing me off waiting 35 minutes past opening time with zero communication till about 12:20 that they were running behind.

I was finally able to stop by the Lucky Tigre after seeing a few IG reviews. We were in Tampa for a soccer tournament and my daughter and I stopped in for dinner.  Immediately loved the look and feel when we arrived. The restaurant  gives a Filipino vibe by adding local/original props, serving glass bottle sodas, adding banana leaf with the plating and traditional ingredients.  We ordered dumplings, lechon kawali and their version of chicken adobo. The kawali was not served with the traditional sauce  and we were surprised by the shredded chicken for the adobo, but the flavors were still very good and the papaya salad was on point. If you are in the area, I recommend you stop in. We will definitely be back to try other items on the menu.

formatted_address: 4908 N 22nd St, Tampa, FL 33610, United States
name: Janniemae's cafe

reviews.text:
Too  Expensive!!! I ordered 4 pieces of chicken and it turns out to be 4 pieces of wings which is still chicken but at least they should tell you. I paid $17 dollars for 4 pieces of wings a little bit of rice and beans. The place is all covered you can't see what's going on inside. I won't ever be back to this food truck.

Edit: oh yes, you're right, I was confused on the total amount. Everything else still stands.!!
BEST Food in central Florida. Being a very rare place that you really get the food you see pictured. The  food was delicious & fresh."
Had the fish and soul food.  Were stuffed.  Can't wait to get back to the homemade banana pudding and strawberry shortcake.

Very good soul food highly recommended please check her Instagram as she changes her menu everyday. I had her green beans and rice and Mac and cheese everything was very tasty and fresh! Will come back again thank you for your service!

I give 1 star because their was sum major errors made on my order:

1. I ordered a fish sandwich dinner, even discussed the condiments & toppings in detail for my sandwich with the order taker... yet I got fish laying on top of rice, no sandwich, no condiments, no toppings, nothing.

2. I ordered baked beans with my dinner, my b.f. asked for green beans with his. Instead, the green beans was served with my order, & the bake beans was on his plate.  My bad for not checking our plates before leaving.

3.  The chicken was dry & tough.  The breaded fish was salty, macaroni n cheese was barely cheesy & cold.  The items that tasted the best were both beans, & their banana pudding.

Overall, the food was mediocre, their customer service was pleasant, but they advised me my order would be complete in 7 minutes.  However, that turned into 15 minutes plus.  Unfortunately, I won't be a repeat customer.

formatted_address: 12208 N 56th St, Temple Terrace, FL 33617, United States
name: Abu Omar Halal - Tampa, FL

reviews.text: My husband and I ordered two arabi meals - a beef and chicken. The shawarma was easily just as good as shawarma I have had in the middle east. The fries and pickles were also so good! I really enjoyed everything and will absolutely be back again!

First time trying Abu Omar. I was in the mood for a Shawarma and stopped by. I ordered their Beef Shawarma. It was delicious. Everything tasted fresh. The fries were freshly cooked and the sandwich came with extra sauce and pickles. Love the pickles! Nothing to complain about, I’ll be back.

One of my biggest pet peeves is paying for outside food and it not being up to par, decent or edible. Some of these places have no pride in what they are serving and it shows. I really wanted to love this food after seeing it on social media. First for starts—their online ordering website will make you think that you are in fact getting a BOGO deal on a meal totaling $24 for 2 when in all actuality, the meal itself is only $14 in store—when you purchase 2, it’s 28 and not the $48+ dollars the website claims before applying this “discount”. Ordering from the website doing this bogo saves you about $4-$5. This should have been my first red flag.🚩

Now let’s get to the food. The rice was super dried out that it was inedible. The kofta was also dried out and they charge you $1.50 for the little squirt of sauce that they give you in the condiments container. The food had no flavor and was old and dry. I nearly choked to death trying to swallow the kofta, no lie.  I am new to this area and this is the 2nd halal restaurant on this strip that I’ve tried, that has left me feeling ripped off due to the unacceptable quality and taste of their food.

I will not patronize again nor will I return. This place was a total waste of money , time and gas. The food went in the trash!

There was no pride or love in the preparation of this meal.

The food is 10 out of 10. I have had the shawarma combo and yesterday tried the shawarma quesadilla and it was amazing. I also tried their falafel and kibbeh and it’s better than the Spanish Quipe, wala. The service is always very welcoming. And the atmosphere is lively. Love that they offer Palestine Soda it’s so good. And the baklava is so good. Just choose anything and I promise you it’s all so scrumptious.

I always order the shawarma bites from here,  they’re absolutely delicious and incredibly tender, especially the beef ones! The flavor is always on point, and the meat is perfectly cooked every time. I usually place my order with Khalid, who’s always friendly, attentive, and makes sure everything is just right. Excellent food and even better service, highly recommend

formatted_address: 4328 W El Prado Blvd, Tampa, FL 33629, United States
name: Nene's Restaurant & Bar

reviews.text:
We celebrated my birthday here with a group of 21 people, and honestly it couldn’t have gone better.
They helped us plan the menu ahead of time, which made everything so much easier. Nothing felt random or chaotic - everything was organized and just made sense.
The place itself is super cozy and warm, perfect for a birthday dinner. Service was great, food came out on time, and no one felt forgotten even with such a big group.
It really felt personal and well taken care of, which I really appreciated.
Would 100% come back and definitely recommend this place for group dinners or celebrations.

Great meal!
We just completed our second trip thru Europe this year and have had lots of good food in many countries. We were on a layover in Tampa and I wanted one more authentic meal before the trip was complete. I googled European food places and a few came up, but Nene’s has a great rating and looked interesting.
We started with Ukrainian salad vinaigrette and Samsa . Both were good but i enjoyed the samsa better. Hot and well seasoned.
We enjoyed this with a couple of beers,  scyturys being one of them.
For dinner
First the good came out hot and steaming.
She had Chakhokhbili, which she said was very good.
I had Uzbek Plov. The lamb was very tender. Rice was perfectly cooked and well seasoned.
We enjoyed a bottle of Vida Rkatsiteli Qvevri . It went well with our meal.
The place was not too busy, and had a great atmosphere. Authentic décor and music. The gentleman serving us was great to talk with snd explain the menu or dishes we were unfamiliar with. (Even suggested I didn’t order the Kan plov as its a dish meant for 4)
We dod not get to enjoy dessert as our main courses were very filling.
Would recommend again to anyone! Thank you Nene’s for a memorable last European meal for our trip.

This is truly one of the best Ukrainian-Georgian restaurants I’ve ever been to! 💛❤️
The people here are incredibly hospitable and kind — it feels like visiting good friends. The food is absolutely delicious, fresh, and made with love.
It’s the kind of place you want to stay longer and come back to again and again. Highly recommend to everyone who appreciates great food and genuine hospitality! 🥰🍷

I will always recommend trying new places and Nene’s is a hidden gem. Cozy vibes, friendly and helpful service, and amazing food. We ordered the Khachapuri, Khinkali, Uzbek Plov, and the three sisters dolma. Boy many places I can think of in the area where you can have Georgian, Uzbek, Azerbaijani, and Ukrainian food. You can tell the food is made with passion.

The best Georgian restaurant on the entire East Coast!
Nene’s in Tampa truly feels like home — warm, cozy, and welcoming atmosphere. The Adjarian khachapuri is absolutely outstanding,  perfectly baked, rich, and authentic.
Highly recommend to anyone who wants to experience true Georgian flavors!

formatted_address: 3701 E Dr Martin Luther King Jr Blvd, Tampa, FL 33610, United States
name: Mama's Soul Food Restaurant

reviews.text: I wish I could give them a zero.. Instead of packing the food in a dinner container, they put chicken in a small container, rice and gravy and cornbread, and small container the peas in a little cup container. When I opened the container with the rice, the cornbread fell out on the floor. Then the rice in the gravy fell on the floor OK so I eat the peas when to open the top for the peas. It broke and it dropped only thing I got to eat was I didn’t eat the chicken and corn fritters I called them back. They asked the manager why was it packed this way, instead of her apologizing I was told to be quiet and let them talk and then I can talk. Never ever ever have I received service like this from you guys and I’ll never give you my money again bad bad bad bad service I got the chicken wing dinner with Black Eyed Peas and rice and I got corn. Fritters I could see if you put the corn fritters on the side never got the Black Eyed Peas on the side and it was just horrible and I spent my money for nothing never will you get my business again? Because my food wasn’t packaged correctly when I opened it up it fell on the floor all between my seats. These are the photos, but they refuse to refund me or talk to me.

The service was really great here at Mama's and the hostess was fabulous however the food was found to be a little lacking in certain areas of taste, at least the dishes that we had. The fried fish sandwich was cooked to long and too hard, most of the flavor was gone by the time it made it to the table. Also the smothered chicken wasn't lacking in taste but made up for it in saltiness (to much for my palate)! I'm sure the rest of the menu would be alright however we didn't have time to sample everything. We we told to visit the other location which may offer a larger variety of soul food items.

Food and service were excellent! Decided to try them while on vacation and i was not disappointed! I had honey wings, Mac n cheese, greens, yams, rice n gravy and cornbread.  Then topped it off with banana pudding.

Hostess/server was pretty nonchalant/rude no help with guidance with the Menu. Fries was pretty burnt but warm. I got a pork Chop sandwich and let me tell you it was the best thing smoking well season still hot. You wanna go for a good piece of season pork chop I recommend this place but the hospitality Gots to do better And stop burning people fries lol

First time dining here we were very pleased with our food I ordered the turkey wings yellow rice black eyed peas Mac n cheese my husband had the fried fish n shrimp we both enjoyed our meals we will definitely be back 😘💕

formatted_address: 4818 E Busch Blvd, Tampa, FL 33617, United States
name: Kreyol Delight

reviews.text:
Kreyòl Delight catered my wedding and the food was AMAZING!! Everyone was raving about it, my parents, my Haitian friends, my American friends! 🤣 Them plates were cleared!!!
She went above and beyond, making sure we had everything we needed!!
Definitely give her food a try and book her for your next event!!!
Ain’t no way I was charged $70 for this SUPER small fish, extra plantains, and 2 drinks. NEVER AGAIN
Made an impromptu stop for some food and enjoyed it all! The cashier was friendly and the flavor was so so good on our pork and fried fish meals. Would highly recommend!

If I could give more than 5 stars, I would. This restaurant catered my wedding of 150 people. The owner was VERY patient, professional & kind. Extremely detailed & communicative. They delivered our food from Brandon to Maitland. The food arrived ON TIME & HOT!! There were no complaints about the food from our guests, not one. Not to mention I booked them a month before my wedding. The only catering company I could ever recommend to others. They did their big one ❤️❤️❤️ thank you for contributing peace & flavor to my wedding; you WILL be seeing me & my family again, for sure!

I’d say one of the top Haitian restaurants in Tampa! Some of the best high quality we’ll prepared food and well seasoned and cooked to perfection. The legume is fresh and rich with great flavors. The plantains are fried just right and the fried turkey was very good tasted seasoned and fresh to eat. If you have a choice to choose between which Haitian restaurants to try then just know you’re not making a mistake for choosing Kreyol Delight.

formatted_address: 11900 N Nebraska Ave Suite #1, Tampa, FL 33612, United States
name: Mom's Restaurant Haitian Cuisine and Bakery

reviews.text: Amazing food amazing service ! Always fill your plate up. It’s one of the best Haitian spots around definitely check it out ! They deserve so much more love ❤️

Honestly speaking, this is hands down the best Haitian restaurant I’ve been to and I’m from the Caribbean! Not to add, as a huge food junkie I’ve spent almost my entire life chasing authentic tastes and savory blends. I have always been culturally inclined on world history and I must say, coming here was a whole geographical education session on matters pertaining today’s society. The food was amazing! Atmosphere was very warm and the lessons learnt could never been paid for! Thank God for Ma and Pa! They are the best! Please say hello if you are ever in the Tampa area!

First time trying Haitian food in Tampa! Hands down the freshest I’ve ever had. Service was fast and Edward is the gentleman who served my mother and I! Super nice and welcoming! We will be back for sure! The griot and plantains mixed with the juiciness of the pikliz which I must say is out of this WORLS! super tasty!

We  were greeted  at the door with such a  warm and friendly welcome by the owner. It was our first time eating here and I'm glad we came. Their meal portions are very generous for what you pay for. The Fried Goat was perfectly seasoned, cooked and crispy, while still being moist and tender falling off the bone. The Stewed  Chicken was full of rich flavor and  juicey. We will definitely be back for more  of this Delicious Authentic Haitian Home cooking.🤩

The food and service was one of a kind! From the beginning of our visit, Edward was kind, funny, and very welcoming! The food speaks for itself but he has no problem selling you on its authenticity, freshness, and flavors! We bought stewed turkey, griot, oxtails, rice with beans, and pikilz. Pikilz is like no other with such a powerful seasoned taste. The oxtails give us Jamaicans a run for our money! The griot was perfect and not dry at all. The stewed turkey was so tender and juicy. Everything was amazing and will be back again and again! Thank you Edward and Mom's Restaurant!!

formatted_address: 2832 S MacDill Ave, Tampa, FL 33629, United States
name: Byblos

reviews.text:
3.5, probably will return - this was my rating in 2021, and I forgot to post. It was a rainy day, and we came in from the back.

Today, it's a sunny Friday evening. Everything looks bright and lovely. I was wondering why everything seems familiar, especially the bar and lockers by the front desk.

We ordered four appetizers / small plates:

Eggplant
Falafel
Calamari: is flat
Burrata

All are good, with pretty large portions. If I remember correctly, their eggplant is the most shapely, and the red sauce is kind of the first too. However, I don't care for the dark, sweet sauce. The raw walnuts taste raw.

I like the falafel the most, especially the pinky pickled turnip (?) — please correct me if I'm wrong.

… so the old me left my cc there. They’ll send back to me on Monday - thanks K!

Want to inform that there is no belly dance anymore. Food was average.. only liked one app that we ordered. Chicken shawarma is awfully it’s close to fajitas than shawarma. Dint try any drinks. Tar tar came with a lot of olive oil which ruined its taste. Fries were good.

This restaurant offers an excellent dining experience with authentic Lebanese cuisine. The manager was incredibly accommodating, finding the perfect table for our group in the quiet corner of the restaurant. The service was impeccable, making it a highly recommended spot!

PHENOMENAL! Best service, incredible atmosphere, outstanding cuisine! We came here as a party of 9 and were BLOWN AWAY! From the very first conversation with the host in reserving a table all the way to the very last minute when we were leaving, we were treated with friendliness, grace and respect. Our Server, Chris was full of life and charisma, cracking joke after joke, making us all laugh and enjoy our time there. He was the most attentive server I have ever experienced in my lifetime. Everytime our glasses were half full he would refill us, he took away dirty plates with promptness, suggested dishes for us and took our orders with precision and ease. He was SO friendly, warm and an honor to have in our company.
Now let me get to the food; dare I say it is the BEST FOOD in all of Tampa? I DO, actually! You can TASTE THE LOVE and THOUGHTFULNESS they put into EVERY DISH!!! Even the fries were perfection, not frozen, house made fresh deliciousness with a light, golden, thin crisp on the outside and a mashed potato consistency on the inside and SO DAMN FLAVORFUL! How do you make the inside of your fries that tasty!?? NEVER IN MY LIFE have I tasted a fry that damn delicious! Don't even get me started on the scallops.......I cut them with my spoon, that is how delicate they were! Very flavorful, you can tell they fry the panchetta first and then the scallops in the grease, but you don't miss out on the fresh element either, especially with the green pea puree; MUAH, to die for! Best scallops I've ever had in my life. And you know I had to try a little of everyone else's dish. I would be here for hours writing if I had to describe each one of their unique flavors. Let me just say everyone loved their dish as much as I loved mine!
In addition, I love when the manager comes to visit the table to see how everything was! So personable and appreciated (also, thank you for my husband's complimentary shot of whiskey for his birthday). This restaurant was so well thought out, from the comfy chairs to the layout and the decor. All I have to say is, if you want to FEEL emotions while you eat and be transported into a different world where the mundane everyday reality seems to dwindle away for an hour or two,  and you want to really enjoy EVERY bite you take, while being treated like royalty, COME HERE!!!!
I am already planning an excuse to come back!
Thank you Chris for your warm-hearted personality and thank you Byblos staff for being so friendly and welcoming. This place deserves a Michelin star!

Love what they did with the space (from the ladder at the bar to the mural on the wall). The staff is lovely. The flavors are really well paired! We like a little more salt, but mostly enjoyed as is. Fave was the beautifully green and super moist falafel with tahini.

formatted_address: 3320 E Osborne Ave, Tampa, FL 33610, United States
name: M&R Café Southern Cuisine

reviews.text: I ordered the catfish with macaroni and cheese and collard greens. The fish was very fresh and perfectly seasoned, placed on a bed of yellow rice. The mac was delicious and had the quintessential cheese pull. Greens were cooked flawlessly. I can tell this food is made with love. The meal included a sweet potato cornbread muffin, which in my opinion beats a lot of restaurants desserts. It was so good I ordered an extra one. To wash all this down, I got a pineapple lemonade that deserves to be sold in stores. The staff is friendly and provided a welcoming atmosphere. If I could give this place more stars I would. Definitely coming back whenever I am able to.

First time tonight.  Great atmosphere.  Nicest women with teeth braces was very welcoming who took my order.   Met the owner and very friendly aswell. Tried the oxtails, greens and Mac n cheese.  5 star. Definitely authentic,  fresh and contagious.  I will return and highly recommend.

My first time tasting their food and it was not a good experience. Don't believe the hype. The chicken was not fresh, the macaroni, yams, and cornbread were dryer than the Sahara Desert. It all seemed like it was warmed up from the previous day, so maybe I shouldn't have gotten there when they first opened. The yellow rice was decent, though.

Never again

I cannot say enough about the food they serve here. It’s fantastic! We had fried shrimp with jerk sauce and baked turkey wings. Both delicious. We drove from Sarasota to eat here, TikTok recommendation, well worth it. Strawberry crunch cake, moist flavorful and not overly sweet. Jerk sauce was top notch. Mango tea was fire. Yellow rice was cooked and seasoned perfectly.Service was friendly and welcoming. Only negative, over priced. I feel if the owner got  her food costs under control she would be unstoppable! We will be back again no doubt.
This place definitely get 4 ☆☆☆☆s. The staff, food & beverages was on point. It was worth the drive & money well spent. They are worth everything they say they were..

formatted_address: 1412 W Waters Ave, Tampa, FL 33604, United States
name: Asher Amens African Cafe

reviews.text: This was my first time trying African food and I was stunned! The food was so flavorful and delicious the plantains were on point and the pounded yam was divine! Would definitely eat here again! Only thing was I was told three meats and I only got two meats and the meats were very small as you can see in the photo… other than that good food.

The vegetables soup was the first thing I tried from this place. It got my taste buds going crazayyy. Love it and I ordered multiple times later on.

Then I orders the egussi soup at least twice, it was soooo delicious. Love it.

Then I order the obono soup and eba ( pounded cassava). Took me by surprise, I did expect the obono soup to be slimy and the eba to be sour. I give the restaurant a call, the owner was so niiice. She said it was suppose to be slimy and cassava is sour because it was my first time. As somebody who hate any food with okra consistency, I was a little mad at first. But when the owner explain to me so nicely, I felt eager to try it. And I Lovee Ittt. I'm going my mother about this, somebody got me an okra consistency meal. Because God knows I absolutely hate Slimy food. But this dish got me loving it.

Then I order the bitter leaf soup. I was youtube video on how to make it. The lady said it was not supposed to be bitter. But it was, absolutely bitter. At first not so much but then it got realllly bitter. I only ate the smoke meat and the fufu.

I also prior to order the bitter leaf soup tried the ayamase soup. My siblings love it and I love it it was sooo delicious.

Still love this place and I definitely look forward to exploring their menu more.

First time having African cuisine and it was a great experience! I had Ogbono soup, Egusu soup, fufu, jollof rice, chicken, goat, beef and a few things I forgot lol. I was with my African friend who showed me the ropes. I really loved the jollof rice with the meats, so much flavor. The ogbono soup was great as well with fufu. The staff is very nice. The hours posted online need to be updated. Hours are Monday-Saturday 11am to 5:30pm. The inside is small so not much seating and no AC, just fans. Overall great experience for my first time.

This was my first time trying African food.....so I will give my honest opinion!
1. Portion size does not match price...I paid $15 for soup and I barely had any juice to dip the fufu in! I feel 3 pieces of meat isn’t worth the price!
2. I was expecting it to be more flavorful not saying that it was bad I feel we could use more seasoning.
3. Fufu tasted like Instant mashed potatoes rolled up in a ball!

So I gave this place 3 stars due to the lack of favor and portions!!

I wish I could give them ZERO STARS ! Literally the worst ! The meat in the Egusi soup was TOUGH, the flavor of the rice was Awful and tasted like metal ! I asked for chicken with my rice and they gave me the toughest beef ever! I’m so disappointed! I didn’t even eat one of the meals we ordered and they still charged! After I mentioned how hard the beef was! Didn’t offer me a new plate or anything ! Do not waste your money ! There’s a big beautiful spacious delicious restaurant right up the street! That serves the same food! GO THERE !

formatted_address: 1606 NW 13th St, Gainesville, FL 32609, United States
name: M&D West African Cuisine

reviews.text: M&D is the best food in Gainesville, and honeslty in the state of Florida. Generous portions of delicious food are always given. The owners are some of the nicest people I’ve met in Gainesville and genuinely care about their customers. I will always make time in my week to pay them a visit, both for their food and kindness!

WOW, WOW, WOW… AMAZING FOOD!! 🥘😋
I decided to try this place today and it was well worth it! They weren’t located at the cricket and moved to the gas station down the road. I order the okra soup with chicken and fufu and it was DELICIOUS. It tastes authentic and the food was ready quick. The lady working there was so nice and welcoming, she gave us samples to try the soups. For the price of $16, you get two servings worth. Amazing food, amazing service, I will DEFINITELY be back!!!
Omg!! We will be back!!! Everything we ordered was beyond delicious! We ate, slept, ate again and slept again! The flavors were sooo good. All I can say is try them! You won't be disappointed!

Really enjoyed their food. The honey suya wings are incredible, and the Egusi soup(stew?) And okra soup were delicious. The wings come with rice, which I declined. The super nice lady at the windows looked at me kinda odd when I said I didn't want rice(carbs). So I asked, "is it deliciously spiced West African rice?" Anyway, it was delicious,  so don't skip the Jollof rice! The flavors and spices are so spot on, in everything we tried! 5 stars!!!
Amazing people with amazing food. High quality soups and addictive rice dishes. Highly recommended. Live long and prosper!!!

formatted_address: 808 N Franklin St Unit 106A, Tampa, FL 33602, United States
name: Nana Street Food

reviews.text: The Chicken shawarma bowl was absolutely delicious. Harissa sauce was what really made it, it added a really nice spice throughout the entire dish.  The owner was super helpful with good advice and pleasant conversation.  We tried the baklava and the creme brulee cheesecake, and the creme blue lay cheesecake was an absolute winner. It may have been the best cheesecake I have ever had.

Food was excellent!!! Everything was flavorful and fresh. The steak shawarma and kofta meatballs were superb. Stratos was so kind and took the time to explain the process and food. He gave wonderful recommendations! Everyone loved the food (which is hard to do with a picky kid in tow - even she was raving!). We left so full and happy.
I’m yum! Love the healthy choices. The hummus was very good. A bowl is enough to share, especially if you get baklava. The staff very friendly answering questions and providing guidance.
Stratos was kind and generous with the portions. Fresh and delicious. Will definitely plan to come back! Ordered the falafel and hummus and salad and lentil soup.

I had an amazing experience at Nana Street Food in Down Town Tampa. Bridgette helped me build my bowl and she was outstanding—very helpful, knowledgeable about the menu, and extremely professional.

The restaurant itself is excellent. The design and style are modern and welcoming, everything was spotless, and the atmosphere was lively yet comfortable. Service was fast and efficient, and the food came out quickly.

Overall, it was a fantastic visit—great food, great team, and a beautiful environment. Highly recommended!

formatted_address: 717 E Martin St Suite 199, Raleigh, NC 27601, United States
name: Hady's Restaurant International Cuisine

reviews.text:
It pains me to do this because I do want to see small business succeed because often poor service by untrained staff tends to be downfall.

Let me just say that this place seems to have a lot of high reviews because most people order and take out food from this restaurant, but our experience was a dine-in one. We drove 45 minutes (from another city) to specifically come eat in this place because it came highly recommended by a friend.

I was a slightly surprised because we were the only people in the entire restaurant. Simply my wife and I. This was around 7:30 PM. Even though I was a little taken back by it; I also understood that this could be normal for a niche restaurant (focused on African cuisine).

Granted that some order clients came sporadically to pick up some takeout orders, the gentleman that was both our hostess and waiter was quite rude. Mind you; we are the ONLY guests in this restaurant. Mind you it’s our first time here, and we want to be guided about the menu and choices. But the young man seemed so impatient and just ready to clock out.

We explicitly told the waiter that we didn’t want spicy food, and wanted options that were non-spicy or mild. Guess what? The food came spicy. After a back and forth with waiter; he went to go get to the chef. The chef came out and started questioning how “sensitive” our palettes and taste buds were because to him the food was not spicy.

Honestly, I was furious at this point. I just ate half of the food that they gave me, but my wife insisted on getting a different dish. But the option she go instead was a dry fish with white rice. No sauce, vegetables, or anything else.

In the end, she took one bit of the fish and we were too mad to continue eating at this place. So we paid $64 for what we got and left. This was an extremely disappointing experience, and I will never be back here.

I’m still giving this place 2-star rating instead of one because the decor and ambiance was nice. The menu options were clearly labeled and visually appealing. The bathrooms were also fairly clean. And there sufficient parking out front. But the staff and service were just so bad.

If the owner(s) ever read this review; I would strongly suggest improving the staff. Because I think you are trying to do something good, but most likely your staff don’t care about your restaurant as much as you do.

AMAZING place to enjoy international cuisine! I have been here multiple times and I continue to go back. Plantain Fufu and Egusi with Goat is to die for! I wish I lived closer but it is worth the hour drive every time. I have told multiple people about this place, they have went and LOVED IT! I wish I could eat their Egusi every day. Get the fried plantains also you will NOT be disappointed they are so sweet! The girl who works in there is very nice she has been my server every time and does a wonderful job. The guy who is sometimes sitting at the register (might be owner or Manager Very tall guy) he is very nice and wonderful to hold a conversation with. They are so kind there and their smiles and friendly ways make you want to come back even though the food is enough to make your mouth water to just think about it

WOW THAT JERK CHICKEN MEAL WAS GOOD! Jerk chicken was spiced so nice. I feel like collards can be hit or miss, but here they were delicious! The plantains were good. We also got the BBQ wings and they were subtle, with a perfect crispy skin. They do bring you bottled water so it might be wise to bring your bottle if that's all you plan on drinking, but it's certainly worth visiting.

Food was fine. The fish didn't taste seasoned, but the  vegetable soup was fine. Meat in every dish except the sides and veggie soup... and prices are $16+ for the soups with a side of fufu or rice, etc. The soups aren't soups! They are more like stews, thick hearty and flavorful. You eat them with your hands and get fufu as the side. Add on sides are $6+ and the waitress will tell you that the fufu that comes with the meal is corn based and not as good and the best is plantain based but it's an upcharge. The upcharge was me paying full price for another side of fufu $6 and not getting the fufu it came with, I don't think they understand how upcharges work, since there was ony a $1 between the 2 types. Ofcourse, there are no refunds so I simply asked for the fufu it would have came with as well. I got a bottle drink that cost $5. Only 1 bathroom per gender in the resturant so I waited through a few people to wash my hands before the meal so it's a cozy place, probably seats 50 people, but it's very nice based on the location. They have a large display upfront that shows pics of the foods and names so you know what it looks like. Waitress was nice as was every staff member I came in contact with. I wouldn't go back as there weren't enough options for me, but I think it's a nice place for someone to try. Expect to pay $20ish. Definitely get the fufu if it's your 1st time eating African cuisine.

Great experience here. The atmosphere was perfect to soak up international music and great food. Everything was cooked fresh. The egusi soup was the perfect mix of spice and savory flavors. Jollof rice with chicken was seasoned to perfection. Mixed reviews on the fufu. It was our first time trying African cuisine so I don’t know if the fufu was prepared traditionally or not. The beef patty was a hit.

The hibiscus drink was delicious. I will try the ginger drink next time. We would definitely return for lunch or dinner.

formatted_address: 406 Blackwell St Suite 100, Durham, NC 27701, United States
name: Ekhaya

reviews.text: Fantastic experience here! Our waiter gave awesome recommendations and the food was delicious. We sat on the patio and it was such a great vibe. We tried a little bit of everything just about and it was all fantastic! Not pictured: oxtails, sausage rolls & sav blanc

Amazing African fusion cuisine in the heart of Downtown Durham. Such a cute little place and within walking distance to DPAC. We loved everything we tried! Started with a delicious mocktail and then the rice bomb and peri peri corn for appetizers. For dinner, we had the Suya chicken kabobs and the Barbere half chicken. Everything was delicious. Cant wait to go back! The only thing that could improve is the service. We had told our waitress we had a show to catch and she seemed to have slowed down even more after hearing that. We waited a really long time for the main course and finally had to remind her before she came rushing out with the items. Service could be a bit better but the food more than makes up for it.

4.5
In short Delicious food at smaller portions for the price..
0.5 for the beignets being not fluffy
But shout out for the fries for being super fluffy.
My favorite was the chicken with peanuts on top for the brunch menú
Heads up you can order only from the brunch or dinner menu
It was nice to sit outside on the patio
Reservations are available
Every dish was enjoyable, the cauliflower curry was a highlight however

Modern take on African cuisine.  Tapas-inspired menu. Not a huge menu list, but the offerings are delicious as well as extremely vegetarian/vegan friendly. We enjoyed the Curried Oxtails with plantain in addition to the Seafood Curry. Both dishes were absolutely delicious! Good portion size and well-seasoned. Ekhaya also has a cocktail and wine list to choose from. My husband enjoyed his Tamarind Old-fashioned while their rosé was quite nice as well. All in all, one of the nicer restaurants in American Tobacco with cuisine you don't find everywhere!

reviews.author_name: The Message LLC The Message LLC
reviews.text: Iam deeply blessed to be a global speaker and food naturally comes with the job. EVERYTHING about the resturant was besutiful. The people, food, and overall atmosphere is something very special. They have built a community establishment that is deeper than just blessed food, they care about the people. The food was the best African food I have personally ever tasted since visiting Kenya. The yellow rice is the best rice I have EVER had in my life! I will FOREVER be grateful I had the experince of this place and I cannot recommend them highly enough, bless yal!

formatted_address: 3520 Capital Blvd, Raleigh, NC 27604, United States
name: Chop Naija Mobile Kitchen & Catering

reviews.text: I’ve been here twice and I gotta say this is the best African Nigerian food I’ve tasted yet. The owners are so nice and the food comes out hot. Equsi soup is my favorite and I will be trying more dishes. 10/10👍🏿. Also the pounded yam fufu and jelloff rice is perfect
As a Nigerian I rate this plate 20/10. I ordered goat , jollof, and puff puff. The food was well spiced and they gave an abundance for the price. Much love I’ll be a re-occurring customer🥂🙏🏾 🇳🇬

I am new to North Carolina and I wanted to try my fiancés native food so I found this lil spot! It’s a lovely food truck nestled in the Corner of the parking lot.. if you don’t know it’s there you could drive right by!
The pictures when I Goggled “Nigerian food near me” was what drew me to this location! I was greeted warmly and I ordered; plantains, Jollof rice , chicken , Egusi soup and fufu! Fast service, they set me up to eat the proper Nigerian way.. I was doing a happy dance with my first bites! It was soooo good! I got to know the owners a bit and enjoyed my beautiful Nigerian lunch .. you took me away with the amazing cuisine, kindness and company ! Good people and good food! Abeg, please try! 🙏

I was excited to try some new Nigerian food but sadly was disappointed. The best part about this dish was the fufu and egusi soup. The meat was dry and bland. The fried chicken wasn’t even fried and tasted like 2 day old chicken, the goat was mostly bone and fat and wasn’t edible. I will not be going here again but the owner was nice, maybe I just got a bad plate.

I really was looking forward to trying this food out so I placed an order on DoorDash. Waited 30 minutes and the store cancelled the order... why confirm it just to cancel it. Very disappointed and frustrated.

formatted_address: 6634 Winding Trail, Raleigh, NC 27612, United States
name: Dounou Cuisine

reviews.text:
The food was OK to good. The table we sat at was awkward it was knee high and made it hard to eat. Very uncomfortable, but we had 6 or more plus 3 kids.
Even though I did enjoy the atmosphere and food, the bill was ridiculous.
It was an OK place charging fine cuisine prices. I've been to a $100 plate place, and although the serving size was tiny, every bite was an experience in flavor.
This place, in my opinion, is overpriced for just OK to good food.

I later found out its a popular hangout for famous celebrities. I guess that explains why they charge so much. I want quality if not quantity for my food. Too often, celebrities spend big bucks without considering the things that little ole me considers.

formatted_address: 406 Blackwell St Suite 100, Durham, NC 27701, United States
name: Zweli's

reviews.text: I had my first experience with Zimbabwean cuisine recently. The vegan options were clearly marked on the menu, which was a plus, and the portion sizes were satisfying. However, the food itself was just okay—nothing that really stood out. I might consider coming back if I were in a pinch, but it's not a place that left a lasting impression.

First time there and the location was partially big. I recommend going Tuesday at lunch its not crowded then and you are sure to be served good. We ordered the ox tails, sausage, and Beef Samosas (comes with a ranch or mayonnaise based sauce really couldn't tell which one it was). With a side of Jolla fries and Chakalaka. The jello price in my opinion was not spicy enough. I had to request a a spicy piri to put in it to get it to be spicy worthy. Some the entires are kinda on the pricy side so I wouldn't recommend eating here all the time but would say it is a good date night space.

P.S if you take out its a little cheaper.

This location seems to have undergone a very nice remodel. The old photos don't look anything like what it looks like now, it's much nicer.
The staff was super friendly and helped us navigate the menu (which is minimal which I like). They said that in order to foster the tradition of family style sharing, you can pick two sides to be "bottomless" for the whole table. I like the idea of not just saying the food should be shared around the table, but actually helping make that happen by providing bottomless sides.
Now to the food - what an experience!! I haven't had food like this before, and was instantly in love with each thing I tried. This is a must visit for anyone who wants to expand their tastes.

Located just a few blocks from the bus station there's easy access. We hopped on the bus station near our house and took it to the terminal (I love Durham's free bus system, it's so easy) and then walked a few minutes to Zweli's. I recommend this restaurant for anyone who wants a unique experience and wants to support a great local restaurant doing things right!

The food was fantastic. I was a little shy on the goat, but I was very surprised. The food was amazing. You must have the plantains also. The service was great also. They made you feel wanted and were happy you were there. Thank You all. Oh by the way they do add on the tip automaticly with an option to tip more when you pay.

their peri peri shrimp skewers were pretty good and the cabbage was amazing (though I'm easy to please when it comes to cabbage, so take that as you will) but wasn't a huge fan of other dishes. everything was good but not great. peanut butter sauce was a little too sweet in my opinion and they really drowned the collards in it. definitely worth a try if you're coming through the area but I just can't justify the price enough to want to come back.

formatted_address: 910 W Main St, Durham, NC 27701, United States
name: Goorsha

reviews.text: This was our second time trying Ethiopian food, and we’re getting more used to the slightly sour wrap and the unique flavors of the main dishes. The sides—Gomen and Misir Alecha—were tasty, but the real highlights were the entrées. The Gored Gored beef and Awaze Tibbs lamb were well seasoned, tender, and juicy. The Shrimp Awaze was a bit spicier than our usual preference, but still enjoyable when eaten with the wrap.

B: the food tasted fresh and the portions were great. The beef was so tender that it felt buttery when you picked it up. It was my first time trying Ethiopian food and was pleasantly surprised with the spice similarities to my own culture! The environment was very welcoming and the staff were attentive.

The portions are incredibly small for what you pay. Ordered Doro Wat, and it came with a singular chicken leg, one boiled egg, and the rest in sauce. With tax and tip it comes out to well over $25 per person. Imagine eating one chicken leg and one egg when you order an entree for dinner.
Vegan entrees were a little better, but still the main dish to injera ratio is way skewed to just eating bread to fill up.
Don’t even get apps, literally one bite for $10.

The food tastes great. Every bite is delicious. But I can’t stress how terrible the portion sizes are at this place for what you pay.

Service is slow as well, no one came to check in on the diners, they clearly have their favorite customers. No water refills. Other tables have to ask for refills. Had to ask the servers for a check.

Overall one of the lackluster Ethiopian restaurants I’ve been to. This place is way overhyped on Eater and other restaurant guides online. Only saving grace is that they’re the only Ethiopian joint in the area.

Came for lunch with a coworker, and we're waited on by the owner, Fasil. Such a genuinely nice guy, and you could absolutely see the pride he had for us to be his customers. There aren't many places you can go and encounter the actual owner AND their appreciation for your business.

We started with Sambusas and Deko sauce. Savory and simple, but the Deko was an incredible touch. I had the Zilzil Alecha, and it was absolutely tender, savory, and decadent. I'm not even sure what my coworker got, but we both were absolutely satisfied with the app and lunch.

Will definitely be back! I've been wanting to get Ethiopian for the longest time, and I am NOT disappointed. Amazing!

Loved the food and the flavor was great! The kashka could have had more meat on it but the flavors were great. I was greeted and sat by a very friendly man and he checked back with me at the end of the meal which was really nice. The service was okay, but could have been in and out a bit quicker.i think my server didn’t notice me because I was tucked away in a corner -not complaining about the corner that’s right where I want to be. I ordered a cherry gin drink (can’t remember the name), and the flavor was good but it was pretty warm so it had a bit more bite that I was expecting. Overall the food is great but I do agree with some other reviews that the portions and service could be a bit better for the price.

formatted_address: 3600 N Duke St #35, Durham, NC 27704, United States
name: Gifted Hands Cuisine

reviews.text: Very good. Tried with my bestie & was sooo good for my first time trying fufu. I am Hard of hearing and when the lady asked if it was good I said No bc I thought She was asking if I wanted more lol 🤣.  I didnt realize until my friend told me after.  I am Pregnant and my baby enjoyed it too. 💗🤗 check them out!

So, we took a trip over to Gifted Hands on N. Duke St. (Used to be Golden Crust) to try out their food.  As I’ve stated before, I usually go to Hady’s Restaurant International Cuisine to get my African food because they have the best African food and awesome service. I do realize that they are from Senegal at Hady’s. I think they are from Nigeria at Gifted Hands. But let me tell you this, I have never received the type of service that I received at this place. Now, I have to extend them some grace because they seemed to have a party going on when we went in to order, and it was loud. With that being said, the first item I ordered wasn’t available and neither were 3 out of the 4 swallows. Ok, that’s fine. Now, I ordered 2 full plates and a side of Jollof rice. This is what I got for $70.78. Not even a full bowl if you combine both meals. I saw the amount of food that was placed in the bowls and I asked if that was the full serving. She said yes. I am so disappointed. When I got home, the food was cold and I had to microwave it. I haven’t even tried the food yet and I am pretty sure I will not be returning to Gifted Hands unless they correct their portion sizes. I feel like I was cheated. This would never have happened at Hady’s. Here it is. Judge for yourself. Now, mind you, the bowls are already smaller than most places. Smh. Now, I won’t say anything about the flavors of the food because people make food differently in different countries. However I will say this, I am a Jollof rice connoisseur. I love it. No matter how many spices you use, you can tell when the rice has been burned. My Jollof rice was burned. It smelled burned. It tasted burnt. 😢 My experience with Gifted Hands was underwhelming.

Delicious food and professional staff. I got okra soup and egusi soup with extra meat, and a beef patty. They were absolutely wonderful, and I will be going back.  There are just two considerations I'd recommend keeping in mind if you come.  First, definitely get extra meat with your soup (as I did) if you want a good amount of protein, as the "default" is just one piece of meat, which can be a large percentage of bone depending on which type of meat you order (and luck of the draw). Second, expect a wait similar to a sit- down restaurant-- this isn't the place for fast food.  But given how much time and energy these dishes take to cook at home,  I'm happy to wait in one of comfortable booths rather than be the one in the kitchen. I'm looking forward to going again and bringing friends.

Please do not eat here. The food is overpriced and does not taste good at all.  I usually go to Hady’s in Raleigh for egusi and fufu and after eating here that’s exactly where I will continue going.  They barely put any soup in the bowl and the chicken was not edible at all. It was hard, dry and rubbery. The beef in the other soup was hard as well.  It was all old. I had to wait another 15 minutes for the fufu and the balls were small.  My fiancé got jollof rice with his plate and it was disgusting. It tasted burnt. I was so angry that I spent $70 on food we could barely eat. Just ridiculous. Never ever ever again. I don’t even know how they are still in business.

I've only been during visits to Durham and the consistency is what I like. I don't think you can ever go wrong with a delicious mash up of Caribbean and African foods. AMAZING 🤏🏾
I was also able to get supplements there like vitters and elderberry.

formatted_address: 904 NE Maynard Rd, Cary, NC 27513, United States
name: Awaze Ethiopian Eritrean Cuisine

reviews.text: This was my second visit to Awaze Ethiopian Eritrean Cuisine, and once again, their food did not disappoint. Everything tastes incredibly fresh, yet it's bursting with flavor. I don't remember the exact names of the dishes we ordered, but you can see them in the photos. The presentation was appealing, and the food tasted even better than it looked. The decor adds a nice touch to the overall experience. The service is decent—not outstanding, but it didn't take away from the experience. I highly recommend giving this place a try!

What can I say about Awaze Ethiopian Eritrean Cuisine? Amazing food. This was my first time eating Ethiopian food, and I was blown away. From the minute I entered the restaurant, a friendly waitress greeted me; she was extremely friendly and answered all my questions. I ordered a meat sampler and was amazed at how well the dish tasted. The spicy sauces blended exceptionally well. I also ordered the Lamb Awaze tips. The lamb was incredibly tender. It's hands down the best food I’ve tried in NC. Take it from me: do yourself a favor and give this restaurant a shot.

The experience has been wonderful every time I visited. The food has been phenomenal. The first visit, I ordered the kitfo. It was prepared clean, and the injera accompanied and complemented it perfectly. It was my very first exposure to Ethiopian food when I had first went, and I did not know what to expect. However, after the first visit, I was very impressed and I came a second time - which is the time of writing my current review.

It’s safe to say, there was a reason I went back. I am glad I did. The service is wonderful, and they do not rush you. The presentation, as showcased in my photos, are dreamy.

I highly recommend Awaze and I am planning on coming back again!

Came to Awaze from Greensboro because we were missing Ethiopian food. The experience didn’t disappoint. Food was delicious and service was great. Highly recommend other folks check them out. For anyone that is new to the cuisine I recommend getting the platters that way you can try a little bit of everything. We normally get a veggie platter and a meat entree.

Ok place in a convenient location. Food tasted a bit bland unfortunately and service is a bit slow. It was a bit busy which I guess is understandable. The mist important factor is the food was not as good that tasty, kind of sick if flavors than what I am used to compared to other Ethiopia place. Staff is friendly though.

formatted_address: 1701 Gorman St, Raleigh, NC 27606, United States
name: By the fireside Cuisine

formatted_address: 800 Shady Summit Way, Raleigh, NC 27603, United States
name: Adonai Waakye

reviews.text: This meal is a full experience. You can tell the food was prepared like a work of art. It tastes sooooo good. The platter was such a generous amount. I rarely leave reviews but had to for Adonai Waakye!
One of the best Waakye I’ve ever had. Every time I’m in town, I always make sure to get some to go back home with. Amazing customer service also, you won’t be disappointed

I ordered 4 for my family. The waakye tastes so good. Both my husband and mother in law wanted more. The waakye stew is the best hands down. I absolutely appreciate how everything was neatly packaged. I thoroughly enjoyed my meal 😉. Fish was well-seasoned, the meat was just right. Excellent customer service. I am very picky with what I eat and how it's presented; Adonai waakye was spot on!

I had the best time at dinner when I ordered waakye from the Adonai team. The food was well cooked, tasted yummy and well packaged. The Adonai team deserves much kudos. I will definitely be back soon!

I'm a bit of a Waakye connoisseur. And for someone who has since moved back to Ghana, Adonai Waakye is still some of the best waakye I've had, period.
Do yourself a favor and order some. It'll give you a taste that is authentically, Ghanaian.

formatted_address: 5720 Capital Blvd c, Raleigh, NC 27616, United States
name: Hady's Restaurant International Cuisine

reviews.text: "I recently had Dinner at the Hady Restaurant located in downtown and I must say that the experience was exceptional. The fufu dish with oxtail was simply delicious! The texture of the fufu was perfectly made, and the oxtail was tender and tasty, impregnated with spices that really awakened my taste buds. The service was equally remarkable, with friendly and attentive staff who helped make our meal even more enjoyable. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking to discover authentic and quality international cuisine. I will go back without hesitation!" So glad for the new location . And congratulations to the owner .
I visited Hady’s restaurant international cuisine 2 years ago. When I went there today the food still the same. Good work keep it up
I always eat at HADY’s. I’m glad now they’re closer to my house. I will visit more
The food is great and the staff are very friendly !!
Great food, great customer service

formatted_address: 2119 S Elm-Eugene St, Greensboro, NC 27406, United States
name: Kingdom Cafe African Restaurant, Greensboro NC

reviews.text: 🥰I got a chance to finally get a taste of this great food. The owners are beautiful awesome people. It didn’t start off well when I first visited, but I’m more than glad and so happy that I’m able to change this review. The food was spectacular. Do not go to MamaPutts!  Come here to eat. this place needs to show every African restaurant owner here in Greensboro how to cook the food was really really good. It was delicious. Customer Service was top-notch.! This was well worth the wait! Please guys come here if you live in the Winston-Salem Greensboro area this food was awesome!♥️ thank you God for allow me to experience this🥰🥰🥰🥰!…
I'm still waiting to try the agusi and pounded yam but I have tried the okra soup and fufu and it was my first African dish. I liked it.. I recommend it if you love good African dishes

I LOVE THEIR FOOD!! The owners are super friendly and make sure they provide you with quality food. I'm looking forward to trying everything on their menu! I would highly recommend this place if you want a taste of African cuisine.

Could you please clarify if you are still in business? Every time I call, you’re always closed, and it’s very frustrating for us as consumers who enjoy your food. Please improve your operations or reconsider running a restaurant if you’re unable to manage it properly. Thank you.
This place is a hidden gem. The couple that owns the restaurant were super sweet and helpful to a first timer like me. Food was so good and super authentic. Definitely will be coming back!

formatted_address: 3540 Maitland Dr, Raleigh, NC 27610, United States
name: Carolina International Mart

reviews.text: The woman at the counter is very lovely and nice. The store is always stocked and clean. I travel 2 1/2 hours just to come here and it's worth it Everytime!! Fish and Goat meat is very fresh!
Very pocket-friendly and fair prices compared to other Africam stores I have been to. I love the variety of items to choose from. Friendly staff too.
New location, bigger store. Looks alot better. Have been waiting for them to relocate for some time now. They are always friendly. Well organized store.
Nice collection of tasty snacks and drinks. I do have to commend the cashier, I was about to spend 10 bucks on a candy pack and she brought it up. She recommended other things that were great.
Serene environment. Polite staffs and good arrangement of items.

formatted_address: 1306 Fayetteville St, Durham, NC 27707, United States
name: New Visions of Africa

reviews.text: Staff is friendly & very helpful. The feeding program there is awesome. community dinners served 1 Saturday of each month, afterschool snacks daily ,as well as supper and pm snacks for sites around the city. Big ups to Mr. Kasib Abdullah for all he does in this community.
It seems as if they operate as a community bread box center. Oh yes! They have free bread on Sundays at 1:30. I don't think the donations or government funds ate being used properly.
No food. No masjid. Rent out the community center for jumuah. No daily salah. Mention of a community food pantry.
it's not a restaurant  anymore .he do hand outs meals for free from 3-6 mon-fri
No money for food!

formatted_address: Please look location on the streets foodfinder, 880 E Chatham St, Cary, NC 27511, United States
name: Ethiopian food truck Merkato cafe’

reviews.text: This was my first time trying Ethiopian food and the lovely owner suggested the Merkato special so I could get alittle taste of everything. This food is AMAZING!!!! So incredible flavorful and a great portion of food. I devoured my plate lol.  Definitely check them out.

Merkato was so good! My friend recommended we try it and I’m so glad we did. The husband and wife cooking are so incredibly kind. Our food was so good and were really nice portion sizes. I could eat those red lentils with injera everyday. Can’t wait to go again!

My husband brought me the veggie plate on a whim one day and I’ve not stopped thinking about it. I’ve since located the truck twice and have gotten additional items including the very delicious chickpea dish. I’m 30 weeks pregnant and cannot get enough!!! Highly recommend. The owners are also super accommodating and kind. Can’t wait to have again and again!

I was excited to try this food since it’s hard to find in Raleigh. I tried the food truck at Tap Yard. The food was fresh, hot, and comforting. I got a few veggies with the chicken, which was seasoned really well. The owner came to check to see how the food was, which was very nice. 😊 I’d definitely recommend.

My husband loves Ethiopian food and was super excited to finally try this food truck since it had amazing reviews. It also has been hard for us to catch it. Unfortunately, I am supremely disappointed in this first (and probably only) visit. I was told a 20-30min wait for our food. My family and I waited inside Fortnight for 30ish minutes before coming back outside to grab our food. We were then told, it’s coming we are next. We decided to wait outside thinking we were really next. We waited another 30min outside before I went back up to the window to check on our food. I was told again, we were next. I asked how much longer and mentioned we had been waiting already for an hour. He then told me 10min more. As we waited more, I noticed he told everyone who ordered 20-30min and everyone who came back up to check on their food that they were “next” or that there were only 4-5 orders ahead of them. When we finally got our food, I noted that we had waited 96min for our food.

I had my young toddler with me and regretted ordering when the wait times given were not realistic or true at all. I drove 20min out of my way to try this food truck. Lastly, the food portions were super tiny compared to the price, making this an expensive to-go meal☹️

formatted_address: 2945 S Miami Blvd Ste 102, Durham, NC 27703, United States
name: Abol Ethiopian Restaurant

reviews.text:
Delicious authentic Ethiopian food. We shared the Doro Wat (very spicy chicken dish) and Veggie Combo. Both were fabulous. The flavors were rich, complex and spiced just right. The servings were very large and provided lunch the next day. The traditional bread was delicious and perfect for scooping up everything.

The service was great, our server was very sweet, patient and helpful in guiding is through the menu.

The atmosphere is not great, very basic, like a sandwich shop. I wish they would upgrade, add nicer tables and chairs and decor to make things cozier.

Would I return for the food, absolutely! I highly recommend this spot for great authentic Ethiopian food.

Abol Ethiopian Restaurant: The Taste of True Ethiopia
Wow, just wow. I had to write this review immediately because my experience at Abol Ethiopian Restaurant was genuinely incredible.
The food is so delicious it’s unbelievable!
I have tried Ethiopian food before, but this was the first time I felt like I was eating the real deal. This restaurant sets the standard for authenticity. Every dish, from the deeply flavorful stews to the fresh, tangy injera, felt crafted with passion and traditional expertise.
I especially loved the sheer depth of flavor in the Key Wat (spicy beef stew) and the creamy, perfectly spiced texture of the Misir Wot (red lentils). The whole platter was a colorful, aromatic feast.
If you are looking for an authentic culinary experience and crave truly delicious, complex flavors, you must visit Abol Ethiopian Restaurant. Stop searching—you've found the real Ethiopian food you've been hoping for! I can't wait to go back.

I was visiting family from out of town and had a craving for Ethiopian food, so gave this place a try. It was sooo yummy and flavorful!

We got the meat and veggie combo, which allows you to taste a bit of everything. The meat portions were big too, so we had some leftovers to take home. Each item tasted unique and nothing was overly spicy. My favorite was the lega tibs!

This is a legit hidden gem and I would recommend it to both Ethiopian food lovers and people interested in trying the cuisine — the combo is easily shared among 4 people.

Stopped by for lunch today. Wasn’t disappointed. My meal was probably the best Ethiopian food I have eaten outside of the DC area. I ordered Lega Tibs and Tikil Gomen, both had generous servings and great flavors. Service was quick and attentive too! I will definitely return!

They are located in an unassuming strip mall but the inside does not match the outside. Once you walk in, you’re hit with wonderful smells and a beautiful space that wants you to sit down. The staff are super nice and the food comes out fast and fresh. Gorgeous colors, wonderful aromas and even better on the tastebuds. And the amount of food you get for the money is an added bonus. They’re somewhat new (only open 4 months), but they’re doing it all correctly. I will be back.

formatted_address: 3815 Hillsborough St, Raleigh, NC 27607, United States
name: Albaraka Mediterranean Market and Grill

reviews.text: The food was surprisingly good. Products on the shelves were non-expired with zero dust on them (like so many other similar stores I have been to). The butcher section was absolutely the best. I’m buying all my meats from here. Customer service was excellent. A young cashier was so pleasant and courteous. The only negative is the strong smell of perfumes they sell in the corner. The smell is so strong it nearly burned my eyes and I hurried to eat my food inside. I have many friends who would not tolerate eating inside with the very strong smell of perfumes.

I had a wonderful experience at Albaraka. The authentic Mediterranean flavors really stood out especially the chicken shawarma and kabob dishes, which were flavorful and well-seasoned. The menu has a nice variety, including wraps, bowls, desserts almost everything.
The staff were friendly and welcoming, and the atmosphere was relaxed. While a few items could be improved, overall I found the food delicious, fresh, and reasonably priced. Highly Recommended.

This is what we call food for the soul - SOUL FOOD!

In Short:
● Reasonable Prices
● Good portion sizes (especially the chicken Shawarma).
● Calm and clean environment.
● Desserts: Phenomenal! (Unfortunately I only took 1 picture of the Dubai chocolate dessert that I absolutely "annihilated", but the lotus cup and the tiramisu along with the other desserts are also VERY good!)

The place is so good I keep it for when I want to treat myself (which, recently, has been nearly every other day). Everytime I head out, I find myself coming here not just for the food but also for the environmental warmth.

Definitely Recommended!

I absolutely love their food every time I visit. The experience is always outstanding, not just because the food is always piping hot and freshly made, but also because of the incredible hospitality and care we receive. If I ever want to impress someone with great food, a calm ambiance, and a perfect restaurant choice, I always choose Al Baraka. The environment is soothing, the food is top-class, and it’s truly my go-to place — always!
Calm supermarket with good food. Recommend the chicken shawarma combo and don’t forget the sweets and bev ✌️🤩

formatted_address: 9650 Strickland Rd, Raleigh, NC 27615, United States
name: Sassool

reviews.text: We had a great experience catering with Sassool for our wedding event. The food was delicious, we got many compliments. It was prepared and set up nicely and on time. They were easy to work with and everything went smoothly at a reasonable price. The staff did a great job replenishing food for our large number of guests. Would highly recommend to anyone needing catering for their event.

Casual atmosphere, friendly staff, and the best Mediterranean food I have had! Salads are super fresh and there is abundance of choices! Hot bar is no different! I suggest checking the website for daily specials and trying to have a ballpark idea of what you want before you get there! We had the spinakopita with the Mediterranean chicken salad and mjadarah, and the salmon over curry rice with kale salad and butternut squash salad. Added a side of hummus and hubs went back for dessert!  Everything was so good and so full of flavor, and portion sizes are big so we have lunch for tomorrow!

Sassool checks all my boxes for a flavorful, nourishing Lebanese Mediterranean meal. I've heard high praises about their delicious meals and decided to order delivery this afternoon. The portions are generous and the meals are so nutritious and flavorful. I decided on the Pick 4 and chose the roasted beet salad, falafel, jalapeño cilantro hummus and Mediterranean chicken salad. I also ordered a chicken kabob with greens. The jalapeño cilantro hummus and pita was a hit for me. The roasted beet salad with mint leaves was so flavorful ! The falafel was tasty but could have been warmer. Everything was perfect and I have food leftover for tomorrow. I also ordered a cheesecake as a treat for later.

It’s a week later and I had a craving again! I ordered the veggie lasagna with beet salad and jalapeño hummus again. This time I had a berry tart for dessert. Everything was perfect again! The vegetable lasagna was so filling and delicious. The tart was delicious !!!!! Packed with so much tart fruit filling!!!!!
Had a really delicious and healthy meal here. There is so much to chose from. All freshly prepared. Even the desserts, they are not too sweet and tasty.

Fantastic selection for vegans/ vegetarians. I always get the pick 4 platter and it’s so hard to pick just 4 items. I love their baba ghanoush so always have to get that, but deciding on the other sides is very hard since they’re all delicious.
My son had the schwarma and said it was the best meal he’s ever had. Now he wants to eat there once a month!

formatted_address: 3721 Sumner Blvd, Raleigh, NC 27616, United States
name: Swahili Grill

reviews.text: Swahili food was really good! I had the Goat Curry, white rice and fries. Service was excellent and the restaurant is very clean. The cooks had no issue showing us what they had and offered us a sample if we wanted. The only downsize was the portion for the price. $15 is a bit hefty for this amount of food, I was expecting a bit more. Overall great experience!!

Nice spot, good was excellent and the service and people were awesome. This was the first time eating here and I will definitely be back. I had the fish with plantain and rice and it was totally incredible. I definitely recommend

What a great experience!  If you're looking for a tasty meal and you enjoy a diverse palette, Swahili Grill is the answer. Everything tasted AMAZING! Ask for a sample if you're between menu choices,  The hospitable folks here will gladly oblige. I had the chicken stew, rice, and spinach.  My coworkers had the curry goat, plantains, and the whole fried tilapia. I sampled the grilled chicken which was also AMAZING! It's where the old Moe's was outside Triangle Town Center mall, a must eat in Raleigh!!

My husband and I ate here for  the first time and everything was great!! The food was fresh, hot and very flavorful.   I had: KuKu Choma (Grilled chicken) with Mbazi and Pilau Rice!!.  He had: Mombasa style Tilapia (Grilled Tilapia with tomato sauce) with Pilau Rice and Plantains!!!.  If you are looking to try something different but good, then this is a place you should visit!!

The food was a delight! Ordered the beef stew with coconut spinach and rice...my wife had the grilled beef with plantains and coconut black eyed peas. Delicious! The staff is cool...will definitely return!

formatted_address: 207 S McNeill St, Carthage, NC 28327, United States
name: Jollof and Company

reviews.text: Absolutely amazing food! The jollof rice was flavorful and perfectly cooked — my husband said it’s the best he’s ever had (and we’ve tried a lot!). The hibiscus (zobo) drink reminded me of home, and I decided to try the abula for the first time — wow, so so good! Everything was 10/10. Highly recommend Jollof and Company

I had the pleasure of having Jollof and Company cater my jobs luncheon and it was so easy to work with Seyi. She was so responsive and helpful from the time I initially reached out. The catering was for 75-100 folks and the food was delivered early. Seyi confirmed with me the day of and also provided to go containers. Customer services was 10/10!

The delivery service was exceptional with flavor-rich dishes. I ordered jollof rice, egunsi (melon soup), asun (peppered goat) & gizdodo and my taste buds were happy. Not too spicy and rightly done!. The business owner was very warm, professional and pleasant to work with. She communicated clearly what to expect and I was not disappointed.

If you have a catering need and you want yummy food for your guests, then jollof & company is your go to! Excited to place another order soon!

Attended Jollof and Chill event and what a vibe! Champagne as soon as we walked in, and amazing food and drinks! Saxophonist was playing throughout and the authentic story telling really added to the memorable experience. We waited to see the menu to add to the experience- highly recommend! Food was tasty, and perfect size- we definitely left super full ! We were on the fence about attending, and I’m so glad we decided to go for our date night!
The jollof was delicious and the beef was flavorful and tender. Also got puff puff, which was fresh out the fryer. Will definitely be ordering again!

formatted_address: 1625 Stanley Rd, Greensboro, NC 27407, United States
name: MamaPut Afrikana Restaurant & Kitchen

reviews.text: If I could give 0 stars I would. I do not eat meat, I am allergic to certain meats so I called this place and spoke with a woman. I asked, are your soups cooked with meat in them. She answered you have to buy your protein separately. I said I understand that but I can’t eat meat so is the egusi cooked with any meat and she replied no, there is no meat in it. I drove 1.5 hour and When I get there I ask her again, is there any meat already in the egusi soup ?  I asked what about the vegetable soup and She replied no it does not have any meat in either one. I purchase both the egusi soup and the vegetable soup, drive home and begin eating the egusi. At first look you cannot tell there are chunks of meat because the egusi is chunky but as I begin to continue eating I begin having an allergic reaction. In a panic I begin searching the egusi and sure enough there is chunks of meat in it , I begin checking the vegetable soup and there are also chunks of meat in it. I immediately call the restaurant and speak with the same lady. I asked why is there meat in both the egusi soup and vegetable soup. I asked you multiple times and you said that it was not cooked with meat in it. She says that is not what I said, she says I said you buy your meat separately and I said ,  no I asked you multiple times was there any meat in the soups I was planning to buy and you straight up told me no. Knowing that there was meat in them. She says you have to tell us that you are allergic to meat and we will tell you that there is meat in all of our dishes. How insane is that? Is me asking is there meat in the soup and saying I CANT EAT MEAT not enough.
